title: Jannik Sinner withdraws from the US Open with knee injury
dek: The world No. 1 pulls out of the year's final Grand Slam after failing to recover in time from the injury that has sidelined him since Wimbledon.
body: Jannik Sinner has pulled out of the US Open. The world No. 1 announced on Instagram that a right knee injury he picked up at Wimbledon has not healed in time for the year's final Grand Slam, ending days of speculation over his fitness.

"Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year," Sinner wrote. "I am of course very sad and disappointed, because New York has a special place in my heart."

The 25-year-old Italian has not played a match since successfully defending his Wimbledon title last month, beating Alexander Zverev in the final. The same knee problem, managed with his medical team in Milan, had already forced him out of the National Bank Open in Canada and the Cincinnati Masters, the two big hard-court tune-up events ahead of Flushing Meadows.

It is the first Grand Slam Sinner has missed since he made his major debut at the 2019 US Open, a run stretching back through his rise to No. 1. He won the title in New York in 2024 and returned to the final last year, where he lost to Carlos Alcaraz.

According to the ATP and US Open organizers, Sinner is the twelfth player to withdraw from the 2026 US Open singles fields since the initial entry lists were released, underlining how heavily the packed post-Wimbledon hard-court swing has taken its toll this season.

His absence reshapes the men's draw at Flushing Meadows, where Alcaraz arrives as the defending champion after beating Sinner in last year's final and will now be the clear favorite without his fiercest rival in the field.

There is no confirmed timeline yet for Sinner's return. His team has indicated the focus for now is on rehabilitation, with the Asian hard-court swing in the autumn seen as a more realistic target for a comeback.

title: Tom Simkhaev wins bronze as Israel post record haul at judo's World Cadet Championships
dek: The 66kg specialist beat Georgia's Giorgi Avaliani for the men's team's first medal of the tournament in Guayaquil, as Israel finished fifth in the overall standings.
body: Tom Simkhaev delivered Israel's third medal of the World Cadet Championships in Guayaquil, Ecuador, taking bronze in the men's up-to-66kg division and giving the men's team its first podium finish of the tournament.

The 18-year-old won the bronze-medal contest against Georgia's Giorgi Avaliani, capping a strong run through the draw that included victories over opponents from Argentina, Colombia and Kazakhstan before he fell in the semi-final.

It capped a record championships for Israeli judo's youngest national team. Three medals and fifth place in the overall team standings is, by the federation's own reckoning, the country's best-ever finish at the under-18 world championships.
Simkhaev's bronze followed two earlier medals won by Israeli judoka during the week, making his the third of the tournament and the first specifically credited to the men's squad.
There was also a near-miss for Yali Yahav, who fought her way to fifth place in the women's up-to-52kg category, narrowly missing out on a fourth Israeli medal in Ecuador.

Shani Hershko, head coach of Israel's national judo teams, praised the performance: "Tom Simkhaev joined today with a bronze medal in the up-to-66kg division, following an excellent day of competition with quality wins and an impressive showing throughout. This is the team's third medal at the championships, and the first for the men's team."

The result adds another name to a judo program that has produced Olympic and world medals at senior level in recent years, and offers an early signal of the depth coming through Israel's youth ranks ahead of future junior and senior competition.

title: "I asked myself if I was still worthy": Dolgopyat on the crisis behind his third European gold
dek: The Israeli floor exercise champion tells Ynet how a fall and a barren year of enforced exile shook his confidence, before he beat back a new generation to win gold again in Zagreb

verificationSources.label: Haaretz — Dolgopyat takes third gold in European Gymnastics Championships
Israel National News — Israel's Dolgopyat wins third European title in floor exercise

body: Artem Dolgopyat stood on top of the podium in Zagreb last Friday with his third European floor exercise title around his neck, but in a special interview with Ynet he admitted how close he had come to believing he no longer belonged there at all.
"I experienced a crisis," the Olympic champion said, describing the period after a fall at last year's European Championships. "I had doubts about my abilities. I asked myself if I was still worthy."

The doubt was compounded by circumstance rather than form alone. Dolgopyat went almost half a year without a competition after Israeli gymnasts were barred from October's World Championships in Jakarta, when the Indonesian government refused to issue them visas and the Court of Arbitration for Sport rejected the Israeli federation's urgent appeal to overturn the decision — a saga the IOC itself condemned as a breach of the Olympic Charter.

He opened the new season by winning floor gold at the World Cup in Cottbus, Germany, a result that quietly answered some of the questions he had been asking himself in private. Zagreb was the one that mattered more.

The final did not go cleanly. On his first tumbling pass, Dolgopyat's heels landed outside the boundary of the mat, the kind of mistake that has cost him major finals before. This time he composed himself through the rest of the routine and posted 14.466, enough to hold off a neutral athlete, Arsenii Dukhno, on 14.333, and Britain's Harry Hepworth, who took bronze with 14.300.

It was Dolgopyat's third European floor title, to go with the ones he won in 2020 and 2022, and it extended one of the more remarkable records in Israeli sport: across Olympic, World and European floor finals he now has 12 medals, and not one of them is bronze — only gold or silver.

The total matches the seven European medals collected by his mentor and predecessor Alex Shatilov, though Dolgopyat's haul is the purer of the two: three golds and four silvers, against a mixed collection for Shatilov that included bronze finishes.

At 29, he was candid about what has changed. Gymnasts he now considers "kids" throw skills reflexively that once separated him from the field, he said, and staying at the top has become a matter of much more careful management of his body and his training load around each element, not just raw execution. He will be 31 by the time of the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, and said he has not yet met the qualifying standard for that Games — a process that continues at a qualifying event in China next year.

Asked about the enduring Israeli argument over who is the country's greatest athlete, sharpened this year by Deni Avdija's breakout season and his selection as the first Israeli NBA All-Star, Dolgopyat waved away any need to choose. "He's the greatest in basketball, I'm the greatest in gymnastics," he said. "He's the most successful in his sport, I am in mine."

For now, he said, the plan is simple: the World Championships in Rotterdam are next on the calendar, and after a year in which merely getting to compete was not guaranteed, he is not taking a start line for granted.

title: How much will it cost to watch Peretz face Solomon in the League Cup?
dek: Southampton and West Ham meet at St Mary's on Tuesday with Daniel Peretz and Manor Solomon on opposite sides, and ONE has priced up what fans will pay to be there

verificationSources.label: Southampton FC - Saints to host the Hammers in the Carabao Cup

body: Two Israeli internationals will find themselves on opposite ends of the pitch on Tuesday night when Southampton host West Ham United in the second round of the League Cup at St Mary's Stadium, and ONE has taken a look at what it will actually cost supporters to be in the stands for it.

Goalkeeper Daniel Peretz starts the season as a Southampton player in his own right after his loan from Bayern Munich was converted into a permanent four-year deal over the summer. Across town in the away dugout's colours will be Manor Solomon, the winger who left Tottenham Hotspur for West Ham in a deal worth roughly £7 million ahead of the new campaign.

Both clubs come into the tie from the Championship, having been relegated from the Premier League, and both are chasing an immediate return to the top flight — which gives an otherwise routine early-season cup fixture an extra edge, since one side's involvement in the competition ends here.

Kick-off is set for 7:45pm local time at St Mary's, with the winner advancing to the third round of a competition that both promotion-chasing clubs would happily go deep in without it derailing their league campaigns.

According to figures from the ticket resale tracker SeatPick cited by ONE, prices for the match vary sharply depending on where in the ground a fan wants to sit. The cheapest tickets start at around $35, standard seats run between roughly $143 and $145, and premium hospitality-style seating can climb as high as $1,400.

As with any resale marketplace, prices are subject to shift with demand in the days before kick-off, and fans are advised to check the authenticity of tickets bought outside official club channels before parting with their money.

For Israeli football followers, the fixture offers a rare early-season novelty: two national team teammates renewing their rivalry in English football's supporting cup competition, with Peretz between the posts for the hosts and Solomon looking to add to his lively start in West Ham colours.
facts: Southampton host West Ham United in the League Cup (Carabao Cup) second round at St Mary's Stadium on Tuesday, 25 August 2026, kick-off 7:45pm.

title: Beitar Nordia Jerusalem post a fifth straight annual deficit, this time 766,000 shekels
dek: The fan-owned club, three tiers below its more famous namesake, saw expenses outstrip income by more than three-quarters of a million shekels in 2025 despite deep salary cuts, financial statements reported by ONE show.

verificationSources.label: English Wikipedia — Agudat Sport Nordia Jerusalem

body: Beitar Nordia Jerusalem closed the 2025 calendar year with a deficit of 766,208 shekels, according to the association's financial statements as reported by ONE — the fifth consecutive year the fan-owned Jerusalem club has finished in the red.
The numbers show total income of 2,523,039 shekels against total expenses of 3,289,247 shekels, leaving the gap of roughly 766,000 shekels that gives the report its headline figure.
It is an improvement on the club's worst year: the deficit peaked at 1,409,952 shekels in 2023, and has been trending down since, ONE reports, largely thanks to belt-tightening on the wage bill.

Salary cuts introduced from the middle of 2024 have sharply reduced the club's top pay packet. The association's highest earner took home 77,482 shekels across all of 2025, ONE reports — a fraction of the 167,928 to 191,792 shekels top earners had received in previous years.

On the expenses side, salaries across the club's operations came to 1,519,749 shekels, with a further 1,590,196 shekels in other operational costs. On the income side, the statements list 136,151 shekels in municipal support, 657,773 shekels in donations from within Israel, and 443,690 shekels in other support and allocations, among the club's revenue lines.

The financial strain came in a difficult season on the pitch. Beitar Nordia's senior team finished bottom of Liga Alef South in the 2025/26 campaign, ONE reports, and was heading for relegation to Liga Bet before the season was halted amid the fighting with Iran — sparing the club the drop.

Beitar Nordia Jerusalem is not to be confused with the top-flight Beitar Jerusalem FC. It is a separate, supporter-owned association founded in 2014 by Beitar Jerusalem fans who opposed racism and violence in the stands and broke away in protest at the influence of the La Familia fan group. The club plays its home matches at the 4,000-capacity Hebrew University Stadium at Givat Ram.

Five straight years of losses illustrate the tightrope facing fan-owned clubs in Israel's lower leagues, where gate receipts and sponsorship rarely cover running costs and associations lean heavily on municipal grants and members' donations to survive.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv close in on Gelbard loan to Kfar Saba as Gurfinkel return nears
dek: The 19-year-old academy left-back is set to join Hapoel Kfar Saba on loan within days, ONE reports, just as Hapoel Tel Aviv push to complete the comeback of former player Yahav Gurfinkel from AEK Larnaca.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv are reshaping their left-back department this week: academy graduate Ofer Gelbard is closing in on a loan move to Hapoel Kfar Saba, ONE reports, just as the Reds push to complete the return of a more familiar face, Yahav Gurfinkel, from Cyprus.

According to ONE, Gelbard's loan to Kfar Saba could be finalized as soon as Sunday. The National League club have been tracking the 19-year-old for some time, and the two sides are now understood to have reached an agreement in principle over the move.

Gelbard, a product of the Hapoel Tel Aviv youth system, signed a lengthy contract extension with the club last season but currently sits as the squad's only reserve left-back behind first-choice Doron Leidner. He spent last season on loan at Maccabi Jaffa before returning to Bloomfield in January, and with regular football hard to come by in Elyaniv Barda's senior squad, a fresh loan to gain minutes makes obvious sense for player and club alike.

The move comes as Hapoel Tel Aviv edge closer to bringing back a player who knows the left flank at Bloomfield well. ONE reports the club are advancing on a deal to sign Yahav Gurfinkel, whose path at AEK Larnaca has been complicated after the Cypriot club brought in a rival for his position. The report describes the signing as very close to being finalized.

Hapoel Tel Aviv had already circled Gurfinkel earlier in the transfer window, with Sport5 reporting in July that the club viewed him as their preferred reinforcement on the left of defence while he weighed whether to stay in Cyprus or return home. Gurfinkel, who came through the Maccabi Haifa academy, previously spent two seasons at Hapoel Tel Aviv between 2022 and 2024 before a move to Chinese Super League side Chengdu Rongcheng and, this past January, a switch to AEK Larnaca on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The timing is no coincidence. Hapoel Tel Aviv are in the middle of the biggest European run in the club's recent history, having eliminated Ludogorets and GKS Katowice in Conference League qualifying before holding Atalanta to a 0-0 draw away in the first leg of their playoff tie last Wednesday. The return leg is set for Thursday at a neutral venue in Miskolc, Hungary, with more than 4,000 Israeli supporters expected to travel to DVTK Stadium as the club chase a place in the competition's league phase.

With a squeezed European and domestic calendar ahead, adding depth on the left — while sending a talented but currently blocked academy player out for regular games — fits the broader picture of a club trying to balance first-team strength with player development.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva/Dimona confirm teenage forward Matan Fogel will stay
dek: The 18-year-old, who reported for Israeli army service on Sunday morning, had already agreed a long-term deal that only became official once the club's place in next season's Premier League was secured.

verificationSources.label: ONE - רשמית: מתן פוגל ממשיך בבאר שבע

Israel Basketball Association - Hapoel Altshuler Shaham Beer Sheva/Dimona roster

body: Hapoel Altshuler Shaham Beer Sheva/Dimona announced on Sunday that Matan Fogel, the 18-year-old forward who came up through the club's system, will remain part of the squad for the 2026/27 season — closing out a deal that had effectively been agreed months ago but only became official once the club's own future in the top flight was settled.

Fogel's morning carried an unusual double significance. Hours before the club confirmed his contract, he reported for compulsory service in the Israel Defense Forces, joining the long list of young Israeli athletes who combine the start of a professional career with national service.

At 1.97 metres, Fogel is a graduate of the Hapoel Emek Yizrael youth system and has represented Israel at youth level, according to ONE, which broke the news of the confirmation. He put pen to paper on a long-term contract with Beer Sheva/Dimona last season but featured sparingly at senior level — five appearances in 2025-26, averaging roughly a minute a game, according to Israel Basketball Association figures — while also getting court time through a dual-registration arrangement with Maccabi Dimona in the National League.

The formal confirmation of his deal was tied to a much bigger story around the club. Beer Sheva/Dimona spent much of August fighting to keep its place in the Israeli Basketball Premier League after the league administration issued a hard ultimatum over the club's finances, with relegation to the National League a real threat and the club's professional operations effectively frozen. A solution was found in the past week, and the southern club confirmed it will open the 2026/27 season in the top flight after all.

That resolution cleared the way for new head coach Doug Spradley — the American-German appointee who takes over the bench for the new campaign after leading ZZ Leiden to a domestic treble in the Netherlands in 2023 and more than two decades on the sidelines in Germany and the Netherlands — to lock down his roster. His staff has now secured the continuation of five players from last season's group: Fogel, Ofri Shitrit, Golan Gut, Noam Avivi and Ido Fleisher, per ONE's report.

For a club that spent the summer fighting off an existential threat, retaining even fringe pieces like Fogel carries symbolic weight — a sign that Beer Sheva/Dimona intends to keep developing its own academy talent rather than simply patching gaps as it rebuilds under a new coaching staff.

With the roster and coaching situation stabilising, attention in the south will now turn to preseason preparations and the shape of the rest of Spradley's squad ahead of the league's return in the autumn.

title: Yaniv Levy steps down from Israel Basketball Premier League directorate
dek: The Basketball Association representative on the league's board announced his departure in a letter to association chairman Amos Frishman, saying it was time to make way after three seasons in the role.

verificationSources.label: ONE - יניב לוי מסיים את תפקידו במנהלת הליגה
Israel Basketball Premier League - Board of Directors

body: Yaniv Levy is stepping away from Israeli basketball's boardroom. The Israel Basketball Association's representative on the Premier League directorate has informed chairman Amos Frishman, in a letter, that he is ending his tenure on the board after roughly three seasons.

ONE reports that Levy's exit is part of a broader wind-down of his public roles rather than any dispute with the league's current leadership. In his letter, he singled out league directorate chairman Ari Steinberg and CEO David Basan for praise, saying the pair had shown effective, steady management during a turbulent period for the sport.

Levy previously headed the Information Department at the Histadrut, Israel's national trade union federation, before taking his seat on the directorate as one of the Basketball Association's public appointees. According to the league's own listing of board members, he served alongside fellow association representatives Naor Galili and Gal Levi as well as several public and club-appointed directors.

In the letter, Levy urged Israeli basketball to keep its focus on merit over politics, writing that "professionals must lead the sport, not job seekers," and that persistence rather than shortcuts is what ultimately delivers results — a message he directed in particular at young players coming through the system.

He also framed his time in sports administration in broader terms, telling Frishman he remains convinced that Israeli sport can serve as a bridge that reduces inequality and opens doors, and that he intends to stay engaged with basketball's future even after leaving the board.

ONE's report does not name a successor for Levy's seat on the directorate, nor does it give a precise date for when his resignation takes effect. The Basketball Association is expected to name a replacement representative in due course.

The departure comes as the league directorate, under Steinberg and Basan, continues to navigate a demanding off-season that has included wage disputes and scheduling talks with the players' organisation ahead of the new Winner League campaign.

title: Augustine Rubit lands in Israel to join Maccabi Ashdod
dek: The 37-year-old power forward, a five-season EuroLeague veteran of Bamberg, Olympiacos, Zalgiris Kaunas and Bayern Munich, touches down on Sunday to complete a move to the Winner League club.

verificationSources.label: ONE - אוגוסטין רוביט ינחת היום ויצטרף למכבי אשדוד
Eurobasket - Markis McDuffie joins M.Ashdod (confirms Rubit among Ashdod's imports)

body: Maccabi Ashdod are adding a serious dose of European pedigree to their frontcourt. Augustine Rubit, a 37-year-old power forward with five EuroLeague seasons on his résumé, is due to land in Israel on Sunday afternoon and complete a move to the Winner League club, ONE reports.

It is a significant statement signing for a club that has spent the summer quietly building. Rubit arrives having logged 143 EuroLeague appearances for four different clubs, starting in roughly half of them, and posting career averages of 9.2 points and 4.2 rebounds in Europe's top competition.

His path to the continent's elite level ran through Germany, where he first made his name at Walter Tigers Tübingen and ratiopharm Ulm before a move to Brose Bamberg established him as a EuroLeague-calibre big man. From there he went to Olympiacos Piraeus, then Zalgiris Kaunas, where he won the Lithuanian championship and cup double in 2020-21, and finally to Bayern Munich, with whom he lifted the German Cup in 2023.

This is not the first time Rubit has been linked with Israeli basketball. He has previously been in talks with both Maccabi Tel Aviv, earlier in his career, and Hapoel Jerusalem, as recently as last season, according to Israeli reporting, though neither move materialised. Ashdod have now got the deal over the line.

The signing comes as Maccabi Ashdod's professional director, Nati Cohen, has been stressing the club's development pipeline alongside its recruitment. In the same report, ONE said five academy graduates — Opal Bachar, Ilai Logsi, Uri Barnet, Eliah Naker and Rotem Gila — will train and compete with the senior squad this season.
"Our agenda is clear," Cohen said. "We are a club with a youth department that has a senior team, not a senior team that has a youth department."
Rubit's arrival fits a broader summer build-up for Ashdod, who have been assembling an experienced import roster for the new Winner League campaign as they look to push up the table.

Rubit has played 143 EuroLeague games across five seasons, averaging 9.2 points and 4.2 rebounds, for Brose Bamberg, Olympiacos Piraeus, Zalgiris Kaunas and Bayern Munich.

body: Israeli football is back this weekend, and Maccabi Tel Aviv go into their trip to Hapoel Jerusalem as clear favourites to open the new Ligat Ha'al season with three points. According to odds published by the betting site ONE, the yellow-and-blue are priced at 1.4 for victory, with the draw quoted at 4.5 and a Hapoel win worth 5.8.

Kick-off at Teddy Stadium is set for 20:15 on Sunday, and the match doubles as an early marker for Kenny Miller, who took interim charge of Maccabi through last season's play-offs before being confirmed as permanent head coach in June.

Hapoel Jerusalem, for their part, go into the game under Lior Zada, who was promoted from assistant to head coach in April after Ziv Arie's departure, guided the club to safety in the top flight, and was rewarded with a full-time contract heading into the new campaign.

The odds reflect how much is expected of Maccabi this season, and Sunday's fixture arrives with a far bigger date already on the club's mind. Having played the first leg of their Europa League play-off away to Greek side OFI Crete last Thursday, Maccabi return to continental action four days after facing Hapoel, when they host the second leg on Thursday with a place in the group stage at stake.

Elsewhere on Sunday, ONE also priced two of the continent's marquee kick-offs. Barcelona finally begin the defence of their La Liga title away to Elche, more than a week after most of the rest of Spanish football got under way — a delayed start LaLiga granted the champions and other clubs whose players went deep into this summer's World Cup. Barcelona, who had ten players reach the semi-finals, are priced by ONE at 1.3 to win, with the draw at 4.9 and Elche's odds standing at 6.6.

Liverpool also open their season on Sunday, away to Newcastle at St James' Park. It is a first competitive outing for new head coach Andoni Iraola, appointed in June after Arne Slot was dismissed following a fifth-place finish that came just a year after he had led Liverpool to the Premier League title.

Newcastle have changed manager too, with Matthias Jaissle taking over from Eddie Howe, and the fixture will bring Alexander Isak back to his old ground for the first time since his move to Anfield. ONE make Liverpool 1.85 to win, with the draw at 3.6 and a home win for Newcastle priced at 3.4.

None of it is a guarantee, of course — odds move with team news before kick-off, and bookmakers have been caught out before. But taken together, Sunday's card gives Israeli football fans a busy afternoon and evening to follow, with Maccabi Tel Aviv's derby-adjacent trip to Jerusalem sandwiched between two of European football's biggest kick-offs of the new season.

title: Dahan's lawyers accuse police of creating false impression an indictment was already decided
dek: The suspended Maccabi Haifa forward's legal team has filed an urgent complaint with Israel's police commissioner, arguing a letter used to justify his 60-day ban wrongly implied a charging decision had already been made.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "Police created a false impression that a decision to prosecute had been made"
ONE - Omer Dahan suspended for two months from all activity
Haaretz - Football association's disciplinary court suspends Omer Dahan, suspected of betting and match-fixing, for 60 days
ONE - Football association demands immediate suspension of Omer Dahan

body: Omer Dahan's legal team has taken the fight over his suspension from Israeli football to the top of the police chain of command, filing an urgent complaint with Police Commissioner Dani Levi that accuses investigators of creating a misleading impression that a formal decision to prosecute the Maccabi Haifa forward had already been made, ONE reported.

The complaint, filed on Sunday by attorneys Amir Cohen, Sharon Braverman and Anan Faro, does not dispute that Dahan remains under investigation. Instead it challenges how that investigation was communicated to the Israel Football Association — communication that became the basis for sidelining him from the game.

The dispute traces back to August 2, when the police's serious and international crimes unit, Lahav 433, sent the football association's prosecutor a letter stating it had completed its investigation into Dahan and intended to recommend criminal charges. The association leaned on that letter when it petitioned the game's disciplinary court for his immediate suspension.

The court granted a 60-day ban on August 19, with the presiding judge finding that "heavy suspicion exists of offences damaging game integrity" and that letting Dahan continue playing under such a cloud was untenable.

Dahan's lawyers now argue that the way Lahav 433 framed its letter blurred a critical legal distinction. "There is a substantial difference between a recommendation and an actual prosecution decision," they wrote in the complaint, according to ONE, adding that "an individual not yet indicted should not be presented to external parties as though the indictment decision already occurred."

Under Israeli procedure, a police recommendation to charge a suspect is not the same as an actual decision to prosecute — that determination rests with state prosecutors, not the investigating unit. The lawyers contend the letter to the football association's prosecutor effectively collapsed that distinction, leaving the association, and by extension the public, with the impression that Dahan's case had already moved from investigation to indictment.

The complaint asks Levi for clarification on three points: whether a formal decision to prosecute actually existed as of August 2, who within the police or prosecution made any such decision, and through what authorised procedure information about the case was shared with an external body like the football association.

Dahan, 25, was arrested on June 14 as one of several suspects detained in a police operation targeting an alleged illegal betting and match-fixing network linked to a criminal organisation from Migdal HaEmek. He has been questioned over suspected illegal gambling, match-fixing, money laundering and tax offences, and has publicly denied fixing or selling any match.

He has not been charged with, let alone convicted of, any offence. His lawyers frame the complaint as a matter of basic administrative fairness and the presumption of innocence, arguing that a suspect's professional livelihood should not be upended on the strength of a police letter that reads as more definitive than the actual state of proceedings against him.

Police had not issued a public response to the complaint at the time of publication, and Dahan's 60-day suspension from all football activity, imposed by the association's disciplinary court, remains in effect regardless of how the commissioner responds.

title: Brentford 3-0 Tottenham: De Zerbi admits Spurs are 'not a team yet' as chaotic opener exposes new project
dek: The Italian's expensively rebuilt side never had a shot on target in the first half at the Gtech Community Stadium, while 20-year-old Archie Gray became the club's youngest-ever competitive captain in a night to forget.

verificationSources.label: Tottenham Hotspur — Archie Gray youngest captain

body: Roberto De Zerbi's first full season in charge of Tottenham Hotspur could scarcely have begun worse. Brentford tore his expensively remodelled side apart 3-0 at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday, and the Italian did not try to dress it up afterwards. "I think we are not a team yet, for a lot of reasons," he said, in comments reported by ONE.

Keane Lewis-Potter and Vitaly Janelt scored either side of half-time, and Michael Kayode added a third just four minutes into the second half. It could have been worse still — Igor Thiago missed a 55th-minute penalty — but Spurs never recovered, failing to register a single shot on target in the entire first half.

De Zerbi, who succeeded Thomas Frank at the north London club before the season, said his team is still missing the basics that turn a collection of new signings into a functioning unit. "We need soul and playing style. When we find both, we'll be dangerous," he said, according to ONE's report.

He pointed to circumstances beyond the tactics board: several players returned late after the World Cup, and a pre-season trip to Australia ate further into training time. The result, he argued, was a side short of the physical conditioning needed to compete with a well-drilled Brentford outfit.

The manager also defended his decision to start 20-year-old Lucas Bergvall in midfield instead of the more experienced Rodrigo Bentancur, even though Bergvall's error contributed to Brentford's second goal. De Zerbi said the youngster would learn from the experience and improve with time.

Tottenham's summer rebuild has been extensive and costly — around £237 million spent on six new signings, according to Sky Sports — and five of those six arrivals were given competitive debuts against Brentford, including Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson in a reshaped back line, plus Sandro Tonali in midfield.

One moment stood out amid the wreckage. With regular skipper Micky van de Ven left out of the matchday squad, De Zerbi handed the armband to Gray, who at 20 years and 163 days became Tottenham's youngest-ever competitive captain — breaking a record held by club great Steve Perryman since a UEFA Cup tie against Lyn Oslo in 1972.

Gray's first taste of the captaincy was a chastening one. "We simply lost too many battles. They fought harder than us everywhere on the pitch," he said afterwards, taking responsibility for the display and acknowledging how galling the defeat would have been for travelling supporters.

The result piles early pressure on a club that finished 17th in the Premier League last season, avoiding relegation only on the final day. A repeat of that struggle was precisely what the summer spending spree was supposed to prevent, and instead Tottenham head into week two already needing answers.

There is no sign of the rebuild slowing down regardless: Tottenham have been continuing talks over Manchester City pair Savinho and Omar Marmoush as De Zerbi looks to add further reinforcements to a squad he insists simply needs time to find its identity.

title: Barcelona's chase for Lukeba hinges on Kounde and Balde's futures
dek: Hansi Flick rates Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba highly, but ONE reports the move only becomes real if Jules Kounde or Alejandro Balde leaves the Camp Nou before the window shuts.
body: Barcelona's defensive rebuild has a domino problem. ONE reports that the club's pursuit of RB Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba is not a straightforward pursuit at all, but a plan that only gets moving once one of Jules Kounde or Alejandro Balde walks out the door.

Hansi Flick is said to rate the 23-year-old Frenchman for his speed, his left foot and his aggression out of the back — attributes the German coach has publicly prized since he arrived at Camp Nou. But Lukeba does not come cheap, and Barcelona's finances mean any incoming fee has to be funded by an outgoing sale first.

That is where Kounde and Balde come in. According to ONE, Flick has left the door open for either defender to leave this summer, and the club would accelerate talks for Lukeba the moment one of them departs.

The irony is that Kounde only just committed his long-term future to the club. Barcelona confirmed in August that the France international had signed a new contract running to 2030, ending speculation over interest from the Premier League after he reportedly turned down an approach to stay put, according to football-espana.net and ESPN.

A new deal, though, has not made him untouchable. Spanish outlets covering the club, including Sport1-Maariv, have described Barcelona's hierarchy as viewing Kounde as a sellable asset if the right offer lands — a reminder that in Barcelona's current financial reality, a long contract can raise a player's price rather than guarantee his place.

Balde's situation looks further along. Multiple outlets, including Forbes and Barca Blaugranes, reported this weekend that the 22-year-old left-back has decided he wants out after growing frustrated with his standing under Flick, with agent Jorge Mendes said to be working the phones to find him a new home before the window closes.

Manchester United have been the club most consistently linked with Balde, having already opened dialogue with his camp as they search for a long-term left-back. Fabrizio Romano has offered a note of caution, however, stating that Balde is not actively pushing for an exit and that any decision remains in the club's hands rather than the player's.

Gerard Martin is currently Barcelona's only recognised natural left-back should Balde leave, which underlines why the club would need Lukeba — even if he is naturally a centre-back — to help solve more than one problem at once, either sliding into central defence or covering across the back line as Flick's squad is reshuffled.

Lukeba himself has been strongly linked with a Bundesliga exit after three seasons in Leipzig, with a release clause reported in the region of 80 million euros, though Leipzig are believed willing to negotiate down from that figure. Arsenal and Manchester United have also been credited with interest in the France Under-21 international turned senior squad member.

For now, ONE frames this as contingent rather than close: no fee for Lukeba has been agreed, and no exit for Kounde or Balde has been finalised. But with the transfer window entering its final stretch, Barcelona's sporting director Deco and Flick appear to be working from the same script — sell a centre-back or a left-back, and the money moves to Leipzig.

title: Ironi Tiberias 1-0 Hapoel Petah Tikva: disallowed Rivollier goal fuels VAR storm on opening day
dek: A stoppage-time offside call denied Hapoel Petah Tikva a point in Nof HaGalil, as the club insisted Franck Rivollier's ruled-out finish was "a completely legal goal."
body: Ironi Tiberias opened the 2026-27 Ligat Ha'al season with a 1-0 win over Hapoel Petah Tikva on Saturday, but the story that dominated the aftermath was not Itamar Shviro's decisive penalty — it was a goal that never counted at all.

Shviro sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot to give Tiberias the lead, and that penalty proved enough for all three points at Barel Stadium in Nof HaGalil, Tiberias's home venue for top-flight matches.

Hapoel Petah Tikva pushed hard for an equaliser and thought they had found one in the 85th minute when Franck Rivollier turned the ball home. Referee Shnir Levi disallowed it after a VAR review, ruling that striker Shvit Mazal — who had been lying on the turf in an offside position during the buildup — got back to his feet and became involved in the passage of play.

The decision infuriated the visitors, and ONE reported the club's forceful response: "a completely legal goal, luck had nothing to do with the play at all," arguing that Mazal never touched the ball or interfered with a Tiberias defender even after standing up, and pointing out the striker was in fact injured during the sequence rather than gaining any advantage from it.

It was a bitter way for Omer Peretz's side to begin the campaign. Petah Tikva dominated long spells of the match without finding a way past a well-organised Tiberias defence, and the disallowed goal compounded a frustrating afternoon on the road.

Rivollier, the man whose effort was chalked off, is back for a second spell at Hapoel Petah Tikva after returning on a free transfer. The France-born forward, who is also eligible for Cameroon, first joined the club in January 2025 from Bulgaria's Spartak Varna and was part of the squad that won the Israeli second-division title before this season's promotion push.

Mazal, the offside player at the centre of the dispute, signed for Hapoel Petah Tikva on a two-year deal this summer. The 24-year-old striker came through Hapoel Tel Aviv's youth system before spells at Beitar Jerusalem, Hapoel Ramat Gan and Ashdod.

Levi, the referee who reviewed the VAR footage and upheld the offside call, was voted Israel's outstanding referee of the past season, adding to the sting of the decision for a Petah Tikva side that made the trip north in numbers — roughly 400 travelling supporters were in the away end.

For Ironi Tiberias, the win offers an ideal start to a campaign in which the club has stated its priority is simply staying in Ligat Ha'al. For Hapoel Petah Tikva, it means an opening-day defeat and a fresh round of debate over marginal offside calls as the new VAR-heavy season gets under way.

title: Maccabi Haifa 2-1 Hapoel Ramat Gan: Bruninho brace opens the season, Cedric Don fined for lateness
dek: Brazilian playmaker Bruninho scored either side of half-time as Maccabi Haifa began the new Ligat Ha'al season with a home win over promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan – though defender Cedric Don was fined after turning up late for the pre-match video session.
body: Maccabi Haifa opened their Ligat Ha'al title defence with a 2-1 win over newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan at Sammy Ofer Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian playmaker Bruninho scoring twice to settle a game that was tighter than the final score suggested.

Bruninho's first arrived in the 22nd minute, a low, first-time strike from 20 metres that flew past the goalkeeper into the corner. He struck again barely a minute into the second half, converting from close range to put the Greens 2-0 up and effectively decide the contest before Ramat Gan had time to settle.

The visitors, back in the top flight after a 13-year absence, pulled one back through Maxim Plakushchenko in the 61st minute — their first Israeli Premier League goal since they were relegated in 2013. It was a proud moment for the club, even if the result extended a wretched record against Maccabi Haifa: Ramat Gan still haven't beaten them in the league since October 1977.

Bruninho, signed from Ukrainian side Karpaty Lviv over the summer, has quickly become the team's most reliable source of individual quality. ONE reported that figures around the club likened his impact to that of past creative players who carried Maccabi Haifa in tight matches, drawing comparisons to Tjaronn Chery and Dia Saba as a genuine tie-breaker in games the team might otherwise have drawn or lost.

Yarin Levi also had his best game since returning to the club, but the mood around him remains complicated. According to ONE, sections of the northern stand again chose not to chant his name during the match, even as other parts of the crowd got behind him — a lingering echo of the criticism he faced over his loyalty after two years away at Beitar Jerusalem before rejoining Haifa in the summer of 2024.

Less welcome news came from the training ground. ONE reported that defender Cedric Don arrived late to the squad's final session before the match and walked in partway through the video review, and that the club intends to fine him rather than let the breach slide. Don joined Maccabi Haifa from Hapoel Jerusalem this summer in one of the most expensive deals in the club's history, on a contract running to 2030.

Despite the win, there was no rush to declare the campaign back on track. ONE reported that inside the club there was satisfaction with periods of Saturday's performance but also an acknowledgement that the defensive gaps exposed by Ramat Gan would need fixing quickly, with a far tougher test — Maccabi Tel Aviv — arriving in round two.

The club is also still working the transfer market before the September 14 deadline, hunting a winger to replace Manuel Benson after his season was ended by injury, according to the report. For now, though, three points and a Bruninho double were exactly the start Maccabi Haifa needed after a difficult pre-season.

title: Charlotte FC beat D.C. United 3-1 as Liel Abada sets up the clincher
dek: The Israel international came off the bench and teed up Pep Biel's third goal as Charlotte rallied from behind to sink D.C. United in MLS.

verificationSources.label: ONE - עבדה בישל בניצחון שארלוט 1:3 על די.סי יונייטד
The Washington Post (AP) - Will Cleary's 1st goal in MLS helps Charlotte beat D.C. United 3-1

body: Liel Abada needed only a dozen minutes off the bench to leave his mark on Charlotte FC's biggest win in weeks, setting up the clinching goal as the hosts came from behind to beat D.C. United 3-1 in MLS on Saturday night.

ONE reports the Israel international was sent on midway through the second half with the scores level, and by the time he left the field Charlotte had turned a losing position into a comfortable victory at Bank of America Stadium.

D.C. United had taken the lead against the run of play through Louis Munteanu's finish in the 55th minute. Charlotte responded almost immediately: David Schnegg drew the hosts level in the 64th, converting a rebound after Morrison Agyemang's header had come back off the woodwork.

Two minutes later rookie Will Cleary headed in his first-ever MLS goal, meeting a corner delivered by Pep Biel to put Charlotte 2-1 ahead. The comeback was completed in the 77th minute when Abada, according to ONE's account, carried the ball down the right and squared for Biel to finish for 3-1.

It capped a chaotic finish to a game that had been goalless and scrappy for long stretches - Charlotte were outshot 10-4 in the first half despite holding 61 percent of possession, only to score three times in twelve second-half minutes once Abada entered the fray.

Charlotte goalkeeper Kristijan Kahlina made three saves to preserve the win, while D.C. United's Sean Johnson had two at the other end as the visitors slipped to a fourth straight match without a victory.

For Abada, the assist extends a productive season in Charlotte colors since his big-money move from Celtic. The 24-year-old winger, a product of Maccabi Petah Tikva's academy, joined the North Carolina club in March 2024 as a Young Designated Player after Celtic accepted a fee reported in the region of $8 million.

He arrived in MLS with pedigree: 51 goal involvements in 112 appearances for Celtic and six trophies, including the 2023 domestic treble, after breaking through at Maccabi Petah Tikva and earning his first senior Israel caps as a teenager.

Saturday's result also has broader implications in a congested Eastern Conference table, with D.C. United now winless in four league outings while Charlotte banked a result that keeps them firmly in the hunt heading into the final weeks of the regular season.

title: Maccabi Netanya score twice in stoppage time to beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 3-2 in youth league
dek: Itai Kihan's late double completed a comeback for Netanya's Youth A side, handing Hapoel Tel Aviv a second straight defeat to open the season.

verificationSources.label: ONE - נערים א׳: הפועל תל אביב סופרת הפסד שני ברציפות
JuniorLeague - Round 1 Maccabi Netanya youth report

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv's Youth A side opened the season with back-to-back defeats after being pegged back late by Maccabi Netanya, who won 3-2 thanks to a stoppage-time double from Itai Kihan.

According to ONE's report on round two of the U-17 Youth A league, Hapoel Tel Aviv looked to be heading for their first points of the campaign after goals from Itamar Ben Meir and Adisu Almo put them 2-1 up going into the closing stages.

But Netanya refused to fold. Kihan struck twice in the added minutes to turn the scoreline around and complete a 3-2 comeback win, sending Hapoel Tel Aviv to the bottom of the table with two rounds gone.

Netanya coach Yuval Akiva was full of praise for the opponents his side had just beaten. "We played against one of the best teams in the league," he said, according to ONE. "Three months ago they beat us 6-1 in the cup final."

That earlier meeting, a heavy defeat for Netanya in a cup final over the summer, made Saturday's turnaround all the sweeter for Akiva's group, even if the stakes of a routine league fixture in August are far lower than a final.

For Hapoel Tel Aviv, the result compounds a difficult start: ONE's report notes this was the club's second consecutive loss in the youth league, having also lost their opening-round derby, leaving the young reds searching for their first points of the season.
The result is an early marker in what is a long campaign for both academies, but for Netanya's Youth A group it is a second bright start in as many weeks after also winning their round-one fixture.

title: Espanyol 1-2 Real Madrid: Carlos Espí's stoppage-time winner rescues Mourinho's return
dek: A 90th-minute strike from summer signing Carlos Espí salvaged victory at Espanyol as José Mourinho began his second spell in charge of Real Madrid.

verificationSources.label: Al Jazeera - "Real Madrid beat Espanyol 2-1 in Jose Mourinho's first game on return"
ESPN - Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid, Espanyol, La Liga report
Real Madrid C.F. - Official Announcement: Carlos Espí

body: José Mourinho's second coming at Real Madrid nearly ended in embarrassment before a substitute nobody was talking about in July bailed him out. Carlos Espí, on for barely half an hour, poked home a stoppage-time winner at Espanyol to hand the Portuguese a 2-1 victory in his first match back in the dugout.

It was Real Madrid's opening fixture of the 2026-27 La Liga season, away at Espanyol on Saturday. Jude Bellingham headed Madrid in front in the first half, only for Alex Calatrava to level for the hosts around the half-hour mark. The game looked destined for a draw until Espí pounced on a loose ball inside the box in the 90th minute and drove it home.

The goal completed a story that reads almost too neatly: Espí was, by common consent, the lowest-profile name among Madrid's summer arrivals, dwarfed in the headlines by Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konaté and Marc Cucurella. Instead it was the 21-year-old from Levante who produced the moment that mattered.

Mourinho's return to the Bernabéu came 13 years after he left in 2013 following a first spell that delivered a league title but ended in acrimony. This time he inherits a squad built around Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior, reinforced by a busy summer rebuild, and a mandate to end Barcelona's recent grip on the Spanish title.

Asked about the narrow win afterwards, Mourinho was generous to the opposition. "I think that we deserved to win but that Espanyol didn't deserve to lose," he told reporters, adding that Espanyol's players had largely stayed together as a group through the summer - unlike his own overhauled squad - which showed in their cohesion on the pitch.

Espí's path to that 90th-minute moment began at Levante, where he scored 20 goals in 66 appearances across three seasons and was voted the division's best under-23 player last term. He is also a Spain youth international at under-19 and under-20 level. Real Madrid moved for him late in the transfer window, signing him on a five-year contract through June 2031 as physical back-up for Mbappé - the kind of old-fashioned target man Mourinho has said he wanted in his squad.

ONE, reporting on the aftermath from Spain, described the Spanish press reaction as effusive, with outlets casting the previously little-known forward as the man who had saved Mourinho's first day back and hailing his composure in front of goal as proof he could be the genuine number nine Madrid have been missing.

Espí had already given a hint of what was coming. He scored his first goal for the club in a pre-season friendly win over Ferencváros earlier this month, a low-key marker that suddenly looks a lot more significant after Saturday's late drama.

For Mourinho, the result is a start rather than a statement - a first league fixture won ugly, with plenty to fix before Madrid's bigger tests arrive. But after a summer of speculation about whether his return would work, the opening afternoon at least ended with three points and an unlikely new name on everyone's lips.

title: Seoul, 6 March 2017: The Night Baseball's Biggest Underdog Beat the Host Nation
dek: Ranked 41st in the world and dismissed as a novelty act, Team Israel walked into a sold-out dome in Seoul and beat South Korea in extra innings — the game that launched the most improbable run in World Baseball Classic history.

verificationSources.label: Jewish Telegraphic Agency — "Israel upsets Korea in first game of World Baseball Classic"
The Times of Israel — "Israel wins thriller in first-ever World Baseball Classic appearance"
ESPN — "Israel beats South Korea in World Baseball Classic opener"
MLB.com — "Israel beats host Korea in extras to open WBC '17"
Chicago Sun-Times — "Israel beats South Korea 2-1 at World Baseball Classic"
Jewish Telegraphic Agency — "Israel advances to World Baseball Classic for first time"

body: Gocheok Sky Dome in Seoul holds just over 16,000 people, and on the evening of 6 March 2017 it was close to full for the opening game of the World Baseball Classic. The host nation, South Korea, was among the favorites to make a deep run in the tournament it was co-hosting. Its opponent, playing its first-ever WBC game, was a team most of the crowd had never heard of: Team Israel.

Israel arrived in Seoul ranked 41st in the world — the only team in the sixteen-nation field outside the top twenty, and some thirty-eight places below Korea. ESPN, previewing the tournament, had called them the "Jamaican bobsled team of the WBC." The roster carried the Star of David on its cap but almost no one on it had grown up in Israel; under the tournament's eligibility rules, and Israel's Law of Return, any player Jewish enough to qualify for Israeli citizenship could play for the team, and general manager Peter Kurz and manager Jerry Weinstein — a 73-year-old lifer of American professional baseball — had built a roster of Jewish-American major and minor leaguers, including Ike Davis, Ryan Lavarnway and Josh Zeid.

Getting to Seoul had taken two tries. In 2012, Israel lost a winner-take-all qualifier game to Spain, 9-7 in ten innings, and missed the 2013 Classic entirely. Four years later, at Maimonides Park in Coney Island, Brooklyn, Israel beat Great Britain 5-2 in the qualifying opener, rallying with four runs in the seventh, then routed the same opponent 9-1 in the championship game on 25 September 2016 to clinch its first-ever berth in the main tournament.

Few outside the clubhouse gave them a chance against Korea. "We're not the underdogs," Weinstein told reporters before the game. "We're pretty much unknown, and I think that's why people think we're underdogs."

The game itself refused to behave like a mismatch. Israel's starter, 38-year-old journeyman Jason Marquis, threw three scoreless innings, and Israel led 1-0 in the second when Tyler Krieger drew a bases-loaded walk that forced in Nate Freiman. Korea tied it in the fifth when Seo Geon-chang, the KBO's reigning batting star, singled to left to score Kim Jae-ho. From there the game tightened into a bullpen duel, six Israeli pitchers combining to hold the home lineup at one run through nine innings, right-hander Josh Zeid working the final stretch with three shutout innings of his own.

The winning rally arrived in the top of the tenth. Ike Davis drew a one-out walk and was replaced at first by pinch-runner Mike Meyers, who moved to third on a Ryan Lavarnway single. After Krieger popped up a bunt attempt, Scott Burcham chopped an infield single toward second base — just enough to score Meyers and put Israel ahead, 2-1. Zeid returned to the mound and retired the side in the bottom of the tenth to close it out.

It was, on paper, one baseball game in the opening round of a tournament Israel was not expected to survive. In practice, it set the tone for something much larger. Israel beat Chinese Taipei and the Netherlands to finish pool play 3-0 — the first team ever to enter the WBC through qualifying and go undefeated in the first round — then went on to beat a Cuban side ranked fifth in the world in the second round in Tokyo. Israel finally lost to Japan and the Netherlands and finished the tournament sixth of sixteen nations, with a 4-2 overall record, a result no one had thought possible when Marquis threw his first pitch in Seoul.

The run became famous well beyond the box scores. The team's cardboard-and-felt mascot, Mensch on a Bench, turned into a minor media phenomenon, and the whole improbable story was later chronicled in the 2018 documentary "Heading Home: The Tale of Team Israel."

For Israeli baseball — a sport played on a handful of fields in a country better known for judo mats and basketball courts — the 2 March 6 win over Korea remains the moment the program stopped being a curiosity. It gave a small federation its first real audience, its first real highlight reel, and, in the years since, a pipeline that has kept sending teams back to the Classic.

title: Ironi Tiberias 1-0 Hapoel Petah Tikva: VAR screen fails as Snir Levi rules out late equaliser
dek: A blank pitchside monitor did not stop referee Snir Levi disallowing Franck Rivollier's 86th-minute leveller, and Hapoel Petah Tikva left their Ligat Ha'al opener furious at both the decision and the stoppage time that followed it, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Hapoel Petah Tikva official site - Franck Rivollier profile

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva's first outing of the new Ligat Ha'al season ended in exactly the kind of chaos no club wants on opening weekend: a 1-0 defeat at Ironi Tiberias, decided not by the football but by a video review that never actually produced a picture.

The visitors were already trailing at the Barel Stadium on Saturday evening when Franck Rivollier appeared to drag them level in the 86th minute. The goal stood as scored on the field, until it was sent upstairs for a VAR check.

That is where it went wrong for Hapoel Petah Tikva, according to ONE. Referee Snir Levi went to the pitchside monitor to review the goal himself, only to find the screen blank and not functioning. He ruled the goal out regardless, and the visiting bench erupted in protest.

ONE reports that Hapoel Petah Tikva's staff argued afterwards there was no way to justify cancelling a goal off a review that never showed the referee any footage at all. They also questioned the stoppage time that followed: Levi added only five minutes in total, despite the review itself having eaten up roughly four of them.

Those complaints were put to match officials once the final whistle went. The response, per ONE, was that the call rested on a factual VAR matter rather than a subjective decision open to dispute — leaving Hapoel Petah Tikva with no route to have it overturned.
Coach Omer Peretz, told the outcome would stand, chose not to pursue the argument any further, the report says.

It is an unwelcome start for a Petah Tikva side with real ambition this season after Peretz steered them into last term's upper playoff and signed a contract extension through 2027-28 on the back of it. Rivollier, for his part, only rejoined the club this summer on a fresh one-year deal with an option for two more, having previously turned out for Hapoel Afula and Bulgaria's Spartak Varna before a spell in Petah Tikva colours that began in January 2025.

For Ironi Tiberias, a club whose own stated aim this season is simply staying in the top flight, three points and a controversy-free scoreline at home were exactly the ideal opening statement — even if the post-match conversation belonged entirely to the officiating rather than anything they did on the pitch.

Match officials told the club the ruling was a factual VAR matter rather than a subjective decision open to appeal, ONE reports.
Coach Omer Peretz did not pursue the complaint further after being told the result would stand.

title: Maccabi Haifa 2-1 Hapoel Ramat Gan: Dego says referee showed the champions too much respect
dek: Newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan's coach Messay Dego accused referee Omer Biran of double standards after his side's Ligat Ha'al return ended in defeat at Sammy Ofer Stadium.
body: Messay Dego spent the best part of two seasons in the Maccabi Haifa dugout before Barak Bakhar's return pushed him out. On Saturday he walked back into Sammy Ofer Stadium as the visiting coach, and he left convinced the referee still had a soft spot for his old club.

Hapoel Ramat Gan, back in the Ligat Ha'al after 13 years away, opened their long-awaited return with a 2-1 defeat. Brazilian midfielder Bruninho scored either side of half-time, in the 22nd and 46th minutes, before Maxim Falkushchenko pulled one back for the visitors in the 61st.

It was the officiating, as much as the result, that occupied Dego afterwards. Speaking to ONE, he turned his frustration on referee Omer Biran, accusing him of double standards he said had no place in Israel's top flight.

"Every touch of ours is a yellow card, [Betayi] gets away with four or five fouls without picking up a second yellow," Dego said, according to ONE, arguing the whistle was far harsher on his newly promoted side than on the champions.

He was equally unimpressed by a lengthy video review before Biran pointed to the spot for Maccabi Haifa. "I asked him what he blew the penalty for — six minutes of VAR checking," Dego said. "Maccabi Haifa doesn't need that kind of help."
His conclusion was blunt. "You can see he gave too much respect to Maccabi Haifa," he said. "That's not the level of the Ligat Ha'al."

There is an edge to the complaint given Dego's own history at the stadium. He managed Maccabi Haifa through the 2023-24 season before making way for Bakhar's return, then took over at Hapoel Ramat Gan and led the club back to the top flight for the first time in 13 years.

Saturday's defeat leaves Ramat Gan with nothing to show from their landmark return beyond Falkushchenko's consolation goal, and the schedule offers little respite. Dego's side face Hapoel Beersheba next, a team he called "the toughest in the country."

title: Artzi: Israel 'understand the importance' of this window before Georgia warm-up
dek: Ahead of Sunday's friendly in Tbilisi and Thursday's crucial World Cup qualifier against Poland, national team forward Netanel Artzi says a depleted squad is locked in despite the absence of Deni Avdija and Ben Saraf.
body: Netanel Artzi knows this is not a window to take lightly. Speaking to ONE ahead of Israel's preparation match against Georgia in Tbilisi on Sunday, the Hapoel Holon forward framed the friendly as the opening test of a camp that will decide far more than one exhibition result.

"We understand the importance of the current window," Artzi said. "As long as there's a chance, we need to come as focused as possible." He added that the Georgia match will "give us the first feel of what things should look like" before the far weightier assignment that follows just four days later.

That assignment is Poland, away in a neutral venue in Latvia on Thursday at 21:00 local time, in the Second Round of European qualifying for the 2027 FIBA World Cup. Israel sit in Group K alongside Poland, Croatia, Germany, the Netherlands and hosts Latvia, with only the top three advancing — making the Poland fixture, not Sunday's exhibition, the true business end of the trip.

Israel travel light on frontcourt experience for the Georgia game. According to ONE, the available squad numbers 13 after Idan Zalmanson and Ilay Dolinski were left out of the group cleared to play. Ynet reported separately that NBA duo Deni Avdija and Ben Saraf were unavailable for the entire window after their clubs declined to release them for national team duty.

Georgia, by contrast, arrive at full strength. ONE reports the hosts will field 16 players for Sunday's match, including two active NBA rostered big men in Sandro Mamukelashvili of the Lakers and Goga Bitadze of the Magic — a considerably higher level of opposition than a routine August warm-up would usually bring.

The buildup itself was disrupted before a ball was bounced. Israel's delegation reached Tbilisi later than planned after strikes at Ben Gurion Airport delayed the squad's departure, compressing an already tight preparation schedule into the final days before kickoff.

For Artzi and a squad missing several established faces, Sunday is as much about finding rhythm together as it is about the scoreline against Georgia. The real examination comes Thursday in Latvia, where a result against Poland will go a long way toward shaping Israel's path through the qualifying group.

title: Beitar Jerusalem thrash Maccabi Petah Tikva 6-0 in youth league opener
dek: Aviv Golan struck a hat-trick as Beitar's Under-15 side ran riot in round one of the Youth League B season, ONE reports.
body: Beitar Jerusalem's academy side opened the new season in emphatic fashion, thrashing Maccabi Petah Tikva 6-0 in the first round of the Youth League B (Super) division, ONE reported.
The result belongs to the clubs' Under-15 sides, made up of players born in 2011, rather than the senior first teams — but it was every bit as one-sided as the scoreline suggests.

Aviv Golan led the rout with a hat-trick, according to ONE, continuing the scoring form that saw him net 25 goals across last season. Ido David, Eliav Uliel and Liam Demari added the other three goals as Beitar cut through Maccabi Petah Tikva's defence at will.
Yaron Talmid's Beitar side were completely dominant from start to finish over Moshe Mor's Maccabi Petah Tikva, who managed no reply of their own on a difficult afternoon to begin the campaign.

It was a mixed opening round elsewhere in the age group. Hapoel Petah Tikva were pegged back late by Maccabi Haifa, drawing 2-2 after Karem Sarkhan's stoppage-time equaliser cancelled out goals from Leav Albez and Itay Tal.

Hapoel Ra'anana and Maccabi Netanya shared the points in a 1-1 draw, while Hapoel Nir Ramat Hasharon beat Hapoel Jerusalem 4-1 and Hapoel Ra'anana Rishon LeZion drew 0-0 with Hapoel Kfar Saba. Hapoel Kiryat Shmona were due to face Maccabi Tel Aviv on August 23 to complete the round, with Hapoel Hadera sitting out on a bye.

For Beitar's academy prospects, the result is an early marker in a division that regularly feeds talent toward first-team squads across the Israeli top flight — and a reminder that Golan, in particular, is a name to watch this season.

title: Netanyahu praises Dolgopyat's third European floor title as 'immense honour and pride'
dek: The prime minister added his voice to a wave of official congratulations after Artem Dolgopyat won floor gold in Zagreb for the third time in his career.
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu congratulated Artem Dolgopyat on Saturday, saying the gymnast "brings immense honour and national pride to the State of Israel time and again," after Dolgopyat claimed his third European floor exercise title in Zagreb.

Dolgopyat won gold in the floor final at the European Artistic Gymnastics Championships on Friday evening with a score of 14.466, adding to the European titles he first won on the apparatus in 2020 and again in 2022.

The gymnast, who trains out of Maccabi Tel Aviv, is the reigning Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion on floor and took silver at the Paris 2024 Games. He has now amassed two Olympic medals, three world titles and eight European medals on the apparatus over the past nine years, an extraordinary run for an athlete competing in one of the most technically demanding disciplines in the sport.

Netanyahu's statement came alongside congratulations from Culture and Sport Minister Miki Zohar, who phoned Dolgopyat directly after the win and pledged that his ministry would "continue promoting sport in Israel and providing all our athletes with the tools they need to succeed," according to ONE.

Israel Gymnastics Federation chairman Avi Sagi also praised the result, saying Dolgopyat "once again proves he is made of the stuff great champions are built from" and has "continued to deliver tremendous achievements for the State of Israel" throughout his career.

Dolgopyat, who was born in Ukraine and immigrated to Israel with his family as a child, has become one of the country's most decorated Olympians and a familiar face at state ceremonies honouring Israeli sport. Friday's gold keeps him unbeaten on the biggest European stage for floor exercise across three separate championship cycles.

title: Espanyol and Real Madrid goalless at half-time in Mourinho's La Liga bow

title: Lugano 2-1 Maccabi Tel Aviv: mistake after mistake leaves European campaign in the balance
dek: A losing night in Switzerland has ONE's podcast panel piling into Maccabi Tel Aviv's recruitment and defensive errors, with Kenny Miller's side needing a comeback in Batumi to stay in the Conference League.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's European campaign is teetering after a chastening 2-1 defeat away to Lugano in the first leg of their Conference League play-off, a result that leaves Kenny Miller's side needing to overturn the tie in Batumi next week just to stay alive on the continent.

Lugano took the lead through Kevin Behrens in the 30th minute, and although Ido Shahar dragged Maccabi level within moments of the restart, Anto Grgic restored the hosts' advantage from the penalty spot in the 54th minute to seal a 2-1 win in front of 3,435 fans in Switzerland.

The return leg is set for 27 August in Batumi, Georgia — the venue Maccabi Tel Aviv have used for their own European 'home' fixtures this season — leaving the Israeli champions needing at least a two-goal swing to progress.

It is the latest blow in what has already been a bruising qualifying campaign. Maccabi were knocked out of Europa League qualifying by CSKA Sofia earlier this month, losing 0-3 in the first leg in Batumi before a spirited 3-1 win in Sofia proved not enough, going out 4-3 on aggregate.

On ONE's football podcast, hosts Raz Amir, Oren Kadosh and Avi Nmeni described a club making the same errors on repeat, pointing to recruitment calls in the transfer market, muddled roles behind the scenes, and individual defensive mistakes that have now cost Maccabi across two separate European ties this summer.

Manager Kenny Miller had struck a defiant tone after the CSKA Sofia exit, saying his side had produced 'a very high level' against the Bulgarians and would be 'in a very good place' if they reproduced it against Lugano. Despite Thursday's result, Sport1 reported that Miller said he left Lugano with 'very positive feelings' about his team's performance.

The podcast also touched on the transfer market, where Maccabi have been trying to add reinforcements before the European window shuts. Nmeni predicted that midfielder Gabi Kanikovsky, a former Maccabi player now at Ferencvaros, would complete a return to the club within a fortnight — a claim that lines up with separate reporting from Sport5 and Walla that the two sides are in negotiations, though no fee or personal terms have been finalised.

Domestically, Maccabi are also plotting for Sunday's Israeli Premier League fixture against Hapoel Jerusalem, with the podcast questioning whether Miller will rotate his lineup given the crowded schedule and the second leg against Lugano just three days later.

For now, Maccabi Tel Aviv's European fate hangs on a result in Georgia. A club that entered the summer with continental ambitions finds itself, as ONE's panel put it, making mistake upon mistake — and running short of competitions left in which to fix them.

title: Inter pick up where they left off with a 4-1 rout of promoted Monza
dek: Hakan Çalhanoğlu's early strike was cancelled out by Gustavo Varela, but three goals in fifteen second-half minutes gave Cristian Chivu's champions a routine opening-day win at San Siro.
body: Inter opened the defence of their Serie A title with a scare before finding their rhythm, beating newly promoted Monza 4-1 at San Siro on Saturday evening in the first round of the 2026-27 season.

Hakan Çalhanoğlu gave the champions the perfect start, driving a shot in from range after just six minutes, but the lead lasted barely twenty. Gustavo Varela levelled for Monza in the 29th minute with a well-taken individual effort, and Cristian Chivu's side went in at the break level at 1-1 having looked, for long stretches of the first half, like a team still shaking off the summer.

Monza, back in the top flight after a season in Serie B and fielding a squad shorn of several injured and suspended players, will have taken real encouragement from that first-half showing under new coach Ivan Jurić, who was taking his first game in the Brianzoli dugout.

Whatever Chivu said at the break worked. Piotr Zieliński restored Inter's lead three minutes into the second half, lobbing goalkeeper Pizzignacco after the Monza stopper had come off his line following a cross from the left by Federico Dimarco.

From there Inter took full control. Francesco Pio Esposito, one of the club's own academy products, made it 3-1 in the 55th minute with an audacious back-heeled finish that had San Siro on its feet, and Yann Bisseck added a fourth on 63 minutes to complete a rout that felt a long way from the uncertain opening period.

The result means Inter began the title defence with all three points, if not with the fluency Chivu will want as the season develops. Ivan Jurić's Monza, for their part, can point to a competitive first half against the champions as a reasonable platform on their return to Serie A.

There was a personal subplot too: Lautaro Martínez started on his 29th birthday but could not add a goal to the celebrations, picking up a yellow card in a match that otherwise belonged to Inter's second-half substitutes and squad depth.

ONE's report on the match, headlined "picked up where it stopped: a big 4-1 for Inter over Monza," framed the result as a continuation of the champions' dominant recent form heading into the new campaign, despite the shaky start against newly promoted opposition.

title: What is pyramid training at the gym, and who is it actually for?
dek: A gradually rising or falling ladder of weight and reps, pyramid training is a staple of serious bodybuilding programmes — but coaches warn it is not a method for beginners.

verificationSources.label: ONE - מהו אימון פירמידה במכון הכושר ולמי הוא מתאים?

body: Anyone who has spent time around a serious weight room has likely heard a coach mention "pyramid training" — a structure in which the weight on the bar and the number of reps per set change together, climbing or falling like the sides of a pyramid rather than staying fixed set after set.

According to ONE's health and fitness section, the method comes in a few distinct shapes. The most common is the ascending pyramid: the lifter starts with a relatively light weight and a high number of reps on the first set, then adds weight while cutting reps on each subsequent set. The early, lighter sets double as a built-in warm-up that primes the muscle without shocking it.

The descending pyramid runs the sequence in reverse. After a separate warm-up, the lifter goes straight into the heaviest work set while energy reserves are freshest, then strips weight off and adds reps as sets go on and fatigue builds.

A third variation — the double, or full, pyramid — combines both directions in a single exercise: weight and intensity climb to a peak in the middle of the set sequence, then taper back down. ONE describes this as producing particularly high metabolic stress and a strong overall training stimulus.

The appeal, per the report, is that pyramid schemes let a lifter chase two goals in one exercise: the high-rep, lighter-weight sets build muscular endurance and hypertrophy, while the heavy, low-rep sets near the top of the pyramid build maximum strength. Cycling through both also helps prevent the plateaus that come from doing the same sets and reps week after week.

ONE is clear, however, that this is not a method for newcomers. The piece recommends pyramid training for intermediate and advanced gym-goers who have already mastered correct technique on the lifts involved, calling it especially well suited to bodybuilders looking to add muscle through carefully controlled, progressive overload.

Beginners, by contrast, are better served sticking to stable weights and consistent rep counts while they build foundational strength and lock in proper form — introducing constantly shifting loads too early, the report notes, works against learning the movement correctly.

The article is credited to Shai Lev, a basketball coach and certified gym and TRX instructor who has edited ONE's health and fitness output since 2013, and carries the standard caveat that readers should check with a qualified professional before adopting any new training programme.

title: Hull City 2-0 Manchester United: newly promoted Tigers stun Carrick's side on opening day
dek: Sky Sports' Ron Walker says Hull's win at the MKM Stadium was built on "blood, guts and fight" - exactly what was missing from a toothless Manchester United.

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports - Hull City 2-0 Man Utd match report
NBC Sports - Michael Carrick reaction after Hull defeat
Fotmob - Hull City 2-0 Manchester United report

body: Michael Carrick's first competitive test since being handed the Manchester United job on a permanent basis ended in humiliation on the opening weekend of the Premier League season, as newly promoted Hull City beat his side 2-0 at the MKM Stadium.

Semi Ajayi gave the Tigers the lead in the 17th minute, capitalising on a defensive mix-up to poke the ball home from close range, and Nobel Mendy doubled the advantage with a firm header just before half-time. United never found an answer.

It was Hull's first Premier League fixture since they were relegated at the end of the 2016-17 season, and reports of the game described it as the club's first-ever league win over United. The Tigers marked their return to the top flight in style, unsettling one of the division's traditional heavyweights from the opening whistle.

Sky Sports' Ron Walker described the win as built on "blood, guts and fight" from Hull. "It felt like they were first to every ball, gave more to reach every header and didn't give United an inch throughout," he wrote. "That was exactly what Man Utd lacked. They didn't look anywhere near as up for it and paid the price." ONE's report on the match framed the defeat in almost identical terms, saying United had shown none of the courage and fighting spirit that carried Hull to victory.

Carrick brought on Marcus Rashford for his first appearance for the club since December 2024, following a spell out of favour under predecessor Ruben Amorim and loan moves away from Old Trafford, but the forward received little service and could not engineer a way back into the game.

"We're bitterly disappointed with the result, but we won't let it knock us," Carrick said afterwards. Pressed on the wider picture, he added that it was "one game, first game of the season" and insisted it "doesn't change the whole course of direction the team is going in or the football club."

Carrick took permanent charge in May, after a caretaker spell following Amorim's January sacking had steered United to third place and back into Champions League contention. The defeat at Hull was his first game since signing a contract through 2028, and it undercut much of the optimism built up over the summer.
ONE's report also pointed to United's defensive vulnerabilities and suggested the club needs reinforcements before the transfer window shuts, with roughly ten days left before deadline day.
For Hull, the result is as good a start as any newly promoted side could hope for - and a rare piece of schadenfreude at Manchester United's expense on the very first weekend of the season.
