title: West Ham 1-2 Charlton: Solomon again the standout as Hammers stumble at home
dek: Manor Solomon was singled out as one of the few West Ham players to emerge with credit from a stoppage-time collapse against Charlton Athletic in the club's first home Championship game of the season.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "סולומון היה השחקן החד והתוסס ביותר שלנו"
Sky Sports - West Ham United 1-2 Charlton Athletic match report
West Ham United - Starting XI: Solomon makes West Ham debut at Burnley

body: Manor Solomon's whirlwind first fortnight in claret and blue continued to produce more than his side's results deserved on Saturday, as West Ham United's first home league game of the season unravelled into a 1-2 defeat by Charlton Athletic at London Stadium.

The Championship newcomers took the lead through Charlton, and although Taty Castellanos was handed a stoppage-time lifeline from the penalty spot, his effort struck the base of the post, leaving West Ham to open their home campaign with nothing to show for it.

Amid the wreckage of a difficult afternoon for Nuno Espírito Santo's side, Solomon was one of the names supporters kept returning to. Steve Eisner, a widely followed West Ham fan analyst, wrote in a post carried by ONE that the Israeli winger "was our sharpest and most lively player in the first half" and "one of the few who looked truly ready for the game today."

According to ONE, Charlton set out to nullify Solomon specifically, doubling up on him for long spells and limiting the space he could work in - a mark of respect, in effect, for a player only two matches into his West Ham career. Even so, a fan rating site handed him a mark of 5, comfortably one of the higher scores dished out to a West Ham player on a day when most ratings sank low.

Solomon's other notable contribution came just before the break, when a shot he dragged goalward from the edge of the box was scrambled behind for a corner by Charlton centre-back Billy Koumetio - about as close as West Ham came to troubling the visitors' goal in the first 45 minutes.

Eisner's critique, as relayed by ONE, extended well beyond Solomon's individual display. He pointed to West Ham's reliance on long balls forced out to the flanks - 38 of them by his count, with only 10 finding a teammate - as evidence the team still lacks a clear attacking identity under Nuno, drawing an unflattering contrast with the more structured approach favoured by David Moyes during his time at the club.

Solomon's early West Ham story has otherwise been a rare bright note in a bruising opening to the season. He signed from Tottenham Hotspur on 10 August, and needed only his full debut - a 2-2 draw at Burnley six days later - to get off the mark, scoring West Ham's second goal in a display that also saw him lead the match for take-ons and shots.

The Israel international arrives at West Ham with an eclectic résumé: three Ukrainian league titles at Shakhtar Donetsk, spells in the Premier League with Fulham and Tottenham, a productive loan at Leeds United during their Championship-winning 2024/25 campaign, and stints in Spain and Italy with Villarreal and Fiorentina.

For West Ham, the manner of Saturday's defeat will sting far more than Solomon's promising cameo will soothe. But with two matches gone in a season already carrying heavy expectations at London Stadium, the early signs are that the club's newest Israeli signing will be one of the more reliable performers whatever unfolds around him.

title: Athletic Club 1-3 Sevilla: ten-man Basques undone as visitors make it two from two
dek: Yuri Berchiche's early red card leaves Athletic Bilbao chasing the game at San Mamés, and Sevilla punish them through Oso, Chidera Ejuke and Isaac Romero.

verificationSources.label: Fotmob - Sevilla vs Athletic Club match centre

body: Sevilla are two games into the new La Liga season and have taken maximum points from both, and this one barely felt like a contest once Athletic Club were reduced to ten men inside a quarter of an hour at San Mamés.

Yuri Berchiche, the veteran left-back, was shown a straight red card in the 11th minute for a foul on the edge of his own box, and Sevilla needed only four more minutes to make the numerical advantage count. Oso pounced after goalkeeper Unai Simón was caught in possession, rolling the ball home to put the visitors ahead.

Athletic, to their credit, did not fold immediately and worked their way back into the game for spells of the first half despite playing a man light. But the second period belonged entirely to Sevilla.

Chidera Ejuke, restored to the side after a summer spent on the fringes and reportedly close to an exit, came off the bench and needed only minutes to make his mark, converting in the 50th minute to double the lead.

Seven minutes later it was 3-0. Isaac Romero, Sevilla's first-choice striker, added a third with a finish that all but ended the contest as a spectacle, leaving Athletic to play out the rest of the afternoon for pride alone.

Aitor Paredes gave the home crowd something to cheer in the 70th minute, heading in from a corner to make it 3-1, but Sevilla's defence held firm from there and never looked in danger of surrendering the points.

The result means Sevilla have won both of their opening two league fixtures, banking six points and an early statement of intent under their current setup. Athletic Club, by contrast, will have to regroup after a chastening afternoon on home soil, undone as much by Berchiche's early dismissal as anything Sevilla did with the ball.

San Mamés, so often a fortress for Athletic in recent seasons, offered little protection this time, and the visitors leave the Basque Country with a result that will have been far more comfortable than the 3-1 scoreline might suggest given how the game was shaped in the opening quarter of an hour.

title: Anan Khalaili endures tough Premier League debut as Crystal Palace fall 2-0 to Everton
dek: The Israeli winger came off the bench at Hill Dickinson Stadium and struggled for service, though Palace-supporting outlets praised his defensive work and a clever assist that almost paid off

verificationSources.label: The Jerusalem Post on the transfer

body: Anan Khalaili's introduction to the Premier League came in defeat. The Israeli winger, signed by Crystal Palace for a club-record fee barely a week earlier, was sent on as a 55th-minute substitute as Palace lost 2-0 away to Everton on the opening weekend of the 2026-27 season.

Goals from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, three minutes before the break, and Thierno Barry, early in the second half, gave Everton their first win of the campaign at the Hill Dickinson Stadium and left Khalaili chasing the game from the moment he stepped onto the pitch.

ONE's review of his cameo was measured rather than glowing: the Israeli "showed his desire to go forward, but barely received the ball from his teammates," the outlet reported, calling it "a difficult game for his Premier League debut."

Sites covering Palace in detail saw more encouraging signs. We Are Palace wrote that Khalaili "dealt well with the defensive battles with Iliman Ndiaye" — Everton's influential forward — "and provided a fantastic cross for Jürgen Strand Larsen, which was headed over Jordan Pickford," a chance that could have hauled Palace back into the contest had it dropped under the crossbar rather than over it.
The Palace Way's take was shorter but no less positive: "He looks like a very promising player."

Khalaili, 21, joined Palace from Belgian champions Union Saint-Gilloise on August 15 in a deal reported at £21 million, a fee the Jerusalem Post described as record-breaking for an Israeli footballer, running to 2031.

Born in Haifa, he came up through Maccabi Haifa's academy before moving to Belgium, where he was a key part of the Union Saint-Gilloise side that won the 2024-25 Pro League title — ending a 90-year wait for the Brussels club's first championship since 1935.

He has also been capped repeatedly by Israel's senior national team and won bronze with the under-20s at the 2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup, arriving at Selhurst Park with a growing reputation even before Saturday's mixed bow.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv's Tal Archel has car broken into in Tel Aviv while team was in Italy
dek: Thieves smashed a window and stole cash and personal items from the centre-back's car, parked at the Wolfson complex, while his teammates faced Atalanta in the Conference League play-offs.
body: It has been an unpleasant few days for Tal Archel away from the pitch. While his Hapoel Tel Aviv teammates were in Bergamo preparing to face Atalanta in the Conference League play-offs, someone broke into his car back home in Tel Aviv, ONE reports.

According to the report, the centre-back's vehicle was parked in the Wolfson complex parking area when it was targeted. The intruder smashed one of the car's windows and made off with cash and personal equipment that had been left inside.

Efforts are now under way to identify the culprit, with investigators reviewing footage from the security cameras installed around the Wolfson parking area in the hope the images will help establish exactly what happened and who was responsible.

The timing added an unwelcome distraction to what was already a demanding week for the club. Hapoel Tel Aviv travelled to Bergamo for the first leg of their Conference League play-off against Atalanta, Maurizio Sarri's Serie A side and the 2023-24 Europa League champions, with the tie finishing goalless on August 20. The second leg is due to be played a week later at a neutral venue in Hungary, with a place in the league phase still up for grabs.

Archel, 23, is a product of Hapoel Tel Aviv's youth system, having joined the club's ranks as a child and worked his way through every age group before making his first-team debut in the 2022-23 Toto Cup against Ashdod. He has since become an established figure in the club's defence and signed a contract extension earlier this year that runs through the 2028-29 season.

There has been no word yet from the club on the incident, and no suspect has been named. ONE's report remains the only detailed account of the break-in so far, though the underlying facts — the team's presence in Italy for the Atalanta tie and Archel's standing at the club — are well established independently.

title: Kani, Bruninho and Saief start as Maccabi Haifa host Hapoel Ramat Gan in league opener
dek: Haifa named a strong attacking three for the Israeli Premier League's season opener at Sami Ofer Stadium, where Hapoel Ramat Gan return to the top flight after 13 years away.
body: The Israeli Premier League returns tonight, and Maccabi Haifa are opening the 2026/27 season at home to a familiar old rival wearing an unfamiliar shirt in the top flight. Hapoel Ramat Gan, back among Israel's elite after 13 years away, arrive at Sami Ofer Stadium for a 20:30 kickoff that has been building interest all week, ONE reports.

Haifa's coaching staff have gone with an attacking look for the opener. According to ONE's report, Omri Glazer starts in goal behind a back line of Yila Betai, Nigel Lonwijk, Pedrão and Wanderson, the Brazilian full-back known at the club as 'Tsunami'. Yarin Levi and Eitan Azulai sit in midfield alongside close-season signing Bruninho, with Kenny Saief, Kenji Gora and Silva Kani forming the attacking trio in front of them.

That front three carries plenty of intrigue. Bruninho arrived from Karpaty Lviv in a reported €1.75 million deal over the summer and impressed in Toto Cup preparation, while Saief and Kani were both prominent in Haifa's Premier League matches before the international break. Their inclusion together, spelled out in the report's headline, signals a Haifa side set up to attack from the first whistle in front of its own supporters.

Hapoel Ramat Gan will not simply be making up the numbers. Promoted after more than a decade in the lower divisions, the club has spent the close season insisting it wants to be taken seriously rather than treated as an obvious relegation candidate, and a positive result in Haifa would go a long way toward proving that point on opening night.

ONE lists Ramat Gan's XI as Amit Raif in goal, with Getachew Yablo, Omer Yitzhak, Fared Ibrahim and Dudi Toyto across the back four. Srđan Mijailović, Ido Oli and Maksim Palkoshchenko operate through the middle, with Luan Campos, David Asenka and Idan Barnes completing the attacking line.

There is a personal edge to the occasion for a couple of Ramat Gan's players. Sport5 reports that Getachew Yablo is set to face his former club for the first time in the league, while Palkoshchenko — another ex-Haifa player — is expected to lead the visitors' attack.

The history between these two clubs stretches back well over a decade without a meeting in the top division. ONE notes the sides last played each other in Ligat Ha'al on 20 January 2013, when Maccabi Haifa won 3-0 away at Ramat Gan, having also won the reverse fixture that same 2012/13 season 2-0.

With that gap now closed, both clubs will be looking to set an early tone: Haifa to show their revamped attack can deliver a winning start at home, Ramat Gan to make clear their promotion was no fluke.

body: Ligat Ha'al kicks off its 2026/27 season on Saturday evening, and Maccabi Petah Tikva open their campaign at home to Ironi Kiryat Shmona knowing they have gone winless against the northern club since a solitary 2-1 victory back in May 2021.

At the other end, ONE's report has Alex Sola and Talles Costa both included in Kiryat Shmona's starting eleven, giving Shay Barda's side an experienced attacking presence to call on from the first whistle.

Squad turnover has been so heavy since that last head-to-head that Mohammed Hindi, Maccabi Petah Tikva's captain, is the only player from either side still involved who featured when the teams previously met.

Kiryat Shmona arrive off a promising preseason, having advanced to the semi-final of the Toto Cup, and Barda will hope that cup form translates into a strong start to the league campaign under the lights in Petah Tikva.

title: The public wants broadcasters, not hype men, argues top Ynet columnist
dek: Guy Leiba says Israeli football commentary has become frightened cheerleading for a mediocre league — and that real journalism means being willing to call a bad match bad.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — העם רוצה שדרים, לא יחצנים (Guy Leiba column)

body: Israeli football's broadcasting problem isn't a lack of knowledge, Ynet columnist Guy Leiba argues in a sharp new piece — it's a lack of courage. His column, published this week under the headline "The public wants broadcasters, not publicists," accuses the country's football commentators of having quietly turned into cheerleaders for a product they should be scrutinising.

Leiba's central charge is structural. Broadcasters and pundits, he writes, live inside the same ecosystem as the players, coaches and agents they're supposed to be covering — they socialise with them, get interviewed by them, follow them on social media and are followed back. That closeness, he argues, has quietly replaced critical distance with self-censorship.

Social media fear looms over everything, according to the column. Say a player had a poor game and expect a hundred angry messages; criticise the crowd and a clip gets cut for pile-on outrage on TikTok; call a marquee match boring and risk being accused of "lowering the product." The result, Leiba says, is commentary engineered to avoid backlash rather than to inform.

He takes aim at the reflexive marketing language broadcasters reach for instead — clichés like "it's ours" and "we missed this" deployed to paper over an Israeli top flight that, in his telling, is a comedown after a World Cup summer, the domestic equivalent of trading Disneyland for a mediocre local water park.

Dull, defensive matches get relabelled "tactical" rather than admitted to be simply bad, Leiba writes — broadcasters manufacturing drama that isn't on the pitch rather than saying plainly that a game underwhelmed.

The column holds up the late Meir Einstein, the veteran Israeli broadcaster who died in 2017, as the standard the current generation has abandoned. Einstein, Leiba writes, could call a poor match poor without flinching, and was willing to challenge misbehaving crowds or officials directly rather than smoothing it over for the audience.

On stadium violence, Leiba is blunt: every time a flare lands on the pitch, he writes, "the usual ritual begins" — expressions of regret from the broadcast booth, but no real pursuit of who is responsible or what should change. Sympathy substitutes for scrutiny.

His closing argument is a plea for respect rather than reassurance: broadcasters, he writes, can "stop fearing the viewer and simply respect them with the truth" instead of manufacturing enthusiasm for a league that, on plenty of nights, does not deserve it.

The piece lands as one of the more pointed pieces of media self-criticism published in Israeli sport this year, aimed less at any single commentator than at a broadcasting culture Leiba says has confused proximity to the game with loyalty to it.

title: Cocaine positive ends Nick Kyrgios's long fall from Wimbledon finalist to world No. 919
dek: The Australian who once branded Jannik Sinner and Iga Świątek's doping cases "disgusting" is now the one provisionally suspended, after a sample from Mallorca in June came back positive for a cocaine metabolite.
body: Ynet's sports desk frames it as the darkest twist yet in the Nick Kyrgios story: the self-styled "bad boy" of world tennis, provisionally suspended this week after testing positive for cocaine, barely a year after he stood in judgment of two of the sport's biggest stars for their own doping cases.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency confirmed that a sample Kyrgios gave at an ATP 250 event in Mallorca on June 22 came back positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine. A WADA-accredited laboratory verified the finding on July 17, and the Australian has been provisionally suspended from playing, coaching or even attending sanctioned events since August 4. The ITIA made the case public on August 19.

Kyrgios did not fight it. "I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it," he wrote in a statement, apologising to "my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me." He said the positive test had been a "wake-up call" and that he would step away from social media and public life for 28 days. His case now goes to an independent tribunal, which will determine any sanction; cocaine is treated by the anti-doping code as a substance of abuse, meaning reduced penalties can apply when use is established as out of competition.

The irony has not been lost on Ynet or on the wider tennis press. Just last year Kyrgios tore into Jannik Sinner and Iga Świątek over their own doping violations, calling the handling of both cases "disgusting" for the sport and accusing the authorities of inconsistency and a lack of transparency. He is now the one facing the same integrity process he once said had failed everyone else.

At 31, Kyrgios is a long way from the player who reached the Wimbledon final in 2022, only to lose to Novak Djokovic, and who once sat as high as No. 13 in the world. Persistent injuries have wrecked the years since; he has played sparingly, and his ranking has collapsed to 919th, a fall that mirrors the physical toll he has spoken about publicly for years.

He built his career, and much of his fame, on confrontation as much as talent — smashing rackets, sparring with umpires and opponents, and cultivating an image at odds with tennis's buttoned-up culture. It made him one of the sport's most bankable, and most polarising, figures, with career prize money north of $12 million across seven titles.

But Kyrgios has also spoken candidly about the cost of that persona. He has described a mental state "created from the moment your brain wants something your body can no longer achieve," and in 2019 admitted to suicidal thoughts during a tournament in Mexico. Ynet's report ties that history directly to the current scandal, framing the cocaine positive as the latest, starkest chapter in a downward spiral rather than an isolated lapse.

Tennis has been here before. Richard Gasquet tested positive for cocaine in 2009 and successfully argued the trace came from kissing a woman in a nightclub. Mats Wilander and Karl Novacek were both banned for three months after positive tests in 1995. Martina Hingis was suspended over a positive cocaine test in 2007 and retired soon after. Björn Borg later admitted to heavy cocaine use after his own playing career ended.

Scientifically, cocaine offers tennis players nothing on court: it is a substance of abuse rather than a performance enhancer, producing a rush of confidence and energy for perhaps 15 to 30 minutes before a crash that leaves users worse off, not better.

For Kyrgios, the question now is less about performance than about what remains of a career already reduced to occasional appearances. A tribunal ruling will decide how long any ban runs, but for a player who built an identity on being tennis's loudest critic of everyone else's failings, the reckoning is now his own.

title: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz to team up for US Open mixed doubles
dek: The 23-time Grand Slam champion and the two-time defending US Open men's singles winner have been handed a wildcard into the revamped mixed doubles event, a marquee pairing for Williams' return to Flushing Meadows.
body: Serena Williams' comeback trail is about to cross with Carlos Alcaraz's return from injury, in one of the most eye-catching pairings tennis has produced in years. The United States Tennis Association confirmed on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz have been awarded a wildcard into the US Open mixed doubles main draw, Ynet reported.

It will be Williams' first appearance at Flushing Meadows since 2022. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion ended a four-year absence from the tour this June, playing singles at Wimbledon and doubles alongside her sister Venus at the Cincinnati Open before now adding a US Open wildcard to her comeback schedule.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, is coming back from his own lengthy layoff. The Spaniard has been sidelined since April with a right wrist injury and only confirmed this week that he will defend his US Open men's singles title, having won the tournament in each of the past two years.

Between them, the pair carry serious pedigree into the doubles draw: Williams' 23 major singles titles include five triumphs in New York, while Alcaraz has collected seven Grand Slam crowns of his own, most recently completing the career Grand Slam at this year's Australian Open.

The mixed doubles event has been reshaped this year specifically to lure singles stars into the format, with shortened four-game sets, no-advantage scoring and a 10-point tiebreak replacing a deciding third set. The changes have already drawn a stacked field, including Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic, 2025 finalists Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud, and defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori.
Alcaraz greeted the news of the partnership on social media with a simple message of excitement directed at Williams, after weeks of speculation fuelled by the pair's public exchanges online.

The mixed doubles main draw is set to open this week, with the champions sharing a $1 million prize. For Williams, it offers a low-pressure route back onto Arthur Ashe Stadium; for Alcaraz, a chance to sharpen his timing in doubles before turning his full attention to defending his singles crown.

title: Zagreb Gold Number Three: Drop the Hedge, Dolgopyat Is Already Israel's Greatest
dek: A third European floor title, an Olympic gold-and-silver double no other Israeli owns, and a world crown besides — the record has stopped being an argument for 'on course' and started being the case, full stop.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz — Dolgopyat takes third European gold, 2026 final

verificationSources.title: Israel National News — Dolgopyat wins third European title
verificationSources.label: Israel National News — Dolgopyat wins third European title in floor exercise

body: Artem Dolgopyat won his third European floor exercise title in Zagreb on Friday, scoring 14.666 to beat Arsenii Dukhno (14.333) and Britain's Harry Hepworth (14.300). It was his first continental gold since 2022 — he had gone silver in 2023, silver in 2024 and a shock seventh in 2025 — and at 29, in a discipline that chews up explosive tumblers by their mid-twenties, it was also a small act of defiance against his own body clock.

The framing around it has been cautious: Dolgopyat is 'on course' to become Israel's greatest-ever athlete, as if the verdict is still pending. It isn't. Line up the ledger and the hedge collapses. Tokyo 2020 Olympic gold on floor — Israel's first Olympic medal in gymnastics. Paris 2024 Olympic silver on the same apparatus, making him the first Israeli to win back-to-back Olympic medals. A World Championship gold in Antwerp in 2023, the first world title an Israeli gymnast has ever won, sitting alongside world silvers from Montreal 2017 and Stuttgart 2019. And now three European floor golds, won nine years apart at the start and end of that span. No Israeli has ever built a trophy case that deep across all three tiers of the sport — Olympics, Worlds, Europeans — let alone sustained it for nearly a decade.

That longevity is the part getting undersold. Elite men's floor exercise rewards fast-twitch power that erodes early; the gymnasts who own the event tend to be in and out of contention within a five- or six-year window. Dolgopyat's peak has run from a world silver at 20 to a European gold at 29. That's not just medal count, it's a career shape almost nobody in his event replicates, and it's why 'on course' — a phrase that implies he still has something left to prove — undersells what's already banked.

The obvious historical rival is Gal Fridman, the windsurfer whose bronze in Atlanta in 1996 and gold in Athens in 2004 made him Israel's first Olympic champion and, until recently, its benchmark. Fridman and Dolgopyat remain the only two Israelis ever to win multiple individual Olympic medals — a fact that alone tells you how thin this country's list of true greats actually is. But Dolgopyat's pair is gold-then-silver rather than bronze-then-gold, and it comes bolted onto a global and continental record Fridman never had to match. This isn't a knock on Fridman, who broke the ground everyone after him walked on. It's just an honest read of two ledgers side by side.

The other names in the conversation prove the same point from a different angle. Yael Arad's judo silver in Barcelona in 1992 was Israel's first Olympic medal of any kind and remains one of the most important moments in the country's sporting history — but it was one medal, one Games. Linoy Ashram's rhythmic gymnastics gold in Tokyo, the first Olympic gold won by an Israeli woman, was similarly a single, brilliant peak rather than a sustained run across multiple cycles. Dolgopyat isn't just deeper than his rivals on a medal table; he's deeper across time, which is the harder thing to manufacture in any sport.

The pushback worth taking seriously is the team-sport one: Maccabi Tel Aviv's basketball side has won six European championships — 1977, 1981, 2001, 2004, 2005 and 2014 — and Tal Brody's 1977 side did more for how Israelis saw themselves in the world than any individual medal since. That history is real and it shouldn't be minimised. But it's also a different unit of measurement. Six European titles were won by dozens of different players across four decades; no single roster member can claim personal ownership of all six the way Dolgopyat owns every centimetre of his own ledger. 'Greatest athlete' is a question about one body doing something extraordinary and repeating it; 'greatest team era' is a different question entirely, and conflating them is how these debates get muddled.

There is a genuine limit to the claim, and it's worth stating plainly rather than glossing over: Dolgopyat is a floor specialist, not an all-arounder, and on the truly global stage of men's artistic gymnastics — next to a Kohei Uchimura or a Kenzo Shirai — he isn't the best gymnast the sport has produced. But 'greatest Israeli athlete' was never that question. It's a domestic bar, set by what this country's sporting culture, funding and depth have actually produced, and against that bar Dolgopyat's specialism is irrelevant. He didn't need to be the best in the world at six apparatus. He needed to be the best in the world at one, repeatedly, for nine years, representing a country that had never produced an Olympic gymnastics medal before he arrived — and he was.

There's a real risk ahead, and it's fair to name it: Los Angeles 2028 will find him 31, an age at which floor specialists are usually watching from the stands rather than the podium. If Zagreb turns out to be his last major final, some will say the résumé stalled short of a third Olympic medal. That's a fair regret to have, but it shouldn't be allowed to retroactively shrink what's already there. The greatest-ever case doesn't rest on what happens in Los Angeles. It rests on a body of work that's already complete enough to stand on its own — an Olympic gold and silver in the same event, a world title, three European crowns — regardless of how the next two years go.

So retire the 'on course' framing. It was a reasonable hedge in 2021, when Tokyo gold was a single extraordinary data point that might have been a peak rather than a plateau. It stopped being reasonable somewhere around Antwerp in 2023, and Zagreb this weekend just underlined the point a third time. Israeli sport doesn't produce arguments like this often — a genuinely uncontested case, built entirely on verifiable results rather than nostalgia or platform. When it does, the least the coverage owes it is to say so without the qualifier.
facts: Dolgopyat won his third European floor exercise title in Zagreb on 21 August 2026, scoring 14.666 ahead of silver medallist Arsenii Dukhno (14.333) and bronze medallist Harry Hepworth of Great Britain (14.300).

He is the reigning Tokyo 2020 Olympic floor exercise champion and the Paris 2024 Olympic silver medallist on the same apparatus (14.966), making him the first Israeli to win back-to-back Olympic medals.
His 2023 Antwerp floor gold was Israel's first-ever World Artistic Gymnastics Championships gold medal; he also won world silvers in Montreal (2017) and Stuttgart (2019).

His prior European floor golds came in Mersin (2020) and Munich (2022); he also has European silvers from Glasgow (2018), Szczecin (2019), Antalya (2023) and Rimini (2024), plus a bronze on vault in Mersin (2020).
Gal Fridman remains the only other Israeli to win two individual Olympic medals: bronze in windsurfing at Atlanta 1996 and gold at Athens 2004, the latter Israel's first Olympic gold.
Yael Arad's judo silver at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics was Israel's first-ever Olympic medal.
Linoy Ashram won Israel's first rhythmic gymnastics Olympic medal and the first individual Olympic gold by an Israeli woman, in the all-around at Tokyo 2020.

title: Dimarco names Lamine Yamal the toughest opponent of his career
dek: Ahead of Inter's Serie A opener against Monza, the Italy wing-back said facing Barcelona's teenage sensation three times left a deeper mark than any other rival — even though he limited him to a single goal.
body: Federico Dimarco has faced no shortage of gifted attackers in his career at Inter Milan and with Italy, but asked to name the single hardest opponent he has ever played against, the left wing-back did not hesitate: Lamine Yamal.

"If I had to think of the toughest opponent I've ever faced, I'd say Lamine Yamal," Dimarco said in an interview carried by Inter's official matchday programme ahead of the club's Serie A opener against Monza, and reported by the Israeli outlet ONE.

The remark carries extra weight given the numbers. Dimarco has come up against the Barcelona and Spain teenager three times, including Inter's dramatic 4-3 Champions League win over Barça in last season's semi-final second leg, and restricted Yamal to just a single goal across those meetings. Even so, he said the Spaniard was the most unsettling attacker he has encountered.

Dimarco also used the interview to play down his own individual honours. He was voted Serie A's Most Valuable Player last season after also setting the division's single-season assist record, but he brushed off the achievement as a new campaign begins. "Winning the MVP award last season doesn't count anymore — we start from zero," he said, adding that the assist record had crept up on him rather than being a target he set out to chase.
According to ONE's report, Dimarco pointed to Inter's Coppa Italia triumph as the most emotionally significant trophy of his career to date, above any individual prize.
He also touched on his footballing influences growing up, naming Brazilian great Ronaldo — "il Fenomeno" — as his childhood idol, alongside former Inter forward Diego Milito.

The comments arrive as Inter prepare to open their 2026/27 Serie A campaign at home to Monza, with Dimarco again expected to be a key figure down the left flank for a side aiming to build on last season's run to the Champions League final.

title: Miller fronts the media as Maccabi Tel Aviv regroup for Hapoel Jerusalem opener
dek: The head coach addressed reporters two days after a 2-1 first-leg defeat to Lugano, with the State Cup holders due to open their Ligat Ha'al campaign away to Hapoel Jerusalem on Sunday.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C. (Kenny Miller appointed head coach)

body: Two days after a bruising night in Switzerland, Kenny Miller sat down in front of Israeli reporters on Saturday for a press briefing streamed live on ONE, previewing Maccabi Tel Aviv's first match of the new Ligat Ha'al season away to Hapoel Jerusalem.

Miller's side travel to the capital for a 20:15 kick-off on Sunday, looking to open their domestic campaign with a response after Thursday's 2-1 defeat away to FC Lugano in the first leg of their Europa Conference League play-off tie.

Lugano took the lead through Kevin Behrens before Ido Shahar levelled for the visitors early in the second half, only for Anto Grgić's penalty to restore the Swiss side's advantage and leave Maccabi a goal down to overturn in next Thursday's return leg at Bloomfield.

ONE's live coverage of the press conference did not carry direct quotes from Miller at the time of publication, with the briefing still being broadcast as the report went up, but the Scot was expected to address both his side's response to the European setback and his selection for the trip to Jerusalem.

It is a significant week for Miller regardless of what he tells the room. The 46-year-old only took permanent charge of Maccabi Tel Aviv in June, having arrived in January as Ronny Deila's assistant and then stepped up as caretaker when Deila left in May — guiding the club to an unlikely Israeli State Cup triumph over Hapoel Be'er Sheva along the way.

That cup run, and the club's subsequent decision to hand him a full-time contract for 2026/27 with an option for a further season, means Sunday's trip to Hapoel Jerusalem effectively opens Miller's first full campaign at the helm, with the Lugano tie still very much alive going into Thursday's second leg.

Hapoel Jerusalem host the opening round of the new Ligat Ha'al season at home, and a Maccabi side already nursing a European setback will want a fast start in the capital before their focus swings back to Europe for the second leg against Lugano.

title: Hull City 2-0 Manchester United: promoted side stuns Carrick's men on opening day
dek: Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy scored either side of half-time as newly promoted Hull City beat Manchester United at the MKM Stadium in the Premier League's opening round
body: "Is this how you open a season?" ONE asked pointedly after Manchester United's return to Premier League action ended in humiliation at the MKM Stadium, where newly promoted Hull City beat Michael Carrick's side 2-0 to open the 2026-27 campaign.

It was a stunning start for Hull, who were back in the English top flight for the first time in nine years, and a grim one for United, who arrived at the seaside-adjacent stadium in East Yorkshire as the visitors expected to make a statement rather than suffer one.

Hull took the lead in the 17th minute. Regan Slater's corner was only half cleared, Oliver McBurnie's follow-up effort cannoned back off the woodwork, and Semi Ajayi reacted fastest to poke the rebound home from close range.

The hosts doubled their advantage just before the break. Slater again supplied the delivery, this time from a free kick, and Nobel Mendy rose above United's defence to power a header past the goalkeeper and make it 2-0 at half-time.

Carrick responded by sending on Marcus Rashford at the interval in search of a route back into the game, and United did enjoy the better of the ball after half-time, according to reports of the match, with nearly 70 percent possession in the second period.

But territory rarely translated into danger. Hull's back line stayed compact and organised, and goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis produced a crucial late save to deny Bryan Mbeumo the goal that might have set up a grandstand finish.

Instead, Hull held on comfortably for a result that will be replayed on highlight reels for weeks: a club fresh off promotion putting one of England's grandest names to the sword on the opening weekend.

For United and Carrick, the defeat means the pressure that always attends the club starts early this season, with questions about the team's cutting edge and its ability to break down a well-drilled defence following them into next weekend's fixture.

For Hull, it was a dream return to the top flight — the kind of afternoon that instantly turns Ajayi and Mendy, both scorers on the biggest stage the club has occupied in almost a decade, into local heroes.

title: Israel's basketball cadets beat Italy 58-53 to finish 13th at European Championship
dek: The under-16 women's national team closes a mixed tournament in Romania with a second win over Italy, but 13th place still means relegation to Division B for next season.
body: Israel's under-16 women's national basketball team – known in Hebrew as the "cadets" – closed out the European Championship in Romania with a 58-53 win over Italy that secured 13th place, ONE reports.

It was the second time in the tournament Israel had beaten the Italians. The teams also met in the opening round, when Israel ran away with a 68-37 win, according to the Israel Basketball Association's own coverage of the event.

The finish carries a sting, though: despite closing on a high note, Israel will play next season in Division B rather than the top tier. ONE reports that Bulgaria, which finished last in the tournament, will host next summer's championship and therefore keeps its place among the elite group, a quirk of the relegation format that worked against the young Israeli side.
Michal Abudraham was the standout in the decisive game against Italy, finishing with 19 points, eight rebounds and six steals before fouling out with six and a half minutes still on the clock.

With their top scorer off the floor, the rest of the roster had to see the game home. Tahel Dogan added 14 points, Rona Tzlal chipped in 13 points and three assists down the stretch, and Eden Fuls scored five as Israel held on for the five-point win.

Coach Daniella Reuven's squad had a bumpy road to the 13th-place game. After the opening rout of Italy, Israel lost in the group phase and were knocked into the placement bracket, then suffered a further defeat to Lithuania that dropped them into the fight for 13th through 16th place.
Israel responded by beating Romania before setting up the rematch with Italy, closing the tournament with back-to-back wins even as the overall finish confirmed the drop to Division B.

For a development-age national team, the placement offers a mixed verdict: genuine quality on display in wins over Italy and Romania, but a group stage that proved costly enough to send Israel down a tier for next year's European Championship.

title: Birmingham 2-2 Bristol City: Eissat goes the distance but Robins still winless
dek: A stoppage-time Demarai Gray penalty snatched a point for Birmingham and denied Lisav Eissat's Bristol City a first win of the Championship season.

verificationSources.label: The72 - Bristol City sign Lisav Eissat

body: Bristol City are still waiting for their first win of the Championship season after Birmingham City snatched a 2-2 draw at St Andrew's with a penalty deep into stoppage time, with new signing Lisav Eissat playing every minute of the frustration.

The Robins twice led through Scott Twine and Dom Ballard, only for Birmingham to claw back level both times and then find a way through in the 95th minute, when Demarai Gray converted from the spot after Rob Atkinson was penalised for fouling Christoph Klarer in the area.
It meant a fourth game of the young season without a win for Bristol City, who opened their campaign with a 2-0 defeat away to Millwall and now sit on a single point from a possible six.

Eissat, the 21-year-old centre-back bought from Maccabi Haifa this summer, again started at the back for head coach Michael Skubula and played the full 90 minutes, part of a settled defensive unit alongside Rob Dickie and George Tanner.
Bristol City confirmed the €2.5 million signing of Eissat from Maccabi Haifa in July, on a four-year deal that made him one of five summer additions as the club moved to strengthen its backline.

Eissat was born in Israel and came through Maccabi Haifa's academy, winning youth titles at under-16 and under-19 level before a breakthrough loan spell at Hapoel Hadera and a return to the Haifa first team, where he made 33 senior appearances.

He represented Israel at every youth level from under-15 to under-21, but opted to switch allegiance and made his senior international debut for Romania in October 2025, in a 2-1 friendly win over Moldova.

For Birmingham, also without a win after opening the season with a goalless draw against Sheffield United, the late leveller offered some relief following a match in which they twice found themselves behind at home.

Bristol City will now look to convert their promising performances into results when they return to Ashton Gate, still searching for the victory that has so far eluded both Skubula's rebuilt side and the club's new Israeli-developed defender.

title: Atalanta land Elmas on loan as Goretzka closes in on free Aston Villa move
dek: Eljif Elmas has completed a loan switch to Atalanta from RB Leipzig, while Leon Goretzka is reported to have reached a verbal agreement to join Aston Villa as a free agent after leaving Bayern Munich.

body: Atalanta moved to bolster Maurizio Sarri's midfield options on Saturday, confirming the signing of Eljif Elmas on loan from RB Leipzig with an option to buy at the end of the season.

The North Macedonia international returns to Serie A after a single season in Germany, having previously played for both Napoli and Torino in Italy. At Atalanta he reunites with sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli, who brought him to Napoli, though he will work under a top-flight coach for the first time in Sarri.

Elmas, 26, made 189 Serie A appearances across his two previous Italian clubs, contributing 19 goals and 13 assists, and Bergamo's move for him was described locally as a surprise, quick-turnaround deal completed with Leipzig in a matter of days.

Away from Bergamo, ONE also reports that Leon Goretzka is closing in on a move to Aston Villa. According to the outlet, the German midfielder is in the process of finalising a switch to Villa Park after leaving Bayern Munich at the end of his contract following eight seasons at the Bavarian club.

Multiple English outlets covering the deal say Unai Emery held a direct call with Goretzka that proved decisive, with a verbal agreement now in place and a medical expected in the coming days. The 31-year-old made 312 appearances for Bayern between 2018 and 2026, scoring 51 goals.

Villa's interest is driven by need: the club lost Youri Tielemans to Manchester United and saw Enzo Barrenechea depart for Benfica this summer, while Amadou Onana is expected to miss most of the season after tearing his ACL on World Cup duty with Belgium.
Neither club has yet issued a formal announcement on Goretzka, so the move remains a reported agreement rather than a completed transfer pending his medical and signature.

title: Dolgopyat's coach: winning that medal felt like giving birth
dek: Sergei Weisberg reflects on Artem Dolgopyat's third European floor title in Zagreb, saying every final is a battle before the real celebration can begin
body: Sergei Weisberg has coached Artem Dolgopyat for close to two decades, since the teenager arrived at Maccabi Tel Aviv from Ukraine, and he still isn't blase about the feeling of watching him win. Speaking to ONE after Dolgopyat claimed gold in the floor exercise final at the European Championships in Zagreb on Friday evening, Weisberg reached for an unusual comparison to describe it.

"Achieving a medal in artistic gymnastics is like giving birth," he told the outlet. "Even just qualifying for a final requires tremendous effort." It was, he said, a relief as much as a celebration, the release of tension that builds through qualification, semi-final and final before an athlete gets anywhere near a podium.
"I'm happy," Weisberg added, according to ONE. "I always believed Artyom could do something extraordinary. He did."

The gold, Dolgopyat's third European title on floor exercise after previous wins in 2020 and 2022, was also his seventh career medal at the championships, a run of consistency at the top of European gymnastics that stretches back to 2018. He has added silvers at four other editions of the event across that span.

It sits alongside an Olympic gold from Tokyo in 2020 and Olympic silver from Paris in 2024, plus a World Championship gold in 2023, giving the 29-year-old one of the most decorated careers in Israeli sport.

Zagreb was not only about the individual final. Dolgopyat also competed in the team event, where Israel finished 10th, a result ONE reports secured the country's berth at the World Championships in Rotterdam in October. His father Oleg was in the arena to watch him compete, according to the outlet.
Looking ahead, Weisberg told ONE the plan now is to keep working on both floor exercise and the all-around discipline as Dolgopyat builds toward a bid for a third Olympics, in Los Angeles in 2028.

ONE also reported that Israeli teammate Ron Piatok was due in the parallel bars final later the same evening in Zagreb, giving the Israeli delegation a second final to watch on a busy night at the championships.

The poll invites readers to weigh in on the season ahead: which match they are most looking forward to, whether they hold a season subscription, and their views on fixtures being scheduled for Saturdays — long a point of friction in Israeli football between secular and religious sensibilities.

On the competitive side, ONE asks fans to predict who will lift the championship plate, which clubs will be dragged into the relegation fight, which team will prove the season's biggest disappointment, which coach will be first to lose their job, and who will finish as the league's top scorer.

The survey turns notably serious when it reaches the stands themselves. ONE asks whether supporters feel safe attending matches, whether fear of violence keeps some fans away from stadiums altogether, and what they make of ticket and subscription pricing — questions that speak to persistent concerns around crowd safety in Israeli football.

The poll is being run alongside the return of ONE's fantasy football game, sponsored by Migdal, which is offering prizes to top performers including package trips to matches abroad and match-day meal vouchers throughout the season.

No results from the survey have been published yet. But by pairing questions about silverware with ones about security and cost, ONE's season-opener poll captures a mood among Israeli football supporters that is about far more than just who ends up champions.

title: Dolinski released from Israel basketball squad to make it to Tulsa on time
dek: The 21-year-old forward will miss this month's World Cup qualifiers against Poland and Latvia after the Israel Basketball Association let him go early so he can begin his studies in the United States on schedule, ONE reports.
body: Ilay Dolinski has been released from Israel's national basketball squad for this month's FIBA World Cup 2027 qualifying window, ONE reported, with the 21-year-old forward instead heading to the United States to begin his studies on time.

Head coach Ariel Beit-Halahmy's squad was preparing for a warm-up match in Georgia on August 23 before flying on to face Poland on August 27 and Latvia on August 30, both World Cup qualifiers. Dolinski needed to be in America by August 26, leaving no way to fit in even the friendly.

The Israel Basketball Association confirmed the decision was made to protect his move abroad. "In order not to harm the continuation of his academic and professional path, his request was granted," the union said, adding it hopes to see him back in national team colours before long.

Dolinski is not the only late change to the squad. Idan Zalmanson was also released from the same training camp after picking up a quadriceps injury, leaving Beit-Halahmy to reshuffle his frontcourt options just days before the Poland fixture.

For Dolinski, the timing is dictated by a big step in his career rather than any setback. The 2.04-metre forward committed to the University of Tulsa in July, joining the Golden Hurricane program for what will be his first season of NCAA basketball after a career built entirely in Israeli and European youth basketball.

He arrives in Oklahoma off a breakout campaign in Israel's top flight, where he averaged 7.7 points and 4.3 rebounds in around 17 minutes a night while on loan at Ironi Kiryat Ata from parent club Hapoel Tel Aviv, who hold his contract through 2029.

The move caps a rapid rise through the Israeli system. Dolinski progressed through the national cadet and under-18 sides before starring for Israel's under-20 team in 2024, and he earned his first senior call-up only this past February.

Missing the August window means Dolinski will watch from afar as Israel opens its World Cup qualifying campaign, but the federation's message was one of patience rather than frustration — a player they clearly view as part of the senior team's future, even if his path there now runs through American college basketball first.

title: Denis Valiyoulin retains discus world title with 49.78m throw in Daegu
dek: The Maccabi Tel Aviv veteran and Israeli national champion won gold in the rain at the World Masters Athletics Championships in South Korea, sealing it with his final attempt.
body: Denis Valiyoulin is a world champion again. The 39-year-old discus thrower, who competes domestically for Maccabi Tel Aviv, won gold in his age category at the World Masters Athletics Championships in South Korea, ONE reports, adding another title to an already decorated career on the veterans' circuit.

The competition, held outdoors in persistent rain, came down to the very last throw. Valiyoulin sent the discus out to 49.78 metres on his sixth and final attempt, the mark that ultimately separated him from the rest of the field.

According to ONE's account of the series, Valiyoulin built toward the winning throw steadily rather than peaking early: he opened with 46.69m, improved to 48.22m on his fourth attempt, 48.77m on his fifth, and then found the extra distance he needed on his last try in the wet conditions.
ONE reports the win means Valiyoulin has successfully defended the world title he took previously, underlining his status as one of the more consistent throwers in his bracket year after year.
At home, Valiyoulin is Israel's reigning national discus champion, a title he has held domestically for several years while also representing Maccabi Tel Aviv in the club's athletics section.

The championships are taking place in Daegu, South Korea, having opened on August 21 and running through September 3, with events split across Daegu Stadium and satellite venues including the Gyeongsan Citizen's Stadium. Organizers say roughly 11,000 athletes from 106 countries are competing across track, field and road disciplines, making it one of the largest masters sporting events in the world.

For Israeli masters athletics, a discipline that rarely draws headlines outside its own community, a repeat world title is a notable result — a reminder that Israeli representation at global veterans' level competition continues to punch above its size.

title: Solomon and Peretz start in England as Khalaili waits on the bench at Everton
dek: West Ham's matchday two starter and Southampton's first-choice goalkeeper both keep their places, while Crystal Palace's record signing hopes for a first Premier League appearance off the bench.
body: Three Israelis are in action across England this Saturday afternoon, with two of them trusted to start and a third left to wait for his chance from the bench.

Manor Solomon keeps his place in West Ham's attack for the home game against Charlton Athletic, the Hammers' second Championship fixture of the season after their relegation from the Premier League last term. Nuno Espírito Santo has stuck with the Israeli winger, who marked his West Ham debut with a goal in a 2-2 draw at Burnley on the opening weekend and looked lively throughout that match. Solomon will be hoping to back up that early impression and help West Ham collect their first points of the campaign in front of their own supporters.

Daniel Peretz continues in goal for Southampton, who host Stoke City looking to bounce back after losing their own Championship opener. Peretz made his move from Bayern Munich permanent this summer after a season on loan at St Mary's, and he heads into the new campaign with the clear backing of the Southampton coaching staff following a strong finish to last season.

Both Solomon and Peretz are effectively fighting to help their clubs off the bottom of the table early, in a season where two of the Israeli national team's higher-profile exports find themselves outside the Premier League for now.

Anan Khalaili's task is different. The winger will start on the bench as Crystal Palace travel to Everton for their Premier League opener at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium, with his manager not yet ready to hand him a first taste of Premier League football from kick-off.

Khalaili joined Palace this summer from the Belgian champions Union Saint-Gilloise, arriving after a proposed transfer to Inter Milan collapsed over medical clearance. Reports in the British press put the fee at around €24.5 million, which would make the 21-year-old the most expensive Israeli player in history.

He arrives with plenty of expectation attached and is regarded as one of Palace's most eye-catching additions of the window. A cameo off the bench at Goodison Park's replacement, Hill Dickinson Stadium, would give Khalaili his first minutes in England's top flight and a first small step toward the regular role he is ultimately chasing.

title: Flick brushes off Alvarez talk, hails Deco's 'fantastic job' before Elche opener
dek: Barcelona's manager declined to discuss the Atletico Madrid striker directly but backed his sporting director's summer work as the champions prepare for their delayed La Liga bow.
body: Hansi Flick used his pre-match press conference ahead of Barcelona's delayed La Liga opener to wave away the transfer saga that has followed his squad through the summer, declining once again to be drawn on Julian Alvarez.

Asked directly about the Atletico Madrid striker long linked with a move to Camp Nou, Flick was blunt: "I don't talk about players from other teams," he said, repeating a line he has used in previous appearances before the media this pre-season.

Instead of engaging with the Alvarez speculation, the German coach turned his praise toward sporting director Deco, crediting him for the work done in the transfer market this summer. "Deco and I know what we want. They have done a fantastic job," Flick said, according to ONE.

That work has already delivered one of the biggest deals of the European summer: Barcelona's signing of Rodri from Manchester City, confirmed on August 18. The Spain midfielder and reigning World Cup Golden Ball winner turned down interest from Real Madrid to join the champions on a four-year contract in a deal reported at around €60 million plus add-ons.

On the unresolved number 9 question, Flick pointed to an option already in his squad rather than a marquee arrival. He singled out 18-year-old Egyptian forward Hamza Abdelkarim, signed from Al Ahly, who has been Barcelona's leading scorer in pre-season with four goals in six friendlies, including a brace on his debut.

Flick has previously described Abdelkarim as someone who shows "great potential" and does "what I ask of a number nine," and he confirmed the teenager will be part of the squad that travels to face Elche.

The manager also touched on Alejandro Balde's situation, stressing that any player in his squad needs to be fully committed and ready to compete at the highest level, leaving the full-back's immediate future at the club somewhat open. Joao Cancelo, meanwhile, was confirmed as available and in contention to feature after an influential campaign last season.

The Elche fixture, scheduled for Sunday night at the Martinez Valero, will actually be Barcelona's first competitive league match of the season. Their original Matchday 1 assignment against Athletic Club was moved to August 27, meaning the trip to Elche doubles as the champions' effective league bow.

For Flick, the message before that kickoff was one of calm rather than urgency over the transfer market: backing the players already at his disposal, and trusting Deco to handle whatever comes next before the window closes.

title: Simeone defends Julián Álvarez as Atlético Madrid recall him to face Villarreal
dek: The Atlético coach hit back at fans jeering the wantaway Argentine striker, insisting Álvarez remains "our player" and will be involved this weekend.
body: Diego Simeone has stepped squarely in front of Julián Álvarez, telling reporters the unsettled Argentine striker is back in his Atlético Madrid squad and will be involved when Villarreal visit the Riyadh Air Metropolitano on Sunday, ONE reports.
"He is in the squad, he is at his pace," Simeone said, ending days of speculation over whether Álvarez would even be considered while his future at the club remains unresolved.

The 26-year-old sat out Atlético's opening 2-0 win over Málaga last week, a game that coincided with a public falling-out between the striker and sections of the home support. Fans unfurled banners reading "Julián Out" and displayed his No. 19 crossed through at the club's training ground, according to beIN Sports, after Álvarez was targeted by insulting chants during the Málaga match at the Metropolitano.

The anger stems from Álvarez's own admission over the summer that he wants to leave for Barcelona, who identified him as their preferred replacement for Robert Lewandowski. Atlético have so far refused to sanction a sale, and Simeone has repeatedly said the club's position is unchanged.

"He is very important, we need him, we will take care of him professionally and he is our player," the coach said, according to ONE, making clear he intends to keep leaning on Álvarez regardless of the noise around him.

Simeone was equally direct on the striker's conduct behind closed doors: "Julián trains in the best way, with respect toward his teammates." It was a pointed rebuttal to any suggestion the forward has been sulking or disruptive since requesting a move.

Asked about the fans turning on one of his players, Simeone said he understood their frustration but drew a line: "I respect the fans absolutely, but I won't accept curses or insults." He struck a similar note when pressed on the wider unrest, telling reporters he respects the Atlético support even as he shields Álvarez from it.

The coach also framed the episode within his broader team philosophy. "Our strength is the team. We don't rely on individual players, but on collective power and the 120% the team can give," he said — a message aimed as much at calming the dressing room as answering questions about one man.

Atlético go into Sunday's game, kicking off at 18:00 Israel time and broadcast live on ONE, looking to build on their opening-day win. Villarreal drew 2-2 with Racing Santander in their own season opener and arrive without the injured Juan Foyth, while Atlético loanee Alexander Sørloth is unavailable to face his parent club.

Whether Álvarez actually starts remains to be seen, but Simeone's message this week has been unambiguous: as long as the striker is at the club, he plays and trains as first-choice, transfer saga or not.

title: Dolgopyat closes in on becoming Israel's greatest athlete after third European floor gold
dek: The gymnast's tally in Zagreb pulls him level with Romanian legend Marian Drăgulescu and puts him within reach of Israeli sporting history, ONE reports.
body: Artem Dolgopyat picked up another gold medal in Zagreb this week, and with it, according to ONE, Israel's greatest gymnast is edging ever closer to a claim on the title of the country's greatest athlete of all time.

The 29-year-old floor specialist won the European Championships final with a score of 14.666, finishing ahead of Ukraine's Arsenii Dukhno (14.333) and Britain's Harry Hepworth (14.300). It was his third European title on the apparatus, adding to golds won in 2020 and 2022.

The victory takes Dolgopyat to seven European Championship medals on floor exercise alone — three gold and four silver — matching the seven collected across a storied career by Romania's Marian Drăgulescu, one of the most decorated floor specialists in the sport's history, who won four gold, two silver and one bronze.

Across all apparatus, ONE counts eight European Championship medals for Dolgopyat, alongside two Olympic medals and three World Championship medals. In major floor finals specifically, he has now medalled 12 times in 15 appearances, missing the podium on only three occasions — a remarkable consistency at the sport's highest level.

ONE frames that body of work as putting Dolgopyat in the conversation for Israel's greatest athlete ever, stacking his haul against two of the country's other outstanding Olympic-sport exports: judoka Arik Zeevi, who won nine European medals including four gold, and swimmer Anastasiya Gorbenko, who has six European golds to her name.

The Ukrainian-born gymnast, who moved to Israel as a teenager, already holds a singular place in Israeli sport as the country's first Olympic gold medallist in an individual event, winning floor exercise gold at the delayed Tokyo Games in 2021 before adding an Olympic silver in Paris three years later.

Should he add to that collection at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, Dolgopyat would become the first Israeli athlete in history to win three Olympic medals — a landmark that, combined with his European and World Championship record, underpins ONE's case for his growing legacy.

For now, the gold in Zagreb extends a run of near-uninterrupted excellence on floor that stretches back to his Tokyo breakthrough, and keeps him firmly on course for Los Angeles with two years still to prepare.

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva have all but wrapped up a deal for the Guinean winger Hamidou Keita, with the player understood to have concluded personal terms with the club ahead of the new Israeli Premier League season, ONE reports.

Keita, 28, is a right winger who holds both Guinean and French citizenship. He was most recently at French club Paris 13 Atletico and has been without a club since the summer of 2025, making him a straightforward free-transfer target for a Petah Tikva side looking to add depth on the flanks.

The finer point, according to ONE, is timing rather than substance: Keita is expected to sign officially only once winger Chipioka Sunga's departure to Portugal's Moreirense is formally completed, a move anticipated to go through within days.

Sunga's exit has been in the pipeline for weeks. ONE and Sport5 have reported Moreirense's offer climbing toward Hapoel Petah Tikva's roughly €800,000 asking price, with the two sides said to have settled in the region of €700,000 plus a 20 percent sell-on clause for the Israeli club.

Petah Tikva are moving quickly to reinvest that fee. Alongside Keita, ONE reports the club is also closing in on a deal for Diego Arroyo, with a signing expected in the coming days as the squad is refreshed for the new campaign.

The recruitment push follows a strong season in which Hapoel Petah Tikva reached the top-half championship playoff group, and the club will be eager to build further momentum when the new Premier League campaign opens against Hapoel Tiberias.
Nothing has yet been made official by either club, but with terms already agreed on Keita's side, confirmation appears to hinge only on the paperwork going through in Portugal.

title: Aiming high: how Hapoel Haifa rebuilt for a shot at the upper playoff
dek: Nine new signings, a reported 30-33 million shekel budget and a fresh contract for Haim Silvas — Hapoel Haifa's summer has been built around one goal: closing the gap on the top of Ligat Ha'al.
body: Hapoel Haifa spent last season fighting to stay in Ligat Ha'al after a mid-year coaching change. This summer, according to ONE, the ambition has shifted dramatically: with a rebuilt squad and a manager who saved them from the drop, the club is now targeting the upper playoff.

ONE reports the Reds have brought in nine new players this summer on an estimated budget of roughly 30-33 million shekels, with owner Yoav Katz said to be ready to sanction at least two more additions before the window shuts.

The headline arrival is a reunion: Nigerian striker William Agada is back at the club after an unsuccessful spell with Real Zaragoza in Spain. Agada previously starred on loan in Haifa, scoring four goals in 18 league appearances before adding two more in the relegation round as the club avoided the drop.

The rest of the incoming list, per ONE and corroborated by Ynet, includes defender Noam Cohen, left-back Ariel Mandi, midfielder Sheik Kheita — reportedly delayed in joining training due to a visa issue — attacking players Shai Elias and Habib Habibullah, plus Tal Naim, Itai Zafrani and Sali Fachima. Midfielder Liran Rotman, signed mid-way through last season, has also had his contract option exercised.

Ten players have left in the same window, among them Rotem Chatuel, Roi Zikri, Andrea Radulovic, Oren Biton, Sana Gomes and Regis Ando, as manager Haim Silvas reshapes the group around a younger, hungrier core while keeping a handful of experienced anchors.

Silvas returned to Hapoel Haifa midway through last season, replacing Gal Arael, and steered the club clear of relegation trouble. That work earned him a contract extension and what ONE describes as a free hand to build the squad for 2026/27 as he sees fit.

The message from inside the club, as relayed by Ynet, has been bullish: with this squad, Hapoel Haifa believe they can "look Maccabi Haifa in the eye" — a pointed reference to their bigger crosstown rival.

Season-ticket sales are reportedly up as the club tries to widen its fanbase beyond the annual Haifa derby fixtures, part of a broader push to make the upper playoff push about more than just survival.

Whether the rebuilt roster can deliver on that ambition remains to be tested once Ligat Ha'al gets under way, but the scale of turnover — nine in, ten out, and a meaningfully larger budget — makes clear this is the most significant squad overhaul Hapoel Haifa have undertaken in several years.

title: Ariel Lugasi: 'I matured mentally, it wasn't simple going through what I did'
dek: The Maccabi Petah Tikva winger opens up on a near year-long ACL nightmare, the mental toll of watching peers move on without him, and why he feels ready as his club returns to the top flight.
body: Ariel Lugasi is back running on a repaired knee just as his club prepares to run out in the top flight again, and the 21-year-old is candid about what it took to get here. "I matured mentally, it wasn't simple going through what I did," he told ONE in an interview ahead of Maccabi Petah Tikva's return to Ligat Ha'al.

The setback that shaped his year came in a match against Kfar Saba, when Lugasi scored a goal for Petah Tikva only to go down moments later with a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Surgery followed, and with it close to a year on the sidelines.

Rehabilitation stretched across roughly ten months of double training sessions, gym work and pitch drills, during which he added five to seven kilograms of muscle. Lugasi credited the club's medical staff and physiotherapists for getting him through it: "They helped me tremendously... that's behind me now."

The physical rebuild, he said, was only part of the battle. Watching teammates and peers continue to progress while he was stuck in recovery weighed on him. "I saw everyone succeeding, maybe that created unnecessary pressure," he admitted, adding that being back on the grass was itself the best remedy: "The best psychologist is being on the grass."

Lugasi has already made his return, featuring in a Toto Cup fixture against Tiberias as Petah Tikva ramped up their pre-season programme. He is wary of the hype building around his comeback. "I hear a lot that people say this is my year. I'm not looking at anyone else," he said, insisting he wants to prove himself without letting expectation weigh him down.

Before the injury derailed his progress, Lugasi was one of the standout names to emerge from Israel's celebrated youth national team under coach Ofir Haim, reaching the final of the European U19 Championship - where Israel lost only to England - and also featuring for the age group in Argentina's Mondialito tournament.

His path from that youth breakthrough to a regular first-team role at Maccabi Petah Tikva stalled once the injury hit, but the club's own trajectory has moved forward: after finishing among the top two in Liga Leumit, Petah Tikva have been promoted back to Ligat Ha'al for the 2026/27 season, giving Lugasi's recovery an extra layer of urgency and opportunity.

He sounded far from finished making his case. "There's still so much more to see, this isn't even a fraction of what I can do," Lugasi said, closing an interview that reads less like a farewell to a difficult year than a warning to the rest of the division.

title: Israel's judo cadets close out best-ever world championship with bronze and fifth place in Ecuador
dek: Tom Simkhaev fought back from a semi-final loss to take bronze and Yali Yahav finished fifth in Guayaquil, rounding off a three-medal campaign that included Ella Bar Lev's gold — Israel's strongest showing yet at the under-18 worlds.

verificationSources.label: IJF.org - Ella Bar Lev judoka profile

body: Israel's under-18 judo team wrapped up its finest World Championship campaign in the country's history in Guayaquil, Ecuador, with Tom Simkhaev claiming bronze in the men's -66kg category and Yali Yahav finishing fifth in the women's -52kg draw.

Simkhaev, the world number one in his age group heading into the event, tore through the early rounds with four straight ippon victories before running into Georgia's Giorgi Kapanidze in the semi-final, where he came up short. He regrouped for the bronze medal bout and beat another Georgian, Giorgi Avaliani, to secure the medal.

Yahav was equally impressive on her side of the draw, winning her round-of-16 and quarter-final contests by ippon against opponents from Mongolia, Colombia and Italy. Her run ended in the semi-final against Kazakhstan's Fatima Sufigaliyeva, and she then lost the bronze medal contest to Portugal's Sofia Gasper, leaving her fifth overall.

Their results capped a three-medal championship for the Israeli delegation in the Ecuadorian port city, where Ella Bar Lev had already won gold in the women's -48kg category earlier in the week — becoming Israel's first-ever cadet world champion — with teammate Agam Noy taking bronze in the same weight class.

One gold and two bronze medals from a single World Cadet Championships is a record for Israeli judo at this level, and it lifted the national team to fifth place in the overall medal table in Guayaquil, an event that drew competitors from 62 countries.

"This is the best junior World Championship we've ever had," national head coach Shani Hershko said, according to ONE, pointing to a younger generation carrying forward the recent success of Israel's senior judo team, which won three medals at the Paris Olympics.

Israel Judo Association chairman Moshe Ponti called it "a very emotional championship" that "shows the deep work Israeli judo is doing" and reflects the professional team's direction, per the same report.
The individual competition in Guayaquil ran from August 20-22, with team events to follow, as the sport's next generation continues to build toward the senior international circuit.

title: Messi fined by MLS for slapping Philadelphia Union's Quinn Sullivan
dek: The Argentine superstar avoided a card during Inter Miami's dramatic 2-2 draw, but the league's disciplinary committee has now punished the off-the-ball slap to an opponent's neck.
body: Lionel Messi has been fined by Major League Soccer for slapping the back of Philadelphia Union midfielder Quinn Sullivan's neck during Inter Miami's fractious 2-2 draw at Subaru Park, ONE reports, with the league's disciplinary committee stepping in after the incident escaped punishment on the night.

The flashpoint came deep into second-half stoppage time, in the 101st minute, after an exchange of words between the two players. Messi delivered a quick, open-handed slap to the back of Sullivan's neck, prompting the referee to intervene before it escalated further.

MLS said the fine — an undisclosed amount, as is standard league practice — was issued for violating its policy on hands to the face, head or neck of an opponent. Messi was not shown a card during the match itself, meaning the punishment came only after a post-match video review.

He was not alone in facing sanction from the same passage of play. Inter Miami defender Ian Fray was also fined for making contact with Sullivan's neck and throat area after the Union player lost his balance and fell into the technical area during the same scuffle.

Tempers boiled over again before the final whistle, with Miami's Yannick Bright and Philadelphia's Cavan Sullivan — Quinn's 16-year-old younger brother — both shown red cards for a separate off-the-ball altercation. MLS's independent review panel later rescinded Cavan Sullivan's card, along with the one-match suspension and fine that came with it.

The chaotic finish overshadowed a productive night for Messi on the pitch. He set up Inter Miami's opener for the first goal before curling home his own effort from 12 yards, taking his tally to 13 goals and nine assists in 17 MLS appearances this season. Indiana Vassilev and teenage defender Neil Pierre scored for the Union either side of the break to secure the draw.

Messi avoided any suspension over the slapping incident, meaning he remains available for Inter Miami's upcoming meeting with Toronto FC. The fine is a reminder that MLS treats head-and-neck contact seriously regardless of a player's profile, even when the referee lets it pass in the moment.

Messi received no suspension and remains available for Inter Miami's next match, against Toronto FC.
