title: Points deducted, coach suspended: Ironi Tiberias' scandal-scarred summer
dek: As the Israeli Premier League season opens, Tiberias carry a six-point penalty and a pending saline-infusion case into what looks like a straight fight against relegation.
body: Ironi Tiberias will begin the new Israeli Premier League season already six points in the red, and that is before anyone even mentions the club's other, unresolved scandal. ONE's season summary paints a club that spent the summer fighting on multiple fronts rather than planning for the campaign ahead.

The points penalty stems from last season's "double contracts" budget-fraud affair. The Israeli Football Association's investigative unit initially sought a 30-point deduction over irregularities in the club's budget reporting, before Tiberias reached a plea bargain in April 2026: eight points were docked from the 2025/26 campaign, a further six carry into this coming season, alongside a 500,000-shekel fine and a freeze on registering new players in the January 2027 transfer window.

That case also cost the club its co-owner. Miki Bitan, Aryeh Kalmenson's partner at both Tiberias and the Doroth insurance group that bankrolls it, was banned from all football activity for seven years starting June 1, 2026, and is now barred from any involvement at the club he helped build.

A second, separate scandal followed almost immediately. Ashdod SC lodged a formal complaint alleging Tiberias players were given excessive saline infusions before a May 3 relegation-playoff match the two sides played, which Tiberias won 3-0. Investigators say the volumes involved exceeded the amount permitted under World Anti-Doping Agency guidelines within a 12-hour window; some reports have put the figures far higher again, though the precise numbers remain disputed.

Head coach Eliran Chodda, technical director Chen Sol, fitness coach Shlomi Vardanto and five players — captain Guy Chadida, David Kaltins, Niv Gutlieb, Sambinia and Yonatan Tapper — were provisionally suspended from July 5, 2026. The case now sits before the Israel Football Association's sports tribunal, with no final ruling yet and a punishment that could reportedly extend to a further points deduction or even relegation.

For Chodda, the suspension effectively ends a five-year spell in charge regardless of the tribunal's eventual verdict — the club does not expect him back on the touchline. Alon Ziv, who holds the required pro coaching licence, has been installed as the new head coach, with Moti Krispiel, previously Chodda's assistant, working alongside him in what amounts to a hurried succession plan.

Owner Aryeh Kalmenson has pushed back hard against the accusations. "They tried to frame us — they want Tiberias to go down a division," he said, according to Ynet, arguing the club has been singled out for harsher and faster treatment than other clubs facing similar suspicions, and that the speed of the sanctions before formal charges were even filed points to a campaign against the club rather than even-handed enforcement.

Off the pitch, ONE reports the club enters the season with a budget of roughly 21 million shekels, of which about 13 million is earmarked for player wages — modest by Ligat Ha'al standards for a club fighting to stay in the division. Season-ticket sales, at under 350 by the club's own count, point to a fan base worn down by two straight summers of scandal rather than transfer excitement.

The playing squad itself has been reshuffled, with departures and new arrivals across the summer as the technical staff try to reset a group unsettled by suspensions and an ownership rift. With key figures still sidelined pending the tribunal's ruling, the exact makeup of the matchday squad for the opening weeks remains unsettled.

Pundits, per ONE, are forecasting a 14th-place finish — bottom of the table — for a club that opens the campaign already docked points and facing the possibility of more sanctions to come. For Tiberias, this season's target was never going to be about European qualification or a cup run; it is simply about surviving both the league table and the sports tribunal at the same time.

title: Alex Tyus lands in Israel to join Hapoel Haifa
dek: The 38-year-old EuroLeague-winning center touches down in Haifa for his fourth spell in Israeli basketball, ONE reports.
body: Alex Tyus is back in Israel. The well-travelled 38-year-old center touched down on Saturday morning to complete a move to Hapoel Haifa, ONE reports, beginning a fourth chapter of his long relationship with Israeli basketball.

Tyus, who stands 2.03m and will wear the number 9 shirt for the Carmel-based club, joins two other new foreign signings already in the country. Jaylen Piage and Robert Allen landed in Israel earlier in the week, and according to ONE all three are due to start training with Hapoel Haifa's squad on Tuesday.

For Israeli basketball fans of a certain vintage, Tyus needs no introduction. He first arrived in the country with Maccabi Ashdod in 2011, before a move to Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2013 turned him into a household name.

It was in yellow that Tyus produced the signature moment of his career, starring in Maccabi's run to the 2014 EuroLeague title, a triumph capped by a final win over Real Madrid in which he played a central role at both ends of the floor. He added Israeli league and cup silverware in the same spell.

A well-worn passport followed, with stops at Anadolu Efes, Galatasaray, UNICS Kazan, Real Madrid and ASVEL among others, before Tyus returned to Israel for shorter spells at Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Jerusalem in recent seasons. Last season he played in Turkey's second tier with Bandırma Bordo Basketbol, where he was among the league's top rebounders.

Tyus is a naturalized Israeli citizen, having received an Israeli passport in 2012 after converting to Judaism during his college years in the United States. That status has allowed him to play in Israel and for club teams without occupying a foreign-player slot in the past.

His arrival gives Hapoel Haifa a proven, championship-pedigree veteran to anchor the frontcourt as the club builds its roster ahead of the new season, adding experience to a rebuilding project on the Carmel.

title: Abukasis rebuilds Bnei Sakhnin as club enters new era under chairman Dukhi
dek: A record wage for Guadeloupe defender Dimitri Cavaré and a fresh boardroom headline a summer overhaul as Yossi Abukasis prepares his first full season in charge.
body: Bnei Sakhnin go into the 2026/27 season looking like a different club to the one that spent last winter fighting off relegation. A new man runs the boardroom, a new record signing anchors the back line, and Yossi Abukasis — the coach who arrived in February to steady the ship — is now overseeing his first full pre-season in charge.

The most visible change is at the top. Mohamed Abu Younes, chairman for some fifteen years and long the public face of the club, has stepped away, with local businessman Khaled Dukhi taking over, according to Ynet.

"My vision is to stabilise the club financially and build a strong foundation," Dukhi said, adding that his priority this season is "professional, competitive and financial stability" rather than any lofty table ambitions.

Sakhnin lost all four of their Toto Cup warm-up matches this summer, but Dukhi waved away the alarm, noting the results came before the squad was fully assembled and that the group is not yet at full strength for league action.

Abukasis himself is a familiar name in Israeli football. A defender who won the title with Hapoel Tel Aviv in his debut season and lifted two more championships with Beitar Jerusalem, he was capped 35 times for the national team and sits in the Israeli Football Hall of Fame.

As a coach he has won the State Cup three times, with Bnei Yehuda in 2018/19, Hapoel Beersheba in 2019/20 and Beitar Jerusalem in 2022/23. A brief spell at Hapoel Tel Aviv in 2024 ended in dismissal, and he was let go by Maccabi Netanya in January 2026 before Sakhnin turned to him on 17 February.

The marquee arrival of the rebuild is Dimitri Cavaré, a 31-year-old right-back who holds both French and Guadeloupe citizenship and has represented Guadeloupe internationally. He arrives from Turkish club Esenler Erokspor after a career that took in Rennes and English side Barnsley.

Ynet reports Cavaré will earn around €250,000 a year at Sakhnin, making him the best-paid player in the club's history — a deal Abukasis is said to have pushed hard for, viewing the Guadeloupean as a defensive anchor for the season ahead.

He is far from the only new face. Goalkeeper Raoul Balvaro, Portuguese defender Sana Gomes, Lithuanian defender Modestas Vorobjovas and Angolan midfielder Carlitos have all joined from abroad, while domestic recruitment has brought in Iyad Abu-Abeid from Bnei Reina, Louis Khalef from Maccabi Netanya and Amit Kardi from Maccabi Tel Aviv.

Going the other way, Sakhnin have moved on close to a dozen players from last season's squad, among them Carlo Brochezz, Hassan Khilo, Arthur Mirniyan and Max Gretchkin, as the club looks to reshape a roster that spent much of last term looking over its shoulder at the drop zone.

ONE reports Sakhnin are working with a summer budget of roughly NIS 20 million, and that Abukasis, speaking after a cup match, said he still wants four or five further additions before the window shuts — with a striker, a creative midfielder and defensive cover all on his list.

The stated ambition is modest but pointed: after finishing among the bottom sides in recent seasons, the target this time is a mid-table finish, somewhere in the 11th-to-13th range, well clear of the relegation fight that has defined Sakhnin's recent history. Whether that is realistic will depend on how quickly Abukasis can complete the squad before the league campaign gets under way.
facts: Yossi Abukasis was appointed Bnei Sakhnin coach on 17 February 2026, after being dismissed by Maccabi Netanya in January 2026.
New chairman Khaled Dukhi has replaced Mohamed Abu Younes, who had led the club for around fifteen years.

Other new arrivals include goalkeeper Raoul Balvaro, defenders Sana Gomes and Modestas Vorobjovas, midfielder Carlitos, plus Iyad Abu-Abeid, Louis Khalef and Amit Kardi from domestic clubs.

title: Hapoel Ramat Gan rebuild almost an entire squad for their Ligat Ha'Al return
dek: Newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan has brought in around 20 new players and let roughly 15 go, as owner Avi Yechiel and coach Masai Dago prepare the club for life in the top flight.

verificationSources.label: ONE — Hapoel Ramat Gan summer summary
Sport1/Maariv — Avi Yechiel officially becomes Hapoel Ramat Gan owner
Walla Sport — Christopher Boniface signs for Hapoel Ramat Gan
Ynet — new era at Hapoel Ramat Gan under new ownership

body: Hapoel Ramat Gan will barely recognise its own dressing room when the Ligat Ha'Al season kicks off. ONE reports that the newly promoted club has brought in roughly 20 new players over the summer while around 15 left, amounting to one of the most sweeping squad overhauls in the division this year.

The rebuild follows a turbulent recent past for the club, which changed hands this summer when former footballer Avi Yechiel completed a takeover and became the club's new owner, promising what he called a 'new era' after Hapoel Ramat Gan had at one point been at risk of financial collapse.

On the touchline, the top-flight campaign will be led by head coach Masai Dago, who arrived from Bnei Yehuda to take charge of a squad that needed rebuilding almost from scratch after clinching promotion from Liga Leumit.

The marquee summer arrival is Nigerian forward Christopher Boniface, who signed a two-year contract with an option for a third season. The 24-year-old, who stands 1.80m, built his career outside Nigeria, breaking through with Van in Armenia's top flight before moving to Ararat Yerevan and, most recently, Al-Harriyat in Qatar's second division — Walla Sport described him as a versatile attacker capable of playing centrally or off the wing.
Hapoel Ramat Gan also added experience in the shape of winger Matan Hozez, 30, who joins after leaving Hapoel Jerusalem this summer for a new chapter in his career.

Beyond those two headline names, ONE's report lists close to twenty further arrivals, among them Brazilian-linked signings Luan Campos and Marcio Silva, defender Tamir Glazer, forward Getachew Yablo, goalkeeper Daniel Tishler and midfielder Marius Nubisi, alongside a string of domestic squad additions rounding out a roster built almost entirely anew for the step up in class.

The overhaul cuts both ways. Among those to leave the club are forward Ezekiel Henty, Mohammed Adams and Nir Barda, part of a group of roughly 15 players no longer with Hapoel Ramat Gan as the squad that won promotion has been largely dismantled and rebuilt for the higher level.
ONE puts the club's overall budget for the campaign at somewhere between 26 and 28 million shekels, funding what the outlet frames as the busiest transfer window of any Ligat Ha'Al club this summer.
Fan interest, by contrast, remains modest for now: ONE reports around 600 season tickets sold so far, a reflection of a club still building its top-flight identity under new ownership.

Looking ahead, ONE's preview panel projects a finish somewhere between eighth and thirteenth place, and puts Dago's chances of seeing out the full season in the job at roughly 75% — both explicitly framed by the outlet as forecasts rather than certainties for a squad this freshly assembled.

For a club that has changed almost everything about itself in a single summer — ownership, coaching staff and the vast majority of the playing squad — the immediate target is simply survival in Ligat Ha'Al, with the more ambitious talk left for another day.

title: Closing the doors: Mourinho wages war on Real Madrid's leaks
dek: Back in charge at the Bernabéu, José Mourinho is clamping down on dressing-room secrecy after a season of public rows, fines and unflattering headlines undermined his predecessor.
body: José Mourinho is not just rebuilding Real Madrid's spine on the pitch. According to ONE, his most urgent project since returning to the Bernabéu has been sealing the club off from itself — choking the leaks that turned last season into a public soap opera.

The trigger, ONE reports, was the fallout from an ugly training-ground clash between Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde that became public knowledge rather than staying inside Valdebebas. Club president Florentino Pérez was said to regard the leak itself as almost as damaging as the incident, reportedly remarking that "the leak is worse because it shows something beyond the argument itself."

The consequences were real and severe: Real Madrid fined both Valverde and Tchouaméni €500,000 each, a punishment widely reported at the time by Sport1/Maariv and Israel Hayom as a club record. Independent Spanish reporting described a heated training-session flare-up that left Valverde needing treatment, with both players later appearing before an internal investigator to apologise to teammates, staff and fans.

That episode, alongside Vinicius Jr's public sniping at previous coach Xabi Alonso and Kylian Mbappé airing frustration over his playing time, left Madrid's dressing room looking porous and fractious just as Mourinho walked back through the door for his second spell in charge.

His response, ONE reports, is to minimise player exposure to the media and tighten control over anything that flows out of the building. Real Madrid have already scaled back the usual pomp around new arrivals — axing traditional fan unveilings and open media access in favour of content produced solely by the club's in-house channel, a shift also flagged by Managing Madrid ahead of the new season.

It is a pattern Mourinho has run before. During his first Bernabéu tenure between 2010 and 2013, he clashed repeatedly with goalkeeper Iker Casillas, at one point branding him "the mole" over suspected leaks — a jibe Casillas later threw back at him defiantly: "Who leaked it? José Mourinho. The mole? Of course."

He took the same approach to Chelsea and Manchester United, where former captain John Terry has spoken about the value Mourinho placed on presenting a united front to outsiders regardless of what was happening internally.

ONE frames the current crackdown as part psychology, part damage control — an attempt to restore what Mourinho calls a "family" feel inside a squad that spent much of last season airing its grievances in public. Whether Real Madrid's notoriously leak-prone dressing room stays quiet under the new regime is likely to be one of the season's more revealing subplots, on and off the pitch.

The club has not commented publicly on the specifics of any internal media protocol, and ONE's report should be read as reflecting the mood and measures described by sources close to the club rather than an official statement.

title: Rodri's move to Barcelona will cost the club more than €200m in total, report says
dek: Add the transfer fee to four years of wages, taxes and commissions and Spain's World Cup-winning midfielder becomes one of the priciest deals in Barcelona's history, according to a cost breakdown reported by ONE.

verificationSources.label: ONE - official Barcelona presentation of Rodri
Haaretz - Barcelona agree deal with Manchester City for Rodri
Ynet - official: Barcelona announce Rodri's signing

body: The headline transfer fee for Rodri's move from Manchester City to Barcelona was never going to tell the whole story, and now the full bill has emerged: according to a cost breakdown reported by ONE, citing the Spanish paper AS, the deal will end up costing Barcelona in excess of €200 million once every euro is accounted for.

The transfer fee itself sits at around €70 million, comprising a fixed sum plus performance-related add-ons, in line with the €60 million-plus-€15 million-in-variables structure both clubs have since confirmed. That figure alone made Rodri one of the most expensive defensive midfielders in the game's history.

But the fee is only the entry cost. Barcelona have committed to a four-year contract, running to June 2030, that pays Rodri around €15 million net per season. Because of Spanish and Catalan tax rates, servicing that net figure costs the club roughly €34 million gross each year - around €136 million in salary alone over the life of the deal.

Add agent commissions and other associated costs on top of the fee and the wages, and ONE's reporting puts Barcelona's total outlay north of €200 million - a number that broadly matches figures of around €210 million reported elsewhere in the European press.

The market logic behind the price tag is straightforward, if uncomfortable for clubs hoping to buy value: Rodri had less than a year left on his City contract, the kind of situation that once meant a cut-price move. Instead, his stock rose sharply after a starring role for Spain at the 2026 World Cup, and suitors were made to pay accordingly.

Barcelona won the race for his signature ahead of Real Madrid, who had also tabled an offer and were left to look elsewhere. Real's response was to turn to Atlético Madrid for Julián Álvarez, offering around €150 million for the Argentine forward - an approach Atlético swiftly rejected.

For Rodri, the switch closes a seven-season chapter at Manchester City, where he became the defensive and tactical anchor of Pep Guardiola's midfield, and opens a new one back in Spain. Barcelona have already completed and unveiled the signing, presenting him as one of the best in the world in his position and pointing to his football intelligence and professionalism.

Whatever the exact final figure - €200 million or €210 million, depending on which outlet's arithmetic you trust - the message from this transfer window is the same one being repeated across Europe this summer: a star entering the last year of his contract is no longer a bargain simply because his deal is running down.
facts: ONE, citing Spanish outlet AS, reports Barcelona's total cost for signing Rodri will exceed €200 million once fees, wages and commissions are combined.
The transfer fee is reported at around €70 million (a €60 million base plus roughly €15 million in variables), paid to Manchester City.
Rodri's deal runs four years to June 2030 at a reported €15 million net per season, costing Barcelona an estimated €136 million in wages over the contract due to Spanish tax rates.
Real Madrid also made an offer for Rodri but lost out to Barcelona.
Real Madrid subsequently offered Atlético Madrid around €150 million for Julián Álvarez; Atlético rejected the approach.
Barcelona have since officially announced and presented Rodri's signing, ending his seven-season spell at Manchester City.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem chief Shai Aharon: "Arie didn't need to leave, maybe that's what saved us"
dek: Ahead of the 2026/27 season, sporting director Shai Aharon reflects on Ziv Arie's mid-season exit, the Cedric Don fallout and a policy of never selling to Beitar Jerusalem.

verificationSources.label: Ynet - "Seven years and one parting": the full story behind Ziv Arie's exit
Sport5 - Ziv Arie: what led to the coach's exit from Hapoel Jerusalem

body: Shai Aharon, Hapoel Jerusalem's professional director, has broken his silence on the club's chaotic 2025/26 season in a wide-ranging interview with ONE ahead of the new campaign, admitting he initially believed coach Ziv Arie's departure was a mistake -- before concluding it may have been exactly what kept the club in Ligat Ha'al.

Arie, who had guided Hapoel Jerusalem up from the second tier and spent seven years in the job, stepped down mid-season after results collapsed. "I didn't think Ziv needed to leave," Aharon told ONE, describing it as one of the hardest moments of his tenure at the club.

Aharon said the two men later spoke following a defeat to Kiryat Shmona, and it was Arie himself who persuaded him the change had been necessary. "Maybe that's exactly why we survived," Aharon told ONE -- a striking admission that parting with a long-serving coach, however painful, may have given the club the jolt it needed to beat relegation.

The numbers behind the crisis were stark. According to Ynet's reporting on Arie's exit, his final campaign yielded just 21 points from a possible 81, with only four wins and 23 goals scored all season -- a return worse than almost the entire division, with only relegation-threatened Bnei Reineh managing fewer goals.

Arie's long-time assistant of four years, Lior Zada, 48, was promoted to replace him and switched the team to a noticeably more attacking approach than his predecessor's cautious setup, Ynet reported at the time.

Aharon also addressed the messy fallout involving forward Cedric Don, telling ONE the widely reported dressing-room incident "was based on a real story" -- while disputing parts of the published account and noting that comments at least as harsh had been directed at other players without making headlines. Don has since left the club, moving on to Maccabi Haifa in 2026.

On one of Israeli football's more sensitive subjects, the Jerusalem derby, Aharon was unambiguous. "There is a policy not to transfer players to Beitar," he said, framing it as a matter of respecting the rivalry and protecting supporters on both sides of the capital's divide rather than a purely footballing call.

He also lifted the lid on the club's finances, revealing that Hapoel Jerusalem begins every season with a deficit of at least five million shekels. With no private owner underwriting the books, the club still leans on donations from Israel and abroad -- support Aharon says has been shrinking in recent years.

That financial squeeze feeds directly into recruitment. Aharon told ONE that signing foreign players has become harder than at any point he can recall, with families increasingly reluctant to relocate to Israel even after the club shows them video presentations and puts them in touch with current squad members for reassurance.

Aharon used the interview, too, to push back on the gulf between Arie's public image and the man he worked alongside for years, arguing responsibility for the caricature that formed around the coach was shared three ways -- between Arie himself, the club, and the media that covered him.

It is a rare piece of self-criticism from inside a club that spent much of last season fighting to stay afloat, and it frames Hapoel Jerusalem's build-up to 2026/27 around a blunt message from its own sporting director: survival came at a cost, but the decisions that caused the pain may be the same ones that kept the club up.

title: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he told Ramsdale straight: Peretz is our No. 1
dek: Head coach Tonda Eckert has laid out the Saints' goalkeeping pecking order in blunt terms, with Daniel Peretz first choice, George Long his deputy, and Aaron Ramsdale left to play under-21 football to stay sharp.

verificationSources.label: OneFootball — Eckert on Ramsdale and the under-21s
Saints Marching — Peretz's rise to No. 1

body: Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has left no ambiguity about his goalkeeping hierarchy, confirming that Daniel Peretz is established as the club's undisputed No. 1 for the season, with George Long as his deputy, while Aaron Ramsdale has been pushed out to under-21 football.

"Daniel was signed as our number one goalkeeper and George Long as our number two for the season," Eckert said, quoted by ONE. "We had a conversation early on, and since I arrived I've worked with Daniel and Longy. We were very clear about the situation." The coach added that he had also spoken to Ramsdale directly about where he stands.

The clarity comes after Ramsdale, needing minutes, asked to be included in Adam Lallana's Southampton under-21 side for a fixture against Blackburn Rovers, playing the full 90 minutes to keep himself sharp while his first-team future remains uncertain.

Eckert praised the 28-year-old England international's attitude in making that request, noting that competitive match time offers benefits a training pitch cannot replicate, even at under-21 level, and that his experience was valuable for a young Saints side.

The situation marks a striking fall for Ramsdale, who arrived at Southampton from Arsenal as their senior, high-profile goalkeeper and went on to make 32 appearances during the club's relegation from the Premier League, before being loaned out to Newcastle United for a Champions League campaign.

Peretz, by contrast, has gone from a mid-season loan arrival from Bayern Munich to first-choice status inside a matter of months. He joined on loan in January and immediately steadied a defence that had been leaking goals under previous goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, keeping eight clean sheets in 22 appearances.

Southampton made the move permanent this summer, and Peretz has since taken the club's No. 1 shirt outright — a rapid rise for the Israel international, who is now the clear starter ahead of an England World Cup winner's understudy in Long and a full England international in Ramsdale.

For Peretz, Eckert's public backing amounts to the strongest endorsement yet of his standing at St Mary's as Southampton prepare for a Championship campaign in which stability between the posts has been a priority all summer.

title: Ido Sa'ar's long road back: Hapoel Haifa youth defender scores after horror leg break
dek: The Haifa-born right-back needed two surgeries and 245 days of rehabilitation after fracturing his tibia and fibula in training — and doctors initially feared he might not walk unaided again — before finding the net for Hapoel Haifa's youth side.
body: Ido Sa'ar spent the better part of a year wondering if he would ever run onto a football pitch again. Last Saturday, the Hapoel Haifa right-back did more than that — he scored, according to a report by ONE, coming off the bench in the 23rd minute of a 2-0 away win over Hapoel Rishon LeZion to net his first goal in almost five years.

The finish capped a brutal rehabilitation. Sa'ar, born in 2008, suffered fractures to both his tibia and fibula after a heavy tackle from a teammate during an internal training match at Hapoel Haifa, ONE reported. The injury required two separate surgeries, and doctors initially feared he might struggle to walk unaided again, let alone return to competitive football.

What followed was 245 days of intensive rehabilitation, according to the report — the better part of eight months of physiotherapy and graded fitness work before Sa'ar was cleared to train again with his Hapoel Haifa Ne'arim A squad, which competes at Liga Leumit level, the top tier for that age group.

The setbacks did not end with the leg break. ONE reported that Sa'ar also shot up to 1.90 metres in height last season, a growth spurt that briefly wrecked his coordination on the pitch, and he was further hampered by a back injury. He used the winter break to work through the physical adjustments before gradually forcing his way back into the squad.
Sa'ar came through Maccabi Haifa's youth ranks before a spell with Beitar Tobruk Netanya's Ne'arim B side, and later returned to his home city to join Hapoel Haifa's Ne'arim A squad, per the report.

His coach, Ram Ben Michael, singled out his character after the goal against Hapoel Rishon LeZion. "He has a golden heart and an iron character," Ben Michael said, according to ONE. "He worked hard to recover."

Football runs in the family. Sa'ar's father, Baruch, is a familiar figure in Haifa's grassroots game — he coaches at the Favela football academy, which partners with Maccabi Haifa, and has been involved in running the Hapoel Rubi Shapira Haifa club.

Hapoel Haifa's youth side are back in action this Saturday, hosting Hapoel Ramat HaSharon at 17:00 at the Beit Nagler pitch in Kiryat Haim — the next step in a comeback that, for a long stretch, looked far from certain.

title: Franck Rivollier explains his move to bitter rivals Maccabi Petah Tikva
dek: Back at Hapoel Petah Tikva after a year across the derby divide, the France-Cameroon forward tells ONE he understands why fans were furious, but insists it was the only option open to him at the time.

verificationSources.label: Africa Soccer - Rivollier returns to Hapoel Petah Tikva

body: Franck Rivollier is training with Hapoel Petah Tikva again this pre-season, but before he plays a single competitive minute back in the yellow-and-black, the forward has had to account for a year spent in the shirt of the club's fiercest local rival.

"Maccabi? I understand the fans, it was the option I had," Rivollier told ONE, addressing head-on the anger that greeted his 2025 switch to Maccabi Petah Tikva, the club on the other side of one of Israeli football's bitterest city derbies.

The 25-year-old had first arrived at Hapoel in January 2025 from Bulgarian side Spartak Varna, helping the club to the Liga Leumit title and promotion back to the top flight. Instead of staying to enjoy the fruits of that promotion, he crossed the divide to Maccabi Petah Tikva that summer, a move that was never going to sit easily with Hapoel's supporters.

At Maccabi he did the job well enough — 32 appearances and six goals across the season, according to figures reported by Africa Soccer, form that helped drag Maccabi themselves up into Ligat Ha'al for the coming campaign. But on July 17, with his contract up, Rivollier signed for Hapoel again as a free agent, this time on a deal running to June 2027.

That back-and-forth is precisely what he was asked to explain, and his answer to ONE was not evasive: he says he grasps exactly why fans felt betrayed, but frames the Maccabi move as pragmatic rather than personal — the door that was open at a moment when Hapoel's was not.

"I'm excited, really excited, because it's a new league for me," he said of the season ahead — a pointed line, since his first Hapoel spell coincided with the club's promotion push in Liga Leumit rather than the top division itself. Ligat Ha'al with Hapoel will, in that sense, be uncharted territory.

He was equally direct about the scale of his and the club's ambitions this time around, telling ONE: "We don't have a team that's just come here to survive in the league," and describing a bond with the group that he says was there "from the first day" of his return.
Personally, his targets are simple enough: goals, assists, and a place as one of the team's key men rather than a squad number — he wears 45 — that just makes up the numbers.

Born in Saint-Étienne and eligible for both France and Cameroon through his mother, Rivollier came up through the Troyes and Lyon academies before a spell in Stade Rennais's youth system, where he has spoken of training alongside players who went on to bigger things, among them Eduardo Camavinga and Jeremy Doku.

His footballing heroes growing up were Samuel Eto'o and Didier Drogba, and he told ONE he has a distant family connection to Eto'o through his Cameroonian mother — a link he mentions with evident pride rather than as a boast.

Whatever the noise around last year's derby switch, Hapoel Petah Tikva have chosen to bring him back regardless, and Rivollier now gets the chance to answer his critics in the way that tends to work best in football: on the pitch, in the league he says he can't wait to finally experience in Hapoel's colours.

title: Kafr Qasim ordered to pay hundreds of thousands of shekels to forward Yaniv Mizrahi
dek: An Israel Football Association arbitrator found the Liga Leumit club negotiated in bad faith and misled the striker over a FIFA transfer ban that eventually pushed him out to Hapoel Afula.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Mizrahi signs for Kafr Qasim under transfer ban
Walla Sport — FIFA transfer ban on Kafr Qasim

body: Kafr Qasim have been ordered to pay forward Yaniv Mizrahi hundreds of thousands of shekels after an arbitrator ruled the Liga Leumit club breached its obligations to him and negotiated with him in bad faith, ONE reports.

The ruling, handed down by the Israel Football Association's mediation and arbitration institute, centres on a memorandum Kafr Qasim signed with Mizrahi in June 2025 covering two seasons. At the time, the club was already under a FIFA-imposed transfer ban — punishment for fielding an ineligible player — that barred it from registering new signings through the opening window of the 2025/26 season.

According to ONE, Kafr Qasim committed to getting the restriction lifted so Mizrahi's move could be formalised. That never happened. The club, the arbitrator found, failed to legitimize the agreement with the relevant budget oversight authorities, leaving the 29-year-old forward in limbo.
Unable to have his contract properly registered, Mizrahi was forced to take a lower-paying role at Hapoel Afula to limit his financial losses, ONE reports.

The arbitrator, Dr. Adv. Dan Chai, did not mince words in his findings, stating that the club "provided the claimant with false representation regarding FIFA's decision status" and criticizing its conduct as bad-faith negotiation, according to ONE.

Kafr Qasim were ordered to pay Mizrahi 175,500 shekels gross in compensation, plus 18,000 shekels (plus VAT) in legal expenses and 12,000 shekels (plus VAT) to cover the arbitrator's fee — all due within 30 days.

The arbitrator fully accepted Mizrahi's claim relating to the 2024/25 season. A separate dispute over the second season covered by the memorandum, 2025/26, was not resolved in this ruling and remains open for further negotiation or a future proceeding.

Mizrahi arrived at Kafr Qasim off the back of an 11-goal league season with Hapoel Ramat Gan, seen at the time as a coup for a club trying to strengthen going into a campaign in which it could not otherwise add reinforcements. The transfer ban stemmed from a FIFA tribunal case in which Kafr Qasim and the Israel Football Association were both found at fault, with the federation itself hit with a suspended fine of 30,000 Swiss francs.

For a National League club still working through the fallout of that case, the arbitration ruling adds a further financial and reputational cost — and a reminder, per ONE's report, that written commitments to players facing regulatory uncertainty carry real legal weight.

title: Arsenal open Premier League defence with 3-0 win over Coventry as Ødegaard vows to 'attack' the title
dek: Christos Tzolis inspires an emphatic opening-day rout as Mikel Arteta's champions declare their intent to add more silverware, not just protect what they already have.
body: Arsenal opened the defence of their Premier League crown in emphatic fashion, brushing aside newly promoted Coventry City 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium, with Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard all on the scoresheet.

But for a club that waited 22 years between league titles, Ødegaard was adamant afterwards that Mikel Arteta's squad has no intention of playing it safe this time around. "We don't feel we need to defend anything," the Arsenal captain said. "We want to do it again and that's our mentality... We want to attack the title and fight for it again."

That framing echoed the report published by Israeli outlet ONE, headlined "We don't want to defend the title, we want to attack it," which highlighted the shift in tone around the Emirates as Arsenal begin life as champions for the first time since Arsène Wenger's unbeaten Invincibles of 2003-04.

Arteta struck a similarly combative note when asked about protecting the trophy his side won on the final day of last season, replying that the aim this year was "attacking another Premier League" rather than simply sitting on what they already hold.

The performance against Coventry backed up the talk. Havertz opened the scoring in the 15th minute, Saka doubled the lead midway through the first half, and Ødegaard added a third early in the second to complete a comfortable afternoon against Frank Lampard's side, who were making their first top-flight appearance in 25 years.

The headline act, though, was Christos Tzolis. The Greece international, signed from Club Brugge for a reported £34 million as Leandro Trossard's replacement, started on the left wing and had a hand in both of the opening two goals — winning back possession to launch the move that led to Havertz's goal, then supplying the cross that Saka finished.

Ødegaard was full of praise for the new arrival. "He played a brilliant game," the Norwegian said of Tzolis. "He's been brilliant all preseason. He's so lively, it's hard to defend against him. He's a really intelligent player — he always looks up and finds the right pass."

Tzolis arrives in north London with a strong scoring record from his season at Club Brugge, where he registered 17 goals and 23 assists, and adds further attacking depth to a squad that also completed the signing of defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa, who was introduced to supporters before kickoff.

Arsenal's title triumph last season ended a run of three straight runner-up finishes behind Manchester City and snapped a wait stretching back to 2003-04 for the club. Arteta became the first Arsenal manager since Wenger to lift the Premier League trophy, doing so after City failed to keep pace on the final day of the campaign.
One match into the new campaign, the message from the Emirates is unambiguous: last season's success is the platform, not the ceiling.

title: Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage shuts down Real Madrid move for Adam Wharton
dek: The new Eagles manager says his prized midfielder is going nowhere this summer, even with Real Madrid, Manchester City and Liverpool all circling.

verificationSources.label: TheHardTackle - Crystal Palace reject Manchester City approach for Adam Wharton
Sky Sports - Crystal Palace appoint Pierre Sage as new manager

body: Pierre Sage wasted no time drawing a line under the summer's biggest story at Selhurst Park. Crystal Palace's new manager confirmed this week that Adam Wharton will not be leaving for Real Madrid before the transfer window closes, telling reporters bluntly that the club needs its midfielder more than it needs the fee.

"I think right now is not the time to do that," Sage said, according to ONE. "We need him." It was as direct a denial as Palace have offered all summer, closing off, for now at least, one of the more persistent transfer sagas in the Premier League.

Real Madrid have been credited with long-standing admiration for the 22-year-old, whose value ONE reports has climbed past £80 million (roughly €93m) after a breakout campaign in which he made 34 league appearances and was named MVP of the Conference League final as Palace won the first major European trophy in the club's history.

Real Madrid are not the only suitors to have come calling. Manchester City and Liverpool have also made contact over Wharton this summer, according to ONE, and both received the same answer Sage gave publicly: the England international is not for sale.

That stance was echoed independently on Friday, when reports emerged that Palace had formally rejected an approach from Manchester City for the player, reinforcing the club's public line that Wharton remains central to its plans under its new head coach.

Sage, the former Lyon and Lens boss who took over at Selhurst Park in June after Oliver Glasner departed following the club's FA Cup and Conference League triumphs, is only just settling into the job. Losing his most influential midfielder before a ball had properly been kicked in the new season was never going to be part of the plan.

The manager framed the decision as one of timing and development rather than a permanent door being shut on a move to Spain. Wharton, Sage suggested, still has more growing to do before a step up to a club of Real Madrid's stature would make sense — for player and club alike.

Palace have not been passive in the market regardless. The club has brought in six new signings this window, including Yeremy Pino's compatriot-style addition Annan Khalili, and Sage indicated one or two more deals could follow before deadline day, though he stressed the club would not rush into anything.

For Wharton, the message is clear: another season anchoring Palace's midfield, with Real Madrid's interest parked rather than pursued. Whether that patience holds beyond this window remains the open question hanging over Selhurst Park.

title: Ronaldo scores as Al Nassr beat Al Riyadh 4-0, and Saudi media credit his marriage for the spark
dek: Back in action for the first time since Portugal's World Cup exit, the 41-year-old struck off the bench to level Al Nassr's all-time scoring record — and commentators in Saudi Arabia say his wedding to Georgina Rodríguez is behind the renewed zest.

verificationSources.label: Goal.com - On the night of Ronaldo's return

body: Cristiano Ronaldo marked his first appearance in six weeks with a goal as Al Nassr thrashed Al Riyadh 4-0 in their Saudi Pro League opener, and the Saudi press has been quick to draw a line between the 41-year-old's renewed sharpness and his recent wedding to Georgina Rodríguez.

"As if the marriage returned his youth to him," was how ONE summarised the tone of the coverage inside Saudi Arabia, reporting that local media described Ronaldo's cameo as delivering a "wonderful level and unmatched passion" for a player who had not kicked a ball competitively since early July.

Ronaldo came off the bench in the 62nd minute at Al Riyadh's stadium and needed just 28 minutes to make his mark, finishing off a move set up by teammate Yahya in the 83rd to complete the scoring. Abdulelah Al-Amri, Angelo and João Félix had already put the result beyond doubt before he arrived.

The goal was his first involvement of the new campaign and moved him level with Mohammed Al-Sahlawi as Al Nassr's leading scorer of the Saudi professional era, with 103 goals in what is now 108 league appearances since he joined the club in January 2023 — a spell that has also produced 19 assists.

It was Ronaldo's first game back since Portugal's World Cup ended in heartbreak on July 6, when Spain beat them 1-0 in the round of 16 through a stoppage-time Mikel Merino header, a result Ronaldo has since suggested marked his last appearance at the tournament.

In between, he and Rodríguez — his partner of eight years — confirmed they had married in a civil ceremony in Cascais, near Lisbon, on August 11, sharing a photograph of their linked hands and wedding bands on Instagram with the caption "C ♥ G". The couple's five children were present at what both described as a private, intimate occasion.

ONE reports that Saudi outlets have leaned heavily into the timing, casting Ronaldo's crisp finish and evident hunger on his return as evidence the wedding had rejuvenated him on the pitch — while also cautioning, in the same coverage, that he will need to manage his minutes carefully at his age rather than push for a starting role too soon.

Whether or not marriage really is behind it, the sharpness was real enough: with one more goal Ronaldo will stand alone as Al Nassr's outright record scorer, a landmark that already looked well within reach before Saturday's substitute appearance in Al Riyadh.

title: Hamza Abdelkarim emerges as a real option to be Barcelona's number 9 this season
dek: ONE reports that the 18-year-old Egyptian, Barcelona's top scorer in preseason, has forced his way into contention to lead the line after the exits of Robert Lewandowski, Ferran Torres and Marcus Rashford.
body: Hansi Flick has spent the summer hunting for a recognised finisher to lead his Barcelona attack after the departures of Robert Lewandowski, Ferran Torres and Marcus Rashford. According to ONE, the answer may already be training with the first team.

The Israeli outlet reports that Hamza Abdelkarim, the 18-year-old Egyptian forward, has become a genuine option to wear Barcelona's number 9 shirt this season after finishing preseason as the club's top scorer, with four goals in the warm-up fixtures.

That tally matches what Lamine Yamal produced in his own breakout preseason and betters the return Ferran Torres posted when he first arrived at the club, a comparison highlighted in Spanish coverage of Abdelkarim's rise. Flick handed him the number 9 shirt for a preseason friendly against Birmingham City, the first time it had been worn in a match since Lewandowski's exit.

Abdelkarim came through the Al Ahly academy in Cairo and made his senior debut for the Egyptian giants in February 2025, reportedly the youngest player to represent the club this century. Barcelona took him on loan to Barça Atlètic in February 2026 with a purchase option attached.

That option was exercised in June, with Barcelona completing a permanent deal worth around €1.5 million plus add-ons and tying the striker to a contract running to 2029. His rapid emergence in preseason has now pushed the club to discuss rewarding him further.

Spanish outlets including Barca Universal and Goal.com report that Barcelona are preparing to raise his release clause roughly tenfold, from €15 million to €150 million, reflecting how quickly his stock has risen since the move became permanent.

Abdelkarim has also broken through at international level. Egypt named him in their squad for the 2026 World Cup in May, and he made his tournament debut in June at 18 years and 165 days old, reportedly the youngest Egyptian ever to feature at a World Cup finals.

ONE's report frames Abdelkarim's form as easing the pressure on Barcelona to bring in an established number 9 before the transfer window closes. The club has also been linked with Folarin Balogun, the American forward on loan at Monaco from Arsenal, but the report suggests Abdelkarim's emergence has reduced the urgency to move for an outside option.

For now, Flick appears willing to let the teenager compete for minutes through form rather than rush into the market for a marquee replacement — a notable show of faith in a player who was in Al Ahly's youth ranks little more than a year ago.

title: Mbappe chases a third straight Pichichi as Real Madrid open the season at Espanyol
dek: Kylian Mbappe has scored 86 goals in two seasons at the Bernabeu and won the last two Pichichi trophies outright — a third in a row would be a feat no Real Madrid player has managed since Hugo Sanchez in the 1980s.

verificationSources.label: Real Madrid CF — Mbappe wins the Pichichi Trophy 2025/26
Real Madrid CF — Mbappe receives the 2024/25 Pichichi Trophy

body: Real Madrid open the 2026/27 La Liga season away at Espanyol on Saturday night, and the storyline that ONE frames ahead of kick-off is simple: can Kylian Mbappe win a third consecutive Pichichi trophy as the Spanish league's top scorer?

It would be an achievement no Real Madrid player has managed since Hugo Sanchez strung together three straight scoring titles in the mid-to-late 1980s. Even Cristiano Ronaldo, for all his goals in white, only ever won it in two consecutive seasons, 2013/14 and 2014/15, before Lionel Messi and others interrupted his run.

Mbappe's case for a third is built on a remarkable opening act in Madrid. According to ONE, he has scored 86 goals in his first two seasons at the club — 31 to claim the Pichichi in his debut campaign and 25 more to retain it last season, a tally of 56 La Liga goals across the two years alone. Real Madrid's own website confirmed both trophies, the 2024/25 award presented in November and the 2025/26 one collected in May.

The Frenchman is also within touching distance of a personal milestone: ONE notes he sits 14 goals short of reaching 100 for Real Madrid, a landmark that could realistically fall before the turn of the year given his scoring rate.

There is a specific subplot to Saturday's trip to the RCDE Stadium, too. ONE recalls that in the corresponding fixture during Mbappe's debut season, then-manager Carlo Ancelotti was furious over a heavy challenge on his forward, telling reporters afterwards that the foul was inexplicable and criticising both the referee's decision and the VAR review. The report frames Saturday as Mbappe's chance to finally get on the scoresheet at a ground where he has yet to find the net for Real Madrid.

None of that changes the scale of the challenge ahead. Only two players in Real Madrid's history have won three or more Pichichis in a row: Alfredo Di Stefano, who took four straight in the late 1950s, and Sanchez, whose four Pichichis across his Bernabeu career included a run of three consecutive titles. Matching that company, as ONE lays it out, would put Mbappe in genuinely rarefied territory for a club that has fielded some of the greatest goalscorers the European game has seen.

For now it is a season-opening storyline rather than a settled outcome — 34 league games lie between Saturday's kick-off and any verdict on the Pichichi race. But few players start a title defence with as strong a platform as Mbappe carries into this campaign, on the back of 59 goals in the 2025 calendar year alone, a mark ONE says matched Ronaldo's best output in a single calendar year for the club.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv 4-0, Ashdod 4-1, Bnei Yehuda 2-0: youth sides open Naarim Bet season with wins
dek: Hapoel Tel Aviv, M.S. Ashdod and Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv all won on the opening weekend of the newly reformed Naarim Bet elite league, ONE reports, with Maccabi Tel Aviv's title defence still to come at Kiryat Shmona.
body: Israel's Naarim Bet age group — the country's 2011 birth-year cohort, roughly the under-15s — kicked off its 2026/27 season this weekend under a freshly reformed league structure, and the opening results went the way of the bigger city clubs.

ONE reports three results from the opening round of the elite division's Red and Orange groups. Hapoel Tel Aviv were the biggest winners on the day, beating Nahalal Yizrael Football Club 4-0 at home, a comfortable start for a club whose senior first team plays at Bloomfield Stadium.
In Haifa, Neve Yosef went down 2-0 at home to a Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv side that will fancy its chances of building on an away win in the group's opening fixture.

In the south, M.S. Ashdod were the day's other big scorers, beating Hapoel Be'er Sheva 4-1 on home turf to open the campaign with a statement result against a club with a strong football pedigree in the region.

The Israel Football Association overhauled the country's youth pyramid for this season, restructuring the boys' age groups — Naarim A, B and C — into elite, national, territorial and district tiers in an attempt to tighten competition, cut travel and give more clubs a realistic route up the ladder. ONE's headline framing of "Red" and "Orange" groups reflects that new elite-division split, though the article does not spell out the criteria behind the grouping in detail.

One opening-round fixture was still to be played as of ONE's report: defending champions of the 2011 age-group, Maccabi Tel Aviv, were due to travel to the country's northernmost top-flight venue to face Ironi Kiryat Shmona on Sunday at 18:30.

It is a long season ahead for all of these age-group sides, but early form in a reformed structure always draws scrutiny — and Hapoel Tel Aviv, Bnei Yehuda and Ashdod have given their group rivals plenty to think about in round one.

title: Serie A shuffles the pack as nine clubs start the season under new coaches
dek: Napoli turn to Massimiliano Allegri, Milan bring in Ruben Amorim and Lazio appoint Gennaro Gattuso, while champions Inter stick with Cristian Chivu — and Israel's Omri Gandelman begins a first full season at Lecce.
body: Serie A opens its 2026/27 campaign this weekend with more fresh faces on the touchline than at almost any point in recent memory. ONE's season preview counts nine of the twenty top-flight clubs starting the year under a new head coach, part of a wider reset after a domestic season that left several traditional powers unsatisfied.

The most eye-catching change is at Napoli, where Massimiliano Allegri has taken over from Antonio Conte at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Allegri, a serial title-winner with Juventus and Milan, returns to a club that won the Scudetto only two seasons ago and now wants a manager who can keep it competitive on two fronts.

Allegri's old job at Milan has gone to Ruben Amorim, hired away from Manchester United on a contract running to 2029. The club backed the appointment with a record outlay, bringing in French forward Gonçalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain as it tries to end a run of underwhelming league finishes.

There has been a domino effect further down the table. Maurizio Sarri left Lazio to take charge at Atalanta on a three-year deal, reuniting with sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli, while Lazio turned to Gennaro Gattuso — fresh off his spell in charge of the Italy national team — to succeed him in Rome.

Not every club felt the need to change course. Champions Inter Milan are sticking with Cristian Chivu, who became only the fifth coach to win the Scudetto in his first season in charge of the club after guiding them to the title in 2025/26. Roma likewise kept faith with Gian Piero Gasperini following a third-place finish last term.

Como offer the feel-good story of the off-season. Cesc Fàbregas stays on after leading the club to a record-equalling fourth place and a first-ever Champions League qualification, an extraordinary rise for a side that plays its home games at the 12,000-seat Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on the shore of Lake Como.

There is an Israeli thread running through the new campaign too. Midfielder Omri Gandelman, who joined Lecce from the Belgian club Gent in January, begins his first full season in Serie A colours as the Salento club looks to consolidate its place in the division.

With so much change on the benches, ONE frames the coming season as one in which Italy's leading clubs are effectively hitting reset — hoping fresh voices in the dugout can translate into sharper football and a stronger showing in Europe than the division managed a year ago.
The opening round kicks off this weekend, with Allegri, Amorim, Sarri and Gattuso all set to take charge of competitive matches for their new clubs for the first time.

title: UEFA fines Hapoel Beer Sheva, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv over fan misconduct
dek: European football's governing body has handed down €47,575 in penalties across three Israeli clubs' Champions League and Conference League qualifiers this summer, with reigning champions Hapoel Beer Sheva shouldering more than half the bill.
body: European football's governing body has sent the bill for a bruising summer of qualifying football to three Israeli clubs at once. UEFA has fined Hapoel Beer Sheva, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv a combined €47,575 for fan misconduct during this summer's Champions League and Conference League qualifiers, ONE reports, with reigning Israeli champions Beer Sheva shouldering by far the heaviest share.

According to the outlet, Beer Sheva were fined across three separate matches for a combined €24,250 — more than half the overall total. UEFA imposed €6,000 over the home leg against Iceland's Víkingur Reykjavík, then two further penalties from the tie with Red Star Belgrade: €10,000 for the home leg, described by ONE as the single heaviest individual fine among all three clubs, and €8,250 for the away leg in Belgrade.

The fines have landed in the middle of an otherwise successful European run for the champions. Beer Sheva lost the first leg away to Víkingur before winning at home to advance on aggregate, then eliminated Red Star Belgrade in the following round to reach the Champions League qualifying play-off, where they now stand two ties from the group stage.

Beitar Jerusalem's punishment was €18,325, which ONE reported came over fan conduct in the away leg of their Conference League qualifier against AEK Larnaca of Cyprus. The source did not detail the specific offences beyond describing them as incidents during the match. Beitar eventually eliminated Larnaca on penalties after the tie finished level over two legs.

Hapoel Tel Aviv drew the smallest of the three fines, €5,000, over incidents in the home leg of their own Conference League qualifier against GKS Katowice of Poland. Despite the penalty, Tel Aviv advanced past the Polish side on aggregate and now face a considerably tougher assignment in the play-off round against Atalanta.

UEFA does not appear to have attached any stadium restrictions or suspended sanctions to any of the three fines, based on ONE's reporting — the clubs' punishment, for now, is purely financial. All three sides remain alive in their respective European qualifying campaigns despite the penalties.

title: Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City: Havertz, Saka and Ødegaard open title defence in style
dek: Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard scored as the champions eased past newly promoted Coventry City on the Premier League's opening night at the Emirates.
body: Arsenal wasted no time reminding the Premier League who is champion. Mikel Arteta's side eased to a 3-0 win over newly promoted Coventry City on Friday night, opening their title defence with three different scorers inside the first 49 minutes at the Emirates.

Kai Havertz broke the deadlock in the 15th minute, meeting a pass from Riccardo Calafiori with a first-time strike steered into the far corner. It set the tone for a half in which Coventry barely got out of their own half.

Bukayo Saka doubled the lead eight minutes later. New signing Christos Tzolis drove a low ball across the box that the Coventry goalkeeper could only parry, and Saka rolled the rebound into an empty net from close range — an instant reward for Tzolis' involvement.

Martin Ødegaard added the third just four minutes after the restart, turning home from close range after Saka and Ben White combined down the right. By then the contest had long stopped being a contest.

The scoreline undersold how one-sided it was. According to Opta data stretching back to 2007, Coventry became the first team in Premier League history to register neither a touch in the opposition box nor a single tackle in the first half of a top-flight match. Their first tackle of the afternoon did not arrive until the 69th minute, with the game already gone.
ONE, reporting on the result from Israel, described the outcome simply as an easy win for the champions to open their campaign — a fair summary of an afternoon Arsenal barely had to strain for.

It was a routine opening statement from a side that arrives in 2026-27 as defending Premier League champions under Arteta, who has now overseen back-to-back seasons of silverware and now a flying start to the title defence itself.

Tzolis' assist came in his first taste of Premier League football since a reported £34 million move from Club Brugge this summer, one of three senior additions — alongside goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer and Piero Hincapié's loan turned permanent — as Arteta reshaped his squad following Leandro Trossard's departure to Beşiktaş.

For Coventry, back in the top flight after promotion from the Championship, the reality check was immediate and, by the numbers above, a historic one. There will be sterner tests of their survival credentials than a trip to the champions on the opening weekend, but few starker warnings of the gap they must close.

title: Real Betis 1-0 Real Sociedad: Riquelme's second-half strike opens the league account
dek: Rodrigo Riquelme's first-time finish in the 63rd minute settled a tight opening at the Estadio de La Cartuja, with goalkeeper Álvaro Valles standing firm as Real Sociedad pushed for an equaliser.
body: Real Betis got their La Liga campaign moving with a hard-earned 1-0 win over Real Sociedad on Friday night at the Estadio de La Cartuja in Seville, a tight and even contest settled by a single moment of quality just after the hour mark.

Rodrigo Riquelme provided that moment in the 63rd minute, meeting a driven cross from Cucho Hernández at the back post with a first-time volley that gave the goalkeeper no chance. It was the only goal of a game in which chances were otherwise scarce.

Manuel Pellegrini's side controlled long stretches of the match without ever fully cutting Real Sociedad loose, and the visitors, last season's Copa del Rey winners, grew into the game as it wore on and pushed hard for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Betis goalkeeper Álvaro Valles was the man standing between Real Sociedad and a share of the points, producing a string of important saves in the final quarter of an hour to preserve his side's clean sheet and see out the win.

The result gives Pellegrini's side a perfect start to the league phase of the new season and three points on the board from their opening fixture, a welcome return after finishing sixth in La Liga last term.

For Imanol Alguacil's Real Sociedad, arriving in Seville on the back of their Copa del Rey triumph, it was a frustrating opening test on the road, with the visitors unable to find a way past Valles despite their late pressure.

Both sides now turn to their next league assignments as the 2026-27 season builds momentum, with Betis's home win in Seville an early marker of the ambition Pellegrini has spoken of for the campaign ahead.

title: Atlético CEO to Álvarez: 'we will help you, we need you'
dek: Miguel Ángel Gil Marín says Julián Álvarez is not for sale at any price below his €500 million release clause, warning Barcelona off a summer-long chase for the Argentine.
body: Atlético Madrid has had enough of hearing about Julián Álvarez's future being decided somewhere other than the Metropolitano. Club CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín used an interview to draw a hard line under the Argentine's transfer saga, insisting the forward stays put unless someone pays his full release clause.

"Atlético, like all great clubs, is built with great players, and I am convinced that Julián is one of them," Gil Marín said, according to ONE. "We will help Julián and continue to care for him so he can give us his full potential."

The comments land roughly two months after Álvarez first made clear internally that he wanted out, with Barcelona identified as his preferred destination. Atlético have not budged since, and Gil Marín's latest remarks read as a direct answer to the pressure campaign around the player.

"We will not allow other clubs and media to decide what we need to do or dictate our sports strategy," the CEO said, a line widely read in Spain as aimed squarely at Barcelona and outlets sympathetic to a move, even though he stopped short of naming the club.

The mechanism Atlético are hiding behind is straightforward and, by Spanish football's usual standards, extreme: a release clause reported at €500 million, written into the contract Álvarez signed until 2030 when he arrived from Manchester City in 2024. Barcelona would have to deposit that sum with La Liga in full — no installments, no add-ons, no discount for a Spanish suitor.

That figure is one reason the club's public posture has hardened rather than softened as the window has worn on. Barcelona's well-documented financial constraints make paying anywhere near €500 million implausible, and Real Madrid's separate approach — a reported €150 million bid — was rejected on the same grounds.

Álvarez, 26, has continued playing for Atlético through the opening weeks of the season while the noise around him has grown louder, a situation the club appears determined to end by simply refusing to negotiate at all.

Gil Marín's framing — that Atlético will keep looking after the player rather than push him toward the exit — suggests the club sees this as a stance to be held indefinitely, not a position that softens as the transfer window narrows.

title: Dolgopyat clinches third European floor title in Zagreb with 14.466
dek: Israel's Olympic champion held off a field of rising young gymnasts to win floor gold at the European Championships, and says the team also hit its qualifying mark for the World Championships.
body: Artem Dolgopyat added another gold medal to his crowded trophy cabinet on Friday, winning the floor exercise final at the European Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Zagreb with a score of 14.466.
It is the third European title of his career on the apparatus that made him famous, following triumphs in 2020 and 2022, and takes his career haul at the continental championships to eight medals.

According to results published by the event organisers, Dolgopyat finished ahead of Arsenii Dukhno, competing under the neutral WG2 designation, who took silver on 14.333, with Britain's Harry Hepworth claiming bronze on 14.300.

"I'm happy it ended well. Winning gold is the most exciting thing I could imagine," Dolgopyat said afterwards, quoted by ONE. "We also achieved the team criteria for Worlds, which was one of our important missions here."

The 29-year-old, who competes domestically for Maccabi Tel Aviv, was frank about facing a new generation of rivals half his age. "At my age, every competition is a battle," he said. "It's fun to finish first against all the new young athletes."
He also flagged what comes next, telling reporters: "Next year is the most important year in my journey," a nod to the build-up already under way toward the next Olympic cycle.

Dolgopyat remains the biggest name in Israeli gymnastics by some distance. He is the Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion on floor, took silver at the Paris 2024 Games, and added the world title in 2023 to two earlier World Championship silvers, from 2017 and 2019.

Israel Gymnastics Federation chairman Avi Sagi hailed the latest medal, calling Dolgopyat a "true champion" who "continues to bring tremendous achievements to Israel on the world's most important stages," crediting his talent, discipline and mental resilience for a career that keeps delivering at the sport's biggest events.

The win also carried team significance: Dolgopyat said Israel had met the qualifying benchmark for the World Championships during the Zagreb meet, a marker with consequences beyond his own individual campaign as the federation plots its path toward the sport's next global showpiece.

title: Johnathan Motley says he sat too much on the bench during his Hapoel Tel Aviv title run
dek: The EuroCup Finals MVP explains why he left Hapoel Tel Aviv for Crvena Zvezda just months after delivering the club's first European trophy.

verificationSources.label: Eurohoops - Motley completes move to Crvena Zvezda
Basketnews - Motley named EuroCup Finals MVP

body: Johnathan Motley delivered Hapoel Tel Aviv its first-ever European trophy last season and walked off with Finals MVP honors for doing it. Three months later, in an interview with ONE, he explained why that triumph wasn't enough to keep him in Israel.

"I think I sat too much on the bench last year, and I feel that wasn't good for me," Motley said, according to ONE, adding that the reduced role didn't fit where he wants his career to go at this stage.

The comments sit awkwardly against the backdrop of what Motley actually produced when it mattered. He was the standout of Hapoel's 2-0 sweep of Dreamland Gran Canaria in the EuroCup final, averaging 22 points across the two games, including a 26-point outing in the clinching win, and was named Finals MVP.

None of that was enough to keep him at Hapoel. According to ONE, Motley had already signed a contract extension with the club, but the Israeli side ultimately approved his release this summer, and he moved on to Crvena Zvezda (Red Star Belgrade) in Serbia.

The switch reunites him with Chris Jones, his running mate in Hapoel's frontcourt-backcourt pairing last season, who also joined Zvezda's roster over the summer. ONE reports the pair pushed for the move together, wanting to keep the partnership going in Belgrade.

There is history at the new club too. Crvena Zvezda's newly appointed sports director, Milos Teodosic, was Motley's teammate at the LA Clippers between 2018 and 2020, giving the move an added layer of familiarity even though the two won't share the court this time.

Motley framed the decision around opportunity as much as loyalty. According to ONE, he said reaching the EuroLeague playoffs, something he says he has never missed in his career, was central to his thinking, a bar Hapoel's EuroCup campaign, for all its success, does not clear.

For Hapoel Tel Aviv, it means saying goodbye to the player who defined its most successful European season to date. For Motley, it's a bet that more minutes and a EuroLeague roster will do more for his career than another title on the smaller stage.

title: Barcelona's Héctor Fort snubs Real Sociedad and Roma to push for Borussia Dortmund move
dek: The 20-year-old right-back, frozen out by Hansi Flick, prefers a switch to the Bundesliga as Barcelona seek up to €20m for his sale
body: Héctor Fort appears to have made up his mind about where his career goes next. ONE reports that Barcelona's academy-produced right-back has settled on Borussia Dortmund as his preferred destination, turning down rival offers as he looks for a way out of Camp Nou.

According to Sky Deutschland, cited by ONE, the 20-year-old rejected interest from Real Sociedad and Roma over the summer, choosing instead to hold out for a move to the Bundesliga club after concluding he has no future under Hansi Flick.

Fort spent last season on loan at Elche, making 14 La Liga appearances and scoring twice — form good enough to earn him the division's Goal of the Month award in December. He returned to Barcelona for pre-season but has failed to convince Flick he deserves a squad role this time round.

Financially, Barcelona are looking for a package worth €15-20 million, ONE reports, though that figure could come down if the Catalans build in a sell-on percentage or a buyback clause to protect their long-term interest in the player.

Other reporting from Germany and Spain suggests Dortmund's own budget for a new right-back sits closer to €10 million, which may force the two clubs to get creative — a loan with an obligation to buy, or a fee weighted heavily toward add-ons, rather than a straightforward permanent transfer.

In the meantime, Fort has been training away from Barcelona's first-team group in recent weeks, a precaution ONE says was ordered by Flick to limit the risk of an injury derailing the move before it is finalised.

Nothing has been signed and no fee has been agreed between the clubs as things stand, but the direction of travel is clear enough: Fort wants Dortmund, and Barcelona are working out how to get a deal for one of La Masia's more promising defensive prospects over the line before the market shuts.

title: Dolgopyat wins third European floor title in Zagreb
dek: The Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion topped the podium with 14.466 points at the European Artistic Gymnastics Championships, taking his continental medal collection to eight and adding another chapter to one of Israeli sport's most decorated individual careers.

body: Artem Dolgopyat claimed his third European floor exercise title on Friday, landing a routine worth 14.466 points in the final in Zagreb to add another chapter to one of the most decorated individual careers in Israeli sport, ONE reported.

The 29-year-old, Israel's Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion on floor and the Paris 2024 Olympic silver medallist on the same apparatus, topped the men's final at the European Artistic Gymnastics Championships, held at Arena Zagreb as part of a championships running from August 19-23.

Dolgopyat had gone in as the form favourite, qualifying with the second-best score in the field at 14.766, before producing a slightly lower but still commanding routine in the final to see off Arsenii Dukhno, who took silver with 14.333, and Britain's Harry Hepworth, who claimed bronze on 14.300.

It was Dolgopyat's third European gold specifically on floor exercise, following continental titles in 2020 and 2022, and takes his overall haul at the championships to eight medals: three gold and four silver on floor, plus a bronze on vault, according to ONE.
The win came in a championships that also saw Israel's men's team finish 10th, a placement that secures qualification for this year's world championships, ONE reported.

Dolgopyat, who competes for Maccabi Tel Aviv, has built his career around the floor exercise, the apparatus that delivered Israel's second-ever Olympic gold at the Tokyo Games in 2021 and a world title in Antwerp in 2023.

Born in Dnipro, Ukraine, he moved to Israel with his family as a child and became a citizen in 2009, growing into arguably the country's most consistent individual medal-winner across the past decade of major championships.
At 29, and with a third continental floor crown now secured in Zagreb, he remains one of Israel's clearest medal prospects heading toward the next world championships and Olympic cycle.

title: Argentina to appeal FIFA bans handed down over World Cup final brawl with Spain
dek: The AFA says it will formally challenge Leandro Paredes' 10-match suspension and other sanctions before FIFA's appeals committee, with the Court of Arbitration for Sport held in reserve as a last resort.
body: The Argentine Football Association has told its players and staff it intends to formally appeal the raft of FIFA sanctions imposed after ugly scenes at the end of the World Cup final, ONE reports, setting up a fight that could ultimately land at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

The punishments stem from ugly scenes at the final whistle in East Rutherford on 19 July, when Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time thanks to Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner, denying Lionel Messi's side a second successive world title. Argentina had already been reduced to 10 men after Enzo Fernández was sent off in the second half.

As full time was confirmed, players from both squads clashed. FIFA's disciplinary committee found Leandro Paredes responsible for three separate assault incidents, including grabbing Spain's Eric García by the throat and shoving Gavi to the ground, and handed the Boca Juniors midfielder a 10-match ban and a $90,000 fine — a suspension that, given the international calendar, will effectively keep him out of the Argentina squad until the middle of 2027.

Nahuel Molina was also sanctioned over two assault counts, including an alleged blow on Spain captain Rodri, and was banned for seven matches with a $90,000 fine of his own. Thiago Almada received a one-match ban and a $30,000 fine, while assistant coach Roberto Ayala — cited for one count of assault and one of unsporting conduct — was suspended for three matches and fined $30,000. Spain's Gavi was separately banned for one match.

FIFA did not stop at individual punishments. The federation itself was fined $321,000 for a string of breaches across the tournament, among them the discriminatory chanting of sections of the Argentina support, and the banner declaring "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" unfurled by players after the semi-final win over England. Argentina were additionally ordered to play their next two home fixtures with the stadium capacity cut by half.

In its statement, the AFA said it would first request FIFA's full written reasoning for each decision "for examination," before lodging formal appeals with the governing body's own appeals committee. Should those appeals fail, the federation said it was "retaining the possibility of resorting in the future to the Court of Arbitration for Sport as a last resort."

The stakes are significant for Argentina's rebuild after the final defeat. Paredes has been one of the more experienced heads in the squad's midfield, and a ban running close to a year would strip Argentina of him through most of the 2026-27 international calendar, including any early World Cup qualifying-adjacent fixtures and friendlies before the next major tournament cycle. Molina's absence for seven matches similarly weakens a defence that already lost Fernández to suspension in the final itself.

FIFA's disciplinary panel has treated Paredes' punishment as comparable in severity to the four-match ban imposed on Uruguay's Luis Suárez in 2014, underlining how seriously the governing body viewed the final-whistle brawl. Whether an appeals committee — or, eventually, CAS — is persuaded to reduce any of the sanctions remains to be seen; Argentina previously succeeded in having a similar Messi-era ban rescinded on appeal, which will give the federation's legal department some cause for optimism this time around.

Assistant coach Roberto Ayala was suspended for three matches and fined $30,000.
The Argentine Football Association was fined $321,000 and must play its next two home matches at 50% stadium capacity.
The AFA says it will request FIFA's full written reasoning and lodge appeals with FIFA's appeals committee, keeping recourse to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in reserve.
