title: Maccabi Petah Tikva 1-3 Maccabi Tel Aviv: champions survive fightback in youth league
dek: Ido Yosef and Itay Mahager struck either side of half-time and Roy Gafni's late penalty settled it, as Dan Roman's holders held off a spirited Petah Tikva response to move to six points from two rounds.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth side served notice that they intend to defend their Israeli Youth Premier League title, beating Maccabi Petah Tikva 3-1 away at HaMoshava Stadium on Friday to move to six points from two rounds of the new 2026/27 season.

The reigning champions were the sharper side before the break. Ido Yosef put them ahead in the 38th minute and Itay Mahager doubled the lead three minutes later, sending Dan Roman's side in at half-time firmly in control.

Petah Tikva responded with intent, making three substitutions at the interval, and the changes paid off when Liam Weinstein, on for Yaakov Michael-Zada, halved the deficit in the 67th minute to set up a tense finish.

Tel Aviv settled the contest from the penalty spot. Roy Gafni converted in the 75th minute to restore the two-goal cushion and take the game away from the hosts, who could not find a way back a second time.

"Satisfied with the first half, relatively, very unsatisfied with the second half," Roman said afterwards, according to ONE. "I think we have a lot to learn from that second period, plenty of mistakes to correct — but it's better to be correcting them when you're winning."

The coach singled out goalkeeper Idan Trau, who was called into repeated action as Petah Tikva pushed for an equaliser. "Trau gives us a lot of confidence, he had an outstanding second half," Roman said, adding that the busy afternoon for his goalkeeper reflected some defensive fragility but also showed exactly what is expected of a third-year youth player who also trains with the senior squad.

Both sides made wholesale changes as the match wore on — Tel Aviv used five substitutes in total, including late switches around Gafni's penalty — typical of a youth fixture being used to test squad depth early in the campaign.
The win keeps Maccabi Tel Aviv perfect after two rounds of the Liga Leumit LeNoar season, with Roman's side already served early warning that title defences rarely come without scares.

body: Israel's under-16 women's national team closed out its FIBA U16 Women's EuroBasket campaign with a statement win, beating hosts Romania 70-51 on Friday in Mioveni in the tournament's 13-16 classification bracket, ONE reported.
Israel set the tone from the opening whistle, racing to an 18-8 lead after the first quarter and stretching the advantage to 37-23 by halftime.
Romania threatened a comeback in the third quarter, cutting the gap to as little as 11 points, but Israel steadied and pulled away again in the fourth to close out a 19-point victory.
Michal Abudram was the standout performer, posting a double-double with 23 points and 15 rebounds. Rona Tzlal added 17 points, going 3 of 4 from three-point range, while Ella Maoz Barda chipped in 8.

The result caps the tournament for Israel in the 13-16 range, but per ONE, that placement already confirms the team's relegation out of Division A, the top tier of European women's U16 basketball, regardless of Friday's outcome.

The championship, staged across Pitești and Mioveni from August 14-22, brought together 16 nations in the region's top age-group women's event. Israel's youth teams have shuttled between Division A and Division B in recent cycles, and Friday's win closes out this campaign before the program regroups a tier down.

title: Atzili tops ONE's ten contenders to be crowned Ligat Ha'al's fantasy king
dek: As the fantasy football game for Israel's top flight reopens for the new season, ONE picks out ten players — from Beitar Jerusalem's priciest man to a pair of newly arrived strikers — most likely to rack up the points.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz — Maccabi Tel Aviv sign Aster Sokler

body: ONE's fantasy football game for Ligat Ha'al is back for the 2026/27 season, and the outlet has picked out ten players it believes give squads the best chance of topping the table — a mix of proven creators, expensive marquee names and two summer arrivals with something to prove.

Heading the list, and priced as the most expensive man in the game at 15 million, is Beitar Jerusalem's Omer Atzili. ONE describes him as a player who is almost automatically involved whenever his side reaches the final third, giving him a regular supply of both goals and assists to fuel a fantasy XI.

Two players are next on the price scale at 14 million apiece. Maccabi Tel Aviv's Dor Peretz is flagged as a midfielder who produces numbers well above the norm for his position, courtesy of sharp positioning and a habit of getting shots away. His Beitar counterpart Yarden Shua, meanwhile, is rated as one of the league's most creative midfielders — a player capable of contributing to a goal without ever pulling the trigger himself.

At 13 million sits Hapoel Tel Aviv's Stav Turiel, whom ONE expects to be central to his club's attacking play again this season, with regular goal involvement anticipated. Turiel was a prominent figure for Hapoel last term, including a late winner in last season's meeting with Beitar Jerusalem.

The 12 million bracket brings in four names. Igor Zlatanovic, the Serbian forward who joined Hapoel Be'er Sheva this summer after four prolific seasons at Maccabi Netanya — 53 goals in 145 appearances — is tipped as his new club's chief goal threat. Maccabi Tel Aviv's Roy Revivo is rated for his dual-threat potential from either defensive or attacking situations, while teammate Aster Sokler, the Slovenian striker signed from Serbia's Radnicki this summer, arrives with real pedigree after netting 15 goals in 29 appearances last season. Rounding out that tier is Hapoel Tel Aviv midfielder Douglas Awuso, expected to be heavily involved in his side's attacking play.

The cheaper end of the list, at 11 million, features Hapoel Be'er Sheva's Eliel Peretz — praised for his ability to break from deep, reach the flank and produce both goals and assists — and Maccabi Haifa forward Guy Malmad, who ONE notes has already shown he can find the net regularly in this league.

The piece is framed as a guide rather than a guarantee: ONE is careful to note that paying top price for the biggest names doesn't automatically translate into fantasy points, and that value can often be found further down the price list.

With the fantasy game reopening as the new Ligat Ha'al campaign gets under way, the list gives fans a starting point for squad selection — built around a blend of the league's most reliable performers and its newest, unproven arrivals.

title: Kiryat Motzkin add Derek Williams and Daniel Nagar as Rehovot sign Niv Lampert
dek: Ahead of a first season in Israel's National League, Maccabi Kiryat Motzkin bolster their frontcourt and backcourt, while Maccabi Rehovot land promising 22-year-old guard Niv Lampert, ONE reports.
body: Maccabi Kiryat Motzkin's roster build continues at pace. With the club preparing for its first season in Israel's National League, the second tier of Israeli basketball, ONE reports the team has added a forward and a guard in quick succession, while fellow National League outfit Maccabi Rehovot has made a signing of its own.

The bigger name of the two Motzkin additions is forward Derek Williams, 31, who stands 1.96 metres and arrives with a well-travelled European resume. He has spent seasons in the British League with London Lions and in France's top flight with Chalon, and he already knows Israeli basketball, having played in the National League for Hapoel Eilat in 2024/25.

Joining him is guard Daniel Nagar, 25, a 1.93-metre backcourt player with plenty of domestic mileage. Nagar has worn the colours of Ramat Gan/Givataim, Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Ma'ale Adumim, played for Elitzur Ashkelon, and turned out for Maccabi Kiryat Gat last season before this move.

The pair give Motzkin two players who have operated at various levels of Israeli and European basketball, adding both experience and size to a squad being assembled from scratch for life in the National League.

Elsewhere, Maccabi Rehovot has strengthened its own backcourt by signing Niv Lampert, according to the same ONE report. The 22-year-old guard, also 1.96 metres, spent the last two seasons with Migdal HaEmek after coming through as a touted junior prospect at Hapoel Galboa/Galil, where he wore the shirt in the 2023/24 campaign.

Lampert was regarded as one of the better young guards to emerge from Israel's youth ranks in recent seasons, and his move to Rehovot gives the club a domestic addition with senior National League minutes already banked.

None of the deals carry confirmed contract terms in ONE's report, and none of the three clubs had issued their own statements at the time of writing, but the National League's summer rebuild is now well underway with pre-season fast approaching.

title: The summer that changed the NBA: LeBron, Giannis and every big move
dek: From LeBron James taking a pay cut to join Philadelphia to Giannis Antetokounmpo's shock exit from Milwaukee, the 2026 NBA offseason has reshuffled the league's power balance like no summer since 2019.

verificationSources.label: NBA.com — Bucks trade Giannis Antetokounmpo to Heat
NBA.com — Jaylen Brown-Paul George trade takeaways
ESPN — Clippers-Raptors Kawhi Leonard trade on hold
Star Tribune — Timberwolves land LaMelo Ball

body: ONE is calling it the summer that changed the league, and it is hard to argue. In the space of a few chaotic weeks the NBA has torn up its old hierarchy, with three separate superstars switching teams and a fourth trade still frozen by a league investigation.

The biggest shock arrived when LeBron James, at 41, agreed to join the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million contract — a fraction of the roughly $52 million he earned last season with the Lakers. James called it his "last decision" after publicly weighing retirement, and he now lines up alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey in a frontcourt built to win now.

Philadelphia did not stop there. The Sixers also landed Jaylen Brown from Boston, sending Paul George and four draft picks the other way in a trade that gutted the core which won the Celtics a championship in 2024. Brown, still only 29, joins James, Embiid and Maxey to give Philadelphia arguably the most star-studded roster it has fielded in a generation.

Even that was overshadowed by Milwaukee's decision to finally grant Giannis Antetokounmpo his wish to leave. The two-time MVP, who delivered the Bucks' first title in half a century in 2021, was traded to Miami along with Bobby Portis. In return the Bucks received Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., guard Kasparas Jakučionis and draft compensation, in one of the most lopsided-looking centrepiece trades of the offseason.

Out West, Minnesota moved to give Anthony Edwards a genuine co-star, acquiring LaMelo Ball from Charlotte after the Timberwolves fell short of the Western Conference finals for the first time in three years. The Wolves parted with Naz Reid and a stack of future picks to pair Ball's playmaking with Edwards' scoring.

Portland made its own bold play for Ja Morant, sending Jerami Grant and Kris Murray to Memphis for the two-time All-Star at what several NBA outlets described as a bargain price. The move complicates life for Israeli forward Deni Avdija, who just made his first All-Star team as Portland's primary ball-handler; how the Blazers now share the offense between Morant and Avdija — and whether the added payroll affects Avdija's next contract before he reaches free agency in 2028 — is one of the more closely watched subplots of the new season.

Not every blockbuster is finished business. The trade sending Kawhi Leonard from the Clippers to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and multiple first-round picks has been on hold for weeks, frozen by an NBA investigation into whether the Clippers circumvented the salary cap through Leonard's $28 million endorsement deal with the now-bankrupt company Aspiration. Owner Steve Ballmer has denied any knowledge of the arrangement, and there is no timetable for when the league's probe, being handled by outside counsel, will conclude.

ONE's rundown of the summer also lists a string of smaller but still significant moves reshaping rosters across the league, including Walker Kessler heading to the Lakers, John Collins to Detroit, Mitchell Robinson to Boston, Anfernee Simons to Philadelphia, Tobias Harris to San Antonio and Norman Powell to Chicago.

Taken together, several American outlets have echoed ONE's framing that this is the most chaotic offseason since 2019, when Kawhi Leonard, Anthony Davis, Paul George, Russell Westbrook, Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving all changed teams in one summer. This time, though, the reshuffling has hit even deeper into the league's established contenders — and left Milwaukee, Boston and the Clippers all rebuilding around what they gave up rather than what they gained.

title: Dego savours 'special feeling' as Hapoel Ramat Gan return to the big league to face Maccabi Haifa
dek: Thirteen years after relegation, Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim open their Ligat Ha'al comeback away to Maccabi Haifa, where coach Messay Dego once made his name.
body: For Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim, Saturday's trip to Sammy Ofer Stadium is the moment thirteen years of waiting comes due. The club open their return to Ligat Ha'al, Israel's top flight, against Maccabi Haifa, and manager Messay Dego says the emotion of getting there is already giving way to nerves about staying there.

"There's a special feeling that's hard to explain," Dego told ONE ahead of kick-off. "It's thrilling to return to the big league, but now the real thing begins. We believe we built well, the foreigners look good, but the league will be the true test."

The venue adds a layer of irony. Dego made his name as a coach at Maccabi Haifa, whom he took over in May 2023, winning the Toto Cup that summer and steering the club to a second-place league finish and a deep European run. He left Haifa and, in October 2025, took charge of Ramat Gan in the second tier — and by the end of the season had guided them straight back into the top flight he had just left.

He won't have his captain for the reunion. Jota, sent off in the 94th minute of Ramat Gan's Toto Cup exit to Beitar Jerusalem on August 17 — a 3-3 draw settled 5-4 on penalties — picked up a second yellow after conceding a penalty for holding an opponent inside the box, and is now suspended for the Haifa game.

One familiar face returns to Sammy Ofer in a different sense: right back Getachu Yiblo, 21, is on loan at Ramat Gan from Maccabi Haifa, the club that developed him through its youth ranks and where he represented Israel at under-19 level. He is expected to make his Ligat Ha'al debut against the parent club that still holds his registration — under a coach, in Dego, who worked with him in Haifa's academy.

Ramat Gan have also freshened up the front line for the step up in class. Cameroonian forward Marius Nobiesi, 29, arrived in the close season and is favoured to lead the attack ahead of the competition for the striker's shirt, while Serbian midfielder Srđan Mihajlović, 32, joined on a free transfer from Čukarički to add experience in the centre of the park.
Not everyone is ready. Matan Hozez, one of the more recent arrivals, is still being eased into the group and will not be involved at Sammy Ofer this weekend.

For a newly promoted side, an opening trip to one of Israeli football's traditional heavyweights is as tough a fixture as the calendar could offer. But for Dego, who has now taken two different clubs in and out of the Sammy Ofer away dressing room within the space of three years, it also doubles as unfinished business — a chance to show the promotion he engineered was built to last, not just an escape from the second tier for a single season.

The season opener is away to Maccabi Haifa at Sammy Ofer Stadium in Haifa, kickoff Saturday, August 22, 2026 at 20:30.

Manager Messay Dego previously coached Maccabi Haifa (2023-2024), winning the Toto Cup and finishing second in the league, before taking charge of Ramat Gan in October 2025 and leading them to promotion.

title: Kroos names Kvaratskhelia his surprise pick for the 2026 Ballon d'Or
dek: The retired Real Madrid and Germany midfielder rates the PSG winger above Rodri, Messi, Bellingham and Mbappe, calling him 'the best player of last season'.
body: Toni Kroos has thrown his considerable weight behind an unexpected candidate for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, naming Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as his player of the year ahead of the field's usual heavyweights.

Writing on Instagram, the retired Real Madrid and Germany midfielder said the Georgian was 'the number one for me', rating him above Manchester City's Rodri, Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe in his personal ranking.
Kroos called Kvaratskhelia 'the best player of last season' and 'the best player currently at the best football club in the world', pointing to PSG's status as European champions.

According to ONE, Kroos argued that none of the more fancied names produced club campaigns consistent enough to match the Georgian's, suggesting Rodri, Bellingham and Mbappe in particular lacked the sustained club-level stability needed to outweigh his case.

Kvaratskhelia finished the season with 19 goals and 11 assists in 48 appearances across all competitions for PSG, including 10 goals and seven assists in 16 Champions League matches as the French club won back-to-back European titles.

The Ballon d'Or is due to be handed out on October 26 in London, with the field of contenders still expected to be dominated by Champions League winners and World Cup performers once nominations are finalised.

Kroos, who retired from both Real Madrid and the German national team after Euro 2024, has become an increasingly outspoken pundit since hanging up his boots, and his intervention adds an unusual voice to a Ballon d'Or debate that has so far centred on the same handful of established superstars.

title: Ronaldo returns for Al-Nassr against Al-Riyadh, needing 24 goals for 1,000
dek: The Portuguese forward is back from an extended break for wedding and World Cup recovery, sitting on 976 career goals as he begins what may be his final professional season.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo is due back in an Al-Nassr shirt on Friday for the first time this season, with his club hosting Al-Riyadh in round two of the Saudi Pro League, and the number hovering over the occasion is a stark one: 976.

That is where Ronaldo's official career goal count stands, according to ONE — 830 for his clubs and 146 for Portugal — leaving him 24 short of becoming the first footballer in history to reach 1,000 in competitive, official matches.

The 41-year-old sat out Al-Nassr's opening-day 3-1 win over Al-Fateh after the club granted him extended leave following Portugal's run at the 2026 World Cup and his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez, whom he married in a private ceremony in Cascais on August 11.

New head coach Ange Postecoglou has been easing his captain back into training over the past fortnight and is expected to hand him a route back into the side against Al-Riyadh, according to ONE's report.

Postecoglou, the former Tottenham and Celtic manager, signed a two-year contract in Riyadh over the summer, taking charge after Jorge Jesus departed following Al-Nassr's Saudi Pro League title win in 2025-26.
The 1,000-goal chase has become the defining subplot of Ronaldo's season, with the striker having said previously that he is certain to reach the mark as long as he stays free of injury.

He is also starting his 25th season as a professional, and has dropped hints that this campaign, his fourth in Saudi Arabia, could be his last — adding extra weight to every goal between now and the milestone.

Nothing is confirmed about when exactly he will get there; 24 goals across a Saudi Pro League and AFC Champions League season is a realistic target for a player who has rarely gone long spells without scoring, even into his forties.

title: Atalanta 0-0 Hapoel Tel Aviv: Bernasconi says Nerazzurri braced for a press that never came
dek: Atalanta wing-back Lorenzo Bernasconi says his side expected Hapoel Tel Aviv to press high in the Conference League play-off first leg — instead the Israeli visitors sat compact and held out for a goalless draw in Bergamo.
body: Maurizio Sarri's first game in the Atalanta dugout ended without a goal, and by full time it was the visitors from Tel Aviv doing most of the celebrating. Hapoel Tel Aviv held out for a 0-0 draw at Bergamo's New Balance Arena in the first leg of their UEFA Conference League play-off, and afterwards one of Atalanta's own players admitted the Israeli side had not played the match Bergamo expected.

"We thought they would come press us hard, but instead they covered a lot of space, and when we approached their penalty area they were very closed," Atalanta wing-back Lorenzo Bernasconi said, quoted by ONE. Rather than pressing high, Hapoel dropped into a deep, compact block and dared Atalanta to break them down.

It worked. Atalanta piled forward for long stretches, but the final product wasn't there. Bernasconi pointed to something beyond tactics too: "They are ahead of us physically too, having already played many matches." Hapoel arrived in Bergamo with a head start in match sharpness, several rounds into their Israeli league campaign while Sarri's side was still finding its feet in preseason.

The numbers back up Bernasconi's read of the game. Atalanta controlled 63 percent of possession and completed 705 passes to Hapoel's 421, pushing into the final third 69 times to Hapoel's 32. Yet Hapoel cleared their lines 23 times, won 69 percent of their tackles and were just as dominant in the air, winning 69 percent of aerial duels.

Atalanta's best chances came either side of the half-hour mark. Nicola Zalewski fired narrowly wide in the 19th minute, and five minutes later goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi was called into a smart save to deny Bernard Boateng from close range. Neither side could find a breakthrough after that, and Atalanta also had to absorb a blow to their squad depth when centre-back Giorgio Scalvini went off injured during the match.

For Hapoel, a scoreless away draw against a Serie A club in a new manager's first competitive test is a solid platform to carry into the second leg. The tie now shifts to Hapoel's temporary European home at DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary, where the Israeli club has been hosting its continental fixtures this campaign, with the return leg set for a week later.

Bernasconi's comments suggest Atalanta will need to be more direct and more clinical if they are to avoid an upset against a side that, by his own admission, matched them physically and defended with far more discipline than Bergamo had bargained for.

title: Musiala left out of German Super Cup squad after second training collapse
dek: Vincent Kompany says Bayern Munich are calm, not panicked, after Jamal Musiala fainted twice in four days during pre-season training ahead of Saturday's clash with Borussia Dortmund.
body: Jamal Musiala will not be involved when Bayern Munich face Borussia Dortmund in Saturday's German Super Cup, after the 23-year-old collapsed on the training pitch for the second time in four days.

Bayern manager Vincent Kompany confirmed the decision to leave Musiala out of the squad, explaining that the German international's medication had recently been adjusted and that the episodes followed as a side effect. "He changed something in his treatment, and then had side effects," Kompany said.
Musiala himself has previously described the incidents as temporary and brief episodes linked to impaired neurological function, stressing there is no serious underlying health risk.

Kompany insisted the club is not alarmed by the situation, which has been monitored for some time. "We've been dealing with this for a while. The initial shock is behind us. We're not in a panic," the manager said, according to ONE.

Sporting director Max Eberl added that Bayern have been in close contact with neurologists and medical staff throughout, saying the club's handling of Musiala's condition has effectively become part of its routine.

German outlets Sportschau and Tagesspiegel, reporting separately on Kompany's press conference, confirmed the club's account that Musiala had suffered collapses during pre-season friendlies within the same week, prompting the decision to keep him out of Saturday's Franz Beckenbauer Supercup against Dortmund.

Musiala is set to train individually over the coming days rather than be reintegrated immediately into full squad sessions, with Bayern wary of overloading him before the Bundesliga season kicks off the following weekend.

title: Ferencváros show interest in Maccabi Netanya's Bassam Zaarura, ONE reports
dek: The Hungarian champions are said to be aware of Netanya's €1.8 million asking price for the 23-year-old midfielder, though his agent insists he is going nowhere this window.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com - Trabzonspor vs Ferencváros, Europa League play-off

body: Another Israeli name has landed on Ferencváros's transfer radar, with ONE reporting that the Hungarian champions have begun looking into a move for Maccabi Netanya midfielder Bassam Zaarura.

According to the report, Ferencváros are already aware of Netanya's valuation of the 23-year-old at around €1.8 million, suggesting the interest goes beyond a casual scouting note and into more serious territory.

Zaarura has been one of the standout performers in Israeli football over the past year, carrying that form into the new season after joining Netanya from Maccabi Haifa in 2023 on a three-year deal. The Shefa-'Amr-born midfielder has previously drawn attention from Poland's Lech Poznań and MLS side Atlanta United, per the same report.

Ferencváros are no strangers to the Israeli market. Gabi Kanichowsky, formerly of Maccabi Tel Aviv, has been on their books since 2024, and ONE suggests the club could ultimately look to Zaarura as a fresh option in a similar mould if talks with Netanya progress.

The Hungarian giants are also very much in-season themselves: they beat Trabzonspor 1-0 away in the first leg of their Europa League play-off on Thursday, with a Champions League football and continental football very much part of the pitch they can offer a target like Zaarura.
ONE adds that Maccabi Tel Aviv have also been keeping tabs on the player domestically, underlining how highly he is rated inside Israel even as the more eye-catching interest comes from abroad.

Not everyone is treating a move as imminent, however. Zaarura's agent, Shlomi Ben Ezra, was quoted pushing back on any sense that a departure is close: "Bassam is 100% committed to Maccabi Netanya and will only play in Israel for them. Any foreign offers will be discussed with the club."

That leaves the story, for now, at the stage of interest rather than negotiation - a name Ferencváros are said to like, at a price they reportedly already know, with Netanya and the player's camp giving no signal they are ready to do business.

title: Premier League's new-manager gamble: can Maresca, Iraola and Alonso survive the pressure?
dek: A record nine Premier League clubs open 2026/27 with a manager who wasn't in the job last season, and ONE asks whether Enzo Maresca, Andoni Iraola, Xabi Alonso and Michael Carrick can handle the league's unforgiving spotlight.

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports — Premier League managers 2026/27: record new bosses, manager changes and tenure
Premier League — Manager line-up complete for 2026/27 season
ESPN — Man Utd name Michael Carrick permanent manager

body: England's top flight has never turned over its technical areas this fast. Nine of the Premier League's 20 clubs begin the 2026/27 season with a manager who wasn't in the dugout twelve months ago — the most first-time bosses on an opening weekend since 1946/47, according to Opta data reported by Sky Sports. ONE's football desk poses the obvious question as the season kicks off: can this new generation actually handle the pressure that comes with the job?

The headline change is at Manchester City, where Enzo Maresca has taken over from Pep Guardiola after his decade of dominance at the Etihad. Maresca arrives from Chelsea, and replacing a manager who redefined the modern game is an entirely different test to any he has faced before.

At Liverpool, Andoni Iraola has succeeded Arne Slot, arriving after three well-regarded seasons at Bournemouth that established him as one of the most sought-after young coaches in English football. He inherits a squad — and a fanbase — with little patience for teething problems at a club that expects to compete on every front.

Xabi Alonso's move to Chelsea completes the picture at the traditional 'Big Six' clubs that changed manager this summer. The Spaniard was dismissed by Real Madrid before Chelsea turned to him — a club that has cycled through managers with more regularity than almost any other in the competition. Survival, more than instant silverware, will define whether he has withstood the pressure.

Manchester United actually made their change first. Michael Carrick was confirmed as permanent manager in May, on a contract through 2028, after steering United to 11 wins from 16 matches as interim following Rúben Amorim's sacking in January — form that secured Champions League qualification and effectively won him the job outright.

Beyond the elite clubs, the churn runs right through the division: Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Fulham, Ipswich Town, Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest have all made changes of their own, taking the league-wide total of new appointments to nine.

The numbers underline how thin patience has worn across the competition. The average managerial tenure heading into the new season, across all 20 clubs, is just 474 days — the lowest opening-day figure of the Premier League era, Sky Sports reported.

The incoming cohort is also unusually young. The average age of a Premier League manager this season is 47.1, the youngest group in twenty years, evidence that clubs are increasingly betting on energy and adaptability over experience in what is now one of the most demanding jobs in world football.

The exception that proves the rule sits at Arsenal, where Mikel Arteta — in the post since December 2019 — is now the division's longest-serving manager by a distance, having overseen 2,432 days in charge. That kind of continuity has become the rarity rather than the norm.

For Maresca, Iraola, Alonso and Carrick, the theory going in is straightforward enough: work the group hard, press from the front, set the tone early. Whether any of that survives contact with a genuine title race, an injury crisis or a bad November is the question ONE's preview leaves hanging over the division as a new era begins.

title: Former Beitar Jerusalem favourite Uri Magbo signs for Hapoel Umm al-Fahm
dek: The 38-year-old left-back, twice a Beitar player and a Toto Cup winner with the club, has joined the Liga Alef North side until the end of the season.

verificationSources.label: SoccerPunter — Hapoel Umm al-Fahm, Liga Alef North 2025/26

body: Uri Magbo, one of the more recognisable journeymen of the Israeli lower leagues over the past decade, has a new club: Hapoel Umm al-Fahm, who play in Liga Alef North, confirmed on Friday that the 38-year-old left-back has signed until the end of the season.

"The experienced left-back Uri Magbo has joined the club until the end of the season," Hapoel Umm al-Fahm said in a statement carried by ONE, adding that Magbo brings "extensive experience and a strong leadership personality" to a squad being rebuilt under coach Tomer Kashtan.

Magbo, for his part, framed the move as buying into a project rather than winding down a career. According to ONE, he said the club and its supporters "deserve at least the Premier League" — a pointed statement of ambition for a side currently competing in Israel's third tier.

The name will mean plenty to Beitar Jerusalem fans. Magbo had two spells in the yellow and black, first arriving in 2015 and featuring in the club's European campaigns, then returning in 2019 for a second stint that produced some of the most vivid moments of his career.

He scored in extra time as Beitar beat Maccabi Tel Aviv to lift the 2019 Toto Cup, and the following year won the competition again with the club. In 2021 he struck a late equaliser against Bnei Yehuda that proved pivotal in Beitar's fight to avoid relegation from the top flight.

Those Beitar years sit at the peak of a long and well-travelled career. Magbo has made more than 450 league appearances and scored around 35 goals, passing through clubs including Maccabi Petah Tikva, Ironi Kiryat Shmona and Hapoel Kfar Saba along the way. Last season he made 31 appearances for Hapoel Hadera.

At Umm al-Fahm he joins a club looking to climb back up the pyramid after relegation from Liga Leumit at the end of the 2024–25 season, and his arrival is being pitched by the club as a statement of intent for the campaign ahead.

title: Alon Ziv: Tiberias squad still not closed as Ligat Ha'al opener nears
dek: Head coach says Ironi Tiberias are still working to strengthen the squad ahead of Saturday's season-opening clash with Hapoel Petah Tikva.

body: Ironi Tiberias open their Ligat Ha'al campaign on Saturday evening at 20:00 with a home game against Hapoel Petah Tikva, and head coach Alon Ziv is making no secret of the fact his squad is still a work in progress.
"The squad still isn't closed," Ziv said this week, according to ONE. "We're working together to strengthen it and looking for players who can improve us."

The report added that Ziv wants to add at least one upgrade in positions where the club feels it lacks depth, including possibly abroad, though he stressed any additions would only come if the right opportunity arose rather than for the sake of activity.

Ziv, who was appointed as Tiberias head coach this summer and shares sideline duties with Moti Crispin - who does not hold a Pro coaching licence - said the emphasis inside the camp has shifted away from squad-building talk and toward the pitch. "We're less dealing with personal feelings right now and more with professional preparation for the season's opening match," he said. ONE reported the team had completed a solid training week built around integrating its tactical approach.

Forward Daniel Golani, who joined Tiberias permanently this summer after impressing on loan from Maccabi Haifa last season, was also quoted ahead of the opener. "We come to every match aiming to take points, to narrow and close the gap," Golani said.

That gap is a pointed reference for Tiberias, who had to fight through a bottom-of-the-table relegation battle last season to preserve their Ligat Ha'al status. Golani framed Saturday's opener, against a Hapoel Petah Tikva side he and his teammates respect, as the first step in avoiding a repeat.
Kickoff at Tiberias is set for 20:00 on Saturday, in what both Sport1 and ONE list as one of two matches launching round one of the 2026/27 Ligat Ha'al season.

title: Israel's show jumping team finishes 26th of 30, misses direct Olympic route at Aachen worlds
dek: Daniel and Mark Bluman, Theodor Boris and Robin Muhr fell short of the top 10 at the FEI World Championships, but two more chances at a Los Angeles 2028 berth remain.

verificationSources.label: Horse & Hound live coverage of the FEI World Championships, Aachen

body: Israel's show jumping team fell well short of a direct ticket to the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics this week, finishing 26th among the 30 nations that contested the team competition at the FEI World Championships in Aachen, Germany, ONE reported.

Only the leading ten squads from that opening round advance to the medal-deciding team final, and only the strongest sides to emerge from that final earn one of the seven direct Olympic berths on offer at Aachen — the United States, as host nation for LA28, does not need to qualify through the event. Israel's tally left the team nowhere near that cut.

The damage was largely done by Daniel Bluman, riding Corby V.V., who picked up 17 penalty points in the team's weakest round of the day. Mark Bluman and Landon de Nyze added eight faults, matched by Theodor Boris and Kazan Z, while Robin Muhr did not take part in the round at all.

Independent live coverage of the championships from Horse & Hound corroborated the toll, reporting that Mark Bluman's eight faults compounded Daniel Bluman's earlier 17 and left Israel's place in the following day's final "in doubt" — doubt that hardened into elimination once the round was complete.

Daniel Bluman remains the team's headline name and by far its most accomplished rider. Colombian-born, he switched allegiance to Israel in 2017 and has since become a fixture in world jumping's top ten rankings, representing Israel at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where the team also finished toward the bottom of the field, in ninth.

Aachen's Soers showground, home each summer to the CHIO Aachen, is hosting this year's world championships as jumping's marquee event on the road to LA28, drawing 51 nations and 146 riders across the team and individual disciplines.

ONE noted the setback does not close the door on Israel entirely. A further set of regional qualifying events is scheduled for 2027, with the top two teams from those competitions still able to book a team berth for Los Angeles. Individual qualification also remains open to any of Israel's riders independent of this week's result.

title: Meir Buchbot signs for Hapoel Beit She'an ahead of new season
dek: The 21-year-old forward, released by relegated Maccabi Bnei Reineh, joins the Liga Alef North club under coach Guy Dayan, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - החלוץ מאיר בוחבוט חתם בהפועל בית שאן
Israel Football Association player registry - Meir Nissim Buchbot
Walla Sport - Bnei Reineh relegated from Ligat Ha'al

body: Meir Buchbot has found a new home for the 2026/27 season, signing with Hapoel Beit She'an under coach Guy Dayan, ONE reports. The 21-year-old forward arrives at the Liga Alef North club as a free agent after being let go by Maccabi Bnei Reineh.

Buchbot's path to senior football has been unusual. He comes from a Haredi family of ten children and only began organised football at 13 and a half, starting out at the Hatzor sports club in the Galilee before working his way up through the lower leagues.

From Hatzor he moved to Tiberias Municipal, where he spent roughly three seasons from 2019/20, before Maccabi Bnei Reineh signed him in December 2022 on a three-year contract. According to ONE, he became the first player to graduate directly from Reineh's youth ranks into the senior squad.

The move paid off in the 2023/24 season, when Buchbot ran riot in the northern youth league as an overage player, scoring 43 league goals plus another in the cup while Reineh's first team was competing in Ligat Ha'al.

He never quite forced his way into that senior side. In 2024/25 he was loaned out to clubs in Liga Alef and Liga Bet North, scoring seven goals, and last season he trained with Bnei Reineh's extended squad without making a first-team appearance during what turned out to be the club's final campaign in the top flight - Reineh were relegated to Liga Leumit after four seasons among the elite.

With his contract at Reineh not renewed, Buchbot now gets a fresh start at Hapoel Beit She'an, a club with its own history of yo-yoing between the divisions after a spell in the top flight in the 1990s and a period of dissolution before being refounded in 2009.
Beit She'an open their season on August 28, hosting Maccabi Tira in the State Cup's fifth round, which will give the new signing an early chance to make his mark.

title: Ziv Arie says decision to join Maccabi Petah Tikva was an easy one
dek: The new head coach, who left Hapoel Jerusalem after seven years, previews Saturday's Ligat Ha'al opener against Ironi Kiryat Shmona.
body: Ziv Arie stood in front of reporters this week as Maccabi Petah Tikva's new head coach, and his message ahead of Saturday's Ligat Ha'al curtain-raiser against Ironi Kiryat Shmona was simple: this felt right. "The decision to come was easy," Arie said, according to ONE. "Once I left Hapoel Jerusalem and there was the option to come here, it's a club that suits me."

The 55-year-old walked away from Hapoel Jerusalem after seven years in charge, one of the longer managerial tenures in Israeli football, before agreeing a one-year contract at Maccabi Petah Tikva, where he replaces Noam Shoham.

He inherits a club on the way back up. Maccabi Petah Tikva needed only a single season in Liga Leumit to earn an instant return to the top flight, finishing among the division's top two sides. Saturday's game against Kiryat Shmona doubles as the club's first fixture back among Israel's elite.

Arie was careful not to underestimate the opposition. Kiryat Shmona, he noted, "made good games and good results" in preseason — a side he expects to provide a tough early test even as his own team, by his own admission, is still finding its feet.

"We're not the finished article yet, but we'll keep improving step by step," he said, pointing to what he has already seen on the training pitch and in the Toto Cup as reason for confidence. "I see good players in training and in the Toto Cup games, and I believe in the roster."

Captain Aviv Salam struck a similar note alongside his new coach, framing the season as part of a longer rebuild following a period that included relegation from the top flight. "We're going through a process to be more stable," Salam said, pointing to a squad built around a mix of young and experienced players as the foundation for that stability.

Kickoff between Maccabi Petah Tikva and Ironi Kiryat Shmona is set for 20:00 on Saturday, the opening whistle of a Ligat Ha'al season in which both Arie and his new club will be looking to show last year's second-tier detour is firmly behind them.

title: Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon beat Maccabi Ironi Ashdod 2-1 after extra time with only nine fit players
dek: Coach Assi Alimelech says sixteen of his squad were sidelined by unfinished medical clearances and two more played through injury as his rebuilding Liga Alef side dug out a State Cup opening-round win.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "לוקח את הלב של השחקנים. מהמשחק? אין מה ללמוד"
Hebrew Wikipedia — Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon (relegation to Liga Alef, ownership, coach)

body: Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon needed extra time, and had nobody left on the bench to bring on, to see off Maccabi Ironi Ashdod 2-1 in the opening round of the State Cup — a scoreline that flattered a night in which the third-tier club could barely field a team.

Coach Assi Alimelech did not dress it up afterwards. "Only nine players passed medical checks and played against Ashdod," he said, of a squad gutted by bureaucracy rather than injury alone. "Two were injured and shouldn't have been in the squad."

The other sixteen players in his group, Alimelech said, simply could not be registered in time — their medical clearances with the Israel Football Association had not come through before kick-off, leaving him to send out a patched-together side with no fit replacements waiting.

"I take their great heart from this match, though there's little to learn from it, as our key players didn't participate," he said, careful to praise the effort without pretending the performance told him much about his actual team.

On the football itself, Alimelech insisted his makeshift XI were rarely troubled. "We controlled the game despite the situation," he said. "Ashdod didn't create chances except for [Yakir] Zilberman's shot." Nir Ramat HaSharon eventually turned the tie in extra time, a result Alimelech called all the more remarkable given his players were, by his own account, running on empty with no substitutions possible.
The win sends Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon through to round five of the State Cup, where they will host Jerusalem FC.

The context matters. Nir Ramat HaSharon spent three straight seasons in Liga Leumit before the Israel Football Association's appeals tribunal ordered them relegated to Liga Alef in July 2025 over failed financial and audit checks — a paperwork collapse rather than a football one. New ownership, led by producer Yoav Gross as chairman with Fredi Tsarfati installed as general manager, took over in January 2026 with an explicit goal of rebuilding and pushing straight back up.

Alimelech, who has previously coached Hapoel Hadera and Kfar Kassem, was brought in as part of that project. His message after the Ashdod win was as much about what comes next as what just happened: "Once I have a full squad, it will be a different world, and expectations will change accordingly."
For now, an ugly, undermanned cup win is what the new-look club has to show for the start of the season — proof of character, in the coach's telling, but not yet proof of anything else.

title: US analysts spell out what Portland need from Deni Avdija this season
dek: With Damian Lillard back from his Achilles injury and Ja Morant now in the backcourt, American analysts say Avdija's job is shifting from lead creator to the Trail Blazers' most adaptable weapon.

verificationSources.label: NBA.com - Trail Blazers add Ja Morant

body: Deni Avdija spent last season learning what it feels like to be the centre of an NBA offence. This season, American analysts are warning him to prepare for the opposite: sharing the ball with the most crowded backcourt Portland has fielded in years.

That is the thrust of an analysis piece flagged by ONE, in which US commentators went player by player through the Trail Blazers' roster and assigned each man a job description for 2026-27 — with Avdija's brief the trickiest of them all.

The Israeli forward is coming off a genuine breakout: a career-best 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.7 assists a game in 2025-26, numbers that earned him his first NBA All-Star selection and turned him into the identity of the Trail Blazers' offence.

That production helped drag Portland back into the postseason for the first time since 2020-21, via a play-in win over Phoenix in which Avdija scored 40 points. The run ended in the first round, where Victor Wembanyama's Spurs closed out the series 4-1, sealing it with a 114-95 win in Game 5.

The roster around Avdija has since been remade. Portland sent Jerami Grant to Memphis in a deal, completed on June 30, that brought back point guard Ja Morant — a bet on a talented but troubled floor general who is still owed the bulk of a five-year, $197 million contract.

More significant still is the return of Damian Lillard. The franchise great tore his Achilles tendon in the 2025 playoffs with Milwaukee, was waived by the Bucks, and chose to sign a three-year deal to come home to Portland rather than chase a title elsewhere. He is expected to be back on the floor for the start of this season after missing all of the last one.

Add in Jrue Holiday, whom the Trail Blazers have reportedly rebuffed trade offers for, plus Scoot Henderson and Shaedon Sharpe, and new head coach Micah Nori inherits a genuine logjam of players who all want the ball in their hands.

That is precisely the problem the American analysis zeroes in on for Avdija. Lillard is pencilled in to stretch the floor and knock down threes, Morant is expected to attack downhill and get to the rim, Toumani Camara is tasked with anchoring the defensive end, and rookie big man Donovan Clingan is asked to hold down the paint on both sides of the ball.

Avdija's assignment does not fit neatly into one column. Rather than running the same shot-creating operation he did en route to his All-Star year, analysts argue he now has to become the connective tissue of the whole roster — scoring when needed, initiating in the frontcourt, defending across positions, and doing it without the same monopoly on possessions.

Ynet's own reporting on the situation strikes a similar note but pushes back slightly on the idea that Avdija is being demoted in importance. Despite the traffic jam of ball-handlers, several US outlets still expect him to remain Portland's primary offensive option, arguing that his all-around game is exactly what lets the roster absorb Lillard and Morant without breaking.

The verdict, in other words, is not that Avdija's season gets smaller — it is that his job gets harder to define. Fewer clean possessions with the ball glued to his hands, potentially, but a wider set of responsibilities and, if the analysts are right, a real chance to be Portland's most valuable player even while touching the ball less.

For a player who only established himself as a franchise cornerstone a year ago, it is an unusual vote of confidence: the Trail Blazers are betting that Avdija's versatility, not his usage rate, is what makes their crowded new roster work.

title: Hapoel Be'er Sheva fly to Baku for Champions League playoff decider against Sabah
dek: The Israeli champions leave Saturday night carrying a 2-1 first-leg lead, with a first-ever place in the Champions League league phase within reach.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "הפועל ב"ש תמריא לאזרבייג'ן כבר מחר בערב"

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva's squad will board a flight for Baku on Saturday night, ONE reports, the next step on a journey that could end in the Israeli champions' first-ever appearance in the Champions League league phase.

According to ONE, the party leaves Israel at 22:00 on Saturday ahead of Tuesday's second leg of the Champions League playoff round against Sabah FK of Azerbaijan, with Ran Kozuk's side carrying a 2-1 lead from the first meeting.

That first leg, played on Wednesday at a neutral venue in Bucharest — the arrangement Israeli clubs have used for UEFA "home" fixtures this season — swung on a late header. Veljko Simić put Sabah ahead inside six minutes after a defensive mix-up, Javon East equalised just before half-time, and Igor Zlatanović nodded in an Eliel Perez corner with 11 minutes left to win it for Hapoel.

A two-legged victory would carry unprecedented weight for the club: Hapoel Be'er Sheva have never before reached the Champions League's league phase, only its qualifying rounds. They arrived at this playoff round by eliminating Red Star Belgrade 3-0 on aggregate, Kozuk's side winning both legs of that tie.

ONE reports that the dressing room is treating the 2-1 cushion as useful rather than decisive, pointing to Sabah's record of staging big comebacks at home this campaign. Kozuk and his staff plan a lighter training session followed by tactical work before the squad flies out, fine-tuning the approach for a ground where the Azerbaijani side have shown they can score in bunches.

Off the pitch, ONE reports that Hapoel's sponsor Eyal Ravid is working with the club to arrange an additional charter flight so more supporters can follow the team to Baku, with tickets for Tuesday's match priced at just 11 shekels for fans of both clubs — a striking price for a continental knockout fixture, and one clearly designed to fill the stands on both sides.

Should Hapoel hold their nerve in Azerbaijan, they would guarantee themselves a place — and the associated prize money and fixture list — in the newly formatted Champions League league phase this autumn, a first for a club that has spent decades chasing continental football's top table.

title: Ella Bar-Lev takes world U18 judo gold as Agam Noy adds bronze in same category
dek: Bar-Lev beat Belgium's Myles Dapau on golden score to win the -48kg title in Guayaquil, while teammate Agam Noy claimed bronze in a rare same-day, same-weight double for Israel.

verificationSources.label: IJF Guayaquil World Championships Cadets 2026 competition page

body: Israel opened the World Judo Cadet (Under-18) Championships in Guayaquil, Ecuador, in style, with two of its judokas sharing the podium in the very same weight category on the very first day of competition, ONE reports.
Ella Bar-Lev topped the -48kg draw, beating Belgium's Myles Dapau in the final by golden score to be crowned world champion, according to the report.

Teammate Agam Noy completed the Israeli sweep of medals in the division, taking bronze after her contest with Brazil's Micaela Santos ended controversially: Santos was penalised for an illegal arm lock, handing Noy the win and the podium spot, ONE reported.

Having two Israeli judokas medal in an identical weight class on the same day is an unusual feat even by the standards of a country that has built a reputation as a judo powerhouse over the past two decades.

"An excellent day of competition for the Israeli team — a historic achievement with two female athletes on the podium in the same weight category," the head coach of Israel's women's youth judo squad, named in the report as Shni Harshko, said. The coach is known internationally as Shany Hershko, who guided Yarden Gerbi to a world title in 2013 and an Olympic bronze in 2016 and now heads Israel's women's national programme.

Israel Judo Association chairman Moshe Ponte, cited in the report as Moshe Ponti, added: "Time and again Israeli judo proves it has a promising future... all honour to the athletes who achieved this tremendous success."

The Cadet Worlds, open to judokas up to age 18, run in Guayaquil from August 20 to 23 and are drawing hundreds of competitors from dozens of countries across the weight divisions, with more Israeli entrants still to compete as the event continues.

Israel's senior judo programme has produced Olympic and world medals over the past decade, including golds and bronzes at the Tokyo and Paris Games, and a strong showing at cadet level is typically read domestically as an early marker of the next generation coming through the federation's pipeline.

title: Bachar weighs lineup dilemmas as Maccabi Haifa open season against Hapoel Ramat Gan
dek: The champions' coach has settled on his back four but is still testing combinations in midfield and attack, with new signing Andrea Novakovic in line for a first appearance, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - רגע לפני ר"ג: ההתלבטויות של בכר לגבי ההרכב

body: Barak Bachar has one settled unit and several open questions to resolve before Maccabi Haifa open their 2026/27 Ligat Ha'al title defence at home to newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan on Saturday evening, ONE reports.
Kickoff at Sammy Ofer Stadium is set for 20:30, and the champions will want to start the campaign cleanly after a bumpy pre-season that included a disappointing cup outing, according to the report.

The back line, at least, appears to have picked itself. ONE reports Bachar has kept the same defensive shape he used on Haifa's recent trip to Jerusalem: Omri Glazer in goal behind Yael Batai, Nigel Lonwijk and Pedrão, with Wanderson "Tsonami" at left-back.

Midfield is where the real head-scratching is happening. The coach has run at least three different combinations in training, per the report - Yarin Levi, Eitan Azulai and Bruninho all in central midfield in one variation, Bruninho pushed out to the left wing in another, with Ali Mohammed and Navot Ratner rotating through the same sessions.

Up front, the choice is between Andrea Novakovic and Silva Kani, with Kenji Gora at risk of dropping to the bench, ONE reports. Novakovic, signed on a free transfer after leaving Bari, only completed his registration with the Israel Football Association on August 20 - meaning Saturday could double as his Haifa debut if Bachar picks him.
There is a smaller dilemma at right-back too, where academy product Iyad Khalili is pushing to replace Cedric Don in the XI, according to the report.

Further up that flank, Haifa are still without a long-term fix. Manuel Benson's serious injury, expected to sideline the Belgian winger for most if not all of the season, has left the club actively searching the market for a replacement right winger.

ONE reports Bachar's stated priority heading into the opener is defensive discipline - avoiding being caught out by Ramat Gan's counter-attacking threat - while he tries to knit a squad reshaped over the summer into a cohesive unit.

Hapoel Ramat Gan arrive at Sammy Ofer Stadium as one of two teams promoted after finishing in the top places of Liga Leumit last season, making Saturday's meeting a first top-flight test for the newcomers against one of the league's traditional heavyweights.

title: Lugano 2-1 Maccabi Tel Aviv: dressing-room fury over 'gifts' as Conference League tie hangs in the balance
dek: Anonymous players tell ONE their own defensive errors, not Lugano, cost Maccabi Tel Aviv the Conference League playoff first leg, with one warning bluntly: keep this up and we'll eliminate ourselves.

verificationSources.label: ONE — match report and dressing-room quotes
Walla Sport — "לא למדה לקח: מכבי ת"א הסתבכה עם 2:1 חלש מול לוגאנו"
Haaretz — Maccabi Tel Aviv lose 2-1 to Lugano
Sport1/Maariv — Kenny Miller pre-match comments on avoiding a repeat of the CSKA Sofia round

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's players did not need reporters to tell them what went wrong in Lugano. They said it themselves, bluntly, in the dressing room afterwards: this defeat was self-inflicted, and if the habit does not stop, Europe will stop too.

The Yellow-and-Blue lost 2-1 away to FC Lugano on Thursday in the first leg of their Conference League playoff tie, a result that leaves next week's return leg — to be played, as has become the norm for Israeli clubs' European "home" fixtures, in Batumi, Georgia — as a must-win for Kenny Miller's side.

Lugano struck first in the 30th minute when goalkeeper Ofek Malika failed to deal with a cross into the box, allowing Kevin Behrens to head in unmarked. Maccabi hit back seven minutes into the second half through Ido Shahar, who finished neatly at the near post after a pinpoint pass from Roy Revivo — a goal the defender scored, fittingly, on his own birthday.

The lead did not survive long. Lugano won a penalty in the 54th minute after Tyrese Asante fouled an opponent in the box, and Anto Grgic converted from the spot to restore the Swiss side's advantage. Revivo almost salvaged a draw late on, his shot from distance crashing back off the crossbar.
"I would've been much happier if we'd won and got a perfect birthday present," Shahar told ONE afterwards. "I'm happy about the goal, but unfortunately we lost in the end."

Other players in the squad were far harsher in their assessment, speaking to ONE on condition of anonymity. "We're not playing well, we're giving opponents easy goals with ridiculous mistakes, we're eliminating ourselves," one said. Another put it more starkly: "If we keep handing out gifts like this, we won't be in Europe this season."

It is not the first time this month the same complaint has surfaced. Sport1-Maariv reported that before the Lugano match, Kenny Miller specifically worked with his players on cutting out the same kind of defensive gifts that had plagued Maccabi in their previous European qualifying round, against CSKA Sofia.

The squad's frustration extends beyond the pitch. According to ONE, several players believe the summer rebuild has left the group short-handed: only winger Aster Sokler has been added as reinforcement, while sporting director Steven Vanharen's public line that the club needed just two more signings is regarded inside the dressing room as an underestimate of the gaps in depth and quality.

The injury list has not helped. Foreign trio Carwin Andrade, Ion Nicolaescu and Christian Blitz all remain unavailable, and midfielder Shgev Yehezkel is also carrying a knock — leaving Miller with a threadbare group to rotate even as some players privately question why he has stuck so rigidly with the same starting XI despite underwhelming individual displays.

None of it changes the maths facing Maccabi now. They must overturn a one-goal deficit in Batumi next Thursday simply to reach the Conference League league phase, with elimination the alternative for a club that has treated continental football as a financial and prestige priority.

There is no time to dwell on it either way. Domestic business resumes first, with Maccabi opening their Israeli Premier League campaign away to Hapoel Jerusalem at Ramat Hasharon Stadium on Sunday, before a home date with Maccabi Haifa at Bloomfield the following week.

For a squad that keeps describing its own mistakes as "gifts," the message from within the camp this week was unusually direct: stop handing out presents, or watch the season's biggest prize disappear before it has properly begun.

title: Oklahoma City, 28 October 2009: The Night an Israeli First Walked Onto an NBA Court
dek: Omri Casspi's 15 points off the Sacramento Kings bench made him the first Israeli-born player in NBA history — and gave a basketball-mad nation a reason to set its alarms for 5 a.m.

verificationSources.label: JTA — "Omri Casspi, first Israeli player in NBA, retires from professional basketball"
Christian Science Monitor — "Israel's Omri Casspi leaps into NBA as his Tel Aviv club totters"
ESPN — Thunder 102, Kings 89 (28 Oct 2009) final score
NBA.com — Kings vs. Thunder game summary, 28 Oct 2009
Times of Israel — "Gal Mekel set to become second Israeli in the NBA"
JTA — "Israeli teen Deni Avdija goes to Washington Wizards with 9th pick, making history"

body: The Ford Center in Oklahoma City was built for Thunder fans, not for history written in Hebrew, but on the night of 28 October 2009 both things happened at once. Midway through the first quarter of a forgettable early-season game between the Thunder and the Sacramento Kings, a 21-year-old rookie forward checked in off the visitors' bench. He hit his first jump shot, and with that one swish Omri Casspi became the first Israeli-born player ever to appear in an NBA game.

It had been four months in the making. On 25 June 2009, the Kings had used the 23rd overall pick in the NBA draft on Casspi, making him the first Israeli-born player selected in the first round of any draft. Sacramento signed him to a two-year contract worth a guaranteed $2.42 million, and the wait for his debut became a small national event back home.

Casspi's path to Oklahoma City had run through Holon, where he was born on 22 June 1988, and through the youth ranks of Maccabi Tel Aviv, whose academy he joined at 13. After a loan season with Hapoel Galil Elyon, he returned to Maccabi for the 2008–09 season, helped the club reclaim the Israeli championship, made the league's all-star team and started for the Israeli national side — the résumé that persuaded an NBA franchise to gamble a first-round pick on a player out of Israel for the first time.

The debut itself was modest by box-score standards: 15 points in 19 minutes off the bench, with three rebounds, in a game the Thunder won 102–89. But the scoreline was beside the point. For a country that had sent generations of talented players to Europe's leagues but never to the NBA, an Israeli in an NBA box score was itself the story.

Israel's Sport 5 network carried the game live and in Hebrew, which meant commentators and diehard fans alike were up at five in the morning local time to watch it. Newspapers ran daily recaps of Casspi's stat line for months afterward, and radio shows led their sports segments with his numbers before Kings games had even finished on the American clock. One Israeli website marked the debut with a line the Christian Science Monitor thought worth quoting back to American readers: "After 2000 years of exile and 63 years of the NBA, he did not disappoint the firm."

The moment carried a bittersweet edge at home. Casspi's rise coincided almost exactly with a financial scandal engulfing Maccabi Tel Aviv, the club that had raised him, after allegations of a Ponzi-like investment scheme connected to the suicide of one of its vice presidents. Commentator Amotz Asa-El used Casspi's debut to argue the two stories were not really in tension: "Omri Casspi is a product of a trend," he wrote. "He shows that fundamentally, what ails Israeli basketball is a curable illness, rather than a terminal disease."

Casspi kept adding to the milestone through his rookie year. On 16 December 2009, in his first NBA start, he scored 22 points — tying the record for the most points by any King in a first career start since the franchise had moved to Sacramento in 1985.

He went on to play a decade in the NBA, moving from Sacramento to Cleveland, Houston, New Orleans, Memphis and Minnesota before a stint with the Golden State Warriors — with whom he collected a championship ring in 2018 despite being waived that spring before the playoffs began. He finished his NBA career with averages of 7.9 points and 4.0 rebounds a game.

Casspi did not stay the only Israeli in the league for long, though he remained its trailblazer. Gal Mekel followed him to the NBA in 2013, signing with the Dallas Mavericks as the league's second Israeli-born player. Deni Avdija went further still in 2020, taken ninth overall by the Washington Wizards — the highest an Israeli has ever been drafted.

Casspi returned to Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2019 for a final domestic chapter and retired from professional basketball in July 2021. But it is the shot he hit in Oklahoma City, in front of bleary-eyed viewers seven time zones away, that opened the door. Every Israeli who has followed him into the NBA since has walked through it.

title: Italian police seize 45kg of fireworks from two Israeli fans before Atalanta clash
dek: Digos officers raided a Bergamo bed-and-breakfast and confiscated smoke bombs and pyrotechnics as the city mounted heavy security for Hapoel Tel Aviv's Conference League playoff visit to Atalanta.

verificationSources.label: ANSA — match result and Sarri debut

body: Italian police confiscated 45 kilograms of pyrotechnic material from a bed-and-breakfast in central Bergamo on the eve of Atalanta's Conference League playoff first leg against Hapoel Tel Aviv, with two Israeli fans identified as having been staying at the property, ONE reports.

The haul, seized by Digos — Italy's specialist police unit — included smoke bombs and flares gathered up during a sweep of city-centre accommodation ahead of Thursday's kick-off. Neither ONE nor Italian outlets covering the operation reported any arrests; the two supporters were simply named as identified in connection with the find, and it remains unclear whether they now face charges.

The seizure came amid an unusually heavy security operation for what was, on paper, a routine European qualifying fixture. More than 1,000 Israeli fans travelled for the match, most on charter flights, with the visiting allocation sold out well before kick-off, according to BergamoNews.

Bergamo police described the deployment as comparable to the kind of operation mounted for a Bayern Munich or Borussia Dortmund Champions League visit — a striking benchmark for a Conference League playoff. Officers held technical meetings at police headquarters and inspected the stadium in the days beforehand, while a nearby construction site was secured specifically to stop loose materials being turned into projectiles.

A restricted traffic zone was extended around the ground, and the meeting point for travelling Hapoel supporters was moved after the original venue became unavailable. Fans were bussed to the stadium under police escort, with no autonomous entry permitted.

Pro-Palestinian demonstrators also gathered near the stadium, ONE reported, in a protest Italian authorities had anticipated and planned around; UEFA regulations bar flags of countries not involved in the fixture from being displayed inside the ground.

The scale of the security response reflects a wider pattern rather than a one-off. Hapoel Tel Aviv, like other Israeli clubs in European competition, has been unable to host UEFA fixtures on home soil because of the ongoing security situation; the second leg of this tie is scheduled for 27 August at a neutral venue in Miskolc, Hungary, rather than in Israel.
On the pitch, the first leg finished goalless, 0-0, in what was also Maurizio Sarri's competitive debut as Atalanta head coach. The tie remains level heading into next week's return fixture.

title: Atalanta 0-0 Hapoel Tel Aviv: Sarri admits the Israelis had the physical edge
dek: In his competitive debut as Atalanta coach, Maurizio Sarri conceded his side were second best physically against Hapoel Tel Aviv in a goalless Conference League play-off opener, with the tie now shifting to a neutral Hungarian venue.
body: Maurizio Sarri's first competitive match in charge of Atalanta produced no goals and, by his own admission, no shortage of problems. The Nerazzurri were held 0-0 at home by Hapoel Tel Aviv in the first leg of their Europa Conference League play-off on Thursday, and afterwards the Italian coach did not hide from the most obvious explanation.

"Hapoel Tel Aviv were better than us physically," Sarri said, according to ONE, pinpointing the gap that stopped Atalanta from turning their possession into chances against an Israeli side playing its first European campaign in more than a decade.

Sarri went further in diagnosing his team's sluggishness in the final third. "Every time we receive the ball we think, and that slows us down," he said, describing a Serie A squad still short of the fluency and automatisms he wants after replacing Ivan Juric over the summer.

It was not all bleak from the Atalanta bench. Sarri pointed to a defensive foundation already forming, noting his side have now kept a clean sheet in three straight matches heading into the new season proper.

He also singled out several young players for praise even amid the frustration in attack, name-checking centre-back Giorgio Scalvini, right-back Odilon Kossounou and defender Rasmus Kristensen as players still developing but already contributing.

Sarri was careful to frame the draw in context, stressing that this Atalanta squad remains a work in progress. "We don't yet have everything we need to aim higher," he said, a reminder that his rebuild in Bergamo is only a few weeks old.

For Hapoel Tel Aviv, the goalless draw away to a Serie A club represents a genuinely strong result and continues an eye-catching run through the qualifying rounds that included a win over Ludogorets to reach the play-off stage.

The tie is not finished, though the return leg will not be played in Israel. Because Hapoel Tel Aviv cannot currently host UEFA matches at home for security reasons, the second leg is scheduled for August 27 at the DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary, with a place in the Conference League league phase on the line.

title: Rayo Vallecano 1-1 Alavés: Mariano Díaz strikes late in Rayo's Butarque exile
dek: Andrei Rațiu's costly backpass let Mariano Díaz snatch a point for Alavés in the 84th minute, as Rayo Vallecano's ongoing stadium saga cost them victory in their first home game of the season.

verificationSources.label: ElDesmarque — Rayo Vallecano 1-1 Alavés, resumen y goles
El Nacional (RD) — Mariano volvió a marcar en la Liga Española

body: Mariano Díaz has wasted no time settling into life at Deportivo Alavés. On Thursday the Dominican striker struck again, curling in an 84th-minute equaliser away to Rayo Vallecano that rescued a 1-1 draw and kept Alavés unbeaten through the opening two rounds of the new La Liga season.

The match was played at Leganés's Butarque stadium rather than Rayo's own Vallecas, with the Madrid club forced into a temporary home while a dispute with the Community of Madrid over renovation work at their historic ground drags on. It was effectively Rayo's first home fixture of 2026-27 — and they came within six minutes of winning it.

Sergio Camello had put the hosts ahead early in the second half, converting from close range in the 47th minute in front of a crowd still adjusting to watching Rayo play on a borrowed pitch. For much of the following half-hour, Rayo looked the likelier side to hold on for the points.

Alavés kept probing, and their leveller came from an unlikely source. Rayo defender Andrei Rațiu played a loose pass back toward his own goal under no real pressure; Mariano read it first, raced through and beat goalkeeper Cárdenas to make it 1-1 in the 84th minute, according to Spanish outlet ElDesmarque.

It was the second goal in as many league matches for Mariano, who also scored as Alavés opened their campaign with a 3-0 win over Getafe. The 33-year-old, a Real Madrid academy product who also had spells at Lyon and Sevilla before joining Alavés last year, has been central to one of the division's better early-season stories.

The point leaves Alavés on four from two matches — a win and a draw — placing them among La Liga's early pace-setters, according to reporting on the match. Rayo, by contrast, remain without a win after also losing 2-1 away to Sevilla on the opening weekend, leaving them on a single point.

For Rayo, the frustration is compounded by circumstance: a team still searching for its footing while playing home games away from its own stadium, with supporters having to travel across Madrid to watch fixtures at a rival's ground.

Alavés, coached by Quique Sánchez Flores, will look to build on the draw as their early-season push continues under a manager known for squeezing results out of a limited squad. For Rayo, the more pressing question is increasingly off the pitch — when Vallecas will reopen.

Mariano Díaz equalised for Alavés in the 84th minute after Rayo defender Andrei Rațiu's misplaced backpass, beating goalkeeper Cárdenas.
