title: León, 20 October 1968: The Draw From a Sombrero That Invented the Penalty Shoot-Out
dek: Israel's Olympic footballers were beaten by lottery, not by play, when a Bulgarian slip of paper ended their run in Mexico. The heartbreak that followed gave the world the penalty shoot-out.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — Israel at the 1968 Summer Olympics
Wikipedia — Football at the 1968 Summer Olympics
JNS — Could the World Cup final be decided by an Israeli innovation?
The Jewish Chronicle — Yosef Dagan obituary
This Day In Football History — 20 October 1968

body: León, Mexico, was a strange place for an Israeli team to make history, but on 20 October 1968 that is exactly what happened — twice over. Israel's footballers, unfancied outsiders at the Mexico City Olympics, had fought their way into the quarter-finals. They would leave the Estadio León, known locally as the Nou Camp, having lost nothing on the pitch and everything to a drawing of lots.

Israel had arrived in León in form. Under coach Emmanuel Scheffer, the team opened Group C by beating Ghana 5-3, with Yehoshua Feigenbaum scoring a hat-trick and Giora Spiegel adding two, then defeated El Salvador 3-1 through goals from Rachamim Talbi, Mordechai Spiegler and Shraga Bar. A 0-2 defeat to Hungary in Guadalajara could not stop Israel finishing second in the group, enough to reach the knockout stage against Bulgaria.

The quarter-final was tight from the first whistle. Bulgaria's Georgi Hristakiev, a defender by trade, put the Eastern Europeans ahead after just five minutes, and for long stretches it looked as though that single goal would be enough. Israel pressed and probed without reward until the 89th minute, when Feigenbaum forced the ball past the Bulgarian goalkeeper to level the score and send the match into extra time.

Thirty more minutes changed nothing. Both defences held, and 1-1 the game stayed. In 1968, world football had no mechanism for a penalty shoot-out — FIFA and the International Olympic Committee still settled deadlocked knockout ties the way they had for decades: by chance. So the referee called the two captains together at the centre circle.

What happened next has become one of the most retold scenes in Israeli sporting history. Slips of paper, one marked with a winning mark and one blank, were placed inside a large sombrero. Israel's captain, Mordechai Spiegler, reached in first and drew the loser. Bulgaria's captain drew the other. On the toss of a coin dressed up as a football tradition, Bulgaria went through to the semi-finals and Israel's Olympic tournament was over.

Bulgaria made the most of their reprieve, advancing to the final before losing to Hungary and taking home the silver medal — a result built, in part, on a piece of paper pulled from a hat in León. For Israel's players, there was nothing to appeal and no replay to demand. The rules of the day made no distinction between misfortune and defeat.

The injustice of it did not sit well back home. Yosef Dagan, secretary-general of the Israel Football Association, and Micha Almog, chairman of the association's technical committee, could not accept that a team's fate should turn on a blind draw rather than the players' feet. In 1969 the pair wrote to FIFA president Sir Stanley Rous, describing the drawing of lots as a cruel and unjust way to decide a match, and proposing an alternative: a shoot-out of five penalty kicks per side, continuing in sudden-death fashion if the teams still could not be separated.

FIFA's International Football Association Board took up the idea, and in 1970 the penalty shoot-out was formally written into the laws of the game. Its first competitive use came that August, in a League Cup tie between Manchester United and Hull City. Dagan received no official credit from FIFA for the innovation, but in Israel his role in the shoot-out's invention has never been in doubt.

There was one more twist. Two years after their sombrero heartbreak, several of that same Olympic side — Mordechai Spiegler and Giora Spiegel chief among them — were back in Mexico wearing Israel's colours, this time at the 1970 World Cup, the only one Israel has ever reached. The team that had been undone by a lottery in León had, almost by accident, changed football's laws for everyone who came after them.

Every shoot-out played since — in World Cups, European finals, and school-yard tournaments — traces a line back to that afternoon in the Nou Camp, when an Israeli captain pulled a losing slip from a Mexican sombrero and two footballing officials decided that fate deserved a fairer contest.
facts: Israel finished second in Olympic Group C in October 1968, beating Ghana 5-3 and El Salvador 3-1 before losing 0-2 to Hungary, to reach the quarter-finals.

The quarter-final against Bulgaria in León on 20 October 1968 finished 1-1: Georgi Hristakiev's 5th-minute goal for Bulgaria was cancelled out by Yehoshua Feigenbaum's 89th-minute equalizer, and the score held through extra time.

With no penalty-shootout rule yet in world football, the tie was decided by a drawing of lots: captains Mordechai Spiegler of Israel and Bulgaria's captain each drew a slip from a hat, and Israel's was the losing one.
Bulgaria advanced to the final, lost to Hungary, and won the Olympic silver medal.

Israel Football Association secretary-general Yosef Dagan, with technical-committee chairman Micha Almog, wrote to FIFA president Sir Stanley Rous in 1969, calling the lots method cruel and proposing a penalty shoot-out format.
The International Football Association Board adopted the penalty shoot-out in 1970; it was first used competitively in a Manchester United v Hull City League Cup tie that August.
Mordechai Spiegler and Giora Spiegel, both starters in the 1968 Olympic quarter-final, went on to represent Israel at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 2-1 as women's derby returns after 24 years
dek: Rubimo Tracy Elizabeth Mozrera and Diana Borges struck as the Athena Cup opened in Yavne, while Hapoel Katamon Yam thrashed Maccabi Kesharonot Hadera 3-0 elsewhere in round one.

verificationSources.label: BE106 Yavne (derby preview, confirms date/venue/24-year gap)

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's reborn women's team beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 2-1 in Yavne on Thursday night, winning the first Tel Aviv women's derby played in 24 years as the Athena Cup opened the 2026-27 season.

The match was hosted by Hapoel Tel Aviv at the city's Jackie Levy Stadium with free admission, a fixture both clubs had billed for weeks as a historic occasion — the derby had not featured on an Israeli women's football calendar since the two sides' senior teams last shared a top flight in the early 2000s.

According to ONE, Maccabi — who now compete as Maccabi ASA Tel Aviv following last year's merger with the ASA Tel Aviv women's club — broke the deadlock through Rubimo Tracy Elizabeth Mozrera in the 52nd minute.

Hapoel hit back four minutes later, with Maria Almatzeri levelling in the 56th to set up a tense finish. But Maccabi struck again through Diana Borges in the 84th minute to seal the derby win and open their Athena Cup campaign with three points.

The victory gives Maccabi ASA Tel Aviv a symbolic start to the post-merger era, coming as the club rebuilds a women's section more than two decades after Maccabi Tel Aviv's original team folded in 2002.
Elsewhere in round one, Hapoel Katamon Yam were the day's biggest winners, thrashing Maccabi Kesharonot Hadera 3-0 through Samdar Cohen and a brace from Zhaylee de Silva Gomes, ONE reported.
Maccabi Holon also opened with a big win, beating Bnot Netanya 4-0, while Hapoel Ra'anana edged Kiryat Gat 2-1 in the day's other fixture — a first round that produced 14 goals across four matches.
The Athena Cup, which opens the domestic women's football calendar each season, continues with round two on Tuesday.

title: Karem Ashkenazi returns to Hapoel Galil Elyon on long-term deal
dek: The 18-year-old guard, capped by Israel's youth team at last summer's European Championship, rejoins the Upper Galilee club after a season with Maccabi Tel Aviv's academy.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — Hapoel Galil Elyon team page

body: Karem Ashkenazi is going home. The 18-year-old guard, who played for Israel's youth national team at last summer's European Championship, has returned to Hapoel Galil Elyon on a long-term contract, ONE reported, closing the loop on a journey that briefly took him away from the club that first spotted him as a young teenager in the Upper Galilee.

Ashkenazi, from Kibbutz Beit Hillel, originally signed with Galil Elyon back in 2023, agreeing to a long-term deal with the club at just 15. He grew up through the Galilee outfit's youth pathway before the war forced a disruption to that plan.

With his family relocating to central Israel during the fighting, Ashkenazi spent last season with Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth academy instead, a stint in which he posted averages of 8.1 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game, according to ONE.

For a small-town club competing against Israel's wealthier basketball powers, keeping faith with players raised through its own system, even through wartime upheaval, is as much a statement of identity as it is a basketball decision.

title: Trabzonspor 0-1 Ferencváros: Kanikovsky handed late cameo in Europa League play-off win
dek: The Israeli international came off the bench for a 29-minute run-out as Ferencváros held firm for an away win over Trabzonspor in the first leg of their Europa League play-off tie.
body: On a warm night at Papara Park, Gabi Kanikovsky was handed 29 minutes of Europa League football off the bench as Ferencváros held on for a 1-0 win away to Trabzonspor in the first leg of their play-off tie, ONE reports.

The contest turned on a single moment early on. Kristoffer Zachariassen rose to meet an Olivér Nagy cross and headed past the Trabzonspor goalkeeper in the 17th minute, a lead the Hungarian champions would not relinquish.

Ferencváros controlled the opening exchanges in Trabzon before their hosts, who fielded Mohamed Salah in search of an equalizer, grew into the game after the break and laid siege to the away goal without finding a way through.

Kanikovsky, capped 16 times by Israel, was introduced in the 61st minute and asked to help see out the lead, working hard defensively as Trabzonspor pushed men forward, according to ONE's account of the match.

His evening ended with a yellow card deep into stoppage time, in the same passage of play that saw a Trabzonspor player sent off in the 96th minute, reducing the hosts to ten men in the closing seconds.

The result leaves Ferencváros firmly in control of the tie heading into the second leg, scheduled for August 27 at the Groupama Aréna in Budapest, with the winner advancing to the Europa League's league phase.

Kanikovsky, a product of Maccabi Tel Aviv's academy born in Ra'anana, came through loan spells at Hapoel Petah Tikva and Hapoel Acre before establishing himself at Maccabi Netanya and, later, back at Maccabi Tel Aviv, where he made 188 appearances and won the Israeli title under Robbie Keane.
He has since moved to Ferencváros and already has a major trophy with the club: the Magyar Kupa, won in May with a 1-0 final victory over Zalaegerszegi at the Puskás Aréna.
For now, though, his role in Trabzon was a supporting one — a late cameo in a result that leaves Ferencváros one game away from the group-stage prize they are chasing again this season.

title: Kattash on Blatt's exit: "We really wanted Tamir, no decision was made to part ways"
dek: Maccabi Tel Aviv opened preseason training with coach Oded Kattash addressing Tamir Blatt's summer move to rival Hapoel Tel Aviv, while a squad missing seven regulars slowly takes shape ahead of the 2026/27 season.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv opened preseason training for the 2026/27 season on Thursday at the Hadar Yosef sports center, and much of head coach Oded Kattash's first session with reporters was spent on a player who is no longer in the building: Tamir Blatt.
"There was no such decision, it's not the time to get into this right now," Kattash said, addressing the point guard's departure to city rival Hapoel Tel Aviv this summer. "We really wanted Tamir."

The coach pushed back on any suggestion that Maccabi had actively chosen to move on from Blatt. "Things simply didn't work out — it's not accurate that there was a decision," he said, without elaborating further on why the two sides ultimately failed to agree new terms.

Blatt spent three seasons in yellow and blue, winning two championships and two State Cups and establishing himself as one of the EuroLeague's most productive playmakers before leaving as a free agent this summer. Maccabi's own farewell statement at the time thanked him for his "significant part" in the club's recent success.

His move took him back to Hapoel Tel Aviv, the club where he began his career, on a three-year contract. The reunion has not gone smoothly: Blatt was recently left out of Hapoel's own preseason training camp, with Eurohoops reporting he has fallen outside head coach Dimitris Itoudis's plans and that the club is exploring options to move him on to another European team despite the fresh deal.
Kattash, for his part, is dealing with a squad that is far from complete a month before the new campaign. Seven regular contributors were absent from Thursday's opening session.

Guards Yam Madar and Roman Sorkin are away on international duty with Israel's national team, while three of the club's summer signings — center Daniel Theis, guard Gabriel Lundberg and forward Jaylen Hoard — have yet to arrive in the country.

Already in camp are the new arrivals who have made the trip: forward Bonzie Colson Jr., guard Jimmy Clark III and center Armando Bacot, who joined this summer on a two-year deal after a season with Fenerbahce.

With last season's European campaign ending in disappointment, Kattash is trying to build cohesion around a roster still being assembled piece by piece — even as questions about the club's most prominent departure continue to follow him into camp.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv risk fresh UEFA punishment after flares at Atalanta
dek: Fans lit pyrotechnics during the Conference League play-off qualifier in Bergamo, risking the activation of a suspended ban only weeks after a €40,000 fine for a similar incident against Ludogorets, Sport5 reports.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - UEFA penalties for Hapoel Tel Aviv and Beitar Jerusalem in Europe

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv's fans lit flares again on Thursday night, this time inside the away end at Atalanta's stadium in Bergamo during the club's Conference League play-off round qualifier, and the club is now waiting to see whether UEFA activates a suspended punishment that has been hanging over it since the summer, Sport5 reports.

The pyrotechnics reignited exactly the kind of trouble that got Hapoel into hot water with European football's governing body only weeks earlier, and the outlet frames the coming days as a genuine test of whether the club's fans have learned anything from the last warning.

UEFA's disciplinary committee had already fined Hapoel Tel Aviv €40,000 and handed down a conditional ban on selling tickets to travelling supporters for one away European match, suspended for two years, after flares were set off during the second qualifying round tie against Ludogorets Razgrad. The club was separately punished for damage its fans caused to that away stadium.

Because that ban is conditional rather than closed, Sport5 reports that a new finding of guilt over pyrotechnics could see it activated immediately - on top of whatever fresh penalty UEFA's disciplinary body settles on once it reviews the match delegate's report from Bergamo.

Hapoel is not the only Israeli club drawing UEFA's attention to fan behaviour this campaign. Beitar Jerusalem were fined €25,000 and given a suspended one-match stadium closure after flares were lit by their own supporters during a Conference League qualifier against AEK Larnaca, Sport5 has separately reported.

No ruling on Thursday's incident had been announced at the time of writing. UEFA's process typically runs on the match delegate's report, meaning any decision - and confirmation of whether the suspended sentence is triggered - is likely to take days rather than hours.
For now, Hapoel Tel Aviv is left hoping that a night of smoke in the away end at Atalanta does not end up costing its own supporters their access to a future European away leg.

body: Emmanuel Boateng's night in Bergamo turned sour in the eyes of Hapoel Tel Aviv's travelling support on Thursday, after the Ghanaian striker spurned a clear-cut chance during the club's Conference League play-off first leg against Atalanta — a miss glaring enough to light up Israeli football's corner of social media while the game was still being played.

Sport5's live coverage collected a string of frustrated reactions from fans watching at home. One supporter wrote that Boateng's miss was "the kind that won't let you sleep at night," while another was blunter still, branding the striker a "פראייר" — a fool — for the way he wasted the opening. A third fan focused on the buildup, praising the quality of the pass that created the chance even as they lamented how it was finished.

Boateng, 30, is in his second spell at Hapoel Tel Aviv. He rejoined the club in February 2026 on an 18-month deal after leaving Turkish side Gaziantep, wearing the number 9 shirt. He first played for Hapoel between 2018 and 2021, and has also had stints in Portugal, Spain and China since leaving Israel.

The play-off tie against Atalanta is the biggest test yet of Hapoel Tel Aviv's European run this summer. The club reached this stage after beating Ludogorets Razgrad and then advancing past GKS Katowice of Poland despite losing the second leg of that round 2-1, going through on the aggregate score across both matches.
The first leg is being played at Atalanta's stadium in Bergamo, with the return fixture set for August 27 — hosted, per Israeli reports, at a neutral venue in Hungary rather than in Israel.

title: Erez Isakov unveils new kit for his Maccabi HaSharon Netanya project
dek: The Big Brother runner-up turned club owner had Sport5 exclusively reveal jerseys branded "The Iskovs" as he met his new players and coach Shlomi Dahan for the first time, with promotion from League C the declared target.
body: Erez Isakov, the runner-up of Big Brother Israel who turned to the lower rungs of Israeli football as his next project, gave Sport5 an exclusive first look on Wednesday at the new kit for his club, Maccabi HaSharon Netanya — shirts stitched with the family name "The Iskovs."

The reveal doubled as Isakov's first sit-down with his coaching staff and squad at the club's Netanya training base, weeks after he completed a takeover of the League C (Liga Gimel) outfit that is being filmed for a docu-reality series about his family.

Ice.co.il reported the deal was struck at roughly NIS 1 million, split 50-50 with the club's previous owners, brothers Ilan and Shimon Atia, who are staying on as full partners and continuing to run day-to-day operations rather than stepping away.

Isakov himself is not just writing the cheques. Sport5 reported he has already passed a medical and intends to register as an owner-player, lacing up for a club he once supported from the terraces before hanging up his own boots at lower-league level.

"We didn't come here to waste time," Isakov said at the meeting, according to Sport5. "We have a top-tier coach and carefully selected good players with one declared goal — to finish first and go up to League B."

That coach is Shlomi Dahan, 46, a lifelong figure in Maccabi Netanya's youth setup who told Israel Hayom he has previously turned down offers from senior-league clubs to stay in Netanya, and who is Shabbat-observant. Isakov's camp has framed his hiring as proof the project is being built on football substance, not just celebrity.

Recruitment is already under way beyond the coaching staff. Reports around the takeover indicated Isakov has been trying to lure Lior Barkovitch — his old teammate from the reality show "Golsstar" — back from retirement to bolster the squad.

For a club that has spent recent seasons in the regional lower divisions after slipping down from Liga Bet, the ambition being talked about — a title push and promotion to League B this season — is a significant jump. Whether the new jerseys prove to be the start of that rise or just the most photogenic part of it will only be answered on the pitch.

title: Ironman Leeds scraps swim leg over toxic algae, leaving athletes furious
dek: Organisers turned the race into a bike-run duathlon after blue-green algae in Waterloo Lake was found well above safe levels, with many competitors saying they learned of the change from social media before getting an official email.
body: The second edition of Ironman Leeds was supposed to open with a 3.8-kilometre swim in Waterloo Lake. Instead, competitors on Sunday found themselves lining up for a duathlon, after organisers scrapped the swim entirely because of a bloom of toxic blue-green algae in the water.

Test results from Waterloo Lake, in Roundhay Park, showed algae concentrations well above the threshold considered safe for the swim to go ahead, organisers said. The decision was taken in conjunction with Leeds City Council and on the advice of the UK Health Security Agency's Environmental Hazards Team, following a spell of hot weather across the UK that triggered the bloom.

Blue-green algae, which thrives in warm, still water, can produce toxins harmful to humans and animals on contact or if swallowed, and lakes affected by it are routinely closed to bathers and open-water swimmers as a precaution.

With the swim leg pulled, the roughly 2,500 entrants who had trained for the full-distance triathlon instead raced a 180-kilometre (112-mile) bike leg followed by a 42.2-kilometre (26.2-mile) marathon, with a rolling time-trial start from transition at 7am.

The change did not go down well. Many athletes said they only found out the swim had been axed through social media posts, before any official notification arrived from the organisers by email — a sequencing that fuelled much of the anger described by British outlets covering the race.

Some competitors also pushed organisers for partial refunds, arguing that paying full price for what was billed as a three-discipline event and then racing only two of them left them out of pocket, though no refund policy has been reported.

Ironman events have been forced into similar last-minute changes before over water-quality scares, and Sunday's call in Leeds underlines how increasingly hot summers are becoming a recurring headache for open-water swimming in triathlon and endurance racing across Britain and Europe.

title: Manchester United rule out any Bruno Fernandes sale this summer
dek: Old Trafford has turned back interest from Galatasaray and Al-Hilal, with the captain's release clause for foreign buyers now expired, ONE reports, citing the BBC.
body: Manchester United have decided the matter before it could even become a saga: Bruno Fernandes is not for sale this summer, whatever lands on the table. ONE reports, citing the BBC, that United will turn down any offer received for their captain.

It is a rare piece of clarity from a club that has spent recent windows agonising over its biggest calls. This one, according to the report, was never really in doubt internally — even as speculation swirled around Fernandes for weeks.

Turkish giants Galatasaray and Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal both made contact over a possible deal, ONE says, but the inquiries went nowhere once it became clear United would not engage and that Fernandes himself had little appetite to leave Old Trafford.

Sky Sports has separately reported that Galatasaray explored a bid worth up to €50 million, only for United sources to insist the 31-year-old midfielder is 'not for sale at any price.' The Portuguese star is said to prefer staying in England and competing at the highest level.

Fernandes's contract situation adds intrigue even amid the certainty over his short-term future. He has one year left on his current deal, with United holding an option for a further season — and, according to ONE, a release clause of £57 million written in for approaches from abroad. Sky Sports reports that clause has since lapsed for this window, leaving United in an even stronger negotiating position should suitors return.

No extension has yet been signed, and that gap has fuelled uncertainty despite the club's public and private commitment to keeping him. ONE notes Fernandes was left stung last year by suggestions he might be pushed toward a lucrative Al-Hilal move rather than handed guarantees over his Old Trafford future.

Management, ONE adds, is acutely aware of how supporters would react to any hint that the club was willing to cash in on its talisman — a factor that has hardened the resolve to keep him regardless of the numbers on offer.

The context makes United's stance easy to understand. Fernandes was named the Premier League's Player of the Season last term after setting a competition assist record, and he heads into his eighth year at the club as captain and, by most measures, its most important player.

For now, the message from Old Trafford is unambiguous: bids are welcome to arrive, but none will be entertained. Whether that translates into a fresh contract before the season gathers pace remains the one loose thread still to be tied up.

title: Atzili and Ansah handed starts as Beitar Jerusalem's attack faces Ramat Gan in Toto Cup playoff
dek: Maxim Falkushchenko starts in midfield for Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim as the sides meet on Monday evening for 7th-8th place in the competition, ONE reports.
body: Beitar Jerusalem go into Monday evening's Toto Cup placement game with their most talked-about attacking pair paired together from kick-off: ONE reports that Omer Atzili and summer signing Eugene Ansah both start as Beitar's front line against Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim, with the sides meeting for 7th-8th place in the competition.

It is not a title Beitar or Ramat Gan will get excited about in itself — the placement games simply sort the Toto Cup group-stage finishers before the Premier League proper kicks off on August 22 — but for Beitar's supporters, the headline is the attacking pairing rather than the position on offer.

Atzili, back at the club where he first made his name between 2013 and 2016, has been the team's talisman of sorts this year: reporting on Beitar's season earlier this year, Israeli media noted the side's results have swung sharply depending on his availability, with the club performing far better when he plays than when he is missing through injury.

Alongside him is Ansah, the Ghanaian forward who joined from Ashdod this summer on a two-year deal. Ynet reported at the time of the signing that Ansah, who can play across the front line as a striker or from either flank, was initially being registered as a foreign player while his Israeli citizenship process moves forward, and is on a reported salary in the region of €250,000 a season.

On the other side, Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim hand a start to Maxim "Max" Falkushchenko, the Ukrainian-born Israeli midfielder who came through Hapoel Haifa's academy before making his senior debut there in 2015. Falkushchenko has been in sharp pre-season form for his current club, having scored twice in a recent friendly win over Bačka Topola.

ONE's report lists the rest of both starting XIs, with Yehonatan Ozer in goal for Beitar behind a back line built around Roy Alimlich and Lial Darai, and Amit Raaif starting in goal for the home side.
Kick-off was set for 20:00 Israel time on Monday, with both clubs using the fixture as a final competitive run-out before the league season begins later this month.

title: Cagliari forward Yael Trepy in intensive care after near-drowning in Sardinia pool
dek: The 20-year-old French striker, who made his Serie A debut for Cagliari in January, was airlifted to hospital in Sassari after losing consciousness in a private pool on his day off.
body: Cagliari have confirmed that one of their young forwards, French striker Yael Trepy, is in intensive care in Sardinia after nearly drowning in a private swimming pool on Sunday afternoon, plunging the Serie A club into an anxious wait just two days after his side's Coppa Italia win.

The 20-year-old was on his day off at a villa in the Costa Smeralda area of northern Sardinia when he got into difficulty in the pool. According to Italian reports, Trepy cannot swim well and had entered the deep end before losing consciousness.
Bystanders pulled him from the water and called emergency services, who airlifted him by helicopter to the Santissima Annunziata Hospital in Sassari for urgent treatment.

ONE, citing the initial examinations, reported that no immediately life-threatening conditions had been identified and that his situation had "gradually stabilised" under close monitoring. Italian outlets covering the story through Sunday into Monday painted a more serious picture: Trepy was intubated on arrival due to respiratory distress, and Tuttosport and Calcio e Finanza both reported that scans found significant fluid in his lungs, complicating oxygen exchange, with doctors placing him in an induced coma to allow treatment to continue. The full picture of his condition is still emerging and may keep evolving over the coming days.
Cagliari have confirmed the hospitalisation through official channels, Il Post reported, but the club has not yet issued a detailed prognosis or a timeline for an update.

Trepy had been on the pitch just 48 hours earlier, starting for Cagliari in Friday's 1-0 Coppa Italia victory over Arezzo in the round of 32 — part of the reward for a breakthrough campaign in Sardinia.

Born in Villeneuve-Saint-Georges in 2006, Trepy joined Cagliari's academy in 2022 after being scouted from French side US Créteil-Lusitanos, signed his first professional contract in August 2024, and helped the club's Primavera side win the 2025 Coppa Italia Primavera, scoring in the final win over AC Milan. He made his senior Serie A debut this January, coming on in a 2-2 draw at Cremonese and scoring in the match.

The news has cast a shadow over Cagliari's pre-season build-up, with supporters and figures in Italian football sending messages of support for the teenager as the club and his family await further word from the hospital in Sassari.

title: Syrian and Lebanese opponents refuse to fight Israeli boys at MMA youth world championships
dek: Harel Levi, 11, and Ben Bitan, 12, advance to the semifinals by walkover in Abu Dhabi after rivals from countries that do not recognise Israel declined to face them on the opening day of the world championships.

verificationSources.label: Abu Dhabi Media Office - IMMAF Youth World Championships opening
BE106 Yavne - Harel Levi qualifies for Abu Dhabi world championship

body: Two young Israeli fighters found out on the opening morning of the world championships that politics can decide a bout before either boxer throws a strike. At the IMMAF Youth World Championships in Abu Dhabi, opponents from Syria and Lebanon simply refused to face them, ONE reported on Monday.

The 2026 IMMAF Youth World Championships opened Monday and run through August 23, drawing what ONE described as more than 1,000 competitors from some 130 countries, one of the biggest fixtures on the amateur MMA calendar. Israel travelled with a delegation of roughly 40 athletes aged 10 to 17, according to the report. Independent coverage of the tournament confirms it opened this week at Abu Dhabi's Mubadala Arena under the patronage of the emirate's leadership.

Harel Levi, 11, was drawn against a Syrian rival on the first day of competition. The opponent never showed up for the bout, and Levi was awarded a technical victory that sent him straight through to the semifinals, guaranteeing him at least a bronze medal, ONE reported.
In a separate bout, 12-year-old Ben Bitan was set to face a Lebanese competitor who also declined to step onto the mat. Bitan, too, was handed a technical win by walkover, per the report.

Neither Syria nor Lebanon maintains diplomatic relations with Israel, and both were among the opponents cited by ONE as unwilling to send their young athletes into competition against Israelis at the children's and youth event.

"The fact that athletes from countries that do not recognise the State of Israel won't compete against Israeli athletes is very unfortunate," Ido Preineta, president of Israel's MMA Federation and Levi's personal coach, said, according to ONE. He added that the delegation would "continue fighting and proudly raising Israel's flag."

Erik Kaplan, president and CEO of the Eilat federation for non-Olympic sports, was blunter in his criticism. "It is grave and regrettable to see that even at these young ages, there are those who choose to boycott Israeli athletes," Kaplan said, calling on international sports bodies to enforce real consequences on federations that refuse to compete.

The withdrawals came on just the first day of a week-long championship, with the rest of Israel's roughly 40-strong youth team still due to fight through to Sunday. Both Levi and Bitan will now continue toward the medal rounds having already banked results without landing a strike.

Ido Preineta, president of Israel's MMA Federation and Levi's coach, criticised the boycott and vowed the delegation would keep competing, per ONE.

title: Sharani Zuberu says he feels 'blessed' after sealing move to Hapoel Jerusalem
dek: The Ghanaian-Togolese defender arrives on a free transfer after four straight Slovak titles with Slovan Bratislava and Champions League nights against Manchester City and Bayern Munich.
body: Hapoel Jerusalem's newest signing says the welcome he received at Teddy Stadium has already told him he made the right call. "I feel blessed to be here. The reception from teammates, coaches and staff was amazing," Sharani Zuberu told ONE this week, days after putting pen to paper with the Ligat ha'Al club.

The 26-year-old Ghanaian-Togolese defender joined Hapoel Jerusalem on a free transfer on August 13, arriving with an unusually decorated resume for an Israeli top-flight newcomer: four consecutive Slovak championships won with Slovan Bratislava.

Zuberu's route to Jerusalem began far from Central Europe. Born in Accra, he started his career at Dreams FC in Ghana before Sparta Prague brought him to their academy in 2018. "I arrived from Ghana to Sparta Prague youth in 2018. I scored a brace in a derby against Slavia," he recalled, pointing to one of the early highlights of his development in Czech football.

After struggling to break into Sparta's first team, he moved on to Dunajská Streda in 2019 before signing for Slovan Bratislava in February 2023 — the move that turned his career around. Over four seasons in Bratislava he made 93 appearances, scoring six goals and adding two assists, while collecting a league title in every one of those campaigns.

He describes himself as a versatile operator rather than a specialist. Deployed mostly at left-back but also used on both flanks and even up front by Slovan, he said: "I am good with the ball, in 1v1, and using available space."

Slovan's dominance at home came with continental exposure that few Israeli-league arrivals can match. Zuberu played through the club's Champions League league-phase campaign, facing Manchester City and a Bayern Munich side built around Harry Kane. "My first Champions League match with Bratislava against Manchester City, I'll always remember it," he said, adding of the Bayern and Atlético Madrid fixtures: "They were amazing in terms of competition quality."

That is the experience Hapoel Jerusalem hope to fold into a Ligat ha'Al squad they are rebuilding around this season. The club shares Teddy Stadium with city rivals Beitar Jerusalem and will be looking to Zuberu's European pedigree to add steel on the flank.

For his part, the defender was clear about what drew him to Israel. "To fulfill myself here, show my best abilities. Compete with the top Israeli teams," he said of his ambitions for the new chapter, with Hapoel Jerusalem preparing to open their 2026/27 Ligat ha'Al campaign later this month.

title: Fixture list released for Israel's National Youth League season
dek: The Israel Football Association has published the 2026/27 schedule for the National Youth League's northern and southern divisions, with the campaign kicking off on September 8.
body: The Israel Football Association has released the full fixture lists for the 2026/27 National Youth League season, ONE reports, giving clubs across the country's northern and southern divisions their first look at a campaign that runs deep into next spring.

The league caters to players born in 2008 and 2009, with dispensation for some 2007-born players still eligible in the category, and is split geographically into a 15-team northern division and a 14-team southern division.
According to ONE, the season opens on September 8, 2026, with the second round of fixtures beginning on February 13, 2027, and the campaign scheduled to run through to May 22, 2027.
In the north, the opening round pairs Kiryat Yam with Hapoel Nahal Galil, while Nir Ironi host Hapoel Kiryat Carmel — fixtures ONE singled out among the round's headline meetings.
The southern division's first round sends Beitar Nordia Jerusalem to Samson Tel Aviv, while Hapoel Ramat Gan travel across the city to face Gadna Tel Aviv.

Gadna Tel Aviv, founded in 1947 to give young players in the south of the city a sporting outlet, is among the oldest dedicated youth academies in Israeli football and counts former Turkey and Israel international Haim Revivo among its most famous graduates.

For the dozens of clubs involved, the published schedule marks the practical start of preparations for a nine-month season that will decide who progresses through Israel's youth football pyramid before the next generation of prospects moves up to senior football.

title: Fantasy football manager unveils new rules for the Ligat HaAl season: goalkeepers rewarded, AI sets prices
dek: Ahead of Saturday's kickoff, the man behind Israel's biggest football fantasy game explains save-based goalkeeper points, an algorithm-driven pricing system and a squad-building tweak.

verificationSources.label: ONE: המהפכה והחוקים החדשים - מנהל הפנטזי על המשחק
ONE: חיכיתם לזה - פנטזי ליגת העל של ONE חוזרת בגדול

body: With the new Ligat HaAl season kicking off this Saturday, ONE has rebuilt significant parts of its popular fantasy football game — and the man who runs it, Amir Yaniv, laid out what has changed in an interview for the outlet's "Conversation of the Day" slot.

The headline change concerns goalkeepers, who Yaniv says have long been short-changed by fantasy scoring systems. Under the new rules, every save a goalkeeper makes earns his fantasy manager a point, while conceding a single goal in a match carries no penalty at all — only the second goal and beyond cost a point each.

Player pricing is also being handled differently this year. Rather than have staff set values by feel, Yaniv said an AI algorithm now calculates what each player should cost, aiming for a more accurate reflection of real form and output across the list.

Managers have also been given more freedom to build lopsided squads: the game now allows up to three players from the same club, up from two previously, opening the door to stacking a team that is expected to be particularly strong this season.

Each manager works with a total budget of 125 million (in-game currency) to fill out a squad. At the top of the price list sits Beitar Jerusalem's Omer Atzili, the single most expensive player in the game.

At Maccabi Haifa, the priciest name is striker Guy Melamed at 11 million, with Brazilian midfielder Bruninho close behind at 10 million — pricing that reflects the club's expected firepower heading into the new campaign.

Ligat HaAl's 14 clubs open the season this weekend, and the fantasy game is free to play through ONE's app or website, with managers signing in via a Google or Apple account. The platform also runs a parallel fantasy competition tied to Spain's La Liga.

As in previous seasons, ONE is dangling incentives to keep managers engaged through the year: weekly prizes throughout the campaign and a grand prize of an overseas trip for two for whoever tops the standings.

For a game that lives or dies on whether its scoring feels fair, the goalkeeper change in particular addresses a long-standing manager gripe — that shot-stoppers were fantasy football's most undervalued asset relative to the games they can single-handedly swing.

title: Beitar Jerusalem brands Maccabi Haifa's Ovadia a "small CEO" in awards row
dek: The Jerusalem club hit back at Maccabi Haifa's complaints over losing the President's Award for Sport, accusing chief executive Itzik Ovadia of sending "harsh and unusual messages" instead of accepting the result.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Andy Ram confirms vote details

body: Beitar Jerusalem has hit back hard at Maccabi Haifa's public grumbling over Israel's President's Award for Sport, taking a direct shot at Haifa chief executive Itzik Ovadia in a statement carried by ONE: "We are surprised that such a large club has such a small CEO."

The jab capped a bitter week in Israeli football's boardrooms. Beitar was named winner of the President's Award for the first time, recognising clubs' community and social-impact work - only for Maccabi Haifa, which had led the field for much of the judging process, to cry foul once the result went the other way.

According to ONE's reporting on the committee's deliberations, Haifa was ahead by less than a single point after the first round of scoring, which counted for 60% of the total and rewarded clubs' social projects. A second round of discussion shifted the balance, and the panel ultimately backed Beitar by a margin ONE put at 90-95%.

Panel chairman Andy Ram, the former Israeli tennis player, made no secret of steering the conversation toward Beitar. "I knew Beitar is authentic, so I thought we should choose Beitar," he told the committee, according to ONE, insisting the outcome was not a consolation prize but a reflection of the club's community work over the past year.

Behind the scenes, the process grew tense enough that Bat El Garbi, who heads the "Values in Sport" initiative that runs the award, urged committee members to keep the deliberations discreet - after what ONE described as a difficult phone call with Ovadia.

Maccabi Haifa's grievance went beyond the scoring itself. The club argued the committee applied inconsistent standards, saying it had previously been marked down over forward Omer Atzili's involvement in one of its projects, only for the panel to raise no objection when Atzili and Dor Micha featured in Beitar's submission.

It was against that backdrop that Beitar's statement accused Ovadia of sending "harsh and unusual messages" to committee members rather than accepting the decision gracefully - the context for the barbed "small CEO" line aimed squarely at Haifa's boardroom.

The award ceremony also handed out lifetime-achievement honours to Maccabi Haifa president Yaakov Shahar and Hapoel Beer Sheva owner Alona Barkat. What was billed as a celebration of Israeli sport's social work instead spilled into a public feud between two of the country's biggest clubs - one run by Shahar, the other owned by Barak Abramov.

title: Kaufman: Gorbenko's run of injuries and illness explains medal-less Europeans
dek: Israel's national swimming coach says a rocky first year of US college swimming, compounded by injuries and illness, cost the defending European 200m medley champion a podium finish in Paris.

verificationSources.label: ONE - המאמן חשף: "לגורבנקו היה רצף פציעות ומחלות"
SwimSwam - 2026 European Championships: Day 5 Finals Live Recap
Ynetnews - Tomer Shuster advances to semifinals at European Swimming Championships
Ynet - לאוניד קאופמן חוזר לאמן את נבחרת ישראל בשחייה

body: Israel's national swimming coach Leonid Kaufman has offered an explanation for one of the more surprising storylines of the European Aquatics Championships in Paris: how Anastasia Gorbenko, the reigning continental champion over 200 metres medley, left the pool without a single medal. Speaking to ONE, Kaufman said the 23-year-old had been battling "a sequence of unplanned injuries and illnesses" through her buildup to the meet.

"It's like the first pancake," Kaufman told ONE, reaching for the well-worn saying about a batch of pancakes rarely coming out right on the first attempt. "It never comes out right in the pan — only the second, third and so on." He tied Gorbenko's setbacks directly to her adjustment to a new life, training load and academic schedule in her first year of US college swimming.

Gorbenko went into the championships as top seed and defending European champion in the 200m individual medley, but finished the final in 2:11.87 — off the pace behind winner Ellen Walshe of Ireland — and left the event without a medal. She fared little better in the 400m medley, an event she has also won continentally in the past, placing seventh in 4:45.07.

It marked an unusually barren championships for a swimmer widely regarded as Israel's greatest, an Olympic finalist at both Tokyo and Paris and the holder of multiple world and European titles. Gorbenko began racing for the University of Louisville this year, her first season inside the US collegiate system, a transition Kaufman pointed to as the root of her physical troubles.

No Israeli swimmer reached the podium at the Paris championships, held August 10-16 at the Paris Aquatics Centre, though several advanced through to semifinals and finals across the week, according to ONE.

One bright spot was Tomer Shuster, who Kaufman singled out for a marked step forward. Shuster clocked an Israeli record of 24.36 seconds in the 50m backstroke, good for fourth place, shaving three-tenths off the national mark that had stood since 2016.

Kaufman argued the disappointment should be read in context rather than as a red flag. He said he expects Gorbenko to bounce back next season, and that the grounding she is getting in the American collegiate system will ultimately serve her well as Israeli swimming builds toward the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Kaufman is not a new face on the Israeli pool deck. He returned to the national team job this year having previously led the program between 1994 and 2016, a stint that included work as part of Israel's coaching staff across five Olympic Games.

Despite the medal drought in Paris, Kaufman said he remains "cautiously optimistic" about where Israeli swimming is heading, pointing to the emerging depth behind Gorbenko as evidence the program is not solely reliant on its biggest name.

title: Football association seeks immediate suspension of Omer Dahan over betting scandal
dek: The Israel Football Association has filed an urgent petition with the disciplinary court to sideline the Maccabi Haifa forward until his criminal case concludes, alleging evidence that he routinely bet on matches involving his own team.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Football association demands immediate suspension of Omer Dahan

body: The Israel Football Association has taken its response to the country's illegal betting scandal a significant step further, filing an urgent petition with the game's disciplinary court demanding the immediate suspension of Maccabi Haifa forward Omer Dahan from all football activity, ONE reported.

Dahan, who spent last season on loan at Hapoel Ra'anana, was one of several people detained on June 14 as police gambling unit Lahav 433 moved against an alleged illegal betting and match-fixing network linked to a gang from Migdal HaEmek. Investigators are examining suspected large-scale illegal gambling, match-fixing, money-laundering and tax offences.

The striker later confirmed publicly that he was the footballer at the centre of the case, after a court-ordered publication ban on his name was lifted. He said he had been through "a difficult economic period" but denied any involvement in fixing or selling matches, insisting he had never harmed a team he played for.

According to ONE, the case moved into a new phase on August 2, when Lahav 433 informed the football association that its investigation had been completed. The association's legal department has now asked the disciplinary court to suspend Dahan from all activity until the criminal proceedings against him conclude, or, at minimum, for 60 days.

Central to the association's petition is evidence it says contradicts what Dahan told police. Investigators allege he bet "as a matter of routine" on matches in the very league in which he played, including games involving his own club — a claim the material submitted to the disciplinary court is reported to support with physical evidence.

The association argued that allowing Dahan to keep playing while under suspicion of such serious offences would "severely damage public confidence in the integrity of matches and the fight against this corrupt phenomenon," according to ONE's report of the filing.
It also pointed to precedent, noting that the disciplinary court has previously suspended players and club officials over criminal allegations considerably less serious than those Dahan now faces.
The disciplinary court had not yet ruled on the association's request at the time of publication, and Dahan has not been convicted of any offence.

title: Ashdod's postponement bid may have a point — but the timing is the problem, Afula's lawyer says
dek: F.C. Ashdod wanted Monday's National League opener at Hapoel Afula pushed back while a disciplinary case against Hapoel Tiberias plays out. The football association's court disagreed, and Afula's attorney says the real issue was never the substance of the claim but when it was filed.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "Maybe Ashdod is right, maybe not, the claim is the timing"
ONE - Hapoel Afula demands Ashdod's petition be rejected

body: F.C. Ashdod goes into Monday's Liga Leumit season opener at Hapoel Afula having lost a legal battle it fought right up to the eve of kickoff — a petition to postpone the match that the Israel Football Association's appeals court threw out after Afula argued the club had simply waited far too long to file it.

Ashdod, relegated from Ligat Ha'al last season, is not just any second-tier club trying to open its campaign. It is also an interested party in a serious disciplinary case against Hapoel Tiberias, the club it fought a direct relegation battle with. The indictment against Tiberias, tied to what has been dubbed the "infusions affair," accuses the club of assisting the use of banned substances and stimulants in preparation for last season's decisive survival match between the two sides, alongside related allegations of crowd violence near that fixture.

Because possible sanctions against Tiberias range from a points deduction to relegation — or even a reversal that could still keep Ashdod in the top flight — Ashdod petitioned to be joined as an interested party and asked for the case to be fast-tracked before this season begins. Its lawyers argued that letting the Liga Leumit season kick off as scheduled, with Ashdod playing as a lower-division side, would create "facts on the ground" that no later ruling could realistically undo.

On that basis, Ashdod asked the appeals court to postpone Monday's trip to Afula. Hapoel Afula pushed back hard, telling the court in a formal response that a one-day postponement would cause serious damage: the match is the club's season-opening showcase at its own stadium, with promotional, organisational and logistical work already completed.

Afula's lawyer, Avishay Ifergan, took the argument public on the radio programme "Sicha HaYom," telling listeners the substance of Ashdod's claim wasn't really the point. "Why didn't they do this a week and a half ago?" he asked, noting that the facts underpinning Ashdod's petition were known well before it was filed — on a Friday, shortly before the start of Shabbat, leaving Afula almost no time to respond.

Afula also pointed to what it called a procedural flaw: the petition, filed as an administrative proceeding, arrived without the supporting affidavit ordinarily required. Separately, the club said it was baffled by comments from attorney Gal'ad Bergman suggesting the disciplinary process against Tiberias wouldn't be resolved quickly enough — noting, according to ONE, that Bergman himself had helped set the very timetable he was now citing as too slow.

The appeals court sided with Afula and rejected Ashdod's request to delay the match, while leaving the door open to revisit the matter if the Tiberias case moves forward. That means Monday's opener goes ahead as planned in Afula, with Ashdod still hoping that a harsh enough verdict against Tiberias could yet change its own fate — even from outside the top division.

Hapoel Afula's attorney Avishay Ifergan argued publicly that the core problem was timing — Ashdod filed its petition late, just before Shabbat, despite knowing the relevant facts well in advance.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem sign Reebok as official kit supplier for 2026/27

body: Hapoel Jerusalem's basketball players will step onto the court next season in Reebok, after the club announced a new official apparel partnership with the global sportswear brand ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, ONE reported.

Under the agreement, Reebok becomes Hapoel Jerusalem's official clothing supplier, providing the team's game uniforms and training wear as well as a broader range of sport and fashion product, according to the report. The deal runs through Sport & More, Reebok's official distributor in Israel.

The club said the tie-up will let it design special editions and limited collections across the season, alongside an expanded merchandise range for players and supporters — with a stated emphasis on keeping special-edition pricing accessible for fans, including the club's youth divisions.

"We're pleased to open this chapter with Reebok," Hapoel Jerusalem CEO Oren Ariely said, according to ONE, framing the partnership as part of the club's push to widen its commercial offering while giving supporters attractive, affordable access to team gear.

Ariely is still relatively new to the role, having taken over as Hapoel Jerusalem's chief executive in September 2025, succeeding Alon Kramer after a two-year tenure. He arrived with two decades of marketing, strategy and digital experience, including senior posts at HOT and El Al's frequent-flyer programme.

Sport & More CEO Peleg Norany welcomed the deal from the distributor's side. "The connection with Hapoel Jerusalem is natural and exciting," he said, according to ONE, describing it as uniting "two brands with strong identity and genuine passion for sport."

Neither side disclosed the financial terms of the agreement. But for a club that plays in front of sellout crowds at the Pais Arena and carries one of the most recognisable shirts in Israeli basketball, a global brand with deep roots in the sport represents a meaningful commercial upgrade heading into the new Winner League season.

title: Hapoel Haifa's fixture anger and Ashdod's court fight over the Tiberias case roil Israeli football
dek: As the 2026/27 season nears, Hapoel Haifa blast a 'distorted' schedule while F.C. Ashdod battles in court to freeze matches over a bribery case involving Ironi Tiberias.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Ashdod petitions supreme disciplinary court over Afula match
ONE - Ashdod partially joined to proceeding against Tiberias

body: Israeli football's build-up to the 2026/27 season is being overshadowed by two separate flashpoints, and ONE's studio coverage this week is dedicated to both: a fixture-list row engulfing Hapoel Haifa in the Premier League, and a courtroom battle in the National League that could reshape who plays where before a ball is even kicked.

In Haifa, the anger centres on a schedule that the club says has left it badly exposed. Hapoel Haifa's opening-round league fixture against Hapoel Be'er Sheva was postponed because Be'er Sheva is still involved in Champions League qualifying playoffs, a knock-on consequence of European football dictating domestic dates.

The reshuffle means Haifa will now begin its season a round late, hosting Hapoel Tel Aviv on August 30, before an immediate away trip to Be'er Sheva on September 2 and then a further difficult away fixture at Maccabi Netanya in round three, whose date has not yet been confirmed.

Club CEO Itay Rak has formally complained to the league management, describing the result as three consecutive tough matches crammed into a single week and saying the decision left Hapoel Haifa "harmed by a distorted fixture list," according to ONE.

Two tiers below, in the National League, a far weightier dispute is playing out in the Israel Football Association's Supreme Disciplinary Court. F.C. Ashdod has petitioned the court to postpone its own opening-round match against Hapoel Afula, in a case that has exposed a rift between the league's administrators and the sport's judicial arm.

At the heart of Ashdod's petition is a serious indictment filed against Ironi Tiberias, which the club is accused of orchestrating a collective bribery scheme around a decisive relegation-survival match against Ashdod last season, alongside separate allegations of failing to comply with earlier disciplinary rulings.

Ashdod argues that letting its opener go ahead before the Tiberias case is resolved would create what its lawyers called "an irreversible sporting reality" — effectively locking in a competitive landscape that could later prove to have been unfairly shaped by the alleged bribery. The club had earlier won a partial victory when the disciplinary court agreed to join it as a party to the proceedings against Tiberias.

Hapoel Afula has pushed back hard, filing a formal response asking the court to dismiss Ashdod's petition outright, both on procedural grounds and on its merits, and rejecting any suggestion that its own scheduled match should be held hostage to a separate club's legal fight.

Presiding over the urgent hearing, Judge Miguel Deutsch offered a pointed reminder to both sides of the standard the court would apply, telling the parties: "You cannot make decisions based solely on speculation," as reported by ONE.

No final ruling on the postponement request had been issued as of ONE's reporting, with a decisive hearing still pending — leaving Ashdod, Afula and Tiberias all waiting to learn whether the National League's opening round will go ahead as planned.

Between Haifa's scheduling grievance and Ashdod's courtroom gambit, Israeli football is heading into its new campaign with off-field controversy already competing for attention with what happens on the pitch.

title: Maccabi Haifa fumes after late committee U-turn hands President's Award to Beitar Jerusalem
dek: ONE reports that Haifa led the scoring before a revote, driven partly by comments from committee chairman Andy Ram, swung the President's Award in Sports to Beitar Jerusalem — reopening old grievances over two players who left Haifa for the capital.

verificationSources.label: ONE - report on the committee dispute
ONE - President's Award in Sports ceremony report
Sport1/Maariv - Beitar Jerusalem wins President's Award, lifetime prizes for Shachor and Barkat

body: A ceremony designed to celebrate Israeli sport's community work has turned into a genuine controversy, with Maccabi Haifa crying foul after the President's Award in Sports slipped away from the club at the last moment in favour of Beitar Jerusalem, according to a report by ONE.

The award, presented by President Isaac Herzog at his official residence in Jerusalem, honours clubs and teams for social and community contributions rather than results on the field. In the top-flight football category this year, the prize went to Beitar Jerusalem, recognised for making the commemoration of its fallen fans "a way of life" through the season.

What has angered Haifa, ONE reports, is how the decision was reached. According to the outlet, Maccabi Haifa was actually leading the committee's initial scoring by two points before the panel abruptly called for a revote.

The trigger for that second vote, ONE says, was a discussion among committee members about the implications of grenade attacks earlier this year on branches of Japonica, the store chain owned by Beitar owner Barak Abramov.

It is what happened next that Haifa's camp reportedly finds hardest to swallow. The committee is chaired by Andy Ram, Israel's former world number one doubles player, who — according to ONE's account of the deliberations — told colleagues he understood Maccabi Haifa's community programme "operates through an external company," while Beitar's work was carried out "personally," making the Jerusalem club the more deserving winner. Ram is reported to have also acknowledged working indirectly with Maccabi Haifa and to have said he felt uncomfortable with the club — remarks that preceded the vote swinging to Beitar.

A Maccabi Haifa source, speaking to ONE, pointed to what they described as inconsistent standards from the committee: the club said it had previously been denied the award altogether because of the involvement of forward Omer Atzili, yet no such objection arose this time even though Atzili and fellow forward Dor Micha — both now at Beitar Jerusalem after leaving Haifa — are on Beitar's books.

Bat-El Garbi, chief executive of Values in Sport, the organisation that runs the committee process on the President's behalf, declined to engage with the substance of the claims when approached by ONE. She dismissed the report as "yellow journalism" and said she was sharing a message she had received from Maccabi Haifa that reflected on the discourse, adding she would pass the matter on.

Publicly, though, Maccabi Haifa played it down. Club CEO Itzik Ovadia struck a notably calmer tone than the frustration attributed to sources inside the club, telling ONE simply: "I don't know about any mess, sorry."

The episode came on a night that was not without recognition for Haifa. Club chairman Jacob Shachor received a lifetime achievement prize at the same ceremony, an honour shared with Hapoel Beer Sheva owner Alona Barkat, while Maccabi Haifa's women's basketball team separately picked up a community-work award of its own.

Whether the disagreement over the football prize develops into anything more than a war of words remains to be seen, but the episode has exposed uncomfortable tension around a ceremony meant to celebrate sport's role away from results and rivalries.

title: Hapoel Be'er Sheva land in Bucharest as over 900 fans follow for Champions League playoff opener
dek: The Israeli champions touched down in Romania on Monday to prepare for Wednesday's first leg against Sabah, a de facto home game being staged outside Israel because of the security situation.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Hapoel Be'er Sheva land in Bucharest, over 900 fans to arrive
UEFA.com - H. Beer-Sheva vs Sabah match info

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva touched down in Bucharest on Monday, the first step of a trip that could carry the club into the Champions League proper for the first time in its history. ONE reports that more than 900 supporters are expected to follow the team to Romania for Wednesday's playoff-round first leg against Sabah FC of Azerbaijan.

It is technically a home fixture for the Israeli champions, but one they cannot play at home. With Israeli clubs barred from hosting UEFA ties on home soil this season because of the security situation, Hapoel Be'er Sheva have relocated their continental games to the Superbet Arena-Giulești, the Bucharest ground of Liga 1 side Rapid Bucharest — and it is there that Wednesday's match kicks off at 22:00 Israel time.

The prize for winning the tie is enormous: a place in the Champions League league phase for the first time in the club's history, guaranteeing at least four more European nights at their adopted Bucharest home. Lose, and Hapoel Be'er Sheva drop into the Europa League league phase instead — still a significant consolation, but a considerable step down from Europe's top table.

They have come this far by producing one of the qualifying rounds' bigger shocks. Hapoel Be'er Sheva eliminated Red Star Belgrade 3-0 on aggregate in the third qualifying round, winning 2-0 away in Belgrade to seal the tie after a first-leg lead at home.
Sabah, for their part, arrive in Bucharest off the back of their own statement win, seeing off Danish champions Aarhus 5-2 on aggregate, a tie they closed out with a 4-0 victory in the second leg.

Manager Ran Kojok has fresh options to work with. Forward Yonas Malede completed his move from Maccabi Tel Aviv in time to be registered for the tie, while defender Matan Baltaxa returns from suspension and is available for selection again after missing the win over Red Star.

According to ONE, the coaching staff's working plan is to stick largely with the XI that saw off the Serbian side, rather than make wholesale changes for what amounts to the biggest match of the club's season so far. Two training sessions were scheduled in Romania — one on Monday evening shortly after landing, and a final run-out on Tuesday before kickoff.

The travelling support is the story that gives this build-up its edge. Well over 900 Hapoel Be'er Sheva fans making the trip to a stadium several thousand kilometres from Be'er Sheva is a striking number for what is, on paper, an away leg for everyone but the club itself — and it points to just how much significance the fanbase is attaching to this tie.

The return leg follows quickly, in Azerbaijan on Tuesday, August 25. Two matches now stand between Hapoel Be'er Sheva and a first appearance in the Champions League league phase — and the first of them begins in front of what should be a raucous, largely blue-and-white crowd in a Romanian stadium that, for one week, becomes home.

title: Ashdod asks football's top court to delay season opener over Tiberias affair
dek: The club argues playing before the Tiberias indictment is resolved would create an irreversible reality; Hapoel Afula says the petition should be thrown out.

verificationSources.label: ONE - MS Ashdod's petition to the Supreme Court
ONE - Hapoel Afula's response to the petition
ONE - indictment filed against Ironi Tiberias

body: Just hours before Ashdod were due to open their Liga Leumit campaign against Hapoel Afula, the club's lawyers were making a very different case entirely — in front of the Israel Football Association's Supreme Court, trying to stop the match from being played at all.

According to ONE, MS Ashdod filed an urgent petition asking the tribunal to postpone the opening-round fixture, scheduled for August 18. The club's central claim is that going ahead with the game now would lock in an "irreversible reality" before the fallout from a serious indictment against Ironi Tiberias is fully known.

The Tiberias case sits at the heart of the request. That club stands accused, ONE has reported separately, of orchestrating a scheme of banned collective infusions for its players ahead of a decisive relegation match against Ashdod at the end of last season — the very fixture that helped decide which of the two clubs avoided the drop.

Should Tiberias ultimately be hit with sanctions such as a points deduction or relegation once the disciplinary process concludes, last season's final placings could effectively be rewritten. Ashdod's argument is that every match played in the meantime, under standings that may not survive scrutiny, narrows the tribunal's room to fix things retroactively.

"Each additional match that takes place before the picture is clarified expands reliance [on the current situation] and narrows future discretion," the club argued in its petition, as reported by ONE.

Hapoel Afula, drawn into a dispute that has nothing to do with them, pushed back hard. Their lawyer, Avishai Ifergan, told the tribunal Ashdod had sat on the request for weeks, filing only on Friday, August 14 — what he called the last possible moment — despite knowing the relevant facts since late July.

Afula's response also raised a procedural objection, arguing the petition lacked a supporting affidavit, which it called "a fundamental defect" in a filing of this kind. The club said postponement would cause it real, avoidable harm — leaving it without a match while rivals played and gained ground in a saga it has no part in — and questioned why only its fixture was being targeted rather than any of Tiberias's own matches in the top flight.

The petition was heard by a Supreme Court panel of judges Miguel Deutsch, Yaniv Vaki and Ortal Klein. Deutsch, according to ONE, sounded openly skeptical of Ashdod's reasoning during the hearing, telling the club's representatives their argument leaned heavily on speculation and that it was "difficult deciding based on hypotheses without concrete facts."

No ruling had been announced by the time of publication. With Ashdod's opening fixture bearing down, the tribunal's decision — whichever way it goes — will land just as the Liga Leumit season gets under way, with a club potentially starting its campaign under a cloud that events at Tiberias could yet lift, or deepen.

body: Gavi Bublil, Maccabi Netanya's longtime operations manager, has moved to shut down a round of social media speculation over his absence from the club's training facility, insisting he has not been dismissed and has not faced any disciplinary process.
"I have never been fired nor summoned for a hearing," Bublil said, according to ONE. "I am currently at home on sick leave due to back pain that occurred after the match against Ramat Gan."

The rumours took hold after Bublil went missing from his usual post at the club's facilities, with Alex Litvinov, who normally manages logistics for the youth teams, stepping in to cover his duties in the interim. That temporary handover was enough to set off chatter that Bublil's near two-decade run at the club was over.
Bublil said the reality was far more mundane: a back injury sustained around the club's match against Ramat Gan has kept him sidelined, and he remains a fully employed member of staff throughout.

He added that CEO Gil Lev asked to visit him while he recovers, and that the two used the meeting to discuss shifting Bublil into a role with lighter physical demands going forward, while preserving his existing salary and conditions.

Bublil described the gesture as consistent with what he called a relationship spanning some 20 years with the club's leadership, and said his focus now is on making sure the wider operation stays settled as Maccabi Netanya's season approaches.

The episode is a reminder of how quickly unverified claims about a long-serving club employee can spread once a routine absence goes unexplained — and how a short, on-the-record statement was enough to close it down.

title: Hapoel Afula demands rejection of Ashdod's bid to postpone season opener
dek: The Liga Leumit club says a last-minute petition from MS Ashdod to delay Tuesday's kickoff, filed over the unrelated Ironi Tiberias saline-infusion case, is legally flawed and tactically timed.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הפועל עפולה דורשת לדחות את עתירת מ.ס אשדוד
ONE - אשדוד לביה"ד העליון: לדחות את המשחק נגד עפולה
Walla Sport - עירוני טבריה על כתב האישום

body: Hapoel Afula has formally asked the Israel Football Association's Supreme Tribunal to throw out a petition filed by MS Ashdod that sought to delay Tuesday's Liga Leumit season opener between the two clubs, arguing the challenge is both procedurally defective and timed to force a rushed decision.

Ashdod's petition, lodged with the federation's top judicial body, asked judges to either dismiss the matter or issue an interim order postponing the August 18 kickoff — not because of anything involving Afula, but because of a separate disciplinary case against Ironi Tiberias.

Tiberias was formally indicted by the Israel Football Association last month over an alleged saline-infusion scandal, with charges that include aiding the use of banned substances in aggravated circumstances, fraud, coordinated testimony and violations of federation regulations and prior judicial rulings. Prosecutors have signalled they may seek penalties ranging from a heavy points deduction to relegation.

Ashdod's argument, according to the petition, is that letting the opening round proceed now risks creating "irreversible facts" on the league table — results banked before the Tiberias case is resolved that could later complicate any remedy the tribunal orders. The club first raised the issue with the league committee's chair on August 13, before escalating to a formal petition.

Afula's response, filed to the tribunal, attacks the petition on several fronts at once. Its lawyers say the filing lacks a required affidavit — a fundamental defect for an administrative proceeding of this kind — and that Ashdod never exhausted the normal channels through league management before running straight to the Supreme Tribunal.

There is also a timing complaint. Ashdod's petition landed on Friday, August 14, hours before Shabbat, despite the underlying facts having been known to the club well before that. Afula's lawyers characterised the move as a deliberate choice to sit on the issue and then spring it at the last possible moment, leaving barely any room for a considered response.

On the merits, Afula stresses it has no stake whatsoever in the federation's case against Tiberias and should not be made to absorb the practical fallout of a dispute it isn't party to. Postponing the opener, the club argues, would leave it at a competitive and organizational disadvantage against sides that complete their round on schedule.
Afula is asking the tribunal to dismiss Ashdod's petition outright, allow Tuesday's match to go ahead as planned, and order Ashdod to cover its legal costs.

The Supreme Tribunal had not issued a ruling as of Monday. Its decision will determine whether the Liga Leumit's opening round kicks off on schedule or whether the Tiberias case casts a shadow over fixtures beyond the club directly involved.

title: Football association's supreme tribunal rejects Hapoel Hadera's bid to field age-exception youth players
dek: Prof. Miguel Deutsch turned down an interim order that would have let three overage 2007-born players line up for Hadera's youth side while the club's Liga Alef senior budget review remains unresolved.

verificationSources.label: ONE - בית הדין העליון דחה את שיתוף חריגי הגיל בחדרה
ONE - סופית: הפועל חדרה תשחק במחוז הדרומי של ליגה א'

body: Hapoel Hadera's hopes of fielding three overage players in the Youth Premier League this weekend were dashed on Thursday, when the Israel Football Association's supreme tribunal rejected the club's request for an interim order permitting the move.

The panel's presiding member, Prof. Miguel Deutsch, ruled that Section 25(a)(1) of the association's registration bylaws explicitly requires so-called age-exception players to be registered with the senior squad before they can turn out for a youth team — a condition Hadera could not yet meet.

At issue is the club's status under new Liga Alef supervision regulations that took effect on July 1. Hadera, newly assigned to the division's southern district, submitted its senior-team budget proposal for review on July 20, and the supervising authorities returned their comments on August 3. That review has still not been signed off, leaving the club's three 2007-born prospects, Guy Papper, Amit Siman-Tov and Refael Ben-Zion, who signed contracts for the 2026/27 season on August 9, unable to be registered with the senior side and, by extension, ineligible to feature for the youth team under the bylaw.

Deutsch did not dismiss Hadera's case outright. He described the club's arguments as "worthy of hearing" even while judging the appeal's prospects of success "apparently not high," and he ordered that the full hearing be scheduled as soon as possible rather than leaving the dispute to drag on.

His reasoning for refusing the interim order was procedural as much as substantive: granting the temporary registration now would have handed Hadera the very relief it is seeking before the underlying appeal has even been heard.

The trio's combined salary allocation for the campaign was set at 75,000 shekels, according to the figures cited in the case — a reminder of just how small-scale this dispute is in financial terms, even as it carries real consequences for three teenagers' season.

Club figures have pushed back hard on the outcome. "Where is the sporting equality?" a Hadera source said, adding that the club "won't give up" and would keep fighting even if, in its view, the tribunal "keeps being technically correct but not wise." Attorney Roey Rozen represented the club in the proceedings, while owner Iti Ben Zev, credited with rescuing Hadera from financial collapse in recent years, has been vocal about the club's frustration with a process he feels has singled it out.

Hadera's argument, in essence, is one of timing and fairness: most of the other clubs in the Youth Premier League have senior sides sitting in higher divisions where budget approvals were already finalised before the season, while Hadera's Liga Alef status placed it under the newer, slower-moving supervision track.

The club's youth side kicked off its Youth Premier League campaign without the three players on Saturday, losing 2-1 away to F.C. Ashdod. With the appeal now set to be fast-tracked, Hadera will be hoping for a swifter resolution before the disadvantage compounds any further.

body: Maccabi Netanya's youth department has locked down its goalkeeping stocks for the next three years, confirming new long-term deals for Ilan Bolitanski and Nikita Shoshulin, while also bringing in forward Itay Barmi on a season-long loan from Hapoel Be'er Sheva, ONE reports.
