title: Amit Cohen: Netanya want, at minimum, to reach the top playoff
dek: The Maccabi Netanya defender says a spirited Toto Cup semi-final exit to Maccabi Tel Aviv only sharpens the club's appetite for a season built around the upper table, Europe and silverware.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC - official result

body: Maccabi Netanya's Toto Cup run ended on Sunday night with a 1-0 semi-final defeat to Maccabi Tel Aviv, but defender Amit Cohen came away insisting the display, not the scoreline, is the truer guide to where his club is heading this season.
"We played an excellent match, it's a frustrating loss and we could have gotten more from this game," Cohen said afterwards, according to ONE. "We're very disappointed we didn't manage to do it."

A single goal from Maccabi Tel Aviv was enough to send the yellow-and-blue through to face Hapoel Tel Aviv in the Toto Cup final, a derby showpiece, while Netanya were left to reflect on a performance they felt deserved more, particularly after dominating long stretches of the second half without finding the finish to match.

For Cohen, the takeaway is less about the exit and more about what it signals for the league campaign to come. "If we play like this in the league, we'll have a good season," he said, before setting out the club's benchmark for the year: "At minimum, reach the upper playoff, compete for Europe and the cup."

It is a pointed marker for a club that spent last season on the outside of the top six, missing out on both the prestige and the roughly one million shekels in bonus money that comes with a top-flight playoff finish. Under coach Roni Levy, Netanya have made no secret of wanting to close that gap and re-establish themselves among Israel's leading clubs.

Cohen, 27, re-signed with Netanya through the 2027/28 season earlier this year, tying his own future to that project after returning to the club having previously come through on loan at Beitar Jerusalem.

The build-up to the Maccabi Tel Aviv tie was not without friction off the pitch. Netanya handed season-ticket holders free entry to the semi-final as a gesture to supporters, but a section of the fan base has been openly critical of CEO Gil Lev, with protests at the club's training ground and, according to Israeli reports, outside his home in the days before kick-off.

There was also transfer business in the background: winger Wilian Ciprian, a January arrival from France, is understood to have turned down an approach from Ironi Tiberias, with his representatives now expected to explore other options before the window shuts.

None of that dented the mood around Cohen's post-match comments, which read as a rallying call rather than an alibi. Netanya open their Israeli Premier League season looking to prove that Sunday's fight, if not the result, is the template for the months ahead.

title: Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City: Maresca admits he's "always worried" after nightmare debut
dek: Riccardo Calafiori struck inside 24 seconds as Arsenal routed City at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in Enzo Maresca's first competitive match in charge, with the Italian pointing to a World Cup-disrupted preparation.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "יש מה לדאוג, אבל צריך לזכור שזו רק ההתחלה"
Manchester City official - Maresca written reaction

body: Enzo Maresca's first competitive match in charge of Manchester City could hardly have gone worse. Arsenal tore into his new side from the opening whistle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Sunday, closing out a 3-0 win in the Community Shield, and the Italian did not try to soften the verdict afterwards. "I'm always worried, even when we win," he said, in comments carried by ONE and City's own channels. "We're only at the beginning."

The traditional curtain-raiser between the Premier League champions and the FA Cup holders pitted last season's title winners, Arsenal, against a City side already being reshaped under its new head coach. Mikel Arteta's team made the stronger case for the shirt in every sense.

Riccardo Calafiori needed just 23 seconds to put Arsenal ahead, meeting Myles Lewis-Skelly's threaded pass on the edge of the box and finishing into the bottom corner — one of the fastest goals in the fixture's history and about as brutal a start as a new manager could suffer.

City responded with three or four decent openings of their own before falling further behind, but could not convert them. Kai Havertz doubled Arsenal's lead in the 28th minute, and Martin Ødegaard, named player of the match, completed the scoring early in the second half to seal a comfortable afternoon for the champions.

Maresca, addressing reporters afterwards, singled out City's failure to close down the ball after Arsenal's second: "I didn't like the first goal we conceded at all, and on the second goal we simply didn't apply any pressure on the ball carrier," he said, according to ONE's report from the post-match press conference.

He also pointed to the disrupted preparation many of his players had going into the game. City fielded four players who had returned from this summer's World Cup with only two or three training sessions behind them, and Maresca said the plan had been to substitute all of them by half-time or an hour at the latest. "I don't know if it's directly related to our physical condition, but we had a lot of players who took part in the World Cup," he said.

It was a jarring way to begin life at the Etihad for Maresca, who was confirmed as Pep Guardiola's successor on June 29 on a three-year contract, arriving after a mid-season departure from Chelsea. He had already built a strong managerial résumé before the move — guiding Leicester City to the Championship title in 2023-24, then leading Chelsea to a fourth-place Premier League finish, the Conference League and the FIFA Club World Cup.

None of that softened Sunday's blow, but Maresca was careful not to let the result define his outlook so early in the job. "It's just the beginning, we have many things that we need to do better," he said. City now turn to the Premier League opener, where the real rebuilding project begins in earnest.

title: Bacot lands in Israel: 'Fans can expect a lot of effort from me'
dek: Maccabi Tel Aviv's new American centre touched down after a ten-hour flight and immediately set out his ambitions for the season under Oded Katash.
body: Armando Bacot Jr. landed in Israel on Monday as Maccabi Tel Aviv's newest centre, and by the time he stepped off a ten-hour flight from the United States he already had a message ready for the yellow-and-blue faithful.
"Fans can expect a lot of effort from me. I will do everything necessary to bring victories," Bacot told ONE on arrival, setting out his stall before he has even trained with his new teammates.
Of the journey itself he was unbothered: "The flight was completely fine — a ten-hour flight, sure, but it wasn't so bad," he said.

The 26-year-old, 2.08-metre American arrives on a two-year contract after a debut European season at Fenerbahçe, where he helped the Istanbul club to the Turkish league title, cup and super cup, though his own EuroLeague minutes were limited — roughly ten a game, for 2.4 points and 1.8 rebounds across 26 appearances.

Before Turkey, Bacot built his name at North Carolina, where he set the program's all-time records for rebounds and double-doubles across a school-record 171 games. He then spent a season with the Memphis Grizzlies' G League affiliate, the Memphis Hustle, putting up 16.8 points, 9.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists a game — numbers that never quite carried over to his rookie year in Turkey.

Head coach Oded Katash, who has led Maccabi to three Israeli championships since returning to the club in 2022, said the club had tracked Bacot for some time: "Armando Bacot is a player we've been following for a long time. He's tall and talented with very high-level offensive abilities. We're confident he has a lot to improve on, and we like that."
Bacot said teammates had already sold him on his new home: "All my teammates said Tel Aviv is the most beautiful place they've played, so I'm very excited," he said.

He joins a reshaped Maccabi frontcourt as the club builds toward the 2026-27 EuroLeague campaign, with the ex-Tar Heel now tasked with proving, in Katash's system, the dominance he showed in college and the G League but has yet to fully replicate in Europe.

body: Michael Yakobov continued his rich vein of international form at the weekend, sweeping both the keirin and match sprint titles at the Grand Prix of Poland in Pruszków, ONE reported.

title: Kiryat Shmona blast referee Yoni Klaz after 2-1 stoppage-time defeat to Hapoel Tel Aviv
dek: A sarcastic parting shot at the whistle followed Ofir Benvenishti's 30th-minute red card and Daniel Daffa's late double, as Kiryat Shmona crashed out of the Toto Cup and into a fresh row over officiating.

body: Ironi Kiryat Shmona did not go quietly after their Toto Cup exit on Sunday night, and by the next day the club had turned the post-mortem into a pointed message aimed squarely at the man with the whistle.

Hapoel Tel Aviv beat Kiryat Shmona 2-1 in the Toto Cup semi-final, needing two goals deep into stoppage time from Daniel Daffa to complete a dramatic turnaround after playing more than an hour with a spare man. The result sends Hapoel Tel Aviv into the first all-Tel Aviv derby in the competition's history, where they will meet Maccabi Tel Aviv in the final in December.

Kiryat Shmona had led since the sixth minute, when Adrian Ogariza put them ahead, and looked to be cruising toward the final until referee Yoni Klaz sent off defender Ofir Benvenishti for a second yellow card in the 30th minute. Reduced to ten men for the rest of the match, the northern club held on deep into added time before Daffa struck twice — in the 90+7th and 90+9th minutes — to turn the tie on its head.

It was the aftermath, not just the scoreline, that Kiryat Shmona wanted to talk about. According to ONE, the club's complaint centred less on the Benvenishti dismissal itself than on what it described as inconsistent treatment of the two benches over the course of the evening.

Coach Shay Barda was shown two yellow cards during the match, while Kiryat Shmona alleged that Hapoel Tel Aviv's technical area escaped any sanction despite repeated protests to fourth official Snir Levy, ONE reported. The club also noted that defender Shay Sabah was injured during the game.

"I wish our football would stick to the rules as strictly for all 250 league games as it did today," Barda said, according to ONE — a pointed dig at how tightly the officials policed his own touchline compared with the opposition's.

The club's statement went further still, signing off with a line dripping in sarcasm: "We wish Yoni Klaz sticks to the letter of the law right through to the end of the season," ONE reported — a jab implying the opposite had been true on this occasion.

For Kiryat Shmona, the defeat ends the Toto Cup campaign early and means a swift return of focus to the Israeli Premier League season ahead. For Hapoel Tel Aviv, Daffa's stoppage-time brace is the story of an improbable passage to a final that will carry extra weight as a derby against their Tel Aviv rivals.

Whether the complaint leads anywhere beyond a strongly worded quote remains to be seen — Israeli clubs regularly air grievances with officiating without formal consequence. But Yoni Klaz's evening in Kiryat Shmona will be remembered locally as much for the row that followed as for the red card that shaped the game.

body: Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon have added two experienced faces from a rival newly promoted to Liga Leumit, confirming the signings of defender Reef Mesika, 37, and forward Yossi Twaaba, 27, both arriving from Maccabi Kiryat Gat, ONE reports.

The move is a curious one on paper: Kiryat Gat won promotion to the National League last season, while Ramat HaSharon are aiming to climb straight back up after being demoted from that same division. But both players evidently see a bigger role waiting for them at Grundman Stadium than a step into Liga Leumit with their old club.

The club has since been taken over by producer Yoav Gross and a group of fellow businessmen, who bought in as the new ownership in January 2026, with Gross installed as chairman. Manager Asi Elimelech, who previously led Hapoel Ra'anana up from Liga Alef, was brought in this summer with the explicit brief of doing the same job again.

Mesika is a well-travelled figure in Israeli football's middle and lower tiers, having represented, among others, Maccabi Netanya, Hapoel Tel Aviv, Hapoel Kfar Saba and Hapoel Ashkelon across nearly two decades as a professional.

Twaaba arrives with sharper recent form. He scored 18 goals last season split between Migdal HaEmek and Beitar Nordia Jerusalem, form that earned him a move to Maccabi Kiryat Gat for the 2025/26 campaign as that club chased and won promotion out of Liga Alef South.

title: Pedrão trains at centre-back as Maccabi Haifa keep Novakovich waiting
dek: Brazilian defender given a vote of confidence in training ahead of tonight's Toto Cup test against Hapoel Jerusalem, while new striker Andrija Novakovich still cannot be registered until a foreign-quota exit is completed.

body: Maccabi Haifa host Hapoel Jerusalem in the Toto Cup on Monday evening (20:00), the final run-out before Saturday's Israeli Premier League opener away to Hapoel Ramat Gan, and the team sheet Barak Bakhar sent out in training carried a couple of clear signals about where his squad currently stands.

The headline one, as ONE reports, is that Pedrão trained at centre-back — a sign the club still believes in the Brazilian after a difficult year in Haifa. Pedrão arrived from Portimonense in the summer of 2024 for a reported €1.3 million but managed only 17 appearances before tearing his meniscus, an injury that kept him out for the rest of last season.

Wanderson Tsunami, the 30-year-old Brazilian brought in on a free transfer after captaining Levski Sofia to a league and cup double, is set to switch to left-back for the Jerusalem match, with Kenny Saief moving to the bench as a result.
In goal, Omri Glazer returns to start, taking over from teenager Glen Alvin, who had been first choice through the early part of preseason since Glazer's return to the club after a decade away.

Further down the bench, ONE notes that the club is easing its younger players in gently — Navot Ratner, Adam Grimberg and Noam Steipman are all named among the substitutes rather than starters for the cup tie.

The bigger story around the squad, though, is the one player who still isn't in it. Andrija Novakovich, the American forward signed on a free transfer after scoring five goals in 33 appearances for a relegated Reggiana side in Italy's Serie B last season, remains outside the squad entirely — not through injury or form, but bureaucracy.

Maccabi Haifa's foreign-player registration is full, with eight non-Israeli players already on the books, and Novakovich cannot be added until one of them departs. The player standing in his way is midfielder Peter Agbah, who holds an offer from a Russian club but, according to ONE, has been hesitant to accept it because of concerns about the security situation in the region.

The club is hopeful the move will still go through in the coming days, and ONE reports Maccabi Haifa could register Novakovich as early as Monday at noon if Agbah's exit is finalised in time — though as of the Jerusalem match, the American remains unable to feature.

Elsewhere in the forward line, Silva Cani — the Israeli-Togolese winger who joined from Beitar Jerusalem after impressing at Bat Yam and beyond — is being given priority for a starting role up front, according to the report.

And Bruninho, signed for a reported €1.75 million on a three-year deal this summer, continues to draw praise inside the club, with ONE describing him as a potential game-changer capable of attracting interest from bigger leagues within a couple of seasons if his form holds.

title: Mourinho: Real Madrid 'starting to look like a team' after 3-0 win over Schalke 04
dek: The Portuguese coach praised his squad's growing cohesion as Madrid closed out an unbeaten pre-season in Gelsenkirchen, days before the La Liga opener at Espanyol.
body: José Mourinho pronounced himself satisfied with his Real Madrid squad after their final pre-season run-out, declaring that "the team is starting to look like a team" as his side wrapped up their summer schedule with a comfortable win away to Schalke 04, ONE reported.

Real Madrid won 3-0 at the Veltins-Arena in Gelsenkirchen, with Kylian Mbappé and Dean Huijsen scoring in the first half before a further goal after the break settled the contest. The friendly also formed part of celebrations marking the 25th anniversary of Schalke's home stadium.

The result left Mourinho's side unbeaten through four pre-season fixtures in his second spell in charge of the club, with the serious business now just days away: Real Madrid open the 2026-27 La Liga season away to Espanyol on Saturday.
"It has been a very good test, a very good final training session before starting the real thing," Mourinho said, in comments carried by ONE and the club's own channels.

The Portuguese coach was especially pleased with how his squad — a mix of long-serving veterans and high-profile summer arrivals — is starting to gel on and off the pitch. "The team is starting to look like a team. Because if we talk about players individually, as I told you, they're either very good or very, very, very good," he said.

Mourinho added that the group has shown genuine unity in training, even among those still adjusting to a new dressing room. "We're playing as a team. There's empathy and collective work," he said, pointing to players who returned early from their summer break to put in extra preparation time.

With the transfer business largely settled and the squad taking shape, Mourinho's message ahead of the competitive season was one of quiet confidence rather than declaration — a coach who has seen enough across four friendlies to believe his group is coming together, without yet claiming it has arrived.

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv needed extra time and a mountain of composure to get there, but they are through to the Toto Cup final - and for the first time in the competition's history, that final will be an all Tel Aviv derby. A 2-1 win over ten-man Ironi Kiryat Shmona on Sunday, sealed by a Daniel Daffa brace deep into the additional 30 minutes, sets up a meeting with Maccabi Tel Aviv in December.

It did not look like heading that way for long stretches. Kiryat Shmona struck first, in the sixth minute, when Adrian Ogrisea converted a cross from Shay Ben David to put the underdogs in front. Hapoel spent the rest of the half chasing the game, only for a numerical advantage to fall into their lap just before the half-hour mark, when Kiryat Shmona defender Ofir Benbenishti was shown a second yellow card and sent off.

Even with an extra man, Hapoel could not find a way through in normal time, and the tie went to extra time still locked at 1-0. That is when Daffa took over. He struck in the 97th minute to level the score, then added a second just two minutes later, in the 99th, to complete the turnaround and send Hapoel into the final.

"We have a group of men who prove to us each time that we have someone to go all the way with. With these players we can face any challenge," sources in the club said afterwards, in comments carried by ONE - a reflection of a squad that has now dug itself out of trouble in cup competition more than once this pre-season.

The win also carried a debut of note. Douglas Owusu, the Ghanaian winger Hapoel signed from Red Star Belgrade for a reported €2.2 million on a three-year deal earlier this month, was introduced in the 60th minute and had a hand in Hapoel's second goal, offering an early glimpse of the direct running that persuaded the club to make him one of its most expensive summer signings.

Manager Eliniav Barda used the semi-final to rotate his squad, resting several regulars with one eye on a considerably bigger assignment this week. Hapoel are due in Bergamo on Thursday to open their UEFA Conference League play-off against Atalanta, with the return leg to follow on August 27 at the DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary, where Hapoel's home leg will be staged.

The Toto Cup final itself will not be played until December, but its billing is already historic: this is the first time in the competition's history that the two Tel Aviv giants have met in the final. Hapoel are chasing only their second Toto Cup title, with their sole previous triumph coming in the 2001/02 season.

For a club juggling a genuine European test against an Italian heavyweight with domestic cup ambitions, Sunday's fightback was as much a statement of depth as of nerve - proof, in the words of those inside the dressing room, that this squad can be trusted to go the distance on more than one front at once.

body: Nuno Espirito Santo made little effort to hide his satisfaction with Manor Solomon's first outing in a West Ham shirt, hailing the Israeli's "wonderful qualities" after a debut goal that briefly looked set to open his account in style. "Solomon played a very good match," the manager said, according to ONE. "I'm happy he found the net, it will greatly contribute to his confidence. He is a super-talented player with the ball, knows how to create excellent combinations on the pitch and brings wonderful qualities to our team."

The praise followed a chastening afternoon at Turf Moor on Sunday, where West Ham led 2-0 with less than 20 minutes remaining before conceding twice late on to draw 2-2 in their first competitive fixture since being relegated from the Premier League - their first season back in the Championship since 2011-12.

Solomon, who joined from Tottenham on 10 August on a three-year deal, was named in Nuno's starting XI and given license to attack down the left. Max Kilman had already headed West Ham in front inside ten minutes when Solomon struck in the 72nd, driving a first-time finish into the roof of the net after Mohamadou Kante squeezed a low ball into the box from the right.

Burnley, playing their own first match back in the second tier, refused to fold. Zian Flemming halved the deficit from the penalty spot in the 83rd minute, then completed his brace deep into stoppage time after West Ham failed to clear a corner, sending Turf Moor into raptures and denying Nuno's side what would have been a perfect start to the campaign.

For Solomon personally, the mixed emotions were obvious. He was substituted in the 89th minute, moments before Flemming's leveller, but still finished the afternoon as West Ham's outstanding performer - completing all four of his attempted dribbles and 23 of his 25 passes while carrying the ball 113 metres up the pitch.

West Ham supporters were similarly effusive in their post-match ratings, marking him among the best players on the pitch and describing him, in fan reaction gathered by ONE, as "exactly the attacking option we were missing" and a "real nuisance" for Burnley's defenders whenever the ball moved forward.

It capped a swift adjustment for the 26-year-old, who arrived at West Ham for an undisclosed fee after struggling to hold down a regular starting role at Tottenham. Nuno had already spoken warmly of Solomon's talent in the build-up to the Burnley trip, and his post-match verdict suggested the manager sees the Israel international as a genuine attacking outlet in a division better known for physicality than craft.

West Ham will hope the late collapse proves a one-off rather than a pattern as they find their feet in an unfamiliar division. On the evidence of his first appearance, though, Solomon looks to have arrived with precisely the qualities his new manager wanted.

title: Flick says Barcelona 'could be missing something' as transfer window nears its close
dek: The Barcelona coach praised the intensity of training after Sunday's 5-2 friendly win over Basel, but left the door open to further transfer business before the Joan Gamper Trophy and the delayed La Liga opener at Elche.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Flick: we're missing something, hope things sort out this week

body: Hansi Flick could not quite shake the transfer talk swirling around Camp Nou, even in the afterglow of a comfortable preseason win. Asked about it after Barcelona's 5-2 defeat of FC Basel in Switzerland on Sunday, the head coach admitted there might still be a gap to fill. "It could be that we're missing something, we'll see during the week," ONE quoted him as saying.

The question was prompted directly by reports linking Barcelona to two significant names this summer: Manchester City's Rodri and Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez, both the subject of persistent speculation in the Spanish press. Flick's answer stopped short of confirming anything was close, but it did nothing to dampen the sense that Barcelona's business is not yet finished.

He was careful, though, not to sound alarmed about his group's readiness on the pitch itself. "There is intensity and quality in training," Flick said, according to ONE, framing the issue less as a talent shortfall and more as a squad still digesting a busy summer of arrivals. "There are many players who recently joined us and we need to connect them," he added.

That process of integration was on full display in Basel. Barcelona were rarely troubled at St. Jakob-Park, playing with the same fluid, positionally flexible attack that carried them to the La Liga title last season, and the 5-2 scoreline offered a reminder of the depth Flick now has to manage across his squad.

The Álvarez links are not new. Barcelona's coach has previously pushed the club not to give up on the Argentine striker, described in other reporting as wanting "one last push" to get a deal for the World Cup winner over the line, with Álvarez said to have made his own preference to leave Atlético clear to manager Diego Simeone.

Rodri's name has circulated in the same conversations, part of the broader question marks Flick was fielding after full time in Switzerland - a sign that, whatever business Barcelona have already done this summer, the club's coach is not treating the squad-building process as closed.

Sunday's friendly was Barcelona's penultimate test before the competitive season begins in earnest. Next up is a historic occasion: the Joan Gamper Trophy against Egypt's Al Ahly at Camp Nou on Wednesday, August 19, marking the first time an African club has been invited to the traditional curtain-raiser and the stadium's first hosting of the fixture since its reopening.

Barcelona's first competitive fixture of the 2026/27 season follows four days later, away to Elche on Sunday, August 23. It is technically round two of the La Liga calendar - Barcelona's original Matchday 1 fixture against Athletic Club was pushed back to accommodate the club's heavy contingent of World Cup finalists, leaving the Elche trip as the campaign's true kickoff.

Flick delivered a domestic treble of La Liga, Copa del Rey and the Spanish Super Cup in his first season in charge in 2024/25, and his message after Basel suggested a coach comfortable with his group's habits but still watching the market closely. Whether that translates into a fresh arrival should become clear, in his own words, sometime "during the week."

title: Ashdod asks football's top tribunal to postpone Afula opener over Tiberias case
dek: The relegated club wants its National League opener delayed, arguing that kicking off before Ironi Tiberias's banned-infusions case is resolved could lock in a result it can never undo.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Ashdod petitions Supreme Tribunal to postpone Afula match
Ashdod Net - MS Ashdod petition to postpone opening round vs Afula
ONE - Indictment filed: Tiberias to stand trial in infusions affair
ONE - Ashdod seeks to join proceedings against Tiberias
ONE - Ashdod asks to freeze league games for both clubs

body: MS Ashdod has taken its battle to stay in contention for a swift return to the Premier League all the way to Israeli football's Supreme Tribunal, petitioning the game's highest disciplinary body to postpone Monday's National League opener against Hapoel Afula.

Attorney Amit Hadad, acting for the relegated club, filed the urgent request asking the tribunal's presidency to either order the match delayed pending a further ruling or, failing that, to grant an interim injunction freezing the fixture altogether. ONE reports the panel was due to convene to hear arguments from both sides on Monday afternoon, hours before the scheduled kickoff.

Ashdod's argument centres on timing rather than football. The club says that playing the match on schedule, before the full implications of a serious indictment against Ironi Tiberias become clear, would create what its petition calls "expanding reliance" that would "diminish future freedom of action" - in effect, an outcome that could never be reversed even if Tiberias is later hit with harsh sanctions.

The case against Tiberias is the reason for the urgency. According to the indictment, filed by the Israel Football Association in late July, club officials arranged banned intravenous infusions for six players in the locker room in the days before a decisive relegation match against Ashdod on May 3, which Tiberias won 3-0. The infusions were administered without a doctor present and reportedly exceeded permitted volumes under association medical rules.

The indictment names owner Miki Bitan as the instigator, alleging he pushed for the infusions after a league game against Ironi Kiryat Shmona and pursued the plan even though he was barred from any involvement in club affairs under a settlement agreement signed only weeks earlier, in April. Tiberias faces charges of aiding the use of banned substances under aggravating circumstances, breaching association regulations, and failing to comply with the earlier court-ordered settlement.

Ashdod, for its part, ended up going down regardless. The club lost 1-0 to Hapoel Jerusalem on May 13, sealing its relegation to the National League after a decade in the top flight - a fall it now argues might have been avoided, or could still be reversed, depending on how severely Tiberias is punished.

Possible sanctions against Tiberias range from a points deduction to relegation from the Premier League, either of which could theoretically open a path for Ashdod to reclaim its top-flight place instead. That is why the club is anxious to avoid banking any results - starting with the Afula fixture - while the case remains unresolved.

This is not Ashdod's first move in the dispute. The club has already asked the Football Association to freeze league fixtures involving both clubs until the Tiberias case is settled, and separately applied to join the disciplinary proceedings as an interested party, pushing for an accelerated timeline so a ruling lands before the 2026/27 season takes full shape.

Hapoel Afula, for now, is simply the opponent caught in the middle of a fight that has nothing to do with them. Whether the National League's opening round goes ahead as planned rests on the tribunal's decision, expected imminently after Monday's hearing.

title: Gorbenko admits disappointment as Israel leaves European Championships without a medal
dek: The six-time European champion says she expected more of herself in Paris, as Israel's swim team goes home without a medal for the first time since 2018 despite four national records.
body: Anastasia Gorbenko didn't try to dress up how the week had gone. "I had expectations, and I'm disappointed with some of my performances," the Israeli swimmer said as the European Championships wrapped up in Paris on Sunday, according to ONE.

It was a blunt admission from a swimmer who has been Israel's standard-bearer in the pool for years, a six-time European champion who came to Paris as the reigning 200m individual medley title-holder. This time there was no gold to defend: Gorbenko finished seventh in the 200 IM final in 2:10.70 after leading for much of the race, Walla Sport reported, fading over the closing metres and unable to repeat her past form on the European stage. Her week also included an early exit in the 50m breaststroke, where she went out in the semi-final.

She wasn't alone. Israel's team left the championships without a single medal, its first blank return at the European Championships since 2018 - a stark line for a programme that has produced multiple continental and world champions in the past two Olympic cycles.

Gorbenko framed the disappointment as part of a longer arc rather than a verdict on where she stands. She described the meet as the opening stretch of her build toward the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, a campaign measured in years rather than a single week in Paris.

Tom Minis, another member of the Israeli squad, struck a more circumspect note about her own progress in Paris. "I didn't know for sure beforehand that this would be the result," she said of a week in which she kept lowering her own numbers.

Minis broke her Israeli record in the 100m backstroke three times over the championships, ONE reported, and her performances were good enough to meet the qualifying standard for the 2027 World Championships in Budapest. She also advanced to the semi-finals of the 200m backstroke.

The team's brightest individual story belonged to Tomer Shuster. The backstroke specialist set two Israeli records during the meet - in the 50m and 100m events - and reached a European final, finishing fifth and just 0.33 seconds outside the medals, according to ONE.
Across the full championships, Israel's swimmers reached 13 semi-finals and five finals, and the team broke four Israeli records in total - three individual marks plus one relay.

Yaakov Tumerkin, the Israeli Swimming Federation's professional director for its elite programme, struck a measured tone in summing up the campaign. He said the team had met its central objectives even though it narrowly missed out on a number of qualifying places it had been targeting.

There was a forward-looking data point buried in the numbers: ten of Israel's 18-strong squad in Paris had already secured qualification for the 2027 World Championships in Budapest, an unusually high strike rate at the first opportunity to do so.

For a federation used to measuring itself in medals, a blank week is hard to spin. But between the records, the World Championship slots already banked and Gorbenko's own insistence that this is merely the start of a four-year cycle, Israeli swimming's leadership is treating Paris as a staging post rather than a setback to be alarmed about.

title: Gashau Ayale takes marathon bronze as Israel win team gold at European Championships
dek: The 29-year-old clocked 2:09:21 in Birmingham to seal an individual medal, and with Tadesse Getahon and Haimro Alame edged Germany by 26 seconds for the team title.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 European Athletics Championships – Men's marathon

body: Gashau Ayale ran himself into an individual bronze medal at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham on Sunday, and then watched two of his teammates confirm the biggest prize of all: gold in the men's marathon team competition.

The race went to Germany's Amanal Petros, who broke the championship record to win outright in 2:09:11, with Italy's Pietro Riva taking silver ten seconds back. Ayale, 29, crossed third in 2:09:21, just ten seconds off the winner and enough to claim the individual bronze.

"It was a difficult race, but the end was good," Ayale said afterwards, according to ONE. "I was relatively behind during the race, but I reached 37km at a good pace and saw their third runner was exhausted, so I identified the opportunity to attack them."

That late move mattered far beyond his own medal. The team result is decided by combining each nation's three fastest finishers, and Ayale's teammates Tadesse Getahon and Haimro Alame came home fifth (2:09:31) and eighth (2:09:45) respectively, giving Israel a combined time of 6:28:37.

Germany's next two scorers, Samuel Fitwi Sibhatu (ninth, 2:09:47) and Richard Ringer (tenth, 2:10:05), left the defending favourites with a cumulative 6:29:03 — 26 seconds slower than Israel, and enough to hand the team title to the Israeli trio.
"This is a huge achievement to win in such a race," Ayale said. "There is great satisfaction here."

Itai Magidi, the professional director overseeing Israel's long-distance running programme, credited the squad's depth for the result. "Fortunately we have depth in the team, so both Tadese Getahun and Aymero Alemayahu managed to bring the team gold at the finish," he said, using the Hebrew-transliterated spellings of Getahon and Alame's names, per ONE.

ONE reports the win extends Israel's run to three straight team golds at the European Athletics Championships, underlining how the country's marathon programme — built largely around Ethiopian-born runners who moved to Israel — has become one of the continent's strongest.

Ayale himself was born in Gojam, Ethiopia, in 1996 to a Beta Israel family and immigrated to Israel at 13, taking up competitive running only at 18. He already holds the Israeli marathon record at 2:04:53, set in Seville in 2024, and won individual bronze at the 2022 European Championships in Munich before finishing 31st at the Paris Olympics in 2024.

Sunday's result gives him a second European Championships medal to go with that Munich bronze, and adds another team gold to an Israeli distance-running group that has quietly built one of the country's most consistent recent success stories in Olympic sport.

title: Raz Hershko falls to Beatriz Souza but salvages bronze at the Lima Grand Prix
dek: The Paris 2024 silver medalist was stopped in the semi-final by Olympic champion Beatriz Souza, then beat Colombia's Brigitte Carabalí by ippon for bronze — with a rematch against Souza now set for August 29 in São Paulo.

verificationSources.label: ONE: רז הרשקו נכנעה לביאטריז סוזה, אך זכתה בארד
Gazeta Esportiva: Spaten Fight Night terá duelo Shogun x Glover no Pacaembu, além de campeãs olímpicas do judô

body: Raz Hershko's pursuit of revenge over Beatriz Souza will have to wait another twelve days. Israel's Olympic silver medalist was beaten by the Brazilian in the semi-final of the +78kg category at the Lima Grand Prix on Sunday, ONE reports, though she recovered to take the bronze medal later in the day.

The draw put Hershko back in front of Souza, the Olympic champion who beat her in the Paris 2024 final, well before the pair's much-anticipated rematch. Souza went on to advance from that semi-final and Hershko was pushed into the repechage bracket, the standard route back to a medal contest in Olympic-style judo.

She took it. In the bronze medal bout, Hershko beat Colombia's Brigitte Carabalí by ippon, the maximum score that ends a contest outright, to secure a podium finish at the Peru leg of the IJF World Tour.

It is a familiar storyline for the two heavyweights. Hershko lost to Souza by waza-ari in the Paris 2024 Olympic final, taking silver in a result that still delivered Israel one of its marquee medals of those Games. Souza, who at roughly 135kg gives away little in physical presence to any rival in the division, has been the standard the rest of the +78kg field has chased ever since.

Hershko has not let that gap close on its own. She won the European title in 2024 and added a bronze at the 2023 World Championships, building a résumé that puts her among the two or three best heavyweights on the planet even without a win over Souza to show for it.

The bronze in Lima keeps that run of podium finishes intact heading into a far bigger stage. On August 29, Hershko and Souza will meet again in a straight rematch of the Olympic final, this time in São Paulo as part of Spaten Fight Night, a major Brazilian combat sports card that is expected to reach millions of television viewers and has built this edition around judo.

The Brazilian promotion has paired the Hershko-Souza rematch with another heavyweight showcase bout, Olympic and world champion Rafaela Silva against Mexico's Prisca Awiti Alcaraz, the 2024 Olympic silver medalist at light-heavyweight, giving the judo card genuine star power alongside its boxing bill at the Pacaembu.

For Hershko, Lima was ultimately a reminder of where she stands: still short of the one win that has eluded her against Souza, but reliably good enough to leave almost every tournament with a medal regardless. São Paulo will be the sternest test yet of whether that gap can finally close.

title: Barcelona reach agreement with Manchester City to sign Rodri
dek: ONE reports the clubs have struck a verbal deal worth roughly €75-76.5m, with paperwork and a medical expected within days as the World Cup's outstanding player prepares to leave the Etihad for Camp Nou.

verificationSources.label: ONE: דיווח - ברצלונה סגרה עם מנצ'סטר סיטי על רודרי

body: Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement in principle for the transfer of Rodri, ONE reports, citing Spanish journalist Fernando Polo, with the clubs said to have struck a verbal deal that leaves only formal documentation and signatures to be completed in the coming days.

It is the resolution of a saga that has run through most of August. Barcelona had gone back to City with a series of improving bids after their opening approach was dismissed as too low, and the two sides are now reported to have finally bridged the gap on both fee and structure.

The exact numbers still vary by outlet. ESPN and Haaretz both put the total package at around €76.5 million, while El Español described it as approximately €75 million in fixed payments plus variables. Other Spanish reporting in recent days has floated a lower base fee closer to €60 million with at least €10 million in add-ons — the kind of discrepancy typical of a deal still being finalised rather than officially announced.

Rodri, 30, had already made his preference clear to Manchester City's hierarchy, formally notifying the club of his wish to leave for Barcelona. ONE reports that Barcelona secured the player's personal consent to the move roughly two weeks ago and spent the intervening period working to meet City's financial demands, with talks accelerating sharply over the past week.

Real Madrid had long been considered the frontrunners for Rodri, particularly in the period around the World Cup, but those talks are reported to have broken down. Barcelona coach Hansi Flick is said to have played a decisive role instead, personally calling Rodri to lay out the tactical project and the central role he would play in a Camp Nou midfield.

Rodri arrives with his stock at an all-time high. He was the outstanding player as Spain won the 2026 World Cup, beating Argentina 1-0 in the final, and he already holds the 2024 Ballon d'Or — the first Manchester City player to win it.

Barcelona are expected to sign him to a four-year contract, with the move set to become official once all three parties — Rodri, City and Barcelona — complete the necessary paperwork, a process ONE's report suggests could wrap up as soon as next week.

At Camp Nou he would join an already crowded and talented midfield featuring Pedri, Gavi, Dani Olmo, Fermín López, Marc Bernal and Frenkie de Jong, giving Flick one of the deepest central-midfield pools in Europe.

The move would end a seven-year spell at Manchester City that began with his 2019 arrival from Atlético Madrid. Rodri became the tactical foundation of Pep Guardiola's midfield, winning the Champions League in 2023 and four Premier League titles among 23 trophies at the club.

Spanish media have framed the deal as a significant prestige win for Barcelona, who see landing the World Cup's best player — and doing so ahead of Real Madrid — as a statement of intent as the Catalan club look to rebuild around a proven winner just seven years after he left Spain in the first place.

title: Dia Saba's double sinks Erzurumspor 3-0 as Liam Hermash suffers 8-0 mauling in Austria
dek: Two contrasting nights for Israelis abroad: a Süper Lig brace for Dia Saba in Amedspor's win over Erzurumspor, and a heavy rout for Liam Hermash's Grazer AK against league leaders Rapid Wien.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Hermash signs for Grazer AK

body: It was a night of contrasts for Israelis playing abroad this weekend, as Dia Saba wrote himself into Amedspor's history books in Turkey while Liam Hermash finished on the wrong end of one of Austria's most one-sided results of the season.

Saba, the Arab-Israeli international from Majd al-Krum, scored twice as Amedspor beat Erzurumspor SK 3-0 in the Süper Lig, striking in the 53rd and 62nd minutes before Gökhan Gül added a third in the 70th. Saba started the game and was withdrawn in the 77th minute, his afternoon's work long since done.

The win was one of the opening results of Amedspor's maiden Süper Lig campaign, the Diyarbakır club's first ever season in Turkey's top flight. Saba signed for the club this summer despite calls from some supporters to boycott him over his ties to the Israeli national team, but his performances have quickly won fans over.

Saba, 33, led the Israeli Premier League scoring charts with 24 goals in the 2017-18 season and has earned 13 caps and three goals for Israel since his senior debut in 2018, with previous spells including Maccabi Netanya and Bnei Sakhnin.
In Austria, it was a far grimmer evening for Hermash, who started for Grazer AK as they were routed 8-0 by league leaders Rapid Wien at the Allianz Stadion in Vienna's Hütteldorf district.

Rapid were already 5-0 up at the interval. Ercan Kara struck twice inside the opening quarter of an hour, Tonni Adamsen scored four times either side of half-time, and further goals from Cvetkovic and Demir completed the humiliation.

It was the heaviest defeat suffered at the Allianz Stadion since the ground opened a decade ago and ranks among the biggest wins in Austrian Bundesliga history, lifting Rapid above LASK and to the top of the table after three rounds.

For Hermash, on loan at GAK from Maccabi Haifa after a season out on loan at Moldovan side Sheriff Tiraspol, it was a harsh introduction to the gulf in quality at the top of Austrian football - and GAK's second defeat in three league matches to open the campaign.
Two very different weekends, then, for two of Israeli football's exports: one celebrated on the terraces of Diyarbakır, the other left to regroup in Graz.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv complete stunning 2-1 comeback to set up first-ever Toto Cup final derby with Maccabi Tel Aviv
dek: Daniel Daffa's double in second-half stoppage time floored ten-man Ironi Kiryat Shmona, sealing a first-ever all-Tel Aviv Toto Cup final after Hélio Varela's early strike had already sent Maccabi Tel Aviv past Maccabi Netanya.
body: For the first time in the competition's history, the Toto Cup final will be a Tel Aviv derby. Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Tel Aviv both booked their places with contrasting semifinal wins on Sunday night, setting up a meeting between Israel's two biggest Tel Aviv clubs when the final is played in December.

Hapoel's win was by far the wilder of the two. Ironi Kiryat Shmona stunned the visitors by going ahead inside six minutes through Peruvian forward Adrian Ugarriza, who scored a club-record 19 league goals for the northern side last season.

Kiryat Shmona's task got even tougher in the 30th minute, when midfielder Ophir Benbenisti was shown a second yellow card and sent off, leaving the hosts to defend a one-goal lead with ten men for well over an hour.

They very nearly pulled it off. Hapoel could not find a way through until deep into second-half stoppage time, when Daniel Daffa struck twice in the space of two minutes - in the 90+7th and 90+9th minutes - turning a ten-man rearguard performance into a 2-1 defeat and sending Hapoel through to the final.

Maccabi Tel Aviv's route was far more straightforward. Hélio Varela, the Cape Verde international winger named in his country's squad for the 2026 World Cup, settled the semifinal against Maccabi Netanya with the only goal of the game in the 17th minute, sending the reigning State Cup holders through 1-0.

Maccabi arrive at the final in imperious form. They beat Hapoel Beer Sheva to lift the Israel State Cup at the end of the 2025/26 season and then beat the same opponents 3-1 in the season-opening Super Cup, the Aluf HaAlufim, going unbeaten into the new campaign.

The derby angle adds extra spice to a fixture that already carries recent history. Hapoel ended a near-12-year winless run against Maccabi in the league in January 2026, coming from behind with two stoppage-time goals to win 2-1 - a result that led to Maccabi sacking their head coach within 24 hours. The two sides met again in May and shared the points in a 1-1 draw.

Now, for the first time, the clubs will meet with the Toto Cup itself on the line rather than league points or a State Cup tie. Both share Bloomfield Stadium as their home ground, adding another layer to a fixture Israeli media are already billing as an unprecedented occasion for the competition.
No exact date for the final has been confirmed. Israeli outlets report only that it is scheduled for December, once the Ligat Ha'al programme pauses for the international break.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Netanya 1-0 to reach Toto Cup final, Miller: 'We must add players before Lugano'
dek: Helio Varela's early goal sent Kenny Miller's side into a derby final with Hapoel Tel Aviv, but the coach used the win to press for signings before Thursday's Conference League play-off opener in Switzerland.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC - official match report

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv booked their place in the Toto Cup final with a 1-0 win over Maccabi Netanya on Sunday, but head coach Kenny Miller used his post-match remarks to press the club's board for reinforcements before Thursday's Conference League play-off opener against Lugano.

Helio Varela settled the semi-final in the 17th minute at Netanya, converting a team move involving Sisoko, Sayed Abu Farhi and Dor Peretz, and it proved enough to send Maccabi through to a Tel Aviv derby final against Hapoel Tel Aviv, with both clubs winning their semi-finals on the same day.

"We must add several players. We will arrive ready for Lugano," Miller said afterwards, according to ONE, making clear that Sunday's cup progress does not paper over gaps in his squad heading into a demanding European week.

The line echoed comments made by captain Dor Peretz before the game, who told the club's official channels: "We have a very high-quality and very good squad here, but yes, this team needs reinforcements and a refresh with a few more players who can push us forward, so that we can compete for all the trophies and in all the competitions."

Miller made four changes from his strongest available XI for the Netanya tie, with Ali Kamara out through injury and Roy Revivo suspended, underlining how thin his options already are before a squad that must also cope with Europe and the league.

Maccabi's need for depth is sharpened by the expected departure of Abu Farhi, the 20-year-old forward who played in Netanya and is closing in on a reported $6 million move to MLS side Colorado Rapids, with the transfer said to be awaiting formal league approval. Abu Farhi is said to remain focused on his current commitments while the deal is finalised.

Thursday's fixture in Switzerland is the first leg of the Conference League play-off round, with the return leg at home on August 27. Maccabi dropped into the Conference League after losing 4-3 on aggregate to CSKA Sofia in the Europa League qualifying play-off, having lost the first leg 3-0 at home before a 3-1 second-leg win in Bulgaria was not enough to turn the tie around.

Netanya, for their part, exit the Toto Cup at the semi-final stage but head coach Roni Levi said he too is looking to strengthen his squad, telling reporters he wants to add "another defender, fullback or winger" before the transfer window closes.

The Toto Cup final between Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Tel Aviv is scheduled for later in the year, with Miller stressing his side will not treat the season's traditional curtain-raiser lightly. "This is not a game to throw away or another warm-up match for the league. We want to win and be in the final," he had said ahead of the semi-final.

For now, though, Miller's focus is squarely on Lugano, a tie Maccabi will enter aware that failure to strengthen before the European window shuts could leave a well-drilled but stretched squad short of numbers just as the season starts to bite.

title: Kiryat Shmona 1-2 Hapoel Tel Aviv: Barda says 'we love drama' after stoppage-time turnaround
dek: Daniel Dappa struck twice deep into stoppage time to send Hapoel Tel Aviv into a first-ever Tel Aviv derby final in the Toto Cup, and coach Elyaniv Barda admitted even he needed convincing.

verificationSources.label: Sport1 - match report and goal detail
Haaretz - both semifinal results and derby final confirmation

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv needed two goals in the last two minutes of a marathon stoppage time to stay alive in the Toto Cup, and coach Elyaniv Barda was still shaking his head about it afterwards. "It seems we love drama," he said. "I believed we could win."

Ironi Kiryat Shmona had led since the sixth minute through striker Adrián Ugarriza and looked set to hold on, especially after going down to ten men when defender Ofir Benvenishty was shown a second yellow card in the 30th minute. For long stretches Hapoel dominated possession without troubling the scoreboard.

The breakthrough finally came in the seventh minute of stoppage time, when Daniel Dappa headed home to level the score. Barely two minutes later, with the clock reading 90+9, Dappa struck again, turning in a shot from Douglas Awosso to complete the turnaround and seal a 2-1 win.

"We did that excellently in the second half, but the ball just refused to enter," Barda said of his side's prolonged pressure before the late double. He was generous in praise of his matchwinner: "I'm very happy for him. He works very hard all week, stayed humble, he's still a kid and knows through hard work he'll earn his minutes."

The Hapoel coach also aimed a pointed complaint at the officiating, arguing the added time on the board did not reflect how long Kiryat Shmona spent with ten men managing the clock. "They made a law against time-wasting and need to implement it," he said. "It's nice to give yellows, but you need to control what happens on the pitch. In my opinion, they should have added 15 minutes."
He tempered the criticism by acknowledging the logic of Kiryat Shmona's approach: "It bothered me a bit, but it's legitimate when a team stays with ten players and wants to preserve the result."

On the losing side, Kiryat Shmona coach Shai Barda was left to make his own case to the officials, questioning several refereeing decisions in the closing stages of a match his side had controlled for long periods despite the numerical disadvantage.

The result sends Hapoel Tel Aviv into the Toto Cup final to face fierce rivals Maccabi Tel Aviv, who beat Maccabi Netanya 1-0 in the other semifinal through an early Leo Arella goal. It will be the first Tel Aviv derby ever played in a Toto Cup final.

title: Turkey beat Israel's cadets 72-61 as group stage closes, Serbia awaits in last 16
dek: A big fourth quarter from the hosts denied Israel's under-16 women after a spirited third-quarter fightback, sending the team into Tuesday's knockout game against Serbia.
body: Israel's under-16 women's national team, the cadets, closed out the group stage of the FIBA U16 Women's EuroBasket 2026 Division B in Konya with a 72-61 defeat to hosts Turkey on Sunday, finishing third in Group B.
Turkey set the early tone, opening up a lead of as much as 12 points during the first half as Israel struggled to find rhythm against the host nation in front of a home crowd.

The cadets responded with their best spell of the game in the third quarter, clawing their way back into contention and going into the final period trailing by just a single point, 49-48, according to ONE.
Turkey had the answers when it mattered most, though, taking control of the fourth quarter and outscoring Israel 24-12 down the stretch to pull away for the 72-61 win.

Michal Abuderham was Israel's standout performer, finishing with 21 points and 10 rebounds. Rona Tzalal added 13 points and three assists, while Ella Maoz Bardea contributed 10 points and five assists, per ONE and IBBA, the Israel Basketball Association.

The result left Israel with a 1-2 record in Group B. The team had opened the tournament with a lopsided win over Italy before losing to Latvia 74-63, IBBA reported, and now falls to Turkey to round out the group phase.
Despite the third-place finish in the group, the cadets advance to the knockout rounds, where they are set to face Serbia in the round of 16 on Tuesday.

It is the second defeat of the tournament for the young Israeli side, but the group stage has shown a squad capable of trading blows with stronger opposition, with the third-quarter comeback against Turkey offering encouragement heading into the knockout phase.

title: Lens 1-0 PSG: Thauvin strike earns ten-man Lens a shock Trophée des Champions triumph
dek: Florian Thauvin's first-half goal was enough for Lens to end Paris Saint-Germain's reign over the French Super Cup, the home side holding out for over an hour with ten men to lift the Trophée des Champions for the first time.
body: Ten-man Lens produced one of the biggest upsets French football has seen in years on Sunday night, beating holders Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 at Stade Bollaert-Delelis to lift the Trophée des Champions for the first time in the club's history.

Florian Thauvin settled the French Super Cup in the 32nd minute, pouncing on a loose ball after Matthieu Udol's shot was scrambled away and coolly slotting past PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov from close range.

The celebrations had barely died down before Lens were reduced to ten men. Seven minutes after the opener, defender Kyllian Antonio was shown a straight red card by referee Jérémie Pignard for a reckless, high tackle on PSG midfielder Maghnes Akliouche - a decision that infuriated the home camp, with Thauvin among those remonstrating with officials on the touchline.

From there, Luis Enrique's PSG, the reigning European and Ligue 1 champions, dominated the ball and pushed men forward but could not find a way through a deep, disciplined Lens defence that held firm for the remainder of normal time.

Lens qualified for the fixture as holders of the Coupe de France after last season's cup triumph, while PSG arrived as Ligue 1 champions - the traditional pairing for the season-opening French Super Cup.

PSG's frustration turned to farce in the 87th minute when Nuno Mendes was sent off in turn, catching Lens wing-back Michal Skoras with an elbow off the ball, leaving both sides briefly with ten men for the closing stages.

Lens saw out the remaining minutes to spark wild scenes at Bollaert-Delelis, sealing a first Trophée des Champions triumph in the club's history despite playing the vast majority of the match a man short.
It was a chastening opening statement of the new season for PSG, who were unable to convert their spells of pressure into clear chances and finish the game with two players sent off to Lens's one.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv presses on with talks to bring Gabi Kanichowsky home from Ferencvaros
dek: ONE reports the yellow-and-blue are still working to close a gap of roughly €500,000 with the Hungarian champions-turned-runners-up over the midfielder's return, more than a year after he left on a free transfer.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have not given up on bringing Gabi Kanichowsky back to Bloomfield, with ONE reporting that talks with Ferencváros over the midfielder have dragged on for more than six weeks and remain unresolved.

The Israeli champions opened the conversation with the Hungarian club in late June, ONE reports, hoping to undo what the club itself now regards as a mistake: letting Kanichowsky leave last year rather than meeting his wage demands on a new contract.

The sticking point is money. Ferencváros initially wanted around €2.5 million for a player who cost them nothing 13 months ago, and while that figure has since eased to roughly €2 million according to the report, the two sides are still described as far apart.

Adding to the complexity, ONE reports that Kanichowsky himself would face an early-return tax penalty of about €250,000 under Israeli law if he leaves Hungary before completing a set period abroad — a cost that would need to be factored into any deal.

Maccabi are said to be watching Ferencváros's Europa League play-off tie against Trabzonspor closely, viewing the Hungarian club's continental fortunes as a potential factor in whether they eventually soften their stance on Kanichowsky.

The player himself is reported to be open to a return to Israel, but any deal would require Maccabi to commit to a long-term contract — the very sticking point that pushed him to Hungary in the first place.

Kanichowsky joined Ferencváros as a free agent in July 2025 after four seasons back at Maccabi Tel Aviv, where he made well over 100 appearances following his academy days at the club and a formative loan spell path through Hapoel Petah Tikva, Hapoel Acre and Maccabi Netanya.

His one season in Budapest ended with mixed fortunes: he won the Magyar Kupa with Ferencváros, but the club's seven-year grip on the Hungarian league title slipped to Győri ETO, who finished top with Ferencváros second.

There is also a personnel thread running through the saga. Maccabi's new sporting director, Steven Van Herren, arrives at the club from Ferencváros, while Robbie Keane — who led Maccabi Tel Aviv to the title before departing for Ferencváros in 2024 — left the Hungarian club earlier this year after 16 months in charge.
For now, ONE frames the situation as a live negotiation rather than a done deal, with the gap between the clubs still, in the outlet's words, complex to bridge.

title: David Roddy lands in Israel: "It will take time to adjust"
dek: The American forward touched down at Ben Gurion Airport to begin his first season with Hapoel Jerusalem after four years bouncing between six NBA franchises.

verificationSources.label: Hapoel Jerusalem official site - David Roddy signing

body: David Roddy touched down at Ben Gurion Airport in the middle of the night between Sunday and Monday, the latest piece of Hapoel Jerusalem's rebuilt roster to arrive in the country ahead of the 2026/27 season.

The 25-year-old American forward, who spent four seasons bouncing between six different NBA franchises, is starting an entirely new chapter: his first taste of European basketball. He follows fellow American Jared Harper, who landed in Israel earlier in the buildup to the new campaign.

"It will take time to adjust to playing outside the US," Roddy admitted on arrival, according to ONE. But he was quick to frame the move in ambitious terms, adding: "The main goal for us is to win the Eurocup and qualify for the Euroleague."
He described himself as a do-it-all competitor, telling reporters he can pass, rebound, shoot and defend, and that he is ready to do whatever coach Sasa Obradovic and the team need to win games.

Roddy, listed at 1.96m, was the 23rd overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, selected by Philadelphia before being dealt to Memphis on draft night. Over four NBA seasons he appeared in roughly 180 games across the Grizzlies, Suns, Hawks, Rockets and other stops, averaging 6.3 points and 2.9 rebounds per game, according to Hapoel Jerusalem's official announcement. He also logged time in the G League, averaging 14.2 points, 5.7 rebounds and 3.5 assists across 53 games there.
He played his college basketball at Colorado State before entering the draft.

The deal with Jerusalem, reported by Sport1 to be worth roughly a million dollars for the season, was finalized during NBA Summer League action in Las Vegas and makes Roddy the fourth import signed under Obradovic this off-season.

"I'm excited to join Hapoel Jerusalem and open this new chapter," Roddy said in the club's official announcement of the signing. "I've heard so many great things about the club and the fans. The conversations with coach Sasha Obradovic made me feel this is the right place. I'm coming to work hard and do everything needed to help the team win."

Obradovic, who took over in Jerusalem after a long European coaching career that included AS Monaco, Crvena Zvezda and Alba Berlin, welcomed the addition: "We're very happy David is joining the Hapoel family. He's an experienced, versatile, physical player who can impact the game in multiple ways. He brings toughness, energy and competitive mentality — exactly what we want."
With Roddy now on the ground, Hapoel Jerusalem's foreign contingent for the new season is taking shape as the club builds toward a Eurocup campaign under its new coaching staff.

title: Makhachev breaks UFC win-streak record, Dern retains title as Noquaout dissects UFC 330
dek: Yaniv Kaminski and Olga Rubin, joined by guest Uri Shokron, break down a loaded UFC 330 card on the latest episode of ONE's Hebrew-language MMA podcast.
body: The morning after UFC 330 delivered a record and a title defense inside the same five rounds of action, the hosts of ONE's Hebrew-language MMA show "Noquaout" sat down to pick through all of it. Yaniv Kaminski and Olga Rubin were joined by guest Uri Shokron for an episode built around one of the promotion's biggest cards of the year.

The headline result from Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena on August 15 was Islam Makhachev's unanimous-decision win over Ian Machado Garry, which kept his UFC welterweight title and stretched his winning run to 17 consecutive fights. That mark pushed him past Anderson Silva's long-standing record of 16 straight UFC victories, a number that had stood since 2012.

Judges scored the five-round main event 49-46, 49-46 and 48-47 in Makhachev's favor. The Dagestani fighter, who moved up from lightweight to add the welterweight belt, again leaned on his wrestling to control the Irishman over the distance rather than finish inside the cage.

On the podcast, the panel worked through what the performance meant for Makhachev's standing at the top of the sport and how Machado Garry's night looked from close range - a measured, grinding fight rather than a highlight-reel statement, but one with genuine historical weight attached to it.

The co-main event got its own segment. Mackenzie Dern defended her women's strawweight title with a matching unanimous decision over Gillian Robertson, also scored 49-46, 49-46 and 48-47, and the hosts broke down the keys to a win that kept her championship reign intact.

Beyond the two title fights, the episode looked ahead. The panel touched on Jean Silva's newly confirmed next assignment - a featherweight main event against Yair Rodriguez at Noche UFC in Glendale, Arizona on September 12, a fight billed as a step toward a title shot for the winner.

The hosts also spent time on UFC flyweight champion Joshua Van, whose frustration with the promotion's booking pace has been a recurring talking point in MMA media, and what it could mean for his next title defense.

"Noquaout" is ONE's regular Hebrew MMA podcast, built around Kaminski and Rubin walking Israeli fight fans through the biggest UFC cards as they happen, with guest voices like Shokron brought in for the bigger nights. The new episode is up now on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

title: Yaakov Shahar: Anan Khalaili is a great pride for Maccabi Haifa
dek: Club owner and CEO salute the winger's journey from the academy to a record-breaking move to Crystal Palace

verificationSources.label: Ynetnews - Crystal Palace unveils Anan Khalaili in record transfer for Israeli player

body: Maccabi Haifa's leadership took a moment on Saturday to salute one of its own, as owner and president Yaakov Shahar and chief executive Itzik Ovadia both issued statements celebrating Anan Khalaili's move to Crystal Palace, the biggest transfer in Israeli football history.

"Anan is a great source of pride for Maccabi Haifa," Shahar said, according to ONE. "We saw him grow here as a child, develop as a player and person, and fulfil a dream through talent, hard work, humility and outstanding character. I wish him continued success and am certain Anan will continue to represent himself, his family, Israeli football and Maccabi Haifa with honour."

Khalaili, a 21-year-old winger from a mixed Jewish-Arab neighbourhood in Haifa, came up through the Maccabi Haifa academy and made 30 senior appearances for the club before leaving for Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise in 2024, where he went on to make 71 appearances and become a Belgian champion.

CEO Itzik Ovadia framed the transfer as vindication of the club's academy philosophy. "Anan's story reflects what Maccabi Haifa believes in — years of investment in player development, sports values, patience, professionalism and faith in our approach," he said. "Anan's move to Crystal Palace is an emotional moment for the entire Maccabi Haifa family — the coaches who guided him, youth department staff, teammates, club employees and supporters who witnessed his first steps."

Crystal Palace completed the signing from Union Saint-Gilloise this week in a deal reported by British and Israeli media at roughly £21 million (about €24.5m/$28m), a fee that makes Khalaili the most expensive Israeli player ever, well above the roughly £15m Sevilla paid for Munas Dabbur in 2019.

The move to south London capped a turbulent summer for the winger. A proposed transfer to Inter Milan collapsed about a month earlier after Khalaili failed to receive medical clearance from the Italian club, before Crystal Palace stepped in to complete a five-year deal.

For Maccabi Haifa, the sale is as much a marketing moment as a financial one — proof, in the words of its two most senior figures, that a club competing outside Europe's major leagues can still produce and sell a player to the Premier League for a record fee.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv thrash Hapoel Tel Aviv 3-0 as Liga Naarim A season kicks off
dek: Aidan Sisei scored twice in the Tel Aviv derby as Maccabi Haifa, Hapoel Beer Sheva and Hapoel Hadera also opened their 2026/27 Liga Naarim A campaigns on Saturday, according to ONE.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv opened their Liga Naarim A season in style on Saturday, brushing aside city rivals Hapoel Tel Aviv 3-0 in the derby fixture that headlined round one of Israel's top youth league for the 2010 age group, ONE reported.

Aidan Sisei did the early damage with a first-half double, and Amir Alnakib added a second-half penalty to complete the scoring as Maccabi sent a statement of intent to the rest of the division on opening weekend.
It was one of eight matches played across the country as the 2026/27 Liga Naarim A campaign got under way, with two further fixtures still to come.

Maccabi Haifa also made a winning start, beating Hapoel Kiryat Shmona 2-0 at home. Defender Ben Landau scored both goals and played the full 90 minutes, an eye-catching return for a centre-back on the opening day of the season.

It was a tougher afternoon for Hapoel Beer Sheva, who lost 3-1 to Beit Yehuda Tel Aviv despite taking the lead through captain Moussa Mousrathi. Ariel Hagg drew Beit Yehuda level before Bar Harosh's double turned the match in the hosts' favour.
Hapoel Hadera also began the season with a defeat, beaten 3-0 by Hapoel Naof Hagalil. Gili Lazarean, Itay Imran and Ahmad Hindawi were on the scoresheet for the winners.

Elsewhere in round one, Hapoel Raanana had a bye, while Beitar Tubruk host Maccabi Netanya and Maccabi Ashdod welcome Beitar Jerusalem in fixtures scheduled for August 16-17 to complete the opening round.

Liga Naarim A sits at the top of Israel's structured pathway for young players born in 2010, feeding talent toward senior academy squads and, ultimately, first-team football at clubs across the country. An eye-catching opening round — headlined by a big derby win for Maccabi Tel Aviv and a rare defensive brace from Maccabi Haifa's Landau — offers an early look at who could break through this season.

title: Tirante stuns Djokovic 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 to reach Cincinnati third round
dek: Argentina's world No. 50 rallies from a set down to end a physically labouring Djokovic's 10-match Cincinnati winning streak in a gruelling second-round battle.
body: Novak Djokovic's return to hard courts lasted barely two and a half sets before it turned into one of the biggest shocks of the season. The world No. 5 was beaten 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 by Argentina's Thiago Agustín Tirante in the second round of the Cincinnati Open, a defeat that took two hours and 44 minutes to complete and left the Serbian visibly struggling in the Ohio heat.

Djokovic started as the player everyone expected, breaking early and cruising through the first set 6-2. But Tirante, ranked 50th in the world, broke back in the sixth game of the second set and never let go of the momentum, closing out the second 6-4 before repeating the trick in the decider.

It was Djokovic's first match since his Wimbledon semi-final defeat to Jannik Sinner, and by the closing games he looked a shadow of the player who dismantled that first set. Reports from Cincinnati described him as physically drained as the contest crept toward the three-hour mark, unable to summon the extra gear that has bailed him out of similar situations for two decades.

The numbers make the loss sting even more. Since 2005, Djokovic had gone 355-13 after winning the opening set at Masters 1000 level — a win rate above 96 percent. Tirante becomes only the 14th player ever to complete that comeback against him, and just the second ranked outside the world's top 30 to do it, joining Argentina's Diego Serra, who managed the same feat back in 2006.

The defeat also snaps a 10-match winning streak Djokovic had built at the Cincinnati event, a tournament he has dominated for years. There was an odd historical footnote attached to the same day: Djokovic equalled Feliciano López's record of 139 career ATP Masters 1000 main-draw appearances, a milestone overshadowed entirely by the result.

For Tirante, it is the signature win of a career that has been quietly building all season. The 25-year-old from La Plata, a former world No. 1 junior who won the French Open boys' doubles title and the Orange Bowl singles crown in 2019, has pushed deep into the draws at the Madrid and Rome Masters this year and reached ATP semi-finals in Båstad and Houston.
The win lifted him into Cincinnati's top 50 bracket with a fresh career-high ranking, and he now moves on to face Spain's Martín Landaluce for a place in the fourth round.

For Djokovic, the loss raises fresh questions about his physical condition just weeks before the US Open, his last realistic shot at a Grand Slam title this season after the Wimbledon setback against Sinner. A second-round Masters exit to an unseeded opponent is a rare occurrence for a player who has built his career on precisely these kinds of straight-forward assignments turning routine.

title: CF Montreal bans two fans over antisemitic abuse of Dor Turgeman
dek: The club confirms indefinite bans and restricts its ultras section as the fallout continues from "death to Israel" chants aimed at the New England Revolution striker on August 1.
body: CF Montreal announced on Friday that two supporters have been permanently barred from Saputo Stadium for their part in the antisemitic abuse directed at Dor Turgeman during the club's MLS match against New England Revolution on August 1, ONE reports.

The club also confirmed that the supporters' section identified as responsible will have its privileges suspended indefinitely, and that the wider ultras group was stripped of its usual banners and drums for Friday's home game against D.C. United, according to ONE and corroborated by the Quebec daily La Presse.

Turgeman, the 22-year-old Ashdod-born forward, was targeted with chants of "free Palestine" and "death to Israel" from the home end shortly after putting New England 2-0 up in the 36th minute of what finished a 2-2 draw. He responded by cupping a hand to his ear and pacing the touchline in front of the jeering section, an image that was widely shared afterwards.

In its statement, CF Montreal said "antisemitism, racism and all forms of hate are not acceptable in Montreal, at Saputo Stadium or in our community," and pledged to "continue its efforts to identify any additional person involved" and permanently ban anyone confirmed to have taken part in antisemitic or other discriminatory behaviour.
The club added it had opened conversations with local Jewish community organisations and planned expanded educational programming and heightened security at Saputo Stadium going forward.

New England Revolution condemned the abuse in the immediate aftermath and said it had reported the incident to Major League Soccer, which launched a joint investigation with the club into the conduct of the fans involved.

Turgeman joined New England from Maccabi Tel Aviv a year ago in a deal reported at roughly $6 million plus $1 million in add-ons, and scored in each of his first three MLS appearances. He has 17 caps and two goals for Israel's senior national team.

The incident is the latest in a string of antisemitic episodes involving Israeli athletes abroad since the war that began in October 2023, and CF Montreal's punishment marks one of the more concrete disciplinary responses from an MLS club to date.
