title: German teenager Johannes Liebmann shatters 1500m freestyle world record in 14:26.79
dek: The 19-year-old became the first man in history under 14:30 for the distance, ripping 3.88 seconds off Bobby Finke's mark at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.
body: Johannes Liebmann produced one of the swims of the year on Saturday, shattering the men's 1500m freestyle world record at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris to become the first man in history to go under 14 minutes 30 seconds for the distance.

The 19-year-old German touched in 14:26.79, slicing 3.88 seconds off the previous world mark of 14:30.67 set by American Bobby Finke when he won Olympic gold in the event at the Paris Games two years ago.

Liebmann led from the opening lengths, briefly pressed by Hungary's Zalán Sárkány before pulling clear over the middle of the race. He closed with a final 100 metres of 56.18 seconds, splitting 28.79 and 27.39 to power away from the field in the closing strokes.
Sárkány took silver, 12.66 seconds adrift, with Germany's Oliver Klemet claiming bronze — a German 1-3 either side of the Hungarian on the podium.
It is a genuinely historic moment for the sport: the last time the men's 1500m freestyle world record fell at a European Championships was in 1927, when Sweden's Arne Borg set the mark.

The world record capped a remarkable weekend for Liebmann, who arrived at the Saint-Denis pool already the new European champion over 800m freestyle after winning that final in a European record of 7:37.59 — shaving 0.35 seconds off the mark he had set himself in Stockholm in April. He was the first German to win that title since it was added to the championship programme in Eindhoven in 2008.

The double gold underlines Germany's rise as a distance-swimming power, built around the training group at SC Magdeburg that has produced a string of European-record holders in the men's freestyle events over the past two years.

The record swim came in the pool built for the Paris 2024 Olympics at the Saint-Denis aquatics centre, now hosting its first major long-course championships since the Games and serving as the primary venue for the 2026 European Aquatics Championships.

Finke's mark had stood for barely two years, one of several Olympic swimming records now under threat as a new generation of distance swimmers targets the deep end of the record book. Liebmann's time leaves him as the outright benchmark in an event where sub-14:30 swimming had, until Saturday, never been done.

It was Liebmann's second gold of the championships after he won the 800m freestyle in a European record of 7:37.59.
It is the first time since 1927 (Arne Borg) that a men's 1500m freestyle world record has been broken at the European Championships.
The race was held at the Saint-Denis Olympic Aquatics Centre, built for the Paris 2024 Olympics.

title: Alavés beat 10-man Getafe 3-0 to open La Liga season
dek: Nahuel Tenaglia, Mariano Díaz and Mikel Rodríguez struck at Mendizorrotza after Kiko Femenía's first-half red card left Getafe a man down for the entire second half.
body: Alavés opened their La Liga campaign with a comfortable 3-0 win over Getafe at Mendizorrotza on Saturday, a scoreline that flattered the hosts only in its margin but not in the balance of the contest once Getafe were reduced to ten men before half-time.

The visitors' afternoon unravelled in the 42nd minute when defender Kiko Femenía was shown a direct red card, leaving Getafe to play the entire second half a man light in front of a Mendizorrotza crowd of 13,923.

Even with the extra man, Alavés could not force the breakthrough straight away. The hosts probed patiently through a stubborn Getafe rearguard for the best part of an hour without finding a way through.
The deadlock finally broke in the 73rd minute, when Nahuel Tenaglia rose to head Alavés in front, rewarding the home side's growing control of the game.

Getafe, chasing an equaliser that never looked likely, instead conceded twice more in a chaotic finish. Mariano Díaz turned in a second in stoppage time — a landmark moment for the former Real Madrid striker, who according to Spanish outlet OKDiario had not scored in a match in more than four years.

Mariano, a product of the Real Madrid academy who won three La Liga titles and two Champions League crowns with the club before moving on, joined Alavés last year and had endured an injury-disrupted, goal-shy spell since arriving at Mendizorrotza.
Mikel Rodríguez completed the rout in the 94th minute, turning a narrow lead into a lopsided final score that will read better than the game for long stretches actually played.
Before kick-off, both sets of supporters observed a minute's silence in tribute to Alavés season-ticket holders who have died and for the victims of a recent earthquake in Colombia.

The result gives Alavés a perfect start to the 2026-27 season, while Getafe will look to regroup after finishing the opening weekend with a red card, a heavy defeat and a mountain to climb after conceding twice in the closing minutes.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva beat Hapoel Petah Tikva 1-0 as comedian's son Koriat scores derby winner
dek: Yonatan Koriat, son of comedian and TV host Shlomi Koriat, struck the only goal as Maccabi edged their crosstown rivals in the opening round of Israel's Under-17 premier youth league.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Petah Tikva Youth (Facebook) - Yonatan Koriat name check

body: Petah Tikva's two clubs kicked off their Under-17 seasons with local bragging rights on the line on Saturday, and it was Maccabi who came out on top, edging Hapoel Petah Tikva 1-0 in the opening round of Israel's premier Ne'arim Alef league.

The only goal of the derby, played at Maccabi's home ground, arrived in the 60th minute and had a familiar name attached to it. Yonatan Koriat, the teenage son of well-known Israeli comedian and television personality Shlomi Koriat, received the ball in the centre of the box and lifted a precise finish over the goalkeeper and into the net.

Maccabi had dominated for long spells without reward. They controlled possession through the first half but could not find a breakthrough, and Hapoel almost snatched the lead against the run of play just before the interval. Eyal Barak was picked out by a cross from Harel Harari and got in behind the Maccabi defence, only for goalkeeper Rotem Ginat to produce a smart save to keep the scores level at the break.

Maccabi pressed on in the second half and eventually turned their control into Koriat's winner just after the hour mark. They almost doubled their advantage deep into stoppage time when Ophir Levi's effort crashed off the crossbar in the 90th minute, with Hapoel unable to find an equaliser despite a late push forward.

According to ONE, which reported the result, the win gives Maccabi a perfect start as the top flight of the youth game returned for the 2026/27 campaign this weekend. Shlomi Koriat, the scorer's father, is a familiar face on Israeli television as a comedian and presenter and lives in Petah Tikva, adding a human-interest hook to what was otherwise a tightly fought local derby between academy sides.

Both clubs now turn to round two. Maccabi Petah Tikva will look to build on the derby win with an away trip to Maccabi Haifa, while Hapoel Petah Tikva, still searching for their first points of the season, host Beitar Tubruk at home.

body: Daniel Chazan, the Israeli-American businessman and player agent who bought into Hapoel Haifa's basketball club less than a year ago, is now negotiating the terms of his own exit, ONE reported.

According to the report, Chazan and Hapoel Haifa's management are in talks over a departure agreement, with the 33-year-old set to leave a club he joined in November 2025 as a co-owner holding close to a 50 percent stake.

It is a strikingly similar pattern to how Chazan arrived at Haifa in the first place. He had held an equivalent co-ownership role at Ironi Nahariya, another National League club, but walked out after a dispute over foreign-player recruitment — Chazan says his agreement gave him sole authority over signing overseas players within an annual budget of $400,000, and that Nahariya breached it by releasing and signing players without his approval.

When he moved to Haifa, Chazan brought a marquee piece of business with him: guard Ryan Turell, the Yeshiva University alumnus who built his reputation in the United States as a trailblazing Orthodox Jewish professional player before continuing his career in Israel. ONE reports Turell, too, is now expected to leave Hapoel Haifa.

Chazan's arrival at Haifa was itself part of a wider reshuffling of the club's ownership. Hapoel Haifa dropped out of the top-flight Premier League and now play in the second-tier National League, and the club has changed hands again since Chazan signed on — in January, 20-year-old Adir Sabag acquired an 80 percent stake in the club's management company, backed by the Nasdaq-listed defence-tech firm VisionWave Holdings, a deal that drew heavy scrutiny in the Israeli press over Sabag's background and the source of the funding.
Neither Chazan nor the club has commented publicly on the departure terms, and no financial details of the exit have been disclosed.

For a club that promised an ambitious rebuild after relegation, the churn at ownership level — three ownership configurations inside a single year — threatens to overshadow whatever is happening on the court as Hapoel Haifa aim for an immediate return to the top flight.

title: Salman and Kojo start for Sakhnin as Badash and Altman lead Hapoel Petah Tikva in Toto Cup fight for 13th
dek: Both clubs, short on confidence after a bruising run of preseason results, name close to full-strength lineups for a Toto Cup ranking match that will settle who finishes 13th, ONE reports.

body: Bnei Sakhnin and Hapoel Petah Tikva have both named their starting lineups for a Toto Cup ranking-round match with an unglamorous but pointed stake: whoever wins finishes 13th in the preseason table heading into the new Israeli Premier League campaign, ONE reports. Kick-off is set for 20:15.

Neither side arrives with much momentum. Sakhnin, the hosts, have lost all four of their home matches in this year's Toto Cup, and coach Yossi Aboksis is under pressure to finally deliver a win on his own turf before the league season begins in earnest.
Aboksis has sent out Ahmad Salman and Matthew Kojo in his starting XI, alongside Andrei Raul, Dimitri Kavar, Maron Gantos and Amit Kardi, among others named by ONE.

title: Tibi handed full debut as Maccabi Petah Tikva visit crisis-hit Tiberias in Toto Cup
dek: Veteran defender starts for the first time since signing, while hosts Ironi Tiberias — playing under the shadow of a disciplinary saga — pair Mansour Badji with Nana Gambel up front.
body: Eitan Tibi will make his first start for Maccabi Petah Tikva when the club travel to face Ironi Tiberias on Saturday evening, with ONE reporting the veteran centre-back handed a full debut in the starting eleven for the first time since putting pen to paper this summer.

Kick-off is at 20:15 at the Barel Stadium in Nof HaGalil, the ground Tiberias have used as their adopted home since 2024 while a new stadium is built in the city itself. The match is a Toto Cup ranking fixture, with the sides competing for 11th and 12th place in the pre-season group phase.

Tibi, 38, arrives at Maccabi Petah Tikva as his seventh professional club after a career that has brought more than 20 trophies, including seven league championships. On signing this summer, he told Ynet he was "happy and excited to sign for Maccabi Petah Tikva, already looking forward to getting onto the grass and giving everything for the club — the goal is clear, a return to the team's natural place, the Premier League."

Tiberias counter with an attacking pair built around youth: Mansour Badji, a 19-year-old forward from Gambia who came through the club's own academy after starting out in Maccabi Haifa's youth system, is paired up front with Nana Gambel, a 24-year-old Ivorian winger who joined the club officially after impressing at its pre-season training camp in Poland.

Both clubs go into the game with similarly patchy Toto Cup form. Tiberias opened their campaign with a win over Bnei Sakhnin but have since lost three in a row, most recently to Maccabi Haifa. Maccabi Petah Tikva have also managed just one win from four, though they arrive with some momentum after beating Ramat Gan in their last outing.

For the home side, the match is being played against a difficult backdrop. Tiberias are contending with a disciplinary storm off the pitch — Sport1-Maariv has reported that the Israel Football Association's prosecutor has moved to file a severe indictment against the club in the so-called "injections affair," on top of a separate points penalty already imposed this season over a "double contracts" case.

None of that changes the stakes on the field on Saturday: a lower mid-table Toto Cup slot, but also a first proper audition for two of the newest arrivals on either side before the Ligat Ha'al season gets under way.

title: Barcelona draw up special plan to get Pedri back to peak fitness
dek: The club is easing its midfielder back in gradually after a World Cup spent managing fitness issues, with the target being sharpest form in spring rather than at the season's start.

body: Pedri returned to Barcelona's pre-season only this week, and the club has no intention of rushing him. ONE reports that Barcelona's medical and fitness staff have drawn up a personalized plan for the Spain midfielder built around one clear priority: not that he peaks for the opening weekend, but that he is at his sharpest in the spring, when the league title and cup competitions are actually decided.

It is a deliberately patient approach, and one born of experience. Pedri's 2025-26 season was repeatedly interrupted by fitness problems, including a tear in the distal biceps femoris muscle of his left thigh that Barcelona confirmed in late October and that kept him out for weeks. He never fully found his rhythm afterwards, playing in patches rather than the sustained, dominant form Barcelona and Spain have come to expect from him.

Hansi Flick has already acknowledged that the club pushed its luck managing him at times last season. On Pedri's fitness, the coach admitted that keeping him on the pitch for the full 90 minutes of Barcelona's Copa del Rey semi-final against Atlético Madrid was a risk the medical staff took — one that, in hindsight, could easily have backfired.

Even carrying that fitness baggage into the World Cup, Pedri still played his part in Spain's triumph. He came off the bench for the closing half hour and extra time of the final against Argentina on July 19, with Ferran Torres eventually settling the tie 1-0 in the 106th minute at MetLife Stadium. Pedri himself forced a save out of Emiliano Martínez with a long-range effort as Spain won their second World Cup, sixteen years after their first in 2010.

That tournament arguably exposed the problem rather than hid it: a player of Pedri's class reduced to managing his body through a World Cup rather than dominating it. Barcelona's new plan is, in effect, an attempt to make sure the same thing does not happen over the course of a full club season.

The bigger picture at Camp Nou is that Barcelona believe they do not need to gamble with him. With Gavi, Fermín López and Dani Olmo all part of the same engine room, and the club still chasing a deal for Manchester City's Rodri, Flick's staff are confident they can field one of the strongest Spanish-based midfields in world football even before Pedri is back to his sharpest.

That depth is what buys Barcelona the patience to handle their most gifted passer carefully. Rather than forcing him through a full-intensity pre-season, the plan is to build his training load gradually, with match sharpness following alongside it — and the real target only arriving once winter turns to spring, when Barcelona expect their season to actually be decided.

body: Israel's under-16 boys' national basketball team closed out a turbulent European Championship campaign in style on Saturday, beating Belgium 85-68 in Oradea, Romania, to finish 13th and — the number that actually mattered — preserve its place in Division A for next summer's tournament, ONE reports.

A defeat would have sent Guy Kaplan's cadets down to Division B for the first time since 2015, a drop that would have reshaped the pathway for an entire age group of Israeli prospects. Instead, back-to-back wins in the placement bracket sent the squad home on a high.
The tone was set immediately. Israel blitzed the opening quarter 24-8, building the kind of cushion that let the team absorb pressure later in the game rather than chase the scoreboard.

Belgium did mount a rally, outscoring Israel 26-18 in the third quarter to cut into the deficit, but the gap built in the first ten minutes proved too much to overturn, and Israel closed out the win comfortably.
Maor Sela was the story of the afternoon, recording a triple-double of 27 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists to top every column for Israel, according to ONE's box score.

Ido Ziv added 20 points, Nitzan Klein chipped in 13 points and six rebounds, and Rotem Ben-David finished with nine points, five rebounds and three assists. Omer Tzvi, Itai Kadam, Yanai Lahmanovich and Eilai Saroya all featured off the bench, with Kadam grabbing eight rebounds alongside his four points.

It capped an up-and-down tournament for the Israelis. They opened with a comfortable 97-75 win over Georgia, but a round-of-16 exit to Germany, 78-75, dropped them out of medal contention and into the bracket fighting to avoid relegation.

A follow-up loss to Italy, 86-75, left almost no margin for error. Israel then had to beat Georgia a second time — winning 91-72 in the rematch — just to earn a direct shot at Division A survival against Belgium.

That shot came on Saturday, and Kaplan's group did not waste it. The FIBA U16 EuroBasket, hosted in Oradea from August 7-15, splits 16 nations into Division A each year, with the bottom finishers relegated to the second tier for the following season.

For a squad still two or three years from senior basketball, the result matters well beyond a single scoreline: continued Division A status means Israel's next generation of prospects keeps facing Europe's strongest youth programs every summer, rather than being demoted to a weaker pool of opposition.

Israel finished 13th of the 16 teams that opened Division A play, a modest final ranking that tells only part of the story of a team that steadied itself after a mid-tournament stumble to get exactly the result it needed when it needed it most.

body: Barcelona have gone back to Manchester City with a third bid for Rodri, this one worth around €70 million, as the Catalan club push to finally land the Spain midfielder before the transfer window closes, ONE reports.

It is the latest step in a saga that has dragged through much of August. Barcelona's opening approach was pitched at roughly €45 million, according to Israeli and Spanish reporting, before an improved second bid in the region of €60-65 million was knocked back. City had been holding out for closer to €80 million for a player they regard as central to Pep Guardiola's midfield since his 2019 arrival from Atletico Madrid.

Sport1/Maariv reported that Barcelona have effectively drawn a line at €70 million, framing it as their final offer rather than an opening position in a fresh round of haggling. ONE's reporting suggests the club believes this package, rather than the previous two, is the one that finally bridges the gap with City.

The urgency on Barcelona's side is rooted in the player himself. ONE reported weeks ago that Rodri had privately told City some time ago that he wants to leave the Etihad, with a move to Camp Nou his clear priority over any other suitor, including reported interest from Real Madrid.

His value has only risen through the negotiation. Rodri was named Golden Ball winner as Spain won the 2026 World Cup, beating Argentina 1-0 in the final to claim the country's second world title, sixteen years after 2010. He also won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, becoming the first Manchester City player to do so.

Walla Sport has gone further, reporting that Barcelona believe they have already agreed the framework of a deal for the 30-year-old, though the figures being cited vary between outlets and neither club has confirmed a fee.

Some of the more optimistic Israeli reporting suggests an agreement could be reached within 48 hours, though ONE has stressed there is still no certainty over the exact timeline or final structure of the package.

For City, losing Rodri would strip out the deepest-lying and most tactically trusted midfielder of the Guardiola era, and any deal is expected to be complicated by the club's reluctance to strengthen a direct continental rival. For Barcelona, signing the World Cup's outstanding player would be a statement of intent as they look to rebuild a midfield around a proven winner.
Nothing is signed yet, and both figures and timing should be treated as developing until either club confirms them.

title: Marseille strip Højbjerg of captaincy after Newcastle transfer refusal
dek: Pierre-Emile Højbjerg turned down a £15m move to Newcastle United, and Olympique de Marseille responded by handing the captain's armband to Timothy Weah.
body: Pierre-Emile Højbjerg has been stripped of the Marseille captaincy after refusing to leave the club for Newcastle United this summer, with the French side handing the armband to American winger Timothy Weah instead.

Newcastle had agreed a fee reported at around £15 million with Marseille for the 31-year-old Danish midfielder, who captains Denmark's national team. Højbjerg, though, made clear he wanted to stay in the south of France and blocked the move, according to reports from ONE and several British outlets.

The refusal has left Marseille's hierarchy furious. The club has been under pressure to trim its wage bill, and Højbjerg's sale to Newcastle would have brought in funds the club were relying on for the rest of the transfer window. Owner Frank McCourt is said to be irritated by the outcome.

Marseille's response was swift and public. Manager Bruno Génésio started Højbjerg in Friday's pre-season friendly against Atlético Madrid at the Stade Vélodrome, which Marseille lost 2-1, but it was Weah who wore the captain's armband rather than the Dane.

Génésio made clear afterwards that the call had not come from him. "It's a decision that was dictated to me by the club's management," he said. "If I want to be completely frank, and I will be, it's not a decision that I agree with."

The episode is an awkward one for Marseille given how recently they committed to Højbjerg long-term. He arrived on loan for the 2024-25 season and the club triggered a mandatory purchase clause reported at around £17 million earlier this year to sign him permanently.

Newcastle, who have been active in the transfer market as part of their Public Investment Fund-backed project, will now have to look elsewhere for defensive-midfield reinforcement after missing out on a player they had already agreed terms to sign.

According to Goal.com, AC Milan are among the clubs monitoring Højbjerg's situation should his position at Marseille become untenable following the captaincy row, though no fresh approach has been reported.

For now, Højbjerg remains an Olympique de Marseille player without the armband he has worn since being installed as club captain, a very public marker of the rift between the player and the club's ownership.

title: Mourinho begins his second Real Madrid era as the season closes in
dek: Thirteen years after his acrimonious exit, José Mourinho is back in the Bernabéu dugout, and his rebooted reign faces its first real test this month
body: Real Madrid's players are back at Valdebebas under a familiar face this month. José Mourinho, 63, is once again in charge of the club he first managed between 2010 and 2013, his return finally confirmed in June and now approaching its first real examination as the new La Liga season begins.

Florentino Pérez pushed the appointment through in June, signing Mourinho to a contract running to 2029, according to Ynet and Haaretz. To free him from his post at Benfica, Real Madrid paid a release fee of around €15 million, roughly equivalent to the manager's annual gross salary in Portugal, Haaretz reported.

He replaces Xabi Alonso, whose brief spell in charge ended amid reported friction in the dressing room. ONE notes that Pérez had been eyeing a Mourinho reunion for some time and never lost faith in him despite a string of underwhelming spells since he last left Madrid, at Roma, Fenerbahçe and Benfica.

The first stint is remembered for its extremes. Mourinho delivered the 2012 La Liga title, ending Pep Guardiola's Barcelona-dominated run, along with a Copa del Rey and a Supercopa, but never the Champions League that Pérez craved. It also produced open conflict with captain Iker Casillas and a exit soured by tension with several players.

The timing added extra noise to his comeback: a Netflix documentary series tracing Mourinho's career had just premiered when his return was confirmed in June, sharpening attention on a reunion that already carried plenty of history, ONE reported.

Squad building has continued through the summer. Bernardo Silva arrived on a free transfer from Manchester City, and Marc Cucurella has also joined, additions meant to reinforce a group still built around Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior, Jude Bellingham, Federico Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni.

According to ONE's report, Mourinho's central task is as much psychological as tactical: restoring discipline after two seasons without a major trophy, and getting Vinícius and Mbappé pulling in the same direction after a first campaign together that was not always harmonious. Some players were reportedly skeptical of his appointment at the outset.

The calendar has been unusual too. La Liga's 2026-27 season opened last weekend, but Real Madrid's start was pushed back because of how many of its players went deep into this year's World Cup, according to beIN Sports and Al Jazeera. title: Chiba 0-4 Machida Zelvia: Neta Lavi plays 81 minutes as club storms to top of J1
dek: Israeli international Neta Lavi started in central midfield as Machida Zelvia routed JEF United Chiba, backing up their opening-day rout of FC Tokyo to move top of Japan's newly reformatted J1 League.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo! News Japan (Football Zone) - J1 round two standings

body: Neta Lavi's new club is off to about as good a start as any team could ask for. FC Machida Zelvia thumped JEF United Chiba 4-0 away at Fukuda Denshi Arena on Saturday, and with it climbed to the top of Japan's J1 League after just two rounds of the newly reformatted 2026-27 season.

The Israeli international started in central midfield for Machida and was withdrawn in the 81st minute, having anchored the visitors through a one-sided afternoon in Chiba. It was a low-key personal display, but a hugely significant collective one for the club he joined a year ago.

Yuta Nakayama opened the scoring in the 18th minute, and Teté Iéngi doubled the lead midway through the first half. Takuma Nishimura and Hoki Nakamura added further goals in the second period, either side of the hour mark, to complete a comfortable 4-0 win in front of 16,884 spectators.

It followed an even more emphatic result on the opening weekend, when Machida beat FC Tokyo 5-1 away at Ajinomoto Stadium on 8 August. Between the two matches, Machida have now scored nine goals and conceded just one, a goal difference that, combined with a maximum six points, puts them clear at the summit ahead of Sanfrecce Hiroshima.

This is the first season the J.League has run its top flight on a European-style autumn-to-spring calendar rather than the traditional March-to-December schedule, so the early standings carry more weight than they normally would at this point in August. Chiba, by contrast, have lost both their opening fixtures and sit in the relegation places alongside Nagoya Grampus and Urawa Reds.

Lavi, a 29-year-old defensive midfielder capped by the Israel national team, arrived at Machida in August 2025 on a permanent transfer from Gamba Osaka, where he had spent two seasons after leaving Maccabi Haifa. He came through the Maccabi Haifa academy and made 197 league appearances for the club across eight seasons, scoring seven goals, before his move to Japan in 2023.

He wears the number 31 shirt for Machida and has established himself as a regular fixture in the club's midfield since his move from Osaka, a run that continued with Saturday's 81-minute shift in Chiba.

With the J1 season still in its infancy, Machida's perfect start and Lavi's growing role in the side will be watched closely back home as one of the more eye-catching Israeli stories developing in Japanese football this year.

body: Israel's two crews at the 470 World Championship in Enoshima, Japan, moved in opposite directions overnight as racing resumed after a spell of light and unpredictable wind, ONE reports.

Roy Levy and Ariel Gal, the reigning 2024 470 Junior European champions who won silver at July's Junior World Championship in Gdynia, had opened this senior Worlds strongly, sitting third overall before slipping to seventh. According to ONE, a difficult day of racing dropped the young pair further still, down to 11th place.
Levy and Gal completed three races in tricky conditions, finishing seventh, 22nd and sixth, before a fourth race was abandoned for lack of wind and left uncompleted.

In the same fleet, Israel's other 470 crew, Nitai Hasson and Noga Tiano, went the other way. ONE reports they climbed to 10th overall after four completed races, having started the day down in 17th and worked their way up through 15th on scores of 15, 34, 5 and 15.

The championship, being sailed off Enoshima Yacht Harbour through 17 August, is shaping up as a tight contest at the top of the fleet, with Spain's Jordi Xammar and Marta Cardona among those leading the Gold Fleet after the opening races, according to Sail-World's coverage of the regatta.
With both Israeli boats now inside the top dozen, the remaining days of fleet racing will decide whether either crew can force its way into medal contention before the championship concludes.

title: Ukrainian amateur tennis 'legend' Slava Kurbanov killed fighting on the front
dek: The Ukrainian Tennis Federation says the veteran of the country's amateur circuit died in combat, the latest of hundreds of athletes lost since Russia's invasion.
body: Slava Kurbanov, a veteran of Ukraine's amateur tennis scene and, by the account of those who played alongside him, one of its most familiar faces, has been killed while carrying out a combat mission on the front line, the Ukrainian Tennis Federation announced this week, according to ONE.
The federation said it learned of Kurbanov's death on August 13, and paid tribute to him as "a remarkable person and good human," adding: "Rest in peace, hero."

Kurbanov volunteered for Ukraine's armed forces in the earliest days of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, and went on, the federation said, to serve in some of the most intense sectors of the front.

Away from the war he was best known on the amateur courts of Ukraine, a regular at tournaments run by the Ukrainian Tennis Club, the "Amateur" series and the "Smash" league - grassroots events that make up the backbone of the country's recreational game. ONE's report described him as a legend of that scene.

Ukrainian sports outlets including Ukrinform, Obozrevatel and Glavcom carried near-identical tributes this week, a sign of how deeply Kurbanov's death has registered within the country's small but tightly knit amateur tennis community.

His death adds to a grim toll that Ukraine's sports ministry has tracked since the invasion began. In January, sports minister Matviy Bidny said more than 760 Ukrainian athletes and coaches had by then been killed as a result of the war, a figure he cited while urging the International Olympic Committee to reconsider its decision to ease restrictions on Russian competitors.

Kurbanov never featured on professional rankings or national squads, but his story has been repeated many times over since 2022: club-level sportspeople, and stars too, across football, boxing, chess and now tennis have left the courts, rinks and rings for the front, and many have not come back.

body: The clock is running out for Israeli fans who want a squad ready before a ball is kicked in Spain this season. ONE Fantasy's La Liga game, backed by insurer Migdal, closes registration tonight, just hours before the 2026/27 campaign begins.

The season opens at Mendizorrotza in Vitoria-Gasteiz, where Deportivo Alavés host Getafe at 20:30 Israel time - independently confirmed as 19:30 CEST kick-off, the traditional curtain-raiser slot for a new La Liga campaign.

The format follows the standard fantasy blueprint: each manager gets a budget of 120 million to assemble a 15-player squad, with 11 starters and four substitutes, deployed in a legal formation such as 4-4-2 or 4-3-3.

A cap of two players per club is built in specifically to stop managers stacking a single dominant side, while goalkeepers now earn points across what ONE describes as "a broader range of parameters," making the position more of a genuine tactical choice than in past seasons.

Captains double their points each round, and a bench player's score will automatically replace a starter's if it is higher at the same position. Squads can be reshuffled without limit until the transfer window shuts, and friends can spin off private mini-leagues alongside the main competition.
Prizes are modest but tangible: the season's overall winner receives a couples' trip to watch an away match, while weekly round winners are rewarded with restaurant vouchers.

ONE tips Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé as the players most likely to top the scoring charts again, after both were the standout fantasy assets of the 2025/26 season, though the site notes it remains to be seen which fresh breakout name emerges to challenge them this time round.

title: Ferran Torres completes move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain
dek: The World Cup final goalscorer signs a five-year contract in Paris in a deal reported at €50 million, reuniting with compatriot Luis Enrique.

verificationSources.label: ONE - המעבר הושלם: פראן טורס חתם בפאריס סן ז'רמן
PSG official announcement - Ferran Torres joins Paris Saint-Germain

body: Ferran Torres has completed his move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain, ending four and a half years at Camp Nou to sign a five-year contract in France, ONE reports.

The Spain forward, who scored the winning goal in extra time as Spain beat Argentina in the World Cup final at the start of this month, will wear the number 9 shirt at PSG and is under contract until 2031, according to the club's official announcement.

PSG had to raise their offer to get the deal done. Barcelona initially rejected an opening bid of €40 million plus €10 million in add-ons, holding out for at least €50 million guaranteed before the two clubs agreed a package reported at roughly €50 million with a further €5 million in bonuses.
Luis Enrique, the PSG head coach, pushed hard for the signing. The two Spaniards worked together in the national team setup, and Torres will now report to him again at club level in Paris.

"I'm delighted to be beginning a new adventure at such an ambitious club as Paris Saint-Germain," Torres said in PSG's announcement. "I'd like to thank president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi, Luis Campos and coach Luis Enrique for giving me the opportunity to join the team, which I hope to help win as many trophies as possible."

Torres missed Barcelona training sessions with the club's permission in the final days of the negotiation as the transfer was finalised. His departure brings Barcelona a significant fee and salary-cap relief at a club that has repeatedly had to manage its wage bill under La Liga's financial rules.

He joins an attacking line at Parc des Princes that already includes Ousmane Dembélé, Kylian Mbappé and Désiré Doué, adding fresh competition up front for a club chasing another Ligue 1 and Champions League double.

The move caps a remarkable few weeks for Torres, who arrived at the World Cup as a squad player and left it as the man who settled the final, a story that has clearly shaped PSG's willingness to pay a premium for him this summer.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv eye Serbian centre-back Nikola Maraš after bizarre Alavés release
dek: The 30-year-old, cut loose by the La Liga club over a training-intensity dispute, has reportedly received an offer and is already checking out apartments in Tel Aviv.

verificationSources.label: B92.net - Nikola Maraš dobio otkaz u Alavesu zbog nediscipline

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have identified an unlikely reinforcement for their backline: Nikola Maraš, a 30-year-old Serbian centre-back who became a free agent last week in one of the stranger contract terminations European football has seen this summer.

ONE reports that the Yellow-and-Blues have already tabled an offer to Maraš, and that the defender has started making inquiries about relocating to Israel, including checking out housing options in Tel Aviv, as he weighs the move.

Maraš was let go by Deportivo Alavés despite a contract that was supposed to run until the summer of 2027. Serbian outlets, including B92, reported that the Spanish club opened disciplinary proceedings against him after training-load data — drawn from GPS and performance-tracking platforms used at the club — indicated he was deliberately working below full intensity in sessions. He was given a chance to explain himself but the club was not persuaded, and terminated his deal outright, a highly unusual step in professional football that drew attention across the Spanish and Serbian press.

For Maccabi Tel Aviv, his availability as a free agent makes him an appealing, low-cost option to strengthen the defence. But ONE's report notes the move is not a formality: it hinges on how the club resolves its broader foreign-player situation, with the Yellow-and-Blues still working out solutions for other overseas players on the roster before space and budget can be freed up for a new arrival.

Maraš stands 1.89 metres and has spent his career mainly as a central defender, with stints in Serbia, Portugal and Spain. He came through Rad Belgrade, where he was eventually made captain, before a 2017 move to Portuguese side Chaves. He joined Alavés on loan in August 2022, and after helping the club win promotion to La Liga that season signed a permanent four-year contract in mid-2023.

His body of work reads as a solid, if unspectacular, journeyman's résumé: over 100 appearances in Serbia's SuperLiga, 57 in Portugal's Primeira Liga, and a mix of Segunda División and La Liga football in Spain, including 16 top-flight appearances for Alavés.

Should the transfer go through, Maraš would arrive with Champions League and top-division European experience — exactly the profile Maccabi Tel Aviv have targeted as they try to bolster a defence facing a heavy fixture load between league and continental commitments this season.
For now, though, it remains a live candidacy rather than a done deal — a player already sold on relocating, a club that has made an offer, and a roster puzzle in Tel Aviv still waiting to be solved.

title: Abu Fani's future at Red Star Belgrade in doubt after Stanković's exit
dek: The Israeli midfielder, brought to Belgrade by Dejan Stanković, faces an uncertain future after the coach who signed him quit and a red card marred the Champions League exit to Hapoel Beer Sheva
body: Mohamed Abu Fani's stint at Crvena Zvezda looked shaky even before it produced its first full season, and now the coach who wanted him in Belgrade is gone. According to ONE, the Israeli international's place at the Serbian champions is under serious threat following Dejan Stanković's resignation this week.

Stanković, who had managed Abu Fani at Ferencváros, made the 28-year-old midfielder his first major request when he took over at Red Star last year, and the club paid the Hungarian side around €1.5 million to sign him. It was framed as a reunion built on trust between player and coach.

That trust no longer sits in the dugout. Stanković quit after Red Star's Champions League qualifying exit to Hapoel Beer Sheva, a tie the Israeli champions won 3-0 on aggregate — beating the Serbian giants 1-0 away on August 4 and 2-0 at the Rajko Mitić Stadium on August 11, goals from Igor Zlatanović and Jabone Isat sealing it in Belgrade.

Abu Fani's own contribution to the double-header did him no favours. He was substituted at halftime in the first leg in Beer Sheva, and in the return match at home he was sent off with a straight red card for violent conduct — shown late in the game after he struck an opponent, Ynet and other Israeli outlets reported, leaving Red Star to see out the tie a man short.
Serbian outlet Mondo, cited by ONE, put it bluntly: "The Israeli did not meet expectations when it mattered most."

With Stanković gone, Red Star have moved fast to appoint a successor. Spanish coach Albert Riera — the former Liverpool and Espanyol winger who has since managed Olimpija Ljubljana, Celje, Bordeaux and, most recently, Eintracht Frankfurt — signed through June 2028 and is set to make his bench debut in the Europa League play-off against Viktoria Plzeň.

ONE reports that Riera favours a 4-1-4-1 or 4-1-2-3 system, formations that may not obviously accommodate Abu Fani's profile as he did under Stanković. According to the report, several Israeli clubs are already monitoring the situation, with a move before the transfer window closes not ruled out.

Should Abu Fani leave now, ONE notes it would rank among the shortest spells by a marquee signing in Red Star's more than 80-year history — a swift unravelling for a transfer that was supposed to reunite player and coach for the long haul.

title: Khalaili tells Crystal Palace: 'I've been following you for a long time'
dek: In his first interview since completing English football's most expensive Israeli transfer, the winger tells Crystal Palace's own channel he had Selhurst Park on his radar long before the deal came together.
body: Anan Khalaili has given his first interview since putting pen to paper on the biggest transfer of any Israeli footballer's career, and his message to Crystal Palace's supporters was blunt: this was no whim.

"I've been following Crystal Palace for a long time," the 21-year-old told the club's in-house media in comments carried by ONE, framing the move less as a leap into the unknown than as something he had quietly been tracking from Belgium, and before that from Haifa.

Khalaili completed his switch from Union Saint-Gilloise this month in a deal reported at around £21 million, making him, according to Ynet and the Times of Israel, the most expensive transfer involving an Israeli player in the sport's history. He has signed a long-term contract running through 2031, with the move still subject to routine international clearance.
He arrives as Palace's fifth signing of the summer, according to ONE, joining Munganduza, Tomiyasu, McNeil and Gassama in a squad being rebuilt around last season's cup success.

Asked about that recent history, Khalaili was generous rather than reverent, telling the club he felt Palace "deserved to win three titles" — before making clear he had not signed simply to admire what came before him. "I'm excited... I can't wait to start," he said.
On the division he is stepping into, his answer was short and unambiguous: "It's the best league in the world."

He was equally direct about what he thinks he offers a manager still shaping his first-choice XI. "I'm strong, I'm fast... I love attacking, but I also love defending," Khalaili said, a description that matches a player who has operated both as a wide defender and as an attacking winger through his career so far.

That career began at Maccabi Haifa, where ONE credits him with 52 appearances and 15 goals, before Union Saint-Gilloise brought him to Belgium in the summer of 2024. He repaid that move quickly: a Belgian Pro League title — Union's first in 90 years — and a Belgian Cup followed, alongside crucial Champions League goals that lifted his profile across Europe.
He has also become a fixture for Israel's senior national team, with 16 caps to his name.

The path to Selhurst Park was not straightforward. A move to Inter Milan collapsed in July after Khalaili failed to clear Italy's strict medical checks, opening the door for Palace to move in ahead of other Premier League interest. Whatever the detour, Khalaili's first words as a Palace player suggest he sees this as the destination he had been aiming for all along.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva plan wide rotation for Toto Cup trip to Hapoel Haifa before Sabah tie
dek: Ran Kozhuhov is set to rest key players from the Red Star Belgrade breakthrough as Beer Sheva manage the squad ahead of their Champions League play-off against Sabah.

verificationSources.label: ONE - לפני סבאח: רוטציה רחבה בב"ש במשחק הדירוג

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva head to Sami Ofer Stadium on Saturday night for a Toto Cup ranking-stage match against Hapoel Haifa, and manager Ran Kozhuhov is expected to send out a heavily rotated line-up, ONE reports.

The club had asked the Israel Football Association to postpone the fixture altogether, arguing that a competitive domestic match so soon after their exertions in Belgrade risked fatigue and injuries with a much bigger European night looming. The request was turned down, according to Walla Sport, leaving Beer Sheva to fulfil the fixture as scheduled.

The timing is awkward for the Negev club. Four days earlier they produced one of the results of their European history, beating Red Star Belgrade 2-0 away to seal a 3-0 aggregate win and a place in the Champions League play-off round, where Azerbaijan's Sabah FK await. The tie already guarantees Beer Sheva a place in at least the Europa League league phase, along with a UEFA prize pot in the region of nine million euros, Walla reported.

With that in mind, the club struck a pragmatic tone over the Toto Cup assignment. "We need to manage the loads correctly," the club said, according to ONE. "We have a very important match in Europe ahead" — while stressing that the side sent to Haifa will still be competitive.

ONE's report named Amir Ganach, Muhammad Abu Romi, Matan Baltaksa, Amit Ochana, Ophir Davidzadeh, Roei Levi, Yoni Stoyanov, Jibril Diop, Itay Chazot, Marco Wolf and Hamudi Kana'an among the players in line for significant minutes — largely squad members who did not feature, or played only briefly, in the second leg against Red Star.

It is a familiar squeeze for a provincial Israeli club balancing a long-awaited European run with a congested domestic calendar. The Toto Cup ranking games carry local pride but nothing like the stakes of a Champions League play-off, and Kozhuhov's selection tonight is as much about protecting his first-choice XI as it is about points in Haifa.

Beer Sheva's first leg against Sabah is set for August 25, with a win sending either side into a competition neither has previously reached in its group or league phase — the backdrop against which Saturday's rotation decisions are being made.

title: Angelidis and Vanharen face the press as Maccabi Tel Aviv prepare for Toto Cup semi-final
dek: Club CEO Jack Angelidis and new sporting director Steven Vanharen fielded live questions on the Revivo and Abu Farhi transfer sagas, Kenny Miller's future and owner Mitch Goldhar, two days before the trip to Maccabi Netanya.

verificationSources.label: ONE — live broadcast: Angelidis and Vanharen
ynet — Colorado Rapids bid for Abu Farhi
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — Dan Glazer signs
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — Toto Cup semi-final vs Maccabi Netanya

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv threw open the doors on Saturday, putting chief executive Jack Angelidis and freshly installed sporting director Steven Vanharen in front of a live camera to take questions from supporters and press two days before a Toto Cup semi-final that suddenly matters a great deal more than the competition's usual billing.

The timing was no accident. The Yellow-and-Blues are still absorbing their exit from Conference League qualifying, and a restless fan base has spent the summer venting about a squad that has shed more than it has added. Angelidis framed the session as a chance to let Vanharen, barely two months into the job, put a face to the club's recruitment plan. "We wanted to showcase Steven and let you ask us directly about the ambition to win everything and compete in Europe," he said.

He did not shy away from the club's two live transfer sagas. On Roy Revivo, whose camp has been pushing for a move, Angelidis insisted the club respects the player but will only negotiate off a formal written offer, not messages relayed through intermediaries. On Sayed Abu Farhi, he confirmed Maccabi have received an offer from Colorado Rapids and that the club retains full control over the terms of any exit — a deal that, according to Israeli reporting this week, has the MLS side bidding around six million dollars for the 20-year-old forward.

Angelidis also pushed back on the season's dominant narrative — that Maccabi are simply cashing in on their best players. "We're not here to develop players to sell them, we want to win," he said, before defending owner Mitch Goldhar directly. "He wanted to rescue the club and build something long-term with a winning culture. It's a bit offensive to hear claims he only wants to sell players when he's absorbing significant losses himself."

Vanharen's arrival is itself a notable piece of the club's rebuild. The 46-year-old Belgian was appointed sporting director on June 10 on a two-year contract, arriving fresh off two seasons at Hungarian club Győr, where he helped the newly promoted side settle into the top flight before steering them to their first championship since 2012-13 and a domestic cup semi-final. His CV also includes spells at Beerschot, Sheffield United and Olympiacos.

Asked about the club's most concrete piece of business so far, defender Dan Glazer's return from Kazakh side Kairat Almaty on a two-year deal, both men pointed to it as the template going forward: targeted signings with a genuine connection to the club rather than a wholesale overhaul. Angelidis said the plan calls for roughly four new arrivals this window, not the six or seven departures some fans fear.

The trickiest question of the afternoon concerned head coach Kenny Miller, whose limited experience in senior management has drawn scrutiny since his appointment. Vanharen defended the call in football terms rather than sentiment. "We spoke to a number of coaches, but a manager needs a strong mentality and a clear philosophy. He shows the aggressive, high-pressing style we want. Changing coaches now carries more risk than sticking with Kenny," he said.

All of it lands two days before the actual football resumes. Maccabi Tel Aviv travel to face Maccabi Netanya at Netanya Stadium on Sunday at 20:00 in a Toto Cup semi-final, with the winner advancing to the final; Hapoel Kiryat Shmona and Hapoel Tel Aviv meet in the other last-four tie at the same time. For a club whose summer has been defined by exits and unrest, it is a low-stakes stage on which to start answering questions with performances rather than press conferences.

title: Kenny Miller fronts live press conference ahead of Toto Cup semi-final against Maccabi Netanya
dek: The Maccabi Tel Aviv head coach previewed Sunday's last-four clash in Netanya, with a Toto Cup final place at stake days after the club's Europa League exit.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "הצטרפו לשידור החי: קני מילר במסיבת עיתונאים"

body: Kenny Miller sat down in front of the cameras on Saturday for a live-streamed press conference at Maccabi Tel Aviv's training base, previewing a Toto Cup semi-final that will decide who reaches next weekend's final.

The Yellows travel to Netanya on Sunday evening, with kick-off at 20:00 at the Miriam Stadium, ONE reports. The hosts, aware of the pull of a rare cup meeting with the country's most storied club, have offered season-ticket holders a free ticket for the night as a gesture to their fans.
Whoever wins goes through to the Toto Cup final. The other semi-final pits Hapoel Kiryat Shmona against Hapoel Tel Aviv, completing a last-four line-up drawn from across the Israeli top flight.

The timing gives the presser extra edge. Miller's team were eliminated from Europa League qualifying by Bulgaria's CSKA Sofia earlier this month, losing the tie after a 0-3 defeat in the first leg — played in Batumi, Georgia, under UEFA's continuing restriction on Israeli clubs hosting matches at home — and dropping out of continental competition altogether. A domestic trophy is now the nearest silverware on the horizon, and Sunday's semi-final carries the weight of that disappointment.

Miller, 46, has been in charge at Maccabi Tel Aviv since January 2026, when he joined the coaching staff before being elevated to interim head coach during the playoffs and guiding the team to the State Cup title. The club made him permanent head coach on 23 June, with owner Mitch Goldhar citing his "professionalism, work ethic and understanding of the standards, values and ambitions expected at Maccabi Tel Aviv," and the deal carries an option for a further year.

As a player, the Scot won 69 caps and scored 18 goals for Scotland as a forward, with three separate spells at Rangers yielding 111 goals in 292 appearances alongside stints at Celtic, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Hibernian, Derby County and Cardiff City before he retired in 2020.

For now, the club has offered no direct quotes from the session beyond confirming it was carried live — the presser itself is the story, a chance for fans to hear from their coach in his own words before a match that will shape the mood heading into the new domestic season.

title: Tokyo, 24 July 2021: The Girl From Gedera Who Gave Israel Its First Taekwondo Medal
dek: Down 29-5 to the eventual gold medalist just hours earlier, 19-year-old Avishag Semberg fought back through the repechage and a wild third-round swing to win bronze — Israel's first medal of the Tokyo Games and its first ever in taekwondo.

verificationSources.label: The Times of Israel — "First Tokyo medal: Avishag Semberg wins taekwondo bronze, Israel's 1st in field"
The Jerusalem Post — "A perfect podium surprise for Israel's Avishag Semberg"
Israel Hayom — "Israel scores first Tokyo Olympics medal as Avishag Samberg wins taekwondo bronze"
The Times of Israel — "Bennett, Herzog cheer taekwondo medalist Semberg: 'You brought national pride'"

body: The scoreboard inside the Makuhari Messe Hall A told a brutal story that morning: 29-5. Avishag Semberg, nineteen years old and fighting in her first Olympics, had just been dismantled in the round of 16 of the women's -49kg taekwondo draw by Thailand's Panipak Wongpattanakit, who would go on to take the gold medal that same day. For most fighters, that kind of scoreline ends an Olympic dream before lunch. For Semberg, it was merely the setup.

Because Wongpattanakit reached the final, her path through the bracket opened a repechage lane — a second chance reserved for fighters eliminated by whoever fights for gold. Semberg took it. In her first repechage bout she overwhelmed Vietnam's Trương Thị Kim Tuyền 22-1, a statement that the earlier beating had not broken her. It set up a bronze medal match against Turkey's Rukiye Yıldırım, and it was there, on the opening day of competition at the Tokyo Games, that Israeli sport wrote a new page.

The bout swung wildly. Semberg raced ahead 13-2 after the first round and extended it to 16-9 through the second, kicking with the fearlessness of someone who had nothing left to lose after the morning's rout. Yıldırım surged back in the third, landing head-kicks and body shots that put her ahead 22-19 with the clock running down. Semberg did not fold. She closed the gap, retook the lead, and closed out the match 27-22. "After the turnaround, I said to myself, 'I want this medal more than she does,' and I did it," Semberg said afterward. "I have an Olympic medal at 19 — it's a dream come true."

The bronze was Israel's first medal of the Tokyo Olympics and the country's tenth Olympic medal overall, but its real significance was narrower and sharper: it was the first Olympic medal an Israeli had ever won in taekwondo. At 19, Semberg also became the youngest Israeli ever to stand on an Olympic podium.

She had not arrived in Tokyo as a favorite. Semberg grew up in Gedera, a town south of Tel Aviv, and discovered taekwondo as a first-grader before joining Israel's junior national setup by sixth grade under coach Yechiam Sharabi. Her Olympic berth was earned only months earlier, at the pandemic-delayed 2021 European Olympic Qualification Tournament in Sofia, Bulgaria, where she went a perfect 12-0 to punch her ticket to Tokyo.
"I'm just a girl from Gedera," she said after the medal was hers. "Can I really be at the top? Yes, you can be at the top — you just need to dream big and dream of it every day."

The reaction back home was immediate. Prime Minister Naftali Bennett phoned to tell her, "You have brought us all national pride! Congratulations Avishag, congratulations Israel!" President Isaac Herzog called it a source of inspiration for a generation: "You've made history," he told her. "You are a source of inspiration for many girls and boys in Israel who will look at you and see that with hard work, you can turn a dream into reality."

For a country whose Olympic medal cabinet had, until that morning, never included a single taekwondo result, Semberg's bronze reframed what was possible in a sport with almost no Israeli tradition at the elite level. It also arrived at a moment — the very first day of taekwondo competition at a Games already reshuffled by a year's delay — when it set the tone for what would become one of Israel's most successful Olympics, with medals still to come from gymnastics and rhythmic gymnastics later that same fortnight.

Semberg would go on to compete again at the Paris 2024 Olympics, but nothing there matched the shock and joy of that first afternoon in Chiba, when a teenager who had been thrashed by 24 points in the morning stood on an Olympic podium by evening, medal around her neck, having simply refused to let one bad fight be the whole story.

title: Álvarez denies apologising to Atlético teammates, demands urgent meeting with club chiefs
dek: The Argentine striker's camp has requested urgent talks with CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín as the Barcelona transfer saga drags on, ONE reports.
body: Julián Álvarez has pushed back hard against reports that he made peace with his Atlético Madrid teammates, with his camp instead pressing the club for urgent crisis talks, ONE reports.

Citing ESPN Argentina, ONE says the striker has not apologised to anyone in the Atlético dressing room and has expressed no regret over his public declaration during the World Cup that he wanted to leave the club. That directly contradicts earlier claims, carried by ONE among others, that Álvarez had made a U-turn and admitted he had been wrong to push for a move.

According to TyC Sports, relayed by ONE, Álvarez's representatives have now asked for an urgent sit-down with Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín in an attempt to break the deadlock. The striker reportedly wants to remind Gil Marín of a commitment he says was made back in February: that if a serious offer arrived, the club would let him go.

That offer has since materialised. Barcelona have tabled a bid in the region of €100 million for the Argentine, only for Atlético to refuse to open negotiations, insisting they have no intention of strengthening a direct La Liga rival.

Álvarez, nicknamed "the Spider," has continued training with the first team and held what was described as a respectful conversation with head coach Diego Simeone, who wants him to stay and build the attack around him. But according to ONE's report, his desire to leave has not wavered.

The saga has already spilled into confrontation away from the training ground, with Atlético having lodged a formal complaint against Barcelona over their public pursuit of the player, ONE has separately reported.

For now, the club and player remain at an impasse: Atlético holding firm on a striker who fired them to domestic and continental success, and Álvarez's camp pushing for a meeting that could determine whether this transfer saga reaches a resolution before the window shuts.

title: Katowice fans give Nazi salute after Hapoel Tel Aviv reach Conference League play-offs with 3-2 aggregate win
dek: GKS Katowice supporters were filmed making apparent Nazi salutes toward the Hapoel Tel Aviv section after Wednesday's second-leg qualifier in Poland, and UEFA says the incident is now under review.
body: The scenes that should have been about Hapoel Tel Aviv's progress to a European play-off instead turned ugly on Wednesday night, after several GKS Katowice supporters were filmed making what appeared to be Nazi salutes directed at the away section following the final whistle in Poland.

ONE reports that the gestures were captured on video and quickly circulated on social media, drawing condemnation as they spread. Multiple international outlets, including Fox News and the Algemeiner, picked up the footage within a day of the match.

The incident capped a bruising European night on the pitch as well. Katowice, roared on by their home crowd, beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 2-1 in the second leg of the Conference League qualifying tie — but it was not enough. Hapoel had won the first leg 2-0 in Tel Aviv and went through 3-2 on aggregate, eliminating the Polish side despite the defeat on the night.

UEFA confirmed it is aware of the footage. The governing body said in a statement that the supporters' conduct is "currently being reviewed," though no disciplinary case or charge against GKS Katowice had been formally opened at the time of reporting.

GKS Katowice itself had made no public comment on its fans' behaviour as of Friday, leaving the club silent on an episode that risks overshadowing what was, on the field, a spirited fight to the finish against the Israeli side.

For Hapoel Tel Aviv, the aggregate win sends them into the Conference League play-off round against Italian side Atalanta. The first leg is scheduled for August 20 in Bergamo, with the return leg set for August 27 at a neutral venue, the DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary.

The club's supporters travelled to Poland in reasonable numbers to back the team through the tie, and Wednesday's result marks another step in a European run that has already carried Hapoel Tel Aviv past Ludogorets and into increasingly testing continental company.

UEFA's review of the Katowice incident will be watched closely by the Israel Football Association and by Hapoel Tel Aviv, who will hope any findings are made public and acted on before their play-off tie with Atalanta gets under way next week.
facts: GKS Katowice supporters were filmed making apparent Nazi salutes toward the Hapoel Tel Aviv section after the August 12, 2026 Conference League qualifying second leg in Katowice, Poland.
Katowice won the second leg 2-1 on the night, but Hapoel Tel Aviv advanced 3-2 on aggregate after winning the first leg 2-0 in Tel Aviv.
UEFA said the incident is currently being reviewed; no formal disciplinary charge had been announced.
GKS Katowice had not issued a public statement on its supporters' conduct as of the time of reporting.

Hapoel Tel Aviv advance to the Conference League play-off round to face Atalanta, with the first leg on August 20 in Bergamo and the return leg on August 27 at a neutral venue, DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary.

title: Israel's gymnastics team finishes 17th in Zagreb, misses out on Worlds berth
dek: Lihie Raz and Roni Shamai could not break into the leading pack in the all-around as Israel placed 17th of 32 nations at the European Championships.

verificationSources.label: Olympics.com – 2026 European Gymnastics Championships qualifiers preview
Wikipedia – 2026 European Women's Artistic Gymnastics Championships

body: Israel's national women's artistic gymnastics team finished 17th out of 32 competing nations in the qualification round of the European Championships in Zagreb, ONE reported, leaving the squad short of a direct route to this year's World Championships in Rotterdam.

The qualification round doubled as the all-around competition at Arena Zagreb, with the top 13 teams booking automatic team berths to the Worlds. Israel's combined score of 146.630 points left it well outside that cut-off, in the 36th edition of the European Women's Artistic Gymnastics Championships.

Lihie Raz, Israel's most decorated gymnast, finished 32nd in the individual all-around with 48.966 points, built from 12.600 on vault, 11.466 on uneven bars, 12.600 on balance beam and 12.300 on floor.
Roni Shamai posted an all-around total of 47.732, also finishing outside the positions that mattered for Israel's hopes of a backdoor qualification route.

According to ONE, the federation had targeted at least one gymnast finishing inside the top individuals in the all-around, which would have secured Israel a group qualification criterion and opened a path to Rotterdam even without a top-13 team finish. Neither Raz nor Shamai got close enough, and that route is now closed.

Raz, 21, remains the benchmark for Israeli artistic gymnastics after becoming the country's first-ever medallist at the European Women's Artistic Gymnastics Championships, taking floor bronze in 2020. Her continued presence in finals at major championships has been central to the sport's rising profile in Israel.

Shamai, 17 and affiliated with Bnei Herzliya, has been one of the squad's fastest-improving members this year, having won gold on uneven bars at the Challenge Cup meet in Bulgaria in May and reached three individual finals there.
The result means Israel will need another route back onto the continental and world stage, with the next major qualification opportunities not expected until later in the cycle.

The top 13 teams in qualification earned berths to the 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam.

title: Munits finishes seventh in all-around final at rhythmic gymnastics Worlds
dek: The Israeli gymnast climbed from 13th in qualifying to seventh in Frankfurt, booking her place in Sunday's hoop final, as teammate Meital Somkin finished 17th.

verificationSources.label: Olympics.com - 2026 Rhythmic Gymnastics World Championships in Frankfurt

body: Daniela Munits closed out a strong week in Frankfurt on Friday evening, finishing seventh in the individual all-around final at the Rhythmic Gymnastics World Championships, one of the better results produced by an Israeli gymnast at this level in recent years, ONE reports.

The 18-year-old, competing for Maccabi Makfet Petah Tikva, totalled 115.650 points across the four Olympic apparatus - hoop, ball, clubs and ribbon - to move up from 13th place in Thursday's qualification round.
The result carries her into Sunday's hoop apparatus final, giving her a second chance to add to what has already been a productive championships.
Her Israeli teammate, Meital Somkin, finished the all-around final in 17th place with a combined score of 106.650, having advanced from 14th in qualifying.

According to ONE, Somkin - still working her way back from a lengthy injury layoff - remains some way off her best form, though her presence in the 24-strong final field was itself a marker of progress.

The Frankfurt championships, staged at the Festhalle, carry extra weight beyond the medals: they serve as the first qualifying event for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, with the top three finishers in the individual all-around each securing a quota spot for their country.

Munits arrived in Germany with a growing reputation on the World Cup circuit. She won gold in ball at the Sofia and Athens World Cup stops in 2024 and was part of the Israeli team that took European clubs gold the same year.
Sunday's hoop final will be Munits's last individual assignment of the championships, and a strong performance would cap what is already her most consistent global campaign to date.

title: How Fabrizio Romano's transfer-news empire is coming apart
dek: A Daily Mail investigation, relayed by ONE, accuses the Italian journalist of trading accuracy for speed and volume — from shaky 'Here We Go' calls to a widely criticised report on Christian Atsu's death.

verificationSources.label: FourFourTwo - Plettenberg/Romano ITK spat over Yan Diomandé
ESPN - Christian Atsu found dead under rubble in Turkey

body: For a decade, three words from Fabrizio Romano — "Here We Go" — have functioned almost as an official confirmation stamp on football transfers. Now, according to a Daily Mail investigation relayed by the Israeli outlet ONE, that credibility is under the heaviest strain of his career.

ONE reports that the investigation examined the scale and methods behind Romano's operation: a combined 140.3 million followers across social platforms, and a pace of more than 100 posted updates a day during peak windows of the transfer market. Critics cited in the piece argue that sheer volume has become a way of burying the calls that turn out wrong.

The central accusation is that Romano too often publishes information fed to him by a club or agent's camp without waiting to confirm it with the other side of a deal — turning provisional briefings into declarations of fact before contracts are actually signed.

This summer's dispute over Yan Diomandé's move from RB Leipzig to Real Madrid became a flashpoint. Romano declared a full agreement and posted his trademark "Here We Go" while Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg publicly disputed that any fee had been finalised, and Diomandé's representatives at Roc Nation Sports issued a statement condemning what they called fabricated reporting around their clients. A deal eventually did go through weeks later, but only after the public spat played out for days.

The investigation also points to Romano's reporting on Ibrahima Konaté, where a claimed Liverpool renewal and a later 'agreement' with Real Madrid were both floated before the defender's contract situation ultimately resolved very differently to how it had first been described — part of a pattern, the piece argues, of confident announcements that shift with the market rather than preceding it.

A similar case cited is João Félix's protracted transfer saga, in which a reported move to Newcastle United was presented as effectively done before the Portuguese forward ended up elsewhere — one of several instances, according to the investigation, where an 'imminent' deal failed to materialise as described.

Ronald Araújo's loan travels were cited as evidence of the sheer repetition in Romano's output: the investigation counted 13 separate posts on the Uruguayan's Liverpool loan speculation, many adding little or no new information between them.

By far the most serious episode raised is from February 2023. In the aftermath of the earthquake that devastated southern Turkey, Romano told his followers that Newcastle-linked Ghanaian forward Christian Atsu had been found alive in hospital. Atsu was in fact already dead; his body was recovered from the rubble of his apartment building days later. ONE's report states no public apology from Romano over the episode has been documented.

The investigation also notes that Reddit's r/soccer community, with 8.8 million members, banned links to Romano's content, citing excessive volume and allegations that some of his material duplicated the work of other reporters without credit.

On the financial side, ONE cites a 2022 report alleging that intermediaries offered Norwegian clubs promotional posts from Romano at prices in the region of roughly $900 to $4,900 per item — raising questions, the investigation argues, about how commercial relationships with clubs and agents sit alongside his news reporting.

None of this has dented Romano's commercial reach, but it has visibly rattled him. Separately, Daily Sabah has reported that Romano has hinted at stepping back from the pace of his current coverage, though he has not framed any change as a direct response to the criticism.

For now, Romano remains the dominant voice in transfer journalism and continues to break genuine, confirmed deals daily. But the investigation ONE is reporting on lands at a moment when rival reporters, clubs and fans are increasingly willing to question whether 'Here We Go' still means what it once did.

Reddit's r/soccer community (8.8 million members) banned Romano's content over volume and alleged plagiarism concerns.

title: Court dismisses child support case against Luka Dončić after stormy hearing
dek: Anamaria Goltes asked to withdraw her Los Angeles petition in favour of an amicable, mutually agreed resolution, but the remote hearing was marked by sharp exchanges between the two sides' lawyers.
body: A Los Angeles County court dismissed the child support claim filed against Lakers star Luka Dončić by his former fiancée, Anamaria Goltes, bringing a stormy, remotely conducted hearing to an abrupt close, ONE reports.

Goltes had filed the petition back in March, seeking child support and legal fees for the couple's two young daughters. Then, days before the hearing, on August 3, her side asked the court to withdraw the case entirely.

"I am withdrawing my Petition for Child Support with the specific intention of resolving this matter amicably and by a mutual agreement which is in the best interests of our children," Goltes said in the filing.

The hearing itself was tense. Dončić's attorney, the high-profile Los Angeles divorce lawyer Laura Wasser, had already moved to have the petition thrown out, telling the court in filings that the "California petition is a clear attempt to forum shop and avail herself of the generous amounts of child support for which California is well-known."

Wasser was then caught off guard when Goltes's attorney, Evan C. Itzkowitz, announced he would seek to drop the case altogether rather than argue it. "I believe Mr. Itzkowitz is going to tell you he seeks to dismiss the proceeding entirely," Wasser told the judge, according to ONE's account of the exchange.

The judge ultimately dismissed the case without prejudice - a ruling that settles nothing on the merits and leaves Goltes free to refile the claim in California at a later date if the two sides cannot reach a private agreement.

Central to Dončić's objection was jurisdiction: neither he nor the couple's daughters are California residents, his lawyers argued, since the children live in Slovenia. He has separately filed his own petition addressing custody and support there.

Dončić and Goltes, both Slovenian natives, had been a couple since 2016. He announced their split in March, shortly after the birth of their second daughter, Olivia; the couple also have an older daughter, Gabriela. Goltes relocated with the children to Slovenia in May.

The Los Angeles filing is not the end of the financial dispute. According to TMZ reporting cited by ONE, Goltes is separately seeking roughly $50 million through proceedings in Slovenia - about $40 million for herself and $10 million earmarked for the two daughters.

The legal drama has played out as Dončić settles into life with the Lakers, for whom he signed a three-year, $165 million contract - keeping one of basketball's biggest stars, and now his messy personal saga, firmly in the spotlight.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv open talks to sign Belgian winger Thibo Baeten
dek: ONE reports the club have approached Go Ahead Eagles over a loan-with-option deal for the 24-year-old, whom Dutch media say is himself keen on a move to Israel.

verificationSources.label: Voetbalprimeur - Go Ahead Eagles-aanvaller Baeten gelinkt aan Maccabi Tel Aviv

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have opened talks with Go Ahead Eagles over a move for Thibo Baeten, ONE reports, as the Israeli champions look to add width on the right flank before the transfer window closes.

Baeten, a 24-year-old Belgian, is primarily a left winger but has also operated on the right, which is understood to be the specific gap Maccabi are trying to fill. His market value is put at around €500,000.

According to ONE, the shape of the proposed deal is a loan with a purchase option that could become obligatory if certain conditions are met — a structure increasingly common in Maccabi's recent recruitment abroad.

Dutch outlet Voetbalprimeur reports that Go Ahead Eagles have already rejected an opening proposal from the Israeli club, though the two sides remain in contact as they try to find a formula both can accept.

The player's own stance appears to be the most encouraging sign for Maccabi: Dutch reports state Baeten is interested in the move and open to joining the Yellow-and-Blue, which could give the Israeli club leverage in further talks with Go Ahead.
Baeten is under contract in Deventer until the summer of 2029, giving Go Ahead Eagles little financial pressure to sell cheaply or quickly, even with the player reportedly receptive to leaving.

He came through Club Brugge's youth system before joining NEC Nijmegen in January 2021, then spent loan spells at Torino and Beerschot before signing permanently for Beerschot in 2023. Go Ahead Eagles bought him that same summer for a reported €400,000.

Since arriving in the Eredivisie, Baeten has been used mainly from the left but has featured across Go Ahead's forward line, and he has represented Belgium at youth level without yet earning a senior call-up.

Nothing is close to being finalised. ONE's report frames this as an opening round of contact rather than an agreed deal, and Go Ahead's rejection of the first proposal suggests Maccabi will need to sweeten their terms if they want to get a deal over the line.
