title: Bezos-backed consortium agrees deal to buy a third of Liverpool
dek: 1892 Holdings, fronted by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia and financed by the Amazon founder alongside the Saverin and Mittal families, values the Premier League champions at up to $7.45 billion in the richest investment ever made in a football club.
body: Fenway Sports Group has agreed to sell roughly a third of Liverpool to a consortium fronted by Jeff Bezos, in a deal that hands the Amazon founder a stake in the reigning Premier League champions without putting him on the club's board.

The buying group, formally named 1892 Holdings after Liverpool's founding year, is led by the British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, son-in-law of steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, ONE reported. Bhatia will become Liverpool's new vice-chairman and join an expanded board, while Bezos's investment vehicle, K5, takes a financial position without a seat at the table.

Also in the group are Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co-founder, and his wife Elaine, investing through their family office EE Capital, along with trusts tied to the Mittal family. K5's Bryan Baum and Elaine Saverin are expected to join the board alongside Bhatia.

The stake sold is close to 30% of the club, according to the reporting, valuing Liverpool at somewhere between £5 billion and £6 billion — figures that translate to roughly $7 billion to $7.45 billion and make this the largest single investment ever made in a football club, eclipsing Sir Jim Ratcliffe's 2024 purchase of a stake in Manchester United, which valued that club at around $5.8 billion.

Fenway Sports Group, which bought Liverpool outright for £300 million back in 2010, will keep majority ownership and day-to-day operational control of the club. The American group first opened talks over outside investment earlier this year as it weighed how to fund the club's next phase of growth without ceding command.

Crucially, the new investors have also secured an option to buy out FSG entirely and become Liverpool's controlling owners within the next 12 months, at a valuation understood to be in the region of $8 billion — a mechanism that leaves open the possibility of a full change of control down the line even as FSG insists it intends to stay on.

FSG president Mike Gordon framed the move as strengthening rather than diluting the club's direction. "Liverpool was always built thinking beyond one season," he said, adding that the new partners' experience "will complement the strong foundation already here."
Bhatia, for his part, struck a similar note of continuity. "We are investing because we deeply believe in Liverpool and its leadership, and expect to support the club's continued success," he said.

The deal is still subject to regulatory approvals and standard closing conditions, and reporting on both sides of the Atlantic has stressed it does not come with a promise of fresh transfer funds — the investment is structured as ownership capital, not a war chest for Arne Slot's squad.

For a club that went from a £300 million takeover to a valuation north of £5 billion in sixteen years, the arrival of one of the world's richest men as a passive shareholder is another marker of how far the Premier League's financial ceiling has risen — and of how much appetite remains among global capital for a stake in England's most successful clubs.
facts: Fenway Sports Group has agreed to sell close to 30% (a third) of Liverpool FC to a consortium named 1892 Holdings.
The consortium is led by Amit Bhatia and includes Jeff Bezos (via K5), Eduardo and Elaine Saverin (via EE Capital) and Mittal family trusts.
The deal values Liverpool at between roughly £5bn and £6bn (about $7bn-$7.45bn), a record for investment in a football club.
Amit Bhatia will become Liverpool's vice-chairman and join the board; Jeff Bezos will not take a board seat.
FSG retains majority ownership and operational control of the club, which it bought for £300 million in 2010.
The new investor group holds an option to become Liverpool's controlling owners within 12 months at a valuation of around $8 billion.
The transaction remains subject to regulatory approval and standard closing conditions.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva's Champions League shock forces a mass clearout at Red Star Belgrade
dek: General manager Zvezdan Terzić says up to ten players will leave as the Serbian giants rebuild under new coach Albert Riera, a week after being eliminated from Europe by the Israeli club.
body: A week after Hapoel Beer Sheva pulled off one of the great Israeli European results of the season, the shockwaves are still rattling Red Star Belgrade's Marakana. ONE reports that the Serbian giants are dismantling large parts of a 33-man first-team squad in direct response to their Champions League elimination — a clean-out general manager Zvezdan Terzić says will touch as many as ten players.

Beer Sheva's win was as emphatic as it was unexpected. Zahi Ahmed's first-half strike settled the first leg 1-0 in the south of Israel on August 4, and a week later in Belgrade, Igor Zlatanović struck in the 61st minute before Javon East added a second late on, completing a 2-0 second-leg victory and a 3-0 aggregate scoreline that sent Red Star crashing out of the third qualifying round.

It was a stunning reversal for a club that had strolled through its two previous qualifying rounds by an aggregate score of 9-0. According to ONE, the elimination is projected to cost Red Star around €30 million in lost Champions League revenue, a hit significant enough to reshape the club's entire transfer-window planning.

The fallout has already claimed a coaching change, with Dejan Stanković making way for the Spaniard Albert Riera. The former Liverpool and Espanyol winger, ONE reports, wants a far leaner squad to work with than the one he has inherited — and Terzić has confirmed the club is obliging him.

Red Star currently carry 33 players in the senior squad; Riera is understood to want that number down to roughly 23 first-teamers plus one or two academy prospects training alongside them. "We have to lighten the load," Terzić said, according to the report, pointing out that a club now negotiating a lower European tier cannot sustain a squad built for the Champions League group stage.

Several of the departures are already effectively decided. Mahmud Bađo, Tomas Handel, Vladimir Lučić, Rodrigo and Šavi Babika have been training apart from the first-team group since before Stanković's exit. Bađo, despite his exile from the main squad, is reportedly the most sought-after of the group, with Terzić saying the club fields multiple enquiries for him every week.

A second tier of players — Franklin Tebo Učena, Nikola Stanković, Timi Maks Elšnik and Bruno Duarte — are expected to leave if acceptable offers materialise before the window closes, rather than being pushed out immediately.
There is also a looming deadline on loan defender Strahinja Eraković, who reverts automatically to parent club Zenit St Petersburg unless Red Star exercise a buyout option before the end of August.

On the incoming side of the ledger, Red Star are leaning on player sales to help offset the European shortfall. Armenian international defender Nair Tiknizyan is the subject of a reported €5 million bid from Olympiacos, with Serbian outlets describing the two clubs as roughly €1 million apart in their valuations.

For Beer Sheva, the story is a footnote to a famous night — the club now turns to a play-off round against the winner of Celje and Ararat-Armenia, with a place in the Champions League league phase still within reach. For Red Star, it is the start of a turbulent transfer window forced almost entirely by an Israeli underdog they were expected to swat aside.

title: British cyclist Finlay Tarling, 19, dies after car strikes him at Volta a Portugal
dek: The NSN Development Team rider, younger brother of Ineos star Josh Tarling, was hit by a vehicle that had entered the course against the direction of racing during stage eight, forcing organisers to suspend the stage and cancel the podium ceremony.
body: British rider Finlay Tarling, one of Welsh cycling's brightest young hopes, died on Friday after a car travelling the wrong way struck him during the eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal. He was 19.

Tarling, who rode for the NSN Development Team, was hit by a vehicle that had entered the course and was not part of the official race convoy, according to Portuguese broadcaster RTP, which was covering the stage live. Race organisers and the Portuguese Cycling Federation confirmed his death shortly afterwards.

The stage was suspended with roughly 20 kilometres still to race once news of the collision reached the peloton. The Portuguese federation said the event would be neutralised and that, "as a mark of honour and mourning," the day's podium ceremony would not go ahead.
Tour organisers said in a statement: "We deeply convey our sincere condolences to Finlay Tarling's family, his teammates, NSN Development Team and all his friends and loved ones."

NSN Development Team paid its own tribute to the teenager. "Fin was a much-loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many," the team said. "He will be deeply missed."

Tarling's death is felt especially keenly in cycling because of his family ties to the sport. His older brother, Josh Tarling, is an Olympic-level rider for Netcompany-Ineos and one of Britain's leading time trial specialists — meaning the tragedy struck at the heart of one of the sport's most prominent cycling families.

NSN Development Team is the feeder squad of NSN Cycling Team, the WorldTour outfit that raced for over a decade as Israel-Premier Tech before its rebrand last November. The team was taken over by a group co-founded by former Barcelona and Spain great Andrés Iniesta, alongside the Swiss investment platform Stoneweg, with Israeli-Canadian businessman Sylvan Adams — the team's longtime co-owner — stepping back from day-to-day involvement as part of the overhaul.
Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro also offered condolences, saying the news of Tarling's death "leaves us deeply shaken."

Tarling had marked himself out as a genuine talent on the track as well as the road. He won silver in the team pursuit at the 2023 Junior European Track Championships and was runner-up at the Junior Chrono des Nations that year, before taking gold with Team Wales in the team pursuit at the 2024 British National Track Championships and adding bronze medals at both the UEC European Track Championships and the UCI Junior World Championships, setting a national record along the way.

Those close to the sport regarded him as a rider particularly suited to time trials and classics-style racing, with a long career expected ahead of him before Friday's tragedy on the roads of northern Portugal.

title: Ciro Immobile retires from football at 36 after injury-hit spell at Paris FC
dek: The four-time Serie A top scorer and Euro 2020 winner with Italy hangs up his boots, ending a career built on nearly a decade as Lazio's talisman.
body: Ciro Immobile called time on his playing career on Friday, announcing his retirement from professional football at 36 after persistent injury problems finally caught up with one of Italian football's great modern strikers.

The Italian told his Paris FC teammates the news in person, fighting back tears as he did so, according to reports from the club's training base. He had joined the French club in January on a contract that ran through June 2027, but has now mutually terminated the deal rather than fight through further injury setbacks.

It was a modest final chapter for a player who leaves the game with 656 appearances and 350 goals across his career. In his last season he made just 12 appearances for Paris FC, scoring twice and adding two assists, a far cry from the numbers that once made him one of Europe's most feared forwards.

Immobile's path to the top was anything but linear. He came through Juventus' academy before a string of loan spells at Grosseto, Siena, Sorrento and Pescara helped him find his scoring touch, and a prolific season at Torino earned him a move to Borussia Dortmund in 2014. Spells in Germany and at Sevilla followed, neither quite matching expectations, before he returned to Italy and found a permanent home.

That home was Lazio, where Immobile arrived in 2016 and stayed for eight seasons, becoming the club's all-time leading scorer and a fixture of Rome's football landscape. He finished his Lazio career with more than 200 goals for the club, surpassing the legendary Silvio Piola along the way.

He was Serie A's top scorer four times, an Italian record that leaves him one behind Gunnar Nordahl's all-time mark of five capocannoniere titles. His finest individual season came in 2019-20, when he struck 36 goals in 37 league games to win the European Golden Shoe outright.

On the international stage, Immobile earned 57 caps for Italy and scored 17 goals, and he was part of the squad that won Euro 2020, beating England on penalties in the final at Wembley after a 1-1 draw. It remains the crowning achievement of his career.

His departure from Lazio in 2024 led to a brief, unsettled spell that took in Bologna before he moved to Paris FC in January, hoping for a fresh start in Ligue 1. Instead, recurring injuries limited him to bit-part appearances and ultimately hastened the end.

Immobile said the time had come to spend more time with his family, who he said had followed him everywhere throughout his career and to whom he owed so much. It is a quiet, family-first exit for a striker who spent the best part of two decades among Serie A's most feared finishers.

title: Kapitolnik ties for fifth in high jump final at European Championships
dek: The Israeli clears 2.23m in Birmingham but three misses at 2.27m cost him a shot at bronze, as Gianmarco Tamberi takes gold.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — 2026 European Athletics Championships, Men's high jump

body: Yonathan Kapitolnik came within one height of a first senior European medal on Friday, clearing 2.23m to finish tied for fifth in the men's high jump final at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.

The Israeli opened cleanly with 2.18m, then needed a second attempt to get over 2.23m after a first-try miss. From there the bar climbed to 2.27m — the height that would ultimately decide bronze — and Kapitolnik failed all three attempts, ending his interest in the podium.
Gold went to Italy's Gianmarco Tamberi, who cleared 2.32m, with Ukraine's Oleh Doroshchuk taking silver at 2.30m. Matteo Sioli completed an Italian one-two in the medals with bronze at 2.27m.
Kapitolnik shared fifth place at 2.23m with Poland's Mateusz Kołodziejski and Britain's Kimani Jack and Joel Clarke-Khan, according to the official results published by European Athletics.

"The competition was good for me," Kapitolnik said, quoted by ONE. "I had a difficult and long season full of injuries... I felt I did my best. The weather wasn't simple... I'm a bit disappointed I didn't make the 2.27."

The 23-year-old arrived in Birmingham off the back of a stop-start year after a 2023 season disrupted by injury. He signalled his return to top form with an indoor personal best of 2.31m in Tel Aviv in February 2025, just shy of his outdoor mark of 2.30m from 2022.

Kapitolnik remains one of Israeli athletics' brightest prospects, having won world and European U20 titles in 2021 and a World University Games gold in 2025, alongside six straight Israeli national titles. A top-five finish in a major senior final, even without a medal, keeps him firmly inside Europe's elite bracket heading into the rest of the season.

title: Yamal, Mbappé and the stars chasing football's rarest treble after Rodri
dek: ONE runs through seven active players — from Lamine Yamal to Julián Álvarez — it rates as the best-placed to join Rodri in winning the World Cup, the Champions League and the Ballon d'Or.

verificationSources.label: ONE — בעקבות רודרי: הכוכבים שרוצים להשלים את הכדורגל
Manchester City — Rodri makes history after World Cup triumph
UEFA.com — Ousmane Dembélé wins 2025 Men's Ballon d'Or
ESPN — Spain World Cup 2026 squad confirmed: Lamine Yamal stars

body: Rodri's Ballon d'Or, won in 2024, already sat alongside a Champions League winner's medal from 2023. But it took Spain beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 World Cup final for the Manchester City midfielder to complete one of football's rarest personal collections. He is now the 11th man in the game's history to have won the World Cup, the Champions League and the Ballon d'Or — and in the days since, ONE has run through the players it believes are best placed to join him.

It is exclusive company. Sir Bobby Charlton, Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer, Paolo Rossi, Zinedine Zidane, Rivaldo, Ronaldinho, Kaká, Lionel Messi and Ousmane Dembélé — who completed his own set only last October by winning the 2025 Ballon d'Or — all got there before Rodri. ONE's list of seven candidates, ranked by the outlet's own reckoning, runs from a teenager barely two years into his senior career to players already well into their careers.

Lamine Yamal tops it. The Barcelona forward already has Euro 2024 and now the World Cup itself with Spain, and after the final in the summer he said he had 'almost completed the set.' He finished runner-up to Dembélé in the 2025 Ballon d'Or voting, and with Barcelona building a squad under Hansi Flick they hope can compete for the Champions League, ONE rates him needing just two more trophies at an age when most players are still fighting for a regular first-team place.

Kylian Mbappé has held a World Cup winner's medal since 2018, when he inspired France to the title as a teenager. What he lacks, ONE notes, is the Champions League — a trophy that eluded him throughout his years at Paris Saint-Germain and has eluded him at Real Madrid so far too — and the Ballon d'Or, where his best finish remains third, behind Messi and Erling Haaland, in 2023.

Jude Bellingham already has the Champions League, lifted with Real Madrid in 2024. The World Cup and the Ballon d'Or are the pieces missing, and ONE points to the obvious question mark over England's prospects of ending their long wait for a major trophy — with the next World Cup not arriving until 2030.

Aurélien Tchouaméni starts furthest back of the seven, with none of the three yet to his name. The France and Real Madrid midfielder was on the losing side in the 2022 World Cup final, but ONE rates him a plausible future Ballon d'Or contender given his growing influence in central midfield.

Vitinha already has a Champions League winner's medal from Paris Saint-Germain's continental triumph and finished third in the 2025 Ballon d'Or voting, behind Dembélé and Yamal. A World Cup with Portugal is the trophy ONE says he is still chasing.

Julián Álvarez may be the closest of all, even if he rarely gets framed that way. The Argentine already has the World Cup, won as a 22-year-old in Qatar in 2022, and the Champions League, lifted with Manchester City in 2023. Only the Ballon d'Or is missing, and ONE notes his continued goalscoring form at Atlético Madrid keeps building the case.

Vinícius Júnior completes the list. Two Champions League titles with Real Madrid put him among the favourites eventually to complete the set, but the World Cup and the Ballon d'Or remain outstanding — and with Brazil's next World Cup not arriving until 2030, when he turns 30, ONE suggests the clock on both is not unlimited.

What the piece really underlines, published in the immediate aftermath of Rodri's own achievement, is just how rare the combination remains even among the players who define the modern game: ten legends spanning six decades, now an eleventh — and, on ONE's own reckoning, seven more names with a route, however narrow, to joining them.

title: Al-Hilal 4-2 Al-Faisaly: Benzema and Neves inspire winning start under Inzaghi
dek: Karim Benzema scored from the penalty spot and Rúben Neves converted twice more as Al-Hilal survived a second-half fightback from promoted Al-Faisaly to open the Saudi Pro League season with a win.
body: Al-Hilal opened their Saudi Pro League campaign in style on Friday night, holding off a spirited second-half comeback from newly promoted Al-Faisaly to win 4-2 at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh.

Karim Benzema set the tone inside 19 minutes, sending the goalkeeper the wrong way from the penalty spot for his first goal of the new season. Malcolm doubled the lead seven minutes later with a well-worked finish from a set piece, and by the half-hour mark Al-Hilal were 3-0 up after Rúben Neves converted a second penalty of the night in the 28th minute.
It was a dominant opening 45 minutes that left Al-Faisaly, playing their first-ever Saudi Pro League fixture after winning promotion from the second tier, chasing shadows.

The visitors, however, refused to fold. Alexandre Mendy pulled a goal back on 59 minutes with a well-taken finish, and five minutes later Théo Bongonda headed in from close range to make it 3-2 and give Al-Faisaly genuine hope of an extraordinary opening-day upset.

Al-Hilal steadied themselves and put the contest to bed in the 82nd minute, when Neves stepped up for his second penalty of the match — and the third awarded to Al-Hilal on the night — to restore the two-goal cushion and seal a 4-2 win.

ONE reported that the result sent an early message to defending champions Al-Nassr, with Al-Hilal having finished runners-up in the Saudi Pro League in each of the last two seasons after losing out to their Riyadh rivals on the final day last term.

The win came under head coach Simone Inzaghi, who has said he wants Al-Hilal to play a more attacking brand of football this season. The Italian left Portuguese defender João Cancelo out of his squad for the opener because of fitness doubts, while forward Darwin Núñez and goalkeeper Yassine Bounou were among the other big names involved as the club begins life without a title for a third straight year.

For Al-Faisaly, the afternoon offered both a reminder of the gulf in class at the top of Saudi football and evidence that the promoted side can trouble even the country's biggest spenders — Mendy and Bongonda both found the net against one of the most expensively assembled squads in the league.

Benzema's penalty was his first goal since moving to Al-Hilal from local rivals Al-Ittihad in February, a switch that followed a breakdown in contract talks at his previous club. The 38-year-old former Real Madrid and France striker will be looking to build on the opening-day goal as Al-Hilal chase a return to the Saudi Pro League summit.

title: Adva Cohen finishes 10th in 3,000m steeplechase final at European Championships
dek: The Israeli record holder closed her Birmingham campaign short of her career-best continental finishes, as Germany's Gesa Felicitas Krause took gold in a tight final.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — 2026 European Athletics Championships, Women's 3000m steeplechase
European Athletics — Krause profile ahead of Birmingham 2026

body: Adva Cohen's European Championships campaign ended in 10th place on Thursday evening, as the Israeli steeplechase record holder crossed the line at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham in 9:38.21 in the women's 3,000m steeplechase final.

The race went to Germany, with Gesa Felicitas Krause taking gold in 9:12.69 to add another continental title to a career already stacked with European medals. France's Alice Finot, the defending champion, settled for silver in 9:14.24, while Germany's Olivia Gürth completed the podium in 9:15.33.

Cohen had booked her place in the 16-woman final by finishing eighth in her heat two days earlier, clocking 9:37.15 to comfortably progress. In the final itself she was unable to find the closing kick that has carried her to faster times this season, drifting back through the field over the closing laps of hurdles and water jumps.

The result sits below Cohen's personal best of 9:19.90, the Israeli record she set at last year's World Championships in Tokyo — a mark that remains the benchmark for Israeli women's distance running.

It is also a step back from her two previous European finals. Cohen finished fifth in Berlin in 2018, still her best continental placing, and eighth in Munich in 2022. A 10th-place finish in Birmingham, while respectable against a strong European field, does not match that trajectory.

At 30, Cohen remains Israel's leading steeplechaser and one of the country's most consistent championship performers, with three World Championships and an Olympic appearance in Tokyo already behind her. Thursday's run in Birmingham adds another data point to a season in which she has already broken her own Israeli record once, but it ends her 2026 European campaign without the medal-contending finish some had hoped for after her form over the summer.

title: Lelior beats Gallina 9.50-5.76 to reach Tahiti Pro semi-final
dek: The Israeli rookie, fresh off eliminating world No. 1 Gabriela Bryan, out-scored local wildcard Kelia Gallina at Teahupo'o to book a semi-final berth in her first Championship Tour season.

verificationSources.label: World Surf League - Anat Lelior event results

body: Anat Lelior is through to the semi-finals of the Outerknown Tahiti Pro, beating French Polynesian wildcard Kelia Gallina 9.50 to 5.76 in a tense quarterfinal heat at the fearsome Teahupo'o reef pass.

It capped a remarkable run through the draw for the 26-year-old from Tel Aviv, who opened the event with a win over Australia's Sally Fitzgibbons (4.16 to 1.67) before producing the result of her young career: a lopsided 12.73-1.46 demolition of Gabriela Bryan, the reigning world No. 1, in round two.

The World Surf League's own recap of that heat put it bluntly, describing the 2026 Championship Tour rookie as "besting World No. 1 Gabriela Bryan in convincing form and sending herself over the ledge throughout her round two clash" — the kind of form that has turned Lelior into one of the storylines of the women's tour this week.

Gallina, surfing in front of a home crowd on the wave that produced some of the sport's most dangerous barrels, pushed the Israeli deep into the heat before Lelior's scoreline pulled clear. It is Lelior's furthest advance yet on the elite tour she only joined this season.

She began the year ranked 17th on the Championship Tour rankings after graduating from the qualifying circuit, and had shown signs of this ceiling earlier in the season with a quarterfinal run in El Salvador, where she beat Stephanie Gilmore and Sawyer Lindblad before also falling to Bryan.

Teahupo'o is not unfamiliar territory. The wave hosted Olympic surfing at the 2024 Paris Games, where Lelior reached the round of 16 and finished ninth overall — a career-best Olympic result that followed a 17th-place finish at Tokyo 2020, her Games debut.

A semi-final berth now leaves Lelior one win from the final of a Championship Tour event in her rookie season, a result that would mark the biggest result by an Israeli surfer in the sport's top tier. Her semi-final opponent and the schedule for the next round had not yet been confirmed at the time of writing.

The Outerknown Tahiti Pro runs at Teahupo'o through August 18, with the women's draw narrowing fast after a stop-start week that saw organisers repeatedly wait out swell and wind conditions before calling the competition on.

title: Russell Westbrook retires after 18 seasons as one of the NBA's most divisive superstars
dek: The nine-time All-Star and 2017 MVP walks away as the league's all-time triple-double king, days after a viral rumour linking him to Hapoel Tel Aviv was exposed as a hoax.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports (Hapoel Tel Aviv rumour debunked)

body: Russell Westbrook, one of the most combustible and record-shattering players of his generation, announced his retirement from the NBA on Wednesday, closing out an 18-season career with a farewell video narrated by actor Michael B. Jordan.

The nine-time All-Star leaves the game as the NBA's all-time leader in triple-doubles, fifth on the career assists list and 14th in career scoring — remarkable longevity for a player built on relentless, high-motor intensity rather than a game that ages gracefully.

His signature season came in 2016/17, when Westbrook averaged 31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists a game for the Oklahoma City Thunder — the first player since Oscar Robertson in 1962 to average a triple-double across an entire campaign. He was named MVP that year after dragging a post-Kevin Durant Thunder team to 47 wins and a playoff berth.

ONE, citing ESPN's assessment of his career, described Westbrook as "fearless and exceptionally self-confident," noting that once Durant left for Golden State in 2016, he "immediately seized the opportunity to become the Thunder's undisputed leader," for better and occasionally for worse.

Drafted fourth overall by the Seattle SuperSonics in 2008 — the franchise that relocated to Oklahoma City a year later — Westbrook spent 11 seasons as the face of the Thunder before a 2019 trade to the Houston Rockets began a well-travelled final chapter of his career. He went on to play for the Washington Wizards, Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Clippers, Denver Nuggets and, in his final season, the Sacramento Kings.
He finishes with career averages of 20.9 points, eight assists and 6.9 rebounds across 1,301 games, having reached the NBA Finals once, in 2012 with the Thunder, without ever winning a championship.

As ONE's report on the American reaction to his retirement put it, Westbrook was as much a cultural figure as a basketball one — his outsized fashion sense and confrontational, no-compromise personality made him a lightning rod with coaches, media and opposing fans throughout his career, even as his statistical dominance was undeniable.

That legacy is already under threat. Denver's Nikola Jokic has piled up 198 regular-season triple-doubles and needs only 11 more to pass Westbrook's mark of 209 — a total Jokic, who posted 34 triple-doubles last season alone, looks on course to surpass before long.

Westbrook's name had also been swirling in an entirely different context in the days before his announcement: a report claiming he was in advanced talks over a move to Israeli club Hapoel Tel Aviv went viral on social media over the weekend. NBA reporter Marc Stein and others quickly shot the story down as "laughably false," tracing it back to a parody account — Westbrook was never seriously weighing a move abroad, and had genuine NBA offers from the Kings and the Wizards before choosing to step away instead.

With the retirement now official, attention turns to Westbrook's Hall of Fame case: a former MVP, a nine-time All-Star and the league's triple-double king, but also a player whose brilliance rarely translated into team success at the very top of the sport.

title: The pricey, the cheap and the bargains: fantasy football's must-know La Liga names
dek: ONE's fantasy football desk breaks down which La Liga stars are worth their price tag for 2026/27 — and flags the picks that could be a trap.

body: With Spain's title race about to kick off again, ONE's Fantasy game — sponsored by Migdal — has published its annual value guide for the 2026/27 La Liga season, sorting the stars worth their price tag from the ones fantasy managers should think twice about.

At the very top of the market sit Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé, both priced at 15 million in the game — the joint-most expensive picks available, reflecting the outsized returns each produced last season.

One tier down, at 13 million apiece, ONE lists Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham alongside Barcelona's Raphinha and Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez. The guide is notably lukewarm on Álvarez, pointing out he managed only eight La Liga goals last season and questioning whether he still justifies a premium price.

Among the mid-priced options, ONE highlights Lee Kang-in at 9 million. The South Korean international, who starred for his country at the 2026 World Cup, completed a move from Paris Saint-Germain to Atlético Madrid in late July on a contract through 2031, and the guide frames him as an attacking-midfield option who could offer good value in his new colours.

The piece also runs through several cheaper options further down the price list that ONE believes could outperform their tag, though a number of the names and club attributions in the original report could not be independently verified against an official squad list or registry in time for this draft.

As with any fantasy guide, the underlying message is about balance: spend big on the two or three players capable of carrying a squad, then look for cut-price picks in good European or domestic form to fill out the rest of the XI.
ONE's full breakdown, including its complete list of budget-tier recommendations, is available on one.co.il.

title: Israeli football fans launch first-ever cross-club union to improve matchday experience
dek: Supporters' groups from 11 clubs across the Premier League and National League have formed a new fans' federation pushing for water bottles in stadiums, shorter queues and better treatment on matchday, ONE reports.
body: For the first time, supporters' groups from 11 Israeli football clubs have joined forces to launch a single body speaking on behalf of fans across the Premier League and National League, ONE reported this week.

The new fans' federation — a cross-club initiative independently confirmed by Sport5 — aims to give supporters a unified voice on issues that have long frustrated matchgoers: entry queues, security arrangements and the treatment of fans inside and outside the stadium.

Among the founding representatives who spoke to ONE were Barak Matzger of Maccabi Haifa's Northern Stand fan organisation and Shai Wolf of Maccabi Tel Aviv's Achim LaSemel group — two of the country's more established supporters' bodies, now sitting at the same table on behalf of rival fan bases.

"The goal is to improve the fan experience," Matzger told the outlet, adding that the federation intends to work "without pressure" and instead build what he called good feelings between supporters, clubs and the authorities who run matchdays.

Wolf was more specific about the wish list. "Expectations are that fan experience improves," he said, citing two immediate priorities: allowing fans to bring water bottles into stadiums, and shortening the queues that regularly build up at turnstiles before kick-off.

Beyond those headline items, the group wants a better ratio of security personnel to fans, improved parking arrangements around grounds that are often hard to reach by car, and greater use of public transport — Tel Aviv's light rail link to Bloomfield Stadium was cited as one example of infrastructure fans should be encouraged to use.

Sport5's account of the launch added further detail, quoting other representatives — among them Ben Buda and Plag Levinson — who raised ticket and concession prices, streamlined entry procedures and a more organised approach to pyrotechnics as further items on the federation's agenda. "People come to stadiums for the atmosphere too, and we cannot lose that," Buda said, while Levinson stressed that club rivalries would not get in the way: "When discussing fan experience, rivalries don't matter... we're organised to bring solutions, not waste time."

With the new season approaching, the federation says it plans regular dialogue with clubs, the league and other stakeholders — an attempt to turn a long list of matchday grievances into a standing channel of communication rather than one-off complaints.

title: New book: Yaakov Shahar ran Maccabi Haifa "like his businesses" — and changed Israeli football
dek: A doctoral study turned book on the 1992-2006 revolution at Maccabi Haifa credits owner Yaakov Shahar with importing corporate discipline into a game that had never seen it before.
body: It is one of the more unlikely footnotes in modern Israeli football: a car importer who bought a struggling Haifa club in 1992 and, according to a new academic study, quietly rewrote the rules of how the sport is run here.

ONE reports on a new book by Dr. Moshe Talsnick, published under the title "The Football Experts" and based on his doctoral dissertation examining Maccabi Haifa's transformation between 1992 and 2006 — the years in which, Talsnick argues, the club evolved from a politically-run sports association into a professional business organisation.

At the centre of that shift was Yaakov "Yankele" Shahar, the businessman behind the Meir Group, Israel's importer of Volvo and Honda vehicles. Shahar took control of Maccabi Haifa in 1992 through his company Kesher Sport, and, per the book, "decided to manage the club like his businesses."

"It succeeded for Yankele, who introduced things that didn't exist in football," Talsnick is quoted as saying, describing a wave of professionalisation that the Israeli game had not seen before a businessman first bought a club.

Among the innovations attributed to Shahar in the book: the appointment of Gai Peleg as the club's first-ever spokesperson, the introduction of sports psychologists and dedicated fitness coaches, and training methods built around specific playing positions rather than blanket regimes for the whole squad.
The takeover itself, according to the book, began life as a three-year trial before Shahar committed to what became a permanent, decades-long ownership.

That history is well documented independently of the book. Shahar, born in 1941, has now owned and presided over Maccabi Haifa for well over three decades, investing more than 150 million shekels in the club along the way and steering it to championships in 1993/94 — his second season in charge, won undefeated — through further titles under Avram Grant and Ronny Levy, and, most recently, three consecutive championships between 2020/21 and 2022/23. Under his ownership Maccabi Haifa has also reached the Champions League group stage three times, a record for an Israeli club.

"The Football Experts" has just been published and is being marketed, in part, directly to Maccabi Haifa's fanbase — a reminder that for the club's supporters, Shahar's business-first approach is not just academic history but the foundation of the modern era they still follow today.

title: Ceuta coach José Juan Romero: 'If it was up to me, we wouldn't play this weekend'
dek: Ahead of AD Ceuta's Segunda División opener at FC Andorra, manager José Juan Romero used his pre-season press conference to speak about the migrant crisis engulfing his city rather than Saturday's game.

verificationSources.label: El Pueblo de Ceuta — fixture details

body: José Juan Romero stood in front of the cameras this week to preview AD Ceuta's opening match of the new Segunda División season, and instead spent much of the press conference talking about something else entirely. "If it were up to me, Ceuta wouldn't play this weekend," the coach said, according to ONE.

It was a striking line from a manager on the eve of a league campaign, but Romero was speaking to the moment. His city has spent the past fortnight at the centre of a severe migrant crisis, after a mass crossing from Morocco triggered emergency talks among EU officials, street protests and days of rolling coverage that Romero feels has still understated how bad things are on the ground.

"It's somewhat embarrassing for me to talk about football with what we're experiencing in Ceuta," he said, adding that "little account is being taken beyond our borders" of the scale of the crisis. He said he knows friends whose children are now too frightened to leave the house, and that even his own family called off a planned visit to the city out of concern for their safety.

Romero drew a direct comparison with Ceuta's last major migrant surge, in May 2021, saying this month's crisis is worse. A demonstration was held in the city on Sunday to press authorities for a stronger response, and Romero suggested more forceful action may follow if the situation does not improve.

The upheaval has not spared the football club either. Romero said the crisis has complicated AD Ceuta's work in the transfer market, limiting the club's room to negotiate and finalise summer signings as the city's institutions and attention are consumed elsewhere.

Despite all of that, Saturday's fixture goes ahead. AD Ceuta open their Segunda División campaign away to FC Andorra at the Nou Estadi d'Encamp on August 15 at 17:00, kicking off a season in Spain's second tier. Romero called the hosts an "extraordinary team that plays excellent football," while confirming defender Josema will miss the trip — a "very significant absence," in his words — with the rest of the first-team squad available and five or six reserve-team players travelling for cover.

For a manager who has led the club since September 2022, the game itself was almost an afterthought next to the message he wanted to send. Romero said he hopes a positive result can offer the city "a thread of hope" at a difficult moment, even as he continues to press for the crisis to receive the attention he believes it deserves.

title: Celta Vigo's La Liga opener against Osasuna postponed after fungus wrecks Balaídos pitch
dek: A fungal outbreak on the Balaídos playing surface, made worse by recent weather, forced La Liga to push the season-opening fixture back to August 27.
body: Celta Vigo's opening fixture of the new La Liga season has been postponed after a fungal outbreak left the pitch at Balaídos unfit for professional football, ONE reports.

The club were due to host Osasuna at home on Sunday, but La Liga, in coordination with both clubs and the Spanish federation (RFEF), called off the match after a disease affecting the grass proved impossible to contain in time.

According to the reporting, a technical inspection just a week earlier had certified the pitch as meeting quality and safety standards, with the fungal treatment appearing to be working. A second, more thorough double inspection was carried out this past week, including an evening check, but conditions had deteriorated again.

Celta's official statement pointed to the weather as the culprit: recent conditions in Vigo had reversed the positive progress the surface had been making, leaving the turf below the standard required for a top-flight match.

The rescheduled fixture will now be played on Thursday, August 27, at 20:30 local time. Celta confirmed that tickets already purchased for the original date will remain valid for the new one, with no action required from supporters.
Celta apologised to fans for the disruption to their season-opening plans, calling the situation exceptional and thanking supporters for their patience.

Osasuna, however, pushed back hard on the decision. The visitors said the two clubs had previously discussed the international break of September 24-25 as a more sensible alternative date, and accused La Liga of a lack of foresight and professionalism in leaving the call so close to kick-off — arguing the late notice disproportionately hurt the travelling side.

Balaídos has been under redevelopment for over a decade and is one of the stadiums under consideration for the 2030 World Cup, with capacity plans of 40,000-44,000 once work is complete — adding an awkward footnote to a ground-condition embarrassment just as Spain's bid for the tournament gathers momentum.

title: Gal Arad misses 200m semi-final by seven thousandths of a second in Birmingham
dek: The Israeli sprinter matched his rival's time on the clock but lost the photo finish to Turkey's Deniz Kaan Kartal at the European Athletics Championships.

verificationSources.label: World Athletics — Deniz Kaan Kartal profile

body: Gal Arad has spent this season chasing a first major semi-final, and in Birmingham on Thursday he came about as close as an athlete can without getting there.

The Israeli sprinter clocked 21.02 seconds in his first-round heat of the men's 200m at the European Athletics Championships, matching the time posted by Turkey's Deniz Kaan Kartal for what looked, on the stadium clock, like a shared 13th place. Photo-finish timing to the thousandth of a second told a different story: Arad's official mark was 21.019 against Kartal's 21.012, ONE reports — a gap of seven thousandths of a second that decided who advanced to the semi-finals at Alexander Stadium and who did not.

It is a brutal way to go out. Arad, 26, races for Maccabi Tel Aviv and has been in the form of his career this year, lowering his personal best to 20.61 seconds in March, a mark still awaiting ratification over its wind reading. He also holds a 100m best of 10.32 seconds and has anchored Israeli relay squads to a national record in the 4x100m.

Kartal, 21, arrived at the championships with a season's best of 20.67 seconds and a Balkan title to his name. The margin between the two on Thursday was the difference between a place in the semi-final program and an early flight home.

Arad was not the only Israeli in action in Birmingham that day. Discus thrower Astel Volano finished 28th in qualifying with a best throw of 51.37 metres, well short of the marks needed to progress, according to ONE.

There was better news from the steeplechase. Adwa Cohen advanced to the final of the women's 3,000m steeplechase after running 9:37.15 in her heat, with that final scheduled for the evening session at Alexander Stadium, due off at 22:25 local time.

The championships, hosted at Alexander Stadium from August 10-16, mark Birmingham's first major athletics event since it staged the 2022 Commonwealth Games at the same venue — and for Arad, a tantalisingly close miss to open the week.

title: Flick keeps Orian Goren in Barcelona's first-team fold as World Cup winners return
dek: The 17-year-old Israeli midfielder from Maccabi Petah Tikva stays part of Hansi Flick's senior group even as Spain's newly crowned world champions rejoin preseason training.

verificationSources.label: Barca Blaugranes — Ferran Torres/World Cup winners return
Barca Universal — Flick names three impressive youngsters

body: Barcelona's dressing room is filling back up with World Cup winners, but Hansi Flick has made a point of keeping one 17-year-old exactly where he is. Orian Goren remains part of the German coach's senior training group, ONE reports, even as the club returns to full strength for the start of the new season.

Goren, born in Ramat Gan in 2009, moved to Barcelona's academy from Maccabi Petah Tikva and has lived and trained at La Masia since 2023. He signed his first professional contract with the club last year, running through 2028, and has quickly become one of the youngest names on Flick's radar — second in age in the wider squad only to the Gambian forward Ebrima Tunkara.

The endorsement from Flick has been public and specific. Asked which of the club's young prospects had stood out to him during preseason work, the coach named three: Tunkara, winger Xavi Espart and Goren, saying the trio had "really impressed" him in training camp.

It is more than just kind words. Goren has already had a taste of senior football, starting as Barcelona beat Club Europa 4-1 in a preseason friendly last month and later coming off the bench against Birmingham City, a game the Catalans lost on penalties after a 2-2 draw. According to ONE, he continues to train alongside fellow academy hopefuls such as goalkeeper Áron Yaakobishvili and Espart rather than being farmed out to Barça Atlètic full-time, at least for now.

The timing matters. Spain's World Cup winners — among them Pau Cubarsí, Dani Olmo and Lamine Yamal — have been steadily rejoining Barcelona training after their run to the title on penalties over Argentina in last month's final in North America, with Ferran Torres scoring the winning goal in extra time. Their return usually squeezes out fringe players, yet Goren has held his place.

Barcelona are also managing an unusually thin midfield. Frenkie de Jong is facing an extended spell on the sidelines, reported by Marca to be close to four months, after picking up a knee problem around the World Cup break — one more reason the club is inclined to keep promising young cover close at hand.

Torres, meanwhile, is on his way out. He has missed training as Barcelona works to finalize his transfer to Paris Saint-Germain, a deal reported to be worth around €50 million plus bonuses and one the club has sanctioned as talks with the French side continue.

None of this guarantees Goren a route into Flick's matchday squads once La Liga begins — Spanish reporting still expects him to spend the bulk of the season with Barça Atlètic in the third tier. But for a teenager who was playing in Israel's youth ranks barely three years ago, simply surviving Flick's preseason cuts alongside the club's World Cup heroes is a considerable marker of trust.

title: ONE launches Rishona, a documentary series tracking Hapoel Rishon LeZion's promotion push
dek: The series will follow the club on and off the pitch this season under new coach Elad Brown, as it tries to end a run of more than a decade outside Israel's top flight.

verificationSources.label: Israeli Football Association – Assi Baldot profile

body: Hapoel Rishon LeZion is getting the fly-on-the-wall treatment. ONE has announced a new documentary series, titled "Rishona," that will follow the club through the coming season as it chases a route back to Israel's top flight.

The premise, as ONE frames it, is simple: how does a club with history, a loyal support base and an entire city behind it find its way back to where it believes it belongs. Cameras will track the squad both in matches and behind the scenes across the campaign.

It is the second entry in what is shaping up as a mini-genre for the broadcaster. "Rishona" follows "Malkat HaShchuna" (Queen of the Neighborhood), ONE's documentary that trailed Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv's season in the HaTikva neighborhood, weaving in veteran Eliran Atar's return to his boyhood club and youngster Jonathan Agyapong, with an original score by Dudu Tassa.

Rishon LeZion enters the new season in the National League, Israel's second tier, still searching for the promotion that has eluded it for years. The club last competed in Ligat Ha'al, the Israeli top flight, back in 2011/12 — and was relegated straight back down after only a single season among the elite.
Last season only sharpened the frustration. Rishon LeZion finished bottom of the top playoff group, losing six of its final seven matches to end the campaign on the worst possible note.

The club has responded by handing the reins to Elad Brown, hired as head coach for 2026/27 after five years in charge of Maccabi Herzliya. Brown has described Rishon LeZion as "a club with tradition, an audience and the potential to be in the Premier League," and has been candid that the National League field this season is unusually strong, with well-funded, well-coached rivals also chasing the two promotion spots.

Part of the appeal for a documentary crew is the club's pedigree. Two graduates of that ill-fated 2011/12 top-flight squad went on to notable careers: Assi Baldot, who scored nine league goals that season but could not prevent the drop, and Omer Atzili, who came through Rishon LeZion's youth ranks and made his top-flight debut for the club in October 2011 before moving on to Beitar Jerusalem and later Maccabi Tel Aviv.

For a club that has spent a decade and a half in the second tier trying to rediscover that level, the series gives Rishon LeZion's promotion push a spotlight well beyond the usual match-day coverage — and puts real pressure on Brown's squad to make the story worth telling.

title: Rodri pushes for Barcelona move as club prepares one last offer to Manchester City
dek: ONE reports the Spain midfielder is piling pressure on his club to sanction a switch to the Camp Nou, with Barcelona readying a final bid after City rejected an earlier package worth up to €70 million.
body: Rodri is actively lobbying Manchester City's hierarchy to let him leave for Barcelona this summer, according to ONE, which reports the Spain midfielder wants the Catalan club to come back to the table with one final, decisive offer.

City knocked back Barcelona's second proposal of €60 million plus €10 million in bonuses, insisting on a fee closer to €80 million for the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner. ONE reports Barcelona are now preparing to return with a last bid worth €65 million guaranteed plus a further €10 million in add-ons, roughly half of which is considered easily attainable.

Rodri has only one year left on his current City contract, a factor Barcelona believe strengthens their negotiating position and could yet force City's hand rather than risk losing him for a reduced fee in twelve months.

Part of City's reluctance, per ONE, is tied to their own business: the club wants proceeds from a Rodri sale to help fund a move for Chelsea's Enzo Fernández, who is being lined up as his eventual replacement in midfield.

The player himself has made his preference clear to the City boardroom, telling them he wants Barcelona and nowhere else. ONE reports he has already turned down a significantly richer financial offer from Real Madrid to keep the Camp Nou move alive — a version of events also carried by Haaretz, which reported Rodri favours Barcelona "over Real Madrid" despite Los Blancos' interest.

The saga has run for weeks and the numbers have shifted steadily. Sky Sports reported City rejecting an initial Barcelona bid as "far too low," while Forbes, citing the Spanish outlet SPORT, described City rejecting a fresh offer even after Rodri had personally agreed terms with Barcelona — underlining how far apart the two boardrooms remain even as the player pushes to get it done.

Rodri, 30, has been one of the most decorated midfielders of his generation since arriving in the Premier League from Atlético Madrid in 2019, winning the Champions League and Ballon d'Or with City in 2023 and 2024 respectively, and lifting Euro 2024 with Spain, whom he captains.

No agreement has been reached between the clubs, and ONE's report makes clear City have yet to move off their asking price. Barcelona's camp, however, believes the gap can be bridged with the improved offer once it is formally tabled.

title: Shuster swims lifetime best to reach 50m backstroke semi-final at Wingate trials
dek: Tomer Shuster clocked 24.62 seconds in the heats, missing the Israeli record by two hundredths and sealing his qualifying standard for the 2027 World Championships, ONE reports.
body: Tomer Shuster produced the swim of his career in the heats of the men's 50m backstroke at the Union Cup national trials in the Wingate Institute pool, touching in a lifetime-best 24.62 seconds to advance to the semi-final in ninth place.

The time left him just two hundredths of a second shy of the Israeli record, ONE reported, and comfortably inside the qualifying standard that Israel's swimming federation has set for the 2027 World Aquatics Championships.

With the swim confirmed, Shuster becomes the sixth Israeli swimmer to lock in a place at the 2027 Worlds, adding his name to a growing squad the national federation is assembling as the qualifying window plays out this summer.

The 22-year-old, who trains with Maccabi Ramat Hasharon under coach Yael Ashkenazi, arrived at Wingate as the reigning Israeli champion in the 100m backstroke — a title he has now won twice, in 2024 and 2026 — and the 2026 national champion over 50m backstroke as well.

He is no stranger to the global stage: Shuster raced the 50m backstroke at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore, finishing 33rd in the heats, and has since committed to swim collegiately for the University of Kentucky from January 2026.

Three other Israelis contested the same event at Wingate without reaching the semi-final. Michael Leitrovsky touched in 25.14 seconds for 27th, Anbar Dantziger went 25.36 for 35th, and Okan Goldin finished 51st in 25.62.

Elsewhere in the session, Israel's men's 4x100m freestyle relay came home 10th in the preliminary heats and missed out on a place in the final, while several Israeli swimmers in the 200m freestyle also failed to advance past the morning round.

Shuster now turns to the semi-final with the Israeli record suddenly within reach — a mark he already looked capable of erasing with a clean swim at Wingate, where the criteria trials continue over the coming days.

title: Roy Levy and Ariel Gal sit third at the 470 World Championship in Japan
dek: The young Israeli duo posted a 10-3-2 scoreline once racing finally got underway in Enoshima, trailing only Switzerland and France in a 74-boat fleet.

verificationSources.label: ONE - פתיחה נהדרת לרועי לוי ואריאל גל באליפות העולם

body: Israeli sailing's brightest young pair opened their senior 470 World Championship campaign in style. Roy Levy and Ariel Gal sit third overall in Enoshima, Japan, after finally getting three races away in a regatta that had been stuck on the beach for days.

ONE reports that the opening day of the championship, run off Japan's Shonan coast from August 10-17, was washed out entirely by rain and a lack of wind. Racing only got going on Thursday, once conditions settled enough for the fleet to head out.

When the boats did race, Levy and Gal made the most of it. They crossed in 10th, 3rd and 2nd across the first three heats, a scoreline that leaves them on just five net points - good enough for third place in a 74-boat fleet from 28 nations, the largest in the class this season.

Only two crews sit ahead of them: a Swiss boat on three points and a French crew on four. It is an early marker, but a striking one for a duo who have spent most of the past two seasons dominating the junior ranks rather than racing at senior World Championship level.
A second Israeli boat is also in the field. Nitai Hason and Noga Tiano sailed to 2nd, 12th and 14th in their opening races and lie 17th overall, according to ONE.

Levy and Gal's rise has been rapid. The pair won the 470 Junior World Championship in Los Alcázares, Spain, last year, having already taken the Junior European title in Vilamoura in 2024, and followed a path through bronze in 2021 and back-to-back silvers in 2022 and 2023. Last month in Gdynia, Poland, they took silver at the Junior Worlds, narrowly missing a second straight junior world title.

This week's event is a different proposition altogether: a full senior World Championship field including Olympic medallists and reigning champions, with the next edition of the Worlds set to help decide qualification berths for the Los Angeles 2028 Games. A strong showing in Enoshima would be an early statement of intent from Israel's most exciting young sailing prospects as that Olympic race begins to take shape.
Racing in Enoshima continues through August 17, with the fleet still to be trimmed for the medal series later in the regatta.

title: Beitar Nordia Jerusalem unveil new kit for 2026/27 season
dek: The fan-owned Jerusalem club rolled out matching yellow-and-black uniforms for every team, from the senior side down to the youth ranks, designed by Itay Dahan of Didaa Studio for a third straight year.
body: Beitar Nordia Jerusalem, the fan-owned club born out of opposition to racism on the terraces, has unveiled new uniforms for every one of its teams ahead of the 2026/27 season, ONE reports.

The rollout covers the full club structure, from the senior side competing in Liga Alef down to the youth divisions, with every age group receiving a kit built to the same standard as the first team's — a deliberate statement of belonging, the club says, rather than a token youth version.

The new set keeps Beitar Nordia's familiar yellow and black colours and its menorah crest, but is built as a modular system that lets the club mix and match combinations of shirts, shorts and socks across the campaign rather than settling on a single fixed home and away look.

The uniforms were designed by Itay Dahan of Didaa Studio, a branding and sports-apparel design house, working in partnership with Umbro. It is Dahan's third consecutive year producing the club's kits, according to ONE.
"As a child who collected football shirts, it's a great honour for me to design uniforms today," Dahan said, adding that the new design puts "more yellow on Jerusalem's streets."

Beitar Nordia was formed in April 2014 by Beitar Jerusalem supporters who broke away in protest at racism and violence associated with parts of that club's fan base, building a cooperative, fan-owned outfit that has since climbed through the lower divisions to Liga Alef.

title: Or Dadia completes move to Maccabi Petah Tikva
dek: The 28-year-old right-back joins for a sixth senior club after helping Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim to promotion, as Maccabi Petah Tikva also add goalkeeper Eilai Tuvim from Hapoel Jerusalem.

verificationSources.label: ONE - רשמית: אור דדיה חתם במכבי פתח תקווה

body: Maccabi Petah Tikva have officially signed right-back Or Dadia, the club confirmed on Thursday, giving newly promoted Wiener League side fresh defensive depth ahead of the coming Ligat Ha'al campaign.

The 28-year-old arrives as a free agent after his contract with Hapoel Be'er Sheva ran its course, most recently having spent last season on loan at Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim, where he helped the club return to the top flight after 13 years away.

Dadia's career has taken in Bnei Lod, Hapoel Be'er Sheva, a loan spell at Aberdeen in Scotland, and Ironi Kiryat Shmona before his stint at Ramat Gan Givatayim. Maccabi Petah Tikva becomes his sixth senior club.

"I'm excited and happy to sign with a club like Maccabi Petah Tikva," Dadia said, according to ONE. "I'm eager to take the pitch and give everything alongside my teammates, with a clear goal - to secure a strong place in the top league, where this club naturally belongs."

That line speaks to Maccabi Petah Tikva's own rollercoaster: the club finished 13th in Ligat Ha'al and dropped down last season, then bounced straight back to the top flight after a single campaign in Liga Leumit.

Dadia is not the only new face at the club this week. Goalkeeper Eilai Tuvim has also joined from Hapoel Jerusalem, becoming Maccabi Petah Tikva's third goalkeeping option alongside Maor Arlich and Dor Chaveron under head coach Ziv Aryeh.
Dadia, who grew up in Hapoel Be'er Sheva's academy and won the Israeli championship, two State Cups and a Super Cup with the club, has also earned one senior cap for the Israel national team.
Neither the length of his new contract nor any financial terms were disclosed in the club's announcement.

title: Lelior stuns world No. 1 Bryan 12.73-1.46 to reach Tahiti Pro quarter-finals
dek: Israel's first surfer on the WSL Championship Tour produced the biggest win of her rookie season, knocking out the world's top-ranked competitor at Teahupo'o.

verificationSources.label: ONE - ליליאור ברבע הגמר עם ניצחון על המדורגת 1 בעולם
World Surf League - Round 2: Full send for Lelior takes out World No. 1 at Tahiti Pro
World Surf League - Anat Lelior athlete profile
Surfer.com - Anat Lelior Makes History as First Israeli Surfer to Qualify for the Championship Tour

body: Anat Lelior, the first Israeli surfer ever to compete on the WSL Championship Tour, delivered the standout result of her rookie season on Wednesday, eliminating world No. 1 Gabriela Bryan in the second round of the Outerknown Tahiti Pro to book her place in the quarter-finals.

Surfing in the heavy, hollow left of Teahupo'o off Tahiti's south coast, Lelior posted a two-wave heat total of 12.73 against Bryan's 1.46 - a rout in conditions that punished any surfer who could not find rhythm in the swell.

It was a genuine upset. Lelior, 26 and from Tel Aviv, had begun the event ranked 17th in the world in her first season on tour, facing a Hawaiian opponent who arrived in Tahiti sitting at No. 1 in the rankings. ONE reported that the defeat was Bryan's earliest exit of the season.
The win sends Lelior through to a quarter-final berth at one of the most demanding stops on the Championship Tour calendar, a result that instantly ranks among the best of her young elite career.

It is also not unfamiliar water for her. Lelior competed at Teahupo'o once before, at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where she finished ninth in the women's shortboard event on the same reef pass. She was also Israel's surfing representative at the Tokyo 2020 Games, placing 17th.

Lelior's route to the Championship Tour was itself a milestone for Israeli sport. She secured her place on the elite tour in March 2026 through a strong finish on the Challenger Series in Newcastle, Australia, becoming the first Israeli surfer - man or woman - to reach the sport's top level.

Raised surfing the inconsistent beach breaks of the Mediterranean in Tel Aviv, Lelior won her first Israeli national title as a preteen and held it for years afterward. She has also collected a gold medal for Israel at the 2022 Maccabiah Games and finished sixth at the 2024 ISA World Surfing Games in Puerto Rico, the best result by an Israeli at that event.

The Outerknown Tahiti Pro continues through August 18, with Lelior now guaranteed a career-best result at the event regardless of how the quarter-final unfolds against a field that has just lost its top seed.

title: Beitar boss Almog Cohen skips full training in Vienna over spying fears
dek: With Beitar Jerusalem needing to overturn a 2-1 first-leg deficit against Austria Wien, coach Almog Cohen kept his starting eleven under wraps after cameras were spotted trained on his side's final session.

body: Almog Cohen used Beitar Jerusalem's final training session in Vienna on Wednesday for almost everything except a rehearsal of his starting eleven. According to ONE, the coach kept the work loose and steered clear of running a structured shape after members of the travelling party noticed cameras trained on the pitch during the session — a precaution born of suspicion that Austria Wien might be trying to pick up clues about Thursday's lineup and game plan before a match Beitar cannot afford to lose.

The caution reflects the stakes. Beitar trail 2-1 from last week's first leg of this Conference League third qualifying round tie and must win in normal time to go through, or force extra time and penalties with a 1-0 or higher-scoring draw. Kick-off at Austria Wien's Generali Arena is set for 19:30 local time.

The first leg, played at Beitar's neutral 'home' venue in Romania, had looked promising for long spells — the Jerusalem side led before conceding twice in the second half to fall behind in the tie. It leaves Cohen's players needing a positive result away from home against opposition many in Israeli football consider stronger than their qualifying-round billing suggests.

Cohen has used team meetings in Vienna to press a simple message on his squad: keep the ball better and play with more composure than they showed in the first leg, where lapses in possession helped invite Austria Wien back into the tie.

There is a squad worry to go with the tactical one. Shon Weissman, who picked up an ankle injury in the first leg, is a doubt for the return. Beitar do get a boost at the back, though: defender Luka Gadirni, who missed the first leg, has recovered from injury and is in line to feature, potentially alongside Brian Karabali in central defence for a side that has been working with a threadbare back line.

Around 1,000 Beitar supporters are expected to be in the Generali Arena stands, part of a travelling contingent the club has leaned on all summer through a run that has already accounted for FK Sutjeska in an earlier qualifying round. Their arrival in Vienna has not been without friction — Ynet has reported that a protest against Beitar is planned in the city, part of the reception the club's travelling support has periodically drawn on the continent.

Amid the build-up, Beitar have also agreed to a more sombre request: the club will display signage at the match appealing for information on Mally and Liel Yahalomi, an Israeli mother and daughter who have been missing in Vienna since Friday, August 7. Israeli media have reported that the country's embassy in Austria and local police are still searching for the pair, last seen near the city's Naschmarkt.

Whichever side survives Thursday advances to the Conference League playoff round, where Sporting Braga or Dinamo Minsk await a place in the competition's league phase — a prize that would be the furthest Beitar have advanced in Europe in years, if Cohen's guarded preparations translate into a result on the pitch.

title: Qingdao, 20 August 2008: The Comeback That Gave Israel Its Only Beijing Medal
dek: After a mid-week collapse threatened to sink his campaign, windsurfer Shahar Zubari clawed back into podium contention and sailed to bronze in the RS:X medal race — the single medal Israel would win at the Beijing Games.

body: Eilat produces desert heat, not swell, but it has always had wind — and it was on the flat, gusty water off Israel's southernmost city that a seven-year-old named Shahar Zubari first stood on a board, taught by his father, Ze'ev "Poodle" Tzuberi, a windsurfing instructor who ran a small operation on the Red Sea shore. By his teens Zubari was already winning age-group world titles; by 2004 he was a world youth silver medalist. The talent was never in question. What Beijing would test was his nerve.

Getting to the 2008 Olympics required beating a legend first. Israel's windsurfing berth for the RS:X class came down to a domestic trial against Gal Fridman, the sailor who had given Israel its first Olympic gold in Athens four years earlier. Zubari, only 21, won the selection — a result that startled a sport where Fridman was still the reigning name in Israeli sailing, and one that put real weight on the younger man's shoulders heading into China.

He arrived at the Qingdao Olympic Sailing Center with form to justify the pressure. Earlier in 2008 he had taken bronze at the RS:X World Championships in Auckland, and once racing began off Qingdao he looked, briefly, like a contender for gold: a win in race one, a third in race two, an early share of the fleet lead in a 35-strong, 35-nation field sailing eleven races, the last of them a winner-take-all medal race for the top ten.

Then the regatta turned. Zubari's series buckled through the middle rounds — a 17th, a 6th, a 19th, an 18th — the kind of run that, in a fleet this deep, can erase weeks of good sailing in a single bad afternoon on the water. Qingdao's Olympic sailing venue was notorious that August for light, fickle breeze; two days of racing were postponed altogether for lack of wind, and the unpredictability punished anyone who lost their rhythm. By the time the fleet reached the closing races, Zubari had slipped outside the automatic medal picture.

He answered with the two results he needed most: a win in race nine, then a fourth in race ten, hauling himself back into the top ten and, crucially, into the ten-boat medal race — sailing's version of a shootout, where points are doubled and nothing from the preceding week can be banked.

On 20 August 2008, the fleet went out for that medal race with New Zealand's Tom Ashley holding a slender overall lead over France's Julien Bontemps, and Zubari needing to beat enough of the fleet to hold off Britain's Nick Dempsey for third. He sailed to second place in the medal race itself — enough. Ashley took gold with 52 net points, Bontemps silver with 53, and Zubari bronze with 58, edging Dempsey, who finished on 60.

It was a podium finish worth more to Israel than the ranking suggests. Zubari's bronze was the only medal the country won at the entire Beijing Olympics — no gold, no silver, one bronze, from an Israeli team of more than forty athletes across a dozen sports. For a small nation whose Olympic medal count could then still be counted comfortably on two hands, a single medal from a single sailor carried the weight of the whole Games.

The story did not end in Qingdao. Zubari went on to win consecutive European Championship titles in 2009, sailed at home in Tel Aviv, and in 2010 in Sopot, Poland, and returned to the Olympics twice more, at London 2012 — where he carried the Israeli flag at the opening ceremony — and at Rio 2016, becoming a three-time Olympian in his class.

But it is the Qingdao bronze that remains the defining image: a 21-year-old from Eilat, having beaten his own gold-medal-winning predecessor just to make the team, dragging himself back from the wrong side of the leaderboard to give Israel the only colour it would take home from Beijing.
facts: Shahar Zubari won bronze in the men's RS:X windsurfing event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, finishing with 58 net points behind gold medalist Tom Ashley of New Zealand (52) and silver medalist Julien Bontemps of France (53), and ahead of fourth-placed Nick Dempsey of Great Britain (60).
The decisive medal race was sailed on 20 August 2008 at the Qingdao Olympic Sailing Center; Zubari placed second in that race to secure the podium spot.
Zubari's bronze was Israel's only medal at the Beijing 2008 Olympics (0 gold, 0 silver, 1 bronze).

Born in Eilat in 1986 and taught to windsurf from age seven by his father, Ze'ev "Poodle" Tzuberi, Zubari beat Athens 2004 windsurfing gold medalist Gal Fridman in Israel's Olympic trials to win the Beijing berth at age 21.
Earlier in 2008 Zubari had already won bronze at the RS:X World Championships in Auckland, New Zealand.
He went on to win European Championship titles in 2009 (Tel Aviv) and 2010 (Sopot), competed at three Olympic Games (2008, 2012, 2016), and carried Israel's flag at the London 2012 opening ceremony.

title: Katowice 2-1 Hapoel Tel Aviv (Hapoel win 3-2 on aggregate): Barda's men reach Conference League playoff
dek: A late collapse cost Hapoel Tel Aviv the second leg in Poland, but their first-leg cushion was enough to send them through to face Atalanta.

verificationSources.label: ONE - ברדה: שלטנו ברוב שלבי המשחק, העיקר שעלינו
Haaretz - הפועל תל אביב הפסידה 2:1 לקטוביץ והעפילה לפלייאוף הקונפרנס ליג
Sport1 - צפו בתקציר: הפועל תל אביב הפסידה 2:1 לקטוביץ' ועלתה לשלב הפלייאוף

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv are through to the Conference League playoff round, but they had to survive a nervy final quarter-hour in Katowice to get there. Elyaniv Barda's side lost the second leg 2-1 to GKS Katowice on Wednesday, yet a commanding 2-0 win in the first leg was enough to carry them through 3-2 on aggregate.

Stav Turiel, who had also scored in the first leg, put Hapoel ahead in Poland in the 23rd minute, and for long spells the tie looked like a formality. Katowice needed two goals just to force extra time, and for most of the night they could not find a way through a well-organised Hapoel defence.

That changed late on. The Polish side equalised in the 83rd minute, then won and converted a penalty in the 90th to snatch a 2-1 win on the night - a genuine scare for the Israeli champions-elect of the tie, even if it ultimately changed nothing on aggregate.

"We were in control of the game for most of its stages," Barda said afterwards, reflecting on how his team had dominated for long periods before the late wobble. "The main thing is that we advanced." According to ONE, the coach acknowledged his side lost some composure as Katowice pushed forward in the closing minutes, allowing the hosts back into the tie before the final whistle confirmed Hapoel's progress.

The aggregate win completes a job that was effectively sealed a week earlier. Hapoel beat Katowice 2-0 in the first leg, played at a neutral venue in Miskolc, Hungary, with Turiel opening the scoring in the seventh minute before Roi Alkoukin doubled the lead six minutes later - a professional, largely comfortable night that made Wednesday's away leg more of a formality than it eventually felt.

Hapoel's home matches in this campaign have been staged in Hungary rather than at Bloomfield Stadium, a continuation of the arrangement Israeli clubs have used in continental competition amid the security situation at home. It has not stopped them advancing.

The reward - and the challenge - is a playoff tie against Atalanta, the Italian Serie A side dropping down from a higher continental competition. The first leg is scheduled for Bergamo on Thursday, August 20, with the return leg back in Miskolc a week later, on August 27.

It is by some distance the toughest test remaining on Hapoel's route into the Conference League league phase, against a club with regular Champions League and Europa League pedigree in recent seasons. But after seeing off Ludogorets and now Katowice across the qualifying rounds, Barda's squad have already shown they will not be overawed by the occasion.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv set for Conference League playoff test against Atalanta
dek: Fresh off an aggregate win over GKS Katowice, the Israeli club now face a far sterner task: Atalanta, the 2024 Europa League champions, stand between Hapoel and the Conference League's league phase.

verificationSources.label: ONE - המשימה הבאה: אטאלנטה בפלייאוף הקונפרנס ליג
