body: Hapoel Tel Aviv's return to continental football keeps getting sterner by the round. Having survived a nervy aggregate victory over Poland's GKS Katowice, the club now knows exactly what stands between them and the Conference League's league phase: Atalanta, the Italian side that lifted the Europa League as recently as 2024.

The draw pits Hapoel against one of the form clubs of European football over the past half-decade. ONE's football podcast, hosted by Itzik Kalpai and Amit Lovintal, spent its latest episode picking apart how far the gap really is and whether manager Elyaniv Barda's side can find a way to trouble a club many still rate among the favorites for the trophy.

The tie is set for two legs later this month. According to reporting from Italy, the first leg is scheduled for August 20 at Atalanta's Bergamo home, now known as the New Balance Arena following last year's naming-rights deal with the American sportswear brand, while the return leg follows on August 27.

That second match will not be played in Israel. Hapoel have been hosting their European fixtures at the DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary, for security reasons since returning to continental competition, and the Atalanta return leg is expected to be staged there as well.

Hapoel's path to this point was not straightforward. ONE reports the club beat Katowice 3-2 on aggregate, winning the first leg 2-0 before a 2-1 defeat in Wednesday's return fixture proved just enough to see them through on the overall scoreline.

Atalanta arrive as clear favorites on paper. The Bergamo club finished seventh in Serie A last season, a downturn that cost them a place in Europe's top two competitions and dropped them into the Conference League instead, but their pedigree remains formidable — this is still the club that stunned Bayer Leverkusen in the 2024 Europa League final under Gian Piero Gasperini.

Raffaele Palladino has been in charge since replacing Ivan Jurić in November, arriving with a reputation built at Monza and, in particular, at Fiorentina, whom he steered to a sixth-place Serie A finish and a run to the Conference League semi-finals last season.

For Hapoel, simply being in this position marks a landmark. The club is playing in Europe for the first time since the 2014-15 season, having finished fourth in the Israeli Premier League to earn the qualifying berth, and every round survived so far has been treated as a bonus by the fanbase that traveled in numbers to Miskolc.

The podcast also touched on the club's more immediate concerns on the domestic front. Hapoel face Kiryat Shmona in a Toto Cup semi-final on Sunday, with the hosts flagging uncertainty over the availability of winger Shanda Silva heading into a packed August schedule that now includes a two-legged date with one of Italy's biggest clubs.

Nobody around Hapoel is pretending the tie is anything but a mismatch on paper. But after knocking out Katowice and with a full house awaiting in Miskolc for the second leg, the sense within the club, as relayed on ONE's podcast, is that there is nothing to lose in taking their shot at Atalanta.

title: Mourinho hails 'many positive things' as Real Madrid beat Deportivo 1-0 in Teresa Herrera Trophy
dek: The new Real Madrid coach rotated his squad heavily as Brahim Díaz's first-half stoppage-time goal settled a pre-season friendly at Riazor.
body: José Mourinho pronounced himself satisfied with his Real Madrid side's progress after a 1-0 pre-season win over newly promoted Deportivo de A Coruña in the Teresa Herrera Trophy at Riazor on Wednesday night.

Brahim Díaz settled the contest in first-half stoppage time, chesting down a long throw from goalkeeper Andriy Lunin before slotting past the Deportivo keeper at his near post. It was enough to secure Real Madrid's tenth title in the historic tournament.

Mourinho, back in Spain for the first time since he was sacked by Real Madrid in 2013, used the game to spread minutes rather than chase a heavy scoreline. "I must make my substitutions and give everyone an opportunity. I don't want to give too many minutes to those players," he said, according to ONE.

He described the opposition as no pushover despite their lower division status until this season: "This was a serious match against a team returning to La Liga. This cup has a long tradition and they did everything. They wanted their cup, and such competition is very good training for us."

Asked about his squad's overall shape three weeks out from the new season, Mourinho was upbeat. "There are many positive things, the team is improving," he said, adding that five players remained absent from training but that he was pleased with their gradual reintegration as the level of opposition has risen through the summer.

Wednesday's match was the 81st edition of the Teresa Herrera Trophy, one of Spanish football's oldest pre-season fixtures, and Real Madrid's first appearance in it since 2013 — Mourinho's last season in charge of the club before his exit that summer.

Vinicius Júnior started and captained the side, his first appearance since signing a new six-year contract at the Santiago Bernabéu, underlining his status as a senior figure in the dressing room under the new coach.
The result kept Real Madrid unbeaten through pre-season, with two wins and a draw so far under Mourinho, who returned to the club in June on a three-year deal after leaving Fenerbahçe.
One more warm-up match remains, against Schalke on Sunday, before Mourinho's competitive bow as Real Madrid host Espanyol in the LaLiga opener on August 22.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv and Beersheba's league openers postponed as European campaigns intensify
dek: Both clubs will play their delayed Ligat Ha'al fixtures in early September after advancing further than expected in continental qualifying, while Maccabi Tel Aviv presses on with its original schedule.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv - Beersheba beat Red Star Belgrade
Haaretz - Hapoel Tel Aviv and Beitar advance in Conference League

body: Ligat Ha'al's opening round will not look the way the fixture list originally promised. Hapoel Tel Aviv and Hapoel Beersheba, Israel's two most in-form clubs on the European stage this month, have both had their round-one league matches pushed back to give them a clear run at decisive continental play-off ties.

Beersheba's rearranged fixture comes off the back of one of the club's finest nights in Europe. The Negev side beat Red Star Belgrade 2-0 in Belgrade on Tuesday to complete a 3-0 aggregate win, sending them into the Champions League play-off round against Azerbaijani champions Sabah Baku. Whatever happens there, Beersheba have already guaranteed themselves a place in at least the Europa League league phase, along with a UEFA prize pot ONE and other Israeli outlets have reported at close to €9 million.

Hapoel Tel Aviv's route has run through the Conference League, where the Bloomfield Stadium club eliminated Bulgarian side Ludogorets 4-2 on aggregate to reach the third qualifying round. Beitar Jerusalem advanced in the same round of the same competition, meaning the two Jerusalem-Tel Aviv rivals whose league opener has now been postponed are still on parallel paths through Europe.

According to ONE's report, both clubs invoked a standing provision that lets teams engaged in European play-offs defer their opening domestic fixture rather than being squeezed between two continental legs. The clause has been available to Israeli clubs in this position for several seasons.

Beersheba's rescheduled match against Hapoel Haifa will now be played on September 2 at 8:00 p.m., ONE reported, while Hapoel Tel Aviv's derby-tinged opener against Beitar Jerusalem — originally pencilled in as one of round one's marquee ties — has been moved to September 3 at 8:30 p.m.

Not every European-bound club chose to delay. Maccabi Tel Aviv, who are also competing in continental qualifying this month, opted against postponing and will open their league campaign against Hapoel Jerusalem on August 23 as originally scheduled, ONE noted.

The Israel Football Association's league management added that fixtures for the following rounds will be published only a few days after UEFA's group-stage draws are made, with the second-round schedule in particular expected to wait until Beitar Jerusalem complete their own third-round Conference League qualifier.

The reshuffling underlines how much is riding on the next fortnight for Israeli football's European representatives. Beersheba's tie with Sabah Baku is the last hurdle before the revamped 36-team Champions League league phase, a stage no Israeli club has ever reached, while Hapoel Tel Aviv and Beitar Jerusalem both still have a route open to the Conference League's own league phase.

For now, domestic business waits. Ligat Ha'al's opening weekend will go ahead without two of its headline fixtures, with clubs and supporters alike watching the European draws before the rest of the early-season calendar is confirmed.

The Israel Football Association's league management says fixtures for further rounds will be announced days after UEFA's group/league-phase draws, with round two expected to follow Beitar Jerusalem's third qualifying round tie.

title: Miller: overturning CSKA Sofia deficit is hard, but not impossible
dek: Maccabi Tel Aviv head into Thursday's Europa League return leg in Sofia trailing 3-0, and coach Kenny Miller says the tie is still there to be won

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC - UEL: Maccabi beaten 3-0 by CSKA Sofia
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC - Miller after the CSKA defeat

body: Kenny Miller does not need reminding how steep the climb is. His Maccabi Tel Aviv side go into Thursday's Europa League third-qualifying-round return leg against CSKA Sofia three goals down, and the Scottish coach knows there is little margin left for error.

"When you're down 3-0 heading into a return match, it's always a tough challenge," Miller said in comments carried by ONE. "However, it's not an impossible one. We must believe we can overturn this deficit."

The first leg, played in Batumi, Georgia last Thursday because Maccabi are currently unable to host European fixtures on home soil, ended in a chastening 3-0 defeat. Miller's assessment in its immediate aftermath, given to the club's own channels, was blunt: "the tie is far from over, but we have a mountain to climb."

That mountain now has to be climbed at the Vasil Levski National Stadium in Sofia, where kick-off is set for 21:00 local time. CSKA Sofia, unbeaten through two rounds of qualifying that included a penalty-shootout win over Qarabag, are facing Israeli opposition for the first time in the club's history.

Miller's message to his players, according to ONE, has centred on learning from the mistakes of the first leg and being ruthless with whatever chances the return offers. Maccabi arrived in this round in form, having eliminated Sheriff Tiraspol 6-0 on aggregate, but were comprehensively outplayed in Georgia.

There was some better news on the injury front, with left-back Roy Revivo in contention to feature after missing the first leg. New arrival Ester Sokler, who had already been introduced to the squad before the trip to Batumi, is also part of Miller's plans for the return.

A win by four clear goals, or any scoreline that overturns the aggregate deficit, would send Maccabi through to the playoff round, where OFI Crete await. Anything less brings a third successive summer of Europa League qualifying elimination into view for the Yellow-and-Blue.

Miller has been at pains to project belief rather than resignation. Whether that translates into a performance capable of matching Thursday's occasion will decide whether Maccabi's European campaign runs into September, or ends in Sofia.

title: Xavi Hernández appointed Netherlands head coach, succeeding Koeman
dek: The Barcelona and Spain great has signed a KNVB contract through the 2030 World Cup, becoming the Dutch national team's first foreign coach since Ernst Happel in 1978.
body: Xavi Hernández, the Barcelona and Spain great who led the Catalan club to the La Liga title in 2023, has been appointed head coach of the Netherlands national team. The KNVB confirmed the move on Wednesday, ending nearly two years out of the dugout for the 46-year-old and handing him one of the most storied jobs in international football.

According to ONE, the Dutch federation had narrowed its search to two main contenders, Xavi and former Belgium and Portugal boss Roberto Martínez, before settling on the Spaniard, who has signed a contract running through the 2030 World Cup.

He replaces Ronald Koeman, who left the post after the Netherlands' early exit from this summer's World Cup. Dutch broadcaster NOS reported that the KNVB's hunt for a successor dragged on for weeks, with Erik ten Hag, Peter Bosz and Arne Slot all declining the job before the federation turned to Xavi.
The appointment makes Xavi only the second foreign-born head coach in the history of the Dutch national team, and the first since Austria's Ernst Happel guided Oranje to the 1978 World Cup final.

"I think it is an enormous honour to become head coach of the Netherlands national team," Xavi said, according to NOS. He spoke of a deep personal connection to Dutch football through Barcelona's La Masia academy, built on the coaching principles of Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, describing himself in footballing terms as "a son of Dutch football" and crediting Louis van Gaal and Frank Rijkaard among the figures who shaped him at the club.
ONE also reports that Xavi intends to bring Patrick Cloet onto his new coaching staff as he assembles his backroom team for the role.

There is a curious symmetry to the appointment. Xavi replaced Koeman as Barcelona coach back in November 2021, and now inherits his job for a second time, this time on the international stage. He also has personal history against Oranje: he started in central midfield for Spain in the 2010 World Cup final in Johannesburg, when Andrés Iniesta's late extra-time strike beat the Netherlands 1-0.

As a player, Xavi won four Champions League titles with Barcelona and lifted the World Cup and two European Championships with Spain. In the dugout, he managed Al Sadd in Qatar before returning to Barcelona in November 2021, guiding the club to the league title in his second full season, and departed at the end of the 2023-24 campaign.

He now takes charge of a Dutch squad moving on from the Koeman era, with the KNVB banking on his pedigree, and the possession-based, positional football he inherited from Cruyff's disciples, to reset Oranje's fortunes heading toward the next World Cup cycle.

title: Fans take the field: new Israeli football supporters' federation launches at Bloomfield
dek: Eleven supporters' groups, from Beitar Jerusalem to Maccabi Haifa, have banded together to press clubs and the league on ticket prices, kick-off times and stadium conditions ahead of the new season.
body: Israeli football's notoriously fragmented fan scene took a step toward organising itself on Wednesday evening, with representatives of eleven supporters' groups gathering at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv to launch a new umbrella body: the Israeli Football Fans Association.

The new federation, according to ONE's report from the launch event, is designed to put the ordinary matchday fan at the centre of decision-making that has traditionally been left to clubs, the league and the Israel Football Association. It is set to formally begin operating with the upcoming season.

Its founding members span the length of the Israeli top flight and beyond: Maccabi Kabilio Jaffa's own fan-owned club, Maccabi Tel Aviv's "Achim LeSmel" association, Hapoel Petah Tikva's "HaAchva HaKchula", Beitar Jerusalem's "HaZhavim", Maccabi Haifa's "HaYitia HaTzfonit" (Northern Bleachers), Hapoel Beersheba's "Vasarmilia", the "Kfar Saba 1928" supporters club, Hapoel Jerusalem's "Katmon" supporters union, Ironi Kiryat Shmona's fan group, Maccabi Petah Tikva's "KIB" and Maccabi Bnei Raina's "UR-16".
That is a striking cross-section of the domestic game — clubs that have been fierce rivals on the pitch for decades, united for the first time in a single body meant to speak for fans as a bloc.

The association's stated priorities read like a checklist of long-standing supporter grievances: bringing down ticket and concession prices, improving how fans are treated inside grounds, cutting queues and speeding up entry to stadiums, pushing for kick-off times that actually suit supporters rather than broadcasters, improving accessibility, and setting clearer standards for crowd conduct.

Barak Matzger, speaking for Maccabi Haifa's Northern Bleachers faction, framed the new body's approach as cooperative rather than combative. "The body's purpose is not to fight the federation or any other entity, but to work with them," he said, according to ONE. "The aim is to make football more respectful and pleasant for all of us."

It is a message aimed as much at sceptical club administrations as at rival fan bases: this is meant to be a lobbying and coordinating body, not a protest movement squaring off against the sport's establishment.

Whether the Israel Football Association or individual clubs formally engage with the new group remains to be seen — ONE's report did not carry any response from the governing body, and the association's real test will come once the season kicks off and its demands on pricing and scheduling meet the practical realities of broadcast contracts and matchday logistics.

For now, though, the symbolism of eleven rival fan bases standing together at Bloomfield, a ground that has itself hosted some of Israeli football's most heated derbies, is notable in a fan culture more often defined by division than solidarity.
facts: A new umbrella body, the Israeli Football Fans Association, was launched at an event at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv on Wednesday evening.

Eleven fan groups are founding members, representing Maccabi Kabilio Jaffa, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Petah Tikva, Beitar Jerusalem, Maccabi Haifa, Hapoel Beersheba, Kfar Saba, Hapoel Jerusalem, Ironi Kiryat Shmona, Maccabi Petah Tikva and Maccabi Bnei Raina.

The association's stated goals include lower ticket and concession prices, better fan treatment at stadiums, shorter entry queues, fan-friendly kick-off times, improved accessibility and clearer standards for crowd conduct.
It is due to begin operating with the upcoming Israeli football season.

Barak Matzger of Maccabi Haifa's 'HaYitia HaTzfonit' (Northern Bleachers) group spoke at the launch, describing the body's approach as cooperative rather than adversarial toward the football authorities.

title: Germany's antitrust watchdog upholds the Bundesliga's 50+1 ownership rule
dek: The Bundeskartellamt closed a years-long review by ruling the fan-ownership regulation legal, but ordered Bayer Leverkusen, Wolfsburg, RB Leipzig and Hannover 96 to fix inconsistencies in how it is applied.
body: German football's fan-ownership model has survived its biggest legal test. The Bundeskartellamt, Germany's federal antitrust authority, announced this week that it has closed its long-running examination of the Bundesliga's 50+1 rule without moving to ban it — a decision ONE reports amounts to "the people having their say" on a regulation that has defined the German game for two decades.

The 50+1 rule requires that a club's fan association retain at least a majority of the voting rights in its professional football operation, no matter how much outside capital flows in. It is the reason Germany has largely avoided the takeover model seen in the Premier League and elsewhere, keeping ultimate control of clubs nominally in members' hands.

The cartel office opened its probe back in 2018 after complaints that the rule illegally restricted competition for investment in professional clubs. In its final assessment, confirmed in an official statement dated 11 August, the authority accepted that 50+1 does limit economic competition — but concluded that protecting club identity and member participation is a legitimate enough goal, under European Court of Justice precedent, to justify that restriction.

The ruling is not, however, a clean bill of health for the Bundesliga and the DFL, the league's governing body. The Bundeskartellamt was explicit that the rule can only remain legally defensible if it is applied consistently across all 36 clubs in the top two divisions, without unjustified exceptions for individual sides.

That is where the pressure now lands on four clubs. Bayer Leverkusen and VfL Wolfsburg have long operated under historic "benefactor" exemptions tied to their founding backers, Bayer AG and Volkswagen respectively. The authority found those permanent carve-outs no longer sit comfortably with recent European case law and wants both clubs moved toward genuine member influence over the professional operation rather than a blanket exemption.

RB Leipzig face a different demand. The club has never claimed a benefactor exemption, instead keeping its registered association's voting membership tightly restricted to a small circle closely tied to Red Bull. The Bundeskartellamt says Leipzig must now open up real, ordinary voting membership to supporters — closing what critics have long called a loophole around the spirit of 50+1.

Hannover 96 come in for pointed criticism too, though of a different kind. The authority questioned how the DFL handled a December 2023 vote on allowing outside investors into the league's media rights, in which supervisory board member Martin Kind was accused of voting against instructions from the club's own fan association. The cartel office said the league did not adequately ensure the rule's requirements were followed in that episode.

None of the four clubs face an immediate sanction, and no formal deadline for compliance was set out in the ruling. But the message from Bonn is unambiguous: the DFL must now enforce 50+1 uniformly or risk reopening the case — and potentially a future prohibition proceeding — down the line.

For a competition that markets its terraces and matchday atmosphere as a point of pride, the outcome preserves the structural quirk that keeps Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund and the rest of the Bundesliga nominally fan-run even as broadcast and sponsorship money keeps climbing. Tuesday's decision effectively tells the league it can keep that identity — as long as it stops making exceptions for its most commercially entangled clubs.
facts: The Bundeskartellamt (Germany's Federal Cartel Office) closed its investigation into the Bundesliga's 50+1 ownership rule with a final assessment confirming the rule is legally defensible, per an official statement dated 11 August 2026.

The probe began in 2018 over complaints that 50+1 illegally restricts investment competition; the authority accepted the restriction but found it justified by the goal of preserving club identity and member participation.
The ruling requires the rule to be applied consistently across clubs, with no unjustified exemptions, or its legal standing could be revisited.

Bayer Leverkusen and VfL Wolfsburg, which hold historic benefactor exemptions via Bayer AG and Volkswagen, were told their current grandfathered arrangements are insufficient and must move toward genuine member influence.
RB Leipzig, which has no benefactor exemption but restricts its registered association's voting membership, must open genuine voting membership to supporters.

The authority criticized the DFL's oversight of a December 2023 vote on private investment in the league's media rights, in which Hannover 96 supervisory board member Martin Kind was accused of voting against his club's fan association's instructions.
No formal compliance deadline or sanction was announced alongside the ruling.

title: Daria Golovaty just misses out on 200m freestyle final at European Championships
dek: The Israeli sprinter trimmed her time again in the semi-finals in Paris but finished 14th overall, as Anastasia Gorbenko prepared to defend her 400m medley title later the same evening.

verificationSources.label: ONE - דריה גולובטי לא העפילה לגמר ה-200 מטר חופשי
SwimSwam - 2026 European Championships: Day 3 Prelims Live Recap

body: Daria Golovaty's push for a first individual final at a major long-course championship fell agonisingly short in Paris on Wednesday, with the Israeli sprinter touching seventh in her semi-final heat and 14th overall in the women's 200m freestyle at the European Aquatics Championships, according to ONE.

Golovaty actually swam faster than she had in the morning, clocking 1:58.48 in the evening semi-final, but it was not enough to break into the top eight who go through to the final. It capped a frustrating night for an athlete who had arrived in the French capital swimming some of the best times of her career.

She had been the standout of the morning session, winning her preliminary heat in 1:58.72 and shaving 1.3 seconds off her seed time - a swim that briefly put her name near the top of the psych sheets before a stronger semi-final field caught up with her, according to SwimSwam's live coverage from the Paris Aquatic Centre.

Born in Ukraine, the 20-year-old Golovaty has held Israeli citizenship since 2006 and swims domestically for Hapoel Bat Yam; she now competes collegiately in the United States for the University of Louisville. She has already won national titles over 200m and 400 yards freestyle in Israel and placed fifth in this same event at the 2024 European Championships in Belgrade, meaning a place in a European final has narrowly eluded her for two summers running.

Israel's medal hopes at these championships instead now rest with Anastasia Gorbenko, who advanced to the 400m individual medley final from seventh place in the morning heats in 4:42.23. Gorbenko, the defending European champion in the event, was due back in the pool for the final at 20:54 local time.

A podium finish for Gorbenko would give Israel its first medal of the meet in Paris - a result that would ease the disappointment of a night in which Golovaty came desperately close to a first individual major final of her senior career, only to fall just short.

body: Maccabi Haifa have moved to add depth between the posts, agreeing a loan deal for Maccabi Netanya goalkeeper Omer Niraon, ONE reported in a first-publication story on Wednesday, ending weeks of back-and-forth negotiation between the two clubs.

According to the report, Haifa will take the 25-year-old on loan and hold a purchase option worth 1.4 million shekels, exercisable at the end of the current season should the club wish to make the move permanent.

The move ends a two-and-a-half-year stay at Netanya, where Niraon arrived in January 2024 and established himself as a regular in goal, most recently drawing interest from a Haifa side reshaping its goalkeeping department this summer.

At Sammy Ofer Stadium he is expected to serve as understudy to Omri Glazer, who rejoined Maccabi Haifa this summer after a spell with Red Star Belgrade in Serbia and signed a three-year contract at the club where his career began. Niraon slots in as the clear second-choice goalkeeper in the squad coach Barak Bachar is assembling for the new campaign.

The reshuffle in goal follows Haifa's sale of Ukrainian goalkeeper Giorgi Yarmakov earlier in the transfer window, which left the club needing to settle both its starting and back-up options before the season gets under way.

Niraon's path to Maccabi Haifa has run through several clubs. He came up through the youth ranks at Maccabi Tel Aviv, Shimshon Tel Aviv and Maccabi Herzliya before joining Bnei Yehuda at 16, making his senior debut in 2018 and becoming the club's first-choice goalkeeper in the 2020-21 season, the year Bnei Yehuda were relegated.

Loan spells followed at Hapoel Rishon LeZion, Hapoel Ramat HaSharon and Bosnian side Zrinjski Mostar before he settled at Netanya. He has also worn the Israel jersey, featuring in goal for the national team at the 2024 Paris Olympics.
ONE's report does not detail any compensation to Netanya beyond the loan structure, and neither club has yet issued an official statement confirming the deal.

title: Messi bids farewell to his father: "I have serious doubts whether I can continue"
dek: Lionel Messi laid his father and lifelong agent Jorge to rest in a private funeral near Rosario, days after posting an anguished tribute questioning his own football future.
body: Lionel Messi buried his father, Jorge, in a tightly private ceremony near Rosario at the weekend, days after the man who shaped and managed his entire career died at 68 following a long illness.

Jorge Messi died in the early hours of Saturday, August 8, at a Rosario medical facility. He was laid to rest the following day at the El Prado Cementerio Parque in Pérez, on the city's outskirts, in a funeral closed to the public and guarded by heavy security. Only close family and a small number of Messi's Argentina teammates were present.

Messi flew in from the United States on a private jet, arriving with his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and their three children. His mother, Celia Cuccittini, and siblings Rodrigo, Matías and María Sol were also there to say goodbye, according to reports from Rosario.

Jorge was far more than a parent to Argentina's captain. He was, in effect, the architect of his son's entire professional life — negotiating the move to Barcelona's academy when Leo was just 13, securing the growth-hormone treatment that let a small boy from Rosario become the player he did, and running his business affairs as his formal agent for two decades.

In a lengthy, emotional post on Instagram after the death, Messi wrote of his fear that he might not be able to carry on in football without his father beside him. "I only played football, and now I have serious doubts whether I can continue," he wrote, according to ONE's report of the tribute, adding that Jorge had been "a father, friend and agent" who was "always the right person at every moment."
"Dad, I still can't believe you have gone," Messi wrote, in quotes carried by ESPN. "It is difficult to imagine that I won't see you again; that we won't speak anymore."

Jorge's illness shadowed what was expected to be Messi's final World Cup this past June and July. "You asked me to play in this last World Cup so many times, and just before it started was when you were at your worst," Messi wrote. "It was the first time you were not at a tournament, but mum told me you would get better and you would be able to travel." It never happened — the tournament in North America was the first of his career his father did not attend in person.

False rumours of Jorge's death had already swept social media during the World Cup, on the same day Messi scored in Argentina's opening group match. The family was forced to issue a statement at the time asking for privacy, calling the false reports "a lack of sensitivity."

Messi said he intends to honour his father by raising his own children the way Jorge raised him, promising he "will miss him so much" but that he will "always be present," especially in the upbringing of his three sons.

Tributes poured in from across football following the news, with Barcelona, Argentina's federation (AFA) and countless former teammates paying respect to a man who spent most of his adult life almost entirely out of the spotlight, despite steering the career of the sport's most decorated player.

title: Ben-Shimon and Israel coaching staff visit Perach Israel special-needs village
dek: The national team head coach led his technical staff on a visit to residents of the Rosh Ha'ayin facility, calling the encounter humbling.
body: Israel's national team head coach Ran Ben-Shimon led members of his technical staff on a visit to the Perach Israel village in Rosh Ha'ayin this week, according to a report by ONE, spending time with residents and the staff who care for them.

The facility houses around 220 residents living with significant functional disabilities, ranging in age from 21 to 86. The delegation toured the grounds, met residents and support workers, and was briefed on the range of programmes the village runs for people who live there permanently.
Alongside Ben-Shimon, the group included fellow staff members Gal Cohen, Guy Luzon, Boni Ginzburg, Biram Kiyael, Moshe Sinai, Fredi David, Ophir Haim, Erik Banado and Dani Bonder, ONE reported.
"We met special and amazing people, both residents and mentors doing sacred work with remarkable energy," Ben-Shimon said, according to the report.

Ginzburg said the trip was a reminder of football's reach beyond results and fixtures. "Football extends far beyond the pitch. This encounter touched us all, and we leave with gratitude for participating," he said. Sinai added that the visit left the group with plenty to reflect on: "The meeting with residents and staff was special and deeply moving."
Yaffit Bergig, the director of Perach Israel, thanked the coaching staff for making time for the visit, saying it created meaningful moments for residents, per ONE's report.

The gesture comes as Ben-Shimon and his staff continue preparations with the national team programme, a reminder that the backroom group's public work this summer has extended well beyond the training pitch.

title: Rapyd's Shtilman demands Recanati family documents in Maccabi Tel Aviv shares fight
dek: Lawyers for the fintech billionaire and club sponsor allege the Recanati family's sale of a stake to American investor Jason Levien was arranged before a rival bid was blocked, and are demanding paperwork within three days.
body: Arik Shtilman, the Rapyd founder and chief executive who is also Maccabi Tel Aviv's main shirt sponsor, has escalated his fight for influence at the basketball club, with his lawyers formally demanding the Recanati family hand over documents on how it sold off part of its newly enlarged shareholding.

According to a report by ONE, attorneys for Shtilman sent an urgent letter to Naftali S.S. Investments, the Recanati-controlled company that holds the family's stake in the club, giving it three business days to produce a set of records related to the transaction.

The letter demands all correspondence with American investor Jason Levien concerning the acquisition of club shares, full financing documentation for the Recanati family's purchase of the Federman family's stake — including the source of the funds used — and any agreements or side arrangements covering the transfer of shares to a third party.

The dispute traces back to July 7, when the Recanati company exercised its right of first refusal to buy out the Federman family's roughly 29% holding in Maccabi Tel Aviv, held through Fedanco Sports, for about $50 million. That move took the Recanatis' stake to 58% and derailed a rival plan under which Shtilman — who already held a 50% interest in Fedanco Sports and a seat on Maccabi's board — had been positioned to buy into the club.
Shtilman had separately floated an offer of roughly $100 million for the Recanati family's entire holding, a proposal that went nowhere as the family instead moved to consolidate control itself.

The dispute took a fresh turn on August 7, when the Recanati family informed fellow shareholders it planned to sell roughly half of its enlarged stake — about 29% of the club — to Levien, a former chief executive of the NBA's Memphis Grizzlies, in a deal again worth about $50 million.

Shtilman's lawyers now argue that sale was effectively agreed well before it was disclosed. Their letter points to a company linked to Levien that was incorporated on July 6 — one day before Recanati exercised its refusal right over the Federman shares — and to the near-identical size and price of the two transactions, calling it, in their words, "a coordinated scheme designed to transfer rights to an unauthorized third party."
Reached for comment by ONE, Udi Recanati gave a brief response: "Unknown to me, no comment."

The confrontation is the latest flashpoint in a months-long ownership battle that has consumed one of Israeli basketball's flagship clubs, pitting one of the country's best-known tech entrepreneurs against the family that has controlled Maccabi Tel Aviv's board. Neither Naftali S.S. Investments nor Levien has yet issued a substantive public response to the specific allegations in Shtilman's letter.

On July 7, 2026, the Recanati family's company exercised its right of first refusal to buy the Federman family's roughly 29% Maccabi Tel Aviv stake (via Fedanco Sports) for about $50 million, raising the Recanatis' holding to 58%.

On August 7, 2026, the Recanati family told shareholders it would sell roughly 29% of the club — about half its enlarged stake — to American investor Jason Levien, a former Memphis Grizzlies CEO, for about $50 million.

Shtilman's lawyers sent Naftali S.S. Investments an urgent letter, per ONE, demanding within three business days all Recanati-Levien correspondence, financing documents (including source of funds) for the Federman-stake purchase, and any side agreements on transferring shares to a third party.

The letter alleges a company linked to Levien was incorporated on July 6, 2026 — the day before Recanati exercised its refusal right — and calls the sequence a coordinated scheme to route shares to an unauthorized third party.
Udi Recanati's only response to ONE was: "Unknown to me, no comment."

title: Ronaldo's message of support for Messi after the death of his father, Jorge
dek: The Portuguese forward left a comment of comfort under Lionel Messi's Instagram farewell to his father, who died last week in Rosario at the age of 68.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo reached out to Lionel Messi this week in the gentlest way two rivals-turned-elder-statesmen of the game know how: a short comment left under his old adversary's own words of grief. According to ONE, Ronaldo wrote beneath Messi's Instagram farewell to his father, Jorge: "A huge hug for you and all your loved ones in this difficult moment, Leo. Stay strong," followed by a heart emoji.

The comment came days after Jorge Messi, who had been both father and long-serving agent to the Inter Miami forward, died on Saturday in a hospital in Rosario at the age of 68. Newell's Old Boys, the club with deep roots in the Messi family's story, said he had been undergoing treatment for an unspecified illness in the months before his death.
Messi and his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, travelled with their three sons to Rosario for a private funeral before the forward posted an emotional tribute to his father on Instagram.

"Dad, I still can't believe that you've gone," Messi wrote. "I don't fall, or rather, I don't want to fall. It's very hard for me to imagine that I'm not going to see you anymore, that we're not going to talk anymore. I know you were suffering and that it's for the best, but you left too soon. We still had a lot left to enjoy together."

He went on to describe how his father had pushed him to play at this year's World Cup despite his declining health, and how he had waited for Jorge's message after every match, growing more worried as the tournament went on and the messages slowed.

It was under that post that Ronaldo's comment appeared, cited by ONE and separately reported by the US-based outlet Bolavip, which published a screenshot of the exchange. The gesture drew tens of thousands of likes and replies from fans on both sides of football's longest-running individual rivalry.

Real Madrid, where Ronaldo built much of his legend, were among the clubs and federations to issue formal condolences to the Messi family last week, a reminder of how far the news travelled beyond Barcelona and Argentina.

Ronaldo and Messi built two of the most decorated careers the sport has seen while pushing each other for the best part of two decades, from the Clásico years in Spain through separate paths at Juventus, Al-Nassr, Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami. Their public exchanges have grown warmer since both moved past their head-to-head prime, each crediting the other for raising his own game.

It is worth noting that this comment, as documented by ONE and Bolavip, is distinct from several other claims about Ronaldo's reaction that spread on social media this week, including of a phone call between the two men — none of which has been confirmed by either player's camp, by any club, or by any federation.

body: Chelsea have completed the signing of left-back Pep Chavarría from Rayo Vallecano, ONE reports, closing out a deal that becomes the biggest outgoing sale in the Madrid club's history.

The move was pushed for by head coach Xabi Alonso, who has been reshaping his defensive options at Stamford Bridge after Marc Cucurella's departure left a gap on the left side. Chavarría, 28, arrives as his direct replacement.

European outlets have not fully agreed on the exact number: ONE puts the fee at roughly €22 million, while several British and Spanish reports describe a €19 million base rising to about €21 million with add-ons. Either way, it is a club-record sale for Rayo Vallecano.
The Catalan defender has signed a five-year contract at Chelsea, keeping him at the club through June 2031.

Chavarría joined Rayo Vallecano from Real Zaragoza in 2022 and grew into one of La Liga's more reliable full-backs, making 125 appearances for the club and helping it reach last season's Conference League final while finishing eighth in the table.

Alongside the confirmed Chavarría deal, ONE also flagged a developing story out of Turkey: according to Turkish media, Dušan Vlahović has agreed personal terms with Beşiktaş on a three-year contract, choosing the Istanbul club's offer as the most lucrative on the table.

The Serbian striker has been a free agent since his Juventus contract expired on June 30, and a move to Beşiktaş would reunite him with head coach Vincenzo Italiano, who managed him during his time at Fiorentina before his transfer to Juventus.

Neither club has yet issued an official announcement on Vlahović, and the transfer is still being reported as an agreement in principle rather than a done deal, even as multiple Italian and Turkish outlets describe it as close to being finalised.

The two stories cap a busy day of transfer activity across Europe, with ONE's report noting several other deals in motion involving Serie A, La Liga and Premier League clubs as the summer window heads toward its close.

body: Israel's reserve men's water polo team made it three wins from three at the European Under-20 Championship Division I on Wednesday, beating Great Britain 11-7 in Oeiras, Portugal, to open the tournament with a perfect record, ONE reported.

The Israelis controlled the match from the first whistle. They led 4-2 after the opening quarter and 6-3 at the break, then pulled clear in the third period to make it 7-4 before closing out the 11-7 win — a far more comfortable afternoon than their previous outing at the tournament.

Gal Cohen was the standout in the pool, scoring three of Israel's 11 goals. The rest of the tally was spread remarkably evenly, with eight different teammates each finding the net once — a sign of the squad's depth heading into the tournament's business end.
The result followed victories over Belgium and Belarus in the group's opening rounds, giving Israel a maximum haul from three matches at the tournament, which runs in Oeiras from August 10 to 16.

Israel Water Polo Association CEO Dana Tartatzky-Gatuah, who is travelling with the squad in Portugal, praised the atmosphere around the team after the win. "There's really good energy here, the coaching staff accompanies the team professionally, seriously and calmly, and you see it in the players," she said, according to ONE. "Yesterday's tough match was an excellent reminder not to be complacent. Today they arrived tense until the last second. There's also quite a bit of Israeli crowd here bringing lots of support, and that really does the heart good — they should just continue like this."

The event is the second tier of European men's Under-20 water polo, sitting below the elite championship, and brings together 12 nations split into two groups of six for a week of group-stage play before the knockout rounds.

Water polo remains a modest but active pipeline sport for Israeli aquatics, and a perfect record through the group phase gives this junior side real momentum to carry into the rest of the tournament in Portugal.

title: Beitar Jerusalem supporters group opens crisis hotline for fans travelling to Vienna amid antisemitism fears
dek: Hod VeHadar says it has coordinated directly with Vienna police and the city's Jewish community security service ahead of Thursday's Conference League qualifier, as anxiety in the Austrian capital is heightened by the unexplained disappearance of an Israeli mother and daughter.

body: Beitar Jerusalem's official supporters association has set up a dedicated operations room to support fans travelling to Vienna for Thursday's Conference League qualifying return leg, amid rising unease over antisemitism in the Austrian capital.

Hod VeHadar, the club's recognised fan organisation, told ONE it has opened direct lines of coordination with the Vienna police and with the city's Jewish community security service ahead of the trip. The centre will act as a support and crisis hotline for supporters who run into antisemitic incidents, emergencies, or simply need help while in the city.
"It is important to us that every fan knows he has an address," said Bar Lavi and Yaakov Sela, spokespeople for the association, in comments carried by ONE.

According to the report, the group has already given Vienna police a detailed briefing on the numbers and routes of Beitar fans expected in the city, including those arriving indirectly via Bratislava and Budapest rather than flying straight in. Supporters have been told that in any crisis situation, their first call should be to the police.

The initiative comes against a tense backdrop in Vienna. Israel's embassy there is still searching for Mali Yahalomi, 50, and her daughter Liel, 23, who have been out of contact since sending a video to relatives on Friday, August 7. Austrian police say they have found no indication so far that the pair's disappearance is linked to a criminal act, but the case has unsettled Israelis in the city and sharpened concerns about their safety ahead of the match.

Beitar arrive in Vienna needing to overturn a 2-1 defeat from the first leg, which the Jerusalem club played as the nominal home side at the Ilie Oană stadium in Romania on August 6. More than 1,000 Beitar supporters are expected to make the trip for Thursday's second leg of the Conference League third qualifying round tie.

As part of the operation, Hod VeHadar has published a set of emergency contacts for travelling fans: Austrian police on 133, a dedicated antisemitism incidents hotline on +43-664-88934555, and an additional support line on +43-1-725756110.

The move reflects a broader pattern this summer of Israeli fan groups and club officials building direct security channels with host-city police forces before European away trips, as clubs try to reassure supporters who are increasingly wary of travelling to matches abroad.

title: Pogoń Szczecin owner calls Hapoel Tel Aviv 'genocidal' before Katowice qualifier, Israeli FA reports him to UEFA
dek: Alex Haditaghi, who has no formal role at Wednesday's actual opponents but owns Poland's Pogoń Szczecin, urged Katowice's players to turn the Conference League decider into a political statement; IFA chairman Shino Zuaretz calls the post 'revolting, distorted and inciting.'

body: Hours before Hapoel Tel Aviv kicked off the second leg of their Conference League qualifier in Katowice, the club found itself under a very different kind of attack — not from the opponents on the pitch, but from the owner of an entirely different Polish club who has made a habit of using football to needle Israel.

Alex Haditaghi, the Iranian-Canadian businessman who owns top-flight Polish side Pogoń Szczecin, published an inflammatory social media post on the eve of Wednesday's match, branding Hapoel Tel Aviv, in his words, as representing "the genocidal Israeli state and the wicked Zionist system behind it," according to ONE.

Haditaghi went further, writing that Israel "should not receive any rights to privilege and legitimacy in UEFA competitions while it commits occupation," and arguing that "Israel is not a European country — it is geographically located in Asia." He also accused the United States, Germany, Britain and France of shielding Israel from consequences in international football, ONE reported.

Haditaghi has no official connection to Katowice, the actual opponents in Wednesday's tie, but he addressed the club's players directly in the post, urging them to turn the match into "a political statement" and to play with enough intensity to make the stadium "shake." He signed off, per ONE, with "Free Palestine. Long live Iran."

The Israel Football Association reacted swiftly. Chairman Shino (Moshe) Zuaretz, who also sits on UEFA's executive committee, called the post "a revolting, distorted and inciting text of racism, vulgarity, lies and incitement," adding that "there is no place in football for people so dark." Zuaretz instructed the federation's legal department to file an official complaint against Haditaghi with UEFA, saying he was confident the governing body would "administer justice."

It is not the first time Haditaghi has used his platform to target Israeli football. In June, he refused to negotiate the sale of two Pogoń Szczecin players, Dimitrios Keramitsis and Leo Borges, to Maccabi Tel Aviv, comparing doing business with an Israeli club to trading with Nazi Germany. Pogoń also staged a pitch-side statement on Gaza before a domestic match against Lechia Gdańsk last September.

The row lands in the middle of a live European tie. Hapoel Tel Aviv won the first leg 2-0 on August 6 at a neutral venue in Miskolc, Hungary — the security arrangement clubs travelling to face Israeli opposition have used before. Katowice, appearing in UEFA competition for the first time in the club's history, reached this stage by beating Slovakia's Žilina after a 1-2 first-leg loss and a 3-1 home win.

Wednesday's return leg kicks off at 19:00 local time in Katowice, with Hapoel Tel Aviv holding a two-goal cushion from the first leg. UEFA had not responded publicly to the Israeli federation's complaint at the time of writing.

body: Tomer Ginat will not be part of Israel's national basketball team for its coming World Cup qualifying window, ONE reports, after the captain was unable to get through full-intensity training this week because of a knee problem.

The Hapoel Tel Aviv forward, who only recently signed a contract extension keeping him at the club through 2030, has been managing the injury without success, according to the report, and the national team has decided not to risk him for a stretch of three games in eight days.

Israel's squad begins its preparations on Sunday, August 16, ahead of a warm-up match in Georgia on August 23. From there the group travels to Latvia for a World Cup qualifying double-header, facing Poland on August 27 and hosts Latvia on August 30.

Those two games count toward the second round of European qualifying for the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027, where Israel sits in a group alongside Croatia, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland and Latvia, with the top three finishers advancing.

With Ginat out, head coach Ariel Beit-Halachmi is turning to Yam Madar to wear the captain's armband for the window. Madar, who has played for Fenerbahçe and FC Bayern Munich in recent seasons and is currently back at Hapoel Tel Aviv, has long been one of the squad's leaders on the floor and is a natural fit to take over the role in Ginat's absence.

Ginat has been a fixture of the senior national team setup for years and has previously played through pain for both club and country; he ended last season early because of a separate shoulder injury. His absence leaves Israel short of its captain and floor general as the qualifying campaign enters a pivotal stretch.

No fresh timeline for Ginat's return was given in the report, and Israel Sports Pulse will update this story once the national team confirms his status for the following qualifying window in November.

title: Gorbenko qualifies for 400m medley final at European Championships
dek: The defending champion clocked 4:42.23 in the heats in Paris to book her place in Wednesday evening's final, keeping Israel's medal hopes alive at the pool.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — Swimming at the 2026 European Aquatics Championships, Women's 400m individual medley

body: Anastasia Gorbenko is through to the final of the women's 400m individual medley at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, safely negotiating Wednesday's heats to give Israel another shot at a medal in the pool.

Gorbenko touched in 4:42.23 to finish seventh fastest of the morning session at the Paris Aquatic Centre in Saint-Denis, comfortably inside the top eight who advance to the evening final, ONE reported.

The 23-year-old from Haifa arrives at the final as the athlete to beat on paper. She is the reigning European champion in the event after winning gold at the 2024 championships in Belgrade, and she took silver at the 2024 World Championships in Doha over the same distance.

The heats were tightly packed at the top. Poland's Justina Kozan led the field in 4:40.47, just ahead of Britain's Amalie Smith and Hungary's Vivien Jackl, with barely two seconds separating the fastest and eighth-placed qualifiers. Gorbenko will need a faster swim than her heat time to trouble that group for a medal.

It capped a mixed morning for the Israeli team in Paris. Daria Golubaty advanced to the semi-final of the women's 200m freestyle after clocking 1:58.72 in her heat, while Leah Polonski narrowly missed the cut in the same event with 1:59.92, according to ONE. Israeli swimmers did not progress from the heats in the women's 100m butterfly or 50m backstroke.

Gorbenko, one of the most decorated swimmers in Israeli history with multiple European and world titles across the medley and breaststroke events, has made the 400m IM something of a signature race. body: Hapoel Jerusalem have signed 18-year-old forward Lior Hershko to a four-year contract running through the 2029/30 season, ONE reported, adding another young prospect to the Jerusalem club's development pipeline.

Rather than keep him in the capital immediately, Hapoel Jerusalem will loan Hershko out to Elitzur Shomron in the National League for the coming season, the report said, a move designed to get the teenager regular senior minutes while he continues training with Hapoel's professional staff.

Hershko, who stands 2.01m, captained Israel's U-18 national team at last summer's European Championship, averaging 6 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2 assists across seven games in the tournament. He came up through the youth ranks at Hapoel Emek Hefer, where he has been tracked as one of the more promising Israeli prospects of his age group.

"Lior is one of the talented and interesting players in his age group, and we greatly believe in his potential," Hapoel Jerusalem sports director Dan Shemir said, according to ONE. Shemir added that the club's strategy is to keep recruiting promising young talents and build pathways that can turn them into significant contributors for the senior Hapoel team down the line.

The loan-to-develop route is a familiar one for rising Israeli teenagers who sign with top-flight clubs before they are ready for regular top-tier minutes, and a season in the National League with Elitzur Shomron should give Hershko exactly that kind of exposure ahead of an eventual return to Jerusalem.

title: Zubimendi's Arsenal future clouded by Bruno Guimarães arrival, ONE reports
dek: The Spaniard started 34 league games in his debut season but was left out for the Champions League final defeat to PSG, and now faces a crowded midfield after Arsenal's £75m swoop for Bruno Guimarães.
body: A year ago, Martín Zubimendi's arrival at Arsenal was treated as the culmination of a three-year chase by Mikel Arteta. Twelve months on, ONE reports that his long-term future at the Emirates is suddenly in question.

The trigger is Arsenal's £75million move for Bruno Guimarães, prised away from Newcastle United this summer in one of the club's marquee deals of the window. The Brazilian's arrival has crowded a midfield that was already stacked with internationals, and Zubimendi is the player squeezed hardest by it.

It is not that his debut campaign was a failure. The Spaniard started 34 Premier League matches, quickly establishing himself as Arteta's defensive pivot and tempo-setter. But when the stakes were highest, he found himself on the outside.

The clearest example came in Budapest on 30 May, when Arsenal lost the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties after a 1-1 draw. With a first European Cup on the line, Arteta turned to 19-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly in central midfield instead, leaving Zubimendi an unused substitute for the biggest match of the season.

There was a smaller but telling moment away at West Ham United too. Zubimendi was thrown on in the 28th minute after Ben White went off injured, only for Arteta to withdraw him himself in the 67th — hauled off for Kai Havertz after just 39 minutes on the pitch as Arsenal chased a winner they eventually got through Leandro Trossard.

Now, with Guimarães joining Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Merino and Lewis-Skelly in competition for midfield minutes, ONE frames Zubimendi as a player at risk of becoming collateral damage in Arsenal's aggressive summer rebuild — a full Spain international with no guarantee of a starting shirt.

The uncertainty has not gone unnoticed elsewhere. Reports gathered by outlets including FootballTransfers, TeamTalk and Caught Offside describe Arsenal setting an asking price of roughly €90million, with Chelsea and Real Madrid both credited with interest. Real Madrid, notably, missed out on Zubimendi last summer when he chose Arsenal instead.

Arteta, however, is said to have no appetite for a sale this window. Having spent three years courting Zubimendi at Real Sociedad before finally landing him, the Arsenal head coach reportedly regards him as central to his long-term plans rather than a player to be cashed in on for squad-balancing reasons.
For now, that leaves Zubimendi in limbo: a title-winning-calibre midfielder whose club does not want to sell him, but whose game time is no longer assured, with deadline day still to come.

title: Abu Farhi transfer terms agreed as Maccabi Tel Aviv striker awaits MLS sign-off on Colorado Rapids move
dek: Colorado Rapids and Maccabi Tel Aviv have settled the framework of a deal worth around $6 million for the 20-year-old forward, with only league approval left before he completes the switch, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Ynet: Maccabi and Colorado reach in-principle agreement
Ynet: MLS side offered $6m with ultimatum
Sport5: $6m bid for Sayed Abu Farhi

body: Sayed Abu Farhi's move from Maccabi Tel Aviv to Major League Soccer has cleared its biggest hurdle. The two clubs have agreed the framework of a transfer worth roughly $6 million, ONE reports, and the only step left is formal approval from MLS league management before the 20-year-old striker can complete his switch to Colorado Rapids.

The fee could rise by up to $1 million through performance-related add-ons, according to ONE, with Maccabi also retaining a small sell-on percentage should the Rapids move him on in future. Ynet, which first reported the clubs reaching an in-principle agreement, put the same headline figure of $6 million and confirmed the additional bonus structure.

Abu Farhi's own camp stands to benefit heavily. His family holds a stake of roughly 17.5 percent in his economic rights, meaning a $6 million sale would net them just over $1 million, with the rest going to Maccabi Tel Aviv, Walla Sport reported as the talks progressed.

The move has not been a simple negotiation. Colorado initially tabled a $6 million bid and, according to Ynet, pushed Maccabi for a same-day answer at one stage, while the Tel Aviv club had been holding out for closer to $8 million. The framework now agreed suggests the sides met close to the Rapids' original number, with add-ons bridging some of the gap.
Under MLS roster rules, Abu Farhi would sign as a young designated talent on the maximum salary permitted for players under 22 — reported by Ynet at $400,000 net across a four-year contract.

The timing is awkward for Maccabi Tel Aviv, who host CSKA Sofia in the second leg of their Europa League third qualifying round tie in Sofia on Thursday, trailing 3-0 from the first leg. ONE notes Thursday's match may be Abu Farhi's last appearance in a Maccabi shirt, depending on whether manager Kenny Miller opts to field him with a move to Denver-area club Colorado already all but agreed.

Abu Farhi has been Maccabi's most productive forward this season, scoring four goals in the club's opening four matches, after a breakout campaign last season that yielded 11 goals and three assists across all competitions. He is a product of Maccabi's academy and has represented Israel at U16, U17, U19 and U21 level.

His expected exit fits a wider pattern at Maccabi Tel Aviv this summer. One player at the club described the current mood as having "the feel of a clearance sale," Ynet reported, amid several departures under new management. Once MLS signs off, Abu Farhi is expected to travel to the United States to finalize the move to Colorado Rapids.

title: Sabah thrash Aarhus 4-0 to set up Champions League play-off duel with Hapoel Beer Sheva
dek: The Azerbaijani club overturned a first-leg deficit in Masazir and says it fears no one heading into a first-ever meeting with Israel's champions.

verificationSources.label: Jerusalem Post – Hapoel Beersheba edges Red Star Belgrade

body: Sabah FC completed a stunning turnaround against Aarhus on Wednesday, hammering the Danish champions 4-0 at home to book a place in the Champions League play-off round — where an Israeli side, Hapoel Beer Sheva, is waiting.

The Azerbaijani club had lost the first leg 2-1 in Denmark, but a rampant second-half display at their Masazir base flipped the tie on its head, sending Sabah through 5-2 on aggregate and one round away from the lucrative league phase.

Standing in their way now are the reigning Israeli champions. Hapoel Beer Sheva reached the same stage by beating Crvena Zvezda (Red Star Belgrade) 3-2 on aggregate, having won the first leg 1-0 at Turner Stadium before holding on in Belgrade. The two clubs have never met before.

According to ONE, Sabah's Lithuanian head coach Valdas Dambrauskas struck a defiant tone after the Aarhus rout, saying his side improve daily and "fear no opponent" heading into the play-off. "We attack everyone," he reportedly added, framing the upcoming tie as another test his team is ready to pass rather than a step up in class.

ONE's report also pointed to history as a source of Sabah's confidence against Israeli opposition: two years ago the club eliminated Maccabi Haifa in Conference League qualifying, winning a penalty shootout after the tie finished level at 6-6 on aggregate across two legs.

Founded only in 2017 with backing from local businessmen and government support, Sabah — whose name translates roughly as "tomorrow" in Azerbaijani — have built a reputation in a short space of time. Nicknamed the Owls and playing in a distinctive pink-and-black kit inspired by the nearby Masazir salt lake, the club has openly said it wants to follow the trail blazed by Qarabag, the Azerbaijani side that has become a fixture in Europe.
ONE cited the Azerbaijani journalist Kenan Mastelaev describing this Sabah squad as the strongest version of the club yet, ahead even of the side that knocked out Maccabi Haifa in 2024.

The play-off tie is set to be played home and away, with the first leg reported for August 18, and represents the last hurdle before the Champions League league phase proper — and the vastly increased prize money and prestige that comes with it. For Beer Sheva, already through one qualifying test against Serbian opposition, it is now a matter of proving the Sabah threat is more bark than bite.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva stun Red Star Belgrade 2-0 to reach Champions League playoff round
dek: Igor Zlatanović and Javon East scored in Belgrade as Ran Kozuk's side completed a 3-0 aggregate win over the Serbian champions, moving within two games of a first-ever Champions League league phase.
body: Hapoel Beer Sheva completed one of the biggest results in the club's European history on Tuesday night, beating Red Star Belgrade 2-0 away at the Rajko Mitić Stadium to seal a 3-0 aggregate victory in the third qualifying round of the Champions League.

The goals came in the second half in Belgrade: Igor Zlatanović put the visitors ahead just past the hour mark before Javon East added a second late on to end any doubt against a Red Star side that had arrived unbeaten and fresh off a 9-0 rout in the previous qualifying round.

It capped a tie Beer Sheva had already tilted in their favour at Turner Stadium a week earlier, when Zahi Ahmed's 38th-minute strike secured a 1-0 first-leg lead — one they defended for more than half an hour with ten men after defender Matan Baltaxa was shown a second yellow card in the 58th minute. Baltaxa served a one-match ban and missed the return leg.

Manager Ran Kozuk's side went to Serbia without their suspended defender and were expected by most Serbian media to be picked apart by Dejan Stanković's Red Star. Instead, the Israeli champions controlled long stretches of the game and could have won by more, according to Kozuk himself afterwards.

"These are immense feelings of pride — the players did it in style," Kozuk said, quoted by Walla Sport and Sport1 after the final whistle. "It could have ended by more than 2-0, but I'm not being greedy."
ONE's headline captured the mood in Israel bluntly, framing the result as Kozuk giving Stanković — the Red Star coach and former Inter Milan and Serbia captain — a footballing lesson on his own turf.
The win sends Beer Sheva into the Champions League playoff round, the last hurdle before the newly expanded league phase, where they will face Sabah FK of Azerbaijan over two legs.

Even before a ball is kicked against Sabah, the achievement already guarantees Beer Sheva at least a place in a European league phase this season — either the Champions League itself or, should they fall in the playoff, a drop into the Europa League — along with a UEFA payment reported by Israeli outlets at close to €9 million.

Should they get past Sabah, Beer Sheva would join Maccabi Haifa, Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Tel Aviv as the latest Israeli side to reach the Champions League league phase proper, with Israeli media describing the club as "180 minutes" from that milestone.

For a squad rebuilt under Kozuk after a difficult recent stretch domestically, beating a Red Star team many had installed as favourites — home and away — represents the clearest signal yet that the project in the Negev is back on track.

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva produced the biggest European qualifying result in the club's history on Tuesday night, beating Red Star Belgrade 2-0 away in Serbia to seal a 3-0 aggregate win and a place in the Champions League playoff round.

Igor Zlatanović broke the deadlock in the 61st minute at the Rajko Mitić Stadium, and Jevon Eisht doubled the lead in the 79th, extending a tie that Beer Sheva had already put one foot into the next round with a 1-0 first-leg win at home through Zahi Ahmed.

The aggregate scoreline against a club of Red Star's stature and Champions League pedigree stunned observers in Serbia. Sport1 reported that pundits there described the tie as one-sided, with Beer Sheva said to have "dismantled" the Belgrade giants without them finding any way back into it.

For Hapoel Beer Sheva, the result means a return to the Champions League playoff round for the third time in the club's history and the first since the 2017-18 campaign, when the Negev side reached the same stage under a different European qualifying format.

Beer Sheva go into the playoff as the reigning Israeli champions, having won the 2025-26 Ligat Ha'al title in May with a 4-2 win over Maccabi Tel Aviv. Manager Ran Kuznetsov, who signed with the club in 2024, has now guided them to a domestic title and a Champions League playoff berth inside the space of a few months.
Kuznetsov was measured but pleased after the final whistle. "I'm proud of the players," he said, according to Sport1. "We could have won by more than 2-0, but I'm not going to be greedy about it."

Beer Sheva now stand two matches from the Champions League group stage proper. Their playoff opponent will be Sabah Baku, the champions of Azerbaijan, in a two-legged tie that will decide who joins Europe's elite competition this autumn.

A win over Sabah Baku would not only deliver group-stage football to Turner Stadium for the first time in the club's history but also guarantee a significant financial windfall from UEFA prize money, a boost that would reshape Beer Sheva's transfer plans regardless of the eventual outcome, since a playoff defeat still drops the club into the Europa League group stage.

For a squad that faced questions over its transfer business and finances heading into the summer, the win in Belgrade is the clearest possible answer: Hapoel Beer Sheva are, for now, the form team of Israeli football on the European stage.

title: Hapoel Be'er Sheva plot spending spree after Champions League windfall
dek: ONE reports that with up to €18.6m secured from the club's Champions League qualifying run, head coach Ran Kozuch wants a foreign striker, a defensive midfielder and an Israeli playmaker before the Sabah play-off.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Kozuch reaction after Red Star Belgrade tie

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva's run to the Champions League qualifying play-off round has done more than fill the club's trophy cabinet with pride — it has filled the bank account, and now the club wants to spend some of it.

ONE reports that Be'er Sheva have already banked €7.9 million from their European qualifying campaign, a figure that could climb to €18.6 million should they get past Sabah FK of Azerbaijan in the play-off round and reach the Champions League league phase itself.

The southern club eliminated Red Star Belgrade 3-0 on aggregate to reach that stage, a result that transformed both the mood and the finances at Turner Stadium heading into the run-in of the transfer window.

According to ONE, head coach Ran Kozuch — who doubles as the club's key decision-maker on recruitment — is now pushing to convert that windfall into squad reinforcements before the Sabah ties, rather than banking it for later in the season.

The wish list, per the report, runs to two foreign signings: a striker and a defensive midfielder, positions Kozuch has identified as priorities if Be'er Sheva are to sustain a push on multiple fronts at home and in Europe.
Domestically, ONE reports interest in adding an Israeli midfielder to the group, with Maccabi Netanya's Maor Levi and Hapoel Petah Tikva's Roee David both named as candidates the club has considered.
David is said to be weighing a move to MLS, but the report suggests Be'er Sheva believe they can put together an offer competitive enough to change his mind and keep him in Israel.

On retention, the priority is Eliel Peretz, whose contract already runs to the summer of 2027. ONE reports the club intends to open formal talks over an extension only once the Sabah fixtures are out of the way, rather than risk unsettling him beforehand.

There is also a departure in the works: Yoav Korn is expected to leave for Maccabi Petah Tikva, according to the report, thinning the squad in an area Kozuch will need to address alongside the incoming business.

Time is tight. ONE notes that the registration window for new signings ahead of the Sabah play-off is narrow, which is pushing Be'er Sheva toward faster decisions than they might otherwise make with a fresh injection of European money.

None of the reported targets amount to done deals yet, and the figures attached to any of the incoming business have not been disclosed. But the scale of the Champions League windfall means Kozuch, for the first time in years, is shaping a squad with genuine financial room to manoeuvre.

title: Savannah, 29 July 1996: The Bronze That Widened Israel's Olympic Horizons
dek: A 20-year-old windsurfer from a Caesarea kibbutz sailed onto the podium at Wassaw Sound and proved, four years after Barcelona, that Israeli Olympic sport was not a one-trick story.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — Sailing at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's Mistral One Design
Wikipedia — Israel at the 1996 Summer Olympics

body: The wind off Wassaw Sound, in the tidal marshes east of Savannah, Georgia, was doing exactly what an Olympic windsurfing fleet dreads and craves in equal measure on the final day of racing: shifting, gusting, never quite settling. Forty-six sailors from forty-six countries had spent a week and a half racing one-design Mistral boards through the Atlanta Games' sailing regatta, and by 29 July 1996 the fleet had worked through nine of its eleven scheduled races before organizers called the series. Among the sailors fighting for the podium was a 20-year-old Israeli, barely known outside his sport, named Gal Fridman.

Four years earlier in Barcelona, Israel had finally broken its Olympic medal drought: Yael Arad's judo silver and Oren Smadja's judo bronze, both won within days of each other in 1992, were the country's first Olympic medals since it had entered the Games in 1952. It was a watershed moment, but it left an obvious question hanging over Israeli sport — could the country produce a medalist in anything other than judo? Atlanta was where that question got its answer, and the answer arrived on a sailboard.

Fridman was born on 16 September 1975 in Karkur and grew up sailing out of Sdot Yam, the kibbutz beside Caesarea whose nautical club has produced generation after generation of Israeli windsurfers. His father, Uri, put him on a board at the age of seven; by eleven he was racing. Windsurfing in Israel was, and largely remains, a Sdot Yam story — a small stretch of Mediterranean coastline that punches enormously above its weight in an Olympic class most countries treat as a niche.

The men's Mistral One Design fleet raced under the format standard to Olympic sailing at the time: eleven races on the schedule, each sailor's two worst results discarded, low net score wins. It rewards consistency as much as brilliance — a single disastrous race can be shrugged off, but a sailor has to be near the front, race after race, for a week and a half of shifting Georgia coastal wind. Fridman did exactly that.

When the series closed after the ninth race on 29 July, the podium read: gold to Nikolaos Kaklamanakis of Greece, the reigning world champion, with 17 net points; silver to Carlos Espinola of Argentina on 19; and bronze to Fridman on 21. New Zealand's Aaron McIntosh, the two-time reigning world champion of the class going into the Games, finished fourth on 27, agonizingly off the medals — a reminder of how unforgiving the discard system could be even to sailors with better overall pedigree than the podium finishers.

It was, in the end, the only medal Israel would win at the Atlanta Games. The Israeli delegation that summer numbered 25 athletes — 18 men and seven women — competing in 26 events across ten sports, with hurdler Lydia Hatuel-Zuckerman carrying the flag at the opening ceremony. None of them but Fridman came home with a medal. For a small team at a Games that many nations' larger federations treated as a numbers exercise, a single bronze from a 20-year-old windsurfer carried outsized weight.

It also carried historical weight. Fridman's bronze was Israel's third Olympic medal in its history, and its first ever won outside the judo hall. Where Arad and Smadja had shown Israel could win, Fridman showed it could win differently — that the country's sporting infrastructure, however modest, could turn out champions on the water as well as on the mat. He was named Israel's Sportsman of the Year for 1996, a 20-year-old suddenly carrying the label of trailblazer.

The story did not end at bronze. Fridman kept racing, kept improving, and in 2002 topped the International Sailing Federation's world rankings after winning the Mistral World Championship in Pattaya. Then, eight years almost to the month after Savannah, he returned to the same one-design windsurfing class at the Athens 2004 Olympics and won gold — becoming Israel's first Olympic champion in any sport, and, for years afterward, the only Israeli athlete to have won two separate Olympic medals.

The lineage he started at Sdot Yam did not stop with him, either. In 2008, a young windsurfer named Shahar Tzuberi — who had beaten Fridman himself for Israel's Beijing team selection — won bronze in the RS:X windsurfing class, Israel's only medal of those Games, echoing almost exactly what Fridman had done twelve years earlier: a lone medal, a lone windsurfer, carrying a small team's hopes across an ocean of wind and water.

None of it happens without that shifting Georgia wind on 29 July 1996, and a 20-year-old from a kibbutz windsurfing club who kept his board in the top three when it mattered most. Judo had opened the door for Israeli Olympic sport in Barcelona. In Savannah, Gal Fridman showed it could be walked through by almost anyone with enough wind at their back.
facts: Gal Fridman (b. 16 September 1975, Karkur) won bronze in the Men's Mistral One Design windsurfing event at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, racing at Wassaw Sound near Savannah, Georgia.

The series concluded on 29 July 1996 after nine of eleven scheduled races; Fridman finished with 21 net points, behind gold medalist Nikolaos Kaklamanakis of Greece (17) and silver medalist Carlos Espinola of Argentina (19).
It was the only medal Israel won at the 1996 Atlanta Games, from a delegation of 25 athletes (18 men, 7 women) competing in 26 events across 10 sports.
It was Israel's third Olympic medal overall and its first ever outside judo, following Yael Arad's silver and Oren Smadja's bronze in judo at the 1992 Barcelona Games.
Fridman was named Israel's Sportsman of the Year for 1996 following the medal.
Eight years later, at the Athens 2004 Olympics, Fridman won gold in the same windsurfing class, becoming Israel's first Olympic champion.
In 2008, fellow Sdot Yam windsurfer Shahar Tzuberi (Zubari) — who had beaten Fridman for Israel's Beijing team spot — won bronze in the RS:X windsurfing class, Israel's only medal at those Games.
