title: Barcelona and PSG reach agreement in principle over Ferran Torres transfer
dek: PSG have agreed a deal worth up to €55m for the Spain forward who scored the winning goal in this summer's World Cup final, with Luis Enrique making a personal pitch to lure him to Paris.
body: Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain have struck an agreement in principle for the transfer of Ferran Torres, according to a report by Israeli outlet ONE, with the Spain forward closing in on a move to Ligue 1 just weeks after scoring the goal that won this summer's World Cup.

ONE reports the fee stands at €50 million guaranteed, with a further €5 million in performance add-ons that could push the total package to €55 million. Those terms line up closely with reporting in France and Spain, including Goal and Barca Blaugranes, who describe the deal as being in its final stages.

Barcelona had initially knocked back an opening PSG offer of €40 million plus €10 million in variables, insisting on a €50 million guaranteed baseline. ONE reports PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi personally authorised the improved bid once it became clear that figure was the price of getting the deal done.

Luis Enrique is described as the driving force behind the move. According to ONE, the PSG coach called Torres directly to lay out the role he would play in Paris — a version of events also reported by L'Equipe in France, which said Enrique reached out personally to a player he already knows well from his time in charge of the Spanish national team.

The report suggests Torres had grown frustrated at Barcelona, feeling he never received a firm vote of confidence from either Deco or former coach Hansi Flick, despite hints in recent interviews that he wanted clearer assurances over his future at the club.

Torres, 26, had one year left on his Barcelona contract. Reports in France indicate he is set to sign terms with PSG running for five seasons, through to 2031, putting him on a deal in line with the club's leading earners.

The move comes little more than three weeks after Torres scored the only goal in Spain's 2026 World Cup final victory over Argentina, a result that made him one of the most sought-after forwards in Europe this summer.

ONE reports Torres was expected at Barcelona's training complex to clear out his locker and say goodbye to teammates before departing for Paris, with the fundamentals of the deal said to have been settled while PSG's hierarchy were in Europe for the Super Cup. Final paperwork was still being completed at the time of writing.

A deal of this scale would rank among the most significant departures from Camp Nou this summer and hands Enrique another attacking option as PSG look to build on a dominant recent run under the Spaniard.

title: Red Star Belgrade move to sack Dejan Stanković after 3-0 aggregate exit to Hapoel Beer Sheva
dek: ONE reports that Crvena zvezda's board acted within hours of a chaotic Champions League qualifying elimination in Belgrade, where Stanković was sent off before Hapoel Beer Sheva completed a stunning 3-0 aggregate upset.

verificationSources.label: B92 — Stanković sent off, clashes with fans
Mozzart Sport — Stanković says goodbye to players, board meeting called

body: Dejan Stanković's second spell in charge of Red Star Belgrade appears to be over almost as abruptly as his first. ONE reports, citing Serbian media, that Crvena zvezda's board moved to dismiss the coach within hours of Hapoel Beer Sheva eliminating the Serbian champions from Champions League qualifying.

The elimination was completed on Tuesday night at the Rajko Mitić Stadium, where Red Star lost 2-0 to Hapoel Beer Sheva in the second leg of their third qualifying round tie, going down 3-0 on aggregate after also losing 1-0 in the first leg the previous week.

Stanković did not even see out the match. According to ONE, he was sent off in the 57th minute for furiously contesting a decision by the Swedish referee, then turned toward Red Star's own supporters as he left the technical area, mocking the whistles raining down from the stands. Serbian reports cited by ONE go further still, alleging he also spat in the referee's direction as he departed.

With qualification lost and his own conduct under scrutiny, Stanković reportedly said his goodbyes to the Red Star squad in the dressing room straight after the final whistle — read in Belgrade as an unmistakable signal that the end had come. The club's board called an emergency meeting for the following day to address what local media described as a full-blown crisis.

As of ONE's report, Red Star Belgrade had issued no official statement confirming a dismissal, and the club's own channels made no mention of a change in the dugout. But the direction of travel described by Serbian outlets, including B92 and Mozzart Sport, pointed toward a departure the club had yet to announce publicly.

For Stanković, it would be a bitterly familiar way to lose the job at the club where he made his name as a player. He walked away from his first spell in charge in August 2022 after Red Star were eliminated from the same Champions League qualifying stage by another Israeli club, Maccabi Haifa, beaten by a stoppage-time own goal that summed up years of continental frustration for the Serbian side.

He returned to Red Star in December 2025, restored to the post that had made him a hero in Belgrade, only for this Champions League qualifying campaign to end the same way it had before — eliminated by an Israeli opponent, this time Hapoel Beer Sheva.

For Hapoel Beer Sheva, the aggregate scoreline stands as a landmark result: eliminating one of the biggest institutions in Balkan football and denying a multiple Serbian champion a place in the next round of Champions League qualifying, a result that will be celebrated in Israeli football long after the coaching fallout in Belgrade is settled.

Red Star's board meeting was expected to decide not only Stanković's fate but the club's direction after a result that costs it the prestige — and the revenue — of another shot at the Champions League group stage.

This is the second time an Israeli club has ended Stanković's Champions League bid at Red Star: Maccabi Haifa eliminated Red Star in August 2022, after which Stanković resigned.

title: Barda downplays Hapoel Tel Aviv's 2-0 cushion ahead of Katowice return leg
dek: Head coach Elyaniv Barda and defender Doron Leidner say the first-leg lead counts for nothing as Hapoel Tel Aviv chase a Conference League playoff-round place against GKS Katowice.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv can complete a return to European group-stage football for the first time in more than a decade on Wednesday, when they travel to Katowice to defend a 2-0 lead from the first leg of their Conference League third qualifying round tie.

The stakes are high: whichever club goes through will face Serie A side Atalanta in the play-off round, one final hurdle from a place in the 2026/27 Conference League league phase. Kick-off in Katowice is set for 18:00 CEST, 19:00 Israel time.

Hapoel took the advantage in the first leg with a 2-0 win at DVTK Stadion in Miskolc, Hungary — the venue used for their home fixture — through goals from Stav Turiel and Roei Alkukin. Katowice, one of the stronger sides in Poland's second tier, have a habit of digging in at home and will need a big display to overturn the deficit.

Head coach Elyaniv Barda was in no mood to treat the tie as settled when he spoke to ONE ahead of the flight to Poland. "The last match is history for us, and we're thinking about the next one," he said, before adding the caution that has defined his approach all season: "Every game starts 0-0, and you can't know what's going to happen."

Barda said his squad had reviewed the first leg in detail and identified where they fell short. "We expect to improve on what we didn't do well enough," he said, indicating some tactical tweaks are likely for the second leg rather than a simple repeat of the first-leg gameplan.

Defender Doron Leidner, on loan at Hapoel from Olympiacos, echoed the coach's wariness. "We gave a hundred percent to get to this point, knowing we're up against a quality team," he told ONE, adding that both sides have now scouted each other closely and know where the other can be hurt.

The tie carries extra weight for a club that has spent years rebuilding after relegation to the second division earlier this decade. Barda has overseen that climb back to the top flight and now into continental competition, and a further step past Katowice would put Hapoel one round from Europe's revamped league phase for the first time in the club's modern history.

Should Hapoel hold on, the reward is a shot at Atalanta — one of the form sides in Italian football in recent seasons — in the play-off round next week, with a league-phase place and its accompanying prize money and prestige on the line.

title: Dresden, 25 November 2008: The Silver That Finally Reached Israel's Chess Team
dek: Boris Gelfand went through the 38th Chess Olympiad unbeaten, Israel handed eventual champions Armenia their only defeat of the tournament, and a nervy final-round win over the Netherlands delivered the national open team's first-ever medal at chess's biggest event.

verificationSources.label: The Jerusalem Post — "Israel wins silver at Chess Olympiad"
Ynetnews — "Israel takes silver medal in Chess Olympiad"
OlimpBase — Israel at the 38th Chess Olympiad, Dresden 2008
ChessBase — Olympiad in Dresden: Closing ceremony and prize giving

body: Chess Olympiads are strange, sprawling affairs — eleven rounds, well over a hundred nations, four boards a side, played out over two weeks in an exhibition hall that could just as easily be hosting a trade fair. In November 2008 it was Dresden's turn, the rebuilt Internationales Congress Center on the banks of the Elbe filling with tables, clocks and the low murmur of concentration for the 38th edition of the world's largest team chess event.

Israel arrived without much fanfare. The team was solid rather than star-studded on paper: Boris Gelfand on board one, flanked by Michael Roiz, Boris Avrukh, Evgeny Postny and the young national champion Maxim Rodshtein. Nobody outside the chess world was tracking their scoresheet as the rounds ticked by. Inside it, though, something was building — Israel kept winning, and kept not losing.

The team that everyone was watching was Armenia, top seeds and, as it turned out, worthy of the billing: they would finish the tournament with only a single blemish on an otherwise perfect run. That blemish belonged to Israel. Somewhere in the middle rounds, Gelfand and his teammates beat the Armenians 2½–1½ — the only match Armenia would lose on their way to gold.

It didn't knock Armenia off course; they regrouped and kept winning everything else. But it kept Israel in the frame, quietly climbing a leaderboard usually topped by chess superpowers. By the ninth and tenth rounds, the pairings were throwing Israel against the kind of opposition — the United States, Russia, Ukraine, China — that had never previously shared a podium picture with the Israeli flag.

At the centre of it all was Gelfand, then forty years old and already a fixture of the world's elite for two decades. He simply did not lose. Ten games, five wins, five draws — an individual board-one silver to go with whatever the team could manage, and the calm, immovable presence that let the four players around him take risks.

The tournament came down to the final round on 25 November, with Israel needing to beat the Netherlands to lock down a podium finish. It was tense rather than emphatic: three of the four boards were drawn, nerves visibly fraying under the weight of what was at stake. It was 25-year-old Michael Roiz, beating 23-year-old Jan Smeets, who supplied the only decisive result of the match — a 2½–1½ win that was enough.

When the final standings were totted up, Armenia had won gold on 19 match points. Israel finished on 18 — silver, one point clear of a three-way tiebreak scrap for bronze that the United States eventually won ahead of Ukraine. It was, by any measure, the best finish in the history of Israel's senior national chess team.

"Over 140 teams have participated in this Olympiad," Israel Chess Federation chairman Aviv Bushinsky said afterwards, "and during the games we even beat Armenia, the team that won the gold." It was the kind of line that only makes sense with the medal already around your neck — pointing to the one result that, on another day, might have gone the other way and changed everything.

There was no great financial fanfare waiting for the players back home; Israeli chess has never had the funding of its Olympic sports. What it had, for a fortnight in Saxony, was a team that punched above its seeding, a board-one anchor who refused to lose, and a scoreline against the eventual champions that read better than anyone had a right to expect.

Israel has sent teams to every Chess Olympiad since without matching that podium finish. Dresden remains the high-water mark — a silver medal, a giant-killing win over the tournament's ultimate winners, and a young champion's cool nerve in the final round, all bound up in a fortnight most of the sporting world never noticed.
facts: The 38th Chess Olympiad ran from 12–25 November 2008 in Dresden, Germany, staged at the Internationales Congress Center.

Israel's open team — Boris Gelfand, Michael Roiz, Boris Avrukh, Evgeny Postny and Maxim Rodshtein — finished second among more than 140 competing nations, taking silver with 18 match points, one behind gold medallists Armenia (19) and one ahead of bronze medallists the United States (17, who won a tiebreak over Ukraine, also on 17).
It was the first team medal won by Israel's senior open squad in the history of the Chess Olympiad.
During the event Israel handed Armenia — who went on to win gold with only that one loss — a 2½–1½ defeat, Armenia's only loss of the tournament.
Israel clinched the silver medal in the final round with a 2½–1½ win over the Netherlands; Michael Roiz's win over Jan Smeets was the only decisive board, the other three ending in draws.
Boris Gelfand, playing board one at age 40, went through the whole tournament unbeaten (5 wins, 5 draws from 10 games) and won an individual board medal.

title: 'Natural fit': the thinking behind Crystal Palace's move for Anan Khalaili
dek: Palace have reportedly agreed a deal worth around £21m for the Israel international, beating Everton, Aston Villa and Newcastle to a player seen as tailor-made for Oliver Glasner's wing-back system.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "התאמה טבעית": הסיבות של פאלאס להחתמת חלאילי
The Times of Israel - Israeli soccer star Anan Khalaili said set to sign with England's Crystal Palace
David Ornstein (The Athletic) on X - Palace finalising Khalaili deal on ~£21m fee, 5+1yr contract
Ynet - Anan Khalaili signs with Crystal Palace in most expensive deal for an Israeli player

body: Crystal Palace are closing in on the signing of Anan Khalaili, and according to ONE the club's pursuit of the Israel international came down to a simple conviction: he is a "natural fit" for the way Oliver Glasner wants his team to play.

The Eagles have reportedly agreed a fee of around £21m with Union Saint-Gilloise, with Khalaili already through a medical in England and personal terms settled on a five-year contract that includes the option of a further season. Reports value the deal at closer to €25-28m once add-ons are factored in, and while the clubs have yet to confirm the numbers publicly, respected transfer reporter David Ornstein described Palace as being "in the process of finalising" the move.

The appeal, as ONE and other outlets covering the deal have framed it, is Khalaili's blend of pace, directness and end product operating from a right-sided role - qualities that slot neatly into Glasner's 3-4-2-1, a system built around attacking wing-backs who overload the opposition's flank. At Union Saint-Gilloise, Khalaili spent last season doing exactly that, and the profile translated straightforwardly to what Palace are trying to build.

Getting there wasn't straightforward for Palace, who saw off competition from Everton, Aston Villa and Newcastle United to land him. Inter Milan had also been in the picture earlier in the summer and looked close to signing him for a fee in the same region, only for the move to collapse after Khalaili reportedly failed elements of his medical - a cardiopulmonary irregularity flagged during testing in Italy that the Serie A club never revived talks around.

That collapse left Khalaili's summer in limbo for weeks before Palace stepped in. The 21-year-old, born in Haifa, made his way through Maccabi Haifa's system before loan spells including at second-division Hapoel Hadera, then left for Belgium and Union Saint-Gilloise, where he established himself as one of the most productive wide players in the Belgian Pro League - contributing around a dozen goal involvements last season across close to 50 appearances.

The transfer, once completed, would make Khalaili the most expensive Israeli player in history, surpassing previous benchmarks for a national team player moving abroad, and it would leave him as the only Israeli currently on a Premier League roster.

He already has 16 caps for Israel's senior national team, and his emergence has been tracked closely by English media over the past year as one of European football's more sought-after young wide players - hence the multi-club chase that ultimately fell Palace's way.

Formal confirmation and unveiling are still pending, with reports in Israel suggesting a presentation could follow within days once the paperwork between Palace and Union Saint-Gilloise is finalized. Until then, the deal remains one being reported rather than officially announced by either club.

title: Uncertainty clouds Messi's return to Inter Miami after father's death
dek: The Argentine remains in Rosario with his family, and no date has been set for when he will rejoin the club after burying his father, Jorge, on Sunday.
body: Lionel Messi has no timetable for returning to Inter Miami, with the Argentine choosing to stay in Rosario with his family in the days after burying his father, Jorge, ONE reports.
Jorge Messi, who was also his son's long-time agent, died on Saturday, August 8, at the age of 68 following a lengthy illness that had been kept largely private among close relatives.

According to ONE, Lionel landed in Argentina on Saturday evening aboard a private jet that flew from Fort Lauderdale to the Islas Malvinas airport in Fisherton, before heading to a private cemetery in Pres, on the outskirts of Rosario.

The farewell ceremony was held behind closed doors at El Prado cemetery on Sunday, with only close family and friends in attendance. Other outlets, including ESPN and Goal, report that Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, their children, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, along with siblings Matías, Rodrigo and María Sol, were also present.

The Argentine Football Association and the national team's coaching staff sent flowers to the funeral, and messages of support, including "Be strong, Leo," were left by well-wishers at the cemetery gates, ONE reports.

By Sunday afternoon, Messi had left the cemetery and travelled to his family's gated residential complex in Ponce, in the Kentucky neighbourhood of Rosario, where he has remained with relatives rather than fly back to Florida.

Before the tragedy, there had been genuine debate over when Messi would rejoin Inter Miami following Argentina's World Cup campaign. Wednesday's Leagues Cup match against Club León, Saturday's MLS fixture at home to Nashville SC, and the August 19 meeting with Philadelphia Union had all been floated as possible comeback points, per ESPN.

That planning has now been overtaken by events. Mundo Albiceleste and other outlets report that Messi is taking an indefinite break from the club, with no return date set as he stays close to his mother and siblings in Rosario.
Inter Miami have not publicly pushed for a timeline, and coach Javier Mascherano's staff are expected to give their captain as much space as he needs before he resumes full training in South Florida.

title: Paul Scholes urges Manchester United to hijack Atletico Madrid's move for Cristian Romero
dek: The Manchester United great branded the Tottenham defender 'an absolute clown' but reckons Michael Carrick could get the best out of him at Old Trafford.
body: Paul Scholes has told Manchester United to try to hijack Cristian Romero's move to Atletico Madrid, even as Tottenham Hotspur edge closer to selling their Argentine centre-back to the Spanish club this summer.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, the United great did not exactly sell the idea gently. "I know it sounds silly, but I like him," Scholes said. "I think he's crazy, a very good defender who does silly things, he's an absolute clown."

Scholes doubled down, calling Romero "a nutcase" in the same breath as praising his ability, and argued the 28-year-old would be relatively cheap business at somewhere between £30 million and £40 million given his trophy haul.

Romero has won the World Cup and two Copa America titles with Argentina, and lifted the Europa League with Spurs last season — a résumé Scholes believes makes him worth the gamble despite his combustible reputation on the pitch.

The pundit's case rests partly on Michael Carrick, who has taken charge at Old Trafford and whose calm, measured touchline manner Scholes thinks could channel Romero's aggression rather than let it boil over into the kind of rash challenges that have brought him repeated bookings and suspensions in England.

Scholes also pointed to United's defensive frailties as the driving reason to move, flagging doubts over the reliability and fitness of Lisandro Martinez as a factor pushing the club to look for reinforcements before the transfer window shuts.

The timing is tight. Tottenham and Atletico Madrid are already deep into negotiations over Romero, with reports putting the two sides only a few million pounds apart on a fee that has been quoted at various points between £30 million and roughly £40 million, still without a full package agreed on bonuses and add-ons.

For now Romero's most likely destination remains Madrid rather than Manchester, but Scholes' intervention has at least put United's name into a conversation that, until now, had been a straight negotiation between Spurs and Atletico.

title: Nikola Jokić plots record $359m supermax deal with the Nuggets — but not until 2027
dek: The three-time MVP could have cashed in this summer, but ESPN reports he is willing to wait a year for a deal that would make him the highest-paid player in NBA history.
body: Nikola Jokić is on course to sign the richest contract in NBA history — he is simply choosing to wait a year to get it. ONE reports that the Denver Nuggets' three-time MVP is eligible for a five-year, $359.5 million supermax extension, but only once he reaches the 2027 offseason.

According to ESPN, which first reported the numbers, Jokić could instead have signed a four-year, $278 million extension with Denver this summer. He and his camp are said to have passed on that option in favour of the far larger deal available to him next year.

To get there, Jokić has to first decline the player option on the final season of his current contract, worth roughly $62.8 million for 2027-28, and re-enter Denver's books as a free agent under the league's supermax rules reserved for players who qualify on accolades.

ONE frames the projected $359.5 million deal as the largest in league history, ahead of the guaranteed money in recent maximum extensions signed by players such as Jaylen Brown and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. The report also notes the new deal is expected to include a no-trade clause.

The delay is being read around the league as a financial calculation rather than any sign of discontent in Denver. Jokić himself has downplayed any drama over the timing, telling reporters recently: "My idea and desire is to stay in Denver. I'll probably sign next year."

Nothing is signed yet — the figures reported are the maximum Jokić would be eligible for under the collective bargaining agreement, and both sides still have a full season to navigate before any extension can be finalised in 2027.

The numbers reflect where Jokić's stock sits after another dominant campaign. He averaged 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 10.7 assists last season, adding to a résumé that already includes three MVP awards and the 2023 NBA championship with Denver.

If the supermax materialises as projected, Jokić's career earnings would approach $724 million, which would make him the highest-paid player in NBA history — a milestone ONE's report frames as fitting for a player Denver has built its entire era around.

For now, the Nuggets and their franchise centre appear aligned on the plan: Jokić stays through this season on his existing deal, and the two sides revisit the record-breaking numbers when the calendar allows it next summer.

title: Real Madrid and Vinicius agree to keep new contract salary secret
dek: The club and forward struck a quiet pact after his deal to 2032, wary of stirring wage disputes with Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham, ONE reports.
body: Real Madrid and Vinicius Junior have decided the one detail of his blockbuster new contract that will not be made public is the number on the payslip, according to ONE, which cites reporting by the Athletic.
The Brazilian winger signed a renewal through 2032 on August 6, ending close to 18 months of on-off negotiations that at times threatened to end with him walking away from the Bernabeu for nothing.

But rather than confirm the financial terms, as clubs often do when unveiling marquee deals, Real Madrid and the player's camp have chosen silence. ONE reports the pair agreed the figures would stay private, a deliberate move to avoid setting a precedent inside the dressing room.

The concern, per the report, is straightforward: a headline-grabbing renewal bonus for Vinicius could embolden other first-team players to demand comparable terms the next time their own contracts come up.

There is also the matter of Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham. Publishing Vinicius's exact salary would invite instant comparisons with his two superstar teammates, comparisons Madrid would rather avoid feeding while all three are meant to be pulling in the same direction.

The numbers that have leaked paint a picture of a negotiation that moved a long way. Vinicius, 26, is reported to have originally pushed for close to 30 million euros net a season plus a substantial signing bonus, while Madrid's opening offer sat around 22 million euros.

ONE reports the final figure ended up above that initial 22 million euro offer, though neither side has confirmed by how much. The breakthrough reportedly came in early August, when the club sweetened its terms enough to close the gap.

Arsenal's interest was real and, by several accounts, played a part in accelerating Madrid's willingness to improve the offer. The Premier League club was said to be ready to make a significant financial effort to prise the forward away from the Spanish capital.
Beyond salary, Vinicius also pushed for improved image-rights provisions in the new deal, seeking terms that better reflect his standing as one of the squad's most marketable and important players.

For now, the exact figure stays behind closed doors at Valdebebas — an unusual bit of discretion for a club that rarely shies away from publicising its biggest signings, but one both sides evidently decided was worth the trade-off.

title: Israel's reserve handball team beat Belgium 19-18 on penalties after late collapse
dek: The Atudah survived a nervy finish at the European Championship, blowing a big third-quarter lead before goalkeeping heroics sealed the shootout win.

verificationSources.label: ONE - אחרי דרמה גדולה בפנדלים: העתודה ניצחה את בלגיה

body: Israel's reserve national handball team needed a penalty shootout to get past Belgium on Tuesday, winning 19-18 in a game that swung from comfortable to chaotic and back again at the European Championship.

The Israelis, known in Hebrew shorthand as the Atudah - the development tier that bridges the youth and senior national sides - controlled the contest for three quarters, building a 13-7 lead midway through the third. From there Belgium clawed back point by point, dragging the match all the way to the wire and forcing extra time before a shootout was needed to separate the sides.

"We controlled the game for three quarters exactly as we wanted," the Israeli coach said afterwards, according to ONE. "Then the final quarter came. We made things far more complicated than necessary, allowed our opponent back into the match, and turned what should have been a calm victory into a dramatic finish."

It was a result the coach framed as a lesson as much as a win, with the team acknowledging it needs to see out games with more composure if it wants to keep progressing through the tournament unbeaten.

Tomer Arzi was central to the escape act, making five significant saves during the match, while ONE reported that Israel's goalkeeper - referred to in the dressing room by the nickname "Messi" - produced the decisive stops in the shootout itself to seal the two points.
The win follows an opening victory over Belarus, 17-11, meaning Israel have taken maximum points from their first two outings at the championship.
Israel's next assignment comes quickly: they face Great Britain on Wednesday at 11:00 Israel time, looking to make it three wins from three as they push to top their group.

title: Miki Berkovich's grandson Ariel promoted to Ironi Ramat Gan's senior squad
dek: Ariel Berkovich, 17, will train with the Israeli Premier League club while also getting minutes in the National League under the double-roster rule, continuing one of Israeli basketball's most storied family lines.
body: The Berkovich name is going back onto an Israeli Premier League roster. Ariel Berkovich, the 17-year-old grandson of Maccabi Tel Aviv and Israeli national team legend Miki Berkovich, has been promoted to the senior squad of Maccabi Ironi Ramat Gan, the club has announced, according to ONE.

Berkovich, a 1.85-metre point guard, spent this past season working his way through Ironi Ramat Gan's youth department, where the club describes him as an athletic, aggressive presence who likes to drive to the basket rather than settle for jump shots.

He will not be limited to the senior bench, either. Under Israeli basketball's double-roster rule, Berkovich will also be registered with Hapoel Gezer/Naan in the National League, the system clubs use to give promising teenagers real minutes in a competitive league while they continue developing alongside the top team.

"Ariel successfully completed his time in our youth department at the club," Ironi Ramat Gan coach Elad Chasan said, per ONE. "Ariel is a wonderful kid, talented, hard-working, and comes from an amazing basketball family."

For Berkovich himself, the step up is the realisation of a childhood goal. "From a young age I've dreamed of playing in the Premier League, and I'm very excited that I've been given this opportunity," he said. "It's a great honour to join Maccabi Ramat Gan's senior team, a prestigious club run with full professionalism."

The surname carries serious weight in Israeli basketball. Miki Berkovich, Ariel's grandfather, is a FIBA Hall of Fame inductee and one of the greatest players the country has produced — a shooting guard who won 16 championships and two European Champions Cups with Maccabi Tel Aviv, including the club's breakthrough 1977 title, and who was later voted MVP of EuroBasket 1979 after leading Israel to a silver medal.

Ariel's father, Roi Berkovich, also played professionally, meaning the teenager's promotion to Ironi Ramat Gan's top flight marks a third generation of the family stepping onto an Israeli senior basketball roster.

Ironi Ramat Gan itself has been on an upward trajectory in recent seasons, winning the National League title in 2022-23 before returning to the Israeli Basketball Premier League, where Berkovich now begins his senior career under close watch — and inevitable comparison to the grandfather whose number hangs in Israeli basketball lore.

title: The temptation of fantasy: is splashing out on stars worth the return?
dek: ONE's Fantasy La Liga guide weighs whether pricey picks like Vinicius Jr and Julián Álvarez actually deliver value, or leave managers short elsewhere on the pitch.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הפיתוי של הפנטזי: האם ההשקעה שווה את התמורה?
ONE - נעים להכיר: השווי של שחקני הרכש הנוצצים בפנטזי

body: With Fantasy La Liga squads being finalised ahead of the new season, ONE's build-day guide asks the question every manager wrestles with: does sinking a big chunk of the budget into the game's marquee names actually pay off in points, or does it just leave the rest of the XI threadbare.

The site's own framing is blunt about the stakes. With a fixed budget, ONE writes, "every million can make the difference between a balanced squad and one dependent on two or three stars" - meaning one expensive pick who goes quiet can sink an entire gameweek.

Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr, among the priciest assets in the game at roughly 13 million, is held up as the clearest case study - electric going forward, but flagged by ONE for inconsistency, a habit of picking up cards, and the rotation risk that comes with Madrid's squad depth.

Raphinha, priced similarly at 13 million, gets a similar caveat: excellent when fit, according to the guide, but with an injury history and competition for minutes that make him a harder set-and-forget pick than his reputation suggests.

Julián Álvarez fares worse in the numbers ONE cites - the World Cup winner managed only eight league goals last season, a return the piece argues doesn't justify his premium price tag in the fantasy game.

Further down the price scale, Barcelona's Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi (10-11 million) are described as high-upside but unproven starters, while Jude Bellingham and Trent Alexander-Arnold both carry injury question marks despite their obvious quality. Pedri, ONE notes, is as gifted as anyone in La Liga but doesn't consistently translate that into fantasy returns.
The guide's bottom line is a case for restraint: sometimes passing on one glamour name to strengthen two other positions on the pitch is the smarter build than chasing star power alone.

title: Papi Turgeman returns to Hapoel Jerusalem as club ambassador
dek: The former point guard and Israel captain, one of the club's two State Cup-winning heroes of the 1990s, is coming home in a new off-court role.

body: Papi Turgeman is coming home. ONE reports that Hapoel Jerusalem has appointed the former point guard as a club ambassador, formalising a role for a man widely regarded as one of the two or three most significant figures in the club's history.

According to the report, Turgeman's brief will be to strengthen ties between the club and its fans, the wider Jerusalem community and sponsors — the kind of behind-the-scenes relationship-building that clubs increasingly lean on their legends to do.
"I am excited and very happy to return home, to the club that was such a meaningful part of my life," Turgeman said, according to ONE.
Hapoel Jerusalem CEO Oren Arieli was quoted calling the appointment a natural one: "Papi is much more than a former player — he is part of our history and DNA."

Turgeman, full name Shalom "Papi" Turgeman, made his senior debut for Hapoel Jerusalem in 1990 and went on to spend roughly a decade at the club, establishing himself as its floor general and eventually captain. He was central to the team that won back-to-back Israeli State Cups in 1996 and 1997.

He also captained the Israeli national team, winning 57 caps, and led the Israel Basketball Premier League in assists in the 1994-95 season — a reflection of the playmaking instincts that made him a fan favourite through the decade.

The move plugs a well-worn Israeli sports tradition of clubs formalising ties with their most beloved former players, giving Hapoel Jerusalem a recognisable face for its fan and sponsor outreach as the club heads into a new season.

title: Beitar Yavne pulls out of Liga Alef, opening the door for Ironi Beit Shemesh
dek: A year after reaching Liga Alef South for the first time in its history, Beitar Yavne has formally scratched its registration for next season — handing the vacated spot to Ironi Beit Shemesh, who return to the division for the first time since 1989.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Beitar Yavne's promotion to Liga Alef South, 2025

body: Beitar Yavne has formally cancelled its registration for next season's Liga Alef South, ONE reports, walking away from a division it only reached for the first time in its history twelve months ago.

The withdrawal is now official with the Israel Football Association, according to the report, and the vacated place goes to Ironi Beit Shemesh, who finished runner-up in the promotion play-off out of Liga Bet South B.
For Beit Shemesh it is a genuinely historic moment: the city has not had a team in Liga Alef since 1989, when Hapoel Beit Shemesh was relegated out of the division after three seasons there.

"We're going up to Liga Alef! Ironi Beit Shemesh is making history and returning to Liga Alef for the first time since 1989!" the club said in a statement carried by ONE. "This is not just the rise of a football team. It is the rise of an entire city."

The circumstances make Beitar Yavne's exit all the more striking. The club, refounded in 2013 after its original incarnation folded in 1997, had climbed from Liga Gimel through Liga Bet before finally reaching Liga Alef South for 2025/26 — a first in its history.

Once there, Beitar Yavne outperformed expectations that had them marked as relegation candidates, instead finishing the season in a position to contest the test games for promotion to Liga Leumit, Israel's second tier.
ONE's report does not give a reason for the club scrapping its Liga Alef registration barely a season after arriving, and no explanation from Beitar Yavne itself has yet been reported.

The immediate effect on the table is straightforward: Ironi Beit Shemesh move up in Beitar Yavne's place, giving Liga Alef South a fresh face for 2026/27 and giving Beit Shemesh's football community a return to a level the city has waited 35 years to see again.

title: Maccabi Haifa's foreign-player logjam leaves new striker Novakovich unregistered
dek: The club has eight overseas players already on the books and must sell or loan one out before Andrija Novakovich can play — and target man Peter Agba is refusing to go quietly.
body: Maccabi Haifa have a striker they cannot put on the pitch. Andrija Novakovich, the American forward of Serbian descent signed from Italy's Reggiana this summer, remains unable to be registered for either the league or the Toto Cup because the club has already filled its quota of eight foreign players — and, per ONE, someone has to make way before he can join the squad list.

It is an awkward problem for a club that moved early and confidently for Novakovich, agreeing a reported two-year deal worth around €300,000 a season and pushing him through medicals not long after the transfer was struck. Since then his own pre-season has been troubled enough on its own terms: he arrived in Israel, caught a significant virus, and has only recently returned to full training, according to Walla! Sport.

Now the registration rule has piled a second delay on top of the first. Maccabi Haifa's eight currently registered foreigners are the Belgian defender Jelle Bataille, Brazilian centre-back Pedrão, Dutch-Surinamese defender Nigel Lonwijk, Brazilian winger Wenderson Tsunami, Ivorian midfielder Cédric Don, Belgian-Nigerian winger Manuel Benson, Brazilian attacking midfielder Bruninho and Nigerian midfielder Peter Agba — a full house that leaves no room for Novakovich until one of them departs.

ONE reports that the club's preferred solution is to move on Peter Agba, who joined from Slovenian champions Olimpija Ljubljana less than a year ago. Agba has drawn interest from clubs in Russia and elsewhere, but according to the report he has turned down proposed loan moves and is in no hurry to leave, even as he registers that the club is pushing hard for a resolution.

Sport5 adds that Agba is understood to be holding out for an attractive permanent transfer rather than a temporary switch abroad, and that Maccabi Haifa would themselves rather sell him outright than send him out on loan and lose him from their long-term plans regardless.

The club is said to want the matter settled within the coming week, with the Ligat Ha'al season opener approaching and every week without Novakovich available representing lost integration time for a player they signed specifically to lead the attack.

Walla! Sport also reports that Maccabi Haifa have, for now, ruled out easing the logjam by cutting Pedrão, suggesting the Brazilian centre-back's place is considered safe even while the broader foreign contingent is under review.

The registration standoff sits alongside a separate contract dispute at the club. ONE reports that talks over a new deal for Israeli player Yarin Levi have grown contentious, with Maccabi Haifa seeking to strip out a clause that would let him leave for a foreign club, even as Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Be'er Sheva are both said to be interested in signing him.
For now, Novakovich trains with a club he still cannot officially represent — a striker signed to solve problems for Maccabi Haifa, currently stuck behind one of his own.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva carry a slim lead into Belgrade, where 50,000 fans could cut both ways
dek: Ahead of tonight's Champions League qualifying return leg at the Marakana, Beersheba-raised journalist Almog Boker says Red Star's massive crowd is as likely to unsettle the hosts as it is to lift them.

verificationSources.label: Tanjug: Red Star lose to Hapoel Be'er Sheva away in UEFA Champions League qualifiers
ESPN match report: Hapoel Be'er 1-0 Red Star (Aug 4, 2026)
Wikipedia: Ran Kojok (Ran Kozuch), Hapoel Be'er Sheva manager

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva head into one of European football's more intimidating amphitheatres on Tuesday night carrying the thinnest of cushions — a single goal — as they try to close out a Champions League third qualifying-round tie against Crvena Zvezda, Red Star Belgrade.

The first leg, played on August 4 at the Haladas Stadium in Szombathely, Hungary, because Beer Sheva's own ground could not host the fixture, produced an improbable 1-0 win. Zahi Ahmed scored the only goal in the 38th minute, pouncing after a mix-up between the Red Star goalkeeper and debutant defender Derrick Luckassen. Beer Sheva then played more than half an hour with ten men after Matan Baltaksa was sent off, and also had a goal by Eliel Peretz ruled out, yet held on.

That result sets up Tuesday's return leg at 21:00 local time at the Rajko Mitić Stadium — universally known as the Marakana — with a place in the Champions League playoff round on the line for the winner.

Discussing the tie on ONE's Sichat HaYom program, journalist Almog Boker, who was born and raised in Beersheba and covers the south for Channel 12, called the task facing Ran Kojok's side "difficult but not impossible," pointing to the coach's accumulated experience navigating European qualifying rounds with the club.

Boker's central point concerned the atmosphere Beer Sheva will walk into: a Marakana crowd of around 50,000 that he framed as a double-edged sword for the hosts rather than a guaranteed weapon. As he put it, that many fans represent "tremendous added strength" for Red Star — but if the home side fails to find a goal early in the second half, the same crowd can just as easily tip into anxiety and pressure on its own team.

On the pitch, Boker flagged goalkeeper Ofir Marciano's composure as central to Beer Sheva's chances of surviving whatever Red Star throw at them, alongside a broader plea for discipline — avoiding the kind of needless bookings and provocations that cost the team a man in the first leg — and for playing through midfield rather than relying on hopeful clearances under pressure.

His verdict was that a draw in Belgrade would be enough to send Beer Sheva through, even while acknowledging the gulf in stature between the sides. Red Star, he said, are "a better team, certainly at home," but that does not rule out an Israeli side that has already shown it can absorb pressure and defend a lead with numbers against it.

A result either way would carry weight well beyond one tie: reaching the Champions League playoff round would be a significant continental scalp for Israeli club football, while elimination would end Beer Sheva's European run at the final qualifying hurdle.

title: Manor Solomon's father: West Ham see him as a significant player, which is what he wanted
dek: Yossi Solomon tells ONE his son chose West Ham over staying at Tottenham because he wanted a real role, not another year as a fringe option, as the Hammers prepare for life in the Championship.

verificationSources.label: West Ham United FC - official announcement
Fabrizio Romano on X - deal terms

body: Manor Solomon left Tottenham Hotspur for West Ham United this month not because London Stadium offered the bigger name, but because it offered him something Spurs would not: a starting shirt. That, at least, is the account given by his father, Yossi Solomon, in an interview with ONE.

"West Ham see him as a significant player, that's what he wanted," Yossi said, describing his son's thinking at 27 as a footballer no longer content to be a squad option. "He arrived at a warm home, a big club."

The move is confirmed and done: West Ham completed the signing for a fee reported by Fabrizio Romano at £5 million fixed plus £2 million in add-ons, with Solomon putting pen to paper on a three-year deal that carries a club option through to June 2030. He will wear the No.10 shirt, primarily as a left winger, though he is comfortable off either flank or through the middle.

It is a peculiar moment for the move, since West Ham are no longer a Premier League club. The Hammers were relegated at the end of last season despite beating Leeds United on the final day, undone when Tottenham themselves avoided defeat against Everton to confirm West Ham's drop after 14 years in the top flight. Solomon now begins life in the Championship, West Ham's first second-tier campaign since 2011-12.

According to Yossi, that context does not worry the family. "We believe they will quickly return to the Premier League," he said, framing the Championship season as a stepping stone rather than a setback.

On why his son left Tottenham, where he had struggled for regular football since joining in 2023, Yossi was matter-of-fact rather than bitter. "He's in good shape, I think he could have stayed," he said, while acknowledging such decisions were never his son's to make. He added that the Spurs manager had been straightforward with Solomon, explaining he was not guaranteed a place in the starting eleven.

The father also reflected on the two stops that preceded Tottenham's exit door. Solomon's loan spell in Spain, at Villarreal, coincided with a hostile atmosphere around his Israeli identity — Jewish community groups in Spain publicly condemned chants directed at him during matches last season. "That wasn't a good decision from the start," Yossi said of the move.

Fiorentina, where Solomon also faced political backlash on arrival in Florence, left a warmer personal impression despite the noise, but Yossi said his son's priority was always elsewhere. "Manor's dream has always been England," he said. "That's the NBA of football."

For Solomon, West Ham now represents the chance to be a first-choice attacker in a league where he has already shown he can produce numbers — his loan year at Leeds in the Championship yielded ten goals and 13 assists in 2024-25, form that helped persuade the Hammers to move for him this summer as their third permanent signing of the window, following Joel Veltman and Keiber Lamadrid.

title: Son of former Hapoel Haifa coach Gal Arel joins Maccabi Haifa's youth ranks
dek: Roy Arel, 11, is leaving four years in Hapoel Haifa's academy to cross Haifa's football divide and join local rivals Maccabi Haifa's Under-12 side for 2026/27, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - Gal Arel appointed Hapoel Haifa coach

body: Roy Arel, the 11-year-old son of former Hapoel Haifa head coach Gal Arel, is swapping the club's red shirt for Maccabi Haifa's green — crossing one of Israeli football's fiercest local divides before he has even reached his teens.

According to ONE, Roy will join Maccabi Haifa's Yeladim Gimel squad, the Under-12 children's category, for the 2026/27 season after four consecutive years in Hapoel Haifa's youth system, running from 2022/23 through the campaign just finished.
He may also turn out for an older Maccabi Haifa youth group when eligible, ONE adds, noting he was given similar dual duty in an older age bracket during his last season with Hapoel Haifa.

The move carries an obvious family subplot. Gal Arel came through Hapoel Haifa's own academy from the age of six and won a youth championship with the club in 2005/06, before a playing career that also took him to Hapoel Beersheba, Hapoel Petah Tikva, Hapoel Akko and spells abroad.

Arel later returned to Hapoel Haifa as an assistant coach and then head coach, taking permanent charge of the first team in June 2025. The tenure ended in January 2026, when he was dismissed after a home defeat to Beitar Ramat Hasharon left the club just a point above the relegation zone. He has since taken over as youth coach at Maccabi Petah Tikva.

Roy will not be the only Maccabi Haifa academy player with divided family loyalties, per ONE — the report describes Ariel Dora, son of Yossi Dora, as another player already established in the green youth ranks despite a background "red at heart."

On its own, Roy Arel's switch is a small piece of business in Israeli youth football's summer churn. But in a city where the Hapoel-Maccabi rivalry runs deep, a coach's son changing colours before he turns 12 is the kind of story that will not go unnoticed on either side of the derby.

title: Sheran Yeini: it would be fun to team up with Eran Zahavi at Maccabi one day
dek: The former Maccabi Tel Aviv captain, now competing on Israel's Dancing with the Stars, says he hasn't ruled out a return to the club — perhaps alongside his old teammate.

verificationSources.label: Israel Hayom — Yeini's Dancing with the Stars debut
Sport1 Maariv — Yeini's 'Ferguson of Maccabi' ambition

body: Sheran Yeini spent more than a decade marshalling Maccabi Tel Aviv's defence and wearing the captain's armband. These days his evenings are booked out by a rehearsal studio instead, but the club is clearly never far from his thoughts.

Speaking to ONE's "Conversation of the Day" during his run on the current season of Israel's Dancing with the Stars, Yeini said learning choreography has, in its own way, been tougher than anything football threw at him. He pointed to the precision the routines demand — the exact angle of a shoulder, the placement of a hand — as a different kind of hard than the physical grind of a match.
Asked whether he could see himself back at Maccabi in some role down the line, Yeini didn't close the door. "I don't rule out being there someday," he told the outlet.

He went further, floating the idea of working alongside Eran Zahavi, the club's former talisman and Israel's record goalscorer, who retired from playing this past January. "It would be fun if Eran and I combined forces at Maccabi someday, to contribute to the place," Yeini said.

It's a pairing with obvious resonance: Yeini as the long-time defensive lynchpin, Zahavi as the club's spearhead, both now several years removed from the pitch and, according to Yeini, both drawn toward business and investment ventures since hanging up their boots.

Yeini retired from professional football in May 2024 at 37, having captained Maccabi through campaigns of varying fortune. "Even with mediocre squads, we achieved accomplishments," he said of those years, a nod to a career that included Israeli league and cup silverware at Bloomfield Stadium.

He still shows up as a fan, telling ONE he catches roughly five Maccabi matches a season now, and joked that supporters have taken to voting for him on the dance show much as they once cheered him on the pitch.

The dancing itself has already produced one emotional moment: partnered with Karin Sorotzinski, Yeini opened the season by dancing to a song originally performed by his late father, the singer and actor Lior Yeini, who died in 2021 — a routine that scored 29 points on debut night, according to Israel Hayom's coverage of the premiere.

It isn't the first time Yeini has spoken publicly about a future in Maccabi's dugout rather than just the stands. In a separate interview with Sport1, he said his dream was to become "the Ferguson of Maccabi Tel Aviv," staying in charge for 25 to 27 years — the kind of long-term project he now suggests Zahavi might one day share with him.

title: Panathinaikos owner says he made a 'serious' offer for Nikola Jokic
dek: Dimitris Giannakopoulos claims he tried to buy out the Nuggets superstar's contract this year and was rebuffed — but insists he will sign him to the Greek club next summer.
body: Panathinaikos owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos has confirmed one of European basketball's most eyebrow-raising rumours: that he tried, this year, to sign Nikola Jokic away from the Denver Nuggets.

Appearing on the Euro Insiders podcast, Giannakopoulos said he submitted what he called "a very serious offer" aimed at buying out the final year of Jokic's contract, sending it to both the three-time NBA MVP and the Nuggets organisation.

"I sent a very serious offer this season, both to the player and to his club, and received an immediate rejection," Giannakopoulos said, according to the podcast and Greek outlets including Ta Nea and SDNA who covered the same interview.

The Panathinaikos owner painted the response as dismissive in the extreme, suggesting the Nuggets barely entertained the idea given Jokic's commitments in the United States. ESPN and Basketnews.com, citing the same podcast appearance, reported that Giannakopoulos described the reply to his approach on buying out the contract as essentially "Who? Greece? Where? Goodbye."

Jokic is tied to Denver for two more seasons worth a combined $121.8 million, but the second of those is a player option — meaning the Serbian centre could opt out and enter unrestricted free agency next summer if he chooses.

That is the opening Giannakopoulos is banking on. "He remains a dream of mine, whom I haven't signed yet, but I will sign next year," he said, vowing to renew his pursuit once Jokic's contract situation opens up.

It is not the first time the Panathinaikos owner has spoken boldly about landing NBA-calibre talent for the Greek champions, and he used the same podcast appearance to heap praise on retired Serbian playmaker Milos Teodosic, calling him "the smartest person ever to play basketball" behind only club legend Dimitris Diamantidis.

Whether an actual pursuit of Jokic is realistic remains doubtful — the reigning MVP-calibre force is widely expected to sign the richest contract in NBA history to stay with Denver — but the episode underlines the ambition Giannakopoulos has attached to Panathinaikos since taking over the club from his father and uncle.

title: Ronald Araújo completes loan move from Barcelona to Liverpool
dek: The Uruguayan defender and Barcelona captain joins on a season-long loan with a €55m buy option, closing out a turbulent year that included a mental-health break spent partly in Israel.
body: Ronald Araújo has completed his move away from Camp Nou, with Liverpool confirming a season-long loan for the Barcelona captain that includes a non-mandatory buy option worth roughly €55 million (£47.1m) next summer, ONE reports.

No loan fee changes hands under the terms of the deal. Liverpool will cover Araújo's wages for the campaign, though the 27-year-old has taken a pay cut on his Barcelona terms to push the move through. He will wear the No. 33 shirt at Anfield.

The Uruguayan arrives to fill the gap left by Ibrahima Konaté, who departed Liverpool for Real Madrid earlier this summer, leaving Andoni Iraola's side short of proven central-defensive cover. Iraola took over at Anfield in June after Liverpool moved on from Arne Slot.

Araújo's departure from Barcelona ends an eight-year association that began when he arrived from Uruguayan side Boston River in 2018. He made more than 200 appearances for the club, won three La Liga titles, two Copa del Rey trophies and three Spanish Super Cups, and was handed the captain's armband earlier this year.

The exit had been coming. Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick made little secret of his reservations about Araújo's fit in his system, remarking pointedly that the defender's style of play was not what he preferred, and increasingly turned to alternatives such as Pau Cubarsí, Andreas Christensen and Gerard Martín at centre-back.

Araújo, for his part, struck an upbeat tone on the move. "I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career," he said in comments carried by Liverpool's official website. "As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly."

The transfer also closes a difficult chapter for the defender away from the pitch. After a high-profile red card against Chelsea in the Champions League last season triggered a wave of criticism and abuse on social media, Araújo took an extended mental-health leave from Barcelona, with Ynet and other outlets reporting he travelled to Israel for what was described as a spiritual recovery journey before returning to full training.
He returns to first-team football with a fresh start on Merseyside, joining a Liverpool defence being reshaped under Iraola following Konaté's exit and a summer of turnover at the club.

title: Harry Kane closing in on new Bayern Munich contract through 2029
dek: The Times reports the England captain is set to extend his stay in Munich by two years, with talks in advanced stages and a signing possible within days.
body: Harry Kane is closing in on a new contract at Bayern Munich that would keep the England captain in Bavaria until 2029, according to a report in The Times relayed by the Israeli outlet ONE.

Kane's current deal runs until the summer of 2027, but Bayern are pushing to extend it by two further years, taking him through to age 36 and ending any lingering speculation over his long-term future at the club.

ONE reports that negotiations are already in an advanced stage, with a signing possible as early as next week once terms are finalised — a timeline echoed by Walla Sport and Sport1, which both describe the club as having confirmed talks are underway.

Financially, little is expected to change at the core of the deal. Kane, already Bayern's top earner on close to €25 million gross a year, is not thought to be seeking a significant base salary rise, though his bonus structure is reportedly being upgraded to reflect personal and team achievements.

The push to tie him down comes off the back of an extraordinary campaign. Kane claimed the Bundesliga's Torjägerkanone for a third consecutive season with 36 league goals in 2025-26 and was crowned Europe's top scorer with the Golden Shoe, finishing the season with 73 goals and eight assists in 65 matches for club and country.

According to the report, Kane's own priorities have shifted since arriving in Munich in 2023. Rather than eyeing a return to the Premier League to chase Alan Shearer's all-time scoring record, he is said to be more focused on winning further trophies with Bayern, where he and his family have settled comfortably.

Talks are being led on Bayern's side by sporting director Max Eberl and chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen, with Kane's father, Pat, and brother, Charlie, representing his interests at the table, the report adds.

The extension talk also serves to quiet recent transfer chatter that had linked Kane with a move to Barcelona or a sentimental return to Tottenham Hotspur — rumours Bayern appear keen to put to bed with a firm, long-term commitment.

Kane has yet to win a major trophy with Bayern despite his individual haul, and a new deal through 2029 would signal the club's belief that silverware, not just goals, remains within reach before his contract runs out.

title: Rehovot municipality confirms new club, Ironi Rehovot, bound for Liga Alef
dek: Mayor Matan Diel unveils a municipally funded football project built around the city's new stadium, while Hapoel Marmorek and Maccabi Sha'arayim stay on in Liga Gimel.

verificationSources.label: ONE — עיריית רחובות הודיעה רשמית על המועדון החדש

body: After nearly two years of behind-the-scenes talks, Rehovot's municipality made it official on Monday: the city will field a new football club, Ironi Rehovot, with a senior side aimed at Liga Alef from next season, pending approval from the Israel Football Association.

Mayor Matan Diel, who led the negotiations between the municipality, its municipal company and local football stakeholders, framed the move as a turning point for a city that has never quite matched its size with its footballing profile. "Rehovot is a city that knows how to dream big, but also understands that fulfilling dreams requires cooperation," Diel said, calling it the laying of "the foundation stone for a new era in Rehovot football."

Ironi Rehovot will run senior and youth divisions and be operated by a private nonprofit organisation rather than directly by the municipality, a structure increasingly common among Israeli cities looking to consolidate scattered local football under one professional banner.

The city's two existing senior clubs, Hapoel Marmorek and Maccabi Sha'arayim, will not be absorbed into the new project. Both will continue playing next season in Liga Gimel, the fourth tier, as part of a framework the municipality says it agreed with both clubs, with continued municipal support and oversight rather than a direct role in the new flagship side.

The idea has been gestating since at least late 2024, when reports first surfaced of municipal officials courting a private investor to bankroll a high-budget team capable of climbing quickly through the divisions. Early versions of the plan also envisioned Rehovot's new stadium, built for roughly 6,000 spectators, as the new club's long-term home.

For Marmorek and Sha'arayim, two clubs that have competed as local rivals in the lower leagues for decades, Monday's announcement is a clear signal that the municipality's ambitions now lie with a fresh institution rather than either of the incumbents.

The next formal step is sign-off from the Israel Football Association on Ironi Rehovot's status and its entry point into Liga Alef, a process the municipality has not yet completed but expects to finalise before the new season begins.

title: William Agada returns to Hapoel Haifa for a second spell
dek: The Nigerian forward, who scored six goals on loan at the club in 2020/21, is back in Israel after a half-season at Real Zaragoza, on a reported annual salary of €180,000.

body: Hapoel Haifa have gone back to a familiar face to freshen up their attack, agreeing terms with Nigerian forward William Agada on a second spell at the club, ONE reported on Monday.
The 26-year-old put pen to paper on a deal that, according to ONE's report, will pay him around €180,000 a year — a return that reunites him with a club he already knows well from the inside.
Agada's first taste of Sammy Ofer Stadium came in the 2020/21 season, when he arrived on loan and finished among the team's top scorers with six league goals in 25 appearances.

He leaves for Haifa this time from Real Zaragoza, where he spent only half a season after a January move to the Spanish second division. Agada made just three appearances for the LaLiga 2 club without finding the net, having become only the third Nigerian to represent Zaragoza in the club's history, following former Super Eagles forward Ikechukwu Uche.

That short Spanish chapter followed three and a half years in MLS. Agada was traded from Sporting Kansas City to Real Salt Lake in April 2025 after scoring 21 goals in 64 appearances for Kansas City, then added a further two goals in 14 games for Real Salt Lake — a combined tally ONE puts at 23 MLS league goals across the two clubs.

Before any of that, Agada made his name in Israeli football. He began at Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem before moving on to Hapoel Jerusalem, where he was the club's top scorer in the 2021/22 season. Between his spells in the capital and his loan year in Haifa, ONE credits him with more than 60 goals in senior Israeli football — the body of work that persuaded the club to bring him back.

Hapoel Haifa owner Yoav Katz welcomed the move, telling ONE: "We are pleased to bring back a player we know well. William is a speedy, quality striker with experience," adding that he expects the forward to make an impact again in Haifa colours.
The deal was brokered by Agada's agent, Shachar Greenberg, per the report.

For Hapoel Haifa, the return gives head coach a proven goal-scoring option with Israeli top-flight pedigree as preparations continue for the new Israeli Premier League season — a low-risk reunion with a player whose record at the club is already on file.

title: Southampton and West Ham drawn together, setting up first Israeli derby in English football
dek: Daniel Peretz and Manor Solomon will face off in the Carabao Cup this month, with Bristol City's Lisav Eissat, a product of Maccabi Haifa's academy, adding a third Israeli-linked name to a crowded Championship.

body: For the first time, two players who have worn the Israel national team shirt will line up against each other in English football this month, after Monday's Carabao Cup second-round draw paired Southampton with West Ham United — sending goalkeeper Daniel Peretz into direct opposition with new Hammers winger Manor Solomon.

The tie is scheduled for the week beginning August 24, with the exact date and kick-off time still to be confirmed once the broadcast schedule is finalised. Both clubs are playing Championship football this season, which is what has brought Peretz and Solomon into the same competitive orbit for the first time.

Peretz completed a permanent move to Southampton from Bayern Munich this summer on a four-year contract, in a deal reported at around €7 million (£6.05m), after impressing during a loan spell at St Mary's that included a stunning FA Cup quarter-final upset of Arsenal. The Tel Aviv-born goalkeeper, who joined Bayern in 2023 as the club's first Israeli player, has become one of the more recognisable Israeli exports in England.

Solomon's arrival at West Ham was only confirmed this weekend, with the winger joining from Tottenham Hotspur in a deal reported at £7m — £5m up front plus up to £2m in add-ons — on a contract running to 2029, with the option of a further year. It is the third English club of his career, following spells at Fulham and Spurs since leaving Shakhtar Donetsk.

West Ham reached the League Cup second round by beating Portsmouth 3-1, with Tati Castellanos scoring twice either side of a Jarrod Bowen goal, ONE reports. That result, and Monday's draw, means Solomon could make his first appearance for the Hammers directly against a fellow Israel international.

A third name adds further intrigue to the Championship this season. Bristol City signed centre-back Lisav Eissat from Maccabi Haifa on a four-year deal this summer, in a transfer reported at around €2.5m. Eissat, 21, came through Maccabi Haifa's academy and represented Israel at youth level, but he now plays his senior international football for Romania, for whom he has four caps.

Beyond the League Cup tie, ONE reports that Southampton and West Ham are also due to meet twice in the Championship itself, on October 24 and December 19, while Bristol City's fixtures against both clubs are scheduled across September, December, January and February — dates that were not independently verified beyond ONE's reporting.

Taken together, it means three players with direct ties to Israeli football — one current Israel international goalkeeper, one current Israel international winger, and one Maccabi Haifa academy product now capped by Romania — will crisscross England's second tier repeatedly over the coming season, a coincidence of relegation and transfer business that Israeli football fans are unlikely to have seen before.

The League Cup meeting will be the first and most direct test: Peretz between the posts for Southampton, Solomon potentially available in a new West Ham shirt, and an occasion that ONE frames as the first competitive fixture in English football history to pit two Israel national team representatives directly against one another.

title: Mourinho decides to keep Endrick at Real Madrid despite Roma and Aston Villa loan interest
dek: The head coach has convinced Florentino Pérez that the Brazilian forward, fresh off a productive loan spell at Lyon, is worth persisting with this season, ONE reports.
body: José Mourinho has told Real Madrid's board to keep Endrick rather than send him out on loan, rejecting interest from Roma and Aston Villa as the Brazilian forward arrives at pre-season with a genuine chance to establish himself under the club's new coach, ONE reports.

Both Roma and Aston Villa had approached Madrid about a season-long loan for the 20-year-old before the transfer window closes, according to the report, with the Premier League club understood to have pushed hardest for a deal. Mourinho's intervention has, for now, closed that door.
Club president Florentino Pérez has fully backed the decision, ONE says, having held a soft spot for Endrick since Madrid moved for him as a Palmeiras teenager three years ago.

The financial numbers explain some of that attachment. Madrid agreed a €35 million fixed fee plus up to €25 million in add-ons for Endrick; factoring in agent fees, salary and bonuses paid since, ONE puts the club's total outlay at more than €80 million.

Faith in the forward has been rebuilt by his form on loan at Lyon last season, where he scored eight goals and set up five more in 21 appearances, according to ONE — a run that helped earn him a place in Brazil's squad at this year's World Cup.

Mourinho reportedly sees Endrick as a tactically flexible option who can play as a conventional centre-forward or drift wide right and cut inside, the role in which he first made his name at Palmeiras.
That versatility does not guarantee minutes. Endrick will still have to compete on merit with the rest of Madrid's forward line for a regular starting place this season, ONE notes.
The door has not been shut completely — ONE reports Endrick has not ruled out revisiting a loan move in January if regular first-team football fails to materialise once the season is under way.

It amounts to Mourinho's first significant call on Endrick's future since taking charge at the Bernabéu, and a signal that the Portuguese wants to judge the Brazilian in training and matches before deciding whether he has a role to play in Madrid's season.

title: Maccabi Haifa encouraged by approach, in no rush with new signings
dek: After a 1-0 win over Bnei Sakhnin closed out their Toto Cup group, the Haifa hierarchy tells ONE the team is taking shape even if the football is still below their standards, with summer arrivals still settling in and decisions looming on Yarin Levi and Dixon Muhammad.

verificationSources.label: ONE - שביעות רצון במכבי חיפה מהגישה, סבלנות עם הרכש

body: Maccabi Haifa's leadership came away from Doha Stadium on Saturday satisfied with what they saw, even if the result itself carried little weight — the club had already been eliminated from the Toto Cup semi-final race before kickoff. According to ONE, sources inside the club say they "saw a team again" out on the pitch, a phrase management is using carefully rather than triumphantly.

The 1-0 win over Bnei Sakhnin was settled in the 54th minute: Bruninho slid a defence-splitting pass through for Cédric Don, whose effort came back off the crossbar, leaving Silva Kani to arrive first and turn the rebound into an empty net. It was Haifa's second straight group-stage win and left them third in Group A on six points from four matches.

Encouraging as the shape looked, ONE reports the club is not getting carried away — officials acknowledge the football on display remains some distance from the standard they expect of themselves once the Ligat Ha'al season is under way.

That caution is tied directly to personnel. Haifa have brought in a wave of new faces this year, Kani among them after his summer move from Beitar Jerusalem, and the club's read is that the squad needs time before it clicks. Newcomers, as one source put it to ONE, are currently going through "the pressure cooker" of adapting to a new dressing room, system and level of expectation all at once.

Patience runs both ways at Haifa this preseason. The club is also being deliberate with its academy products rather than rushing them into the side. Navot Ratner, who played a significant role in the first team last season, has been left out of the matchday squad in recent outings — not, according to the club's messaging, as a demotion but as part of a philosophy that treats promising youngsters as squad options rather than automatic starters, easing them in without loading on pressure too soon.

Elsewhere in the squad, Dixon Muhammad's near-term future looks set to be away from Sammy Ofer Stadium. The 18-year-old, brother of Haifa forward Ali Muhammad, is expected to move on loan to Hapoel Kfar Saba, with the parent club retaining an option to recall him in January. ONE reports the call owes more to a crowded roster of foreign players than to any lack of faith — staff reportedly rate him as a genuinely talented prospect.

The more pressing item on the club's desk is Yarin Levi. ONE says no formal offers for the midfielder have landed yet, but Haifa's leadership wants the speculation around him resolved sooner rather than later, wary of a saga dragging into the season. The club's read of its own supporters is that most are firmly behind Levi staying — and that the fairest answer to the noise will come from what he produces on the pitch.

None of it changes the bigger picture: with the Ligat Ha'al opener approaching, Haifa's hierarchy is choosing to read Saturday's dead-rubber win as a signal that the pieces are beginning to fit, while bracing supporters for a settling-in period before the new-look squad shows its true level.

title: Morant has arrived in Portland, but this should stay Avdija's team, US analysts argue
dek: As Ja Morant joins the Trail Blazers roster following his trade from Memphis, American commentators say Deni Avdija's breakout All-Star season means Portland's identity should still run through him.
body: The debate over who really runs the Portland Trail Blazers has flared up again since Ja Morant's arrival this summer, and ONE's roundup of American commentary lands firmly on one side: this is still Deni Avdija's team, and it should stay that way until Morant proves otherwise on the floor.

Portland acquired the two-time All-Star guard from the Memphis Grizzlies in a trade that sent Jerami Grant and Kris Murray back to Memphis, ending a turbulent chapter of Morant's career and handing the Blazers a genuine offensive weapon when healthy.

But as ONE notes, the framing among Portland-focused analysts, including a widely cited piece from Rip City Project, is that the trade only works if the Blazers remember whose team this has become. "This is still Avdija's world and Morant is just living in it," the outlet's analysis argued.

The case for Avdija is not sentimental. The Israeli forward turned in a breakout season that culminated in his first NBA All-Star selection, becoming the first Trail Blazer picked since Damian Lillard in 2023 and the first Israeli ever named to the All-Star Game.

He averaged 25.5 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.7 assists per game this past season, ranking among just three players in the league to hit that combined statistical mark, while starting every game he played and anchoring Portland's offense as a point-forward.

That role, commentators warn, is exactly what could be squeezed if the Blazers lean too heavily on Morant as a traditional lead guard. Rip City Project's analysis put it bluntly: limiting Avdija to a standard wing rather than a primary ball-handler "is to take away part of what makes him a special talent."

Portland's season ended with a five-game playoff exit to the San Antonio Spurs, and the front office's answer was to add star power around Avdija rather than replace him at the top of the rotation. The roster now features Morant alongside Avdija, Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday, a genuinely loaded backcourt-and-wing mix by recent Blazers standards.

The comparison American analysts keep reaching for is Jalen Brunson's Knicks: a team built patiently around a home-grown centerpiece who earned his standing through availability and winning basketball, not name recognition, and who shouldn't be nudged aside the moment a bigger name walks through the door.

For Avdija, the coming season now carries a different kind of pressure than the one that made him an All-Star. He built Portland's culture during a stretch when the roster around him was thin; the test now is whether that culture survives the arrival of a player with Morant's talent, and his baggage.

How Blazers coaching staff choose to split ball-handling duties between Morant and Avdija will be one of the more closely watched subplots of the NBA offseason, and the answer will say plenty about how Portland actually views its two stars heading into the new campaign.
