If Maccabi Tel Aviv lose to CSKA Sofia, they would drop into a Conference League playoff tie against the winner of Lugano (Switzerland) and Runavik (Faroe Islands).

Beitar Jerusalem play FK Austria Wien in Conference League qualifying on August 6; the winner would face Sp. Braga in the playoff round if Braga also beat Dinamo Minsk, with Braga hosting the first leg on August 20.

Hapoel Tel Aviv face GKS Katowice in Conference League qualifying on August 6 and 12; the winner would face 2024 Europa League champions Atalanta in the playoff round, first leg in Bergamo on August 20.
Braga's coach is Carlos Carvalhal, a former Manchester City assistant, and their squad includes captain Ricardo Horta and 39-year-old veteran Joao Moutinho.

title: Siraj Nassar, once a Hapoel Beer Sheva mainstay, signs for Maccabi Bnei Eilat
dek: The 35-year-old forward, who made more than 160 appearances for the Negev club last decade, joins Eilat's ambitious rebuild in League B
body: Siraj Nassar has agreed to sign for Maccabi Bnei Eilat ahead of the 2026/27 League B (Liga Bet) season, ONE reports, taking the veteran forward's well-travelled career into the desert city as part of the club's ambitious rebuild.

Nassar, 35, is best remembered in the Negev for a very different postcode. He spent six seasons at Hapoel Beer Sheva between 2009 and 2015, racking up more than 160 appearances and over 20 goals for the club during a period that helped establish him as one of Israeli football's most durable journeymen.

Since leaving Beer Sheva he has turned out for Hapoel Tel Aviv, Bnei Sakhnin and Hapoel Acre, before settling into a long run as a reliable presence in the lower divisions from 2018 onward — most notably a productive spell at Shimshon Kafr Qasim.

Last season he was on the books of Hapoel Ironi Karmiel in Liga Alef (National League) North, making 24 appearances and scoring twice before the campaign was cut short by the security situation, according to ONE's report.

His move to Bnei Eilat now drops him back down to League B, but the club insists that is only the starting point. Under new ownership, Bnei Eilat are running a project explicitly built, in their own words as relayed by ONE, around "reaching the National League within three years at full strength." Sport5 has separately reported on an ambitious ownership push at the club aimed at rebuilding it from the ground up with a serious budget and recognisable names.

Nassar is not the only experienced arrival: ONE lists fellow veterans Gil Yitzhak and Gidi Kaniuk as part of the same recruitment drive, with Kobi Refuah taking charge as head coach of the new-look squad.

For a player who once patrolled the top flight in front of tens of thousands at Turner Stadium, it is a modest return in football terms — but for Bnei Eilat's project, landing a forward with his pedigree and goal record is exactly the kind of statement signing the ownership is chasing.

title: Hapoel Petah Tikva weigh alternatives and won't wait much longer for Arroyo
dek: Coach Omer Peretz wants the Bolivian defender on loan from Shakhtar Donetsk, but a collapsed side deal in Ukraine has left Petah Tikva only a few more days of patience before they turn elsewhere.

verificationSources.label: ONE (background, June report on Arroyo talks)

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva are already sketching a plan B for their central defence, ONE reports, with the pursuit of Shakhtar Donetsk's Diego Arroyo stuck in limbo and the club unwilling to keep the position open indefinitely.

Head coach Omer Peretz is said to strongly want the young Bolivian international, but according to the report Petah Tikva will give the deal only a few more days before actively pursuing other candidates for the role.

The holdup, per ONE, sits in Ukraine rather than Israel. Shakhtar Donetsk had been closing in on a defender from Genoa who would have allowed them to let Arroyo leave on loan, but those talks collapsed, leaving Shakhtar needing to find a fresh replacement before they sanction his move.

Arroyo, a 21-year-old defender who has represented Bolivia at senior level, joined Shakhtar in one of the more notable transfers involving a Bolivian player in recent years. Petah Tikva have been eyeing him as a loan reinforcement for the coming season.

The uncertainty comes at an awkward moment for the club, who lost their most recent preseason outing to Hapoel Ramat Gan and now turn to a home fixture against Maccabi Netanya on Wednesday evening, kicking off at 19:45.

There was more encouraging news out of the treatment room, with Gabon international Alex Musonda back in running work after his injury lay-off. The defender, on loan from Cypriot champions Aris Limassol, is not expected to be rushed back but is targeting a return in time for the start of the league season.

For now, Petah Tikva's business is defined by patience rather than action: Peretz has his preferred target, but with Shakhtar's own reshuffle unresolved, the club's ultimatum on Arroyo is the clearest sign yet that they are not prepared to wait indefinitely to strengthen the back line.

title: Beer Sheva prepare for Red Star Belgrade test as Solomon's Tottenham exit edges closer
dek: Hapoel Beer Sheva chase a first-ever Champions League league phase as they meet Red Star Belgrade in the third qualifying round, while Manor Solomon's camp pushes for a permanent move away from Tottenham.

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva head into the biggest European fixture of their season on Tuesday, hosting Red Star Belgrade in the third qualifying round of the Champions League, with a place in the playoff round — and a shot at the competition's league phase for the first time in the club's history — on the line.

The southern club arrive on the back of a 2-0 aggregate win over Víkingur Reykjavík, a result that has already guaranteed Beer Sheva a minimum of Conference League group-stage football this season regardless of what happens against the Serbian giants.
The first leg kicks off Tuesday at 20:30 local time, played on what is designated as Beer Sheva's home ground in Hungary. The return leg follows a week later in Belgrade, on August 11 at 21:00.

The stakes go beyond simply advancing: whichever side goes through will face the winner of Aarhus of Denmark and Azerbaijan's Sabah in the playoff round, and will do so with seeded status inherited from Red Star's considerably higher European coefficient — a meaningful structural edge in the draw.

Red Star travel with a squad that includes Mohamed Abu Fani, familiar to Israeli fans from his time at Maccabi Haifa, and are led by 37-year-old Austrian forward Marco Arnautovic, his country's all-time leading scorer. Israeli pundit Gai Tzarfati said this week he believes "Hapoel Beer Sheva can advance past Red Star," a view echoed across the Israeli sports press ahead of kickoff.

While Beer Sheva's squad focuses on Belgrade, attention in England remains fixed on Manor Solomon, whose push to leave Tottenham Hotspur this summer has intensified. Head coach Roberto De Zerbi has told the Israeli winger he is not part of his plans for the season, despite Solomon featuring in Spurs' pre-season fixtures.

Solomon's agent, Ronen Katzav, has been unusually blunt in public. "The goal will be a permanent transfer, not a loan," Katzav said, adding that "statistically speaking, the last week of the window is the busiest" — a signal that a deal may not be resolved quickly.

Katzav went further on his client's standing at Tottenham: "He wants to be dominant and make an impact, and that probably won't happen at Tottenham. It doesn't seem like the right place for him, and they've given up on him too easily along the way."

West Ham United have emerged as the club most actively engaged, with reports in England indicating the two sides are in talks over a permanent deal and that clarity on whether it can progress could come within 48 to 72 hours. Other reporting suggests the move could just as easily slide until closer to the September 1 deadline, with Solomon's camp keen to weigh all options first.

ONE's live "Chat of the Day" broadcast tied the two stories together on Tuesday, running both the Beer Sheva build-up and the latest on Solomon's situation alongside brief speculation about judoka-turned-federation-official Oren Smadja possibly moving into politics — chatter the program flagged without further detail.

For Beer Sheva, Tuesday's opening leg represents the most concrete of the week's storylines: a result on the pitch in Hungary that will shape their European campaign, even as the Solomon transfer saga in England continues to play out in agents' statements and takeover talks rather than a signed contract.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem sign Serbian center Dušan Miletić on one-year deal
dek: The 28-year-old, fresh off a Romanian title and a Eurocup quarter-final run with Cluj-Napoca, joins new coach Saša Obradović's reshaped roster after a brief stop in Lebanon.

verificationSources.label: ONE - דושאן מילטיץ' חתם בהפועל ירושלים

body: Hapoel Jerusalem have added another body to their rebuilt frontcourt, agreeing a one-year contract with a club option for a second season with Serbian center Dušan Miletić, ONE reported.

Miletić, 28 and 2.14 meters tall, arrives in Jerusalem on the back of arguably the best season of his career. Playing for Romanian club U-BT Cluj-Napoca in 2025/26, he helped the side win the domestic championship and reach the Eurocup quarterfinals, a run that put him firmly on the radar of clubs across Europe.

His numbers back up the profile Hapoel were chasing. Across Eurocup play this past season, Miletić averaged 12.6 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks per game, Ynet reported, figures that speak to a mobile, well-rounded big man rather than a purely paint-bound center.

The move to Israel did not come directly from Romania. Miletić spent roughly a month with Lebanese club Al Riyadi Beirut after leaving Cluj-Napoca, before talks with Hapoel Jerusalem advanced and led to this week's signing, according to ONE.

He joins a Jerusalem side being reshaped by new head coach Saša Obradović, the veteran Serbian trainer who took over the bench in June after leaving Red Star Belgrade, replacing Yonatan Alon. "We are happy to add Dušan to Hapoel's family," Obradović said, according to ONE. "He is an experienced player with high basketball intelligence and a competitive approach. Beyond his presence in the paint, he is an excellent rebounder, very versatile, and brings toughness, physicality and outside shooting."

Miletić struck a similar note. "I am very happy to join Hapoel Jerusalem," he said. "I have played against Hapoel before, so I know what a great club this is. I am excited to wear the red jersey and fight for the team."

The signing continues a busy off-season in the capital, where Jerusalem have also brought in NBA guard Shake Milton, per ONE, as Obradović assembles a squad meant to compete on multiple fronts domestically and in the Eurocup.
Financial terms of the Miletić deal were not disclosed.

title: Former Beersheba boss Elisha Levi: 'Nobody gives Beersheba a chance, but I think it's 50-50'
dek: Ahead of tonight's Champions League qualifier in Belgrade, the coach who once dragged Beersheba off the bottom of the table says their balance and organisation make them a real match for Red Star.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — playoff opponent would be Aarhus or Sabah

body: Nobody outside Beer Sheva expects much from Hapoel Beersheba tonight in Belgrade, but Elisha Levi — the coach who once dragged the club out of the relegation zone and up the Ligat Ha'al table — isn't buying the pessimism.

"No one gives Beersheba a chance, but in my opinion it's 50-50," Levi said in an appearance on the show Sicha HaYom, previewing the Champions League third qualifying round first leg against Red Star Belgrade. "With all due respect to the Star, Beersheba isn't a less good or less organised team."

The match kicks off at 20:30 Israel time on Tuesday at the Rajko Mitić Stadium, with Beersheba arriving in Serbia off the back of a 2-0 aggregate win over Iceland's Vikingur Reykjavik in the second qualifying round.

Red Star are the heavier favourites for good reason: the Serbian champions steamrolled Larne of Northern Ireland 9-0 on aggregate in the previous round, including a 5-0 away win, and arrive with a squad built for a genuine Champions League run.

Levi's case rests on structure rather than star power. He argued Beersheba's shape and midfield balance can neutralise a technically stronger opponent, pointing to the platform manager Ran Kozhuk has built since guiding the club to the Israeli championship last season.

It is a squad, though, playing its first European fixture without Kings Kangwa. The Zambian forward, who set up nine goals in 33 league games during Beersheba's title-winning campaign, was sold to Panathinaikos last month for a fixed fee reported at roughly €3.8 million, with add-ons that could push the total closer to €4.5 million.

Filling that creative gap falls in part to Eliel Peretz and Hamudi Kana'an, both floated by Levi as options to rotate into the role Kangwa vacated, alongside the continued presence of veteran Miguel Vitor anchoring the midfield.
Pressed for a scoreline, Levi hedged rather than gambled: "I think it's even, in my opinion a draw — 0-0 or 1-1, I'm obviously guessing."

The stakes stretch beyond bragging rights. Should Beersheba spring the upset over the two legs, Ynet has reported they would be seeded into the playoff round against either Aarhus of Denmark or Sabah of Azerbaijan — one more step from the group-stage riches Israeli clubs have chased for years.

title: Zasno, Saief and Benson return to Maccabi Haifa squad, but Glazer fitness doubt clouds Toto Cup night
dek: Three key men are back in full training ahead of Tuesday's Toto Cup meeting with Ironi Dorot Tiberias, but goalkeeper Omri Glazer left Monday's session early after reporting sensitivity in a previously troublesome area.
body: Maccabi Haifa have three key men back in the fold as they build toward the new season, but the mood around Tuesday night's Toto Cup group game against Ironi Dorot Tiberias was tempered by a fresh scare over goalkeeper Omri Glazer, ONE reported.

Right-back Zohar Zasno, winger Kenny Saief and Belgian forward Manuel Benson have all returned to the matchday squad after extended spells out, giving coach Yaniv Katan a deeper pool of options as Haifa look for their first competitive win of preseason.

The good news was offset by concern over Glazer. The goalkeeper reported sensitivity in the area of a previous problem during Monday's training session and left early, with his participation in the 20:00 kickoff against Tiberias left undecided pending assessments throughout the day, ONE said.

It is the latest twist in a difficult preseason for Glazer, who has been managing a knee issue since the early stages of Haifa's summer preparations, according to Sport5's coverage of his fitness tests.
Glen Alwin, who deputized in goal when Glazer was previously sidelined, is expected to start again on Tuesday if the club's number one is withheld as a precaution.

Haifa are still without several other regulars. Brazilian defender Wanderson Soares, known as "Tsunami," remains out after a concussion sustained in a preseason match, winger Ali Mohamed is nearing a return of his own, and forward Andrija Novakovich continues to be held back by fitness issues.

Tuesday's fixture is part of the Toto Cup group stage, the traditional pre-season tournament Israeli top-flight clubs use to sharpen up before the Ligat Ha'al campaign proper begins on the weekend of August 22.

body: Israel's under-16 boys' national team, known as the cadets, opens its European Championship campaign on Friday in Oradea, Romania, taking on Georgia in the opening round of Group C at the FIBA U16 EuroBasket Division A, ONE reported.

The group draw has not been kind to Guy Kaplan's squad. After Georgia on Friday, Israel faces Greece on Saturday and then Spain on Sunday — three sides with strong youth basketball pedigrees, all inside the space of three days.

Division A is the top tier of European men's youth basketball, and this year's tournament, running from August 7 to 15 in Oradea, doubles as Romania hosting one of three FIBA youth European championships this summer.

Israel arrives having just wrapped a preparation tournament in Latvia, where the results were mixed: two games against the Latvian hosts split one win and one loss, a defeat to Georgia — the very team Israel opens against on Friday — and a victory over Ukraine.

Kaplan named a 12-man squad for Oradea: Yanai Lachmanowitz, Rotem Ben David, Omer Tzvi, Uri Frischman, Ido Ziv, Nitzan Klein, Tomer Katzir, Omer Solomon, Itay Kadam, Maor Sala, Liam Danieli and Eilai Saroya.

He is joined on the bench by assistant coaches Neta Kromer and Yaniv Rubins, with Safi Tzook managing the delegation on court, Bar Gil as physiotherapist, Kobi Pliva handling strength and conditioning, and Alon Ben Zaken heading the wider delegation.

A strong showing in Group C would set up a favourable path through the knockout rounds and matters for more than pride — placement at Division A level feeds directly into the pipeline that Israeli basketball leans on to develop future senior internationals.

title: Dinamo Bucharest reject Craiova's €700,000 bid for Israeli defender Nikita Stoinov
dek: Universitatea Craiova's opening offer for the 20-year-old centre-back fell well short of Dinamo's asking price, ONE reports, though the Romanian champions are not giving up on their pursuit.
body: Universitatea Craiova, the reigning champions of Romanian football, went in for Dinamo Bucharest's Israeli centre-back Nikita Stoinov this week — and were sent away with a firm no. ONE reports that Dinamo rejected the offer within days of it landing, unwilling to entertain a fee anywhere near what Craiova were prepared to pay.

According to the report, Craiova's opening bid was €700,000. Dinamo's response, relayed by Romanian outlets Antena Sport and Digisport, was blunt: they will not sell for less than €3 million, a valuation both sites describe as strikingly high by Liga I standards.

The gap between the two numbers tells its own story. Dinamo have made clear internally that Stoinov is not a player they are looking to move on quickly, whatever interest he attracts from elsewhere in the league.

Stoinov, 20, arrived in Bucharest last summer from Maccabi Netanya, the club that produced him through its youth system. Romanian reports at the time put the fee at somewhere between €400,000 and €450,000, making him one of Dinamo's most expensive signings of that window.

He has settled quickly. Across his time at the club he has made 46 appearances and scored once, and he has started all three of Dinamo's league matches so far this season, an ever-present at the heart of the defence.

Craiova's interest is not casual. Head coach Filipe Coelho has identified the Israeli as a target to strengthen a defensive line he wants rebuilt, and ONE reports that talks between the clubs took place as recently as last week before the formal offer was tabled and knocked back.

The Romanian champions are expected to return to the table, according to the report, with a fresh approach likely once Dinamo's Europa League qualifying commitments are out of the way and the transfer picture in Bucharest becomes clearer.

For Stoinov, the interest from a club of Craiova's standing is another marker of his rapid rise. Already capped by Israel's senior national team, he has gone from a fringe figure at Netanya to a wanted man in Romanian football inside little more than a year.

title: All-Israeli team to referee Lech Poznań's Europa League qualifier
dek: Orel Grinfeld will take charge of Lech Poznań's clash with KÍ Klaksvík, with every match official on UEFA's appointment sheet Israeli, ONE reports.
body: UEFA has handed the next round of Europa League qualifying to a fully Israeli refereeing crew, appointing Orel Grinfeld to take charge of Lech Poznań's third qualifying round opener against the Faroese club KÍ Klaksvík, ONE reported.

The first leg kicks off on Thursday, August 6, at Poznań's Enea Stadion, with the Polish side hosting a tie that will decide who advances a step closer to the Europa League's group phase. Klaksvík host the return leg in the Faroe Islands the following week.

Grinfeld will be flanked by fellow Israelis Roy Hassan and Idan Yarkoni as assistant referees, with Gal Levi appointed fourth official. Daniel Bar Natan takes the VAR booth, assisted by Eli Hacmon — meaning every official named for the match is Israeli.

It is another significant continental assignment for Grinfeld, who in 2018 became the first Israeli referee promoted into UEFA's elite category, the top tier reserved for officials who regularly take charge of Champions League and Europa League fixtures. He made his Champions League debut that season in a group-stage meeting between Real Madrid and Viktoria Plzeň.

Polish outlets covering the pairing noted that the appointment has attracted some attention locally given the current regional climate, with Gol24 reporting that the return leg in the Faroe Islands will instead be overseen by a Croatian referee.

For Israeli officiating, though, the assignment fits a familiar pattern: despite Israeli clubs and national teams facing scheduling disruption in some competitions in recent seasons, UEFA has continued to trust Israeli referees with regular European fixtures — Grinfeld's latest booking a fresh sign of that standing.

title: Luka Dončić says his summer break from basketball fuels his motivation
dek: The Lakers' new undisputed leader, sidelined for the whole playoffs by a hamstring injury, says he is fully recovered and used his usual offseason formula to recharge before a roster overhaul in Los Angeles.

verificationSources.label: ESPN – LeBron James informs Lakers he plans to play elsewhere in 2026-27
ESPN – Sources: Lakers trading Ayton to Wizards for Hardy, future picks
Bleacher Report – Luka Doncic Updates Injury Status, Reacts to Lakers Getting Swept by Thunder

body: Luka Dončić has confirmed he is fully fit again after a summer spent deliberately staying away from the game that consumed his entire season, telling fans his recovery from a serious hamstring injury "went really well" and that he is now "100% healthy."

"I took a real break from basketball in the first weeks after the season ended to recover my body," the Lakers star said, in comments reported by the Israeli outlet ONE. "My recovery went really well and I'm 100% healthy again."

Dončić described the approach as a personal ritual rather than a reaction to the injury that wrecked his 2025-26 playoffs. "Taking a break from basketball is something I do at the beginning of every summer," he said. "It's a different way of doing things, but it works for me. When I allow myself to miss the game a little and try new things, it gives me motivation to return to playing."

The break followed a painful end to the season for the Lakers. Dončić suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on April 2 in a regular-season game against Oklahoma City, an injury later found to be more severe than first believed once he was examined in Spain. It kept him out of the entire playoff run.

Los Angeles got past Houston in six games in the first round without him, but the depleted Lakers were swept 4-0 by the eventual champion Thunder in the Western Conference semifinals, losing the series-ending Game 4 115-110.

Dončić now heads into next season as the Lakers' unquestioned leader after LeBron James, who spent eight seasons in Los Angeles, informed the club in late June that he would not be returning and has since moved on to the Philadelphia 76ers for what will be his 24th NBA season.

The roster around Dončić has also been reshaped over the summer. The Lakers traded center Deandre Ayton, who had spent just one season in Los Angeles, to the Washington Wizards for guard Jaden Hardy — a former Dallas Mavericks teammate of Dončić's — and two future second-round picks, a move that followed the club's acquisition of Walker Kessler from Utah.
ONE's report also noted departures including Rui Hachimura, Marcus Smart, Luke Kennard and Jaxson Hayes as Los Angeles remade its supporting cast around its Slovenian star.

According to the report, Dončić is planning to host a training camp for Lakers teammates in Slovenia in August, reportedly offering to cover the cost of their flights from the United States as he looks to build early chemistry with a retooled roster ahead of training camp.

With his health no longer in question and a full offseason behind him, the 27-year-old now carries the Lakers' hopes as the franchise tries to move past a playoff exit that Dončić could only watch from the sidelines.

title: Neymar: I'm not thinking about retirement, I have a contract with Santos
dek: The Brazilian forward, who last week ended his international career, says he will only weigh his club future once his Santos deal runs out in December.
body: Neymar has moved to calm any talk of hanging up his boots altogether, insisting his only firm plan is to see out his contract at Santos through December — even as he has already closed the book on his international career.
"I am not thinking about retirement. I have a contract with Santos until December, and I want to do my best for the club," Neymar said, according to ONE.

He was clear that any decision on what comes next will wait. "After that I will consider my options. Stay, leave, retire, continue playing... I don't know, there's still time until December and we'll see what happens," he added.

The comments come roughly a week after Neymar confirmed he was done playing for the Seleção, following Brazil's Round of 16 exit from the 2026 World Cup. He leaves international football as Brazil's all-time leading scorer, with 80 goals in 130 caps across four World Cups.

The 34-year-old's club situation remains genuinely open. Brazilian reports have suggested he is not expected to sign a new deal at Santos once his current contract expires, leaving the destination of one of the sport's biggest names unresolved for now.

Adding another layer to the story, Neymar's father and long-time adviser, Neymar Sr., recently suggested a Seleção return could not be entirely ruled out, saying: "I cannot guarantee he is done with the national team 100%. Maybe he will come back."

Neymar responded to his father's remarks with a lighthearted comeback rather than a rebuttal, according to ONE, making clear the door he closed on Brazil duty is not the one he's focused on right now — his priority, in his own words, is finishing the job at Santos.

title: UFC flyweight Allan Nascimento dies in his sleep at 34
dek: The Brazilian fighter was found unresponsive after an apparent heart attack, less than two months after his last octagon appearance.
body: UFC flyweight Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34 after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep, the promotion confirmed on Monday, in a sudden loss that has stunned the mixed martial arts community.
The Brazilian, from São Paulo, was found unresponsive in the early hours of the morning. A medical team was called and attempted to resuscitate him, but he was pronounced dead at the scene.

"This morning, Monday, August 3, our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight Allan Nascimento was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep," the UFC said in a statement. "Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene."

The organisation extended its "deepest condolences" to his family, friends, teammates and loved ones, a message echoed across the sport as tributes poured in from fighters and fans who knew him as "Puro Osso".

Nascimento built a respected 12-year professional career, compiling a 22-7 record across 29 fights, with the bulk of his wins coming by submission. He went 4-2 across six appearances inside the UFC's flyweight division.

His most recent fight came on June 20, when he dropped a three-round split decision to Mitch Raposo at a UFC Fight Night card in Las Vegas — a defeat that, in hindsight, marked the final appearance of his career.

Nascimento was born on September 11, 1991, and had been a fixture of the flyweight scene for over a decade, fighting his way onto the UFC roster after building his name on the Brazilian regional circuit.

News of his death, first reported in Israel by ONE, has since been confirmed by outlets across the MMA world, with the UFC's own tribute serving as the clearest account of what happened in his final hours.

title: Idan Vered still waiting on Rehovot city hall over new club plan
dek: The former Beitar Jerusalem forward says he submitted a detailed proposal two years ago, but with the Liga Alef season three weeks away, Rehovot's municipality still won't commit to a timeline.

body: Idan Vered is still waiting for Rehovot city hall to make up its mind. Three weeks before the new Liga Alef season kicks off, the 37-year-old former Beitar Jerusalem forward says the municipality has yet to give him a clear answer on a proposed new club he has been pitching for two years, ONE reports.

Vered, who also won titles with Maccabi Haifa and became the first Israeli to play in Serbia's top division with Red Star Belgrade, has spent the past two years in talks with the city about launching a fresh, municipally backed football project in Rehovot. "I've been in talks with the municipality for the last two years. I submitted them a proper plan and everything," he told ONE.

The idea, as Vered has presented it, is not a merger of Rehovot's two long-standing lower-league rivals, Hapoel Marmorek and Maccabi Sha'arayim. If he does sign on with the city, ONE reports it would be to front an entirely new club under municipal sponsorship, kept separate from either of the old nostalgic sides.

The municipality's response so far has been noncommittal. A city spokesperson told ONE that "contacts on the matter are ongoing," without offering any indication of when, or whether, a decision is coming.

It is not the first time Rehovot has floated building a club from scratch rather than folding its existing teams together. City officials have discussed a new municipal side with professional management as their preferred long-term route, banking on a newly built stadium in the city to help drive it forward. More than a year on, the project remains just that: a plan on paper.

Hapoel Marmorek, for its part, is not waiting around. ONE reports the club is pressing on with preparations for the 2026/27 Liga Alef season regardless of how the municipal saga plays out, with an opener away to Hapoel Hadera as the new stadium in Rehovot edges toward hosting matches.

Liga Alef's new season is set to begin on August 28. Whatever Vered and the municipality eventually decide, it will need to happen quickly to have any bearing on how Rehovot's football landscape looks once the whistle blows.

title: Beitar Jerusalem warn: Austria Wien are better than people in Israel think
dek: Almog Cohen's side left for Romania to fine-tune preparations for Thursday's Conference League qualifier, with Luka Gadrani and Tomer Yosefi back from injury for the neutral-venue opener against a 24-time Austrian champion.
body: Beitar Jerusalem flew out to Romania to complete their preparations for Thursday's Conference League third qualifying round tie against Austria Wien, a fixture the club itself is treating with far more caution than the casual assumption back home that this is a routine step for a team with continental pedigree of its own.

According to ONE, Beitar moved up their departure time in order to fit in an extra training session on Romanian soil before their final work-out ahead of kick-off, wary of arriving undercooked for what the club has called one of the season's most important opening assignments.

The message from within the camp, relayed by ONE, was blunt: "Austria Wien is much better than people in Israel think. We expect a difficult match ahead of us." It is a deliberate attempt to manage expectations around a club that has won the Austrian title 24 times and lifted the domestic cup on 27 occasions, making it one of the most decorated names in Austrian football.

The first leg, on August 6, will not actually be played in Vienna or Jerusalem but on neutral ground in Ploiești, Romania — hence Beitar's choice to base their final preparations in the country. The return leg follows a week later, on August 13, at Austria Wien's Franz-Horr-Stadion, known commercially as the Generali Arena.

Both clubs arrive on the back of contrasting routes through the qualifying rounds. Beitar needed a penalty shootout to see off Cypriot side AEK Larnaca in the previous round, while Austria Wien advanced far more comfortably, beating Latvia's FK Liepāja 5-1 on aggregate. It will be Beitar's first competitive meeting with an Austrian club in a UEFA tournament.

There was better news on the injury front. Georgian centre-back Luka Gadrani and Israeli midfielder Tomer Yosefi have both recovered from their respective knocks and travelled with the squad, giving head coach Almog Cohen extra options he did not have in the closing weeks of preparation.

Cohen, who moved from Beitar's sporting director's office into the head coach's role for the 2026/27 season, is expected to finalise his starting eleven only after Wednesday's last training session in Romania, with the make-up of the attacking positions understood to be the main outstanding decision.

For a club still building trust in a first-year coach, a credible showing against one of Austria's traditional powers would carry weight well beyond the two legs themselves — beginning with a tie the players themselves are refusing to take lightly.

title: Ter Stegen completes season-long loan move from Barcelona to Ajax
dek: The Germany goalkeeper, squeezed out of the Barcelona team by Joan García, passed his medical in Amsterdam and reunites with coach Michel at a club where Israeli international Oscar Gloukh is already a first-team regular.
body: Marc-André ter Stegen is officially an Ajax player. Barcelona's long-serving goalkeeper completed a season-long loan move to the Dutch champions on Tuesday, ONE reported, after passing a medical in Amsterdam that closed out weeks of stop-start negotiations between the two clubs.

The move ends a difficult year for the 34-year-old German international, who lost his place between the posts at Camp Nou after Joan García established himself as Hansi Flick's first-choice keeper. Ter Stegen still has a contract at Barcelona running beyond this season, but with no realistic path back into the side, both club and player concluded a temporary exit made sense.

According to the report, the two clubs had reached an in-principle agreement on the loan some time ago, with the main sticking point being how to split ter Stegen's salary, reported at close to €20 million a year - a sum Ajax could never have carried alone. Barcelona will continue to cover the large majority of those wages, with Ajax picking up a smaller share, and a purchase option has been built into the deal.

The move reunites ter Stegen with head coach Michel, who took over at Ajax this summer after previously managing him during a loan spell at Girona in the second half of last season. Ter Stegen's time there was hampered by a hamstring injury that limited him to just two appearances, but it was evidently enough to convince Michel to pursue him again once he arrived in Amsterdam.

"Marc possesses an exceptional track record and his capabilities are well-known to everyone," Ajax sporting director Jordi Cruyff said, according to ONE. "He brings quality to us immediately. We know each other well from before, and I look forward to working with him again. We worked on this move for a long time, and we're pleased he signed and can begin his journey with us."

For Israeli football fans, the transfer carries an extra layer of interest: ter Stegen joins a dressing room that already includes Oscar Gloukh, the Israeli international who has been a regular for Ajax since arriving from Maccabi Tel Aviv. Israeli outlets picked up the story in part through that connection, framing Europe's newest arrival in Amsterdam as a new teammate for Gloukh rather than simply another Barcelona departure.

Ter Stegen has been Barcelona's goalkeeper since joining from Borussia Mönchengladbach in 2014, winning a string of domestic and European honours and serving for a period as club captain. His fall down the pecking order this past year, culminating in this loan, marks the clearest sign yet that his long stint as one of the position's benchmark performers in Spain is drawing toward its close, at least for now.
At Ajax, he arrives as a proven, high-level presence for a club looking to strengthen its goalkeeping department as it competes on multiple fronts domestically and in Europe this season.

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv look set to add a fresh option out wide, with the Serbian outlet Sportal reporting that the club has agreed a deal with Red Star Belgrade for winger Douglas Owusu — a report ONE picked up and relayed on Tuesday.
According to that report, the two clubs have closed the deal for the 20-year-old, with Owusu's contract at Hapoel expected to be signed as soon as Tuesday itself.
The fee being reported is around €2.5 million — roughly €300,000 more than Red Star paid to sign him only seven months earlier.

Owusu, a Ghanaian-Serbian winger nicknamed "Baggio," joined Red Star from Radnik Surdulica in January 2026 in a deal worth close to €2.2 million, arriving in Belgrade with a reputation as one of the most exciting young wide players to come through Serbia's lower tiers.

His time at the club never quite took off. He made 13 appearances for Red Star, scoring twice and adding one assist, with coach Dejan Stanković recently noting that Owusu had experienced difficulties since joining, after being benched for bigger names in the squad.

Sportal's report suggests a swift move could allow Hapoel to register Owusu in time to feature in the club's Conference League campaign this season, adding pace and directness to the wings before the European ties resume.

The move has not gone through a full confirmation cycle at either club. A day earlier, the Serbian outlet hotsport.rs described Hapoel's interest only as that — an interest, with no official confirmation of any submitted offer — a reminder that the fee and timing here should still be read as a developing report rather than a completed transfer until either club issues its own statement.

Should it go through as reported, Owusu would become the latest reinforcement for a Hapoel side building toward continental football, adding a young attacking option as the club shapes its squad for the season ahead.

According to ONE, the betting markets at Winner leave little doubt about who is expected to come out on top. Red Star are priced at 1.65 to win, with a draw available at 3.30 and Beer Sheva out at 3.75 to cause an upset on their European bow.

title: Table tennis prodigy Omer Gadot becomes first Paralympic athlete admitted to Wingate academy
dek: The 12-year-old, already Israel's Paralympic table tennis champion and ranked third nationally against non-disabled rivals, will train inside the country's flagship elite sports program for the first time in its history.

body: For the first time, a Paralympic-track athlete has been accepted into Wingate Institute's Academy for Sports Excellence, the national program that has nurtured generations of Israel's leading young Olympians. ONE reports that the breakthrough belongs to Omer Gadot, a 12-year-old table tennis player from Ramat Gan who lives with a lower-limb disability.

Gadot's admission is being described by those around him as a precedent-setter rather than a one-off exception. He arrives at Wingate not as a curiosity but as a genuine prospect: he is currently ranked third in Israel in his age group in the country's general table tennis rankings, competing directly against players without disabilities.

His Paralympic résumé is just as striking. Gadot recently won the Israeli Paralympic table tennis championship, beating Aviv Gordon 3-0 in the final — a rival roughly two decades his senior — to claim the national title, according to ONE.

He trains at the Spivak Club in Ramat Gan and at Hapoel Petah Tikva under coach Dani Bobrov, himself a former Paralympic table tennis competitor who now works as an administrator in the sport. Bobrov, born with an orthopaedic condition that affects walking, competed internationally for Israel and reached quarterfinal stages at both European and world championships before moving into coaching, according to independent Israeli sports reporting on his career.

"His acceptance to Wingate Academy represents more than personal achievement," Bobrov said, according to ONE. "This sets a precedent that could open doors for many others in Israeli Paralympic sport."

Wingate, located near Netanya, is Israel's central hub for elite athlete development and coach education, and has historically built its excellence program around Olympic-stream prospects. ONE's report frames Gadot's acceptance as the first time the academy has folded a Paralympic athlete into that structure.

Separate Israeli coverage of Gadot's rise, published before this latest milestone, has detailed a young athlete who took up table tennis only in the past two to three years and quickly outgrew expectations, training seriously enough to be tracked as one of Israeli disability sport's most promising juniors.

For Israel's Paralympic movement, still building its pipeline toward future Games, Gadot's dual status — competitive against able-bodied peers and already a national Paralympic champion — makes his Wingate breakthrough a marker worth watching well beyond one athlete's personal story.

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva face the biggest examination of their European summer on Tuesday evening, opening the UEFA Champions League third qualifying round against Serbian champions Red Star Belgrade in a first leg staged, as has become customary for the club's home European fixtures, in Hungary rather than the Negev.

Kick-off at the Haladás Sportkomplexum in Szombathely is set for 20:30 Israel time, with roughly 250 travelling Beersheba supporters set to be outnumbered by an estimated 400 Red Star fans making the trip from Belgrade.

"We all know this task is the hardest there is, but football is football," the club said in comments carried by ONE. "If we come with madness in our eyes and tactical discipline, we can narrow the gaps."

Manager Ran Kojok struck a similar note in his own remarks, framing the tie as a chance for his players to punch above their financial and experiential disadvantage. "This is the beauty of football — big gaps narrow in the face of heart and soul," he said, according to the report.

The gap in resources and continental pedigree is real. Red Star arrive on the back of a 9-0 aggregate demolition of Northern Ireland's Larne in the second qualifying round and have won four straight matches, making them clear favourites to advance to the play-off round.

Beersheba's route here was far less serene. They lost the first leg of their second-round tie 2-1 away to Iceland's Víkingur Reykjavík before rallying for a 2-0 win in the return fixture — also played in Hungary — to progress 3-2 on aggregate. ONE noted that victory snapped a three-match losing run and was only the team's first win in five matches, leaving lingering questions over their current form after a difficult stretch since clinching the Israeli title in May.

Kojok has yet to settle on his midfield selection, weighing up Eliel Peretz against Mohammed "Hamoudi" Kna'an as he looks to fill the creative void left by Kings Kangwa, who departed for Panathinaikos during the close season. A final call is expected close to kick-off.
In defence, Itay Rotman is set to partner captain Miguel Vitor at centre-back, with Jibril Diouf making way, per ONE's report.

Whatever happens over the two legs against Red Star, Beersheba have already secured continental football beyond this tie: ONE has separately reported that the club has locked in a place in next season's Conference League league phase, guaranteeing a "European winter" and revenue of at least €3.3 million even if they fall short of the Champions League play-off round.
The return leg in Belgrade is scheduled for next week, with Red Star needing to protect their status as one of the favourites to reach the Champions League league phase outright.

title: Jérémy Doku reveals he was given a banned substance during his World Cup health scare
dek: The Manchester City and Belgium winger says he received cortisone, a drug on WADA's prohibited list, after a lung problem left him coughing blood in the United States.
body: Jérémy Doku has given the fullest account yet of the frightening illness that derailed his World Cup, and it comes with a detail that raises eyebrows well beyond the medical tent: the Belgium winger says the treatment he needed included cortisone, a substance on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list.

"I could cry from the pain," Doku said of the days when his condition was at its worst, according to ONE, which reported the confession from the Manchester City forward. He described being administered cortisone to manage the crisis, medication that can trigger a positive doping test unless specifically cleared for use.

That clearance came through, ONE reports: FIFA's anti-doping process granted Doku a Therapeutic Use Exemption, the formal mechanism that allows athletes to take an otherwise banned drug for a genuine medical need without breaching the rules. Without it, the same treatment could have opened him up to a doping case rather than a sympathetic headline.

The saga began in the best possible way, with Doku starting Belgium's World Cup opener against Egypt and playing until the 86th minute of a 1-1 draw. It was afterwards that his body started to turn on him: a cough that would not shift developed into something far more serious.

Multiple outlets, including ESPN and OneFootball, have separately reported that Doku's condition escalated to the point where he was coughing blood and struggling to breathe, with tests eventually showing fluid in his lungs. He required an emergency hospital visit in the middle of the night to get it under control.

The illness cost him Belgium's second group game, against Iran, for which he was ruled out entirely. Belgium's medical staff and FIFA's doctors worked through the tournament to manage a player who, by his own description, was in some of the worst physical distress of his career.

There was a parallel, personal drama unfolding at the same time. While Doku was being treated, he learned that his wife had gone into labour weeks before her due date. He left the Belgium camp and flew home for the birth of his first child, a son the couple named Praise, before rejoining the squad.

Cortisone is effective at calming acute inflammation, but it is not without cost to an elite athlete: it can weaken muscles and tendons and complicate a quick return to peak physical condition. Doku never fully recaptured his sharpest form for the rest of the tournament, a knock-on effect of both the illness and its treatment.
He did make it back for Belgium's final group match, and the Red Devils advanced through the group stage before their World Cup run ended in the quarter-finals, where they were beaten by Spain.

The episode leaves Doku with an unusual footnote to a World Cup that also brought him fatherhood: a legitimately treated illness that, on paper, involved a banned substance, resolved only because the paperwork with FIFA's doctors was done correctly and in time.

title: Vinicius Jr's agency chief flies to London amid fresh Arsenal speculation
dek: Michael Yormark, president of Roc Nation Sports International, set off a wave of transfer chatter with a cryptic social media post as Real Madrid stand firm on their contract offer to the Brazilian.
body: Michael Yormark, president of Roc Nation Sports International, boarded a flight to London this week and posted a two-line message on Instagram that was enough to set off a fresh round of transfer speculation: "London, here I come. Let's go."

Roc Nation represents Vinícius Júnior, and ONE reports that the exact purpose of Yormark's trip has not been confirmed — but the timing, with the Brazilian winger's Real Madrid future unresolved and Arsenal circling, was enough to fuel talk of a possible move to England.

According to ONE, Real Madrid have told Vinícius that their latest contract offer is final and that no further negotiation will take place, leaving the decision in the player's hands. The 25-year-old has become one of the most scrutinised figures at the Bernabéu this summer as the club pushes for a long-term renewal.

Arsenal, fresh off ending their 22-year wait for the Premier League title and reaching the Champions League final before losing to Paris Saint-Germain, have been repeatedly linked with Vinícius as they look to strengthen the left side of their attack. The Gunners sold Leandro Trossard to Besiktas last month, and Gabriel Martinelli has struggled for consistency in that position.

The speculation has already prompted a public response from Vinícius's camp. Roc Nation issued a statement in recent days condemning what it called "fake and damaging" reporting on the player's future, accusing unnamed outlets of publishing unverified claims for attention.

No club has confirmed that talks over a transfer are underway, and ONE is careful to note that Yormark's London visit has not been officially tied to Arsenal or any other Premier League side. For now, the trip itself is the only confirmed fact — everything else remains speculation swirling around one of world football's most closely watched contract sagas.

title: Sacked by Tveria, Maurice Ozen resurfaces as Migdal HaEmek's youth chief
dek: Days after being let go by Ironi Tveria, the veteran coach known for the club's historic 2013/14 promotion has taken over the academy at Hapoel Migdal HaEmek.

body: Maurice Ozen has a new address barely a week after Ironi Tveria showed him the door. ONE reports that the 49-year-old, who spent the last four seasons running the club's youth department, has agreed to become professional manager of the academy at Hapoel Migdal HaEmek.

Ozen's exit from Tveria closes out a spell that began in the 2022/23 season, during which he steered the club's youth side up from the National Youth League into the National League, where it competed for three straight campaigns. His departure was confirmed separately when Ynet reported that Yuval Shtrit has since been installed as the new coach of Ironi Tveria's youth team.

At Migdal HaEmek, a Liga Alef club owned by Shlomi Ohion, Ozen's brief is to build out an academy that currently fields only five youth teams. According to ONE, the club wants to grow its own talent pipeline rather than rely on the transfer market to stock the senior squad.

Ozen arrives with a long history in Israeli football's lower and middle tiers, most closely tied to Hapoel Beit Shean, where he spent years as both a player and later a coach and is remembered as something close to a club institution.

His most celebrated feat came with Tveria itself, back in 2013/14, when he led the club up from Liga Alef to the National League through the promotion playoffs, beating Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem home and away. ONE notes it remains the only such playoff promotion of its kind since the format was introduced, a big part of why Ozen is spoken of in Israeli football circles as a specialist in engineering promotions.
The Migdal HaEmek post marks the seventh club of Ozen's coaching and playing career, according to ONE's report.

title: Beitar Jerusalem leave Uri Dahan out of Conference League squad as Tiberias make their move
dek: Manager Almog Cohen omitted the centre-back from the trip to face Austria Wien after Ironi Tiberias approached the club, though Dahan is said to be holding out for a move abroad.

verificationSources.label: Beitar Jerusalem official site — Almog Cohen appointment

body: Beitar Jerusalem's coach Almog Cohen has sent an unmistakable message to Uri Dahan: the centre-back was left out of the squad travelling to Romania for Thursday's Europa Conference League third-round qualifier against Austria Wien, according to Sport5.

The trip, ahead of a tie that will be played in Ploiești because of the ongoing legal uncertainty affecting Beitar's home fixtures, was supposed to be a routine squad selection. Instead it confirmed what Dahan had already sensed over the summer — that he has slipped to fifth choice at centre-back under Cohen and can expect little playing time this season.

Sport5 reports that Ironi Tiberias have now formally approached Beitar over signing the 26-year-old, and the club has given its blessing for talks to take place. Dahan, however, is said to be prioritising a move abroad over staying in Israel's top flight, and is in no rush to commit to Tiberias.

Beitar are believed to be open to letting him leave given his contract runs only until the end of the coming season, meaning the club risks losing him for nothing next summer if a transfer isn't found now.

Dahan has been a fixture in Jerusalem since arriving on loan from Maccabi Haifa two seasons ago, making 57 appearances and winning the State Cup before signing a permanent three-year deal in July 2024. His fall down the pecking order accelerated after Beitar brought in Luka Gdrani this summer, pushing Dahan further back in the queue at the heart of defence.

For Beitar, the priority for now is Thursday's first leg against Austria Wien, a club with 24 Austrian league titles and a history that includes several former Israeli players. The return leg is scheduled for August 13 in Austria, with a place in the Conference League play-off round at stake.

Whether Dahan is part of that picture beyond this transfer window remains to be seen — but his absence from the travelling party to Romania was as clear a signal as any that his time at Teddy Stadium may be drawing to a close.

title: Pogačar to ride the Vuelta a España for the first time since 2019
dek: The five-time Tour de France champion will chase cycling's elusive Grand Tour triple crown when UAE Team Emirates-XRG lines up in Monaco on 22 August.
body: Tadej Pogačar will return to the Vuelta a España for the first time since 2019, UAE Team Emirates-XRG confirmed this week, setting up a bid for the one Grand Tour still missing from the Slovenian's remarkable palmarès.

The Vuelta was Pogačar's Grand Tour debut back in 2019, when, riding for the same team as a 20-year-old, he finished third overall behind Primož Roglič and Alejandro Valverde while winning three stages to announce himself to the sport. He has not started the race since.
"I'm excited to say I'm going back to La Vuelta," Pogačar said in the team's announcement. "It was my first ever Grand Tour back in 2019 and an amazing experience."

In the years since, Pogačar has become the dominant rider of his generation, winning the Tour de France five times and adding the Giro d'Italia to his collection in 2024. Only the Vuelta has eluded him among the sport's three three-week races.

Should he win it, Pogačar would become the ninth rider in history to complete cycling's career triple crown of all three Grand Tours, following Jacques Anquetil, Felice Gimondi, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, Alberto Contador, Vincenzo Nibali, Chris Froome and, most recently in 2026, Jonas Vingegaard.
The 2026 Vuelta a España opens on 22 August with an individual time trial in Monaco before three weeks of racing conclude in Granada on 13 September.
UAE Team Emirates-XRG have named an eight-rider squad built around Pogačar: João Almeida, Jay Vine, Pavel Sivakov, Pablo Torres, Domen Novak, Ivo Oliveira and Kevin Vermaerke complete the line-up.
The announcement ends weeks of speculation over whether Pogačar would target a Tour-Vuelta double in the same season, a feat managed by only three riders in history — Anquetil, Hinault and Froome.

title: Padded bras and 'chest fairings' spark a policing row at the Tour de France Femmes
dek: Several Women's WorldTour teams have asked the UCI to check riders for oversized, padded sports bras before today's time trial, reviving a fight over an unlikely aerodynamic edge.

verificationSources.label: BikeRadar — Padded bras cause controversy at Tour de France Femmes ahead of stage four time trial
Cyclingnews — Extra clothing checks at Tour de France Femmes after reports riders may be padding bras for aero gains
Canadian Cycling Magazine — Is 'bra doping' a thing at the Tour de France Femmes?

body: Ahead of stage 4 of the Tour de France Femmes, this is not a story about doping in the pharmacological sense — it's about bras. Several Women's WorldTour teams have gone to the UCI in a formal push to check that no rider is wearing an oversized, heavily padded sports bra as an illegal aerodynamic aid before today's 21-kilometre individual time trial from Gevrey-Chambertin to Dijon.

The claim, reported across the cycling press and picked up by Israeli outlet Shvoong, is that extra padding stuffed into a bra can smooth and round out a rider's chest into what aerodynamicists call a "chest fairing" — a shape that channels air more efficiently around a body hunched low over aero bars, shaving fractions of a second off every kilometre.

It sounds trivial until the numbers are laid out. A 2024 study in the Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics found that the largest chest fairing tested reduced drag by 3.6% and could save at least 0.78 seconds per kilometre — over a 20-to-30km test, enough to separate a stage winner from the rest of the field.

Aerodynamicist Bert Blocken, the Eindhoven University of Technology professor who spent years advising Visma-Lease a Bike's time-trial riders, put it plainly: "We're talking about a chest fairing, which changes the airflow around the body and reduces pressure on the thighs. You won't gain tens of seconds. But think about a 20- to 30-km time trial can save enough seconds to make the difference."

The same research traced similar chest-shaping effects at the 2023 Tour de France men's time trial, the 2023 Road World Championships time trial in Glasgow, the 2024 Paris Olympics time trial and the Giro d'Italia Women — suggesting the practice is not new, only newly scrutinised.

The UCI has not stayed silent. Its stage 3 jury report at this year's race pointedly cited Article 1.3.032 of the regulations, which bars "non-essential elements" and any clothing or accessory — a rule that already covers helmets, glasses, shoes and radio devices — that could modify a rider's morphology. Teams have pushed further, asking that inspections after the time trial be carried out specifically by female commissaires.

What makes this harder to police than a straightforward equipment breach is precisely what makes it contentious: officials cannot simply ban sports bras, and riders' natural body shapes vary hugely, meaning any check risks scrutinising women's bodies in a way the men's peloton never is. No individual rider or team has been named or accused; the complaints lodged with the UCI are procedural, asking the governing body to enforce an existing rule rather than pointing at a specific competitor.

The row also lands amid a broader UCI clampdown on marginal aerodynamic gains — the governing body recently banned front jersey pockets on similar grounds, arguing they too could be used to alter a rider's silhouette for a speed advantage.

All of which puts extra weight on today's test through Burgundy's wine country. Stage 4 is the only individual time trial on this year's route, and with the general classification still unsettled, any rider found gaining time through equipment rather than legs would face far more scrutiny than a mid-race controversy over bra padding.

title: Moscow, 30 May 2012: The Queen Trap That Cost Israel Its First World Chess Champion
dek: Boris Gelfand, the quiet grandmaster from Rishon LeZion, took Viswanathan Anand to a tiebreak for the World Chess Championship — and came within one blundered queen of making history.

verificationSources.label: The Week in Chess — Anand retains title after tiebreak win
The Week in Chess — Game 8: Anand wins in 17 moves
ChessBase — 'Gelfand, you are awesome!' The Challenger returns to Israel
Chess.com — Anand vs. Gelfand, World Chess Championship 2012

body: For three weeks in May 2012, inside the Engineering Building of Moscow's State Tretyakov Gallery, a 43-year-old immigrant from Minsk sat across a chessboard from the best player on earth and refused to lose. Boris Gelfand, ranked a modest 20th in the world against defending champion Viswanathan Anand's fourth, had no business being within touching distance of the World Chess Championship. By the time the match reached its final tiebreak day, he was one rapid game away from becoming Israel's first world champion in any sport governed by a global federation.

Gelfand's path to Moscow had been built on patience rather than flash. Born in Minsk in 1968, he was Soviet junior champion at 17 and European junior champion at 19, earning his grandmaster title in 1989 and cracking the world's top three by the summer of 1990. In 1998, with the Soviet chess machine gone and his career established, he emigrated to Israel and settled in Rishon LeZion, quietly becoming the country's highest-rated player for the next decade and a half while the game itself struggled for attention against Israel's football and basketball obsessions.

His route to a title shot ran through two grinding campaigns few outside chess noticed at the time: winning the 2009 World Cup in Khanty-Mansiysk, and then the eight-player 2011 Candidates Tournament in Kazan, where he eliminated Gata Kamsky, Shakhriyar Mamedyarov and finally Vladimir Kramnik to earn the right to challenge Anand. It made him, at 43, the oldest first-time world title challenger in decades — and the first Israeli to ever contest the sport's ultimate prize.

The match itself, backed by a $2.55 million prize fund, opened on 11 May 2012 and settled into a wary, high-precision stalemate. All twelve classical games ended in draws, six of them in fewer than 30 moves, as both men probed for the smallest structural edge and found none. It was, by the standards of elite chess, an unusually tense and airless contest — until Game 7 broke the pattern.

On 19 May, Gelfand beat Anand in 38 moves to take his only lead of the match, and Israeli chess fans allowed themselves, for the first time, to imagine the unimaginable. The response came almost immediately. In Game 8 the very next day, Anand won in just seventeen moves — the shortest decisive game in World Chess Championship history. Gelfand's queen, sent forward on an ambitious raid, was trapped by Anand's quiet 17.Qf2; Gelfand had calculated the position days earlier and simply missed the move over the board. He resigned within minutes, and the match was level again at 4–4.

Neither man could land another blow across the remaining four classical games. The scoreline held at 6–6 after twelve games, sending the championship to a rapid-play tiebreak on 30 May — a format that favoured Anand, the sharper and more experienced speed player. Anand won the first tiebreak game outright; the next three were drawn. He took the playoff 2½–1½, and with it the match, 8½–7½, retaining his title for a third consecutive defence.

Gelfand flew home to a reception no Israeli chess player had ever received. Dozens of fans and children from his hometown met him at Ben Gurion Airport carrying signs reading "Gelfand, ATA TOTACH" — Hebrew slang for "you're awesome." Asked what had decided the match, he was characteristically understated: "It was simply a matter of luck." He used the moment to press a different point, telling reporters that chess in Israel was still "regarded as a pastime for elderly people in the park" and calling for state investment in young talent.

No Israeli has come as close to a world chess title since. Gelfand continued competing for Israel at the top level for another decade, representing the country at Olympiads from Dresden to Istanbul, but the 2012 match in Moscow remains the high-water mark: twelve classical games without defeat against the world's best player, undone in the end by seventeen moves and a single queen that wandered one square too far.
facts: Boris Gelfand, born in Minsk in 1968, emigrated to Israel in 1998 and settled in Rishon LeZion, becoming the country's top-ranked chess player.
He earned his 2012 title shot by winning the 2009 World Cup and the 2011 Candidates Tournament in Kazan, beating Gata Kamsky, Shakhriyar Mamedyarov and Vladimir Kramnik.
All twelve classical games of the World Chess Championship 2012 in Moscow ended in draws, leaving the match level at 6–6.
Gelfand won Game 7 in 38 moves on 19 May 2012 — his only win of the match — before Anand replied by winning Game 8 in just 17 moves, the shortest decisive game in World Chess Championship history.
Viswanathan Anand won the rapid tiebreak 2½–1½ on 30 May 2012, taking the match 8½–7½ and retaining his title for a third consecutive defence.
Had Gelfand won, he would have become Israel's first world chess champion; he remains the only Israeli to have contested a World Chess Championship match.

title: Norway's Haugset Storms to Yellow With 88km Solo Raid on Tour de France Femmes Stage 3
dek: Sigrid Ytterhus Haugset rode alone for nearly 90 kilometres to win into Poligny, staging the longest solo breakaway victory in the modern women's Tour de France and becoming the first Norwegian to wear yellow.

verificationSources.label: Official Tour de France Femmes — Stage 3 result
ProCyclingUK — GC and jerseys after stage 3
Cyclingnews — Haugset stuns field with solo attack
Cycling Weekly — 'It's unreal', Haugset takes stage 3

body: Sigrid Ytterhus Haugset delivered the most audacious ride of the young 2026 season on Monday, soloing the final 88.5 kilometres of stage 3 of the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift to win alone into Poligny and seize the yellow jersey. It is the longest winning breakaway in the five-year history of the modern women's Tour, eclipsing Annemiek van Vleuten's 62-kilometre raid in 2022, and it made the 27-year-old Uno-X Mobility rider the first Norwegian ever to lead the race.

The stage covered 156.5 hilly kilometres from Geneva, Switzerland, into the Jura hills of eastern France, finishing in the cheese-making town of Poligny. The route was front-loaded with climbing: the category-1 Col de la Faucille (11.4km at 6.3%) came inside the first hour, followed by the Côte de Lajoux and the category-2 Col de la Savine, before a late sting on the Côte de Chaux-Champagny in the closing 30 kilometres.

The race blew apart early. Lorena Wiebes, the Dutch sprinter who had won both opening stages and carried the yellow jersey out of Switzerland, was dropped on the lower slopes of the Col de la Faucille, ceding the overall lead before the race had even crossed into France. An 11-rider move went clear soon after over the Côte de Lajoux, and it was from that group that Haugset launched alone on the Col de la Savine with more than 80 kilometres still to race.

What followed was a masterclass in defiance. Riding through 34°C heat, crosswinds and a headwind on the run to the line, Haugset built and defended a gap that at times looked precarious as two-time world champion Lotte Kopecky drove the chase from the group behind. But the bunch, wary of burning matches a day before an individual time trial in Dijon, never fully committed, and Haugset's advantage held all the way to Poligny.

She crossed the line 1 minute 24 seconds clear of Kopecky (SD Worx-Protime), with Marianne Vos (Visma-Lease a Bike) winning the sprint for third from the chase group at 2:48. Usoa Ostolaza Zabala, Kim Le Court-Pienaar, Noemi Rüegg, Célia Géry, Cédrine Kerbaol, Malwina Mul and Monica Trinca Colonna completed the top ten, all credited with the same time as Vos.

"It's unreal," Haugset said afterwards, describing an effort so extreme that she was left, in her words, so dizzy at the finish she could barely lift her arms off the bars. It was the Norwegian road champion's first WorldTour victory since stepping up to Uno-X Mobility, and the first Grand Tour stage win of her career.

The result reshuffles the general classification entirely. Haugset leads outright, with Le Court-Pienaar (AG Insurance-Soudal) the closest challenger at 2:02. Demi Vollering (FDJ United-Suez) sits third at 2:06, with Noemi Rüegg (EF Education-Oatly), Marianne Vos, Cédrine Kerbaol, Elisa Longo Borghini (UAE Team L'IMAD), Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney (Canyon-SRAM), Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (Visma-Lease a Bike) all rounding out the top ten at 2:10.

Wiebes, despite losing yellow, retains the green points jersey on 111 points after her two stage wins, with Haugset and Rüegg among those chasing behind her in that competition. Pieterse claimed the polka-dot mountains jersey with 18 points from her climbing on the day's four ranked ascents, ahead of Nikola Nosková and Haugset herself. Paula Blasi of the newly rebranded UAE Team L'IMAD — formerly UAE Team ADQ — leads the white jersey for best young rider, level on time with Isabella Holmgren and Antonia Niedermaier.

The fifth edition of the Tour de France Femmes, which began with a Grand Départ in Lausanne on Saturday, continues Tuesday with an individual time trial in Dijon before the race turns south through the Massif Central and the Alps, including a first-ever summit finish on Mont Ventoux, en route to a Nice finale on August 9. For now, though, the story is Haugset in yellow — a result almost nobody in the bunch saw coming when she rolled off the front on the Col de la Savine.

title: Turgeman answers 'Death to Israel' chants with a goal as Montreal rally for 2-2 draw
dek: The Israeli forward says he was targeted by antisemitic abuse from CF Montréal fans and shoved by the home goalkeeper after celebrating his goal; MLS, the Revolution and Montreal have all opened investigations.
body: Dor Turgeman scored, stood in front of the home end with his arms out, and set off a scene that had nothing to do with football. Saturday night's MLS match between CF Montréal and New England Revolution at Stade Saputo ended 2-2, but the story out of Montreal was what the Israeli forward says he heard from the stands before he ever touched the ball.

Turgeman, a 22-year-old from Ashdod who joined the Revolution from Maccabi Tel Aviv last August, says sections of the Montreal crowd chanted 'Death to Israel' and 'Free Palestine' at him for much of the game, abuse that broadcast microphones picked up. When he scored in the 36th minute to put New England 2-0 up — his fourth league goal of the season — he turned to face the jeering fans and held his celebration, a gesture he later said was deliberate.

'Israel is above everything for me,' Turgeman said afterward. 'I'm proud to be Israeli and proud of the national team I represent, so I made a gesture to show I wasn't listening to their curses and hatred toward my country.' He added that he had never experienced anything like it during a game in the United States, and that he would react the same way if it happened again.

The celebration triggered chaos. Montréal goalkeeper Sébastian Breza sprinted the length of the field and shoved Turgeman to the ground as cups and bottles rained onto the pitch from the stands; players from both sides poured in to separate the two, and the referee booked Breza with a yellow card. Montreal came back from two goals down to salvage a 2-2 draw in the second half.

Breza offered an unusual explanation for his part in the confrontation. 'I felt like I wanted the crowd to get more into the game,' he said. 'I wanted to push the crowd and get them to push the guys.'

New England moved quickly. 'The Revolution strongly condemn the antisemitic and discriminatory abuse directed at forward Dor Turgeman by CF Montreal supporters during Saturday's away match,' the club said in a statement, reporting the incident to MLS. 'There is zero tolerance for abuse, harassment, or discrimination in our game, and this behavior must be unequivocally condemned. Antisemitism and all forms of hate have no place in our sport, our stadiums, or our communities.' The club added it expects 'those responsible' to be held accountable.

CF Montréal, for its part, said it does 'not tolerate discrimination, or hateful behavior of any kind,' and that it is 'reviewing the matter' in coordination with MLS and the Revolution to establish the facts. Major League Soccer confirmed it is 'aware of reports of antisemitic and discriminatory chants' directed at Turgeman and said the incident is under investigation. No disciplinary findings had been announced as of Monday.

Turgeman has been one of the Revolution's most productive attackers since arriving on MLS's U22 Initiative rule, scoring five goals with four assists in his first 18 appearances for the club after a decorated run through Maccabi Tel Aviv's academy and first team that included two Israeli championships and a Super Cup. Saturday's goal, and the response it drew, has turned him into an unlikely flashpoint in a league now grappling with how to police its own stands.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv's muted unveiling of Tamir Blatt hides an immediate loan plan
dek: The club confirmed the point guard's return from rival Maccabi Tel Aviv with only a stats sheet and no quotes — ONE reports the silence is deliberate, because Blatt is expected to be loaned out again almost at once.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv confirmed this week that point guard Tamir Blatt is coming back to the club, on a three-year contract that runs through the 2028/29 season. It is the kind of signing that would normally get the full treatment from a Winner League giant — except Hapoel barely said anything about it at all, and ONE reports that the silence was very much the point.

The 29-year-old arrives from city rival Maccabi Tel Aviv for a second spell in red, but the club's official statement stuck to the bare essentials: his statistics and his playing history, and nothing else. No welcome quote from Blatt, no line from the coaching staff, no fanfare of any kind.

That stood out because it is not how Hapoel have handled other arrivals this summer. When American forward Eugene Jermon signed, the club put out an announcement with enthusiastic quotes from both the player and management. Blatt, a far bigger name with a far richer resume, got a fraction of the treatment.

According to ONE, the explanation is simple: Hapoel do not actually plan to have Blatt suit up for them this season. The intention, as the club sees it internally, is to loan him out again almost immediately — which made an elaborate unveiling feel pointless.

That loan expectation is echoed elsewhere. Sportando has reported that ASVEL of France and clubs in Rome are among the sides interested in taking Blatt for the coming campaign, though no destination has been finalised.

Blatt's own story with Hapoel goes back much further than this contract. He began his top-flight career at the club before moving on to Alba Berlin, where he won a German league title and a German Cup, and then to Maccabi Tel Aviv, where he added two Israeli championships and five Israeli Cups to his collection. His return, roughly nine years after he first left, closes the loop.

The financial terms, first reported by Ynet and Walla Sport, put the deal at around $1.7 million a season — a significant commitment for a player Hapoel may not even use this year, which only sharpens the question of why the club chose to announce it so quietly.

The move also fits into a broader reshuffling at the top of Israeli basketball this summer. Eurohoops has reported that Yam Madar is expected to head the other way, from Hapoel to Maccabi, alongside Blatt's switch — even if the two clubs have not presented it as a formal swap.

For now, Hapoel's low-key handling of the announcement reads less like indifference and more like pragmatism: with Blatt likely to spend the season somewhere else on loan, there was little upside in selling a headline the club has no intention of delivering on court.

title: Vince Cole returns to Otef Darom as Lior Hershko heads to Elitzur Shomron
dek: ONE reports the forward is going back to the Gaza-border community club for a second National League season, while an 18-year-old from Hapoel Emek Hefer's youth ranks takes his old spot in Samaria.

body: Vince Cole is going back to where his Israeli career began. ONE reports the 1.98m forward has agreed to rejoin BC Otef Darom for the club's second season in the National League, reuniting with coach Barak Peleg after a year away.

Otef Darom is not a typical roster addition story. The club was launched after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack as a joint project of the Israel Basketball Association, the Tekuma recovery administration and the Eshkol Regional Council, built to give the shattered Gaza-border communities something to rally around. Cole was part of that inaugural 2024/25 squad before leaving for a season in Samaria.

That spell paid off handsomely. Playing for Elitzur Shomron last season, Cole averaged 21.7 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.3 assists a game, numbers that made him one of the National League's more productive imports and explain why Peleg wanted him back in the Otef Darom project he has led from its founding.

Filling the vacancy Cole leaves behind at Elitzur Shomron is a considerably younger prospect. ONE reports the 18-year-old, 2.02m forward Lior Hershko is moving up from Hapoel Emek Hefer's youth department to take his place.

Hershko arrives with a growing reputation. He has just finished his third consecutive summer with Israel's youth national team at a European championship, this time wearing the captain's armband — continuing a family tradition, since both his parents captained Israel's national volleyball teams.

At club level he helped Hapoel Emek Hefer reach the national youth final this past season, averaging 12.2 points and 7.4 rebounds a game in the top junior division, production that persuaded Elitzur Shomron to hand him a senior roster spot rather than another year in the youth ranks.

The move to a National League team is a natural next step for a club with an unusual story of its own. Elitzur Shomron, representing the settlements of the Samaria Regional Council, has climbed from Liga Bet to the National League inside five years and plays its home games in a roughly 300-seat hall in Kfar Tapuach, well short of what a Premier League promotion would eventually require.

ONE's report also notes a separate signing in the same transfer window: Maccabi Petah Tikva has added naturalized Israeli guard Kairi Brown, a 27-year-old, 1.83m combo guard who joins from Elitzur Yavne by way of Hapoel Tzfat, where he averaged 12 points and 6 assists per game last season.
