title: Peretz and Kanaan battle for Kangwa's old role as Beer Sheva ready for Red Star Belgrade
dek: Ran Kozuch has yet to pick between Eliel Peretz and Mohamad Kanaan for the playmaking role vacated by Kings Kangwa, as Hapoel Be'er Sheva prepare to face Serbian champions Red Star Belgrade in the Champions League third qualifying round.
body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva have one significant selection puzzle left to solve before Tuesday's Champions League third qualifying round opener against Red Star Belgrade, and Ran Kozuch had still not settled on an answer heading into the club's final training session, according to ONE.

The dilemma centres on who fills the playmaking role vacated by Kings Kangwa, sold to Panathinaikos in a deal reported at roughly €3.8 million plus bonuses. Kangwa was Be'er Sheva's Israeli Footballer of the Year last season and his departure, ONE says, has left "a big void" in the side.

Eliel Peretz and Mohamad "Hamudi" Kanaan are the two candidates. Peretz made an impact off the bench in last week's win over Vikingur Reykjavik, while Kanaan has also been drilled in the role in training alongside winger Lucas Ventura, the outlet reports. Kozuch is expected to name his XI only on matchday.

Elsewhere the picture looks more settled. Itay Rotman, who came on during the Vikingur second leg, is competing with veteran Miguel Vítor for a place in central defence, with the rest of the attacking unit from that victory expected to be kept largely intact.

Be'er Sheva reached this stage by beating the Icelandic champions 3-2 on aggregate, losing 2-1 away before winning 2-0 in the return leg — itself played at a neutral venue in Hungary rather than at home, a quirk that will again apply against Red Star.

Tuesday's tie kicks off at 20:30 Israel time (17:30 UTC) at the Haladás Sportkomplexum in Szombathely, Hungary, with Be'er Sheva once again unable to call on home advantage in front of their own supporters.

Red Star Belgrade arrive as the more fearsome name on paper. Serbia's champions have swept through their previous two qualifying ties by an aggregate score of 9-0, and Tuesday's meeting will be the first ever between the two clubs.

For Be'er Sheva, closing the Kangwa-shaped gap in midfield without disrupting the momentum built against Vikingur is the priority — and whichever of Peretz or Kanaan gets the nod will do so against considerably stiffer opposition than Iceland's champions.

title: Ceferin plots Club World Cup boycott and lines up Al-Khelaifi to challenge Infantino
dek: UEFA's president is preparing to sabotage FIFA's 2029 Club World Cup and is grooming Paris Saint-Germain's Nasser Al-Khelaifi as a rival for football's top job, ONE reports.
body: European football's power struggle with Gianni Infantino is escalating into open warfare. ONE reports that UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin is preparing an unprecedented boycott aimed at paralysing FIFA's 2029 Club World Championship, while simultaneously grooming Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi as the man to unseat Infantino altogether.

According to the report, the plan being drawn up in Nyon would go well beyond a symbolic protest. The idea is to choke the 2029 tournament of everything it needs to function — halting cooperation with FIFA's operational machinery and denying the event official sponsorships and host locations, effectively strangling Infantino's pet project before a ball is kicked.

ONE notes the timing is no accident. The 2029 edition is still without a confirmed host, secured financing or committed sponsors, leaving it exposed to exactly the kind of coordinated squeeze UEFA and its allies are reportedly considering. Frustration among major European clubs over solidarity payments still owed from the expanded 2025 Club World Cup, held in the United States, is said to be adding fuel to the fire.

That grievance, per the report, is being used to justify a broader refusal to fall in line behind Infantino's future ventures — sentiment that has been building for months rather than appearing overnight.

The dispute over FIFA's direction is well documented beyond ONE's report. UEFA's 55 member federations have already voted to boycott FIFA competitions in protest at Infantino's proposal to sell a minority stake in the World Cup to private investors, branding the plan "irresponsible and indefensible" and declaring that "the World Cup is not for sale." Asia's confederation, through its president Sheikh Salman, has called the scheme "totally unacceptable."

It is against that backdrop that Čeferin's second, more personal manoeuvre becomes significant. ONE reports he is actively promoting Al-Khelaifi as a candidate to challenge Infantino for the FIFA presidency, with the UEFA chief viewing the Qatari as an ideal, well-resourced alternative capable of drawing support from federations well outside Europe.

Al-Khelaifi is no peripheral figure to make that case for. The 52-year-old has run Paris Saint-Germain since 2011, chairs the European Club Association and beIN Media Group, and sits on both UEFA's executive committee and the FIFA Council — while overseeing PSG's back-to-back Champions League triumphs in 2025 and 2026.

Qatari associates quoted elsewhere insist he has no personal hunger for the job. A representative close to Al-Khelaifi has said he has "absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest in the FIFA role," and that it would take considerable persuading to change his mind — a line that tracks with ONE's characterisation of reluctance on his part even as UEFA pushes him forward.

The mechanics of any challenge are not immediate. Candidates for the FIFA presidency must formally register by November 18, with the election itself not due until March 2027. Infantino has held the post since 2016 and has faced no opposition in either of his two re-election campaigns, in 2019 and 2023.

Whether Čeferin's dual strategy — starving the 2029 tournament while building a rival candidacy around Al-Khelaifi — actually forces Infantino's hand remains to be seen. But the scale of the confrontation being described marks one of the most serious threats yet to his grip on world football's governing body.

title: Maccabi and Hapoel Tel Aviv clash over Ghanaian winger Owusu as knee doubt clouds move
dek: ONE reports the two Tel Aviv rivals wanted very different terms for Red Star Belgrade's young wide man, with an undisclosed knee issue from a collapsed Czech deal adding a question mark to the chase.

verificationSources.label: ONE — Hapoel CEO in Belgrade to advance Owusu deal

body: Tel Aviv's two big rivals rarely want the same player badly enough to actually compete for him, but this summer both Hapoel and Maccabi Tel Aviv found themselves chasing the same Red Star Belgrade winger — and, according to ONE, doing so on very different terms.

Douglas Owusu, the 20-year-old Ghanaian wide man who joined the Serbian champions from Radnik Surdulica back in January, was first flagged by Maccabi as a potential addition to freshen up their attack. But the yellow side's interest came with a catch: Maccabi wanted only a loan, not a permanent deal.

Hapoel, by contrast, were prepared to go all the way and pay a transfer fee for Owusu outright — a pursuit that fits their summer needs after selling their own top winger, Loizos Loizou, to Red Star Belgrade in June in a deal ONE and Serbian outlets valued at around €3.5m, with Hapoel keeping a 10 percent sell-on clause.

ONE reports that Maccabi's caution traces back to reporting out of the Czech Republic. According to the outlet Deník Sport, Viktoria Plzeň had also been circling Owusu but walked away from a move after his medical examination in Pilsen turned up a knee problem — one whose exact nature was never disclosed publicly.
That scare appears to have spooked Maccabi into treating a loan as the safer route, while Hapoel judged the risk worth taking for a permanent signing.

The structural gap between the offers mattered to Red Star, who according to ONE were more inclined to do business with a club willing to pay now rather than simply borrow the player — tilting the picture in Hapoel's favour over their local rivals.

The finances are not straightforward, though. A separate ONE report says Red Star has been asking around €2.2m for Owusu — down sharply from an earlier €3.7m valuation of the player — but still above what Hapoel had budgeted for the position, leaving the fee as the last obstacle to a deal that ONE describes as otherwise close to being finalised, with Hapoel's leadership travelling to Belgrade to push it over the line.

Owusu himself has looked a smart pickup for Red Star since his January move: a direct, quick wide player who scored in a league win over his old club Radnik earlier this year and has continued to feature for the Serbian champions.

For Hapoel, landing him would plug the creative and attacking gap left by Loizou's departure with a like-for-like profile — a young, fast winger from the same Belgrade club, just heading in the opposite direction.

Nothing is signed yet, and the knee concern flagged by the Czech press means Hapoel will want their own medical staff satisfied before committing. But as things stand, ONE's reporting points to the Reds, not Maccabi, holding the stronger hand in Tel Aviv's quiet transfer derby.

title: New England Revolution condemn antisemitic abuse of Dor Turgeman in 2-2 Montreal draw
dek: The club filed a formal complaint with MLS after CF Montréal fans chanted "Death to Israel" at forward Dor Turgeman, who answered with a goal and was later shoved by the home goalkeeper.
body: New England Revolution have formally condemned antisemitic abuse directed at forward Dor Turgeman during Saturday's MLS away match at CF Montréal, reporting the incident to league leadership and declaring "zero tolerance" for the behaviour.

The trouble unfolded at Stade Saputo, where the Israeli striker was targeted throughout the game by chants of "Death to Israel" and "Free Palestine" from sections of the Montreal crowd, according to multiple reports from the scene.

Turgeman, a 22-year-old from Ashdod who joined the Revolution from Maccabi Tel Aviv, answered in the 36th minute with a goal that put New England 2-0 up. He celebrated by turning to the hostile supporters, arms out, and cupping a hand to his ear; teammate Peyton Miller did the same alongside him.

Fans then threw objects, reportedly cups and bottles, onto the pitch. Montreal goalkeeper Sebastian Breza ran the length of the box to confront Turgeman and shoved him to the ground, sparking a brief scuffle between players from both sides. Breza was shown a yellow card.
The match itself finished level, CF Montréal fighting back for a 2-2 draw.

Breza later said he had pushed Turgeman simply to "energise" the home fans, while Revolution head coach Marko Mitrovic said he was too far from the incident, 70 to 80 yards away by his own estimate, to say exactly what happened.

Turgeman was unrepentant about his celebration. He said the abuse does not happen at his team's games in the United States, "only in Canada," and added that "Israel is above everything for me." He said he had no regrets and would "do exactly the same thing again."

CF Montréal issued its own statement saying the club "does not tolerate discrimination or hateful behaviour of any kind" and that it was reviewing the incident in coordination with the Revolution and MLS.

New England Revolution went further in a formal club statement issued Monday. "There is zero tolerance for abuse, harassment or discrimination in our game, and this behaviour must be unequivocally condemned," the club said, adding that "no player should ever be subjected to abuse because of their race, ethnicity, religion or identity."

"Antisemitism and all forms of hate have no place in our sport, our stadiums or our communities," the statement continued, with the club saying it stands fully behind Turgeman and welcomes MLS's swift response to the complaint.
Turgeman arrived in New England last September in a reported $5.5 million move, one of the biggest signings in Revolution history, and has become a regular scorer for the club since making his debut.

title: Schalke pull out of Lindstrøm loan, Napoli threatens legal action
dek: Jesper Lindstrøm flew to Germany and passed a medical, but Schalke walked away from the loan hours later, and Napoli says it is ready to fight the collapse through the courts.

verificationSources.label: ONE report on the collapsed Schalke-Napoli deal
Get Football News Germany on the stalled Lindstrøm move
TuttoNapoli on Napoli's statement threatening legal steps

body: Schalke 04 have walked away from a loan deal for Napoli's Jesper Lindstrøm just hours after the Danish winger flew to Germany and completed his medical, and Napoli is furious enough to be weighing legal action, ONE reports.

The move had been billed as a formality: a loan with no fee attached, built around an option for Schalke to buy Lindstrøm outright for around €5 million plus performance bonuses, with conditions that could have turned that option into an obligation. Instead, the Bundesliga club pulled the plug before signatures were exchanged.

ONE lays out a timeline of the collapse. At 1pm, Schalke told Napoli it was withdrawing, citing a shift in "squad-building priorities" after two players were injured over the weekend. Napoli responded within half an hour, at 1:22pm, offering to simply accept the contract version Schalke itself had proposed. It made no difference: Schalke confirmed at 5:32pm that the deal was off for good.

Napoli's reaction, in an official club statement carried by ONE and Italian outlets including TuttoNapoli, was pointed. The club said it reserves "the right to take all appropriate steps before the competent authorities to protect our rights," language widely read in Naples as an explicit threat of legal action against the German club.

Napoli's version, echoed across the Italian press, is that Schalke's excuse about injury-driven squad needs was invented to escape an agreement it had already effectively signed off on, with Lindstrøm having been cleared to fly out and undergo a medical.

German outlets tell a different story. Bild and Sky Germany reported that Schalke felt Napoli tried to rewrite the terms at the last minute, pushing to convert the agreed purchase option into a mandatory buy clause the Bundesliga side had never signed up for. Get Football News Germany described Schalke as accusing Napoli of failing to honour the verbal agreement the two clubs had reached.

Lindstrøm, 26, is a Denmark international who came through Brøndby's academy before a breakout move to Eintracht Frankfurt in 2021, where he won the Europa League in 2022. Napoli paid Frankfurt around €30 million for him in 2023, a fee that has never been repaid in performances: loan spells at Everton and, more recently, Wolfsburg both underwhelmed.
For now, Lindstrøm is expected to return to Naples with his future unresolved, a player both clubs seemed to want moved on but neither could agree how to actually let go of.

title: Ran Kozuk: Hapoel Beer Sheva prepare for Red Star Belgrade like any other game
dek: The reigning Israeli champions travel to Belgrade for the first leg of a Champions League third qualifying round tie against the Serbian champions, and their coach insists the routine does not change against a bigger name.

verificationSources.label: ONE report on Ran Kozuk's pre-match comments

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva's head coach Ran Kozuk has waved away any suggestion that facing Red Star Belgrade requires a different kind of preparation, telling ONE that his staff have approached the Champions League qualifier exactly as they would any other match.

"In principle, we prepare like for every game," Kozuk said. "We understand the opponent we face, their qualities and advantages." It is a familiar line from a coach who has spent the summer trying to keep his squad's routine unchanged even as the games get bigger.

The reigning Israeli champions travel to Belgrade for the first leg of the Champions League's third qualifying round on Tuesday, kicking off at 20:30 local time against a Red Star side that has never previously met Beer Sheva in a competitive fixture.

Kozuk described a preparation process that started inward before turning to the opposition. "First we discussed ourselves a lot, but also the Star, its advantages and significant players and the things it does very well," he said, a nod to homework on a squad regarded as the strongest continental test Beer Sheva has faced this summer.

Beer Sheva only reached this stage after a scare against Icelandic champions Víkingur Reykjavík. They lost the first leg 2:1 away, then produced a battling 2:0 win in the return fixture — played at a neutral venue in Hungary, as Israeli clubs' home European matches currently are — to advance 3:2 on aggregate.

Red Star arrive as considerably heavier favourites on paper. The Serbian champions, one of the Balkans' most storied clubs, breezed through their opening two qualifying rounds this summer without conceding, according to reports, underlining the scale of the task now facing Kozuk's side.

For Beer Sheva, simply reaching a third qualifying round represents genuine progress on the European stage, and comes on the back of a landmark domestic campaign. Kozuk led the club to the Israeli championship in May, beating rivals Maccabi Tel Aviv 4:2, a year after guiding them to the State Cup with a win over Beitar Jerusalem.

A first-leg defeat in Belgrade would not necessarily end Beer Sheva's European hopes, with the return leg still to come roughly a week later. But Kozuk's message to his players, filtered through his comments to ONE, was one of composure rather than reinvention: treat the occasion like any other, and let the preparation speak for itself.

title: Report: Hapoel Tel Aviv agree deal with Red Star Belgrade for winger Douglas Owusu
dek: The 20-year-old Ghanaian has already won a Serbian title and cup with Crvena zvezda and is seen in Tel Aviv as the long-awaited replacement for Loizos Loizou, who left for Belgrade in a club-record sale.

verificationSources.label: Red Star Belgrade official profile — Douglas Owusu

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have reached an agreement with Red Star Belgrade over Ghanaian winger Douglas Owusu, ONE reports, in a move the Israeli club hopes will finally solve a problem it created for itself two months ago.

That problem has a name: Loizos Loizou. The Cypriot winger left Bloomfield Stadium for Red Star Belgrade in June in the biggest sale in Hapoel Tel Aviv's history, a deal reported at up to €3.8 million, and the club has been searching for a like-for-like successor on the right flank ever since. According to ONE, they believe they have found one at the very club that took Loizou off their hands.

Owusu, 20, is a right winger prized above all for his speed and directness. He is not a household name yet, but his rise has been rapid. He began his professional career at Asekem in the Ghanaian top flight before moving to Serbia in the summer of 2024, joining second-division side Radnik Surdulica.

At Radnik he was a driving force, racking up double-digit goal and assist numbers as the modest club won promotion to the Serbian Super Liga. That form earned him a move to Red Star Belgrade in January 2026, with reported interest from clubs including Norway's Bodø/Glimt and Czech side Viktoria Plzeň before Red Star won the race.

At Crvena zvezda, Owusu has continued to progress. ONE credits him with 13 appearances, two goals and an assist for the club so far, and he has already collected three trophies before his 21st birthday: the Serbian second-tier championship with Radnik, then the Serbian Super Liga title and the Serbian Cup with Red Star.

It is that combination — pace, end product and a habit of winning even as a squad player — that has caught Hapoel's eye. The club's football staff reportedly rate him highly and see him as a genuine game-changer who could give Ran Kozuch's side the kind of width and directness Loizou used to provide.

Neither club has confirmed the transfer publicly, and no fee has been disclosed. ONE's report describes an agreement between the two clubs rather than a signed contract, so the move should still be treated as a deal in progress rather than a done one.

If it does go through, Owusu would arrive in Tel Aviv with a resume well beyond his years — and with the unusual distinction of following the very player he is meant to replace, in reverse, along the Belgrade-to-Tel Aviv pipeline.

title: Semenyo says Maresca's simple instructions are 'music to my ears' after Guardiola's exit
dek: The Ghana international who scored Manchester City's FA Cup final winner says life under the new manager is refreshingly direct, even as he admits Pep Guardiola's departure stung.
body: Antoine Semenyo is not pretending the last few months at Manchester City have been simple. The Ghanaian winger, who arrived from Bournemouth in January, says he is still processing the fact that the manager who signed him barely got to coach him for half a season before walking away.

Pep Guardiola left City in May after ten trophy-laden years at the club, closing out his reign with a domestic cup double. Semenyo, according to comments carried by ONE, described the timing as tough on a personal level. "You want to get better, you want to improve every season and he definitely helped me with that... but obviously sad for him to leave," he said of Guardiola, who had promised to work on his all-round game.

The transition mattered more than most for Semenyo. City paid Bournemouth a reported £64-65 million for him in January, one of the biggest fees of the winter window, and he repaid it almost immediately: in May he scored the winning goal in City's FA Cup final victory over Chelsea at Wembley, an inventive back-heel flick off an Erling Haaland cross that made him the first Ghanaian ever to score in an FA Cup final.

Guardiola's successor is a familiar face at the Etihad. Enzo Maresca, who left Chelsea mid-contract for the job, spent years on Guardiola's City coaching staff before management spells at Leicester and Chelsea. His appointment was confirmed in late June on a three-year deal, with Chelsea receiving a reported compensation package for releasing him early.

Where Semenyo's excitement really shows is in describing the day-to-day instructions. He told reporters Maresca's message for his wide players is deliberately uncomplicated: "Enzo is just stay out wide and when you get the ball, just create opportunities. So it is music to my ears."

It is a marked contrast, by his own account, to Guardiola's more intricate positional demands. Semenyo pointed to what he saw of Maresca's Chelsea sides, where the wingers were pushed high and given license to operate largely on their own terms — exactly the kind of one-on-one, take-the-full-back-on football that plays to his strengths as a direct, powerful runner.

Semenyo's first half-season in Manchester was already a personal breakthrough: 21 goals for club and country, a Premier League Player of the Month award along the way, and now a Wembley moment that will follow him for the rest of his career.

For a squad adjusting to life without the manager who defined an era, Semenyo's comments read as a small but useful signal — a big-money new arrival who says he understands exactly what is being asked of him, and likes it.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv's Belić has successful surgery on fractured foot
dek: The Serbian loanee, who broke down in his European debut against Sheriff Tiraspol, is targeting a return around November after an operation at Assaf Harofeh.
body: Kristijan Belić has come through surgery on his fractured foot successfully, Maccabi Tel Aviv's medical staff confirmed, drawing a line under a grim start to the Serbian midfielder's loan spell in Tel Aviv.

The 25-year-old, on a season-long loan from AZ Alkmaar, went down with what ONE described as complex fractures in multiple locations of the metatarsal bone in his foot during his very first appearance for the club, in the Europa League qualifying tie against Sheriff Tiraspol.

The operation was carried out at Shamir Medical Center, Assaf Harofeh, by Maccabi's team physician Dr Dror Lindner, who heads the hospital's sports injuries and arthroscopic surgery unit, alongside Dr Amit Gal'ed and Dr Najib Shakir.

ONE reports the procedure went smoothly and that Belić will now move into rehabilitation with the club's medical and physiotherapy staff. Israeli outlets covering the injury in the days before the operation put his expected return somewhere between late October and mid-November, a lengthy spell out for a player who had barely had time to introduce himself to supporters.

Belić arrived in Tel Aviv in August 2025 on loan from the Dutch side, with an option to make the move permanent, after spells at AZ and, before that, Partizan Belgrade. Born in Sint-Truiden to Serbian parents, he has represented Serbia at senior international level since 2024.

According to Sport1-Maariv, the club has no plans to freeze his registration slot despite the long layoff, with the coaching staff continuing to assess reinforcements elsewhere in midfield. Belić would in any case have been unavailable for Israeli league fixtures until the competition's fourth round due to a separate suspension carried over from a prior disciplinary matter.

The injury landed at an awkward moment for Kenny Miller's squad, which is already missing midfielder Ion Nicolaescu through injury as it juggles a busy European qualifying schedule alongside domestic preparations.
For Belić, the focus now shifts entirely to rehab, with the club targeting a return to full training in the closing weeks of the year rather than any rushed comeback.

title: Oren Smadja weighs Knesset run with Gilad Erdan's new party
dek: The judo great and former national team coach confirms talks with the ex-Likud minister over a place on his new political list, though he says nothing is decided.

verificationSources.label: Times of Israel — Erdan, Edelstein new party

body: Oren Smadja, the most decorated figure in Israeli judo and the man who guided the national team to three straight Olympic bronze medals, is weighing an unlikely next chapter — a run for the Knesset alongside former minister Gilad Erdan.

ONE reports that Smadja confirmed he is in active talks over a place on the new political party Erdan is putting together ahead of the next election, though he stressed no decision has been made. "There are conversations and meetings, but nothing is yet closed," Smadja said. "I greatly appreciate Gilad Erdan for his steadfast positions and achievements at the UN and as ambassador to the US. We have a good and strong familiarity between us."

Speaking separately to Ynet, Smadja said he has been fielding a number of approaches lately. "With Gilad I have many years of acquaintance, and we discuss many subjects, much beyond politics," he said, adding that he is currently prioritising time with his family but would consider a return to public life if the timing and opportunity were right.

Erdan, who served as Israel's ambassador to the United States and later as its envoy to the United Nations, is expected to formally launch his new right-of-centre party within days, according to Ynet and the Times of Israel. Veteran Knesset member Yuli Edelstein, who left Likud after two decades in the party, is reported to be the most advanced of Erdan's recruits and a likely number two on the list.

The would-be Erdan-Edelstein list, sometimes dubbed a Likud offshoot in Israeli political coverage, has polled at around five seats in recent surveys, with talks of the party positioning itself as a centrist alternative open to a broad unity government.

Smadja, 56, would bring genuine sporting stature to any list he joins. He won bronze in judo at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, becoming the first Israeli man to medal at the Games — a day after Yael Arad became the first Israeli of either gender to do so.

He went on to become one of Israeli sport's most successful coaches, leading the national judo team for some fifteen years before stepping down from the role in May 2025. Under him, Or Sasson won bronze at Rio 2016, Israel's mixed team took bronze at Tokyo 2020, and Peter Paltchik claimed bronze at Paris 2024. He also helped develop Sagi Muki into a world champion in 2019.
For now, Smadja's political future remains genuinely open. As he put it himself, the conversations with Erdan are real — but far from finished.

body: Amit Harel, an 18-year-old goalkeeper who grew up in Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv's youth academy, has signed for Liga Alef North side Tzeirei Tamra, ONE reports, opening a new chapter as he moves into senior football for the first time.
Harel came through Bnei Yehuda's youth department and had been training with the senior squad's expanded roster, though he had yet to make a competitive appearance for the first team.

According to ONE, the move is a particularly significant one for the young goalkeeper — the first stop of his adult career in which he is expected to genuinely compete for the No. 1 jersey rather than simply provide cover.
Last season he was Bnei Yehuda's starting goalkeeper in the top-flight youth league and wore the captain's armband in several matches, experience the club hopes will help him handle the step up.

Tzeirei Tamra's coaching staff, led by Musa Diab, has identified the goalkeeper's shirt as one of the most important positions to sort out as they build the squad for the coming campaign, ONE reports.

The switch represents a natural progression from youth to senior football, handing Harel professional responsibility from the very start of his adult career rather than easing him in through loan spells or bench duty.
Liga Alef North is a competitive third-tier division, and Harel will now have to show he can cope with the physicality and pace of men's football after making his name at youth level.

Tzeirei Tamra, based in the northern town of Tamra and formed in 2013 as a successor to Hapoel Bnei Tamra, play their home games at the Osama Ghanim Stadium and will be looking to Harel to shore up a position the club's coaching staff clearly see as a priority this summer.

title: Omri Kende: plenty of well-known players still gamble
dek: The former Hapoel Tel Aviv defender, who battled a gambling addiction and debts to loan sharks as a teenage player, says the problem remains widespread in Israeli football and that he now wants to help rather than expose names.

verificationSources.label: Kan - Kende's rise, collapse and recovery from gambling

body: Omri Kende spent his career fighting for playing time as a right-back at Hapoel Tel Aviv, but these days he is better known for a different fight - the one against a gambling addiction that very nearly wrecked him as a teenager. In a new interview with ONE, he said the problem he lived through has never really gone away in Israeli football.

"There are plenty of well-known players who gamble," Kende told the site, adding that the list includes fathers of some of Israel's better-known current players. He was careful to frame the comment as a warning rather than an expose, saying his aim was "to highlight the problem and help" - not to name names.

Kende's own story is the reason anyone is asking him. He developed a serious gambling habit at 18 and 19, in his early years on Hapoel Tel Aviv's books, and ran up debts with grey-market lenders that spiralled beyond his control. The club suspended him in October 2008 once those debts came to light, and a club official personally lent him money to help cover what he owed.

The addiction cost him more than money. Kende admitted to ONE that he lied to a young Hapoel Tel Aviv teammate, Dani Bonder, about changes to training sessions in order to gain an edge in their rivalry for a starting spot. Asked whether he had done it more than once, he answered simply: "all the time." Looking back, he called it his biggest regret from that period - "Dani is my regret, he's a golden guy, but we were competing for the position."

None of it stopped him building a genuine career. Kende went on to win the Israeli championship with Hapoel Tel Aviv in 2009-10 and lifted three State Cups with the club, before later spells with Romania's Astra Giurgiu, Hapoel Haifa, Maccabi Netanya and Hapoel Jerusalem.

Since hanging up his boots, Kende has become something of a media fixture, discussing his rise, collapse and recovery on podcasts and television, according to public broadcaster Kan. He says he now works informally with players still fighting the battle he once did.

His message to them, as he laid it out to ONE, is that recovery starts with honesty rather than concealment - admitting the truth to yourself before anyone else, rather than trying to hide a habit that, in his experience, rarely stays hidden for long inside a football dressing room.

Gambling among Israeli footballers is not a new concern - cases involving current and former players surface most seasons - but Kende's willingness to put his own name and story behind the warning sets him apart from the usual anonymous hand-wringing about the issue.

title: Israel finish seventh in team free final at European artistic swimming championships
dek: The squad lifted its score from the preliminary round in Paris, but France and Ukraine both raised their level in the final to leapfrog the Israelis.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 – team roster and championship schedule

body: Israel's artistic swimming team finished seventh in the team free routine final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris on Monday, ONE reports, a solid if unspectacular finish to one of the two finals the squad reached this week.

The Israelis scored 214.2970 in the final, an improvement on the 206.4693 they posted in the preliminary round, where they had sat fifth. But the final is decided fresh, and two rivals had more left in the tank.

France and Ukraine both raised their level when it mattered and pushed past Israel's total, dropping the team two places down the standings from where it had stood after the morning heats, according to ONE's report.

The routine was performed by Yogev Dagan, Kati Konin, Alexandra Larman, Noga Levy, Lior Makmel, Leah Makmel, Aya Mazor and Noya Tzrfati. Dagan's presence in the lineup reflects the sport's recent shift toward mixed group routines, with men now integrated into what was for decades an exclusively female discipline.

The result came in the middle of a packed week for the Israeli delegation at the Paris championships, which opened on July 31 and runs across six events over six days: free duet, technical duet, mixed technical duet, free group, technical group and the acrobatic routine.

Israel's program has been on a steady upward trajectory, highlighted this season by a bronze medal in the acrobatics event at a World Cup stop in Paris, the team's first podium finish at that level, according to Sport5.

The squad is not finished in the French capital. It returns to the pool tomorrow evening for the technical group final, the second of its two group finals this week, with the free duet also among the events already contested by the wider delegation.

title: Ganeah a nightmare to face, Ventura the key man, warns Red Star Belgrade's own analyst
dek: Ahead of Tuesday's Champions League qualifier, Serbian coach Dusan Matovic tells Serbian media that Amir Ganeah's dribbling and Lucas Ventura's control in midfield make Hapoel Be'er Sheva a far tougher out than Red Star might expect.

verificationSources.label: Jerusalem Post - Hapoel Beersheba advances to face Red Star Belgrade

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva have not lacked confidence since claiming the Israeli championship in May, but the scouting reports arriving from Belgrade this week suggest Red Star are taking Ran Kozhuk's side seriously, too.

Speaking to Serbian media ahead of Tuesday's Champions League third qualifying round first leg, Dusan Matovic — a Serbian coach who spent time as an assistant at Maccabi Haifa and Bnei Sakhnin before joining Hapoel Tel Aviv's staff — gave his club's press a detailed breakdown of the Israeli champions, and two names stood out.

"He's a winger who is very difficult to deal with," Matovic said of Amir Ganeah, the 22-year-old who has become one of Be'er Sheva's most dangerous attacking outlets. According to Matovic, Ganeah is dynamic off the left flank but consistently looks to cut inside onto his stronger right foot, where he is at his most effective at exploiting gaps in a defence.

Ganeah has been one of the stories of Be'er Sheva's title-winning campaign, breaking into a settled first team and contributing goals and assists from the wing as Kozhuk's side won the league ahead of Maccabi Tel Aviv.

Matovic reserved his other key warning for Lucas Ventura, the Brazilian midfielder Be'er Sheva signed permanently from Portimonense after initially holding only half his rights. "He's the key player in midfield," Matovic said, pointing to Ventura's role in dictating tempo and applying pressure high up the pitch — the platform, in his view, from which Be'er Sheva's game is built.

The club rewarded Ventura for that influence in January by buying out the remaining 50 percent of his contract from the relegated Portuguese club, and later triggered an option extending his deal through 2028.

For all the individual praise, Matovic's central message to Red Star was tactical: break Be'er Sheva's high press early, or spend the night chasing the ball against a side he called well organised and a genuinely difficult opponent, even while naming Red Star the favourites given their squad depth and experience.

The tie is a first-ever meeting between the clubs. Red Star arrive having demolished Northern Irish champions Linfield 9-0 on aggregate in the previous round, while Be'er Sheva needed a come-from-behind effort of their own, losing the first leg 2-1 away to Iceland's Vikingur Reykjavik before winning the return 2-0 to progress 3-2 on aggregate.

A win over Red Star would send Be'er Sheva into the Champions League group phase for the first time in the club's history, a step beyond even Kozhuk's title-winning season — capping a run that already includes Israel's championship, secured with a 4-2 win over Maccabi Tel Aviv.

title: Stanković fights his demons as Red Star Belgrade prepare to meet Hapoel Be'er Sheva
dek: The Red Star coach, still haunted by a 2022 Champions League elimination at the hands of Maccabi Haifa, says only the group stage will do as his side faces Israel's champions in the third qualifying round.
body: Dejan Stanković closes his eyes and pictures Red Star Belgrade lining up in the Champions League group stage. That is the only image the Serbian coach says he allows himself to see, even with a tricky Israeli obstacle standing directly in the way this week.

"I dream of leading Red Star to the Champions League," Stanković said, according to ONE. "I close my eyes and see the team in the Champions League. We could talk about the Europa League, where we have a better chance, but no. The aspiration is only the Champions League."

He was equally blunt about what failure would mean. "There will be great anger if we don't reach it. I put my head on the block. Great disappointments come from high expectations," he said, framing the tie as a test he has no intention of failing.

The demons in the article's title are not abstract. Stanković was in charge of Red Star in August 2022 when the Serbian champions were eliminated in Champions League qualifying by Maccabi Haifa, 5-4 on aggregate, undone by a late own goal in the second leg. He resigned days later, a defeat he has previously described as staying with him "like a bone in the throat."

Four years on, another Israeli team stands between him and the competition he craves. Red Star face Hapoel Be'er Sheva, the reigning Israeli champions, in the third qualifying round, with the first leg on Tuesday, August 4, at a neutral venue in Szombathely, Hungary, and the winner advancing to the playoff round — one tie from the league phase itself.

Stanković returns to Red Star's bench with real momentum behind him. Since coming back in December after a difficult spell at Spartak Moscow, he has steered the club to a sixth consecutive Serbian championship, finishing 13 points clear of the runner-up, and Red Star have blitzed their first two European qualifying rounds by a combined 9-0.

Hapoel Be'er Sheva arrive having grinded their way past Icelandic champions Víkingur Reykjavík, winning the second leg 2-0 at a neutral venue to progress 3-2 on aggregate, and go into the tie missing four players through injury.

It will be the first-ever meeting between the two clubs, though Stanković's history with Israeli opposition looms large over the build-up regardless. As a player he won everything there is to win in Europe, lifting the 2010 Champions League with Inter Milan under José Mourinho after a career built in Red Star's academy, Lazio and Inter.

For Stanković, beating an Israeli club in qualifying now carries the weight of unfinished business as much as ambition. Red Star have the aggregate scoreline and the recent history in their favour; Hapoel Be'er Sheva have already shown, against Víkingur, that they can grind out results away from home when it matters most.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv fined €40,000 and told to play behind closed doors over flares
dek: UEFA's punishment for pyrotechnics set off against Sheriff Tiraspol will empty the stands for the Europa League qualifier against CSKA Sofia.

verificationSources.label: Ynet - UEFA orders ticket sales halted

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have been fined €40,000 by UEFA's disciplinary committee and ordered to play their next European home fixture without a single fan in the stands, ONE reports, closing out a punishment process that has hung over the club since last month.

The sanction stems from pyrotechnics set off by Maccabi supporters during the club's Europa League second qualifying round tie against Sheriff Tiraspol of Moldova, a night that also produced a thumping 6-0 aggregate win — 5-0 away and 1-0 at home — to send the Yellows through to the third qualifying round.

According to the Maccabi Tel Aviv website's own account of the tie, around 700 travelling and home supporters lit flares and torches right from kickoff, the kind of display that reliably draws UEFA's attention regardless of the result on the pitch.

UEFA had already flagged the case before handing down a final ruling: Ynet reported that the governing body ordered Maccabi to halt ticket sales for the upcoming third qualifying round match against CSKA Sofia while the disciplinary process ran its course. That match will now go ahead, but with an empty stadium.

The closed-doors order applies to the first leg against the Bulgarian side, scheduled for Thursday, August 6, with the return fixture in Sofia a week later on August 13. Whoever advances from that tie enters the play-off round for a place in the Europa League league phase.

It is not the first time this season that Maccabi's fans have cost the club financially in Europe — supporters were fined €20,000 in December for racist chanting during a match in Stuttgart — and the pattern of sanctions is becoming a recurring headache for a club otherwise enjoying a strong run in the competition.

The punishment also lands awkwardly for head coach Kenny Miller, confirmed as Maccabi's permanent manager in June after leading the team to the Israeli State Cup title as caretaker. He will now have to prepare his squad for a continental qualifier played in a silent, spectator-free stadium before an away leg that could decide their European campaign.

Israeli clubs have already spent recent seasons hosting European fixtures away from home due to the security situation, often in Serbia; an empty house for the CSKA Sofia leg adds a further, self-inflicted complication to an already unusual set of circumstances for European away days that are meant to be home games.

title: Ironi Tiberias's Boys B side crowned northern champions, promoted to the national league
dek: An unbeaten campaign, the division's best attack and defence, and a title-winning coach's second crown in four years — Ironi Tiberias's youth side book their place in next season's national league.
body: Ironi Tiberias's Boys B (Ne'arim Bet) youth side have wrapped up the 2025-26 season as champions of the northern regional division, an unbeaten campaign that also secures the club a place in next season's national league, ONE reports.

The squad, coached by Moshe Ben Hamo, went the entire league programme without defeat, finishing eight points clear of the second-placed side. ONE lists the final record as 20 wins and three draws from 23 matches, with the club's own youth-football site JuniorLeague putting it slightly differently at 19 wins and three draws — both sources agree the team lost none of its games all season.

Tiberias were also the division's most potent attack and its meanest defence: ONE credits the team with 127 goals scored, comfortably the most in the league, against just 16 conceded, the fewest of any side.

The league's top scorer, according to ONE, was Uri Levi with 22 goals for the Boys B team — he added three more appearing for the club's younger Boys C side during the campaign. Yehali Ohayon (listed by ONE as scoring 20, and by JuniorLeague as 19) was the division's second-highest scorer, while defender Tomer Kobi also chipped in with three goals from the back.
"Collective discipline and tactical discipline are key factors in this achievement," Ben Hamo said, according to ONE. "Everything I asked the players to do, they did in the best way possible."

JuniorLeague's report on the same title adds further context: it is Ben Hamo's second regional championship in four years, after he led the club's Boys C side to the northern title back in the 2021-22 season. The site also notes the scale of the turnaround — Tiberias had finished only fifth in the regional table the previous season before storming to the title this time round.

The championship is more than a trophy for the youth department. Promotion to the national league next season means Tiberias's age group will now be tested against the country's strongest youth academies rather than regional opposition, a significant step up the development pathway for a club with senior-team ambitions of its own.

For now, the club can point to a squad that scored freely, defended solidly and barely dropped points all year — a platform Ben Hamo and his players will hope to build on at the higher level next season.

title: Ferran Torres on his Barcelona future: "You can never know what will happen"
dek: The World Cup-winning forward says he is contracted to Barcelona for now, but stayed carefully non-committal amid mounting reports of Paris Saint-Germain interest.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports - PSG and Barcelona set for talks, Ferran Torres "open to leaving"
Barca Blaugranes - Barcelona must pay €8m to Man City if Ferran Torres extends contract

body: Three weeks after scoring the goal that won Spain the World Cup, Ferran Torres was asked the question that has followed him into pre-season: will he still be a Barcelona player when the new La Liga campaign kicks off? His answer, reported by ONE, gave little away. "Right now I have a contract with Barcelona," Torres said, "but honestly, in football you can never know what will happen."

It is the kind of studiously careful line footballers reach for when a move is genuinely in the air, and in Torres's case the speculation has been building for weeks. Paris Saint-Germain, the reigning European champions, have been repeatedly linked with the 26-year-old, and reports in Spain and France in recent days have described the French club as going "all out" to sign him, with a basic agreement on personal terms already in place ahead of any formal talks between the two clubs.

The Luis Enrique connection only sharpens the narrative. The PSG coach managed Torres and the rest of Spain's squad through their World Cup triumph before returning to club football in Paris, and he is widely reported to be one of the driving forces behind PSG's pursuit.

Barcelona's own position is complicated by the small print of the deal that brought Torres from Manchester City. His contract at Camp Nou runs until the summer of 2027, but any extension would trigger an additional clause worth around €8 million payable to City, on top of the roughly €65 million Barcelona already paid for him in 2021 and 2022. That has left the club yet to open formal renewal talks, even as the transfer noise around Torres grows louder.

None of it has dented what he did for Spain in July. Torres came off the bench in the World Cup final against Argentina and struck the winner in extra time, in the 106th minute, as Spain won 1-0 in New Jersey to claim their second world title. It made him only the second Spaniard, after Andrés Iniesta, to score a World Cup-winning goal.

That heroics has not automatically secured his place in Hansi Flick's attacking plans for next season. Barcelona have already strengthened out wide this summer, completing deals for Newcastle's Anthony Gordon and Borussia Dortmund's Karim Adeyemi, both signed until 2031 as the club reshapes its forward line following the league title win.

For now, Torres remains a Barcelona player with no departure confirmed by either club. But his own words, and the scale of PSG's reported interest, suggest this transfer saga is only just getting started.

title: Infantino turns to the Trump administration as pressure mounts over his FIFA future
dek: After his plan to sell a stake in the World Cup's commercial rights collapsed, the FIFA president reportedly sought a show of support from the White House - only for the State Department to deny any call was even scheduled.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Infantino under pressure, turns to Trump administration
Al Jazeera - FIFA's Infantino sought Trump backing after failed World Cup stakes sell-off plan
Goal.com - FIFA responds: did Trump ignore Infantino's calls about saving his position?

body: Gianni Infantino has reached out to the Trump administration for a show of public backing as he fights to hold on to the FIFA presidency, according to a New York Post report picked up by ONE and, in turn, by the New York Times, BBC and Le Equipe.

The scramble follows the collapse of Infantino's plan to sell roughly a 20 percent stake in a new commercial entity that would have overseen FIFA's competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors - a deal that could have unlocked up to $4.2 billion and reportedly involved Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital. FIFA shelved the plan on Friday after fierce resistance from stakeholders, but the damage to Infantino's standing was already done.

UEFA led the backlash, voting to boycott FIFA competitions if the sell-off went ahead and later declaring it no longer had confidence in Infantino's leadership. Wales's football association withdrew its support for his re-election bid, and England was reported to be considering following suit.

The unrest reached inside FIFA's own headquarters. Chief operating officer Kevin Lamour told the Associated Press he felt "deceived," saying he had known nothing of the secret talks behind the deal, and reports described an internal push among FIFA executives - nicknamed "Project Kill the Monster" - aimed at forcing Infantino out.

Against that backdrop, Infantino was said to have arranged private talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. One source told the New York Post the stated purpose was to discuss how football could serve as "a form of soft power for America," while adding: "we all know it is about protecting the position."

FIFA and the US State Department quickly pushed back on that framing. Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs Dylan Johnson said there were "no plans" for Rubio to speak with Infantino and "no call this morning," and FIFA itself denied any such meeting had been scheduled.

The episode has also exposed cracks in a relationship Infantino has cultivated closely with Donald Trump - the two appeared together at the World Cup final on July 19, and Infantino presented Trump with FIFA's inaugural Peace Prize back in December. Since the sell-off plan fell apart, however, Infantino has reportedly tried repeatedly to reach Trump by phone without success, leaving him, in the words of people close to the situation, increasingly isolated.

With his re-election bid now facing open opposition from national federations and his own executives, the coming weeks look set to test whether Infantino's political relationships can outlast the fallout from a deal that never even got off the ground.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv eye Red Star winger Owusu as Loizou replacement
dek: The Tel Aviv club have made initial inquiries for Ghanaian-Serbian winger Douglas Owusu, but Red Star Belgrade's asking price is proving a stumbling block, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv — Loizou on his Red Star move

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv are looking back toward Belgrade for their next piece of transfer business, just weeks after selling their prize academy winger there in a club-record deal. ONE reports that the Tel Aviv club have opened an inquiry for Red Star Belgrade winger Douglas Owusu as they search for a replacement for the departed Loizos Loizou.

According to the report, Hapoel's professional staff have already made initial contact over Owusu, whom they view as "a fast player with high individual ability" and rate highly enough to have identified him as a direct alternative to Loizou in the squad.

The obstacle, ONE says, is money. Red Star are said to be demanding roughly €2.2 million for the winger — a figure well beyond what Hapoel have earmarked for the position, leaving the deal, in the outlet's words, "far from simple" at this stage of the window.

Hapoel are not ruling it out entirely, though. Per the report, the club could revisit the move later in the transfer window if Red Star's valuation comes down, rather than walking away from the target outright.

The interest comes with an obvious backstory. Loizou, the Cypriot winger who came through Hapoel's system, completed his own move to Red Star this summer in a transfer reported at up to €3.8 million — the biggest sale in the Tel Aviv club's history — after signing a four-year contract in Belgrade.

Owusu, an 18-year-old winger who holds both Ghanaian and Serbian citizenship, only joined Red Star himself in January 2026 from fellow Serbian side Radnik Surdulica, and went on to win the Serbian Super Liga title in his first months at the club.

For now, the story is an early-stage inquiry rather than an active negotiation, and any move would hinge on Red Star softening their financial demands as Hapoel continue reshaping their attack for the season ahead.

title: Hapoel Holon chief Lanziano to Hapoel Tel Aviv owner Yanai: focus on your own team
dek: Amid a 13-1 league vote to curb newly naturalized players, Eitan Lanziano used a radio slot to needle Ofer Yanai over Hapoel Tel Aviv's lone dissent - and to lay out Holon's shrinking budget for next season.
body: Eitan Lanziano rarely misses a chance to speak his mind, and on ONE's "Today's Conversation" show this week the Hapoel Holon chairman used the platform to send an unusually pointed message to Ofer Yanai, the owner of Hapoel Tel Aviv, in the middle of Israeli basketball's row over naturalized players.

The backdrop is a proposal pushed through by Maccabi Tel Aviv chairman Shimon Mizrahi and Bnei Herzliya owner Eldad Akunis, which would stop a player who naturalizes to represent Israel's national team from being registered as a domestic "Israeli" player in the league for two years afterward. When it came to a vote among the Premier League's clubs, 13 backed the measure - only Hapoel Tel Aviv voted against it.

Lanziano did not hide his irritation at Hapoel Tel Aviv's stance. "No matter what they propose, they're always against it," he said of the club, adding that he hoped the vote would prove to be "the right and just decision."

He went further, framing the lopsided count as a sign of dysfunction rather than principle. Thirteen clubs, he argued, rarely agree on anything - yet on this issue they lined up unanimously against a single dissenter, which he read as evidence of a wider lack of solidarity in the league rather than a considered objection from Hapoel Tel Aviv.

That set up the line that gave the interview its headline: a direct message to Yanai to "focus on his own team in basketball and less on what's around him." Lanziano added that he wished Hapoel Tel Aviv success in Europe this season, but said he was "too small" to be offering Yanai advice.

The conversation then turned to Holon's own finances, and Lanziano did not sugarcoat the picture. The club's budget for the coming season has slipped from roughly 17-18 million shekels a year ago to about 16 million now, even as some rivals in the capital and Tel Aviv continue to spend heavily on imported talent.

That gap didn't rattle him. "It doesn't matter how many foreigners they bring in - only five can play," he said, before adding that Holon would simply do "what we've done in previous years" - compete on a leaner roster against far richer clubs.

Asked what he would do with a much bigger budget, Lanziano kept his ambitions modest and specific: "I don't need 200 million. Give me 50," he said of a hypothetical domestic boost, and for a Eurocup campaign, "give me 100... I'll compete, not win. I won't exaggerate or make empty promises."

It was a characteristically blunt outing from one of Israeli basketball's more combative club chairmen - part defense of a rule change that squarely benefits the league's established powers, part running commentary on a Hapoel Tel Aviv ownership he clearly feels is punching above its seniority.

title: Kvaratskhelia rolls into PSG training in a new electric Rolls-Royce
dek: The Georgian winger turned heads at PSG's Campus base this week, arriving for pre-season training in a Rolls-Royce Spectre reportedly worth close to half a million euros.
body: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia found a new way to make an entrance when Paris Saint-Germain reported back for pre-season training at the Campus PSG in late July: he pulled up in a brand-new, fully electric Rolls-Royce Spectre.

ONE's motoring desk reports that the Georgian winger's arrival stopped teammates and staff in their tracks, with the gleaming coupe drawing far more attention around the training pitches than the session itself.

The Spectre is Rolls-Royce's first fully electric model, powered by two motors producing roughly 585 horsepower and capable of 0-100 km/h in about 4.5 seconds, according to ONE, which also noted the car's signature starlight headliner and rear-hinged coach doors. Depending on specification, the model is priced anywhere from roughly $422,000 to $600,000; French outlet Foot Parisien, which separately reported on the same appearance, put Kvaratskhelia's particular car at about €429,000.
It caps a lucrative and decorated stretch for the 25-year-old, who arrived in Paris from Napoli in January 2025 and was a key figure as PSG swept to a domestic and European treble in 2025-26.

There was no suggestion in either report of any football business behind the visit — simply a star player treating himself before diving into preparations for the new Ligue 1 and Champions League campaign.
As ONE put it, on the pitch or off it, Kvaratskhelia "knows exactly how to steal the show."

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv drawn against Atalanta in toughest possible Conference League test
dek: Israel's European hopefuls must first eliminate Poland's Katowice before a playoff meeting looms with Atalanta, the Italian side who won the Europa League in 2024.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com – Conference League third qualifying round draw
Atalanta BC official site – playoff draw confirmation
ESPN – Ludogorets 2-2 Hapoel Tel Aviv match report

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv now know exactly what could be waiting for them at the business end of Conference League qualifying, and it does not get much tougher. Thursday's UEFA playoff draw in Nyon paired the Israeli side with Atalanta, the Italian club who won the Europa League just two years ago — but only if Hapoel first get past a qualifying tie against Poland's GKS Katowice. ONE described it simply as "the hardest there is."

That qualifier comes first. Hapoel face Katowice in the Conference League's third qualifying round, with the first leg on Thursday, August 6, and the return a week later in Poland on August 12. Because of the security situation in Israel, Hapoel's home leg will again be played at their adopted European base, DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary.

Katowice arrive off the back of their own comeback story, having beaten Slovakia's MŠK Žilina to reach this round. It is no gimme tie for the Israeli side, who will need to manage a two-legged, cross-continental trip before they can even think about Bergamo.

Hapoel's own path to this point has already carried some drama. They eliminated Bulgarian champions Ludogorets Razgrad 4-2 on aggregate, sealing the win with a 2-2 draw away in Razgrad in which forward Emmanuel Boateng scored twice — the second, in the 58th minute, effectively closing out the tie after Ludogorets had briefly threatened a comeback.

Should Hapoel get past Katowice, the reward is a playoff tie against Atalanta, with the first leg in Bergamo on August 20 and the return, again in Miskolc, on August 27. It would be a first taste of continental group-phase football for the Israeli club in well over a decade if they can navigate both rounds.

Atalanta, for their part, are entering the Conference League for the first time in the club's history, having finished seventh in Serie A last season — a campaign that saw them fall short of the Champions League places they had grown used to occupying in recent years.

The Italian side remain one of the more fashionable names in European football regardless of their league finish. Atalanta lifted the Europa League in 2024, thrashing Bayer Leverkusen 3-0 in the Dublin final on the back of an Ademola Lookman hat-trick, ending a 61-year wait for a major trophy.

They go into this campaign under Raffaele Palladino, who took over as head coach in November 2025 after Ivan Jurić was dismissed. Palladino has been backed to keep Atalanta competitive on multiple fronts, and a Conference League run would be a new experience for a club more used to Champions League nights at what is now known as the New Balance Arena in Bergamo.

For Hapoel, simply reaching that stage would be a considerable achievement, let alone competing with a squad of Atalanta's Serie A pedigree. But European football for Israeli clubs has been defined this year by matches played far from home as much as by results on the pitch, and Miskolc's DVTK Stadium will again be the improbable stage if the Katowice tie goes their way.
Nothing is decided yet. Thursday's draw only sets the shape of the road ahead — first Katowice, then, potentially, one of Italian football's most talked-about clubs of the last two seasons.

title: Halfon tells Haziza: Netanya is your chance to reclaim the spotlight
dek: Netanya great Podi Halfon says Dolev Haziza, cut loose by Maccabi Haifa, can be "a king" at his new club if he seizes the moment

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Toto Cup match report

body: Dolev Haziza spent much of the summer feeling unwanted. Now, according to one of Maccabi Netanya's most decorated former players, he has landed exactly where he needs to be to prove Maccabi Haifa wrong.

Podi Halfon, a Netanya icon from the club's celebrated sides of the late 1970s and early 1980s and now a regular sports commentator, used an appearance this week to address Haziza directly. "You arrived at Netanya - this is your opportunity to return to the spotlight," Halfon said, according to ONE. "Take the players and lead them. You can be a king in Netanya."

The message carries weight because of the manner of Haziza's exit from Haifa. After seven years at the club, the 31-year-old winger was told by sporting director Lior Rafalov this summer that he no longer figured in the team's plans - a conversation Haziza reportedly did not see coming, having believed he might finish his career in the port city. He completed a move to Netanya in late July.

Halfon suggested the psychological toll of that rejection might have hit Haziza harder than an earlier setback at Haifa, and offered him some perspective on age: "31 today is like 23 back then," he said, framing Netanya as a genuine second act rather than a wind-down posting.

The comments landed the day after Netanya's Toto Cup rhythm was interrupted. Roni Levy's side, unbeaten in their two previous outings this pre-season, were beaten 3-2 by newly-promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan at Miriam Stadium on Sunday, in round three of the competition. Luan Campos put Ramat Gan ahead before Maor Levi teed up Matias Dabbah to level, only for David Asnake and Maxim Falkushchenko to restore and extend the visitors' lead in the second half. Dabbah's stoppage-time consolation, set up by Haziza on his full debut, arrived too late.
Halfon was pointed about the manner of the defeat, singling out "a serious mistake by Grigory Morozov" on Ramat Gan's opening goal as symptomatic of the sloppiness that undid two good results.

That did not stop him using the result to press a wider argument about Netanya's ambitions this season. The club is reportedly targeting a finish in the fourth-to-sixth range, but Halfon wants more. "I would aim higher," he said. "I want to reach the day when Netanya declares it wants to compete for every title."

Levy, back for a second spell in charge of Netanya after being appointed in January 2026 to replace Yossi Abukasis, now has a pre-season audience watching closely to see whether Haziza's arrival - and Halfon's endorsement of it - translates into results once the Israeli Premier League campaign begins in earnest.

title: Alonso faces selection headache as Chelsea swell to 41 players
dek: The new Blues boss admits trimming the squad is inevitable after a summer spending spree approaching €400m, with Jordan Henderson and Pep Chavarría still to arrive at Stamford Bridge.

verificationSources.label: Chelsea FC – Xabi Alonso appointed manager

body: Xabi Alonso has been in the Chelsea job barely a month, and already he has a problem most managers would envy on paper but dread in practice: too many players.

According to ONE, the Spaniard, who took over at Stamford Bridge on a four-year deal after Chelsea finished sixth in the Premier League last season and missed out on European football entirely, now has 41 senior players at his disposal. With only 11 starting spots and five substitutes permitted per match, and no continental campaign to help spread the load, the numbers simply do not add up.

That is despite owner Todd Boehly having already committed close to €400m in transfer spending this summer. Chelsea are still not done: ONE reports the club remains in the market for Jordan Henderson, the former Liverpool captain who left Brentford and is reported by multiple outlets to be closing in on a free-transfer move to west London, and Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarría, with reports elsewhere in the past few days pointing to an agreement worth around €25m.

Adding further to the congestion, Mykhailo Mudryk has resumed team training after the Court of Arbitration for Sport partially upheld his appeal against a doping suspension, ruling his ban should run only as long as time already served. The Ukrainian winger had been frozen out of Cobham since late 2024.

Among the summer's marquee arrivals is Morgan Rogers, signed from Aston Villa for a fee reported at £117m, a deal that made him the club's record signing and, by some counts, the most expensive British player ever sold.

Alonso, for his part, has been careful not to commit to a target figure for his final squad. "Not too many, but also not too few. Exactly how many? I cannot state a number," he said, quoted by ONE. "We must maintain options, as we may face injuries and changing circumstances."

He was more direct about what comes next. "We must remember that there will likely continue to be some movement," Alonso said — an acknowledgement that follows several sales already this summer, with ONE reporting further departures, whether permanent exits or loans, are effectively unavoidable before the window closes.

For a club under BlueCo ownership that has churned through five permanent managers since 2022, the task now facing Alonso is as much about subtraction as addition: turning a swollen, expensively assembled squad into a coherent group capable of competing on only one front this season.

title: Armoni Brooks turns down Maccabi Tel Aviv, set to sign for Valencia Basket
dek: ONE reports the American guard's flirtation with Maccabi has ended over security concerns about relocating to Israel, sending him to Valencia as ASVEL's financial collapse forces him back onto the market.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's chase for backcourt reinforcement Armoni Brooks appears to be over, and not the way the club hoped. ONE reports that the American guard is instead heading for Valencia Basket, with the Israeli champions' advanced talks with him breaking down.

Brooks became available after his own club, ASVEL Villeurbanne — the French project built around Tony Parker — was forced to slash its operating budget from roughly 59 million euros to around 24 million after a major funding source fell through. Multiple European outlets reported the club is now working through unpaid dues to last season's squad and shedding recently signed players it can no longer afford, Brooks among them.

That sudden availability had made him one of the more coveted names on the market, and Maccabi moved quickly. According to ONE, the Israeli club held advanced negotiations and viewed the 28-year-old as an ideal fit to strengthen the guard rotation — with one added motive: insurance against a possible exit for Lonnie Walker IV, who is reportedly working toward a mutual split from Maccabi despite still being under contract, with Partizan Belgrade among the suitors.

But per ONE's reporting, the deal foundered not over money but over Brooks' own reservations about relocating to Israel with his family given the security situation in the country. The outlet says that concern, rather than any competing financial offer, was the decisive factor in him looking elsewhere.

Valencia is where ONE says he will land for next season. Spanish outlet Deportevalenciano separately reported the club is in advanced conversations with Brooks, describing him as fitting the scoring, three-point shooting profile Valencia wants to add to its backcourt. It's worth noting the picture elsewhere in Europe has been less settled — Sportando and other outlets had Real Madrid as the frontrunner for Brooks in recent days, with Valencia, Partizan and Crvena Zvezda all also in the mix — so the move has not yet been formally announced by either Valencia or Brooks himself.

Brooks is no stranger to big-name European suitors chasing him. The Waco, Texas-born guard went undrafted out of Houston in 2019 and bounced through the G League before NBA stints with the Rockets, Raptors and Nets. He moved to Europe in 2024, joining Olimpia Milano, where he won last season's Italian league and cup double and was named MVP of the Italian Cup — form that made him a EuroLeague-wide target the moment ASVEL's finances collapsed.

For Maccabi, missing out on Brooks leaves the backcourt question unresolved just as the Walker situation drags on. The club has been busy elsewhere this window, with reported moves for Daniel Theis and Armando Bacot, but a proven, three-point shooting guard of Brooks' recent pedigree does not come around often on the open market in early August.

ASVEL, for its part, is reportedly turning to Kyler Edwards as a possible replacement for Brooks, part of a broader scramble to reshape a roster that was meant to challenge for Europe's top honors before the budget news hit.

title: Beitar Jerusalem learn potential Conference League playoff foes: Braga or Dinamo Minsk
dek: Beitar's reward for eliminating AEK Larnaca on penalties is a daunting third-round tie with Austria Vienna – and the winner of a Braga-Dinamo Minsk playoff pairing waiting for whoever comes through.
body: Beitar Jerusalem now know exactly what stands between them and a place in the Conference League's league phase for the first time in the club's history, ONE reported on Monday: the winner of a playoff pairing between Portugal's Braga and Belarusian side Dinamo Minsk.

The catch is that the reward is entirely conditional. Almog Cohen's side must first get past Austria Vienna in the third qualifying round, a tie that opens at Teddy Stadium on Thursday, August 6, before the return leg in Vienna a week later on August 13.
Only if Beitar eliminate the Austrian club would the Braga-or-Dinamo-Minsk fixture become relevant, with the playoff round set for August 20 and 27 and Beitar hosting the first leg.

It is a route into territory Beitar have never reached. As ONE put it, the club has still never tasted a European campaign that runs into the winter — something a playoff-round appearance, let alone progression into the league phase itself, would finally deliver.

Getting this far already required nerve. Beitar won the first leg of their second qualifying round tie away to AEK Larnaca 1-0, but needed a dramatic penalty shootout to see out the Cypriot side and reach the third round, underlining how fine the margins have been on this run.

Austria Vienna, one of Austrian football's most decorated clubs, represent a significant step up in profile from Larnaca, and their own path to the playoff would run through the same Braga-Dinamo Minsk winner that awaits Beitar if Cohen's team turns the tie the other way.

For now, the immediate task is simple and unforgiving: beat Austria Vienna over two legs, starting at home this Thursday, or the conversation about Braga, Dinamo Minsk and a first European winter never gets past the hypothetical stage.

body: Genia Berkman, the face and captain of Hapoel Nof HaGalil for the better part of two decades, is leaving the club. ONE reports that the 34-year-old defender has ended a 16-year association with the institution and signed with Hapoel Beit She'an.

It is the end of an era in the Lower Galilee. Berkman joined as a boy at the club's academy when it still played under the name Hapoel Nazareth Illit, rose through every age group and eventually became captain of the senior side, missing only a two-year stretch away at Hapoel Kfar Saba between 2018 and 2020.

By ONE's count he leaves with 496 official appearances and more than 40 goals in club colours, one of the most durable and recognisable careers in Israel's regional leagues over the past decade and a half.

"I'm leaving with my head held high, knowing I gave everything of myself," Berkman said in a statement carried by ONE, describing a club that "shaped me as a person" and taught him about "commitment, loyalty, sacrifice and true love for the symbol." He acknowledged, too, that "not always does the ending look like we dreamed," before thanking coaches, teammates, staff and supporters for the years together.

Along the way Berkman was part of a promotion, a Toto Cup triumph and a run to the State Cup semi-final, honours that made him something close to a totem for a club still known to many veteran fans by its old name.

The farewell comes at a low point for Nof HaGalil, who were relegated to Liga Alef this past season after finishing bottom of the pack in the relegation playoff group, a drop that has reshaped the squad the captain is now leaving behind.

His next stop, Hapoel Beit She'an, plays in the same Liga Alef North division, meaning Berkman effectively swaps dressing rooms rather than levels — a lateral move for a player evidently determined to keep playing regularly rather than wind down.

For Nof HaGalil, the task now is rebuilding without the player who had been synonymous with the club through relegations, promotions and cup runs alike; for Berkman, a new chapter starts a short drive south, at a club chasing its own climb back up the pyramid.

title: Moshe Sabag confirms 'offer with a lot of money' as Kiryat Gat eyes Liga Leumit return
dek: The manager who rebuilt Kiryat Gat's football project from the fourth tier says a rival club made an approach, but for now insists his focus stays on the team he calls 'my baby.'

body: Moshe Sabag has spent five years dragging Kiryat Gat football back from the dead, and on Sunday he revealed that someone else has noticed the work he has done.

Appearing on the "Sicha HaYom" podcast, the club's professional manager said a rival had been in touch about poaching him. "Yesterday a club contacted me," Sabag said, before confirming, when pressed, that the approach came with "an offer with a lot of money." ONE reports that the interested club is Hapoel Nir Ramat Hasharon, a Liga Alef side relegated from Liga Leumit last season.
Sabag played it down rather than confirm any move. "It doesn't matter," he said of the offer, while stopping short of ruling out a future away from the club he helped build from nothing.

That reluctance is easy to understand given the story he has authored in Kiryat Gat. The original Maccabi Kiryat Gat, which had spent two spells in Liga Leumit earlier this century, collapsed under accumulated debt in 2020. Sabag, a former player at the club, refounded it with Ilan Kanfo that year in Liga Gimel, the fourth tier of Israeli football.

The rebuild has been rapid. Kiryat Gat won promotion to Liga Alef at the end of the 2024/25 season, and by the end of March 2026 had gone up again, securing a return to Liga Leumit for the first time in over a decade.

On the podcast, Sabag described the current men's squad — the one he calls "my baby" — as "young and good, with some experienced veterans and foreign players," and said he was confident the group would hold its own at the higher level this season.

One problem still trails the club's rise: it has no home ground. Kiryat Gat currently trains in the nearby town of Sha'arayim and plays its home fixtures in Rehovot. Sabag said work has now begun on a permanent solution, a new stadium in Kiryat Gat with roughly 6,000 seats.

He also addressed the women's side, which he oversees alongside the men's team. Several of Israel's leading female players have been leaving for soccer scholarships in the United States, Sabag said, including two of his own squad members. In response, the club has brought in Zohar Kaminski as the new coach, with Sabag saying he believes she can restore the team to championship contention.
For now, Kiryat Gat's growth and its search for a permanent home look set to remain Sabag's priority — even with a payday from Ramat Hasharon reportedly on the table.
