title: Hansi Flick says Orian Goren has "tremendous quality" — and the Israeli teenager is proving it
dek: Barcelona's manager singled out the 17-year-old from Savyon among a cluster of La Masia prospects shining in preseason, saying this year's crop of youngsters is the strongest of his tenure.

verificationSources.label: Barca Universal (English translation of Flick's remarks)

body: Hansi Flick has publicly vouched for Orian Goren, telling reporters during Barcelona's preseason that the Israeli teenager "has tremendous quality and he's proving it," according to ONE.

The endorsement came as Flick was asked about the crop of La Masia academy players he has folded into first-team training this summer, a group Goren has been a prominent part of since Barcelona's tour and warm-up fixtures in England last month.

Flick framed his answer around a wider point about the squad he now has at his disposal. "When I compare it with my first year here in 2024, I think this season we have more quality," he said. "More quality in the squad, more quality among the young players, and more quality from La Masia."
Within that assessment, he picked out two names specifically: Ebrima Tunkara and Goren. "Ebrima is a great talent," Flick said. "And Orian as well."

It is the latest sign of how far Goren has risen in barely three years at the club. Born in Savyon on March 15, 2009, he joined Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth department at eight before his family relocated to Spain, where he passed trials to enter Barcelona's academy in his early teens.

Barcelona handed him his first professional contract at 16, a deal running to 2028, and he made his senior debut for the club in a preseason friendly this summer — becoming, by some distance, one of the youngest players to appear for Flick's first team. He has also represented Israel at under-17 level.

Tunkara, the other player Flick highlighted, is even younger. The 16-year-old, born in Gambia, has been one of the stories of Barcelona's preseason and was named player of the tournament at this summer's under-17 European Championship after a run of a goal and four assists.

A third academy graduate, 18-year-old Xavi Espart, has also been drawn regularly into first-team training under Flick and already has senior minutes to his name, having come on as a substitute in a Champions League match against Newcastle United in March.

None of it guarantees Goren regular football with Barcelona's senior side this season — he is expected, for now, to continue his development with the reserve team, Barça Atlètic — but Flick's willingness to name him unprompted, alongside a squad that includes Lamine Yamal and Pedri, is itself the headline in Catalonia.

For Israeli football, still working out how to turn rare talents like Goren into a durable pipeline to Europe's top clubs, that kind of comment from a manager who has just won the league and is chasing more silverware this season carries real weight.

body: Willy Agada wants to go back to Haifa. ONE reports that the Nigerian striker is pushing for a second spell at Hapoel Haifa and is currently waiting on the club to come back to him with acceptable contract terms, even as a rival Israeli suitor circles with a richer offer.

That rival is Bnei Sakhnin, who according to the report are currently putting more money on the table than Hapoel Haifa for the 26-year-old forward. Agada, for his part, is said to be holding out for Haifa's answer rather than jumping straight to the higher bidder — a sign of how fondly he remembers his first stint at Sammy Ofer Stadium.

That fondness is easy to explain. Agada arrived at Hapoel Haifa on loan for the 2020/21 season and finished as the club's second-highest scorer with six league goals, including two crucial strikes in the relegation round that helped steer the team clear of the drop. Across his time there he scored eight goals in 30 appearances.

His career kept climbing after Haifa. He moved on to Hapoel Jerusalem, then crossed the Atlantic for Major League Soccer, scoring 27 goals in 103 appearances for Sporting Kansas City and Real Salt Lake. In January this year he returned to Europe on a free transfer to Real Zaragoza in Spain's second tier — a move that now appears to have run its course, with the striker back on the market and Israel back on his radar.

Hapoel Haifa's transfer business isn't limited to Agada's saga. Dutch winger Jayden Braaf, who has come through Manchester City's academy system and had spells at Borussia Dortmund, Udinese and Fortuna Sittard, has arrived in Israel and started training with the club on trial.

Manager Haim Silbes is said to be treating the Braaf audition with caution, weighing the 23-year-old's undoubted talent against a history of injuries and past disciplinary issues before deciding whether to hand him a contract.

Off the pitch, Hapoel Haifa used the moment to present their home jersey for the 2026/27 season: a red-and-black design with stripes across the shirt, fronted by a graphic rendering of the letter "H" for Hapoel Haifa.

The kit reveal lands with the club in good form. Hapoel Haifa beat local rivals Maccabi Haifa 3-2 in their Toto Cup derby and sit well placed in their group as they push for a place in the competition's semi-finals.
For now, though, the headline business remains unresolved: whether Hapoel Haifa move quickly enough to beat Sakhnin's offer and bring their old No.9 home.

title: Tech billionaire Nikesh Arora leads $1bn bid for NBA Europe's London franchise
dek: Palo Alto Networks chief spearheads a consortium chasing one of the new league's most coveted licences, as more than 120 groups circle 12 target cities ahead of a planned 2027 launch.
body: The battle for ownership of NBA Europe's flagship London franchise has produced the league's biggest number yet: a bid of more than $1 billion, roughly £740 million, led by Palo Alto Networks chief executive Nikesh Arora, ONE reports.

Arora, 58, has assembled an investor consortium chasing what the report describes as one of the most prestigious and sought-after licences in the planned competition. He is no stranger to sports ownership, having previously fronted the 'Tech Titans' group that bought a 49% stake in the London Spirit cricket franchise for £145 million.

The London market is not short of suitors. Qatar's QSI, which owns Paris Saint-Germain, has been linked to a Paris franchise, while the RedBird fund behind AC Milan is pursuing a licence in its own city. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has also been mentioned as circling the London slot, underlining how contested the capital's franchise has become.

Independent reporting from ESPN and Sportico confirms the scale of interest: more than 120 prospective ownership groups have lodged initial proposals across the NBA's 12 target cities, with bids spanning from $500 million up to and beyond the $1 billion mark in the most competitive markets.

Those 12 cities are London, Paris, Milan, Madrid, Barcelona, Berlin, Munich, Athens, Istanbul, Rome, Lyon and Manchester. Twelve will hold permanent franchises in the new competition, with four further places determined annually through a qualifying system, taking the league to 16 teams in total.

NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the response from investors reflected serious confidence in the project. 'We're extremely encouraged by the final bids we received for permanent franchises in a new NBA and FIBA-backed league in Europe, which reflect the tremendous interest and momentum around this project,' Tatum said, adding that it represents 'the biggest influx of capital European basketball has ever seen.'

Commissioner Adam Silver has previously said the league is targeting a launch in the second half of 2027, run in partnership with FIBA, world basketball's governing body, which has long overseen Europe's domestic and continental club competitions.

No sale has been completed and the NBA has not publicly confirmed an ownership group for London or any other city — the figures reported so far describe bids, not finalised agreements, and the process of awarding franchises is still ongoing.

Still, the scale of the numbers signals how the NBA sees the European project: a business bet on basketball's growth on the continent large enough to draw tech billionaires, sovereign wealth funds and football club owners into the same bidding war for a sport that, in most of these markets, does not yet have a top-flight professional home.

title: If Beer Sheva get past Red Star, Aarhus or Sabah await in Champions League playoff
dek: Sport5 maps out Hapoel Beer Sheva's route to the Champions League league phase — and the seeding boost a win over Red Star Belgrade would bring.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv on the Red Star draw

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva's Champions League ambitions still hinge entirely on getting past Red Star Belgrade, but Sport5 reported on Sunday that the next round of the draw has already sharpened the picture of exactly what awaits if they do.

Ran Kozuk's side face the Serbian giants in the third qualifying round, with the second leg in Beer Sheva scheduled for August 11 after the first leg in Belgrade. Win that tie, and a place among the competition's final 36 teams would be just one round away.

That prize is a playoff-round meeting with the winner of Aarhus GF of Denmark against Sabah FK of Azerbaijan, who face off for the right to play whoever emerges from the Israel-Serbia tie. First legs are pencilled in for August 18-19, with the return legs a week later on August 25-26.

There is a silver lining even in a daunting assignment: because Red Star carry a considerably higher UEFA coefficient than the Israeli champions, Beer Sheva would enter the playoff draw as the seeded side if they get through — avoiding heavyweight names such as Celtic, Dinamo Zagreb or Slovan Bratislava, according to Sport5.

Sabah, based in Baku, are not unfamiliar to Israeli football. Founded only in 2017, the Azerbaijani side won their first national championship last season and have already left a mark on an Israeli club in Europe, eliminating Maccabi Haifa on penalties in Conference League qualifying in August 2024.

Aarhus arrive with rather more history behind them. The 145-year-old Danish club won their first league title in 40 years this past season and reached this stage of the Champions League path with a dramatic penalty-shootout victory over Poland's Lech Poznań.

Should Beer Sheva instead lose to Red Star, their European campaign would not be over: the club would drop into the Europa League playoff round against Viktoria Plzeň of the Czech Republic, with legs scheduled for August 20 and 27, Sport5 reported.

For now, though, every scenario is still theoretical. None of it matters unless Beer Sheva can do what no Israeli champion has yet managed against Red Star Belgrade — win the tie and keep alive a bid to reach the Champions League league phase for the first time in the club's history.

title: Beat CSKA Sofia and Maccabi Tel Aviv will meet Crete's OFI in the Europa League play-off
dek: The draw has paired the winner of Thursday's tie against the Bulgarians with OFI Crete, a club with a fresh Israeli connection through returning midfielder Dan Glazer.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC official site

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv still have a Bulgarian hurdle to clear, but Sport5 reports that UEFA's conditional draw has already sketched out what comes next: if the yellow-and-blue get past CSKA Sofia, their Europa League play-off opponent will be OFI Crete, the surprise package of Greek football this season.

First things first. Maccabi host CSKA Sofia in the third qualifying round at Bloomfield Stadium, with the first leg on August 6 and the return in Sofia a week later on August 13. Win that tie and a place in the play-off round — one step from the Europa League league stage itself — awaits.

According to the draw outlined by Sport5, the play-off would pit Maccabi against OFI Crete over two legs, the first away in Greece on August 20, the return eight days later on August 27. That home leg, per ONE's reporting, would once again be staged in Batumi, Georgia — the neutral venue Israeli clubs have continued to use for home European fixtures amid the ongoing security situation.

OFI Crete arrive as one of the feel-good stories of the Greek season. Founded in 1925 and based at the 26,240-capacity Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion, the club won the Greek Cup for the first time since 1987 in April, beating PAOK 3-2 after extra time, with Aaron Leya Iseka converting the decisive penalty. That triumph guarantees OFI a league-stage European campaign for the first time in the club's history — at minimum in the Conference League, with the Europa League play-off offering a route to the bigger prize.

Before this run, OFI's only previous continental experience was a brief entry into the 1995-96 Intertoto Cup three decades ago, making their current campaign uncharted territory for a club used to mid-table Super League Greece football.

Sport5 flags two attacking names to watch if the tie materialises: Taxiarchis Foundas, the Greek winger who was OFI's leading scorer with nine league goals last season, and Argentine winger Tiago Nunes, both valued in the region of €1.5-2 million.

There is also a personal thread running through the potential pairing. Dan Glazer, the Israel international midfielder who rejoined Maccabi Tel Aviv this summer, spent the 2023-24 season in Crete, making 27 appearances for OFI before moving on to Russia's Pari Nizhny Novgorod and then Kairat Almaty, where he won the Kazakhstan title and reached the Champions League. Should the tie go ahead, Glazer would face the club where his European journey began.

The stakes for Maccabi go beyond one attractive fixture. Should they instead lose to CSKA Sofia, ONE reports they would drop into the Conference League play-off, where possible opponents include Braga, Dinamo Minsk and Dinamo Kyiv — a reminder of how much hinges on this week's meeting with the Bulgarians before any Crete trip becomes real.

title: Shtilman raises Maccabi Tel Aviv bid to $150m, gives Recanati family a Sunday deadline
dek: The Rapyd founder says refusing his improved offer for the Recanati family's 58% stake would be "insane", as the battle for control of the basketball club intensifies
body: Arik Shtilman, the Rapyd founder and Maccabi Tel Aviv's main shirt sponsor, has turned up the pressure on the Recanati family, telling ONE's "Sicha Hayom" programme that refusing his latest takeover bid for the club would be "insane".

Shtilman has submitted an improved offer to buy the Recanati family's 58% stake in the basketball club for $120 million — a $20 million premium on the price Udi and Shai Recanati paid to acquire the Federmann family's shares earlier this year — plus a further $30 million he is prepared to inject directly into the club's coffers to strengthen the roster.

According to the offer, reported by Walla Sport and Sport1, the additional $30 million investment would not dilute any other shareholder's holding, with the stated aim of putting Maccabi back among Europe's elite.
Shtilman has set a deadline of Sunday for the Recanati family to respond, Sport1 reports, having delivered the proposal directly to Udi and Shai Recanati.

It is Shtilman's second attempt to force his way into full control. He had originally agreed, via the Federmann family's Fedanco Sports vehicle, to buy a 50% stake in Fedanco — effectively 14.5% of the club — and join the board. That deal collapsed in July when the Recanati family exercised its right of first refusal, buying out Fedanco's entire 29% holding for $50 million and lifting their own stake to 58%, freezing Shtilman out.

About a week and a half ago Shtilman came back with a $100 million bid for the full 58% Recanati holding, only to raise it again to the current $120 million-plus-$30 million package after the family did not engage, according to Ynet.

On air, Shtilman argued any rational owner would take the money, framing his offer as fair value plus a premium and pointing to his willingness to leave the Recanatis a minority stake of 5-10% if they wished to remain involved.

He also dismissed a rival bid from the American businessman Jason Levin, who has been negotiating with the Recanati family to buy roughly half of their holding for around $50 million, telling ONE that Levin lacks the financial firepower to properly back the club.

The saga has become one of the most closely watched ownership sagas in Israeli basketball this summer, with Maccabi Tel Aviv — 12-time Israeli champions and six-time EuroLeague winners — caught between competing suitors while its playing budget and European ambitions hang in the balance.

dek: Ironi Tiberias trained on Monday for Tuesday's Toto Cup finale against a Maccabi Haifa side already out of contention, with talks over Slobodan Drapić stalled and Eliran Hudeda still suspended.

body: Ironi Tiberias trained on Monday with one eye on a Toto Cup fixture that carries no real stakes and another on a coaching search that is dragging into its second month, according to ONE.

The club hosts Maccabi Haifa at Sammy Ofer Stadium on Tuesday at 20:00 in the fourth and final round of their group-stage section, with both sides already eliminated from playoff contention. Tiberias go in with three points from three matches, while Maccabi Haifa remain winless after two games and have nothing left to play for beyond pride and squad rotation.

The bigger story in Tiberias remains the empty seat on the bench. Head coach Eliran Hudeda has been provisionally suspended since early July, after Israel's National Anti-Doping Agency opened a case into banned saline infusions allegedly administered to players before a match, a scandal that also touched the club's technical staff, Haaretz has reported.

Slobodan Drapić, the veteran Serbian-Israeli coach who has previously managed Beitar Jerusalem, Ironi Kiryat Shmona and Bnei Sakhnin among others, remains the leading candidate to take over, ONE said, but no agreement has been reached with him or with any alternative. The sides are stuck on contract terms and, specifically, on an exit clause that would let Tiberias part ways with Drapić should Hudeda's suspension eventually be lifted and he return to the touchline.

On the pitch, the club is weighing its options with winger Nana Gamble, an Ivorian import who has divided opinion among the coaching staff — technically comfortable on the ball but, in the staff's view, lacking the pace to hold down a regular spot. A final call on his future is expected only after Tuesday's match, ONE reported.

Tiberias will not be moving for Itamar Guetta, with the price tag judged too high once development compensation owed to Maccabi Netanya is factored in, according to the same report. There was better news on the fitness front: defender Ron Unger, withdrawn in the first half of the recent defeat to Kiryat Shmona with hamstring tightness, has trained fully since and is available for selection against Maccabi Haifa.

Away from team matters, Tiberias used the update to point to progress on its long-awaited new municipal stadium. Work has picked up markedly since a change of contractor several months ago, the club said, though every seat already installed will need to be replaced after manufacturing defects left them discoloured and prone to cracking. Officials said that, at the current pace, the venue could be ready to host home league matches by next January.

title: Omri Kende: 'I lied to teammates that there was no training, just to make the lineup'
dek: The former Hapoel Tel Aviv right-back opened up on Power Couple about the manipulation, gambling and deceit that shadowed his playing career — and the daily fight to be honest now.

verificationSources.label: Hebrew Wikipedia - Omri Kende career record
Srugim - separate Kende interview on gambling addiction

body: Omri Kende has spent years being asked about the goals he didn't score and the tackles he didn't make. On Channel 13's reality show Power Couple, he was asked about something far harder to admit: the lies he told to stay in the team.

"I grew up crooked, I grew up on lies in football, I grew up on schemes," the former Hapoel Tel Aviv right-back said, according to ONE. "I would lie to players that there was no training, so they wouldn't show up — when really there was, just so I could be in the lineup."

It is a strikingly candid confession from a player who, for a period, was one of the most promising young defenders to come out of Hapoel Petah Tikva's academy, graduating to the senior side at just 16 and a half before a 2008 move to Hapoel Tel Aviv reshaped his career.

At Hapoel Tel Aviv, Kende was part of the club's dominant run at the turn of the decade, winning the Israeli championship in 2009/10 and three consecutive State Cups. He later played in Romania for Astra Giurgiu, and back home for Hapoel Haifa, Maccabi Netanya and Hapoel Jerusalem before retiring.

But running alongside the trophies, Kende has said in this and previous interviews, was a gambling addiction that consumed him. On Power Couple he described the compulsion bluntly, saying he came "from the world of gambling," chasing urges at the expense of those closest to him.

The addiction was not new information — in 2011, Kende was reportedly targeted in an extortion scheme by figures tied to organized crime over debts he had run up gambling, a case that drew police attention at the time. In a separate interview cited by Srugim, Kende has said his club owner once handed him a check to cover a 200,000-shekel debt before he had even finished explaining it.

He has also spoken previously about a heart attack he suffered in 2016 while filming a television production, an episode he has described as a breaking point that led to two years of depression at home.

On the show, Kende turned to fellow contestant Assi Buzaglo — himself a former footballer — as the person he felt able to be fully honest with, calling him his "place of refuge." He contrasted that ease with his relationship with his wife, Doreen, saying he still struggles to hold her gaze: "My wife Doreen I don't understand in the eyes, and you I understand in the eyes."

Kende framed his current life as a daily discipline rather than a finished transformation. "Every morning I wake up and look in the mirror and say: today I won't lie," he said — a small ritual, by his own account, against the habits that once shaped an entire career.

These days, according to other reporting on his post-retirement life, Kende lectures to young people about the dangers of gambling and online betting, presenting his career as a cautionary tale rather than a highlight reel.

title: Get past Red Star and Be'er Sheva would face Aarhus or Sabah for a place in Europe's top table
dek: ONE maps out the Israeli champions' route to a maiden Champions League league phase: first a daunting third-round tie with Red Star Belgrade, then potentially a play-off against Danish side Aarhus or Azerbaijan's Sabah.

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva have not kicked a ball against Red Star Belgrade yet, but ONE has already sketched out where the road leads if the Israeli champions get through — and it runs to either Denmark or Azerbaijan.

The Beer Sheva pass on this qualifying route begins in earnest on Tuesday, when the club hosts Red Star at a neutral venue in Hungary, the Haladás Sportkomplexum, in the first leg of their Champions League third qualifying round tie. The return match follows in Belgrade on August 11. The Serbian champions arrive in ominous form, having beaten Northern Ireland's Larne 9-0 on aggregate in the previous round.

Get past the Serbs — known in Hebrew football shorthand simply as "HaKochav," the Star — and Beer Sheva would advance to the play-off round, one tie away from a first-ever berth in the Champions League's revamped league phase. Their opponent there, ONE reports, would be the winner of a separate third-round meeting between AGF Aarhus of Denmark and Sabah FC of Azerbaijan.

That Aarhus-Sabah tie was set when UEFA drew the third qualifying round on July 20. The play-off round's first legs are scheduled for August 18-19, with the return fixtures on August 25-26 — meaning Beer Sheva, if they advance, would know their next opponent barely a week after finishing off Red Star.

Regardless of how the Red Star tie unfolds, Beer Sheva have already banked continental football for the season: by reaching this stage of Champions League qualifying, the club has guaranteed itself a place in this season's Conference League league phase at minimum, Israeli outlets reported after the win over Vikingur Reykjavik that got them here.

That victory over the Icelandic champions was not straightforward. Beer Sheva lost the first leg in Reykjavik 2-1, with Kings Kangwa's away goal the only bright spot, before completing the turnaround with a 2-0 win at home to advance 3-2 on aggregate.

Kangwa will not be involved in the Red Star assignment, however. The Zambian midfielder, named the Israeli league's Footballer of the Year after a 12-goal season that helped deliver the title, completed a permanent move to Panathinaikos this summer in a deal reported at a fixed €3.8 million, potentially rising to €4.5 million with add-ons.

Red Star present a serious step up regardless of who lines up without Kangwa. The Belgrade club carries genuine European pedigree — they remain the only side from the former Yugoslavia to have won the old European Cup, lifting it in 1991 — and their travelling support is among the most fervent on the continent.

For Beer Sheva, under coach Uri Malmilian, the prize at the end of this run would be historic: the club has never featured in the Champions League's group or league phase, and doing so would bring a windfall in UEFA prize money along with a spot among Europe's elite 36 clubs this autumn.

Nothing is decided yet. Tuesday's first leg against Red Star is the only fixture that matters right now, and the Aarhus-Sabah tie still has to produce a winner before Beer Sheva's hypothetical play-off opponent is confirmed.

title: Tottenham ready to sell Manor Solomon to West Ham, Sport5 reports
dek: The Israel international winger wants a permanent move after two years out on loan, and the Championship-bound Hammers see him as a replacement for Crysencio Summerville.

body: Tottenham Hotspur are prepared to let Manor Solomon leave for West Ham United this summer, according to a report from Sport5, with the Israel international winger pushing for a permanent exit after two seasons spent almost entirely out on loan.

Solomon, 27, returned to Spurs training this pre-season having spent the last two campaigns away from north London, most notably in the Championship with Leeds United, as well as loan spells at Villarreal and Fiorentina. None of those moves produced a lasting foothold in Tottenham's first-team plans.

It was at Elland Road that Solomon made his biggest impact. In the 2024-25 season under Daniel Farke he scored 10 goals and set up around a dozen more as Leeds stormed to the Championship title and an immediate return to the Premier League, with the Israeli among the division's most creative attacking players over the campaign.

That form is exactly what has caught West Ham's eye. The Hammers were relegated from the Premier League last season and are now rebuilding for a Championship campaign, and they have already sold their own standout winger, Crysencio Summerville, to Saudi club Al-Hilal in a deal reported by Sky Sports at up to £60 million.

West Ham view Solomon as a like-for-like replacement, banking on the fact he has already proven himself at this level and knows the division well. According to Sport5, Tottenham are open to sanctioning a sale rather than sending him out on a third straight loan.

Solomon's camp has made clear that another temporary move is not what the player wants at this stage of his career. He has two years left on his Tottenham contract, giving Spurs some leverage in valuation talks, though his lack of regular football in recent seasons works the other way.

Financially, the numbers are relatively modest by Premier League standards: Transfermarkt currently rates his market value at around €9 million, and West Ham held an option to sign him permanently for roughly €10 million during a previous loan spell that was not taken up.

No transfer fee, contract length or timeline has been agreed, and reports in England suggest the two London clubs are due to sit down in the coming days to discuss structure and valuation. Solomon's representatives have indicated the situation could still run until close to the end of the August window.

For Solomon, it is a chance to finally settle after a stop-start few years since joining Tottenham on a free transfer from Shakhtar Donetsk. For West Ham, it would be a quick, relatively low-cost fix for the winger position they left short by cashing in on Summerville.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are closing in on a new body for the paint. Sport5 reports the club has reached an agreement with free-agent American center Armando Bacot, who arrives after a difficult single season at Fenerbahçe.

The deal, as described by Sport5, runs for two years and would slot the 26-year-old, 2.08-metre Bacot in as Maccabi's second foreign center, playing behind Daniel Theis in Oded Kattash's frontcourt rotation for the 2026/27 campaign.

Bacot's stock has fallen sharply since he left American college basketball. Last season in Istanbul, under Šarūnas Jasikevičius, he barely featured — 2.4 points and 1.8 rebounds across 26 EuroLeague appearances, in just 10 minutes a night. His domestic-league numbers were healthier: 6 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 17.5 minutes, shooting 49.4 percent from the field.

The move independently surfaces in Turkish basketball media too. Eurohoops' Turkish edition separately reported Maccabi preparing a two-year contract for Bacot after the club's earlier pursuits of Bruno Fernando and Marcus Bingham fell through, with Fenerbahçe having already confirmed it was parting ways with him along with several other frontcourt players.

Before his move to Turkey, Bacot spent five seasons at North Carolina, establishing himself as one of the most productive big men in Tar Heels history, then had a brief stint with Memphis's G-League affiliate, where he averaged 16.8 points and 9.5 rebounds a game, shooting 46.5 percent on twos and 33.3 percent from three.

Maccabi's coaching staff reportedly view the signing as a bet on upside rather than what Bacot showed in his one EuroLeague season — the belief being that a bigger role and more minutes under Kattash could unlock production closer to his college and G-League form than his bit-part year in Istanbul.

Per Sport5, the agreement effectively completes Maccabi's roster build for next season, with one loose end still hanging over the squad: the future of guard Lonnie Walker IV, whose status with the club remains unresolved.
Neither Maccabi Tel Aviv nor Bacot's representatives have issued a formal announcement, and the move should be treated as a reported deal rather than an official unveiling until the club confirms it.

title: Hapoel Ramat Gan 3-2 Maccabi Netanya: Feldman admits press was 'not good enough' as frustration grows
dek: A Matheus Dabo brace and a competitive debut for Dolev Haziza weren't enough to save Netanya from a Toto Cup upset, as the club vowed not to repeat last season's defensive collapse.

verificationSources.label: ONE - תסכול במכבי נתניה: אסור לנו לחזור לעונה שעברה

body: Maccabi Netanya's perfect start to the season came to an abrupt end on Sunday, as newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan Giv'atayim came from behind to win 3-2 at Netanya Stadium in the Toto Cup group stage. It was the manner of the loss, more than the result itself, that stung: three goals conceded from two headers and a penalty against a side that had never played top-flight football before this season.

Luan Campos headed Ramat Gan in front in the 33rd minute, but Matheus Dabo levelled six minutes later, finishing off a through ball from Maor Levi. David Asuka restored the visitors' lead with another header just after the hour, and Maxim Palkoshchenko put Ramat Gan 3-1 up from the penalty spot in the 61st minute. Palkoshchenko, a former Netanya player who was honoured with a pre-match tribute, chose not to celebrate against his old club. Dabo's second goal, in the 87th minute, set up a tense finish but arrived too late to salvage a point.

According to ONE, the club's own post-match assessment was unusually blunt for a preseason cup tie. "We cannot concede goals like that and go back to last year," a club statement said, "we need to stop this and solve the problem" — a pointed reference to the defensive frailties that undermined Netanya for long stretches of last season.
Defender Beni Feldman echoed the frustration on the pitch. "This wasn't a good enough game," he said. "I think our pressing wasn't good enough, and we'll need to move and control the game more."
The 3-2 defeat ended a run of two straight wins to open Netanya's Toto Cup campaign and left Hapoel Ramat Gan, promoted over the summer, still unbeaten in Group B.

Feldman, a young centre-back who signed a contract extension through the 2027/28 season and has been earning regular minutes under coach Roni Levi, was also asked about his own progress and the club's ambitions. "I'm integrating well and working hard in training and outside of it," he said. Asked about the target for the season, he did not hedge: "We are aiming for Europe."

Behind the scenes, ONE reports Netanya's management is working to bring in reinforcements at centre-back, with the club potentially even looking at two new foreign defenders. The expectation inside the club, according to the report, is that once a foreign centre-back arrives, one of the current Israeli options in that position could leave.

There was a bright spot amid the defeat: Dolev Haziza made his first competitive appearance for Maccabi Netanya, coming off the bench in the 65th minute. He almost scored with his first touch before being denied by the Ramat Gan goalkeeper, and later teed up Dabo's late second goal.

Missing from the squad was Bassem Za'arura, whose strong start to the season has reportedly caught the eye of clubs abroad — ONE named Polish side Lech Poznań among those interested in the midfielder. Israeli defender Itay Ben Shabbat also did not feature.

For Netanya, the group-stage cup defeat carries little direct cost beyond pride and points, but the club's own words suggest the alarm is about pattern, not just one bad afternoon: a young squad still finding its identity under Levi, and a defence the club itself says cannot afford to repeat the mistakes of a difficult 2025/26.

title: UEFA draw narrows play-off opponents for Israel's four surviving clubs
dek: Hapoel Beersheba, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv all learned their conditional next-round rivals in Nyon on Monday, with none of the four ties actually decided yet.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC - potential play-off opponents
Jerusalem Post - guide to Israeli clubs in Europe
Jerusalem Post - Hapoel Beersheba to face Red Star Belgrade

body: Monday brought a strange kind of clarity to four Israeli clubs still fighting for a place in Europe this season: UEFA staged three separate play-off round draws in Nyon, mapping out exactly who each of them could meet next — even though not one of their current ties has actually been decided.

Hapoel Beersheba, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv are all still mid-tie in the third qualifying round, with first legs played or due on August 6 and return legs on August 13. Monday's draws, reported by ONE, effectively sketched two paths for every club — one if they advance, another if they are eliminated or dropped into a lower competition.

Hapoel Beersheba went first, drawn at 1pm for the Champions League play-off round on condition they get past Red Star Belgrade, the Serbian giants and 1991 European champions who stand between them and that stage. Should Beersheba go through, they would face one of a cluster of possible opponents: Austria's LASK Linz, Norway's Viking, or the winners of Zalgiris–Ararat Armenia, Kairat Almaty–Levski Sofia or Aarhus–Sabah.

Maccabi Tel Aviv were next, drawn at 2pm for the Europa League, contingent on beating Bulgaria's CSKA Sofia, whom they host in Batumi and Tel Aviv over the two legs. According to Maccabi's own club website, victory would send them into a play-off bracket built around the winner of Thun–Vikingur Reykjavik, Cypriot side OFI Crete, or the beaten side from Aarhus–Sabah or Dinamo Zagreb–Zalgiris.

Lose to CSKA Sofia, though, and Maccabi drop instead into the Conference League play-off pool — a very different looking group that includes Portugal's Braga, Azerbaijan's Qarabag (via a tie with Dynamo Kyiv), Partizan Belgrade and Switzerland's Lugano, the club confirmed.

Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv, both chasing Conference League football, were drawn together in the day's final session at 3pm. Beitar still have to see off Austria Wien, while Hapoel Tel Aviv must first get past Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad. Advance, and both would land in the same possible bracket — one that, notably, includes Atalanta and Freiburg, sides who enter the Conference League play-off round directly through their leagues' qualifying routes, along with Greece's Panathinaikos.

None of the four clubs will know their actual play-off opponent until after the third qualifying round return legs on August 13. The play-off ties themselves follow quickly — first legs on August 20, second legs on August 27 — with barely a fortnight separating the two rounds before the various league and group phases open in September.

It leaves Israeli football with four separate roads still open into continental competition this year, spread across all three UEFA club competitions, but every one of them running through a genuine test in the coming ten days before any of Monday's paper pairings become real fixtures on the calendar.

title: Maccabi Ramat Gan light up a season-ticket campaign with Edgar, the arena's new star
dek: The basketball club's ad agency reimagines Israel's iconic 1979 lottery jingle for Zisman Hall, with new signing Roey Pritzky and longtime arena staffer Edgar Finkelstein fronting the push to fill seats.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "Edgar... light the lights" campaign report

body: Maccabi Ironi Ramat Gan have gone digging through Israeli advertising folklore to sell tickets for the season ahead, borrowing - and gently rewriting - one of the most recognisable lines in the country's television history.

The basketball club's new campaign film, produced by the agency Shneiderman Tzofan, riffs on the famous 1979 Mifal HaPayis lottery commercial in which a character named Chaim is told to "light the lights, please." In Ramat Gan's version the plea goes to Edgar instead - "Edgar... light the lights" - and the moment he flips the switch on Zisman Hall becomes the film's central image for a club trying to switch its fans back on for 2026-27, according to ONE.

Edgar is not an actor brought in for the shoot. ONE reports that Edgar Finkelstein is a long-serving member of Zisman's backroom staff, and the club chose to put him - rather than a player or a coach - at the emotional centre of the video, alongside Rubi Ben Atiya, described by the club as the hall's veteran, near-legendary manager.

Two of the summer's new arrivals also appear in the spot: guard Roey Pritzky and the newly signed Joaquín Shokman, both presented as symbols of the rebuild the club is asking its supporters to buy into.

Pritzky's arrival is the more independently documented of the two. The 2022 Israeli Rookie of the Year signed a two-year contract with Ramat Gan this off-season after a season at Hapoel Jerusalem, following a run through Israel's youth national teams and a place in the senior squad for the pre-Paris 2024 Olympic qualifying tournament, according to be106 reporting on the signing. "Our goal is to break into the top playoff," Pritzky said after putting pen to paper.

The club's own messaging around the campaign leans hard on nostalgia and renewal in the same breath: "We call upon all the supporters who have accompanied us over the years to come home," it said. "Together with an energetic younger generation, we will fill Zisman's stands and relight the lights."

The pitch is squarely about seats. Zisman Hall has been Ramat Gan's home since 1993 and holds roughly 1,400 to 1,500 fans, modest by Israeli top-flight standards, and the club has pushed subscription renewals hard this summer, publishing its 2026-27 pricing list with a discounted window for existing members before general sale opens.

None of it changes the basketball reality Ramat Gan faces: a club trying to rebuild competitively in the Israeli Basketball Premier League while also rebuilding its matchday atmosphere, using a 47-year-old jingle as the hook to get both jobs done at once.

title: Tottenham ready to sell Manor Solomon as West Ham weigh Championship move
dek: The Israel international has made just six appearances for Spurs since 2023, and newly relegated West Ham see him as ready-made reinforcement for their push back to the Premier League, ONE reports.
body: Tottenham are prepared to let Manor Solomon leave this summer, and West Ham have emerged as the leading suitors for the Israel international, according to a report in the English press relayed by ONE.

West Ham's interest is rooted in need as much as admiration. The Hammers were relegated to the Championship after finishing 18th in the Premier League, and are already reshaping their squad for the promotion push, having sold winger Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal for a reported £68 million. Solomon, ONE reports, is seen in east London as a direct replacement who could offer regular game time rather than a place on the fringes of a top-flight squad.

That lack of first-team football has been the story of Solomon's time in north London. He signed for Tottenham on a free transfer in 2023 after impressing on loan at Fulham, but has made only six official appearances for the club since, with manager after manager preferring other options in wide areas.

Spurs instead farmed him out on loan for two full seasons. In 2024-25 he joined Leeds United, where he thrived: 10 goals and around a dozen assists as Leeds won the Championship title outright and returned to the Premier League at the first attempt.

This past season took him further afield still. Solomon spent the first half of 2025-26 on loan at Villarreal in La Liga before a mid-season move to Fiorentina in Serie A, before returning to Tottenham this summer still searching for a settled home.
None of that has resolved his situation at Spurs, and ONE's report suggests the club now regards a permanent sale as the likeliest outcome, with West Ham the club best placed to negotiate one.

The report gives no indication yet of a fee or the shape of a deal, and any move may not be quick — the winger's camp is said to be weighing up options with an eye on keeping his path back to regular football open, which could leave the situation unresolved deep into the transfer window.

Tottenham have other loan business in motion too. Young winger Mikey Moore, who impressed on loan at Rangers last season, is separately closing in on a loan switch to Bundesliga side FC Köln, part of a broader summer clearout of fringe attacking options at the club.

For Solomon and Israel's national team, a permanent move to a club prepared to build around him would mark a return to the kind of regular football that made his Leeds loan the standout campaign of his career so far.

title: Adelson breaks silence on Hapoel Jerusalem crest row: "I think about what's best for this club"
dek: The Hapoel Jerusalem owner addresses the leaked rebrand that angered supporters last season, promising a new crest and a meeting with fan representatives before the Israeli basketball season begins.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — logo alternatives sent to fans after petition
Israel Hayom — Adelson's ownership and background

body: Matan Adelson has broken his silence on the crest controversy that soured relations between Hapoel Jerusalem's ownership and its supporters last season, telling ONE that every decision he has made since taking over the club has been guided by one question: what is actually best for Hapoel Jerusalem.

"Since arriving, my single focus is determining what serves Hapoel Jerusalem best long-term," Adelson said, in comments that amount to the fullest public explanation yet of a rebrand plan that blew up in the club's face when it leaked online before it was ever formally presented.

According to a report by Walla Sport last month, a new emblem commissioned from a branding agency leaked on social media roughly a week and a half before a planned unveiling event. The reaction was immediate: fans opposed to any change to the club's traditional symbol launched a petition that gathered around 1,200 signatures within two hours.

Facing that backlash, the club froze the rebrand and instead sent three alternative crest designs to season-ticket holders and prospective buyers for a 24-hour vote, while the special reveal event itself was pushed back to around the start of the new season, Walla reported.

Adelson conceded the club mishandled the rollout. "Unfortunately, before we could present our vision properly, it leaked, and people saw only an image without context," he told ONE, acknowledging that the images fans reacted to online were never meant to be judged in isolation.

He was unapologetic, however, about his willingness to make unpopular calls. "Leadership means making difficult decisions, not just easy ones," he said. "Not everyone will accept my choices, but I bear responsibility for them."

Adelson told ONE he now plans to sit down with fan representatives directly and will unveil the finished crest before the new season tips off, framing the visual refresh as an attempt to modernise the club's identity without erasing its history.

He described the logo as one strand of a wider set of changes at the club, alongside an expansion of the professional and administrative staff and the rollout of new digital platforms for supporters — part of a broader push, in his telling, to reconnect a fan base that has grown frustrated with the ownership.

"I want success and a stronger community. I cannot achieve this alone — it requires players, coaches, staff, sponsors, and believers," Adelson said, closing on a conciliatory note aimed at supporters he needs back onside before the campaign starts.

Adelson, son of the late Sheldon and Miriam Adelson, bought Hapoel Jerusalem in 2023 and holds roughly 90 percent of the club, with a fan association owning the remainder. The team, now sponsored as Hapoel Midtown Jerusalem, plays out of the Pais Arena in Malha and is chasing a return to continental competition this season.

For now, the crest itself remains unrevealed, and it is the fans' mood rather than the final design that will determine whether Adelson's intervention has actually closed the rift before the Israeli Basketball Super League season begins.

title: European Open Water Swimming Championships dive into the Seine tomorrow with four Israelis in the water
dek: Yonatan Ahdout headlines an Israeli quartet on the river that hosted the 2024 Olympics, as the national program eyes a first Israeli berth for Los Angeles 2028.

verificationSources.label: Sortiraparis - European Swimming Championships 2026 open-water schedule

body: Four Israeli swimmers step into the Seine on Tuesday as the European Open Water Swimming Championships open in Paris, on the same stretch of river that carried the marathon swimming events at the 2024 Olympics.

The open-water program runs from August 4 to 8 as part of the wider 2026 European Aquatics Championships, and features the Olympic-distance 10km, a 5km race and a 3km knockout format, with racers navigating a looped course and a current that has already been flagged as a major tactical factor.
Water quality in the Seine has drawn scrutiny at past events staged on the river since the Paris Games, and organisers have again been monitoring conditions in the build-up to this week's racing.
Israel's team is built around Yonatan Ahdout of Hapoel Jerusalem, who will swim both the men's 10km and 5km before joining the rest of the squad in the 3km knockout.

In the women's 10km, Israel is represented by Ofek Adir of Hapoel Bat Yam and Emily Golos and Rebecca Androvich, both of TLV Swim. Adir will also race the 5km, and all three women join Ahdout in the knockout event.

According to Sport5, national head coach Nil Mizrahi has framed the week in Paris as a staging post rather than an end in itself, with the program's stated aim to qualify at least one Israeli swimmer for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The same three returning swimmers - Ahdout, Adir and Androvich - all posted personal best times at last year's European Championships in Stari Grad, Croatia, finishing in a range of 19th to 22nd place.

Those results, modest on paper, were treated internally as evidence of progress for a squad still building toward its first continental medal, and this week's races in front of Parisian landmarks offer the clearest test yet of how far that progress has come.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva save their strongest side as Ligat Ha'al return looms
dek: Ziv Arie is calmly steering his newly promoted squad through a winless preseason, resting regulars, chasing a Yoav Koren loan and edging toward a Marko Rakonjac deal before the top-flight opener.

verificationSources.label: Israel Hayom — Hapoel Jerusalem 1-0 win, Demeshkan goal

body: Three straight preseason defeats and still no points on the board would usually set off alarm bells at a newly promoted club. At Maccabi Petah Tikva, it hasn't — because coach Ziv Arie has barely used his strongest team yet, ONE reports.

Maccabi Petah Tikva secured their return to Ligat Ha'al in May, finishing among the top two in Liga Leumit after just one season down, with the top flight due to kick off on August 22. Arie, who took over that same month after seven years in charge of Hapoel Jerusalem, has used the warm-up fixtures to manage fitness rather than chase results.

The latest setback came on Sunday, a 1-0 loss to his old club at their temporary home in Rehovot — his first meeting with Hapoel Jerusalem from the opposite touchline. Vitali Demeshkan scored the only goal in the 47th minute, teed up by Oved Almagor.

It was Maccabi Petah Tikva's third consecutive preseason loss, but according to ONE the pattern is by design: Arie has repeatedly fielded weakened lineups stocked with younger players, wary of injuries to his first-choice group with the real campaign fast approaching.
The club gets one more chance to close out preparations on a brighter note when they host Hapoel Ra'anana next Sunday, a fixture they hope will finally deliver a first result of the preseason.

There was better news on the fitness front. Defender Itay Tibor, sidelined since last season, has returned to full training and could be handed minutes against Ra'anana as he works his way back into contention.

Off the pitch, the squad is still being shaped. Forward Marko Rakonjac, who played under Arie at Hapoel Jerusalem, landed in Israel last Friday and is set to undergo medical tests before signing a deal through the rest of the season with an option for another, negotiated through agent Ziv Solomowitz.

Maccabi Petah Tikva are also pushing to add width, working on a loan for Hapoel Beersheba's Yoav Koren, who impressed on loan at Hapoel Kfar Saba last season. Beersheba have generally been reluctant to loan out players this summer, but a resolution is expected once their Champions League qualifying tie with Crvena Zvezda Belgrade — first leg August 4 or 5, second leg August 11 — is out of the way.

For now, the message from HaMoshava Stadium is patience: a winless preseason is an acceptable price if it means the strongest possible Maccabi Petah Tikva side is ready to run when Ligat Ha'al football actually counts.

title: Legendary Kiryat Shalom canteen operator sues Maccabi Tel Aviv over eviction
dek: Zion Blas, who ran an informal kiosk at the club's training ground for decades, is seeking more than 500,000 shekels after Maccabi moved to shut it down and demolish the site.

verificationSources.label: ONE: "מפעיל המזנון המיתולוגי בקריית שלום תבע את מכבי"
Ynet: "מזנון המריבה: האוהד השרוף של מכבי תל אביב תובע את המועדון"

body: For decades he was as much a fixture of Maccabi Tel Aviv's Kiryat Shalom training ground as the pitches themselves. Now Zion Blas, the man who ran the complex's informal canteen, is taking the club to court over the way it ended.

Blas is suing Maccabi Tel Aviv for 520,482 shekels, ONE reports, after the club moved to shut down the kiosk he had operated at the training facility in south Tel Aviv. The claim splits into 420,482 shekels for lost profits, calculated from the canteen's average earnings between 2014 and 2020, and 100,000 shekels for what he describes as non-pecuniary damages and emotional distress.

According to the lawsuit, Blas's connection to the club stretches back to the 1960s. He has described himself in the filing as a simple man who found a neglected shed on the grounds, rehabilitated it himself and turned it into a working canteen that served players, staff and visitors for years, Ynet reports.

He says he was told at the time that he could run the kiosk for the rest of his life. A formal agreement dated May 19, 2002 told a different story on paper, and a further declaration was signed in 2016. Blas's suit asks the Tel Aviv District Court to annul both documents, arguing they do not reflect what he was actually promised and should not be treated as binding.

The dispute came to a head on December 31, 2023, when Maccabi issued Blas a formal notice to vacate the shed within 14 days, telling him the site was being demolished and rebuilt as an internal club facility, according to ONE. The club reportedly warned that anything left behind would be disposed of.

Blas is represented by attorney Shay Elias, who filed the claim after an earlier demand letter to the club failed to resolve the matter. For its part, Maccabi's response, delivered through the club's attorney Yael Margelit, struck a conciliatory note even while defending the eviction: she said the club held "great respect" for a man she called "a known and beloved figure," and that Maccabi's door would always be open to him.

That olive branch appears to have been followed up. ONE reports that Blas's legal team proposed a settlement meeting in January 2026, with Maccabi's lawyers responding the following month by inviting him to coordinate directly with club management.

There is no indication in either report that the case has been resolved or that a trial date has been set. For now, the canteen that outlasted generations of Maccabi Tel Aviv players remains shuttered, and the argument over what Blas was owed for running it is playing out in a courtroom rather than at the training ground gate.

title: Satoransky: I wanted to cut my workload, and Hapoel Tel Aviv want to win the Euroleague
dek: The Czech guard explains why he left Barcelona for Tel Aviv after 18 months of back pain, and why he believes Hapoel's new ownership can chase Europe's biggest prize.
body: Tomas Satoransky says the move that took him from FC Barcelona to Hapoel Tel Aviv this summer came down to one simple calculation: he wanted to keep playing in the Euroleague, but he could no longer do it carrying the workload Barcelona had put on him.

"I wanted to stay in the Euroleague and reduce the load," the 34-year-old Czech guard said in an interview quoted by ONE. "That was the main motivation." He signed a one-year deal with Hapoel, reportedly worth around $1.5 million with an option for a further season, and is expected to slot in as the club's third guard in the rotation behind Dimitris Itoudis' first-choice ball-handlers rather than as the primary playmaker he was for much of his career.

The health picture behind the move is stark. Satoransky revealed he has been dealing with joint pain in his lower back for a year and a half, and that he sees no explanation for it beyond years of accumulated strain. "For the last year and a half I've suffered from joint pains in the lower back," he said, describing a cycle in which a heavy Euroleague workload — around 30 minutes a night at Barcelona — left him with little recovery time before Spanish league fixtures came around just days later, feeding what he called a domino effect of physical breakdown.

With only five non-EU players permitted on a Euroleague roster, clubs like Barcelona lean hard on that limited group across both European and domestic competition, and Satoransky suggested that squeeze was central to his physical decline. Reducing his minutes and sharing the guard workload at Hapoel, he indicated, was the only realistic way to keep playing at the level he wants without breaking down further.

He was notably blunt about his old club's board. "Barcelona was a huge disappointment in how the football club's management treated the basketball team," Satoransky said, pointing to a lack of reinforcement and investment in the roster that left the basketball section short-changed compared with the football operation. He spent four seasons in Catalonia, most recently averaging 7.0 points, 4.3 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 0.7 steals per game in EuroLeague action in 2025/26 while shooting 49.4 percent on twos and 48.9 percent from three.

By contrast, he described real enthusiasm for what he found waiting in Tel Aviv. "Now we have owners at Hapoel with vision, and we definitely want to win the Euroleague," he said — a rare, unguarded statement of ambition from a player who spent the better part of a decade at one of the competition's traditional powers before switching allegiances.

The family side of the decision mattered too, according to the interview: his wife backed the move and the change in lifestyle that comes with relocating to Israel, treating it as a shared decision rather than simply following his career.

Satoransky's arrival gives Hapoel Tel Aviv a EuroLeague-tested table-setter with a title résumé, even in a reduced role, as the club builds out its guard rotation for a season in which it has again set itself ambitious continental targets.

title: Maccabi Haifa release record signing Matías Nahuel after injury-hit flop
dek: The Argentine-Spanish forward's four-year, record €2.5 million contract is torn up nearly two years early, closing the book on an injury-hit spell that ended with a loan to Poland's Jagiellonia Białystok.

body: Maccabi Haifa have released Matías Nahuel, closing the book on the most expensive transfer in the club's history less than two years after it was made, without it ever delivering the impact it promised, ONE reports.

The Argentine-Spanish forward arrived in Haifa on September 18, 2024, when Maccabi paid a reported €2.5 million to sign him from Śląsk Wrocław — a club-record fee for an Israeli side that had spent big before but never on a single player at that price.

He signed a four-year contract meant to run through the summer of 2028, and he came with genuine pedigree: a Villarreal academy product who had played across Spain's lower divisions and briefly for Olympiacos before finding his best form in Poland's Ekstraklasa with Wrocław, the form that first put him on Israeli scouts' radar.

It never translated at Maccabi. Across roughly a season and a half in the Carmel, Nahuel made about 23 appearances and scored three goals, numbers well short of what a club-record fee was supposed to buy.

Injury compounded the problem. He underwent surgery to repair a torn quadriceps tendon that was expected to keep him out for around four months, a blow that gutted a season already short on end product. "Unfortunately, the injuries did not allow me to show the potential in a giant club like Maccabi Haifa," he wrote on Instagram at the time, thanking supporters while vowing to fight his way back.

He did return, but not to regular football. His playing time shrank further once Barak Bahar took over as head coach, and Nahuel increasingly found himself on the fringes of a matchday squad his fee was supposed to anchor.

In January 2026, Maccabi sent him out on loan to Jagiellonia Białystok in Poland for the rest of the season — in effect an admission that the transfer had already failed and that both club and player needed a change of scenery.

Now, per ONE, Maccabi Haifa have gone further and released Nahuel outright, ending his contract roughly two years before it was due to expire. There is no reported fee recouped and no sale to offset the outlay: the club's record purchase leaves with nothing to show for it beyond three goals and long stretches on the treatment table.

It stands as a cautionary footnote to Maccabi Haifa's transfer business — a reminder of how quickly a marquee signing can turn into dead weight on the wage bill when injuries and form conspire against a player at the same time.

title: Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim sign Nigerian midfielder Christopher Boniface
dek: Newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim add the Nigerian attacking midfielder on a two-year deal as they rebuild for a first Ligat Ha'Al campaign in 13 years.

body: Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim, freshly promoted to Ligat Ha'Al after 13 years away from Israel's top flight, have added another piece to their rebuild: Nigerian attacking midfielder Christopher Boniface has signed with the club, Sport5 reports.

The 24-year-old has put pen to paper on a two-year contract that includes a club option for a third season, giving Ramat Gan's coaching staff a player they hope can add craft and legs to midfield ahead of senior-flight football.

Boniface arrives from Al-Kharaitiyat in Qatar's second division, where Sport5 says he contributed goals and an assist last season. Before his move to the Gulf, he spent time in Armenia with FC Van and Ararat Yerevan, spells that first put him on the radar of Israeli scouts.

He becomes the latest name in what has been a busy rebuilding summer at the club. Brazilian winger Luan Campos has arrived from Romanian football, Portuguese defender Jota Gonçalves has joined from Portugal's second tier, and Kazakhstan-based left-back Farid Ibrahim has also signed, alongside domestic additions Maksim Falkowski and Tamir Glazer.

The scale of the incoming class reflects the size of the challenge facing Messay Dego's squad. Ramat Gan sealed their return to the top flight only on the final day of the Liga Leumit season, drawing 1-1 away at Hapoel Kfar Saba to edge into the last promotion spot.

It ends a 13-year exile from Ligat Ha'Al for the Ramat Gan-Givatayim club. Rather than opening at their old home ground, the newly promoted side are set to begin the 2026/27 season at a new 6,000-seat stadium in Rehovot, with the league campaign kicking off on August 22.

With the opener under three weeks away, further arrivals are expected before the squad is finalised. For now, Boniface gives Ramat Gan a goal-contributing midfielder from the past two seasons abroad to throw into a Ligat Ha'Al squad still very much taking shape.

title: Ex-Barcelona forward Milan Gurović pulls stranger from burning car in Belgrade
dek: The former Serbian international, a Spanish league and Korać Cup winner with Barcelona, freed a trapped driver seconds before his Audi was engulfed in flames.
body: Milan Gurović spent a decade and a half being paid to move quickly on a basketball court. On Sunday afternoon in Belgrade, that same instinct may have saved a stranger's life.

The 50-year-old former Barcelona and Serbia forward was driving home through New Belgrade when he saw a car swerve suddenly and come to a stop near a Lidl supermarket at the junction of Dušana Vukasovića and Vojvođanska streets, Serbian outlets reported. Within moments, the Audi was on fire with the driver still inside.

Gurović did not wait for help to arrive. He got out of his own vehicle, ran to the burning car and pulled the trapped man free, according to Telegraf and other Serbian media who spoke to witnesses and officials at the scene.

The driver, identified only as Milan J., 48, had become stuck when his seatbelt jammed as the flames spread. Sport5, citing the same reports, said only seconds separated the rescue from what could have become a fatal accident.
"He prevented a tremendous tragedy," Serbian media covering the incident said, describing how quickly the fire consumed the vehicle once Gurović had pulled the driver clear of it.

Firefighters reached the scene shortly afterwards with two vehicles and seven crew members, but by then the Audi was destroyed. The rescued driver was taken to Belgrade's Emergency Center, where doctors found he had suffered no burns or serious injuries, only smoke inhalation. Prosecutors were notified of the incident, as is standard procedure in Serbia for such accidents.

Gurović is remembered in Serbia as one of the most gifted forwards of his generation. Born in Novi Sad, he made his name at Peristeri in Greece before joining Barcelona in 1998, where he won the Spanish ACB league and the Korać Cup in his first season at the club.
He went on to play for AEK Athens, Málaga, Partizan and Crvena zvezda, among other clubs, finishing his career at Galatasaray in 2009. Across 49 EuroLeague appearances he averaged 12.6 points a game.
With the Yugoslav and Serbian national teams he won gold at EuroBasket 2001 and the 2002 FIBA World Championship, and later served as the first captain of Serbia's newly formed national side in 2007.
None of that, Sunday's events suggested, mattered as much to Gurović as being in the right place at the right moment — and having the nerve to act on it.

Gurović freed him moments before the vehicle was fully engulfed in flames.

Firefighters arrived afterward with two vehicles and seven crew and extinguished the blaze; the car was destroyed.

Gurović played for Barcelona from 1998-2000, winning the Spanish league and Korać Cup, and later starred for Partizan, Crvena zvezda and Galatasaray, plus Serbia's national team, winning EuroBasket 2001 and the 2002 World Championship gold.

title: Shmulik Daniel awarded bronze at European Rowing Championships after Ukrainian rival's disqualification
dek: The 41-year-old Israeli Paralympic sculler crossed the line fourth in Varese, but a successful Israeli protest over his rival's strapping handed him the podium spot.
body: Shmulik Daniel has a European Championship medal to show for a career built on unlikely comebacks — though this one arrived a few hours after he had already left the water thinking he had missed the podium.

The 41-year-old Israeli para-rower crossed the line fourth in the PR1 men's single sculls final at the European Rowing Championships in Varese, Italy, clocking 9:35.95 over the 2,000-metre course. Third place on the water went to Ukraine's Roman Polianskyi.

But the Israeli delegation lodged a protest, arguing that Polianskyi had not properly fixed the strapping required in the PR1 classification, which covers rowers with the most limited trunk and leg function. World Rowing's jury upheld the protest, relegating Polianskyi to last place and promoting Daniel to bronze.

Polianskyi, competing at his first regatta since last year's world championships, had been delighted to reach the podium before the ruling went against him. "It is very hard for me because in Ukraine it's not easy to get enough nutrition, and also you cannot sleep with the sirens," he said afterward, reflecting on training conditions back home.

For Daniel, the medal is the latest chapter in a story that began far from the water. He was seriously injured in 2005, at age 20, during a military operation in the Mount Dov area on Israel's northern border, sustaining a spinal injury that left him wheelchair-bound.

He took up single sculls rowing several years later and steadily climbed the international ranks: 13th at the 2018 European Championships, then sixth at the following edition, a result that secured his place at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics. He finished sixth in Tokyo and fourth at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.
Varese now gives him his first European Championship medal — bronze, on a course where he had finished fourth in 2021.

The result also continued a strong week for Israel's Paralympic rowing squad in Varese. The evening before Daniel's race, Shahar Milfelder and Saleh Shahin won bronze in the PR2 mixed double sculls, with Germany taking gold and Ukraine silver in that event.

Milfelder and Shahin, Paralympic bronze medallists themselves from Paris 2024, have been among Israel's most consistent para-rowing crews over the past two seasons, and their result in Varese underlined the depth Israel now has across multiple para-rowing boat classes heading toward the next Paralympic cycle.

title: Rehovot revives push to merge Hapoel Marmorek and Maccabi Sha'arayim into one city club
dek: ONE reports that mayor Matan Dil is driving a fresh draft agreement to unite the two rival lower-league sides before the 2026/27 season kicks off on August 28, a year after a similar merger fell apart.
body: Rehovot's long-running football soap opera is back for another episode. ONE reports that intensive talks are once again underway to merge the city's two veteran rival clubs, Hapoel Marmorek and Maccabi Sha'arayim, into a single senior team — with city hall hopeful this time of landing the deal before the 2026/27 season kicks off on August 28.

The clubs occupy neighbouring rungs of the amateur pyramid: Marmorek currently play in the third-tier Liga Alef South, Sha'arayim a division below in Liga Bet. Under the plan being finalised, Maccabi Rehovot's youth setup would also fold into the new entity, giving the city a single pathway from junior football through to a senior side for the first time in decades.

Mayor Matan Dil is personally steering the process, with municipal officials sitting directly in the negotiations rather than leaving it to the clubs alone. According to ONE, the draft documents are now in a near-final form, and the tone around the talks is described as considerably more optimistic than in previous rounds.

That optimism comes with a caveat: this is not the first time Rehovot has tried this. A comparable merger drawn up roughly a year earlier reached an advanced stage before it collapsed, undone in part by resistance from sections of both fan bases who did not want to see their club's identity dissolved into a new municipal brand.

The terms now on the table are designed to head off exactly that objection. As before, the municipality would clear the outstanding debts carried by both clubs and take over administrative management of the merged side, which would play its home games at the newly built Rehovot Stadium rather than either club's existing ground.

Crucially, Marmorek and Sha'arayim would not simply disappear. Both could continue to exist in parallel as fan-run outfits in the fifth-tier Liga Gimel under their old names and colours, giving supporters attached to nearly 80 years of local history a team of their own to keep following even as the senior operation is rebranded.

The timing adds an extra layer of complication. Marmorek only appointed Daniel Tolmasov as head coach in late June, a routine pre-season move that now looks premature if the merger goes through — a unified club would almost certainly need to settle the coaching question from scratch.

Underneath the logistics sits a simpler financial reality: two clubs chasing the same limited pool of local sponsors, municipal grants and fans has left both operating under chronic debt, with neither realistically positioned to climb the pyramid alone. A single, properly funded city club is the pitch city hall has been making, on and off, for years.

For now it remains exactly that — a pitch. ONE's report describes talks as advanced but not signed off, and Rehovot has been here before. Whether this attempt succeeds where last year's did not should become clear in the coming weeks, with the new season bearing down fast.

title: Arbitrator sides with Mohammed Awad in wage dispute against Tzeirei Tamra
dek: A labour arbitrator has ordered the Liga Alef club to pay roughly 78,000 shekels in unpaid wages, bonuses and pension contributions after rejecting the club's settlement defence.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הבוררת הכריעה: ניצחון גדול למוחמד עואד

body: A labour arbitrator has ruled decisively in favour of footballer Mohammed Awad in his wage dispute with Liga Alef club Tzeirei Tamra, ONE reports, ordering the club to pay him roughly 78,478 shekels covering unpaid salary, bonuses, pension contributions and other entitlements.

Awad spent three seasons at Tzeirei Tamra, from 2022 through 2025, and was part of the squad that helped the club win promotion to Liga Alef for the 2024/25 campaign. He argued he had fulfilled his side of the deal while the club repeatedly fell short on payments owed to him.

Represented by attorney Ohad Cohen, Awad's original claim sought about 108,000 shekels in total, covering unpaid wages, compensation for salary arrears, a promotion bonus, pension and severance contributions, vacation payouts and recuperation ('hav'ara') allowances.

Arbitrator Alona Bumgartan rejected the club's defence, which had leaned on signed settlement documents purporting to close out the dispute. According to ONE, she found those documents did not meet the legal requirements for a valid waiver, ruling they had not been freely signed and pointing to what she described as improper pressure from the club on the player.

The final award breaks down as 8,000 shekels for unpaid wages, 5,000 shekels in compensation for the salary arrears, a 15,000-shekel promotion bonus, 25,300 shekels for pension and severance shortfalls, 8,762 shekels in vacation pay, 6,416 shekels in recuperation fees, additional compensation on top of that, and a further 10,000 shekels in legal costs awarded against the club.

The case is a reminder of how often wage disputes surface in Israel's lower football tiers, where clubs operate on tight budgets and players frequently turn to arbitration to recover money they say they are owed even after helping a team achieve promotion on the pitch.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv give trial to free-agent left back Bilal Shaheen
dek: The 23-year-old, released by Ironi Kiryat Shmona in the summer, has trained with the Reds this week as cover for Doron Leidner while primary target Yahav Gorfinkel stalls in Cyprus.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have quietly opened a trial for a free-agent left back, giving Bilal Shaheen a run in a red shirt this week as the club searches for cover at a position that has become a genuine concern heading into Europe.

Shaheen, 23, has trained with the first team since earlier this week after his contract at Ironi Kiryat Shmona expired at the end of last season, leaving him without a club. According to Sport5, the arrangement is a straightforward mutual look — a chance for Eliniv Barda's coaching staff to assess him before any commitment is made, with no final decision yet taken.

The vacancy exists because Hapoel are still waiting on their preferred option. Yahav Gorfinkel, who starred for the club before moving abroad, remains under contract to AEK Larnaka in Cyprus and has not resolved whether he will leave the club to return to Tel Aviv. That uncertainty has pushed the technical staff to widen the search rather than sit and wait.

The immediate need is depth behind Doron Leidner, the incumbent left back who returned to Hapoel Tel Aviv on loan from Olympiacos last year. Leidner's history of fitness problems is part of why the club wants a proven alternative in reserve rather than relying on academy cover alone.

Shaheen's situation makes him an attractive stopgap even without a transfer fee changing hands. Because he came through Kiryat Shmona's own development pathway and is currently a free agent, Hapoel would owe the northern club only a modest training-compensation payment rather than negotiate a fee, should the trial turn into a contract.

The timing adds pressure to reach a verdict quickly. Hapoel Tel Aviv open their Conference League third qualifying round away — though effectively at a neutral Hungarian venue — against GKS Katowice on Thursday, hosting the first leg at DVTK Stadium in Miskolc before travelling to Poland for the return fixture on August 12.

For now, Shaheen remains an trialist rather than a squad member, and Sport5's report gives no indication he will be involved in the Katowice tie either way. The club's stance, as relayed by the outlet, is that this is impression-gathering rather than a done deal, with the final call resting on how he performs in training over the coming days.
Whether Hapoel ultimately turn to Shaheen may hinge less on his own audition than on Gorfinkel's decision in Cyprus — a call the club is still waiting on as their European campaign approaches.

title: Ashdod's role in Tiberias doping-case hearings sharply limited by IFA arbitrator
dek: Nir Liubin rules Ashdod may argue only over penalties in the Ironi Tiberias banned-infusions case, not the main proceedings, with a preliminary hearing set for August 5.

verificationSources.label: ONE: Ashdod demands to join proceedings against Tiberias

Walla: Ashdod presses to speed up the Tiberias infusions case
