body: Nir Liubin, the Israeli Football Association's chief disciplinary arbitrator, has partially granted M.S. Ashdod's bid to join the explosive case against Ironi Tiberias over banned intravenous infusions — but he has sharply restricted what Ashdod can actually do inside the hearing room, Sport5 reports.

Tiberias is under indictment for allegedly organising banned saline infusions for several players before last season's bottom-of-the-table relegation playoff against Ashdod, with officials accused of procuring 12 bags of 1,000ml solution and administering more than the permitted volume, according to Haaretz's report on the charge sheet. The IFA prosecution has asked for a deduction of at least 30 league points, a 500,000-shekel fine and lengthy suspensions for players and staff, Walla and Ynet have reported.

Ashdod has a direct stake in the outcome: it finished on the wrong side of that same relegation playoff and was sent down to Liga Leumit, while Tiberias stayed up in Ligat Ha'al. The club argues that if the infusions affected the result, it — not Tiberias — should have kept its top-flight place, and its attorney, Amit Hadad, had asked the disciplinary court for a broad role in shaping the case, ONE reported.

Ashdod's original demands were far-reaching: an accelerated timetable to resolve the matter before the 2026/27 season opens in roughly three weeks, an injunction stopping Tiberias from registering its squad, and a right to be consulted before any settlement between the IFA prosecution and the club.

Liubin rejected the attempt to let Ashdod impose positions and preconditions before any evidence is heard. He also dismissed a separate objection from Tiberias, which had argued Ashdod had no standing to intervene at all since it was not a direct opponent in the disciplinary matter itself.

After the IFA prosecution agreed to bring Ashdod into the proceedings in a limited capacity, Ashdod withdrew most of its original claims — a retreat the arbitrator praised in his written ruling, per Sport5.

The scope that remains is narrow: Ashdod may attend the hearings and present its position only on penalties and consequences, not run its own line of argument through the main evidentiary hearing on whether Tiberias broke the rules in the first place.

Liubin's ruling also noted an eight-point gap between the two clubs at the end of last season, a detail Sport5 flagged without further elaboration — presumably bearing on whether any points deduction handed to Tiberias could realistically alter where each club finished.
A preliminary hearing in the case is scheduled for August 5, with Liubin instructing both clubs to avoid personal accusations and to keep the proceedings dignified.

The wider picture, according to a separate Sport5 report, is that league officials do not appear to be preparing Ashdod for a return to the top flight: the budget oversight body has not directed the club to draw up a Ligat Ha'al budget, which the outlet reads as a sign that Tiberias is expected to survive the case — facing a heavy points penalty and fine, but not relegation.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv rejects fired coach Messay Dego's 1.74 million shekel lawsuit
dek: The club branded the claim "audacious" and insisted its return to the Israeli Premier League came despite Dego, not because of him.

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv has come out swinging against Messay Dego, the coach it sacked in December 2024, after he filed a labor court lawsuit demanding 1,740,394 shekels in unpaid wages and benefits.

In a scathing public statement, the club described the claim as an act of "audacity" and accused Dego, whom it called a coach "earning enormous wages," of trying in bad faith to "grab money not owed to him." "It takes considerable audacity to demand payment at the stated rate without working," the club said.

Dego's suit, filed with the labor court, seeks wages he says the club stopped paying from June 2025 despite a contract that was meant to run through the end of the 2025/26 season. It also includes a promotion bonus of roughly 250,000 shekels and housing and vehicle benefits worth about 600,000 shekels, according to the claim reported by Ynet and ONE.

Central to Dego's argument is that Hapoel Tel Aviv's promotion back to the Israeli Premier League was, in his view, a professional achievement he laid the groundwork for even though he did not see it through. He says his dismissal was handled poorly, delivered in what he called a "humiliating" manner that reached him through the media before any official club notice.

Hapoel Tel Aviv sees it very differently. The club's rebuttal, carried by Sport5, put it bluntly: "We reached the league not thanks to Massaï, but in spite of Massaï." Its position is that Dego, who had the largest budget in Liga Leumit at his disposal, was let go after 14 rounds with the team well off the pace for the automatic promotion places.

Dego departed the club in December 2024, and Eliniv Barda was brought in as his successor. Barda went on to guide Hapoel Tel Aviv to the Liga Leumit title and an immediate return to the top flight in April 2025, a turnaround the club is now citing as evidence that Dego's methods, not his absence, were the problem.

The dispute has been simmering for months. Dego's camp reportedly sent Hapoel Tel Aviv a warning letter weeks before filing suit, which the club chose not to answer, according to Ynet's reporting on the case.

With both sides now on the record and the claim in the labor court's hands, the financial and reputational fight looks set to run well beyond the pitch, with Hapoel Tel Aviv making clear it intends to contest the demand in full rather than settle.

body: Maccabi Haifa received a welcome update on Omri Glazer's fitness on Sunday, with the club reporting a significant improvement in the goalkeeper's injured leg less than a week after he was carried off in tears.

Glazer went down clutching his knee during Maccabi Haifa's Toto Cup defeat to Ironi Kiryat Shmona after a collision with his own teammate, defender Wanderson, who caught him awkwardly in the challenge. Wanderson himself remains sidelined, still working his way back from a concussion sustained in the same passage of play that injured Glazer, according to ONE.

Elsewhere in the squad, Andrea Novakovic is unavailable after picking up a virus, while winger Manuel Benson is being gradually integrated into the group and is expected to eventually take over from Cedric Don on the right flank.

Summer signing Yair Mordechai, who scored twice during Maccabi Haifa's training camp in Hungary, has been left out of consecutive sessions, an indication of just how stiff the competition for places has become in Bakhar's squad ahead of the new season.

title: Tribunal lets Ashdod join disciplinary case against Tiberias, but only as observer
dek: The football association's disciplinary tribunal partially granted Ashdod's request to be recognised as an interested party in the injections-affair case against Tiberias, while blocking the club from cross-examining witnesses and rejecting a faster timetable.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Ashdod's request to join proceedings
Haaretz - Tiberias indicted over prohibited substances
Sport1/Maariv - Tiberias owner's response to Ashdod

body: M.S. Ashdod will have a seat, but not a voice, in the disciplinary proceedings that could yet decide whether the club remains in the second tier or is handed back its place in Ligat Ha'al. The football association's disciplinary tribunal ruled on Ashdod's request to join the case against Ironi Tiberias only partially, ONE reported, granting the club observer status while refusing it any active role in the hearings.

The tribunal recognised Ashdod as an "interested party," meaning representatives can attend hearings and present the club's position in writing or in person. But the panel drew a firm line around what that status actually allows: Ashdod cannot cross-examine witnesses, cannot pose questions during proceedings and cannot otherwise intervene in the evidentiary process, according to ONE.

"Joining a party that is not the accused is an exceptional step that requires caution," the tribunal wrote in its decision, underlining that Ashdod's involvement would stay strictly limited to that of an onlooker rather than a participant with standing equal to the prosecution or the defence.

The tribunal also rejected Ashdod's separate request to speed up the timetable. A preliminary hearing remains scheduled for Wednesday, August 5, with dates for the evidentiary stage to be fixed only once that session takes place - not the accelerated, pre-season resolution Ashdod had been pushing for.

The case against Tiberias stems from what has become known in Israeli football as the "injections affair." The association's indictment, filed last month, accuses club officials of arranging saline injections for players in bulk - reportedly some 12 large bags totalling around a litre - administered without proper medical supervision and, the charge sheet alleges, under pressure applied to the players themselves.

Tiberias faces charges including assisting the use of prohibited and stimulant substances under aggravated circumstances, breaching association regulations, failing to comply with a judicial body's decisions, and additional counts related to alleged obstruction and coordinated false testimony. Possible sanctions span fines of up to 380,000 shekels, further points deductions, relegation and even suspension from all football activity.

Ashdod's interest in the outcome is direct and, by its own account, costly. The club argues it was harmed at the sharpest possible moment: the alleged conduct is said to relate to the period around a decisive relegation-playoff fixture between the two sides last season. Ashdod finished bottom of Ligat Ha'al's lower playoff and was relegated to Liga Leumit after ten straight seasons in the top flight, while Tiberias avoided the drop despite having already had eight points docked over a separate, unrelated case involving alleged double contracts.

In its application to join the case, Ashdod's legal team argued the club was "the sporting side harmed most directly" by the events under investigation and asked the tribunal for interim measures to stop Tiberias registering for the 2026/27 season until the case is resolved, along with a ruling that would land before that season begins. Both the interim request and the accelerated schedule were rebuffed in this decision, ONE reported.

Tiberias has pushed back hard in public. Club owner Arie Kalmenson accused Ashdod of running a "coordinated and orchestrated campaign to blacken" his club, calling the legal manoeuvring an attempt to "harness legal procedures for an unsporting outcome" after Ashdod's relegation was sealed on the pitch. He noted Tiberias finished eight points clear of Ashdod by season's end and said the indictment itself would be disproved in the tribunal, not settled through what he described as a media campaign.

For now, the practical stakes remain unresolved. Ashdod's presence in the room from Wednesday's preliminary hearing gives the relegated club visibility into a case that could, depending on the eventual verdict and any sporting sanction attached to it, still affect where each side plays its football in 2026/27 - even if Ashdod will be watching rather than arguing.

title: Deni Avdija: 'Not everyone is happy that I'm Israeli, it bothers me less'
dek: The Portland Trail Blazers forward addresses the hostility he sometimes draws over his nationality, while looking ahead to a new NBA season and a second All-Star bid.

verificationSources.label: Times of Israel — Avdija's breakout season

body: Deni Avdija has grown used to a kind of scrutiny that has nothing to do with his jump shot or his rebounding numbers. Speaking in a television interview cited by Sport5, the Portland Trail Blazers forward addressed head-on the friction that sometimes follows him onto NBA courts because of where he is from.

"Not everyone is happy that you're Israeli, but that's reality. It bothers me less," Avdija said, according to Sport5, when asked directly about carrying his nationality with him across American arenas.

It is not the first time the 25-year-old has spoken on the subject. In separate interviews carried by N12 and Haaretz earlier this year, Avdija described feeling hostility from crowds at times and said the increased attention on his identity has come hand in hand with his rising profile in the league, even as he insisted he draws far more support than hostility from Israeli and Jewish fans who turn out with flags at his games.

The comments come off the back of a breakout campaign in Portland. Avdija earned his first NBA All-Star selection during the 2025-26 season, a run that included three triple-doubles and a 41-point outburst against Houston, and saw him ranked among the league's top players in scoring, assists and efficiency, according to the Times of Israel.
He also led Israel's national team to the round of 16 at EuroBasket 2025, the country's first appearance that deep in the tournament in a decade, before losing to a Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Greece.

Looking ahead to the coming NBA season, Avdija told the interviewer his priorities are straightforward: "I want to be part of a winning team," he said, adding that he hopes to reach the All-Star game again while staying healthy throughout the year.

Asked about his personal life, Avdija kept things light, saying he is not chasing a relationship but is not ruling one out either. "I'm very focused on my career, but I'm living life, I'm going with the flow," he said, per Sport5.
On visits home, he said the first order of business is always the same: sitting down to a meal cooked by his mother, and making time with his parents before diving back into his NBA schedule.

title: Red Star Belgrade, CSKA Sofia and Austria Wien await Israel's four European hopefuls
dek: Hapoel Be'er Sheva, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv all discover this week whether they advance towards the play-off round of Europe's three club competitions.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC – official site
UEFA.com – Ludogorets vs Hapoel Tel Aviv match page

body: It is the busiest week of the Israeli football calendar outside the domestic season itself: within the space of nine days, all four Israeli clubs still alive in Europe learn whether they are one step closer to the lucrative league phase of the Champions League, Europa League or Conference League, or heading out of the continent altogether.

Hapoel Be'er Sheva, champions of Israel last season, carry the flag in the top tier. Having eliminated Vikingur Reykjavik of Iceland 2-0 in the second qualifying round, the Negev side now face Serbian giants Red Star Belgrade in the Champions League third qualifying round, with the first leg on August 4 and the return in Be'er Sheva a week later, on August 11.

Sport5 reports that the tie already guarantees Be'er Sheva a soft landing: even a defeat to Red Star drops them into the Europa League play-off round rather than out of Europe, worth a minimum €3.17 million to the club, rising to €4.31 million more should they get past the Serbs and reach the Champions League play-off itself.

Maccabi Tel Aviv's route into Europe came through last season's State Cup triumph, and having seen off Moldovan side Sheriff Tiraspol - with the return leg played in Batumi, Georgia rather than the contested Tiraspol ground - they now meet CSKA Sofia of Bulgaria in the Europa League third qualifying round, first leg on August 6 and the second on August 13, per Sport5's report.

As with Be'er Sheva, defeat would not end Maccabi's European summer: a loss to CSKA Sofia sends the Yellow-and-Blue into the Conference League play-off round instead, with Sport5 citing a guaranteed €750,000 in prize money already banked and a further €3.17 million on offer if they progress in the Europa League.

Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv, both of whom qualified for the Conference League through their league placings, do not enjoy the same cushion. Having progressed past Cypriot side AEK Larnaca in a second qualifying round tie that finished level on aggregate after two tense legs, Beitar now face Austria Wien of Austria in the third qualifying round, also scheduled for August 6 and 13, Sport5 reports.

Hapoel Tel Aviv, meanwhile, advanced past Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad and have been drawn against GKS Katowice of Poland over the same two dates. Sport5 puts a place in the Conference League play-off round at €750,000 for either club, with €550,000 already guaranteed simply for having reached this stage - but for both Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, there is no parachute: lose this tie and the European campaign is over.

That asymmetry is the real story behind the numbers. Israel's two highest-ranked entrants are cushioned by UEFA's tiered qualifying system, which drops losing sides down into the next competition down rather than eliminating them outright; Beitar and Hapoel Tel Aviv, starting in the Conference League itself, have no such safety net and are playing knockout football in the truest sense.

Winners of all four ties move into the play-off round, the last hurdle before the revamped league phase of each competition, with first legs pencilled in for August 18-20 and the second legs a week later, August 25-27, according to Sport5.

For a football association whose clubs' European coefficient underpins Israel's access to the continent's most valuable competitions, a strong showing from all four sides this month carries weight well beyond the clubs themselves - both financially and for the country's standing when the next qualifying draw is made.

title: Inside the 2026 World Cup's penalties: committing early beat reading the goalkeeper
dek: A Ynet review of all 22 penalties taken at the tournament found takers who picked their corner in advance scored more often than those who tried to read the goalkeeper, with most kicks kept low and over 40% arriving in a match's final half hour.

verificationSources.label: Han, Li, Zhang, Memmert & Han (2025), International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
NPR: Spain beats Argentina to win 2026 World Cup

body: A month after Spain edged Argentina in extra time to lift the 2026 World Cup, the small print of the tournament is still being picked over — and one of the more interesting threads to emerge concerns what actually separates a scored penalty from a missed one.

In its KICK column, Ynet writers Manor Ohiyon and Tamir Bar reviewed all 22 penalty kicks taken over the course of the tournament and split the takers into two camps: those who picked their corner before the referee's whistle and were not for turning, and those who waited to read the goalkeeper's dive before committing.

On this sample, the numbers tilt heavily toward committing early. Of the 12 penalties struck to a predetermined corner, ten went in — an 83.3% conversion rate. Of the ten taken on a goalkeeper-dependent basis, six were scored, for 60%.

The column is upfront that a gap drawn from just 22 kicks does not clear the bar of statistical significance — the sample is too small to crown one method definitively superior. But the direction of the numbers, it argues, still points somewhere useful: under the extreme pressure of a World Cup penalty, simplicity appears to travel better than improvisation.

Where takers actually aimed reinforces that idea. More than half of the 22 penalties were struck to the goalkeeper's low right corner, and the large majority were kept down rather than lifted — the low, hard, rehearsed shot rather than the audacious dink or a blast to the top corner.

Timing mattered too. Roughly 41% of the penalties awarded across the tournament came in the final half hour of matches, a concentration the column reads as evidence that fatigue and pressure both spike late in games — precisely when a rehearsed routine is worth the most.

The piece sets its findings alongside a peer-reviewed study published this year in the International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching by Zidong Han, Guosong Li, Yufei Zhang, Daniel Memmert and Bo Han, which tracked 64 in-match penalties across the 2014, 2018 and 2022 World Cups. That research found the keeper-dependent, wait-and-react approach had grown more common by 2022 — and had actually scored at a higher rate that year, a reminder that the debate shifts from tournament to tournament rather than settling into fixed science.

Its reading of 2026, though, comes down on the side of certainty over cleverness: the players most likely to score, it argues, were not the ones trying to out-guess the goalkeeper in the moment, but the ones who had already decided exactly what they were going to do and simply executed it under the lights of the World Cup.

More than half of the 22 penalties were aimed at the goalkeeper's low right corner, with most shots kept low.
About 41% of the tournament's penalties came in the final 30 minutes of matches.
Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 World Cup final on July 19, 2026.
A 2025 peer-reviewed study by Han et al. found keeper-dependent penalty strategies grew more common and scored at a higher rate at the 2022 World Cup.

title: World Cup sensation Vozinha mobbed by hundreds of fans on arrival in Chile
dek: The 40-year-old Cape Verde goalkeeper who became one of the breakout stars of the World Cup landed in Santiago on Sunday night to a chanting, flag-waving crowd as he joins Colo Colo.
body: Santiago's international arrivals hall turned into a cauldron of noise late on Sunday night as several hundred Colo Colo supporters, some with young children in tow, packed the terminal to greet a goalkeeper most of them had never heard of two months earlier.

Vozinha, the 40-year-old Cape Verdean shot-stopper who became one of the World Cup's most talked-about figures, touched down in the Chilean capital shortly after 8.30pm local time and emerged from customs roughly half an hour later alongside Colo Colo sporting manager Daniel Morón, to chants, white-and-black banners and, in an unusual sight for a Santiago airport, a scattering of Cape Verde flags.

It capped a slow-burning transfer saga: Colo Colo, Chile's most decorated club, announced in late July that it had agreed an 18-month deal with the goalkeeper, only for his travel to be delayed by visa paperwork before he finally touched down this weekend.

The reception reflected how far Vozinha's profile has travelled since Cape Verde's historic first-ever World Cup appearance. He made seven saves in a goalless draw with eventual champions Spain, a performance that, at 40 years and 12 days old, made him the oldest player to appear in a nation's debut World Cup match.

He followed that up with eight more stops against defending champions Argentina, a match Cape Verde ultimately lost 3-2 after extra time, but one that only deepened the goalkeeper's cult following worldwide.

His Instagram account, which had roughly 50,000 followers before the tournament, has since swelled into the tens of millions, one of the more remarkable social-media surges to come out of the World Cup, and voters in FIFA's fan poll selected him for the tournament's Dream Team alongside Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Michael Olise.
"I'm very happy to represent Colo Colo," Vozinha told reporters at the airport, according to Chilean outlets, thanking supporters for their patience through the delayed move.

The scenes were striking given the circumstances: a Sunday night in the middle of the Chilean winter, yet fans still turned out in numbers to welcome a player who will now compete for a starting spot at the Estadio Monumental.

Vozinha, whose full name is Josimar José Évora Dias, earned his nickname as a boy on the island of São Vicente, where, according to Cape Verdean accounts of his upbringing, he would run to his grandmother after tough knocks during street games, and the name stuck for the rest of his career.

Before this year he had spent much of his career as a journeyman in Portugal's second tier, far from the spotlight now trained on him after Cape Verde's run turned him into one of the sport's most improbable global stories.

title: Barcelona waits on Álvarez, but stays calm about the striker position
dek: The Catalan club's roughly €100 million offer for Julián Álvarez remains unanswered by Atlético Madrid, but ONE reports Barcelona see no reason to panic or overpay before his August 10 return to training.
body: Barcelona's chase of Julián Álvarez has stalled at Atlético Madrid's front door, but ONE reports the club is refusing to let the impasse rattle it — insisting there is no need to panic, and no intention of overpaying, over the striker position left open by Robert Lewandowski's exit.

The Catalans have had an offer of around €100 million on the table for the Argentine forward, but Atlético have given no formal response. Rather than negotiate, the Madrid club has taken its objections public and lodged a complaint against Barcelona with the Spanish football federation over the way the approach has been conducted — a complaint Barcelona's legal department is now reviewing, according to the report.

Atlético's position has not moved: Álvarez is contracted until 2030 and carries a release clause reported at €500 million, and the club insists it will not sell him this summer at any price short of that figure, regardless of what Barcelona or the player himself want.

That has not stopped Álvarez making his own preference clear. During the World Cup in North America, the striker said he believed it was in everyone's interest for his club to negotiate his departure — stopping short of naming Barcelona directly, though reports in Spain have long described the move to Camp Nou as his dream.

Manager Hansi Flick has pushed hard behind the scenes for the deal, reportedly messaging Álvarez personally to assure him Barcelona will keep fighting for the signing, and he is said to regard the 26-year-old as the ideal successor to Lewandowski up front.

The date to watch is August 10, when Álvarez — like the rest of Argentina's World Cup finalists — is due back at Atlético's Madrid training base for pre-season. How he presents himself that day, and whether he pushes publicly for an exit, is expected to say a great deal about where the saga goes next.

For now, though, ONE reports Barcelona are treating their bid as fair and are not about to be rushed into a panic move. The club already has Lamine Yamal, Raphinha and Ferran Torres available in attack, and reasons that, absent Álvarez, there is currently no alternative centre-forward on the market who matches Lewandowski's level anyway.

That composure gives Barcelona room to wait out Atlético rather than escalate the offer — but with a release clause five times the size of the current bid and a rival federation complaint in play, the standoff shows no sign of resolving itself before Álvarez walks back into Atlético's dressing room next week.

title: Hapoel Ramat Gan beat Maccabi Netanya 3-2 but insist 'nothing resembles the league'
dek: Two wins from two in the Toto Cup have the newly promoted club encouraged, but Ramat Gan's own verdict is that cup form counts for little once Liga Leumit begins.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia - Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim F.C.

body: Hapoel Ramat Gan have won both their Toto Cup group games this summer, the latest a 3-2 fightback against Maccabi Netanya on Sunday. The club's own reaction, though, was strikingly sober: cup football, they said, tells you almost nothing about what awaits in Liga Leumit.

Sunday's win in Netanya was not straightforward. Brazilian forward Luan Campos put Ramat Gan ahead in the 33rd minute, only for Mateus Daabo to level for the hosts six minutes later. David Asencka restored the lead just after the hour, and Maksim Palkoshchenko added a third from the penalty spot in the 61st minute before Daabo pulled one back late on to make it 3-2.

Palkoshchenko's goal carried its own subplot. The 30-year-old spent the past three seasons at Maccabi Netanya before joining Ramat Gan as a free agent this summer, and his old club held a brief ceremony in his honour before kick-off. He chose not to celebrate when his penalty went in.

The result made it two wins from two in the Toto Cup group stage for Ramat Gan, who return to competitive league action for the first time since winning promotion back to Liga Leumit for the 2025-26 season.

"There are many good points that make us optimistic, and we need to work hard on the less good things," the club said in a statement carried by ONE. "Our goal first is to complete the squad and come as prepared as possible for the league." The message, echoed in the report's headline, was blunt: nothing in the Toto Cup resembles what the league will demand.

Manager Messay Dego has praised his players' tactical discipline and application through the two Toto Cup rounds, according to the report, even as the club frames the results as a work in progress rather than a statement of intent.

Among the summer's more significant additions is João Paulo Jota Gonçalves, a Portuguese defender signed on a two-year deal from Vizela, where he had captained the second-division side and previously featured for Portugal's under-21 squad. He has been installed as Ramat Gan's captain for the new campaign.
Ramat Gan are back in Toto Cup action on Wednesday against Hapoel Jerusalem in the competition's knockout stage, with squad-building for the league still very much the priority behind the scenes.

title: Leeds 4-2 Liverpool: Calvert-Lewin double sinks Reds after 2-0 collapse
dek: Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored twice from long throw-ins as Leeds United overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Liverpool in Chicago, closing out both clubs' pre-season tours.
body: Liverpool's pre-season ended in embarrassment at Soldier Field on Sunday, as Leeds United came from two goals down to win 4-2 and hand Andoni Iraola a harsh lesson in his final run-out as the club's new head coach.

For 45 minutes it looked routine. Luke Chambers put the Reds ahead after seven minutes, and Florian Wirtz, back on the scoresheet in his second pre-season outing since his big-money move from Bayer Leverkusen, doubled the lead five minutes before the break after being teed up by Jeremie Frimpong.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke tore up his team at the interval, sending on Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Harry Wilson, and the substitutions transformed the game. Brenden Aaronson pulled one back on the hour mark, and from there Liverpool's defence simply came apart.

Calvert-Lewin, the former Everton striker now at Elland Road, headed home two long throw-ins from Ethan Ampadu either side of a Sean Longstaff strike, turning a comfortable Liverpool lead into a 4-2 defeat inside little more than 20 second-half minutes.

ONE reports that Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai was blunt in his post-match assessment of the collapse, saying the team had been undone by exactly the kind of set-piece failings that dogged them for spells last season. "We conceded two goals from set pieces and we must address this. Last season we saw how crucial corners and long throw-ins became," he said.

The result was Iraola's first defeat since arriving at Anfield to replace the sacked Arne Slot, and it will sting more for how avoidable it looked. Two goals scored from the same long-throw routine, delivered by the same player, is precisely the sort of preventable pattern a new coaching staff wants ironed out before the campaign, not repeated inside it.

There were individual positives for Liverpool amid the wreckage. Wirtz's goal continues an encouraging pre-season for the German playmaker, while academy graduate Trey Nyoni again caught the eye with an energetic display in midfield. Frimpong, whose fitness had been a concern, also came through the match without further injury trouble.

The friendly, played in front of a crowd of 49,128 at Soldier Field, was the closing fixture of both clubs' United States tours. Liverpool and Leeds now return to England to complete their preparations, with the Premier League season kicking off in roughly three weeks.
For Iraola, the priority is clear: turn a defence that leaked four goals in half an hour into one that can hold a lead, before the opening weekend arrives for real.

title: Italy 17-12 Israel: young water polo team falls at European under-20 championship
dek: Mia Tiroush's four goals were not enough as Israel slipped to defeat in Oeiras, with a tougher test against defending champions Spain up next.

body: Israel's national under-20 women's water polo team went down 17-12 to Italy on Sunday in their second group match at the European U-20 Championship in Oeiras, Portugal, ONE reported.
Unlike their opening game against Greece, the Blue-and-White made a sluggish start this time, and Italy took control early and never let it go, according to the report.
Mia Tiroush was Israel's standout, scoring four goals. Tava Dorfman added three and Carmel Rachum chipped in two, while Maya Katzir, Yuval Raz and Shir Weissman each found the net once.

Greek head coach Orestis Salachas struck a defiant note despite the result. "I am very proud of my team, because it showed heart, passion and a strong will to win until the last moment," he said, according to ONE.

The tournament, running August 3-9 in Oeiras, brings together the continent's top eight under-20 women's sides in Division 1, split into two groups of four, with the top two from each advancing to the quarterfinals. Israel and Italy both qualified for the top tier on the strength of their finishes at the 2024 European Championship.

Israel's group finale comes against Spain, the defending European champions, who have yet to drop a point in the group phase — a stern follow-up test for a young Israeli side still finding its footing at this level.

title: Five federations that backed Infantino's World Cup investment plan before it collapsed
dek: Czech Republic, Qatar, Kuwait, Sri Lanka and Lebanon stood by the FIFA president's $20bn plan to sell World Cup rights to private investors — before he was forced to scrap it under fierce opposition from Europe and beyond.
body: Gianni Infantino spent late July fighting for his political survival inside FIFA, and when the scheme he had built to secure it finally collapsed on July 31, only a handful of the game's 211 member federations had been prepared to say, on the record, that they still backed him. According to Sport5, five of them did: the Czech Republic, Qatar, Kuwait, Sri Lanka and Lebanon publicly defended the FIFA president's plan to sell a stake in future World Cups to private investors before he was forced to abandon it.

The scheme, unveiled by Infantino in late July, would have seen FIFA sell a minority stake in a new commercial entity built around the World Cup to outside investors, in a venture reported to be valued at up to $20 billion — Sport5 put the sum FIFA hoped to raise at around €15 billion. Reports named Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital as the investor group being lined up to lead the deal.

To secure the votes he needed, Infantino offered every one of FIFA's 211 member associations an immediate payment of $20 million, with a further $66 million promised in installments through 2038, if they backed the plan when it came to a vote.

The proposal triggered the fiercest institutional revolt of Infantino's presidency. UEFA, CONMEBOL, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation all issued formal statements opposing the sale, and UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin urged European federations to withdraw their support and, if necessary, move to weaken Infantino's path to another term or push him out altogether.

Amid that wall of opposition, only one European federation broke ranks. Czech FA president David Trunda said he saw "pragmatic benefits" in working closely with Infantino, telling reporters he could "see the positive impact of Fifa's intentions," and arguing the money could fund youth development and grassroots infrastructure at home.

Qatar, host of the 2022 World Cup, went further still. The Qatar Football Association issued a statement praising Infantino's "wisdom" and declaring its "full support for his efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally."

Kuwait and Sri Lanka's federations reaffirmed their confidence in Infantino's leadership without elaborating in detail, while Lebanon's association said the proposal could still be reworked by FIFA's relevant committees "in a way that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity" — support with a caveat, but support nonetheless.

None of it was enough to save the plan. Facing threats of a boycott from European federations and internal claims that Infantino had misled FIFA's own staff over the deal's terms, the FIFA president abandoned the proposal on July 31 — a rare and striking retreat for a leader who has seldom lost an internal argument since taking charge of world football's governing body in 2016.

The episode leaves Infantino's authority visibly dented ahead of an expected bid for a further term as FIFA president, and it puts on the record exactly which federations were willing to stand publicly with him when most of the game would not.

title: Daniel Theis nears Maccabi Tel Aviv deal that would rank among the club's richest ever
dek: Sport5 reports the German center has agreed a two-year, roughly $2.2 million-a-season contract, tying Lonnie Walker IV as the second-best-paid foreign signing in Maccabi Tel Aviv history behind Carlos Arroyo's 2008 record deal.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have reportedly reached agreement with German international center Daniel Theis, with Sport5 reporting a two-year contract worth close to $2.2 million a season — a deal that would place him among the very richest imports the yellow-and-blue have ever signed.

That figure, per Sport5's accounting of the club's foreign payroll, would make Theis, level with guard Lonnie Walker IV, the second-highest-paid overseas player in Maccabi Tel Aviv's history. Only Carlos Arroyo's fabled $2.5 million contract for the 2008-09 championship season, still the benchmark more than fifteen years on, sits above it.

Walker, who joined Maccabi on a three-year, $10 million deal with NBA exit clauses, currently holds the title of the club's best-paid active player. Theis moving in alongside him at roughly $2.2 million a year would underline how aggressively Maccabi has been willing to spend to rebuild its roster this off-season.

Theis, 34, is one of European basketball's most decorated big men of the past decade. He spent eight seasons in the NBA across six franchises — most notably two stints with the Boston Celtics, with whom he reached the NBA Finals in 2022 — before returning to Europe.

With Germany's national team, Theis has been a fixture through three EuroBasket campaigns and was a key rotation piece in the run to gold at the 2023 FIBA World Cup, having also helped Germany to a bronze medal at EuroBasket 2022.

The move to Israel comes out of upheaval in France. Theis had signed with ASVEL Villeurbanne at the start of the summer, but the club's well-documented financial difficulties turned him into one of the hottest available names on the EuroLeague market within weeks.

Maccabi was not alone in circling. Hapoel Tel Aviv showed early interest, and Barcelona reportedly stayed in the conversation after missing out on center Moses Wright, according to Sportando's reporting on the chase. Maccabi is said to have pushed to close the deal quickly and has offered Theis the role of starting center.

The club has been busy reshaping its frontcourt and backcourt all summer, working around a returning core that has included guards Yam Madar and Scottie Wilbekin and forward Bonzie Colson, as it tries to build a squad capable of competing on both the domestic and EuroLeague fronts.

As of now the agreement remains a media report rather than a confirmed transfer. Israel Hayom's Tomer Givati described the talks as being at an advanced stage rather than finalized, and Maccabi Tel Aviv has not issued an official announcement or confirmed the contract's financial terms.

If it closes as reported, Theis would give Maccabi a proven, championship-tested center just as the club looks to reassert itself at the top of Israeli basketball and push deeper into the EuroLeague this season.
facts: Sport5 reports Maccabi Tel Aviv have reached agreement with German center Daniel Theis on a two-year contract worth approximately $2.2 million per season.

The reported salary would make Theis, tied with Lonnie Walker IV, the second-highest-paid foreign player in Maccabi Tel Aviv's history, behind only Carlos Arroyo's $2.5 million deal for the 2008-09 season.
Theis, 34, was leaving ASVEL Villeurbanne amid the French club's financial difficulties, making him a sought-after free agent on the EuroLeague market.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva beat Hapoel Jerusalem 1-0 as Aryeh reflects on his Jerusalem exit
dek: Ziv Aryeh's new side won his first meeting with the club he led for seven years, though the coach was already looking ahead to Sunday's clash with Hapoel Ramat Gan.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — the full story behind Aryeh's Hapoel Jerusalem departure
Walla Sport — Lior Zada named Hapoel Jerusalem coach
Hapoel Jerusalem FC on X — Zada appointment

body: Ziv Aryeh's first competitive meeting with the club he ran for seven seasons ended in his favour. Maccabi Petah Tikva beat Hapoel Jerusalem 1-0 in a Toto Cup fixture on Sunday, and the new man in the away technical area made sure to acknowledge where he came from.
"It was good at Hapoel Jerusalem and good that it was. Now it's fun at Maccabi Petah Tikva," Aryeh said afterward, quoted by Sport5.

Aryeh resigned from Hapoel Jerusalem in April after seven years in charge, a run that made him one of the longest-serving coaches in Israeli top-flight football. He took over at Maccabi Petah Tikva in late May, and Sunday's derby-of-sorts against his old club was the first real test of the new relationship.

It was not an entirely happy afternoon for the coach despite the result. "I didn't like our start. We were weak," Aryeh said, adding that a red card during the Toto Cup match "is the worst" for a squad still building fitness and cohesion in preseason. "It hurts our training."

He was already turning the page. "Our goals are to rest over the next two days and prepare for Hapoel Ramat Gan," Aryeh said, adding that the club expects to bring in more players before the Premier League campaign begins.

Aryeh also spoke warmly of the man who brought him to the club. "I have a great connection with Avi Luzon," he said of Maccabi Petah Tikva's longtime owner, who has run the club since the early 1990s.

On the other side, Hapoel Jerusalem were represented by Lior Zada, Aryeh's former assistant, who was handed the job on a permanent basis for 2026-27 after guiding the club to safety in the closing rounds of last season. Zada played down the result, saying there was little riding on it beyond "a good feeling," with his focus on moving the club past a difficult previous campaign.

Maccabi Petah Tikva captain Mohammad Hindi offered his own read on the game, saying that after the red card the team "went backward" and had to lean on several inexperienced players for the rest of the match.

Neither result carries league points — the Toto Cup is played out before the Premier League season proper gets underway — but for Aryeh, the fixture carried an obvious personal edge as he begins life away from the club that defined the past seven years of his coaching career.

title: Dolev Haziza clashes with old club as Hapoel Ramat Gan beat Maccabi Netanya 3-2 in Toto Cup
dek: The winger's first appearance in Netanya colours brought an assist, a yellow card and a heated flare-up with former teammate Maksim Palkoshchenko in a five-goal Toto Cup thriller.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv video piece on Haziza's debut

body: Dolev Haziza's first outing in Maccabi Netanya colours will be remembered for more than the scoreline. The winger, who joined Netanya only last week after seven years at Maccabi Haifa, was booked for clashing with Hapoel Ramat Gan defender Maksim Palkoshchenko in the closing stages of a wild 3-2 Toto Cup defeat at Myriam Stadium on Sunday.

With the match deep into stoppage time, Haziza and Palkoshchenko tangled while contesting the ball near the touchline. Team-mate Zhota pushed Haziza to the ground as the confrontation spilled over, and referee Matheus Dabo had to step between the two sides before showing Haziza a yellow card.
There was an added layer to the flashpoint: Haziza spent the 2017-18 season on loan at Ramat Gan, making his return to Myriam Stadium, this time in an opponent's shirt, a genuinely charged occasion.

For most of the afternoon, though, Haziza gave Netanya reason for optimism. He was named among the substitutes for his debut and came on in the 65th minute, immediately looking sharp and forcing a good save from the Ramat Gan goalkeeper soon after his introduction.

His most telling contribution arrived in the 87th minute, when he drove down the left and delivered a dangerous ball across goal. Silva got a touch but could not finish it off, and the loose ball fell to Matheus Dabo, who prodded home from close range to pull Netanya back to 3-2.

It was not enough to salvage a result. Louan Campos had opened the scoring for Ramat Gan in the 33rd minute, only for Dabo to equalise six minutes later. David Asanke restored the visitors' lead just after the hour, and Palkoshchenko made it 3-1 from the penalty spot in the 61st minute — notably choosing not to celebrate, reportedly out of respect for his former club.

The win kept Hapoel Ramat Gan, one of this season's Toto Cup newcomers, unbeaten in Group B, according to Sport1. For Netanya, the defeat is a footnote next to the bigger story: a first glimpse of Haziza in the yellow-and-blue after his high-profile arrival from Haifa, a move that returns the 31-year-old to the city of his birth.

Haziza, capped by the Israel national team and a regular for Maccabi Haifa since 2019, will be looking to make a calmer impression when Netanya begin their Israeli Premier League campaign in the coming weeks.

title: Nili Block beats Isabel Oliveira as ONE's podcast recaps a blockbuster GFN1 night
dek: The Knockout podcast welcomed Nili Block into studio to break down her decision win at Gordon Fight Night 1, with Rafi Aronov's flag-waving knockout and the Gordon brothers' record-setting Menora Hall show also on the agenda.

verificationSources.label: Israel Hayom — Ahavat Hashem Gordon beats John Linker at Menora Hall
Maariv Sport1 — Ministry of Sport honours Rafi Aronov

body: ONE's weekly combat-sports podcast, Nokaut ("Knockout"), pulled up a studio chair for Nili Block this week, and the multiple Muay Thai and kickboxing world champion had a big win to talk through: a judges' decision over Isabel Oliveira on the card that just delivered the biggest kickboxing and Thai-boxing night Israel has ever staged.

That card was GFN1 — Gordon Fight Night 1 — held on July 27 at Tel Aviv's Menora Mivtachim Arena and billed as the largest event of its kind ever put on in Israel. Hosts Yaniv Kaminski and Olga Rubin walked Block through the build-up, including, she said, how hard it was to land an opponent because so many fighters turned the fight down before Oliveira agreed to step in.

Block, a veteran of the Israeli combat-sports scene with a string of Muay Thai and kickboxing world titles to her name, used the studio slot to talk through her entrance, her preparation and the scorecards that ultimately went her way.

GFN1 itself was the headline story of the night regardless of Block's result. All three Gordon brothers — Ahavat Hashem, Ruach Hashem and Kivdei — competed professionally on the same card in front of a sellout crowd, with Ahavat Hashem Gordon topping the bill by defeating John Linker and Ruach Hashem Gordon facing Moldovan fighter Maximus Bjanotta.

The podcast didn't stop at Menora Hall. Kaminski and Rubin also devoted a segment to Rafi Aronov, the Israeli welterweight whose knockout win for Cage Warriors has become one of the sport's most talked-about moments in Israel over the past year.

Aronov, a police officer in Israel's elite Yasam unit who took part in repelling the Hamas attack on Ofakim on October 7, 2023, beat Brad Wheeler by second-round TKO at Cage Warriors 192 in London, forcing referee Mark Goddard to step in after a string of punches. He walked into the arena carrying the Israeli flag and dedicated the win to fallen IDF soldier Reei Biran.

According to ONE, the episode has Aronov reflecting on that night's emotional weight, what it meant to fight under the flag in a European organisation, and his response to critics — material that, paired with the fresh GFN1 result, made for a packed instalment of the show.
The Nokaut episode is available now on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

title: Dolev Haziza: 'I don't accept this defeat' as Netanya debut ends in 3-2 loss to Hapoel Ramat Gan
dek: Making his first appearance for Maccabi Netanya after seven years as Maccabi Haifa captain, Haziza reflected on a painful exit from Haifa and a rough opening night in orange.
body: Dolev Haziza's first night in a Maccabi Netanya shirt did not go the way he wanted. Netanya lost 3-2 at home to Hapoel Ramat Gan in a Toto Cup fixture on Sunday, and the new arrival, so used to winning at Maccabi Haifa, made no effort to hide his frustration afterwards.

"I don't accept such a defeat," Haziza said. "We shouldn't concede three goals at home." It was a blunt assessment for a player only a few days into his new club, but one that reflected the standards he carried over from seven years at Haifa.

There was a lighter note too. Haziza supplied the assist for Netanya's second goal, a reminder of the quality that made him one of the most reliable creative players in the Israeli Premier League over the past half-decade.

The bigger story, though, was simply being back on a pitch competing. "I missed playing. I went through difficult things at the start of the season," he said, alluding to a torrid few weeks before the move materialised.

"I'm trying to suppress the last six weeks," Haziza added. "I was captain at Haifa for seven years." He did not go into detail on exactly what soured his final months at the club, saying only that he would address it at another time.

The exit itself was abrupt after such a long and decorated stay. Haziza joined Maccabi Haifa in the summer of 2019 and became a central figure in the most successful period in the club's modern history, wearing the captain's armband through three consecutive championships and a run in the Champions League group stage. Haifa ultimately informed him this summer that he was outside the club's professional plans for the coming season, effectively ending his time there.

Maccabi Netanya, under coach Roni Levy, moved quickly to take advantage. Levy held direct talks with Haziza and pushed hard for the signing, and the two sides agreed a two-year contract reportedly worth around $250,000 per season. As part of the exit terms, Maccabi Haifa also contributed roughly NIS 400,000 toward his outstanding salary.

For Netanya, landing a player of Haziza's pedigree, a three-time champion and full Israel international, is a statement of intent as the club aims to build a squad capable of competing higher up the table. Haziza said he wants to help the team draw crowds back to the stadium and be ready for the matches ahead, starting with the rest of the Toto Cup campaign before the league season begins in earnest.

The defeat to Ramat Gan will sting regardless of the context. But for a player trying to move past a difficult exit from the club where he spent almost a decade, simply pulling on a new shirt and playing 90 minutes again was, in its own way, the point.

title: Rio de Janeiro, 29 August 2013: The Forty-Three Seconds That Made Yarden Gerbi Israel's First World Judo Champion
dek: A 24-year-old from Netanya beat five opponents by ippon in one night at the Maracanãzinho, finishing the French European champion in under a minute to win Israel's first-ever gold at a Judo World Championships.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — 2013 World Judo Championships, Women's 63 kg
The Times of Israel — 'Judoka bags first World Championship gold for Israel'
Ynetnews — 'Israeli Judoka Yarden Gerbi wins gold, makes history'
Haaretz — 'Golden Girl Yarden Gerbi on Top of the World Championships'

body: The Ginásio do Maracanãzinho in Rio de Janeiro had hosted basketball finals and rock concerts, but on the night of 29 August 2013 its mats belonged to judo, and to a 24-year-old from Netanya who had spent the whole tournament refusing to let a single fight go the distance.

Yarden Gerbi arrived at the 2013 World Judo Championships as the world number one in the under-63kg division, having won successive Grand Slam titles in Baku and Moscow earlier that year. She had been training since the age of six under coach Shany Hershko at the Meitav Netanya club, and by 2013 she already held five Israeli national titles. What she did not yet have was a global one.

She set about fixing that with brutal efficiency. Gerbi opened the tournament by beating El Salvador's Karla Catola Quijano in 45 seconds, and kept winning by ippon through every subsequent round. In the semifinal she faced Japan's Kane Abe, the world number four, and pulled off a grinding chokehold to force a submission after two minutes and 47 seconds — her longest fight of the day, and still one that never reached the judges.

That set up a final against Clarisse Agbegnenou, the reigning European champion from France and, by most accounts, a genuine friend of Gerbi's on the international circuit. Friendship did not survive first contact. Gerbi took Agbegnenou down, secured a chokehold, and had the match won by ippon in 43 seconds — the shortest, and biggest, fight of her career.

It was Israel's first-ever gold medal at a Judo World Championships, in either the men's or women's draw. Gerbi was only the fifth Israeli to win any medal at the event, following Yael Arad, Oren Smadja, Arik Ze'evi and Alice Schlesinger — but the first to stand on the top step.

The reaction at home was immediate. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu telephoned to congratulate her, calling the win a "fantastic achievement" and praising what he described as her "swift, elegant" style. President Shimon Peres invited her to his residence, telling her she had won through "wisdom, clarity and strength" and calling her, admiringly, "a real pistol."

Gerbi herself, still catching her breath trackside in Rio, put it more simply: "I'm so happy that it really ended this way. I had a great competition... Nothing can be better than this. I cried a little for my parents; they also cried."

The gold did not come from nowhere. Gerbi had already collected a bronze at the European Junior Championships in 2008 and a Maccabiah silver in 2009, climbing steadily through the ranks under Hershko's guidance before her breakthrough season in 2013. Rio confirmed what her results that year had been suggesting: for a few months at least, nobody in the world beat Gerbi at 63 kilograms.

She would not have the division to herself for long. Agbegnenou reversed the result a year later, beating Gerbi in the 2014 World Championship final, and went on to become one of the most decorated judoka in history. But Gerbi's own story was far from over — she added a European Games bronze in 2015 and, in Rio again three years after her world title, an Olympic bronze at the 2016 Games, Israel's first judo medal there since Ze'evi's bronze in Athens.

Gerbi was named Israel's Sportswoman of the Year in December 2014, and retired from competition in October 2017, saying simply that "the fire that once burned bright has faded." Six years after her night in the Maracanãzinho, Sagi Muki would win the men's world title in Tokyo — but it was Gerbi, in 2013, who first proved an Israeli judoka could stand at the very top of the sport's world stage.

For a country whose judo medals had, until then, always come in silver or bronze — Arad's Barcelona silver, Smadja's Barcelona bronze, Ze'evi's run of Olympic and world bronzes — Gerbi's 43 seconds in Rio de Janeiro were the first time the gold actually landed.
facts: Yarden Gerbi (Israel) won the women's -63kg gold medal at the 2013 World Judo Championships, held at the Ginásio do Maracanãzinho in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on 29 August 2013.

Gerbi trained from age six under coach Shany Hershko at the Meitav Netanya club and was ranked world number one in the -63kg category going into the 2013 championships.
She went on to win Olympic bronze in the same weight category at the Rio 2016 Games and was named Israel's Sportswoman of the Year in December 2014.
Gerbi retired from competitive judo in October 2017 after 22 years in the sport.

title: Galán and Chingotto beat Leal and Guerrero 6-2, 5-7, 7-6 to win Pretoria P1
dek: The Spanish-Argentine pair survive a match point against them in the decider to end a five-final losing run at Premier Padel's first stop in South Africa.
body: Alejandro Galán and Federico Chingotto are champions again. The Spanish-Argentine duo beat Javier Leal and Francisco Guerrero 6-2, 5-7, 7-6 in a final that stretched beyond two hours to win the Premier Padel P1 title in Pretoria on Sunday, ending a run of five runner-up finishes that had stretched back to the spring.

It was the pair's first trophy since Buenos Aires in May, after finals lost in Rome, Valladolid, Bordeaux, Valencia and Malaga had left them chasing a title for almost three months, according to Argentine outlet La Nación.

The final followed the pattern of their recent near-misses before finally breaking the other way. Galán and Chingotto raced through the first set 6-2, only for Leal and Guerrero — appearing in their first Premier Padel final together — to seize control at altitude and level with a 7-5 second set.

The decider went to the wire. Serving for the title at 5-4 in the third, Galán and Chingotto were broken back, handing their opponents a break point of their own before order was restored and the set went to a tiebreak, which the second seeds closed out 7-5.
"Today the Chingalán mode came out," Chingotto said afterwards, referencing the nickname fans have given the partnership, according to padelspain.net. "When they broke us at 5-4, I asked for it."

The route to the final had already tested them against the very best. Galán and Chingotto eliminated third seeds Lebrón and Augsburger in the quarterfinals, then beat top seeds Agustín Tapia and Arturo Coello — the world No. 1 pair — in the semifinals, arguably the statement result of their week.

The win was worth 1,000 ranking points, the pair's 18th title together and their sixth of the 2026 season. It cut the gap to Tapia and Coello atop the Premier Padel Race from roughly 1,530 points to 890 — 9,440 to 8,550 — with several events still to play this year.

Pretoria was the first Premier Padel event staged in South Africa, part of the tour's push to widen its footprint beyond Europe and Latin America. At roughly 1,339 metres above sea level, the thinner air produced a faster, lower-bouncing ball that early on suited the more attacking Leal and Guerrero before Galán and Chingotto adjusted.

For a partnership that has dominated men's padel since linking up, the manner of the win — recovering from a break down in the decider against opponents playing their maiden final — mattered almost as much as the trophy itself.

title: Katowice fight back to beat Radomiak 3-1, sending a warning to Hapoel Tel Aviv
dek: GKS Katowice recovered from a goal down to see off Radomiak Radom in the Ekstraklasa, offering an ominous glimpse of the side Hapoel Tel Aviv must face in next week's Conference League qualifier.

verificationSources.label: Jerusalem Post on Hapoel Tel Aviv's advance past Ludogorets

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have a week to prepare for the toughest leg of their European summer, and Sport5's Hebrew coverage of Sunday's Ekstraklasa round carries a clear message for the Reds: their next opponent, GKS Katowice, do not know how to lose ugly.

Katowice trailed Radomiak Radom 1-0 at the break after Ibrahima Camara's 37th-minute strike, but they tore the game apart after the interval. An Abdoul Tapsoba own goal in the 58th minute levelled things, Belarusian forward Ilya Shkurin put them ahead in the 67th, and Bartosz Nowak added a third deep into stoppage time to seal a 3-1 win.

Polish outlet sportowefakty, cited by Sport5, described a side that keeps finding another gear under pressure: "They demonstrate character repeatedly, showing strong ability. Over 20 shots this early in the season is impressive."

Shkurin, in particular, is the player Hapoel Tel Aviv's defenders will need to know inside out. Przegladsportowy, also quoted by Sport5, wrote that the 27-year-old "is performing excellently — scoring, assisting, using head and foot, even defending when needed."

It is not an isolated purple patch. Shkurin scored the winning goal that eliminated Slovakia's Žilina in the previous round of Conference League qualifying, the result that sent Katowice through to face Hapoel Tel Aviv in the third qualifying round in the first place.
That tie is now the club's main focus. The first leg is scheduled for Thursday, August 6, in Tel Aviv, before the sides travel to Katowice in southern Poland for the return.

Hapoel Tel Aviv arrive on the back of their own European test, having eliminated Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad 4-2 on aggregate. Emmanuel Boateng scored twice in a 2-2 second-leg draw after Elyaniv Barda's side had built a first-leg cushion, completing a run that has taken the club from the second tier to continental qualifiers within little more than a year.

Sport5's framing is unambiguous: Katowice arrive with confidence, goals and a proven capacity to come from behind, and Hapoel Tel Aviv will need a sharper defensive night than the one Radomiak produced if they are to protect their advantage heading into the second leg.

title: UEFA threatens legal action against Gianni Infantino over World Cup sell-off plan
dek: European football's governing body has warned the FIFA president to preserve every document tied to the abandoned $4.2 billion privatization scheme, escalating a governance crisis that has already cost him a key ally.
body: UEFA has fired a formal legal warning at Gianni Infantino, telling the FIFA president in a letter dated Tuesday that it is "actively considering legal steps, arbitration, and regulatory complaints" over his abandoned scheme to sell private stakes in the World Cup.

The letter, reported by The Telegraph, orders Infantino and FIFA to immediately locate and preserve every document and piece of electronic correspondence connected to the plan, warning that "any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice may constitute spoliation of evidence." UEFA has given him five business days to confirm compliance.

The dispute centres on the FIFA Forward Enterprise, a proposed commercial subsidiary that would have taken over running FIFA's biggest properties, including the World Cup and Club World Cup. The plan aimed to raise as much as $4.2 billion by selling a minority stake in a company valued at around $20 billion, with Infantino pitching it as a way to "turbocharge the development of the game globally."

Reporting on the proposed investors named Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner, through his Thrive Capital vehicle, alongside Trump-aligned media executive Greg Maffei — details that fuelled suspicion in European football circles that the deal was being negotiated in secrecy with a narrow circle of private backers.

UEFA's 55 member federations, including Israel's, threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments outright if the sale went ahead, a stance CNN and other outlets described as unprecedented unity from a body that rarely confronts FIFA so directly.

Facing that revolt, FIFA withdrew the proposal on 31 July. But UEFA did not stand down. In a blistering statement the following morning, it welcomed the climbdown while branding the scheme "the shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through," and declared it had formally "lost confidence" in Infantino's leadership.

The political cost has already landed close to Infantino. Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to the FIFA president and a former U.S. Soccer chief, resigned on 1 August, saying he had opposed the privatization plan "unequivocally."

CONCACAF piled on too, calling the episode symptomatic of Infantino's "poor governance and leadership" and demanding what it called "a comprehensive reckoning with this presidency" — a rare instance of a second confederation joining UEFA's criticism rather than shielding the FIFA president.

Infantino is due to stand for re-election as FIFA president next year, and the scale of the backlash — from Europe's boycott threat to CONCACAF's rebuke and now UEFA's evidence-preservation letter — has opened the first serious question marks over whether he survives the vote.

For now, the World Cup sale itself is dead. What UEFA is pursuing is accountability for how close it came to happening, and whether Infantino's own conduct in negotiating it broke FIFA's governance rules — a fight that, on the evidence of Tuesday's letter, is only beginning.

title: CF Montréal 2-2 New England Revolution: club condemns fans' antisemitic abuse of Dor Turgeman
dek: The Canadian club says it does not tolerate discrimination after a section of home supporters chanted 'Death to Israel' at forward Dor Turgeman, who answered with a goal before goalkeeper Sebastian Breza shoved him to the ground.
body: CF Montréal moved on Sunday to publicly address the behaviour of a section of its own support, after Israeli forward Dor Turgeman was targeted with chants of "Death to Israel" during Saturday night's Major League Soccer draw with New England Revolution at Stade Saputo, ONE reports.

New England took an early grip on the game, going 2-0 up inside the first half hour — Carles Gil converting a penalty before Turgeman doubled the lead in the 36th minute. It was the goal, and what followed it, that defined the night.

Witnesses in the stadium, including reporters covering the match, described a section of Montreal supporters directing anti-Israel abuse and repeated chants of "Death to Israel" at the 22-year-old throughout the contest. After scoring, Turgeman ran toward the section that had targeted him and celebrated with a defiant "can't hear you" gesture, arms spread and a hand cupped to his ear.

The response from the stands was immediate: fans hurled cups and bottles onto the pitch. Montreal goalkeeper Sebastian Breza then confronted Turgeman and shoved him to the ground, sparking a brief scuffle between players from both sides. Breza was shown a yellow card for his part in the incident.

Montreal fought back in the second half, with Brayan Vera and Prince Owusu scoring either side of the hour mark to salvage a 2-2 draw and deny the Revolution what had looked like a comfortable away win.

According to ONE, CF Montréal subsequently issued a statement acknowledging "discriminatory remarks directed at one of the players" during the match. The club said it "does not tolerate any form of discrimination or behaviour that encourages hatred," and confirmed it was investigating the incident in coordination with MLS and New England Revolution to establish the facts and decide on further action.

Turgeman, raised in Ashdod, joined New England from Maccabi Tel Aviv in September under MLS's U22 Initiative. He won two Israeli championships and an Israeli Super Cup with Maccabi before the move, and has ten senior caps for the Israel national team.
He has settled quickly into life in MLS, becoming just the tenth player in league history to score in each of his first three appearances for his club.

The abuse in Montreal was not reported in isolation: several outlets covering the match noted it came amid a wider pattern of antisemitic incidents recorded in Canada in recent months, adding weight to the scrutiny now facing both the club and the league over how they respond.

title: Kangwa: 'I had a 99% chance of missing the Vikingur game' before Panathinaikos exit
dek: The departing Hapoel Beer Sheva star tells ONE how a transfer complication nearly cost him a Champions League qualifier, and explains why the war in Israel was one factor in his move to Greece.

verificationSources.label: Africa Soccer - Kangwa transfer fee details
Lusaka Times - Kangwa completes Panathinaikos move

body: Kings Kangwa came within a whisker of missing the biggest night of his farewell season in Israel. The Zambian midfielder, who completed a move from Hapoel Beer Sheva to Panathinaikos in the last week of July, has revealed that a transfer complication almost ruled him out of the Champions League qualifier that sent his old club through to the next round.

"There was a 99% chance I wouldn't play against Vikingur because of that situation, but in the end we managed to fix it," Kangwa told ONE, without spelling out the precise nature of the problem beyond it being tied to the timing of his exit from Beer Sheva.

The tie in question was Beer Sheva's Champions League second qualifying round meeting with Vikingur Reykjavik. Kangwa had already scored in the first leg in Iceland, a 2-1 defeat on 21 July, before setting up the second goal as Beer Sheva won the return fixture 2-0 at Turner Stadium on 29 July to go through 3-2 on aggregate — his last significant contribution in a Hapoel shirt.

Days later the transfer to Athens was confirmed. Panathinaikos are reported to have paid a fixed fee of around €3.8 million, with a further €700,000 in add-ons taking the total package to roughly €4.5m, on a contract running to June 2030 — terms neither club has officially itemised.

Kangwa leaves Beer Sheva with a decorated two-year record: he was named Israeli Footballer of the Year for the 2025-26 season after a 12-goal campaign, won the Israeli league title the same year, and had already lifted the Israeli Cup in 2024-25 and the Israel Super Cup in 2025-26.

He was candid about the toll of the war in Israel on his decision to move on. "It was very difficult. War is not something you can joke about. Where I come from there is no war and no fighting, so for me and my family it was very hard," he said. "Everyone told me, 'You need to go home,' and you can understand them — but Hapoel Beer Sheva supported us and gave us all the support we needed." He confirmed the conflict was "one of the reasons" behind his decision to leave.
Money was not the deciding factor, he insisted, listing offers he turned down to sign for Panathinaikos: interest from New York City FC, from clubs in Russia and "from many clubs in Bulgaria."

Kangwa also addressed why he never crossed to one of Beer Sheva's domestic rivals during his time in Israel. Asked about interest from Maccabi Tel Aviv and Maccabi Haifa, he was unequivocal: "I preferred Beer Sheva. It was the right place for me." On any prospect of an Israeli return down the line, he added: "My preference is only for Hapoel Beer Sheva in Israel."

For now, the 27-year-old midfielder begins a new chapter in Athens, with a club that beat off competition from three continents to land one of the Israeli league's standout performers of the past two seasons.

title: CSKA Sofia 2-1 Dunav Ruse: Zwart on target again ahead of Maccabi Tel Aviv clash
dek: Joel Zwart's third league goal of the season set up a comeback win over bottom club Dunav Ruse, with CSKA Sofia now turning to a Europa League qualifier against Maccabi Tel Aviv this week.
body: CSKA Sofia let the bottom club in Bulgaria's top flight take an early lead on Sunday, but Dutch forward Joel Zwart hauled the home side level and a late strike from Facundo Rodríguez completed a 2-1 comeback win over Dunav Ruse at the Vasil Levski National Stadium — a result that matters well beyond Sofia, with the club four days from hosting Maccabi Tel Aviv's Europa League qualifier.

Dunav Ruse, without a point after their first two matches of the season, stunned the hosts in the 10th minute when Radoslav Apostolov finished from close range to put the visitors ahead. CSKA needed only seven minutes to respond, Zwart converting to level the scores and continue his hot start to the campaign.

The Dutchman, signed as CSKA's central striker this summer, has now scored three times in three domestic league matches. He struck twice against Botev Plovdiv in the previous round, and Bulgarian outlet Bgonair described Sunday's display as further proof that the club's new No. 9 is finding his rhythm at exactly the right moment.

The winner did not arrive until the 79th minute, when Rodríguez drove home what Bulgarian media called a "bombastic" strike to settle a nervy afternoon. CSKA had, in the words of one local report, been "playing with fire" against a side sitting last in the table, but the comeback ultimately proved comfortable enough.

The victory lifts Hristo Yanev's side to fourth place in the Bulgarian First League with seven points from three rounds, two behind early pacesetters Levski Sofia and Ludogorets Razgrad. Dunav Ruse remain rooted at the bottom, still without a win after three straight defeats to open the season.

Cypriot captain Yannis Pittas, who has scored four goals in all competitions so far this term, is expected to continue leading CSKA's attack alongside Zwart as the club juggles league form with a season-defining European assignment.

That assignment arrives on Thursday, when CSKA Sofia travel to face Maccabi Tel Aviv in the first leg of the UEFA Europa League third qualifying round, with the return fixture set for Sofia the following week. A place in the play-off round — and a shot at reaching the Europa League group stage — is at stake for both clubs.

For Maccabi's scouts, Sunday's win offered a fresh look at the team they will meet on the continent: a CSKA side building momentum domestically behind an in-form striker, even if their occasional defensive jitters against a struggling opponent will not have gone unnoticed in Tel Aviv.

title: CF Montreal condemn 'hatred of any kind' after fans target Turgeman with anti-Israel abuse in 2-2 draw
dek: Dor Turgeman was subjected to chants of 'Death to Israel' at Stade Saputo before scoring and celebrating in front of the crowd that abused him, sparking a bottle-throwing incident and a confrontation with Montreal's goalkeeper.
body: Dor Turgeman answered the ugliest reception of his young career the only way that mattered: with a goal, and then a celebration he refused to hide from the fans who had been abusing him all night.

The Israeli forward was on the end of chants of "Death to Israel" from sections of the Stade Saputo crowd during New England Revolution's MLS trip to face CF Montreal on Saturday night. In the 36th minute he doubled his side's lead to 2-0, then wheeled away and celebrated directly in front of the home supporters who had been targeting him, arms spread wide.

The reaction from the stands was immediate and ugly. Cups and bottles rained down onto the pitch, and Montreal goalkeeper Sebastian Breza confronted Turgeman and shoved him to the ground, earning a yellow card as players from both sides had to be separated.

Montreal fought back from 2-0 down to salvage a 2-2 draw, but the result was overshadowed by what had happened in the stands. CF Montreal moved quickly to condemn the abuse, with the club stating it "will not tolerate discrimination or behaviour filled with hatred of any kind," according to Sport5.

The club said it was aware of "offensive remarks directed at the player by fans" and confirmed it is "investigating the case, in contact with MLS and New England Revolution, establishing facts and taking appropriate measures."

Turgeman, 22, was raised in Ashdod and came through the youth ranks before breaking into Maccabi Tel Aviv's first team, where he won two Israeli Premier League titles and scored 24 goals in 80 appearances, including a loan spell at Beitar Tel Aviv Bat Yam. He signed for New England Revolution last August in a deal reported at roughly $6 million plus performance bonuses, and became the first player in the club's history to score in each of his first three MLS appearances.

He has also represented Israel 18 times at senior level, scoring twice, after coming through the junior national teams that reached the final of the 2022 European U19 Championship and won bronze at the 2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

Saturday's episode is the latest instance of Israeli athletes facing hostile, politically charged crowds since the war in Gaza began, a pattern that has repeatedly put leagues and clubs in the position of having to publicly police their own supporters. MLS and CF Montreal's response, promising a joint investigation with New England Revolution, will be watched closely for what, if anything, follows it.
