title: David Moses tops the boards at U18 Eurobasket but is left off the all-star five
dek: The Israeli center led the European under-18 championship in rebounding and efficiency and finished among its top scorers, yet FIBA's five-man team of the tournament went to five players from elsewhere, Sport5 reports.

verificationSources.label: FIBA U18 EuroBasket 2026 - Israel team profile
FIBA - Aronov, Musis lead Israel shock over Greece
Jerusalem Post - Israel's unbeaten U18 run ends against Slovenia

body: Israel's under-18 basketball team is coming home from the FIBA U18 Eurobasket without the individual honour many in the Israeli game felt its best player had earned. David Moses, the towering center who topped the tournament's rebounding and efficiency charts, was left off FIBA's official all-star five for the competition, Sport5 reported - the outlet's headline framing the omission with a blunt question: was he robbed?

Moses, listed on FIBA's own tournament site under the transliteration David Musis, was by most statistical measures the most productive big man in Trento and Rovereto. According to Sport5, he finished the championship as its leading rebounder at roughly 11 boards a game, topped the efficiency ratings at better than 24 per outing, and was the tournament's second-highest scorer behind only its official MVP.

FIBA's own tournament reporting backs up the scale of his numbers: the governing body's site had the 2.11-metre center as the competition's top rebounder and most efficient player through the group and knockout rounds, praising his ability to dominate the glass, finish around the rim and block shots while also showing a reliable jump shot.

None of that was enough to earn him a place in the five-man team of the tournament. Sport5 reported that FIBA's all-star five went to Diego Niebla of Spain, France's Hugo-Yimga Moukouri, Germany's Leonard Kroger, Italy's Chikh Niang and Slovenia's Stefan Joksimovic, who also collected the MVP award.

Joksimovic's case for the top individual prize was straightforward enough. The Slovenian forward starred in the quarter-final that ended Israel's tournament, scoring 28 points and pulling down 10 rebounds as Slovenia edged a back-and-forth contest 95-87, having led Israel's unbeaten run through the group phase and the round of 16.

That quarter-final was tight until the closing stretch - Israel led 78-77 early in the fourth quarter - before Slovenia pulled clear, helped by a lopsided 50-38 advantage on the boards. It was the first defeat of the tournament for Nadav Zilberstein's squad, which had opened with a run of group-stage and knockout wins, including an upset of Greece.

The loss to Slovenia dropped Israel into the classification bracket for fifth through eighth place rather than the semi-finals, and the team went on to finish seventh overall, according to Sport5 - a respectable result for a squad that had entered the knockout rounds unbeaten but well short of the medal contention its form had suggested.

For Moses individually, the tournament nonetheless amounted to a breakout showing on the European stage: a teenage Israeli big man finishing among the competition's statistical leaders in rebounding, efficiency and scoring, even if the recognition that usually follows those numbers went to five players wearing other countries' jerseys.

title: AZ Alkmaar rout 10-man PSV 4-0 as ex-Maccabi Tel Aviv man Weslley Patati scores in Dutch Super Cup
dek: Weslley Patati, sold by Maccabi Tel Aviv for a club-record fee this summer, curled home AZ's second goal as Ronald Koeman's old club overwhelmed a PSV side reduced to ten men to win the Johan Cruijff Schaal.
body: Less than three months after Maccabi Tel Aviv sold him for a club-record fee, Weslley Patati was already collecting silverware in Dutch colours. The Brazilian forward scored as AZ Alkmaar tore apart a 10-man PSV Eindhoven, winning 4-0 to lift the Johan Cruijff Schaal, the curtain-raiser to the new Eredivisie season.

The contest was effectively decided inside six minutes at PSV's Philips Stadion, where midfielder Joey Veerman was sent off for a reckless challenge on AZ striker Mexx Meerdink. PSV, the defending Eredivisie champions, were left to play more than 80 minutes with ten men against a rejuvenated AZ side.

Meerdink made the extra man count himself, heading AZ in front in the 25th minute. The lead held into the second half, when Patati stepped forward to double it: found by Peer Koopmeiners on the edge of the box, he cut inside and curled a left-footed finish into the far corner in the 51st minute.

It was a landmark moment for Israeli football as much as for AZ. Patati spent last season lighting up the Israeli Premier League with Maccabi Tel Aviv before AZ paid a club-record fee, reported in Dutch and Israeli media at around seven to eight million euros, to sign him this summer — the largest sum ever paid for a player leaving an Israeli club.

AZ were not finished. Elijah Dijkstra added a third in the 58th minute, and substitute Calvin Stengs, making his first appearance since rejoining the club, won a penalty that Ro-Zangelo Daal converted to complete the 4-0 scoreline.

The victory was AZ's second Johan Cruijff Schaal in their history, and their first since 2009, when they also beat PSV to the trophy. For Patati, it was the perfect early return on a transfer that raised eyebrows for its size when it was struck — a statement that the fee, and the faith AZ showed in a player plucked from Israeli football, may already be paying off.

title: Agent turf war over Yan Diomande delays his unveiling at Real Madrid
dek: A dispute between Roc Nation and the Ivorian winger's former management team, Maxidel, has stalled his reported €100m move from RB Leipzig, with FIFA now reviewing the case.
body: Real Madrid's marquee summer signing has been held up not by a medical or a fee squabble with RB Leipzig, but by a bitter fight between two of the player's own representatives. According to ONE, the dispute is what has kept Yan Diomande from being officially presented at the Bernabéu despite terms already being agreed.

Diomande, 19, was the find of last season's Bundesliga: an Ivorian winger who scored 12 goals and added eight assists as Leipzig finished third, earning the league's award for best young player. That breakout campaign is why Real Madrid moved for him this summer, with the fee reported to be north of €100 million.

The transfer itself was never really in doubt. Personal terms with the player were said to be all but settled, and Real Madrid believed they had a deal in place with Leipzig. The complication is over who actually represents Diomande, and who is entitled to the commission on the move.

Real Madrid negotiated the transfer through Roc Nation, the American agency founded by Jay-Z, which has been handling the player's affairs in the current talks. But Maxidel Management, run by former Ivory Coast international Max Gradel, says it still holds the rights to represent Diomande, having arranged his original move to Leipzig.

Maxidel has filed a formal complaint with FIFA alleging a breach of contract, arguing its mandate over the player runs until he actually leaves the German club. That claim is now enough to hold up the paperwork: FIFA can decline to process an International Transfer Certificate while a representation dispute of this kind is unresolved.

The fallout has reportedly left Real Madrid frustrated with Roc Nation rather than with the player. Ivorian journalist Malick Traoré was quoted saying the club felt misled after discovering Diomande was still tied to a contract with other agents it had not been told about.

With FIFA now examining Maxidel's complaint, Real Madrid may have to seek provisional registration clearance to get the deal over the line while the agents fight over commission. Until that is resolved, the club cannot formally unveil the winger it has already agreed to pay well over €100 million for.

title: Joan García targets Barcelona's sixth Champions League title after World Cup glory
dek: Fresh off lifting the World Cup with Spain, Barcelona's goalkeeper says the club must chase Europe's biggest prize without letting the pursuit become an obsession.
body: Two weeks after lifting the World Cup with Spain, Joan García has already fixed his sights on the next prize: winning the Champions League with Barcelona for the first time.

"I've been at Barcelona for a year. We won La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup, and this year I won the World Cup, so obviously the objective for next season is the Champions League," the 25-year-old goalkeeper said, according to ONE. "The World Cup is the biggest trophy in international football, and the Champions League is the closest equivalent at club level."

García was one of eight Barcelona players in Spain's World Cup-winning squad, and started as Spain beat Argentina in the final in the United States on July 19. It capped a rapid rise for a goalkeeper who was playing for Espanyol little more than a year earlier, before Barcelona activated his release clause in June 2025.

His first season at Camp Nou delivered the league title and the Spanish Super Cup, but the Champions League was where it went wrong: Barcelona were eliminated by Atlético Madrid in the quarter-finals, and García failed to keep a single clean sheet in nine European appearances - part of a wider slump that saw the club go a club-record run of matches in the competition without shutting out an opponent.

That history is presumably part of why García is careful to frame the coming season's target with caution rather than certainty. "It has to be somewhere in the middle," he said. "Becoming obsessed isn't good, because the negative effect can be very big if you don't achieve the objective. But we have a lot of confidence that we can do it."

A sixth European Cup would put Barcelona level with the very top of the competition's all-time roll of honour. The Catalans have lifted the trophy five times - in 1992, 2006, 2009, 2011 and 2015 - and currently sit alongside Liverpool and Bayern Munich, one behind record holders Real Madrid.

García also touched on speculation surrounding his teammate Ferran Torres, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer. "He's a great player who gives us a lot both on and off the pitch," García said. "If I could choose, of course I'd keep him."

For García personally, the last thirteen months have been a near-uninterrupted ascent - from Espanyol's number one to Barcelona's undisputed starter, to a World Cup winner's medal with Spain. The Champions League, the one major trophy still missing from that run, is now the explicit target for 2026-27.

García was part of Spain's squad that won the 2026 FIFA World Cup, beating Argentina in the final on July 19, 2026.
In his first season at Barcelona (2025-26), García helped the club win La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup.
Barcelona were eliminated from last season's Champions League by Atlético Madrid in the quarter-finals, and García kept no clean sheets in nine European appearances that campaign.
Barcelona have won the European Cup/Champions League five times: 1992, 2006, 2009, 2011 and 2015.
García named the Champions League as his stated priority for the 2026-27 season, per ONE.

title: Haziza makes bow as Netanya fall 3-2 to Ramat Gan Givatayim in Toto Cup
dek: The former Maccabi Haifa captain came off the bench for his Maccabi Netanya debut and said he is trying to suppress a difficult final month and a half at his old club.

verificationSources.label: ONE — match report, Netanya 2-3 Ramat Gan Givatayim
ONE — preview, Haziza named in squad for debut
Sport1/Maariv — Haziza signs two-year deal with Netanya
Sport5 — Haziza contract terms and compensation

body: Dolev Haziza finally pulled on a Maccabi Netanya shirt on Sunday night, and the occasion did not go the way the Diamonds would have scripted it. Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim came from behind to win 3-2 in the Toto Cup, with Haziza sent on as a substitute for his first competitive minutes since leaving Maccabi Haifa.

The 31-year-old winger, who left Haifa last month after seven years, was, by ONE's account, lively from the moment he entered, drifting to the left flank and setting up Matheus Dabo's second goal of the night in the 87th minute — too late to rescue a result that had slipped away from Roni Levi's side.

Luan Campos opened the scoring for Ramat Gan Givatayim in the 34th minute before Dabo levelled for Netanya five minutes later. The visitors then pulled away in the second half, with a goal credited to Eden Barnes/Dov Asanko in the 53rd minute and Maxim Felatschenko converting a penalty in the 61st to make it 3-1, by which point Netanya's night was already unravelling.
"I don't accept a defeat like that. We shouldn't be conceding three goals at home," Haziza said afterwards, according to ONE, even as he tried to process his own return to action.

The bigger story for Haziza was personal rather than tactical. "I missed playing. Personally and emotionally I was down, whatever way it was portrayed," he said, referring to his final weeks at Maccabi Haifa before the move across the coast to Netanya. "I'm trying to suppress the last month and a half I went through, because at the end of the day I spent seven years at Maccabi Haifa."

Haziza did not elaborate publicly on what exactly made the period so difficult, but his comments confirm it was an unhappy exit from a club where he had been a central figure for the better part of a decade.

He joined Haifa in the summer of 2019 and grew into one of the dressing room's leaders, captaining the side for the first time in a Champions League qualifier against Slovan Bratislava in August 2023 when regular skipper Sherjil Cheron was unavailable. He won three straight Israeli championships with the club (2020/21, 2021/22 and 2022/23) and played a leading role in its Champions League group-stage campaign.

According to Sport5 and Walla Sport, Haziza signed a two-year contract with Netanya on a reported salary of roughly $250,000 per season after the move was finalised on July 24, with Haifa due around 400,000 shekels in compensation for the early termination of his contract.

Netanya had already opened their Toto Cup campaign without him, with reports beforehand noting he had not been considered fully match-fit and had been left out of the squad against Hapoel Jerusalem before working his way back into contention for Sunday's tie.

For Roni Levi's team, the defeat interrupts what had otherwise been a positive start to preparations, and the manager will now have a fully available Haziza to work into a rotating squad ahead of the new Ligat Ha'al season. For the player himself, Sunday's cameo was less about the scoreline and more about simply being back on a pitch competing — a first small step in putting a turbulent summer behind him.

Netanya lost the match 3-2, with Ramat Gan Givatayim's goals coming from Luan Campos, a goal at the 53rd minute, and a Maxim Felatschenko penalty; Matheus Dabo scored twice for Netanya.

Haziza left Maccabi Haifa after seven years (2019-2026), during which he won three consecutive league titles and once captained the side in a 2023 Champions League qualifier.
He signed a two-year contract with Maccabi Netanya, finalised on July 24, 2026, reportedly worth around $250,000 per season, with Haifa receiving roughly 400,000 shekels in compensation.

title: Left-back Bilal Shahin trials with Hapoel Tel Aviv after leaving Kiryat Shmona
dek: The 23-year-old, a free agent since parting ways with Kiryat Shmona this summer, is training with Elyaniv Barda's squad as the club weigh whether to sign him as competition for Doron Leidner.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Shahin named round's Winner MVP at Kiryat Shmona

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have brought left-back Bilal Shahin in for a trial, giving the 23-year-old a chance to earn a contract after his exit from Kiryat Shmona this summer, ONE reports.

Shahin spent last season as Kiryat Shmona's first-choice left-back, and his form there was good enough that ONE's readers voted him the round's outstanding performer after he shut down winger Dan Biton and helped his side to a clean sheet. His time at the club ended with this summer's transfer window.

He is now training with the Hapoel Tel Aviv squad under head coach Elyaniv Barda, according to the report, with the club's staff using the sessions to judge whether he is worth a contract offer. No decision has been made yet — ONE describes it as a mutual look, with Shahin equally auditioning the club as he searches for his next move.

Financially, the report notes that a permanent deal would be straightforward for Hapoel Tel Aviv: since Shahin came through Kiryat Shmona's development ranks, signing him would require only a training compensation fee to his old club rather than a transfer fee.

If he does earn a contract, Shahin would be competing for playing time with Doron Leidner, the left-back on loan at Hapoel Tel Aviv from Greek club Olympiacos since last season. Leidner, a Hapoel academy product himself before his move to Piraeus, has held down the position for Barda's side.

The trial comes as Hapoel Tel Aviv build out their squad for a season that already includes European football: the Reds advanced through Conference League qualifying over the summer, beating Ludogorets on aggregate, and Barda's coaching staff have been active in assessing depth options across the squad as a result.

There is no confirmed timeline for when a decision on Shahin will be made, and ONE's report stops short of saying a deal is close. For now, the defender remains an unattached player training on trial, hoping to convince Hapoel Tel Aviv's coaching staff before pre-season commitments intensify.

title: AZ Alkmaar 4-0 PSV: Weslley Patati scores as Dutch press hail ex-Maccabi winger's 'crazy potential'
dek: The Brazilian netted in a lopsided Johan Cruijff Schaal final against ten-man PSV, giving Dutch outlets fresh reason to rave about the winger Maccabi Tel Aviv sold for a club-record fee last year.
body: AZ Alkmaar opened the Dutch season by taking PSV apart 4-0 in the Johan Cruijff Schaal on Sunday, and the club's record signing put his name on the scoresheet in front of a Philips Stadion crowd that had come to watch the champions start their title defence.

PSV's afternoon unravelled early. Joey Veerman was sent off in the ninth minute, and AZ spent the rest of the match turning a numbers advantage into a rout, with Mexx Meerdink, Weslley Patati, Elijah Dijkstra and Ro-Zangelo Daal all getting on the scoresheet.

Patati's goal, AZ's second of the afternoon, arrived in the 51st minute. Peer Koopmeiners picked him out and the Brazilian finished first time into the top corner - the kind of moment that has followed him around since he first turned heads at Maccabi Tel Aviv.

Dutch football accounts and newspapers were quick to talk him up afterwards. One widely followed Dutch football account wrote that Patati "has crazy potential with the ball, and could develop into an incredible player," adding that he was one "we'll need to follow for years ahead, at bigger clubs," Sport5 reported.

AD, the Dutch newspaper, wrote that Patati "showed again why AZ believes in him so much," adding that "he's dangerous every time he has the ball, and finished with an amazing goal." De Telegraaf struck a more cautious note, suggesting that once Patati "improves his decision-making and becomes stable without the ball, he'll be a great player" - while adding that reaching that level is "a tough task."

The goal comes at a useful moment for the 22-year-old. Under coach Lee-Roy Echteld, Patati had lost his automatic starting spot this year as Ro-Zangelo Daal broke into the side and Isak Jensen shifted onto the right flank, pushing the Brazilian into more substitute appearances than he would like. He had responded with a strong pre-season, finishing as AZ's top scorer in the warm-up friendlies.

Patati arrived at Maccabi Tel Aviv from Santos in September 2024 and quickly became one of the Israeli champions' most important attacking players, contributing 13 goals and 10 assists in 39 appearances in his final season in yellow and blue as the club won the league title and Toto Cup.

AZ signed him from Maccabi in August 2025 for a fee reported at roughly 7.3-7.5 million euros - a club-record incoming transfer for the Eredivisie side - with Maccabi said to have retained a sell-on percentage on any future move.

For AZ, the win was only its second Johan Cruijff Schaal, the traditional Dutch curtain-raiser between the reigning league champions and cup winners, following an earlier triumph in 2009. For Patati, it was a reminder to Dutch football that the price tag Maccabi commanded for him last summer was not accidental.
facts: AZ Alkmaar beat PSV 4-0 in the Johan Cruijff Schaal (Dutch Super Cup) at Philips Stadion in Eindhoven on August 2, 2026.
PSV played from the ninth minute with ten men after Joey Veerman was sent off.
Weslley Patati scored AZ's second goal in the 51st minute, assisted by Peer Koopmeiners.
Dutch outlets including a widely followed Dutch football account, AD and De Telegraaf praised Patati's potential after the match, per Sport5.
Patati, a Brazilian winger, played for Maccabi Tel Aviv from September 2024 before AZ signed him in August 2025 for a club-record fee reported at roughly 7.3-7.5 million euros.
At Maccabi Tel Aviv, Patati contributed 13 goals and 10 assists in 39 appearances in his final season, helping the club win the league title and Toto Cup.
It was AZ's second Johan Cruijff Schaal title, after 2009.

title: Haitian-born Kiki Ramos scores as Argentina's Under-17s draw 1-1 with Ecuador
dek: Stephen 'Kiki' Ramos, adopted from Haiti as a baby after the 2010 earthquake, marked his Argentina Under-17 debut with the equaliser against Ecuador — a landmark Sport5 frames against decades without a Black player in the national team picture.
body: Argentina's Under-17 national team have not gone a full year without producing a headline, but this one arrived from an unlikely angle. Stephen "Kiki" Ramos, a 17-year-old forward born in Port-au-Prince, marked his international debut by scoring the equaliser in a 1-1 friendly draw with Ecuador — and, in doing so, became the first Haiti-born player ever called up to any Argentina Football Association national side, according to Argentine outlets including La Nación and Infobae.

The match itself was a low-key affair, played behind closed doors at León Kolbowski Stadium in Atlanta, Buenos Aires province, as the second of two warm-up friendlies against Ecuador ahead of this year's Under-17 World Cup. Argentina fell behind before Ramos, introduced from the bench, levelled the scores in the second half on his first appearance in the shirt.

It was a dream first cap. Ramos has been on Vélez Sarsfield's radar since he was six years old, when a neighbour who supported the club brought him along to train at the Fortín's academy in Liniers. He has since worked his way through every age group at the club, and last season's tally in the youth ranks — 12 goals — helped push him into the national team picture. Some in Argentina have already begun comparing his pace, physical strength and take-on ability to Vinícius Júnior.

The story behind the player is what has made this moment resonate well beyond a routine youth friendly. Ramos was born in Haiti on 3 April 2009 and placed in an orphanage as an infant amid his birth family's economic hardship. An Argentine family had already begun adoption proceedings before the devastating January 2010 earthquake struck the country; Ramos left for Buenos Aires with three other children shortly afterwards and grew up in the Villa Devoto neighbourhood.
"Ya me siento argentino" — I already feel Argentine — Ramos told Infobae this week, describing the call-up as a dream and Argentina as simply home.

Sport5's report frames the debut against a specific historical marker: Héctor Baley, the Afro-Argentine goalkeeper whose paternal grandfather emigrated from Senegal, was part of Argentina's 1978 World Cup-winning squad and again in 1982 — after which, in the Israeli outlet's telling, four decades passed without a Black player featuring for the senior national team. That precise framing should be read with some caution; a Greek outlet covering the same story cited a 44-year gap rather than 40, and the broader question of Black representation across Argentina's national teams has itself been the subject of periodic debate in the country's own sports media. What is not in dispute is that visible representation has been rare, and that Ramos — still only at Under-17 level — is being watched as a possible name to eventually change that at senior level, not one who already has.

For now, his rise is being managed within the youth pathway. Diego Placente's Under-17s are building toward the FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, running from 19 November to 13 December this year in an expanded 48-team format, and the Ecuador friendlies were part of that preparation window.

Whether Ramos ultimately breaks into Vélez's first team, let alone graduates to Lionel Scaloni's senior squad, remains a long way off and unproven. But a 17-year-old scoring on his first appearance for any Argentina national side, with a personal story running through an earthquake, an adoption and a boyhood trip to a Liniers training ground, was always going to travel further than a routine scoreline suggested.
facts: Stephen "Kiki" Ramos was born in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on 3 April 2009.
He was adopted by an Argentine family as an infant and relocated to Buenos Aires around the time of the January 2010 Haiti earthquake, growing up in the Villa Devoto neighbourhood.
Ramos joined Vélez Sarsfield's youth academy at age six and has progressed through every divisional level, scoring 12 goals for the club's youth side last season.
He made his debut for Argentina's Under-17 national team in a closed-doors friendly against Ecuador at León Kolbowski Stadium in Atlanta, scoring the equaliser in a 1-1 draw.
Argentine outlets including La Nación and Infobae report he is the first Haiti-born player ever called up to any Argentina Football Association (AFA) national team.
Argentina's Under-17s, coached by Diego Placente, are preparing for the FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, running 19 November-13 December 2026.

Sport5 framed the debut against Héctor Baley, the Argentina goalkeeper of Senegalese descent who played in the 1978 World Cup-winning squad and the 1982 squad, though the exact number of years cited since a Black player featured for Argentina varies between reports (Sport5 says 40, another outlet says 44).

title: Noga Reshef claims under-21 jiu-jitsu world title in Abu Dhabi
dek: The Israeli fighter beat a home favourite on a golden-point sweep to win gold in the under-63kg final, as the national anthem rang out on Emirati soil and Yoav Solomon added bronze.

verificationSources.label: isport.co.il — Reshef's European U21 silver, March 2026
Abu Dhabi Media Office — 2026 Ju-Jitsu World Championship dates and venue

body: Noga Reshef is a world champion. The 20-year-old from Eilat won gold in the under-21, under-63kg category at the Ju-Jitsu International Federation's World Championship in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, beating a home-nation finalist in a final so tight it was settled by golden point.

Reshef broke the deadlock with a sweep deep into the extra period, snatching the decisive score in front of a crowd firmly behind her Emirati opponent. Moments later, the Hatikvah was played inside the arena at Abu Dhabi's Mubadala venue — the site of the JJIF's flagship event, running from 1 to 9 August and drawing more than 1,500 competitors from around the world.

It capped a rapid rise for Reshef, who had gone into the tournament as a European silver medallist rather than a champion. She finished second in the same under-63kg U21 division at the European Championship in Greece in March, meaning Sunday's gold in Abu Dhabi represents a genuine step up — a world title to sit above a continental runner-up medal.

She was not the only Israeli to leave the mat with a medal. Yoav Solomon added bronze in the men's under-56kg category, beating a competitor from Singapore in the fight for third place — a second podium finish for the Israeli delegation on the opening day of the championship.

"The team opened the World Championship with excellent results against some of the world's strongest athletes," national coach Amir Boaron said, according to Sport5, framing the two medals as a strong start rather than the finish for an Israeli squad that will keep competing in Abu Dhabi through the rest of the week.

The setting carried its own significance. Israel's ambassador to the UAE, Yossi Sheli, attended the competition in person and presented the medals to the Israeli winners, according to the report — a reminder that Israeli athletes now compete, and are publicly honoured, on Emirati soil under the framework of the Abraham Accords.

For Reshef, already named young sportswoman of the year by the Eilat sports federation for 2025, the gold in Abu Dhabi is the biggest result of her career so far and pushes her into the top tier of Israel's junior jiu-jitsu program heading into the rest of the world championship.

title: Otef Darom land Maccabi Tel Aviv prospect Tamir Gold as Ashkelon add two imports
dek: The Gaza-envelope Liga Leumit club keeps building around promising Israeli talent, while Ashkelon strengthens its roster with a forward and a guard from abroad.
body: Otef Darom, the Liga Leumit club built to give the communities of the Gaza border region a team of their own, has added one of Israeli basketball's promising young prospects. Nineteen-year-old forward Tamir Gold is moving from Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth ranks to the National League side for the coming season, ONE reports.

Gold, who stands 2.04 metres, was a standout in the fifth season of Israel's Premier Youth League, averaging 15.5 points and nine rebounds a game as his side won both the championship and the cup. He has also represented Israel's under-19 national team, appearing at the 2025 FIBA World Championship and shooting 50 percent from three-point range while contributing 7.7 points per game.
"I'm very happy to join the club," Gold said. "I'm looking forward to starting the season, meeting the team and the fans."

Otef Darom head coach Barak Peleg welcomed the signing, describing Gold as a versatile forward capable of playing multiple positions up front and a player who fits the club's broader agenda of developing young Israeli talent.

The club itself is barely two years old. Otef Darom was launched in 2024 as a joint project of the Israel Basketball Association, the Tekuma Administration and the Ashkelon Regional Council, created to give communities of the Gaza envelope a sporting presence in the aftermath of the October 7 massacre and the war that followed. It plays home games at the roughly 500-seat Rotem Hall in Kibbutz Magen and is chaired by retired IDF general Tal Rosso.

The team's debut season in 2024/25 was rough on the scoreboard - Otef Darom finished bottom of the table with a 2-31 record, though it avoided relegation. Last season brought a marked turnaround: a 13-17 record was good for ninth place and a run to the playoff quarterfinals.

Elsewhere in the National League, Ashkelon has moved to bolster its own roster with two new imports, according to the same ONE report. Forward Kingsley Okonkwo, 26 and 2.01 metres tall, arrives after spells with Ornesa in Spain's second division and in Uruguay's top flight. The club has also signed guard Austin Tillman.

Neither Ashkelon addition has yet been confirmed through an official club statement, but the moves point to the club's ambitions of building a more competitive squad as Liga Leumit sides prepare for a new campaign in which both clubs will look to build on last season's respective finishes.
facts: Tamir Gold, a 19-year-old, 2.04m forward, is moving from Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth system to Liga Leumit club Otef Darom, per ONE.
Gold averaged 15.5 points and 9 rebounds in the fifth season of Israel's Premier Youth League, helping his team win the championship and cup.
Gold played for Israel's U19 national team at the 2025 FIBA U19 World Championship, averaging 7.7 points and shooting 50 percent from three.
Otef Darom was founded in 2024 by the Israel Basketball Association, the Tekuma Administration and the Ashkelon Regional Council to represent Gaza-envelope communities after October 7.
Otef Darom finished last (2-31) in its debut 2024/25 season but avoided relegation, then improved to ninth (13-17) with a playoff-quarterfinal run in 2025/26.
Ashkelon has signed forward Kingsley Okonkwo (26, 2.01m), previously of Ornesa in Spain's second division and a club in Uruguay's top flight, plus guard Austin Tillman, per ONE.

title: Xabi Alonso says he 'barely watched football' after his Real Madrid exit
dek: The new Chelsea manager tells The Athletic that his short, turbulent spell at the Bernabéu left him with one lasting scar — but insists it has healed as he begins life at Stamford Bridge.

verificationSources.label: ESPN — Why Chelsea hired Xabi Alonso now, and what went wrong at Real Madrid
Al Jazeera — Chelsea appoint Xabi Alonso as new manager
Al Jazeera — Alonso sacked by Real Madrid, replaced by Arbeloa
ESPN — Xabi Alonso: Real Madrid 'scar' has healed

body: Xabi Alonso has opened up about the months that followed his abrupt Real Madrid exit, telling The Athletic — in an interview cited by the Israeli outlet ONE — that he largely switched off from the sport he has spent his adult life inside, saying he 'disconnected and barely watched football' once his time in Madrid was over.

The admission comes seven months after Real Madrid parted ways with Alonso in January, following a 3-2 defeat to Barcelona in the Spanish Supercopa final that proved the final straw in a reign lasting barely half a season. He was replaced at the Bernabéu by Álvaro Arbeloa, his former teammate and the coach of the club's reserve side, Castilla.

'Luckily, I haven't collected many scars over the course of my career. I have one, but it's healing,' Alonso said, reflecting on the Spanish spell that began with lofty ambitions and ended far sooner than anyone at the club had planned.

'Looking back, I try to focus on the positives and work out what didn't work. I turned inward a lot, thinking about what I could have done better, because things didn't unfold the way I expected,' he added, describing how he used the enforced break largely for himself rather than immersing himself in the game from the sidelines.

Reports at the time of his Madrid departure pointed to a breakdown in his relationship with several senior players — Vinícius Júnior, Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde among them — who reportedly struggled to buy into his methods, a dynamic widely cited by outlets including ESPN as central to his downfall.

Alonso's time away did not last long. Chelsea announced in May that he would take over as manager on a four-year deal, succeeding Enzo Maresca and beginning his reign on 1 July, a return to the Premier League nearly two decades after his playing days at Liverpool.

Speaking to reporters during Chelsea's preseason tour, Alonso said the Madrid 'scar' has now closed, and that he arrives with fresh motivation for the challenge ahead. He also pushed back on the gloom that surrounded Chelsea at the end of last season, insisting the situation at Stamford Bridge was 'not as bad as it looked.'

The 44-year-old's coaching résumé remains one of the most eye-catching in Europe: before Madrid, he led Bayer Leverkusen to an unbeaten Bundesliga title and the DFB-Pokal in 2023-24, the first league championship in the German club's history.
Chelsea open the new Premier League campaign with a London derby, the first real test of whether Alonso's healed 'scar' translates into results back in English football.

title: Two Benfica coaches arrive in Hadera to overhaul the club's youth academy
dek: Paulo Reis and André Salvado, both formerly on Benfica's coaching staff in Lisbon, have begun work at Hapoel Hadera as the Israeli club imports the Portuguese giant's youth methodology.
body: Two coaches carrying Benfica's name on their CVs have swapped Lisbon for Hadera, and they have not wasted any time getting to work. Paulo Reis and André Salvado touched down in Israel recently and have already begun sessions at Hapoel Hadera's training facilities, Sport5 reports.

The pair will serve as coordinators of the club's youth department, tasked with implementing Benfica's professional methodology across every age group at Hadera and working directly with the club's own coaching staff to raise standards throughout the pathway.

Reis, 50, arrives with a physical education degree and more than two decades of coaching experience spanning adult and youth football in Portugal and China. Seven of those years were spent on Benfica's own staff, working across multiple age groups at the Lisbon club.

Salvado, 36, brings a different but complementary background: over 15 years in the game, including a spell as an analyst for Benfica's senior team during Champions League campaigns, with a focus on tactical analysis and player development.

The appointments are the practical rollout of a cooperation agreement between Hapoel Hadera and Benfica that was announced in June, one of several moves by the club's new ownership to rebuild its football department from the ground up.

Management rights at Hapoel Hadera passed earlier this year from Yakir Schwartz to Itai Ben Zev, the chief executive of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, a change of control that coincided with the push to bring in outside expertise for the youth ranks.

The timing is not accidental. Hadera's youth setup has been on the rise, with the club's flagship youth team recently promoted back to the top tier of the national youth league, while its Under-17, Under-15 and Under-13 sides are already competing at that level too.

City and club officials have framed the Benfica tie-up in ambitious terms, talking of a project — linked in part to the community-focused Tony Ruanda initiative — aimed at nurturing local talent to the point where Hadera could one day produce a player of the calibre of Bernardo Silva.

A fuller unveiling is still to come: senior Benfica representatives are due in Hadera on August 21 for a press conference laying out the partnership's professional plans in detail, with Reis and Salvado already several weeks into the groundwork by then.

title: Israel take fifth in mixed duet technical final at European Championships in Paris
dek: Lior Makmel and Yogev Dagan closed out the technical routine final on 193.8017 points, with Dagan continuing his trailblazing run as one of the first men in Israeli artistic swimming.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — Artistic swimming at the 2026 European Aquatics Championships, mixed duet technical routine

body: Israel's mixed duet pairing of Lior Makmel and Yogev Dagan finished fifth in the technical routine final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, Sport5 reported, closing out their round with a score of 193.8017 points.

The placing, corroborated by the official results, put the Israeli pair clear of the bottom half of an eight-country final staged at the Centre Aquatique Olympique in Saint-Denis, the venue built for artistic swimming and diving at the 2024 Paris Olympics and now hosting this summer's European Championships.

Great Britain's Isabelle Thorpe and Ranjuo Tomblin took the title on 229.6783, narrowly ahead of Italy's Lucrezia Ruggiero and Filippo Pelati on 229.0092. A pairing of neutral athletes, Alina Rumiantseva and Zakhar Trofimov, took bronze with 215.9201, with Spain's Carla Lorenzo and Jordi Cáceres fourth on 210.8584 — all four clear of Makmel and Dagan. Portugal, Germany and Bulgaria filled the places below Israel.

For Dagan, the result is another step in an unusual and closely watched career. Born in August 2007, he switched from competitive pool swimming as a young teenager after his coach, Svetlana Belcher, suggested he try artistic swimming — a discipline where mixed pairs, as in ice dance, have only recently become part of the international programme. He went on to become the first Israeli boy to compete in the team event at a European Championships, at 14, and was part of the group that won bronze in the team routine at last year's Europeans.

Makmel, born in January 2009, trains with A.L.E Mazkeret Batya, the club that has become the production line for much of Israel's current artistic-swimming generation, regularly supplying the national team's duet and group lineups.

The Paris Championships run from 31 July to 16 August, with the artistic swimming programme concentrated in the opening week; the mixed duet technical routine was decided on 2 August. Israel's artistic swimmers have become a fixture in European finals in recent years, a marked shift for a programme that was a marginal presence on the continental circuit barely a decade ago.

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva did not let Kings Kangwa go without a fight. According to his agent, Nir Karin, the club put a substantial new contract on the table in an attempt to keep hold of its star midfielder before he completed his move to Panathinaikos this week.

"Many teams wanted him, but the professional challenge mattered most to him," Karin said on ONE's "Sicha Hayom" podcast, describing Beer Sheva's counter-offer as surprisingly generous even by the standards of a player who had just delivered a title-winning season.

Kangwa ultimately chose ambition over comfort, opting to test himself in the Greek Super League rather than remain in Beersheba, where he had already established himself as one of the Israeli league's most influential players.

The move was completed this week, with Beer Sheva confirming the sale of the 27-year-old Zambian to the Athens giants in what ranks among the largest transactions in the club's history. Reports in Israel and Greece put the fee at roughly €3.8m to €4m, with add-ons capable of pushing the package higher, and Beer Sheva also retaining a 25 percent sell-on clause on any future transfer.
Kangwa signed a four-year contract with Panathinaikos running through 2030 and will wear the number 42 shirt, on a salary reported at close to €1m a season before bonuses.

His departure closes a hugely productive two-year spell in Israel. Kangwa was named the Israeli league's Footballer of the Year for the 2025-26 season after a 12-goal campaign, and he collected a full trophy set at the club — the Israeli championship, the State Cup and the Israel Super Cup.
He had arrived at Beer Sheva in July 2024 after a decorated run at Red Star Belgrade, where he won back-to-back Serbian league and cup doubles.

The path to Panathinaikos was not entirely straightforward. Walla Sport reported that Kangwa had been close to a move to AEK Athens before that club stepped back, and Panathinaikos moved quickly to close the deal with both Beer Sheva and the player once the opening emerged.

For Beer Sheva, the sale represents a financial windfall but also the loss of the player who had done more than anyone to define its recent success — a departure the club tried, and ultimately failed, to prevent with money alone.

title: Benfica pair to lead Hapoel Hadera's youth academy as Portuguese partnership begins
dek: Paulo Reis and André Salvado arrive from Lisbon to run Hadera's youth department and spread Benfica's methods through every age group, the first concrete step in a wider club transformation under new owner Ittai Ben-Zeev.
body: Hapoel Hadera's youth department has two new coordinators, and they have arrived by way of one of Europe's great development factories. ONE reports that Paulo Reis and André Salvado, both formerly of Benfica Lisbon, have taken charge of overseeing every age group at the club, from the promoted youth side down through the U-17s, U-16s and U-15s.

Reis, 50, holds a degree in physical education and has spent more than two decades coaching, including seven years inside Benfica working across multiple youth age groups. His CV also includes stints in Portugal and China, plus time helping run Estoril Praia's senior squad.

Salvado, 36, has spent 15-plus years in the game, working as an analyst on Benfica's first team during a period that included Champions League football and Portuguese league titles. He too has coached and developed young players in Portugal and China, and is described as bringing particular expertise in tactical analysis and squad leadership.

Their job in Hadera is not simply to coach — it is to import a methodology. According to Sport5, the arrangement calls for the pair to implement Benfica's development principles across the club's teams, train up local staff, and build long-term processes rather than deliver a quick fix.

The appointments are the first visible product of a much bigger shift at the club. Control of Hapoel Hadera has passed from Yakir Schwartz to Ittai Ben-Zeev, the CEO of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, with former Hapoel Be'er Sheva chief executive Asi Rahamim installed as the owner's representative, according to Bizportal and Sport5.

Hadera mayor Nir Ben Haim welcomed the Benfica tie-up in comments carried by Sport5: "We're bringing knowledge, professionalism and world-class standards, and we believe Israel's next great talents can grow here in Hadera."

Ben-Zeev struck a similar note, framing the move as building "a professional, stable club connected to the city while operating by international standards — a shift that will impact generations of children."

The Benfica link is also tied to a third strand: the Tony Rwanda project, which Rahamim continues to oversee as sporting director. Sport5 describes a trilateral model connecting Lisbon, Rwanda and Hadera, with at least one Rwandan player expected to join Hadera's youth setup as an early step.

For Hadera, the timing matters. The club's youth team has just won promotion to the top division, and its U-17, U-16 and U-15 sides are all already playing in the senior league — giving the incoming Portuguese staff, in the club's own words, "a significant foundation for collaboration" rather than a rebuild from scratch.

title: Iraola's plan for Liverpool: everything will run through Wirtz
dek: The new Liverpool head coach wants to shift Florian Wirtz into a central number 10 role, according to ONE, with Mohamed Salah's departure opening space for the German to become the team's focal point.

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports - Iraola named Slot's successor

body: Andoni Iraola has been at Anfield only a matter of weeks, but ONE reports that his blueprint for the new season already has a clear centre of gravity: Florian Wirtz.

The Basque coach, who replaced the sacked Arne Slot on a two-year deal, is planning to pull Wirtz inside from the flank he so often occupied last season and install him as a genuine number 10, playing directly behind the striker.

"We need all players in good condition, but especially Florian," Iraola said, according to ONE. "He is a very complete player, and I believe we will try to add more qualities to those he already has."

It is a notable change of emphasis. Under Slot, Wirtz was shuffled between the left wing, a false nine and the occasional spell centrally, and while his talent was never in doubt, his debut Premier League campaign never quite matched the hype that greeted his British-record move.

ONE reports that Wirtz finished his first season in England with seven goals and ten assists in 49 appearances across all competitions - a solid if unspectacular return for a player Liverpool paid a club-record fee to sign, reported by Sky Sports at around £116.5m plus add-ons.

Slot paid the price for a chastening second season, in which Liverpool slipped to a fifth-place finish and were eliminated from the Champions League, and he was sacked on May 30 despite having won the Premier League title only a year earlier.

Iraola arrives after three impressive seasons at Bournemouth, where he built a reputation as one of the Premier League's sharpest tactical minds on a modest budget, and he was the only candidate formally interviewed for the Liverpool job.
The departure of Mohamed Salah, who left Anfield as a free agent in March after mutually agreeing to terminate his contract a year early, has also reshaped the attacking picture that Iraola inherits.

With Salah's spot on the right no longer a fixture, and the forward line open to reshuffling, Iraola appears to see an opportunity to build his attack around Wirtz's passing and creativity rather than ask him to adapt to a system designed for others.
Wirtz himself has sounded receptive to the switch. "I was always more like a number 10," he said this week, confirming he had discussed the role with his new coach and adding, simply, "let's see."

For a player signed to be Liverpool's next talisman, a central role finally built around his own strengths - rather than around the team he joined - may be exactly what his second season in England needs.

title: CF Montréal 2-2 New England Revolution: Turgeman's father says only 'a small group' cursed his son amid Death to Israel chants
dek: Gabi Turgeman defended the crowd that abused his son during Saturday's MLS draw in Montreal, insisting most fans 'love him' — while asking why the CF Montréal goalkeeper who shoved the striker only saw yellow.
body: Dor Turgeman's father has come to the defence of the Montreal crowd that hurled antisemitic abuse at his son during Saturday night's MLS clash, telling ONE that only "a small group" was responsible and that, overwhelmingly, "they love him."

The comments came a day after New England Revolution's 2-2 draw at CF Montréal's Stade Saputo turned ugly. Sections of the home support chanted "Death to Israel" and other anti-Israel slogans through much of the game, with some fans waving Palestinian flags, according to reports from the stadium.

Turgeman, 22, answered in the only way a striker can. He scored in the 36th minute to put New England 2-0 up, then wheeled away with his arms thrown up toward the sky in the celebration his father describes as entirely typical for him — not a message aimed at anyone in the stands.

The goal did not calm things down. Objects, including cups and bottles, were thrown from the crowd toward the pitch, and CF Montréal goalkeeper Sébastian Breza confronted Turgeman and shoved him to the ground, picking up a yellow card in the process.
"I don't understand why he wasn't sent off after that push," Gabi Turgeman said of Breza, arguing the goalkeeper deserved harsher punishment than a caution for the shove.

Montreal fought back to salvage a 2-2 draw, denying New England what would have been a statement road win, but the story of the night was the abuse Turgeman absorbed and how he chose to respond to it.

His father framed the episode as an isolated ugly moment rather than a reflection of how Turgeman has been received in North America. "I think it's a small group," he said of the fans responsible for the chants, insisting the broader reception the striker has had since crossing the Atlantic has been warm.
"He's in a good place, with his girlfriend, having a good spell in the United States, and everything is fine," Gabi Turgeman added, describing his son as settled in Boston both on and off the field.

Turgeman joined New England from Maccabi Tel Aviv last August in one of the priciest deals in the club's history, reported by MLS outlets at roughly $5.5-6 million through the league's U22 initiative, with the move running through the 2028 season and a club option for 2029.

He arrives with pedigree: two Israeli championships and an Israeli Super Cup with Maccabi Tel Aviv, plus 10 caps for the Israel national team, after a 2024-25 season in which he scored 16 goals and added three assists in 32 games as the Yellow-and-Blue retained the title.
"He's with the team for three years and I want him to give his maximum," his father said, looking past Saturday's incident toward the rest of Turgeman's contract in New England.

Neither MLS nor CF Montréal had issued a formal statement on the chanting by the time of writing, though the episode is likely to draw scrutiny given the league's conduct policies around discriminatory abuse from supporters.

body: Maccabi Netanya's perfect start to this season's Toto Cup carries into Sunday evening, when Roni Levi's side host newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan at Netanya Stadium in a Group B fixture that could also produce a first appearance for the club's marquee summer arrival.

ONE reports that Dolev Haziza has been included in Netanya's matchday squad and is in line to be given his first minutes for the club, more than a month after his move from Maccabi Haifa was finalised. According to the report, Haziza is expected to be an option off the bench rather than an immediate starter as he continues to build match fitness.

The winger's arrival closed a seven-year spell in Haifa, where he wore the captain's armband, won three consecutive championships and played Champions League football — spells that made him one of the most recognisable names to move this summer. Walla Sport and Sport5 reported that Haziza signed a two-year contract with Netanya, with Maccabi Haifa paying him compensation after the club's new sporting director, Lior Refaelov, told him in pre-season talks that he was not part of the first-team plans for 2026/27.

Sitting across the pitch will be a very different kind of newcomer. Hapoel Ramat Gan, freshly promoted to the top flight, have handed a start to Ido Oli, a 20-year-old central midfielder who joined on a season-long loan from Maccabi Tel Aviv this summer, according to local outlet BE106.

Oli, a product of Maccabi Tel Aviv's academy who has represented Israel at youth level including the under-21s, spent last season out on loan in the National League with Hapoel Kfar Shalem. Ramat Gan also brought in fellow Maccabi Tel Aviv loanee Daniel Tichler as part of the same close-season swoop.

The visit to Netanya comes in Group B of the Toto Cup, where Levi's side head into round three unbeaten, having built a perfect record of six points from two matches. A win would extend that run and keep Netanya on course to top the section heading into the knockout rounds.

Ramat Gan, for their part, arrive as one of the competition's surprise packages, having already picked up notable results since returning to the top division after their promotion. The Toto Cup remains Israel's third-tier knockout competition by prestige, but early-season minutes carry real weight for a newly promoted club still finding its feet — and for a squad now blended with several Maccabi Tel Aviv loanees.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv open talks to sign guard Quincy Olivari from Trento
dek: The Israeli champions have approached the Italian club about a deal for the 25-year-old guard, though sources rate the odds of prising him away as slim.

verificationSources.label: Sportando - Quincy Olivari joins Dolomiti Energia Trentino
Eurohoops - Fenerbahce officially parts with Bacot

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have opened talks to sign guard Quincy Olivari, targeting the 25-year-old barely a month after he committed his future to Italian club Trento, ONE reported on Sunday.

Olivari, 1.91m, only put pen to paper with Dolomiti Energia Trentino in July, his first move into European basketball after going undrafted out of the 2024 NBA draft. He landed an exclusive rights deal with the Los Angeles Lakers that was later converted into a two-way contract, spending last season on assignment with the Lakers' G League affiliate South Bay Lakers and, later, the Detroit Pistons' Motor City Cruise, where he averaged 11.8 points, four rebounds and 3.3 assists over 29 games.

Before turning professional he built his reputation in American college basketball, transferring from Rice to Xavier for the 2023-24 season and putting up 19.2 points and 5.6 rebounds a game as one of the Big East's more productive scorers.

According to ONE, any move to bring him to Tel Aviv would require Maccabi to compensate Trento to release him from a contract he has barely begun, and the outlet frames the chances of the Italian club agreeing as low even as the Israeli side pushes to explore the option.

The interest in Olivari is not happening in isolation. ONE reports Maccabi are simultaneously in talks with guard Armoni Brooks, 28, though optimism about completing that deal is similarly muted, as the club works to reshape its backcourt ahead of the new season.

On the front line, the report adds that Maccabi expect to finalise the signing of Armando Bacot. The American big man is available after Fenerbahce confirmed this summer that he would not be kept on despite helping the Istanbul club sweep the Turkish League, Turkish Cup and Presidential Cup during the 2025-26 season.

Taken together, the moves point to a busy, multi-track recruitment drive at Yad Eliyahu as Maccabi's front office works the market for both backcourt scoring and frontcourt size before EuroLeague and Israeli Premier League commitments resume — even if, on Olivari specifically, the club may end up coming away empty-handed.

title: Katzrin's football comeback is complete as club returns to Liga Gimel
dek: Eight years after its previous senior team folded, the Golan Heights town is fielding an adult side again this season, backed by local sponsor Mey Eden and a youth pipeline that has already produced an Israel international.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הקאמבק הושלם: קצרין חוזרת למפת הכדורגל הישראלי

body: Katzrin is getting its football club back. According to ONE, the Golan Heights local council has registered an adult team to compete in Liga Gimel, the fifth and entry-level tier of Israeli football's regional pyramid, for the coming season - ending an eight-year absence from senior competition for a town that has quietly become one of the north's more productive football nurseries.

The comeback closes a gap that opened when Maccabi Katzrin, the previous senior side, finished near the bottom of its Liga Gimel group in the 2017/18 season and disbanded shortly after. Since then, the town of roughly 8,500 residents has kept producing players through its youth ranks without a senior team of its own for them to eventually join.
"We're returning to Liga Gimel in a big way," Yehuda Doah, head of the Katzrin local council, said, according to ONE. "Prepare to see the pitch full of life, with football players and packed crowds."

Yogev Suysa, the council's sports director, is overseeing the relaunch, and Mey Eden - the mineral-water company whose bottling plant draws on the nearby Salukia spring in Katzrin - is returning as the club's main sponsor and financial backer, ONE reported.

The town's youth production line is the strongest argument for reviving the senior side. Idan Nachmias, the Israel international centre-back who joined Bulgarian champions Ludogorets Razgrad this year after spells at Ironi Kiryat Shmona and Maccabi Tel Aviv, came up through Katzrin's academy, according to the report, alongside defenders Itai Ben Shabbat and Deen Meymoni and midfielder Elroei Cohen.

None of that guarantees an easy return. Liga Gimel is split into eight regional districts and sits as the lowest, most amateur rung of Israeli football, with only the district champions promoted to Liga Bet each season - the same unforgiving level that swallowed Katzrin's previous side.

The council is tying the club's revival to the town's wider calendar: Katzrin marks its 50th anniversary in July 2027, and officials want a settled football team, rather than another false start, to be part of that milestone.

title: Diomande can surpass Yamal, says former Leganes captain
dek: Sergio Gonzalez, who played alongside the Ivory Coast winger at Leganes, believes the incoming Real Madrid signing Yan Diomande has no ceiling on his potential.

verificationSources.label: ESPN - Real Madrid set to sign Yan Diomande in €135m deal
Infobae - Sergio Gonzalez interview on Diomande

body: Sergio Gonzalez spent five seasons in the Leganes dressing room, the last of them as club captain, before saying goodbye this summer. But nothing in those years quite prepared him for the teenager who arrived from the reserve squad midway through last season - and now, watching Yan Diomande close in on a move to Real Madrid, Gonzalez believes the young Ivorian has license to dream bigger than most of Spain expects.

"If you ask me, he is capable of reaching his level and going beyond," Gonzalez said, in comments carried by Spanish media and relayed by Israeli outlet ONE, when asked whether Diomande could match Lamine Yamal, the Barcelona teenager regarded as the continent's benchmark for young talent. Diomande, he said, can reach Yamal's level "and even surpass him."

It is a bold marker to set. Yamal, also 19, is already a Ballon d'Or contender and the player most of Europe measures its brightest prospects against. Gonzalez is not claiming Diomande has caught up - only that, in his eyes, there is no obvious ceiling on how far the winger can still go.

He traces the realisation back to a behind-closed-doors friendly during a spring international break, when Diomande - only a handful of matches removed from Leganes' reserve side - lined up against the senior squad and scored in a heavy defeat for the first team. From his first touch, Gonzalez has recalled, it was clear something unusual was on the pitch: a player who pairs quick, direct dribbling with real product in front of goal.

Off the field, Gonzalez describes Diomande as shy and unassuming. On it, he is audacious - comfortable attacking with either foot and unfazed by contact. That contrast has followed his rapid rise: a Rangers academy product at 16, a breakout campaign at Leganes, then a big-money move to RB Leipzig last July that has already been overtaken by talk of something far bigger.

Real Madrid are reported to be closing in on a deal worth up to €135 million including add-ons, which would rank among the largest fees ever paid for a teenager. His market valuation has jumped from around €20 million to more than €90 million in barely fifteen months - a trajectory that stands out even by the game's inflated modern standards.

Diomande arrived at this summer's World Cup with rising hype and left with more of it. He played every minute of Ivory Coast's group-stage campaign and was named man of the match in the team's win over Ecuador, completing more dribbles and creating more chances than anyone else on the pitch that day.

For Gonzalez, the real uncertainty is not talent but temperament - whether a player he calls shy by nature can carry the weight of the Real Madrid badge and the scrutiny that comes with it. The transfer has not yet been formally completed by either club, but if it goes through as reported, Madrid are betting the answer is yes.

title: Angelo Tsagarakis joins Maccabi Ironi Ramat Gan as player development director
dek: The French-Greek 3x3 specialist and world championship shooting medallist has signed a two-year deal to work under Pini Gershon developing the Ramat Gan club's youth pipeline.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv - Tsagarakis's earlier ties to the club

body: Maccabi Ironi Ramat Gan have brought in one of European 3x3 basketball's best-known shooting coaches to work inside their development system. ONE reports that Angelo Tsagarakis, the 42-year-old French-Greek former player, has signed on as the club's player development director for the next two years.

Tsagarakis's brief is broad: he will oversee shooting mechanics and individual offensive skill work across every age group at the club, from the youth ranks up to the senior roster, with a particular emphasis on first-step quickness and one-on-one scoring ability.

He arrives into a structure built around Pini Gershon, the veteran Israeli coach who returned to Ramat Gan as professional director after more than three decades away, and he is expected to coordinate closely with the club's long-serving youth department head. According to ONE, Tsagarakis is due to relocate to Israel with his family in early September, ahead of the new season.

Club chairman Chen Sneiderman made clear how much the club wanted this hire. "Bringing Angelo to Maccabi Ironi Ramat Gan was our main goal for the upcoming season, and I'm happy to announce to every player at the club that we've done it," he said, according to ONE.

The appointment is not a cold introduction. Tsagarakis already has a relationship with the Ramat Gan club, having previously travelled to Israel as a guest of Gershon to run shooting and skills clinics for its youth teams, and having worked with some of those same players remotely in the past. This deal formalises that connection into a full-time, contracted role.

On the court, Tsagarakis built his reputation in 3x3 basketball rather than the traditional five-a-side game, after a playing career that ran from 2008 to 2019 across French clubs including JL Bourg-en-Bresse and Paris-Levallois, and Greek sides such as Aries Trikala and Ionikos Nikaias.

It was with France's national 3x3 team that he became a recognisable figure in the discipline, helping the side to a bronze medal at the 2017 FIBA 3x3 World Cup in Nantes. In the individual long-range shooting contests held alongside that tournament and the following year's European Championship in Bucharest, he took the top prize both times, cementing his reputation as one of the format's premier marksmen.

For Ramat Gan, a club with a large youth base and ambitions to keep producing players who can push into the senior team, landing a coach with that specific shooting pedigree is being pitched as a statement of intent rather than a marginal addition to the staff.

title: Barcelona look to copy Real Madrid's academy cash-in formula
dek: Deco is reportedly studying how Real Madrid turned academy graduates into nearly €200 million this summer, with young full-back Jofre Torrents the first test case of the model at Camp Nou.

verificationSources.label: Crónica Global (El Español) — Real Madrid se autofinancia el mercado de fichajes con la venta de canteranos
VAVEL España — El Real Madrid genera más de 186 millones por sus canteranos
Football España — Jofre Torrents loan exit: Ajax vs Racing Club

body: Barcelona have decided the smartest move in this transfer window isn't necessarily finding the next signing — it's copying the rival across town. ONE reports that the club has identified Real Madrid's method of monetising academy graduates and wants to build the same machine at Camp Nou.

The numbers explain the envy. Real Madrid have generated close to €196 million this summer by selling players who came through their La Fábrica academy, according to Spanish outlets including Crónica Global and VAVEL, funding more than €300 million of fresh spending without touching the club's own reserves.

The list is long: Gonzalo García's move to Fulham was worth around €40 million for 70% of his rights, with the sale of César Palacios adding roughly €10 million more. Nico Paz's transfer to Como carried an €80 million buyback clause, while Víctor Muñoz, Mario Gila (to Milan) and Álvaro Rodríguez (to Bournemouth) brought in further seven-figure sums.

The trick, as Barcelona see it, isn't just selling talented kids for a fee — it's the structure behind the sales. Real Madrid typically keep a percentage of a departing player's economic rights and insert a cut-price buyback option, so the club profits again if the player breaks through elsewhere, or can bring him home cheaply if he becomes a star.

Barcelona's own academy output has made them nothing like that money this summer. Iñaki Peña's exit to Elche and Ansu Fati's move to Monaco brought in only around €14 million combined, according to Crónica Global's reporting — a fraction of Madrid's haul from a similarly stocked academy.
Sporting director Deco is described in that report as "taking note of the rival" and pushing to embed the same sell-and-retain template into Barcelona's own transfer dealings going forward.

The first concrete example, per ONE, is 19-year-old left-back Jofre Torrents, who is set to join Ajax on a loan deal. The Dutch club would hold an option to buy 50% of his rights for around €5 million, while Barcelona would keep a buyback clause reportedly worth in the region of €20 million if he goes on to fulfil his promise.

ONE reports Barcelona want that framework — loan or sale, a retained stake, and an affordable route back — to become the default for future academy departures, with names like Ez Abde and Jan Virgili mentioned as players where a similar structure could apply down the line.

The push reflects the financial squeeze La Liga's spending rules have placed on Barcelona in recent years, making internally generated income from academy sales an increasingly attractive substitute for outside investment.
None of the fees involved have been confirmed officially by either club, and Torrents's move to Amsterdam still needs to be finalised before the market closes.

title: Rodri transfer talks stall as Manchester City hold firm on €75m Real Madrid price tag
dek: Real Madrid have opened direct talks for the Ballon d'Or holder but are refusing to go above €50m, leaving roughly €25m between the two clubs, according to ONE.
body: Real Madrid's pursuit of Rodri has hit a financial wall. According to ONE, Manchester City are refusing to move off a €75 million valuation for their Spain international, leaving the deal stuck despite direct contact between the two clubs.

ONE reports that Madrid have set their own ceiling at €50 million, meaning roughly €25 million still separates the parties with no obvious middle ground yet found. Other outlets tracking the saga, including Sky Sports, TheHardTackle and Yahoo Sports, describe the same standoff, with some suggesting an eventual fee closer to €65 million could emerge as a compromise.

Rodri, 30, is contracted to City until June 2027 after arriving from Atlético Madrid in 2019. Per ONE, personal terms with Real Madrid have effectively already been agreed, with a prospective contract at the Bernabéu running through 2030 — meaning the football side of the move has moved faster than the financial one.

City's asking price reflects both the player's stature and his remaining contract length: this is essentially their last realistic window to sell him for a significant fee before his deal runs down further.

ONE reports that Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez is open to restructuring the offer around performance-related bonuses and variable clauses, a mechanism that would let Madrid formally stay under their stated ceiling while still giving City a path to a higher effective fee if the add-ons are triggered.

Rodri arrives at this negotiation as the reigning Ballon d'Or winner, having claimed the 2024 award after anchoring both City's midfield and Spain's run to European and World Cup success. He has been one of Pep Guardiola's most trusted lieutenants since his move from Atlético for a fee in the region of €70 million.

For now, the two sides remain at an impasse. Madrid's stance, as relayed by ONE, is that they will not go beyond their €50 million limit without the deal being reshaped through add-ons — leaving City to decide whether to hold out for their full valuation or accept a structured package to get a deal done this summer.

title: Red Star Belgrade are favourites, but Hapoel Beer Sheva can cause trouble, says ONE pundit
dek: Ahead of Tuesday's Champions League third qualifying round first leg in Beersheba, Guy Tzarfati writes that Kings Kangwa's departure has weakened Hapoel Beer Sheva, but a high press could unsettle the Serbian champions.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com — Crvena Zvezda vs H. Beer-Sheva match page

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva have two days to ready themselves for the heaviest test of their European summer: hosting Red Star Belgrade at Turner Stadium on Tuesday in the first leg of the Champions League's third qualifying round.

Progress, or even just a workable scoreline to take to Belgrade, would keep alive the Israeli champions' hopes of reaching the play-off round and a lucrative shot at the group phase. Defeat to one of the continent's grandest names would end that dream at the first serious hurdle.

Writing on ONE, pundit and Maccabi Haifa assistant coach Guy Tzarfati laid out why Red Star should be considered favourites — an experienced, disciplined squad built for occasions like this one, with a second leg in Belgrade still to come that will carry one of Europe's most intimidating atmospheres.

Red Star arrive off the back of a 4-0 aggregate win over Northern Ireland's Larne in the previous round, and they can field Israeli international Mohamed Abu Fani — a player well known to Beer Sheva's staff from his years with Maccabi Haifa and the national team before moves to Ferencváros and then Belgrade. Tzarfati says Abu Fani has settled into the Serbian champions seamlessly.

Alongside him, Red Star have Aleksandar Katai, named Serbian SuperLiga player of the season after topping the league's scoring charts with 24 goals, and 37-year-old former Austria international Marko Arnautović — the kind of experience and quality Tzarfati flags as a genuine problem for Beer Sheva to solve.

Beer Sheva reached this stage on merit, beating Iceland's Víkingur Reykjavík 2-0 in the second leg to seal the aggregate win in the previous round. But the campaign has already cost them their best player: Kings Kangwa, voted Israel's Footballer of the Year for 2025-26 after a 12-goal season, was sold to Panathinaikos for a reported €3.8 million in the middle of the qualifying run.
Tzarfati is blunt about what that departure means, pointing to Kangwa's absence as a significant weakening of Beer Sheva's attacking threat at the worst possible moment.

Yet he does not write the Israeli champions off. His case for an upset rests on a specific tactical idea: if Beer Sheva press high and force Red Star to build out from the back under pressure in their own half, they will be imposing a kind of discomfort the Serbian side rarely faces domestically — and one that could unsettle a team more used to dominating the ball itself.

"Red Star are the preferred side, but Beer Sheva can cause them trouble," is how Tzarfati summed up the tie for ONE — a verdict that leaves plenty of room for a positive result in front of the Beersheba crowd on Tuesday.
The return leg is scheduled for August 11 at the Rajko Mitić Stadium in Belgrade, where a crowd of over 50,000 will await whatever scoreline Beer Sheva carry with them from the first leg.

title: Damascan and Almagor start for Hapoel Jerusalem as Ziv Aryeh returns to face old club
dek: Both sides are still chasing a first Toto Cup win as kickoff nears in Rehovot, with the former Hapoel Jerusalem manager now in the Maccabi Petah Tikva dugout

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Vitalie Damascan signs for Hapoel Jerusalem
Walla Sport - Maccabi Netanya beat Hapoel Jerusalem 3-1 in Toto Cup

body: Hapoel Jerusalem and Maccabi Petah Tikva kick off the third round of Group B in the 2026/27 Toto Cup on Sunday evening at the new municipal stadium in Rehovot, with both clubs still searching for their first win of the pre-season competition.

The game has an added edge on the touchline. Maccabi Petah Tikva are coached by Ziv Aryeh, who spent seven years in charge of Hapoel Jerusalem before leaving in April and being appointed at Petah Tikva on May 27, replacing Noam Shoham. Sunday marks his first match against his old club since the switch.

ONE reports Hapoel Jerusalem will start Nadav Zamir in goal behind a back line of Idan Cohen, Li-On Mizrahi, Tamir Haimovich and Noam Malmud, with Netanel Shprao, Sani Abdulsalam and Andrew Idoko in midfield feeding a front three of Vitalie Damascan and Ohad Almagor.

Damascan's inclusion is notable in its own right. The Moldovan forward, who signed with Jerusalem this summer, has already worn the colours of both Petah Tikva clubs' city, having spent 2024/25 at Maccabi Petah Tikva before a short, difficult spell at Beitar Be'er Sheva that ended in relegation despite four goals and three assists.

Maccabi Petah Tikva's named XI, per ONE, has Maor Erlich in goal, with Muhammad Hindi, Ido Cohen and Guy Dazent anchoring the defence and Liran Hazan involved further forward alongside Noam Shemesh and Kyle Spence.

Neither club has anything to show for the group stage so far. Hapoel Jerusalem opened with a 3-1 defeat to Maccabi Netanya, while Maccabi Petah Tikva have taken zero points from two outings, beaten 1-0 in a local derby before falling 2-1 to Netanya as well.

Jerusalem's decision to stage the fixture in Rehovot rather than at Teddy Stadium reflects a wider pre-season squeeze on pitches around the country, with the club having already confirmed it will use the new municipal ground there for its Ligat Ha'al opener too.

Kickoff is set for 19:45, with both sides using the group stage to sharpen their squads before the top flight begins in earnest — and with Aryeh, in particular, eager for a result against the club where he built his reputation.
