title: Ajax win 3-1 in Gloukh cameo, Keller's Debrecen fall 4-2 at Újpest
dek: Oscar Gloukh came off the bench for 19 minutes in Ajax's pre-season victory over Volendam, while new Debrecen signing Rotem Keller started before being subbed off as his side slipped to a second straight defeat in the Hungarian top flight.

verificationSources.label: Sofascore - Ajax beat Volendam 3-1 as Gaaei stars

body: Two Israelis had contrasting Sundays in Europe, one tasting victory off the bench in Amsterdam, the other absorbing a second straight defeat in Hungary.

Oscar Gloukh came on as a substitute for Ajax and played the final 19 minutes as the Dutch giants beat Volendam 3-1 in a pre-season friendly. Anton Gaaei opened the scoring before Marcos Leonardo added a second from the penalty spot, both in the first half, and debutant striker Tolu Arokodare rounded off the win after the break.

It was a low-key cameo rather than a statement performance for Gloukh, who is building toward his first full Eredivisie season in an Ajax shirt after his move from Red Bull Salzburg. The 22-year-old, capped more than 20 times by Israel, is expected to be a regular fixture in Ajax's attacking midfield once the competitive campaign kicks off.

In Hungary, the news was less kind for Rotem Keller. The Israeli-Hungarian left-back started for Debreceni VSC away to Újpest FC in round two of the NB I, but was withdrawn at the start of the second half as Debrecen went down 4-2.

The result left Debrecen with back-to-back defeats to open the season, following a 2-0 loss to Puskás Akadémia FC in the opening round. It is a tough start for a club that finished fourth last term and will be looking to Keller's arrival to shore up a defence that has already conceded six goals in two matches.

Keller, 23, signed for Debrecen this summer on a three-year deal after leaving Maccabi Netanya, where he made more than two dozen league appearances last season. Versatile enough to play at left-back or centre-back, he had previously spent time in Hungarian football with Diósgyőr and holds dual Israeli-Hungarian citizenship.

Both players are part of a small but growing group of Israelis now plying their trade across Europe's leagues, and their next assignments will offer quick chances to bounce back: Ajax return to competitive action as their Eredivisie campaign approaches, while Debrecen host Nyíregyháza Spartacus in round three looking to arrest their slide.

title: Israel beat Haudenosaunee 7-4 for historic first lacrosse world championship bronze
dek: Jordyn Lipkin inspires an unbeaten pool stage and a quarter-final win over Australia as Israel's women claim the country's maiden World Lacrosse Championship medal in Tokyo.
body: Israel's women's national lacrosse team made history in Tokyo on Sunday, beating the Haudenosaunee Nationals 7-4 in the bronze-medal game to win the country's first-ever medal at a World Lacrosse Women's Championship, ONE reported.

The result capped a remarkable run through the Nissin Foods 2026 World Lacrosse Women's Championship, a 16-team tournament that has been running in Tokyo since July 24, with the semifinals and medal games staged at Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium.

Israel went through pool play unbeaten before edging Australia 12-11 in a frantic quarter-final. The run to a medal game came to a temporary halt in the semifinals, where top-ranked and eventual finalist the United States beat Israel 19-7.

That defeat sent Israel into the bronze-medal match against the Haudenosaunee Nationals, the Indigenous Six Nations team that had itself been chasing a first-ever women's world championship medal after falling to Canada in the other semifinal.

Jordyn Lipkin was named player of the match in the bronze-medal game, according to ONE, and finished the tournament as its leading scorer with 19 goals and 25 total points, adding six ground balls along the way.
"This is a tremendous privilege to represent something far greater than ourselves," Lipkin said, according to ONE's report. "We made history and showed the world what Israel's team is capable of."

The medal is a landmark moment for a program built largely on a mix of Israeli-born players and Jewish athletes from North America, competing under the Israel Lacrosse Association, which has held full World Lacrosse membership since 2011. Israel's women had never previously finished on the podium at a global championship.

The achievement also arrives at a pivotal time for the sport: lacrosse is set to return to the Olympic program at Los Angeles 2028 in the fast-paced Sixes format, raising the stakes and the profile for programs like Israel's as they look to build toward a first Olympic berth.

The United States advanced to face Canada in Sunday's gold-medal game, but for Israel, a nation with no lacrosse tradition to speak of a generation ago, bronze in Tokyo stands as the biggest result in the sport's short Israeli history.

Lacrosse is scheduled to return to the Olympic program at Los Angeles 2028 in the Sixes format.

title: Ex-Maccabi Haifa chief Chizik: transfer reform is 'shameful', players aren't a spreadsheet
dek: Itamar Chizik, the man who ran Maccabi Haifa's football operations for 14 years, tears into a shake-up of Israel's player-transfer arbitration system — and warns Haifa itself has no title chances this season.

verificationSources.label: ONE — Beitar to pay 240,000 shekels for Vorko
Haaretz — Maccabi Haifa names Bakhar as coach, Refaelov as sport director

body: Itamar Chizik ran Maccabi Haifa's football department for fourteen years and later chaired Israel's Players' Status Institution, the body that rules on transfer compensation disputes. So when he goes on record calling a shake-up of that same system "shameful," the football establishment tends to listen.

Speaking on ONE's podcast Sicha HaYom, Chizik said the reform that collapsed the arbitration panel from three adjudicators down to a single decision-maker was pushed through without proper consultation with the people who actually work the system. "Players aren't an Excel spreadsheet — it's shameful what's being done," he said, arguing that a player's value hinges on far too many variables to be settled by one person applying a rigid formula.

He pointed to a concrete example: the recent case of Daniel Vorko, whose move from Hapoel Ramat Gan to Beitar Jerusalem went to arbitration after the two clubs couldn't agree a training-compensation fee. Hapoel Ramat Gan had asked for 1.2 million shekels for a player it developed into a youth international; the committee settled on just 240,000 shekels, a figure ONE itself reported when the ruling landed.

For Chizik, the Vorko case is exhibit A for a wider complaint — that clubs pouring years of investment into developing young talent are left short-changed once that talent moves on, with neither the Youth Committee leadership nor the coaching staff who actually work with the players consulted on how compensation gets calculated.

The conversation then turned to his old club. Chizik does not believe Maccabi Haifa can compete for the championship this season, saying the squad still lacks the defensive depth and midfield cover a title challenge requires.

He was pointed about who he holds responsible for that gap, saying the club's new sport director, Lior Refaelov, is "not suited" to the professional-management role — a notable line given Refaelov was only installed in the post in May, alongside Barak Bakhar's confirmation as head coach for the new season.

On owner Yankel Shachor, who has faced a wave of fan protests since the spring over the club's direction, Chizik was more measured, saying Shachor "understands football" even while some of his calls are open to question.

He was, however, unambiguous about the supporters themselves, saying their campaign against Shachor had "crossed the line of good taste" — a reference to a protest movement that has included stadium banners and stickers plastered around the owner's home and offices demanding he sell the club.

Taken together, Chizik's remarks land as a dual warning shot: a governance complaint aimed at the body that once employed him, and a gloomy squad assessment aimed at the club that shaped his career, at a moment when Haifa's boardroom and its stands are already at odds.

Chizik said Maccabi Haifa will not compete for the championship this season, citing gaps at the back and in midfield.

title: Rafael Aronov stops Miroslav Brož in 1:56 to win OKTAGON debut in Prague
dek: The Beersheba police officer needed less than two minutes to knock out home favourite Miroslav Brož in a hostile Štvanice arena, opening his contract with one of Europe's biggest MMA promotions in style.

verificationSources.label: ONE — reported title: "הקהל שרק בוז וגמרתי את זה תוך פחות משתי דקות"
ONE — preview: "ב-19:30 בערוץ ONE2: רפאל ארונוב בקרב ענק"
Cageside Press — 'Oktagon 92: Szabova vs. Pudilova Full Results'
iSport.cz — 'Oktagon 92 ONLINE: Čechům se na Štvanici nedaří, Brožovi návrat do klece zhořkl'

body: Rafael Aronov walked into a cage full of enemies on Saturday night and left it inside two minutes. The Beersheba police officer stopped local favourite Miroslav Brož by TKO at 1:56 of the first round at Prague's Štvanice tennis stadium, winning his promotional debut for OKTAGON, one of Europe's fastest-growing MMA organisations.

Aronov, who fights at 67 kilograms and is nicknamed "THE ISRAELI COP," opened with elbows and punches before dropping Brož and finishing him with strikes on the ground. The referee stepped in as Brož, a popular and notoriously aggressive fighter on the Czech scene, absorbed a sustained barrage he could no longer answer.

The atmosphere was never going to be friendly. Brož, nicknamed "Inkvizitor," was making his own return to the cage after more than two years away, and the Štvanice crowd had come out for him. Czech outlet iSport described his comeback as souring in front of his own fans.
"The crowd just booed, and I finished it in under two minutes," Aronov told ONE's Shihat HaYom podcast, describing the hostile reception he faced fighting a beloved hometown fighter on foreign soil.

The win opens a four-fight contract Aronov has signed with OKTAGON, a promotion that broadcasts across Europe and has been steadily building its roster with fighters cut loose from bigger organisations. According to ONE, the reigning champion at Aronov's weight has since moved on to the UFC, leaving a vacancy Aronov has made clear he intends to chase.

It is the latest stoppage in a career built almost entirely on early finishes. Aronov, a champion of both Israeli and Romanian promotions, has won all eight of his professional fights by stoppage — four knockouts and four submissions — including four victories in Cage Warriors, the UFC-affiliated organisation where he made his breakthrough. His most recent win there came by rear-naked choke in 90 seconds against England's Ben Fatchés-Kelly.

Away from the cage, Aronov serves as an officer in Israel's Yassam special police units, based in Beersheba. He was among the officers who responded to the Hamas assault on Ofakim on October 7, 2023, an episode that has followed him into every subsequent walkout and interview, according to the Jerusalem Post.

That dual identity — police officer and finisher — has become central to how Aronov presents himself, and Saturday's KO in front of a jeering foreign crowd was another chapter in a story he has leaned into rather than shied away from since October 7.

body: Maccabi Kiryat Malachi have added two more names to their squad list for the coming Liga Alef South campaign, with forward Shachaf Sapir and teenage left-back Sualio Kramuko both putting pen to paper, ONE reports.

Sapir, 23, arrives with experience of the division after splitting last season between Maccabi Atai Bialik and Samson Tel Aviv, scoring two goals and five goals respectively for the two clubs. He came up through the youth ranks at Ironi Kiryat Shmona before working his way through the lower leagues.

Kramuko, 19, is the more speculative addition. Born to an immigrant family from Africa, the left-back has progressed through junior football locally before a recent spell with Hapoel Kfar Selem's youth setup, and he now joins Kiryat Malachi's first team squad for what would be a significant step up.

According to ONE, the pair's arrival follows the club's earlier capture of playmaker Rotem Piumi, part of a broader rebuild that head coach Tzvika Levi is overseeing as Kiryat Malachi prepare for another season in Israel's third tier.

Neither signing is likely to move the needle nationally, but for a club with limited resources working in Liga Alef South, filling out the squad with a proven lower-league scorer and a promising young defender is the kind of incremental business that decides whether a season is competitive or a struggle.
No contract length or fee was disclosed in the report, and Kiryat Malachi have not yet confirmed further incomings, though further squad news is expected as pre-season progresses.

body: About 2,000 Hapoel Tel Aviv supporters have already secured tickets for next week's Conference League third qualifying round opener against Poland's GKS Katowice, ONE reports, with the club bracing for one of its heaviest travelling followings of the summer.

The first leg is set for Thursday, August 6, at the DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary — the same neutral venue that hosted Hapoel's previous European "home" tie. Combined with Katowice's own support and local interest, ONE reports the total crowd is expected to reach around 3,500.
Hapoel reached this stage by beating Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad 2-0 in Miskolc on July 23, then holding on for a 2-2 draw away in Razgrad a week later to advance 4-2 on aggregate.
The return leg against Katowice is scheduled for August 13 in Poland, with the winner moving another step closer to the Conference League's league phase.

The build-up is not without controversy: ONE reports Hapoel are awaiting a possible further UEFA sanction after fans set off pyrotechnics during the away leg in Razgrad. The club already carries a suspended penalty from the first Ludogorets tie — a €25,000 fine and a conditional 10% partial closure of the stadium for future European home matches, suspended for two years — stemming from similar incidents in that opening game.

Even so, the scale of the ticket sales for a fixture staged more than 2,000 kilometres from Tel Aviv underlines how far Hapoel's support base is prepared to travel this European campaign, and the club will be hoping the same numbers translate into an atmosphere strong enough to help see off Katowice over the two legs.

title: Richarlison's Tottenham future in doubt as De Zerbi admits confusion
dek: The Brazilian scored a stoppage-time winner against Chelsea in Sydney, but his manager says the striker has sent mixed signals about staying beyond his final contract year.

verificationSources.label: ONE — reported title: בדרך החוצה? "לפעמים ריצ'רליסון רוצה לעזוב"
ESPN — 'Richarlison sometimes says he wants to leave Tottenham - Roberto De Zerbi'
Sky Sports — 'Chelsea 1-2 Tottenham: Richarlison scores injury-time winner in Sydney friendly'

body: Richarlison scored deep into stoppage time to give Tottenham a 2-1 win over Chelsea in a heated pre-season friendly in Sydney, but the celebrations barely lasted before his manager was fielding questions about whether the forward even wants to stay at the club.

Roberto De Zerbi, whose side finished the game with ten men after Kevin Danso's red card, made no attempt to paper over the uncertainty when asked about Richarlison's contract, which runs only until the end of the 2026-27 season. "I don't know if he will stay because I love him very much... but in the end you have to respect what he wants to do," the Italian said, according to ONE.

De Zerbi went further, describing conversations with the Brazilian as genuinely mixed. "Sometimes he says he wants to stay and sometimes he wants to leave. We'll need to talk about it anyway," he said, adding that he "didn't understand well" which way Richarlison was leaning.

It is a curious backdrop for a player who had just delivered the winning moment. Tonali had put Spurs ahead in the 19th minute with a deflected effort before Chelsea's Estevao levelled almost immediately, and Danso's dismissal three minutes into the second half left Tottenham to see out an hour a man light in front of 80,363 fans at Stadium Australia. Richarlison settled it with virtually the last kick of the game, pouncing on a loose ball after Jamie Donley's shot cannoned back off the post.

It was the fourth win in four pre-season matches for De Zerbi's side, and the manager was quick to stress he has no interest in pushing Richarlison out the door. "He's an important player, you can't easily find another striker like him," he said, praising the 29-year-old's professionalism and work ethic even amid the uncertainty over his long-term plans.

Richarlison joined Tottenham from Everton in the summer of 2022 in a deal reported at around £60 million with add-ons, and has become a fixture of the club's forward line through some difficult seasons, including last term's run to Premier League safety. He posted a career-best 43 appearances for Spurs in 2025-26, finishing among the club's top scorers in the league.

ONE reports that Tottenham have committed well over £200 million to summer recruitment, a spending spree the outlet frames as evidence the club is already lining up cover in case Richarlison does push for an exit before his contract runs out next summer.

For now, nothing is resolved. De Zerbi's comments suggest no formal transfer request has been lodged and no renewal talks have taken place, leaving Richarlison's next move as one of the more intriguing subplots of Tottenham's pre-season as the Premier League opener approaches.

title: Maccabi Yavne tie down defender Yuval Kol and midfielder Amit Persko for another season
dek: The newly merged Liga Alef club has extended two 20-year-old academy products as it rebuilds around head coach Ofer Tsalaffah.
body: Maccabi Yavne have secured the futures of two of their homegrown 20-year-olds, announcing that right-back Yuval Kol and attacking midfielder Amit Persko have both signed on for the 2026/27 season, the club confirmed through ONE.

Kol, a product of Nes Tziona's youth setup who also featured intermittently for the senior side in Liga Bet, is described by the club as a player who brings commitment and seriousness to every session, and his extension is being framed as part of the stability Maccabi Yavne are trying to build heading into the new campaign.

Persko arrives with a broader résumé for his age. He spent two and a half seasons in Beitar Jerusalem's Liga Alef youth ranks before a half-season loan spell at Hapoel Ramat Hasharon in 2024/25, where he scored five goals and set up several more from midfield and the wing. The club has pointed to his pace, technical ability and hunger to progress as reasons for keeping him.

Both signings land just over a week after Maccabi Yavne completed a formal unification with crosstown rival Beitar Yavne, with the combined club continuing to play under the Maccabi "Zvi" Yavne name in Liga Alef South. Yavne mayor Roi Gabbai called the merger "an important day for football in Yavne," according to Sport5's Double Pass, while former Beitar Yavne official Asher Sitrit is set to help run the newly unified operation.

The rebuilt squad is being assembled under head coach Ofer Tsalaffah, a veteran of Israel's lower leagues who has previously delivered promotions with clubs including Hapoel Petah Tikva and Maccabi Nes Tziona and is contracted at Yavne through 2027.

Kol and Persko's extensions follow two other recent additions to the squad: defender Dudi Tiram, a former Ligat Ha'al captain at Maccabi Netanya with experience in the National League and abroad, and young winger-forward Chigozie Aiwu.

For a club aiming to climb back through the divisions after decades outside the top flight — Maccabi Yavne's only major honour remains the 1985 Toto Cup — holding on to academy talent like Kol and Persko while adding experienced heads such as Tiram is being pitched internally as the model for progress this season.

title: Tokyo, 28 August 2019: The Night Sagi Muki Became Israel's First Male World Judo Champion
dek: In the Nippon Budokan, Sagi Muki fought through a rival who wouldn't shake his hand to win gold at -81kg — never knowing that, on the other side of the draw, an Iranian friend had just thrown a match rather than risk facing him.

verificationSources.label: The Times of Israel — 'Israel's Sagi Muki takes gold at judo world championships'
The Jerusalem Post — 'Israeli judoka Sagi Muki wins gold medal at World Championship'
Haaretz — 'Israeli Judoka Sagi Muki Ascends to World Championship Final'

body: The Nippon Budokan is judo's cathedral, the arena Kanō Jigorō's sport built its Olympic legend in back in 1964, and on 28 August 2019 it was host again — this time to the World Judo Championships, a dress rehearsal for the Tokyo Games less than a year away. In the men's under-81 kilogram category, Israel's Sagi Muki, a two-time European champion who had already spent a decade fighting his way toward this exact mat, was seeded among the favourites. By the end of the day he would be a world champion. The manner of it — and the story unfolding out of sight on the other side of the draw — would make the date one of the most quietly extraordinary in Israeli sporting history.

Muki tore through the early rounds. He won his first four bouts by ippon, judo's cleanest kill — a full point, fight over, no need for the judges. It was the form of a man who had waited a long time for this moment: a herniated disc had cost him a shot at the Rio Olympics in 2016, and he had rebuilt himself since, winning European titles in 2015 and 2018 and climbing back to the top of the world rankings.

The semi-final brought Egypt's Mohamed Abdelaal, and a tighter contest — Muki won it by waza-ari, judo's half-point, rather than ippon. It also brought an ugly coda. When the bout ended, Muki offered his hand. Abdelaal turned and walked off the mat without taking it, a scene that echoed Egyptian judoka Islam El Shehaby's refusal to shake Israeli Ori Sasson's hand at the Rio Olympics three years earlier. Muki's response afterward was measured rather than triumphant: he said he was sorry Abdelaal hadn't shaken his hand, and that he was pleased to have shown, in his words, "the beautiful face of Israel." Egypt's own foreign ministry later criticised Abdelaal's conduct.

In the final, Muki faced Belgium's Matthias Casse, the reigning European champion. It was close — by Muki's own account afterward, he came near to losing and had to dig for everything he had. He got there with 1 minute 21 seconds left on the clock, throwing Casse for a fifth ippon in six fights that day, this one built from two waza-ari scores stacked into a full point. Muki dropped to the mat, then rose to be draped in the Israeli flag as Hatikvah played inside the Budokan. "This is my first time as world champion, and it's a very special moment for me," he said. "I finally did it." Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent his congratulations, praising Muki for "bringing a lot of respect and pride to all of us."

It was only Israel's second world judo title, and its first won by a man. The first had come six years earlier and half a world away, when Yarden Gerbi won gold at -63kg at the 2013 World Championships in Rio de Janeiro, choking out France's Clarisse Agbegnenou in the final. Muki's win in Tokyo placed him alongside her in a very short list.

But the full shape of 28 August 2019 didn't become clear until later. On the other half of the draw, Iran's Saeid Mollaei — the reigning world champion, and the man many expected to meet Muki in the final — had been drawn to face Casse in the semi-final. He lost. At the time it looked like an ordinary defeat. It was not. Mollaei later told the International Judo Federation that Iranian officials had pressured him for days to avoid a possible bout against an Israeli, and that Iran's Olympic Committee president warned him, minutes before he stepped onto the mat, that security officials were at his parents' house in Tehran. Mollaei said he deliberately threw the semi-final to Casse, then lost his bronze-medal bout as well, leaving the tournament without a medal rather than risk facing Muki.

Mollaei went public with the story after the championships, telling the IJF he was too afraid to return to Iran. The federation's investigation corroborated his account and led to a four-year suspension of Iran's judo federation over its long-standing policy of forcing athletes to withdraw rather than compete against Israelis. Mollaei sought asylum, eventually settling in Germany; he went on to compete under the Mongolian flag and later for Azerbaijan.

What makes the story remarkable is what came after the politics. Muki and Mollaei, drawn together by a scandal neither of them chose, became friends — genuine ones. They finally faced each other on a judo mat for the first time at the Budapest Grand Slam in 2021, more than two years after Tehran had made sure it wouldn't happen in Tokyo. Mollaei won that bout. The two embraced afterward, and Mollaei later told interviewers he would never forget the kindness the Israeli team had shown him when he had nowhere else to turn.

Muki's own career kept climbing. Two years after Tokyo 2019, he returned to the Nippon Budokan for the delayed 2020 Olympics and won bronze in judo's inaugural mixed team event, adding an Olympic medal to his world title. But 28 August 2019 remains the pivot: the day an Israeli man stood on top of a judo world championship podium for the first time, in a story that turned out to be as much about the fight he never had to have as the ones he did.

title: Tiberias admit their squad is too small to survive in the league
dek: A home Toto Cup defeat to Kiryat Shmona exposed painfully thin depth, as the doping-hit club scrambles to reinforce before an away trip to face Maccabi Haifa.

verificationSources.label: ONE — בטבריה יודעים: הסגל קצר ולא מספיק לליגה

body: Ironi Tiberias have spent the summer fighting a fine, a transfer registration ban and a stack of docked points over an unprecedented doping affair. Now, with the new Ligat Ha'al season about to begin, the club has quietly admitted a second problem that could prove just as damaging: the squad simply is not big enough.

The alarm went up over the weekend. Tiberias lost 0-1 at home to Ironi Kiryat Shmona in the Toto Cup on Saturday, and ONE reports that club officials left the game convinced the current roster will struggle in the league even if not a single further point is deducted.

Goalkeeper Ido Sharon put it in blunt terms once the final whistle went. "This is a Toto Cup game, but as we prepare for the league, we have a short squad and it's hard to play three matches in eight days," he said, according to ONE.

Ron Unger picked up a knock during the defeat and could be rested for the next fixture, thinning the options further. The club has made one addition — attacker Gal Ma'atuk arrived from Hapoel Petah Tikva, with his registration approved on Friday — but ONE reports the mood inside Tiberias is that far more reinforcement is needed, and fast.

The urgency has a hard deadline attached. As part of the plea agreement that settled the club's doping case earlier this year, Tiberias are barred from registering any new players in the January 2027 transfer window, meaning whatever business they manage now may be all the help they get for a long stretch of the campaign.

The case that triggered all of it still hangs over the dressing room. Israel's national anti-doping agency provisionally suspended coach Eliran Chodada and five players over suspected banned infusions, and disciplinary hearings for the five are set to open this week. The club has consistently denied deliberate wrongdoing, arguing the financial discrepancies behind the case were technical errors in salary-cap accounting rather than doping-related.

None of that offers Tiberias any relief on the pitch. They are already carrying a points deduction into the new season as part of the settlement, on top of a roughly half-a-million-shekel fine, and they open their league business away to Maccabi Haifa on Tuesday.

With a squad this stretched and points already gone before a ball has been kicked in anger, every fixture now carries extra weight for a club fighting simply to prove it belongs in the division it is straining to stay in.

title: Berkovic predicts a battle for 4th-8th at Maccabi Haifa, calls Beitar's Almog Cohen gamble a mistake
dek: Eyal Berkovic tells ONE he doesn't see Barak Bachar surviving if Haifa's struggles continue, and says Beitar Jerusalem's decision to make Almog Cohen head coach will not end well.
body: Eyal Berkovic rarely softens an opinion, and on ONE's Sicha Hayom programme this week he delivered both a concrete forecast for Maccabi Haifa's coming season and a blunt verdict on the managerial upheaval at Beitar Jerusalem.

On Haifa, the former Israel international turned outspoken pundit was direct. "At least for now, it looks like they'll compete for places four to eight," he said, sizing up a squad he clearly does not see challenging at the very top of Ligat Ha'al next season.

He went further on head coach Barak Bachar, suggesting the club's patience will run out fast if results don't improve once the league gets under way. "If it continues like this in the league too, I don't see Barak Bachar continuing," Berkovic said, according to ONE.

It was the situation across town, at Beitar Jerusalem, that drew his sharpest words. The club begins the new season with Almog Cohen in the dugout after a summer that saw Barak Yitzhaki depart the post he had held for two and a half seasons, a spell that included a title race against Hapoel Be'er Sheva last term.

Independent reporting on the split, in Haaretz and Israel Hayom, described a pay dispute at the centre of it: club owner Barak Abramov had offered to raise Yitzhaki's monthly salary from 50,000 to 70,000 shekels plus performance bonuses, an offer Yitzhaki reportedly felt undervalued him against coaches like Ran Kozuk and Bachar. Cohen, until then the club's technical director, was promoted to replace him.

Berkovic isn't buying the money explanation. "Over five thousand shekels it fell apart? Come on," he said, dismissing the salary gap as the real trigger. His own theory is that Cohen's professional involvement, not Beitar's wallet, is what pushed Yitzhaki out: "In my opinion they interfered with Yitzhaki professionally, and that's why he left."

He was just as skeptical that Cohen's own move to the touchline will end well. "I think it's a bad decision by him," Berkovic said of the switch from the boardroom to the bench, predicting a short honeymoon with a notoriously demanding fan base — two or three bad results, in his view, would be enough to turn the Teddy Stadium stands against the new coach.

Berkovic, an attacking midfielder who played for West Ham United, Southampton, Manchester City, Blackburn Rovers and Portsmouth during his career, has become one of Israeli football's most prominent — and most willing to needle — broadcasters since retiring, and his verdicts on both Haifa and Beitar are likely to follow both clubs into the new campaign.

title: Beitar right to stand by Miguel Silva after Larnaca shootout drama, says Kornfein
dek: Former Beitar goalkeeper and club CEO Itzik Kornfein says Jerusalem were right to keep faith with Miguel Silva, who turned villain into hero with two penalty saves against AEK Larnaca.
body: Miguel Silva went from tragic figure to shootout hero inside the same wild European night, and according to Itzik Kornfein, Beitar Jerusalem's decision to keep backing their goalkeeper through the swing was exactly the right call.

Appearing on ONE's Sicha Hayom programme, the former Beitar goalkeeper and one-time club CEO argued that the way Beitar's dressing room and staff stood behind Silva after his costly mistake helped the Portuguese recover in time to save the tie in the Conference League third qualifying round shootout against AEK Larnaca.

"Beitar did well to back Miguel Silva," Kornfein said, the comment that gave the segment its title, adding that the goalkeeper remains one of the squad's leaders this season despite his lapses in concentration.

The context was dramatic. Beitar had won the first leg in Jerusalem 1-0, but the return in Cyprus swung wildly: Larnaca twice forced the Israeli side level before Silva was beaten late to send the tie to extra time at 2-2, and Larnaca then edged 3-2 ahead deep into the additional 30 minutes.

That left the tie level at 3-3 on aggregate and set up a shootout in which Silva atoned in the most emphatic way, saving two penalties to send Beitar through 4-3 and into the next qualifying round, where they will meet Austria Wien.

Kornfein's reading was that the release of pressure after the saves effectively erased the earlier error from the ledger. "The pressure eased on him once he saved those penalties," he said, predicting Silva will keep his place as Beitar's first-choice goalkeeper.

He was not blind to the flaw that put Beitar in that position in the first place, though. Kornfein pointed to Silva's occasional trouble dealing with high balls and crosses under pressure as the recurring issue behind his mistakes.

His prescription was practical rather than punitive: more work with a mental coach and closer video analysis of exactly those situations, rather than any suggestion of dropping a goalkeeper he still rates highly.

Looking ahead, Kornfein flagged Austria Wien as a considerably tougher examination than Larnaca, and one where Beitar's goalkeeper is likely to be tested again if they are to advance further in Europe.

title: Only donkeys don't change their minds: pundit backs Maccabi Haifa's tactical rethink
dek: Radio analyst Nisan Kanias says the pain of two Toto Cup defeats was worth it for Barak Bachar's system change before the season proper — but reckons Haifa still need at least three signings, starting with a fit goalkeeper.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — Haifa 0-3 Kiryat Shmona, Glazer and Tsunami hurt
Sport1 — Hapoel Haifa 3-2 Maccabi Haifa derby summary

body: Maccabi Haifa's pre-season has produced almost nothing but bad headlines — a derby defeat, a heavy loss to Kiryat Shmona and a goalkeeper stretchered off in tears. But according to one of the club's own local voices, the pain has a silver lining.

Haifa opened their Toto Cup campaign by losing the Haifa derby 3-2 to Hapoel Haifa — the first time Hapoel had beaten their rivals in the competition since 1997. Barak Bachar's side then followed up with a 3-0 defeat to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, a result that left the technical staff with far bigger problems than the table alone suggests.

The Kiryat Shmona game turned into a nightmare in a different way: goalkeeper Omri Glazer suffered a serious knee injury in a collision with teammate Wenderson Tsunami and had to be helped off the pitch in tears, with Tsunami himself also picking up a knock.

Glazer's injury has exposed just how thin Haifa are between the posts. Backup Sherif Kiwuf is already out with a long-term injury of his own, and third-choice Giorgi Yarmakov has since left the club for Ukraine — leaving Bachar, for now, without a fit senior goalkeeper on the books.

Speaking on ONE's Sihat HaYom programme, Haifa radio analyst Nisan Kanias argued that the club's response — a change to their tactical system ahead of the league season — was overdue but well timed. "Only donkeys don't change their minds, and it's good they changed it before the league starts," he said of Bachar and sport director Lior Refaelov.

Kanias was unbothered by the run of Toto Cup results itself. "Winning the Toto Cup is nice, but not beyond that," he said, framing the real value of the tournament as a testing ground rather than a trophy worth chasing — better, in his view, for Haifa to work through their problems now than to carry them into the league opener.

That still leaves Bachar with a squad short in specific areas, according to Kanias, who put the number of players still needed at a minimum of three. Top of the list is a left-back, with Tsunami — who has been filling that role — now facing time on the sidelines.

Kanias also flagged the right wing, where doubts persist over Manuel Benson's fitness after the winger has been carrying an Achilles tendon issue, and, most urgently after Sunday's events, a recognised backup goalkeeper.

On that front, Kanias floated two realistic names: former Haifa and Israel goalkeeper Josh Cohen, now playing in MLS, and free agent Gad Amos, both of whom he considers credible options to shore up the position before the Israeli Premier League season begins.

With the league opener approaching fast, Haifa's transfer business over the coming days may end up mattering as much as anything they do on the pitch — and Kanias's shopping list gives a clear sense of where the club's most urgent gaps still lie.

dek: After a second straight Toto Cup win, defender Nemanja Ljubisavljević pointed to the summer departures of Cristian Martínez and Yair Mordechai as proof that hard work at Kiryat Shmona gets rewarded.

body: Kiryat Shmona are two players lighter after a summer of sales, and their manager's dressing room is choosing to see it as a selling point rather than a setback.

The northern club made it two Toto Cup wins from two on Saturday, edging Tiberias 1-0 away at Barel Stadium in Nof HaGalil courtesy of a 61st-minute goal from Abdullazadeh, following an emphatic 3-0 win over Maccabi Haifa in their previous outing.

It was afterwards, discussing the club's summer business, that centre-back Nemanja Ljubisavljević turned the conversation toward the two biggest names to have left Kiryat Shmona this off-season. "Two important players left the team - Martins and Mordechai - and I'm happy for them advancing," the Serbian said. "They're an example to us all that with the right work and the right performances, we can achieve the same thing."

He also gave a window into a difficult week for the squad. "We arrived emotionally drained after the big win over Haifa, but we talked it through in the dressing room and agreed we needed to work harder," Ljubisavljević said, explaining a performance he described as more of a grind than the rout that preceded it.

The player he referred to simply as "Martins" is Cristian Martínez, the Panamanian right-back who arrived at Kiryat Shmona on loan from Plaza Amador in July 2024 and quickly became a first-team fixture. His stock rose sharply this year: he started all three of Panama's group games at the 2026 World Cup in June, drawing attention from clubs across Europe.

That interest turned into a transfer this summer, with Sport5 confirming Martínez has signed for Slovan Bratislava of the Slovak top flight, in a deal reported to be worth around €800,000 to Kiryat Shmona - a significant fee by the standards of Israel's second-tier clubs.

Yair Mordechai's exit followed a similar arc. The winger, long tracked by several of Israel's bigger clubs, signed a four-year contract with Maccabi Haifa in May, with Kiryat Shmona due a development-fee payment reported in the region of NIS 800,000 to 1 million once the move was finalised.

Both departures leave holes in a squad now leaning on newer faces to fill them, and Saturday's clean sheet carried its own subplot: goalkeeper Daniel Tenenbaum, who spent time at Tiberias earlier in his career, kept out his old club without conceding.

Peruvian forward Adrian Ogrisha made his first appearance of the pre-season campaign in the win, with the club moving to dampen speculation linking him with a move abroad. Kiryat Shmona said no formal offer for the striker exists, despite reports of interest from a Chinese club earlier in the window.

For a club that has built its recent identity on developing players and cashing in when the offers arrive, Ljubisavljević's framing of Martínez and Mordechai as role models rather than losses is a deliberate message to the squad he is still building around them.

title: Rakonjac set for medical and Maccabi Petah Tikva contract after leaving Hapoel Jerusalem
dek: The Montenegrin forward, who scored twice in a half-season in the capital, is joining the Liga Leumit club on a deal through the end of the season with an option for another year.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Rakonjac signs for Hapoel Jerusalem (January 2026)

body: Marko Rakonjac is heading for a medical and a contract signing at Maccabi Petah Tikva, ONE reported on Sunday, ending his brief spell at Hapoel Jerusalem barely seven months after he arrived in the capital.

The Montenegrin forward flew into Israel on Friday and was due to join his new club that evening — fittingly for a friendly against the very team he is leaving, Hapoel Jerusalem. According to ONE, he is set to sign a contract running through the end of the season with a club option for a further year.
Rakonjac's agent, Ziv Solomowitz, brokered the move to Petah Tikva's Liga Leumit side, per the report. No transfer fee has been disclosed.

It is a short stay in the capital. Rakonjac signed for Hapoel Jerusalem as the club's first winter acquisition in January 2026, telling reporters at the time that he believed in the team and was determined to help drag it away from the bottom of the table. He managed two goals in half a season there before this exit, ONE said.

The 25-year-old forward has a well-travelled career behind him. Raised in the Čukarički academy in Serbia, he broke through as a teenager with 11 goals in a single season before Spartak Moscow paid a reported €2.5 million for him. Loan spells followed at Crvena Zvezda, Bačka Topola and Hungary's Diósgyőr, and he spent last season at Greek club Asteras Kritis, managing only one goal in 17 appearances across all competitions.
He has also represented Montenegro at national-team level.

For Maccabi Petah Tikva, the move is part of a broader push to strengthen ahead of the new Liga Leumit campaign. ONE reported the club is also chasing a defensive reinforcement and remains in talks over a possible move for Yoav Koren, currently on Hapoel Be'er Sheva's books.
The signing still needs Rakonjac to clear his medical before it is made official, but ONE's report leaves little doubt the paperwork is a formality at this stage.

title: Infantino eyed $30 million salary in scrapped FIFA World Cup investment plan
dek: The Times revealed the FIFA president stood to earn more than ten times his current pay through the now-abandoned Forward Enterprise scheme, despite his repeated denials that he would personally profit.
body: For months, Gianni Infantino insisted he had nothing personal to gain from his plan to sell off a slice of the World Cup. According to an investigation by The Times, cited by ONE, that claim does not hold up: the scheme the FIFA president devised would have paid him a salary of more than €30 million a year, plus bonuses — roughly ten times the €3 million he currently earns.

The plan centred on a new FIFA subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise, through which Infantino proposed selling 20 percent of the World Cup's broadcasting and marketing rights to outside investors. FIFA projected the sale would raise around €3.65 billion for the organisation.

The Times reported that once his presidential term ends, Infantino was positioned to step into a commissioner or chief-executive role at the new entity, with an annual reward reported elsewhere at roughly £47 million — a payday that would have dwarfed his existing compensation package.

To win support, Infantino built financial incentives directly into the vote. All 211 FIFA member associations were entitled to vote on the proposal, with those backing it promised roughly $35 million each in development funding, while associations that opposed the plan were offered a far smaller sum, reported at around $9 million.

The scheme triggered a fierce backlash. UEFA and CONCACAF led opposition among the confederations, and UEFA's 55 member nations agreed last Thursday to consider boycotting the World Cup and other FIFA competitions if the plan went ahead. UEFA described the process as a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal."

Facing that united front, Infantino announced FIFA had scrapped the investment plan entirely. He has not indicated any intention to step down, but the episode has left several federations saying they no longer trust his leadership.

The revelations add to a difficult stretch for the FIFA president, whose close ties to political figures including Donald Trump and his push to expand FIFA competitions have already drawn scrutiny. The gap between Infantino's public assurances and the compensation structure now reported by The Times is likely to keep the pressure on him in the coming weeks.

FIFA has not detailed what, if anything, will replace the Forward Enterprise proposal as a source of additional World Cup revenue, leaving the question of how the federation intends to grow its commercial income unresolved for now.

The plan involved selling 20 percent of World Cup broadcasting and marketing rights, projected to raise about €3.65 billion for FIFA.

title: Israel's artistic swimming team reaches European final despite injury scare
dek: A late call-up for teenager Noya Tzarfati after a training-ground concussion to Yaara Sharabani helped Israel's group secure a place in Monday's team free final in Paris.
body: Israel's artistic swimming team is through to Monday's team free final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, ONE reports — a result made sweeter by the fact it came after a training-ground injury scare threatened to disrupt the group just days before competition began.
The Israeli group finished fifth in qualifying with a score of 206.4693, according to ONE, enough to book the country's third appearance in this final at a European Championships.
The achievement came without Yaara Sharabani, who suffered a concussion in training the week before the championships and was ruled out of the event, ONE reports.
Noya Tzarfati, the youngest member of the national squad, was called into the lineup on short notice to replace her and helped steady the group through qualifying and into Monday's final.
The eight swimmers who competed in Paris were Yogev Dagan, Katy Konin, Alexandra Lerman, Noga Levi, Lior Makmel, Leah Makmel, Aya Mazor and Tzarfati, per ONE's report.

The Israeli delegation traveled to Paris as part of a broader push at the 2026 European Aquatics Championships, which opened July 31 and run through August 5 at the Saint-Denis Olympic Aquatic Centre — the pool built for the Paris 2024 Olympics — with swimming and diving events following later in the program.

Artistic swimming, formerly known as synchronized swimming, has quietly become one of the deeper pockets of Israeli Olympic sport in recent years, with the national program producing regular continental finalists across its duet and group disciplines.

The team free final is scheduled for Monday at 5 p.m. Israel time. A fifth-place qualifying score makes a medal a stretch against the continent's traditional powers, but reaching the final again is itself a marker of how far the program has come — and this time it did so while absorbing a last-minute personnel crisis.

body: An Italian mechanic and content creator has spent roughly a year turning a 1993 Fiat Panda into what he hopes will be recognised as the world's narrowest drivable car — a viral novelty item carried by ONE, but with no sporting content whatsoever.

The builder, named in coverage as Andrea Marzi (also rendered Andrea Marazzi in other outlets), sliced the Panda lengthwise in his family's workshop and rebuilt it with a drastically narrowed central section, down to about 50 centimetres wide — roughly the width of one person.

The single-seat result keeps the Panda's original roof, headlights and door handles, but swaps the factory engine for a scooter motor and a 24-volt battery, giving it a top speed of about 15 km/h and a range of roughly 25 km per charge.

It is not road-legal and was built, according to the reporting, as an art project and a bid at a Guinness World Records title for the narrowest car ever made, after debuting at an Italian event for Fiat Panda enthusiasts.

title: Elitzur Netanya sign highly rated teenage center Omri Orland
dek: The second-tier club add 16-year-old prospect Omri Orland from Hapoel Emek Hefer, with coach Shay Seglovitch framing the move as part of a push back to the top flight.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Elitzur Netanya sign Omri Orland
Israel Hayom - profile of Omri Orland

body: Elitzur Netanya have added one of Israeli basketball's most talked-about teenage prospects, announcing the signing of 16-year-old center Omri Orland from Hapoel Emek Hefer, ONE reports.

Orland, who turns 17 in September, is younger than most of his peer group but is already being projected as a future leading big man. In last season's youth competition he averaged 12.5 points, 3.9 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.3 steals per game, numbers that have made him a fixture of Israel's youth national teams and, according to Israeli media, a player scouts around Europe are starting to track.

The move has a family thread running through it. Orland's father, Yehoa Orland, played for Netanya earlier in his career - turning out for Barak Netanya, one of the identities the Netanya basketball club has carried, between 2011 and 2014 - and has since built a coaching career of his own in the Israeli Premier League.

"Our main goal is building a strong team to return Elitzur Netanya to the top league," head coach Shay Seglovitch said, according to ONE. "We believe successful teams should also be homes for talented young Israeli players. When we have opportunities to develop Israel's basketball future through hard work and professional development, we always seize them. We're happy Omri is joining us and wish him great success."

The signing fits a familiar pattern for a club currently working its way through the lower tiers of Israeli basketball: build around a competitive senior roster while giving a pathway to prospects from the region's youth systems, with Orland's arrival billed as both a basketball and a development move rather than a marquee free-agent addition.
No contract length or financial terms were disclosed in the report.

title: Grenade thrown at Japanika branch in Hadera in tenth attack on Beitar owner's restaurant chain
dek: The overnight blast at an under-construction outlet in Hadera, which caused no injuries, is the latest strike in a month-long underworld feud engulfing the Japanika chain owned by Beitar Jerusalem's Barak Abramov.
body: A grenade was thrown before dawn on Sunday at an under-construction branch of the Japanika restaurant chain in Hadera, the latest blow in a criminal underworld feud that has repeatedly targeted the sushi empire controlled by Beitar Jerusalem owner Barak Abramov.

Police said the device struck the commercial section of a new residential complex on Herbert Samuel Street at around 4:20 a.m., damaging a storefront that already bore Japanika signage though the branch had not yet opened. No one was hurt, and officers from the Hadera station were at the scene collecting evidence as the investigation opened.

ONE, citing Eli Senior, head of the crime desk at Channel 13 News, reported that this is now the tenth known attack on the chain in a wave that began in mid-July. Grenades, a pipe bomb and gunfire have been directed at Japanika branches in Netanya, Afula, Herzliya, Givatayim, Kiryat Ono and Ramat Gan over the past month, with property damage but no casualties.

Police are investigating whether the attacks form part of an escalating dispute between the Musli and Jarushi crime families. Abramov himself is not a suspect in the affair, but he has increasingly been perceived as aligned with figures in the Jarushi family, a perception investigators believe has made his restaurant network a target for parties linked to the rival Musli organisation.

"It's deliberate — they're choosing the early hours," Senior said on Channel 13's Today's Conversation, according to ONE, noting that attackers have consistently struck at times and locations with no people present. But he cautioned that the pattern could shift: "It could happen again, and a grenade can cause real harm if it goes off when people are around."

Abramov, whose personal fortune has been estimated at roughly 600 million shekels, took control of Beitar Jerusalem in the summer of 2022 after buying the club from Moshe Hogeg, steering it from the brink of collapse to a side now competing for the championship. His restaurant holdings sit under Landora Group, the company he chairs, which also owns the Japanika chain now at the centre of the feud.

The security crisis around Japanika comes even as Landora has drawn interest from institutional investors: Bank Leumi's investment arm, Leumi Partners, has reportedly been examining a deal to buy a 20 percent stake in the group. No arrests have yet been announced over Sunday's Hadera attack specifically, and police say the broader investigation into the campaign against the chain continues.

title: Every game makes us readier for the league, say Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim
dek: New arrivals Farid Ibrahim and Tomer Haran join the squad as Masai Dego's side use the Toto Cup to sharpen up before the Liga Leumit season.

verificationSources.label: Sport1 - squad news ahead of Netanya trip

body: Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim travel to Maccabi Netanya on Sunday for their second Toto Cup fixture of the pre-season, and the club's line on the tournament is unambiguous: every outing between now and the Liga Leumit opener is treated as a rehearsal, not a formality.

"Each match will bring us more prepared for the league," the club said, adding that it is "a shame our squad isn't complete" so that these games could provide even sharper preparation. The comment reflects a squad still very much under construction just weeks before the second-tier campaign begins.

Ramat Gan opened their Toto Cup account with a 2-1 win over Hapoel Petah Tikva, and coach Masai Dego - who took over from Michael Zandberg in the top flight last autumn before the club's relegation to Liga Leumit - now has two fresh faces to work into the group.

Left-sided defender-cum-midfielder Farid Ibrahim has completed his move from a club in Kazakhstan and took part in his first training session with his new teammates this week. Goalkeeper Tomer Haran, 27, has also signed, agreeing a one-year deal with an option for a second season after a career that has taken him through Maccabi Jerusalem as well as stints in Germany, Slovenia and Uruguay.
"I'm happy and excited to join Hapoel Ramat Gan. I love working hard and being part of a club with high ambitions," Haran said of the move.

Three trialists - Erik Menashe, Frank Erozzi and Abubakar Dosso - remain in training with the squad while the club's management decides on their futures, part of a broader push to bring in four more foreign players on top of the two already signed, filling out the five overseas slots available under Liga Leumit rules.
On the Israeli side of the market, Noam Schwartz of Maccabi Tel Aviv is among the names the club continues to weigh as it looks to round out the squad domestically as well as abroad.

The message from within the club is one of urgency without panic: the Toto Cup fixtures against sides like Petah Tikva and Netanya matter less for their results than for what they reveal about a squad still finding its final shape before Liga Leumit football resumes in earnest.

title: Buffon says he would have picked Antonio Conte to coach Italy
dek: The former Azzurri goalkeeper says Conte was his first choice as the Italian federation searches for a permanent successor to Gennaro Gattuso, with interim boss Silvio Baldini his second pick.

verificationSources.label: ONE - בופון: הייתי בוחר באנטוניו קונטה למאמן איטליה
The National - Andrea Pirlo out of running for Italy job amid row over link to Russian betting company
Fox Sports - Gattuso resigns as Italy boss after World Cup qualifying failure
Goal.com Italia - Perché Silvio Baldini non sarà il ct dell'Italia anche da settembre
beIN Sports - Conte's contract officially terminated by Napoli

body: Gianluigi Buffon has waded into Italy's chaotic hunt for a new national team coach, saying that if the choice were his alone, Antonio Conte would already have the job.

"If I were the sporting director, I would first propose Antonio Conte, then Baldini and then others," Buffon said, according to a report by Israeli outlet ONE, putting the former Juventus and Inter boss firmly ahead of the other names being floated in Rome.

It is a significant intervention from a man who, until April, sat inside the federation himself. Buffon resigned as the Azzurri's delegation chief alongside federation president Gabriele Gravina after Italy lost on penalties to Bosnia and Herzegovina in the World Cup qualifying play-off, extending the country's absence from the tournament to a third straight cycle. Gennaro Gattuso quit as head coach days later.

The search for Gattuso's successor has since turned into one of Italian football's messier sagas. New federation president Giovanni Malagò, elected in June, brought in Paolo Maldini and Leonardo as sporting directors with a mandate to identify the next coach, and the pair moved to install Andrea Pirlo.

That plan collapsed within weeks. Pirlo's role as an ambassador for the Russian betting company Fonbet, which also sponsors Russia's national side, triggered a political storm and objections from Italian lawmakers; Malagò vetoed the appointment, and Maldini and Leonardo resigned just two weeks into their jobs.
Buffon did not hold back on that episode either, describing the handling of the Pirlo affair as "a clumsy, unsuccessful political attempt," per ONE's report.

With no permanent coach in place, Silvio Baldini has been running the team on an interim basis. Buffon's endorsement of him as his second choice is notable given Baldini has himself played down his chances of keeping the job long-term, telling reporters ahead of Italy's recent friendlies that he lacks "that curriculum" for the post on a permanent basis.

On Roberto Mancini, the Euro 2020-winning coach and, alongside Conte, one of the two names most consistently linked with the vacancy, Buffon was more measured. He called Mancini "technically the right choice" but made clear his personal preference remained Conte.

Conte, who led Napoli to the Scudetto in May before the two sides parted by mutual agreement in June, has been strongly linked with a return to the Italy dugout he last occupied between 2014 and 2016, when he took the Azzurri to the Euro 2016 quarter-finals.

Buffon also revealed he had turned down an administrative offer from Maldini and Leonardo during their brief spell in charge, saying he needed time with his family after decades without an extended break away from football.

More broadly, the 48-year-old argued Italian football's problems run deeper than any single appointment. "We've heard many words for years, but nothing becomes a real project," he said, adding that coaches in Italy "are afraid to give young players a chance" and that the sport has "completely changed in the last 20 years" while Italy has been slow to adapt.

title: Hapoel Hadera appeals ruling that cut Abdach transfer compensation by 57%
dek: The newly relegated club wants an arbitrator's decision on training fees for Bashar Abdach's move to Maccabi Petah Tikva thrown out, alleging the process was rushed and inconsistent with other rulings that same week.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הפוסק שינה החלטה וחתך דרמטית את דמי ההשבחה
ONE - סופית: הפועל חדרה תשחק במחוז הדרומי של ליגה א'

body: Hapoel Hadera has taken its fight over training compensation for Bashar Abdach to football's appeals process, petitioning to have a ruling that slashed the club's payout by 57 percent thrown out entirely.

The dispute centres on money Hadera says it is owed for developing Abdach before his move to Maccabi Petah Tikva. On July 14, arbitrator Dr. Dan Chai ordered Maccabi to pay 325,000 shekels in training compensation - but that decision was voided the same day over a procedural error.

A revised ruling issued on July 20 slashed the figure to just 140,000 shekels, a cut of 185,000 shekels, or 57 percent, with no detailed explanation offered for the scale of the change, according to ONE.

Hadera's petition, filed through lawyer Reuven Rozen, argues the revised decision effectively ignored the arguments the club had submitted. It also points to a procedural detail it considers suspicious: Maccabi's representative paid the arbitrator's fee just nine minutes after being notified, a pace the club says helped push the ruling through before it could respond.

The petition further claims that no receiving club had been formally identified in the case when the reduced figure was set, yet Maccabi Petah Tikva signed Abdach within 24 hours and paid exactly 140,000 shekels - the same number the arbitrator had just landed on.

Hadera also says the award is out of step with the arbitrator's own recent record, noting that Dr. Chai issued rulings of 240,000 and 450,000 shekels in comparable training-compensation cases the very same week.

The club's case leans on Abdach's profile as justification for a higher fee: it says the defender made 14 appearances in the top flight and has worn the captain's armband for Israel at youth international level, credentials Hadera argues merited a larger training award than the one he received.

In its petition, Hadera is asking for the July 20 decision to be annulled outright, for the case to be reassigned to a different arbitrator, and for an interim order preventing Abdach's registration with Maccabi Petah Tikva while the appeal is heard.

The compensation fight lands at a painful moment for the club. Hadera was relegated at the end of last season and has since been placed in the southern division of Liga Alef, the third tier, making every shekel of training compensation more consequential to its finances.

title: Don't write him off: Endrick answers Real Madrid's new signing with a goal
dek: Days after Real Madrid signed forward Carlos Espí to add to an already crowded attack, Endrick cut through the noise with a goal against Fiorentina and won praise from José Mourinho.

verificationSources.label: ESPN — Endrick scores as Real Madrid get draw in Mourinho's return
ESPN — Real Madrid sign Carlos Espí from Levante
ESPN — Fulham agree fee with Real Madrid for Gonzalo García

body: Real Madrid's forward line got even more crowded this week, but Endrick's answer was about as loud as it gets: a goal inside 12 minutes on his first pre-season appearance, in a game his side went on to draw 2-2 with Fiorentina.

The backdrop is a squad reshuffle up front. Gonzalo García's departure to Fulham looked, briefly, like it might open a route back into José Mourinho's plans for the young Brazilian. Instead, Real Madrid moved fast to replace him, activating the release clause to sign 21-year-old Carlos Espí from Levante on a deal running through June 2031, ONE reports.

With Kylian Mbappé an undisputed starter through the middle, Espí's arrival means the competition for minutes behind him is as fierce as ever — a dynamic ONE described as working "like a food chain": the moment one forward leaves, another leaps to seize the opening.

Endrick, for his part, chose not to complain. He had returned to Madrid only days earlier following a loan spell at Lyon and Brazil's World Cup campaign, and needed just three training sessions before Mourinho threw him into the Fiorentina friendly.

He made the most of it. In the 12th minute he controlled a ball into the box and finished left-footed for the opener, then stayed on for more than 70 minutes despite his evident lack of match sharpness.
"This is a fantastic effort with a lot of meaning," Mourinho said afterwards, according to ONE. "I told him thank you for what he gave us."

The friendly, played in Klagenfurt, Austria, ended level after Fiorentina scored twice in the second half to cancel out Madrid's early lead. Espí himself made his Real Madrid debut off the bench, coming on in Endrick's place.

It is a small return fixture in the context of a career that has stalled since Endrick's big-money move from Palmeiras two years ago. He managed only sporadic appearances under Carlo Ancelotti and then Xabi Alonso, and a hamstring injury kept him out for months before the loan to Lyon was arranged last December — a spell in which he found something closer to his best form.

Real Madrid attached no obligation to buy when they brought him back this summer, and with Mbappé and now Espí both ahead of him in the pecking order, Endrick's path to regular football at the Bernabéu remains narrow. But as ONE put it: don't eulogize him yet.

title: Arnautović eyes his Champions League dream as Red Star await Hapoel Beer Sheva
dek: The veteran Austrian striker, fresh off retirement from international football, is one goal-scoring threat standing between Hapoel Beer Sheva and the Champions League league phase.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com - H. Beer-Sheva vs Crvena Zvezda match info
Irish News - Arnautovic at the double as Larne outclassed in Belgrade
Tribuna - Arnautovic in tears remembering promise to Mihajlović

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva's push for the Champions League league phase runs into one of European football's more sentimental late-career stories this week: Marko Arnautović, now 37, lining up for Red Star Belgrade with the trophy he has chased his whole career finally within reach.

ONE reports that Arnautović, who joined Red Star as a free agent after his Inter Milan contract expired, sees the club he supported as a boy as his last realistic route to Champions League silverware — a motivation the Austrian has made no secret of since arriving in Belgrade.

Beer Sheva and Red Star meet in the third qualifying round, with the first leg in Beer Sheva on August 4 and the return in Belgrade on August 11. The winner advances to the league phase; the loser drops into the Europa League qualifying path.

Ran Kozuch's side, fresh off winning the Israeli Premier League title, reached this stage by beating Vikingur Reykjavik 3-2 on aggregate in round two — a tie they trailed after a 2-1 defeat in Iceland before winning 2-0 at home to go through.

Red Star arrive in far more emphatic form. They thrashed Northern Irish champions Larne 9-0 on aggregate in the previous round, capped by a 5-0 demolition in Belgrade in which Arnautović scored twice, either side of the break, to go with strikes from Aleksandar Katai and Osman Bukari.

Arnautović's move to Red Star last summer was itself a story soaked in emotion. He turned down a reported €6 million offer from boyhood suitors Rapid Vienna to sign in Belgrade instead, telling reporters at his unveiling that he had promised the late Siniša Mihajlović — his mentor at Bologna, who died of leukaemia in 2022 — that he would one day wear the red and white.
"I had promised Siniša I would come to Red Star, and now I am here," Arnautović said at the time, recalling how the pair used to talk about the club daily during their time together.

The striker has since become Austria's most-capped and highest-scoring international, finishing his national-team career with 49 goals in 137 appearances before retiring after Austria's last-32 exit to Spain at the 2026 World Cup.

For Beer Sheva, the assignment is stark: contain a Serbian champion in ruthless scoring form, spearheaded by a 37-year-old still adding to a résumé that includes a Champions League winner's medal earned on the bench with Inter in 2010, and stop him doing it again on Israeli soil in the first leg.
A result at home on August 4 would give Kozuch's side something concrete to defend in Belgrade a week later, and keep alive a run that has already outlasted one European campaign this summer.

title: Besiktas unveil David DeJulius as Murcia digs in and threatens FIBA and legal action
dek: The former Maccabi Tel Aviv guard was presented by his new Turkish club within a day of finishing second in Spain's scoring race, but UCAM Murcia insists it never released him and is readying a fight through FIBA and the courts.

verificationSources.label: Sportando - UCAM Murcia responds to Besiktas
Blog de Basket - DeJulius returns to EuroLeague with Besiktas

body: Besiktas presented David DeJulius as their marquee guard signing on Saturday, framing it as his return to the EuroLeague. Within hours, the unveiling had curdled into a full-blown ownership dispute with the American's previous club, Spain's UCAM Murcia.

Murcia's response was blunt. The club said it had granted no release, or "letter of freedom," to a player it insists remains under contract through the 2027-28 season following an extension signed in March. Departing now, Murcia argued, was not appropriate "without having previously reached a separation agreement."

DeJulius has become one of Liga Endesa's most compelling stories over the past year. In his lone season in Murcia, the 27-year-old American guard averaged around 17.7 points and 4.4 assists a game, finishing second in the Spanish league's scoring charts and earning a place on its all-star five.

His route to Spain ran through Israel. DeJulius spent the 2024-25 season with Maccabi Tel Aviv, a EuroLeague stint that never fully took off, before moving to Murcia last summer and blossoming into a genuine offensive weapon in Liga Endesa.

Murcia's statement did not soften what comes next, saying the club would keep "defending its rights, both at FIBA and through the courts, against anyone acting to its detriment" - language that leaves little room for a quiet resolution.

Sport5 quoted Spanish journalist Gerard Solà describing the standoff in stark terms: "There's a big mess here. Besiktas announced DeJulius's signing, but he's still bound to Murcia. Either they reach an agreement, or he cannot play for his new team. Otherwise this ends in court."

Turkish and Spanish outlets reported that Besiktas moved to complete the signing by triggering a buyout clause in DeJulius's Murcia contract, though no figure has been made public, and it is unclear whether the two clubs have even begun negotiating a fee.

DeJulius, for his part, has already said his goodbyes, posting a farewell message thanking Murcia's fans and staff for the season - a sign he considers his time in Spain over even as the paperwork stays contested.

Until FIBA or a Spanish court settles the release question, DeJulius's immediate future in Istanbul remains clouded. Besiktas have their man on paper, but Murcia has made plain it intends to fight for compensation before he takes the floor in EuroLeague colours again.

body: Barak Bachar is preparing to throw a teenager into the deep end. With Maccabi Haifa still searching for their first points of this Toto Cup campaign, the coach is set to start 19-year-old Glenn Alvin in goal on Tuesday against Ironi Tiberias, Sport5 reports.

It will be Alvin's first competitive start for the senior side. The young keeper has already had a taste of first-team action this summer, coming on as a substitute during the 3-0 defeat to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, where he was said to have "displayed good ability" in his cameo.

His chance has come about through misfortune elsewhere. Omri Glazer, Haifa's first-choice goalkeeper, picked up an injury in that same loss to Kiryat Shmona and will not be available for the trip against Tiberias, leaving Bachar with little alternative but to trust his academy product between the posts.

There is a second absentee to work around in midfield. Ali Mohamed, the Niger international who has become a regular in Bachar's engine room, felt discomfort in his ankle during the Kiryat Shmona match. Scans have not revealed any significant damage, according to Sport5, but he has not been training this week and will sit out against Tiberias, with a return to full training expected before the weekend.

There is better news on the fitness front elsewhere in the squad. Yarin Levy, who had been sidelined by a virus, is fit again and set to return to the starting lineup, while veteran winger Kenny Saief has resumed full training for the first time in three months after a long spell on the sidelines.

The context adds urgency to Tuesday's fixture. Maccabi Haifa have lost both of their opening group-stage matches in this year's Toto Cup - beaten 3-2 by local rivals Hapoel Haifa in the derby before the heavier 3-0 defeat to Kiryat Shmona - and Sport5 frames the Tiberias game as a chance for Bachar's side to show "improved capability" after that rocky start.

For Alvin, it is a significant opportunity to stake a claim as more than just emergency cover, at a club that has historically been willing to trust academy graduates when injuries create an opening. How he performs against Tiberias is likely to shape how quickly Bachar turns to him again once Glazer is back to fitness.

title: CF Montréal 2-2 New England: Turgeman defies antisemitic chants, clashes with rival goalkeeper
dek: Israeli forward Dor Turgeman celebrated his goal in front of the crowd that had abused him all night in Montreal, sparking a shoving match with goalkeeper Sebastian Breza and a shower of bottles from the stands.
body: Dor Turgeman had already heard enough by the time he found the net. New England Revolution's Israeli forward put his side 2-0 up away to CF Montréal on Saturday night, and instead of running to his own bench he sprinted toward the section of Stade Saputo where home supporters had spent the evening hurling abuse at him.

Fans in that section had directed antisemitic chants at Turgeman through the first half, including calls of "Death to Israel," according to Israeli outlets Sport1 and Walla who covered the match. Turgeman, born in Ashdod and capped 18 times for Israel's national team, scored in the 36th minute to double his side's lead and turned it into a moment of open defiance.

He cupped a hand to his ear and spread his arms toward the crowd that had been jeering him, a gesture that immediately drew a furious response from the stands and from Montreal's own goalkeeper, Sebastian Breza, who came running from the edge of the box to confront him.

Breza shoved Turgeman to the ground as players from both sides piled in to separate them; the referee produced a yellow card for the goalkeeper once order was restored. Bottles were then thrown from the crowd in Turgeman's direction as he made his way back for the restart.

Explaining his reaction afterward, Breza offered an answer that sidestepped the abuse Turgeman had faced all night: "I wanted the fans to get more into the game. I wanted to push the crowd, so the crowd would push us," he was quoted as saying by Sport1.

The match itself swung dramatically after the break. New England had led 2-0 at the interval through Turgeman and a Carles Gil goal, only for Montréal to claw back through Brayan Vera and a Prince Owusu equaliser in the 59th minute, leaving the game level at 2-2 — a result that stretched Montréal's winless run in MLS to six matches, per ESPN and TSN.

For Turgeman, the goal continued a red-hot run since his move to MLS. The 22-year-old joined New England Revolution from Maccabi Tel Aviv last August for a reported $6 million fee and scored in each of his first three league appearances, a Revolution club record. Saturday's strike extended his recent scoring form to back-to-back matches.

The confrontation is the latest instance of an Israeli athlete facing hostility from opposing fans in North America and Europe since the war in Gaza began, with chants and gestures aimed squarely at nationality rather than football. Turgeman's response — refusing to back down and celebrating directly in front of his abusers — has already drawn wide attention on Israeli sports media.
MLS and CF Montréal had not issued a formal statement on the chanting or the confrontation at the time of writing.

title: Beitar Jerusalem brace for a flood of 4,000 fans as Austria Wien tie looms in Romania
dek: Sport5 reports demand for Thursday's Conference League qualifier in Ploiești has outstripped anything seen so far this European run, with the club lobbying airlines for extra capacity.

verificationSources.label: Ynet: Beitar warn fans ahead of Romania trip
FK Austria Wien: travel offer for the away trip in Romania

body: Beitar Jerusalem are used to travelling well in Europe, but even by their own standards the numbers heading to Romania this week are startling. Sport5 reports that roughly 4,000 Beitar supporters are expected in Ploiești for Thursday's Conference League third qualifying round first leg against Austria Wien — a scale of travelling support the club says is unmatched so far in this European campaign.

As in the previous round against AEK Larnaca, Beitar are staging their "home" leg in Romania rather than Israel, with Ploiești hosting the fixture before the tie shifts to Vienna for the return on August 13. The arrangement has become familiar to the club's fans, who have now made the trip east in growing numbers at each stage of the qualifying run.

Demand has been so heavy that Beitar have approached airlines directly to request additional flight capacity on routes to Romania, according to Sport5, as supporters scramble for seats to follow the team. Under UEFA regulations, Austria Wien's own following in Ploiești will be capped at just 750 tickets — an allocation Beitar expect to receive in return when they travel to Vienna for the second leg.

On the pitch, head coach Almog Cohen has been pressing his players to raise their level after scraping past AEK Larnaca on penalties in the previous round. Cohen, who took over in May after Barak Yitzhaki's departure, has told the squad they need to work harder and play with more composure if they are to see off an Austria Wien side with plenty of continental pedigree of its own.

Pitch conditions have also been a talking point in the build-up. After players complained the grass in Ploiești ran too fast and made the ball difficult to control during the Larnaca tie, Beitar have asked the venue's groundskeeper to trim it further, within the limits UEFA permits.

There was a squad boost of sorts with defenders Luka Gadrani and Tomer Yosephi both back in the frame, though neither is considered fully match-fit. Sport5 reports the more realistic expectation is that both will be in contention for minutes in the second leg in Vienna rather than Thursday's opener.
Midfielder Yarden Shua, who has been troubled by a virus, reported feeling better over the weekend, and the club is hopeful he has shaken it off in time to contribute to the tie.

Forward Sean Weissman, who joined Beitar this summer after several seasons in Austria most recently with Blau-Weiss Linz, has been passing on what he knows of Austria Wien and the atmosphere Beitar are likely to face when the tie returns to Vienna next week.

For a club whose away support has become one of the storylines of its European run, the numbers converging on Ploiești this week say as much about the mood around Beitar as anything happening on the training pitch.
