title: Winner odds make Hapoel Jerusalem and Maccabi Netanya favourites for Toto Cup round three
dek: The Israeli bookmaker rates both newly promoted Maccabi Petach Tikva and Hapoel Ramat Gan as underdogs as round three of the Toto Cup group stage is played on Sunday evening.

verificationSources.label: ONE: "ב'ווינר' קבעו: הפייבוריטיות למשחקי גביע הטוטו"

body: Israeli bookmaker Winner has put its numbers on Sunday evening's third round of the Toto Cup group stage, and the market leaves little doubt about who it expects to come out on top in both fixtures.

Hapoel Jerusalem are priced at 2.15 to beat Maccabi Petach Tikva, with the draw offered at 2.95 and a Petach Tikva win paying 2.70, according to the odds published by ONE. It is a tight enough spread to suggest bookmakers see a competitive match rather than a mismatch, even with Jerusalem the nominal favourites.

The gap is far wider in the evening's other fixture. Maccabi Netanya are rated a heavy 1.45 to see off Hapoel Ramat Gan at home, with the draw at 3.70 and an away win priced all the way out at 4.65 — among the more lopsided prices of the round so far.

The odds reflect where the four clubs currently sit in Israeli football's pecking order. Both Maccabi Petach Tikva and Hapoel Ramat Gan arrive in Ligat Ha'al as this season's promoted sides, having finished first and second respectively in the 2025-26 Liga Leumit, with Petach Tikva crowned champions of the second tier.

That promotion has made them the divisions's new boys for the Toto Cup's group phase, a pre-season tournament in which clubs are drawn into regional pools before the top finishers advance to a knockout quarter-final stage. title: Niv Eliasi closes in on move to Greek side Levadiakos
dek: Hapoel Be'er Sheva's goalkeeper is set to leave the newly crowned Israeli champions on loan for the Greek Super League after losing his starting spot in the title run-in, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE: "בדרך לליגה היוונית: ניב אליאסי מתקרב ללבדיאקוס"

Sport1/Maariv: "אחרי ששיפרה את ההצעה: ניב אליאסי בדרך לקבוצה חדשה"

body: Niv Eliasi, until recently billed as Hapoel Be'er Sheva's goalkeeper of the future, is closing in on a move to Greece, with ONE reporting that the 24-year-old has all but agreed to sign for Super League side Levadiakos.

According to the report, the move is being structured as a loan with a purchase option, and Eliasi was expected to fly out to finalise the paperwork within days after already visiting the club and the city to weigh up the switch.

ONE reports his new salary in Greece will be around €300,000 gross per season - a rise on what he currently earns in Be'er Sheva - and that Levadiakos hold an option to sign him outright, with a further clause allowing the Greek club to cash in should a bigger domestic rival come calling for him.

Levadiakos, who play in the Boeotia region north of Athens, finished fifth in the Greek Super League last season and have pursued Eliasi's signature for much of the summer, according to Hebrew reports.

The move caps a rapid fall down the pecking order for Eliasi, who started most of last season as Hapoel Be'er Sheva's first-choice goalkeeper before head coach Ran Kozuk turned to Ofir Marciano for the run-in, a switch that helped steer the club to the Israeli championship in May.

He was not part of the squad registered for Hapoel Be'er Sheva's Champions League qualifying tie against Red Star Belgrade, with Jonathan Shani deputising between the posts instead - another sign, ONE noted, that his departure is close.

As Israel's champions, Hapoel Be'er Sheva have already eliminated Vikingur Reykjavik to reach the third qualifying round, where Red Star Belgrade await, and are guaranteed at least a place in this season's Conference League group stage regardless of that tie's outcome.

Eliasi signed a five-year contract with Hapoel Be'er Sheva in 2021 and has previously spent time on loan at Hapoel Ramat HaSharon. He was also part of Israel's squad at the 2024 Paris Olympics, underlining the goalkeeping pedigree that first attracted Greek interest this summer.

title: Grenade hits Japanika branch owned by Beitar Jerusalem's Barak Abramov in Hadera
dek: The under-construction sushi outlet is the latest target in a weeks-long wave of grenade, gun and arson attacks on the chain owned by the Beitar Jerusalem boss, amid a feud between rival crime families.

verificationSources.label: Sport5: "לאחר מס' שבועות: סניף ג'פניקה נוסף הותקף"
Times of Israel liveblog: grenade tossed at Japanika in Hadera

Ynet: Abramov — "the violent events at Japanika will not affect Beitar"

body: A hand grenade was thrown early on Sunday morning at a Japanika branch still under construction in Hadera, Sport5 reported, the latest strike in a weeks-long wave of attacks on the sushi chain owned by Beitar Jerusalem's owner, Barak Abramov.

No one was hurt. The grenade hit the commercial section of a new residential development, where the Japanika outlet had not yet opened, causing damage to the site rather than to any person, according to the report. Police were called to the scene and cordoned off the area to investigate.

It is far from an isolated incident. Japanika branches around the country have been hit by grenades, gunfire and arson attempts over recent weeks, with locations in Afula, Netanya, Kiryat Ono, Ramat Gan, Givatayim, Herzliya and Rosh Pina all targeted, according to Hebrew media reporting from Ynet, Walla and Kan.

Abramov built Japanika into a nationwide chain of more than 40 branches through his Landora Group, before buying Beitar Jerusalem — the club he has supported since childhood — from Moshe Chogeg in 2022, taking on roughly 60 million shekels of accumulated debt in the process.

Police suspect the attacks are fallout from a feud between the Mosli and Jarushi crime organisations. Investigators believe Abramov, who first grew close to members of the Mosli family after buying Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv in 2016, shifted his allegiance toward the Jarushi side for protection following an armed robbery at his home in 2023 — a move detectives think was seen as a betrayal by the Mosli camp and made his restaurant chain a proxy target.

Abramov has given testimony to police as part of the investigation. He has previously told Ynet that the violence engulfing his restaurant business would not spill over into Beitar Jerusalem, insisting the club's football operations remain separate from his commercial troubles.

Beitar itself has not been directly targeted in the wave of attacks and opened its 2026/27 season this month with no reported change to security arrangements at Teddy Stadium. Still, the escalating campaign against its owner's other business interests continues to hang over the club just as the new campaign gets under way.

Police said the Hadera case remains under investigation, with detectives examining whether it is linked to the broader dispute. No arrests had been announced in connection with Sunday's incident specifically.

title: Without Kangwa, Hapoel Beer Sheva weigh their options for Red Star test
dek: Aliel Peretz is the leading candidate to fill the void left by Kings Kangwa's sale to Panathinaikos as Beer Sheva prepare for their Champions League qualifier in Hungary.

verificationSources.label: ice.co.il on the Kangwa sale fee
Walla Sport on the Kangwa-Panathinaikos deal

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva head into Tuesday's Champions League third qualifying round first leg against Red Star Belgrade with a gap to fill up front, after talisman Kings Kangwa completed his move away from the club just days before the tie.

The Zambian winger, who returned to Beer Sheva for a second spell after stints at Red Star and Kortrijk, has signed for Panathinaikos in a deal reported by Israeli outlets to be worth around €3.8m, potentially rising to €4.5m with bonuses — a fee that could stand as the biggest sale in the club's history.

According to Sport5, Aliel Peretz is the leading candidate to step into Kangwa's role in the side that owner Alona Barkat's club will send out for the trip to Hungary, where the tie's first leg is being staged.

Itay Rotman, who impressed after coming off the bench in the second-round win over Vikingur Reykjavik, is also in contention to start, while Zehai Ahmad and Amir Ganach are both said to be in the mix for a recall to the lineup.

The squad picture is complicated further by absences elsewhere. Victor João remains out through injury, and defender Ayalon Almog — who has yet to return to full training — is expected to leave the club before the transfer window closes.
Winger Niv Eliassi is also on his way out, with Sport5 reporting he was set to finalise a move to Greek club Levadiakos on the day of the report.

On the incoming side, new signing Pedro Amador is expected to travel with the squad and could see minutes in Hungary. The Portuguese left-back joined from Atlanta United on a four-year contract in a transfer confirmed by the MLS club in late July.

Beer Sheva reached this stage of qualifying by beating Vikingur Reykjavik 2-0 in the second leg for a 3-2 aggregate win, while Red Star advanced with a 5-0 aggregate rout of Larne. Around 200 Israeli supporters are expected to make the trip to Hungary for the first leg, with a larger away following anticipated for the return fixture in Belgrade a week later.

For coach Ran Kozuk, the timing is awkward: reshaping his attack for one of the biggest European nights in the club's recent history, days after losing his most influential attacking player to a marquee sale.

title: Konin and Mazor climb to eighth in duet free final at European artistic swimming championships
dek: The Israeli pair improved through every round in Paris, edging out Britain, Switzerland and Georgia in the sport's showcase event.
body: Katy Konin and Aya Mazor finished eighth in the free duet final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris on Saturday, capping an improved showing from Israel's artistic swimming duo at the continent's showcase event.

Scoring 248.8000 points at the Olympic Aquatics Centre in Saint-Denis, the pair climbed from 11th place in the preliminaries. Sport5 reports their artistic impression mark rose by almost five points between the two performances, alongside a cleaner execution and greater difficulty in the routine.
The final tally was enough to finish ahead of duets from Britain, Switzerland and Georgia, with Belarus placed just behind them in ninth, according to the report.

Eighth is a modest placing by medal standards, but for a program that has spent recent years chasing parity with Europe's traditional powers, jumping three spots between prelims and final says as much about the trajectory as the ranking itself.

Mazor is one of the more established names in Israel's current artistic swimming generation. She competed in the mixed duet technical alongside Yogev Dagan at last year's World Aquatics Championships, experience that showed in the composure of the Paris routine.

The championships mark the first time the European Aquatics Championships have been held in France since Strasbourg in 1987, staged at the same Saint-Denis venue that hosted artistic swimming at the 2024 Olympics.

Konin and Mazor's work in Paris is not finished. Israel's team was scheduled to compete in the free group routine preliminaries the day after the duet final, giving the delegation another chance to add to its tally before the championships close out later in the week.

title: Baribo scores again as DC United draw 2-2 with Nashville SC
dek: The Israeli forward's late equaliser extended his hot streak, Idan Toklomati set up Charlotte FC's opener in a loss to Chicago Fire, and Or Blorian started for Sporting Kansas City in a busy MLS weekend for Israelis abroad.
body: Tai Baribo keeps finding the net. The Israeli forward pulled DC United level with a 77th-minute finish from the left side of the box, capping a second-half fightback that earned his side a 2-2 draw against East Division leaders Nashville SC on Saturday.

DC United had trailed 2-0 before Baribo's intervention, set up by a pass from Louis Munteanu. He played the full 90 minutes and picked up a yellow card along the way. According to ONE, it was his third goal in as many outings since MLS returned from its break for the World Cup.

Baribo, capped 23 times for Israel, arrived at DC United earlier this year in a cash trade from the Philadelphia Union, where he had established himself as an MLS All-Star and a two-time Player of the Month. He came through the Maccabi Petah Tikva academy before moving to Austria's Wolfsberger AC and then MLS.

There was Israeli involvement further up the East table too. At Soldier Field, Idan Toklomati combined with Pep Biel for the opening goal as Charlotte FC took an early lead against Chicago Fire, the two forwards trading passes in an 18th-minute give-and-go that Biel finished into the top corner.

It was not enough. Robert Lewandowski, playing at home for Chicago Fire for the first time, scored twice to complete a 2-1 comeback win and end Charlotte's four-match unbeaten run. Toklomati was withdrawn in the 86th minute, while fellow Israeli international Liel Abada, also in Charlotte's XI, was substituted in the 77th.

Toklomati, 21, is a product of the same Maccabi Petah Tikva pipeline as Baribo. He joined Charlotte in 2024, has four senior caps for Israel, and was named to the MLS Team of the Matchday last September after scoring his first career hat-trick.

Out west, Or Blorian played all 90 minutes at centre-back as Sporting Kansas City fell 2-0 at home to Houston Dynamo, with Adalberto Bouzat scoring the decisive goal in the 71st minute. It was a fourth straight defeat for Blorian's new club since he arrived on a pre-contract in June.
Blorian joined Sporting KC after leading Hapoel Be'er Sheva to an Israeli Premier League and Super Cup double last season, and has since been called into the Israel national team setup.

Between them, the trio's weekend summed up the growing Israeli presence across MLS this season — a goal, an assist and a full 90 minutes at the back, spread across three different time zones on the same Saturday night.

title: Hapoel Haifa 2-1 Bnei Sakhnin: Avuxis says he won't let Gomes' red card slide
dek: A stoppage-time bicycle-kick winner from teenage substitute Muataz Hamed sank Bnei Sakhnin in the Toto Cup, but coach Yosef Avuxis' post-match focus was on Saná Gomes' second-half dismissal.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Hapoel Haifa's third straight win

body: Yosef Avuxis was in no mood to let it slide. Hours after Bnei Sakhnin's stoppage-time collapse against Hapoel Haifa, the Sakhnin coach made clear that Saná Gomes' second-half sending off would not simply be filed away as one of those things.

Sakhnin lost 2-1 in a Toto Cup third-round tie at Doha Stadium on Saturday that swung wildly in the closing minutes. Alon Turjeman had put Haifa ahead in the 35th minute — his fourth goal in three matches — before Mathew Cudjoe levelled for the hosts in the 90th+5th minute with a fine strike off the underside of the crossbar. Two minutes later, 18-year-old substitute Muataz Hamed, on the pitch for barely ten minutes, scored his first senior goal with an overhead kick to snatch the win for Haifa.

Gomes had already left the pitch by then. The Bissau-Guinean left-back, who joined Sakhnin from Haifa this summer, was shown a second yellow card in the 82nd minute and sent off — visibly wound up throughout a match against the club he had just left, according to ONE's report.

"I'm aware that sometimes it 'escapes' Gomes, and I intend to address this — we'll talk to him," Avuxis said. "This is his first mistake with us. We'll speak with him, because next time it happens it will already be something different."

It was not an isolated incident for the 27-year-old. Gomes ran into repeated disciplinary trouble last season while at Hapoel Haifa, with a history of losing his composure and picking up red cards — the pattern Avuxis is now looking to break early in their working relationship.

Haifa were also reduced to ten men, with Dario Žoparić dismissed for a second yellow in the 73rd minute, so for the final quarter of an hour both sides were playing a man short. It made Hamed's late intervention, arriving off the bench, all the more striking.

Avuxis was more upbeat about the performance itself than the result. "The second half was exceptional, and that gives me confidence going forward, especially with several players unavailable," he said. "Of course it's disappointing to concede that goal at the end, but we need to learn from it — and it's better this happens in the Toto Cup than in the league."
The defeat was Haifa's third straight win of the preseason cup campaign, continuing an impressive run under their current setup as they build momentum before the Israeli Premier League gets underway.

Off the pitch, Sakhnin's business continues. Newly signed defender Dimitri Cabrera, the Guadeloupe international who arrived after 24 appearances for Auxerre last season, is set to begin training with his new club. Sakhnin are also still pursuing striker William Agada — a target, ONE reports, that Hapoel Haifa are chasing as well.

title: Ronaldo reportedly set to marry Georgina Rodríguez next week in his birthplace
dek: The Israeli outlet ONE, citing The Sun, reports the couple will wed at Funchal Cathedral in Madeira and celebrate at the Savoy Palace hotel — though no date has been confirmed by Ronaldo or Rodríguez themselves.

verificationSources.label: ONE: "Where he was born: Ronaldo expected to marry next week"

body: Cristiano Ronaldo is expected to marry his long-time partner Georgina Rodríguez next week, in the Portuguese island city where he was born, the Israeli outlet ONE reported on Sunday, citing the British tabloid The Sun.

According to the report, the ceremony is planned for the cathedral in Funchal, Madeira, with the reception to follow at the nearby Savoy Palace, a luxury hotel on the island. The Sun reported that hotel guests were told two floors and the bar areas would be closed off on Friday and Saturday, fuelling speculation that the closures are tied to the wedding.

Ronaldo, 41, and Rodríguez, 32, have been together since 2016 and have built a blended family that includes children from a previous surrogacy arrangement as well as two daughters of their own. The couple got engaged last August, and Ronaldo has spoken publicly in the months since about wanting to settle down with her.

"I hope to arrive at my wedding with the World Cup," Ronaldo said earlier this year in an interview with Piers Morgan, referring to next summer's tournament in North America — while also describing Rodríguez as the only woman he wanted to build a family and grow old with.

Funchal Cathedral, a late-Gothic church dating to 1514, sits close to the hospital where Ronaldo was born in 1985, giving the reported choice of venue a symbolic pull back to his roots on Madeira. Reports of the couple planning to marry there, with the Savoy Palace hosting the celebration, first surfaced late last year.

The timing has been harder to pin down. Ronaldo and Rodríguez were photographed on a yacht off Majorca last week wearing matching diamond rings, which only intensified wedding chatter, but the couple has not confirmed a date publicly.

A separate rumour that swept Portuguese media this week — claiming the pair would marry on August 1st at the Quinta da Regaleira estate in Sintra, based on what was said to be a leaked invitation — was knocked down by the celebrity magazine ¡HOLA!, which found the venue was open to tourists and hosting an evening show on the supposed wedding date.

That debunked claim referred to a different venue entirely from the Funchal plan cited by ONE and The Sun, but it underlines how much speculation is swirling around the couple as Ronaldo's summer break winds down and his return to pre-season training with Al-Nassr approaches.

Nothing here has been confirmed by Ronaldo, Rodríguez or their representatives, and the exact date remains unofficial. ONE's report should be read as the latest tabloid account of the wedding planning rather than a confirmed announcement.

title: Barcelona and Real Madrid weigh moves for Athletic Bilbao's Aymeric Laporte
dek: Athletic Club insist their World Cup-winning centre-back is not for sale below €80m, even as both Spanish giants monitor his situation.

verificationSources.label: Goal.com — Bilbao shock Barcelona with Laporte's price

body: Barcelona and Real Madrid have both been credited with interest in Aymeric Laporte this summer, but Athletic Bilbao's message hasn't wavered: their World Cup-winning centre-back is going nowhere cheaply. ONE reports that the Basque club has told the two Spanish giants they will need roughly €80 million to prise him away.

It is a striking number given that Laporte only returned to Bilbao a year ago. The 32-year-old, a product of the club's academy, came back from Al-Nassr in 2025 on a deal running through June 2028, having left for Manchester City back in 2018.

His timing was vindicated in style. Laporte was a fixture in Spain's run to the 2026 World Cup title, forming a defensive partnership with Barcelona's own Pau Cubarsí that helped La Roja concede almost nothing across the tournament.

That form is exactly why Barcelona came calling. Sporting director Deco watched several of Spain's matches in the United States during the World Cup and was reportedly struck by what he saw, with the club said to be planning direct talks with Laporte's representatives about a move.

Early reporting suggested Barcelona might get him relatively cheaply, with some outlets floating a release clause as low as €12-15 million. Athletic Club moved quickly to shut that down, insisting the real release figure sits at roughly €80 million — a number designed, in effect, to end the conversation.

Real Madrid have also been linked, but the noise around that interest has since cooled. Reports in Spain suggest Los Blancos weighed a move before deciding against it, put off by both Laporte's age and the scale of Bilbao's asking price.

For Athletic, the stance reflects how much the club values a player who chose to come home rather than stay in Saudi Arabia, and who has since become one of the most reliable centre-backs in La Liga and a World Cup winner to boot. Officially, he remains not for sale.

With most of Europe's major leagues still to resume for 2026-27, stories like this one will keep circulating through August — but for now, any deal for Laporte would require one of Spanish football's two superpowers to meet a price Bilbao clearly doesn't expect them to pay.

title: Former Israel cycling team rider Noa Boruchovich dies at 30

The site, which covers running, cycling, triathlon and swimming, said she passed away at her home; no cause of death has been disclosed.

Boruchovich was one of the country's most accomplished road cyclists over the past decade, according to the report, winning Israeli titles across multiple age categories and representing the national team in competitions abroad.
She was crowned Israel's junior national champion in 2014, Shvoong said, and later added the national title in the women's under-23 elite category as she progressed through the sport.
Before settling on cycling, she had also competed as a swimmer in her youth, the outlet reported, before turning to two wheels and establishing herself among Israel's leading riders.

After stepping back from competitive racing, Boruchovich joined the Israel Police and worked as an investigator, according to the report — a second career in public service that followed her years in elite sport.

She was due to be laid to rest on Friday at the military cemetery in Modiin, Shvoong said, with tributes to her circulating among current and former national-team riders and coaches on social media in the days since her death was announced.

Israel's competitive cycling scene is small and close-knit, and news of Boruchovich's death has been felt widely across it. No separate statement from the Israel Cycling Federation had surfaced at the time of writing.

title: CF Montréal 2-2 New England Revolution: Turgeman targeted by bottles and 'death to Israel' chants
dek: Sport5 reports ugly scenes at Stade Saputo after the Israeli forward's goal celebration, with bottles thrown from the stands and goalkeeper Sebastian Breza's shove on Turgeman drawing only a yellow card.
body: Dor Turgeman's equalizer for New England Revolution at CF Montréal on Saturday night should have been the highlight of his week. Instead, the Israeli forward's goal celebration touched off ugly scenes at Stade Saputo that are still being argued over long after the final whistle.

New England trailed twice in Montreal before Turgeman's finish made it 2-2, and rather than wheel away toward his own bench, he ran to plant himself in front of the home end. Bottles were thrown down at him from the stands, according to Sport5's report on the match.

The confrontation escalated when CF Montréal goalkeeper Sebastian Breza went after Turgeman and shoved him, drawing a roar of approval from the Montreal crowd behind his goal. The referee's response was a yellow card, nothing more, for a physical reaction Sport5 said many home supporters felt was fully justified.

According to Sport5, the abuse aimed at Turgeman went beyond the shove. The outlet cited reporter Caleb Fungres as saying fans near the visitors' section could be heard directing hostile chants at the Israeli international through the match, including the phrase "death to Israel," alongside other insults.
English-language soccer commentator Ross Goldman was quoted condemning the scenes outright: "What happened tonight in Montreal ... is racism and has no place anywhere."

Sport5 described the fallout since as a genuine mess, with online reaction split rather than uniformly sympathetic to Turgeman. Much of the criticism online, the outlet reported, has been directed at the player's provocative celebration rather than at the fans who threw objects and chanted at him, with Montreal's supporters drawing the greater share of public backing.

Turgeman, 22 and born in Ashdod, joined New England from Maccabi Tel Aviv last year through the MLS U22 Initiative and has become a regular fixture in the Revolution's attack. He has also become a fixture for Israel, collecting caps for the senior national team and scoring in November's World Cup qualifier against Moldova.

The draw itself was rescued for Montreal by a late strike from Brayan Vera, according to La Presse's coverage of the match, meaning both sides walked away with a point from a night that will be remembered far more for what happened in the stands than for anything in the 2-2 scoreline.

Neither CF Montréal nor MLS had issued a formal statement on the chants or the confrontation as of publication, and Sport5's account of the specific abuse directed at Turgeman has not yet been independently corroborated by Canadian outlets covering the match.

title: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew: Messi returns, but Casemiro own goal mars home debut
dek: Luis Suárez and Noah Allen goals were not enough for Inter Miami as new signing Casemiro turned into his own net on his home debut and Columbus's Brais Méndez struck a late equaliser.

verificationSources.label: Inter Miami CF official match recap

body: Lionel Messi's first appearance for Inter Miami since Argentina's World Cup triumph ended without the fairytale finish, as his club were held to a 2-2 draw at home by Columbus Crew on Saturday night — a result remembered as much for a costly error from one of Miami's own new arrivals as for the captain's comeback.

The biggest storyline belonged to Casemiro. The Brazilian midfielder, one of Inter Miami's marquee summer signings, was making his home debut when he turned a clearance into his own net in the 34th minute. It was his first own goal at club level since 2011, when he was still coming through at São Paulo, and it dragged Columbus level just as Miami looked to be cruising.

Miami had led through a moment of real quality. Luis Suárez chipped in a long-range strike in the 16th minute to open the scoring, his 10th league goal of the season — a return that makes him only the fifth player in MLS history to record 10-plus goals and five-plus assists in each of his first three seasons in the league.

Noah Allen restored Miami's advantage right at the end of the first half, heading home from a Suárez assist in stoppage time to make it 2-1 at the break. It looked for a while like it might be enough to hold off a Columbus side missing several regulars on international duty of its own.

Messi and Rodrigo De Paul, both back in South Florida after Argentina's World Cup campaign, were named among the substitutes rather than starting. Messi came on in the 53rd minute to a rousing reception at Chase Stadium but could not add the goal that would have completed the story, going close but failing to beat David Ochoa in the Columbus goal.

Columbus would not be denied an equaliser of their own. Brais Méndez, the Spanish playmaker signed from Real Sociedad for a club-record fee just weeks earlier, curled home a free kick in the 84th minute to make it 2-2 and snatch a point on the road — his first goal since arriving in MLS.

The draw stretched Inter Miami's unbeaten run to seven matches, a stat the club will take some comfort from even as questions linger over Casemiro's settling-in period following his high-profile move. The team is currently being run on an interim basis by sporting director Guillermo Hoyos, who took charge after Javier Mascherano's resignation earlier this year.

Attention now turns quickly to continental competition: Inter Miami host Atlético de San Luis on Wednesday in the opening phase of the 2026 Leagues Cup, with Messi expected to push for a full return to the starting lineup.

title: Ex-Manchester City winger Jayden Braaf lands in Israel for Hapoel Haifa trial
dek: The free-agent Dutch forward, capped at youth level by the Netherlands, arrived on Sunday evening to train with the Toto Cup pace-setters, but coach Haim Silbas is wary of his disciplinary history.
body: Jayden Braaf, the Dutch winger who came through Manchester City's academy without ever making a first-team appearance, arrived in Israel on Sunday evening to train with Hapoel Haifa, ONE reported, as the club weighs whether to hand the 23-year-old a contract.

Braaf has been without a club since his contract at Serie A side Hellas Verona was terminated by mutual consent in September 2025. He spent last season out on loan at Salernitana and has previously turned out for Udinese, Borussia Dortmund's reserve side and Fortuna Sittard, without ever cementing a regular starting role at senior level.

The Amsterdam-born forward, who also came through Ajax and PSV Eindhoven's youth ranks before City signed him, was capped by the Netherlands at under-15, under-17 and under-18 level and was part of the Dutch squad that won the UEFA European Under-17 Championship in 2019. He was also named Manchester City's EDS Players' Player of the Year for 2019-20.

The trial comes at an encouraging moment for Hapoel Haifa, who have won all three of their group games in the Toto Cup, the season-opening domestic competition, including a 3-2 derby victory over city rivals Maccabi Haifa and a 3-1 win over Ironi Tiberias, results that have them well placed heading into the semi-final stage.

But head coach Haim Silbas, who returned to the club for a second spell this year, made clear a trial is exactly that. "We're searching for players who make a difference," he said, according to ONE. "If he fits in all aspects, disciplinary and physical, then he'll stay here."

ONE noted that Braaf carries a mixed reputation, with disciplinary issues and injury setbacks having disrupted his career in Europe — factors Silbas is said to view as a genuine risk alongside the player's obvious technical ability.

No agreement has been reached, and ONE's report makes clear this is only an audition. Hapoel Haifa are expected to assess Braaf over training sessions in the coming days before deciding whether to pursue a permanent deal.

title: Tear gas grenade thrown at Hadera site of Beitar Jerusalem owner's restaurant chain
dek: Police opened an investigation after a smoke grenade was hurled at a Japanika branch under construction in Hadera, the latest in a string of attacks on the sushi chain owned by Beitar Jerusalem chairman Barak Abramov.
body: A tear gas grenade was thrown overnight at a Japanika restaurant site under construction in Hadera, ONE reports, the latest in a monthslong wave of attacks on the sushi chain owned by Beitar Jerusalem chairman Barak Abramov.

According to the report, no one was hurt in the incident. Hadera police officers and a bomb disposal unit were called to the scene, and the force said in a statement that its personnel "began investigative procedures and evidence collection" to establish the background and circumstances.
Abramov, through his representatives, again denied any wrongdoing in connection with the attacks, ONE reports, maintaining his complete innocence in the affair.

The Hadera incident follows a string of grenade and pipe-bomb attacks on Japanika branches across the country over the past month, hitting outlets in locations including Rosh Pina, Kiryat Ono, Netanya, Givatayim, Ramat Gan and Afula, according to Israeli media reporting on the campaign.

Police have linked the wave to an escalating turf war between the Jarushi and Musli organized crime families, with investigators saying Abramov is perceived by one side as aligned with a rival network — a characterization he has publicly rejected, telling investigators he does not understand where the accusations against him originate.

Abramov, 46, built the Japanika chain from a single franchise into one of Israel's largest sushi-restaurant networks before folding his hospitality holdings into the Andorra Investments group. He took over as Beitar Jerusalem's owner and chairman in 2022, ending years of turbulent ownership changes at the storied Jerusalem club, and previously owned Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv, whom he led to two State Cup titles.

The repeated targeting of his business empire has become an unwelcome sideshow to his stewardship of Beitar, a club that has itself endured a turbulent run of owners in the past decade. Police have said they are treating the broader campaign as a serious and potentially dangerous escalation between rival crime organizations rather than an isolated dispute.
No arrests were reported in connection with the Hadera attack as of Sunday, and police said the investigation into the incident remains open.

title: Bruno Guimarães set for Arsenal medical on Monday in £80m Newcastle deal

body: Bruno Guimarães is set to undergo a medical at Arsenal's London Colney training base on Monday, the final procedural step in a transfer that has been building for weeks, ONE reports.

According to the report, Arsenal have agreed a package worth close to £80 million to prise the Brazil international away from Newcastle United, structured as an initial fee of around £70m with a further £10m in add-ons.
The 28-year-old, who captains Newcastle, is set to sign a five-year contract once the medical is cleared, with an official announcement expected early in the week.

ONE notes that manager Mikel Arteta has pursued the midfielder for a long time, with Arsenal having seen earlier approaches for Guimarães turned down before finally striking an agreement with Newcastle this summer.
Guimarães himself pushed hard for the move, according to the report, even delaying his arrival at Newcastle's pre-season training camp in Spain so as not to jeopardise the negotiations.
Personal terms were already in place well before the medical was scheduled, leaving Arsenal needing only to finalise the fee with Newcastle to get the deal over the line.

Arteta reportedly views Guimarães as the answer to Arsenal's long search for a commanding presence in central midfield, valuing the leadership, quality and physical power he has shown in four seasons in the Premier League.

If completed as expected, it would rank among the marquee departures from Newcastle since the club's Saudi-backed takeover, and a statement signing for an Arsenal side already sitting as reigning champions.

title: Baribo salvages DC United's 2-2 draw, Turgeman strikes in Montreal, Toklomati sets up Charlotte in 2-1 loss to Chicago
dek: Three Israelis were involved across MLS's Saturday slate: Tai Baribo's late leveller rescued a point from 2-0 down, Dor Turgeman struck again in a wild draw at Montreal, and Idan Toklomati teed up Charlotte's opener before Robert Lewandowski's double sank them in Chicago.
body: Three Israeli forwards were all over MLS scoresheets on the same night, with Tai Baribo and Dor Turgeman both scoring and Idan Toklomati laying on a goal, as ONE reported from Saturday's slate of matches in the United States.

Baribo did the most dramatic work. DC United trailed Nashville SC 2-0 at Audi Field after Sam Surridge converted a penalty and a follow-up from Mohammed, set up by Hany Mukhtar, doubled the visitors' lead. Silvan Hefti pulled one back before Baribo levelled it at 2-2 in the 77th minute, finishing off an assist from Louis Munteanu to rescue a point for the hosts.

It continued a rich run for the 28-year-old, who has scored in three straight matches since MLS returned from its break for the World Cup, according to ONE. Baribo, born in Eilat, arrived at DC United in December 2025 in a $4 million trade from Philadelphia Union, where he had been the Supporters' Shield winners' top scorer, and signed a five-year Designated Player contract through 2029-30.

Turgeman was on target in a different kind of thriller in Montreal. New England Revolution raced into a 2-0 lead at Stade Saputo through Carles Gil and the Israeli forward, who struck in the 36th minute, only for CF Montréal to fight back through Brayan Vera and Prince Owusu in the second half to salvage a 2-2 draw. Turgeman was substituted in the 73rd minute.

It was another productive outing for the 24-year-old, who joined New England via the MLS U22 Initiative last September after 145 professional appearances between Maccabi Tel Aviv and Beitar in Israel, and who has continued to find the net regularly since his move.

In Chicago, Toklomati played provider rather than scorer. He combined with Pep Biel for Charlotte FC's opener at Soldier Field, the pair working a give-and-go before Biel finished into the top corner in the first half — but the visitors couldn't hold on. Robert Lewandowski, making his home debut for Chicago Fire following his move to MLS, equalised soon after and struck again in the 68th minute for the winner as Chicago won 2-1.
Toklomati, 21, has been Charlotte's leading scorer this season and is a regular in Marco Silva's — sorry, Charlotte's — matchday XI alongside his Israel national team commitments.

Taken together, the weekend underlined how deep the Israeli presence in MLS now runs, with three different players featuring prominently for three different clubs on the same night — a draw salvaged, a draw shared, and an assist in defeat, but goal involvement across the board.

title: Levi keeps Maccabi Netanya's strong lineup for Ramat Gan test, sets up Haziza's debut
dek: Netanya can reach the Toto Cup semi-finals tonight, and new signing Dolev Haziza looks set for his first minutes since arriving from Maccabi Haifa.
body: Maccabi Netanya host Hapoel Ramat Gan at Netanya Stadium this evening in the quarter-finals of the Toto Cup, and manager Roni Levi is set to name another strong side as his team chase a place in the semi-finals, ONE reports.

The headline note in Levi's team news is the possible first appearance of Dolev Haziza. The attacking midfielder signed a two-year contract with Netanya last month after seven years at Maccabi Haifa, where he served as club captain and won three championships, and according to ONE he is expected to be introduced from the bench, most likely in the closing quarter of the match.

Haziza's move was one of the more notable Israeli transfers of the summer. Walla Sport reported he arrives to "bring experience and quality," and Sport5 has reported his salary at around $250,000 a season.

Levi will have to solve his attacking puzzle without Christian Nwatshako. The Nigerian winger will not arrive in time for the match, ONE reports, leaving the manager to find an alternative option in the final third.
One beneficiary looks set to be Maor Levi, who is in line to return to the starting eleven after catching the eye in Netanya's recent Toto Cup win over Maccabi Petah Tikva, according to ONE.

In defense, Alon Azogui, Grigory Morozov and Bakari Konata are all expected to start. Bassem Za'arura is unavailable, with Nadav Nidam coming in for him. In goal, Levi looks set to stick with Beni Feldman, whose recent form has satisfied the manager, ONE adds.
Based on ONE's reporting, Netanya's likely matchday group includes Samuel Silva, Azogui, Konata, Feldman, Morozov, Omri Shamir, Nidam, Maor Levi, Oz Bilu, Alex Talpa and Matheus Dabo.

Off the pitch, Netanya asked the league to hold a minute's silence before kick-off in memory of Eli Shgav, the club's former owner, who died a day earlier, ONE reports. Shgav bought Netanya ahead of the 2013/14 season, led the club to promotion in his first year in charge and stepped away from ownership in November 2014.

A win would be a significant step toward the Toto Cup semi-finals for Netanya, who reached this knockout round in good form; Israel Hayom reported the club had already beaten Hapoel Jerusalem 3-1 during the group phase of the competition.

title: Novakovich's rotten luck, Muhammad hurt again as Kenny Saief returns to full training at Maccabi Haifa
dek: The new American-Serbian forward is still laid low by a virus, winger Ali Mohamed goes down again days after his own comeback, and Barak Bachar resets his tactics following back-to-back Toto Cup defeats.
body: It has been a rough opening to pre-season for Maccabi Haifa, and Sunday brought a mixed bag of injury news as the club tries to regroup before the league campaign begins in earnest.

Andrija Novakovich, the American-Serbian forward the club signed to boost its attack, has still not kicked a ball for his new team. According to ONE, the striker has been laid low by a virus for nearly a week and missed Saturday's 3-0 Toto Cup defeat to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, leaving him without any chance to make a first impression during his onboarding period.

That loss in Kiryat Shmona followed a 3-2 derby defeat to Hapoel Haifa in the opening round, and the pair of results have all but ended Maccabi's hopes of advancing from the Toto Cup group phase before the league even kicks off.

There was a fresh injury blow too. Midfielder Ali Mohamed, the Nigerien international who had only just recovered from a quadriceps problem, returned to the side against Kiryat Shmona but came away with a new issue — foot inflammation that has put him back into treatment, ONE reports, with the club hoping he can return to training within days.

The one piece of good news concerned Kenny Saief. The veteran Israeli winger, who has been out since the end of last season, is back in full training and is regarded internally as a potentially significant boost once he is ready to be reintegrated into the squad.

Maccabi's injury list does not end there. Goalkeeper Omri Glazer is also sidelined, with a knee ligament strain that is expected to keep him out for around two weeks, while Wanderson — known to fans as "Tsunami" — remains unavailable after being concussed.

With the results going the wrong way, head coach Barak Bachar used a team meeting to announce a tactical rethink. "The formation we played until now did not work, and from now on we will return to play our regular formation: 4-3-3," he told his players, according to ONE.
Maccabi Haifa are next in action on Tuesday against Tiberias, a game Bachar will hope produces both a first win of the summer and a clearer picture of who he actually has available to pick from.

title: Uroš Medić stops Daniel Rodriguez in 30 seconds as UFC's Serbian debut sets a finishes record
dek: Serbia's first-ever UFC card produced ten first-round finishes and a stunning homecoming knockout for Uroš Medić in the main event at Belgrade Arena.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia: UFC Fight Night: Medić vs. Rodriguez
UFC.com: UFC makes history in Serbia

body: The UFC's first-ever visit to Serbia will be remembered as one of the most violent nights in the promotion's history, and it ended exactly as the sold-out Belgrade Arena crowd wanted it to: with hometown favourite Uroš Medić flattening Daniel Rodriguez inside 30 seconds.

Medić needed barely half a minute to close the show in Saturday's main event, dropping Rodriguez with punches for a TKO that capped a card built almost entirely on early finishes rather than decisions.

It was the exclamation point on a historic evening for Serbian combat sports. The Belgrade Arena show marked the UFC's debut in the country, and the promotion confirmed the card set new records for both the most first-round finishes (ten) and the most total finishes (twelve) in a single UFC event.

The co-main event was almost as brutal. New Zealand's Navajo Stirling needed just 2:56 of the first round to stop former UFC light heavyweight champion Jan Błachowicz with a barrage of elbows and punches on the ground, extending his own unbeaten professional record to 11-0.

Serbia's fighters had a rocky start to the main card before Medić's finale. Duško Todorović, Vlasto Čepo and Miloš Janičić — all fighting in front of their home fans — went a combined 0-3, with Robert Valentin submitting Todorović via guillotine choke at 4:14 of round one, Gilbert Urbina stopping Čepo with strikes in just 1:01, and Noah Gugnon tapping out Janičić with a rear-naked choke at 1:21.

The home losing run was snapped by Aleksandar Rakić, the Austrian-born fighter of Serbian descent who was making his heavyweight debut after four years struggling at 205lbs. Rakić out-worked veteran Marcin Tybura for a clean unanimous decision, sweeping all three scorecards 30-27 to get his hand raised for the first time since March 2021.

By the time Medić stepped in for the headline bout, the Belgrade crowd had already witnessed nine finishes across the undercard and main card, and the Serbian welterweight duly delivered the loudest one — ending Rodriguez's night with a first-round knockout that sent the arena into raptures.

The result is a landmark moment for MMA in the Balkans: the UFC had never staged a show in Serbia before this weekend, and the reception at Belgrade Arena, allied to the sheer volume of finishes, is likely to put the country firmly on the promotion's list for a return visit.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv in talks with Armoni Brooks after ASVEL's financial collapse
dek: The Israeli champions have opened contact with the free-agent guard, but Sport5 reports his hesitation is personal, not financial, over moving his family to Israel.

verificationSources.label: Sportando: ASVEL crisis, Brooks back on market

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have opened talks with free-agent guard Armoni Brooks, Sport5 reported on Saturday, as the EuroLeague champions look to reinforce a backcourt that could soon lose Lonnie Walker IV.

Brooks, 28, only signed with ASVEL Villeurbanne this summer, arriving in Lyon as one of the headline names in Tony Parker's ambitious rebuild of the French club. That project has since unravelled: ASVEL's original budget of close to €59 million collapsed after the club failed to secure the financial guarantees behind it, and it has been forced to submit a scaled-back plan of roughly €24 million to French regulators.

The fallout has pushed several of ASVEL's marquee summer signings back onto the market, Brooks among them, alongside Daniel Theis, Nick Weiler-Babb and Sylvain Francisco, who has since joined Panathinaikos.

According to Sport5, there is no financial gap standing between Maccabi and Brooks — the club is prepared to meet his price. The sticking point, the report says, is personal: Brooks has reservations about uprooting his family and children to relocate to Israel, and Maccabi are continuing to work to change his mind.

The 1.94m guard was named MVP of the Italian league last season while starring for Olimpia Milano, and followed that with a solid EuroLeague campaign at ASVEL — 13.1 points and 3.5 rebounds a game on 41.6% three-point shooting across 38 appearances.

Sport5 frames the approach as part of a broader guard-market push by Maccabi this off-season, which has also seen the club register interest in both Theis and center Armando Bacot as it reshapes its roster following a title-winning campaign.
Walker's own future in Tel Aviv remains unresolved, with reports in recent weeks suggesting the sides are working toward a separation — adding urgency to Maccabi's search for backcourt depth.
For now, Sport5 stresses that nothing is decided: talks are ongoing, and, in the outlet's words, "the final word has not been said" on whether Brooks will end up in yellow and blue.

title: Maccabi Haifa's Toto Cup hopes fade as Hapoel Haifa pull clear at the top of Group A
dek: A derby defeat and a heavy home loss have left the club on zero points after two rounds, with neighbours Hapoel Haifa yet to drop a single one.
body: Maccabi Haifa's hopes of escaping the group stage of the Toto Cup have all but disappeared, Sport5 reported, after two matches without a point left them rooted at the bottom of Group A just as neighbours and old rivals Hapoel Haifa pulled clear at the summit.

The damage was done inside the season's opening fortnight. Maccabi Haifa lost the first Haifa derby of the campaign 3-2 to Hapoel Haifa, then were beaten 3-0 by Ironi Kiryat Shmona, leaving them without a win, a goal difference of minus four, and zero points from two games.

The derby loss carried extra sting. Ynet reported it was Maccabi Haifa's first defeat to Hapoel Haifa in a Haifa derby in 29 years, and club officials moved quickly to steady supporters, telling the outlet: "Don't rush to write our obituary."

There has been no respite since. Hapoel Haifa needed a stoppage-time goal to beat Bnei Sakhnin 2-1 in round three, Alon Turgeman's 35th-minute strike separating the sides before Sakhnin levelled deep into added time and Hapoel Haifa snatched the winner moments later to stay unbeaten.

The Toto Cup's ten non-European teams are split into two groups of five, with only the two group winners advancing to the semifinals, where they meet Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Tel Aviv, the two clubs seeded straight through as Israel's continental representatives.

According to Sport5's table, Hapoel Haifa lead Group A on nine points from three matches, ahead of Kiryat Shmona on six from two, Ironi Tiberias on three from three, and Sakhnin and Maccabi Haifa level on zero from two.

Maccabi Haifa are not yet mathematically eliminated — they would need to win out while hoping Hapoel Haifa slip up at least twice — but with their city rivals still unbeaten through three rounds, Sport5's own assessment was blunt: the realistic chance of topping the group has now all but gone.

title: Stuck in Germany: Leipzig freeze out Real Madrid over Diomande
dek: RB Leipzig have gone silent on an improved Real Madrid bid for teenage winger Yan Diomande, still holding out for a fixed €120m fee, ONE reports.
body: Real Madrid's pursuit of Yan Diomande has hit a wall of silence in Leipzig. ONE reports that the Bundesliga club failed to respond to an improved offer from the Spanish giants within 24 hours, leaving a deal that once looked close to touching down in limbo.

The 19-year-old Ivorian winger has been one of the stories of the year in German football, and Madrid have been chasing him hard since agreeing personal terms with the player weeks ago. PSG, once seen as a rival suitor, have already withdrawn from the race.

The sticking point is money. Leipzig want €120 million as a fixed, unconditional fee, and according to ONE they are refusing to accept any structure built around bonuses or performance-related add-ons. Real Madrid had previously seen an offer in that region turned down before returning with the improved bid now sitting unanswered on Leipzig's desk.

Diomande himself appears to be applying pressure from within. He sat out Leipzig's friendly against Werder Bremen citing illness, and ONE reports he may also skip the club's upcoming training camp in Austria using the same excuse — a not-so-subtle signal of where he wants his future to lie.

Madrid had hoped to have the transfer wrapped up by the end of the weekend. That deadline has now slipped, but sources on both sides described the standoff to ONE as posturing rather than a genuine breakdown, with a resolution still expected within the next day.

The player has been a revelation since joining Leipzig from Leganes for a modest fee last year, contributing 12 league goals and eight assists as the club finished third in the Bundesliga. He then took his form to the World Cup, starring for Ivory Coast as they reached the round of 32.

Should the move go through with its variables triggered, Diomande would become one of the most expensive teenagers in football history, with a total package reportedly capable of reaching around €135 million — a figure that would put him in the same bracket as Real Madrid's record outlays for Jude Bellingham and Eden Hazard.
For now, though, the deal is stuck exactly where the Hebrew headline suggests: in Germany, waiting on a club that has stopped picking up the phone.

title: Kiryat Shmona edge Tiberias 1-0 in Toto Cup as Barda hails players' character
dek: A heavily rotated Ironi Kiryat Shmona side needed a 61st-minute strike from new signing Rufat Abdullazade to see off Ironi Tiberias, and manager Shai Barda said the workmanlike win said more about his squad than the performance did.
body: Ironi Kiryat Shmona shrugged off a laboured performance to beat Ironi Tiberias 1-0 in the second round of the Toto Cup on Saturday, and manager Shai Barda made clear afterwards that he cared far more about the result than the display.
"This shows a type of character," Barda said of the victory. "We didn't play well today, but the win is important."

The only goal, scored at Ramat Hasharon Stadium, arrived in the 61st minute from Rufat Abdullazade, a new arrival to the club who marked his first goal in Kiryat Shmona colours with an emotional response. "I feel excellent. First goal and I'm happy to be here," he said, adding that he had found Israel "an amazing country" since joining.

Barda's explanation for the disjointed performance was straightforward: he sent out nine changes from his previous lineup, still trying to work fresh faces and returning squad members into a settled unit before the competitive season begins in earnest. "We changed nine players, it will take time to connect," he said.

For Tiberias, the defeat was their second in a row in the competition, and assistant coach Moti Crispin did not shy away from the toll that squad rotation and absences are taking on his group. "The rotation is overwhelming us. We can see fatigue," Crispin said, pointing to missing players as a growing concern for a side already leaning on inexperienced squad members.

Tiberias player Ido Sharon, who has found himself playing alongside youth-team reinforcements while regulars are unavailable, struck a more optimistic note, saying he still believed the club would meet its targets for the season despite the current thin numbers.

The Toto Cup remains largely a proving ground at this stage of the Israeli football calendar, giving coaches like Barda room to experiment with personnel before league points are on the line — even if it means his side wins ugly along the way.

title: Maccabi Netanya left stung as Nwachukwu snubs move for Qarabağ switch
dek: The Nigerian winger had reportedly agreed to join the Israeli club on a two-year deal, only for his agent to inform Netanya over the weekend that he had chosen Azerbaijan's Qarabağ instead.

body: Just days after Maccabi Netanya appeared to be closing in on a new left winger, the deal has fallen apart in embarrassing fashion: Christian Nwachukwu, the Nigerian prospect the club thought was on his way to Israel, has instead opted to join Qarabağ in Azerbaijan, Sport5 reports.

According to the outlet, Nwachukwu's agent, Satio Chachmon, informed Netanya over the weekend that his client had decided to take the Qarabağ option rather than follow through on the two-year deal the two sides had reportedly already agreed.

Nwachukwu, 20, remains the property of Sheffield United, who signed him from Bulgarian side Botev Plovdiv in February 2025 for a fee in the region of €1.2 million on a contract running to 2027. He made his name at Botev before the move to England, and spent this past season out on loan at Serikspor in Turkey, gaining minutes as a left-sided winger comfortable cutting in from either flank.

Netanya, still rebuilding under American owner Ross Kastin's Aliya Capital Partners, had been working through the structure of a loan with an option to buy — precisely the kind of development project Kastin has said he wants to build his squad around rather than paying for the finished article.

Sport5 notes that visa complications had already been cited in recent weeks as a hurdle to getting Nwachukwu onto Israeli soil, a warning sign in hindsight that the move was less advanced than it appeared.
Kastin, according to the report, was left frustrated by how the deal unraveled, and the club says it will now look for an alternative left-sided option before the transfer window closes.

The setback comes as coach Roni Levi, back for a second spell in charge at Netanya since being appointed in January, prepares his squad for Sunday's league fixture against Hapoel Rishon LeZion. Levi is expected to rotate personnel, with Bakary Konata, Maor Levi, Alon Azoogi and Giorgi Morozov in line for minutes.

Bassem Zarura will miss out through injury, Omri Shamir returns to the squad, and Dolev Chaziza, the club's summer arrival from Maccabi Haifa, is set to be included in a first-team squad for the first time.

For a club that has made developing and trading young talent central to its rebuild, losing a target to a rival offer before he even arrived is an unwelcome reminder of just how competitive that market has become.

title: Avuksis says Sakhnin still targeting four or five more signings
dek: The Sakhnin manager used a stoppage-time Toto Cup defeat to Hapoel Haifa to look ahead, insisting his squad still needs reinforcements before Ligat Ha'al kicks off.
body: Yossi Avuksis was already looking past a bruising Toto Cup exit on Saturday night. Hours after Sakhnin lost 2-1 to Hapoel Haifa in a match decided by two goals deep into stoppage time, the manager used his post-match remarks to talk about what is still missing from his squad: four or five more players before the Ligat Ha'al season begins.

"We have three or four players we've already brought in, and by the time the league starts they'll arrive in match fitness," Avuksis said, according to Sport5. "We want to sign another striker, midfielder and defender - overall four or five more players. I believe in this team and I'm leaving very encouraged."

The defeat itself looked avoidable. Alon Torgeman put Hapoel Haifa ahead in the 35th minute, and Sakhnin appeared to have salvaged a draw when Mateo Kojo equalised in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time. The relief lasted barely two minutes: Moataz Hamed struck the winner for Haifa in the seventh minute of stoppage time to complete the turnaround.

"It's frustrating to lose this way - we'd already come back at the last moment," Avuksis said. "I felt we were much better in the second half. You need to learn from these things. We didn't deserve to lose, but that's football."

Both sides finished the match with ten men. Hapoel Haifa's Dario Zoparic was sent off for a second yellow card in the 73rd minute, and Sakhnin's Sana Gomes followed him down the tunnel nine minutes later. Avuksis was sympathetic toward his own defender afterwards. "I told him to be careful, because any foul would get him a second yellow," he said. "When you're gassed you don't think as clearly as you should, but he'll learn from this too."

Avuksis returned to Sakhnin in February for a second spell in charge, having previously managed the club between 2015 and 2017, and he has already been active in the transfer market this summer. The club has brought in Raul Balbarau, a 25-year-old Romanian defender who joined from Petrolul Ploiesti, along with a left-back who moved on after turning down a new deal at Hapoel Haifa.

With the new Ligat Ha'al campaign now only weeks away, Avuksis made clear the current squad is still a work in progress. His comments suggest Sakhnin's business is far from done, even as the club tries to build fitness and cohesion among the reinforcements already through the door.

title: Ferrari's Luce electric car sells out its 2026 run — but this is not a sports story
dek: Sport5 reports Ferrari has sold out its first electric model within two months, a business and automotive story with no competition, match or sporting event attached to it
body: The Sport5 article behind this brief ("He who laughs last laughs best: Ferrari Luce sold out") is a piece of automotive business news, not a sports report — it concerns Ferrari's road-car division and carries no match, competition or athlete content of any kind.

Sport5, citing the carmaker, reports that Ferrari has sold out its entire planned 2026 production run of the Luce — its first fully electric model, previously known during development as the Elettrica — in roughly two months.

The Luce starts at around €550,000 (about $640,000), among the priciest cars Ferrari has ever offered, with independent outlets Electrek and Robb Report confirming the sellout of the roughly 500-unit 2026 allocation before a single customer car has been delivered; deliveries are not due to begin until October.

Demand was strongest out of China, according to the reporting, and held up despite sharp early criticism of the car's exterior styling when it was unveiled and a dip in Ferrari's share price that followed.
Ferrari has set a longer-term target of about 2,500 Luce units by 2030 — roughly 600 a year, or about 5% of the company's total annual output.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv urged to sign Eli Dasa as pundits flag two priority positions
dek: ONE's podcast panel says Maccabi Tel Aviv must move fast in two areas of the squad, with a return for free-agent captain Eli Dasa top of the wishlist after the Europa League win over Sheriff Tiraspol.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — Europa League result vs Sheriff
Walla Sport — Eli Dasa free agent, Maccabi yet to move
Haaretz — Maccabi Tel Aviv exercise option on Christian Blitz

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's Europa League run has bought the club goodwill, but ONE's team podcast says the summer rebuild is still not finished — and its panel has zeroed in on two areas of the squad that need urgent reinforcement before the transfer window shuts.

The Yellow-and-Blues booked their place in the third qualifying round by beating Sheriff Tiraspol 6-0 on aggregate, thrashing the Moldovan side 5-0 away on July 23 before closing it out 1-0 at Bloomfield Stadium on July 30. They now face CSKA Sofia for a spot deeper in Europe.

That progress hasn't stopped ONE's panel — Raz Amir, Avi Nmeni and Shaked Amiram — from pressing the case for further business, debating on air how much of a difference two well-chosen signings could make to a title challenge that starts in earnest this month.

The loudest call came from Nmeni, who urged the club's management to "go and bring Eli Dasa at any cost." The Israel national team captain is a free agent after his contract at NEC Nijmegen in the Netherlands expired, and according to Walla Sport he has yet to receive an official approach from Maccabi even as clubs elsewhere in Europe and in the United States circle for his signature at right-back.

Dasa is no stranger to the club — he came through Maccabi Tel Aviv between 2015 and 2019, including under Vladimir Ivic during a championship season, before leaving for Dynamo Moscow in 2022 after turning down a new contract at the time. Reuniting him with the Yellow-and-Blues would fill a defensive slot the panel clearly rates as urgent.

The second thread of the discussion was less about who to sign than a decision already made. The panel questioned why Maccabi chose to retain Christian Blitz over the summer rather than pursue alternatives in midfield. The Serbian arrived on loan from AZ Alkmaar last season and became the club's first confirmed signing of the 2026/27 campaign when Maccabi exercised a €1.3 million purchase option, tying him down to a contract through 2029.

That decision has looked shakier at times, with Israeli outlets reporting injury concerns around Blitz this summer that have complicated the club's recruitment planning in central midfield — part of why the panel felt the position still needs addressing rather than considered settled.

Not every name discussed was an external target. Ilai Ben Simone's recent playing time drew praise from the panel as a sign the club may also be able to lean on academy or squad options rather than the market alone to cover its gaps.

For a club that has spent the close season adding depth in pieces rather than with one marquee arrival, the ONE panel's message was blunt: two positions remain unresolved, and with a European tie against CSKA Sofia and a league title bid both on the horizon, the window to fix them is closing fast.

title: Two days left to catch the early price for Beer Sheva's night race
dek: Registration for September's Light Run festival in Beer Sheva rises at midnight on Sunday, with a half marathon, 10km and family distances on offer through the city under floodlight.

verificationSources.label: Official Light Run Beer Sheva 2026 site

body: Runners who have been putting off signing up for Beer Sheva's Light Run have a shrinking window: Sport5 reports that entry prices for the city's night race jump at midnight on the night of August 2-3, giving latecomers only two more days to lock in the cheaper rate.

The event, now a fixture of the Israeli running calendar, returns to the streets and river park of the Negev capital on Wednesday, September 9. It is organised by the Beer Sheva Municipality and produced by the Shvoong company, run this year in partnership with the IDF.

The night format is the draw. Runners set off after dark under stadium-style lighting rigs along courses that Sport5 says meet athletics union certification standards, built for genuine personal-best attempts rather than just a scenic jog.

There is something for every level of runner. The competitive card covers the half marathon (21.1km), 10km and 5km, while a recreational programme of 2.5km, 1km and 500m brings families, children and first-time runners into the same night.

A total prize pool of 18,000 shekels will be split among the winners of the headline categories, according to the report, giving the elite fields a genuine incentive alongside the mass-participation atmosphere.

Sport5 describes a running festival built around a 'Saluting Security Forces' theme, with thousands of civilian runners expected to take to the course alongside serving soldiers and their commanders — a recurring element of the Beer Sheva race in recent editions.

The evening does not end at the finish line. Organisers have built an expansive post-race expo featuring sport and lifestyle vendors and experience zones, with international DJ Skazi and the live band Rockville booked to headline the entertainment programme.
Registration remains open through the event's official website, with organisers using the looming deadline to push a final wave of early sign-ups before the higher price tier kicks in this weekend.

title: South America's marathon record holder missing for six weeks as mother pleads for his return
dek: Daniel do Nascimento, the Brazilian Olympian who ran the fastest marathon ever by a non-African-born athlete, has not been seen since he walked out of his family home in São Paulo state in June carrying only a backpack.
body: Daniel do Nascimento, the Brazilian distance runner who holds South America's marathon record, has not been seen or heard from for six weeks, and his mother has gone public with a desperate appeal for his safe return.

The 28-year-old was last seen leaving his family's home in Paraguaçu Paulista, in the interior of São Paulo state, at around 7pm on June 19, according to relatives. He was carrying only a black backpack and gave no indication of where he was going.

A witness later told the family that Nascimento had been seen walking toward the town of Assis, roughly 35 kilometres away, and had stopped to ask for water, saying he still had a long way to go. Nothing has been confirmed since.

His mother, Valdirense de Paula Ferreira, and his five siblings waited weeks before filing an official missing-person report with São Paulo's civil police on July 27, more than a month after he disappeared. The case has since been handed to the state's General Investigations Department in Assis, though no sightings have been confirmed publicly.

"A mother's feeling... a thousand things go through your head," Ferreira told Brazilian outlet G1. She said she believes she has lost around 10 kilograms of weight from the stress of not knowing where her son is. "When it rains, you think about a lot of things. It's very difficult," she said.

Nascimento turned 28 on July 29 while still missing. His mother marked the day with an emotional message on Instagram: "Congratulations, Daniel! Come back home. May God bless you, light your path, and bring you home safely."

Before his disappearance, Nascimento was one of the standout distance runners of his generation. He represented Brazil in the marathon at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and, at the 2022 Seoul Marathon, ran 2:04:51 to finish third behind two Ethiopian runners — a time that remains the South American and Brazilian national record, and the fastest marathon ever recorded by a runner born outside Africa.

His career unravelled in 2024, when out-of-competition tests taken in Rio de Janeiro that July returned positive for three banned anabolic substances — drostanolone, metenolone and nandrolone. The finding ruled him out of the Paris Olympics, and the Athletics Integrity Unit subsequently handed him a five-year ban running from July 2024 to July 2029, which will also keep him out of the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

Ferreira has said her son has struggled with psychological problems, and reports in Brazil have noted that contact between Nascimento and anti-doping officials and his own management team grew increasingly sparse through late 2024 and into 2025 before he vanished entirely in June.
For now, the family says it is relying on the public for any information, hoping someone who saw him on the road toward Assis — or anywhere since — comes forward with a lead.

title: Israeli sports-tech startup Marquee raises $6.5 million led by Axel Springer
dek: The Tel Aviv-founded company, whose AI platform already serves more than 20 clubs and federations including Premier League and Serie A sides, will use the funding to push into basketball and American football and open its first US and UK offices.
body: An Israeli sports-tech company that started life as an analytics side project for an Arsenal supporters' community has just landed one of the more eye-catching funding rounds of the summer for the industry. Marquee, which builds an AI platform that pulls together the scattered data professional clubs already hold and turns it into usable decisions, has raised $6.5 million, ONE reported, in a round led by the German media giant Axel Springer SE.

Joining Axel Springer in the round are Welltech Ventures, Apex Capital, AnD Ventures, 97212 Ventures and JCP, according to the funding announcement corroborated by Yahoo Finance and a GlobeNewswire press release. The company says the fresh capital will go toward accelerating product development, expanding its AI, engineering and data science teams, and opening its first commercial offices in the United States and the United Kingdom.

Marquee's pitch is that clubs are not short of data - they are short of a way to use it. The platform does not collect new information so much as stitch together what a club already has in separate systems, from scouting and performance metrics to medical and financial records, and surface insights within seconds rather than the weeks a manual review might take.

CEO and co-founder Dean Bracha (דין ברכה) built the company alongside chief technology officer Jonathan Hazut (יונתן חזות), chief operating officer Dror Rosenfeld (דרור רוזנפלד) and chief data officer Tal Darchi (טל דרחי). Bracha has said most sports organizations use only somewhere between 4% and 15% of the data they already possess - the gap Marquee is trying to close.

The product's roots are unusually specific: the founding team first built its recruitment and analytics tools for an online Arsenal fan community, work that later caught the attention of professional club staff and pushed the founders toward building for the industry itself.

That pivot has moved quickly. Marquee is now live with more than 20 professional clubs and federations across multiple countries, including Tier 1 clubs in the Premier League and Serie A as well as Major League Soccer organizations, alongside clients in Israel. The company currently employs around 15 people.

Steven Berelowitz, a partner at Welltech Ventures, framed the investment as a bet on Marquee's position rather than just its growth. "Marquee stood out because they are applying AI to one of the most complex, data-rich environments in professional sports," he said, adding that the firm sees the company positioned to define how AI is used across the sport.

The new money is earmarked in part for expansion beyond football. Marquee plans to roll out dedicated basketball and American football products later in 2026, with early conversations already under way with NBA and EuroLeague teams as it looks to replicate its football traction in other sports.

This is not Marquee's first outside backing. Earlier in 2026 the company closed a smaller pre-seed round whose investors included Wix co-founders Avishai Abrahami and Omer Shai and 365Scores founder Ami Sirkis - a roster that signalled early confidence from Israel's tech and sports-media establishment well before Axel Springer's involvement.

title: Vinícius Júnior's solution to a Real Madrid deadlock: a signing bonus
dek: The Brazilian winger's camp wants a lump-sum bonus rather than a bigger salary to break a stalled renewal — pointing to the terms Kylian Mbappé received a year ago.
body: Real Madrid's long-running contract stand-off with Vinícius Júnior has narrowed to a single sticking point, and it isn't the number on his monthly payslip. According to ONE, the Brazilian's representatives have concluded that a one-off signing bonus, not a higher salary, is the only way to raise his earnings without blowing up the club's pay structure.

Vinícius currently earns around €18 million net a year at the Bernabéu. Real Madrid tabled an offer of roughly €20 million net back in January 2025, which his camp turned down. The gap between the two sides was never really about the base wage, ONE reports — it is about how the rest of the package gets delivered.

His representatives' argument leans heavily on precedent. Kylian Mbappé, on a broadly comparable annual salary, was given a substantial signing bonus when he arrived as a free agent from Paris Saint-Germain last year. Vinícius's side wants the same mechanism applied to a renewal rather than a fresh arrival.

Real Madrid have consistently resisted, according to the report, wary that handing an existing player a signing-on bonus — rather than a genuinely new arrival — would invite every other dressing-room star to demand the same treatment.

The dispute has been reported elsewhere in Spain in similar terms. Mundo Deportivo has also flagged the bonus as the friction point in the talks, and Martin Cid Magazine noted this week that Madrid gave Mbappé a renewal-style bonus "it refuses to offer Vinícius Júnior," even as the sides work through other ways to lift his overall package.

Three outcomes remain live, per ONE: a renewed deal at Real Madrid, a summer move to Arsenal, or simply running his contract down to a free transfer when it expires in 2027 — with the added risk for Madrid that he could sign a pre-contract with a rival club as early as January if nothing is resolved.

Arsenal have not gone away as suitors. Sporting director Andrea Berta has held talks over several months, and sources described to ONE how highly manager Mikel Arteta rates the winger: "Mikel Arteta loves him very much. If he doesn't renew, we will be there."

For now, Real Madrid are said to be trying to close the gap through the structure of the deal rather than a straight bonus payment — a guaranteed base with bonuses that could push his total package toward the salary his camp is seeking. Talks are expected to intensify in the coming days as Vinícius returns to pre-season training, though — as a flurry of conflicting reports out of Madrid this week shows — the situation remains fluid and could shift again before anything is signed.
