title: Ludogorets 2-2 Hapoel Tel Aviv (4-2 agg): Barda's biggest scalp yet sends Reds into Conference League third round
dek: Emmanuel Boateng's second-half brace and a first-half penalty save from Assaf Tzur secured a 2-2 draw in Bulgaria, completing a 4-2 aggregate win that ended Ludogorets' run of European group-stage football and put Elyaniv Barda's side into a tie with Poland's Katowice.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv are back in Europe for the first time in twelve years, and they marked the occasion by knocking out a club that had made continental football an annual habit. A 2-2 draw away to Ludogorets in Razgrad on Thursday night sealed a 4-2 aggregate victory in the Conference League second qualifying round, and sent the Reds through to face Poland's Katowice in the third round.

The night in Bulgaria was never going to be straightforward. Omri Altman found Emmanuel Boateng inside the area in the 16th minute and the Ghanaian striker finished coolly to put Hapoel 3-0 up on aggregate, seemingly putting the tie beyond reach before it had properly begun.

Ludogorts hit back hard. Bernard Tekpetey pulled one back in the 47th minute and Alberto Salido made it 2-1 on the night seven minutes later, turning a comfortable evening into a nervous one and briefly threatening to drag the tie to extra time.
Boateng settled it. His second goal of the night, in the 58th minute, restored Hapoel's two-goal cushion on aggregate and proved decisive, even as Ludogorets pushed for a third that never came.

The other pivotal moment came earlier, in the 39th minute, when goalkeeper Assaf Tzur guessed correctly and saved a penalty from Kwadwo Duah. Had that gone in, the tie would have looked very different heading into the second-half turnaround.

The aggregate scoreline was built in Tel Aviv a week earlier, when Hapoel won the first leg 2-0 at Bloomfield Stadium through goals from Altman and centre-back Chico, giving Elyaniv Barda's side a cushion they never entirely relinquished.

As ONE's coverage framed it, eliminating Ludogorets ranks as the biggest achievement of Barda's spell at Hapoel Tel Aviv so far. The Bulgarian champions had reached the group or league phase of a European competition in every campaign since 2015/16 — a run of continental pedigree that ended on Thursday night against a club operating on a fraction of their budget.

A senior club figure summed up the scale of the result afterwards: "We defeated an opponent with a budget four times larger than ours. We've maintained the club's tradition and achieved something enormous here. We're not stopping here," they said, according to Walla! Sport.

There was also a note of caution attached to the celebration, with the same source warning: "If we don't approach Katowice with the exact same mentality we brought to Ludogorets, we'll have a problem."

Barda, who took charge of Hapoel Tel Aviv in December 2024 after leading Hapoel Be'er Sheva to a State Cup and a Toto Cup crown as well as a Conference League group-stage run, has now guided the Reds from the second tier to the brink of the competition's group phase in little over a year.

Hapoel's reward is a third qualifying round meeting with GKS Katowice, who overturned a 1-2 first-leg deficit against Slovakia's Žilina by winning the second leg 3-1. It is the first time Hapoel Tel Aviv have played in Europe since a 2014-15 Europa League qualifying exit to Astana, and one more two-legged tie now stands between them and a first group-stage campaign in the club's history.

title: Real Madrid 2-2 Fiorentina: Mourinho sees 'three different faces' in his first game in charge
dek: The Portuguese head coach praised a fast start, admitted fatigue undid a 2-1 lead, and singled out a raw debutant for criticism after his first match back in a Real Madrid dugout.
body: José Mourinho's first match back in a Real Madrid dugout finished the way his team played it: in three distinct chapters. Real Madrid drew 2-2 with Fiorentina in a preseason friendly at the Wörthersee Stadion in Klagenfurt, Austria, on Saturday, and the Portuguese head coach's post-match verdict captured a performance that swung from thrilling to threadbare inside 90 minutes.

Endrick struck in the 12th minute and academy graduate Alexis Ciria added a second on his first-team debut in the 24th to put Madrid 2-0 up, before Roberto Piccoli halved the deficit for Fiorentina just before the break. Moise Kean levelled early in the second half, heading home to make it 2-2, and neither side found a winner.
'I loved it all,' Mourinho said afterwards, according to ONE. 'I saw three different faces of the team: a fresh one, a tired one, and a third that was extremely tired.'

The first face, he said, was the one Real Madrid showed before the break — sharp, dominant and, in his view, worth more than a 2-1 half-time lead. 'We produced a high-quality first half and could easily have gone ahead by three or four goals,' he said.

The second face arrived once Fiorentina's physicality began to tell. Mourinho pointed to Kean's power as the problem for his two teenage centre-backs, Joan Martínez and Mario Rivas, both fielded in defence for the first time in a first-team fixture, saying fatigue undid the control his side had shown early on.
By the closing stages, Mourinho described a third version of his team: exhausted, but still organised enough to keep possession and see out the closing minutes without conceding again.

One player did not escape criticism. Substitute Carlos Espí, brought on in the 75th minute and nearly a match-winner with a late header, had trained with the squad only once before kick-off, and Mourinho said it showed, describing him as still 'waking up from a dream.'

Ciria's goal was the highlight of the night for Real Madrid's academy, with Lacosta and Lamini also making their senior debuts alongside him and Rivas. 'Mourinho asked me to have confidence and enjoy myself,' Ciria said of his instructions before going on.

The friendly was played without several first-choice players. Vinícius Júnior, Bernardo Silva and Brahim Díaz were all absent and are expected to report for pre-season training on Monday, leaving Mourinho to lean heavily on youth in his first outing since taking charge.

title: Deni Avdija gets a new frontcourt partner as Jeremy Sochan signs with Portland
dek: Fresh off winning the NBA title with the Knicks, the Polish-American forward has agreed a one-year deal with the Trail Blazers, teaming up with Israel's Deni Avdija.
body: Deni Avdija is about to have some new competition — and company — in Portland's frontcourt. ONE reports that Jeremy Sochan has agreed a one-year contract with the Trail Blazers as a free agent, giving the Israeli forward a fresh running mate up front for the coming season.

The move, first reported by ESPN's Shams Charania and confirmed by Sochan's agent Darius Visokkas, caps an eventful few months for the 23-year-old, who holds both Polish and American citizenship and was the ninth overall pick in the 2022 draft by San Antonio.

San Antonio waived Sochan on February 11, and just two days later he signed with the New York Knicks, who went on to win this year's NBA championship. Sochan finished the season as part of that title-winning roster before hitting free agency again this summer.

For his career, the 6-foot-8 forward averages 9.9 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.5 assists a game, built around the defensive versatility and relentless energy that made him a lottery pick out of Baylor. Portland is betting that profile fits alongside its existing young core.

That core now includes Avdija in a more prominent role than ever. The Israeli international has been one of the league's better value contracts since arriving from Washington in February 2024, playing on a four-year, $55 million rookie extension that runs through 2027-28.

Portland cannot formally negotiate a new extension with Avdija until the 2026 window opens on October 21, but the Trail Blazers are expected to make that a priority once they can, given how far his production has outpaced his modest cap number.

Sochan's arrival adds depth and defensive length to a frontcourt already anchored by Avdija, giving Portland another young, switchable forward as it looks to build out its roster around him heading into next season.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv sign American guard Eugene German
dek: The 28-year-old, fresh off a productive CBA stint with Beijing Ducks, joins Dimitris Itoudis's roster on a deal through the 2026/27 season.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have added another ball-handler to their backcourt, officially announcing the signing of American guard Eugene German through the end of the 2026/27 season, the club confirmed via ONE.

German, 28, stands 1.83m and arrives in Israel off the back of a strong four-year run in China's CBA, most recently with Beijing Ducks, where he averaged 18.3 points, 3.1 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game while shooting an efficient 54.2 percent on twos and 40.1 percent from three.
He had most recently been playing in Puerto Rico with Indios de Mayagüez, posting 17.4 points, 4.5 assists and 3.5 rebounds across eight appearances before Hapoel moved to bring him to Tel Aviv.

A native of Gary, Indiana, German built his reputation at Northern Illinois University, where he left as the program's all-time leading scorer after a career that made him a fixture on the Huskies' backcourt from 2016 to 2020. His professional path since has taken him through Europe, Turkey and China, including stops with Qingdao and Fujian before his move to Beijing.
"I'm excited to join this organization and team," German said of the move. "You can expect me to bring energy every moment on the court and give everything."

Hapoel's general manager, Georgios Chinas, framed the signing as a boost to an already crowded guard rotation: "Eugene is a talented addition to our guard position who will bring another dimension to our game."

Head coach Dimitris Itoudis, who will oversee German's EuroLeague debut this season, praised his scoring versatility, saying the American "knows how to score points in different ways and contribute in various manners," and that he was looking forward to adding that dimension to an already strong roster.

The deal continues what has been an active off-season rebuild for Hapoel Tel Aviv as the club prepares for another EuroLeague campaign, with German set to add scoring punch and playmaking depth to the backcourt alongside the rest of Itoudis's returning group.

title: Kiryat Shmona beat Tiberias 1-0 as Barda demands action on home stadium saga
dek: Manager Shai Barda said the Toto Cup win over Ironi Tiberias mattered less than the club's long wait for a usable home ground, telling reporters it is time for action rather than talk.

verificationSources.label: Sport1 - Barda contract extension at Kiryat Shmona

body: Ironi Kiryat Shmona made it two wins from two in this year's Toto Cup group stage on Saturday, beating Ironi Tiberias 1-0 at the Barel Stadium, but manager Shai Barda used his post-match remarks to push a different subject back to the top of the agenda: the club's stubbornly unresolved home stadium crisis.

The win followed a 3-0 rout of Maccabi Haifa in Kiryat Shmona's previous group outing, giving Barda's side a perfect record so far in the competition. Yet the manager was in no mood to dwell on the performance itself.
"There's really nothing to take from this match, except the victory," Barda said, according to ONE, adding that "the defense wasn't good today in my opinion."

It was when he turned to the club's wider circumstances that Barda's tone sharpened. "I've talked about it enough. It's time for action on this matter," he said, referring directly to Kiryat Shmona's continued lack of a home ground.

The club has not been able to play at its own stadium for roughly a year and a half, after the venue was left unusable by war-related damage. In that time Kiryat Shmona have been forced to shuttle between temporary venues across the country, including Saturday's fixture away at Tiberias' Barel Stadium despite having been the nominal home side for the tie.
Barda credited the club's supporters for continuing to show up regardless, saying they "deserve credit for coming to encourage us wherever we play."

The stadium issue has followed Barda through a period that has otherwise gone well for him personally: he agreed a two-year contract extension with Kiryat Shmona this year, having joined in the summer of 2023 after the club's relegation and steered it straight back to the top flight within a single season.

At the other end, Tiberias were without a permanent head coach on the touchline, with assistant Moti Krispil overseeing the side. Krispil said his squad remains "short and not complete," and indicated the club expects to confirm a permanent appointment before long.

For Kiryat Shmona, the Toto Cup form offers early encouragement heading into the new season - but as Barda made clear, the club's off-field situation remains the story that will not go away until the stadium question is finally settled.

title: Girona 1-4 Arsenal: Havertz, Tzolis and teenager Dowman shine in preseason opener
dek: Kai Havertz, debutant Christos Tzolis, 16-year-old Max Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all scored as Mikel Arteta's side opened their summer programme with a comfortable win in Catalonia.
body: Arsenal opened their preseason programme in style on Saturday, beating Girona 4-1 at the Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia in a friendly that gave Mikel Arteta an early look at both his big-money summer arrival and his most talked-about academy prospect.
Kai Havertz put the Gunners ahead inside 16 minutes, finishing off a move started by 16-year-old Max Dowman, who turned away from his marker before slipping the German through on goal.

Christos Tzolis doubled the lead in the first half with a deflected finish on his full debut, a tidy start for the Greece international signed this summer from Club Brugge for a reported £34m as Arsenal's replacement for Leandro Trossard, who left for Besiktas.

Girona, preparing for their own La Liga season, briefly threatened a comeback early in the second half when Arnau Martinez headed home from close range to make it 2-1 and give the home crowd something to cheer.

Arsenal responded within minutes. Dowman, again at the centre of things, struck a powerful effort from outside the box to restore the two-goal cushion, before Gabriel Jesus added a fourth shortly after to put the result beyond doubt.

The teenager's display — a goal and an assist inside a little over an hour on the pitch — was the standout individual performance of the afternoon, with Arteta using the second half to rotate heavily and give academy players extended minutes against senior opposition.

It was the first of four preseason fixtures for Arsenal, who face Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday, host Como at the Emirates on August 12, meet Manchester City in the Community Shield in Cardiff on August 16, and open their Premier League campaign at home to Coventry City on August 21.

For a club that has spent heavily this summer, a comfortable win laced with goals from a new signing and a homegrown teenager was an encouraging opening statement, even if the true examination of Arteta's squad will only come once the competitive season begins.

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv are working the phones for frontcourt reinforcements, and according to ONE, one name near the top of the list is Nick Richards, the 28-year-old American center who spent last season bouncing between the Chicago Bulls' rotation and the trade market.

ONE's exclusive report describes Richards as one of two senior candidates the Reds are weighing for a center spot, though the outlet is careful to note he has not yet given his approval for a move to Europe. That is the crucial caveat: this is a club target, not an agreed deal.

Richards, a 7-footer out of the University of Kentucky, was the 42nd pick in the 2020 NBA draft by New Orleans and has since logged more than 300 regular-season games across stints with Charlotte, Phoenix and Chicago, built on efficient interior scoring and rebounding rather than perimeter range.

He enters the market as an unrestricted free agent this summer after Chicago's offseason business left him unsigned, giving Hapoel and other suitors a genuine opening if he decides an EuroLeague payday and playing time outweigh chasing another NBA training-camp deal.

The Richards interest is not happening in isolation. ONE also has Hapoel pursuing Maxi Kleber, the veteran German forward-center who was renounced by the Lakers last month, a pursuit independently reported by Eurohoops and HoopsHype in recent days as Kleber explores EuroLeague offers.

Beyond those two, ONE says the club is also keeping tabs on D'Angelo Russell, the 2015 second overall pick now with Memphis, as part of what the report calls an 'intensive' rebuild of the roster for next season.

None of this is confirmed business yet. Hapoel have not commented publicly, and Richards' camp has given no indication he is close to committing to a move abroad, but the club's frontcourt shopping list for 2026-27 is clearly taking shape.

body: Israel's second-tier Liga Leumit continued its summer squad-building on Saturday, with three clubs confirming basketball moves ahead of the 2026/27 season, according to a report by ONE. Elitzur Ashkelon signed forward Omer Sadeh, Maccabi Rehovot added guard Yanir Binyamin, and Ironi Nahariya announced it had persuaded forward Uri Nadler to stay put.

Ashkelon officially confirmed Sadeh, 24, a 2.00-metre forward who returns to the National League after a season with Bnei Herzliya, ONE reported. Before that stint in Herzliya, Sadeh played for Hapoel Kfar Saba, where he averaged 13.4 points and 4.5 rebounds a game.

Nahariya, for its part, held on to one of its own: Uri Nadler, 23 and 1.95 metres, has signed on for another season at the club, the report said.

"I'm very glad Nadler is continuing with us for another season," Nahariya head coach Reuven Neiberger said, according to ONE. "Uri is a fighter in every sense of the word who hasn't yet shown his full ability on the court, and I'm sure that next season the fans will enjoy his fighting spirit and his special qualities out there."

Nadler himself struck a similar note. "I'm happy to continue what we've built together, grateful for the trust, and I'm going into the new season with a lot of motivation and a desire to give everything for the team," he said. "I can't wait for the season to start and to see the fans again."
None of the three clubs disclosed contract length or financial terms, and all three moves are part of routine roster turnover ahead of a National League season that is still weeks from tipping off.

title: Real Madrid 2-2 Fiorentina: Mourinho's first game in charge ends in a second-half collapse
dek: Two goals up inside 24 minutes, Real Madrid lost their grip after the break as Fiorentina came back to draw in Mourinho's opening match of his second spell at the club.

verificationSources.label: ESPN - Real Madrid 2-2 Fiorentina, as it happened

body: José Mourinho's second spell in charge of Real Madrid began the way so many of his sides have ended up before: two goals to the good, in cruise control, and then unable to hold on. Real Madrid let a 2-0 lead slip against Fiorentina in Klagenfurt, Austria, drawing 2-2 in Mourinho's first match back at the helm.

The game, played at the Wörthersee Stadion on Saturday evening, was Real Madrid's opening fixture of preseason. Endrick put the Spanish giants ahead in the 12th minute with a left-footed finish from inside the box, and academy forward Alexis Ciria doubled the lead 12 minutes later, scoring on his first-team debut.

Marca's account, cited by ONE, described the opening 45 minutes as unmistakably Mourinho's Real Madrid: "serious, combative, uncompromising, competitive and committed." Endrick in particular was singled out for his hunger and intensity, even if his eagerness occasionally got the better of his decision-making.

It did not last. Roberto Piccoli pulled a goal back for Fiorentina in first-half stoppage time to make it 2-1, and the Italian side kept pushing after the restart. Moise Kean, introduced from the bench, headed in the equaliser in the 58th minute to complete the comeback.

According to Marca's report, relayed by ONE, Mourinho "looked gloomy" during the water break as his side's control of the match evaporated — a visible read on a manager who built his reputation on precisely the kind of discipline that went missing after half-time. The Portuguese watched his team, in the paper's words, "lose absolute control" and "completely fall apart."

Real Madrid also handed debuts to two other new arrivals on the night: wing-back Denzel Dumfries and midfielder Carlos Espí both featured for the first time in Real Madrid colours, part of the squad Mourinho is assembling for his return to the touchline at the Santiago Bernabéu.

It was a low-stakes result — a mid-summer friendly rather than anything with points attached — but the split personality of the performance will not have escaped Mourinho, whose sides have historically prized exactly the control and management of games that disappeared once Fiorentina found their rhythm.

Real Madrid's preseason schedule continues in the coming weeks as Mourinho works towards his first competitive match back in charge, with the closing exchanges in Klagenfurt offering an early reminder of the work still to do before the new season begins in earnest.

title: Wiebes Wins Uphill Sprint to Seize Yellow as Tour de France Femmes Opens in Lausanne
dek: Lorena Wiebes out-kicked Kim Le Court-Pienaar and European champion Demi Vollering on a punchy Stage 1 finish above Lake Geneva, while Océane Mahé took the polka-dot jersey and Paula Blasi the white on the opening day of the 2026 race.

verificationSources.label: Cyclingnews — Wiebes claims Stage 1 and first yellow jersey
ProCyclingUK — Paula Blasi, white jersey / season form

body: Lausanne, Switzerland — The 2026 Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift got under way on Saturday with a stage that was billed as flat and rode nothing like it, as Lorena Wiebes powered up the final ramp into Lausanne to win Stage 1 and pull on the race's first yellow jersey.

The 137-kilometre loop out of and back into the shores of Lake Geneva was officially classified as a sprinters' stage, but it packed four categorised climbs into its finale, including the decisive Côte Saint-François — 2.5 kilometres at an average 4.6 percent — that crested just short of the line. It was enough to sort the pure sprinters from the rest without derailing the fastest woman in the bunch.

A four-rider breakaway animated the early kilometres, building a lead of close to six minutes before the peloton wound it back in with roughly six kilometres to go, setting up a reduced, uphill sprint among the general classification favourites and the strongest fast finishers left standing.

Wiebes, racing for Team SD Worx–Protime, timed her effort perfectly, launching her sprint with about 400 metres remaining and holding off every rival who tried to come around her. Neither Kim Le Court-Pienaar nor Demi Vollering could close the gap once the Dutch rider hit full speed on the rise.

It was Wiebes's tenth career stage win at the Tour de France Femmes and, by her team's count, the 132nd victory of her professional career — numbers that underline why the 27-year-old, a two-time European champion, remains the rider every sprint finish in this race is built around.

Kim Le Court-Pienaar, riding for AG Insurance–Soudal and representing Mauritius, took second at four seconds back, with Vollering of FDJ United–Suez completing the podium six seconds behind Wiebes after the bonus seconds were tallied at the line. Fenix–Premier Tech's Puck Pieterse rounded out the front group in fourth, ten seconds down.

The stage was not without incident. Zoe Backstedt and Le Court-Pienaar were both involved in early crashes, and Laura Tomasi became the race's first abandonment after a fall triggered a concussion assessment that ruled her out for the rest of the Tour.

Behind the podium, the general classification took early shape: Noemi Rüegg (EF Education–Oatly), Elisa Longo Borghini (UAE Team L'IMAD), Kasia Niewiadoma (Canyon//SRAM), Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (Team Visma | Lease a Bike), Cédrine Kerbaol (EF Education–Oatly) and Marlen Reusser (Movistar) all finished in the same group as the podium finishers to round out the top ten, separated from Wiebes by ten seconds or less.

Wiebes's stage win also hands her the green points jersey with 50 points to start the race. Frenchwoman Océane Mahé, of the Ma Petite Entreprise team, claimed the polka-dot mountains jersey after sweeping maximum points on the stage's earlier categorised climbs, finishing the day on eight points ahead of Idoia Eraso.

The white jersey for best young rider went to 23-year-old Spaniard Paula Blasi of UAE Team L'IMAD, who finished in the same time as the GC group. Blasi arrives in career-best form, having won the Vuelta Femenina overall after overhauling Anna van der Breggen on the Angliru, plus victories at the Tour Féminin des Pyrénées and Volta a Catalunya — though her team has said she will ride in support of its designated leaders rather than for the overall this fortnight.

Saturday's stage opened the fifth edition of the Tour de France Femmes, which runs through August 9 across nine stages and 1,174.7 kilometres — the longest route and most total climbing in the race's short history — before a first-ever summit finish atop Mont Ventoux and a closing circuit race in Nice.

Paula Blasi (UAE Team L'IMAD), the reigning Vuelta Femenina champion, leads the best young rider (white jersey) classification.
Laura Tomasi abandoned the race after a crash and concussion assessment — the first abandonment of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes.
The 2026 Tour de France Femmes is the race's fifth edition, running August 1–9 over nine stages and 1,174.7km, the longest route in its history.

body: Hapoel Holon have added another piece to their frontcourt for next season, announcing the signing of American forward Brandon Johns Jr. from Portuguese club Sporting CP, according to a report by ONE.

Johns, 26, stands 2.03m and is described by the club as a versatile power forward capable of playing both interior positions, a profile Holon has been actively targeting as they rebuild their roster for the 2026/27 Israeli Basketball Super League season.

The signing comes as Holon reshapes its squad around Kronitz, who was handed a contract extension through the 2027/28 season after steering the club through a turbulent 2025/26 campaign. title: Ron Boaron keeps finding the net — on the pitch and in Israel's Special Olympics football
dek: The 31-year-old Liga Gimel striker splits his week between scoring goals for Hapoel Ramat Yisrael, coaching Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth ranks and running Special Olympics Israel's football programme.

verificationSources.label: ONE - נהנה להבקיע: רון בוארון כובש גם במגרש החברתי

body: Ron Boaron's week does not fit neatly into one job description. At 31, he is still turning out as a centre-forward in Liga Gimel, Israel's third tier, while also coaching Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth ranks and, for the past year, running Special Olympics Israel's football programme. According to ONE, he has no intention of giving up any of the three.

On the pitch, Boaron plays for Hapoel Ramat Yisrael in the Tel Aviv district section of Liga Gimel, where ONE reports he has scored 27 goals across his last two seasons. Before joining the club, he turned out for Hapoel Tzafririm Holon and Spartak Rishon LeZion, and he came up through the youth systems of Maccabi Yehud and Maccabi Hashekem Chen.

Boaron's coaching career has grown alongside his playing one. He started as an assistant with Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth section before being promoted to head coach of the club's Under-13 boys' team, a role he now combines with his own playing commitments and match days.

He describes the overlap between the roles as feeding into itself rather than pulling him in different directions: playing keeps him close to the game at grassroots level, coaching sharpens how he reads it, and both inform his newest job — building an inclusive football structure for athletes with intellectual disabilities.

A year into that post, Boaron coordinates Special Olympics Israel's football branch, which runs the Ligat Shavim inclusive league in partnership with the Israel Football Association. It is a programme built around unified teams, where athletes with and without intellectual disabilities play alongside one another.

The highlight of his year in the role came in Paris, where he helped organise Israel's Special Olympics unified squad for the World Championships. The team finished fourth — a result independently confirmed by the Jerusalem Post, which reported that Israel's unified side, competing under the name Toto Equals, reached the semi-finals of the Special Olympics Unified Football World Cup before finishing in fourth place overall.

ONE quotes Boaron describing the Special Olympics work as a calling rather than just a job, a sentiment that runs through how he talks about all three of his football lives — playing, coaching and now administration.

Looking ahead, Boaron told ONE his priority is not chasing a move up Israel's football pyramid himself, but continuing to develop young players through Maccabi Petah Tikva's academy while growing the Special Olympics football programme he now oversees.

title: Golan Druze club Bnei Mamba's youth team wins league title, dedicates it to Majdal Shams victims
dek: A year after a Hezbollah rocket killed three of the club's own teenage players on a Majdal Shams football pitch, Bnei Mamba's youth side won 19 of 20 matches to top the Northern District and return to the national tier after a four-year absence.

verificationSources.label: Zman Yisrael - club history and the Majdal Shams attack
Times of Israel - Majdal Shams attack

body: A year on from the darkest day in its history, Bnei Mamba's youth team has given the Druze villages of the Golan Heights something to celebrate. The club, representing Majdal Shams, Mas'ada, Buq'ata and Ein Qiniyye, has won the Northern District's Liga HaAlufot youth championship, sealing an emphatic return to Israel's national league structure after four years away.

The numbers tell their own story of dominance: 19 wins from 20 matches, 103 goals scored and just 20 conceded. Bnei Mamba finished level on points with Hapoel Arraba but claimed top spot on a superior win percentage, 95% to 90%, with Hapoel Matte Asher a further six points back in third.
Tiam Rabah led the goalscoring charts with 22, with Lian Turbiyeh close behind on 20, according to ONE's report on the season.

But for a club founded in 2015 to give the four Druze communities a shared footballing home, the number that matters most this season has nothing to do with the table. On July 27 last year, a Hezbollah rocket struck a football pitch in Majdal Shams during a youth match, killing 12 children and teenagers and wounding dozens more in the deadliest single attack on northern Israel since the war began. Three of the dead, Amir Abu Salah, Johnny Abrahim and Hazem Abu Salah, wore Bnei Mamba's colours.
"We dedicate this achievement to those killed in the Majdal Shams disaster," said Wajdi Alqish, the club's professional manager and one of its longest-serving figures, after the title was confirmed.

Alqish also pointed to what carried the squad through a season played in the shadow of grief. "The family atmosphere characterising this team, the friendship and love among players and supportive parents, were the added value," he said, crediting head coach Akram Ibrahim's staff for rebuilding a group that had to return to competition only months after burying teammates.

The title carries symbolic weight beyond the Golan's football pitches. Bnei Mamba was built as a bridge for a younger Druze generation more open to engagement with Israeli institutions than their parents, many of whom for decades declined Israeli identity documents in favour of ties across the Syrian border. A youth side from four small villages topping a national-tier table, a year after burying three of its own, is being read locally as proof the project survived its hardest test.

Promotion now sends Bnei Mamba's youth ranks back into the higher national league from which they had been absent since 2022, giving the villages a bigger stage for a generation of players who returned to training with an empty space in the squad that no result can fill.

The club scored 103 goals and conceded 20; it topped the table over Hapoel Arraba on win percentage (95% to 90%) after finishing level on points, with Hapoel Matte Asher third.
Top scorer Tiam Rabah netted 22 goals, with Lian Turbiyeh scoring 20, per ONE.
The title secures Bnei Mamba's return to Israel's national youth league tier after a four-year absence.
Bnei Mamba represents the four Druze communities of Majdal Shams, Mas'ada, Buq'ata and Ein Qiniyye in the Golan Heights and was founded in 2015.

On July 27, 2024, a Hezbollah rocket hit a football pitch in Majdal Shams during a youth match, killing 12 children and teenagers, including three Bnei Mamba players: Amir Abu Salah, Johnny Abrahim and Hazem Abu Salah.
Professional manager Wajdi Alqish dedicated the championship to the victims of the attack.

title: Eli Segev, former Maccabi Netanya owner, dies at 73
dek: The businessman, who steered Netanya back into the Israeli Premier League during a brief and turbulent spell in charge, suffered a stroke in Johannesburg before his condition turned fatal, ONE reports.
body: Eli Segev, the businessman who owned Maccabi Netanya during one of the more chaotic chapters of the club's recent history, has died at the age of 73, ONE reported on Saturday.
According to the outlet, Segev suffered a stroke in Johannesburg, South Africa, on Tuesday. His condition subsequently deteriorated, and he died as a result of heart failure.

Segev bought into Maccabi Netanya together with fellow businessman Yossi Maor ahead of the 2013-14 season, when the club was playing in the second-tier Liga Leumit. In their first campaign at the helm, the pair guided Netanya straight back up into the Israeli Premier League.

The promotion did little to settle the club. ONE notes that Segev's short reign was marked by upheaval on and off the pitch, including a mid-season managerial change that saw Yossi Mizrahi replaced by Roni Levy.

Segev walked away from Maccabi Netanya in November 2014, saying at the time that his involvement with the club and its management had "directly and significantly damaged" his private business interests.
His ties to Israeli football predated the Netanya venture by decades: Segev's first foray into the sport came in the 1980s, when he spent roughly two years working with Hapoel Haifa.
After cutting ties with Netanya, Segev moved his business dealings to South Africa, where he had been based in the years leading up to his death.

The stakes in Tulcea are significant for Israel. Twenty nations were split into four groups of five for Division B, with the top two finishers in each section advancing to the quarterfinals and the leading three teams overall in line for promotion back to Division A, FIBA's tournament preview notes.

Group B also contains Bulgaria and Ukraine, meaning results against Switzerland and Norway will weigh heavily on whether Israel's youngsters can finish among the section's top two and keep their promotion hopes alive.

title: Trabzonspor make audacious move for Salah as Pitarch nears Fulham switch
dek: The Turkish champions have reportedly offered the Egyptian superstar a lucrative two-year deal, while Real Madrid's Thiago Pitarch edges towards reuniting with Álvaro Arbeloa at Craven Cottage.
body: Two of European football's more intriguing late-summer sagas took a step forward on Saturday, with ONE reporting that Trabzonspor have tabled a stunning offer for Mohamed Salah, even as Real Madrid's teenage midfielder Thiago Pitarch edges closer to joining Fulham.

According to the report, Trabzonspor moved for Salah once talks over an alternative Süper Lig destination, Beşiktaş, stalled. The Turkish side are said to have proposed a two-year contract worth around €17 million a season, with the Egyptian forward's camp reportedly reacting positively to the terms.

ONE's report adds that Salah is expected to consult his family before making any decision on his next move, with his current Liverpool deal edging toward its end and a switch away from Anfield increasingly framed in Turkish media as a live possibility.

The picture is far from settled, however. Trabzonspor president Ertuğrul Doğan has publicly and repeatedly rejected the idea that a deal is close, telling Turkish outlets in the past two days that Salah 'is not on our agenda' and that 'there is no agreement' with the player, despite the swirl of reports linking the two parties.

That contradiction — a reported offer and a positive player reaction on one side, a flat denial from the club's own president on the other — means the story remains very much a developing one rather than a done deal, and should be read with that caveat.

In a separate transfer thread, Fulham are reported to be closing in on a deal for Pitarch, the 18-year-old Real Madrid midfielder who made his first-team debut for the Spanish giants in February under then-coach Álvaro Arbeloa.

Arbeloa left Real Madrid this summer and was appointed Fulham's head coach in July, and the Craven Cottage club has already leaned heavily on that connection: Fulham agreed a reported €50 million package with Real Madrid in recent weeks to sign attacking pair Gonzalo García and César Palacios, both graduates of the same Real Madrid Castilla group Arbeloa oversaw.

Pitarch would be the third of that group to follow Arbeloa to west London. Reports in the Spanish press describe him as keen on the reunion, though he is currently carrying a knock, and Real Madrid are said to be weighing whether a move abroad would benefit his development — with the possibility of a buy-back option built into any deal, mirroring the structure used for García and Palacios.
Neither transfer has been confirmed by any of the clubs involved, and both stories should be treated as reports rather than completed business for now.

title: Inter beat Manchester City 3-1 on penalties as Maresca's reign begins with defeat
dek: Divin Mubama and Benjamin Pavard traded early goals in a 1-1 draw at the Hong Kong Football Festival before Inter held their nerve from the spot against a City side missing three penalties in a row.
body: Enzo Maresca's first game in charge of Manchester City ended the way so many of Pep Guardiola's cup ties used to: on penalties, and this time on the losing side. Inter Milan came from behind to draw 1-1 in Hong Kong on Saturday and then won the shootout 3-1, spoiling the new manager's debut at the Hong Kong Football Festival.

City made the brighter start at the Kai Tak Stadium, with 42,826 inside the new venue to watch the sides open their pre-season campaigns. New signing Antoine Semenyo, a £62.5million arrival from Bournemouth, drove down the left and squared for Divin Mubama to tap in from close range in the 14th minute.
Inter needed only six more minutes to respond. A cross from Jamal Iddrissou was not properly cleared by the City defence, and Benjamin Pavard reacted first inside the box to level it at 1-1.

Neither side found a second goal despite half-chances after the break — Vitor Reis struck the crossbar and Ryan McAidoo hit the post for City — and the match went to penalties, as pre-season friendlies at the tournament are decided rather than ending in a draw.

There City fell apart from twelve yards. Rayan Ait-Nouri, Abdukodir Khusanov and Nico all missed in succession, leaving only Claudio Echeverri to convert for the English side. Inter made no such mistake, with Piotr Zieliński, Mattia Mosconi and Matteo Lavelli all scoring to seal a 3-1 shootout win.

It capped an eventful few weeks at the Etihad, where Maresca replaced Guardiola after the Catalan's decade in charge yielded 20 trophies including the treble. "Many positive things, especially minutes for the legs which at this moment is important," Maresca said afterwards. "In two weeks we have the first official game so it's important to prepare the legs and body. I am happy with the performance."
Semenyo, making his first appearance since completing his move from Bournemouth in the winter window, was named the game's outstanding performer for his work down the left flank in the first half.

For Inter, the result offers an early marker under their own new-look squad ahead of the coming Serie A season, with the club still missing several first-team regulars who were involved deep into this summer's World Cup.

title: Arbitrator reverses himself, slashes Hapoel Hadera's training fee for defender Abdach by more than half
dek: Dr. Dan Chai cut his own compensation award for young defender Bashar Abdach from 325,000 to 140,000 shekels just six days after the original ruling, ONE reports, easing the path for the 20-year-old to leave the relegated club.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Hapoel Hadera exercises Abdach option

body: It is not every day that a football arbitrator changes his mind about his own ruling, let alone slashes it by more than half inside a week. But that is exactly what happened in the dispute over Hapoel Hadera's training compensation for young defender Bashar Abdach, ONE reports.

Dr. Dan Chai, one of the arbitrators who sit on Israeli football's Player Status Institution, issued his first decision on July 14, ordering that Abdach's training compensation — the fee due to the club that developed a player when he moves on — be set at 325,000 shekels.

Six days later, on July 20, after receiving further detailed submissions from the parties, Chai returned with a sharply revised figure: 140,000 shekels, a cut of more than 57 percent from his original number.

The reasoning for the reversal centred on the fact that, according to ONE, "no concrete receiving club was presented" to the panel — meaning there was no signed contract or defined salary terms from a professional side lined up to take Abdach, which undercut the case for a high valuation.
The ruling also weighed Abdach's thin track record at the top level: barely more than a dozen senior appearances, hardly the resume that commands a six-figure training fee on its own.

Abdach, a 20-year-old centre-back, is very much a Hapoel Hadera product. He joined the club's academy at 14 and a half, made his senior debut last season, and had his contract option exercised by the club as recently as 2025, according to Walla Sport.

His timing has not been kind to Hadera. The club won promotion to the Ligat Leumit for the 2025-26 season only to finish bottom of the table and drop straight down to Liga Alef, ending a seven-year absence from the third tier. A smaller squad and a shrinking budget make it easy to see why a promising academy defender wants to move on, and why the club, in turn, is fighting hard to extract every shekel it can from his departure.

For Hadera, the revised ruling is a serious financial setback, cutting the expected windfall from a player they nurtured for years. For Abdach, it removes a significant obstacle: a lower training fee makes him a cheaper, more attractive signing for whichever club ultimately takes him on.

The Player Status Institution's rulings are not standard football-desk fare, but this one matters because it shows just how much discretion a single arbitrator wields over a young player's market value — and how quickly that number can move once both sides make their case in full.

dek: Bryan Mbeumo's penalty and late winner turned around a preseason final in Stockholm after Arnau Ortiz's early opener, ONE reports, as United sharpen their form before the new Premier League season.
body: Manchester United came from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 at Stockholm's Strawberry Arena on Saturday, with Bryan Mbeumo scoring both goals to seal the preseason Snapdragon Cup and extend his impressive start since arriving from Brentford, ONE reported under the headline "Continuing to impress."

Arnau Ortiz put Atletico ahead inside five minutes, curling a shot from outside the box beyond the United goalkeeper and into the far corner — a sharp, early blow for a Red Devils side still building match sharpness for the new season.
United needed until the 53rd minute to respond. Mbeumo stepped up and calmly converted from the penalty spot after Jorge Castillo was penalized for a foul on Shea Lacey inside the area.

The Cameroon international struck again in the 74th minute, turning home a low delivery from Jack Fletcher's work down the right to complete his double and flip the contest United's way. Atletico's best chance to level again came when Rodrigo Mendoza's header cannoned back off the post.
The victory settled the Snapdragon Cup, one of several summer friendlies United have used to build fitness and combinations before the competitive campaign resumes.

Player-of-the-match honors went to Mason Mount, whose display drew praise from former United winger Ben Thornley on MUTV: "It's a superb performance from him. In general, it's been an all-round excellent team performance."

Mbeumo's brace continues a strong opening chapter at Old Trafford. The winger arrived from Brentford last summer in a deal reportedly worth up to £71 million, quickly became a first-choice starter, and finished the 2025-26 season as United's joint-top league scorer with 11 goals, level with Benjamin Sesko.

With preseason winding down, United face two more notable tests before the season proper: two-time reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on August 8, then Leeds United at Dublin's Croke Park on August 12. The Premier League campaign opens for United at home to Hull City on August 22.

title: AS Monaco basketball club excluded from French leagues after financial collapse
dek: Reigning Betclic Elite champions are barred from both French divisions for 2026-27 after owner Alexey Fedorychev's assets were frozen and a Jamal Mashburn-led rescue bid missed its deadline.
body: AS Monaco's basketball club, the reigning champions of France's Betclic Elite, has been formally excluded from both the top flight and the second-tier Elite 2 for the 2026-27 season, ONE reports — a stunning fall for a team that lifted the domestic title only weeks earlier.

The French Basketball Federation's appeals chamber confirmed the ban after rejecting Monaco's challenge to an initial ruling by the league's financial oversight body, the DNCCG, which had found the Roca Team unable to guarantee its economic viability for the coming season.

The collapse traces back to the club's principal owner and sponsor, Alexey Fedorychev, whose assets have been frozen amid an international legal case linked to Ukraine. Italian authorities in Florence reportedly seized around €41 million of his holdings, cutting off the funding that had underwritten Monaco's budget.
Without that backing, the club fell heavily into arrears — reports put its debts at roughly €24 million — and was hit with delayed wages and EuroLeague fines even as it kept winning on the court.

A rescue plan did emerge. Former NBA All-Star Jamal Mashburn fronted an investor group that reached an agreement with Monaco's ruling family, proposing to slash the club's budget from more than €38 million to somewhere between €10 million and €12.5 million, along with fresh banking guarantees.

It was not enough, or not in time. The appeals chamber had already granted Monaco a series of extensions — a hearing on July 20, then a final deadline of July 31 — to file the required documentation. The federation said the club "was not able to produce the requested documents within the given timeframe," automatically confirming the sanction.

The exclusion strips Monaco of a place in either division at a stroke, just weeks after the club won its third Betclic Elite title in four seasons and stood as one of the wealthiest, most successful outfits in European basketball.

It carries consequences beyond France, too. Monaco has been a regular in the EuroLeague, and reporting around the case points to the club being steered toward a five-year EuroCup license instead — a marked step down — while French basketball stands to lose one of its EuroLeague places as a result.

Monaco has not exhausted its options. A club in this position can still contest a federation ruling before France's national Olympic committee and, ultimately, the administrative courts, though nothing in the reporting so far suggests that route is likely to reverse the decision before the new season begins.

For now, the reigning champions of France have no league in which to defend their title — a stark illustration of how quickly a club's fortunes can turn when its financing rests on a single benefactor.

title: Solomon shines again for Tottenham, but English media say he still isn't used enough
dek: The Israeli winger set up Sandro Tonali's opener in a preseason win over Chelsea in Sydney, drawing praise from British reporters even as his camp pushes for a permanent exit this summer
body: Manor Solomon did what he usually does when Tottenham give him a run-out: he made things happen. And once again, the reaction from around the club afterwards was the same familiar refrain — why isn't he playing more?

ONE reports that the Israeli winger was one of the standout performers as Tottenham beat Chelsea 2-1 in Sydney on Saturday, a preseason friendly billed as part of the Sydney Super Cup and the first time the London rivals have met outside the UK in 117 years of fixtures between them.

Solomon supplied the assist for the opening goal, driving forward on a quick break down the right before feeding Sandro Tonali on the edge of the box. Tonali's first-time effort took a deflection off Levi Colwill that wrong-footed Chelsea goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe and rolled in — the new club-record signing's first goal for Spurs. Estevao equalised for Chelsea within two minutes, before Tottenham, reduced to ten men after Kevin Danso's second-half red card for a foul on Joao Pedro, held on for a Richarlison winner deep into injury time.

It was Solomon's contribution that caught the eye of the English press, according to ONE. Football London gave him a match rating of 7 and wrote plainly: "Manor Solomon looked lively, Tottenham don't use him enough." The same outlet noted he was one of the few Tottenham players who consistently exploited the team's rapid transitions in Sydney.

ONE also cites the BBC praising Solomon's "great assist with an accurate wide delivery" for the Tonali goal, while a Tottenham supporters' site singled out the intelligence of his pass into the Italian's path. The consensus across the coverage was that Solomon offered something different going forward — even in a match his team ultimately won playing a man short for most of the second half.

The underuse question, though, is not a new one, and it comes with real stakes attached this summer. Solomon's agent, Ronen Katzav, told reporters in late July that his client wants a permanent move away from Tottenham this transfer window, having spent recent seasons away from north London on loan in search of regular football.

That search paid off in the Championship: on loan at Leeds United in 2024-25, Solomon contributed 10 goals and 12 assists in 39 league appearances as Leeds won the title and returned to the Premier League. It was easily his most productive extended run of club football since his Shakhtar Donetsk days.

West Ham United have been named among the clubs monitoring his situation, with the transfer window's 1 September deadline still weeks away and no resolution reported yet on his future at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

That is the backdrop against which Saturday's cameo landed. A player angling for an exit producing his team's assist of the match, and being told publicly by English reporters that his own club isn't using him properly, is an awkward but familiar contradiction for Solomon — evidence, depending on who you ask, either that he still has a role to play in north London or that his talent is being wasted on the fringes.

title: More than $20,000 a ticket: US Open prices hit record highs
dek: Resale seats for the men's final at Flushing Meadows have topped $20,900, according to ONE, as tennis grapples with an affordability gap even as prize money and revenue keep climbing.

verificationSources.label: Forbes - 2024 US Open by the numbers
Yahoo Sports - US Open ticket prices

body: The US Open does not begin until August 31, but the numbers around it are already breaking records — and not just on court. ONE reports that resale tickets for the men's singles final on September 13 have topped $20,900, the highest price ever recorded for a seat at the tournament.

It is not only the marquee final driving the market. According to the report, a courtside seat for an exhibition featuring Roger Federer is going for close to $12,000, while even a first-round ticket in the vast Arthur Ashe Stadium can run past $400. A basic grounds pass, by contrast, still starts at $65.

Independent tracking of the resale market backs up the scale of the surge: some listings for the 2026 men's final have been quoted as high as $30,000, with over 430,000 fans reportedly in the queue for presale access to Ashe for that match alone.

The prices sit against a backdrop of extraordinary financial growth for the tournament's organiser. The United States Tennis Association reported $623.8 million in revenue for 2024, with $559.6 million of that generated by the US Open itself, and an operating profit above $277 million.

Prize money has climbed sharply too. ONE cites a total purse of $90 million for the tournament, a 20 percent jump on the previous year, with singles champions each collecting $5 million — figures that mirror the well-documented rise in Grand Slam payouts as players push for a bigger share of Slam revenues.

The tension between those two trends — soaring ticket prices for fans and rising, but still contested, prize money for players — is the crux of the report. As ONE puts it, the biggest matches at the sport's showcase events are increasingly "accessible only to wealthy individuals and commercial enterprises."

Some of that revenue is being funnelled into the site itself. The USTA is in the middle of an $800 million renovation of the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows, rebuilding Arthur Ashe Stadium's interior, adding roughly 2,000 courtside seats and a new player performance centre, funded entirely by the governing body with no city money involved. The project is due for completion in 2027.

For now, though, the story at Flushing Meadows this summer is less about the tennis and more about what it costs to watch it — a dynamic organisers will be reminded of again once the gates open in four weeks.

title: Bangkok United 1-0 Chiang Mai: Yonatan Cohen scores winner on early outing for Thai club
dek: The Israeli winger, unveiled by Bangkok United last month, struck in the 11th minute to settle a preseason friendly against Chiang Mai.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - Cohen signs for Bangkok United

body: Yonatan Cohen needed only 11 minutes to make his mark in Bangkok United colours, scoring the only goal as the Thai club beat Chiang Mai 1-0 in a preseason friendly on Saturday, ONE reported.

The Israeli attacking midfielder was handed an early chance to impress and took it, finishing off a move to settle the contest before the hour mark had even arrived. It was a tidy first statement for a player still finding his feet at a new club in a new country.

Cohen completed his move to Bangkok United last month on a one-year deal, with Sport5 reporting his salary at around €300,000 for the season. He was officially unveiled in the club's kit shortly afterwards.

The switch to Thailand is the third stop abroad for the 30-year-old, who previously spent the 2021/22 season with Pisa in Italy's Serie B and 2024/25 with Melbourne City in Australia's A-League, where he scored in the club's title-winning campaign.

Before heading to Thailand, Cohen spent last season back home with Hapoel Petah Tikva, contributing four goals in 22 appearances as the club returned to the Israeli Premier League. Earlier in his career he won three championships with Maccabi Tel Aviv and two cups split between the yellow-and-blue and Beitar Jerusalem.

For Bangkok United, the friendly serves as part of preparations for the coming Thai League 1 campaign, with Cohen expected to add creativity from the flank as the club builds its squad around its new Israeli signing.
A single goal in a summer friendly will not define his time in Thailand, but for a player only just settling in, an early winner is exactly the kind of start he would have wanted.

title: Portugal 30-22 Israel: youth handball team drop into placement round at European Championship
dek: Israel's under-18 men's side were level at half-time in Belgrade but faded badly after the break, closing Group C's preliminary round with a single point at the M18 EHF Euro.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 European Men's U-18 Handball Championship

body: Israel's men's under-18 handball team saw their preliminary-round campaign at the European Championship unravel on Saturday, going down 30-22 to Portugal in Belgrade in their final Group C fixture, ONE reported.

The result leaves Israel with just a single point from three games at the M18 EHF Euro, the continental youth championship being staged across Serbia through August 9. Group C also threw up a 33-29 defeat to Croatia and a draw with the Czech Republic, meaning the young Israelis now drop into the tournament's lower bracket rather than fighting for a top-eight finish.
For long stretches the Portugal game looked winnable. Israel matched their more fancied opponents shot for shot in the first half, with the teams locked at 15-15 heading into the break.

The second half told a different story. Portugal's offence found its rhythm and Israel's finishing and defensive shape both dropped off, with the visitors from the Iberian Peninsula pulling steadily clear to close out an eight-goal win.

Jonathan Pelech was Israel's standout performer, finishing as the game's top scorer with eight goals from 24 attempts — a busy, if not always efficient, night in attack. Nevo Masika chipped in four goals, while goalkeeper Ruben Ouanono mixed saves at the other end with a goal of his own.

The tournament format means the top 14 finishers across all groups qualify for the World Championship, while the bottom four sides face relegation from the top tier altogether — a scenario Israel will now be working hard to avoid.

Israel's exact finishing position in Group C, third or fourth, was still to be determined at the time of writing, hinging on the outcome of Saturday's late meeting between Croatia and the Czech Republic. That result will also decide who Israel face next as they aim for the placement matches that lead to a 9-16 finish rather than the bottom bracket.

It is a tougher path than the young Israelis would have wanted after their opening exchanges against Portugal suggested they could compete with the group's strongest sides — but a heavy second-half collapse has instead sent them chasing damage control for the rest of the week in Serbia.

title: From Kfar Chabad's yeshiva to Liga Alef: Hapoel Marmorek's new left-back Shnior Sofer
dek: A 25-year-old who didn't kick a ball in an organised league until he was 16 has turned down bigger offers to join Danny Tolmasov's rebuilding project in Rehovot.
body: Not every signing announcement comes with a conversion story, but Hapoel Marmorek Rehovot's newest full-back has one worth telling. Shnior Sofer, 25, has put pen to paper with the Liga Alef club, and as ONE reports, his path to organised football only began at an age when most professionals are already established.

Sofer grew up as a yeshiva student in Kfar Chabad, the Chabad-Lubavitch community near Lod, and by his own account never played in a structured league as a boy. "Until age 16, I never played in a professional framework at all," he told ONE, describing a late start that makes his current trajectory all the more unusual.

That changed when he joined the youth ranks at Nahalat Yehuda, his entry point into competitive Israeli football. From there he worked his way into the senior game at Hapoel Ashdod, breaking through with a season that produced ten goals, according to the report, before a brief stint further north with Umm el-Fahm in Liga Alef North.

Now he moves to the club's southern equivalent, joining a Marmorek side that, per ONE, is bracing for a demanding season under coach Danny Tolmasov, who is trying to build a competitive squad on a limited budget simply to hold the team's place in the division.

Sofer, who plays as an attacking left-back, said the decision to sign came down to trust rather than money. He turned down offers with higher wages, telling ONE he chose Marmorek because he knows Tolmasov from before and believes the coach's belief in him will pay off on the pitch.
His transfer was arranged through his representative, attorney Shai Avni, according to the Rehovot outlet BE106, which also confirmed the move to the Marmorek defence.

For his own season, Sofer has set himself ambitious personal targets: 12 goals and 15 assists from full-back, along with regular 90-minute appearances. It's the kind of statement more often heard from an attacker than a defender, but it fits a player who sees the position as a platform to attack from rather than just defend.

Beyond this season, his stated aim is a breakout campaign that opens the door to professional football, whether that ends up being in Israel's higher divisions or overseas. For a club fighting to stay afloat in Liga Alef South, a player with that hunger — and that story — is a useful addition regardless of the numbers he ultimately posts.

title: Nasty, aggressive and precise: Daniel Worko's road into Beitar Jerusalem's lineup
dek: From night shifts at a gas station to Israel's Under-20 side, the young midfielder repaid Beitar's faith after a shaky start at Hapoel Ramat Gan.
body: A little over a year ago, Daniel Worko was a fringe figure at Hapoel Ramat Gan, working night shifts at a gas station to make ends meet while trying to force his way into a struggling lower-league side. Today, ONE reports, he is a fixture in Beitar Jerusalem's starting lineup — one of the more improbable breakthroughs in Israeli football this year.

Worko was not always the player Beitar signed. At Ramat Gan he began as a winger before coach Oren Kadosh pulled him back into a deeper role, using him as a defensive midfielder and playmaker in the number six position. According to ONE, those around the club describe him bluntly: nasty in the tackle, relentlessly aggressive, unafraid of bigger opponents, and precise on the ball — with an appetite for coaching and self-improvement that stood out even before anyone outside Ramat Gan was paying attention.

The early signs were not promising. ONE reports that Worko scored an own goal in his senior debut and, by his own admission, spent weeks doubting whether he belonged at that level. He kept working — including those overnight shifts behind a cash register — and kept training, and the performances gradually caught up with the ability his coaches saw in him.

The breakthrough came through an eye-catching season in Ramat Gan's midfield, one strong enough to earn Worko a call-up to Israel's Under-20 national team under coach Guy Luzon. That recognition, ONE notes, is what first put him firmly on Beitar Jerusalem's radar.

Signing him was not straightforward. ONE reports that Beitar's professional director, Almog Cohen, had to convince club owner Barak Abramov that Worko was worth more than a squad-filling backup, while Hapoel Ramat Gan initially demanded as much as 1.2 million shekels in compensation for a player who was set to become a free agent. Beitar ultimately paid 240,000 shekels to complete the deal, according to ONE — a figure that, if confirmed by the Israel Football Association's player status committee, would represent a considerable saving on Ramat Gan's opening demand.

Other outlets covering the original transfer gave a similar picture with slightly different numbers: Sport5 reported Ramat Gan had sought around one million shekels in "appreciation fees," with the final sum left for the player status committee to decide, while Walla! Sport confirmed the compensation issue was still open when the deal was announced.

Worko signed a three-year contract with Beitar, with an option for a fourth, on wages of roughly 20,000 shekels a month before bonuses — a salary Walla! Sport reported was set to rise each year of the deal. "I am very happy and excited to fulfill a dream and arrive next season at Beitar Jerusalem," he said at the time, quoted by Walla! Sport, while also making clear his immediate priority was different: helping Hapoel Ramat Gan win promotion before he left.

Beitar's football management made no secret of their ambitions for him. Ynet reported that the club's hierarchy expected Worko to play a "significant role" in the squad from his very first season in Jerusalem, rather than serve as a bit-part option behind more experienced midfielders.

That expectation has now been met. Worko has moved from unknown lower-league discovery to a player Beitar's coaching staff trust in their first-choice midfield — a rapid rise that, ONE's report makes clear, was built less on natural talent alone than on the grinding work ethic that got him through those gas-station shifts in the first place.

title: UEFA says it has lost confidence in Infantino as scrapped World Cup investment plan sparks resignation calls
dek: European football's governing body says the FIFA president has lost the trust of "the football family" after his push to sell a stake in World Cup profits to private investors collapsed under a threatened boycott and a wave of internal resignations.
body: Gianni Infantino is facing the deepest crisis of his FIFA presidency after abandoning a plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private investors, with UEFA declaring it has lost confidence in his leadership, ONE reports.

The Israeli outlet's report, headlined "Infantino has lost control, he must resign," reflects a week of open revolt inside world football's governing body that culminated in FIFA scrapping the scheme on Friday.

The plan, known internally as FIFA Forward Enterprise, would have sold roughly a 20 percent stake in World Cup commercial profits to a group of private investors led by Joshua Kushner's Thrive Eternal, based on a valuation of around $20 billion and designed to raise about $4.2 billion for FIFA.

In exchange, member federations were promised $20 million each upfront, doubling their existing $10 million commitments, rising to $22 million through 2034 and $24 million through 2038, according to reporting on the proposal's terms.

UEFA led the resistance, voting 55-0 among its member associations to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the World Cup itself, if the sale went ahead. "Some things are simply too important to sell," the European body said. "The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will."

UEFA went further this week, stating plainly that "the current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family" — language read across Europe as a direct call for Infantino to step aside or face a formal no-confidence vote.

The pressure has been compounded from inside FIFA's own Zurich headquarters. Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino's senior adviser and a former Goldman Sachs banker who had represented FIFA on the White House task force for the 2026 World Cup, resigned in protest, saying: "I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup."

FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, then issued his own extraordinary statement to the Associated Press, saying staff had been "deceived" by the secrecy around the deal and describing it as "the project of one person." Lamour did not resign but said the moment called for football's political leaders "to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions," adding: "if that means I lose my job then so be it."

CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation also issued statements rejecting the investment plan, though neither went as far as UEFA's boycott threat, leaving Infantino more isolated among the continental confederations that underpin his political base.

Infantino confirmed on Friday that FIFA was dropping the proposal, saying the divisions it had caused had become counterproductive. He has not resigned and has given no public indication that he intends to, instead signalling a wish to keep working with his critics.

His position is not immediately at legal risk: the next FIFA presidential election is scheduled for March 19, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco, with the deadline for rival candidacies falling on November 18 this year. Any move by UEFA to force him out before then would likely require an extraordinary congress or a formal no-confidence mechanism that has never previously been tested against a sitting FIFA president.

For now, the episode has left Infantino's authority visibly diminished less than three weeks after he presided over the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup — and has handed UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin, long a rival power centre within world football's governance, a rare position of open leverage over FIFA's leadership.

title: Birmingham City beat Barcelona on penalties after 2-2 draw, but Adeyemi's debut impresses
dek: Karim Adeyemi played 45 minutes on the right wing in Barcelona's pre-season friendly at Birmingham City, and while Hansi Flick's side lost the shootout, Catalan media gave the new signing's first outing an encouraging review.
body: Karim Adeyemi's first outing in a Barcelona shirt ended in defeat, but it was the German winger's own performance, not the scoreline, that dominated the Catalan press the morning after.

Barcelona lost 3-2 on penalties to Birmingham City at St Andrew's on July 31 after the pre-season friendly finished 2-2 following 90 minutes, but Hansi Flick handed Adeyemi a full 45 minutes on the right flank as part of a plan to split the squad across two different lineups and get an early look at his new signing.
ONE reported that Adeyemi announced himself early, setting up a promising chance for Ferran Torres inside the first five minutes with an incisive pass that almost produced a goal.

According to the Spanish daily Sport, cited by ONE, Adeyemi showed "speed, constant movement forward and a personality to demand the ball" during his time on the pitch, with the paper's verdict summed up as a player who "passed the first test."

The Catalan coverage framed the display as reason for optimism among Barcelona supporters, even without a goal or assist to his name, pointing to his work rate and willingness to track back as much as his attacking threat.

Adeyemi joined Barcelona from Borussia Dortmund earlier in July after around a week of training with his new teammates before Flick opted to fast-track him into the starting XI for the trip to England. Reported figures for the transfer fee have varied by outlet and have not been confirmed by either club.

The friendly itself was a lively one: Birmingham took the lead through August Priske's header from an Alex Cochrane cross before Barcelona hit back twice, only for the English side to level again and eventually prevail in the shootout, with goalkeeper James Beadle the hero with two saves.
Jude Bellingham, who came through Birmingham's academy before his move to Borussia Dortmund and now stars for Real Madrid, was in the stands to watch his old club take on Barcelona.
For Adeyemi, the result mattered far less than the impression left in his 45 minutes — an early marker as Flick's squad continues its preparations before the new season.

title: Victory boss subsidises Hapoel Beer Sheva fan packages for Red Star Belgrade tie in Hungary
dek: Sponsor Eyal Ravid is cutting €100 off travel packages for the Champions League qualifier, which Hapoel will host in Szombathely rather than at home.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz - Hapoel Beer Sheva advance past Vikingur

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva's main shirt sponsor is putting his hand in his pocket to get more fans on planes for next week's Champions League qualifier against Red Star Belgrade, with the reigning Israeli champions again forced to stage a 'home' European fixture outside the country.

ONE reports that Eyal Ravid, owner and chief executive of the Victory supermarket chain, is personally subsidising €100 off every travel package sold through the Golasso agency for the first leg, dropping the price from €599 to €499 per person. The package covers flights, hotel and a match ticket.

The third qualifying round tie against the Serbian champions will be played in Szombathely, Hungary, where Hapoel have been hosting their continental fixtures rather than at home in Beer Sheva. The second leg follows a week later at Red Star's own stadium in Belgrade.

According to ONE, the club is anxious to maximise the number of traveling Israeli supporters in Hungary, aware that the atmosphere could matter given what is coming in the return leg: Red Star's home crowd regularly numbers in the tens of thousands, and the visit to Belgrade is expected to be an intimidating occasion regardless of the first-leg result.

Red Star arrive in eastern Europe on the back of a 9-0 demolition of their second-round opponents, underlining the scale of the test facing Hapoel, who beat Vikingur Reykjavik 2-0 in the previous round to secure at least a place in next season's Conference League league phase.
ONE also reports a dispute brewing over ticket allocation, with Red Star said to be pushing Hapoel to hand over more than the mandatory 5 percent of tickets reserved for the visiting club's fans.

On team news, left-back Pedro Amador has been included in the squad for the tie, per the report. Winger João Victor, still working his way back from injury, remains a doubt, while defender Gabriel Diouf has been cleared to play after what turned out to be only a minor muscle strain sustained in Hungary.

Victory's sponsorship of Hapoel Beer Sheva has previously extended beyond shirt branding into fan initiatives, including a raffle for European away-trip packages during the club's run in the Europa League against Inter Milan.

title: Rafael Aronov steps into the OKTAGON cage for the first time, live on ONE2 tonight
dek: The Beersheba police officer turned finisher takes on Czech veteran Miroslav Brož in Prague as he debuts for one of Europe's biggest MMA promotions

verificationSources.label: OKTAGON MMA — official OKTAGON 92 event page
The Jerusalem Post — profile of Rafael Aronov

body: Rafael Aronov walks out under the open Prague sky tonight for the biggest fight of his career, making his debut for OKTAGON — one of Europe's largest MMA promotions — on the card at Štvanice island's central tennis stadium.

The bout airs live in Israel on ONE2 at 19:30, with Yaniv Kaminsky and Olga Rubin on commentary, giving local fans a rare chance to watch an Israeli fighter headline this kind of stage on home television.

Aronov, who fights under the nickname "The Cop" for his day job as a police officer in Beersheba, built his reputation in Cage Warriors, where all eight of his career wins have come by stoppage — four knockouts and four submissions, without a single decision needed.

He carries more than a fight record into the cage. Aronov was among the officers who engaged Hamas terrorists in Ofakim during the October 7 attacks, an episode that has become part of how he is introduced to European audiences unfamiliar with his story.

His opponent, Miroslav Brož — known in the Czech scene as "Inkvizitor," the Inquisitor — is a former ice hockey goaltender who played for Slavia Prague and Hradec Králové and represented the Czech national junior team before a career-ending injury pushed him toward MMA in 2013. He has since built a 17-4-1 record and come out of retirement specifically for this bout.

The two meet at an 80kg (176lb) catchweight on a card that OKTAGON has built around Will Fleury against Zelim Muradov for the promotion's light heavyweight title, alongside a women's bantamweight headliner between Lucia Szabová and Lucie Pudilová.
"I've wanted to fight in this organization for a long time," Aronov told ONE ahead of the bout. "It's going to be non-stop action — don't blink."

For Aronov, beating a well-known local name in front of an OKTAGON crowd — an organization built on packing out stadiums with raucous, partisan support — would be the kind of statement debut that turns a Cage Warriors standout into a genuine name on the European circuit.
