title: What actually happens if you do 100 push-ups a day for a month?
dek: ONE's fitness desk breaks down the physical and mental toll of the viral push-up challenge, from the brutal first week to what changes — and what can go wrong — by day 30.

verificationSources.label: Eat This, Not That — 100 push-ups a day for a month results
Built With Science — 100 push-ups a day for 30 days

body: It sounds like a simple enough dare: knock out 100 push-ups a day, every day, for a month, and see what happens. ONE's fitness desk took the challenge apart piece by piece, and the honest answer is that the first fortnight is nothing like the last.

The opening days are the hardest part psychologically as much as physically. Chest, shoulders and arms are left burning with soreness, and ONE's health and fitness editor Shai Lev describes it bluntly as a mental and physical struggle for anyone not already used to high daily rep counts.

That changes as the body adapts. Muscular endurance climbs steadily through the month, and by the back half most people can string together far more reps before needing to break, rather than grinding out sets of ten throughout the day.

The visible payoff shows up in the upper body — a tighter, more defined look through the chest, shoulders and arms. ONE also makes the point that a push-up is really a plank in motion, so the core is working the whole time too, alongside gains in posture and shoulder stability.

None of it is without risk. The piece flags joint overload as the real danger of a daily, unbroken 100 — particularly through the elbows and shoulders — with inflammation or joint pain a realistic outcome for anyone who skips proper form or never lets the joints rest.

Lev is clear that the challenge is decided as much off the floor as on it: protein intake, sleep quality and technique are named as the factors that separate a month of real progress from a month of accumulated strain.

Independent write-ups of similar month-long push-up challenges echo the same arc — a brutal opening stretch, noticeable strength and definition gains by the back half, and the occasional joint niggle for those who push through pain rather than around it.

For ONE, though, the bigger takeaway isn't really physical. The most consistent change reported over 30 days of daily push-ups is the discipline itself — the habit of showing up for a small, hard task every single day. The article carries an explicit caveat that it is written for educational purposes only, and recommends checking with a qualified professional before taking on a challenge like this.

title: Orian Goren shows his class as Barcelona draw 2-2 with Birmingham City
dek: The 17-year-old Israeli midfielder made his second straight senior appearance in a preseason friendly, drawing praise from the Spanish press before Birmingham won the game on penalties.
body: Orian Goren keeps giving Barcelona reasons to talk about him. The 17-year-old from Petah Tikva made his second consecutive appearance for the club's senior side on Friday, coming off the bench in a preseason friendly against Birmingham City and, once again, catching the eye of the Catalan press.

Goren entered in the 62nd minute at St Andrew's, Birmingham's home ground, replacing midfielder Marc Casadó. He played the final 28 minutes as Hansi Flick's understrength squad, missing several first-team regulars during the club's pre-season training camp in England, searched for a way past a determined Championship side in front of a packed house.

The match itself ended in heartbreak for the Spanish champions. August Priske headed Birmingham in front in the first half, before teenage forward Hamza Abdelkarim leveled from the penalty spot and then put Barcelona ahead just after the hour. Jhon Solis dragged Birmingham level again at 2-2 to force a shootout, which the English side won 3-2.

Goren's own contribution drew notice regardless of the result. Barcelona's official website flagged him for showing quality in midfield, and the Spanish sports daily Sport rated him 6 out of 10, writing that he "showed qualities of a good footballer from midfield, but lacked more daring."
Mundo Deportivo was similarly complimentary, noting that the Israeli "sought to impact the match," looking to link play and create chances from the center of the pitch during his cameo.

Flick, asked generally about the group of academy players given minutes against Birmingham, said "the young players showed how good they are" — a nod to the broader crop of La Masia graduates Barcelona is blooding in preseason, Goren among them.

It was the second straight outing with the seniors for Goren, who had already come on in the second half of Barcelona's earlier warm-up win, a 4-1 victory in which Spanish media likewise praised his composure on the ball.

Goren joined Barcelona's academy in 2023 from Maccabi Petah Tikva and signed his first professional contract with the club at just 16 — a notable landmark for an Israeli player at La Masia. He is a regular for Israel's youth national teams, having represented the under-17 side in European Championship qualifying.

His rise through the ranks has been steady rather than sudden: in the 2025/26 season he made 36 appearances for Barcelona's youth sides, scoring four goals and adding an assist, including a long-range strike in the Copa Catalunya final as Barça's Juvenil side beat Espanyol.

Whether Friday's cameo translates into a place closer to Flick's first-team plans remains to be seen — Barcelona open their La Liga campaign against Elche on August 23 — but for now, the teenager keeps adding to a growing file of favorable reviews from the Spanish press.

title: Will he play? Question mark hangs over Messi ahead of Inter Miami's clash with Columbus Crew
dek: The Argentine returned to training this week after the World Cup final, but coach Guillermo Hoyos would not confirm his involvement in Saturday's home game.
body: Lionel Messi is back on the training pitch with Inter Miami, but whether he is fit to face Columbus Crew this weekend is, for now, an open question. ONE reports that the Argentine captain's status for Saturday's game remains genuinely uncertain, with the club yet to commit either way.

Messi rejoined his teammates in Fort Lauderdale on Wednesday, arriving back early after Argentina's run to the 2026 World Cup final ended in a defeat to Spain. Under FIFA's post-tournament rest rules he was entitled to as much as three weeks off; instead he chose to report back to Inter Miami well ahead of that deadline.

Asked directly whether his captain would be available against Columbus, head coach Guillermo Hoyos stopped short of a promise. "He arrived recently, so we haven't had the chance to discuss it properly yet," Hoyos said. "But we're happy he and De Paul have returned."

Rodrigo De Paul, who also reported back this week after Argentina's tournament, appears to be in a similarly uncertain spot — grouped by his coach with Messi as a player whose immediate workload has not yet been decided.

US outlets covering the club suggest Inter Miami may lean toward caution, holding Messi out of the Columbus fixture altogether rather than risk him after a long, physically taxing summer, and instead easing him back in once the Leagues Cup begins in midweek.

That competition brings a concentrated run of home fixtures at Chase Stadium: Atlético San Luis on August 5, Monterrey on August 8, and León on August 12, giving the club three chances to reintroduce Messi gradually without the travel demands of an away trip.

Whatever is decided, Inter Miami head into the weekend in excellent form. They arrive on a six-match winning streak and sit second in the Eastern Conference, meaning there is no pressing need to gamble on their biggest asset before he is ready.

Kickoff against Columbus Crew is set for Saturday evening in Florida — the early hours of Sunday in Israel — with Hoyos expected to finalise his selection, and his stance on Messi, only in the build-up to the match.

title: Alongside foreign options, Maccabi Tel Aviv also weighing Maccabi Netanya's Oz Bilu
dek: With Emir Sahiti's future at Bloomfield uncertain, ONE reports the club has sent offers abroad for a new wing option — but a familiar domestic name is back on the list too.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — 'The solution for the wing? Oz Bilu candidate for Maccabi Haifa'
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — Sahiti joins Maccabi on loan from Hamburg
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — Kervin Andrade joins Maccabi Tel Aviv

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's search for a new wing option this summer has mostly pointed abroad, but according to a report by ONE, a familiar Israeli name has quietly resurfaced on the club's list: Maccabi Netanya's Oz Bilu.

The need is real. Emir Sahiti, who arrived at Bloomfield in January on loan from Hamburg SV and lit up the second half of the season on the flank, saw that loan run out on June 30. His long-term future at the club has not been settled, and ONE reports that finding a wing reinforcement — whether Sahiti stays or not — has become a genuine priority for the yellow-and-blue.

The club's primary route, per the report, runs overseas: Maccabi Tel Aviv have already submitted offers to several foreign wing candidates, none of whom are named in the report. That reflects the squad's current composition — the club already has eight foreign players registered, a number that shapes how much further room there is to add more import players without offloading elsewhere.

It is against that backdrop that Bilu's name has come back into the conversation, ONE reports — not as the current plan, but as an Israeli contingency should the foreign pursuit stall. The club is said to be monitoring him rather than actively negotiating.

It would not be the first time. Maccabi Tel Aviv looked at the 25-year-old last summer as well, before ultimately going a different route and bringing in Sahiti. Bilu has also been the subject of interest elsewhere in the league — Sport5 has reported in the past that Maccabi Haifa explored a trade for him built around Gai Malmed, a deal that never materialized.

Bilu enters the picture in career-best form. He had his strongest season yet at senior level in 2025/26, scoring 10 league goals and adding four assists in 31 appearances after coach Roni Levy moved him back out to the wing following a spell as a central striker and No. 10. Netanya rewarded him this summer with a contract extension through the end of the 2027/28 season, underlining how central he has become to the club — and making any move for him anything but straightforward.

Maccabi Tel Aviv's summer to-do list extends beyond the wing search. The club is also managing an injury to forward Ion Nicolaescu and has yet to resolve the situation around Venezuelan forward Kervin Andrade, who joined from Brazil's Fortaleza last September.

For now, there is no indication of direct contact between Maccabi Tel Aviv and either Bilu or Maccabi Netanya. He remains, in ONE's telling, a name worth watching rather than an active target — but one the champions clearly have not crossed off.

body: Real Madrid did not need to sell a single first-team player this summer to post one of the most eye-catching numbers of the transfer window. According to ONE, the club has already generated €181.5 million from academy departures alone since the market opened — a figure the outlet describes as "incomprehensible" for a squad that graduated relatively few first-teamers this cycle.

The headline sale is Nico Paz, whose move to Como was made permanent for €60 million. The Argentine playmaker spent last season on loan in Italy before Real Madrid cashed in fully, turning a player who never made a senior appearance for the club into one of the biggest cheques the academy has ever produced.

Gonzalo García, the striker who forced his way into Xabi Alonso's plans with a string of impressive substitute displays, is heading to Fulham in a deal worth around €40 million, with Real Madrid reported to have kept a sell-on percentage and a buy-back option should he ever be needed again. His Castilla teammate César Palacios is following him to Craven Cottage in a companion deal worth roughly €10 million.

The rest of the total comes almost entirely from sell-on clauses attached to players Madrid let go years ago at knockdown fees, only to collect again once those clubs cashed in themselves. Víctor Muñoz's move from Osasuna to Liverpool, reported at around €20 million, triggered a clause that sends a large slice back to Valdebebas. Mario Gila's switch from Lazio to AC Milan did the same, earning Real Madrid roughly €15 million from a deal in which the Italian defender never actually wore the first team's shirt.

Álvaro Rodríguez, sold on by Elche to Bournemouth, produced a similar windfall of around €12.5 million to €15 million depending on the final structure of the deal, while Jacobo Ortega's move to Strasbourg added roughly €8 million and Mario Martín's switch to Getafe brought in €3.5 million. Smaller sums from Álex Jiménez and Víctor Valdepeñas rounded out the tally ONE cites.

It is a business model Real Madrid has refined for years: sell young talent early, often for modest fees, but insist on sell-on percentages that pay off handsomely if the player develops elsewhere. Barcelona has built its recent identity around trusting academy graduates like Lamine Yamal in the first team; Madrid, under Florentino Pérez, has instead treated La Fábrica as a financial engine that funds the purchase of the readymade stars the club prefers to field.

Other outlets tracking the same figures suggest the total has kept climbing since ONE's report, with Yahoo Sports citing academy income approaching €196 million once Palacios' move to Fulham is fully processed — and the summer window still has weeks to run. Real Madrid's previous record for academy sales in a single summer, set in 2017, stood at roughly €102 million, a mark this year's total has already smashed several times over.

None of the fees are formally confirmed by Real Madrid itself, and several of the sell-on figures — Gila, Rodríguez and Muñoz in particular — depend on the precise percentage clauses in contracts that are not public, which is why reported totals vary from outlet to outlet. But the broad picture is consistent everywhere it has been reported: this is the most lucrative academy summer in the club's history, and it is not over yet.

title: Kaufman lays out Israel swimming's road to Los Angeles 2028, built around Gorbenko
dek: The veteran national coach tells ONE the team will skip the 2028 European Championships for a third altitude camp, as he confronts a wave of retirements and the pull of American college swimming.

verificationSources.label: University of Louisville Athletics - Anastasia Gorbenko
Ynet - Toumarkin appointed swimming federation professional director

body: Leonid Kaufman has been here before. Now 67 and back in charge of Israel's national swimming team after guiding it through five Olympic Games, he has used an interview with ONE to sketch out, in detail, how he intends to get Anastasia Gorbenko and the rest of the squad to Los Angeles 2028 in the best shape of their careers — and it means skipping a major championship along the way.

The headline decision is stark: Israel will not send its Olympic-bound swimmers to the 2028 European Championships. Instead of racing in Europe in the same year as the Games, the team will use the window for a third consecutive high-altitude training camp, on top of two already planned earlier in the cycle.

"Before Rio 2016 this strategy didn't work well," Kaufman told ONE, explaining the thinking behind the change. "We prefer peak condition at Los Angeles, not before." The implication is pointed — Israel's swimmers arrived in Rio having already hit their competitive peak at earlier meets that year, and paid for it with underwhelming results in Brazil.

Kaufman was brought back into the role roughly a year and a half ago specifically to avoid a repeat of that outcome, with Los Angeles as the target. It is his second spell steering the program after guiding Yakov Toumarkin to seventh in the 200m backstroke final at London 2012 — still the best Olympic finish by an Israeli swimmer.

Gorbenko sits at the heart of the new plan. Israel's biggest swimming star of this generation, she has stacked up world and European titles and reached Olympic finals, but a Games medal has so far eluded her. She now trains and studies at the University of Louisville, where she has already broken pool and school records since arriving.

Before any of the Los Angeles planning plays out, there is a more immediate target: the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, where the swimming programme runs from August 10-16. Kaufman's stated goal for that meet is five finals and at least one medal, with the men's 4x200m freestyle relay flagged as Israel's best shot.

The interview also doubled as an admission of a harder problem facing Israeli swimming: burnout. Three swimmers — Tomer Frankel, Gal Cohen Groumi and Ron Polonsky — have retired from the sport altogether, Frankel and Cohen Groumi walking away at just 24 and 23.

"When a swimmer or athlete feels exhausted, they can retire," Kaufman said. "A swimmer reaches burnout around age 23 or 24." It is a blunt acknowledgment that the current system, built heavily around the American college pipeline, is taking a toll.

That pipeline is itself a source of tension for Kaufman. Around 90% of Israel's elite swimmers now study at US colleges, a path he sees as a necessary compromise rather than an ideal one. "College is a compromise because swimmers combine studies with training, making swimming secondary," he told ONE.

His proposed fix, for 2027 and 2028 specifically, is to ask the country's top swimmers to delay enrolling in college for a year and train full-time in Israel through the Olympic year itself — a deliberate break from the college-first norm that has taken hold in Israeli swimming.

Kaufman was also asked about his working relationship with Toumarkin, the swimmer he once coached to that landmark London 2012 result and who has since retired and been appointed professional director of the Israeli Swimming Federation's elite teams. "We're equals," Kaufman said. "Jacob isn't above me and I'm not above him."

Two years out from Los Angeles, the outline is now public: fewer high-stakes races in the Olympic year itself, more controlled altitude work, a push to keep top swimmers training at home for longer, and Gorbenko — still chasing that first Olympic medal — as the program's clearest reason for optimism.

title: Haaland's summer holiday delivers an unlikely photo op: Michael Jordan
dek: The Norway striker, still riding the high of a breakout World Cup, shared a picture embracing the basketball legend on the French Riviera before Manchester City's preseason begins

verificationSources.label: Fox Sports - England v Norway quarterfinal

body: Manchester City's pre-season may already be under way, but Erling Haaland is still savouring the summer of his career — and on Friday he added an image to the highlight reel that had nothing to do with football at all.

The Norwegian striker, holidaying in Saint-Tropez on the French Riviera, ran into Michael Jordan and posed for a photo with the NBA icon. Haaland posted the picture on Instagram with a caption that needed no translation: "No caption needed."

It is the kind of image that explains itself — two of sport's most recognisable faces, arms around each other, sunglasses on, on a break from the spotlight that follows them both. Fans online were quick to dub it a meeting of "two GOATs."

Haaland has earned the downtime. He was one of the standout performers of the 2026 World Cup, helping Norway reach their first ever quarterfinal at the tournament after eliminating Brazil 2-1 in the last 16, a game in which he scored twice.

Norway's run ended in heartbreak against England, who won 2-1 after extra time thanks to a Jude Bellingham brace, with Andreas Schjelderup's early goal not enough to see the Norwegians through. Haaland went into that quarterfinal having scored seven times in the tournament, tied for third on the World Cup's scoring charts, but could not add to his tally against Jordan Pickford and England's defence.

Since Norway's exit, Haaland's summer has played out as a string of celebrity moments — from a Dolce & Gabbana show in Taormina with his girlfriend, Isabel Haugseng Johansen, to now a Riviera run-in with Jordan. Manchester City, meanwhile, are already back in training and are due to play three pre-season friendlies in Asia before opening their competitive season away to Arsenal on August 16.

title: Bachar reverts Maccabi Haifa to back four after Toto Cup double defeat
dek: Training this week has focused on rebuilding a flat back-four defensive shape as Haifa try to regroup before hosting Ironi Tiberias, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv — Kiryat Shmona 3-0 Maccabi Haifa report, injuries to Glazer and Wanderson

body: Barak Bachar spent Friday's training session on shape and patterns rather than sprints, and the message from the pitch at Maccabi Haifa's training ground was unmistakable: the back three that has malfunctioned through the opening weeks of the Toto Cup is gone, at least for now. ONE reports that Bachar worked heavily on drills built around four defenders, a return to the system that underpinned his most successful years in Haifa.

The rethink comes after a miserable opening to the 2026/27 campaign. Maccabi lost the Haifa derby 3-2 to Hapoel Haifa, then were beaten 3-0 by Ironi Kiryat Shmona, conceding all three goals before half-time. Goalkeeper Omri Glazer and centre-back Wanderson de Freitas Soares — known throughout Israeli football as 'Tsunami' for the ferocity he brings to challenges — were both injured and substituted in that game, adding an injury crisis to a run of poor results.

With Wanderson sidelined, ONE reports Shon Goldberg is being lined up to fill the left side of the back four, while new arrival Nigel Lunuwayck and Noam Steinman are also being worked into the reshaped defensive unit. There is better news in midfield and further forward: Yarin Levi is back in full training after being knocked out by a virus, giving Bachar another body to rotate through a squad that has looked short of options.

The most encouraging sign, according to the report, is the return of Manuel Benson to full training. The winger has been sharp in sessions this week, and Haifa's coaching staff believe his reintegration alone can lift a team that has managed only fitful attacking football so far this preseason. Until he is fully match-ready, the forward line is expected to be shared between Cedric Don, Kenji Gora and Guy Melamed.

The immediate opportunity to show the new shape is working comes on Tuesday, when Maccabi Haifa host Ironi Tiberias at Sami Ofer Stadium in the Toto Cup's home-stage group, kicking off at 17:00. Tiberias arrive with problems of their own, and ONE frames the fixture as a chance for Haifa to arrest a losing run before it hardens into a wider crisis.

There is context to the urgency. Bachar only returned to Maccabi Haifa on 21 October 2025, five months after being dismissed, for what is now his third spell in charge. His previous stint, from 2020 to 2023, delivered three consecutive league titles and the club's first-ever Champions League group-stage campaign — a period against which any stumbling start will inevitably be measured.

For now, the club's message is a pragmatic one: go back to what worked. A settled back four, a fit Benson and a winnable fixture against Tiberias give Bachar the ingredients to start correcting course before the Winner League season proper gets underway.

title: From Sofia to Katowice: Maccabi and Hapoel discover their European qualifying foes
dek: Maccabi Tel Aviv will face CSKA Sofia and Hapoel Tel Aviv take on GKS Katowice as both clubs push for European group-stage football in August.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com - M. Tel-Aviv vs CSKA Sofia

body: Both of Tel Aviv's leading clubs now know exactly who stands between them and a place in the group stage of European football this autumn, after a week of qualifying results across the continent settled two ties that will shape their August.

Maccabi Tel Aviv completed a comfortable passage past Sheriff Tiraspol, winning 6-0 on aggregate after a 5-0 rout in the first leg and a 1-0 second-leg win in Moldova sealed by a Roy Revivo free-kick. That result sends them into the Europa League's third qualifying round against CSKA Sofia, who needed penalties to see off Azerbaijan's Qarabağ after two goalless draws either side of extra time.

CSKA Sofia arrive as a club in transition. They finished fourth in Bulgaria's top flight last season but did lift the domestic cup, beating Lokomotiv Plovdiv on penalties, and are preparing to move into a new stadium in September. Their squad carries some recognisable names for a side of their size, among them Italian midfielder Stefano Sensi, Cypriot forward Ioannis Pittas and Ivorian defender Jean-Philippe Gbamin.

According to ONE, all is not calm behind the scenes in Sofia. Bulgarian journalist Theodore Borisov described an ongoing rift between head coach Hristo Yanev and the club's ultras, who have grown frustrated with his cautious, defensive approach, compounded by a recent change of sporting director.

Hapoel Tel Aviv, meanwhile, learned their third qualifying round opponent in the Conference League: GKS Katowice, the Polish club that stunned Slovakia's MSK Žilina 4-3 on aggregate in the previous round. Hapoel reached this stage themselves by eliminating Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad.
The first leg is set for Thursday, August 6, with the return fixture in Katowice a week later on August 13 — the winner advancing to the play-off round, one step from the competition's league phase.

Katowice's story this season has real substance behind it. The club returned to Poland's Ekstraklasa last year after a 19-year absence, guided by coach Rafał Górak, who has taken the team up from the third division since taking charge in 2019. They finished fifth in their first season back, ten points behind champions Lech Poznań, with midfielder Bartosz Nowak — voted the league's best player after a campaign of 9 goals and 12 assists — the standout performer.

Polish journalist Kacper Janoczka told ONE that Katowice's home form and support could make life awkward for Hapoel: the club has not lost at home since November, and the atmosphere at their stadium, he said, gives players "tremendous spirit and energy."

For both Tel Aviv clubs, the assignments look winnable but far from straightforward — CSKA Sofia and Katowice are unfamiliar opponents with genuine momentum of their own, and neither Maccabi nor Hapoel can afford to treat the third qualifying round as a formality if they want European football to stretch into the autumn.

title: Tokyo, 7 August 2021: The Ribbon That Fell and the Gold That Stayed
dek: Inside an empty arena in a pandemic-locked city, Linoy Ashram became the first Israeli woman to win Olympic gold — and ended two decades of Russian rule over rhythmic gymnastics' biggest individual prize.

verificationSources.label: ESPN — 'Israel's Linoy Ashram beats ROC twins to win gold'
Times of Israel — 'Rhythmic gymnast Linoy Ashram wins Israel's 3rd-ever Olympic gold'
Jerusalem Post — 'Russian team attacks Ashram's win, Israel fires back'
Times of Israel — 'World gymnastics group dismisses Russian complaints over Ashram's gold'
Israeli Olympic Committee — official athlete profile
JNS — 'Olympic gold medalist Linoy Ashram to retire from rhythmic gymnastics'

body: The Ariake Gymnastics Centre could hold twelve thousand people. On the morning of 7 August 2021 it held almost none. Japan was under a COVID-19 state of emergency, spectators had been barred from every Tokyo Olympic venue, and the only sounds in the hall as the rhythmic gymnastics individual all-around final began were music, ribbon and rope slapping the mat, and the murmurs of a few dozen coaches and officials. Linoy Ashram's own family, back home in Rishon LeZion, could not be there. She would find out later that they had watched, like everyone else in Israel, on television.

Ashram was 22, a gymnast who had spent fifteen years working her way up from a local club, Hapoel Rishon LeZion, under coach Ayelet Zussman. She arrived in Tokyo with a strong résumé — European all-around champion in 2020, world medals in 2017, 2018 and 2019 — but no individual world title, and no realistic path past the two women who had owned the discipline for years: identical twins Dina and Arina Averina, competing under the neutral ROC banner because Russia itself was serving a doping-related ban from major competitions.

Dina Averina came in as the heavy favourite, a two-time world all-around champion chasing the one title that had eluded her. For three rotations — hoop, ball, clubs — the two were locked together, trading tenths of a point. Then came the ribbon, rhythmic gymnastics' most unforgiving apparatus, and Ashram dropped hers mid-routine. In a sport where a single break can end a medal hope, it looked, for a moment, like the gold had gone with it.

It hadn't. When the final scores were posted, Ashram had 107.800 points to Averina's 107.650 — a margin of exactly 0.150, built less on the ribbon than on the difficulty and execution she had banked across the other three apparatus. Belarus's Alina Harnasko took bronze on 102.700, well clear of Arina Averina in fourth. Ashram sank to the floor, then to her knees, hands over her face, as the Israeli flag rose over an arena with no crowd to cheer it.

It was, by any reading, a landmark. Ashram became the first Israeli woman ever to win an Olympic gold medal, and it was Israel's third gold in the country's Olympic history — arriving less than a week after Artem Dolgopyat's floor exercise title in artistic gymnastics, a different discipline entirely, but a coincidence that made those six days in early August 2021 the most successful stretch Israeli sport had ever produced at a single Games.

The result did not go unchallenged. Russian officials reacted with fury: Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused judges of 'forgery in front of the whole world,' and the Russian Olympic Committee lodged a formal appeal. Ukrainian judge Lydia Vinogradnaya, defending the scoring, pointed out that Ashram had opened up what she called a 'simply enormous' lead of 1.9 points over Averina in the body-difficulty category alone, performing elements of higher technical value throughout. The International Gymnastics Federation reviewed the appeal and dismissed it outright, stating it could 'confirm that no bias or irregularities were identified in the judging panels.'

Ashram's coach, Zussman, answered the controversy with something closer to bemusement than defiance. 'Let me enjoy first place and the fact that I have an Olympic champion,' she said, adding that in Ashram's case, 'this was her best competition ever.' It was also, pointedly, not unprecedented: Averina herself had won a world title in 2018 after dropping her own ribbon, a detail Israeli commentators were quick to note once the Russian objections went public.

Back home, the reaction reached the top of Israeli political life. President Isaac Herzog phoned Ashram directly, telling her it was 'a tremendous pride to the whole country' and that 'when we saw the tears flowing from your eyes, the Israeli flag being raised, Hatikvah being played and the gold medal on your neck — we were excited to the point of tears.' Prime Minister Naftali Bennett called her 'a real-life Wonder Woman' who had 'made the entire nation happy.' Ten days later, on 16 August, the two hosted the full Tokyo delegation at Beit Hanasi in Jerusalem to mark the achievement in person.

For Ashram, the empty arena and the absent family made the moment strange even as it unfolded. She would later describe a 'mixture of feelings' at winning the biggest title of her career with no one there to see it live except cameras and officials. The medal ceremony, the anthem, the flag — all of it happened in near-silence, a gold-medal moment stripped of the roar that usually accompanies one.

Ashram never returned to that level of competition. In April 2022, at a press conference in Tel Aviv, she announced her retirement from competitive gymnastics, closing a career that had produced one Olympic title, three World Championship medals and a European crown — and, for one morning in a locked-down Tokyo, had denied the Averina sisters the one prize that had always been presumed to be theirs.
facts: The rhythmic gymnastics individual all-around final was held on 7 August 2021 at the Ariake Gymnastics Centre in Tokyo, with no spectators permitted due to Japan's COVID-19 state of emergency.
Linoy Ashram won gold with a total score of 107.800, edging Dina Averina of the ROC (107.650) by 0.150 points; Alina Harnasko of Belarus took bronze on 102.700.
Ashram, born 13 May 1999 in Rishon LeZion, trained from age seven at Hapoel Rishon LeZion under coach Ayelet Zussman.

She was the first Israeli woman to win an Olympic gold medal in any sport, and it was Israel's third Olympic gold overall, coming days after Artem Dolgopyat's floor exercise gold in artistic gymnastics.

The Russian Olympic Committee formally appealed the result to the IOC after Ashram dropped her ribbon mid-routine; the International Gymnastics Federation rejected the appeal, finding no bias or irregularities in the judging.
Ashram retired from competitive rhythmic gymnastics in April 2022, having also won a European all-around title (2020) and three World Championship medals (2017–2019).

title: FIFA scraps World Cup privatization plan after confederation revolt
dek: Gianni Infantino abandoned the sell-off of a $20 billion commercial subsidiary days after a senior adviser resigned and UEFA threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments.
body: FIFA has formally abandoned its plan to sell a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup, ONE reports, ending weeks of turmoil that saw a senior adviser to president Gianni Infantino resign and Europe's governing body threaten to boycott FIFA tournaments altogether.

The scheme, built around a new subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise, would have seen FIFA sell up to 20% of the company — which was to control commercial rights linked to the men's and women's World Cups and Club World Cups — to outside investors. JP Morgan had valued the vehicle at roughly $20 billion.

FIFA said in a statement that the project had "created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place," and confirmed the proposal "will not advance."

The climbdown followed a rapid collapse in support among FIFA's member confederations. UEFA formally voted to boycott future FIFA competitions if the plan went ahead, warning that "no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive." CONCACAF and, most damagingly for Infantino, the Asian Football Confederation joined the opposition in the plan's final days.

The pressure was compounded by the resignation of Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to Infantino and a trusted figure inside FIFA's leadership, who quit on Friday calling the sell-off "a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game."

Infantino had defended the idea as it first emerged, insisting "nobody is selling football" and that a full sale was something FIFA "wouldn't even consider." But the structure on the table would still have handed a fifth of the new commercial entity to private investors, reportedly including a New York investment firm founded by Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner.

FIFA had tried to win over sceptical member associations by offering each of them roughly $53 million in support of the plan, but the money failed to blunt the backlash from national federations and continental bodies that saw the move as ceding control of the sport's flagship event to outside capital.

There is no Israeli angle to the story directly, but the outcome matters for every federation, including the Israel Football Association, whose future World Cup revenue distributions were bound up in how FIFA's commercial rights are ultimately structured.
For now, FIFA's existing commercial model for the World Cup remains unchanged, and Infantino's office has given no indication of a revised proposal in the immediate future.
facts: FIFA has scrapped its plan to sell a 20% stake in a new commercial subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise, that would have managed World Cup and Club World Cup rights.
JP Morgan had valued FIFA Forward Enterprise at approximately $20 billion.
UEFA voted to boycott FIFA competitions if the plan proceeded; CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation also opposed it.
Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, resigned in protest on Friday, July 31, 2026.
FIFA said the project 'will not advance' after concluding it had created irreconcilable divisions among member associations.
Reported investors in the plan included a firm founded by Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner.

title: Vinícius Júnior agrees personal terms with Arsenal, ONE reports
dek: The Real Madrid winger has struck a preliminary agreement with the Premier League champions on his own terms, according to ESPN Brazil — though Madrid have yet to discuss a sale and insist they will not raise their own offer.

verificationSources.label: Football365 — Arsenal 'agree personal terms' with Vinícius Júnior
AFTV — Arsenal agree personal terms in principle with Vinícius Júnior
Sky Sports — Vinícius Jr set to stay at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest

body: It landed in the small hours as one of those transfer-market bombshells that make you check the date twice: ONE reported overnight, citing ESPN Brazil, that Vinícius Júnior has reached a preliminary agreement with Arsenal on personal terms — a dramatic twist in the future of one of the world's most coveted attackers.

The framing from ESPN Brazil, as relayed by ONE, is that Arsenal — freshly crowned Premier League champions after ending a 22-year wait for the title — believe they can prise the Brazilian away from the Bernabéu while his current Real Madrid contract still has time left to run, rather than waiting for a cheaper move once it nears expiry.

According to the report, Arsenal have put what is described only as "a massive contract" on the table for the winger. No concrete salary figure has been confirmed by either club, though separate British reporting this week has pegged Vinícius's existing Real Madrid pay at up to £400,000 a week, a level Arsenal would need to match or beat.

Vinícius's Real Madrid deal runs until June 2027. ONE reports that the Spanish club has signalled it will not improve its own financial offer at this stage and is simply waiting on the player's response, with no further round of talks scheduled. He is expected back at Real Madrid's training ground on Monday.

The player himself has previously struck a very different tone about his future in Madrid. "I have always said that my desire is to play here for many more years, make history and receive the love of the fans," Vinícius has said of his relationship with the club — a quote that now sits awkwardly alongside the overnight reports of personal terms with Arsenal.

The ONE story is not an isolated one. Arsenal-focused outlets including HandofArsenal and Football365 also described a breakthrough on "personal terms" as of July 31, reporting that Vinícius's representatives at Roc Nation are preparing to enter formal negotiations with Real Madrid armed with what those reports call a "monstrous offer" from the north London club.

It is worth being precise about what has and hasn't happened. Personal terms with a player are one thing; a transfer requires Real Madrid's cooperation, and there is no indication the Spanish champions have agreed to sell, discussed a fee, or scheduled a medical. Several reports frame this as Arsenal positioning themselves rather than a deal that is close to completion.

Indeed, the picture is genuinely contested. Other reporting from the same period — including Sky Sports' transfer coverage — suggests Real Madrid are working on the opposite outcome: a lucrative renewal designed to keep Vinícius well beyond 2027, built around a base salary reported in the region of €20 million net with bonuses that could push it toward €30 million, which would make him the club's best-paid player.

Real Madrid's calculus is straightforward regardless of which report proves accurate: with only a year left on his deal after this season, the club faces the familiar dilemma of cashing in now or risking losing a generational talent for a smaller fee, or nothing at all, in twelve months' time.

For Arsenal, the interest fits a pattern of ambition since finally winning the title under Mikel Arteta. Vinícius, still only 25, has been a Champions League winner and a Ballon d'Or contender in recent seasons, and any move would rank among the most significant transfers in the Premier League's history if it ever materialises.

For now, nothing is signed, no fee is agreed, and Real Madrid have made no public statement about a willingness to sell. What is confirmed is that the personal-terms report has been picked up widely enough, and attributed clearly enough to ESPN Brazil, to be treated as a live and serious storyline — one that will be tested when Vinícius returns to Real Madrid training this week.

Arsenal are the reigning Premier League champions, having won the 2025-26 title to end a 22-year wait.
Vinícius Júnior's existing Real Madrid contract runs until June 2027.
Real Madrid have indicated they will not improve their financial offer and are awaiting the player's response, according to ONE.
Vinícius is expected to return to Real Madrid training on Monday, with no further negotiations yet scheduled.
Other outlets, including Football365 and AFTV, independently reported an agreement in principle on personal terms around July 31, 2026, with Roc Nation said to be preparing talks with Real Madrid.
Separate reporting this week suggested Real Madrid are instead preparing a renewal offer to keep Vinícius beyond 2027.

title: Mastantuono set to leave Real Madrid on loan after underwhelming debut season
dek: The Argentine teenager was missing from Real Madrid's friendly against Fiorentina as his temporary exit nears completion, with Serie A clubs leading the chase for his signature.
body: Real Madrid have decided to send Franco Mastantuono out on loan for the coming season, ONE reports, with the Argentine winger left out of the club's preseason friendly against Fiorentina in Austria as the move enters its closing stages.

Mastantuono arrived at the Santiago Bernabéu just over a year ago in one of the most expensive transfers in Argentine football history. Real Madrid triggered his €45 million release clause at River Plate, with the full package — including taxes and add-ons — rising above €60 million.

The move has not paid off as hoped. According to ONE, the 19-year-old managed fewer than 1,500 minutes across all competitions in his debut campaign, contributing three goals and a single assist, numbers well short of what was expected given his price tag.

Competition for places has only intensified. Bernardo Silva joined Real Madrid on a free transfer from Manchester City in June, and the club are separately closing in on a deal for RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, a fee reported near €120 million that would make the Ivorian winger one of the most expensive signings in the club's history.

ONE reports that several Italian clubs have shown concrete interest in taking Mastantuono on loan, with Fiorentina to the fore and both Roma and Milan also monitoring the situation. Interest from the Premier League, including Fulham, has also been noted.

A return to River Plate, where Mastantuono made his name before the move to Spain, has been ruled out. Real Madrid's stated preference, per the report, is for him to continue his development within Europe.

Fabrizio Romano corroborated the substance of the story on Wednesday, writing that Real Madrid have confirmed internally that Mastantuono will leave on loan and that the club indicated a preference for a European loan over any Argentine return.

Despite sending him out, Real Madrid are not believed to be entertaining a permanent sale. The club still regards Mastantuono as part of its longer-term plans and wants regular football elsewhere to prepare him for a firmer foothold back at the Bernabéu.

title: Flick: I'm not dreaming, I'm focused on the players I have
dek: Barcelona's coach shrugs off Julián Álvarez talk after a penalty-shootout defeat to Birmingham City, hailing teenage forward Hamza Abdelkarim's derby brace on debut.
body: Hansi Flick used his first press conference of preseason to close down the transfer chatter swirling around his Barcelona squad, insisting he is thinking only about the players already on his books.

"I'm not dreaming. I focus on the squad I have now and the players who are here," Flick told reporters after Barcelona's preseason opener at Birmingham City. "I'm here, and what I see is that we have a lot of quality."

The remark landed against the backdrop of Barcelona's long chase for Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez, a pursuit Joan Laporta has pushed hard this summer even as Diego Simeone looks increasingly likely to keep the Argentine at the Metropolitano. Flick did not name Álvarez directly, choosing instead to talk up the squad already at his disposal.

That squad gave him plenty to like at St Andrew's, even in defeat. Birmingham City took the lead through August Priske before 18-year-old Hamza Abdelkarim struck twice — first from the penalty spot, then from close range after goalkeeper James Beadle spilled a long-range effort — to put Barcelona 2-1 up. Jhon Solís leveled for the hosts late on, and Birmingham won the shootout 3-2, with Beadle saving three Barcelona spot-kicks.

It was Abdelkarim's full debut for Barcelona's first team, and Flick made no attempt to hide his satisfaction with the young Egyptian forward, who joined permanently from Al Ahly after starring for Egypt at the World Cup.

"He's very humble, and he has a wonderful personality," Flick said. "He always tries to give his best, and he has huge potential. As a striker, you have to be present in those situations inside the box, and he was there today — that's what I ask of a No. 9."

"We have a big goal for this season, but everything depends on how we work every day," Flick added. "The most important thing is the players' effort, their mentality, and the team's dynamic. Playing together, in unity, is what matters most."

Flick was also asked about Marcus Rashford, whose loan spell from Manchester United is not being made permanent. "His situation wasn't easy, and sometimes loan deals don't turn into permanent transfers," the coach said. "We'll miss him, but we have to accept it. It was a pleasure to work with him — a great player and a great person."

There was a warmer note on the club's confirmed summer arrivals. Anthony Gordon, signed from Newcastle United for an initial €70 million, and Karim Adeyemi, brought in from Borussia Dortmund for around €22 million, both featured against Birmingham. "Anthony has shown how excited he is to be at Barcelona, and I'm very happy he's part of the squad," Flick said, while noting Adeyemi was still finding his feet after only a week of training.

With Ferran Torres also expected to carry over last season's form, Flick's message as preseason continues was one of patience over panic: build with what is already there, and let the transfer market sort itself out.
facts: Barcelona lost to Birmingham City 3-2 on penalties after a 2-2 draw in a preseason friendly at St Andrew's on July 31, 2026.
Hamza Abdelkarim, Barcelona's 18-year-old Egyptian forward signed permanently from Al Ahly, scored both Barcelona goals on his first-team debut.

title: Bolivian defender Diego Arroyo set to land in Israel this week for Hapoel Petah Tikva loan
dek: The Shakhtar Donetsk centre-back's visa has been approved and his agent calls it "a decisive day" for the move, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Arroyo expected in Israel by midweek
ONE - earlier report on stalled Arroyo talks
Shakhtar Donetsk - official announcement of Arroyo signing

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva are closing in on a loan deal for Bolivia international centre-back Diego Arroyo, with ONE reporting that the Shakhtar Donetsk defender is expected to land in Israel by the middle of the week.

The move had looked stuck in past weeks, but ONE reports that Arroyo's work visa has now been approved, clearing the main obstacle and allowing the paperwork to move forward. His agent, Rafi Epstein, told the Sport Radio programme "Sicha HaYom" that "the direction is positive and this is a decisive day" for the transfer.

Arroyo, 21, is a product of Bolivian football who came through Club Bolívar before a loan spell with Bahia's under-20 side in Brazil. Shakhtar signed him from Bolívar in February 2025 on a five-year contract, and he has also been capped by the Bolivia national team.

A loan to Petah Tikva would give the 21-year-old regular football away from Ukraine's war-disrupted top flight, while handing Omer Peretz's side a young, internationally capped centre-back to add depth to their back line.

Should he arrive as expected, Arroyo is set to pair at the heart of defence with Alex Moucketou-Moussounda, the Gabonese centre-back who joined Hapoel Petah Tikva from Aris Limassol and is contracted to the club. Peretz, who led Petah Tikva to promotion in his first season before guiding them into last term's upper playoff for the first time in over two decades, has been steadily rebuilding his squad ahead of the new campaign.

The club's recruitment work does not stop there. ONE also reports that Petah Tikva are pursuing Roei Zarihan, a defender at Hapoel Rishon LeZion, with a committee decision on the transfer fee expected within roughly two weeks. Zarihan has already begun training with Petah Tikva in the meantime to stay match-fit while the paperwork is finalised.

Nothing is signed yet on either front, and Petah Tikva have not confirmed the moves themselves - but if Arroyo does land in Israel this week as ONE anticipates, the club could have two new defensive additions in place within a fortnight.

title: Union Saint-Gilloise beat Club Brugge 5-4 on penalties to win Belgian Super Cup as Khalaili scores
dek: Anan Khalaili converted his spot kick as Union held their nerve to beat Club Brugge 5-4 on penalties after a 1-1 draw, avenging last year's final to lift the Belgian Super Cup in Bruges.

verificationSources.label: TeamTalk - Nottingham Forest pursuit of Khalaili

body: Anan Khalaili converted his spot kick as Union Saint-Gilloise beat Club Brugge 5-4 on penalties, after a 1-1 draw, to win the Belgian Super Cup at the Jan Breydel Stadium in Bruges on Friday night, ONE reports.
Brugge had led since the 49th minute, when Nicolò Tresoldi struck four minutes into the second half, before Union's Kevin Mac Allister equalised with 13 minutes left to force the shootout.
Khalaili had been introduced as a 61st-minute substitute while his side trailed, and stayed on the pitch long enough to take - and score - Union's second penalty in the shootout that followed.

Promise David, Khalaili, Andi Zeneli, Marco Zorgane and Relebohile Mofokeng were all on target from the spot for Union; Brugge's Cheveyo Tsawa was the only player of the ten takers to miss, his effort saved, leaving Mofokeng to net the winning kick and hand Union the trophy.
It was sweet revenge for Union, who had lost last year's Super Cup meeting with the same opponents 2-1 at their own Joseph Marien Stadium.

Khalaili, 21, born in Haifa to an Arab-Israeli family, joined Union from Israeli football in 2024 for a reported €6.5 million and was a key figure as the club won its first Belgian league title in 90 years last season.

His performances this year had earned him a move to Inter Milan in a deal reportedly worth up to €30 million - which would have made him the most expensive player in Israeli football history - but Ynet reported the transfer collapsed this summer after Khalaili failed the mandatory cardiac screening required by Italian football authorities.

With the Inter deal dead, English reports say Nottingham Forest have moved to take advantage, opening talks for the winger; Union are said to have rejected Forest's opening bid of around €20 million as too low, with the Belgian champions holding out for a fee closer to what Inter had agreed.

For now, Khalaili remains a Union Saint-Gilloise player, and Friday's shootout heroics gave him and the club's Israeli-linked fanbase a first trophy of the new season - possibly his last in Union colours before a Premier League move materialises.

Brugge's Cheveyo Tsawa was the only player of ten takers to miss a penalty; Relebohile Mofokeng scored the winning spot kick for Union.
Union lost last year's Super Cup final to the same opponents, 2-1, making this a repeat fixture with a reversed result.

title: Bnei Sakhnin sign Guadeloupe defender Dimitri Cavaré on club-record salary
dek: The 31-year-old free agent has signed for close to €250,000 a season, the richest deal in the northern club's history, according to ONE.
body: Bnei Sakhnin have completed the signing of Guadeloupe international defender Dimitri Cavaré, and according to ONE the 31-year-old has been handed close to €250,000 a season - the richest contract the northern club has ever given a player.

Cavaré, who stands 1.84m and holds both Guadeloupe and French citizenship, arrives as a free agent. He spent last season with Turkish second-tier side Esenler Erokspor, making 25 appearances there, after two years at Ümraniyespor in the Turkish top flight. Agent Yaron Barnes brokered the move, ONE reported.

It is the second time Sakhnin have gone after him. Head coach Yossi Abukasis and his assistant Ohad Kadosh first tried to bring Cavaré in while the pair were together at Maccabi Netanya, only for that deal to fall through - according to ONE, landing him this time was a priority once the two took charge in Sakhnin.

Cavaré came through the academy at Rennes and was sold from Lens to Rennes for a reported €3 million in 2015. He then spent three seasons in England with Barnsley, from 2017 to 2020, before a spell in Switzerland and his subsequent move to Turkish football.
He has been capped for Guadeloupe at international level, giving Sakhnin's back line experience against Caribbean and CONCACAF-region opposition as well as several years in European football.

Sport5 separately confirmed the transfer, reporting that Sakhnin's management see the defender as a key figure for the coming campaign, though the salary figure itself has been reported only by ONE and has not been confirmed by the club.

The record-breaking deal underlines how far Sakhnin are prepared to stretch their budget this summer as they try to strengthen a squad that stumbled at the first hurdle of the Toto Cup, losing their opening group match to Hapoel Tiberias.

Abukasis's side are next in action against Hapoel Haifa, still searching for their first win of the pre-season cup competition, with Cavaré now in the squad as the club's marquee close-season addition.

title: Petitions demand Spain strip Messi of Princess of Asturias award after World Cup final row
dek: More than 30 Change.org campaigns are calling on Spain's royal foundation to revoke Lionel Messi's prize, after ugly scenes marred Argentina's 1-0 extra-time defeat to Spain in the World Cup final.
body: Lionel Messi is facing an unusual backlash in Spain, where more than 30 separate petitions on Change.org are demanding that the Princess of Asturias Foundation revoke, or at least reconsider, the sports award it handed him barely two months ago — after his conduct during and after the World Cup final infuriated a section of Spanish fans.

Messi was named winner of the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports on June 3, becoming the first individual footballer to receive one of Spain's most prestigious honours. The formal presentation ceremony, usually a grand royal occasion in Oviedo, is scheduled for October.

The row traces back to July 19, when Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the World Cup final, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal in the 106th minute as Argentina, reduced to ten men, fell agonisingly short of a successive title.

What tipped fans from disappointment into outrage, according to the petitions, was Messi's behaviour in the closing stages and at the trophy ceremony. He appeared to push for Marc Cucurella to be sent off after the Spain defender briefly covered his mouth while talking during play — an act that, under this tournament's directive, risked a straight red card.

The complaints go further than the Cucurella incident. Petition organisers also point to Argentine players turning their backs during the medal presentation and to further confrontations in the tunnel area after the final whistle, framing the episode as a pattern of disrespect rather than a single flashpoint.

One of the largest petitions, started by a campaigner identified only as Javier, had gathered more than 1,500 signatures by late July. It argues Messi showed "behaviour that is not sportsmanlike and disrespectful," contradicting "the values of honour and integrity that sport promotes." A second, from an organiser named Laura, contends that revoking the prize would "restore trust in the fairness and rigour of these honours."

English-language outlets covering the same campaign, including GiveMeSport and Colombia One, put the tally at roughly 30 petitions in total, with the biggest nearing 3,000 signatures as of July 30 — a reminder that the numbers are moving quickly and vary slightly depending on when each outlet checked.

The controversy has not stayed confined to online petitions. FIFA has opened a disciplinary investigation into the scenes after the final whistle, with reports naming Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes and assistant coach Roberto Ayala among those whose conduct is under review.
According to ONE, Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente described the post-match scenes as "intolerable and unacceptable," adding an official voice to the criticism aimed at the Argentina camp.

The Princess of Asturias Foundation itself has made no public statement on whether it will act on the petitions, and the October ceremony remains on the calendar for now. Whether a wave of online pressure translates into any formal reconsideration of Messi's award is, at this stage, an open question.
facts: Lionel Messi was announced as winner of the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports on June 3, the first individual footballer to receive the honour.
Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the World Cup final on July 19, 2026, with Ferran Torres scoring the winner in the 106th minute; Argentina finished the match with ten men.
More than 30 Change.org petitions have been launched calling on the Princess of Asturias Foundation to revoke or reconsider Messi's award.

title: Uefa threatens World Cup boycott as pressure mounts on Fifa's Gianni Infantino
dek: European federations, backed by Asian and North American confederations, are prepared to boycott Fifa competitions over a plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup to private investors — with a senior advisor's resignation and talk of a 2027 rival deepening the crisis around the Fifa president.
body: Gianni Infantino is facing the gravest challenge of his ten years running world football's governing body, with Uefa and two other continental confederations now threatening to boycott Fifa's own competitions — the World Cup included — unless the Fifa president abandons a plan to sell a slice of the tournament to private investors.

The proposal at the heart of the row would spin off Fifa's commercial operations, including the World Cup and Club World Cup, into a new subsidiary valued at tens of billions of dollars, with roughly 20% of it sold to outside investors. The lead investor identified in reporting is a New York investment firm founded by Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

Uefa, which represents 55 of Fifa's 211 member federations, has called the move 'irresponsible and indefensible', accusing Infantino's leadership of pushing the plan through without properly consulting the countries that make up the organisation. Its members have voted to boycott all Fifa competitions if the sale goes ahead.

The Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, the governing body for North and Central America, have since joined Uefa in rejecting the proposal — leaving Infantino isolated against three of Fifa's six continental confederations at once.

To try to win over the federations still weighing the plan, Infantino has sweetened the offer: member associations who approve it would see guaranteed funding for the next four years double from $10 million to $20 million, with projected Fifa payouts through 2038 rising to roughly $86 million per federation, against about $36 million without the deal. Members have been told to decide by September 19.

The internal strain has already produced one high-profile departure. Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to Infantino and a former US Soccer president, resigned from his role in protest at the plan — a rare public break from within Infantino's own camp.

Speculation has also turned to who might challenge Infantino when Fifa members next elect a president, in March 2027. Reports in recent days have named Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi as a possible rival candidate, though he is said, so far, to be uninterested; Uefa officials are reported to be searching for a heavyweight figure willing to stand against him.

Infantino, first elected in 2016 after Sepp Blatter's resignation and re-elected in 2019 and 2023, has already confirmed at April's Fifa Congress in Vancouver that he intends to seek a further term in 2027. Under Fifa's statutes a president is limited to three four-year terms, but because his initial 2016-2019 stint completing Blatter's term is not counted as a full term, a win in 2027 would let him serve until 2031 before hitting that cap.

For now, more than 200 of Fifa's federations are reported to still be backing Infantino, and no formal move to remove him is on the table. But the scale of the Uefa-led revolt — and the prospect of Europe's teams sitting out Fifa events — makes this the most serious institutional crisis of his presidency, with the September 19 funding deadline and the build-up to September's Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland the next flashpoints to watch.

title: Barcelona sign Belgian teenager Jesse Bisiwu on five-year deal
dek: The 18-year-old winger arrives from Club Brugge for around €8.5 million, becoming the third piece of Barcelona's attacking rebuild this summer.
body: Barcelona have officially confirmed the signing of Jesse Bisiwu, an 18-year-old Belgian winger, from Club Brugge on a five-year contract running through June 30, 2031, ONE reports.

The deal is worth in the region of €8.5 million, according to ESPN and other outlets tracking the negotiation, with Club Brugge retaining a 20 percent cut of any future sale. Barcelona had an earlier bid of around €10 million rejected before the two clubs settled on the lower guaranteed fee plus the sell-on clause.

Bisiwu, born on January 22, 2008, began his career at Louvain before joining Club Brugge's academy in 2020. He made his senior debut for the club's reserve side, Club NXT, in the Belgian second division at just 15 years old, going on to make 36 appearances there.

At youth level he featured 14 times in the UEFA Youth League for Brugge, scoring three goals, and was named to the Best XI of the 2025 European Under-17 Championship after helping Belgium reach the semifinals.
He becomes Barcelona's third attacking addition of the summer, following the arrivals of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United and Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.
According to FC Barcelona's official announcement, Bisiwu is also only the third Belgian to represent the club's first team, after former captain Thomas Vermaelen and Jan Goyvaerts.
Barcelona confirmed the move on their social channels with a short post reading, "Welcome, Bisiwu! The player has signed until 2031," alongside the club crest.

A debut could come quickly: Bisiwu is expected to be part of Barcelona's squad for a three-team preseason tournament in Udine on August 8, though it will be up to head coach Hansi Flick to decide how quickly he is integrated into the senior group.

title: Special guest: why Jude Bellingham returned to St Andrew's for Barcelona's visit
dek: The Real Madrid and England midfielder went back to the club that raised him, watching from the stands as Birmingham City drew 1-1 with Barcelona in pre-season
body: Jude Bellingham spent Friday evening exactly where his career began, back in the stands at St Andrew's, as Barcelona rolled into Birmingham for a pre-season friendly against the club that raised him.

ONE reports that the Real Madrid and England midfielder was pictured smiling among the crowd, drawing a warm reception from Birmingham City supporters who still regard him as one of their own, even six years after he left.

Bellingham is on his summer break following England's run to a bronze medal at the 2026 World Cup, and rather than staying away from a football pitch he chose to spend part of it revisiting the ground where his professional story started.

That story is well documented on both sides of the fixture. Bellingham joined Birmingham's academy at just seven years old and rose through the ranks until, in August 2019, he made his senior debut at 16 years and 38 days, becoming the youngest player ever to appear for the club.

He went on to make 44 appearances and score four goals in a single Championship season before Borussia Dortmund paid a reported €23 million to sign him in the summer of 2020, a fee that made him, at the time, the most expensive 17-year-old in football history.

Birmingham later retired his number 22 shirt, a gesture the club said was meant not simply to honour Bellingham but to hold him up as an example of talent, hard work and dedication for the academy players coming up behind him.

Barcelona, missing eight first-team players including Lamine Yamal, Pedri, Gavi, Dani Olmo and Pau Cubarsí, used the friendly to give minutes to fringe and youth players under Hansi Flick, and it doubled as the first appearance for new signing Karim Adeyemi in Barcelona colours.
Birmingham, unbeaten in five warm-up matches under manager Chris Davies heading into the game, matched their illustrious visitors for large stretches of the contest.

The match finished 1-1, with August Priske putting Birmingham ahead in the 31st minute before Hamza Abdelkarim levelled from the penalty spot for Barcelona 11 minutes later, a fair result between a Championship side in form and the reigning La Liga champions fielding a much-changed line-up.

The occasion also revived a sliver of shared history between the two clubs: in 1960, Birmingham became the first English side to reach a European final, losing to Barcelona over two legs in the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup.

title: Llorente breaks silence on viral Ibiza photos with World Cup winner Ferran Torres
dek: The Atlético Madrid star addressed the online speculation sparked by embrace photos with Spain teammate Ferran Torres, insisting confidence — not fear of showing affection — is what makes a man masculine.
body: Marcos Llorente has had enough of dodging the question. Days after photos from an Ibiza getaway with Spain teammate Ferran Torres went viral — one frame showing Torres kissing the Atlético Madrid man on the cheek mid-hug — Llorente used an Instagram question-and-answer session to address the speculation head-on.
"It surprises me that in 2026 there's still debate about two men showing each other affection," he wrote, responding to a follower who asked why the pictures had caused such a stir.

He didn't stop there. "For me, there's nothing more masculine than a man who is confident in himself, who isn't afraid to show affection to a friend," Llorente added, turning the online chatter back on itself.

The photos were taken during a group holiday on the Balearic island shortly after Spain's 2026 World Cup triumph, when several members of Luis de la Fuente's squad went away together to unwind. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final on July 19, with Torres himself scoring the winning goal in the 106th minute.

Images of the trip, showing Llorente and Torres unusually close and affectionate on camera, quickly racked up millions of views and split opinion online. Some users speculated about a romantic relationship; others, as several Spanish outlets and Israel's Mako noted, pointed out that close physical affection between male friends is simply more culturally accepted in Spain than the reaction suggested.

Llorente is married to Patricia Noarbe, known widely as Paddy, an influencer with a large following of her own; the couple have a young daughter. Mako reported there is no indication or statement suggesting Torres is gay, and noted the Barcelona forward had recently split from influencer Martina Alegro before Spain's World Cup semi-final.
Rather than laugh the moment off or ignore it, Llorente chose to engage directly — and pointedly reframed the story as one about comfort with masculinity rather than anyone's sexuality.

For two players who were central to a European champion's World Cup run just weeks ago, the episode is a reminder of how closely footballers' private lives are scrutinised the moment the tournament trophy is lifted.

title: Kiryat Shmona rout Maccabi Haifa 3-0, then refuse to get carried away before Tiberias test
dek: Shay Barda's side tore through Maccabi Haifa's defence in their Toto Cup opener, but the message from the club is blunt: forget it and focus on Ironi Tiberias.
body: Kiryat Shmona barely had a night to enjoy the biggest scoreline of their pre-season before the club moved to shut down any talk of momentum. Days after tearing Maccabi Haifa apart 3-0 in their Toto Cup group-stage opener, the message from inside the club, as reported by ONE, was blunt: "We have nothing to fall back on, it was just one game."

The result itself was emphatic. Niv Gabay opened the scoring in the seventh minute, Amadou Sania doubled the lead in the 23rd after Haifa's defence imploded, and Ariel Sharatzki added a third before the half-hour mark was out. By half-time the contest was effectively over, with the visitors from the north cutting through a Haifa side that looked unprepared at the back.

The night carried a cost for Maccabi Haifa beyond the scoreboard. Goalkeeper Omri Glazer was taken off in tears after a collision left him with a knee injury, with a teammate nicknamed "Tsunami" also forced off with a head knock. An MRI subsequently showed only a mild ligament strain for Glazer, with Haifa hopeful of having him back within about a month, while his teammate was found to have suffered a mild concussion, Walla! Sport and Sport5 reported. Haifa coach Barak Bachar was blunt in his own assessment afterwards, telling Walla! Sport: "We're very soft and we break too easily."

None of that is Kiryat Shmona's concern, according to ONE's report, and the club is determined not to let a one-sided scoreline against a rival breed complacency. Shay Barda's group now turn to Ironi Tiberias in their next Toto Cup group fixture, aiming to keep their perfect start intact.

Barda, who has managed the club since 2023 and signed a contract extension keeping him in charge through the 2026/27 season, is expected to make only minor changes to the side that dismantled Haifa, ONE reports.

There is one change forced on him regardless. Peruvian forward Adrian Ugarte, who has been out through injury, returned to training but is not expected to be risked from the start — the club's plan, per ONE, is to have him ready on the bench rather than rush him back into the XI against Tiberias.

Further forward planning is also underway. Brazilian newcomer Thales Costa has been training with the squad in recent days but still needs a little more time to integrate, with ONE reporting he is being lined up to feature when Kiryat Shmona take on Hapoel Haifa in their following group match.

For now, though, the club's tone is one of controlled ambition rather than celebration. A 3-0 win over Maccabi Haifa is a statement result in any pre-season competition — but as far as Kiryat Shmona are concerned, it buys nothing beyond bragging rights until Tiberias have been dealt with too.

title: Real Madrid complete surprise deal for Levante striker Carlos Espí
dek: The 21-year-old forward becomes the club's replacement for Gonzalo García after Madrid moved fast to beat Brighton and Hull City to his signature.

verificationSources.label: ONE: מצאה מחליף - ריאל מדריד החתימה את קרלוס אספי

body: Real Madrid have pulled off what ONE is calling the quiet deal of the summer, confirming the signing of Levante striker Carlos Espí in a move completed within hours rather than the drawn-out sagas that usually accompany a Bernabéu arrival.

The 21-year-old centre-forward joins on a five-year contract running to 30 June 2031, with Madrid activating the €25 million release clause written into his Levante deal to get the transfer over the line immediately, according to ONE's reporting and confirmed in Real Madrid's own official announcement.

The move fills the gap left by Gonzalo García, who departed for Fulham this summer, and gives Madrid a different kind of number nine to the one he replaces: a physical, aerially dominant target man rather than a mobile, pressing forward.

ONE reports that the deal moved at a startling pace once Madrid re-entered the race, with Levante close to sanctioning a sale to Brighton and other suitors, including Villarreal and reported interest from Manchester City, also circling before the Spanish champions swooped. English clubs Hull City and Brighton were both prepared to trigger the release clause themselves.

At 1.94 metres, Espí built his reputation on heading rather than pace or dribbling. Last season he ranked second in La Liga for the proportion of his goals scored with his head among players with ten or more league strikes, behind only Atlético Madrid's Alexander Sørloth, per ONE's analysis.

The numbers behind the move are modest by Bernabéu standards but tell their own story: Espí scored 11 La Liga goals last season, either side of an injury-hit stretch, as Levante fought off relegation, and finished the campaign as the league's best young player under the age of 23.

Across three seasons since joining Levante's academy from UD Alzira in 2022, he made 66 appearances and scored 20 goals for the Valencia-region club, having been born locally in Tavernes de la Valldigna. He has represented Spain at both under-19 and under-20 level.

This is not the first time Madrid have looked at him. ONE notes the club made an approach as far back as March 2024, only for Levante to knock it back and keep their emerging forward for another 18 months of development.

Reports in Spain have tied the signing to head coach José Mourinho, who is said to have pushed hard for Espí's recruitment and persuaded club president Florentino Pérez to move quickly rather than risk losing him to a Premier League rival.

There was no unveiling fanfare befitting a marquee superstar arrival, and Espí will have to fight for minutes in a squad packed with attacking talent. But if his heading power and finishing translate from the Ciutat de Valencia to the Bernabéu, ONE suggests this understated deal could yet rank among Madrid's shrewdest business of the summer.

title: UEFA orders Maccabi Tel Aviv to freeze ticket sales for CSKA Sofia tie amid pyrotechnics probe
dek: The Israeli champions face a disciplinary case after fans set off flares and fireworks during last week's win over Sheriff Tiraspol, with ticket sales frozen for the visit of CSKA Sofia in Europa League qualifying.
body: UEFA has ordered Maccabi Tel Aviv to immediately halt ticket sales for their next Europa League qualifier, freezing sales for the home leg against CSKA Sofia while a disciplinary case against the club runs its course.

ONE reports that European football's governing body opened the proceeding over the use of pyrotechnic devices by Maccabi supporters, instructing the club to "freeze ticket sales until completion of the disciplinary process and a decision on the matter."

The trouble stemmed from Maccabi's own "home" leg against Sheriff Tiraspol in the second qualifying round, where fans in the yellow-and-blue section lit dozens of flares and fireworks as the match kicked off. Because Israeli clubs currently stage their UEFA home fixtures abroad due to the security situation, that leg was played at the Adjarabet Arena in Batumi, Georgia, on July 30.
Maccabi won that night 1-0, completing a 6-0 aggregate rout of the Moldovan side after a 5-0 first-leg victory on July 23, and advanced comfortably to the third qualifying round.

Their reward is a tie with CSKA Sofia of Bulgaria, who reached this stage by beating Qarabag on penalties. Maccabi's first leg — again designated a home match and therefore likely to be staged at another neutral venue outside Israel — is scheduled for Thursday at 19:00, with the return fixture in Sofia a week later, on August 13.
It is that opening leg for which ticket sales have now been suspended, leaving supporters waiting on UEFA's ruling before they can buy in.
The club said it is cooperating fully with UEFA throughout the process and pledged to update fans as soon as ticket sales can resume for the next European home game.

It is the second time this season Maccabi has drawn UEFA's disciplinary attention over crowd conduct: the club was already fined and handed a two-year suspended ban on away ticket sales in December over supporters' chanting during a Europa League trip to Stuttgart. A further sanction now, even a fine, would come with the club already on notice.
