title: Hapoel Hadera add defender Uri Zaretzki and midfielder Uri Tako
dek: The third-tier club fills out its squad with a promoted 19-year-old academy defender and a 22-year-old midfielder, days after losing an appeal over its regional group placement.
body: Hapoel Hadera used the closing days of July to add fresh legs to their roster, confirming the signings of defender Uri Zaretzki and midfielder Uri Tako as the club builds toward a new season it did not entirely choose the shape of.

Zaretzki, 19, moves up from Hadera's own youth ranks after what ONE described as a strong run of progress that persuaded the club's technical staff to fast-track him into the senior squad. He arrives with previous youth experience at Karmiel, Asher and Hapoel Haifa, according to the report, though no contract length was disclosed for the young defender.

Tako, 22, joins on a deal running through the end of the season. A product of Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth academy, he has more recently turned out for Tzeirei Tira and Hapoel Herzliya before agreeing terms with Hadera, ONE reported.

The timing is notable. The signings land only days after a football association appeals tribunal rejected Hapoel Hadera's bid to be moved out of the southern regional group of Liga Alef and into the northern group, ruling instead that Tira's greater seniority gave it the stronger claim to the switch, ONE reported separately. Hadera will now open the season exactly where it did not want to be — a longer, less convenient regional draw than the club had lobbied for.

Against that backdrop, filling out the squad with a promoted academy prospect and a versatile midfielder reads as pragmatic squad-building rather than a marquee statement of intent. title: Galil Elyon bring back forward Maurice Camp, Ashdod add French-league center Qudus Wahab
dek: Two Israeli Premier League clubs strengthened their frontcourts this week, with Hapoel Galil Elyon turning to a familiar face and Maccabi Ashdod importing size from France's top flight.
body: Two Israeli Premier League clubs went shopping for frontcourt help this week, and ONE reports both moves are now done: Hapoel Galil Elyon have brought back a proven scorer in Maurice Camp, while Maccabi Ashdod have gone to the French top flight for a Georgetown-trained center in Qudus Wahab.

Camp, an American forward who turns 36 later this year, stands 2.03 metres and is no stranger to Israeli basketball — this will be his fourth stop in the Premier League, following spells at Maccabi Ramat Hasharon, Bnei Herzliya and, most recently, Elitzur Netanya.

It was at Netanya last season that Camp made his case for another contract in Israel, averaging 16.5 points and 6.7 rebounds a game. Galil Elyon, who play out of the Galilee and Golan region, are banking on him repeating that kind of production in the north.

His career has taken him well beyond Israel and the United States: stints in Hungary, Spain, China, Argentina, Estonia and Lebanon are all on his résumé, the profile of a well-travelled journeyman forward who has found a level he can dominate at in the Israeli top flight.

Down south, Maccabi Ashdod have moved to solidify their interior with Qudus Wahab, a 26-year-old, 2.11-metre center who arrives from Cholet in France's Betclic Élite after a season averaging 5.4 points and 4.1 rebounds there, with sharper numbers in the FIBA Champions League — 6.4 points and 5.6 rebounds, including a 12-point, four-block outing against Hapoel Holon.

Wahab's path is an unusual one for an Ashdod import: born in Nigeria, he moved to the United States at 15 and worked his way through Georgetown — where he played under Patrick Ewing — before transferring to Maryland and finishing his college career at Penn State.
He turned pro with Lavrio in Greece, posting 10.1 points, 6.8 rebounds and better than a block a game as a rookie, before making the jump to France with Cholet last season.
Wahab is Ashdod's third confirmed import of the summer, joining returning guard Robert Turner and new arrival Isaiah Hill as the club rebuilds its roster ahead of the coming Israeli season.

Neither club has announced official unveiling events, but with both signings now reported across multiple Israeli outlets, Galil Elyon and Ashdod appear to have their frontcourt reinforcements in place well before preseason training ramps up.

title: Mudryk cleared to return to football as Chelsea doping saga ends
dek: The Ukrainian winger, sidelined since November 2024, says the ordeal was "the most difficult period" of his career after the FA and WADA resolved his meldonium case with immediate effect.
body: Mykhailo Mudryk has been cleared to play football again with immediate effect, after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved the doping case that has kept the Chelsea winger out of the game for more than a year and a half.

The Ukrainian, 25, was provisionally suspended in December 2024 after a routine test taken the previous October returned a positive result for meldonium, a heart medication on WADA's banned list. He had not played competitively since November 2024 and initially faced a four-year ban.

Speaking to ONE about the ordeal, Mudryk did not hide how hard the layoff had been. "This was the most difficult period in my career," he said. "I learned a lot about myself and I'm ready to return stronger."

The breakthrough came after WADA updated its own testing and reporting procedures in the two years since Mudryk's sample was taken. In a statement explaining the resolution, the FA said that "if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations would have resulted."

Rather than continuing to fight the case through the Court of Arbitration for Sport, where he had lodged an appeal, Mudryk accepted that he had committed the anti-doping rule violations as charged and agreed to a period of ineligibility equal to the time he had already served — effectively closing the file immediately.

Chelsea welcomed the outcome, pointing to "advances in applicable scientific reporting standards" that it said vindicated its player, and said the club would support his "reintegration into the squad."

Mudryk is expected to link up with Chelsea's squad on their pre-season tour of Hong Kong, working under new manager Xabi Alonso, who began his tenure at Stamford Bridge on 1 July 2026. Reports in England suggest the club could still send him out on loan first to rebuild match sharpness before fully integrating him into Alonso's plans for the season.

Mudryk arrived at Chelsea from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023 in a deal worth up to £89 million, one of the most eye-catching signings of the Todd Boehly ownership era. His time in England has since been defined as much by inconsistency and, latterly, this suspension as by the searing pace that made him one of the most sought-after wingers in Europe.

For now, the ruling gives him a clean slate: eligible to train and play immediately, with his first real test being whether he can rediscover the form that persuaded Chelsea to make him one of their biggest investments in years.

title: De Zerbi says Tottenham's £237m spending spree is 'not finished' as Savinho chase continues
dek: The head coach says the club has completed only '60 per cent' of its rebuild after breaking its transfer record twice in 48 hours.
body: Roberto De Zerbi has a warning for the rest of the Premier League: Tottenham Hotspur are not done spending. Even after committing £237 million to rebuilding his squad this summer, the Italian head coach says the club has completed only "60 per cent" of the project he has in mind, with one more marquee attacking signing still being chased.

The spree has already reshaped Spurs. Sandro Tonali arrived from Newcastle United for a reported £100 million, while Mateus Fernandes followed for around £85 million — the two deals breaking Tottenham's transfer record twice inside 48 hours. Defender Jan Paul van Hecke was added too, and the club used the free-agent market shrewdly to bring in Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and back-up goalkeeper Martin Dúbravka.

According to De Zerbi, the shopping list is not yet closed. Manchester City winger Savinho has been reported as one of Tottenham's leading targets to complete the attacking overhaul, with the Brazilian said to be open to leaving the Etihad Stadium in search of regular first-team football.

Asked whether the scale of the outlay weighs on him, De Zerbi waved it away. "Zero pressure," he said. "You know why? Because a taxi driver in London stopped me to congratulate me on the transfer market." He recalled the driver telling him, "You are spending a lot of money," before he asked who the man supported — the reply was Arsenal, De Zerbi's point being that even rival fans recognise what Tottenham are trying to build.

The coach's broader argument is that Spurs have no choice but to match the market. He pointed to Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal as clubs that have all spent heavily to stay at the top table, framing Tottenham's outlay as the price of genuinely competing rather than simply making up the numbers.

De Zerbi also described his personal approach to negotiations in typically blunt terms. "In the transfer market, when I want one player I become like a shark," he said. "No chance to say no!" It is a mentality that fits a summer in which Tottenham have twice smashed their own transfer ceiling in the space of two days.

The context matters. Tottenham only narrowly avoided relegation last season, and De Zerbi's remit since taking over has been as much about rebuilding confidence as personnel. A club that spent last spring fighting to stay in the Premier League is now being backed to challenge closer to the top of it — a shift De Zerbi is clearly keen to sell to a fanbase that has heard promises before.

Whether Savinho or another forward arrives before the window shuts, De Zerbi's message is consistent: this is not a one-off splurge but a project still being assembled, and by his own count, still less than two-thirds finished.

title: Even China's emperor wouldn't get Bayern talking about Olise, says Hoeneß
dek: Bayern Munich's honorary president mocked fresh Real Madrid speculation over Michael Olise, insisting the France winger is going nowhere this summer
body: Bayern Munich have had enough of being asked about Michael Olise's future. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß used a trademark piece of theatre to shut the door on renewed Real Madrid speculation, ONE reports, delivering a line that has now travelled well beyond Munich.

"Even if the emperor of China came, we wouldn't even discuss Olise with him," Hoeneß said, according to the report — a way of stressing that no visitor, however grand or well-funded, is going to talk Bayern into a sale.

The comment was aimed squarely at Real Madrid, who have been strongly linked with a move for the French winger this summer. Spanish and German outlets have reported Los Blancos could be prepared to go as high as roughly €200 million for the 24-year-old, a figure that would rank among the most expensive transfers in the sport's history.

Olise arrived at Bayern from Crystal Palace in the summer of 2024 and quickly became one of Bundesliga's most watchable attackers, signing a long-term contract that runs to 2029. He has since made himself close to undroppable under the club's coaching staff.

Hoeneß went further than simply denying contact with Madrid, framing Olise as part of an attacking unit the club regards as untouchable. "We have the best attacking trio in the world: Olise, Luis Díaz and Harry Kane," he said. "We're not thinking about selling any of them."

The rumours have gathered pace partly because of Olise's form for France at the 2026 World Cup, where he was among the tournament's leading providers with five assists — the kind of showing that tends to sharpen interest from Europe's biggest clubs.
For now, though, Bayern's message is blunt and, in Hoeneß's telling, faintly amused: the speculation can run as long as it likes, but nobody at Säbener Straße is picking up the phone.

title: Hapoel Haifa to give former Manchester City winger Jayden Braaf a trial
dek: The out-of-contract Dutch winger, once one of English football's hottest academy prospects, is set to be assessed by Haifa and could feature in a Toto Cup game against Ironi Kiryat Shmona, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הפועל חיפה הודיעה: ג'יידן בראף יגיע להתרשמות

body: Hapoel Haifa have called up free-agent winger Jayden Braaf for a trial, with the Dutchman set to be run out in a Toto Cup fixture against Ironi Kiryat Shmona while the club takes a close look before deciding whether to offer him a contract, ONE reported.

The 23-year-old was one of the most hyped young talents to emerge from Manchester City's academy in the late 2010s, prized enough that several major European clubs were said to be circling before he even turned 18. He eventually left City on a free transfer for Borussia Dortmund in 2022.

Injuries disrupted his development in Germany and he never established himself in Dortmund's first team. What followed was less a breakout and more a tour of loan spells: a loan at Udinese in Serie A, then a move to Hellas Verona, first on loan and then on a permanent deal reportedly worth around €1 million.

Verona did not work out either. Braaf was farmed out again, to Eredivisie side Fortuna Sittard back in his native Netherlands and then to Serie B club Salernitana, before Hellas Verona terminated his contract by mutual consent on 1 September 2025.

He has been without a club for almost a year since - a striking fall for a player who came through the youth systems at Ajax and PSV Eindhoven before Manchester City signed him at 15, and who won the UEFA European Under-17 Championship with the Dutch national team in 2019.

For Hapoel Haifa, the move carries little risk. Braaf is a free agent, and a look at him in a Toto Cup match costs nothing beyond finding out whether the winger, still only 23, has anything left to offer an Israeli top-flight side hunting for attacking depth.

Nothing has been signed, and ONE's report stops short of promising a contract will follow the trial - but the fact that Haifa are giving him a run against Kiryat Shmona suggests the club believes there is still enough talent there to be worth the look.

title: Beitar Jerusalem are a level above us, admits Austria Wien's Ranftl before Conference League qualifier
dek: Right-back Reinhold Ranftl says Austria's league opener matters more than the third qualifying round tie, while head coach Stefan Helm calls Beitar a fair test for a place in the Conference League's league phase.

verificationSources.label: Israel Hayom - Beitar eliminate AEK Larnaca
Jerusalem Post - Beitar begins new era under coach Almog Cohen
Transfermarkt - Jonas Feddersen to Austria Wien

body: Reinhold Ranftl isn't dressing this one up. Ahead of Austria Wien's Conference League third qualifying round tie with Beitar Jerusalem, the veteran right-back told ONE that Beitar are, in his own words, "currently a level above us" — and that Austria's domestic season opener matters more to him than the European assignment, which he called "a bonus."

The two clubs have never met in a major UEFA competition before. The first leg is set for August 6, with the return a week later, on August 13, in Vienna. As has become routine for Beitar in Europe, their "home" leg won't be played anywhere near Jerusalem: with Israeli clubs still unable to host continental fixtures on home soil because of the security situation, Beitar will again use their base in Ploiești, Romania.

Both sides arrived here by very different routes. Austria Wien eased past Latvia's FK Liepāja 5-1 on aggregate, wrapping the tie up with a 3-1 win in the second leg. Beitar's path was considerably more nerve-shredding: a 1-0 win away to Cyprus's AEK Larnaca in the first leg was nearly undone by a 3-2 defeat after extra time in the return fixture at Ploiești, squaring the aggregate at 3-3, before Beitar held their composure in the penalty shootout to go through.

That context makes Ranftl's assessment notable rather than mere courtesy. "Right now Beitar are a level above us," the 34-year-old said, according to ONE. "We need to understand that the league opener is more important — Europe is a bonus."

Head coach Stefan Helm struck a more measured tone with the same outlet, pushing back gently on his player's read of the tie. "Beitar are more or less at our level," Helm said. "It's a fair challenge for us, and we'll need to give everything we have to get through."

ONE put a number on the gap in resources: Austria Wien's squad is valued at roughly €23 million against Beitar's approximate €17 million. It's a real but hardly enormous difference for a club with Austria Wien's pedigree — 24 Austrian league titles in their history, even if the most recent came back in 2013, and a fourth-place finish in the Bundesliga last season.

There was a lighter subplot to Austria's build-up in the win over Liepāja. Jonas Feddersen, the 19-year-old defender who joined Austria Wien from Borussia Dortmund's academy this summer, scored on his home debut for the club. "I think I made a good impression," he told ONE. "The fact the ball went in just like that, in my first home match — maybe fate had a hand in it too."

The stakes for both clubs are considerable: the winner advances directly into the Conference League's league phase, a lucrative and prestigious destination neither side will want to let slip in a two-legged tie. For Beitar, playing under new head coach Almog Cohen after his summer promotion from the club's sporting director role, reaching the league phase would be an emphatic marker for his first European campaign in charge.

Whatever Ranftl or Helm believe about the gap between the sides on paper, Beitar have already shown in Cyprus that they can grind out a tie under pressure. Austria Wien, for their part, sound wary enough of that resilience to be talking about giving everything just to survive it.

title: Beitar draw Austria Wien, Austrian football's fallen empire, in Conference League play-off
dek: The Violets have 24 league titles and a 1978 European Cup final to their name, but Beitar Jerusalem's third-round opponent arrives with the financial muscle of an ambitious rebuild rather than the aristocracy of old.

verificationSources.label: NÖN - Austria Wien beat Liepāja, meet Beitar
UEFA.com - Austria Wien vs Liepāja match info

body: Beitar Jerusalem now know exactly what stands between them and the Conference League league phase: a club that once ruled Austrian football and is trying, slowly and without Red Bull's billions, to find its way back toward the top.

Austria Wien await in the third qualifying round after beating Latvia's FK Liepāja 2-0 away and 3-1 at home for a 5-1 aggregate win, a comfortable passage that ONE describes as putting the Viennese side visibly ahead of where they were in their previous Conference League campaign, when they were thrashed 4-0 by Hapoel Beer Sheva in 2022.

The tie is scheduled for Thursday, with Beitar's side of the draw shaped by the club's now-familiar European reality: because Beitar cannot host UEFA matches in Jerusalem, the first leg goes ahead on neutral ground in Romania, before the return leg at Austria's Franz-Horr-Stadion (Generali Arena) in Vienna's Favoriten district on August 13.

Historically, this is one of the heaviest names Israeli football has drawn in years. Austria Wien have won the Austrian championship 24 times, second only to great rivals Rapid Wien's 32, and reached the European Cup final in 1978 before losing to Nottingham Forest. In 1985 they pushed Liverpool in the European Cup quarter-finals.

But that pedigree has curdled into nostalgia. Austria's last title came in 2013 - considered a genuine upset at the time - and Red Bull Salzburg's financial takeover of Austrian football since has left the Vienna club scrapping for European places rather than domestic silverware, finishing third and then fourth in Stephan Helm's first two seasons in charge.

Helm, 43 and now into his third year as head coach, is central to ONE's framing of the club's project: a coach without harsh words for his players, credited with a deep tactical understanding and a willingness to adapt his system to the opponent in front of him. His own assessment of his ambitions ahead of this campaign was blunt - "I'm hungrier than ever," he said.

The squad Beitar will face is not short of experience. Centre-back Alexander Dragović has earned around 100 caps for Austria and played at both Euro 2016 and Euro 2020, giving the side a leader who has operated at the highest level of the international game even as his club has slipped from it.

Further forward, German striker Johannes Eggestein carried much of Austria's attacking threat last season with nine goals and six assists, while South Korean utility man Lee Kang-hee and central midfielder Manfred Fischer round out a squad ONE frames as more balanced than the group Beer Sheva dismantled three years ago.

For Beitar, who advanced past AEK Larnaca via a 1-0 aggregate scoreline decided on penalties, the tie represents a considerable step up in class - a club with continental pedigree, however faded, and a coach openly hungry to restore some of it. The two legs will decide who reaches the Conference League's league phase for 2026/27.

title: Arsenal closing in on €90m deal for Bruno Guimarães
dek: Newcastle's Brazil international has agreed personal terms and the two clubs are finalising a fee, according to ONE and L'Équipe, as the Premier League champions push through a marquee summer signing.
body: Arsenal appear to be on the verge of landing one of the summer's most sought-after midfielders. ONE reports, citing French outlet L'Équipe, that the Premier League champions are in the final stages of a deal to sign Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães, with the transfer expected to be wrapped up within days.

The two clubs have reached an agreement in principle around a base fee of €90 million, according to the report. Bonus payments on top of that figure, along with agent fees, are still being ironed out, but the framework of the deal is said to be in place.

It has been a drawn-out negotiation. Newcastle rejected two earlier Arsenal offers, worth €70 million and €80 million respectively, as they held out for a fee closer to €100 million for their 28-year-old captain. The Gunners' improved bid appears to have finally bridged the gap.

Guimarães, for his part, is reported to have made the move to north London his priority over the past month, with personal terms on a five-year contract already understood to be agreed between player and club.

The Brazilian has been one of the standout central midfielders in the Premier League since arriving at St James' Park from Lyon in January 2022 for an initial €50 million. He has since become Newcastle's captain and a fixture for Brazil, winning 48 caps and starring at this summer's World Cup, where he scored four goals and was named his country's outstanding player.

Should the move go through, Lyon stand to benefit as well. ONE and L'Équipe report that Guimarães' former club are due more than €8 million through a sell-on clause written into the original transfer that took him to Tyneside.

For Arsenal, adding Guimarães would represent a significant statement of intent from Mikel Arteta's newly-crowned champions, reinforcing a midfield already at the core of last season's title triumph. For Newcastle, losing their captain and on-field leader would be a blow, even at a fee that reflects his standing as one of the league's premier holding midfielders.

Nothing has been confirmed by either club, and as with any deal still being negotiated, the final numbers and timing could yet shift. But the direction of travel, per ONE's report, points firmly toward Guimarães swapping Newcastle black-and-white for Arsenal red.

title: Fifa adviser Cordeiro quits in protest at Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan
dek: Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to Gianni Infantino and a member of the White House World Cup task force, resigned calling the plan to sell a stake in the tournament "a bad deal for football".
body: Gianni Infantino's push to bring private money into the World Cup has claimed its first senior casualty inside his own camp. Carlos Cordeiro, one of the FIFA president's most trusted advisers, resigned on Friday, saying he could not stand by a plan he called "the worst deal for world football".

Cordeiro did not go quietly. In his resignation statement he wrote that he had "no part in this proposal" and opposed it "firmly and unequivocally" — an unusually blunt break from a figure who had operated at Infantino's side for years, including a seat on the White House Task Force for the 2026 World Cup in the United States.

The plan at the centre of the row would spin FIFA's commercial operations — the rights to the men's and women's World Cups and the Club World Cup — into a new subsidiary, tentatively valued at $20 billion, with up to 20 percent sold off to outside investors. FIFA says the sale would raise roughly $4.2 billion.

Cordeiro rejected the logic outright. "Selling a permanent stake in football's most valuable asset to raise $4.2 billion makes little sense," he said, arguing it amounted to "mortgaging football's future without any compelling justification" for an organisation that operates debt-free and sits on billions in reserves.

The identity of the prospective anchor investor has only sharpened the controversy: Thrive Eternal, a firm launched by Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump. The proposed tie-up with a Kushner-linked fund has fed criticism that the deal is as much about political proximity to Washington as football finance.

FIFA has framed the plan as a way to sharply increase support for its 211 member associations, lifting the federation development budget for 2027-2030 to $20 million per association, up from $8 million currently, with an optional $20 million advance available immediately from the proceeds.

That pitch has not softened the opposition. UEFA has already accused Infantino of "crossing a line", insisting the World Cup is not FIFA's alone to sell, and ONE reports that European, North American and Asian confederations had all pushed back on the proposal even before Cordeiro's resignation.

Cordeiro, a former U.S. Soccer Federation president and one-time Goldman Sachs banker, was seen as a bridge between Infantino and American football and political interests — making his public break all the more damaging to a plan already fighting for support on several continents.

With his own senior adviser now among the plan's most visible critics, Infantino finds himself increasingly isolated on an initiative he has pitched as transformative for FIFA's finances but which, for now, has united much of the sport's governing establishment against him.

Cordeiro also served on the White House Task Force for the 2026 World Cup and is a former U.S. Soccer Federation president and ex-Goldman Sachs banker.

The proposed anchor investor is Thrive Eternal, a firm launched by Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.
UEFA has publicly opposed the plan, accusing FIFA of 'crossing a line', and Cordeiro said the deal made little sense for a debt-free organisation with billions in reserves.

title: Ter Stegen closes in on Ajax loan as Brentford smash transfer record for Sangaré
dek: Barcelona's goalkeeper is set to sign for Ajax on a season-long loan this weekend, while Brentford have agreed a club-record £41m deal for Mali midfielder Mamadou Sangaré.
body: Two of the more eye-catching pieces of transfer business in Europe this week are edging towards completion, ONE reports: Marc-André ter Stegen's surprise switch to Ajax, and Brentford tearing up their own record books to land a Malian midfielder few outside France had heard of a year ago.

Ter Stegen, still Barcelona's captain on paper, is set to join Ajax on a season-long loan through June 2027, with no option or obligation to buy attached to the deal. At 34, and having lost his place in Hansi Flick's plans, the German international goes in search of regular football again.

The financial mechanics explain why this deal took weeks to untangle. Barcelona, still constrained by La Liga's spending rules, will cover the bulk of ter Stegen's substantial wages — as much as 90 percent, according to reporting cited by ONE — with Ajax picking up no more than 10 percent themselves.

The move has a personal thread running through it: Ajax head coach Míchel worked with ter Stegen during the goalkeeper's loan spell at Girona in 2025-26, and it was the Spaniard who pushed for him at the Johan Cruyff Arena this time round.

Ter Stegen travelled to Amsterdam on Friday, with a medical and formal signature both pencilled in for Saturday. Transfer insider Fabrizio Romano described the deal as "never in doubt." If the paperwork clears before the end of Friday, he would be eligible for Ajax's Conference League qualifying tie; either way, he is expected to be available for the Eredivisie opener away at Zwolle on August 9.

Brentford's business is smaller in profile but bigger in scale for a club that has built its reputation on shrewd, modest recruitment. The Bees have agreed a fee in the region of £41m (roughly €48m) for Mamadou Sangaré, a 24-year-old Malian midfielder at RC Lens — comfortably the largest sum Brentford have ever committed to a single signing.

It eclipses the £36m Brentford paid Bournemouth last summer for winger Dango Ouattara, which had stood as the club's previous benchmark. Sangaré becomes, by some distance, the first Brentford player to command a fee north of £40m.

Sangaré's route to west London has run through Austria and northern France: he was signed from Mali by Red Bull Salzburg as an 18-year-old before a move to Lens, where his form in Ligue 1 is reported to have drawn interest from Manchester United, Chelsea and Liverpool before Brentford moved decisively.

According to Sports Mole and TeamTalk, the deal has also been framed as a succession plan of sorts, with Brentford anticipating Jordan Henderson's departure for Chelsea and looking to Sangaré to help rebuild the midfield around that gap.

Neither deal was fully signed, sealed and delivered at the time of writing. Personal terms for Sangaré are reported to be agreed, with the transfer expected to be finalised within days once the formalities are completed, while ter Stegen's move still awaits Saturday's medical and signature in Amsterdam.

Barcelona will cover as much as 90 percent of ter Stegen's wages during the loan, with Ajax paying no more than 10 percent.
Ajax head coach Míchel previously worked with ter Stegen at Girona during the 2025-26 season and requested the move.
Ter Stegen's medical and formal signing in Amsterdam were scheduled for Saturday, with travel completed on Friday.
Brentford have agreed a club-record fee of around £41m (roughly €48m) for Mali midfielder Mamadou Sangaré from RC Lens.
The Sangaré fee surpasses Brentford's previous record of £36m, paid to Bournemouth last year for Dango Ouattara.
Sangaré, 24, began his European career at Red Bull Salzburg before moving to RC Lens.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva dealt blow as Adar Ratner is found to have torn meniscus
dek: An MRI scan has confirmed a meniscus tear for the young centre-back, ONE reports, with the club weighing surgery against conservative treatment while pressing on with its search for attacking reinforcements.
body: Maccabi Petah Tikva have been handed an unwelcome fitness setback just as pre-season ramps up, with ONE reporting that defender Adar Ratner has been diagnosed with a torn meniscus.

The initial prognosis had sounded relatively encouraging, according to the report, but a follow-up MRI scan told a different story, revealing the tear even as it ruled out any damage to the anterior cruciate ligament.

ONE reports that Ratner faces around two months on the sidelines, though there is a scenario in which he could keep playing through the issue for a further two weeks depending on which treatment path the club and medical staff settle on.

That decision is still open: Maccabi Petah Tikva are weighing conservative management against surgical intervention, a call that will shape not just Ratner's timeline but how his knee holds up over the rest of the campaign.

The 23-year-old centre-back, contracted to the Petah Tikva club through 2029, has been a fixture in the squad's plans, and the injury lands at an awkward moment as the team shapes its squad ahead of the new season.

ONE's report is at pains to stress that the setback should not derail the club's broader recruitment plans. Maccabi Petah Tikva are still pushing ahead with reinforcements in attack, with striker Marco Rekoniatz expected in Israel within 24 hours to undergo a medical and sign through the end of the season.

Rekoniatz previously played under Ziv Aria, Petah Tikva's current manager, during Aria's spell at Hapoel Jerusalem, where he scored twice in the league last season — a familiarity that appears to have smoothed the move.
For now, the focus at the club shifts to Ratner's recovery timeline, with an update on the surgery-versus-rehab decision likely to follow once the medical staff have completed their assessment.

title: Maldini leads tributes to Franco Baresi: 'What will we do without our captain?'
dek: AC Milan's one-club legend and Italy's 1994 World Cup captain has died at 66, prompting grief across Italian football from Paolo Maldini, Gianluigi Buffon and even the club's fiercest rivals.

verificationSources.label: CNN - AC Milan and Italy legend dies at 66

body: Franco Baresi, the defender who spent two decades marshalling AC Milan's back line and captained Italy into the 1994 World Cup final, has died at 66. AC Milan confirmed the news in a statement that captured the mood inside the club: "The entire history of AC Milan is in tears."

The club went further in a fuller tribute, one that framed Baresi as inseparable from its identity. "His example and integrity will remain forever embedded in the club's DNA, just like his iconic number 6 shirt," the statement read. "The condolences that AC Milan extend to the family of Franco Baresi in this difficult time are shared by every Rossonero, who feels this loss as their own."

No tribute carried more weight than the one from Paolo Maldini, the defender Baresi mentored and eventually handed the captaincy to at San Siro. ONE reported Maldini's words in full: "You protected me when I was a child, guided me as a young man, and inspired me as an adult. You were the greatest footballer I have ever had the honour of playing alongside." It was Maldini's anguished question - what will we do without our captain? - that summed up how deeply Baresi's death has been felt inside the club he served for his entire career.

Reports in the Spanish press, including AS, said Baresi had been fighting an illness for close to a year that began with surgery to remove a pulmonary nodule in August 2025, after which he started a course of immunotherapy. AC Milan did not disclose a cause of death in its own statement, but the club noted his last public appearance had come at the opening ceremony of the Milan Winter Olympics in February.

Baresi's career was, in the truest sense, a one-club story. He made 710 appearances and scored 31 goals for Milan across 20 years, having made his Serie A debut at 17 in the 1977-78 season, and served as club captain for 15 of those seasons - a rare stretch of loyalty in modern football.

The trophy haul that followed was extraordinary: six Serie A titles, three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups, two UEFA Super Cups and four Italian Super Cups, most of it won as the defensive foundation of Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello's all-conquering Milan sides of the late 1980s and early 1990s.

With Italy, Baresi was part of the squad that won the 1982 World Cup in Spain, even though he did not play in the tournament. He became the Azzurri's mainstay through the following decade and captained the side to the 1994 World Cup final in the United States, playing through a serious knee injury to appear against Brazil before Italy lost the match on penalties.

Gianni Rivera, who played alongside Baresi at Milan between 1977 and 1979 as the younger man broke through, recalled how quickly he made his mark. According to ONE, Rivera said Baresi debuted early and rapidly established himself as one of the finest defenders in Italian football.

Fabio Capello, who coached Baresi through Milan's most dominant years, described him as a figure who commanded respect and served as a role model, saying his humble character inspired teammates never to give up on the pitch.

Gianluigi Buffon, then a 17-year-old goalkeeper making his own debut, remembered facing Baresi on 19 November 1995 as an experience he never forgot - sharing a pitch, he said, with a genuine champion.

Tributes crossed the usual battle lines of Italian football. Inter Milan, Baresi's fiercest rival across the Milan derby for two decades, acknowledged him as a defining figure not just of that rivalry but of Italian football history. Juventus, similarly, praised his talent, class, leadership and conduct both on and off the pitch.

Italian Football Federation president Giovanni Malagò and prime minister Giorgia Meloni both added their own tributes, each stressing the same theme that ran through the day: that Baresi wore only two jerseys in his career, Milan's and Italy's, and never wavered from either.
facts: Franco Baresi, the former AC Milan and Italy defender, has died at 66.
He spent his entire 20-year professional career at AC Milan, making 710 appearances and scoring 31 goals, and served as club captain for 15 seasons.
He won six Serie A titles, three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups, two UEFA Super Cups and four Italian Super Cups with Milan.
He was part of Italy's 1982 World Cup-winning squad, though he did not play in that tournament, and later captained Italy to the 1994 World Cup final, where they lost to Brazil on penalties.
Paolo Maldini led tributes, calling Baresi 'the greatest footballer I have ever had the honour of playing alongside.'
Reports in the Spanish press said Baresi had undergone surgery for a pulmonary nodule in August 2025 followed by immunotherapy; AC Milan's own statement did not give a cause of death.
Tributes also came from Gianni Rivera, Fabio Capello, Gianluigi Buffon, Inter Milan, Juventus, Italian Football Federation president Giovanni Malagò and prime minister Giorgia Meloni.

title: Casemiro: my dream was always to play alongside Leo Messi
dek: The Brazilian midfielder used his official Inter Miami unveiling to reflect on years of trying to stop Messi as a rival, and what it now means to have him as a teammate.
body: For years Casemiro's job was to stop Lionel Messi. Now, as he put it at his official Inter Miami presentation this week, he finally gets to enjoy him instead.

"I always wanted to be with the best, I dreamed every day of being with him and playing with him," the Brazilian midfielder said of Messi, according to ONE. "Every player dreams of playing with one of the best of all time."

Casemiro went further in describing the Argentine, who has spent the past three seasons transforming Inter Miami into MLS champions. "He's one of the gods, if not the god of football," he said, adding that he wants to "enjoy being with him, help him win, make him even greater."

The 34-year-old joined Inter Miami as a free agent after his Manchester United contract expired at the end of last season, closing out 14 years in Europe with Real Madrid, Porto and United that brought 21 trophies, including five Champions League titles.

It is a strange turn for a player who spent much of his career on the opposite side of the Messi story. Casemiro faced him repeatedly in El Clasico for Real Madrid against Barcelona, and again as Brazil met Argentina in World Cup qualifying and Copa America football, rarely with much joy.
"The amount of problems Messi gave me, of course I dreamed of playing with him," Casemiro said. "I could never stop him, I always needed help from my teammates."

Before signing, Casemiro said he sought advice from fellow Brazilian Kaká, who knows the league from his years at Orlando City, and he made clear the move to Florida was his first choice despite interest elsewhere. "I had many options, I had offers in Italy, I had many teams reaching out, but I am exactly where I want to be," he said.

He has already featured for his new club, playing the full 90 minutes as Inter Miami beat CF Montreal 1-0 last weekend in his MLS debut. The signing arrives with the midfield depth Inter Miami have lacked while leaning heavily on Messi's attacking output, and Casemiro's stated aim now is straightforward: help the Argentine keep winning.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv close in on Daniel Theis as Armando Bacot deal also nears
dek: The yellow-and-blue are rebuilding their frontcourt around two experienced EuroLeague centres, while Lonnie Walker moves toward an early exit.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's summer frontcourt rebuild is taking shape, with ONE reporting that the club appears close to signing German centre Daniel Theis, whose candidacy the outlet says it was first to report.

Theis, 34, stands 2.03m and is expected to leave ASVEL Villeurbanne this summer after the French club ran into financial difficulties, according to the report. Sportando, citing Israel Hayom's Tomer Givati, separately reported that Maccabi have opened advanced negotiations with the veteran big man.

The competition for his signature is real. Sportando's reporting adds that Hapoel Tel Aviv showed early interest in Theis, while Barcelona also remain in the race after missing out on Moses Wright, underlining how sought-after the experienced centre is around the EuroLeague this window.

Alongside Theis, ONE reports that Maccabi are also on the verge of adding another big man, American centre Armando Bacot Jr., who spent last season at Fenerbahce. The 26-year-old, 2.08m, is expected to sign with the yellow-and-blue.

Bacot's move to Israel would mark a reset after a difficult debut EuroLeague season. Under Fenerbahce coach Sarunas Jasikevicius he saw limited minutes, averaging just 2.4 points and 1.8 rebounds in EuroLeague play, a sharp comedown from his college numbers at North Carolina, where he set the program's career rebounding record. Turkish and EuroLeague outlets have reported Maccabi are lining up a two-year contract for him.

The double swoop for size comes as Maccabi manage a parallel departure at the other end of the roster. ONE reports that guard Lonnie Walker is moving toward an exit, with the club estimating the transaction will close around $600,000.

Walker joined Maccabi a year ago on a guaranteed three-year deal worth more than $2.2 million annually, built with an NBA opt-out clause each summer, but he failed to land an NBA contract this offseason. He averaged 15.2 points and 2.2 assists last season and has reportedly been offered to Partizan Belgrade and Real Madrid as Maccabi and the guard work toward an amicable split.

None of the moves has been made official by the club as of Thursday, and each remains, in ONE's framing, a matter of advanced talks rather than a done deal. But taken together, they point to a significant reshaping of Maccabi's roster heading into the new EuroLeague season, swapping perimeter scoring for size and experience up front.

title: Curtis Jones clashes with Szoboszlai as Liverpool's pre-season harmony cracks
dek: Video of the midfielder remonstrating with teammates after a win over Wrexham has fuelled talk of a dressing-room rift — and, according to ONE, a threat to walk away from the club altogether.
body: Curtis Jones was filmed in an animated, arm-waving confrontation with Dominik Szoboszlai moments after Liverpool's final whistle against Wrexham in New York on Wednesday, and by Thursday the clip had become the biggest talking point of the club's pre-season tour.

Footage circulating on social media shows Jones squaring up to Szoboszlai at full time, clearly agitated, before Kostas Tsimikas and Jeremie Frimpong moved in to separate the pair and calm things down. What exactly triggered it has not been confirmed by the club.

ONE reports that Jones was heard telling teammates: "Listen, I'm done. I can't stay at this club anymore." The Israeli outlet did not specify how the quote was obtained, and no other outlet has independently verified that precise wording — so it should be read as ONE's report of what was said, not a confirmed, on-record statement from Jones.

The row played out despite Liverpool winning the game itself. Rio Ngumoha struck the only goal of the friendly at Yankee Stadium, latching onto a Szoboszlai pass and seeing his shot deflect in, continuing an encouraging pre-season for the teenager on the club's United States tour.

It is also the first pre-season under Andoni Iraola, who took over at Anfield in June after Liverpool sacked Arne Slot following a troubled defence of the Premier League title. A dressing-room flare-up this early is an unwelcome headline for a new manager still assembling his group.

British outlets covering the same footage have floated a specific theory: that Szoboszlai, standing in as captain, handed the armband to Tsimikas rather than Jones, and that decision — not tactics or effort — is what set Jones off. Liverpool have not commented on the cause.

The timing adds another layer. Jones has been strongly linked with a move to Inter Milan, with Italian reports describing manager Christian Chivu as keen on signing him, though Liverpool are said to be holding out for a fee in the region of €40 million while Inter have so far declined to meet that valuation.

Reaction among Liverpool supporters has been unforgiving. Several fan outlets ran pieces over the past day arguing Jones should be sold, with the word "toxic" attached to descriptions of the dressing-room mood — a striking overreaction, perhaps, to a pre-season friendly, but a sign of how thin patience is running.

Liverpool's US tour continues on Sunday against Leeds United in Chicago, the next chance for Iraola to show the group has moved past the incident before a Premier League season that will already be judged against last term's collapse.

title: Lookman is shaping up as Atlético Madrid's answer to life after Griezmann
dek: With Antoine Griezmann gone to Orlando City and Julián Álvarez's future unsettled, ONE reports Diego Simeone is building his new-look attack around Ademola Lookman, the Nigerian forward who scored twice inside the first half of a preseason rout of Getafe.
body: Atlético Madrid spent a decade organising its attack around Antoine Griezmann. Now that he is gone, to Orlando City of all places, Diego Simeone appears to have settled on his successor — and, according to ONE, it is Ademola Lookman.

Griezmann's departure this summer, confirmed back in March and finalised when the transfer window opened in July, closed out ten years in which he became one of the defining attacking figures of the Simeone era. His move to Orlando City, on a two-year MLS deal, leaves a real void at the top of the Atlético side.

Lookman arrived in Madrid before Griezmann had even left, signed from Atalanta last winter for a reported €35 million on a contract running until 2030. The Nigeria international scored within weeks of his debut and has been positioned by Simeone as the player to carry the attacking load going forward.

The timing matters. Julián Álvarez's own long-term future at the club is clouded by Barcelona's pursuit of him — a saga serious enough that Spain's federation has opened disciplinary proceedings against Barcelona over alleged unauthorised approaches. With that uncertainty hanging over the Argentine, ONE reports Simeone has extra reason to build his forward line around a player he trusts to stay and lead it.

Lookman offered an early demonstration of why. In Atlético's preseason opener against Getafe in Los Angeles, which the Rojiblancos won 4-1, he needed barely five minutes of game time to score twice, both goals arriving in the first half — the kind of instinctive, predatory finishing that made him one of Serie A's most feared forwards.

Simeone's own assessment, relayed by ONE, is more measured than gushing. "Lookman brings us goals, more goals than overall play," the coach said. "He can still improve his overall play and defensive work. We need him to adapt to the team's way of playing in those aspects." It reads less like faint praise than a coach setting out exactly what he expects from his new focal point.

Tactically, ONE reports Simeone is using Lookman as a second striker who drifts left, rather than pinning him to a fixed wing role — an attempt to let him hunt space and finish chances rather than track back as a orthodox winger, while still demanding the defensive discipline Atlético sides are built on.

The dressing room appears to be buying in early. ONE reports that captain Koke has already talked up the Nigerian's importance to the group, describing him in terms that suggest the squad sees him as the new spearhead rather than just another summer arrival.

According to ONE's numbers, Lookman was directly involved in a goal every 106 minutes for Atalanta last season and scored roughly every 153 minutes, with 20 assists to his name — figures the outlet says made him more efficient in front of goal last term than either Griezmann or Álvarez.

What Atlético are banking on, beyond the output, is character: a forward who demands the ball, takes responsibility in big moments, and carries the same decisive streak that defined his three seasons turning Atalanta into a Champions League regular. Replacing a ten-year totem is never simple, but Simeone's early signs suggest he believes he has found the man to try.

title: Barcelona could face points deduction as Spanish federation opens Álvarez tampering probe
dek: The Royal Spanish Football Federation has launched disciplinary proceedings against Barcelona after Atlético Madrid accused the club of illegally courting Julián Álvarez, with a three-point La Liga deduction among the sanctions on the table.
body: Barcelona are facing the threat of a three-point deduction in La Liga after Spain's football federation opened a formal disciplinary investigation into the club's pursuit of Atlético Madrid striker Julián Álvarez, ONE reports.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) launched the extraordinary proceedings under its disciplinary code after Atlético lodged an official complaint accusing Barcelona of making repeated, unauthorised contact with Álvarez over several months in an attempt to lure him away from the club.

Atlético went public with its grievance, describing Barcelona's conduct as harassment and taking the complaint to both the Spanish federation and FIFA. The Madrid club argues the approaches came while Álvarez remained firmly under contract, which runs until the summer of 2030.

The saga gained fresh fuel when Álvarez himself spoke publicly during Argentina's 2026 World Cup campaign, saying on June 22 that he wanted to "fulfil his dream" — remarks widely read in Spain as an acknowledgement of Barcelona's interest.

According to ONE, the sanctions available to the RFEF against Barcelona under Section 93 of its disciplinary code are severe: a deduction of three points in next season's La Liga table, partial or full closure of the club's facilities for a number of matches, a ban on registering new players for one or more transfer windows, and financial fines.

Álvarez himself is not shielded from the process. The RFEF could suspend him for anywhere between one month and two years, with a minimum four-match ban should he be found to have breached the rules, and he could also be ordered to compensate Atlético for the period he is unable to play.

The case will now proceed through Spain's extraordinary disciplinary procedure, with Barcelona and Atlético each submitting written arguments before a disciplinary instructor rules on whether the regulations were actually broken.
Crucially, the opening of an investigation does not mean sanctions are inevitable — Barcelona have been formally notified and will get the chance to mount a defence before any verdict is reached.

Still, the scale of the potential punishment is striking for a club already navigating tight financial fair play constraints under La Liga's spending rules, and it adds a fresh layer of tension to a transfer pursuit that Atlético insists crossed a clear line.

title: Beitar Jerusalem beat AEK Larnaca 4-3 on penalties, replaying their 2016 escape almost move for move
dek: A 1-0 win in Cyprus, a 3-2 collapse at home and a nervy shootout — a decade after eliminating Omonia Nicosia the exact same way, Beitar Jerusalem lived through it all again in the Conference League.

verificationSources.label: ONE — match report on the Larnaca tie
Walla Sport — Beitar win 0-1 away at Larnaca
Sport1/Maariv — Beitar beat Larnaca on penalties
ESPN — Beitar 1-0 Omonia, first leg, July 14, 2016
Transfermarkt — Omonia Nicosia vs Beitar Jerusalem, July 21, 2016

body: Beitar Jerusalem needed a penalty shootout and two saves from Miguel Silva to see off AEK Larnaca in Conference League qualifying this week — and for anyone who has followed the club long enough, the whole tie played out like a rerun of a European night from exactly ten years earlier.

The numbers line up almost too neatly. In the first leg in Cyprus, Beitar won 1-0 away. In the return leg at Teddy Stadium, they lost 3-2 after extra time. The aggregate finished level at 3-3, and Beitar went through anyway — this time on penalties, 4-3, after Silva denied two Larnaca kicks.

Omer Atzili was at the heart of it in normal time, winning and converting a penalty to make it 1-1 on the night before halftime, then producing a stunning strike from outside the box in the 87th minute to put Beitar 2-2 and, briefly, back in front on aggregate. Silva then erred in stoppage time, allowing Larnaca to snatch a third goal in the 92nd minute and force extra time, before Beitar's goalkeeper redeemed himself in the shootout.

Manager Almog Cohen's side had already shown they could win away in Cyprus without conceding, a rarity for an Israeli club on the road in Europe. Losing the home leg by the same 3-2 scoreline they once suffered against a different Cypriot opponent, a decade to the summer, is the detail that gives the story its edge.

That earlier tie came in July 2016, against Omonia Nicosia in Europa League qualifying. Beitar won the first leg 1-0 at home, then lost 3-2 away in Nicosia — an aggregate score, 3-3, identical to this year's. Back then, away goals still decided ties level on aggregate, and Beitar's two goals scored in Cyprus were enough to send them through over Omonia's none scored in Jerusalem.

According to ONE, the scorers in that 2016 defeat that somehow still counted as progress were Amir Agayev and Killian Sheridan, the latter a forward who had earlier played for Hapoel Ironi Kiryat Shmona. UEFA has since scrapped the away-goals rule altogether, which is exactly why this year's identical aggregate needed a shootout rather than a countback.

It is a coincidence rather than a pattern with any deeper meaning — different opponents, different competition names, a different rulebook — but it is still a striking one for a club whose European qualifying campaigns are rarely straightforward. Both ties involved Cypriot opposition, both were built on an away win followed by a home defeat by an identical scoreline, and both ended with Beitar's name in the next round's draw.
For this season's squad, the more immediate takeaway is simpler: a difficult two-legged tie is behind them, and Beitar remain alive in the Conference League qualifying rounds heading into August.

A decade earlier, in July 2016, Beitar beat Omonia Nicosia 1-0 at home in the first leg of a Europa League qualifier, then lost 3-2 away — an identical 3-3 aggregate, with Beitar advancing on the since-abolished away-goals rule.
ONE reports the 2016 second-leg scorers for Beitar were Amir Agayev and Killian Sheridan, the latter formerly of Hapoel Ironi Kiryat Shmona.

title: Melbourne, 26 January 2008: The Final That Made 'Andyoni' Israel's First Grand Slam Champions
dek: On a scorching Saturday at Rod Laver Arena, Jonathan Erlich and Andy Ram beat France's Arnaud Clément and Michaël Llodra to win the Australian Open men's doubles title — the first Grand Slam trophy ever lifted by an all-Israeli pair.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz — Israeli Duo of Ram, Erlich Win Australian Open Doubles Title
International Jewish Sports Hall of Fame — Jonathan "Yoni" Erlich

body: Rod Laver Arena empties out fast once the marquee singles matches finish, but on the evening of Saturday, 26 January 2008, a knot of Israeli flags stayed pressed against the railings. Down on court, two players who had spent a decade grinding through Challenger towns and Tuesday-afternoon doubles slots were serving out the biggest match of their careers. When Jonathan Erlich's final backhand volley dropped away from Arnaud Clément, he and Andy Ram had won 7–5, 7–6(4) — and Israel, for the first time, had a Grand Slam champion built entirely at home.

It sounds like a modest thing to call the men's doubles final a country's defining tennis moment, but for Israel it was exactly that. Ram had already won two Grand Slam mixed-doubles titles, at Wimbledon in 2006 with Vera Zvonareva and at the French Open in 2007 with Nathalie Dechy — proof he belonged at the top of the sport. What Melbourne gave Israel that Erlich's and Ram's other titles could not was a trophy shared by two Israelis, won as an Israeli team, under an Israeli flag raised twice.

Both men had arrived in Israel as small children of Latin American immigrant families. Erlich was born in Buenos Aires in April 1977 and moved with his parents to Haifa before his first birthday. Ram was born in Montevideo, Uruguay, in April 1980, and his family settled in Jerusalem when he was five, which is where he first picked up a racket. Years later the two met through Israel's Wingate Institute tennis program and began partnering on tour, eventually becoming so inseparable in Israeli sports pages that they were simply known as "Andyoni."

Their breakthrough had come five years earlier, at Wimbledon in 2003, where Erlich and Ram reached the men's doubles semifinals — the first time any Israeli had gone that deep into a Grand Slam draw in any discipline. It cost them nothing in ambition; if anything it convinced them doubles was where they could win majors, even if the majors themselves stayed just out of reach for years afterward.

Melbourne in January 2008 finally delivered it. Seeded eighth, Erlich and Ram opened the tournament with an unusual first-round assignment: an all-Israeli derby against Dudi Sela and Harel Levy, which they won in straight sets. They then beat Scott Lipsky and David Martin, outlasted the Czech pairing of František Čermák and Lukáš Dlouhý, and downed Marc Gicquel and Fabrice Santoro in the semifinal to reach a final against the seventh-seeded French duo of Clément and Llodra — themselves former Davis Cup stalwarts and no easy final-round obstacle.

The final swung on small margins. Erlich and Ram took the first set 7–5, then had to survive a tighter second set that went to a tiebreak, closing it out 7–4 to seal the match 7–5, 7–6(4). It was, as Israeli and international press noted at the time, the first Grand Slam trophy ever won by an all-Israeli doubles team — a distinction that, for all of Israel's individual Grand Slam success in mixed and singles play since, still stands.

The Melbourne title also marked the peak of Erlich and Ram individually: in July 2008, only months after the final, both men reached a career-high doubles ranking of world No. 5, the highest either would ever attain.

Their partnership kept paying off for Israeli tennis well beyond Melbourne. In September 2009, Erlich and Ram won the decisive doubles rubber as Israel stunned Russia 3–0 in a Davis Cup World Group quarterfinal in Tel Aviv, beating Marat Safin and Igor Kunitsyn in five sets after Harel Levy and Dudi Sela had already won both opening singles. It sent Israel into its first and, to date, only Davis Cup World Group semifinal.

Erlich played on tour until 2022, closing out a career built almost entirely on doubles craft rather than singles firepower; Ram retired in 2014. Between them they turned a nickname into a genuine Israeli sporting institution. But it is the Melbourne afternoon in January 2008 that remains the reference point — the moment two sons of immigrant families, raised on Israeli hard courts, put an Israeli team's name on a Grand Slam trophy for the only time in the country's history.

In September 2009, Erlich and Ram won the clinching doubles rubber as Israel beat Russia 3–0 in a Davis Cup World Group quarterfinal in Tel Aviv, sending Israel to its only Davis Cup World Group semifinal.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv freezes CEO hearing until chairman returns from vacation
dek: Owner Ofer Yanai postpones the disciplinary process against Tzachi Reichenstein, saying the club cannot function with both its chairman and CEO away at the same time.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have hit pause on the process to remove their basketball CEO, Tzachi Reichenstein, after owner Ofer Yanai decided the club could not go leaderless while its chairman is on a pre-planned vacation, ONE reported.

The disciplinary hearing, which threatened to end Reichenstein's tenure, had been building for weeks after chairman Oren Chason took his seat in the boardroom and clashed with the CEO over how the club should be run, Ynet reported earlier.

With Chason set to be away for around three weeks, Yanai - who controls 56% of the club - concluded that Hapoel Tel Aviv could not operate without either its chairman or its CEO fully in place, according to ONE, and shelved the hearing until Chason is back.

In an email to staff, Yanai stated that all club employees report to Chason during his absence, ONE reported - a message read internally as reinforcing the chairman's authority even while the CEO's own position remains unresolved.

Reichenstein has maintained that under the terms of his contract, only Yanai - not the chairman - holds the power to dismiss him, a dispute over authority that sits at the heart of the rift, according to ONE and Ynet's earlier reporting on the breakdown between the two men.

Chason, who previously chaired the Israel Football Association and ran the country's sports leagues authority, was installed atop Hapoel Tel Aviv's basketball operation only in recent weeks. Sources told Ynet the disagreements between him and Reichenstein were serious enough that the two may simply be unable to keep working together.

For now, the hearing is expected to resume once Chason returns from his break, at which point the club's ownership will move to decide Reichenstein's future. Ynet has separately reported that Tomer Yaron, currently CEO of Hapoel Beersheba/Dimona since 2016, is seen as a possible successor should Reichenstein ultimately be removed.

title: Beitar Jerusalem beat Larnaca 4-3 on penalties to reach Conference League third round
dek: Miguel Silva atoned for a stoppage-time error with two penalty saves as Beitar Jerusalem survived a 3-3 aggregate thriller against AEK Larnaca in Romania to set up a third-round meeting with Austria Wien.
body: Beitar Jerusalem needed every last drop of nerve to survive AEK Larnaca in the second qualifying round of the Conference League, coming through a penalty shootout 4-3 after a pulsating tie finished 3-3 on aggregate, ONE reported.
The victory sends Almog Cohen's side into the third qualifying round, where they will meet Austria Wien with a place in the competition proper still four rounds away.

Beitar had done the hard part first, winning the away leg in Cyprus 1-0 on July 23 through a Brian Carvalho free-kick in the 77th minute, struck after Larnaca defender Mike van der Hoorn was sent off five minutes earlier.

That slender lead looked precious going into the return fixture, which Beitar nominally hosted but which UEFA required to be staged outside Israel because of the ongoing regional security situation. The match was played at the Ilie Oană Stadium in Ploiești, Romania, under heavy police presence, with Beitar's own security team overseeing crowd arrangements.

Larnaca struck first through Hrvoje Miličević, who converted a penalty in the 26th minute to level the tie on aggregate. Beitar hit straight back before the break when Omer Atzili sent Miguel Silva's opposite number the wrong way from the spot in first-half stoppage time.

Miličević restored Larnaca's lead with a second penalty early in the second half, only for Atzili to produce the moment of the night, a stunning strike from around 25 metres in the 87th minute to make it 2-2 in the match and put Beitar back in front on aggregate.
The celebrations were short-lived. Larnaca substitute Riad Bajić snatched a stoppage-time equaliser after a mistake by Silva, dragging the tie level again at 3-3 on aggregate and forcing extra time.
Neither side could find a winner over the additional 30 minutes, Jordan Shoea spurning Beitar's best chance from close range, and the outcome was left to penalties.

It was there that Silva made amends. The Portuguese goalkeeper saved two of Larnaca's spot-kicks as Beitar converted all four of theirs, sealing a 4-3 shootout win and sparing his side's blushes after his part in the late equaliser.
It capped a good night for Israeli clubs in Europe: Hapoel Tel Aviv also advanced in the same round, beating Ludogorets 2-2 in their second leg to progress 4-2 on aggregate.

Beitar now turn to a first-ever meeting with Austria Wien, hosting the first leg on August 6 before the return in Vienna a week later on August 13, as Cohen's squad continues its bid to reach the Conference League group stage.
facts: Beitar Jerusalem beat AEK Larnaca 4-3 on penalties after a 3-3 aggregate draw to reach the Conference League third qualifying round.
The first leg finished AEK Larnaca 0-1 Beitar Jerusalem in Cyprus on July 23, 2026, with Brian Carvalho scoring the only goal after a Larnaca red card.

The second leg, nominally a Beitar home game, was played at the Ilie Oană Stadium in Ploiești, Romania, on July 30, 2026, because UEFA does not permit matches inside Israel amid the regional security situation.
Larnaca won that leg 3-2 (Hrvoje Miličević twice, Riad Bajić in stoppage time) despite two Omer Atzili goals, leveling the tie 3-3 on aggregate and sending it to extra time.
Goalkeeper Miguel Silva saved two penalties in the shootout after a mistake of his had contributed to Larnaca's stoppage-time equaliser.
Beitar will face Austria Wien in the third qualifying round, hosting the first leg on August 6 before traveling to Vienna for the return on August 13.
Hapoel Tel Aviv also advanced to the same round on the same night, beating Ludogorets 4-2 on aggregate.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv on alert as Sofia clash becomes the fight for Europe
dek: With CSKA Sofia confirmed as their Europa League third-round opponent, victory would lock in Conference League football and a seeded play-off spot — defeat risks a much tougher route through qualifying.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC (official) — UEFA draw Maccabi's next opponents

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv now know exactly who stands between them and a seeded route through Europa League qualifying: CSKA Sofia, confirmed as their third-round opponent after the Bulgarians outlasted Qarabağ of Azerbaijan on penalties. ONE frames the tie in blunt terms — this, more than the last round, is the fight for Europe.

Sofia needed a shootout to get there, winning 5-4 on spot-kicks after 120 goalless minutes. It was hardly a statement performance, and ONE reports that has bred some quiet confidence around Maccabi's camp — tempered by the knowledge that a side reaching the third qualifying round of a UEFA competition is rarely there by accident.

That caution looks justified once the Bulgarian champions' squad sheet is examined. CSKA Sofia added Stefano Sensi this summer, the former Inter Milan and Italy midfielder who arrived after his release clause at Cypriot club Anorthosis was triggered for a reported €200,000. Sensi won two Serie A titles and two Italian Super Cups during his time in Milan — a level of pedigree Sheriff Tiraspol, swept aside 6-0 on aggregate in the previous round, simply did not carry.

The numbers behind the tie explain why ONE is treating it as decisive rather than routine. Beat CSKA Sofia and Maccabi go into the Europa League play-off round as a seeded side, with Conference League group-stage football already guaranteed regardless of how that play-off goes. Lose, and the club drops into the unseeded bracket of Conference League qualifying instead — a bracket that could throw up a considerably stronger opponent from one of Europe's leading domestic leagues.

The first leg is set for August 6 in Batumi, Georgia — still Maccabi's adopted home ground while the security situation in Israel keeps the club's continental fixtures away from Bloomfield Stadium — with the return leg in Bulgaria a week later, on August 13.

Off the pitch, ONE reports the club is managing a separate situation involving defender Tyrese Asante. The Dutch centre-back, who arrived from ADO Den Haag in the summer of 2024 and has since collected a league and cup double in Israel, stayed home in Tel Aviv rather than travel for the Sheriff tie while he recovers from what the outlet describes as a prolonged illness.

Maccabi expect to lose Asante to Serie A before the transfer window shuts. ONE names Lazio, Monza and Udinese among the interested parties, though Monza's pursuit appears furthest along: Walla Sport and Sport1 have separately reported an official approach from the newly promoted club, with Maccabi holding out for a fee in the region of €4 million.

None of that changes the immediate picture. Asante remains a Maccabi player, and with Sofia now standing directly in the way of a guaranteed European group stage, the transfer business will have to wait its turn behind two legs that could define the club's continental year.

title: Beitar Jerusalem beat AEK Larnaca 4-3 on penalties to reach Conference League third round
dek: Miguel Silva erased an extra-time lapse with two penalty saves as Beitar advanced 3-3 on aggregate, with Omer Atzili's second-leg brace forcing the shootout in Ploiești.
body: Beitar Jerusalem needed the full 120 minutes, and then a penalty shootout, to get past AEK Larnaca and into the third qualifying round of the Conference League — and by the end of an eventful night in Romania, the story belonged to goalkeeper Miguel Silva.

Silva had been the game's tragic figure for long stretches, having erred in a way that helped drag AEK Larnaca back into the tie and force extra time. But with the shootout level, the Portuguese goalkeeper turned the match on its head, saving two penalties to send Beitar through 4-3 on spot-kicks after the sides had finished level at 3-3 on aggregate.

The club were unequivocal in backing their goalkeeper afterwards. "Miguel Silva is our goalkeeper and we're with him through thick and thin — he's one of our leaders this season," the club said, adding that he "contributed to advancing us to the next stage with two huge penalty saves."

The second leg itself, played at the Ilie Oană Stadium in Ploiești after Beitar again hosted their "home" fixture in Romania, finished 3-2 to the Cypriot side across normal and extra time. Omer Atzili scored twice for Beitar, while Harwaja Milićević struck twice and Riad Baich added a third for AEK Larnaca to send the tie to penalties.

That result meant Beitar's 1-0 first-leg win in Larnaca on 23 July — a match in which they became the first Israeli club to beat a Cypriot side away from home in that fixture — was not enough on its own, and the tie went to away goals' successor: extra time, then the shootout Silva decided.

Beitar's coach, Almog Cohen, was credited by the club with keeping the squad's composure through the twists. "He believed in the players and gave them confidence that we'd win the match," the club said of its manager, who moved from the sporting director's office to the touchline this summer.

Individually, right-back Nana Antwi was singled out for a performance the club described as "Champions League level," with Atzili also praised for a night in which he was Beitar's most consistent attacking threat. Defender Boris Annu, by contrast, was said not to have shown his usual level.
There were also concerns raised over the pitch in Ploiești, with the surface said to have hampered Beitar's technical game — a factor the club will hope to avoid when the run continues.

Beitar's reward is a third qualifying round meeting with Austria Wien, with the sides due to open the tie in Romania again before meeting in Austria the following week. Beitar Jerusalem were not alone among Israeli clubs advancing this week — Hapoel Tel Aviv also progressed to the same round in their own European qualifier.

For Silva, who signed for Beitar in January 2023 and started in the club's 2023 State Cup final win over Maccabi Netanya, it was a night that swung from low to high inside 90 dramatic minutes of shootout football — exactly the kind of moment that, on nights like these, decides whether a European run continues or ends.

title: Avdija, Lillard and Morant: Portland's star glut leaves one question before title contention
dek: ONE reports that general manager Joe Cronin has built a Trail Blazers roster stacked with three capable No. 1 options — with All-Star Deni Avdija in pole position to become the team's long-term centerpiece.

verificationSources.label: ONE - source analysis on Portland's roster hierarchy
ESPN - Grizzlies trade Ja Morant to Trail Blazers
Forbes - Damian Lillard on his return to Portland after Achilles injury
CBS Sports - Trail Blazers hire Micah Nori as head coach
Blazer's Edge - Deni Avdija's 2025-26 season recap and stats

body: Deni Avdija spent the second half of last season carrying Portland almost single-handedly. Now the Trail Blazers have to work out what to do with him just as the roster around him has suddenly become overloaded with scoring options. ONE frames it as the one thing still missing before Portland can be taken seriously as a genuine championship contender: a clear hierarchy among the team's alpha players.

The Blazers head into 2026-27 with three players capable of being a team's primary option. Damian Lillard is back in Portland on a three-year, $42 million contract with a no-trade clause after being waived by Milwaukee, and is targeting a full return from the ruptured Achilles tendon that ended his 2025 campaign. Ja Morant arrived from Memphis in a trade agreed in late June that sent Jerami Grant and Kris Murray the other way. And then there is Avdija himself, who broke out as an All-Star last season while Lillard was sidelined and Portland's other guards were hurt.

That, according to ONE, is exactly the problem general manager Joe Cronin has created. The report says Cronin has built a deep, talented squad without settling who is Portland's true No. 1 option, who is the No. 2, and who fills out the third tier — with too few clearly defined role players beyond forward Toumani Camara and young center Donovan Clingan to balance out so many shot-creators.

Avdija's case is not in question statistically. He averaged 25.5 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.7 assists a game last season on 47/36/80 shooting splits, taking over as Portland's primary ball-handler and shot-creator after Jrue Holiday went down with a calf strain and Scoot Henderson was already out with a hamstring injury. It earned him his first All-Star selection — a landmark for Israeli basketball — and, on ONE's assessment, leaves him in the strongest position of the three to be the Trail Blazers' long-term centerpiece.

Whether that holds once Lillard and Morant are both healthy and on the floor is the question ONE poses without answering. Lillard turned 36 this month and has not played since April 2025, so few expect him to instantly reclaim the shot volume that made him a nine-time All-Star the first time he wore a Portland jersey. Morant, for his part, has played only 79 games across three injury- and incident-hit seasons since his last All-Star year in 2023, and has spoken of the move west as a chance to start over.

Portland also enters the season under a new head coach after an unusually turbulent offseason. Micah Nori, previously the lead assistant in Minnesota, was hired after Chauncey Billups was arrested by the FBI in the autumn as part of a wide-ranging illegal gambling investigation and never returned to the bench.

ONE quotes Nori laying out how he wants his team to play: "We won't be a team that sits and hopes the opponent misses. We'll force opponents into tough shots. Offensively, as long as the clock is running, we'll run too. We won't pull out the ball, look to the bench and wait for set plays. We'll play at a high pace and with clear spacing."

That up-tempo identity is, in part, a bet that Portland's glut of shot-creators can coexist better in transition and space than in a slower, half-court pecking order. It also raises the stakes on training camp: with Lillard, Morant and Avdija potentially all healthy together for the first time, Nori will have to decide quickly who closes games and who plays off the ball.

For now, Avdija looks like the safer bet of the three. He is 25, owed a modest $24 million over the next two seasons on the extension he signed after arriving from Washington, and comes into camp as the incumbent All-Star rather than a returning veteran managing an Achilles injury or a newcomer still learning a new system.

How Portland resolves the hierarchy around him, ONE argues, will determine whether last season's run to the playoffs — the franchise's first postseason appearance since 2021 — was the start of something bigger, or a ceiling reached with too many stars and not enough order.
