title: AEK Larnaca chase first-ever European comeback against Beitar Jerusalem
dek: Mauro Camoranesi's Cypriot side have never overturned a first-leg deficit in Europe — and now must do it against a Beitar team that dominated the opener.
body: Mauro Camoranesi's AEK Larnaca travel to Ploiești, Romania, on Thursday evening chasing something the Cypriot club have never once managed in Europe: overturning a first-leg deficit. A week after losing 1-0 at home to Beitar Jerusalem in the second qualifying round of the Conference League, Larnaca know that anything less than victory ends their campaign.

The tie carries an unusual backdrop. UEFA continues to bar competitive matches from being staged inside Israel this season because of the security situation, so Beitar are hosting their leg roughly 2,500 kilometres from Jerusalem, at Ploiești's Ilie Oană Stadium — the workaround Israeli clubs have used throughout this summer's qualifying rounds.

On the pitch, Beitar arrive with both the aggregate lead and the stronger claim to it. Colombian centre-back Brayan Carabalí settled last Thursday's first leg in Larnaca with a curling free-kick in the 77th minute, moments after AEK were reduced to ten men when defender Mike van der Hoorn was sent off for hauling down forward Timothy Muzie as he broke clear on goal.

Beitar were the sharper side well before the red card, too, finishing the night with 16 shots to AEK's three and 64% of possession — numbers that will have done little to settle nerves in Larnaca this week.

AEK had their moments in the first half, with Imad Faraj Layouni striking a post and Ilija Bajić heading against the opposite upright from the rebound, but could not turn territory into a goal. They now face the harder of the two remaining outcomes: with away goals no longer doubling as a tiebreaker under UEFA's rules, a repeat 1-0 scoreline for the Cypriots would send the tie to extra time, while nothing less than a two-goal winning margin sends Beitar out in normal time.

ONE reports that history is squarely against Camoranesi's team: in every previous European tie where AEK Larnaca lost the first leg, they have gone out. The Cypriot outlet's coverage still struck a defiant note, framing Thursday's task as an attempt to "climb a mountain" and citing the domestic view that "every situation has a first occurrence" and that Camoranesi's players "believed and continue believing strongly in their capabilities."

Camoranesi, the 2006 World Cup winner with Italy and a Juventus favourite as a player, will go into the second leg without Van der Hoorn, who is suspended after his sending-off, leaving Hrvoje Milićević to help marshal a defence that has already shown it can be exposed by Beitar's directness and set-piece threat.

For Beitar, closing out the tie would extend a European run the club's supporters have craved and add to what has already been a strong week for Israeli sides in continental qualifying. A place in the Conference League's third qualifying round — with the prize money and exposure that comes with it — is one result away, though Jerusalem will be wary of a Larnaca side with nothing left to lose on Thursday night.

title: Maccabi, Beitar and Hapoel Tel Aviv all favourites to advance in Europe on Thursday night

body: All three Israeli clubs still alive in European qualifying go into Thursday evening's second legs as heavy favourites with the betting markets, after building commanding first-leg cushions a week ago.

Winner, the Israeli betting operator, has Maccabi Tel Aviv at odds of just 1.25 to see off Sheriff Tiraspol, according to ONE, with a draw priced at 4.40 and an outright win for the Moldovan champions at 6.60 — reflecting just how remote a Maccabi collapse looks after last week's result.

Kenny Miller's side thrashed Sheriff 5-0 away in the first leg of the Europa League second qualifying round on July 23, with Sayed Abu Farchi scoring twice and further goals from Dor Peretz, Sagiv Yehezkal and Issouf Sissokho. The return leg is at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv, and Maccabi need only avoid a five-goal swing to reach the third qualifying round.

Beitar Jerusalem, under new head coach Almog Cohen, carry a slimmer but still healthy advantage into their Conference League qualifier against AEK Larnaca. ONE reports Winner has Beitar to win outright at 1.95, a draw at 3.10 and an AEK win at 2.95 — odds that make the tie close to a coin-flip on the night, even though Beitar won the first leg 1-0 in Cyprus.

That narrower price gap makes sense given the stakes: a 1-0 lead is the kind that can be overturned by a single away goal or two, and Beitar will need a disciplined defensive display at home in Jerusalem to close it out.

The best value for an upset, per the markets cited by ONE, lies with Hapoel Tel Aviv's opponents. Ludogorets Razgrad are priced at just 1.65 to win outright at home in Razgrad, against 3.75 for an away win for Hapoel and 3.35 for a draw — odds that acknowledge Elyaniv Barda's side are defending a two-goal Conference League lead but travelling to a considerably stronger and more experienced Bulgarian outfit.

Hapoel won the first leg 2-0, with Omri Altman and Chico on the scoresheet in Miskolc, Hungary, where the tie was staged. Barda has guided Hapoel from the second tier to a European campaign in just over a year, and Thursday's trip to the Huvepharma Arena is by some distance the club's toughest test of the qualifying rounds.

Taken together, the numbers tell a familiar story of this Israeli European summer: after strong first legs, Maccabi look all but through, Beitar are favoured but far from safe, and Hapoel — despite their cushion — are the outsiders on the night as they defend a lead in Bulgaria.

title: Miller tells Maccabi Tel Aviv players to build a run of good performances before Sheriff return leg
dek: Fresh off a 5-0 first-leg rout, the head coach wants consistency and further improvement as the Europa League tie is played out in Batumi.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC (official) — Europa League: Maccabi beat Sheriff 5-0

body: Kenny Miller had a simple message for his Maccabi Tel Aviv players as they trained for tonight's Europa League second qualifying round return leg against Sheriff Tiraspol: don't relax, build on what has already gone right. "We need to build a sequence of good matches," the head coach told his squad, according to ONE. "I want to see more of what we did in the first two matches and see improvement in things we worked on."

The words carry weight given where Maccabi stand. They travelled to Moldova eight days ago and tore Sheriff apart 5-0, a result that all but settles the tie before the sides even meet again. Sayed Abu Farchi headed the opener inside five minutes and later added a penalty, with Dor Peretz, Sagiv Yehezkel and Issouf Sissokho also on the scoresheet in Tiraspol.

That performance came only days after Maccabi had put three past Hapoel Be'er Sheva in the Super Cup, meaning Miller's side head into tonight's second leg having scored eight goals without reply across their two most recent matches — the kind of form the coach now wants to protect rather than treat as a given.

Because Sheriff's ground in Moldova's breakaway Transnistria region cannot host the return fixture, the second leg is being played at a neutral venue in Batumi, Georgia, with roughly 1,000 Israeli supporters expected to make the trip. No side has ever overturned a 5-0 first-leg deficit in a two-legged European tie, so Maccabi go into the match firm favourites to reach the third qualifying round.

That has left Miller with a selection dilemma rather than a tactical one. With qualification effectively secured, he is weighing whether to rotate his midfield, with winger Helio Varela — who only recently returned to training after Cape Verde's run at the World Cup — among the options he could bring into the side.

Miller himself is still a relative newcomer to management. The former Scotland striker joined the club in January as Ronny Deila's assistant, was handed the reins on an interim basis during the play-offs, and steadied a chaotic dressing room well enough to lead Maccabi to the Israel State Cup title. He was then confirmed as permanent head coach, and tonight's tie is his first taste of a European campaign in the job.

There is also a transfer subplot playing out around the squad. ONE reports that Abu Farchi, the match-winner in Tiraspol, has attracted scouting interest from Italian clubs Genoa and Torino, though the outlet cautions that work-permit complications could yet complicate any move for the 20-year-old forward.

For now, the focus in the camp is squarely on finishing the job against Sheriff and carrying the momentum of the last fortnight into the group stage of the Europa League, whichever opponents that eventually brings.

title: Serbian preview of a Red Star Belgrade–Beer Sheva Champions League tie is now moot
dek: ONE reported Red Star Belgrade as 90% favourites for a mooted Champions League qualifying clash with Hapoel Beer Sheva, but Beer Sheva were eliminated by Vikingur Reykjavik before the tie could happen

verificationSources.label: Total Football Analysis — Vikingur Reykjavik 2-1 Hapoel Beer Sheva

body: ONE ran a preview this week under the headline "90% in favour of the Star against Beer Sheva", framing a potential UEFA Champions League third qualifying round tie between Serbian champions Red Star Belgrade and Israeli champions Hapoel Beer Sheva.

Serbian journalist Vladimir Novaković told the outlet Red Star were clear favourites, praising coach Dejan Stanković's tactical progress in his second spell in charge: "He is very thorough, and you can see he has learned a lot from José Mourinho."

The preview noted Red Star's freshly rebuilt squad for the European campaign, including summer arrival Mohanad Abu Fani — the Israeli international midfielder who joined from Ferencváros — alongside defender Derek Lukassen and forward Marco Arnautović.

It also dwelled on the Serbian club's psychological scar tissue against Israeli opposition: a Champions League qualifying exit to Maccabi Haifa four years ago and a more recent defeat to Cyprus's Pafos, both cited as reasons for lingering caution despite the lopsided odds.

That framing has since been overtaken by events. Hapoel Beer Sheva did not reach the third qualifying round at all — they were eliminated by Iceland's Vikingur Reykjavik, going down 2-1 in the second leg at Turner Stadium in Beersheba on 29 July to lose the tie 4-2 on aggregate after a first-leg defeat in Reykjavik.

Red Star Belgrade, for their part, cruised past Northern Ireland's Larne 9-0 on aggregate, including a 4-0 win in the first leg, and will instead face Vikingur Reykjavik — not Beer Sheva — for a place in the play-off round.
The mooted Red Star–Beer Sheva showdown that prompted ONE's preview will therefore not take place, and this story is held rather than published as live news.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem to play EuroCup home games in Belgrade again this season
dek: The club says the arrangement is temporary as it continues to push for a return of European fixtures to Israel.
body: Hapoel Jerusalem confirmed this week that their home games in this season's EuroCup will once again be played abroad, at the Ranko Žeravica Hall in Belgrade, Serbia — the same arena the club used for its European fixtures last season.

The club stressed the move is temporary, to remain in place "until further notice" from the competition's organisers. In its statement, Hapoel Jerusalem said it "continues to work and do everything in its power to return home games to Israel," adding that "there is nothing like seeing the arena painted red" — a reference to the club's colours and its hope to have its own fans back inside an Israeli hall for European nights.

The relocation extends an arrangement that has kept Israeli clubs playing their continental home fixtures on neutral, mostly European soil since the security situation following the war made European basketball authorities reluctant to send visiting teams and their travelling parties to Israel.

Hapoel Jerusalem open the new EuroCup campaign at home — in Belgrade — to Germany's Rostock Seawolves on September 29. Their group also includes Le Mans of France, San Pablo Burgos of Spain, Cedevita Ljubljana of Slovenia, Aris of Greece, Tortona of Italy and Riga of Latvia.

The Jerusalem club's history in the competition runs deep: they remain, together with Hapoel Tel Aviv, one of only two Israeli sides to have won it. Hapoel Jerusalem lifted the old ULEB Cup — the tournament's previous name — in 2004, beating Real Madrid 83-72 in Charleroi to claim the club's first European title. Hapoel Tel Aviv added Israel's second EuroCup crown last year.

Ranko Žeravica Hall, a roughly 5,000-seat arena in the New Belgrade district named after the late Yugoslav coaching great, has become a familiar stop for Israeli sides in recent seasons. For Hapoel Jerusalem's players and staff, the hope remains that the away-from-home routine will not last the length of the campaign.

title: Goalkeeper Ariel Bardugo stays in Liga Alef North, switches to Hapoel Baqa al-Gharbiyye
dek: The Maccabi Haifa academy product leaves Hapoel Beit She'an for a new home in the fourth tier, one of several new faces arriving at the Triangle-area club this summer.
body: Ariel Bardugo is staying put in Liga Alef North, but he will do it in different colours. ONE reports that the 24-year-old goalkeeper has agreed to join Hapoel Baqa al-Gharbiyye for the coming season, leaving Hapoel Beit She'an after a campaign in which the club finished fifth in the table.

Bardugo came up through the Maccabi Haifa academy before building his senior career almost entirely in the lower reaches of Israeli football. He was the regular goalkeeper at Hapoel Ar'ara and later at Hapoel Bu'eine, then spent a season as backup at Hapoel Kfar Saba in Liga Leumit before dropping back down to Liga Alef North with Beit She'an, where he was the club's number one last season.
The move to Baqa al-Gharbiyye represents a fresh start at the same level rather than a step up, and according to ONE it slots him into a squad that is being actively rebuilt this summer.

Bardugo is not the only new arrival. The club has also brought in defender Bayan Abu Ria, 20, along with attacking players Bahjat Bashir, 28, and Walid Darwish, 30, as it looks to strengthen across the pitch ahead of the new campaign.

A core of last season's squad remains in place, including captain Yousef Awadi, 36, forward Firas Talhami, 24, defender Raz Harenshzon, 21, and midfielder Atef Musa, 28 — the kind of continuity clubs at this level lean on while integrating new signings.
For Bardugo, the switch is less about ambition than stability: another shot at being the first-choice goalkeeper in the same division, at a club investing in new faces around him.

title: Mollaei tells Sagi Muki: "Israel was presented to me as one that murders people"
dek: The Iranian former world champion, ordered by Tehran to withdraw rather than face Muki at the 2019 World Championships, opened up about years of anti-Israel propaganda at a reunion event in Netanya.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "Israel was presented to me as one that murders people"

body: Saeid Mollaei stood on the mat at the Pais Arena in Netanya and told a crowd of around 400 people something he says he once believed without question: that Israel was a country that "murders people."

"Israel was presented to me as one that murders people," the Iranian-born judoka said at the "Judo Without Walls" event, according to ONE. "I was told negative things about it constantly, but ultimately I discovered he is an athlete like any other athlete" — a reference to Sagi Muki, the Israeli world champion he was once ordered never to face.

The two men's story goes back to the 2019 World Judo Championships in Tokyo, where Mollaei arrived as the defending champion in the -81kg category. Under pressure from the Iranian regime, which does not permit its athletes to compete against Israelis, he was instructed to withdraw rather than risk meeting Muki in the semi-final — an episode that caused an international outcry and led the International Judo Federation to suspend Iran's federation.

Muki went on to win gold in Tokyo that year. Mollaei, fearing for his safety, fled and eventually settled in Germany before being granted Mongolian citizenship, competing under Mongolia's flag at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, where he won a silver medal.

What followed was an unlikely friendship, forged first online and then in person on the judo circuit, that has since drawn interest from Hollywood: Deadline reported in March that Fox, working with production companies Fulwell and Sipur, is developing a documentary about the two athletes' story, tentatively titled "Blood Brothers."

In Netanya, Mollaei went further than simply describing a friendship, telling the crowd how deep the propaganda he grew up with had run. "I grew up taught, unfortunately, with negative values toward Israelis," he said, according to ONE. "I understood that the Israeli public is not the enemy, but friendly to me."

He closed with a wish that stretched beyond the two of them. "My dream now is to bring these two flags together in Iran one day," Mollaei said. "We must fight for freedom in our lives and for this connection."

The Netanya event doubled as something of a homecoming for Muki, who was born and raised in the city and announced his retirement from competitive judo in February. He now runs a judo club for children there, and the reunion with Mollaei — once a forbidden opponent, now a central figure in his life story — played out just a few kilometres from where his own career began.

title: Liverpool prepare offer worth more than €120m for PSG's Bradley Barcola
dek: ONE reports the Premier League champions are readying one of the biggest bids in their history for the France winger, though Paris Saint-Germain are said to be holding out for around €170m.
body: Liverpool are preparing to test Paris Saint-Germain's resolve with a formal offer worth more than €120 million for winger Bradley Barcola, according to a report by ONE.

The Israeli outlet, citing English reporting, says the bid would rank among the most expensive in Liverpool's history if it goes through — but PSG are believed to be holding out for a far higher fee, with French reports putting their valuation at around €170 million.
Barcola, 23, has established himself as one of the more prominent young talents in French football, operating primarily as a left winger for the Ligue 1 champions and the France national team.

ONE reports that Liverpool's hierarchy has already opened discussions with the player's representatives, and that Barcola himself has shown willingness to move to Anfield — a detail that, if accurate, would help unlock a deal despite the gap in valuation.

The interest comes as Liverpool search for a direct replacement on the flank following Mohamed Salah's departure as a free agent at the end of last season, a void the club have made clear they intend to fill with a marquee signing.

Independent English reporting broadly corroborates the shape of the story: Sky Sports, ESPN and other outlets have reported Liverpool preparing an opening proposal in the region of €105-120 million, potentially rising with performance-related add-ons, while maintaining that PSG's asking price sits close to €170 million.

Sport1 in Israel has also reported on PSG's stance, noting that English suitors — with Liverpool and Arsenal both named — have been tracking Barcola amid uncertainty over his long-term future in Paris.

With the transfer window still open and PSG reluctant to lower their asking price, the two clubs remain some distance apart. Liverpool's move is being read as an opening gambit rather than a final offer, and further rounds of negotiation are expected before any deal, if it happens, is concluded.

title: Yarin Gavri joins Tzeirei Tamra ahead of club's second Liga Alef North season
dek: The 24-year-old left-sided defender and winger, a Hapoel Haifa youth product, arrives after two seasons with Hapoel Beit She'an as the promoted Galilee club builds for its second campaign in the third tier.
body: Yarin Gavri has found a new club for the season ahead, signing with Tzeirei Tamra, ONE reports, as the Galilee side reinforces its squad following promotion to Liga Alef.

The 24-year-old is a left-sided defender who can also operate as a winger, giving Tzeirei Tamra's coaching staff added flexibility down the flank as they map out their second season in Liga Alef North.
The deal was completed through the Play It representation agency, with agent Oran Ben Shterling on hand for the signing, according to the report.

Gavri came up through the youth ranks at Hapoel Haifa before moving into senior football with Maccabi Ahi Nazareth in Liga Leumit, Israel's second tier. He has since played in Liga Alef with both Maccabi Ata-Bialik and, most recently, two seasons with Hapoel Beit She'an.

Tzeirei Tamra earned their place in Liga Alef North by winning promotion from Liga Bet North A, and are looking to build on a solid first campaign at the higher level under young local coach Mousa Diab.

Adding an experienced Liga Alef campaigner like Gavri, who arrives having just come through a full two-year cycle at Hapoel Beit She'an, fits the club's stated aim of consolidating its status in the third tier rather than simply making up the numbers.
No further financial or contractual details of the move were disclosed in the report.

title: Falkoshchenko and Oli start as Hapoel Ramat Gan begin top-flight return against Hapoel Petah Tikva
dek: Cohen and Mazal handed starts as in-form, promoted Hapoel Petah Tikva visit Ramat Gan's new Rehovot home in round two of the Toto Cup.

verificationSources.label: Sport1 Maariv - preview, Ramat Gan's 13-year top-flight return
Sport1 Maariv - Petah Tikva 1-0 derby win over Maccabi Petah Tikva

body: Hapoel Ramat Gan's long wait to get back among Israeli football's elite reaches the pitch tonight, and the club has already named the players tasked with making the moment count: striker Maxim Falkoshchenko and forward Ido Oli lead the line as Ramat Gan open their Ligat Ha'al comeback in the Toto Cup group stage.

The visitors are Hapoel Petah Tikva, and the fixture kicks off at 20:00 at Ramat Gan's freshly built home ground in Rehovot, according to ONE, which published the confirmed lineups for both sides ahead of round two of the competition.

For Ramat Gan, this is more than just another cup fixture. It is their first competitive match back in the top flight since the 2012/13 season, ending a 13-year absence, and it doubles as the inaugural game at their new stadium. The squad has been almost entirely rebuilt for the step up, with only goalkeeper Amit Rayif, captain Dudu Tuyito and winger David Asenka retained from the side that won promotion.

Falkoshchenko arrives as one of the summer's more notable Ligat Ha'al arrivals, having signed for Ramat Gan after leaving Maccabi Netanya, and he is expected to shoulder much of the attacking responsibility as the newcomers find their feet at this level.

Petah Tikva, also newly promoted, travel in far better rhythm. They opened their season on July 25 with a 1-0 derby win over Maccabi Petah Tikva, settled by a stunning late strike from Noam Cohen in the 89th minute in front of roughly 3,500 of their own supporters.

Cohen starts again tonight, and he is joined in Petah Tikva's XI by forward Shavit Mazal, both named in ONE's published lineup for the trip to Rehovot. Head coach Omer Peretz has otherwise rotated his side given the squad's current depth, having already used the derby win to build momentum into the new campaign.

History leans toward the visitors. Petah Tikva have won each of the last two meetings between these clubs, 1-0 and 2-1, both on the road - a record Ramat Gan will be keen to break as they christen their new ground.
None of that changes what tonight is really about for the home side: a first taste of Ligat Ha'al football in over a decade, with a rebuilt squad and a new stadium both making their bow at once.

title: Daniel Darzi joins Hapoel Kfar Saba on season-long loan from Maccabi Haifa
dek: The 19-year-old midfielder, who signed a contract through 2030 with Haifa last year, moves to the club's Liga Leumit satellite side in search of regular senior football.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - Vizinger appointment at Kfar Saba
Walla Sport - Hapoel Kfar Saba 2025/26 season

body: Daniel Darzi, one of the more promising products to come through Maccabi Haifa's academy in recent years, is heading out for regular senior football. ONE reports that the 19-year-old midfielder signed a season-long loan deal with Hapoel Kfar Saba on Wednesday.

The move keeps Darzi within the Haifa family in every sense. Kfar Saba, who play in Liga Leumit, became Maccabi Haifa's official satellite club ahead of the 2025/26 season, a arrangement designed precisely to funnel academy graduates like Darzi into senior football without cutting the parent club's ties to them.

The fit is reinforced by the man now in the Kfar Saba dugout. Shachar Vizinger, appointed as head coach in June, previously worked as an assistant under both Barak Bachar and Messay Degu at Maccabi Haifa before taking charge of Hapoel Tel Aviv's youth side last season. His familiarity with Haifa's academy pipeline made him a natural landing spot for a player like Darzi. Darzi's agent, Avi Nmani, negotiated the loan terms.

Darzi, who captained Maccabi Haifa's youth team, put pen to paper on a new contract with the club through 2030 back in November, a deal that reflected how highly the club rates him. But senior minutes have been hard to come by in Haifa's first-team squad, and last season he made just four appearances in the top flight, two of them starts, along with two outings in the State Cup.

Where he did shine was for Haifa's youth side, where Darzi scored around ten goals last season and established himself as the standout attacking presence in an age group the club has invested heavily in developing.

The loan to Kfar Saba is a conventional next step for a talented teenager who needs first-team minutes more than he needs to sit on a Ligat Ha'al bench. A productive season in Liga Leumit would put him back in the frame at Maccabi Haifa once his loan expires next summer.

title: "I aspire to the very top" — but Rishon LeZion's new coach admits he can't match Bnei Yehuda's budget
dek: Elad Brown, freshly installed at Hapoel Rishon LeZion after five years reviving Maccabi Herzliya, says his squad's spending power trails Liga Leumit's traditional heavyweights even as he targets a return to the top flight.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Brown appointed Rishon LeZion coach
BE106 — club announcement of Brown's appointment

body: Elad Brown has barely had time to unpack at Hapoel Rishon LeZion, but the new coach is already being candid about where his club stands financially in Liga Leumit — and it isn't near the top.

In an interview with ONE ahead of the new season, Brown said he wants to aim as high as possible but acknowledged the gap in resources between his squad and the division's better-funded clubs. "I aspire to the highest possible, but proportionally we're not like Bnei Yehuda, Bnei Reina or Ashdod — we're not close to there," he said.

Asked about player salaries at his new club, Brown was careful not to put a figure on it but made clear the ceiling is modest by the league's standards. "It's good, but it doesn't approach Liga Leumit's biggest earners," he said.

Brown, 45, was confirmed as Rishon LeZion's coach in late May, taking over from David Marton on a one-year deal and working through agent Adam Kidan. The move ended a five-year spell at Maccabi Herzliya, where he took the club from Liga Alef into the National League's upper playoff bracket and, this past season, came within touching distance of promotion to Ligat Ha'al before falling short.

That near-miss with Herzliya, he said, is exactly why he is wary of setting hard targets for Rishon LeZion this early. "I don't know yet, it's too early to say. With Herzliya, as an example, nobody counted us in and we were still in contention going into the final round — so talking about expectations now isn't right," Brown said. "As a coach I aspire to get there. Whether it happens, I don't know."

The rebuilding job in front of him is substantial: only two players have been retained from last season's Rishon LeZion squad, meaning Brown is essentially assembling a new team from scratch heading into pre-season.

He identified two specific gaps still to fill — a further central defender expected to arrive later in the window, and an additional creative midfielder to help link play. Stylistically, he wants a team built on effort and intensity rather than reputation. "A team that fights, runs, tries to play attractive football and hopefully rises eventually," is how he described his ambition for the group.

Rishon LeZion have been outside Ligat Ha'al for 15 consecutive seasons, and Brown's appointment was framed by the club as the start of an effort to end that drought. His comments this week suggest he sees the project as a longer rebuild rather than a one-season sprint, even as bigger-spending rivals like Bnei Yehuda set the pace in the division.

title: GFN 1 producer Moti Lasry: "my goal is to build the biggest event in Israel"
dek: Days after a sold-out 11,000-strong fight night put Israeli combat sports on the world map, producer Moti Lasry tells ONE that a sequel is coming around January — with interest already arriving from Miami and France.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports - GFN 1 fight card, date and venue

body: Two days after the Menora Mivtachim Arena in Tel Aviv shook to the biggest combat-sports night Israel has staged, the man who built it from scratch is already talking about the next one. Moti Lasry, the producer behind GFN 1: Israel vs. the World, told ONE he expects a follow-up event around January — and that the ambition now is nothing less than the largest event in the country.

GFN 1 sold out Menora Mivtachim Arena on July 27 with three Israeli brothers, Ahavat Hashem, Ruach Hashem and Kibedy Gordon, each fighting a different international opponent on the same card under Muay Thai rules. In the headline bout, Ahavat Hashem Gordon beat Brazilian veteran and former ONE Championship bantamweight title challenger John Lineker by unanimous decision in front of roughly 11,000 fans, a result that drew coverage from MMA outlets well beyond Israel.

Lasry, whose background is largely in mainstream event production rather than combat sports, does not pretend the operation was smooth. "It's the craziest project we've done, because we barely know how to do this," he told ONE, describing a crash course in flying in international fighters, coordinating broadcast logistics and filling an arena for a sport with a limited track record of drawing crowds in Israel.

The numbers he gave ONE illustrate the scale of the gamble. Production alone cost roughly 2.5 million shekels, he said, with close to 400 suppliers involved in pulling the night together, on top of travel and accommodation for fighters brought in from Brazil, Moldova, Mexico and elsewhere.

Lasry also pointed to a community element to the event: around 2,000 tickets, he said, were distributed free to orphans and to wounded Israelis. It is the kind of detail promoters often use to soften the commercial edge of a big-ticket production, but paired with a sold-out arena it points to an event that reached well beyond a hardcore fight crowd.

Not every story from the build-up was flattering. Lasry recounted an incident in which a fighter was accused of stealing pickles worth 275 shekels from a vendor. According to his account, the fighter apologized and cried when confronted, saying he had wanted a souvenir from Israel; Lasry says he covered the cost himself rather than let it escalate.

Looking ahead, Lasry was unambiguous about his intentions. "My goal is to build the biggest event in Israel," he told ONE, adding that GFN has already fielded outside interest in taking the concept abroad, with offers from Miami and France to stage similar nights.

For now, the next Israeli date is pencilled in for around January, Lasry said, with no opponents or venue confirmed. Given the international attention GFN 1 pulled toward Tel Aviv, in a discipline that rarely gets a mainstream Israeli platform, the sequel will be watched closely both at home and by promoters abroad.

title: UEFA's 55 federations to hold emergency meeting over FIFA's World Cup investment plan
dek: European football's governing body says Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in a new commercial arm crosses "a red line," as a fan group demands his resignation.
body: UEFA is pulling all 55 of its member federations into an emergency virtual meeting this week, alarmed by a FIFA plan to sell outside investors a stake in a new commercial vehicle built to run the World Cup and its other flagship events.

The proposal, first reported internationally and covered by ONE, centres on a subsidiary FIFA is calling FIFA Forward Enterprise. It would bundle broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing rights together with tournament operations, then sell minority, non-controlling stakes to private investors.

According to reporting on the plan, FIFA has pitched an initial equity valuation of roughly $20 billion for the new entity, with an eye on raising as much as $4.2 billion from outside capital later this year. Thrive Capital, the firm led by Josh Kushner, has emerged as the investor group expected to lead the deal, with JP Morgan advising.

FIFA's pitch to its member associations is financial: the governing body says the arrangement would push football development funding beyond $10 billion, with grants of roughly $40 million flowing to each of its 211 member federations, ONE reports.

UEFA is not buying the framing. In a statement quoted by ONE, the European body said "the soul and governance of football are not assets to trade" — a line echoed in wider reporting, where UEFA has also said the plan "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross" and insisted "none of us are the owners of football, it is not FIFA's to sell."

The fan advocacy group FSE went further, with ONE quoting its demand for accountability at the top of the game: "The World Cup is not for sale, enough with this farce" — language that amounts to a call for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to step down.

UEFA, under president Aleksander Čeferin, has now summoned its full membership — all 55 national federations across Europe — to an emergency session this week to hash out a common response, rather than let individual associations react piecemeal to a plan they say they learned about largely through the press rather than official FIFA channels.

Other confederations have voiced similar frustration. CONCACAF and the AFC in Asia have both said they found out about the equity-sale proposal through media reports rather than direct communication from Zurich, adding to the sense that Infantino moved on this without building consensus first.

It is not the first time UEFA has used the threat of collective action to check an Infantino initiative. FIFA shelved its plan for a biennial World Cup back in 2021 after facing down a similar wall of European opposition, and reporting around this week's meeting suggests a boycott threat is being discussed again as leverage, though no formal decision has been taken.

FIFA maintains that any restructuring of this scale would still need sign-off from its member associations and its ruling Council before it could proceed — meaning this week's UEFA gathering is as much about shaping that eventual vote as it is about registering protest.

For now, the story is a governance fight rather than a settled outcome: FIFA has not walked back the proposal, and UEFA has not confirmed what form its pushback will take once its 55 members compare notes.
facts: FIFA has proposed a new commercial subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise, to run and monetise its events including the World Cup.
The plan values the new entity at roughly $20 billion and would sell outside investors a stake worth up to $4.2 billion.

FIFA argues the plan would lift development funding past $10 billion, with about $40 million earmarked for each of its 211 member federations.
CONCACAF and the AFC have separately said they learned of the equity-sale plan through media reports rather than official FIFA channels.

title: Israel Football Association lays out development plan for new season
dek: Federation technical staff briefed club youth directors in Shefayim on a new development league, an analytics push and a scouting pilot aimed at reaching players wherever they are.

verificationSources.label: ONE — ההתאחדות חשפה את תוכנית הפיתוח לעונה החדשה
Ynet — יריב טפר מונה למנכ"ל ההתאחדות לכדורגל

body: The Israel Football Association's technical department gathered the professional directors of Israeli clubs' youth departments at the National Team House in Shefayim this week to lay out its development programme for the coming season, ONE reports — a rare sit-down between the federation's coaching hierarchy and the people who run academy football on the ground.

Federation CEO Yariv Tefer, who took over the administrative side of the association last August after more than two decades inside the organisation, opened the meeting by stressing that dialogue between the technical department and the clubs, rather than instructions handed down from above, is what will move Israeli youth football forward.

The bulk of the presentation came from Boni Ginzburg, technical director of Israel's youth national teams, who set out roughly half a dozen priorities for the season ahead: a new development league, a fresh cycle at the football academy, a UEFA-designed project for "late developers" — players who mature technically or physically later than their peers — a programme to advance football in Arab communities, expanded coach education and a dedicated goalkeepers' project within the national-team pathway.

"Youth club departments are our most important partners," Ginzburg told the room, according to ONE. "Staying connected to the field and sharing knowledge is what will develop Israeli football professionally."

On the data side, Adam David, the federation's head of technology and analytics, unveiled IFAnalytics, a new system for processing players' performance data, and described joint projects with clubs on physiological monitoring aimed at addressing the so-called relative age effect — the well-known bias toward players born earlier in the selection year — across the youth divisions.

Scouting chief Moshe Sinai and his assistant, Idan Genot, outlined upgraded methods for identifying talent for the development centres, the academy and the youth national teams, and previewed a pilot scheme called "Reaching Every Player Everywhere," which will let staff share video of prospects from Israel and abroad through a dedicated platform.

Noa Greenberg Drori, head of the federation's medical department, presented a monitoring partnership with VALD, the athlete-testing technology group already used elsewhere in the federation's operations, that will build individual physiological profiles for players and pass professional recommendations on to their clubs. Grant Slobin gave further detail on the testing protocols involved, while Eli Sudai, the academy's professional director, closed the technical presentations with plans for its next intake and closer coordination with clubs even after players move on from the programme.

From the clubs' side, Itai Mordechai, professional director of Maccabi Haifa's youth department, welcomed the session. "An important and meaningful day," he said. "The professional ideas and work processes presented here will strengthen cooperation between the federation's technical department and the clubs."

The presentation, as reported, did not include a budget figure or a firm start date for the new development league or the academy's next cycle — detail likely to follow as pre-season preparations continue ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

title: Croatia 33-29 Israel: youth handball team fall in European Championship opener despite leading for 45 minutes
dek: Yonatan Flach's 14 goals were not enough to hold off a late Croatian surge as Israel's under-18 side opened the Belgrade tournament with a narrow collapse.

verificationSources.label: EHF EURO - M18 EHF EURO 2026 official competition page (Croatia 33-29 Israel result)
Wikipedia - 2026 European Men's U-18 Handball Championship

body: Israel's under-18 handball team opened its European Championship campaign in Belgrade with heartbreak on Wednesday, leading for most of the match before fading to a 33-29 defeat to Croatia, ONE reported.

The game, the first of Group C at the M18 EHF EURO 2026, is being staged across three Belgrade venues from July 29 to August 9, with 24 nations competing for places at next year's IHF Men's Youth World Championship. Israel shares the group with Croatia, Czechia and Portugal.

For long spells it looked like Israel might spring the upset. Captain Yonatan Flach, the top scorer of the qualifying campaign, set the tone again, finishing the night with 14 goals and providing the score that decided the first half.

A goal at the buzzer from Flach put Israel two goals clear, 17-15, at the interval, capping a first half in which the Israeli side, coached by Dor Russo and Assaf Sitton, matched the more fancied Croatians blow for blow.

The contest tightened further after the break, with the sides level at 22-22 midway through the second half. That was as good as it got for Israel: Croatia found another gear in the 45th minute and grabbed their first lead of the match.

Israel refused to fold. A goal from Noam Levi pulled the gap back to a single point, 30-29, with the finish still in the balance, but Croatia's superior physicality in the closing stages proved decisive.
Croatia pulled clear in the final minutes to seal a 33-29 win, according to ONE's report.
Behind Flach, Rom Tuvias and Gav Dagni each scored four for Israel, with Roei Ganel, Tomer Michalis and Ido Malul contributing two apiece and Levi adding his one crucial strike.
Israel will look to open its account in the tournament on Thursday against the Czech Republic, with a Group C campaign already needing a response after the opening setback.
facts: Croatia beat Israel's under-18 men's handball team 33-29 in their opening Group C match of the M18 EHF EURO 2026 in Belgrade, Serbia, on July 29, 2026.

Israel closed to within one goal at 30-29 through a Noam Levi goal before Croatia pulled away to win 33-29.
Israel's under-18 side is coached by Dor Russo and Assaf Sitton.

The tournament, hosted across Belgrade venues from July 29 to August 9, 2026, serves as a qualifying event for the 2027 IHF Men's Youth (U19) World Championship; Israel's group also includes Czechia and Portugal.
Israel are next scheduled to face the Czech Republic in their second Group C match.

title: Pochettino closing in on new USMNT contract through 2030, ONE reports
dek: The Argentine coach is in advanced talks to extend his stay with the United States men's national team for a second World Cup cycle, despite a bruising round-of-16 exit to Belgium.
body: Mauricio Pochettino is closing in on a new contract to remain head coach of the United States men's national team through the 2030 World Cup, ONE reports, with the Argentine and US Soccer said to be in advanced talks over a second four-year cycle together.

Pochettino's original deal was tied to the 2026 World Cup cycle, and both sides had agreed to shelve any decision on his future until after the tournament US Soccer co-hosted this summer alongside Mexico and Canada.
The Americans topped their group on home soil and won a knockout-round match for the first time in a decade, a genuine marker of progress under Pochettino since his appointment in September 2024.

The run ended painfully, however, with a 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the round of 16 that exposed how far the squad still has to travel before it can be considered a serious contender on the biggest stage.

That uneven finish has not derailed the negotiations. US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson said the federation remains fully engaged in extending Pochettino's stay, describing the talks as active and forward-looking.
"We are in active talks with Mauricio and his team about the future," Batson said, according to reports cited by ONE. "We all share the belief that the best days of American soccer are still ahead."
Pochettino himself struck a similarly upbeat tone in the aftermath of the Belgium loss, signalling he was open to staying on rather than using the World Cup exit as a natural exit point of his own.
"We have built a very good relationship, I am happy here," he said, pointing to the bond he has forged with US Soccer's staff and players over the past two years.

The main uncertainty hanging over the renewal is European interest. Pochettino has been repeatedly linked with vacancies in the Premier League and with AC Milan during his USMNT tenure, and any concrete offer from a major club could still complicate a deal that both sides otherwise appear to want.

For now, though, the direction of travel points toward continuity: a coach who delivered a first knockout win in ten years and the framework of a squad U.S. Soccer believes can peak by the time the 2030 World Cup arrives in Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

title: Tiberias owner Kalmenson: Ashdod's legal bid to return to the top flight is "doomed to fail"
dek: Aryeh Kalmenson hit back at MS Ashdod's attempt to use a doping indictment against Ironi Tiberias to reverse its relegation, insisting the two clubs finished eight points apart on merit.

verificationSources.label: ONE - "ניסיונות נואלים": קלמנזון במתקפה על אשדוד

body: Aryeh Kalmenson, the owner of Ironi Tiberias, has launched a sharp public attack on MS Ashdod, accusing the relegated club of trying to claw its way back into Israel's top flight through the courts rather than on the pitch.

"The attempts by MS Ashdod to return to the top league through legal means, after failing to do so sportingly, are doomed to fail," Kalmenson said, according to ONE. "It's regrettable to see these futile attempts to use legal proceedings for an entirely unsporting outcome."

The dispute centres on an indictment filed by the Israeli Football Association against Tiberias over allegations that club staff administered intravenous saline treatments to players in excess of permitted volumes ahead of a lower-table playoff match against Ashdod last season, and then attempted to obstruct the ensuing investigation.

Ashdod has since petitioned the disciplinary tribunal to join those proceedings as an interested party, demanding an accelerated timetable and immediate interim measures before the 2026/27 season kicks off - arguing that any eventual sanction against Tiberias would otherwise be "emptied of meaning due to the passage of time."

Kalmenson rejected any link between the new indictment and Ashdod's relegation. "The claims in the indictment have no connection to MS Ashdod's loss to Tiberias, and ultimately the gap between the teams at season's end stood at eight points in Tiberias' favour," he said.

That gap is borne out in the final 2025/26 table: Tiberias finished ninth in the relegation round with 36 points, while Ashdod ended 13th with 28, sending Ashdod down to Liga Leumit alongside Maccabi Bnei Reineh.

Notably, Tiberias reached that final tally despite already absorbing an eight-point deduction of its own this season, imposed after a separate, settled case over irregular player contracts that also carried a further six-point penalty for 2026/27 and a 500,000-shekel fine.

Kalmenson did not stop at the legal substance of Ashdod's push. "MS Ashdod's attempts to influence decision-makers through an aggressive media campaign will not succeed," he said, accusing the club of waging a public-relations battle alongside its courtroom effort.

The case now sits with the Israeli FA's disciplinary court, which must weigh Ashdod's request to fast-track a ruling against the season's looming start - a timeline that could determine whether Tiberias opens 2026/27 in the Premier League or facing fresh sanctions that reopen the relegation question entirely.

title: Ashdod's lawyer: minimum punishment for Tiberias must be relegation
dek: Amit Hadad says Ironi Tiberias "acted with malice" over banned IV infusions given to players before the win that sent Ashdod down, and is demanding the club be barred from registering players until the case is resolved.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "מינימום הורדת ליגה לטבריה, היא פעלה בזדון"
ONE — Ashdod seeks to join proceedings against Tiberias

body: Ironi Tiberias has spent 2026 lurching from one disciplinary crisis to the next, and now the club that finished directly behind it in the relegation battle wants the harshest possible outcome. Amit Hadad, the prominent Israeli lawyer representing F.C. Ashdod, said on ONE's Sicha HaYom programme that anything short of relegation for Tiberias would be an inadequate punishment.

"This wasn't done by mistake, it was done with malice," Hadad said of the club's conduct, arguing that the Israel Football Association's disciplinary court cannot treat the case as an isolated lapse given Tiberias's recent history.

The new case centres on a match-eve incident from three days before Tiberias faced Ashdod in a lower-playoff fixture on 3 May, which Tiberias won 3-0. According to the indictment reported by Haaretz, club officials arranged for players to receive intravenous saline infusions in quantities exceeding what is permitted without proper medical justification or qualified supervision — a breach of both Israel Football Association regulations and anti-doping rules. Ashdod was relegated from Ligat HaAl at the end of that campaign; Tiberias avoided the drop.

Hadad pointed to Tiberias's earlier scandal this year as evidence of a pattern rather than a one-off. In April, the club accepted a plea agreement over a separate case involving double contracts and falsified financial documents, under which it was docked eight points immediately, a further six points for 2026/27, fined 500,000 shekels and barred from registering players in January 2027. "They already had double contracts and forged documents," Hadad said, noting that penalty proved too lenient to deter further wrongdoing.

Ashdod has now filed an urgent application with the Football Association's disciplinary court to join the infusions case as an interested party. The club is asking for the proceedings to be fast-tracked to a ruling before the new season opens, for interim measures blocking Tiberias from registering players in the meantime, and for a guarantee that no settlement can be reached without Ashdod first being heard on any sanction.

Hadad framed the scale of the alleged scheme — described in the indictment as involving a dozen one-litre IV bags procured through outside parties, along with alleged pressure on players and later attempts to tamper with evidence — as without precedent in Israeli football. He said the Football Association's disciplinary court is due to hear the matter within days, with the 2026/27 Ligat HaAl season set to kick off on 22 August.

Tiberias has previously pushed back on the double-contracts allegations, insisting the club's financial reporting did not amount to wrongdoing, though that dispute ultimately ended in the accepted plea deal. The club has not yet issued a detailed public response to the infusions indictment covered in this report.

For Ashdod, the stakes go well beyond principle. The club argues it suffered direct competitive and financial harm from results against a Tiberias side it alleges was gaining an unlawful edge in matches that shaped the relegation picture — including the very fixture at the heart of the new case.

title: Rio de Janeiro, 12 August 2016: The bow that never came, and the bronze that did
dek: Or Sasson beat Islam El Shehaby in the first round of Olympic judo, and it was the handshake that never happened that made the world watch — but it was three more fights, and a loss to a legend, that made the medal his.

verificationSources.label: Times of Israel — IOC to probe Egyptian judoka's refusal to shake Israeli's hand
ESPN — Egyptian judoka refuses handshake with Israeli opponent after loss
CNN — Islam El Shehaby and Or Sasson handshake: Any punishment?
BBC — Egyptian judoka Islam El Shehaby 'sent home for handshake snub'
Haaretz — After Dramatic Day, Or Sasson Wins Israel's Second Medal in Rio Olympics
Times of Israel — Or Sasson wins Israel's second judo bronze at Rio Games

body: The mat at Carioca Arena 2 does not care about politics. That is the whole premise of judo, a sport built on bows and grips and the assumption that two strangers who have just tried to throw each other to the floor will, when it is over, shake hands. On the afternoon of 12 August 2016, that assumption broke in full view of a near-capacity Rio crowd, and Or Sasson was standing in the middle of it.

Sasson, a 25-year-old Israeli heavyweight, had drawn Egypt's Islam El Shehaby in the round of 32 of the men's over-100kg category. It was their first meeting. Sasson won it clearly, throwing El Shehaby twice, and turned to offer the customary handshake and bow that closes every judo contest. El Shehaby backed away, shaking his head, and walked off the mat to a chorus of boos. The referee called him back and ordered him to bow; he gave a brief, grudging nod and left again, still booed.

"I was educated to respect my opponents, no matter who they are," Sasson said afterward. "We always shake hands at the end of the fight. I stretched out my hand, but he didn't go with it." His coaches, he later admitted, had warned him it might happen. It did not stop him competing. "I knew to put that incident aside," he said. "Politics doesn't matter when I'm on the mat."

The incident traveled far faster than the tournament itself. The International Olympic Committee's Disciplinary Commission opened a review and, days later, issued El Shehaby a "severe reprimand for inappropriate behaviour," ruling that his conduct was "contrary to the rules of fair play and against the spirit of friendship embodied in the Olympic Values." The Egyptian Olympic Committee sent him home before the closing ceremony. El Shehaby, for his part, was unrepentant, saying a handshake was not an obligation written into judo's rules and that it happens between friends. He announced his retirement from judo soon after.

For Sasson, the story did not end with the walk-off. He still had a tournament to win. He beat his way through the next two rounds before running into Teddy Riner in the semifinal — the Frenchman who would leave Rio unbeaten in more than a decade of major competition, a wall of a man en route to his second Olympic gold. Sasson lost by waza-ari, but Riner shook his hand warmly at the final bell, a small and pointed contrast to the morning's headlines.

That defeat sent Sasson into the bronze medal bout against Cuba's Alex García Mendoza, a tight, grinding contest with almost no clean scoring chances from either man. It was decided, in the end, on penalties — the kind of unglamorous, attritional finish that heavyweight judo often produces when two exhausted competitors refuse to give the other an opening. Sasson had fewer penalties. He had his medal.

It was Israel's second bronze of those Games, both won in judo within four days of each other: Yarden Gerbi had taken the first, in the women's 63kg category, on 9 August, ending a twelve-year wait for an Israeli medal at a single Olympics being doubled up. Sasson's medal was his first Olympic podium finish — he would add a second, in the mixed team event, five years later in Tokyo — and it made him, that week, one of the most searched Israeli athletes in the country's Olympic history, for reasons that had almost nothing to do with judo technique.

What lingers from that day is not really the scoreline against García Mendoza, tight as it was. It is the split-second on the mat when El Shehaby turned his back, and the split-second after, when Sasson's hand was still out. Broadsheets from the BBC to CNN to Al Jazeera ran the image; Israeli papers followed Sasson through the rest of the draw. The bow that never came became, briefly, bigger than the Games themselves. The bronze that did come was the part Sasson actually built.
facts: Or Sasson (ISR) defeated Islam El Shehaby (EGY) in the round of 32 of the men's over-100kg judo category on 12 August 2016 at Carioca Arena 2, Rio de Janeiro — not in the bronze-medal bout itself.
After the win, El Shehaby refused to shake Sasson's hand and gave only a curt, forced nod when the referee ordered him back to bow; he was loudly booed by the crowd.

The IOC Disciplinary Commission issued El Shehaby a 'severe reprimand for inappropriate behaviour,' finding his conduct 'contrary to the rules of fair play and against the spirit of friendship embodied in the Olympic Values'; the Egyptian Olympic Committee sent him home before the closing ceremony.
Sasson lost his semifinal to France's Teddy Riner, the eventual gold medalist, by waza-ari.
Sasson won the bronze medal by beating Cuba's Alex García Mendoza in the bronze-medal match, a close contest decided on penalties.
This was Sasson's first Olympic medal and Israel's second medal of the Rio 2016 Games, after Yarden Gerbi's judo bronze (women's 63kg) on 9 August 2016.
Sasson later won a second Olympic medal (bronze) as part of Israel's mixed judo team at the Tokyo 2020 Games.

title: Every 48.5 minutes, a goal: the numbers behind Niv Gabai's fast start
dek: A debut goal for Maccabi Haifa, a strike against his old club days into a loan at Ironi Kiryat Shmona, and a contract clause guaranteeing him playing time — Sport5 crunches the numbers on one of Israeli football's most efficient teenagers.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — יעילות קטלנית: המספרים של ניב גבאי
Walla Sport — רשמי: ניב גבאי הושאל ממכבי חיפה לעירוני קרית שמונה
Sport1/Maariv — רשמי: ניב גבאי הושאל ממכבי חיפה לקבוצה בליגת העל

body: Some strikers need a whole season to prove a point. Niv Gabai has needed 187 minutes.

Sport5 did the arithmetic this week on the 19-year-old forward's short senior career and arrived at a startling ratio: a goal or an assist every 48.5 minutes on average, across four goal contributions in barely three hours of first-team football.

The latest data point came days after he swapped Maccabi Haifa for a loan at Ironi Kiryat Shmona. Thrown into the Toto Cup meeting between the two clubs, Gabai scored in the 7th minute against the very academy that raised him, helping set Kiryat Shmona on their way to a 3-0 win.

It was not the first time he had made an instant impact. Gabai's senior bow for Maccabi Haifa came off the bench in a 4-1 rout of Maccabi Tel Aviv, when he was sprung through by Abdoulaye Seck, rounded goalkeeper Aviram Melika and rolled the ball in within minutes of his introduction — the type of cameo that gets a name circled in a coach's notebook.

That notebook, though, belongs to Barak Bachar now, and Bachar was not planning to lean on Gabai heavily this season at Sammy Ofer Stadium. Last term he made eight Ligat Ha'al appearances for Maccabi Haifa's first team, scoring twice and adding an assist — promising numbers for a teenager, but not enough to force his way past Haifa's senior forward line.

Gabai is a product of the Maccabi Haifa academy that reached the UEFA Youth Champions League quarter-finals last season, eliminating Barcelona along the way — the kind of pedigree that had clubs lower down the table circling before Kiryat Shmona moved to secure him with something more concrete: real minutes in the top flight.

According to Sport5, the loan agreement includes a clause obliging Kiryat Shmona to give the striker at least 40% of available playing time this season — a contractual guarantee, not just a promise, that turns Gabai's efficiency numbers into a running experiment rather than a one-off curiosity.

If he keeps scoring at anything close to his current rate once those minutes start piling up, Maccabi Haifa may find themselves regretting how little rope they gave him — and Kiryat Shmona will have found a bargain loan just as their season begins to take shape.

Last season he made eight Ligat Ha'al appearances for Maccabi Haifa, scoring two goals and adding one assist.
He has joined Ironi Kiryat Shmona on a loan until the end of the season, with the deal reportedly including a clause guaranteeing him 40% of playing time, according to Sport5.
On his first appearance for Kiryat Shmona he scored in the 7th minute against parent club Maccabi Haifa as Kiryat Shmona won the Toto Cup meeting 3-0.

title: Sa'ar Fadida closes in on move to Ironi Tiberias
dek: The out-of-contract attacking midfielder, released by Hapoel Haifa this summer, is in advanced talks with the Ligat Ha'al club, Sport5 reports.
body: Sa'ar Fadida is closing in on a return to Ligat Ha'al service with Ironi Tiberias, with Sport5 reporting the 29-year-old attacking midfielder is deep into negotiations over a move to the Sea of Galilee club.
According to the report, most of the substantive terms have already been agreed between Fadida's camp and Tiberias, with only a handful of final clauses left to settle before any deal is signed off.

Fadida would arrive as a free agent after his contract with Hapoel Haifa lapsed this summer. He had joined Haifa in February, arriving mid-season from Maccabi Bnei Reineh, and made just nine appearances for the club, scoring twice — once in the league and once in the State Cup.

Sport5 reports that Fadida drew interest from several other clubs after becoming a free agent, a reflection of the market for an attacking midfielder comfortable playing through the middle or off either flank.

A move to Tiberias would be another stop in a career that has taken him around Israel and briefly abroad. Spells with Hapoel Hadera and a season with Olimpija Ljubljana in Slovenia preceded a productive two-year stint with Maccabi Bnei Reineh, where he scored eight goals in 62 appearances before his short return to Haifa this year.
For Ironi Tiberias, landing Fadida would add attacking depth to a squad preparing for a second successive season in Ligat Ha'al, the club's first sustained run in the top flight in years.
Nothing has been signed yet, and Sport5's report stops short of confirming a completed transfer. For now Fadida remains a free agent, with his next club expected to be settled in the coming days.

title: Fighter beaten by Ruach HaShem Gordon caught stealing from Carmel Market shop
dek: Security footage aired on Channel 13 shows the Moldovan fighter, defeated by Gordon a day earlier, helping himself to goods from a Judaica stall in Tel Aviv.
body: A day after losing on points to Israel's Ruach HaShem Gordon, the Moldovan fighter he fought was caught on camera helping himself to goods from a Judaica stall in Tel Aviv's Carmel Market, Sport5 reported Tuesday.

Footage aired on Channel 13's investigative programme HaTzinor showed the fighter, named in Israeli reports as Maximus Bejenoutas, picking souvenirs and religious ornaments off a stall and walking away without paying. Sport5 put the value of the missing goods at "hundreds of shekels."

The stall's owner, identified as Sharon Solimanzadeh, did not hold back when the footage was put to her. "I'm asking the whole world to see this," she said. "It's not pleasant to steal from a business that's struggling to stay afloat."

The theft came less than 24 hours after Bejenoutas had shared a ring with Gordon at a Gordon-family fight card in Tel Aviv on July 27. Gordon, employing a low-kick game plan that visibly swelled his taller opponent's lead leg by the second round, took a clean unanimous decision after three rounds.

It was the latest step in the rise of Ruach HaShem Gordon, one of seven siblings in an Israeli fighting family whose names all incorporate HaShem, the Hebrew word for God. In 2023, at just 19, he became the first Israeli man to win an IFMA world Muay Thai title, in the up-to-57kg division, and that same year added a Rajadamnern Stadium championship in Bangkok — a first for an Israeli fighter in Thailand.

Gordon's win over Bejenoutas came on a card that also featured his brother Khabib, who scored what ONE.co.il described as an impressive knockout earlier on the same bill — making the shoplifting footage an awkward postscript to an otherwise strong night for the family.

Organisers of the event condemned the theft when asked for comment, while making clear their responsibility as promoters extends only to what happens inside the ropes, not to a beaten fighter's conduct once he leaves the venue.
Sport5 did not report whether police had been called in over the incident, and there was no immediate response from Bejenoutas or his camp.
facts: Ruach HaShem Gordon, an Israeli Muay Thai fighter, beat his Moldovan opponent by unanimous decision after three rounds at a Gordon-family fight card in Tel Aviv on July 27, 2026.
Footage aired on Channel 13's HaTzinor programme showed the defeated Moldovan fighter taking items from a Judaica stall in Tel Aviv's Carmel Market the following day.
The stall's owner, named in Sport5's report as Sharon Solimanzadeh, said the stolen goods were worth hundreds of shekels and criticised the theft publicly.
Event organisers condemned the theft but said their duty of care covers conduct inside the competition, not outside it.
Ruach HaShem Gordon is one of seven siblings in an Israeli fighting family whose names all include HaShem (God); in 2023 he became the first Israeli man to win an IFMA Muay Thai world title.
Gordon's brother Khabib also fought and won by knockout on the same July 27 card, per ONE.co.il's report.

title: Pogačar's record-tying fifth Tour de France win dissected on Israeli cycling podcast
dek: Sport5's Shvoong panel, including former Israeli Tour rider Guy Niv, broke down the Alpe d'Huez drama, Isaac del Toro's white jersey and the Champs-Élysées finale from Paris.

verificationSources.label: NPR on Pogačar's fifth Tour de France win
Cyclingnews on the final classifications and stage 21

body: The Tour de France wrapped up in Paris on Sunday with Tadej Pogačar sealing a record-equalling fifth title, and Sport5's cycling podcast wasted no time getting into it. The channel gathered its regular Shvoong panel — Guy Dar and Guy Niv — for a special episode dedicated to picking apart the three-week race, with reporter Yordan Gazit joining live from the French capital.

Gazit had travelled to Paris for the finish and watched the closing, shortened stage around Montmartre and the Champs-Élysées in person before dialling into the recording to relay what the atmosphere was like on the ground as Pogačar's team celebrated down the finishing straight.

Niv brought a rider's-eye view that few Israeli broadcasters can offer: he became the first Israeli cyclist to start and finish the Tour de France, riding for Israel–Premier Tech in 2022, before retiring from professional racing and moving into commentary and podcasting on the sport back home.

The headline fact the trio kept returning to was simple — Pogačar's fifth yellow jersey pulls him level with Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Induráin as the most successful riders in Tour history. He finished with an overall time of 73 hours, 56 minutes and 26 seconds, roughly six and a half minutes clear of Belgium's Remco Evenepoel in second.

Much of the conversation turned to what the panel called the sport's next generation, embodied by Isaac del Toro. Pogačar's UAE Team Emirates–XRG teammate took the white jersey as the race's best young rider, a result the hosts read as a signal of who might eventually challenge the Slovenian at the very top.

They also revisited the tension of the mountains, singling out the stage to Alpe d'Huez as the race's most dangerous and dramatic day in the high peaks. Richard Carapaz's breakaway victory there was enough to lock up the polka-dot King of the Mountains jersey, closing out a mountains battle the podcast described as tighter than the final margins suggested.

Mads Pedersen's points win, sealed after a strong closing week on the flatter stages, rounded out the jersey sweep the panel worked through — alongside the finish itself, where Mathieu van der Poel took the shortened, crash-marred final stage into Paris while Pogačar rode it out safely in yellow.

It made for a lighter, more reflective edition than the panel's usual stage-by-stage coverage — three broadcasters talking through a Grand Tour they had just spent three weeks living inside, with one of their own having once raced it himself.
facts: Tadej Pogačar won the 2026 Tour de France, his fifth title, tying the record for most overall wins alongside Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Induráin.
Pogačar's overall time was 73 hours, 56 minutes and 26 seconds, about six and a half minutes ahead of runner-up Remco Evenepoel.
Isaac del Toro, Pogačar's UAE Team Emirates–XRG teammate, won the white jersey as the race's best young rider.
Richard Carapaz won the polka-dot King of the Mountains jersey, sealed with a breakaway win on the Alpe d'Huez stage.
Mads Pedersen won the green points jersey; Mathieu van der Poel won the shortened final stage into Paris.
Sport5's Shvoong cycling podcast — Guy Dar, Guy Niv and Yordan Gazit, the last reporting from Paris — recorded a special episode reviewing the finished Tour.

title: Maccabi Haifa's Toto Cup hopes narrow to the slimmest of margins
dek: Two defeats in two games have left the Greens bottom of their group, needing an unlikely chain of results elsewhere just to reach the semi-finals.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport on the Haifa derby
Jerusalem Post on the derby result

body: Maccabi Haifa's bid for an early piece of silverware before a ball is even kicked in the league season is all but over. Two matches into the Toto Cup group stage, the Greens have lost both, and Sport5 lays out just how narrow their route back into contention has become.

It began with the derby. Hapoel Haifa beat their city rivals 3-2 at Sammy Ofer Stadium on July 25, racing into a three-goal lead before Maccabi mounted a spirited but ultimately futile fightback in the closing stages. The result mattered beyond the three points: it was Hapoel Haifa's first win over Maccabi Haifa in the Toto Cup since 1997.

Three days later, on July 28, Maccabi's week got worse. They were beaten 3-0 away to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, conceding all three goals inside the first half in what several Hebrew-language reports described as an unconvincing, sluggish display from Barak Bakhar's side.

The cumulative effect leaves Maccabi Haifa bottom of Group A after two rounds, without a point and with a goal difference of minus four — worse than fellow strugglers Bnei Sakhnin, who also have zero points but a healthier goal tally. Hapoel Haifa lead the group on six points, with Kiryat Shmona and Ironi Tiberias both on three.

The Toto Cup's group phase is an Israeli football fixture of its own kind: played before the league season proper gets under way, it splits ten non-European clubs into two five-team groups, with the top two in each advancing to semi-finals against the Tel Aviv giants competing in Europe that season.

That is the prize Maccabi Haifa are now chasing from an almost impossible position. Sport5's arithmetic is blunt: the Greens would need to win both of their remaining group games, against Bnei Sakhnin and Ironi Tiberias, while simultaneously hoping Hapoel Haifa lose their two remaining fixtures and Kiryat Shmona also drop their final two matches. Only that combination would be enough to lift Maccabi Haifa back to the top of the table.

Sport5 frames it, fairly, as a very slim chance rather than a dead one — the group is not yet finished, and results in a five-team mini-league can still swing. But it is a long way from where a club of Maccabi Haifa's stature expected to be starting the new campaign.

Bakhar, addressing the derby defeat, acknowledged his side were second-best for long spells but pointed to their response after going 3-0 down as a source of encouragement, saying the team's approach improved markedly once changes were made. He flagged the sluggish attacking play in the opening exchanges as the area most in need of fixing before the group's remaining rounds.

For a club used to setting the pace domestically, back-to-back defeats in a competition Maccabi Haifa had not featured in at this stage since 2020/21 have raised early questions about squad sharpness heading into the new season. The Greens now need results to fall their way as much as they need to win their own remaining fixtures if they are to avoid an early exit from the Toto Cup altogether.

title: Ironi Kiryat Shmona stun Maccabi Haifa 3-0 in Toto Cup rout
dek: Shay Barda's side scored three times before the break as Barak Bakhar's Haifa slumped to a second straight defeat in the pre-season competition.
body: Ironi Kiryat Shmona tore into Maccabi Haifa on Tuesday evening, scoring three times inside the first 33 minutes and cruising to a 3-0 win in Group A of the Toto Cup that left the two-time reigning league champions with plenty to fix before the season proper begins.

Niv Gabay opened the scoring in the seventh minute — a pointed detail given he spent last season on loan at Kiryat Shmona from Haifa itself, and duly punished his parent club. Amadou Sagna doubled the lead on 23 minutes, and Ariel Sharetzky added a third ten minutes later to complete the rout before half-time.

"In the first half there was one team on the pitch," Kiryat Shmona coach Shay Barda said afterwards, a blunt summary of a period in which his side simply overran Barak Bakhar's Haifa from kick-off. Barda said he was satisfied with the performance but added a note of caution, telling reporters the players "shouldn't be dazzled by the result."
The second half brought no way back for Haifa. The scoreline held at 3-0 to full time, with Kiryat Shmona content to see out a lead that had already been settled well before the interval.

It was a chastening evening for Haifa in other respects too. Goalkeeper Omri Glazer was at fault for the opening goal and left the pitch in tears after being substituted, one of two Haifa players forced off through injury during the match.

The defeat was Haifa's second in as many Toto Cup outings, having now shipped six goals across their first two matches of the pre-season competition. Walla's coverage described it as "not a simple evening" for the club, framing the result as an uneasy sign with the new league campaign approaching.

For Kiryat Shmona, the win offers an early marker of intent in a tournament used by Israeli top-flight clubs largely for fitness and squad building ahead of the competitive season, even if Barda himself was reluctant to read too much into a single-sided first half.

title: Barak Bachar needs to recalculate his course at Maccabi Haifa before it's too late
dek: After a second straight preseason defeat and six goals conceded in a week, ONE's football panel says the Haifa coach must abandon his back-three system before the league season even starts.

verificationSources.label: ONE - match report, Maccabi Haifa 0-3 Kiryat Shmona
Ynet - Hapoel Haifa derby win report

body: Maccabi Haifa's start to the new season has gone from worrying to alarming, and the alarm is now ringing loudest around head coach Barak Bachar. Two matches into preseason, the reigning force of Israeli football has lost twice and shipped six goals, leaving supporters asking hard questions of a manager brought back specifically to restore order.

The latest blow came in the Toto Cup, where Ironi Kiryat Shmona beat Haifa 3-0. Niv Gabay struck inside seven minutes, Amadou Seneya doubled the lead on 23 and Ariel Shartzky completed the rout just before the half-hour, prompting ONE to describe the champions as having simply 'fallen apart.'

It followed directly on from a 3-2 derby defeat to Hapoel Haifa - Maccabi's first loss in that fixture in 29 years - in which Hapoel raced into a 3-0 lead through Yaad Gonen, a Noam Stapman own goal and Alon Turgeman, before Iad Halali and Eitan Azoulay pulled two back too late to matter.

Bachar did not hide his frustration after the Kiryat Shmona defeat. 'We cannot show up like this even in a training match,' he said, according to ONE. 'We drew many conclusions from this match, we will learn from it. We break too quickly, there are problems and we are aware of them ... We should not concede three goals in two different matches in less than a week.'

Compounding the mood, goalkeeper Omri Glazer was forced off injured during the Kiryat Shmona game, reviving concerns about Haifa's lack of a proven deputy between the posts - a problem the club has yet to solve convincingly heading into the new campaign.

On ONE's football podcast, pundits Assi Mamen, Gidi Lipkin and Amir Yaniv went further, arguing Bachar 'needs to recalculate his course' before the situation spirals further. Their central complaint centres on his insistence on a back-three system that has been repeatedly exposed, alongside a midfield they say has offered no control in either defeat.

This is Bachar's third spell in charge at Sammy Ofer Stadium. He returned in October 2025 on a contract running through the summer of 2028, brought back specifically to recapture the identity that delivered three straight championships between 2020-21 and 2022-23 - a run that ended a decade-long title drought for the club.

None of that history buys much patience in Haifa, where preseason cup results are usually shrugged off but rarely arrive alongside this level of defensive collapse. With the Ligat Ha'al opener now close, ONE's panel framed the next fortnight as the moment for Bachar to prove the alarm is premature - or confirm that a deeper overhaul, tactical and otherwise, is overdue.
