title: Dinamo Zagreb complete stunning comeback to eliminate Thun in Champions League qualifying
dek: Moris Valinčić's extra-time strike sends the Croatian champions through 4-3 on aggregate after Thun led 2-0 inside 22 minutes at Stadion Maksimir.

verificationSources.label: GNK Dinamo Zagreb official site (qualifying path)

body: Dinamo Zagreb produced one of the great European comebacks of this qualifying summer on Tuesday night, hauling back a two-goal deficit and outlasting ten-man Thun through extra time to reach the third qualifying round of the Champions League.

The Croatian champions trailed 2-0 inside the opening 22 minutes at a heaving Stadion Maksimir, only to score three times, survive a red card controversy in their favour, and finish the job through Moris Valinčić's rasping strike in the 112th minute.
It completed a 4-3 aggregate win over the tie, after the first leg in Switzerland had ended 1-1, and it means Zagreb avoid the ignominy of an early European exit that once looked distinctly possible.

Thun, appearing composed and clinical early on, went ahead through Brighton Labeau's fourth-minute finish before Marco Bürki doubled the lead in the 22nd minute, putting the Swiss side 3-1 up on aggregate and firmly in control of the tie.

Zagreb needed a response and got one just after the hour, when Dion Drena Beljo converted to make it 2-1 on the night in the 67th minute — the same minute in which Bürki, Thun's second scorer, was shown a red card after a VAR review upgraded the original sanction.

Reduced to ten men and clinging to a slender aggregate lead, Thun could not hold out. Lukas Kačavenda levelled the tie at 2-2 on the night — 3-3 on aggregate — with just over ten minutes of normal time remaining, sending the match into extra time.

The additional 30 minutes were tense and largely even until Valinčić, a Zagreb right-back not renowned for his finishing, drove in from distance in the 112th minute for a goal that settled the contest and sent the home crowd into raptures.

The 3-2 win, secured after extra time, was enough to see Dinamo Zagreb through to the third qualifying round on away goals' modern equivalent — away-leg away form matters little now, but the away goal Thun conceded and could not answer proved decisive across the tie's balance sheet.

Zagreb's reward is a tie against Lithuanian champions Kauno Žalgiris, who eliminated KÍ Klaksvík of the Faroe Islands in the earlier round, according to the club's own qualifying-path preview published before the draw was confirmed.
Thun, for their part, drop into the Europa League qualifying path, a consolation route that nonetheless keeps Fabio Celestini's side in continental competition for at least one more round.

For Dinamo, the win extends a recent European pedigree that has repeatedly seen the club recover from difficult positions in qualifying rounds rather than folding under early pressure, a habit their supporters have grown to expect from this squad.

Zagreb's third qualifying round tie with Žalgiris is scheduled for early August, with the first leg on 4 or 5 August and the return a week later, giving the Croatian champions little time to recover from Tuesday's draining extra-time win before the next examination of their squad depth.
facts: Dinamo Zagreb beat FC Thun 3-2 after extra time at Stadion Maksimir on 28 July 2026, in the second leg of the Champions League second qualifying round.
Zagreb won the tie 4-3 on aggregate after the first leg in Switzerland finished 1-1.

title: Panathinaikos lodge offer for Sylvain Francisco as ASVEL's finances unravel
dek: Sport5 reports the Greek giants have proposed at least €3 million a season over three years for the in-form point guard, days after his French club slashed its budget by €35 million.
body: Barely three weeks after Sylvain Francisco put pen to paper on a reported €5 million-a-season contract with LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne, Panathinaikos are already trying to pull him away from it. Sport5 reports that the Greek club has lodged a concrete offer for the French point guard worth at least €3 million a year over a minimum of three seasons.

The timing is no accident. ASVEL, the Lyon-area club chaired by former NBA champion Tony Parker, has been plunged into a financial crisis just as its ambitious summer rebuild was taking shape. Having initially presented French basketball's financial oversight body, the DNCCG, with a record budget plan of €59 million, the club has since been forced to submit a revised proposal of just €24 million — a cut of some €35 million.

That collapse has left ASVEL unable to guarantee it can meet the payments promised to several of its new signings, Francisco included, according to the reporting. Multiple players who arrived in Villeurbanne this summer are said to be exploring their options as a result.

Francisco himself is not currently pushing for a way out, per the reports circulating around the club. Having only just committed his future to the project, he is said to be waiting to see whether ASVEL can stabilise its finances before entertaining anything concrete from elsewhere — even as suitors like Panathinaikos test the water.

The interest is easy to understand. The 28-year-old, Paris-born guard was the standout story of last season's EuroLeague, inspiring Žalgiris Kaunas to a strong campaign with 16.5 points and 6.5 assists per game to go with 2.9 rebounds and 39 percent shooting from three. He was named EuroLeague MVP for October and earned a spot on the All-EuroLeague First Team — the first of his career.

It was that breakout form that persuaded ASVEL to make him a marquee arrival this summer, part of a rebuild that also brought in Daniel Theis, Nick Weiler-Babb, Armoni Brooks, Both Gach and Yves Pons. Francisco's NBA exit clause has already lapsed, meaning any move from here would be to another European club rather than across the Atlantic.

For Panathinaikos, a move for Francisco would fit a pattern: the Greens have circled the guard before, in earlier stages of the offseason, only to see him commit to Villeurbanne. Sport5's report suggests they have not given up, and ASVEL's sudden vulnerability has reopened the door.

Nothing is imminent. Francisco is contracted, ASVEL insists its project remains alive, and the guard has given no public indication he wants to leave. But with the club's budget nearly halved in a matter of weeks, the situation is one to watch closely as the EuroLeague season approaches.

title: Rodri undergoes minor back surgery, City confirm he'll be fit for season opener
dek: The World Cup-winning captain had the procedure in Madrid and was discharged the same day, with Manchester City saying no prolonged rehabilitation is required.
body: Rodri has undergone minor back surgery in Madrid, with Manchester City saying the World Cup-winning captain will be fit for the start of the new season and does not require an extended rehabilitation.

ONE reports that the Spanish midfielder had been feeling discomfort in the area for some time before opting for the procedure. He was discharged the same day and has since begun his planned summer holiday.

"Rodri underwent a successful minor back surgery," the club said in a statement carried by ONE. "The midfielder had suffered from discomfort over a period of time, but has now undergone a procedure to resolve the issue and will begin a short recovery period."

The timing is delicate. British outlets including Sky Sports had reported over the past week that a back operation could rule Rodri out of City's Community Shield date with Arsenal and the early rounds of the Premier League, given the club had yet to confirm a firm return date at that stage. City's own messaging around this completed procedure is more upbeat, framing it as routine and pointing to a season-opener return.

Rodri arrives at pre-season as arguably the most decorated player in the world game right now. He captained Spain to the World Cup title this month, was named the tournament's outstanding player, and already holds the 2024 Ballon d'Or after a career under Pep Guardiola in which he has swept up Premier League, Champions League and FA Cup honours.

That profile has made the back issue a talking point well beyond injury news. Rodri has one year left on his City contract, expiring in June 2027, and Real Madrid have identified him as a priority target to rebuild their midfield. Barcelona also explored a move after Frenkie de Jong's injury, though Sport1 reports Paris Saint-Germain have already stepped back from the race after Luis Enrique concluded his existing midfield options were sufficient.

City are said to be working on a contract extension for Rodri while simultaneously bracing for the possibility he moves on, with reports suggesting the club has set a substantial asking price should a suitor come calling this summer.

For now, the immediate story is medical rather than commercial: a routine-sounding operation, a same-day discharge, and a club insisting its captain-in-waiting for club duties will be ready when the competitive season begins.

title: Shock: Moldovan fighter filmed stealing from a Tel Aviv shop before losing to Ruach Hashem Gordon
dek: CCTV footage aired on Channel 13 showed Maximus Bejanotta taking items from a Carmel Market Judaica store hours before he fell to a judges' decision at the sold-out Gordon brothers' fight night, ONE reports.
body: A Moldovan Muay Thai fighter due to step into the ring on the biggest night of his career was caught on security camera stealing from a shop in Tel Aviv's Carmel Market just hours before the bout — and then lost the fight too, ONE reports.

Maximus Bejanotta, brought in to face Israeli fighter Ruach Hashem Gordon on the GFN 1 fight card, was filmed helping himself to merchandise inside a Judaica store in the market. The footage aired on Channel 13's investigative programme "HaTzinor" and showed him taking items "without any shame," according to ONE's report.

The shop belongs to a woman identified only as Sharon, an Iranian-born widow, ONE reported. Israel Hayom separately carried the story under the headline "Without shame: Ruach Hashem Gordon's rival filmed stealing in the Carmel Market," corroborating the account.
Bejanotta's night went from bad to worse. Hours after the CCTV clip emerged, he lost his Muay Thai bout to Gordon on the judges' scorecards at the sold-out Menora Mivtachim Arena in Tel Aviv.

The bout was part of GFN 1, the first fight card built around all three Gordon brothers — Ahavat Hashem, Ruach Hashem and Kibudi — fighting together on Israeli soil against international opposition. Organisers billed it as the first major international combat-sports event held at the Yad Eliyahu arena since security concerns pushed top-flight basketball fixtures abroad, and the venue sold out for the occasion.

In the main event, Ahavat Hashem Gordon extended his unbeaten record to 12-0 with a judges' decision over Brazilian John Linik, dropping the opening round before rallying with punches and kicks in the second. Kibudi Gordon needed less than 45 seconds to finish Mexico's José Alberto Quiñones with a head-kick knockout.

Ruach Hashem Gordon, 22, arrived with the heaviest résumé of the three brothers: he is the reigning 2023 IFMA world champion at 57kg — the first Israeli man to win a Muay Thai world title — and a silver medallist at the 2025 World Games. Bejanotta, by contrast, had fought only once before as a professional Muay Thai fighter, in the ONE Championship organisation, a bout he also lost.

The theft, aired to a national television audience just hours before Bejanotta even set foot in the ring, has become the more talked-about story to come out of the card — an unwanted footnote to what organisers had hoped would be remembered as a landmark night for Israeli Muay Thai.

body: It has been a wretched week and a half for Maccabi Haifa in the Toto Cup, and Barak Bachar isn't hiding from it. After his side were beaten 3-0 by Ironi Kiryat Shmona, the manager conceded the performance was "unequivocally disappointing" but insisted the picture will look completely different once the Ligat Ha'al season actually kicks off.

The defeat to Kiryat Shmona followed hard on the heels of another loss, 3-2 to local rivals Hapoel Haifa in the Haifa derby, where the Greens surrendered a two-goal cushion before falling in a frantic finish. Two matches, two defeats, and a squad that Bachar himself describes as still under construction.

"This is unequivocally disappointing. We are learning," Bachar said after the final whistle against Kiryat Shmona, according to Sport5. He pointed to gaps in tactical discipline as the root of the problems and said corrective work was already underway on the training ground before the competitive season opens.

"It's better this happens now, when we can fix a lot of things quickly," the coach added, framing the back-to-back Toto Cup defeats as a useful, if painful, diagnostic exercise rather than a genuine crisis.

Maccabi Haifa have undergone a significant summer rebuild, and several of the new faces are still bedding in. Dutch defender Nigel Lonwijk, who joined permanently from Wolverhampton Wanderers in a deal reported at around £500,000, is among the arrivals Bachar is easing into the side alongside other close-season signings.
Goalkeeper Omri Glazer picked up a knock during the recent matches but is said to be managing it, with no indication the issue will keep him out for long.

Bachar's message throughout has been one of patience: the Toto Cup group stage, which opens the Israeli football calendar every summer, is being used to test personnel and systems rather than chase results, and he has signalled more lineup changes are coming as he works towards his first-choice XI for the league opener.

Whether that reshaped Maccabi Haifa can turn Toto Cup lessons into league points will become clear once the Ligat Ha'al season begins, but for now Bachar's promise is unambiguous: what fans have seen so far is not what they will get when it actually matters.

title: Shake Milton agrees deal with Hapoel Jerusalem worth $1m a year
dek: The free-agent American guard, released by Partizan Belgrade earlier this month, has agreed personal terms on a one-year contract with Sasha Obradović's rebuilt Hapoel Jerusalem roster, Sport5 reports.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — Milton agrees terms with Hapoel Jerusalem

body: Hapoel Jerusalem have found their next guard, and he arrives with seven NBA seasons on his resume. Shake Milton has agreed personal terms on a one-year contract worth $1 million with the Reds, Sport5 reports, capping a chase that also involved city rivals Maccabi Tel Aviv.

Milton, 29, is a 1.96m combo guard who spent parts of seven seasons in the NBA after Philadelphia drafted him 54th overall in 2018 out of SMU. He went on to appear in well over 300 NBA games across stints with the 76ers, Minnesota Timberwolves, Detroit Pistons, New York Knicks, Brooklyn Nets and Los Angeles Lakers, his most productive spell coming in Philadelphia, where he once dropped 39 points in a loss to the LA Clippers.

He made the jump to Europe last summer, signing a two-year deal with Partizan Belgrade that was billed as his introduction to EuroLeague basketball. It did not go smoothly: a hand fracture disrupted his season, and he managed only modest returns of 6.9 points a game on 49.5 percent shooting from inside the arc while in and out of the Serbian club's rotation. He fared better in Adriatic League play, averaging closer to 12 points a night. Partizan activated an opt-out clause in his contract earlier this month and released him, making him a free agent.

That availability quickly put him on Israeli radars. Israel Hayom first reported him as a target for Maccabi Tel Aviv, who were said to be exploring him as a possible replacement for Lonnie Walker. Hapoel Jerusalem, though, moved into pole position, and according to Sport5 the two sides have now come to an agreement.

Milton becomes the fifth new face of the summer at Pais Arena as coach Sasha Obradović overhauls the Jerusalem roster following his own arrival on a three-year contract in June. The Serbian coach, who has previously taken charge of AS Monaco, Crvena Zvezda and Alba Berlin in the EuroLeague, is reshaping the squad from the backcourt out, and a guard with Milton's NBA pedigree and shooting pedigree fits the profile he has been chasing.

For Hapoel Jerusalem, who play in the Israeli Winner League and continental competition, adding an NBA-tested guard at this stage of the market is a statement of intent after a summer already built around Obradović's arrival. The club has not yet issued a formal unveiling of the signing, and the deal is being reported at this stage as agreed personal terms rather than a signed, announced contract.

Milton's route to Jerusalem underlines how quickly value can shift for fringe NBA players once they test the European market: waived by the Lakers last July, still just 29 and with legitimate NBA-level tools, he now heads to Israel look to rebuild his stock after an injury-hit season in Belgrade.

title: Green card frees up international slot for Ilay Feingold at New England Revolution
dek: Sport5 reports the Israeli defender has been granted US permanent residency, handing his MLS club a valuable roster boost as he settles into his second season in New England.
body: Ilay Feingold has picked up some welcome news away from the pitch. Sport5 reports that the Israeli defender has been granted a United States green card, a change in status that reclassifies him as a domestic player under MLS roster rules and frees up an international slot for New England Revolution.

Under MLS regulations, clubs are capped on the number of players who occupy international roster spots, with permanent residents counted as domestic players alongside US and Canadian citizens. By securing his green card, Feingold no longer ties up one of the Revolution's limited slots, giving the club extra flexibility to pursue another overseas signing without needing to trade for additional international spots, as clubs regularly do around the league.

The 21-year-old right-back joined New England from Maccabi Haifa in January 2025 on a three-year deal through the 2027 season, with a club option for 2028, signed through the league's U22 Initiative. The move was reported at the time to be worth around $2.5 million to the Israeli club, with Maccabi Haifa also retaining a sell-on percentage.

Feingold made 37 appearances for Maccabi Haifa's first team before crossing the Atlantic, and he has become a regular fixture in New England's backline since, capable of playing at both right-back and centre-back. He has started the majority of the Revolution's matches so far this season.

He arrives with an established pedigree at youth level for Israel, including a bronze medal at the 2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup and a runner-up finish at the 2022 European U-19 Championship. He was also part of Israel's squad at the 2024 Paris Olympics and has since earned his first senior caps for the national team.

Feingold is not the only Israeli in New England's dressing room. Forward Dor Turgeman, signed from Maccabi Tel Aviv in a big-money move last September, has also become a key contributor and a regular call-up for Israel's senior side, giving the Revolution a growing Israeli contingent on both sides of the pitch.

For a club still building out its roster in a league where international slots are treated as a tradable commodity, the paperwork change is a quietly significant boost — one less roster headache as New England looks to add further reinforcements before the MLS season reaches its business end.

title: Hapoel Haifa's Silvas tempers optimism after Torgeman brace sees off Tiberias
dek: Alon Torgeman scored twice and ex-Tiberias forward Wahib Habiballah struck against his old club as Hapoel Haifa won 3-1 in the Toto Cup, but manager Haim Silvas warned against reading too much into a pre-season competition.

body: Hapoel Haifa put down an early marker for the new season on Tuesday evening, beating Ironi Tiberias 3-1 at Sammy Ofer Stadium in round two of the Toto Cup group stage — though the mood inside the home camp afterwards was measured rather than jubilant.

Alon Torgeman put the hosts ahead inside eight minutes and restored their lead in the 33rd after Qais Ghanem had levelled for the visitors midway through the first half. Wahib Habiballah, who signed for Haifa from Tiberias this summer on a two-year deal, completed the scoring in the 76th minute — fittingly, against the club he had just left.

Manager Haim Silvas, back at Haifa for a second spell in charge, was careful not to get carried away by the result. "There's modest optimism, but we have to remember this is only the Toto Cup," he said, according to ONE, describing his side's pre-season form as "a process of trial and learning" in which players are visibly improving from one game to the next.

Torgeman, 35, said he is enjoying his best form in years. "I've never felt better in the last three years," he said, adding that goals are secondary for him right now to making sure the squad is properly prepared for the league campaign ahead.

For Tiberias, manager Moti Krispin had little to dress up. He said his players had performed poorly, particularly before the break, and described Haifa's approach as "intensive and controlled." Asked about reports of organizational unrest at the club, Krispin declined to be drawn, saying he preferred to keep the conversation on football.

Tiberias player Itamar Shviro offered a more forgiving reading of the display, saying the club's younger players are using the Toto Cup to learn on the job while the more experienced squad members try to lead by example on the pitch.

The Toto Cup group stage exists precisely for moments like this: a low-stakes proving ground where clubs experiment with personnel and shape fitness before the Israeli league season resumes in earnest. Silvas's caution, and Krispin's frankness, both reflect a shared understanding that Tuesday's result — however lopsided in the closing stages — will count for little once the real season begins.

body: Kervin Andrade came back from an eventful break away from Maccabi Tel Aviv, having spent time with family in Venezuela through the aftermath of an earthquake there, only to find his immediate future at the club still unresolved. According to ONE, Maccabi are now actively trying to send the 21-year-old out on loan before the season gets going in earnest.

The report describes "a mutual search, both from the club and from the player's circle," to find a team willing to take Andrade until the end of the season. The preference, ONE says, is a move overseas, with the priority simply being regular football rather than any particular league or region.

Crucially, Maccabi are not looking to attach a purchase option to any deal. The club wants what ONE calls a "dry loan" — one that leaves the door open for Andrade to return to Kiryat Shalom, Maccabi's training base, and force his way back into the picture at a later date.

The timing is awkward for Andrade regardless of where he ends up. He is still working through a suspension stemming from the brawl at the Israel State Cup final between Maccabi and Hapoel Be'er Sheva, for which he and several other players from both clubs were sanctioned as part of a disciplinary plea deal. ONE reports the outstanding portion of that ban will keep him out of an upcoming cup semifinal and the opening five rounds of the league.

None of that has stopped him being included in Maccabi's travelling party for Wednesday's Europa League second qualifying-round second leg against Sheriff Tiraspol, where the club will be looking to see out passage to the next round of the competition.

Andrade arrived at Maccabi in September 2025 in a move from Brazil's Fortaleza, signing a four-year contract and taking the number 10 shirt. Game time has been hard to come by since: with nine foreign players currently on Maccabi's books and a squad already stretched for minutes, there simply isn't a regular path onto the pitch for him this season.

That crowded foreign contingent is part of the calculation. ONE notes Maccabi could register two further foreign signings if both Andrade and fellow overseas player Nicolaescu move on, giving the club fresh space to work with under Ligat Ha'al's quota rules.

For all the uncertainty over his immediate club, the report suggests Maccabi have not given up on Andrade long-term — he is said to have returned from his leave in good spirits and training well, with the loan framed as a stopgap to get him playing rather than a step toward pushing him out for good.

title: Ironi Tiberias search for stand-in coach as Drapić's name emerges
dek: The Galilee club need a caretaker after head coach Eliran Chuda's suspension in a banned-infusions case, and out-of-work manager Slobodan Drapić has been floated as a candidate, ONE reports.

body: Ironi Tiberias are looking for a stand-in head coach, and the name doing the rounds is a familiar one in Israeli football: Slobodan Drapić, according to a report from ONE.

The Galilee club find themselves in an unusual bind. Head coach Eliran Chuda was provisionally suspended earlier this month by Israel's National Anti-Doping Agency, one of several figures at the club caught up in a case centred on intravenous infusions allegedly given to players before a match against Ashdod.

The complaint that triggered the case came from Ashdod, who alleged Tiberias players received more than 100cc of saline infusions before facing them. Tiberias have disputed any wrongdoing, arguing the substance was legal and administered within World Anti-Doping Agency limits, while prosecutors are reportedly seeking sanctions ranging from lengthy suspensions to a lifetime expulsion for some of those implicated.

That has left the club needing a coach in a hurry, and the succession plan is awkward. Assistant Moti Krispiel does not hold the Pro licence required to take permanent charge of a Ligat Ha'al team, so youth-team coach Morris Ozen has stepped in as a stopgap. ONE reports the club regards that arrangement as unsustainable beyond the very short term.
The preferred solution, according to the report, is to bring in an experienced coach on a temporary contract to bridge the gap until Chuda's case is resolved and, potentially, he is able to return.

Drapić fits that profile. The Serbian-born Israeli has been out of work since Maccabi Bnei Reineh dismissed him last year, the latest stop in a well-travelled career that has taken in two spells at Beitar Jerusalem, plus stints at Maccabi Netanya, Ironi Kiryat Shmona, Hapoel Tel Aviv and Maccabi Sakhnin.

Tiberias' coaching vacancy is just one of several problems facing the club this summer as they prepare for the new season, with the Toto Cup group stage already under way. No appointment had been made as of ONE's report, and for now Drapić remains a name in the frame rather than a confirmed candidate.

title: From West Ham captain to pizza courier: the story of Iyiola Adebayo
dek: Released by West Ham at 16 after a serious shoulder injury, a once-promising academy captain ended up delivering pizzas for Domino's before finding a new path through a players' welfare programme.
body: Six months. That is how long it took Iyiola Adebayo to go from captaining West Ham United's youth side to delivering pizzas for Domino's just to make ends meet, a fall from a promising academy career that ONE has revisited as part of a wider look at how football deals with the players it discards.

Adebayo joined West Ham's academy at the age of eight, entering the same production line that had already turned out Rio Ferdinand, Joe Cole and Declan Rice. He was talented enough to be handed a development scholarship ahead of the rest of his age group, a marker the club reserves for its most promising prospects.

The trajectory changed in his very first year on scholarship terms, when a dislocated shoulder derailed his progress. He still managed appearances for West Ham's under-21 and under-23 sides and wore the captain's armband for the youth team, but at 16, and while still not fully recovered from his injury, he was released.

What followed was a familiar but brutal cycle for released academy players: trials at other clubs while operating, by his own estimate, at only "probably 50-60% of what I was capable of" because of the lingering injury. Nothing came of them.

"Sometimes I didn't want to be there, I wanted to go home. It was very difficult," Adebayo has said of that period, describing how deeply his sense of self had been tied up in being a West Ham player. To get by, he took a part-time job delivering pizzas for Domino's.

The turning point came through the Premier League Futures programme, launched in 2017 to support players released between the ages of 18 and 24, as well as academy prospects under 16 who are let go without a professional contract. Adebayo was initially reluctant to take part, but a former head of education at West Ham pointed him toward it, and he eventually engaged with the scheme.

Now 23, Adebayo is completing a sponsored degree in football business and marketing at the University Campus of Football Business. He has also begun delivering mental health and lifestyle workshops to current academy players through Sporting Chance, the welfare charity founded by former Arsenal captain Tony Adams.

His plan is to move into player care within a club before transitioning to the business or commercial side of the sport, a route that keeps him inside the game he grew up in without needing a professional contract to justify it.

It is a story ONE frames as a reminder of English football's brutal release rate at academy level, and of the small but growing infrastructure, in programmes like Premier League Futures and charities like Sporting Chance, built to catch the players who fall through.

title: Mancini returns to coach Italy, with Ranieri alongside him
dek: The Euro 2020-winning coach is back for a second spell in charge of the Azzurri, with Claudio Ranieri installed as technical director after a chaotic search that saw Paolo Maldini quit within weeks.
body: Roberto Mancini is coming back to finish a job he never wanted to leave unfinished. Italy's football federation confirmed on Tuesday that the 61-year-old will return for a second spell as national team coach, with Claudio Ranieri installed alongside him as technical director, ONE reports.

FIGC president Giovanni Malagò announced the appointments at a press conference, ending weeks of turmoil over who would try to drag the Azzurri back to a World Cup they have now missed three tournaments running. "I believed it was right for Roberto Mancini to become head coach of the Italy national team, for a number of reasons. I take full responsibility for this decision," Malagò said, according to reports from the announcement.

Mancini needs no introduction to Italian fans. He led the national team to European Championship glory at Euro 2020, one of the great redemption stories in Italian football after the Azzurri had failed to even qualify for the 2018 World Cup. He walked away from the job in August 2023 to take over Saudi Arabia's national team, a lucrative move that ended in mutual separation last year.

He returns to a federation in disarray. Gabriele Gravina resigned as FIGC president in April after Italy's World Cup qualifying campaign collapsed with a defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina — the third straight cycle in which the four-time champions have failed to reach the tournament. Malagò was elected his successor in June.

The search for a new coach then descended into chaos of its own. Paolo Maldini and Leonardo were brought in to oversee the process but lasted barely 16 days before resigning, after pushing hard for Andrea Pirlo to get the job. Malagò blocked Pirlo's candidacy over an undisclosed commercial tie to a Russian betting company that neither he nor the federation's technical leadership had been aware of, ONE reports.

Before turning to Mancini, Italian football's leadership had also made a run at Pep Guardiola. Maldini and Leonardo reportedly flew to Barcelona with a full project proposal for the Manchester City manager, only for Guardiola to turn it down for personal reasons.

That left Mancini, a coach with an actual trophy on his Italy CV, as the obvious fallback — and Ranieri, 74, as the calming presence the federation wanted next to him. Ranieri will serve as technical director and president of Club Italia, effectively taking on the administrative and organisational side of the operation while Mancini focuses on the pitch.

Both men have reportedly already signalled they are willing to work within the federation's financial constraints as they take on the job, a notable gesture given the fallout from the Maldini-Leonardo episode and the wider mess Italian football finds itself trying to clean up.

Mancini and Ranieri were due to be presented together at a press conference, with the immediate task in front of them unenviable: rebuilding a national team that has now spent a decade on the outside of world football's biggest stage looking in.

title: IFAB confirms Embolo should not have been sent off against Argentina
dek: Football's law-making body says the VAR review that turned a yellow card for Argentina's Leandro Paredes into a match-changing red for Switzerland's Breel Embolo misapplied the mistaken-identity protocol.
body: IFAB, football's law-making panel, has confirmed what Switzerland suspected all along: Breel Embolo should never have been sent off against Argentina in the World Cup quarter-final that ended their tournament.

The clarification, published Monday, addresses one of the most contentious refereeing moments of the entire 2026 World Cup — a VAR intervention that swapped a yellow card from one player to another and, in doing so, changed the identity of the offence itself.

The incident happened in the 72nd minute of the July 11 quarter-final in extra time territory of the tournament's knockout stage, moments after Switzerland had drawn level at 1-1. Embolo went down under a challenge from Argentina's Leandro Paredes, and the referee initially cautioned Paredes for the foul.

VAR officials then called the referee to the pitchside monitor, but not to confirm the caution — instead they flagged what they described as a case of mistaken identity. On review, the officials decided Paredes had committed no foul at all, and that Embolo had in fact dived. The yellow card was switched to Embolo for simulation, his second of the match, and he was sent off.
Argentina went on to win 3-1 after extra time, eliminating Switzerland from the World Cup with a man advantage for the closing stages.

IFAB's clarification, aimed at referees rather than at overturning the result, states plainly that the mistaken-identity review protocol was used incorrectly. "A yellow card, which is not a second yellow card, can only be reviewed to identify the player who committed a predetermined offence — the offence itself cannot be examined or changed," the board said, according to reporting on the ruling.

In practice, that means VAR was entitled only to correct who was cautioned for the original foul call, not to reclassify the incident as simulation and pin an entirely different offence on a different player. By doing both, the review overstepped what the mistaken-identity mechanism was designed for.

IFAB did note that widening the protocol to specifically cover diving and simulation cases has been discussed positively, but stressed any such change would require the board's formal rulebook review and approval process before it could be introduced — it cannot be applied retroactively or on the fly.

The finding will offer little practical comfort to Switzerland, whose World Cup run ended that night in Argentina's favor regardless of the ruling. But it adds Embolo's case to the small list of VAR decisions a governing body has since acknowledged, in its own words, got the law wrong.

IFAB noted a proposal to extend the mistaken-identity protocol to cover diving and simulation cases was received positively but requires its formal rulebook review process before any change can take effect.
The ruling does not alter the match result; Argentina's progression in the World Cup stands.

title: Cucurella keeps his word, tattoos Spain coach de la Fuente's face
dek: The Real Madrid left-back vowed before the World Cup final that he would ink his national team coach onto his skin if Spain won it all — and he has, ONE reports.
body: Marc Cucurella does not make promises lightly. Before Spain's World Cup final against Argentina, the left-back told Fox Sports he would get "a small tattoo" of national team coach Luis de la Fuente's face if La Roja lifted the trophy. ONE reports that he has now followed through.

Cucurella revealed the finished piece on social media in the days after the final, honouring a pledge he made half-jokingly but clearly meant to keep. The portrait was done by Ganga, a tattoo artist whose past clients include LeBron James and Georgina Rodríguez.

At the time he made the promise, Cucurella was cagey about exactly where the tattoo would go, saying only that it needed to be visible enough that people would notice and ask about it. "I still don't know where and when. I need to think about it well and see where to put it," he said before the final.

De la Fuente, for his part, reacted with amusement when told his players were promising to have his face permanently inked onto their bodies, joking that his squad are people who keep their word — a line that has aged well.

The gesture caps a remarkable summer for Spain. Fran Torres scored in the 106th minute as Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in New Jersey on July 19 to win their second World Cup, 16 years after their first in 2010.
The triumph also completed a rare double: Spain became the first nation to hold both the men's and women's World Cups at the same time, on the back of a 38-game unbeaten run.

Cucurella was one of the standout performers of Spain's campaign, and his next assignment is a fresh one. He completed a summer move from Chelsea to Real Madrid, in a deal reported at around €60 million (€55m plus add-ons), signing a contract through 2032.

He is expected to link up with Real Madrid's pre-season squad shortly, joining fellow new arrivals Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Bernardo Silva as Los Blancos reshape their squad for the season ahead.

body: Hapoel Upper Galilee have found their answer to a hole in the backcourt, confirming on Tuesday that guard Itay Moshkovitch has signed with the club for a second stint, ONE reports.
Moshkovitch, 26, previously wore the club's colours during the 2022/23 season. His return fills the gap left by Yuval Sznajderman, who has departed the Galilee for Hapoel Eilat.

"His return represents far more than just another signing," the club said in a statement carried by ONE. "It symbolises continuity, a genuine connection to our club's values and belief in the path we're building together. We are confident that his heart, fighting spirit and character will help us throughout the season."

The statement continued: "Itay already knows the club, the fans and the unique spirit of the Galilee, and now he returns with more experience, greater confidence and the same commitment to give everything on the court in every game."

According to ONE, Moshkovitch arrives from Elitzur Netanya, where he averaged 7.5 points, 2.4 assists and 2.7 rebounds a game last season. Other Israeli outlets, including a July 2025 announcement from Ironi Nes Ziona, had listed that club as his most recent destination for the 2025/26 campaign — a discrepancy in his exact last stop that this outlet could not fully resolve from the available reporting.

Whichever club he is arriving from, Moshkovitch's career has been a well-travelled one for a player still only 26: spells with Elitzur Netanya, Hapoel Upper Galilee, Hapoel Haifa and Maccabi Ramat Gan have all featured since he broke through as a National League standout in his early twenties.

Hapoel Upper Galilee, based at the Heichal HaPais in Kiryat Shmona and drawing support from across the Galilee panhandle, are shaping their roster for the coming Israeli Premier League season with a mix of continuity and fresh faces — and in Moshkovitch's case, a bit of both at once.

title: Rotem Piumi to begin senior career at Maccabi Kiryat Malachi
dek: The 20-year-old forward, an academy graduate of Maccabi Petah Tikva who spent a season and a half at Hapoel Ra'anana, has signed with the Liga Alef South club.
body: Rotem Piumi is about to find out what senior football feels like. The 20-year-old forward, raised through Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth ranks, has signed with Maccabi Kiryat Malachi of Liga Alef South, the club announced on Tuesday.

Piumi spent three seasons in Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth divisions before breaking into the first team, where he featured for a season and a half. He then moved on to Hapoel Ra'anana, where over another season and a half he scored 11 goals — the kind of return that persuaded Kiryat Malachi to bring him south.
According to ONE, Piumi is the third player Kiryat Malachi have signed out of Hapoel Ra'anana's ranks this window, following goalkeeper Lior Shauer and defender Sahar Ruitman through the door.
"I'm happy to sign with the club and be part of the family," Piumi said. "Thank you for the trust — I'm looking forward to repaying it on the pitch and helping the team reach its goals, God willing."

The move comes as Kiryat Malachi prepare for a fourth straight season in Liga Alef South, Israel's third tier, under new ownership after businessman Ezra Lati took over the club, with Tzvika Levi staying on as head coach.

Kiryat Malachi reached Liga Alef South via the promotion playoffs and play their home games at the modest Nino Stadium, which holds around 1,000 spectators. For a player only now stepping into senior football full-time, it is a fitting stage to make his mark before, potentially, bigger clubs come calling.

title: Israel's girls' water polo team fall 10-4 to the Netherlands at U16 Worlds
dek: A tough second defeat in Zagreb sends the young team into the 9th-16th place classification round, but coach Idan Kaftori praised a fighting display.

verificationSources.label: Ynet - Israel open tournament with win over South Africa
World Aquatics - Women's U16 Water Polo Championships 2026

body: Israel's under-16 girls' water polo team suffered its second defeat of the World Aquatics Women's U16 Championships on Tuesday, going down 10-4 to the Netherlands at the Mladost swimming complex in Zagreb, Croatia.

The young Israelis were competitive early on, trailing just 2-1 after the first period, but a strong Dutch second quarter opened the gap to 6-2 by half-time and the Netherlands controlled the rest of the game from there, according to ONE.
Ori Grodman scored twice for Israel, with Yahli Rokach and Shani Yaakobovich adding a goal apiece in a losing effort against one of the traditional powers of women's water polo.
The result is Israel's second loss of the tournament, which means the team now moves into the classification round to play for 9th through 16th place rather than continuing to compete for a medal.

Head coach Idan Kaftori struck a defiant tone afterwards, telling ONE that "the players deserve great credit for a very fighting performance," while adding that "now we have to pick ourselves up and win tomorrow."
Israel had opened the championship in fine form on Saturday, beating South Africa 12-7, with Grodman and Rokach both scoring three goals in that match and Rokach named player of the game.
Zagreb is hosting both the men's and women's U16 World Championships this summer at the Mladost complex, with 60 national teams taking part across the two events between 25 and 31 July.

This is the third edition of the women's tournament since it was launched in 2022, following stagings in Greece and Malta, and the Netherlands - who beat Germany on the opening day - remain among the field's strongest sides.
Israel's placement matches later in the week will determine the team's final position at just its third appearance on this global stage.

title: Two years after the Majdal Shams attack, Bnei Mamba keeps growing
dek: The Golan Druze club lost three young players when a rocket struck its home pitch and killed 12 children; two years on, ONE reports the club has expanded to eleven teams and become a symbol of the community's resilience.
body: Two years to the week since a rocket fired from Lebanon tore into a football pitch in Majdal Shams and killed 12 children, the small Golan Druze club that lost three of its own players in the strike says it has not just survived the tragedy but grown through it, ONE reports.

Bnei Mamba is not a conventional club name but an acronym drawn from the four Druze villages of the northern Golan Heights it represents — Masaada, Majdal Shams, Buq'ata and Ein Qiniya. What began as a single senior side in the mid-2010s has, even through catastrophe, become the sporting backbone of the whole plateau.

On the afternoon of July 27, 2024, a missile struck the football field in Majdal Shams while children and teenagers were playing. Twelve were killed and dozens more wounded in one of the deadliest single strikes on Israeli territory since the war on the northern front began. Israel and Western governments attributed the rocket to Hezbollah; the group denied firing it, blaming an errant Israeli air-defense interceptor instead — a dispute that remains unresolved.

Three of the twelve who died were Bnei Mamba players: Amir Abu Saleh, 16, Hazem Abu Saleh, 15, and Johnny Ibrahim, 13. Their deaths on their own pitch, in the colors of their own club, left a wound the community is still living with.
"The disaster continues to accompany our thoughts," the club's coach, Wajdi Alqish, told ONE. "We lost players; this will follow us our whole lives."

Yet the numbers Alqish now oversees tell a story of stubborn expansion rather than retreat. Bnei Mamba fields eight boys' teams — including a youth side competing in the national league — alongside two girls' teams, a girls' youth team and a veterans' squad, according to the club.
"We continue to play, grow and develop," Alqish said. "Our club models coexistence — children from regional kibbutzim now want to join us. These are the best responses to murderous terrorism."

A memorial ceremony was held in Majdal Shams this week marking two years since the strike, attended by relatives of the victims and local officials. A monument shaped like a football now stands in the square beside the pitch, dedicated to the twelve children who were killed there.

The pitch itself was rebuilt and reopened in a ceremony in August 2025, its reconstruction funded in part by donor families from abroad, the Jerusalem Post has reported, turning the site of the attack back into the place where Bnei Mamba's teams train and play.

For a club that could easily have folded under the weight of what happened on its own field, the growth Alqish describes — more teams, more players, more communities drawn in — stands as the Golan's own quiet answer to the attack that defined it two years ago.

title: Kozuk banks on grass pitch as Hapoel Beer Sheva chase Champions League comeback
dek: Coach Ran Kozuk says his side, needing to overturn a 2-1 first-leg deficit against Vikingur Reykjavik, will finally have a real grass pitch under their feet in Szombathely — and intends to use it.
body: Hapoel Beer Sheva head into Wednesday night needing a comeback, and their coach believes the surface under their feet might finally help.

Ran Kozuk, speaking to reporters ahead of the second leg of the club's Champions League second qualifying round tie against Vikingur Reykjavik, noted that the return match will be played on a proper grass pitch — a contrast, he said, to the conditions the team faced in Iceland. "We're finally playing on grass and we'll try to use that too," Kozuk said, according to ONE, while cautioning that the surface alone would not hand his side a decisive edge.

Beer Sheva, the reigning Israeli Premier League champions, go into the second leg trailing 2-1 after last week's defeat in Reykjavik, where Vikingur snatched the win with a late goal. The Israeli champions need at least a two-goal winning margin at the final whistle to progress directly to the third qualifying round; a narrower win would send the tie to extra time and potentially penalties.

As with previous continental campaigns, Beer Sheva's home leg is not being played at their own Turner Stadium in the Negev. The match is instead being staged at a neutral venue in Szombathely, Hungary, with kickoff set for 20:30 local time on Wednesday.

Kozuk was blunt about what needs to change from the first leg. He said the team must show far greater defensive aggression than it did in Iceland, and pointed to several attacking patterns the squad had drilled in training that never surfaced during the 90 minutes there.

The coach was complimentary about the opponent, describing Vikingur as "an excellent team" and stressing that advancing will require hard work rather than any shortcut. Iceland's champions eliminated Hungary's Gyor in the previous round before taking the lead in this tie.

For Beer Sheva, the stakes extend beyond bragging rights. A place in the third qualifying round would keep alive their run toward the Champions League league phase and, at minimum, a guaranteed continental fallback place should they eventually fall short in a later round.

body: Hapoel Ashkelon have gone back to a familiar face to lead their dugout, appointing Ami Jerbi as head coach for the 2026/27 season, ONE reports.

The move takes Jerbi out of the club's front office, where he had most recently been serving as chief executive, and puts him back on the touchline at the reformed south-coast club he has represented in various roles down the years.

"I am excited and proud to get the opportunity to coach Hapoel Ashkelon, a club dear to my heart," Jerbi said, according to ONE. "I thank the management for their confidence and commit to doing my best daily with the professional staff and players to build a committed, fighting team that will represent the city, supporters and club symbol with honour."
Club management pointed to Jerbi's deep familiarity with Hapoel Ashkelon and his accumulated experience on the touchline as the reasons behind the appointment, ONE reported.

That coaching background includes stints as an assistant at Ashkelon itself under Yuval Neeim and Massai Dago during the club's top-flight years, as well as a spell as an assistant to Shlomi Dora at Liga Leumit level.
Jerbi has also managed in his own right, leading Ironi Ashdod to a league promotion as head coach before later taking over at Maccabi Netivot.

Hapoel Ironi Ashkelon itself is a young project: the club was re-established under its current name in May 2025 after a re-registration with the Israel Football Association, and has been building back up through the regional leagues from Liga Gimel. title: Omri Glazer in tears as knee injury mars his Maccabi Haifa return
dek: The goalkeeper, back at Maccabi Haifa this summer, needed on-field treatment and was replaced after twisting his knee in a first-half collision during the Toto Cup trip to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE – Tsunami and Bruninho handed debuts
Walla Sport – Glazer returns to Maccabi Haifa
Sport1 Maariv – Glazer's Maccabi Haifa return

body: Omri Glazer's homecoming at Maccabi Haifa hit its first real setback on Tuesday, with the goalkeeper carried off in tears after twisting his knee during the club's Toto Cup trip to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, ONE reports.

The incident happened in the 23rd minute with the Greens already trailing 2-0. According to ONE, Glazer's own teammate, the Brazilian defender Wanderson "Tsunami," accidentally caught him as the two competed near the goal, and the goalkeeper twisted his knee awkwardly in the collision.

Glazer needed treatment from Magen David Adom paramedics on the pitch before he could be moved, and ONE describes him leaving the field in tears, unable to continue. He was withdrawn immediately and taken straight down the tunnel.

Young goalkeeper Glen Alwyn came on to replace him — an unplanned, high-pressure introduction for the 18-year-old, who only recently earned a place on Maccabi Haifa's first-team bench after coming through the club's academy.

The timing stings. Glazer, an Israel international, returned to Maccabi Haifa this summer on a three-year contract, rejoining the club where he made his name before spells at Hapoel Be'er Sheva and, most recently, Red Star Belgrade in Serbia.

Tuesday's tie was already a chance for Barak Bachar to reset after an underwhelming start to the Toto Cup, in which Maccabi Haifa lost the Haifa derby 3-2 to Hapoel Haifa in their opening group game. Bachar had again turned to his summer arrivals, starting Tsunami alongside fellow new signings Bruninho and Nigel Lonwijk.
ONE's report does not give a diagnosis or an expected recovery timeline for Glazer — the club is yet to confirm the extent of the damage, and scans are expected to follow before any timetable is set.

For now, the club and its supporters are left waiting anxiously on the results, with a goalkeeper who had barely settled back into the dressing room facing the prospect of missing the start of the new Ligat Ha'al season.

title: Tsunami and Bruninho handed full debuts as Maccabi Haifa chase a Toto Cup response
dek: Barak Bachar starts three of his summer signings away to Ironi Kiryat Shmona as the Greens look to shake off their opening-round derby defeat to Hapoel Haifa.
body: Barak Bachar is giving three of Maccabi Haifa's headline summer arrivals their first taste of competitive action together, naming Bruninho, Wanderson "Tsunami" and Nigel Lonwijk in his starting eleven for Tuesday's Toto Cup trip to Ironi Kiryat Shmona, ONE reports.

The match, the second round of the Toto Cup group phase, kicks off at Miriam Stadium with Maccabi Haifa needing a response after an unexpected 3-2 loss to city rivals Hapoel Haifa in their opening fixture of the campaign.

That derby defeat left the Greens without a point from their first outing, and Bachar has clearly decided the moment is right to fast-track his new signings into the side rather than easing them in gradually.

Bruninho, the Brazilian midfielder who arrived from Ukrainian side Karpaty Lviv for roughly €1.5 million — a fee that can rise to about €1.8 million with add-ons — starts having signed a three-year deal in Haifa. The 26-year-old, an Atletico Mineiro academy product, scored 17 goals and set up eight more across two seasons at Karpaty.

Alongside him comes Wanderson, known to Israeli fans as "Tsunami," a 30-year-old Brazilian left-back who joined this summer after captaining Levski Sofia and, more recently, playing in Turkey's second tier. Born in Belém, Pará, the 1.89-metre defender also holds Bulgarian citizenship and is expected to add height and experience to Bachar's back line.

The third debutant, Nigel Lonwijk, is a 23-year-old Dutch-Surinamese defender signed from Wolverhampton Wanderers for around €500,000 on a three-year contract. A product of PSV's youth academy who moved to England as a teenager, he is the club's sixth summer addition alongside Omri Glazer, Yair Mordechai, Tsunami, Bruninho and Andrea Novakovich.
Omri Glazer starts in goal behind a reshaped back line, with Itai Ahood also involved as Bachar experiments with personnel before the Ligat Ha'al season proper gets under way.

Ironi Kiryat Shmona, managed by Shai Barda, are playing their first official match of the new season and go into it on the back of a mixed preseason that included a 0-0 draw with Hapoel Haifa and a 2-0 defeat to Bnei Yehuda.
History strongly favours the visitors: Maccabi Haifa have won each of their last six league meetings with Kiryat Shmona, the most recent of them a comfortable 4-1 victory.

For Bachar, the priority is less about the head-to-head record and more about seeing how quickly his rebuilt squad can gel — with Tsunami, Bruninho and Lonwijk all thrown in together from the first whistle, the Toto Cup trip to the Galilee doubles as an early audition for the season ahead.

title: Gvardiol extends Manchester City contract as Henderson closes in on Chelsea
dek: The Croatian defender ties himself to the Etihad through 2031 while the veteran England midfielder edges toward a free transfer from Brentford under Xabi Alonso.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports — Gvardiol signs new Man City contract to 2031
Sky Sports — Chelsea interested in signing Jordan Henderson
Football365 — Romano: 'here we go' coming very soon on Henderson deal

body: Manchester City moved to end any uncertainty over one of their first-choice centre-backs this week, confirming that Josko Gvardiol has signed a new long-term contract that will keep the Croatian at the Etihad Stadium through the summer of 2031, with an option for a further year.

The 24-year-old arrived from RB Leipzig in the summer of 2023 and has quickly become one of Pep Guardiola's most trusted defenders, comfortable at both centre-back and left-back. In two seasons in Manchester he has made 122 appearances and scored 13 goals, and has helped the club collect six major honours along the way — the Premier League, the FA Cup, the League Cup, the FIFA Club World Cup, the UEFA Super Cup and the Community Shield.

OneFootball reported that Gvardiol explained his decision to commit his long-term future to City in simple terms, saying the club remains "the best club in the world to be at" — remarks that draw a line under the periodic transfer speculation that had surrounded him.

While City tied down a player very much part of its long-term core, Chelsea worked the market from the opposite direction, closing in on a rather different kind of signing: a 36-year-old free agent whose days as a Premier League regular were thought by many to be behind him.

ONE reports that Jordan Henderson is heading to Chelsea, with the veteran England midfielder having all but agreed to leave Brentford on a free transfer. Fabrizio Romano and other British outlets describe the move as effectively agreed in principle, with a formal announcement expected once the paperwork between the clubs is completed.

The move fits what Xabi Alonso has been seeking since taking permanent charge at Stamford Bridge ahead of his first full season: a senior, experienced voice to steady an otherwise young dressing room. According to British reports, Chelsea's pursuit of Henderson gathered pace after an earlier approach for Bayer Leverkusen's Granit Xhaka failed to progress.

For Henderson, it would be a fourth club in as many years since he left Liverpool, where he had been captain, in the summer of 2023. He spent a season in Saudi Arabia with Al-Ettifaq, returned to Europe with Ajax, and then came back to the Premier League with Brentford last summer — and could now make a short move across west London to Chelsea.

Between them, the two stories capture two very different transfer-market instincts at two of the Premier League's traditional heavyweights this summer: City banking on a 24-year-old they intend to build around for years to come, and Chelsea reaching for the ballast of a player who has seen almost everything English football has to offer.

title: Thousands turn out as Maccabi Netanya hold open training session
dek: Smoke grenades, storming fans and a festive mood at the club's training ground as Roni Levi's side build momentum ahead of a second Toto Cup test against Maccabi Petach Tikva.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Roni Levi appointed Netanya coach

body: Maccabi Netanya threw open the gates of their training ground this week, and thousands of supporters answered the call, packing the facility for a session that felt more like a pre-season carnival than a routine work-out.

According to ONE, the yellow-and-black faithful arrived with smoke grenades and pyrotechnics, and hundreds streamed onto the pitch even before the squad had been formally introduced to the crowd. The atmosphere, the outlet reported, was exceptionally festive from the first whistle.

The turnout comes with real momentum behind it. Netanya opened their Toto Cup campaign on July 25 with a 3-1 win away over Hapoel Jerusalem in their Group B fixture, a result that has lifted expectations heading into the new season.

Bassam Zaroura put Netanya ahead early before Israel Daffa equalised for Jerusalem, and Oz Biloo restored the lead before half-time. The scoring was capped in the 75th minute by 16-year-old Yarin Abuhatzeera, who struck his first senior goal with what was described as an excellent finish just days after coming through the club's youth ranks.

It was Abuhatzeera, along with summer signing Dolev Haziza, club captain Karem Jaber and midfielder Maor Levi, who drew the loudest ovations at the open session, with fans showering the group in what ONE called abundant encouragement and support throughout the workout.

Haziza arrived at Netanya this summer on a two-year deal after his contract at Maccabi Haifa was terminated, one of several moves the club has made to strengthen the squad under new head coach Roni Levi, who returned to Netanya on an 18-month contract having previously managed the club back in 2015.

By the end of the session, fans had mobbed the players so thoroughly that several were left, in ONE's description, stripped down to just their shorts, before posing for photos with supporters. Merchandise stalls and family-oriented attractions were also set up around the ground to make a day of it.

Levi and his squad now turn their attention to Wednesday, when Netanya travel to face Maccabi Petach Tikva in their next Toto Cup Group B outing, looking to build on the derby win over Hapoel Jerusalem and the wave of enthusiasm it has generated among supporters.

title: Winger Mohammad Graba leaves Maccabi Haifa academy for Kiryat Shmona
dek: The teenage attacker signs a three-year academy deal with Ironi Kiryat Shmona after a productive U-17 season in Haifa, ONE reports.
body: Ironi Kiryat Shmona have added a promising young winger to their academy ranks, signing Mohammad Graba away from Maccabi Haifa, ONE reported on Tuesday.

According to the report, the deal was struck through agent Noam Markowitz and runs for three seasons, taking Graba through the core of his development years at the club's youth setup in the Upper Galilee.

The move caps a strong campaign for Graba in Haifa's colours. He made 27 appearances for Maccabi Haifa's U-17 side last season, starting 18 of them, and scored seven goals while contributing several assists as the team finished fourth in its division, ONE said.

Graba's path to Haifa's academy ran through Beitar Haifa and MK Nahalal before he was picked up by one of Israel's flagship youth programmes. The switch north to Kiryat Shmona is designed, per the report, to give him a clearer route toward first-team football rather than simply a bigger name on his CV.
He joins a youth department run by Omer Levinson, who is beginning his fifth consecutive season in charge of Kiryat Shmona's academy sides.

Those age-group teams have had an unusual few years: ONE noted that Kiryat Shmona's youth squads avoided relegation in three separate seasons because of disruption to the league caused by the war, a reminder of how deeply the conflict has touched even grassroots competition in the north.

For now, Graba's move is a bet on development rather than an immediate first-team story — but Kiryat Shmona's academy has fed players up before, and the club will hope his scoring form from Haifa's U-17s travels with him.

title: Maccabi Haifa favourites to end winless start against Ironi Kiryat Shmona
dek: Bookmakers make Haifa clear favourites for Tuesday's Toto Cup group game in Netanya, with the club still chasing its first win of preseason after an opening derby defeat.

verificationSources.label: Sport1/Maariv — Hapoel Haifa beat Maccabi Haifa 3-2 in the derby

body: Maccabi Haifa go in search of their first win of preseason on Tuesday evening, installed as clear favourites by Israeli bookmakers for a Toto Cup group game against Ironi Kiryat Shmona, with kick-off set for 20:00 in Netanya.

According to ONE, punters make Haifa 1.5 to win the match outright, with a Kiryat Shmona victory paying 4.1 and a draw priced at 3.75 — odds that reflect Haifa's standing as one of Ligat Ha'al's traditional heavyweights even before the new league season has begun.

The stakes are more than academic. ONE reports that anything short of victory would complicate Haifa's progress in their Toto Cup group and add unwanted pressure on the squad just weeks before the 2026/27 league campaign kicks off.

The concern traces back to the opening round of the competition, when Haifa were beaten 3-2 by city rivals Hapoel Haifa in the Haifa derby — a result that leaves them still hunting a first competitive win of the preseason. Sport1 reported that Yaad Gonen was among the scorers for the winning side.

Ironi Kiryat Shmona take the nominal home role for Tuesday's fixture despite the match being staged in Netanya rather than at their own ground. Little has been reported publicly about their own preparations, but a club fighting for results in Ligat Ha'al will see an under-strength Haifa as a rare chance to cause an upset.

For Barak Bakhar's squad, the fixture is really about rhythm and confidence rather than the Toto Cup table itself — a chance to erase the sour taste of the derby defeat and arrive at the start of the league season with some momentum behind them.
Kick-off in Netanya is at 20:00 on Tuesday.

title: Elias signing at Hapoel Haifa was a joint call with players, says owner Katz
dek: Yoav Katz says the squad had a say in landing the pricey midfielder from Hapoel Be'er Sheva, while staying coy on the club's captain and on Yaad Gonen's murky registration card.

verificationSources.label: ONE - on Yaad Gonen's registration card

body: Hapoel Haifa's decision to break the bank for Shay Elias this summer was not made by the coaching staff alone, owner Yoav Katz has revealed, in a wide-ranging interview in which he confirmed that squad members were consulted before the club committed to the midfielder.

Elias, 27, joined Haifa this close season after leaving Hapoel Be'er Sheva, where his four-year contract had run its course. A product of the Hapoel Tel Aviv academy, he had also been linked with interest from Beitar Jerusalem before opting for the move north.

The size of the outlay surprised plenty of observers around the league, and Katz did not shy away from explaining how the call was reached. "This was a shared decision, not only with the professional staff, but also with players who took part in making it," he said.
"We don't usually dismiss the opinions of our players," Katz added. "In this case there were players we consulted with, and it ended up being a joint decision."

Pressed on whether the club's captain specifically had been part of those conversations, Katz stopped short of confirming it directly. "I've already said too much," he replied, declining to elaborate further.

The comments came as Hapoel Haifa wind down preparations for the new Ligat Ha'al season, days after producing a comeback 3-2 win over city rivals Maccabi Haifa in a preseason derby, with teenage forward Yaad Gonen among the scorers.

Gonen's name also surfaced elsewhere in the interview, this time on a more sensitive subject: the ownership of his registration card. Katz was confronted with documentation, reportedly dated August 2024, showing that Hapoel Akko holds roughly 35 percent of the financial rights to any future sale of the young forward.

Katz was notably guarded when asked to clarify the arrangement. "I need to check that, I'm not sure you're right," he said, before adding that Hapoel Tel Aviv had approached the club about buying into Gonen's card some two years earlier. "I don't want to get into details I'm not familiar with right now," he said.

Between the Elias transfer and the questions over Gonen's future, the interview offered a rare glimpse into how collaboratively — and how cagily — Katz is willing to operate as Hapoel Haifa build a squad they hope can push near the top of the table this season.

title: Bucharest hotel greets Beitar fans in Hebrew ahead of Larnaca return leg
dek: The Radisson Blu handed hundreds of travelling supporters a Hebrew-language house-rules notice as Beitar Jerusalem prepare to host AEK Larnaca "at home" in Romania.
body: Beitar Jerusalem's travelling support got an unusually warm welcome on arrival in Bucharest this week: a printed note, in Hebrew, from hotel management asking politely for good behaviour rather than the usual generic house rules.

The Radisson Blu, where hundreds of Beitar fans are staying ahead of Thursday's Conference League second qualifying round return leg against AEK Larnaca, greeted guests with the line: "Dear Beitar supporters, we are happy to host you again with us. Please honour us with basic procedures," ONE reports.

Because Beitar cannot stage European fixtures at home in Israel, the club is again hosting a continental tie on Romanian soil, this time at Stadionul Ilie Oană in Ploiești, roughly an hour's drive from the capital, with kick-off set for 20:30 on Thursday.

Beitar arrive with the tie firmly in their favour. They won the first leg in Larnaca 1-0 last week, Brayan Carabali settling it with a 77th-minute free-kick after AEK defender Mike van der Hoorn was sent off, according to ESPN's match report.

More than 3,000 Beitar supporters are expected to make the trip to Romania for the second leg, ONE has reported separately, underlining how the club's away-from-home "home" games have become a mass pilgrimage for its fan base.

The Radisson Blu's note laid out a fairly standard set of expectations for a large group booking: no noise from fans between midnight and 5am, no flags hung from windows, no outside food brought into the lobby, no smoking or drug use in rooms, no stickers on the walls, and no pyrotechnics anywhere on hotel grounds.
It closed on a notably friendly note, signing off with: "We love and wish success to Beitar and the State of Israel," per ONE's report.

The tone stands in contrast to the mood around the first leg, when Romanian police issued fans a formal warning that using pyrotechnic devices is illegal under Romanian law and can lead to arrest, Ynet reported ahead of that trip.
For a club now well used to shuttling its biggest European nights between Cyprus, Serbia and Romania, a hotel simply asking nicely counts as a good day.

title: League chair defends women's basketball funding, points to college exodus as the real distortion
dek: Dana Sander, who chairs the Women's Basketball Premier League management, tells ONE that state funding per point is equal to the men's game, and blames a US college pipeline for driving up wages for a shrinking pool of eligible young Israeli players.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Israeli-player budget breakdown by club
Walla Sport - Sander appointed league chair

body: Dana Sander, who chairs the management of Israel's Women's Basketball Premier League, pushed back this week against criticism that state sports funding unfairly favours the women's game, telling ONE's "Today's Conversation" programme that the real distortion in Israeli basketball economics has nothing to do with federation bias and everything to do with American colleges.

Her comments were a direct response to ONE's own reporting on the government's "Israeli player" incentive scheme, which showed women's top-flight basketball clubs are set to receive an average of roughly NIS 1.989 million each in 2026 - on paper more than men's Premier League clubs or top-tier women's soccer sides draw from the same pot.

Sander rejected the idea that this makes the system unequal. "The amount per point is identical for men and for women," she said, arguing the women's game's total allocation looks large mainly because it has grown fastest: she described a "dramatic increase" for women's basketball, against what she put at roughly a 20 percent rise for the men's game, alongside a substantial boost for women's soccer over the same period.

The real reason her sport's numbers stand out, she said, is that the Sports Ministry attaches far stricter conditions to women's basketball funding than to any other funded team sport. To draw full support, clubs must field at least five Israeli-eligible players under 26 and two under 22 - quotas that men's basketball teams, and every other funded discipline, do not face. "No other team sport demands more conditions of women than of men," she said, singling out basketball as the exception.

It is that quota system, Sander argued, that produces the actual distortion referenced in the interview's headline - and its root cause, in her account, sits 9,000 kilometres away on American campuses. She said roughly 14 young Israeli players leave every year for US college basketball scholarships, chasing deals she put at $200,000-$300,000 net over the life of a contract - money no domestic club can come close to matching.

That annual exodus shrinks the pool of Israeli-eligible prospects each summer, just as clubs are required to fill age-banded roster slots to qualify for their funding. The result, by her telling, is bidding wars among Israeli clubs for a handful of young players who choose to stay - a straightforward supply-and-demand squeeze on wages, not a funding formula skewed against men.

As examples of clubs operating under identical terms, Sander pointed to Maccabi Ra'anana and Bnei Herzliya, two Premier League sides she said received equal allocations under the current scheme, and noted that Israel currently has two women's clubs competing in European competition - evidence, in her view, that the league's investment is translating into on-court results rather than simply inflating budgets.

Sander took over as volunteer chair of the league's management in 2024, succeeding Hila Kanister Bar David after a five-year tenure. A former basketball player herself and now chief executive of the real-estate finance firm Arno Capital, she has repeatedly framed her mandate in personal terms, saying she took the unpaid role out of love for the sport and a determination to restore the league to what she has called its "glory days."

The funding debate is unlikely to end with one interview. ONE's reporting on the Israeli-player budget breakdown triggered the criticism Sander was answering, and with the Sports Ministry's criteria under renewed scrutiny across multiple sports, her defence of basketball's quota system sets up a rematch the next time budget figures are published.

title: Coach says the NBA is a real option for Israel prodigy David Musis
dek: Nadav Zilberstein made the claim after the 18-year-old center starred in Israel's stunning overtime win over Greece at the U18 EuroBasket in Italy.

verificationSources.label: FIBA — Aronov, Musis lead Israel shock over Greece

body: A day after David Musis powered Israel's under-18 team past Greece in overtime, his national coach went further than the box score — saying the raw, fast-improving 18-year-old could eventually make it all the way to the NBA.

"With the right decisions at each stage, even the NBA is an option for him," Nadav Zilberstein told ONE, describing Musis as a player capable of reaching "the highest levels" of the sport if his development is handled correctly.

The praise came on the back of a genuine statement game. Israel erased a nine-point deficit in the final 90 seconds of regulation to force overtime against Greece at the FIBA U18 EuroBasket in Trentino, Italy, eventually winning 93-84. Musis finished with 26 points, 19 rebounds, four three-pointers and three blocks, with teammate Aviv Aronov adding 30 points in the win.

Musis is an unusual physical proposition even by the standards of a competition built around teenage prospects: a 2.10-metre center who has added a genuine three-point shot to his game in only a few years of serious basketball. He grew up in Holon, starting out in soccer before switching codes, and came up through Hapoel Holon's youth ranks before a move three years ago to Ramat Hasharon, where his rapid improvement caught the attention of national team scouts.

That trajectory has already translated into a college commitment: Musis has verbally committed to Florida Atlantic University, an NCAA Division I program that reached the Final Four in 2023, as he weighs a path that could take him through American college basketball before any professional decision.

Zilberstein, who is coaching the youth national team through the tournament, called the current group "a very special team" that is "very athletic" compared with previous Israeli age-group sides, pointing to size and talent across the roster as reasons for optimism — with Musis singled out as the standout among them.

Israel closed the group phase with a 3-0 record and now moves into the knockout rounds, where they are set to face Denmark on July 29. The tournament in Trentino and Rovereto is the inaugural edition of the FIBA U18 EuroBasket, running from July 25 to August 2 with reigning champions Spain and hosts Italy also in the field.

For a program that has produced NBA talent in recent years, a teenage center already drawing NBA comparisons from his own coach — however early and heavily caveated — is the kind of story Israeli basketball will want to keep following through the rest of the tournament.
