title: Kibedy Gordon wants more GFN nights — but admits the pressure is intense
dek: The kickboxer, who knocked out his opponent alongside winning brothers Ahavat and Ruach on a landmark Tel Aviv card, says he is now eyeing a UFC contract.

verificationSources.label: MMAmania — Lineker loses GFN 1 main event
Ynetnews — Natan Levy on GFN card

body: A day after headlining the biggest Muay Thai and kickboxing show ever staged in Israel, Kibedy Gordon sat down with ONE's Shichat HaYom programme and admitted the night brought him more nerves than any fight of his own career.

"We want [more events], but it's stressful," Gordon said, reflecting on GFN 1: Israel vs. The World, the promotion he and his two brothers built and headlined on Monday night at the Menora Mivtachim Arena in Tel Aviv.

The show was fronted by a triple main event featuring all three Gordon brothers on the same card for the first time. Ahavat Gordon beat former UFC bantamweight contender John Lineker by unanimous decision in the marquee Muay Thai bout, while Ruach Gordon defeated Maximus Bejenuta and Kibedy himself stopped Jose Alberto Quiñonez by knockout in under a minute.

Kibedy told ONE that fighting himself is one kind of pressure, but watching his younger brothers compete is another matter entirely. "When I fight, the pressure is on me. This time the pressure was tripled, because of my brothers," he said, adding that seeing them in the ring was harder to sit through than stepping into it himself.

Despite the toll, he said the family has no intention of stopping at one show. Asked about his own future, Gordon pointed beyond the promotion he co-founded. "I'm aiming for UFC, and as for my brothers — maybe one of them gets an offer from one of the major leagues too," he said.
Ahavat Gordon, fresh off beating Lineker, is due to marry soon, according to the report — a rare piece of good news timed for right after the biggest win of his career.

The Gordon brothers organised GFN in partnership with Yaniv Kaminski, pitching it as an "Israel vs. the World" showcase and drawing international names, including Lineker and Quiñonez, to fight in Tel Aviv. Also on the card was Israeli UFC veteran Natan Levy, who fought American Lando Vannata in a kickboxing bout.
ONE reports the family is already planning to bring the promotion back, with the next major GFN event expected within a few months.

title: Maccabi Herzliya sign striker Emmanuel Apeh, goalkeeper Sean Ben Nesher set to return
dek: The Liga Leumit club has moved to rebuild its attack and its goalkeeping department ahead of the new season, with a young forward also heading out on loan to Hapoel Kfar Kassem.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Ben Nesher's move to Hapoel Tel Aviv

body: Maccabi Herzliya are reshaping their squad for the coming Liga Leumit season, and ONE reports the club has completed the signing of Nigerian forward Emmanuel Apeh, who returns to Israeli football for a second stint after a brief spell at M.S. Kiryat Yam.

Apeh, 29, spent last season with Kiryat Yam, where he scored three goals, following a well-travelled career that took him through the Spanish lower divisions with clubs including Alcalá, Lorca and Celta Vigo's reserves, before spells in Azerbaijan and with Al Ittihad Alexandria in Egypt. His move to Herzliya was brokered through agent Yaron Barnes, according to the report.

The more eye-catching piece of business, however, is between the posts. ONE reports that goalkeeper Sean Ben Nesher is set to return to Herzliya after a season on loan at Hapoel Tel Aviv, where he served as third-choice keeper behind the club's senior options and saw little first-team action.

Ben Nesher, still only 20, came up through Maccabi Haifa's youth ranks before moving on to Hapoel Akko and then Herzliya, where he spent two seasons establishing himself as a regular before signing with Hapoel Tel Aviv alongside fellow youngster Itay Shavit. According to the report, the goalkeeper opted to return to Herzliya in search of genuine playing time as a No. 2, rather than remain a bit-part figure in Tel Aviv.

Herzliya have also brought in a second goalkeeper, Matan Zalmanovich, to fill the void left by Tal Bomstein, who is taking a break from football, ONE reports. Zalmanovich joins after three years with Ironi Kiryat Shmona and has previous top-flight experience with Nes Ziona and Hapoel Kfar Kassem; his move was arranged through agent Noam Markowitz.

Elsewhere in the same report, Hapoel Kfar Kassem have loaned in 18-year-old forward Ravid Ulitzky from Hapoel Tel Aviv's youth system. Ulitzky scored 11 league goals in the youth ranks last season, including what ONE describes as a hat-trick winner in a derby, and will now be reunited with Shahar Wizinger, his former youth coach, at Kfar Kassem. The move was arranged through agent Adam Kidan.

None of the deals carry reported contract lengths or fees, and Liga Leumit clubs typically finalise this kind of squad business through the closing weeks of the summer. Herzliya finished last season needing a promotion-relegation playoff to preserve their second-tier status, drawing 1-1 with Hapoel Kfar Saba in that decider, so both goalkeeping depth and fresh attacking options will be closely watched heading into the new campaign.

title: Maccabi Haifa were not complacent, just unprepared, and Bachar erred, says ONE pundit
dek: Analyst Nissan Kaniyas says Barak Bachar's tactical setup cost Maccabi Haifa in a 3-2 Toto Cup defeat to Hapoel Haifa, the neighbours' first win over their rivals in the competition since 1997.
body: Maccabi Haifa's pre-season derby against Hapoel Haifa was meant to be a low-stakes runout. Instead, at Sammy Ofer Stadium on Saturday, it turned into an old wound reopened: Hapoel Haifa raced into a three-goal lead, survived a spirited late Maccabi rally, and held on to win 3-2 - their first victory over their city rivals in the Toto Cup since 1997.

The result matters little in the standings; the Toto Cup is a pre-season tournament that decides seeding rather than titles. But the manner of the defeat was enough to dominate the conversation on ONE's Sicha Hayom program, where commentator Nissan Kaniyas offered a blunt verdict on coach Barak Bachar's afternoon: Maccabi Haifa did not underestimate their neighbours, he argued, but they were nowhere near ready for them.

Hapoel Haifa, coached by Chaim Silvas, took the lead in the 30th minute when Yoad Gonen struck from around 20 metres. Three minutes later a Hapoel cross was turned into his own net by young Maccabi defender Noam Steinman, and the hosts looked to be cruising. Alon Torgeman then curled home a free-kick early in the second half to make it 3-0 in the 58th minute, despite a double substitution Bachar had made at the interval.

Maccabi Haifa found a response only after falling three behind. Iad Khalili headed one back in the 75th minute and Etan Azoulay rifled in a long-range effort four minutes later to make it 3-2, but the comeback ran out of time and Hapoel Haifa held on for a historic win.

According to Kaniyas, the damage was done long before the second-half goal that put the game out of reach. He said Bachar had erred in his set-up, deploying a 3-6-1 shape without the personnel to make it work, and suggested a conventional back four would have served the team better against a Hapoel Haifa side that pressed with intent from the first whistle.

"In every lineup Barak puts out, he wants to win - he just didn't anticipate Silvas leading 0-3," Kaniyas said on air, framing the defeat less as complacency than as a coach caught out by his own team's lack of readiness three goals down inside 33 minutes.

The broader concern raised on the program was squad depth rather than a single afternoon's team selection. Kaniyas flagged gaps at right-back and in central midfield as areas Maccabi Haifa still need to address before the league season begins, alongside the unresolved situation around Yonatan Levy's future at the club.

Bachar, who returned to Maccabi Haifa for a third spell in October 2025 after leading the club to three straight championships in an earlier stint, still has time to fix the issues before competitive football resumes. But a first Toto Cup loss to Hapoel Haifa in nearly three decades is the kind of result that will keep the pressure on him in the meantime.

title: João Pedro's nine-minute hat-trick gives Xabi Alonso a wild winning start at Chelsea
dek: The Brazilian struck three times in nine second-half minutes as Chelsea outlasted Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 in a chaotic pre-season friendly in Sydney.
body: Xabi Alonso's first match in the Chelsea dugout turned into a ten-goal fairground ride, and it took a nine-minute hat-trick from substitute João Pedro to spare the new manager an opening-night embarrassment. Chelsea beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 at Accor Stadium in Sydney, in a pre-season friendly that swung five times before the Brazilian settled it late on.

It did not look like it would need rescuing early on. Chelsea led inside six minutes through Dastan Satpayev, only for the Australian side to hit back twice, through Anthony Pantazopoulos and then a second from Hammond, to turn the game around before half-time. Dario Essugo pulled Chelsea level again just before the break with a goal in the 38th minute.

The chaos continued after the interval. Jamie Gittens put Chelsea back in front in the 66th minute, but Western Sydney would not go away, replying through Dylan Scicluna and Awan Lual to leave the Premier League side trailing 4-3 with the clock running down.

That is when Alonso's half-time reshuffle paid off. The Spaniard had used the friendly to test a young, experimental XI before sending on a wave of first-team regulars, and among them was João Pedro, whose introduction changed the entire complexion of the match.

The Brazilian forward, signed from Brighton last year and one of Chelsea's most productive forwards through the second half of last season, scored three times inside nine minutes — in the 80th, 85th and 89th — to turn a 4-3 deficit into a 6-4 win and hand Alonso victory in his managerial bow.

ONE, reporting on the match from Israel, framed it as an evening of "plenty of praise for the attack, but no shortage of question marks for defense" — a fair summary of a game in which Chelsea's back line conceded four times in a glorified training exercise even as their forwards ran riot.

Alonso, who officially replaced Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge on 1 July, is using the pre-season tour of Australia to assess his squad depth before the new Premier League campaign, with Chelsea scheduled to play Tottenham Hotspur in their next tour fixture.

Results in pre-season friendlies count for little in the standings, but for a manager taking his first steps at a new club, an entertaining win — however scrappy defensively — is a far easier story to tell than a defeat, and João Pedro's burst of finishing gave Alonso exactly that.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva eye free-agent striker Marko Rakonjac
dek: The Montenegrin forward, released by Hapoel Jerusalem, is reported as a leading candidate to reinforce the newly promoted club's attack

verificationSources.label: One.co.il on Hapoel Jerusalem's earlier negotiations with Rakonjac

body: Maccabi Petah Tikva, back in the Israeli Premier League after a season in the second tier, are shopping the free-agent market for attacking reinforcements, and Sport5 reports that Montenegrin striker Marko Rakonjac has emerged as a leading candidate to join.

The 26-year-old centre-forward is currently without a club after leaving Hapoel Jerusalem, where he arrived in January and made 14 appearances, scoring twice as the capital side secured its top-flight status through the second half of the season.

Standing 1.91 metres, Rakonjac built his reputation in Serbia with Cukaricki before Lokomotiv Moscow signed him on a four-year contract in 2022. He never established himself in Russia and instead built a career largely out on loan.

Those loan spells took in Red Star Belgrade, where he featured as the club won the domestic double, as well as Serbian side TSC and Hungary's Diosgyor, before a spell with OFI Crete in Greece preceded his move to Israel.
He has a single senior cap for Montenegro, won in 2022, to go with earlier appearances for the country's under-17, under-19 and under-21 sides.

According to Sport5, Rakonjac is not the only forward on Maccabi Petah Tikva's radar. The club is also said to be finalising a season-long loan for Yoav Koren, who already joined the squad's training camp, with an agreement reportedly in place between the two clubs.

Koren scored eight goals across all competitions last season for Hapoel Kfar Sava in the National League and would add depth to a Petah Tikva squad being rebuilt under manager Avi Luzon for the step back up to the top flight.

Nothing has been signed with Rakonjac, and Sport5's report describes him only as a candidate under consideration rather than a completed deal — a distinction worth keeping in mind as Petah Tikva continue to build their squad for the new season.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem's 16-year-old defender leans towards Ukraine over Israel
dek: Michael Vakselmen holds dual citizenship, and his father says a Ukraine call-up would be an easy choice — even as Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Be'er Sheva and Beitar Jerusalem circle the teenager.
body: Hapoel Jerusalem believe they have a defender worth fighting for on their books — the trouble is that the country he may end up representing isn't Israel. Sport5 reports that 16-year-old Michael Vakselmen, four years into his development at the club, is being pulled toward Ukraine's national team rather than Israel's, and his family sounds in no hurry to talk him out of it.

Vakselmen holds both Israeli and Ukrainian citizenship, a legacy of family roots that gave him the option of a second flag from birth. According to Sport5, that dual status has now turned into a genuine recruitment question, with Ukrainian interest emerging alongside the usual chase from Israeli clubs.

His father, Rostislav Vakselmen, left little doubt about where his son's heart lies when he spoke to the outlet. "When an offer comes to play for Ukraine's national team, it won't be a question at all — he will play for it," he said.

The teenager plays left-footed centre-back, and his father's description of him to Sport5 leaned on some heavyweight comparisons: a defender in the mould of Virgil van Dijk and Fabio Coentrão, praised for his tactical reading of the game and a passing range the family put at around 40 metres. Those are a parent's words, not an independent scouting verdict, but they capture the scale of the buzz building around a player still four years short of senior football.

That buzz has not gone unnoticed inside Israel. Sport5 reports that Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Be'er Sheva and Beitar Jerusalem have all shown interest in signing Vakselmen away from Hapoel Jerusalem, and that Israel's national team setup has also been keeping tabs on him with an eye toward a future call-up.

The interest doesn't stop at Israel's borders. According to the report, clubs from Spain's top flight made attempts to recruit him earlier this year — a sign that his profile is being tracked well beyond the local game.

For now, Hapoel Jerusalem's response is to try to lock him down rather than risk losing him for nothing. Sport5 says the club is preparing a new contract aimed at keeping Vakselmen in Jerusalem rather than releasing him to a rival suitor.

Dual-nationality cases like this are not unusual in Israeli football, where waves of immigration from the former Soviet Union have left plenty of young players eligible for a second national team. What makes Vakselmen's case notable is how openly the family is signalling a preference for Ukraine at such an early stage — long before any formal approach from either federation has been confirmed.

Nothing here is decided. No call-up, contract offer or federation approach has been made official, and a 16-year-old's path can shift many times before a senior debut for anyone. But the early positioning, as laid out by Sport5, suggests Hapoel Jerusalem may be developing a defender for someone else's national team.

title: Lewandowski's Barcelona gamble cost him €200 million, agent Pini Zahavi reveals
dek: The Polish striker turned down a lucrative Saudi offer to wait for a Barcelona renewal that never came, before eventually joining Chicago Fire in MLS.
body: Robert Lewandowski's gamble to hold out for a new Barcelona contract instead of banking a fortune in Saudi Arabia ended up costing him roughly €200 million, according to his long-time agent Pini Zahavi, who has now laid out the financial fallout from one of this year's most dramatic transfer sagas.

Zahavi said Lewandowski turned down a two-year Saudi offer worth around €100 million a season back in January 2026, choosing instead to keep faith with Barcelona even as his contract in Catalonia ticked down toward its June expiry.

"I told him he would not get this offer in summer, but he decided to wait," Zahavi said, according to ONE. Asked why the striker refused such a fortune, the agent was blunt: "Because he wanted to play at Barcelona."

That loyalty was not rewarded. Zahavi said club president Joan Laporta was in favour of keeping Lewandowski for a further season, but sporting director Deco and head coach Hansi Flick would not commit to guaranteeing him a starting role — a condition the 37-year-old considered essential before signing on.

With Barcelona unwilling to renew, Zahavi shopped his client around Europe. Milan and Juventus both made contact, but according to the agent neither Italian giant could match the financial terms Lewandowski was seeking. Porto went further still: club president André Villas-Boas personally phoned the striker to try to bring him to Portugal, only to be turned down.

None of it led anywhere, and Lewandowski left Barcelona as a free agent when his contract expired at the end of June. He eventually found his next chapter far from Europe, agreeing a two-year deal with Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer that runs through the 2027-28 season.
The move made him a Designated Player in MLS, with multiple reports placing his salary among the highest in the league, behind only Inter Miami's Lionel Messi.

Zahavi, the veteran Israeli super-agent who has brokered some of football's biggest deals over four decades, was speaking publicly for the first time about the collapsed Barcelona renewal, filling in a saga that had puzzled observers of the Polish striker's abrupt exit.

For Barcelona, the episode leaves an awkward footnote to Lewandowski's four seasons at the club, in which he won three La Liga titles and a Copa del Rey and twice topped the division's scoring charts, only to leave for nothing once his contract lapsed.

title: The teenager chasing Ronaldo's shoes at the Bernabéu carries a private tragedy behind him
dek: Yan Diomande has gone from an unnoticed Leganés debutant to a €100m-plus Real Madrid target in little over a year, but ONE reports the Ivorian winger's rise is shadowed by the death of his 15-year-old sister, Roxane.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הטרגדיה של דיומנדה שרוצה להיכנס לנעלי רונאלדו
ESPN - Real Madrid set to sign Yan Diomande in €135M deal

body: Real Madrid are closing in on the signing of Yan Diomande, the 19-year-old RB Leipzig winger, in a deal reported by ONE to be worth well over €100 million — a staggering fee for a player who, barely 18 months ago, was going largely unnoticed in Spain's second division.

ONE reports Leipzig have been holding out for around €120 million while Madrid's opening offer sat closer to €110 million, with the gap expected to close soon. Other outlets, including ESPN, have put the total package as high as €135 million including add-ons once terms are finalised — a reminder that the exact figure is still being negotiated rather than confirmed.

The rise has been dizzying. Diomande made his professional debut for Leganés in March 2025 — against Real Madrid, of all sides — and barely registered. Leipzig plucked him from the Spanish second tier for around €20 million after only a handful of appearances, a bet sporting director Marcel Schäfer said would eventually be repaid many times over. He was right within a year rather than the several he predicted.

In his first full Bundesliga season, Diomande scored 12 goals and added eight assists in 33 appearances as Leipzig secured Champions League qualification, form that earned him the league's Young Player of the Season award. Two-footed and explosively quick, he draws comparisons to Ousmane Dembélé; friends nicknamed him "Roberto Carlos" back home for the power of his shot.

He then took that form to the World Cup, becoming the youngest player ever to represent Côte d'Ivoire at the tournament. He played the full 90 minutes in a 1-0 win over Ecuador, set up a goal in a 2-1 loss to Germany, and teed up Nicolas Pépé for the winner against Curaçao that sent the Ivorians through to the round of 32.

The Leganés route to the top has echoes of Samuel Eto'o, who was loaned to the same club by Real Madrid decades ago before becoming a Barcelona great — folklore Spanish scouts like to point to when a Leganés discovery breaks through. ONE frames Diomande's ambition in similarly outsized terms: not simply joining Real Madrid, but hoping to walk the same path to greatness that Cristiano Ronaldo carved out at the Bernabéu.

But the story ONE tells is not only about a transfer fee or a highlight reel. Weeks after that first senior appearance for Leganés, Diomande received a phone call from Côte d'Ivoire: his younger sister, Roxane, had died at 15 after her drink was spiked at a party.

He has written about the loss in an essay for The Players' Tribune titled "Dear Roxane," describing a numbness that has never fully lifted. "I feel nothing anymore," he wrote. "Like I'm not even human. Since your death, I'm empty."

Roxane, according to his account, was one of the few people who believed unconditionally in his talent during the years he was overlooked by academies and clubs. Diomande says he now dedicates every appearance to her memory, carrying forward a belief in him that she held before almost anyone else did.

As he stands on the brink of a move that would make him one of the most expensive teenagers in football history, the two threads of his story — a generational talent arriving at the world's grandest club, and a young man still processing an unimaginable loss — remain, as ONE's report makes clear, impossible to separate.
facts: Yan Diomande is a 19-year-old Ivorian winger (born November 14, 2006, in Abidjan) currently at RB Leipzig.

ONE reports Real Madrid and Leipzig are negotiating a transfer fee reported between roughly €110-120 million, with other outlets citing packages up to €135 million with add-ons — the final figure is not yet confirmed.

Diomande moved from Leganés to Leipzig for around €20 million in 2025 after only a handful of appearances, and was named the Bundesliga's Young Player of the Season after recording 12 goals and eight assists in 33 games.
He became the youngest player ever to represent Côte d'Ivoire at a World Cup, helping the team reach the round of 32 at the 2026 tournament.
His 15-year-old sister, Roxane, died after her drink was spiked at a party, weeks after his professional debut for Leganés in 2025.
Diomande wrote about his grief in a Players' Tribune essay titled 'Dear Roxane,' and says he dedicates his career to her memory.

title: Tiberias lawyer says IFA spokesman is announcing the verdict before the hearing
dek: Kobi Levi has fired off a warning letter accusing Shlomi Barzel of pre-judging the club's fate in the banned infusions case, days before the disciplinary tribunal convenes.
body: Ironi Tiberias's legal team has turned its fire on the Israel Football Association's own spokesman, accusing him of deciding the club's guilt in public before a single witness has been heard.

In a warning letter to the IFA, attorney Kobi Levi said Shlomi Barzel's comments on the ONE programme "Sicha Hayom" crossed a line a spokesman should never cross. "He's not acting as a spokesman, he's stating what the final result will be," Levi said, arguing Barzel effectively told viewers the outcome before the disciplinary tribunal has convened.

Levi also took aim at the wording of the indictment itself, calling it "a big joke," and objected to Barzel's on-air description of Tiberias as an organisation "protecting its own soldiers" — language he says paints the club as guilty while the case is still open.

The dispute is the latest flashpoint in what has become one of Israeli football's most damaging institutional cases this year: the so-called infusions affair, in which the IFA has indicted Tiberias officials over banned intravenous treatments given to players.

According to the indictment, club staff administered saline infusions above the permitted volume — more than 100ml — to several players ahead of a lower-table playoff match against Ashdod last season, in breach of the association's anti-doping rules.

Those charged include head coach Eliran Hodeda, technical director Chen Sol, team manager Gabriel Cohen, fitness coach Shlomi Vaderro, staff member Aviv Jibli and the club's suspended owner, Miki Bitan. Prosecutors are seeking suspensions ranging from six years to lifetime bans.

Tiberias has firmly rejected the allegations, insisting the saline infusions were within the permitted volume and administered under proper professional supervision — and it is that gap between the club's account and the association's case that Levi says Barzel is not entitled to close for the public in advance.

The IFA's prosecutor in the case, Aryeh Kalmenson, has indicated there will be no plea deal, setting up a full contested hearing. That hearing is scheduled for next week, and Levi's letter is widely read in Tel Aviv as an attempt to get the tribunal — and public opinion — to treat the process as still open.

Barzel, a former Haaretz sports editor who has run the IFA's communications since 2013, has become a frequent and outspoken voice on the case in Israeli sports media. Whether the association responds formally to Levi's complaint, or lets Barzel's comments stand, will say much about how seriously it treats the appearance of prejudgment in a case it is itself prosecuting.

title: Bnei Herzliya chief hits back: 'We took a title from the big Maccabi, something Hapoel couldn't do'
dek: Chairman Eldad Akonis defends his club's standing against a Maccabi Tel Aviv dig, pointing to a State Cup and a rare playoff upset, as a bitter fight over rules for naturalized players rumbles on.

verificationSources.label: Kan - Bnei Herzliya eliminate Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2022 playoff semifinal
Walla Sport - Kadin Carrington naturalization background

body: Eldad Akonis does not do quiet diplomacy, and he was not about to let a dig from Maccabi Tel Aviv pass without an answer. Told that a Maccabi figure had brushed off Bnei Herzliya as "the small Maccabi," the Herzliya chairman produced his receipts.

The jab came from Ofer Yanai, a senior figure in the Maccabi Tel Aviv basketball set-up, amid a wider row over how Israeli basketball naturalizes foreign-born players. Akonis was not going to let the insult sit, and used it to relitigate his club's place in the domestic pecking order.
His first exhibit was February 2022, when Bnei Herzliya beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 87-82 in the State Cup final to lift the trophy for just the second time in the club's history.

The second, and the one Akonis leaned on hardest, came four months later: Bnei Herzliya eliminated the reigning champions, Maccabi Tel Aviv, 2-1 in a best-of-five playoff semifinal, a series capped by a 96-74 rout. It sent the small club from Herzliya into a championship final for the first time ever - and did so against a Maccabi side that had lost a playoff series only rarely in three decades.

"When people talk about big and small, success isn't only measured by budget," Akonis argued, framing that playoff run as proof his club had done something even Hapoel, Israeli basketball's other historic power, has almost never managed against Maccabi.

From there the conversation turned to the issue that actually prompted it: the increasingly heated argument over naturalized players in Israeli basketball. Akonis wants a rule forcing any player who takes Israeli citizenship to spend two full seasons proving himself before he can play for a club as an Israeli - rather than immediately filling a domestic roster spot.

The proposal is a direct response to the naturalization of Hapoel Jerusalem guard Kadin Carrington for the Israeli national team, a process that dragged on for close to a year and was pushed through without full consensus among the clubs. In its wake, the Israel Basketball Association agreed a committee would vet the identity of the next player put forward for citizenship.

Akonis pointed to Danny Wolf - the Brooklyn Nets' 2025 draft pick who also plays for Israel as a naturalized international - as the standard he wants the system to protect. "We have the best naturalized player in the world," he said, arguing that a proper naturalization process should produce players of that calibre rather than a shortcut for league rosters.

Not everyone on the board agrees. Association chairman Amos Frischman has pushed back on Akonis's call to tighten the rules further, leaving the two men - and their clubs - on opposite sides of a dispute that looks far from resolved as the new season approaches.

title: Uefa moves to scale back VAR and hand authority back to referees
dek: Europe's 55 football associations have signed off on a shake-up that limits video review to clear and obvious errors, ONE reports, as the confederation looks to speed up matches and cut down on marginal interventions from next season.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports — Uefa refereeing chief issues VAR warning
ESPN — VAR risks becoming too microscopic, says Uefa referee chief
UEFA Convention on Referee Education and Organisation 2026 (PDF)

body: Uefa is preparing to loosen the leash on VAR. According to a report by ONE, the governing body and all 55 of its member associations have agreed to a package of refereeing reforms for the 2026/27 season that will restrict video review to "clear and obvious errors" and hand more trust back to referees on the pitch.

The plan, as described by ONE, instructs video assistants to intervene only when the on-field referee has clearly missed a serious incident or made an obvious mistake — not to re-examine marginal or subjective calls that were reasonable in real time. Reviews themselves are also meant to be shortened, on the logic that a long, drawn-out check is itself a sign the original decision was not a clear error to begin with.

ONE reports the reforms are due to apply across all of Uefa's domestic and international competitions from next season, with referees expected to apply the criteria consistently across the Champions League, Europa League, Conference League and national-team fixtures alike.

The push lines up with public comments in recent months from Roberto Rosetti, Uefa's director of refereeing, who has repeatedly warned that VAR has drifted from its original purpose. "We forgot the reason why VAR was introduced. We forgot a little bit. Everywhere," Rosetti has said, arguing that technology works well for factual calls like offside but becomes counterproductive when used to second-guess subjective judgment calls.

Rosetti has also cautioned against what he called "microscopic VAR intervention" — video officials picking apart incidents frame by frame in search of fouls or handballs that would never have been given without the benefit of slow-motion replay, frustrating supporters who feel matches are being re-refereed from the video room.

ONE ties the reform effort to fallout from this summer's World Cup, citing a disallowed goal for Iran and a VAR-awarded penalty for Belgium among the flashpoints that intensified scrutiny of how intrusive video review has become at the top level of the game.

Beyond VAR itself, ONE reports the package includes measures aimed at increasing effective playing time — reformed procedures around goal kicks, throw-ins, substitutions and injury stoppages designed to cut down on time-wasting — plus an expanded captain-referee communication protocol modelled on the one trialled at Euro 2024, intended to reduce mass protests and improve dialogue on the pitch.

Uefa's own referee convention framework, which all 55 associations sign up to, already enshrines the principle that VAR should communicate replay information "only in relation to clear and obvious errors or serious missed incidents" — the standard ONE says will now be applied more strictly in practice from 2026/27.

Uefa has not yet published a formal statement detailing the full reform package, and it remains to be seen how the tighter threshold will be codified for match officials in day-to-day protocol documents. The broader direction, though, fits a governing body increasingly uneasy with how far video review has been allowed to reach into subjective refereeing calls.

body: Amid the knockouts and judges' scorecards that made GFN 1: Israel vs. the World a landmark night for the Gordon brothers' new promotion, one bout on the Menora Mivtachim Arena card carried a different kind of weight entirely.

Major Dor Gabay of the Golani reconnaissance unit stepped through the ropes for an exhibition bout against Russian fighter Aleksei Shardanov, dedicated to IDF soldiers wounded in the war. Gabay was discharged from hospital only three and a half weeks before the event, ONE reports.

He was wounded on May 8, 2025, in Rafah, when an explosive device detonated during operations; a fellow soldier was killed in the same incident. Gabay, who has served 11 years in the IDF, has been undergoing rehabilitation at Sheba Medical Center since.

The bout was arranged with the help of Shagai Dobev, a rehabilitation coordinator who has worked with wounded soldiers since October 7, according to ONE. Dobev told the outlet the programme gave wounded troops a sense of purpose, a training camp and a reason to be up and working at seven in the morning rather than drifting through the day.
For Gabay, getting into the ring at all was the point. "I want all the wounded to see this and understand it's possible," he told ONE after the bout.

He said he carried the fight for a fallen friend, a soldier he named only as Yam, and described the atmosphere at the arena as electric. Far from satisfied with an exhibition outing, he said he is already looking past it: "Next time I want three rounds, a full fight without concessions."

The bout was tucked into a card built around the Gordon brothers themselves, with Ahavat Hashem Gordon beating former ONE Championship bantamweight champion John Lineker in the main event and Kibedy Gordon and Ruach Hashem Gordon also winning on the night. But for the wounded soldiers the event was dedicated to, Gabay's few minutes in the ring were the story that mattered most.

title: Bnei Sakhnin weigh move for free agent Rotem Hatuel
dek: The club is split over signing the former Hapoel Be'er Sheva favourite, but with the Israeli market short on proven forwards the option is being seriously examined, Sport5 reports.

verificationSources.label: Rotem Hatuel — Hebrew Wikipedia career record

body: Bnei Sakhnin are weighing a move for free-agent forward Rotem Hatuel as they fill out their squad for the 2026/27 season, Sport5 reports, though the club is understood to be split over whether the 28-year-old still has enough in the tank.

Hatuel built his name at Hapoel Be'er Sheva, where a five-year spell brought 27 goals in 107 appearances and a best campaign of 16 goals and three assists. He won the State Cup with the club in 2021/22 and the Israeli Supercup the following year, and earned his only Israel cap in a 2022 friendly against Malta.

The picture has since dimmed. Hatuel lost his place in Be'er Sheva once Ran Kojok took charge, and went out on loan first to Hapoel Tel Aviv and then, last season, to Hapoel Haifa, where he managed three goals and two assists in 26 league games. He is now on the market as a free agent.

According to Sport5, opinions inside Bnei Sakhnin are divided on whether to take a chance on him, but there is an acknowledgement that Israel's free-agent pool is thin on proven scoring options, and the club is said to be examining the move seriously ahead of the new campaign.

The Hatuel enquiry comes alongside other business at the club under manager Yossi Abukasis: forward Loai Halaf has officially joined Sakhnin, while the club is also weighing a return for Saher Tajji, sold to Beitar Jerusalem two years ago in a deal that included Ahmad Salman, after a difficult spell there.
For Hatuel, a move to Sakhnin would offer a route back to regular football after a year on the margins — and a chance to prove there is still substance behind the reputation he built in Be'er Sheva.

title: Maccabi Haifa weigh free move for Hapoel Petah Tikva goalkeeper Omer Katz

body: Maccabi Haifa have added a second name to their goalkeeping shortlist, according to a Sport5 report published Tuesday: Omer Katz, the 28-year-old who has guarded Hapoel Petah Tikva's net since the 2020/21 season.

Sport5's Yigal Goldstein reports that Haifa are looking at signing Katz without paying a transfer fee, framing him as a lower-cost route to strengthening the position between the posts. Petah Tikva, for their part, currently have no plans to let him leave.

The interest in Katz comes as Haifa's preferred target for the job, Maccabi Netanya's Omer Nireon, has stalled. According to the report, Netanya's financial demands for their 25-year-old goalkeeper have proven too steep, pushing Haifa to explore alternatives rather than wait the deal out.

Katz has made 176 appearances for Hapoel Petah Tikva since arriving in 2020, establishing himself as the club's first-choice goalkeeper through their climb back to the Israeli Premier League. He was named the National League's goalkeeper of the season during that promotion campaign.

His path there ran through several clubs. Katz came up through the Maccabi Herzliya academy before joining Maccabi Tel Aviv, where he spent time on the books between 2009 and 2017, and later played for Ramat Hasharon and Beitar Tel Aviv Ramlah before settling in Petah Tikva.

For now, this is a name being floated rather than a deal in motion — Sport5 frames it explicitly as a fallback plan, and Petah Tikva's resistance to releasing their No. 1 goalkeeper means any move would likely require Haifa to either sweeten the approach or wait out the transfer window.

Haifa's chase for a new goalkeeper option sits alongside a separate, ongoing story around Nireon, whom Ynet has also reported as a target — underlining how unsettled the position remains for the club this summer.

title: Who really stands to profit if Hapoel Haifa sell breakout star Yaad Gonen?
dek: A messy 2024 settlement with a former youth chief means Hapoel Haifa would keep only a slice of any transfer fee for their academy graduate
body: Yaad Gonen has become the name on everyone's lips in Haifa football after his derby-defining display for Hapoel Haifa, but ONE reports that any future sale of the 20-year-old would barely enrich the club that developed him.

According to the outlet, Gonen's contract runs through the end of next season, and his registration belongs to Hapoel Haifa. But the money that would flow from a transfer is a different story entirely: roughly 35 percent would go to Hapoel Haifa, another 35 percent to National League club Hapoel Akko, and around 30 percent to Gonen himself.

That three-way split traces back to an August 2024 settlement, ONE reports, struck between Hapoel Haifa owner Yoav Katz and Tzahi Nakash, the club's former youth academy director, to close out a long-running financial dispute between the two men. As part of that deal, a chunk of the economic rights to Gonen's future sale was signed over to Hapoel Akko.

The practical upshot, per the report, is that if Hapoel Haifa were to cash in on their academy product, the club that raised him would end up sharing top billing on the payout with a National League side that has no role in his development, while Gonen and Hapoel Akko would be the biggest beneficiaries rather than Hapoel Haifa.
Katz himself is quoted saying he has "already begun receiving inquiries" about Gonen, suggesting interest is building even before any formal move materialises.

The timing of the report is no accident. Gonen was one of the standout performers as Hapoel Haifa came from behind to beat Maccabi Haifa 3-2 in the Haifa derby, scoring from around 20 metres after being teed up by Ariel Mendy and also playing a part in the sequence that produced Noam Steipman's own goal.

It capped an emotionally loaded afternoon for the player: Gonen started out in Maccabi Haifa's youth system before switching across the city to Hapoel Haifa's academy at around age 12, and he punished his old club in front of a packed Sammy Ofer Stadium.

None of this means a sale is imminent — no club has yet made an offer, and the ownership split only becomes relevant if and when Hapoel Haifa actually agree a fee. For now it is a structural quirk hanging over one of Israeli football's most promising young talents just as his stock starts to rise.

title: Football clubs cry foul as sports ministry's 140m shekel 'Israeli player' fund favours basketball
dek: The Ministry of Culture and Sport is handing out roughly 140 million shekels this year through its long-running incentive scheme for fielding home-grown players, but a change to the funding formula has left top-flight football clubs with a smaller slice than women's basketball, and they are not happy about it.
body: Israel's Ministry of Culture and Sport is preparing to distribute close to 140 million shekels this year through its long-standing "Israeli player" incentive scheme, ONE reports, but the way the money is being carved up between sports has ignited a row among top-flight clubs.

The fund is not, despite its singular name, a payment tied to one footballer or basketballer's move. It is an annual grant the ministry pays out to Israeli clubs across several sports based on how much game time they give to Israeli-eligible players, a mechanism designed to encourage domestic development rather than reliance on imports.

According to the figures reported by ONE, men's Premier League football clubs are set to receive the largest single allocation, roughly 2.5 million shekels per team. But it is the sums below that which have caused the uproar: women's Premier League basketball clubs are in line for about 1.989 million shekels each, ahead of men's basketball clubs on roughly 1.584 million.

Women's Premier League football clubs, by contrast, are set for around 1.206 million shekels, with women's National League basketball teams receiving about 747,000 shekels. Men's volleyball clubs are pencilled in for roughly 432,000 shekels and men's handball clubs for about 374,000 shekels, ONE's breakdown shows.

The sticking point for football officials is the gap between the men's and women's basketball allocations and the money going to women's football, given that a football squad fields eleven players at a time against basketball's five and therefore carries far higher running costs per team.

ONE reports that clubs affected by the reshuffle were blunt in their frustration, with representatives complaining that "we built budgets and suddenly, without warning, they cut ours significantly," and questioning why basketball was prioritised in the recalculation.

The ministry, per ONE, has changed the criteria used to calculate the grants, moving away from a formula weighted toward popularity and instead giving more weight to a sport's genuine operating costs and to closing historic gaps in women's sport funding.

A ministry statement carried by ONE was unapologetic about the shift: "The ministry will not apologize for investment in women's sport," it said, framing the change as deliberate policy rather than an oversight.

The "Israeli player" scheme has been a fixture of state sports funding for several years, with ONE and other outlets having covered its annual reallocation before, and it channels money directly to clubs rather than to the sport's governing federations.

For now the figures reported are the ministry's allocations for the year rather than a final, audited settlement, and clubs on the losing end of the recalculation are likely to keep pressing the ministry publicly in the coming weeks.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv set a €7m price tag on rising forward Abu Farchi
dek: Genoa, Torino and Russian clubs have sent scouts to watch the 20-year-old, but Sport5 reports Maccabi Tel Aviv intend to keep him for at least another season.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have made clear that anyone wanting to take Sayed Abu Farchi off their hands this summer will have to pay handsomely for the privilege. Sport5 reports that the club have fixed his price tag at around €7 million, a figure the outlet says reflects both his age and his emerging talent.

The 20-year-old centre-forward has been attracting foreign scouts in recent weeks, with Sport5 naming Genoa and Torino among the Italian clubs to have watched him, alongside reported interest from clubs in Russia. The scouting activity, the report stresses, remains at an early, exploratory stage.

The attention has been sharpened by Abu Farchi's start to the new season. He got on the scoresheet in Maccabi's 5-0 rout of Sheriff Tiraspol in Moldova on July 23, heading home from an Ido Shahar cross inside the first five minutes as Maccabi took control of their Europa League qualifying tie. The return leg in Tel Aviv is set for July 30.

Born in Baqa al-Gharbiyya, Abu Farchi came through Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth ranks, joining the academy as a child before making his senior debut as a substitute in a Conference League qualifier against Celje back in August 2023. He spent last season split between loans at Kafr Qasim and Maccabi Bnei Reineh to gain first-team experience.

This year the club have brought him back in from the cold and handed him a genuine role in the first-team squad as they look to reassert themselves domestically, wearing the number 34 shirt in a Maccabi side rebuilt around a younger core.

Despite the scouting interest, Sport5 reports that Maccabi Tel Aviv have no intention of cashing in immediately. The club, according to the report, want to keep Abu Farchi for at least one more season before entertaining any sale, judging the summer window unlikely to produce an offer that meets their valuation.

January is being framed as a more realistic moment for a transfer, with Sport5 suggesting Major League Soccer could emerge as a suitor by then — a competition described as his preferred destination for financial reasons, should Maccabi's stance soften.

Abu Farchi has already featured for Israel at every youth level from the under-16s to the under-21s and has won one senior cap, adding an international dimension to a profile that has clearly caught the eye of scouts well beyond Bloomfield Stadium.

title: Nottingham Forest's €20m offer for Khalaili turned down by Union Saint-Gilloise
dek: Union Saint-Gilloise have rejected an opening bid from the Premier League club for Anan Khalaili, weeks after his record Inter Milan move collapsed over a failed medical.
body: Anan Khalaili's chaotic transfer summer has taken another turn: Sport5 reports that Nottingham Forest have had a bid of around €20 million rejected by Union Saint-Gilloise for the Israeli winger, citing The Athletic.

The Forest package is said to break down as €17.5 million guaranteed plus a further €2.5 million in performance-related add-ons — a sum the Belgian champions consider well short of the player's value, and comfortably below the €25 million fee Inter Milan had already agreed for him earlier this month.

That Inter deal, which would have been the most expensive transfer of an Israeli player in history, collapsed after Khalaili was denied medical clearance by Italy's Olympic Committee (CONI). He had passed Inter's own medical at Humanitas Hospital, but follow-up cardiac screening required under Italy's stricter registration protocols flagged an irregularity that kept him from being cleared to play in Serie A.

Doctors involved in the process noted that such findings on cardiac screening have become increasingly common since the pandemic, reportedly turning up in roughly one in three or four players tested, and usually requiring specialist review before any final sign-off. Crucially, the finding does not stop him playing in Belgium, and he returned to Union Saint-Gilloise duty without restriction.

Speaking after the Inter move fell apart, a frustrated Khalaili insisted there was nothing wrong with him. "I feel healthy and good," he said, pointing to a heavy workload over the past two seasons as evidence of his fitness.

Khalaili, 21, joined Union Saint-Gilloise from Maccabi Haifa in the summer of 2024 for around €6.5 million, a move that has paid off spectacularly for the Belgian club. He made 52 appearances last season, contributing six goals and six assists as Union SG competed in the Champions League.
The right-sided attacker has also become a regular for Israel, winning 15 caps for the national team as his stock has risen rapidly on the continent.

Nottingham Forest's opening approach is unlikely to be their last word if they remain serious. English interest in Khalaili has been building since the Inter collapse, with Newcastle United and other Premier League clubs reported to be monitoring his situation.

For now, Union Saint-Gilloise appear determined to hold out for a fee closer to what Inter were prepared to pay, leaving Khalaili's next move — and the size of the record it might set — still unresolved.

title: Shviro and Badji set to start for Tiberias in Toto Cup trip to Haifa
dek: Itamar Shviro and Mansour Badji are pencilled in to start as Ironi Tiberias visit Hapoel Haifa in the second round of the Toto Cup, after both made an impact off the bench against Bnei Sakhnin.
body: Ironi Tiberias head to Sami Ofer Stadium on Tuesday evening to face Hapoel Haifa in the second round of the Toto Cup, and according to ONE, two players who barely started a competitive minute a week ago are now expected to be in the XI.

Itamar Shviro and Mansour Badji are both pencilled in to start after coming off the bench in Tiberias's last outing, a dramatic 2-1 comeback win over Bnei Sakhnin, and playing a part in the turnaround, ONE reports.

Shviro, 27, is a two-cap Israel international centre-forward who arrived in Tiberias after a loan spell at Hapoel Tel Aviv, where he helped the club win promotion back to the top flight. He came through Hapoel Be'er Sheva's academy and has also worn the shirts of Ironi Kiryat Shmona and Maccabi Netanya.

Badji, a 21-year-old Gambian winger, is only now getting a look-in with the senior squad after two seasons out on loan at Maccabi Yaffo. He first joined Tiberias's youth ranks in 2023, following a brief spell in Maccabi Haifa's academy, and was a prolific scorer at youth level before heading out on loan.

Assistant coach Moti Crispel, speaking to ONE ahead of the trip to Haifa, played down any notion of a fixed pecking order in the squad. "Every match stands on its own," he said. "Against Sakhnin I decided to start with players who are being tested in the squad, good timing before the season. I don't like using the terms 'strong lineup' or 'weak lineup' - they're all strong. We make specific adjustments per match."

Crispel added that he was pleased with the character his side showed to beat Sakhnin and set the same target for Haifa. "We approach Hapoel Haifa with the same objective: win through actions, not words, done properly and humbly," he said.
Hapoel Haifa arrive on the back of their own eye-catching start to the Toto Cup, having beaten local rivals Maccabi Haifa 3-2 in a derby opener in Bayit Alef, the tournament's northern section.
Kick-off at Sami Ofer Stadium is set for 19:45 on Tuesday, with both clubs still shaping their squads and rotation patterns before the Israeli league season proper gets under way.

title: Zidane appointed France's new head coach, succeeding Deschamps
dek: The former Real Madrid and France great has signed a four-year deal to lead Les Bleus through the 2030 World Cup, ending a long wait for a job he says he always wanted.
body: France finally has its man. Zinedine Zidane was officially unveiled on Tuesday as head coach of the French national team, taking over Les Bleus more than a year after first sitting down with federation president Philippe Diallo to discuss the job.

The appointment ends 14 years under Didier Deschamps, who stepped away after guiding France to a fourth-place finish at the 2026 World Cup. Zidane, capped 108 times as a player and the scorer of two goals in the 1998 World Cup final, becomes the country's most decorated footballing son to take charge of the senior team.

According to reports confirmed by multiple outlets including France 24 and Goal.com, Zidane has signed a four-year contract that runs through the 2030 World Cup, giving the federation long-term continuity around a squad still built on the generation that reached three of the last four World Cup finals.

The move has been a long time coming. Deschamps told Diallo of his intention to step down back in January 2025, and Diallo held his first substantive talks with Zidane the following month. Further meetings over the ensuing months were needed to settle the details before Tuesday's announcement.

"I had offers during these five years, and I turned them all down for the French national team," Zidane said of his decision to hold out for the post rather than return to club management. "It was the only thing I wanted to do."

Diallo, unveiling his pick, called it "an exceptional moment" for French football. "We needed to find a solution to extend this golden generation," the federation president said, framing the appointment as a bridge between Deschamps' World Cup-winning era and the next cycle.

Zidane has not held a coaching role since leaving Real Madrid in 2021, but his managerial record remains one of the most striking in the modern game: three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018, plus two La Liga crowns across his two spells at the Bernabéu.

Former teammate Laurent Blanc, who won the World Cup alongside Zidane in 1998, backed the appointment, noting his old captain's pedigree at both ends of the game. Karim Benzema, who played under Zidane at Real Madrid, said simply: "He is a legend and like an older brother. I am very happy."

Zidane is expected to be formally presented to the France squad and press in the coming days, with his first matches in charge likely to come once the new international window opens after the September 1 start date reported around his deal.

For a French federation eager to keep a talented core together beyond the Deschamps years, the symbolism of handing the reins to 1998's on-field hero is hard to miss — even if the scale of the task, replacing a World Cup and European Championship-winning coach, is just as real.

title: Nottingham Forest bid around €20m for Israeli winger Anan Khalaili
dek: The Premier League club's offer for the Union Saint-Gilloise star was turned down, ONE reports, as Khalaili's camp holds out for the fee Inter Milan agreed before that deal collapsed over a failed medical.

body: Nottingham Forest have moved to the front of the queue for Anan Khalaili, tabling an offer of around €20 million for the Israeli winger, according to a report by ONE.

The Premier League club's proposal to Royale Union Saint-Gilloise is structured as a €17.5m base fee plus up to €2.5m in performance-related add-ons, along with a modest sell-on percentage for the Belgian club, ONE reported.

Union Saint-Gilloise have turned the offer down, according to the report — though Khalaili's family have pushed back on that account, suggesting the negotiation is not as settled as it has been presented.
Khalaili's representatives are said to be holding out for a fee closer to €28m, the number Inter Milan had agreed before that deal collapsed just two weeks earlier.

The Inter move fell apart in mid-July when Khalaili failed a round of medical tests. Inter president Beppe Marotta confirmed the transfer was off after Italy's Olympic Committee, CONI, declined to clear the 21-year-old to play in the country following further examinations — a call that sat with the committee rather than Inter's own medical staff.
Israeli reports at the time described the issue as a condition Khalaili was born with, though the precise diagnosis has not been made public.

Born in Haifa, Khalaili came through the Maccabi Haifa academy before moving to Union Saint-Gilloise in 2024, where he has established himself as one of the most sought-after wingers outside Europe's top five leagues. He has represented Israel from junior level up to the senior national team.

Forest are not alone in the chase: ONE's report notes Bournemouth and Newcastle United have also been credited with interest as the saga around Khalaili continues to draw a crowd of Premier League suitors.

With Khalaili's camp still targeting a figure close to what Inter were prepared to pay, the standoff over valuation looks set to run — and could determine whether Forest return with an improved bid or wait for Union Saint-Gilloise to lower their asking price.

title: Israel's youth handball team opens its first European Championship against Croatia
dek: The under-18 side begins group play in Belgrade on Wednesday having qualified for a European Championship for the first time, with captain Yonatan Flach fresh off a scoring surge in the qualifiers

verificationSources.label: ONE - youth team qualifies for European Championship

body: Israel's under-18 boys' national handball team steps onto the court in Belgrade on Wednesday for a match its federation has waited years to schedule: a first-ever appearance at a European Championship, opening against Croatia at 13:00 local time.

The occasion is the M18 EHF EURO 2026, hosted by Serbia and running through August 9 with 24 nations split into groups. Israel landed in Group C alongside Croatia, the Czech Republic and Portugal, with the top 14 finishers overall advancing to next year's World Championship.

Getting here was itself the achievement. Israel booked its spot by finishing runner-up in a qualifying tournament in Klaipėda, Lithuania, opening with a commanding 41-23 win over Estonia before a 34-27 loss to the Czech Republic. The group came down to a decider against the hosts, which Israel won 33-32 to lock up second place and the ticket to Serbia.

Captain Yonatan Flach, who plays his club handball at Hapoel Rishon LeZion, carried much of that qualifying run. He was named player of the match twice and finished as the tournament's leading scorer with 36 goals, an average in double figures across the three games.

Coach Dor Rosso struck a measured tone ahead of the opener rather than the bravado of a team simply happy to have arrived. "We arrive humbly to show what we've worked for," he said, according to Sport5. "Our team is composed of good people and fine athletes."

The squad Rosso has built for Belgrade runs 18 players deep, the product of what the federation has described as two years of preparation aimed squarely at reaching this stage - a target the group met when it secured qualification last summer.

After Croatia, Israel closes its group phase against the Czech Republic and Portugal, both kicking off at 13:00 local time, before the standings determine which of the tournament's knockout or placement rounds the team plays into.

The appearance lands alongside a broader run of momentum for Israeli handball at underage level, with the country's reserve squad separately qualifying this year for global-level competition - giving the federation two youth national teams on the road at once, a rare position for a program of Israel's size.

title: Blitz to have foot surgery as more than 1,000 Maccabi fans head to Batumi
dek: Christian Blitz faces months out after re-injuring his foot in the rout of Sheriff Tiraspol, as Maccabi Tel Aviv prepare to host the second leg — and a huge travelling support — in Georgia.
body: Christian Blitz will undergo surgery on his fractured foot on Wednesday, a day before his Maccabi Tel Aviv teammates fly out to try to finish off Sheriff Tiraspol in the second leg of their Europa League qualifier in Batumi, ONE reports.

Blitz's setback came in freak circumstances during the 5-0 rout of Sheriff in the first leg, which Ynet also confirmed — sent on as a substitute in the 64th minute on his comeback from a previous spell out through injury, he lasted barely eight minutes before going down again.

According to ONE and Sport1, the diagnosis has since hardened: multiple fracture points in the metatarsal bone of his foot. He is due to have the break repaired at Assaf Harofeh Hospital, with the club estimating he will not return to full training until around November — roughly four months out, partly because an international break and the Ligat Ha'al winter pause will eat into his rehabilitation window regardless.

None of it will dent the mood heading into Thursday, not after a first-leg scoreline so lopsided it barely needed a return fixture to settle. Maccabi need only a routine evening in Georgia to close out the tie and advance to the Europa League's third qualifying round — or the Conference League play-off round, depending on how the continental seeding falls.

That match, and potentially another in the same stadium the following week, will unfold nowhere near Bloomfield Stadium. Maccabi Tel Aviv are hosting all their 2026/27 European fixtures at the Adjarabet Arena in Batumi, the modern stadium on Georgia's Black Sea coast, rather than in Tel Aviv.

It hasn't dampened the travelling support. ONE reports more than 1,000 yellow-shirted Maccabi fans are expected in Batumi for Thursday's game, many treating the trip as a long weekend rather than a straight there-and-back — Georgia has become a popular short-haul destination for Israeli travellers, and a European away day gives supporters a ready-made excuse to go.

Should Maccabi get past Sheriff, the club has already scheduled a third qualifying round tie for the same Batumi venue on Thursday, August 6, meaning Kenny Miller's side's away-from-home European campaign is only just getting started.

Miller is expected to use Thursday's game to freshen up his side, according to ONE, with more minutes likely for Tyrese Asante and Hélio Varela — though Asante's situation is complicated by transfer interest, with Serie A side Monza reported to be in talks over the Dutch defender's future. Kervin Andrade could feature if a proposed loan deal for him falls through, while summer signing Ester Sokler remains unavailable for selection this round.

For Blitz, the focus now shifts entirely to recovery. A player who had only just worked his way back from one injury before suffering another within minutes of his return faces a long road back — one his club will hope ends well before the business end of the season.

title: Israel to send six rider-horse pairs to equestrian world championships in Aachen
dek: Dressage and jumping combinations travel to Germany next month for a championship that doubles as qualifying for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: World of Showjumping - Mark Bluman joins Israeli team

body: Israel will send six rider-and-horse combinations to next month's FEI World Championships in Aachen, Germany, ONE reports — a rare campaign spanning both show jumping and dressage in the same trip.

The championships run at the historic Aachener Soers grounds from August 11 to 23 and double as the first qualifying event on the road to the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, raising the stakes for every pair well beyond rankings and medals.

Five of the six combinations go in jumping. Daniel Bluman, currently ranked ninth in the world, partners Corby V.I.; his cousin Mark Bluman rides Landon de Nyze; Theodore Boris is paired with Kazan Z; Robin Muhr — the Monaco-born Israeli who jumped at the Paris 2024 Olympics — rides Foudjoua de Stel; and Isabella Russekoff, another Paris Olympian, teams with C Pier 2 as the reserve combination, according to ONE.

The sixth pair carries historic weight. Micah Deligdish and Carpe Diem de Massa will represent Israel in dressage — the country's first dressage entry at a world championship since 2010, ONE reports, with delegation head Dr. Amichai Alprobovitz noting that Deligdish qualified only ten months after giving birth.
Alprobovitz framed his ambition for the individual events modestly but pointedly: "I hope at least one rider qualifies for the finals, where the best 25 pairs compete," he told ONE.
Thirty-two nations have entered the team competition, with ten advancing to the final and the top seven nations — excluding the United States — securing qualification places toward Los Angeles 2028.

Bluman, who switched from competing for Colombia to Israel in 2016, finished 16th at the last edition of the championship four years ago in Herning, Denmark. His cousin Mark only joined the Israeli team at the end of June, giving the family two riders on the same squad for the first time at a major championship.

For Muhr and Russekoff, Aachen is a chance to build on Paris, where both competed in individual and team jumping for Israel. The championships arrive a little over two years before Los Angeles, with qualification places narrowing the margin for error for every nation involved.

title: Barcelona enter the race for Rodri as Real Madrid appear close to a deal
dek: Catalan radio reports the champions have made contact over the World Cup Golden Ball winner, even as Real Madrid still look best placed to sign him

body: Barcelona have thrown themselves into the race for Rodri, just as his move to bitter rivals Real Madrid appeared to be all but agreed, according to a report from Catalan radio.

Journalist Oriol Domenech, broadcasting on Catalunya Radio, said the Spanish champions have opened contact to check on the Manchester City captain's situation, a late twist that arrives after weeks in which a Rodri switch to the Bernabéu had looked close to settled.

Barcelona's move is tied in part to their unease over Frenkie de Jong, who is managing a torn medial collateral ligament in his right knee, picked up while playing for the Netherlands at the World Cup. De Jong has so far opted against immediate surgery, with his case due to be revisited in roughly three weeks and a lay-off of five to six months possible if an operation does become necessary.

"The club expects de Jong to return in good condition, but at Barcelona they assess that a top-level defensive midfielder is still missing," Domenech explained, adding that Barça have been making inquiries across the top tier of available midfielders, which is why it is "not surprising" they are now asking about Rodri specifically.

Rodri, 30, is under contract at City until the summer of 2027 and enters this saga at the peak of his standing in the game. He won the 2024 Ballon d'Or, then captained Spain to the World Cup title this month, beating Argentina 1-0 in the final and collecting the Golden Ball as the tournament's outstanding player.

Real Madrid, however, remain the club best placed to land him. Multiple reports out of Spain in recent days describe personal terms as effectively agreed between Rodri's camp and the Bernabéu, with Los Blancos having spent heavily this window as they push to build a midfield around him.

Manchester City are said to be holding out for a fee in the region of €80 million should a deal with Real Madrid go through, a figure that has not stopped Barcelona from testing the waters regardless of their weaker financial position this summer.

For now, Domenech's report amounts to an inquiry rather than a formal offer, but it is enough to unsettle a transfer saga that Madrid had largely expected to have wrapped up by this stage of the summer.

title: More than 3,000 fans to accompany Beitar Jerusalem for Larnaca return leg in Romania
dek: Beitar travels to Ploiești on Thursday holding a 1-0 aggregate lead over AEK Larnaca in the Conference League, backed by one of its biggest away travelling parties in years - and a stern police warning over pyrotechnics.
body: Beitar Jerusalem will be backed by one of the largest away followings it has taken abroad in years when it lands in Romania for Thursday's Conference League second-leg qualifier against AEK Larnaca, with more than 3,000 supporters expected to make the trip, ONE reports.

The tie is finely poised: Beitar go into the second leg holding a 1-0 aggregate lead after winning the first meeting in Cyprus, a game settled by a Brayan Carabali free-kick after AEK defender Mike van der Hoorn was sent off.
Because AEK's home leg is being staged away from Cyprus, Thursday's decider will be played in Ploiești, just outside Bucharest, with kickoff set for 20:30 local time.

Beitar's travelling delegation departs Israel on Wednesday at 15:15 on a dedicated Israir charter to Bucharest, before continuing on to Ploiești for the match. The flight is scheduled to return to Israel on Friday.

According to ONE, close to 2,000 travel packages had already been snapped up by supporters even before the club's own ticket sale opened, with the total following expected to top 3,000 - among the biggest away crowds Beitar has taken to Europe in recent seasons.

The club has also circulated a pointed warning to its fans, relaying guidance issued after consultation with Romanian police: pyrotechnics, flares, torches and other flammable materials are strictly forbidden under Romanian law, with offenders liable to arrest. Drugs are likewise banned.
On the pitch, defender Luka Gadrani and midfielder Tomer Yosefi have both been included in the travelling squad, though their availability for Thursday's match remains uncertain, ONE reports.
The winner of the tie advances to the Conference League's third qualifying round, one step closer to the competition's group-stage playoffs.

title: Israel's under-18 team rank among Europe's most efficient scorers at EuroBasket
dek: After a perfect 3-0 group stage in Trento and Rovereto, Israel sit second in the championship for scoring and efficiency, with Aviv Aronov and David Musis leading the numbers.

verificationSources.label: FIBA U18 EuroBasket 2026 - Israel team profile

body: Israel's under-18 national basketball team has emerged as one of the statistical stories of the group stage at the 2026 FIBA U18 EuroBasket, finishing pool play unbeaten and ranking among the tournament's most productive offensive sides heading into the knockout rounds in Trentino.

The team went 3-0 in Group A, opening with a 93-84 overtime win over Greece, following that with a 91-77 defeat of France, and closing the group with an 84-80 win over Austria to finish top of the pool.

Across those three games Israel are averaging 89.3 points per game, second only to Germany's 96, and their offensive efficiency rating of 94 also ranks second among all teams at the championship - one of the clearest signs yet of a young squad's scoring depth this summer.

The shooting numbers back it up: Israel rank third in two-point percentage at 53% and fourth from three-point range at 30.4%, while their 98 free-throw attempts across three games, converted at 75.5%, are among the heaviest workloads at the rim in the draw. Rebounding is the one area lagging behind, with Israel 12th in the field on the glass.

Guard Aviv Aronov has driven much of it, leading Israel with 26.7 points per game after scoring 30 against Greece and 31 against France, and topping the entire championship in free-throw attempts - the product of an aggressive, downhill style that has repeatedly put opposing defences in foul trouble.

David Musis has been just as central. The forward is averaging 24 points and a tournament-high 12 rebounds per game, and his efficiency rating of 27.3 is the best of any player at this EuroBasket, ahead of teammate Aronov's 22.7 in the same category.

Lior Hershko rounds out the trio of standouts, ranking fourth in the tournament for steals at 2.7 per game, part of an Israeli defence that, while unheralded in the raw team numbers, has done enough to close out three tight victories.

The run has been built under head coach Nadav Zilberstein, a long-serving figure in Israeli youth and senior national team basketball circles, whose side now moves into the round of 16 as Group A winners.
Israel are set to face Denmark, who advanced as the fourth-placed team from Group B, in the round of 16 at the Palasport A. Marchetti in Rovereto, with a place in the quarterfinals on the line.

The 2026 U18 EuroBasket, the 41st edition of the championship, is being staged across Trento and Rovereto through August 2, with the continent's best under-18 talent using the tournament as a springboard toward senior international careers - exactly the stage on which Aronov and Musis are now making their names felt.

body: Avi Yechiel has officially become the owner of Hapoel Ramat Gan, ONE reports, after the last of the legal and bureaucratic hurdles - including formal approval from the Israel Football Association - were cleared this week.

The sign-off closes out a process that began in late April, when management rights at the club were first passed from previous owner Amir Hamias to a purchasing group fronted by Yechiel, at the time still pending federation ratification.

"This is a significant and emotional milestone, the official start of a new era at the club," Yechiel said, according to ONE, adding that he and his group intend to "keep working quietly, responsibly and patiently" while pursuing a clear long-term vision for Hapoel Ramat Gan.

Yechiel, a former defender who won four caps for the Israel national team, made his name with Hapoel Petah Tikva before spells at Maccabi Tel Aviv, Maccabi Petah Tikva and Hapoel Beer Sheva. He later moved into administration, serving as CEO of Hapoel Petah Tikva before turning to ownership.

When his takeover was first announced publicly in late May - a day after Hapoel Ramat Gan secured its return to Ligat Ha'al - Yechiel told Sport1 he was "proud to join a prestigious and important club in Israeli football," pledging to build a stable, competitive organisation in keeping with the values the club has carried since 1927.

Club CEO Moshe Barket, a retired police commissioner, had held signing authority as caretaker while the federation reviewed the transfer, with Hamias thanked by the new ownership for his role in the handover negotiations.

According to ice.co.il, two private individuals are financing Yechiel's purchase but have asked to stay out of the spotlight, even though their identities will be disclosed to the Football Association's ownership and financial oversight committees. "You can understand them - they all know football and the media," Yechiel said of their reluctance to go public.

The finalised sale lands Hapoel Ramat Gan in the top flight for its centenary year, giving Yechiel's group a full campaign to stabilise a club that has spent recent seasons shuttling between ownership groups and divisions.

title: Halaili keeps Maccabi Haifa's faith as Wanderson Tsunami joins the squad picture
dek: Barak Bakhar reshapes his lineup for the Toto Cup clash with Ironi Kiryat Shmona, rewarding Halaili after his derby goal and unveiling new defender Wanderson Tsunami for the first time.
body: Maccabi Haifa go looking for their first win of the Toto Cup campaign on Tuesday evening, hosting Ironi Kiryat Shmona at 20:00 with manager Barak Bakhar reshuffling his side after a chastening derby defeat.

Haifa were beaten 3-2 by Hapoel Haifa in the Toto Cup opener on Saturday, having trailed 3-0 inside an hour through Yoad Gonen's 30th-minute strike, a Noam Steipman own goal three minutes later and an Alon Turgeman free-kick just after the hour. A spirited late rally through Iaad Halaili in the 75th minute and Eitan Azulay in the 79th was not enough, with Hapoel goalkeeper Yoav Gerafi making a crucial save in the 88th to seal the win.

Halaili's goal in that defeat has earned him another chance in Bakhar's XI, according to ONE. Club officials are said to rate the youngster highly, with one describing him as possessing "very high technical ability" and adding that "if he keeps working hard, he can go on to have a breakthrough season."

The bigger talking point around the squad photo, though, is the first appearance of new signing Wanderson Tsunami. The Brazilian left-back, whose full name is Wanderson de Frias Suarez, completed his medical and signed a two-year contract with Haifa around July 19 after building a reputation in Bulgaria, where he twice captained Levski Sofia.

Bakhar has also recalled winger Kenji Gorré and forward Ali Muhammad to the lineup, while new signing Nigel Lunuwick and forward Pedro are included in the matchday squad as Haifa continue to integrate their summer arrivals.

Going the other way, striker Andrea Novaković and Yarin Levi both drop out with a virus, while defender Goni Naor and Zohar Zasno have been left out after their performances were singled out for criticism following individual errors in the derby.

Haifa's hierarchy was blunt in its assessment of the derby collapse, with a club source telling ONE that "the approach in the first 60 minutes was so slack it really stood out" and calling for a sharper attitude from the players in front of their own supporters against Kiryat Shmona.
