title: Tomer Ginat extends Hapoel Tel Aviv contract through 2030
dek: The EuroCup-winning forward has committed to four more years in red, a deal that will give him 12 total seasons with the club across two spells.

verificationSources.label: ONE - תומר גינת האריך את חוזהו בהפועל ת"א עד 2030
ONE - ההבטחה של ינאי לגינת: יהיה אלוף ישראל ואירופה

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have tied down one of the faces of their recent success, announcing that forward Tomer Ginat has extended his contract through the 2029/30 season, ONE reported.

The new deal adds four years to Ginat's current stay in red. Combined with his first spell at the club from 2016 to 2020, the extension means the 31-year-old will have spent 12 seasons in total wearing Hapoel colours by the time it expires.

Ginat, a 6-foot-8 power forward born in Gesher Haziv, returned to Hapoel Tel Aviv in 2022 after two seasons in France with Metropolitans 92. Since coming back, he has become one of the squad's most reliable figures, both on the floor and in the locker room.

He played a central role last season as Hapoel won the EuroCup, averaging 8.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists while shooting 65.4 percent from inside the arc over the course of the championship campaign.
"It's time to complete the mission in Israel and win the championship," Ginat said of the new agreement, according to ONE.

Head coach Dimitris Itoudis, who led Hapoel to that EuroCup title and was named the Israeli league's Coach of the Year for 2024/25, backed the club's decision to lock in his forward long-term. "I cannot imagine Hapoel's future without Tomer Ginat," Itoudis said. "He always places the team first."
General manager George Chinas framed the extension as a statement of loyalty on both sides. "The captain stays home," Chinas said. "Tomer committed for life with his family."

In a companion piece published by ONE, club owner Ofer Yanai went further, promising that Ginat would eventually retire in Hapoel Tel Aviv colours as a champion of both Israel and Europe. "That's a promise," Yanai said, "and one I'll do everything to keep."

Ginat is also a regular for the Israeli national team, having made his senior debut in 2017 and featured at EuroBasket 2025. He underwent knee surgery in March, and locking in his long-term future comes as he works his way back from that injury.
The extension continues a pattern of Hapoel prioritising continuity around its core group as it chases a first Israeli championship in years to go alongside its European silverware.

title: Israeli players' organization honors legendary referee Avraham Klein
dek: Nir Alon and Moshiko Mishalov presented Klein, who officiated three World Cups, with a shield recognizing his decades of service to Israeli refereeing.
body: Avraham Klein, the most decorated referee Israeli football has produced, was presented with a shield of appreciation by the Israel Football Players Organization, ONE reported, as the union honored what it called his exceptional contribution to the game and to international officiating.

"Today's meeting, and especially receiving a shield of appreciation from an organization that represents football players and athletes, moves me particularly," Klein said on receiving the award, according to ONE.

Nir Alon, head of the Histadrut's Sports Division, which oversees the players' organizations across Israeli football, basketball, volleyball and handball, called Klein "a symbol of excellence, integrity and professionalism, who represented the State of Israel with honor on the biggest stages in the world."

Moshiko Mishalov, the IFPO's chief executive, put it more simply: "Everyone who has lived Israeli football grew up with the name Avraham Klein." He added that Klein set standards of professionalism that inspired generations of players and officials who followed him.

The tribute is the latest in a long line of honors for a man widely regarded as the finest referee Israel has ever produced. Klein was born in Timișoara, Romania, in March 1934, survived the Holocaust as a child and immigrated to Israel in October 1948 at the age of 13.

He went on to officiate at three FIFA World Cups. At Mexico 1970 he took charge of the group-stage meeting between holders Brazil and England, won 1-0 by the Brazilians, and served as fourth official for Brazil's 4-1 win over Czechoslovakia in the same tournament.

At Argentina 1978 he refereed matches including Argentina against Italy, and was widely seen as a leading candidate to take charge of the final itself — until the host nation objected to his appointment.

His defining moment came at Spain 1982, when he refereed Italy's 3-2 win over Brazil in the second round, a match still remembered as one of the greatest in World Cup history. He was later named fourth official for the final, in which Italy beat West Germany 3-1 to lift the trophy.

Klein's standing with FIFA has endured well beyond his playing days on the pitch. He received a special FIFA award in 1984, was made an honorary citizen of Haifa in 2010, saw items from his personal collection go on permanent display at the FIFA Museum in Zurich in 2017, and was appointed an honorary ambassador of the museum in 2022 — a role in which, ONE noted, he has continued to represent Israeli football at major international fixtures.

The IFPO shield adds a domestic honor from the game's current players to a career already decorated at the highest level of world football, a reminder of how deeply Klein's name remains woven into Israeli football's sense of itself.

title: Daniel Peretz on his Southampton move: 'It was an easy decision'
dek: The Israeli goalkeeper, who completed a permanent €7 million switch from Bayern Munich after an impressive loan spell, says his heart was always set on staying at St Mary's.

verificationSources.label: Southampton FC official announcement of the permanent signing
The Jerusalem Post on the permanent transfer

body: Daniel Peretz has explained why he never seriously weighed another option once Southampton made clear they wanted him permanently, telling ONE that the decision to leave Bayern Munich for the Championship club was "easy" despite the team's failure to win promotion back to the Premier League this year.

"From the first moment I arrived here in January, I felt at home and received a very warm welcome," the 26-year-old goalkeeper said, according to ONE. He added that the club's sporting vision persuaded him, but that in the end the pull was emotional as much as professional: "My heart always told me I wanted to stay here."

Peretz arrived at St Mary's on loan from Bayern in January, having spent the first half of the season out on loan at Hamburger SV without a single league appearance. The move to Southampton reignited his career almost immediately. He made 26 appearances across all competitions and kept nine clean sheets during a 21-match unbeaten run in the Championship, according to ONE's reporting, with other outlets crediting him with eight clean sheets across that same streak and standout displays against Premier League opposition including Fulham, Arsenal and Manchester City as Southampton reached the FA Cup semi-finals.

Southampton's promotion bid ultimately unravelled off the pitch rather than on it. The club was thrown out of the Championship play-offs after admitting to unauthorised filming of a rival's training session, with Middlesbrough taking their place in the final against Hull City, and Southampton were also docked four points for next season. It made Peretz's decision to commit his future to a second-tier side, rather than push for a move to a Premier League or bigger European club, all the more notable.

The switch was made permanent in June, with Southampton paying Bayern a fee reported at around €7 million for a player who had made only four Bundesliga appearances for the German giants after signing there in 2023. He has now put pen to paper on a four-year contract at St Mary's.

Southampton have already handed him the number one shirt, and Peretz made his first appearance of pre-season in a friendly against Eintracht Braunschweig, playing 45 minutes and keeping a clean sheet in a 1-0 win.

Born in Tel Aviv, Peretz came through the Maccabi Tel Aviv academy before his move to Bayern Munich three years ago made him the first Israeli player in the Bavarian club's history. He has since earned 12 caps for Israel's senior national team.

title: Kiryat Shmona to postpone Yair Mordechai ceremony until league clash with Haifa
dek: The club wants to give its former player of the season "full honour" rather than mark his departure in Tuesday's Toto Cup opener, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Ynet - Mordechai signs for Maccabi Haifa

body: Ironi Kiryat Shmona have shelved plans to give Yair Mordechai a send-off ceremony on Tuesday, deciding the club's former talisman deserves a bigger stage than a Toto Cup opener, ONE reports.

The northern club host Maccabi Haifa - the team Mordechai joined this off-season - in their opening Toto Cup fixture on Tuesday, kicking off at 20:00. A tribute had been mooted for that occasion, but the club now says it will wait.

According to ONE, Kiryat Shmona explained the decision as a matter of respect: with the desire to give Mordechai "full honour," the ceremony will instead be held when the two clubs meet in the league later this season, rather than at Tuesday's preseason cup tie.

It is an unusual scheduling choice, but a telling one - it signals the club sees Mordechai's departure as worthy of a proper league occasion in front of a fuller house, not a curtain-raiser before the campaign has even begun.

Mordechai, 22, is a product of the Kiryat Shmona academy and became one of the more prized young forwards to come through it in recent years, culminating in being voted the club's Player of the Season last term.

He made close to 100 league appearances for Kiryat Shmona and scored 19 goals along the way, according to Ynet, with a standout final campaign of 10 goals and six assists that caught the eye of the country's bigger clubs.

Maccabi Haifa moved for him this off-season, and Mordechai did not hide his excitement on completing the switch. "I'm fulfilling a childhood dream today, signing for a giant club like Maccabi Haifa," he told Ynet at the time.

For Kiryat Shmona, Tuesday's Toto Cup meeting is instead being treated as a straightforward preseason test - their first outing since wrapping up last season - against the very club that has just taken their homegrown star, with the emotional send-off saved for another day.

title: Shimon Abuhatzira named coach of Maccabi Netanya's women's team
dek: The former Israel international striker, and father of teenage sensation Yarin Abuhatzira, takes charge of the club's young women's program.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 on Maccabi Netanya's women's team formation

body: Maccabi Netanya have turned to a familiar face to lead their women's team into the new season. The club has appointed Shimon Abuhatzira, a former Israel international striker, as head coach of the women's squad, ONE reported on Monday.

Abuhatzira, 39, was born and raised in Netanya and hangs up a long playing career to take his first senior coaching post at the club that shaped him. As a forward he shared the Israeli Premier League's Golden Boot in 2008-09 with 14 goals for Hapoel Petah Tikva, then went on to win the title with Ironi Kiryat Shmona in 2011-12 before finishing runner-up in the scoring charts a year later with 15 goals. He also had spells at Larissa in Greece, Maccabi Haifa, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Ra'anana, and won three caps for the Israel national team after making his debut in October 2012, before retiring in 2020.
The club confirmed the news through its own social channels, welcoming Abuhatzira and wishing him luck in the new role.

The job puts him in charge of a program that is still finding its feet. Maccabi Netanya's women's team is barely two years old, formed after the club absorbed the roster of Maccabi Emek Hefer in a merger announced in September 2024. The team competes in the National League, one tier below the top flight of Israeli women's football.

There is also a family thread running through the appointment. Abuhatzira is the father of Yarin Abuhatzira, the 16-year-old forward already breaking into Maccabi Netanya's senior men's squad and drawing comparisons in the Israeli press to Barcelona's teenage star Lamine Yamal after becoming the youngest goalscorer in Toto Cup history. The younger Abuhatzira has since signed a new multi-year contract with the club, with reports suggesting Netanya would be reluctant to turn down an offer in the region of three to four million euros should one arrive.

For now, the elder Abuhatzira's focus shifts to preseason preparations with the women's squad, as Maccabi Netanya looks to build out a fuller women's program alongside the emergence of its next generation of talent on the men's side.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv basketball club signs three-year sponsorship deal with Zoho
dek: The Indian technology giant, which recently opened its first Israeli office in Tel Aviv, becomes a new club partner through the end of the 2028/29 season.

verificationSources.label: Isra-Tech — Zoho to open its first office in Israel

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's basketball club has a new partner off the court: the club announced a fresh sponsorship agreement with Zoho, the Indian software giant, that will run for three seasons through the end of 2028/29.

Zoho is a privately held technology company headquartered in Chennai, India, that builds more than 60 business applications used by over 150 million people worldwide, and employs more than 19,000 staff. The deal marks the company's entry into Israeli sports sponsorship as it builds out its presence in the local market.

The tie-up lands soon after Zoho opened its first Israeli office, in Tel Aviv, following a year of double-digit growth for the company in the country. Separate reporting on the office opening put 2024 growth in Israel at 24%, part of the rationale the company has given for investing directly in the market rather than working through it remotely.

Under the agreement, Zoho's branding will appear on court-side signage at Maccabi's home games — including on the free-throw circle — as well as on the team bus and on the big screen at the club's arena, giving the company recurring visibility across the season.
Club chairman Shimon Mizrahi welcomed the partnership, calling it "a major honor" and describing the pairing with Zoho as "a winning combination."

Tomer Guzlan, Zoho's Israel operations manager, said the company was "proud to stand alongside Maccabi Tel Aviv, a club embodying our values — uncompromising excellence, professionalism and innovation with purpose."

Basketball club CEO Avi Ben Tal and VP of marketing and sales Doron Jamchi — himself a former Maccabi playing great — both framed the deal as part of a broader strategy of aligning with major global brands; Jamchi called it "a connection between two brands believing in innovation, excellence and continuous growth."

Neither side disclosed the financial terms of the agreement. It adds to a sponsorship portfolio at Maccabi that already includes Rapyd as the club's main shirt sponsor under a seven-year deal signed in 2023, reflecting the growing commercial weight of Israel's most decorated basketball institution.

title: Leeds urged to move for Manor Solomon at £20m after another eye-catching Spurs cameo
dek: Football Insider's Harry Burton says Daniel Farke's side should act quickly for the Israeli winger, who again impressed in Tottenham's preseason win over Auckland FC, according to ONE.
body: Leeds United have been handed fresh reason to revive their interest in Manor Solomon, with ONE reporting that Football Insider journalist Harry Burton has urged the club to move quickly for the Israeli winger at a fee of £20 million.

Solomon, who spent last season on loan at Elland Road under Daniel Farke and played a significant part in Leeds' promotion back to the Premier League, remains on Tottenham Hotspur's books, with two years still to run on his contract in north London.

The renewed push follows another eye-catching display from the 27-year-old, who was named player of the match by FotMob after Tottenham's 2-0 preseason friendly win over Auckland FC. Solomon created six chances, completed 80 per cent of his passes and made six tackles in 79 minutes on the pitch.
"Manor Solomon catches the eye, Leeds should make a quick move for the deal at £20million," Burton wrote, according to ONE's report.

Farke worked closely with Solomon during his Championship promotion campaign and is understood to believe he can again get the best out of the winger, who has spent much of his time in England shuttling between clubs and dealing with fitness setbacks since arriving from Shakhtar Donetsk in 2023.

ONE's report frames Solomon as a player seeking a settled, permanent home after years of instability, while Leeds are said to be actively searching for reinforcements out wide as they prepare for a first full season back in the Premier League.

The £20 million valuation lines up with figures floated elsewhere in the British press in recent weeks, suggesting Tottenham could be willing to cash in on a squad player with limited first-team minutes rather than let his contract run down further.

Nothing is yet formal on either side: Solomon travelled with Spurs' senior squad on their preseason tour, and no bid has been confirmed by either club, leaving the widely reported interest as speculation for now rather than an agreed deal.

title: Kyle Kuzma blasts NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani over viral Netanyahu video
dek: The Milwaukee Bucks forward, a close friend of Israeli international Deni Avdija, called Mamdani 'a mayor playing president' after the mayor's clip on Netanyahu drew tens of millions of views.
body: Kyle Kuzma has never been shy about wading into topics well outside the paint, but this week the Milwaukee Bucks forward found himself at the centre of a genuinely global storm — one that started with New York City's mayor and ended up tangled with Israel's prime minister.

The trigger was a video posted by Mayor Zohran Mamdani addressing Benjamin Netanyahu's expected appearance at the United Nations General Assembly in New York this September. In the clip, Mamdani called Netanyahu a 'war criminal,' said he was 'not welcome in New York City,' and acknowledged the city itself lacks the legal authority to enforce the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant against him — while urging the federal government to act instead. The video spread fast, racking up tens of millions of views within days.

Kuzma, a nine-year NBA veteran, quote-posted the clip on X with a blunt three-word verdict: 'A mayor playing president.' He followed it with a longer post reading, in part: 'This is 2026. People cosplaying as things they don't have the authority, the talent, or the track record to actually be. Just for content.'

The exchange itself became a moment. Kuzma's remarks were reported to have pulled in close to 100 million views on X within five days, turning a basketball player's aside into one of the more widely discussed political flashpoints of the week.

Not everyone was convinced by the tone. A number of users suggested the phrasing read like it had been generated rather than typed by Kuzma himself, prompting the forward to respond with characteristic sarcasm: 'All my tweets are AI sourced from Chatgpt, guys... Let me just shut up and dribble.'

The episode carries an added layer for Israeli readers given Kuzma's history. He spent parts of three seasons with the Washington Wizards alongside Deni Avdija, the Israeli international forward, and the two built a genuine relationship that extended off the court, including a widely shared appearance by Kuzma at a Jewish wedding celebration.

Kuzma, who won an NBA championship with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 before moving to Washington and then to Milwaukee in a February 2025 trade, has built a reputation as one of the league's more outspoken voices on social media, rarely shying away from commentary beyond basketball.

Mamdani, a Democratic Socialist who took office as mayor earlier this year, has made his position on Netanyahu a recurring public theme since taking City Hall. Neither his office nor Kuzma had issued any further comment on the exchange at the time of writing.
facts: Kyle Kuzma, Milwaukee Bucks forward, publicly criticized NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani after Mamdani posted a viral video addressing Benjamin Netanyahu.

Mamdani's video called Netanyahu a 'war criminal,' said he was 'not welcome in New York City,' and said the city lacks legal authority to enforce the ICC arrest warrant, urging federal action instead.
Kuzma responded on X, calling Mamdani 'a mayor playing president' and writing that people are 'cosplaying as things they don't have the authority, the talent, or the track record to actually be.'

title: Following Cazorla's path, Ander Herrera goes home to Real Zaragoza
dek: The former Manchester United and PSG midfielder has left Boca Juniors to rejoin the club that raised him, now stuck in Spain's third tier for the first time in 77 years.
body: Ander Herrera is going home. The 36-year-old Basque midfielder has left Boca Juniors and signed for Real Zaragoza, the club where he was formed as a teenager, on a one-year deal that will see him play in Spain's third division for the first time since he broke through there in the mid-2000s.

The move closes a loop. Herrera left Zaragoza for Athletic Bilbao in 2011, then spent five years at Manchester United and four more at Paris Saint-Germain before a spell in Argentina with Boca Juniors, where he departed after a change of coaching staff left him without a role in the squad, according to ONE.

He returns to a club in crisis. Zaragoza finished bottom of the Spanish second division last season with just 36 points from 42 matches, sealing relegation to the third tier after 77 years spent almost entirely in the top two flights of Spanish football.

"Zaragoza is my life," Herrera said, according to ONE. "I'm fulfilling an old dream, and I'll do the maximum to restore it to greatness. In ten years, it should be back in the first division and even competing for titles. That's how it must be."

The financial terms underline the sentimental nature of the move. Spanish federation rules require a minimum salary of around €25,000 for a registered professional, but ONE reports that Herrera has arranged for that money to be redirected straight into a club rehabilitation fund rather than taking it as personal pay.

Independent Spanish outlets, including Aragón Digital and Cope, confirmed the core of the deal on 14 July: Herrera signed to lead the new project at Zaragoza, with the explicit target of pulling the club out of what one report called "the hell of the Primera RFEF."

ONE frames the transfer as a direct echo of Santi Cazorla's celebrated 2023 return to Real Oviedo, another boyhood homecoming built on a reduced financial arrangement. Cazorla took the Spanish football minimum wage and waived his image rights so that ten percent of shirt-sale revenue would go to Oviedo's youth academy, before leading the club back to La Liga two seasons later.

Whether Herrera can engineer anything close to that turnaround from the third tier is another matter. Zaragoza's fall has been sharp: a club with two European trophies and a Copa del Rey as recently as 2004 has spent over a decade sliding through Spanish football's middle tiers before finally dropping out of the professional pyramid's top two divisions altogether.

For Herrera, who captained Athletic Bilbao's academy generation before his big move and went on to lift the Europa League with United and multiple Ligue 1 titles with PSG, this is described in his own words as one last project rather than a retirement lap — a bid to give something back to the club that made him.

title: Premier League moves to close the goalkeeper injury loophole
dek: From next season any player treated for an injury must stay off the pitch for a full minute — a rule aimed squarely at goalkeepers who buy their team a tactical break, after Daniel Farke accused Gianluigi Donnarumma of doing exactly that.
body: When Gianluigi Donnarumma sank to the turf inside the hour at Elland Road last November, nobody in the stadium guessed the stoppage would end up rewriting a law of the game. As Manchester City's goalkeeper received treatment, Pep Guardiola used the free break to gather his outfield players for fresh instructions — and City went on to win 3-2 through a late Phil Foden goal. Leeds manager Daniel Farke was livid afterwards, accusing Donnarumma of a 'fake injury' that let City 'bend the rules.' English football has now acted.

According to a report by Israeli outlet ONE, the sport's authorities are introducing a new law for the 2026/27 season aimed squarely at goalkeepers who go down injured to buy their team a break in play. The Football Association confirms that from next season, any player who receives on-field assessment or treatment — or whose injury stops the match — must stay off the pitch for at least one minute once play resumes, up from the previous 30 seconds.

The change follows an independent stakeholder survey commissioned by the Premier League: 73% of respondents said goalkeeper time-wasting was a genuine problem, and 85% pointed specifically to goalkeeper 'tactical time-outs' — moments when a keeper goes down and forces a total stoppage that an outfield injury does not require, handing the bench a free team talk.

Unlike an outfield player, a goalkeeper cannot simply walk off for a minute without leaving his team without a shot-stopper. ONE reports that the fix settled on gives the manager a short window — around 10 seconds — to nominate an outfield player who serves the one-minute absence in the goalkeeper's place, with the captain forced to leave instead if no name is given in time. Neither the Premier League nor the FA's published law summary spells out that exact selection mechanism in the same detail, though the underlying principle — that someone from the team must sit out a full minute whenever a goalkeeper's treatment halts the game — matches the confirmed rule change.

The one-minute sanction applies, in the FA's wording, 'barring certain exceptions' — a category expected to cover collisions between team-mates, fouls committed on the goalkeeper himself, visible bleeding, suspected concussion and injuries serious enough to require an immediate substitution.

It sits alongside a wider set of changes to next season's laws: a five-second countdown for goal kicks and throw-ins, after which possession switches to the opponents, and a 10-second limit for substituted players to leave the field. It also builds on an earlier IFAB reform limiting goalkeepers to eight seconds of holding the ball before conceding a corner, part of a running campaign — one FIFA's chief refereeing officer Pierluigi Collina has spoken about publicly — to squeeze dead time out of matches.

Farke himself stopped short of accusing City of cheating. 'It is within the rules,' he said afterwards. 'If we don't educate our players in football, what to do in terms of fair play, sportsmanship... it is nothing I personally like, but if it is within the rules I can't complain about it.' His comments, and the broader frustration with goalkeeper stoppages, appear to have fed directly into the review that produced the new law.

As with most contested amendments to the laws of the game, the change begins as a trial in English football before IFAB, the sport's global lawmaking body, assesses its impact ahead of possible wider adoption from 2027/28. For coaches like Guardiola, the free tactical timeout via an injured goalkeeper may be numbered — someone in his XI will now have to pay for it.
facts: The Premier League/FA confirm that from 2026/27, any player receiving on-field treatment, or whose injury stops the match, must leave the pitch for at least one minute after play resumes — up from 30 seconds.
An independent stakeholder survey found 73% believe goalkeeper time-wasting is a Premier League problem, and 85% specifically flagged goalkeeper 'tactical time-outs.'

Because play cannot resume while a goalkeeper is being treated (unlike with outfield players), coaches have used the stoppage to regroup — as happened when Manchester City's Gianluigi Donnarumma went down during a match at Leeds.
Leeds manager Daniel Farke accused Donnarumma of a 'fake injury' that let Pep Guardiola address his team, after City came from behind to beat Leeds 3-2 via a late Phil Foden goal.

ONE reports managers will have a short window (around 10 seconds) to nominate an outfield player to serve the one-minute absence on the goalkeeper's behalf, with the captain leaving by default if nobody is named — a specific mechanic not detailed in the official law summaries reviewed.
The change follows IFAB's earlier introduction of an eight-second limit on how long goalkeepers may hold the ball before conceding a corner.

title: Israel's youth basketball team completes perfect group stage in Italy
dek: Oren Trushkin and Omri Orland say summer training paid off as the U18 side beat Austria to finish Group A unbeaten and reach the quarterfinals.
body: Israel's national under-18 boys basketball team closed out the group phase of the FIBA U18 European Championship in Italy with a perfect record, beating Austria to complete a 3-0 run through Group A and set up a place in the quarterfinals.

The Austria game carried little competitive weight of its own — Israel had already clinched top spot in the group after wins over Greece and France — but Nadav Zilbershtein's squad won comfortably regardless, extending an unbeaten start to the tournament.

Forward Oren Trushkin, who scored 12 points in the win, pointed to the work done in training camp as the reason for the form. "We did the work in the group stage, we trained hard all summer at a high level and it's paid off," he told ONE.

Point guard Omri Orland, who added 7 points, said the group-stage form now counts for little with the knockout rounds beginning. He said a "combination of focus and professionalism" would be needed if Israel are to get past the quarterfinal, according to ONE.

The perfect group stage was built on statement wins rather than narrow escapes. Israel needed overtime to see off Greece 93-84 in the tournament opener, before following up with a more comfortable 91-77 win over France that secured first place in Group A with a game still to play.

Aviv Aronov has been the headline act of the group phase, scoring 30 points and adding six assists against Greece before backing it up with 31 more against France. David Moisis has been just as prominent inside, posting 26 points and 19 rebounds against Greece and 25 points and 8 rebounds against France.

Trushkin, an 18-year-old, 2-metre forward who averages 20.3 points, 10 rebounds and 3.4 assists a game for his club side, Hapoel Gilboa/Ma'ayanot, was already named to the tournament's team of the round earlier in the competition — reflecting the size and scoring Israel have brought to Italy.
Orland, a 1.90-metre playmaker from Hapoel Emek Hefer, is regarded as one of the more intriguing names in the squad, and his composure running the offense has been central to Israel's fast start.
With Group A wrapped up, Israel now turn to the knockout stage knowing that the professionalism Orland spoke of will be tested against sterner opposition than they faced in the group phase.

title: Gordon brothers make history with triple debut as Ahavat Gordon takes on John Lineker
dek: All three sons of the fighting family share one card for the first time at Menora Mivtachim Arena, headlined by a Muay Thai clash between Ahavat Gordon and former UFC and ONE champion John Lineker.
body: Tel Aviv's Menora Mivtachim Arena is hosting a scene Israeli combat sports has never produced before: three brothers from one family fighting on the same card, on the same night, under the banner of a promotion they built themselves.

The event, GFN 1: Israel vs. The World, is the debut show for Gordon Fight Nights, organized by the Gordon brothers together with Yaniv Kaminski. ONE reports roughly 11,000 fans packed the hall, with the card broadcast live on Channel ONE.
Ahavat Gordon, Ruach Gordon and Kibedy Gordon are each competing on the bill, a first for the family and, organizers say, for Israeli kickboxing and Muay Thai more broadly.

The headline bout pits Ahavat Gordon in a Muay Thai clash against Brazil's John Lineker, a former UFC bantamweight standout who went on to become a ONE Championship bantamweight MMA world champion. It is being billed as the toughest opponent of the young Israeli's career.

Gordon has built his reputation fighting abroad in hostile arenas. He most recently stopped a Turkish opponent by knockout at UTMA 17 in a bout where, he told Ynetnews afterward, the crowd had jeered him — a win he called "the best answer" to the taunts.
Elsewhere on the GFN 1 card, Ruach Gordon meets Maximus Bejenuta and Kibedy Gordon faces Jose Alberto Quiñonez, while Natan Levy squares off with Lando Vannata in a separate kickboxing bout.
The night's opening fight is already in the books: Gai Mor Alon took a unanimous decision over Lithuania's Aronas Grodis to get the card underway.
The Ahavat Gordon–Lineker main event had not yet been fought as this report was filed, with the broadcast still running live on Channel ONE.

title: Israel youth coach: Orian Goren's "DNA" resembles Xavi, Iniesta and Pedri
dek: Ophir Haim, who guided Israel's age-group sides to a European final and a World Cup semi-final, says the 17-year-old La Masia midfielder's ball retention already recalls Barcelona's greats.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - Orian Goren compared to Pedri
Ynet - Goren's first Barcelona senior minutes

body: It takes a bold coach to mention a 17-year-old in the same breath as Xavi Hernandez, Andres Iniesta and Pedri. Ophir Haim, who has spent the past few years guiding Israel's age-group national teams to a European final and a World Cup semi-final, did exactly that this week when asked about Orian Goren, the Israeli midfielder rising through Barcelona's academy.

"His DNA is very similar to their players, whether it's Xavi and Iniesta in the past or Pedri and Gavi today," Haim said, according to ONE. "He has many things he still needs to improve, in my opinion he should look for goals more, but you cannot take the ball from his foot no matter how strong you are. It's very hard to pressure Orian, he doesn't lose the ball."

It is a striking endorsement from a coach not prone to hyperbole. Haim led Israel to the final of the 2022 European Under-19 Championship, losing 3-1 to England after extra time, before taking largely the same group to the 2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Argentina, where Israel knocked out Brazil on the way to the semi-finals.

Goren, born in Savyon on March 15, 2009, is the player Israeli football now watches most closely from abroad. He began at Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth ranks at eight before his family relocated to Spain, where he passed Barcelona's academy trials at 14 and joined La Masia in 2023.

He has since progressed through Barcelona's junior sides as a technically gifted attacking midfielder, comfortable as a No. 8, a false nine or on the left, and signed his first professional contract with the club as a teenager still a year shy of senior football.

That senior football arrived this preseason. Goren came off the bench for Barcelona in a 4-1 friendly win over Europa CE at the Joan Gamper training complex, the club's opening match of preparations for the 2026/27 campaign under Hansi Flick, who fielded a squad heavy on academy prospects with several first-team regulars rested.

According to ONE, Goren has since taken part in a closed Barcelona training match and is expected to travel with the squad to the club's pre-season training camp in England — another marker of how quickly his stock has risen inside the club.

The Pedri comparison is not new, and Goren has addressed it himself. "Both of us play position 8 and manage the game," he told Sport5 earlier this year. "Many people say our playing style reminds one another." He was quick to add some perspective: "But that's Pedri. There's still much to aspire to."

For Haim, the priority is making sure Israel does not lose track of Goren as Barcelona's development machine takes over. The midfielder has already earned seven caps and a goal for Israel's Under-17s and three more at Under-19 level, and the federation clearly wants him locked into the senior pathway even as his club career accelerates in Catalonia.

Nobody in Tel Aviv or Barcelona is pretending Goren is the finished product Haim's comparison implies — the coach's own caveat, that he needs to add goals to his game, made that clear. But for a country that has produced few genuine La Masia prospects, a teenager drawing Xavi and Iniesta comparisons from his national-team coach is news worth savoring.

title: Israel basketball chief to club owner: if we're corrupt, go to the police
dek: Amos Frishman pushes back on Ofer Yanay's repeated corruption claims as the row over naturalizing American center Dan Oturu for the national team spills into public view.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Yanay's version of the naturalization dispute
Eurohoops - Ofer Yannay, Hapoel Tel Aviv owner

body: Amos Frishman has had enough of being called corrupt. The chairman of the Israel Basketball Association used an interview with ONE to fire back at Hapoel Tel Aviv owner Ofer Yanay, telling him that if he genuinely believes the association is corrupt, the answer is simple: go to the police, not the airwaves.

"You can't just keep saying, over and over, that we're corrupt," Frishman said. "It bothered me because Ofer keeps attacking the basketball association without end. If the association really is corrupt, he should go to the police and let them look into it properly."

The clash traces back to the association's naturalized-player system, which determines which foreign-born player can be fast-tracked for Israeli citizenship and eligibility for the national team. Frishman said the board asked him to set up a committee to establish the criteria, insisting the group only discussed general principles rather than specific candidates.

Yanay tells a more pointed version of events. In a companion interview with ONE, the Hapoel Tel Aviv owner said Frishman himself had approached him months earlier about naturalizing American-born center Dan Oturu as the club's next candidate, and that he sank roughly two million dollars into meeting the league's requirements, including signing Oturu to a contract without a buyout clause.

According to Yanay, the process stalled once rival clubs realized Oturu would be the one to benefit. He says pressure then built to rewrite the rules so the naturalization advantage would be reserved for what he called elite clubs, not Hapoel Tel Aviv.

Asked directly about Oturu, Frishman was more measured than dismissive. "He's a great player," he said, "but there's still a way to go before he becomes the national team's next naturalized player." It was a notable hedge from the man who oversees the committee deciding exactly that question.

The interview ranged well beyond the naturalization fight. Frishman said the association is working on a new arrangement to help players secure accommodations for army service up to age 30, with eligibility to be confirmed through medical checks carried out by the national team's own doctor.

He also addressed the situation of Deni Avdija, the Portland Trail Blazers forward and Israel's highest-profile NBA export, saying a back injury has complicated insurance arrangements around his national-team availability. "Only Portland can decide whether he comes," Frishman said, a reminder that Avdija's club holds the final word regardless of what Tel Aviv wants.

On the administrative side, Frishman confirmed the league's management has signed a one-year extension to run the competition, a routine item that nonetheless underlines how much organizational business is riding on an association currently fending off public accusations of corruption from one of its most prominent club owners.

Frishman closed by returning to his central point: that the sniping needs to either be substantiated through proper channels or dropped. "The most important thing," he said, "is that the basketball association stays clean." Whether that settles anything with Yanay remains to be seen — the two have clashed publicly before, and this dispute, tied directly to who gets the naturalization slot, is unlikely to be the last word.

title: Kangwa inducted into Hapoel Beer Sheva's hall of fame as Panathinaikos move nears
dek: The Zambian midfielder was honoured by the club he inspired to a league and cup double, just days before completing a big-money switch to Greece.
body: Kings Kangwa took his place in Hapoel Beer Sheva's hall of fame on Monday, a farewell gesture from the club as the Zambian midfielder puts the finishing touches on a move to Panathinaikos, ONE reports.
"Some moments in football will stay with you forever," Kangwa said, according to ONE. "I'm excited to enter Hapoel Beer Sheva's hall of fame. This recognition means more than words can describe."
The 27-year-old arrived in Beer Sheva in July 2024 from Red Star Belgrade and needed only two seasons to make himself one of the most influential imports in the club's recent history.

He was central to Hapoel's run to the Ligat Ha'al championship, and he also collected the State Cup and the League Cup during his spell at the club, honours ONE credits directly to his impact in midfield.
Kangwa's form was recognised individually too — he was named the league's Player of the Season, capping a campaign in which his goals and creativity repeatedly turned games in Beer Sheva's favour.

That body of work has now taken him to Greece. Panathinaikos have moved to sign him, with Greek and Zambian outlets, including ZamFoot, reporting a package in the region of €4 million and a contract running to 2030 — terms Hapoel Beer Sheva have not themselves confirmed.

Kangwa is not quite done in yellow and black, however. His last assignment for the club is expected to be Wednesday's European qualifier away to Víkingur Reykjavík, before the move to Athens is finalised.

For a club that has built its recent identity on developing and cashing in on overseas signings, Kangwa's hall of fame induction is a rare formal marker — an acknowledgement that his two years in the Negev left a lasting mark before he moves on to a bigger stage.

title: Eric García: winning the Champions League with Barcelona is next

body: Eric García barely had time to celebrate one trophy before setting his sights on the next. Days after coming off the bench to help Spain beat Argentina in the World Cup final, the Barcelona defender declared that lifting the Champions League with his club is now the target that matters most.
"Every player wants to win, to win titles, and that's what we're here for," García said, making clear that a World Cup winner's medal has not softened his hunger for European silverware.

García, 25, was one of eight Barcelona players in Spain's squad in the United States, and his World Cup involvement had an almost cinematic shape to it: he did not play a single minute until the final itself, when he was sent on during extra time at MetLife Stadium as Luis de la Fuente's side protected a 1-0 lead.

That lead came from a Ferran Torres strike in the 105th minute, breaking a stalemate that had run through 98 goalless minutes of normal time against a Lionel Messi-led Argentina. It handed Spain a second World Cup title, its first since 2010.

García was quick to point to the mental side of that breakthrough. He said it was "no coincidence" that Torres was the man who scored the winner, explaining that both of them have worked with a sports psychologist throughout their careers and crediting that preparation for helping the squad handle the pressure of a final.

He also reflected on his own long wait for a role in the tournament, saying he had spent the whole month preparing for a chance that might never come — and that it finally arrived in the biggest game of all.

The Barcelona academy product, who returned to the club after a loan spell at Girona and has re-established himself as a first-team regular in Hansi Flick's defence over the past two seasons, is due back at Barcelona's training ground on 12 August to begin pre-season work ahead of the new campaign.

For a player who has already won a World Cup, a La Liga title and a Copa del Rey with Barcelona, the Champions League is the conspicuous gap in his honours list — and, on this evidence, the one he is now most determined to close.

title: Ironi Tiberias officials indicted over banned blood transfusions to players
dek: Israel's anti-doping prosecutor says some players received infusions of more than 100ml with no medical justification, and is seeking bans of up to a lifetime for six club figures.

body: Israel's National Anti-Doping Agency has filed a formal indictment against six figures at Ironi Tiberias, alleging the Israeli Premier League club administered banned transfusions to players — in some cases more than 100 millilitres — with no medical justification whatsoever, ONE reported.

Named in the indictment are head coach Eliran Hodada, team manager Gabriel Cohen, fitness coach Shlomi Vaderro, technical director Chen Sol, suspended club owner Miki Bitan, and staff member Aviv Jibli. The agency's prosecutor argues the transfusions were given, in the words cited by ONE, "without medical consultation, without medical justification, without medical supervision, without proper medical protocol" — circumstances the prosecution called of "considerable severity."

The indictment also accuses club officials of obstructing the investigation and failing to comply with disciplinary orders once the probe was under way, on top of the core charges of administering and aiding the use of a prohibited method under the World Anti-Doping Code.

Prosecutors are seeking suspensions ranging from four to eight years up to permanent expulsion from organised sport, depending on each defendant's proven level of involvement, along with a minimum of 500,000 shekels in costs to cover the investigation and disciplinary process.

The case traces back to a complaint filed with the Israel Football Association by F.C. Ashdod on June 21, alleging Tiberias players had received more than 100 cubic centimetres of saline solution ahead of a match — a volume that breaches anti-doping infusion limits regardless of the substance's legality.

That complaint triggered an investigation, and on July 5 the anti-doping agency handed down interim suspensions to coach Hodada, technical director Sol, fitness coach Vaderro and five Tiberias players, pending the fuller inquiry that has now produced this week's indictment.

Tiberias have disputed the allegations from the outset, insisting the fluids administered fell under the 100cc threshold and describing them as "legal and entirely clean" under WADA rules. The club branded the interim suspensions "draconian" and "unprecedented," saying they were imposed without a hearing or laboratory testing, and has accused Ashdod of trying to engineer the league table through the complaint.

The transfusion case lands on a club already under severe strain. Tiberias are separately facing a second indictment, over alleged parallel "dual contract" payments to players outside official salary filings, with the association's prosecution seeking a 30-point deduction that would send the team from mid-table to bottom of the standings.

Owner Bitan, already suspended over the transfusion allegations, has vowed to fight the case, with the club saying it will "confront all claims with confidence" at the disciplinary tribunal. A hearing date is expected to be set in the coming days.

For a club that was hit with a 14-point deduction over a previous financial breach only last season, the transfusion indictment adds a doping dimension to a disciplinary crisis that now threatens both Tiberias' league status and the careers of several of its staff.

title: Ironi Tiberias hits back at infusion-scandal charge sheet, calls it 'riddled with speculation'
dek: The Ligat Ha'al club says the Football Association's indictment over recovery infusions relies on assumptions rather than evidence, and accuses investigators of serious procedural failures.

verificationSources.label: ONE - club's formal response to the indictment
Ynet - prosecution seeks bans of six years to life

Emek Mynet - profile of owners Klemenzon and Bitan

body: Ironi Tiberias has come out swinging against the Israeli Football Association's disciplinary charge sheet in the club's infusion affair, dismissing the document as a work of guesswork rather than proof.

In a strongly worded statement carried by ONE, the Ligat Ha'al club said the indictment was "riddled with continuous hypotheses, circumstantial assessments and attempts to create an atmosphere, instead of relying on solid facts and evidence."

Central to the club's defence is a point it wants readers not to lose sight of: there is no allegation of banned or dangerous substances. "There is no use of forbidden materials," the club said. "The indictment does not deal with poisoning, forbidden materials or drugs" — the case, it insists, turns solely on whether players received routine intravenous saline for recovery.

Tiberias went further, claiming the prosecution's own document concedes it holds no scientific documentation of the quantities administered to players, and instead rests on what the club called "conservative assumptions" and average estimates rather than measured fact.

The club also accused investigators of "serious failures" in how the probe was conducted, alleging premature bias against Tiberias, breaches of fundamental due-process rights, and a failure to properly summon or question key club officials before conclusions were drawn.

The affair dates back to a complaint filed with the Football Association by Ashdod, alleging Tiberias players received more than 100cc of saline solution ahead of a playoff match between the two sides — a complaint that triggered the wider investigation.
The fallout was immediate: the club's head coach and five players were provisionally suspended in early July while the association's prosecution built its case, before the formal indictment followed.

According to Ynet, the association's prosecution is seeking severe sanctions against those implicated, with suspensions sought ranging from six years up to lifetime bans for individuals connected to the club.

Tiberias has also pressed a selective-enforcement argument, saying at least one senior player told investigators that recovery infusions of this kind are common practice in Israeli football and named another established top-flight club where he says he experienced the same treatment — evidence the club claims has sat with the association for weeks without triggering a parallel inquiry.
"There cannot be one law for Tiberias and another for established clubs with large budgets," the club has argued in earlier statements on the affair, a theme it repeated in Monday's response.

The club is owned by businessmen Arye Klemenzon and Miki Bitan, who took over Ironi Tiberias's management in 2021 through their Dorot insurance group and steered it from the lower divisions up to Ligat Ha'al promotion in 2024 — the status now under threat depending on how the case unfolds.

Tiberias says it will contest the charges before the football disciplinary tribunal with legal arguments and evidence of its own, with sanctions up to and including points deductions or relegation potentially on the table if the indictment is ultimately upheld.

title: Iffe Lundberg signs new contract with Maccabi Tel Aviv
dek: The Danish guard, a standout in last season's Israeli league title run, has agreed a two-year deal worth roughly $1.85m a season, with a club option for a third, ONE reports.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have moved to secure one of the driving forces behind last season's Israeli league title, agreeing a new contract with guard Iffe Lundberg, ONE reports.

The deal, reported by ONE on Monday, will keep the 31-year-old Dane in yellow for two more seasons, with the club holding an option for a third. ONE puts his salary at roughly $1.85 million a season before bonuses, a rise on the terms he signed when he first arrived in Tel Aviv.

Lundberg joined Maccabi last season from Partizan Belgrade, where he had just won the ABA League title under Zeljko Obradovic. He settled quickly into Oded Katash's rotation and became one of the team's most reliable perimeter options, the kind of player the club chairman openly credits with steadying the roster through a demanding year.

His production backs up the faith: 11.0 points and 3.6 assists a game in the EuroLeague, rising to 17.5 points and 4.0 assists in Israeli league play, according to ONE. He was singled out as one of the standout performers of the playoff final as Maccabi claimed the domestic championship.
"I am very excited to continue this journey with Maccabi," Lundberg said. "This is where I can fulfil my potential."
Club chairman Shimon Mizrahi framed the extension as part of a broader philosophy. "Signing Iffe Lundberg reinforces our continuity principle," he said.

Katash, who has leaned on Lundberg as a vocal presence in the locker room as much as a scorer, added: "We are very happy Iffe continues with us. He is an experienced leader who has integrated very well with the team."

Lundberg's path to Tel Aviv ran through some of Europe's biggest clubs. He won a Danish championship with Horsens IC, played for CSKA Moscow and Virtus Bologna, and in 2022 became the first Dane to appear in an NBA game, turning out for the Phoenix Suns before returning to Europe.

With the extension in place, Maccabi head into pre-season with their backcourt anchored around a player who has already shown he can produce when games matter most, a reassuring signal for a club still shaping the rest of its roster before the new EuroLeague campaign.

title: Tomer Hemed emerges as candidate for Brighton assistant coach role
dek: The Israeli forward turned academy coach is reportedly in the running to replace Andrew Crofts, who left the Amex for Tottenham, according to ONE.

verificationSources.label: We Are Brighton – 8 contenders to replace Andrew Crofts

body: Tomer Hemed built a second Brighton career from the bottom up, taking charge of the club's under-18s after hanging up his boots. Now, according to ONE, he is being spoken of as a contender for a job several rungs higher: assistant head coach to Fabian Hurzeler on the Seagulls' first team.

The vacancy opened when Andrew Crofts left the Amex this month to join Roberto De Zerbi's new coaching staff at Tottenham, ending a 13-year association with Brighton that took him from midfielder to Hurzeler's trusted assistant. The club confirmed the departure itself, thanking Crofts as he moves on to reunite with De Zerbi in north London.

ONE reports that Hemed is among the names under consideration to fill the role — a striking twist for a player who retired from professional football only a few years ago and chose to stay inside Brighton's academy set-up rather than chase a late playing move elsewhere.

Hemed's route back to relevance has been built quietly. He signed for Brighton from Almería in 2015, scored 11 league goals in the club's promotion-winning 2016-17 campaign, and finished his Albion playing career with 33 goals in 108 appearances before retiring to join the academy staff as a coach and mentor to the club's younger players.

He worked his way onto the under-18s' bench, initially as an assistant, then stepped into caretaker charge alongside Steve Menzies when head coach Bjorn Hamberg left in January to take the manager's job at Sweden's Elfsborg. Hemed has since been confirmed as head coach of the age group in his own right.

According to ONE, his first full season in sole charge produced a fourth-place league finish and a record points total for the squad — form the club can point to as evidence he is developing fast, whatever is ultimately decided about the first-team post. Hemed said finishing fourth "demonstrates the commitment, resilience and belief shown by players and staff daily."

Not everyone is convinced the jump makes sense just yet. The Brighton fan outlet wearebrighton.com, which also listed Hemed among the contenders for Crofts' old job, cautioned that leaping from under-18s coaching to a Premier League first-team bench "would be quite the leap" — a reminder that a shortlist mention is a long way from an appointment.

Brighton have not put a public timeline on the decision beyond indicating one will come soon, and no formal shortlist or interview process has been confirmed. If Hemed misses out, he stays exactly where he has spent the past two years: developing the next generation of Albion players, some of whom he may yet end up coaching again at a higher level regardless.

title: Dibah returns to defence as Hapoel Haifa rotate for Tiberias test

body: George Dibah is set to return to the heart of Hapoel Haifa's defence when Chaim Silbes's side take on Ironi Tiberias in round two of the Toto Cup on Tuesday, with the coach using the low-stakes fixture to freshen up a squad that is only two days removed from a derby win over Maccabi Haifa.

ONE reports that Dibah will come back into the centre of the back line in place of the Croatian defender Dario Zuparic, while Sally Pahima is pencilled in to open as the link player just behind Yoad Gonen, who leads the line as the out-and-out striker.

Dor Malul, the 37-year-old captain, continues at right-back, with Noam Cohen filling in on the left side of the back four as Silbes spreads minutes around a squad still shaking off the effects of Sunday's derby.

"We're playing Tiberias tomorrow in the Toto Cup, and it's an important part of our preparation," Silbes said, according to the source, making clear he intends to rotate broadly and manage his players' workload rather than field a full-strength XI.
Itai Zafrani, the 19-year-old forward on loan from Maccabi Tel Aviv since the summer, remains sidelined through injury and will again miss out.

The rotation comes on the back of a thrilling 3-2 win over Maccabi Haifa in the Haifa derby that opened the 2026/27 Toto Cup. Gonen struck the opener, Noam Steitman turned the ball into his own net for Hapoel's second, and Alon Torgeman curled in a free-kick to make it 3-0 before Maccabi rallied late to make the scoreline respectable.

Tiberias arrive at the fixture in form of their own. Ironi Tiberias came from behind to beat Bnei Sakhnin 2-1 in their opening match, with Iyad Abu Abeid's 37th-minute strike cancelled out by Ron Unger before Mansour Badji completed the turnaround two minutes later.

Now in its 42nd edition, the Toto Cup remains Israeli football's third-ranked domestic competition, and while the destination of the trophy is not Silbes's priority this week, the minutes and match sharpness on offer make it a useful staging post before the league season resumes in earnest.

title: Israeli teenager Orian Goren joins Barcelona's senior squad for England training camp
dek: Days after his first-team debut, the 17-year-old midfielder has been included in Hansi Flick's travelling party to St George's Park.
body: Orian Goren boarded a flight with Barcelona's senior squad on Monday, one of a handful of teenagers included in Hansi Flick's travelling party for a preseason training camp in England — a reward, ONE reports, for the way the 17-year-old Israeli has forced his way into the coach's plans this summer.

The camp is based at St George's Park in Staffordshire, the English FA's national football centre, where the squad is due to train through August 2 before a friendly against Birmingham City at St Andrew's on July 31. Barcelona previously used the facility to prepare during their treble-winning 2014/15 campaign.

Goren's invitation follows his first senior appearance for the club, coming off the bench in a closed-doors friendly against the Catalan side UE Europa that Barcelona won 4-1. He was praised afterwards for a positive impact in his minutes on the pitch, according to Spanish reporting relayed by ONE.

Born in Savyon on March 15, 2009, Goren came through Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth system before Barcelona brought him into La Masia in 2023. He signed his first professional contract with the club at 16, and has since been capped by Israel at both under-17 and under-19 level.

The Spanish paper Sport has previously described him as the most technically gifted player in Barcelona's youth ranks, drawing comparisons — stylistically, as an attacking midfielder comfortable drifting to the left — with academy graduates such as Andrés Iniesta and Pedri.

The timing has helped his cause. Barcelona are missing a string of first-team regulars who spent the summer at the World Cup: Pedri, Gavi, Dani Olmo and Lamine Yamal were all part of the Spain squad that won the tournament on July 19, and are only trickling back into training in stages.

That has left gaps for Flick to fill from within, and the German has made a point of leaning on La Masia products in the meantime. "La Masia is how we do things," he said of his approach to blooding academy talent during preseason.

For Goren, a place on the plane to England is not a guarantee of more first-team minutes, but it puts him in daily training alongside the club's senior professionals during a period when squad places are genuinely up for grabs.

Barcelona's stay in England continues with further preseason work before the group returns to Spain to prepare for the new La Liga season, with Goren's next appearances likely to offer the clearest sign yet of how far Flick is willing to trust him.

title: Israeli shooting federation chief lands on world body panel alongside Lebanese official
dek: Michael Roher's appointment to a top ISSF committee that also seats a Lebanese Olympic Committee representative comes as Israel and Lebanon pursue a US-brokered framework agreement, ONE reports.

body: Israel's shooting federation chairman has, on paper at least, become a colleague of a Lebanese Olympic official, ONE reported on Monday — an unusual crossover for two countries with no diplomatic ties, arriving as their governments pursue a fragile new understanding.

According to the outlet, Michael Roher, chairman of the Israel Shooting Federation, was named temporary chair of the International Shooting Sport Federation's Judicial and Constitutional Committee, the body's internal legal and statutory panel.
Sitting alongside him on the same committee, ONE reports, is Boutros Jalakh, a representative of the Lebanese Olympic Committee, who was appointed a temporary member.

The reshuffle was triggered by the resignation of Biserka Vrbek, the Croatian official who had chaired the ISSF's statutes and eligibility work; Vrbek, an Olympic shooter at the 1984 Games before moving into federation administration, had been serving a term running through 2026.

ONE frames the appointments explicitly against the backdrop of the recently signed framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon, brokered by the United States, which aims to wind down decades of hostilities between the IDF and Hezbollah.

Sport has occasionally offered a rare, low-stakes channel for contact between countries that otherwise have no formal relations, since technical federations like the ISSF operate under international sporting statutes rather than bilateral diplomacy.

There is no indication in ONE's report that Roher and Jalakh have yet met or communicated directly; the appointments simply place both officials on the same committee roster within the Lausanne-based governing body for Olympic shooting sports.

The story is a small but symbolically notable footnote to the broader diplomatic track between Jerusalem and Beirut, illustrating how a state-to-state accord can filter down into corners of international sport far removed from politics.

title: 1,400 Hapoel Tel Aviv fans set to travel to Razgrad for Conference League return leg
dek: The away end at Ludogorets Arena sold out fast as Hapoel look to protect a 2-0 first-leg lead in Bulgaria on Thursday, in the club's first European campaign in 12 years.
body: About 1,400 Hapoel Tel Aviv supporters are due to make the trip to Bulgaria for Thursday's Conference League second qualifying round return leg against Ludogorets, ONE reports, with the away allocation at the Huvepharma Arena in Razgrad selling out quickly once tickets went on sale.

It caps a fortnight of remarkable fan mobilisation for a club that had not featured in European competition for 12 years. Roughly 5,000 Hapoel supporters travelled to Miskolc in Hungary for the first leg on July 23, effectively adopting the DVTK stadium as a raucous home end, and the club came away with a 2-0 win courtesy of goals from Omri Altman and Chico.

Hapoel play home European fixtures in Hungary rather than in Israel under UEFA's current arrangements, a workaround that has not dampened enthusiasm among the club's fan base — if anything, ONE suggests it has sharpened the appetite to follow the team on the road.

Coach Elyaniv Barda is expected to send out largely the same XI that beat Ludogorets in the first leg, according to the report, wary of tinkering with a side that controlled long stretches of that match. Barda, the former Hapoel and Israel international striker, took over at the club and is overseeing its first continental run in over a decade.
One absentee remains Roy Korin, who according to ONE is continuing his recovery and rehabilitation work and was not part of the group that beat Ludogorets in Hungary.

Off the pitch, the report notes the club is actively working the market for foreign reinforcements, with particular focus on Brazil, as it looks to strengthen a squad that will need depth if it advances into the third qualifying round.

Ludogorets, who won 14 straight Bulgarian championships before finishing third last season, are no pushovers at home and will throw everything at overturning the deficit in front of their own supporters. But a 2-0 cushion, according to the report, has left Hapoel's management confident they can get the job done and complete the aggregate qualification.

With away days like this drawing four-figure travelling contingents twice in a row, Hapoel's return to Europe already looks like more than a novelty — it is shaping into one of the bigger stories of the Israeli football summer, regardless of Thursday's outcome in Razgrad.

title: Maccabi Rishon LeZion strengthen frontcourt with Nathan Kuta signing
dek: The Israeli club has added the Dutch-Belgian big man after two productive seasons in France's second division.
body: Maccabi Rishon LeZion have added size and rebounding to their frontcourt, announcing the signing of Dutch-Belgian big man Nathan Kuta ahead of the new Ligat Winner season, ONE reports.

The 26-year-old, who stands 2.04 metres (6-foot-8), arrives in Israel after two seasons with Orléans in France's second-tier LNB Pro B, where he established himself as one of the division's more productive frontcourt players.
Last season at Orléans, Kuta averaged 12.1 points, 6.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game, numbers that made him a target for clubs looking to add a physical presence in the paint.

Before his stint in France, Kuta spent three seasons with Spirou Charleroi in Belgium's top division, the club where he first built his reputation as an aggressive rebounder and finisher around the rim.

In its announcement, Maccabi Rishon LeZion described the new arrival as a player who "brings significant presence in the paint, plays with considerable power, toughness and intensity, dominates rebounding battles and finishes at high percentages near the rim."

Kuta is also a Netherlands international, having represented the country in World Cup and European Championship qualifying windows, giving him experience at senior national-team level alongside his club career.
No contract length or financial terms were disclosed in the club's announcement.
The move adds another size option to Rishon LeZion's roster as the club builds toward the upcoming Ligat Winner campaign.

title: Tambi Segas returns to Hapoel Umm al-Fahm for second spell
dek: The well-travelled midfielder rejoins the Liga Alef North club ahead of 2026/27, reuniting with coach Tomer Kashtan after a journeyman few years since leaving Bnei Sakhnin.

verificationSources.label: ONE - תאמבי סגס חתם בהפועל אום אל פאחם

body: Hapoel Umm al-Fahm have brought back a familiar face for their 2026/27 Liga Alef North campaign, with ONE reporting that midfielder Tambi Segas has signed for the club for a second time.

The 32-year-old joins a squad being rebuilt under coach Tomer Kashtan, who previously worked with Segas during a spell at Kafr Qasim. No contract length or financial terms were disclosed in the report.

Segas, who is from the Circassian community of Kafr Kama in the Lower Galilee, came up through Bnei Sakhnin's youth academy and went on to make his name as one of the club's breakout talents, spending four and a half seasons in the first team.

His move from Sakhnin took him to Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv, who were State Cup holders at the time. Across two and a half seasons in the Hatikva Quarter, Segas scored in a Europa League qualifier against Neftçi Baku, before being relegated with Bnei Yehuda to the National League in 2020/21.

The years since have taken him around the Israeli game: a stint at Kafr Qasim under Kashtan, an earlier spell at Umm al-Fahm in 2023/24 in which he scored four goals, a season at Maccabi Herzliya, and most recently Hapoel Hadera, who were relegated to Liga Alef during his time there.
Segas also represented Israel's youth national team, earning five caps earlier in his career.

Umm al-Fahm themselves survived a difficult recent period after the Israel Football Association froze relegations during the season disrupted by the Iron Swords war, and the club is now building toward next season with Kashtan in charge and several familiar names, Segas among them, returning to the fold.

title: Yavne municipality ends saga with merger of Maccabi and Beitar football clubs
dek: Mayor Roi Gabbay brokers a deal uniting Maccabi Tzvi Yavne and Beitar Yavne under one banner, ending months of uncertainty over the city's senior football scene.

verificationSources.label: ONE - primary report on the Yavne merger announcement

Wikipedia - Beitar Yavne F.C. club background

body: Yavne's municipality has drawn a line under months of behind-the-scenes wrangling over the city's senior football set-up, brokering a formal merger between its two adult clubs, Maccabi Tzvi Yavne and Beitar Yavne, ONE reported.

The agreement was signed off at a meeting in the office of Mayor Roi Gabbay, bringing together two clubs that had both competed in Liga Alef South last season - one tier below Liga Leumit - and had increasingly found themselves competing for the same pool of players, sponsors and civic backing in a single small city.

Under the terms of the deal, the unified operation will play on under the Maccabi Tzvi Yavne name, with the club's existing badge and colours preserved. Beitar Yavne's registered association will stop fielding a separate senior team for the length of the agreement, folding its playing operation into its former cross-town rival.

The new leadership line-up blends figures from both sides. Asher Shetrit, who chaired Beitar Yavne, takes over as chairman of the merged body, while Asaf Ohana, formerly Maccabi's chief executive, stays on to run day-to-day and football operations. Felix Alimelech, Avi Ohion, Shalom Swissa and Avraham Biton were named to the board, with attorney Ram Sharon and Gal Pershker appointed to the audit committee, according to ONE.

Gabbay, who hosted the signing, framed the deal as a pooling of long-divided civic resources. "We successfully united forces and resources for one shared goal - to push Maccabi Yavne toward achievements," the mayor said.

The word "saga" in ONE's own framing points to a messier backdrop than a simple handshake. The merger comes after other Liga Bet clubs had separately pressed competing claims to Beitar Yavne's Liga Alef status, ONE reported, adding administrative uncertainty to a city that had ended up fielding two senior teams in the same division, sharing the same municipal stadium.

That overlap was itself a fairly recent development. Beitar Yavne reached Liga Alef for the first time in its history only ahead of the 2024-25 season, stepping into a vacancy left when Adom Ashdod withdrew from professional football, ONE reported at the time - a rapid rise that suddenly put two Yavne clubs in the same tier as Maccabi Tzvi Yavne, a club with a far longer history at that level.

For a city of under 60,000 people, running two parallel Liga Alef operations had strained both clubs' budgets and, at times, left playing squads on both sides thin - the kind of duplication municipal officials have periodically tried to resolve in Israel's lower leagues.

Practical details - fixtures, squad composition and exactly where the new Maccabi Tzvi Yavne will sit when Liga Alef South resumes - remain to be settled. But with the municipality's backing and a shared boardroom now in place, Yavne heads into the close season with one football club to build around rather than two competing for the same limited resources.

title: Abukasis says it's disappointing that foreigners won't come to Sakhnin
dek: The Bnei Sakhnin coach says the club has made attractive offers to overseas targets this preseason, only to be turned down as it searches for a defender and a striker.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - Sakhnin's summer camp and defensive search

body: Bnei Sakhnin's manager, Yossi Abukasis, has admitted this summer's recruitment drive has left him frustrated, saying overseas targets keep turning down good offers to move to Israel.

"We are very short on players, we have young players from the youth ranks. There are things that are not in our control," Abukasis said, according to ONE. "We offer nice proposals to foreign players who decide not to come to Israel. It disappoints me."

Abukasis, who took over at Sakhnin in February, is currently overseeing a preseason training camp in Hungary as the club prepares for the return of Ligat Ha'Al action, with the squad still short of reinforcements in key positions.

The club is actively working to add both a defender and a forward from abroad. Among the names linked is striker William Agada, who spent a loan spell at Hapoel Haifa in the 2020-21 season and, per ONE, has again attracted interest from Haifa this summer — though a deal for Sakhnin has proven difficult to advance.

Reluctance among foreign players to relocate to Israel has been a recurring theme across the league since the outbreak of war in October 2023, and Abukasis's comments suggest it remains a live obstacle for a club outside the traditional top tier trying to compete for value signings.

On the players already through the door, ONE reports Lithuanian arrival Modestas Vorobjovas has made a stronger early impression than fellow new signing Carlitos, giving Abukasis at least some options as he shapes his squad for the campaign ahead.

With preseason friendlies approaching, the coach's frustration underlines the practical squeeze facing Sakhnin: a threadbare group leaning on academy graduates while trying to close gaps at both ends of the pitch before the new Ligat Ha'Al season gets under way.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem eye Maccabi Haifa midfielder Itay Ahoud on loan
dek: The capital club is chasing the young Haifa academy product to strengthen its midfield, but the move hinges on a loan decision that is entirely out of its hands.

body: Hapoel Jerusalem's summer rebuild has a new name attached to it: Itay Ahoud, the young Maccabi Haifa midfielder who has emerged as a target for the capital club as it looks to add depth before the new Ligat Ha'al season, ONE reports.

The interest is real, but the deal is not close. According to the report, Ahoud's move to Jerusalem cannot advance until Maccabi Haifa itself decides whether it even wants to loan the player out this season — a call the Haifa club has yet to make. Until then, Hapoel Jerusalem can only wait.

Ahoud, born on September 21, 2006, is one of Maccabi Haifa's own academy products and has been earmarked as a rare talent in the club's youth pipeline, having previously been named the club's outstanding player at youth level. He operates in central midfield, comfortable both screening the back four and stepping into possession.

He is not unfamiliar with senior football away from Haifa. Ahoud spent last season out on loan at Hapoel Kfar Saba, gaining regular first-team minutes, before returning to Sammy Ofer Stadium ahead of this campaign to compete for a place in the Haifa squad — which is precisely why the champions have been in no rush to sanction another loan.

For Hapoel Jerusalem, adding a combative young midfielder on loan would fit a squad still being reshaped after a difficult 2025/26 campaign, which ended with the club 12th and stuck in the bottom playoff group.

Part of that reshaping was enforced rather than chosen. Ziv Arie, the coach most closely identified with Hapoel Jerusalem over the past seven years, left the club in the spring and signed a one-year deal to take charge of Maccabi Petah Tikva in May.

The two clubs' paths are about to cross again regardless of how the Ahoud pursuit plays out. Hapoel Jerusalem are due to face Maccabi Petah Tikva in the Toto Cup, which will mark Arie's first game back against his former team since the split.

The club has chosen not to mark the occasion with a farewell ceremony at that fixture, judging a Toto Cup tie too low-key an occasion for a coach it regards as one of the defining figures in its recent history. Jerusalem instead intend to honour Arie properly at a league match later in the season, when the stadium is fuller and the stakes are higher.
