title: Israel's U18 basketball team beats France as Zilberstein hails their athleticism
dek: Coach Nadav Zilberstein says his young side has more raw athletic talent than any other Israeli national team he has worked with, after Aviv Aronov led a 91-77 win over France at the U18 EuroBasket in Trento.

verificationSources.label: FIBA — France vs Israel, Group Phase, FIBA U18 EuroBasket 2026
FIBA — Israel team page, FIBA U18 EuroBasket 2026

body: Israel's under-18 men opened their European basketball championship campaign with a statement: two wins from two games, the second a 91-77 defeat of France that head coach Nadav Zilberstein said reflects a squad with more raw athletic ability than any other Israeli national team he has worked with.

The win over France came in Trento, one of two host cities for the FIBA U18 EuroBasket 2026, and moved Israel to the top of Group A, Sport5 reported. Aviv Aronov, the tournament's early breakout scorer, again led the way, finishing as Israel's top scorer with 28 points, according to FIBA's official game record, against a French side that reached last year's European final.

It followed an even more dramatic opener. Israel needed overtime to beat Greece 93-84 in their tournament curtain-raiser, with Aronov contributing 30 points and six assists and David Musis adding 26 points as Israel twice clawed back from double-digit deficits.

Discussing the France win, Zilberstein pointed to that resilience as much as the talent. "We are an excellent team, capable of doing beautiful things if we stay focused together," he said, according to Sport5 — before adding the line that will carry weight with Israeli basketball followers: relative to the country's other national teams, this group has "exceptional athletic talent."

He reserved specific praise for Aronov, calling him "a very special player and scorer" who is "constantly committed" on the floor, while noting — with the candour of a coach managing a teenager's game — that he sometimes forces shots he does not need to take.

Zilberstein also framed the tournament in developmental terms, telling Sport5 the group is being shaped with an eye on eventually feeding Israel's senior national teams, and describing the squad as psychologically tough enough not to be rattled by a deficit — a trait borne out against Greece.

Israel next face Austria to close out the group phase, with Zilberstein flagging Wednesday's follow-up fixture as the one that matters most for carrying the momentum forward. title: Hapoel Tel Aviv register interest in free agent big man Maxi Kleber
dek: The Israeli runners-up have added the German forward-center, fresh off nine NBA seasons with Dallas and the Lakers, to their list of targets as he weighs a return to Europe.

verificationSources.label: Heavy.com - Lakers linked to Kleber Europe move report

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have joined the chase for Maxi Kleber, according to a report from ONE, which says the Israeli runners-up have registered interest in the German forward-center as he weighs his next move following nine seasons in the NBA.

The 34-year-old, 2.08-metre big man became an unrestricted free agent this summer once his contract with the Los Angeles Lakers ran out, and has been exploring a return to Europe rather than chasing another NBA deal. BasketNews reported earlier this summer that Kleber was testing his market in the EuroLeague, and ONE's report marks the first time his name has been specifically tied to Hapoel Tel Aviv.

Kleber's road to the NBA ran through Germany and Spain: he came up at Würzburg, spent time at Obradoiro in the Spanish league, then had two seasons at Bayern Munich before Dallas gave him his NBA break. He spent the bulk of his American career with the Mavericks, before being included in the blockbuster deal that sent Luka Dončić to the Lakers in February 2025.

His numbers had faded by the end: after averaging 6.0 points and 4.2 rebounds across his NBA regular-season career, with 5.9 points and 3.6 rebounds in the playoffs, Kleber managed just 2.0 points and 2.0 rebounds in 43 games in his final campaign with the Lakers.

The interest comes as Hapoel Tel Aviv reshape their EuroLeague roster for next season. The club has already announced the signing of forward Zach LeDay on a two-year deal after his productive year with Olimpia Milano, and separately confirmed a contract extension for center Dan Oturu. At the same time, center Johnathan Motley is reported to be in advanced talks to leave for Crvena Zvezda, leaving the frontcourt in flux.

Nothing has been signed, and ONE's report describes interest rather than an agreement, so any move for Kleber remains speculative for now. Hapoel Tel Aviv, runners-up in recent Israeli league finals, are nonetheless continuing to shop actively for reinforcements as they build toward another European campaign.

title: Hapoel Emek sign young guard Ran Solomon in return to the top flight
dek: The 21-year-old Hapoel Holon academy product joins Sharon Avrahami's squad after a season down in Liga Artzit with Hapoel Chevel Modiin
body: Hapoel Emek have added a young guard to Sharon Avrahami's roster, confirming the signing of 21-year-old Ran Solomon ahead of the new Winner League season, ONE reports.

Solomon, who stands 1.85m, is a product of the Hapoel Holon youth system and spent time with the Holon senior squad before dropping down a level last season to Hapoel Chevel Modiin in Liga Artzit. His move to Hapoel Emek now brings him back into Israel's top flight.
"It is a great honour to join such a big team as Hapoel Emek," Solomon said following the signing. "I look forward to meeting the fans and hope to help the team achieve its goals."

Avrahami, who has overseen a productive rebuild in the Jezreel Valley, welcomed the addition in similarly warm terms. "I am very happy Ran is joining us," the coach said. "Ran is a young and talented player with a fighter's mentality, and I am confident he will integrate excellently with us."

The signing continues a busy close season for Hapoel Emek, who reached the Winner League playoff quarter-finals last term and have also recently brought in guard-forward C.J. Alby as they look to build on that run.

For Solomon, the move represents a chance to re-establish himself at the top level after a formative season in the third tier, arriving at a club that has shown it is prepared to trust younger players inside a squad built around Avrahami's system.

title: Vildoza turns down Maccabi Tel Aviv, signs with Partizan Belgrade
dek: The Argentine point guard, quietly explored by the yellow-and-blue as a backcourt option, has instead put pen to paper on a two-year deal with the Serbian giants after a short, rocky spell in Bologna.
body: Luca Vildoza will not be wearing yellow next season. The Argentine point guard, one of the names Maccabi Tel Aviv had quietly explored as a possible addition to their backcourt, has instead signed a two-year contract with Partizan Belgrade, ONE reported on Sunday.

According to the outlet, Maccabi had identified the 30-year-old as a leading candidate to strengthen the roster, but the club will now have to look elsewhere after Vildoza opted for the Serbian powerhouse instead.

The move caps a short and turbulent stint in Italy. Vildoza joined Virtus Bologna on a three-year contract last summer that included exit clauses, but left after just a single season once new coach Alex Mombro arrived and began reshaping the roster.

Partizan is not unfamiliar territory in a roundabout way. Vildoza has previously worn the colours of Crvena Zvezda, Partizan's fierce Belgrade rival, meaning he now becomes one of the rare players to have represented both clubs. He has also turned out for the two dominant forces of Greek basketball, Panathinaikos and Olympiacos, giving him a rare résumé across four of the most storied clubs in Serbian and Greek hoops.

The pedigree behind the move is considerable. Vildoza won a EuroLeague title with Panathinaikos in 2024, then lifted a Greek League crown with Olympiacos the following season while helping the Reds reach the EuroLeague Final Four. Earlier in his career he had spells at Baskonia and a brief run in the NBA with the Milwaukee Bucks.
Internationally, the point guard has been a fixture for Argentina, helping the Albiceleste reach the final of the 2019 FIBA World Cup and featuring for his country at the Tokyo Olympics.

For Maccabi Tel Aviv, the news means a return to the drawing board in the guard market as the club continues shaping its roster for the season ahead, with ONE's report making clear the interest in Vildoza did not progress beyond an early stage.

title: Abu Fani shines in Red Star Belgrade win as Hleihel scores again for Gangwon
dek: Mohammad Abu Fani impressed before being booked and substituted in Red Star Belgrade's 3-1 win over Vojvodina, while Abdallah Hleihel struck a stoppage-time goal for Gangwon in South Korea, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Press.rs – Abu Fani signs for Crvena zvezda

body: Israeli footballers turned in eye-catching performances across three different leagues over the weekend, with Mohammad Abu Fani drawing the most attention as his new club, Red Star Belgrade, brushed aside Vojvodina 3-1 in the Serbian SuperLiga, according to ONE.

Abu Fani, deployed in Red Star's midfield at the Rajko Mitić Stadium, set up three clear chances for teammates during his 62 minutes on the pitch before he was replaced. He also picked up a yellow card in the 43rd minute, one of the few blemishes on an otherwise composed display.

The Israel international arrived at Red Star on 1 July in a reported deal worth around €1 million from Ferencváros, with a further €300,000 in potential add-ons, signing a contract through June 2029. Sunday's fixture, part of the second round of the new Serbian season, offered an early glimpse of why the Belgrade giants were prepared to spend big to bring him in.

Elsewhere, another Israeli forward gave his club's supporters something to cheer even in defeat. Abdallah Hleihel - transliterated in some databases as Khalaihal - struck deep into stoppage time for Gangwon FC in a 2-1 defeat to FC Anyang in South Korea's K League 1.

The goal, arriving in the 90+6th minute, was Hleihel's seventh in the league this season, ONE reported, underlining the impact he has made since signing for Gangwon in January. Born in the Galilee town of Jish, Hleihel moved to South Korea from Bnei Sakhnin, where he had played since 2023.
In Moldova, defender Tomer Katz was in action as Politehnica UTM Chișinău fell 2-0 to city rivals Zimbru Chișinău, rounding out a mixed weekend for Israel's contingent of players based overseas.

Taken together, the results capture the scattered nature of Israel's football diaspora this summer: a marquee arrival settling in at one of the Balkans' biggest clubs, a Galilee-born striker finding the net regularly in East Asia, and a young defender learning his trade in Eastern Europe.

title: Salah, Vlahović and Alaba head a glut of big-name free agents still hunting for clubs
dek: Weeks into the European transfer window, ONE reports a striking list of decorated internationals remains without a contract, led by Liverpool's former talisman and two former Champions League winners.

verificationSources.label: Football Italia - Vlahović to leave Juventus
beIN Sports - Real Madrid confirm Alaba departure

body: Pre-season friendlies are underway and squad lists are all but finalised across Europe's major leagues, yet a striking number of decorated internationals remain without a club as the summer transfer window enters its final stretch. ONE ran through the list of proven, high-profile free agents this week, and it reads like a five-a-side team of champions.

The headline name is Mohamed Salah. The Egyptian forward, 34, left Liverpool as a free agent this summer after nine years at Anfield, and multiple Turkish and English outlets report he is closing in on a move to Beşiktaş. His camp had initially been linked with a lucrative switch to Saudi Arabia, but reports from Turkey suggest Salah and his family are reluctant to relocate to the Gulf and would prefer Istanbul.

Beşiktaş's club president has confirmed talks took place, while accusing Salah's representatives of raising their financial demands once the interest went public. Reported terms have ranged as high as €12.5 million a year, but as of this week no deal had been signed or officially announced by either side.

Dušan Vlahović is the other headline forward on the market. The Serbian striker's Juventus contract expired on June 30 after wage negotiations broke down — his camp had been seeking a base salary in the region of €8 million net plus significant signing bonuses, well above what Juventus was prepared to offer. Bayern Munich, Chelsea, Newcastle United and Barcelona have all made contact with his representatives, making the 26-year-old one of the most sought-after free agents of the summer.

David Alaba's situation is a reminder of how fast a career can turn. Real Madrid confirmed the Austrian defender's free-agent departure after five seasons in the Spanish capital, during which he won two La Liga titles and two Champions League crowns following his own free transfer from Bayern Munich in 2021. A ruptured ACL suffered in December 2023 cost him roughly 13 months on the sidelines and has clouded the end of his time at the Bernabéu. He leaves alongside club captain Dani Carvajal, whose own free-agent exit from Madrid was confirmed separately.

Leon Goretzka completes the list of headline departures. The German midfielder left Bayern Munich as a free agent after eight seasons once his contract expired this summer, ending a trophy-laden spell at the record Bundesliga champions. Juventus have been the most consistent suitors, reportedly discussing a deal worth around €7 million net plus a signing bonus near €10 million, though Arsenal, Tottenham, AC Milan and MLS side Chicago Fire have all been credited with interest at various points.

ONE frames the group as an unusually rich crop for any club still shopping this late in the window — proven winners and full internationals available without a transfer fee, at a stage of the summer when most rosters are supposed to be set.

None of the moves described is finished business. Salah's Beşiktaş switch, in particular, is still being negotiated rather than signed, and Vlahović's and Goretzka's next clubs remain unresolved as talks continue with several suitors apiece. The one certainty is that all four have already left their previous employers, and whichever teams do land them will be getting proven quality at no transfer cost.

title: Arsenal ready record-breaking wage to prise Vinicius Junior away from Real Madrid
dek: Sport5 reports the Gunners will break their pay structure to sign the Brazilian winger as his Real Madrid contract renewal stalls
body: Arsenal are prepared to tear up their own wage structure to land Vinicius Junior, according to a Sport5 report that says the club will dangle one of the richest contracts in its history to prise the Brazilian winger away from Real Madrid this summer.

The interest is not new, but the report frames it as Arsenal going "all the way" — willing to blow past their existing pay ceiling rather than let a stalled Real Madrid renewal become someone else's opportunity.

Vinicius, 26, is heading into the final year of the five-year deal he signed in 2022, and talks over an extension in Madrid have dragged without resolution. Real Madrid have offered around €20 million a year net to keep him, while the player and his camp are said to be holding out for closer to €30 million, according to Spanish reporting cited by Sport5 and Walla — with a further signing bonus reportedly discussed on top.

That gap has left the door ajar. Mikel Arteta has made the Brazilian his priority target to overhaul Arsenal's left flank, with Julián Álvarez, Bradley Barcola and Juan Diomande mentioned as alternative options should the move fail, Walla reported. Sky Sports and other British outlets have described Arsenal's stance as agreed "at all levels" internally, though talks between the two clubs remain at an early stage with no formal approach yet.

The scale of what it would take is the real story. Arsenal's current top earner, Bukayo Saka, sits on roughly £300,000 a week — a figure some British reports say Arsenal would need to nearly double, with a package in the region of £400,000 a week floated as the kind of offer required to get a deal done.

Real Madrid's own position adds pressure from the other side. Club president Florentino Pérez is said to be frustrated by the scale of Vinicius's wage demands, and with the player entering the last season of his contract, Madrid would reportedly rather sell for a fee now than risk losing him for nothing next summer. Spanish reports have floated a fee in the nine-figure range as the price Real Madrid would set.

Not everyone at the Bernabéu wants him gone. New head coach José Mourinho, who took over at the club in June, has said he wants his three biggest names retained, naming Vinicius alongside Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham as players who should stay regardless of the noise around them.

Arsenal have already been reshaping their forward options this summer, selling Leandro Trossard to Beşiktaş and bringing in Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. Gabriel Martinelli, the incumbent understudy on the left, managed only a single Premier League goal last season — underlining why Arteta wants an upgrade at almost any cost.

For now this remains speculation rather than an agreed transfer: no direct negotiations between the clubs have been confirmed, and Vinicius has previously said Real Madrid is "the club of my dreams." But with his contract situation unresolved and Arsenal signalling genuine intent, it is a story both clubs will be forced to address before the transfer window closes.

title: Dani Olmo rejects Roberto Ayala's apology over World Cup final punch
dek: Spain's title-winning midfielder says the Argentina assistant coach's explanation for striking him after the final whistle only proves he isn't truly sorry.
body: Dani Olmo has broken his silence on the ugliest postscript to Spain's World Cup triumph, dismissing Roberto Ayala's apology for striking him after the final whistle as insincere and, in his word, dishonest.

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final on July 19 at the 2026 World Cup, with substitute Ferran Torres scoring the winner in the 106th minute to secure the country's second world title. The celebrations were quickly overshadowed by ugly scenes on the pitch.

In the chaos that followed the final whistle, Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala, the former centre-back known as 'El Ratón', became involved in a confrontation with Olmo. Video that circulated widely on social media appeared to show Ayala grabbing Olmo and striking him, with some clips suggesting a blow to the face or throat.

Ayala later said he regretted the incident but pushed back on the characterisation of it, insisting it was 'more of a push than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be.' He also said the flashpoint was 'a reaction to something he said,' suggesting Olmo had provoked him verbally in the heat of the moment.

Olmo, quoted by ONE, rejected that framing outright. 'Someone who says they're sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, is surely not sorry, because he is lying,' he said. 'I didn't say anything to him, so he doesn't need to apologise.'

The Spain forward went further, arguing that genuine remorse cannot coexist with self-justification. 'What truly defines us is not the mistake, but the courage to take responsibility,' he said, adding that footballers carry a responsibility as role models for children and future generations watching the world's biggest stage.

Olmo also used the moment to reflect on how Spain won the tournament, crediting collective effort over individual brilliance. He pointed to the squad's rigorous preparation, fitness work, nutrition, rest management and mental conditioning as the real foundations of the triumph, rather than any single moment of magic.

The Ayala footage had already caused a stir beyond the two men directly involved. At least one prominent Argentina-focused account on social media reposted the clip in support of Ayala's actions, drawing a backlash from fans who argued there was no place for violence in football regardless of the result.

Ayala, a World Cup runner-up as a player with Argentina in 1990 and a veteran of a long career in Spain and Italy, has not offered a fuller apology since Olmo's comments were published. For now, the dispute stands as an awkward coda to a final that will otherwise be remembered for Torres' extra-time winner and Spain's second world title.

title: Arsenal prepare record contract to test Real Madrid's grip on Vinicius Junior
dek: The Telegraph reports Arsenal are ready to smash their wage structure for the Brazilian winger, exploiting a stalled contract standoff at the Bernabéu even as José Mourinho moves to convince him to stay.
body: Arsenal are preparing to offer Vinicius Junior a contract that would be the biggest in the club's history, the Telegraph reported at the weekend, as the Premier League club moves to test Real Madrid's grip on their increasingly restless Brazilian forward.

According to that report, picked up by ONE, Arsenal are ready to pay wages in excess of £400,000 a week to land the 26-year-old — a package designed to match or beat what he currently earns at the Bernabéu, with the club's hierarchy insisting finance will not be the obstacle if the move is pursued.

The audacious approach lands at a delicate moment in Vinicius's own contract saga with Real Madrid. He is currently on close to €15m a year net; Madrid have offered him €20m to extend, but the player is said to be holding out for nearer €30m net a season — north of £550,000 a week — leaving the two sides at an impasse, according to reporting widely carried in the English press this week.

Complicating any Arsenal move is Real Madrid's new head coach, José Mourinho, who has made clear internally that he wants to build his side around Vinicius rather than sell him, with the winger seen as central to the club's push for a 16th European Cup. Mourinho is reported to be ready to hand Vinicius greater on-pitch responsibility as a signal of his long-term importance to the project.

Vinicius himself, per recent Spanish media reporting, has indicated a preference to stay at Real Madrid rather than force his way out, even with the contract talks stalled. He and the club are due to sit down for further negotiations before the end of July.

None of that appears to have discouraged Arsenal. Manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta have been searching for reinforcements out wide since Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, and Vinicius's contract standoff in Madrid has been read at the Emirates as a rare opening to pursue a marquee attacker who would ordinarily be unavailable.

The Athletic has reported that pursuing a move for Vinicius has been approved "at all levels" of the Arsenal hierarchy, though there have been no club-to-club talks with Real Madrid yet and no guarantee the interest develops into a concrete bid.

Vinicius's contract at the Bernabéu runs to June 2027. Should he enter next season without a signed extension, Real Madrid could face a choice between cashing in on one of their prize assets or risking losing him for nothing a year later — precisely the scenario Arsenal appear to be positioning themselves to exploit.

title: Pogačar seals fifth Tour de France title as van der Poel wins Paris finale
dek: The Slovenian joins Anquetil, Merckx, Hinault and Indurain on five Tour wins, beating Remco Evenepoel by 6:26 as Mathieu van der Poel took a dramatic final stage around Montmartre.
body: Tadej Pogačar rolled into Paris on Sunday to claim his fifth Tour de France title, joining Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain as the only riders in the race's history to win it five times.

The 27-year-old Slovenian, riding for UAE Team Emirates-XRG, becomes the youngest of that group to reach five titles. Lance Armstrong's seven victories remain stripped from the record books following his doping conviction, leaving the quintet as cycling's recognised benchmark.

Pogačar had the race won well before the final stage, finishing 6 minutes 26 seconds clear of Belgium's Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) in the general classification, with Mexico's Isaac del Toro completing the podium in third. According to ONE, he had shown superiority across every discipline of the three-week race, from the high mountains to the time trials and the flat stages, mixing raw strength with sharp tactical judgement.

The final stage itself, though largely ceremonial for the yellow jersey, was anything but processional. Organisers shortened stage 21 to 88.7km after police normally assigned to the Paris route were redeployed to fight wildfires in the south of France, reshaping the finale into three laps of a circuit built around the cobbled Butte Montmartre before the traditional finish on the Champs-Élysées.

Repeated attacks on the Montmartre climb turned the run-in into one of the most chaotic closing stages in years. Mathieu van der Poel of the Netherlands, riding for Alpecin-Premier Tech, attacked alongside Pogačar on the final ascent, helped force a frantic chase in the closing kilometres, and still had the legs to win the sprint on the Champs-Élysées ahead of Jasper Philipsen and Mads Pedersen.

Isaac del Toro's third place is itself a landmark: at 22, the UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider became the first Mexican ever to stand on the Tour de France podium, and he also secured the white jersey as best young rider. He credited his team leader for helping shepherd him through a gruelling final week, saying Pogačar had shown what a good friend he was as the Slovenian shifted into a protective role once his own title was secure.

France's Paul Seixas, only 19, finished fourth on his Tour debut, the youngest rider to start the race since 1937 and the best-placed Frenchman in the general classification. He had been within 24 seconds of the final podium spot before losing time on the brutal Alpe d'Huez stage.

Mads Pedersen sealed the points classification's green jersey, while Ecuador's Richard Carapaz took the polka dot jersey as king of the mountains, rounding out a jersey sweep that had effectively been settled before the Paris stage.

The race was also marked by the shock departure of two-time champion Jonas Vingegaard, who crashed heavily on stage 15 near Plateau de Solaison, fracturing his collarbone in a pile-up that also involved several of his Visma-Lease a Bike teammates and briefly caught up del Toro. It was the first time in six Tour appearances that the Dane failed to finish.

"Maybe at the beginning we didn't have the best relationship, but in the last two years, we became good rivals, respected rivals," Pogačar said of Vingegaard afterwards, reflecting on a rivalry that has defined the Tour for the past several editions.

Asked about the race that so nearly slipped away at various points, Pogačar summed up the unpredictability that still haunts even a dominant champion: "It's the Tour, three weeks, a lot of s*** can happen."

He also hinted, not for the first time, that his run of dominance will not last forever. "I definitely will not be doing this for too much long time, I think," he said, though few in the sport are taking that as a firm timeline given his current form.

The victory also extended Pogačar's stage-win tally at this year's race to five, taking his career total to 26 Tour de France stage wins, fourth on the all-time list, as he cements his place among the sport's true greats.

title: Maldini could quit as Italy technical director if Pirlo appointment collapses, ONE reports
dek: The man given full control over Italy's coaching search is said to be weighing resignation as the federation freezes Andrea Pirlo's path to the national team job over his ties to a Russian betting firm.
body: Paolo Maldini is prepared to walk away from his job running Italy's football rebuild if the federation ultimately blocks Andrea Pirlo from becoming national team coach, ONE reports, describing a standoff at the top of the Azzurri just as they try to recover from missing a third straight World Cup.

Maldini was installed as the Italian federation's technical director after Gennaro Gattuso resigned in April, and accepted the job only on condition of full autonomy over choosing the next coach. Having failed to lure Pep Guardiola to Coverciano, Maldini and his Brazilian advisor Leonardo settled on Pirlo as their one and only candidate for the post.

According to ONE, that is precisely the problem: Maldini regards Pirlo as the sole appointment worth making, and has openly dismissed alternatives such as Antonio Conte and Roberto Mancini as inadequate for the project. Italian reporting has described Mancini, said to be the federation president's own preference, as furious at being passed over.

The appointment has since stalled. Federation president Giovanni Malagò has paused formal talks with Pirlo to examine his position as global ambassador for Fonbet, a Russian-owned betting company, and his reported links to Russian businessman Sergei Lomakin — an association that sits awkwardly given the state of Italy-Russia relations since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

The freeze has become as much a political story as a football one. Azione party leader Carlo Calenda argued that anyone who engaged in pro-Russian promotion since 2022 should not hold a national position, European Parliament vice-president Pina Picierno called the prospective hire "a serious mistake," and sports minister Andrea Abodi has also voiced reservations, according to Israeli outlets citing the Italian press.

Pirlo's camp insists the row can be resolved. His legal team says the Fonbet ambassador deal is contractually bound to his coaching job at United FC in Dubai, meaning it would lapse automatically once that contract ends. Pirlo is said to be working to terminate the Emirati deal so formal negotiations with the federation can begin — talks the FIGC has refused to open while he remains under contract elsewhere.

For Maldini, the stakes are personal as much as professional. He left AC Milan after disputes with owner Jerry Cardinale, and took the federation role specifically to have the final say on football matters that he was denied at club level. Watching Rome block his one chosen candidate, ONE suggests, would be read by Maldini as exactly the kind of interference he left Milan to escape.

The federation, meanwhile, is running short on time. Italy needs a permanent coach in place well before it can begin building toward its next major tournament cycle, and a resignation by Maldini so soon after his appointment would plunge the rebuild into fresh chaos rather than the fresh start it was meant to deliver.

Nothing is settled: Malagò has not ruled on whether Pirlo's commercial ties disqualify him, and no timeline for a decision has been made public. But ONE's report frames the coming weeks as a test not just of Pirlo's candidacy, but of whether Maldini was really handed the authority the federation promised him.

title: Haaland's former Molde teammate predicts he will eventually join Real Madrid
dek: Magnus Wolff Eikrem, who played alongside Erling Haaland at Molde as a teenager, tells Diario AS he is convinced the Manchester City striker will end up at the Santiago Bernabéu.
body: Erling Haaland has heard the Real Madrid talk attached to his name for years, but this time it comes from someone who watched him grow up in the game. Magnus Wolff Eikrem, who played alongside Haaland at Molde when the striker was still a teenager finding his feet in Norwegian football, says he has no doubt where his old teammate will eventually end up.

"I think it is something that could perfectly happen," Eikrem told Spanish outlet Diario AS. "In fact, I am convinced it will happen someday. I won't say completely sure, but I do see many possibilities."

Eikrem and Haaland were teammates at Molde in 2018 and 2019, the period in which Haaland broke into the senior side before his move to Red Bull Salzburg launched him toward stardom at Borussia Dortmund and then Manchester City.

Eikrem argued that a switch to the Bernabéu would take Haaland's career to a level even City cannot offer. "Real Madrid's power of attraction around the world is immense, and although he is at a great club like City, I think he would reach a higher level at Madrid," he said.

He also predicted Haaland would thrive alongside Madrid's current stars rather than struggle to fit in. "The best players in the world play there, and Erling is one of them," Eikrem said. "I believe he would score a huge number of goals, fit in well, win over the fans, and enjoy playing surrounded by so many great stars."

Beyond the football, Eikrem was keen to describe the personality behind the goals, calling Haaland low-maintenance in the dressing room despite his global profile. "Haaland does not cause problems," he said. "He is a humble person who works hard, he does not seek to take all the spotlight, he has a good relationship with his teammates, and he adapts to any situation."

Eikrem recalled that even at 16, when nobody could have forecast the scale of what Haaland would become, his dedication already stood out — arriving at training with a smile, staying behind for extra work, and showing an early interest in nutrition that was unusual for a player his age.

None of this amounts to concrete transfer business. Haaland remains contracted to Manchester City heading into the 2026-27 season, now under new manager Enzo Maresca following Pep Guardiola's departure from the club in the summer, and there is no indication of an imminent move to Spain. Eikrem's comments are one former teammate's reading of where Haaland's career is heading, not a report of contact between the two clubs — but with Real Madrid's interest in the Norwegian a recurring theme for several years now, it is the kind of testimony that keeps the speculation alive.

title: Tiberias owner rejects plea deal, vows to fight banned-infusions case to the end
dek: Ari Kalmanzon says Ironi Tiberias will not settle the tribunal case over banned pre-match infusions, insisting the saga that followed a 3-0 win over Ashdod will go all the way to a ruling.
body: Ironi Tiberias owner Ari Kalmanzon says there will be no negotiated way out of the banned-infusions case hanging over his club, telling ONE Radio bluntly: "In the current case there is no plea deal, we are going all the way."

The affair goes back to a relegation-zone survival match in which Tiberias beat Ashdod 3-0 in round 30 of Ligat Ha'al, a result that helped push Ashdod below the safety line and down into the National League. Ashdod's response was to file a formal complaint with the Israel Football Association, alleging Tiberias players had been given banned intravenous infusions before kick-off.

According to reporting on the complaint, the infusions administered were around 800ml — roughly eight times the 100ml limit WADA permits within 12 hours of competition, a rule that exists specifically because large infusions can be used to mask other doping.

The Football Association, working alongside Israel's National Anti-Doping Agency, opened an investigation and provisionally suspended five Tiberias players — reported as David Kaltins, Guy Hadida, Niv Gutlib, Sambinya and Yonatan Taffer — along with three staff members, among them head coach Eliran Hodida and technical manager Chen Sol.

The case has since escalated well beyond those temporary suspensions. The anti-doping agency's legal counsel has filed an indictment with the Sports Doping Tribunal seeking suspensions ranging from several years to a lifetime ban for six people connected to the club, accusing them of "absolute indifference and blatant disregard" for player welfare. The proceedings against the players themselves are described as separate and still ongoing.

Before that indictment landed, the Football Association had offered Tiberias an exit route: a plea deal involving a 10-point deduction in return for closing the case before the playoffs. Tiberias rejected the terms, and talks broke down entirely after the club's lawyer, Nir Enbar, resigned from the case.

Kalmanzon insists nothing improper was given to the players — that it was a standard, legally purchased saline solution used for medical recovery, with no attempt to conceal anything. "No forbidden substance was given," he has said, casting Ashdod's complaint as a last-ditch move by a team fighting to beat the drop.

He goes further in the ONE interview, alleging the investigation has singled his club out unfairly and predicting the players will ultimately face only the lowest tier of a negligence charge, if any. He frames the scrutiny as selective rather than even-handed across the league.

It marks a notably different approach from an earlier, unrelated case involving the club — over irregular player contracts — in which Kalmanzon did agree to a plea deal rather than drag players through repeated hearings. This time, he says, Tiberias has chosen to contest every step rather than settle.

The dispute has already cost the club beyond the tribunal room. Kalmanzon has spoken previously about sponsorship and recruitment difficulties tied to the case, landing at a sensitive point of preseason as Tiberias tries to build a squad while the affair still hangs over its coaching staff.

For now, the tribunal process continues on separate tracks for players and staff, with Tiberias's ownership publicly committed to fighting the charges through to a verdict rather than accepting any further reduced settlement.

title: Itzik Aharonovich: 'Everything begins and ends with Barak Bakhar' at Maccabi Haifa
dek: The Haifa radio pundit tore into the coach's positional calls and squad management after a chastening derby defeat, arguing effectiveness — not tactics — is the real problem.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — Hapoel Haifa beat Maccabi Haifa 3-2 in the derby

body: The morning after Maccabi Haifa's alarming collapse in the Haifa derby, one of the club's most persistent radio critics wasted no time pointing the finger — squarely at head coach Barak Bakhar.

"Everything begins and ends with Bakhar," Itzik Aharonovich, the Haifa radio commentator and a regular guest on ONE's 'Sichat HaYom' podcast, said in an appearance discussing the greens' preseason troubles.

The trigger was Saturday's Toto Cup derby, in which Hapoel Haifa beat Maccabi Haifa 3-2. Bakhar's side fell three goals behind before a late two-goal rally fell just short of a full comeback, a result that has reopened old questions about the coach's methods less than two months after he was confirmed to stay in the job.

Aharonovich's central complaint was tactical: he said Bakhar too often deploys players out of their natural positions, singling out the decision to push defender Shon Goldberg into an unfamiliar deeper role as part of a back three. "Sometimes he has a problem — he puts players in positions that aren't theirs," he said, describing the team's on-field structure as "a circus."

He was sharpest on the club's handling of Goni Naor, the midfielder who returned to Maccabi Haifa on July 1 after his loan spell ended. Naor was reportedly told he was not part of the coach's plans for the new season before being restored to the derby squad anyway — a reversal Aharonovich suggested has done lasting damage. Bakhar, he said, may have effectively "finished" Naor's career at the club.

Aharonovich was equally unconvinced by the club's other returning loanee, Yarin Levi, who came back to Maccabi Haifa after a spell at Beitar Jerusalem and is expected to start alongside Yair Mordechai in midfield. He dismissed the idea that Levi solves the team's problems, calling him "not an aggressive player" and someone who is "difficult to work with."

Not every verdict was negative. Aharonovich praised Bruninho, the Brazilian attacking midfielder Maccabi Haifa signed from Ukraine's Karpaty Lviv for roughly €1.75 million on a three-year deal, saying he had impressed even in limited minutes since his move — though he questioned whether the club is getting the best out of him.

For Aharonovich, the debate isn't really about formations or philosophy. "The problem isn't tactics or style — it's effectiveness," he said, arguing Maccabi Haifa's issues run deeper than any single system.

The criticism lands at a sensitive moment for the club. Maccabi Haifa confirmed on May 27 that Bakhar would continue as head coach for 2026/27, with former captain Lior Refaelov stepping into a newly created sporting director role alongside him. The derby defeat, and the reaction it has produced from one of Haifa's loudest football voices, suggests that arrangement is already under scrutiny before a ball has been kicked in the league proper.

title: Ahavat Gordon vows to topple former world champion Lineker at Tel Aviv debut card
dek: The Israeli Muay Thai fighter says he deliberately picked the hardest test available for his brothers' new promotion — and expects to send the former UFC and ONE Championship world champion to defeat in front of a home crowd.

body: Tel Aviv's Menora Mivtachim Arena stages a fight card on Monday night that its own promoters have spent weeks framing as a statement of intent, and the man carrying the main event insists he wanted it that way. Ahavat HaShem Gordon, the Israeli Muay Thai fighter fronting his family's new promotion, meets Brazilian veteran John Lineker in the headline bout of GFN 1: Israel vs. The World.

Lineker is not a soft opening assignment. The 36-year-old "Hands of Stone" spent years as a top-five UFC bantamweight contender before moving to ONE Championship, where he won the bantamweight MMA world title and has since been fighting his way through ONE's Muay Thai ranks. He lost that MMA belt to Fabricio Andrade in February after the bout was stopped in the fourth round, but remains one of the most recognisable names to ever step into an Israeli ring.

Speaking to ONE ahead of the card, Gordon made clear the matchup was no accident. "We insisted on bringing a tough opponent, not an easy one," he said, describing the search for a credible international name for his promotion's debut rather than a routine win.

He was equally direct about where that leaves the fight itself: Lineker, he acknowledged, "won titles" and carries a résumé most fighters on this card could only dream of — but, in Gordon's own words to ONE, "he's going to fall." It's the kind of line pre-fight interviews are built on, respect for the opponent's history paired with total confidence in the outcome.

The bout sits atop a card built around Gordon and his two brothers, Ruach HaShem and Kibedy, who co-promote GFN alongside Yaniv Kaminski. Rather than a single headliner, Monday's show is structured as a triple main event: Ruach Gordon faces Maximus Bejenuta and Kibedy Gordon meets Jose Alberto Quiñonez, both in separate Muay Thai bouts, with Ahavat HaShem's clash against Lineker top of the bill.

The undercard adds further international depth, with former UFC lightweight Natan Levy — an Israeli fighter with his own top-level pedigree — taking on Lando Vannata in a kickboxing matchup, part of a program the Gordon brothers have pitched as a serious, standalone Israeli fight promotion rather than a one-off exhibition.

Gordon has said his camp trained in Thailand in the buildup, the kind of dedicated preparation typically reserved for a fighter's biggest test to date — which, by his own account, is exactly what Monday represents.
GFN 1: Israel vs. The World goes ahead on Monday, July 27, at the Menora Mivtachim Arena in Tel Aviv, with Ahavat HaShem Gordon's clash against John Lineker as the night's marquee attraction.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv complete €1m signing of Šeško's Slovenian 'neighbour', Ester Sokler
dek: The 27-year-old striker, who grew up 30km from Manchester United's Benjamin Šeško and shared a club with him for two seasons, arrives from Radnički 1923 on a two-year deal with a squad number 9 shirt.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have finally landed the striker they chased for weeks, confirming the signing of Slovenian forward Ester Sokler from Serbian club Radnički 1923 in a deal ONE reports is worth around €1 million.

ONE's angle on the story leans on an unlikely piece of geography: Sokler grew up in Krško, barely 30 kilometres from Radeče, the hometown of Manchester United's rising star Benjamin Šeško. The two even played for the same club for close to two years, per the report, before their careers forked in very different directions.

The Israeli champions have signed Sokler, 27, on a two-year contract with a club option for two further seasons, with local reporting putting his wages at roughly €350,000 a season. He has been handed the number 9 shirt.

Sokler's route to Tel Aviv was not a smooth upward curve. He came through Krško's youth ranks before spells at Brežice 1919, Celje and Radomlje in Slovenia, then joined Aberdeen in 2023 for a reported six-figure fee.

Scotland did not go to plan. Despite manager Jimmy Thelin publicly praising his work rate and calling him one of the club's best defensive forwards, Sokler managed only three goals in 49 league appearances for Aberdeen, mostly from the bench.

The revival came in Serbia. Sent to Radnički 1923 on loan, he scored six goals in his first 12 matches and prompted the club to make the move permanent for around €200,000. He finished the 2025/26 season with 15 goals in 29 appearances in all competitions, including two hat-tricks, and helped Radnički survive a relegation fight.
That form also earned him a first senior cap for Slovenia, coming off the bench in a 1-1 friendly draw with Cyprus in June.

Scouting reports describe a hardworking, off-the-ball forward with good movement and positioning rather than a natural creator — the kind of striker who thrives on service rather than manufacturing his own chances, which will put pressure on Maccabi's midfield to supply him.

"I'm proud to join Maccabi, a club with a rich history and big ambitions," Sokler said in a statement carried by the club. "I know what's expected here, and that's exactly what attracted me to this challenge."

For Maccabi Tel Aviv, the deal ends a transfer saga that had run for weeks, with Israeli outlets reporting on and off throughout July that a move for the Slovenia international was close. He now becomes the club's central attacking option heading into the new season.
facts: Maccabi Tel Aviv have signed Slovenian striker Ester Sokler from Serbian club Radnički 1923 for a reported fee of around €1 million.

title: Stav Lemkin: it was hard to find a quiet place — in Holland you can live
dek: The Israeli defender tells ONE how John van den Brom's arrival and Jan Streuer's faith turned his difficult first months at Twente around — and why the Netherlands feels like a rare patch of calm after Ukraine and Israel
body: Stav Lemkin has lived through enough upheaval for one career already — war in Ukraine, war at home in Israel — so when the 23-year-old defender talks about what he values most in his new life at FC Twente, it isn't a trophy or a starting shirt. It's quiet.

"In recent years it was hard to find peace," Lemkin told ONE. "Here we can live normal lives and go where we want." It's a striking line from a footballer, but Lemkin's path to Enschede has run through two of the most disrupted places in world sport over the past few years.

He joined Shakhtar Donetsk in 2023, only for the club — like all of Ukrainian football — to keep operating in exile and under the shadow of the war. A loan spell back home at Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2024-25 then coincided with the war in Israel and its impact on daily life and on the domestic league. Twente, by comparison, has offered something rarer for Lemkin than minutes on the pitch: stability.
"When there are no other things bothering you, you can concentrate on football," he said, describing the mental shift the move has allowed him.

The transfer itself, completed last summer for a reported €1.5 million on a three-year deal, was not an immediate success story. Lemkin has needed time to adjust to Dutch football's pace and demands, and by his own account struggled to establish himself in his first months at De Grolsch Veste.

The turning point, he says, was the coaching change in September, when Twente dismissed Joseph Oosting and brought in John van den Brom. Since then, Lemkin has become a regular fixture in the Twente back line.

He also credited Jan Streuer, the club's professional director, for making him feel wanted from the very start of the negotiations that brought him from Shakhtar. "He made clear how much he wanted me at Twente," Lemkin said. "That gave me a lot of confidence."

"I knew Twente was an excellent place for young players to make their next step," he added, framing the move as a calculated career decision rather than simply an escape from difficult circumstances at his previous clubs.
Looking back on the choice to leave Shakhtar for the Eredivisie, Lemkin was unequivocal. "I've never regretted the decision," he said. "I'm really happy here and proud to play for this club."

For an Israeli defender who came through the Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Tel Aviv academies before his move abroad, the comments are a reminder of how much off-the-pitch context now shapes careers in the modern game — and how a club like Twente, mid-table in the Eredivisie but stable and patient, can offer something that bigger, more turbulent situations elsewhere could not.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv owner accuses basketball federation of playing politics with Oturu naturalization
dek: Ofer Yanai says federation chairman Amos Frishman personally asked him to naturalize centre Dan Oturu for the national team — then, he claims, rival clubs moved to change the rules once it became real.

verificationSources.label: Sportando - Hapoel Tel Aviv extends Dan Oturu through 2029

body: Ofer Yanai does not usually pull punches, and he did not here. The Hapoel Tel Aviv owner has accused the Israel Basketball Association of playing politics with the naturalization of his American centre Dan Oturu, telling ONE that federation chairman Amos Frishman personally approached him months ago asking for help fast-tracking Oturu's citizenship so he could play for the national team.

According to Yanai's account, granting Frishman's request would have meant reworking Oturu's Hapoel Tel Aviv contract to strip out buyout and exit clauses — a restructuring Yanai says would have cost the club in the region of $2 million.

Oturu, 26, is one of the most productive big men in Europe. Drafted 33rd overall by the LA Clippers in 2020, the American-Nigerian centre moved through Turkey with Anadolu Efes before joining Hapoel Tel Aviv, who have since extended his contract through the 2028-29 season. Last EuroLeague campaign he averaged 13.9 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.4 blocks while shooting 71 percent on two-point attempts, setting a EuroLeague single-season record for made two-pointers along the way.

Yanai's complaint, as relayed by ONE, is about timing and motive. Now that Oturu's path to Israeli citizenship and international clearance looks close to reality, he claims representatives of Maccabi Tel Aviv are pushing to change the federation's eligibility rules — a naturalization route he says has traditionally been reserved for Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Jerusalem alone.

The dispute comes as the Israel Basketball Association has set up a special committee to formalize its procedures for naturalizing foreign-born players for the national team, an initiative first reported by ONE.

"If the federation acts in the interest of Israeli basketball, Oturu will be the national team's starting centre," Yanai said, according to the report. "If the federation acts corruptly, then Benaya Sror will start instead."

That second name is a pointed one. Sror, 26, is an Israeli-born centre who came through the Maayanot and Hapoel Galil Elyon youth system before spells at Maccabi Ramat Gan and now Elitzur Netanya. He recently earned his first call-up to the senior national team ahead of Israel's World Cup 2027 qualifying matches, making him the homegrown alternative Yanai is holding up against a naturalized Oturu.

ONE's report does not include a response from the Israel Basketball Association or from Frishman to Yanai's specific allegations, and the claims as published rest on Yanai's own account of private conversations. The episode nonetheless exposes a familiar fault line in Israeli basketball: which clubs get access to the national team's naturalization slot, and who decides.

title: Roma weigh loan move for Endrick as Milan's bid for Gerard Martín is rejected
dek: Real Madrid's José Mourinho wants his young forward to stay put, while Barcelona has knocked back an opening €20m offer for defender Gerard Martín.
body: Roma's transfer planners are exploring a paid loan for Real Madrid forward Endrick, according to a Gazzetta dello Sport report picked up by ONE, as the Italian club looks for attacking reinforcements ahead of the new season.

The idea rests on simple logic: Endrick, still only 19, faces fierce competition for a starting shirt in the Real Madrid attack, and Roma believe that congestion could make his club receptive to a season-long loan with add-ons, potentially including a future buy-option and a buy-back clause protecting Madrid's interests.

The Brazilian has already spent time away from the Bernabéu once. He was sent out on loan to Lyon for the second half of last season to find regular football, and the experience did not derail his international standing — he was still called into Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad for the World Cup.

Complicating any approach, though, is the man now in charge at the Bernabéu. José Mourinho took over as Real Madrid's head coach in June after the club moved on from Xabi Alonso and then interim boss Álvaro Arbeloa earlier in 2026, and ONE reports that Mourinho wants Endrick to stay and fight for his place, with the player himself said to be inclined to remain in Madrid.

There is an added layer of history here. Mourinho's previous spell in Serie A, at Roma itself, ended in his dismissal in January 2024, and relations with the Friedkin ownership have reportedly stayed frosty since — hardly the ideal backdrop for the same Roma hierarchy to now be negotiating with Mourinho's new club over one of his own squad players.
None of that has stopped the contact from happening, ONE says, though the report stresses the operation is still at an early, exploratory stage rather than a concrete bid.
Elsewhere in Tuesday's transfer news, Barcelona has rejected an opening approach from AC Milan for left-back Gerard Martín, with the Rossoneri's offer said to be worth €20 million.

Martín, 24, has become an increasingly trusted name in Hansi Flick's Barcelona side and has even been talked up as a future Spain candidate, which explains the Catalan club's reluctance to sanction an exit at that price — other reporting on the saga has suggested Barcelona's valuation sits well above Milan's opening number.

For now, both stories sit at the same stage: contact made, nothing agreed, and two clubs — Roma and Milan — needing to raise their offers if they want to turn interest into transfers before the window closes.

title: Messi and De Paul excused from MLS All-Star Game, no punishment this time
dek: A week after Argentina's World Cup final defeat, Messi and Rodrigo De Paul have been withdrawn from Wednesday's showcase in Charlotte under a mandatory rest agreement — sparing them the ban that followed last year's snub.
body: Lionel Messi will miss Wednesday's MLS All-Star Game for the second year running — but this time, unlike last summer, nobody at league headquarters is reaching for the rulebook.

Messi and Inter Miami teammate Rodrigo De Paul have both been withdrawn from the All-Star roster for the game against a Liga MX All-Star XI at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte on Wednesday night, with the accompanying Skills Challenge held the evening before. Both players had been voted onto the squad by fans.

The pair are covered by a mandatory rest window rather than any injury. Under FIFPro's player-welfare guidelines, footballers are entitled to up to 21 days off following a major international tournament, and MLS and the players' union agreed before this season that clubs would hold individual conversations with each returning World Cup player to set an appropriate recovery and return-to-training schedule.

"After players complete their World Cup participation, each club will hold individual discussions to determine appropriate rest schedules," the league said in confirming the exemption — language that, this time, removes any question of discipline.

The timing traces back to Argentina's run to the World Cup final on July 19 at MetLife Stadium, where Messi played the full 120 minutes as his side lost 1-0 in extra time to Spain. He still finished the tournament with the Silver Boot for eight goals and the Silver Ball as the competition's second-best player, medals that came with a physical toll the rest agreement is designed to offset.

It is a markedly different position from a year ago. In 2025, Messi and Jordi Alba sat out the All-Star Game without securing prior league approval and were both hit with a one-match suspension under an MLS rule that bars any snubbing player from his club's next fixture — in Messi's case, a home game against Inter Miami's Eastern Conference rivals FC Cincinnati.

Inter Miami's ownership was furious at the time. Managing owner Jorge Mas branded the sanction "draconian" and said Messi was "extremely upset" at being suspended for a match his club had chosen to rest him for on medical grounds. "It's a bad rule, but it's a rule nonetheless," Mas said then, while insisting the decision to sit Messi and Alba out had been the club's call, not the players'.

This year's carve-out effectively resolves that dispute for World Cup finalists: because the rest period is pre-agreed rather than a unilateral snub, no suspension applies, and Messi and De Paul can be reintegrated into the Inter Miami squad on a schedule set jointly by the club and league, with a return expected in early August.

MLS has filled the gaps left by Messi and De Paul, along with two unrelated late withdrawals. Chicago Fire forward Philip Zinckernagel replaces Hugo Cuypers, who left MLS altogether after a move to Liga MX side CF Monterrey, while Houston Dynamo's Guilherme steps in for the injured Mbekezeli Mbokazi. Nashville's Andrés Cubas and Inter Miami's own Yannick Bright fill the two slots vacated by De Paul and Messi.

The rest of the World Cup contingent due to feature includes Son Heung-min, Thomas Müller, Tim Ream, Max Arfsten and Peter Musa for MLS, against a Liga MX side featuring Keylor Navas, Gilberto Mora and Jesús Gallardo — none of whom played in the final and so fall outside the extended rest window applied to Messi and De Paul.
facts: Lionel Messi and Rodrigo De Paul have been withdrawn from the 2026 MLS All-Star Game roster ahead of the fixture against Liga MX All-Stars on Wednesday, July 29, 2026 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte.

MLS and the MLS Players Association agreed before the 2026 season that clubs would set individual post-World Cup rest schedules for returning players, consistent with FIFPro guidelines allowing up to 21 days' recovery time.
Messi played all 120 minutes as Argentina lost the World Cup final 1-0 to Spain in extra time on July 19, 2026 at MetLife Stadium, finishing with the Silver Boot (8 goals) and Silver Ball.
In 2025, Messi and Jordi Alba were suspended for Inter Miami's next league match after missing the All-Star Game without prior league approval; owner Jorge Mas called the punishment "draconian."
Because the 2026 absence falls under the pre-agreed rest arrangement rather than an unapproved snub, no suspension applies to Messi or De Paul this time.

MLS named Philip Zinckernagel, Guilherme, Andrés Cubas and Yannick Bright as roster replacements for Hugo Cuypers (transferred to CF Monterrey), Mbekezeli Mbokazi (injury), De Paul and Messi respectively.

title: Real Madrid agree personal terms with Yan Diomande on five-year deal
dek: The Ivory Coast winger has given Real Madrid the green light to leave RB Leipzig, though a transfer fee reported above €100m still needs to be finalised between the two clubs.
body: Real Madrid have reached agreement on personal terms with Yan Diomande, with the RB Leipzig winger giving his definitive green light to a five-year contract that would keep him at the Bernabéu until 2031, ONE reports.

The 19-year-old Ivory Coast international has emerged as one of the most coveted young attackers in Europe after a breakout debut season in the Bundesliga, and Madrid moved quickly this week to push the personal terms of the deal over the line.

According to ONE, Madrid's opening proposal to Leipzig stands at more than €100m, while Spanish outlets are citing a package in the region of €115-120m once add-ons are included — a figure still to be agreed between the two clubs rather than confirmed.

Fabrizio Romano has separately reported that Real Madrid's initial bid of €90m fixed plus €10m in performance-related add-ons was knocked back by Leipzig, who value their player considerably higher and are yet to accept an improved offer.

Manager José Mourinho is understood to have personally sanctioned the pursuit, telling the club's board he wanted more pace in his forward line — with Diomande earmarked as the fifth major arrival of Madrid's summer rebuild, following Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konaté and Bernardo Silva.

Paris Saint-Germain remain a complicating factor. Diomande had reportedly agreed personal terms with PSG earlier in the summer and given the French club an initial preference, but Madrid have since overtaken them in the race, according to Romano and Managing Madrid.

Diomande joined RB Leipzig from Spanish side Leganés last summer for around €20m and instantly established himself in the Bundesliga, scoring 12 goals and adding eight assists in 33 appearances as Leipzig secured Champions League qualification for 2026/27 — form that earned him the division's Rookie of the Year award.

His stock rose further at this summer's World Cup, where he became the youngest Ivorian ever to feature at the tournament. He played the full 90 minutes in Ivory Coast's 1-0 win over Ecuador, set up his side's goal in a 2-1 loss to Germany, and teed up Nicolas Pépé in a 2-0 win over Curaçao that sent the Elephants through to the round of 32.

With personal terms now settled, attention shifts to the boardroom negotiations between Madrid and Leipzig, where the size of the fee — and whether the Bundesliga club can be persuaded to sell one of its prize assets this window — will determine how quickly the move is completed.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv complete signing of Slovenian striker Ester Sokler
dek: The 27-year-old arrives from Serbia's Radnički 1923 Kragujevac after single-handedly dragging the club away from relegation, with the fee reported at close to €1 million.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have found their new number 9. The club has confirmed the signing of Slovenian striker Ester Sokler from Serbian outfit Radnički 1923 Kragujevac, ONE reported, ending a transfer saga that Serbian media had been tracking for weeks.

Sokler, 27, arrives with a modest scoring pedigree on paper but a season that turned heads across the Balkans. Loaned to Radnički in January and signed permanently soon after when the club exercised its buy option, he scored 15 goals in 29 league appearances as Radnički scrapped its way to safety in the Serbian SuperLiga, narrowly avoiding relegation despite what ONE described as a chaotic campaign.

The move has been reported as one of the biggest transfers out of Serbia's top flight this summer — notable, Serbian outlet Naslovi.net pointed out, for not involving either Crvena zvezda or Partizan, the country's two traditional powerhouses. Radnički is set to collect a seven-figure fee, put by ONE at around €1 million.

The contract terms differ slightly depending on the source: ONE reports a two-year deal with an option for two further seasons worth roughly €300,000 net per year, while Serbian outlets including B92 describe a three-year contract closer to €400,000 per season. Neither club has published exact figures, and the discrepancy has not been resolved.

Sokler's route to Israel has taken in three countries in four years. He came through Slovenian football at Celje before joining Kalcer Radomlje in 2022, then moved to Scotland with Aberdeen in 2023, where two seasons in the Premiership brought only a handful of goals before he dropped into the Serbian top flight on loan this past January.

It was that switch to Radnički that revived his career. Freed from a bit-part role in Scotland, he became the club's talisman, and his form did not go unnoticed at home: Slovenia head coach Boštjan Cesar handed him a senior call-up in June, and Sokler marked the occasion by coming off the bench to score an 85th-minute equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Cyprus at Stadion Stožice, replacing Žan Vipotnik.

"I know the expectations that come with wearing this shirt, and that's exactly what attracted me to this challenge," Sokler said, according to ONE. "I will give everything to help the team achieve its goals."

He will wear the number 9 for Maccabi Tel Aviv and joins a squad being reshaped by coach Kenny Miller ahead of a season that will again carry the weight of domestic title expectations alongside a European campaign.

For a club that has made a habit of mining lesser-known leagues for attacking reinforcements, Sokler fits a familiar profile: a proven scorer from a modest environment, arriving with a point to prove and, now, a maiden senior international goal already on his CV.

The transfer fee to Radnički is reported at around €1 million; contract length is reported as two years plus a two-year option (ONE) or three years (Serbian outlets), with salary estimates of roughly €300,000-€400,000 net per season.

title: Abuhatzira and Cohen mark first senior goals on Toto Cup opening weekend
dek: Yarin Abuhatzira sealed a 3-1 Maccabi Netanya win over Hapoel Jerusalem and Noam Cohen struck a derby winner for Hapoel Petah Tikva, each netting his first senior goal as the Toto Cup got under way.
body: Two teenagers wrote themselves into their clubs' history books on the opening weekend of the Toto Cup, each scoring his first senior goal within a day of one another — and each carrying a family name Israeli football already knew well.

At Netanya Stadium on Saturday, Maccabi Netanya beat Hapoel Jerusalem 3-1 in Group B's opening fixture. Bassam Zaarura and Oz Bilu combined for two first-half goals, before 16-year-old Yarin Abuhatzira, introduced from the bench, drove home a chance in the 75th minute to put the result beyond doubt.

ONE describes it as Abuhatzira's first official senior goal, and one his coach Roni Levi will have taken particular satisfaction in — the youngster has been tipped internally as one of the outstanding prospects to emerge from Netanya's academy this season.

The goal carries extra resonance because of his surname. Yarin is the son of Shimon Abuhatzira, the well-travelled former striker whose senior career took in Hapoel Petah Tikva, Maccabi Haifa and Beitar Jerusalem among other clubs, and who also earned caps for the Israel national team.

A few hours away, in the Petah Tikva derby, Hapoel Petah Tikva edged Maccabi Petah Tikva 1-0 at HaMoshava Stadium — the sides' first meeting since Maccabi's relegation and Hapoel's promotion re-shuffled the local pecking order.

It was goalless and tight for long stretches under Hapoel coach Omer Peretz, until Noam Cohen settled it in the 89th minute with a rising strike from around 20 metres that flew into the top corner, sparking wild celebrations among the home support.

According to ONE, it was Cohen's first senior goal too, and it came with its own family thread: he is the grandson of Salva Barzilai, a name long associated with the Hapoel Petah Tikva dressing room and one still fondly remembered by supporters.

The Toto Cup's opening rounds are traditionally where Israeli top-flight clubs blood their academy graduates, with squads still building toward the league season proper — and this weekend produced two textbook examples of why coaches use the competition that way.

For Netanya and Hapoel Petah Tikva alike, the derby-day and group-stage wins matter less in the table than the glimpse they offered of what their youth systems are producing heading into the new campaign.

title: Ousted investor warns Maccabi Tel Aviv could face bankruptcy
dek: Weeks after being squeezed out of the club's ownership structure, tech entrepreneur Arik Shtilman says the Recanati-controlled club is sitting on losses that could run into the hundreds of millions of shekels - even as he tables a rival $100 million bid for control.

verificationSources.label: Ynet - Shtilman's offer for Recanati shares
Israel Hayom - Shtilman pushed out of ownership

body: A month and a half after buying his way into Maccabi Tel Aviv's ownership structure only to be squeezed straight back out of it, tech entrepreneur Arik Shtilman is sounding the alarm over the club's finances - and putting a fresh, rival offer on the table to take control himself.

Appearing on ONE's "Sichat HaYom" podcast, Shtilman said Israel's most decorated basketball club could be heading toward bankruptcy if its ownership and spending patterns do not change, describing its finances as sitting atop what he called "an enormous pit, historic in scale."

According to ONE's report, Shtilman put projected losses at around 100 million shekels for the coming season alone, 70 to 80 million shekels the year after that, and 50 to 70 million shekels annually even in a season when Maccabi returns to the EuroLeague - warning that cumulative losses could run into the hundreds of millions of shekels over the coming years without new capital and new management.

The warning lands against a messy backdrop. Shtilman, the founder and chief executive of payments company Rapyd, was brought into Maccabi's ownership picture in May as part of a deal to take a 50% stake in Fedanco Sports, the investment vehicle through which the Federman family held roughly 29% of the club.

That plan collapsed when the Recanati family, which already controlled the largest share of Maccabi, exercised its right of first refusal on the Federman stake, paying an estimated $50 million to buy out the family directly rather than let Shtilman in alongside them - leaving him on the outside of the ownership structure after barely six weeks.

Rather than walk away, Shtilman has since gone in the opposite direction: tabling a non-binding offer of $100 million for the Recanati family's own 58% controlling stake, held through Naftali Investments - a valuation that matches what the Recanatis themselves paid to seize control from the Federmans. His proposal reportedly calls for 30 days of due diligence and a close within 90 days, subject to corporate approvals.

The counter-bid arrives as the Recanatis are separately said to be negotiating a sale of half of their own holding - 50% of their stake - to American businessman Jason Levin for around $50 million, a sign that the family currently running the club is itself weighing how much of it to keep.

Shtilman's bankruptcy warning has to be read in that context. He is not a neutral outside observer but an active rival claimant for control, and he has argued publicly that the Recanatis lack the resources and long-term plan to keep Maccabi solvent - making the case that only new ownership, implicitly his own group, can head off a slide toward insolvency.

Even so, the figures he cited would be alarming for a club with more European and domestic titles than any other in Israeli basketball, and they add a financial dimension to what has already been a turbulent off-court summer around the team's ownership.

Neither Maccabi Tel Aviv nor the Recanati family had issued a public response to Shtilman's remarks at the time of ONE's report, and the loss projections have not been independently verified against the club's own financial disclosures.

title: Machpod: Hapoel Petah Tikva won't repeat last season's heroics
dek: The club great played down expectations after a derby win over Maccabi Petah Tikva, citing a threadbare budget and a reshaped squad under Omer Peretz.
body: Eli Machpod delivered a dose of realism to Hapoel Petah Tikva's fanbase this week, telling ONE's studio show that he does not expect the newly promoted club to match last season's remarkable run to the top-six playoff.
"I don't think Hapoel Petah Tikva will have a season like last year," Machpod, one of the club's most decorated former players, said in the aftermath of the derby against Maccabi Petah Tikva.

Hapoel won that match 1-0 at HaMoshava Stadium in the opening round of the Toto Cup, with Noam Cohen settling a scrappy occasion with a goal in the 89th minute. Machpod was unimpressed by the overall quality, dismissing it as a below-average contest.

His skepticism about the season ahead stems largely from the scale of turnover in the squad that Omer Peretz guided from the second tier to a top-six finish - the club's first appearance in the upper playoff in more than two decades.

Several contributors from that campaign have already left, and Machpod pointed to the club's financial reality as the reason further departures are likely. "There's no money, so there's nothing to do," he said. "If a suitable offer comes for players, they'll be sold."

That comment lands against a backdrop of reports that Hapoel Petah Tikva are pushing for a higher transfer offer for Zambian winger Chapyuka Songa, one of the more coveted names to emerge from last season's promotion push.

In their place, the club have brought in fresh faces at the back. Left-back Yazan Nassar, a summer signing from Hapoel Tel Aviv, and defender Avishai Cohen were both handed derby debuts, alongside winger Guy Badash.

Machpod's forecast for the coming campaign has Hapoel Petah Tikva locked in a battle for sixth place with Maccabi Netanya, rather than another surprise push toward the top of the table. He was harsher still on the cross-town rivals, predicting Maccabi Petah Tikva will instead be fighting to avoid relegation.

None of this reflects any lack of faith in Peretz himself. The 40-year-old, who has overseen the club's rise since arriving before last season, signed a contract extension through 2027/28 in the close season, with his salary reported to have risen by roughly a third.
For a club still adjusting to life back in the Israeli top flight, the message from one of its own icons is clear: last season's overachievement was the exception, not the new baseline.

title: Hapoel Kfar Saba sign striker Yoav Solel, Hapoel Afula bring in defender Yifrach
dek: Two Liga Leumit clubs move on their squads for the new season, with Kfar Saba landing a goal-scoring teenager from Hapoel Petah Tikva and Afula adding a defender whose family already has ties to the club.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Nehorai Yifrach and Hapoel Afula
Walla Sport - Hapoel Kfar Saba Liga Leumit table 2025/26

body: Two Liga Leumit clubs used the close season to freshen up their squads, with Hapoel Kfar Saba and Hapoel Afula both completing signings this week, ONE reports.

Kfar Saba have brought in Yoav Solel, a 19-year-old striker, on a three-year contract after his release from Hapoel Petah Tikva. According to ONE, Solel scored nine league goals last season and hit 13 in a youth league campaign two years earlier, numbers that made him a target for a Kfar Saba side looking to add firepower up front. He is represented by agent Assaf Schwartz.

Kfar Saba finished seventh in Liga Leumit in the 2025/26 season, with 13 wins, eight draws and 12 defeats and a goal difference of 48 for and 44 against, a mid-table campaign that leaves the club looking to push higher with fresh attacking options.

In Afula, the club has added a defender named Yifrach, arriving from Hapoel Beit Shean of the third-tier Liga Alef North, ONE reports. The 20-year-old, who grew up in Kiryat Shmona, is represented by Fisher Sports alongside agents Roey Simoni and Satya Chachmon, and the move represents a step up two divisions for a player Afula hope can shore up their back line.

The signing carries an extra layer of interest given the family name: Yifrach is the brother of striker Nehorai Yifrach, who came up through Maccabi Haifa's youth ranks before joining Hapoel Afula on loan last season. According to Walla Sport, Nehorai made 23 league appearances for Afula, scoring twice and adding two assists, before a broken fibula sustained in training cut his campaign short with the club's medical staff estimating a two-to-three month recovery.
Neither club has published financial details of either deal, and ONE's report did not include quotes from either signing or from club officials.
Both moves are part of the broader housekeeping Liga Leumit sides are working through before pre-season proper gets under way, as clubs firm up their rosters for the campaign ahead.

title: Yoav Poryan leaves the Sharon region to sign for Shimshon Tel Aviv
dek: The 23-year-old defender joins Uri Gutman's Liga Alef South side after consecutive seasons with Hapoel Herzliya and Kfar Saba 1928.

verificationSources.label: Double Pass (Sport5) - Liga Alef South coverage

body: Yoav Poryan, a 23-year-old defender who has spent his young career shuttling between clubs in the Sharon region, has signed for Shimshon Tel Aviv ahead of the new season, ONE reported.

Poryan came up through Hapoel Kfar Saba's youth department and is now entering his fourth consecutive season in Liga Alef, Israel's fourth tier, after two campaigns at right-back for Hapoel Herzliya and, most recently, a season in central defence for Maccabi Kfar Saba 1928.

That last season was a heavy workload: according to the report, Poryan made 25 appearances for Kfar Saba 1928, 20 of them starts, and logged 2,100 minutes on the pitch — the most of anyone on the roster.

He now moves to Shimshon Tel Aviv, the historic Tel Aviv club that once played at Bloomfield Stadium in Israel's top flight before a turbulent spell that included a merger with Beitar Tel Aviv and, later, a rebuild from scratch. The team competes in Liga Alef South under coach Uri Gutman.
"My heart told me Shimshon Tel Aviv would be the right place for my advancement," Poryan said, according to ONE, adding that he is confident hard work will bring success at his new club.

The move keeps Poryan in Israel's fourth tier but shifts him from the Sharon clubs where he made his name to one of Tel Aviv's more storied lower-league sides as it continues to rebuild its senior team.
