body: Barcelona have a problem entirely of the good kind: one of their forwards just scored the goal that won Spain the World Cup, and now everybody wants him. ONE reports that the club is increasingly anxious it could lose Ferran Torres, with the 26-year-old still undecided over a new contract at Camp Nou and Paris Saint-Germain waiting in the wings.

Torres's current deal runs only until June 2027, and according to the report he has yet to give Barcelona a positive answer on an extension the club has already put on the table. That hesitation has not gone unnoticed in Paris — PSG have registered serious interest and, per the report, are able to offer financial terms Barcelona simply cannot match given their ongoing wage constraints under La Liga's financial fair play rules.

Adding to the complication, extending Torres's contract would trigger an additional payment of around €8 million ($9m) owed to his former club, Manchester City, under the terms of his 2022 transfer to Barcelona — a bonus clause tied to the length of his stay that further squeezes an already tight budget.

ONE's report ties Torres's mood in part to Barcelona's parallel pursuit of a new No. 9. The club has made Atletico Madrid's Julián Álvarez their priority target to solve a long-running centre-forward problem, and Torres is said to be uneasy about a move that would again push him toward the margins of the attack rather than through the middle, where he has increasingly established himself.

The timing could hardly be more pointed. Torres was Spain's unlikely hero in the 2026 World Cup final on July 19, scoring the extra-time winner in a 1-0 victory over Argentina at New Jersey's MetLife-area venue to give Spain their second world title. The goal, struck from inside the box in the 106th minute after Argentina had been reduced to ten men, transformed a player who had spent much of the tournament fighting for a starting shirt into a national hero.

It capped a strong individual season for Torres at club level too: 21 goals and three assists in 49 appearances for Barcelona, including 16 La Liga goals — a tally that made him Spain's top-scoring player in the division last season, level with teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.

None of that has settled his future. PSG's approach is said to include direct contact from manager Luis Enrique, who knows Torres well from his time overseeing the Spanish national team set-up and has been personally selling the Parisian project to the forward.

Barcelona's dilemma, as ONE frames it, is stark: risk losing a player who has just become a World Cup winner for nothing next summer, or cash in now while his value — freshly inflated by that final goal — is at its peak. Neither option sits comfortably with a club that would clearly prefer to build around him.

For now, nothing is resolved. Torres has not rejected Barcelona's offer outright, nor has he committed to it, and the report stresses this remains a genuine dilemma rather than a done deal in either direction. But with PSG circling and Barcelona's own transfer business complicating matters further, the coming weeks look set to decide where one of the World Cup's biggest breakout stars plays his club football next season.

title: Neymar answers poker critics with a brace and a card-dealing celebration
dek: The Santos forward scored twice, including a stoppage-time penalty, to salvage a 2-2 draw with Chapecoense — then mimicked dealing cards and swinging a golf club to mock the backlash over his poker tournament appearance
body: Neymar picked the loudest possible stage to answer his doubters. With Santos trailing Chapecoense deep into their Brasileirão meeting at Vila Belmiro on Saturday, the forward scored a stoppage-time penalty to complete a brace and rescue a 2-2 draw — then turned his celebration into a pointed message aimed squarely at the critics who had questioned his commitment days earlier.

ONE reports that Neymar opened the scoring in the 36th minute with a first-time finish from open play, part of a slick move involving winger Álvaro Barreal. Chapecoense hit back through Marcinho shortly after half-time, and when Santos defender João Ananias turned the ball into his own net, the visitors from Santa Catarina found themselves ahead against a Santos side seemingly staring at a damaging home defeat.

Neymar restored parity from the penalty spot after Gustavo Caballero was brought down by Bruno Matias inside the area, with the spot-kick arriving in the closing stages to snatch a point for Peixe. The result leaves Santos 14th in the 20-team table, still well clear of bottom-placed Chapecoense.

It was the celebration, not just the goals, that dominated the conversation afterward. According to ONE, Neymar mimicked dealing out poker cards on the turf before grabbing the corner flag and swinging it like a golf club — an unmistakable jab at the criticism he had faced for attending the BSOP Winter poker tournament in São Paulo while Santos were playing a Copa Sudamericana qualifier against Universidad Central de Venezuela without him.

That earlier absence had triggered a wave of backlash in Brazil, with fans and pundits questioning why a player who had asked for extra time to focus on a fitness recovery programme was instead pictured smiling at a card table. Neymar had already fired back on social media before Saturday's match, insisting he trained that morning, had only just returned to full training, and was using an off day that did not compromise his recovery. "Can I train, or are you going to keep criticising me? Mind your own business," he wrote, according to multiple outlets covering the episode.

The pitch-side rebuttal against Chapecoense landed with Brazilian media exactly as Neymar intended. ONE cites local coverage crediting him with single-handedly keeping Santos competitive, underlining how central his form remains to a club leaning heavily on him during a stop-start return from Al-Hilal.

The afternoon carried a sting in the tail, though. Neymar was booked during the second half after continuing to argue with an opponent, and the yellow card completed an accumulation that rules him out of Santos' next league fixture, at home to Athletico on August 9 — meaning the goals and the theatrics both came in what will be his final Brasileirão appearance for a few weeks.
For now, the story is a familiar one for Neymar: criticism, a defiant response, and a celebration built to make sure nobody misses the message.

title: Teenage prodigy Yarin Abuhatzira set to sign new Maccabi Netanya contract this week
dek: The 15-year-old, dubbed 'the Israeli Lamine Yamal' by the club's development staff, is closing in on a long-term deal that would scrap his release clause, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "ירין אבוחצירה אמור לחתום השבוע על חוזה חדש"
ONE — "התקדמות במגעים לחוזה חדש לירין אבוחצירה"

body: Maccabi Netanya's most talked-about teenager is about to put pen to paper. ONE reports that Yarin Abuhatzira, the 15-year-old forward who has already trained and travelled with the senior squad, is expected to sign a new long-term contract with the club this week.

The deal on the table, according to the report, runs for a minimum of three years and would remove the modest release clause — worth a few hundred thousand shekels — that currently sits in his existing youth terms, replacing it with an upgraded professional contract as he graduates into the senior set-up.

Talks accelerated when Abuhatzira's father, former Israeli international striker Shimon Abuhatzira, travelled with the player's agent, Nir Amir, to the club's pre-season training camp in Poland to push the negotiations forward. Club chairman Gil Lev has been personally involved in getting an agreement over the line.

The younger Abuhatzira only turns 16 on Monday, but he is already regarded as one of the most exciting prospects to come through Netanya's academy in years. He has been training and touring with the first team under special league dispensation that allows him to feature for the seniors well below the usual age threshold.

He has scored twice for the senior side in a 5-0 friendly win over Poland's Cracovia Kraków during the training camp, and recently netted on his senior debut to become the youngest scorer in this season's Toto Cup.

Beni Lam, the club's professional development director, has been effusive about the winger, telling reporters he is "the Israeli Lamine Yamal" and that "Ligat Ha'Al is merely a stepping stone toward higher European levels" for him. His youth coach, Ofir Haim, has compared his blend of speed and explosiveness to a mix of former Israel forwards Ronen Harazi and Omer Atzili.

The numbers from his junior career back up the hype: 29 goals in the third-tier youth division, 21 in the second tier and 23 at the top level, en route to becoming one of the most productive scorers to pass through Netanya's youth ranks.

Family history runs through the story. Shimon Abuhatzira won the Israeli Premier League title with Ironi Kiryat Shmona in 2011-12 and earned caps for the senior national team during a career that also took in Hapoel Petah Tikva and Maccabi Haifa. The family relocated from Kiryat Shmona to Netanya when Yarin was 10, and he has come through the Sar-Tov academy system ever since.

Nothing has been signed yet, and ONE's report stresses the deal is expected rather than confirmed — but with the club chairman, the player's family and his representatives all pulling in the same direction, Netanya appear close to tying down one of the most promising teenagers in Israeli football before bigger clubs come calling.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva vow to be ready for the league despite Toto Cup derby defeat
dek: New coach Ziv Aria's first match ended in a 1-0 loss to Hapoel Petah Tikva, but the club says reinforcements will arrive before Ligat Ha'al kicks off

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport on Yoav Koren loan interest

body: Maccabi Petah Tikva opened their season with a defeat, going down 1-0 to city rivals Hapoel Petah Tikva in the first round of the Toto Cup, but the club insists the result says nothing about its readiness for the Ligat Ha'al campaign proper.

The derby was settled by a stunning late strike from Noam Cohen, who found the top corner from roughly 20 metres out in the 89th minute to hand Hapoel bragging rights in the city's first derby of the new season.

For Maccabi, it was a chastening backdrop to Ziv Aria's first match in the dugout. Aria, who spent seven years on Hapoel Jerusalem's staff before agreeing a one-year deal to take over at Maccabi this summer, watched his new side toil for long spells before Cohen's late winner.

He replaces Noam Soham, who steered Maccabi back to the top flight at the first attempt last season only to be moved on rather than kept for the club's return to Ligat Ha'al - a decision that still colours how this rebuilt squad is being read from the outside.

Speaking to ONE after the loss, club officials were candid about the gap between the group that started the Toto Cup opener and the one they intend to field once the league begins. "We knew we weren't fully ready and that we still need to add players," the club said, according to ONE. "Once we add [Ariel] Logasi, who is injured, we're still missing three players for the front line. We will be ready by the time the league starts."

Logasi's return alone will not close that gap. ONE reports Maccabi are working to bring in Yoav Koren, a Hapoel Beersheba player who spent last season on loan at Hapoel Kfar Saba and scored seven goals there - form that has put him in demand this summer. Beersheba, per the report, are in no rush to sanction another loan move.
The club is also said to be chasing a right-back solution through Maccabi Tel Aviv's Noam Schwartz, though ONE cautions that any loan agreement there remains unresolved for now.

Squad turnover is not only about incomings. ONE reports Omer Shirazi is expected to leave and link up with Soham at his new club, while captain Mohammad Hindi - a long-serving figure at Maccabi - did not feature in the derby loss, with the report suggesting his standing in the squad is under review despite his years of service.

None of it, Maccabi maintain, threatens their readiness for kick-off. The message from Petah Tikva this week is that a subdued Toto Cup curtain-raiser is being treated as exactly that - an exhibition, not a verdict - while the rebuilding work continues in the transfer market before the league campaign begins.

The move gives Bnei Yehuda a fresh attacking option heading into pre-season, with the club looking to build on last term's Liga Leumit playoff campaign as they push for a return to the top flight.

title: Abu Dhabi, 28 October 2018: The night Hatikvah finally played in the Gulf
dek: A year after organisers silenced Israel's anthem for a judo champion in the UAE, Sagi Muki won gold on the same mat — and heard Hatikvah ring out where it never had before.

verificationSources.label: The Jerusalem Post — "Hatikvah plays for first time in UAE as Israeli judoka wins gold medal"
Ynetnews — "In first, national anthem played at Abu Dhabi after Israeli judoka nabs gold"
European Judo Union — "Historic win in Abu Dhabi for Israel's Muki"
CNN — "Israeli judo star Tal Flicker wins gold in UAE; officials refuse to play anthem" (2017)
CNN — "International Judo Federation suspends Abu Dhabi Grand Slam and the Tunis Grand Prix" (2018)
Wikipedia — "2018 Judo Grand Slam Abu Dhabi" (results confirmation)

body: The Mubadala Arena in Abu Dhabi was packed and loud on the evening of 28 October 2018, but for Israeli judo the noise that mattered was the one nobody was sure would come: the opening bars of Hatikvah, played over a Gulf sound system for an Israeli gold medallist for the first time in history.

It had not been that way twelve months earlier. At the same Abu Dhabi Grand Slam in October 2017, Tal Flicker won gold in the men's under-66kg category, but tournament organisers refused to raise the Israeli flag or play its anthem, citing the UAE's lack of diplomatic ties with Israel. Instead, the International Judo Federation's own flag and anthem were used on the podium — while Flicker, standing beneath them, quietly sang Hatikvah to himself.

The episode drew international attention and formal censure. In July 2018 the IJF's executive committee suspended both the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam and the Tunis Grand Prix, declaring it would not sanction events until organisers guaranteed equal treatment — flags, anthems and all — for every competing nation. The federation framed it as a stand against discrimination in sport, and it worked: the UAE government provided the guarantees, and the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam returned to the calendar that autumn with Israeli symbols permitted for the first time.

Into that reopened arena stepped Sagi Muki, competing in the men's half-middleweight (-81kg) division. His route to the final was hard-fought, and the final itself, against Belgium's Matthias Casse, tighter still: Muki picked up two shido penalties and came within one more of disqualification before the bout went to golden score. There, he threw Casse for the score that settled it, and the gold medal was his.

What followed was the historic part. As Muki stood on the podium, the Israeli flag was raised over the arena and, for the first time in the country's sporting history, Hatikvah was played inside the United Arab Emirates. Israel's Minister of Culture and Sport, Miri Regev, who had travelled to Abu Dhabi with the delegation, was visibly emotional as she sang along from the stands.

Coverage of the moment spread quickly through Israeli and international media — a judo mat, of all places, had become the setting for a small but unmistakable diplomatic marker, two years before the Abraham Accords formally opened relations between Israel and the UAE.

Muki's career did not stop there. Less than a year later, at the 2019 World Judo Championships in Tokyo, he met Casse again — this time in the world final — and beat him once more, becoming the first Israeli man to win a judo world title.

The Abu Dhabi ban and its reversal remain a small but telling chapter in Israeli sport: proof that a single bout, and a single anthem finally allowed to play, could carry weight far beyond the scoreboard.
facts: Sagi Muki beat Belgium's Matthias Casse by ippon in golden score to win men's -81kg gold at the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam on 28 October 2018.
It was the first time Israel's anthem, Hatikvah, was played at a medal ceremony inside the United Arab Emirates.

A year earlier, at the same event, gold medallist Tal Flicker had the Israeli flag and anthem withheld; organisers played International Judo Federation symbols instead while Flicker sang Hatikvah to himself.
In July 2018 the International Judo Federation suspended the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam and the Tunis Grand Prix until their organisers guaranteed equal treatment of all competing nations.
Israel's Minister of Culture and Sport, Miri Regev, attended the 2018 ceremony and was visibly emotional as the anthem played.
Ten months later, in Tokyo, Muki beat Casse again in the final of the 2019 World Judo Championships to become the first Israeli man to win a judo world title.

title: Ester Sokler set to land in Israel ahead of Maccabi Tel Aviv signing
dek: The Slovenian striker is flying in to complete a reported €1 million move from Serbia's Radnički 1923, fighting off interest from Red Star Belgrade and Partizan.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's chase of a new frontman is reaching its final stretch. Sport5 reports that Ester Sokler, the Slovenian striker at Serbian side Radnički 1923, is set to land in Israel overnight into Sunday ahead of completing his transfer to the Yellow-and-Blue.

The move, according to Sport5, is worth in the region of €1 million to Radnički, who signed Sokler permanently in January 2026 after a season-long loan spell. Israel Hayom and Sport1 both report the fee and the club's advanced position in the deal, with Sokler expected to undergo a medical before putting pen to paper.

Maccabi's interest did not go unchallenged. Israel Hayom reports that Red Star Belgrade, Vojvodina and city rivals Partizan Belgrade all made a run at the 27-year-old, but that Maccabi's financial offer proved the most attractive, tipping the race in the Israeli club's favour.

Sokler is no stranger to physically demanding schedules. Sport5 notes he featured for 66 minutes in Radnički's league fixture against Novi Pazar last weekend, evidence he arrives in Israel already match-sharp rather than needing time to build fitness during pre-season.

The Slovenian's numbers have been eye-catching. Sport5 credits him with 11 league goals for Radnički in the 2025-26 campaign, continuing a scoring streak that began during his loan spell from Aberdeen, the Scottish Premiership club he had joined in the summer of 2023.

Born in Krško on 4 June 1999, Sokler has climbed steadily through the ranks of Slovenian football before making his move abroad, and he earned his first cap for the Slovenia national team in a friendly against Cyprus in June 2026.

According to ONE, the push to bring Sokler to Bloomfield Stadium has come in part from Maccabi's new professional manager, who reportedly sees significant upside in the forward and views him as a central piece of the squad's attacking rebuild.

The signing would add to what has already been a busy window for the champions. Sport5 notes Maccabi has also brought in Christian Beetz and Dan Glazer this summer, and the club is continuing to search for a right winger to succeed Amir Sehiti.

Nothing is official yet — the reported fee, wages and precise signing date are still transfer-market reporting rather than a club announcement, and Maccabi Tel Aviv has not yet confirmed the move on its own channels. But with Sokler already in the air, the formal unveiling appears to be a matter of days, not weeks.

title: Doubts grow over Raphaelov and Bachar's rebuild at Maccabi Haifa after derby defeat
dek: A Toto Cup loss to Hapoel Haifa - the club's first in the competition since 1997 - puts an early dent in the sporting director and coach's plans to reshape the squad.

verificationSources.label: Sport1 Maariv - Toto Cup match report

body: Maccabi Haifa's rebuilt football operation got its first real test on Saturday, and it did not go the way sporting director Lior Raphaelov and head coach Barak Bachar would have wanted.

Two days earlier, the pair had sat together at a press conference to lay out their vision for 2026/27, talking about forging a group with real character and repairing the bond with supporters, according to ONE.

Instead, Maccabi opened the season with a 3-2 Toto Cup defeat to local rivals Hapoel Haifa - the first time Hapoel have beaten their neighbours in the competition since 1997, a statistic that will sting far more than a single group-stage result normally would.

There were notes of continuity out on the pitch. Omri Glazer, back at the club for a second spell, started in goal and wore the captain's armband, with Kenji Gorré - the player Raphaelov has since named as the club's first captain for the season - still away on international duty and expected to join up only once his summer commitments end.

Off the pitch, the turnover that defined Maccabi's summer was still being felt keenly. Dolev Haziza, a fixture at the club for seven years, and Abdulai Seck, in his fourth season, have both left, while Goni Naor - who had reportedly already been told he was out of the club's plans - was thrown into the derby and was involved in the mistakes that led to Hapoel's goals, according to Sport1.
Raphaelov's plan also includes a three-captain system for the season, with Glazer and Ali Mohamed set to share leadership duties alongside Gorré once the squad is back to full strength.

Bachar, who returned for a third spell in charge after being let go only months earlier, has been open about the scale of the job in front of him. "I've changed - what happened last season cannot come back," he told Walla Sport, referring to a campaign that ended with Maccabi Haifa down in fifth place.

That finish is why the club chose to keep Bachar rather than replace him, while handing broader control of the football side to Raphaelov as sporting director - a restructuring meant to give the coach more support, not less scrutiny.

One defeat in the Toto Cup will not define whether that restructuring works. But it has sharpened the questions Raphaelov and Bachar will face all season: whether the squad has the depth to cope with departures like Haziza's and Seck's, whether new arrivals are ready to contribute immediately, and whether the promised team identity shows up once the games start to matter.

title: Ankalaev overpowers Guskov with fifth-round TKO in Abu Dhabi return
dek: Stepping in as a late replacement, Bogdan Guskov ran into a resurgent former champion who ground him down over four rounds before Magomed Ankalaev finished him with strikes at Etihad Arena.

verificationSources.label: Sherdog - UFC Abu Dhabi play-by-play and records

body: Magomed Ankalaev needed only one entrance back in the cage to remind the light heavyweight division why he was wearing UFC gold barely a year ago, grinding down late replacement Bogdan Guskov over five rounds before finishing him with strikes on the canvas in the main event at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi.

The stoppage came at 2:41 of the fifth round, referee Marc Goddard stepping in as Ankalaev poured down ground-and-pound on a Guskov who had absorbed increasing punishment through the championship rounds.

It was hardly a vintage headline fight before that final flurry. Ankalaev out-worked Guskov on the feet through the first three rounds and controlled him against the fence and on the mat in the fourth, patiently building toward a finish rather than chasing an early one.

Guskov was a late addition to the card. He stepped in after Khalil Rountree Jr., originally slated to headline opposite Ankalaev, withdrew with an injury less than two weeks before fight night - a short-notice assignment Guskov accepted after, by his own account, few other contenders wanted the fight at all.

For Ankalaev, the win was as much about repairing his own résumé as beating an opponent. He had taken the UFC light heavyweight title from Alex Pereira at UFC 313 last year, only to lose it back inside 80 seconds when Pereira reclaimed the belt by first-round TKO at UFC 320. Saturday's bout was contested at a non-title 205 pounds.
The victory moves Ankalaev's UFC record to 13-2-1, with one no-contest, and 20-2-1 overall - a résumé that still ranks among the deepest in the division despite the Pereira setback.

Guskov's night ended a genuine run. He had gone unbeaten in five straight fights before Saturday, and his only previous UFC loss had come by submission to Volkan Oezdemir back in September 2023. He falls to 18-4-1 overall.

Speaking afterward, Ankalaev thanked his short-notice opponent rather than dwelling on the fight's slow pace. "I want to say thank you to Bogdan for coming in here and saving the fight," he said, acknowledging that without Guskov's willingness to step in, Abu Dhabi would have lost its main event entirely.

Ankalaev then turned his attention to the top of the division, calling out champion Carlos Ulberg for a light heavyweight title shot. Ulberg has held the belt since knocking out Jiri Prochazka for the vacant title at UFC 327 but has been sidelined ever since following surgery on a torn ACL, leaving his return timeline - and the title picture above Ankalaev - unsettled for now.

title: Zamir admits disappointment as Netanya move collapsed, pledges commitment to Hapoel Jerusalem
dek: The Hapoel Jerusalem goalkeeper addressed the transfer talk after his side's 3-1 Toto Cup opening defeat to Maccabi Netanya.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Zamir on the Netanya transfer talk
Walla Sport - Maccabi Netanya 3-1 Hapoel Jerusalem match report
Walla Sport - Lior Zada appointed Hapoel Jerusalem coach

body: Nadav Zamir did not try to hide it: a summer move to Maccabi Netanya that never materialized still stings. Speaking after Hapoel Jerusalem's season-opening Toto Cup defeat to the very club he was linked with, the goalkeeper told reporters, as quoted by ONE, that the collapsed transfer was a source of real frustration even as he threw his weight fully behind his current employers.

"It's clearly disappointing that the move didn't happen, but Hapoel Jerusalem is one of the best clubs in the country," Zamir said, according to ONE, which did not detail why the switch fell through. "It's an honor to be here, and I hope both I and the team have a better season than last year."

The comments came hours after Maccabi Netanya beat Hapoel Jerusalem 3-1 at Netanya Stadium on Saturday evening, in the opening round of Group B in the Toto Cup, the pre-season tournament that serves as the traditional curtain-raiser for Ligat Ha'al clubs ahead of the league campaign.

Bassam Zarour put the hosts ahead in the tenth minute and Oz Biloo doubled the lead midway through the first half, before Israel Dafna pulled one back for Jerusalem. Netanya sealed the win late on through 15-year-old Yirin Abuhatzira, who scored on his senior debut, according to Walla Sport.

Zamir, who was between the posts for the defeat, was candid about his own role in it. "I can't say we played poorly, but we made too many mistakes, including myself, and ultimately that cost us goals," he said, per ONE's report.

Head coach Lior Zada was equally blunt in his own assessment, saying his side "handed out too many gifts" in the first half and "didn't enter the match well, giving Netanya what they excel at." He added that the team "conceded again and again" and has "many things to improve" defensively before the league campaign begins.

Zada, who took interim charge in April after Ziv Arie's departure and was confirmed as full-time coach for 2026-27 having steered Hapoel Jerusalem to safety in the closing rounds last season, said reinforcements are still needed. "We still lack players in midfield and attack; we have plans to sign players and will strengthen with three or four more," he said. "It's a difficult summer, but we're patient, and I'm genuinely optimistic about this season."

Zamir, 25, has been Hapoel Jerusalem's first-choice goalkeeper since joining from Ironi Kiryat Shmona in 2023, and any interest from Maccabi Netanya would have represented a return to Ligat Ha'al rivals rather than a step up, since both clubs play in the top flight this coming season. For now, though, he remains part of a squad still being reshaped for a campaign that begins in earnest next month.

title: Barcelona turn to Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi as Alvarez pursuit stalls, ONE reports
dek: With Atletico Madrid refusing to sell Julian Alvarez, Barcelona have reopened talks over the 20-year-old French forward as a long-term successor to Robert Lewandowski — though Bournemouth insist he is not for sale.

verificationSources.label: Barca Blaugranes — Bournemouth chief's message on Kroupi
Sportingpedia — Atletico stand firm on Alvarez

body: Barcelona's search for a long-term replacement for Robert Lewandowski has taken an unexpected turn towards the English south coast, with ONE reporting that the club has revived its interest in Bournemouth striker Eli Junior Kroupi after its pursuit of Julian Alvarez stalled.

According to the report, sporting director Deco has put Kroupi's name back on the table having first tracked the 20-year-old Frenchman during his breakout season at Lorient. Barcelona had preferred Alvarez, but Atletico Madrid's leadership has repeatedly and publicly refused to sell the Argentine this summer, with club president Enrique Cerezo insisting he would not accept even a €200 million offer.

That impasse, ONE reports, has pushed Barcelona to look again at Kroupi as a cheaper and more attainable alternative up front, even if he offers a very different profile to the ageing Lewandowski, whom Barcelona expect to move on from before long.

Kroupi joined Bournemouth for around €13 million after finishing as Ligue 2's top scorer with Lorient, a move he made despite the club's relegation from Ligue 1 — a decision widely read at the time as a mark of his character. He has since become one of the Premier League's most closely watched young forwards, scoring 13 goals in 35 top-flight appearances in his debut English season.

That form has made him one of the most sought-after teenagers — now 20 — in Europe. Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich have all been linked with the France Under-21 international over the past year, according to the wider reporting around the player.

Bournemouth, however, are giving no indication they intend to let him leave. ONE quotes the club's stance as refusing to sell "even for €100 million," a line consistent with comments attributed to Bournemouth's football hierarchy, led by president of football operations Tiago Pinto, in Spanish outlet Marca, which has reported Kroupi has been formally marked as untouchable at Dean Court this summer.
Kroupi is under contract with the Cherries until 2030, and the club is under no financial pressure to sell a player it signed for a fraction of his current valuation just eighteen months ago.

For Barcelona, already stretched by the financial gymnastics required to register new signings under La Liga's spending rules, meeting or approaching a fee of that size for a forward with only one full Premier League season behind him would represent a significant gamble — one the club has not yet shown it is ready to make.

No bid has been reported, and Bournemouth's public position suggests any approach would be rejected outright. The story, as ONE frames it, is for now a reflection of Barcelona's shifting priorities as the Alvarez chase drags on, rather than confirmation of an imminent move for Kroupi.

title: Fenerbahçe closes in on Johnny Juzang as Maccabi Tel Aviv also circled the guard
dek: The Turkish champions are deep in negotiations for the American guard fresh off a stint at Zenit St. Petersburg, according to a report, in a chase that had also drawn interest from Maccabi Tel Aviv and Olympiacos.
body: Fenerbahçe are in advanced negotiations to sign Johnny Juzang, the American guard who spent the second half of last season with Zenit St. Petersburg, according to a report by the Israeli outlet ONE.

The 25-year-old, listed at 2.01 metres, has emerged as one of the names Fenerbahçe are chasing as they retool after a bruising exit from this year's EuroLeague Final Four, where they were beaten 79-61 by Olympiacos in the semifinal.

Juzang is no stranger to being pursued by Israeli basketball either. Ynet reported earlier this summer, citing Italian journalist Matteo Andreani, that Maccabi Tel Aviv was tracking him as it hunts for NBA-experienced reinforcements alongside newly signed guard Lonnie Walker and ongoing talks with Jeff Dowtin Jr. That same report named Olympiacos and Fenerbahçe as competitors for his signature, the same two clubs now in the mix months later.
Should the move to Istanbul go through, it would end any lingering hope in Tel Aviv of adding Juzang to the roster.

Juzang's route to European basketball has been unusual. Undrafted out of college despite a strong NCAA Tournament run with UCLA, he spent three seasons with the Utah Jazz on a mix of two-way and standard contracts before being waived in the summer of 2025.

He then signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves on an Exhibit 10 deal, was elevated to a two-way contract, and was ultimately released after hitting his 50-game NBA active-roster limit under two-way rules.

That release led him to Zenit St. Petersburg in February 2026, his first taste of professional basketball outside the United States. Over 17 games in Russia he averaged 14.0 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists, numbers that appear to have caught Fenerbahçe's attention.
Before turning pro, Juzang played a season at Kentucky before transferring to UCLA, where he earned third-team All-American honors as a junior in 2022.

Fenerbahçe have already been busy rebuilding this offseason, adding Shane Larkin, Trent Forrest, Ignas Sargiūnas, Shabazz Napier, Braxton Key, Will Clyburn and Marcus Bingham as they look to go a step further in next season's EuroLeague after last season's semifinal defeat to Olympiacos.
Neither Fenerbahçe nor Zenit has commented publicly, and ONE's report describes the talks as advanced rather than concluded, so a formal announcement has not yet followed.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv closing in on guard Eugene German after Motley's exit
dek: The Israeli champions are in advanced talks with the American combo guard, per ONE, as they rebuild their backcourt following Johnathan Motley's move to Crvena Zvezda.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv are closing in on American guard Eugene German, according to a report from ONE, as the reigning EuroCup champions move to fill the backcourt hole left by Johnathan Motley's departure.

German, 28, is a 1.83m combo guard who is fresh off his most recent stop in Puerto Rico with Indios de Mayagüez, where he averaged 17.4 points, 3.5 rebounds and 4.5 assists across eight league games, per ONE's figures.

The American arrives with an itinerant pro resume built almost entirely overseas. After going undrafted out of Northern Illinois University in the 2020 NBA Draft, he has played across Greece, Turkey, China and now the Caribbean, with his Turkish spell producing averages around 18 points a game.

At Northern Illinois, German left as the program's all-time leading scorer with 2,203 points, one of the more prolific runs in Mid-American Conference history, before turning pro without an NBA path opening up for him.

Independently, Sport5 has also reported Hapoel in advanced negotiations for a guard, naming German alongside Jamir Young as the two leading candidates, with the club running parallel talks and looking to close with one of them.

The vacancy has opened up after Johnathan Motley, last season's EuroCup Finals MVP, completed his move away from Hapoel to Crvena Zvezda (Red Star Belgrade), leaving a sizeable gap in a backcourt and frontcourt mix that helped deliver the title.

Hapoel have already moved on the perimeter this summer, confirming a one-year deal for Czech guard Tomas Satoransky following his release from Barcelona after a career that also included six NBA seasons.
Sport5's reporting suggests any German deal is likely to be a short-term contract for several months rather than one running through the full season, though the precise length has not been settled.
Nothing has been signed yet on either side, and both ONE and Sport5 frame this as advanced talks rather than a completed transfer, so the move is not yet official.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv fear three-month absence for Belić after foot fracture
dek: The Serbian midfielder was helped off in tears just eight minutes after coming on in the Europa League qualifier at Sheriff Tiraspol, in the latest setback of an injury-ravaged year.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz (Maccabi exercise permanent option on Belić)

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's relief at a thumping start to their European qualifying campaign has been tempered by grim medical news: Kristijan Belić, the Serbian midfielder known in the Hebrew press as Christian Blitz, is facing up to three months out with a fractured foot, Sport5 reports.

Belić had only just been passed fit after an earlier fitness scare and was sent on as a 64th-minute substitute in Maccabi's Europa League qualifying first leg away to Sheriff Tiraspol on July 23. He lasted just eight minutes before pulling up and signalling for the bench.
He was helped from the pitch in tears, with club staff visibly shaken on the touchline. Maccabi went on to win the match 5-0, but the result was overshadowed by the sight of yet another Belić injury.

Scans back in Israel have now confirmed the club's worst fears — a fracture in the foot, with Sport5's initial assessment putting his recovery window at up to three months, a spell that would carry him well past the Europa League qualifying rounds and deep into the domestic season.

It is a cruel continuation of a season that has repeatedly been derailed by fitness problems for the 25-year-old. Belić has already lost long stretches of playing time this year to a complete quadriceps tear and, more recently, a back complaint that limited his availability even before this latest blow.

The timing stings all the more given how highly the club rates him. Belić arrived on loan from AZ Alkmaar last August, and Maccabi moved in June to exercise their option and sign him permanently on a contract running to 2029, having seen him rack up 23 appearances and two assists in his debut campaign.
For now, Maccabi must plan around his absence for the Europa League return leg and beyond, a fresh test of squad depth just as continental and league commitments begin to overlap.
Sport5 describes the diagnosis as an initial estimate, with a fuller prognosis likely to follow once the club's medical staff complete their assessment of the fracture.

title: Peretz can't guarantee Songa and Roei David will stay at Hapoel Petah Tikva
dek: The Hapoel coach savoured a derby win over Maccabi Petah Tikva to open the Toto Cup, but admitted he cannot promise his two most closely watched players will still be at the club when the transfer window shuts.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — Peretz post-match remarks on Songa and Roei David
Ynet live match tracker — Hapoel Petah Tikva 1-0 Maccabi Petah Tikva, full time

body: A stoppage-time strike from an academy graduate gave Hapoel Petah Tikva bragging rights in the season-opening derby, but it was a throwaway line about two of his most important players that lingered longest after coach Omer Peretz's press conference.

Asked directly whether winger Chipyoka Songa and midfielder Roei David would still be at the club by the time the transfer window closes, Peretz refused to offer any assurances. "I cannot guarantee anything, this is football," he said, acknowledging that an unexpected offer for either player could force the club to sell regardless of its own plans for the squad.

It was a notably candid admission from a coach fresh off a derby win, and a reminder that even a player who has just signed fresh terms is never entirely safe from a lucrative bid. Songa, a Zambia international who joined from Nes Tziona's academy in 2023, put pen to paper on a three-year extension through 2027/28 after Hapoel exercised their purchase option on him, and has since become one of the more admired wingers in Israeli football.

Roei David, a product of the same production line that Peretz has leaned on heavily since taking charge, started in central midfield in Saturday's derby and remains a fixture in Hapoel's plans — for now.

The match itself, played in front of 3,729 spectators at HaMoshava Stadium, was settled deep into stoppage time. Noam Cohen, another graduate of the Hapoel academy, drove a shot from distance past Maccabi goalkeeper Maor Arlich in the 89th minute to seal a 1-0 win in the first round of the Toto Cup.

Peretz pointed to Cohen's goal as proof of concept for the pathway he has tried to build between the club's youth sides and the first team. "The academy is giving us answers," he said, framing the development work as central to how Hapoel intend to compete without the transfer budgets of Israel's bigger clubs.

Across the technical area, Maccabi Petah Tikva coach Ziv Arieh, who took over in late May after leaving Hapoel Jerusalem, put the defeat down in part to fatigue among several of his key players rather than any tactical shortcoming.

Both coaches were keen to play down the significance of the result itself, describing the derby more as a useful pre-season workout than a fixture to draw sweeping conclusions from at this early stage of the campaign.

For Hapoel Petah Tikva, though, the more pointed storyline is the one Peretz raised unprompted: a club enjoying the fruits of its academy work while bracing for the possibility that its brightest products, Songa and Roei David included, could be sold from underneath it before the season gets fully under way.

title: Maccabi Netanya's 16-year-old Abuhatzira becomes youngest scorer in Toto Cup history
dek: Roni Levy says Yarin Abuhatzira's ability will earn him more minutes after the teenager struck in a 3-1 opening win over Hapoel Jerusalem.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — Roni Levy on Yarin Abuhatzira
ONE — Abuhatzira signs new Maccabi Netanya contract

body: On the very first competitive night of Israel's new season, it was a 16-year-old who made the history books. Yarin Abuhatzira came off the bench to score for Maccabi Netanya as they beat Hapoel Jerusalem 3-1 in the opening round of the Toto Cup, becoming, according to Sport5, the youngest goalscorer in the competition's history.

Netanya controlled large parts of the match, with Bassam Zarura also on the scoresheet and setting up a second goal on a night head coach Roni Levy could point to for both the present and the future of his squad.
"Abuhatzira? I think the kid is showing his ability in training and in practice matches, and it's very high," Levy said afterwards. "Because of that ability, he'll play and he'll get minutes."

It is the kind of endorsement that carries weight coming from Levy, who has already handed the teenager senior minutes and training-camp time this pre-season. Abuhatzira is the son of Shimon Abuhatzira, the former Israel international striker, and has torn through the club's youth ranks as a prolific finisher at every age group before breaking into first-team contention.
Levy was equally pleased with Zarura, praising the forward's physical presence as a weapon Netanya can lean on through the campaign.

The win capped a productive return for Levy himself, who is in his second spell in charge of Maccabi Netanya, the club where he grew up as a player. He was appointed in January on an 18-month deal to replace Yossi Abuksis, arriving after a spell at Hapoel Haifa and with a résumé that includes three straight Israeli titles at Maccabi Haifa in the mid-2000s.

It was a rougher evening for Hapoel Jerusalem, who fell behind early and never fully recovered. Manager Lior Zada, who only took over from Ziv Aryeh in April, admitted his side looked "in shock" for large stretches before finding a better level in the second half.
Goalkeeper Nadav Zamir, usually a reliable presence between the posts, also conceded he was uncharacteristically error-prone on the night.

For Netanya, the Toto Cup curtain-raiser offered an early glimpse of the kind of squad depth Levy will be counting on once the Ligat Ha'al season gets under way — with a teenage forward suddenly very much part of those plans.

title: Ironi Tiberias fight back to beat Sakhnin in Toto Cup opener amid scandal turmoil
dek: Assistant coach Moti Crispiel said he told his players to set aside the club's doping-related suspensions and focus on football, after a 2-1 comeback win over Bnei Sakhnin.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz - Tiberias coach and five players suspended

body: Ironi Tiberias opened their 2026/27 campaign with a gritty comeback on Saturday evening, coming from 1-2 down to beat Bnei Sakhnin 2-1 in their opening Toto Cup group match at Ramat Hasharon — a rare bright spot for a club still reeling from a scandal that has gutted its coaching staff and dressing room.

Tiberias fielded the side without head coach Eliran Houdda, who along with five first-team players remains provisionally barred from involvement by Israel's National Anti-Doping Agency in what the Israeli press has dubbed "the infusions affair" — an investigation into banned intravenous treatments allegedly administered to players at the end of last season.

Prosecutors are now seeking sanctions against six club figures tied to the case, ranging from lengthy suspensions to lifetime bans, according to Walla, Haaretz and Ynet. Houdda, general manager Gavriel Cohen, fitness coach Shlomi Vidraro, technical director Chen Sol, the club's suspended owner Miki Bitan and staff member Aviv Givli are all named in the proceedings.

With Houdda sidelined, it fell to assistant coach Moti Crispiel to take charge for the trip to Ramat Hasharon, and he made clear before kickoff that he wanted the turmoil left at the door. He had told the players simply to set everything aside and concentrate on the football, he said afterwards.
It nearly didn't work. Tiberias were poor for long stretches of the first half and slipped 2-1 behind as Sakhnin punished a sluggish start to the game.

A round of second-half substitutions changed the complexion of the match, though, and Tiberias fought their way back to snatch the win. "I'm happy the players knew how to put everything aside and win," Crispiel said, according to ONE.

For Sakhnin, the defeat carried its own warning signs. Head coach Yossi Abuksis — back for a second spell in charge after being appointed this summer following his dismissal at Maccabi Netanya — acknowledged that his side had controlled the opening 45 minutes without turning that dominance into a lead they could protect.

Abuksis added that his squad is still far from complete for the season ahead, saying he needs six or seven more signings before the Ligat Ha'al campaign begins, after several targeted foreign players turned down moves to Israel.

The win offers little more than a morale boost for Tiberias, whose off-field situation remains unresolved. The anti-doping prosecution's push for lengthy or lifetime bans against six club figures is still pending, but for one evening in late July, a group-stage comeback was treated as proof the squad can still function as a team.

title: Netanya open season with 3-1 win over Jerusalem as 15-year-old Abuhatzira scores
dek: Yarin Abuhatzira, two days short of his 16th birthday, struck late on as Maccabi Netanya beat Hapoel Jerusalem in the opening round of the Toto Cup.

body: Maccabi Netanya opened their 2026/27 campaign with a 3-1 win over Hapoel Jerusalem in the first round of the Toto Cup on Saturday, but the result was overshadowed by a 15-year-old who is fast becoming the most talked-about name in Israeli football.

Yarin Abuhatzira, who turns 16 on Monday, came off the bench and settled the contest in the 75th minute, running through one-on-one after being sent clear by a long ball forward and finishing coolly past the Jerusalem goalkeeper.

Netanya had led twice before that. Bassem Zarura opened the scoring in the 10th minute, tapping in after a cutback from Oz Bilu, before Israel Daffa levelled for Jerusalem in the 23rd when a shot deflected in off a defender. Bilu restored the hosts' lead five minutes later, capitalising on a mistake from Nadav Zamir in the Jerusalem back line.
Abuhatzira's goal was described by Sport5 as his first in senior, official competition for the club he has represented since childhood.

The teenager is the son of Shimon Abuhatzira, a well-known striker of the previous generation, and has trained with Netanya's first-team squad for the best part of a year despite not yet being old enough to sign a full professional contract. He has already been earmarked by the club as one of the outstanding prospects in the country, and reports in the Israeli press over recent months have linked his development to a future big-money move once he is eligible to leave.

Saturday's match also marked the competitive start of Roni Levi's second stint in charge of Maccabi Netanya. Levi, who returned to the club he supported as a boy in January after leaving Hapoel Haifa, replaced Yossi Abuksis and is looking to build on a positive finish to last season.
In the day's other Toto Cup fixture, Ironi Tiberias beat Bnei Sakhnin 2-1, with Ron Unger and Mansour Badji turning the match around after Iyad Abu Abid had put Sakhnin ahead.

For Netanya, three points and three points of local intrigue: a maiden senior goal for arguably the most exciting teenage talent to emerge from the club's academy in years, delivered two days before he is even old enough to call himself sixteen.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv eye Jahmir Young and Shake Milton to replace Lonnie Walker
dek: With Lonnie Walker's Tel Aviv exit gathering pace, the Israeli champions are weighing an undrafted Miami Heat summer-league standout against a battle-tested former Sixers guard now free after Partizan cut ties with him.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are already plotting the next move in their backcourt, and it looks like Lonnie Walker's time in yellow and blue is running out. According to Sport5, the club and the American guard are edging toward a mutual parting of ways, and Maccabi have quietly identified two possible replacements.

One is a name few Israeli fans will recognise yet: Jahmir Young, an undrafted 1.88-metre combo guard who lit up the NBA Summer League with Miami this month, averaging 20.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.0 assists a game. Young went unpicked in the 2024 draft after college stints at Charlotte and Maryland, and Sport5 notes Hapoel Tel Aviv also explored signing him before opting for Eugene Germain instead.

The other option carries far more pedigree. Shake Milton spent seven seasons in the NBA with Philadelphia and the Lakers, appearing in 359 games, before moving to Europe last season with Partizan Belgrade. His EuroLeague debut was modest — 6.9 points a game while managing injury issues — though he was sharper in the Adriatic League, shooting 46.9 percent from three on his way to 11.9 points a night.

Milton is now a free agent after Partizan exercised an opt-out clause and confirmed it would not continue with him for next season, a move the Belgrade club announced on social media as it turns to other guard options. Serbian outlets have since floated Maccabi Tel Aviv as a possible landing spot, a link Sport5 also reports.

Walker's own situation has been building for weeks. Reports out of Spain and Serbia have suggested EuroLeague rivals, including Real Madrid, are monitoring his availability, with his Maccabi contract believed to carry NBA opt-out windows each July that give him a route back to the league if he wants it.

The guard's frustration with the Israeli league boiled over during the recent playoffs, when he publicly criticised the decision to press ahead with the postseason schedule amid the season's turmoil, telling reporters at the time that players were "not robots."

Neither Young nor Milton has been confirmed as a signing, and Sport5's report frames both as names Maccabi have simply marked as options rather than targets already in advanced talks. Still, the fact that the club is scouting both an emerging Summer League riser and a proven if inconsistent NBA veteran suggests the Walker decision is close.

Maccabi Tel Aviv open their EuroLeague campaign in the coming months and will want backcourt clarity well before then, particularly with the club again expected to challenge on multiple fronts domestically and in Europe.

title: Bayern Munich shut down Real Madrid talk over Michael Olise
dek: Sporting director Christoph Freund insists the France winger's future is not in question, dismissing reports linking him with a stunning move to Real Madrid
body: Bayern Munich have moved quickly to close down talk of a blockbuster move for Michael Olise, with sporting director Christoph Freund declaring that speculation over a switch to Real Madrid "doesn't concern us at all."

Freund fielded the question after Bayern's pre-season friendly defeat to Wehen Wiesbaden, and his answer left little room for interpretation: Olise, he said, will again be a central figure for the club this coming season, exactly as he was in the last one.

The Frenchman signed for Bayern from Crystal Palace in the summer of 2024 for around €53 million and needed almost no time to settle. He is under contract at the Allianz Arena until June 2029, and according to reports in the German and Spanish press, Bayern are already working on extending that deal to 2031, with his wages set to rise from roughly €15 million to around €25 million a year.

The numbers behind Bayern's determination to keep him are hard to argue with. Olise finished last season with 22 goals and 31 assists in 52 appearances across all competitions, including 15 goals and 19 assists in the Bundesliga alone, form that earned him the league's Player of the Season award. In the Champions League he added four goals and seven assists as Bayern reached the semi-finals.

The Real Madrid rumours had gathered pace over recent days, with some reports in Spain suggesting the European champions could be readying an offer in the region of €223 million, a figure that would shatter the world transfer record. Real Madrid themselves issued a statement denying any contact with Olise, his representatives or those around him.

Freund's comments were the clearest signal yet from Bayern's side that the club regards the matter as settled. Olise, who took part in this summer's World Cup with France, is currently on vacation and is expected back in Munich for the start of pre-season training with no suggestion of a departure.

For Bayern, the message is less about reacting to a single rumour than about protecting the identity of a squad built around Olise, Harry Kane and Luis Diaz up front. Losing their standout performer of the season, even to a fee north of €200 million, was never seriously on the table.

body: Christian Blitz is facing what could be a lengthy spell on the sidelines after Maccabi Tel Aviv confirmed the Serbian midfielder has fractured a bone in his foot, ONE reported on Saturday.

The injury happened during Thursday's Europa League second qualifying round first leg against Sheriff Tiraspol in Moldova, a match Maccabi won 5:0. Blitz, who was himself only just back from an earlier injury, was sent on as a 64th-minute substitute but lasted just eight minutes before being caught by what ONE described as a strong step on his foot during a challenge, forcing him off again in the 72nd minute.
He needed crutches to leave Moldova, and a full round of medical tests after the squad returned to Israel confirmed a fracture in one of the metatarsal bones in his midfoot.

ONE reports the initial recovery estimate is around three months, though the outlet is careful to note that timeframes for this type of injury are notoriously hard to pin down — Blitz could be back sooner, or the layoff could stretch on longer than first thought.

It is a cruel blow for a player who has struggled to stay fit since arriving in Israel. This is already Blitz's fifth injury of the season, with the 25-year-old having missed more than 20 matches across all competitions since his move.

Blitz joined Maccabi Tel Aviv on loan from AZ Alkmaar last season and quickly became one of the team's most important performers when available, making 23 appearances and scoring twice. The club moved this summer to exercise its option on the Serbian, who came through OFK Belgrade's youth system and later spent time in West Ham United's academy, signing him on a permanent deal running through 2029.

His fresh setback lands at an awkward moment for Maccabi's midfield planning as the club works through a busy transfer window. Slovenian striker Ester Sokler, closing in on a move from Serbian side Radnički 1923, landed in Israel on Saturday evening for medical examinations ahead of formally signing with the yellow-and-blue.
For now, the priority is simply getting Blitz through rehabilitation. Maccabi's medical staff are expected to reassess his recovery timeline in the coming weeks as he begins treatment.

title: Bachar vows Maccabi Haifa will sharpen up after Toto Cup derby defeat to Hapoel Haifa
dek: The Greens threw away a two-goal cushion and lost 3-2 to their city rivals in the season-opening Toto Cup match, but manager Barak Bachar insists there is 'plenty to work with'.
body: Maccabi Haifa opened their 2026/27 campaign with a chastening result in the Haifa derby, going down 3-2 to city rivals Hapoel Haifa in the opening match of the Toto Cup — the first time Hapoel have beaten the Greens in the competition since 1997.

Barak Bachar's side were second best for long spells, falling behind to a first-half strike from Yoad Gonen and an own goal, before Alon Torgeman made it 0-3 early in the second half. Substitutes Iad Halili and Etan Azulai pulled two goals back late on, but the comeback fell just short.

"This is an excellent preparation match to learn from mistakes," Bachar told reporters afterwards, choosing to frame the derby loss as a useful staging post rather than a cause for alarm this early in preseason.
"There is a lot of work, and there is also material to work with," he said, according to ONE, pointing to the response his players produced once trailing by three goals.

The manager singled out his bench for praise. "The substitutes added quality and helped us control the game," he said, before setting out his demands for the weeks ahead: "We will be more aggressive and sharp, that's the aspiration."

Bachar rang the changes at the break after his starting eleven, by his own admission, had looked short of ideas, sending on newly appointed vice-captain Kenji Gora among others to try to change the shape of the game.

Gora was named Maccabi Haifa's captain for the new season in the club's preseason announcement, with Omri Glazer handed the vice-captaincy — though it was Glazer, back involved after five years out of the frame and regaining the goalkeeper's jersey he lost last season, who wore the armband in Haifa.
The defeat came despite an encouraging buildup: Maccabi Haifa's squad returned from a training camp in Hungary where they beat Scottish side Nairn County and drew 3-3 with the Hungarian club Paks.

It is Bachar's third spell in charge at Maccabi Haifa. He returned in October 2025, five months after being let go, and signed a contract running through the summer of 2028. His task now is to turn preseason lessons into results before the Toto Cup group stage and the Ligat Ha'al campaign proper get under way, with the club still expected to add to the squad before the window closes.

body: Maccabi Haifa have sold goalkeeper Georgi Yarmakov to Ukrainian side Metalist Kharkiv, Sport5 reported, bringing to a close a transfer saga that ran through much of the summer.

The outlet put the fee at around €2.8 million, with the total climbing toward €3 million once add-on clauses are triggered — a hefty return on the roughly €100,000 Haifa paid to sign the 24-year-old from Oleksandriia back in the summer of 2024.

Yarmakov, born in Kyiv and from a Ukrainian Jewish family that later settled in Holon, came through Shakhtar Donetsk's academy before loan and permanent spells at Oleksandriia. He made his Israeli Premier League debut for Haifa only last August, but quickly became a fixture between the posts.
He started 37 league matches for Maccabi Haifa last season and kept 12 clean sheets, establishing himself as one of the club's standout performers even as speculation over his future grew.

According to Walla Sport, Yarmakov made clear he wanted to leave and did not rule out a return to Ukrainian football, with talks between the two clubs progressing steadily before Metalist's offer was accepted.

Haifa had already moved to cover the position, confirming goalkeeper Omri Glazer on a three-year deal after his return from Red Star Belgrade. The 30-year-old previously won the title with Haifa in the 2020/21 season.

"I always felt I had another chapter to write here, and today I'm happy to come back and close the circle," Glazer said after signing, according to Haaretz. "I'm excited to wear the green shirt again, return to Sami Ofer, meet the green crowd, and give everything in every training session and every game for the club."

With Yarmakov's exit and Glazer installed as first choice, Haifa have also been working the market for goalkeeping depth, with reports linking them to Maccabi Netanya's Omer Niron as a potential number two.

For Yarmakov, the move represents a homecoming of sorts to Ukrainian football, where he was previously part of the country's Olympic squad at the Paris 2024 Games, and a fresh chapter after two seasons in Israel that raised his profile considerably.

Gonen's celebrations after both goals were aimed squarely at the Maccabi Haifa end, according to Sport5, and the needle escalated further when referee Gal Leibovich sent off Hapoel goalkeeping coach Itai Zilpha following furious protests from the Maccabi bench.
The atmosphere boiled over again in the 38th minute, when cups thrown from the stands rained onto the pitch and struck Zuparic, who went down and required treatment before play could continue.
The Sammy Ofer Stadium announcer intervened directly, warning Maccabi Haifa supporters to stop throwing objects onto the field, Sport5 reported. Play resumed once Zuparic was able to continue.
This was the first meeting of the season between the two Haifa clubs, and derby matches between them have a long history of spilling over into confrontations both on the pitch and in the stands.

title: Israel's under-16 girls open water polo world championship with big win over South Africa
dek: Trailing early in Zagreb, the young Israeli water polo team rallied to beat South Africa 12-7 in their World Championship opener, with Yahali Rokach and Ori Grodman scoring three goals apiece.
body: Israel's under-16 girls water polo team opened the World Aquatics Women's U16 Championship in Zagreb with a statement result, beating South Africa 12-7 to launch the tournament on a high.
It did not start smoothly. Israel conceded the first two goals of the match and looked rattled before settling, then reeling off five unanswered goals to seize control.

By the break Israel led 6-4, and the young team pulled away further in the third quarter, outscoring South Africa 4-1 to open up a 10-5 cushion it would not relinquish before the final whistle sealed the 12-7 win.

The scoring was spread across the squad. Yahali Rokach and Ori Grodman each found the net three times, Yara Huvino Garcia added two, and Tamara Salmon-Michaeli, Inbar Yanko, Alma Tauber and Tamar Orchan all scored once.
Rokach's performance earned her Player of the Match honours in Israel's opening outing of the championship.

"The excitement was evident at the start, and then once the girls composed themselves they showed they're the stronger side," head coach Idan Kaftori said afterwards. "Tomorrow we have a very tough match against Hungary, one of the gold medal contenders."
Israel's Water Polo Association chair, Rona Freund-Amitzur, called it "a wonderful victory that gives the players confidence right at the opening of the World Championship."
Association CEO Dana Tartzki-Gatoa said the result was "an excellent start to a significant summer for Israeli water polo," adding that the team "showed character and demonstrated real ability."

The championship, the first of two World Aquatics under-16 events being staged in the Croatian capital this summer, is being played at Zagreb's Mladost aquatics complex from July 25 to 31, with the boys' edition to follow in August at the same venue.
Israel returns to the pool on Sunday to face Hungary, a considerably sterner test as the young team looks to build on its opening statement.

body: Bnei Yehuda have gone shopping in Moldova, confirming the signing of Brazilian winger Zé Flores from league champions Sheriff Tiraspol, ONE reported on Saturday.

The 27-year-old, born in Rio de Janeiro, has put pen to paper on a one-year contract that carries club options for two further seasons, according to the report. His move was brokered by agents Tamir Azizov and Kfir M. of the A.G Pro Agency.

Flores arrives with a solid pedigree in Moldova. ONE reports he spent two seasons at Sheriff Tiraspol after earlier spells in Italy and Lithuania, establishing himself as a regular attacking threat on the flank for the Tiraspol club.

Last season was his best yet: 11 goals from the wing as Sheriff won the Moldovan Cup. He had already featured for the club four times in the fledgling 2026/27 campaign — two Europa League qualifying ties and two league fixtures — before the move to Israel was finalised.

He now joins a Bnei Yehuda side rebuilding in Liga Leumit, Israel's second tier, where the Tel Aviv club reached the upper playoff bracket last season and will hope fresh attacking options can fire a push back toward the top flight.

"I'm very excited to join Bnei Yehuda," Flores said, according to ONE. "From the first moment I felt the club's strong desire to bring me and their trust in me... I'm already waiting to wear the orange shirt." He cited the club's history and passionate fanbase as factors in choosing the move.

title: Khalaili back in action with an assist as Union Saint-Gilloise edge Lille
dek: The Israeli winger, whose blockbuster move to Inter Milan collapsed over a failed medical, made an instant impact off the bench in a pre-season friendly in Brussels.
body: Anan Khalaili was back on a football pitch on Saturday for the first time since his headline-grabbing move to Inter Milan fell apart, and he needed only a few minutes to make his mark. The Israeli winger came off the bench for Union Saint-Gilloise and teed up the goal that beat Lille 2-1 in a pre-season friendly at Stade Joseph Marien in Brussels.

Louis Patris had put the Belgian champions ahead in the 25th minute before Lille, reduced to ten men after Saad Boussadia was sent off just after the half-hour, equalised through Gaëtan Perrin midway through the second half. Union SG restored their lead soon after, and this time an Israeli boot was involved in the build-up.

Khalaili was introduced in the 72nd minute and within two minutes had set up Besfort Zeneli for what proved the winning goal, ONE reported. It was a low-key stage for the 21-year-old's comeback — a summer friendly rather than a competitive fixture — but a significant one given the turbulent few weeks he has just had.

Khalaili had appeared set to complete a move to Inter Milan after the Serie A club reportedly beat Napoli to an agreement with Union Saint-Gilloise. According to Israeli reports, the transfer collapsed at the medical stage after Italy's Olympic committee, CONI, withheld the fitness clearance he needed to be registered — a rare and unusual reason for a deal of that size to fall through.

With Inter out of the picture, attention has swung back to Napoli, who Israeli outlets report have already reached an agreement with Khalaili on personal terms and are now negotiating with Union Saint-Gilloise over a fee. The Belgian club is said to be holding out for around €25 million, while Napoli's offer stands at roughly €18 million plus add-ons.

Khalaili joined Union Saint-Gilloise from Maccabi Haifa in the summer of 2024 for around €7.5 million and has since become one of the most sought-after Israeli players in Europe, helping the Belgian side to the league title and, this past season, the Belgian Cup.

For now, with his next club still unresolved, Saturday's outing offered a reminder of why so many clubs are chasing his signature — and gave Union Saint-Gilloise's coaching staff a timely reassurance ahead of the new season that their prized winger remains sharp, whoever ends up paying for him.

With those absences, and with recent signing Nigel Lonwijk having managed only a single training session since arriving, Naor has been drafted back into the matchday squad and could feature in central defence for the derby.

The timing underlines how thin Haifa's options are as they head into a season opener against their local rivals. For Naor, who was on the fringe of being frozen out entirely, the derby offers an unscheduled chance to be seen in action again, even if his longer-term standing at the club remains unresolved.

The 28-year-old, who left Northern Illinois University as the program's all-time leading scorer with 2,203 points, has spent the past few seasons bouncing between some of the more competitive leagues outside the NBA — Greece's top flight with Ionikos Nikaias, Turkey's Merkezefendi Belediyesi, and most recently China's CBA, where Sport5 says he averaged close to 18 points and around five assists a game while shooting well over 40 percent from three-point range. Slotting German into that mix on a short-term arrangement suggests the club see him as competition and depth for the backcourt rather than a marquee starter from day one.
According to Sport5, the length and structure of the deal reflect exactly that: a trial-style contract for the opening months of the season, with performance determining whether it gets extended.

The report adds an intriguing knock-on detail — if German settles in and performs, Tyler Ennis, who was hampered by injury for large parts of last season, could be loaned out to make room in the guard rotation.

title: Carapaz conquers Alpe d'Huez as Pogačar closes in on record-equalling fifth Tour title
dek: Richard Carapaz survived the race's hardest day to win solo into Alpe d'Huez after Sepp Kuss crashed twice while leading, and Tadej Pogačar now goes to Paris all but assured of a historic fifth yellow jersey.
body: Richard Carapaz rode into the record books at Alpe d'Huez on Saturday, soloing to victory on the hardest stage of this year's Tour de France after American rival Sepp Kuss crashed twice in the closing kilometres while leading the race up the mountain.

Stage 20 was always going to be brutal: a 144km slog from Bourg-d'Oisans over the Col de la Croix de Fer, the Col du Télégraphe and the Col du Galibier before a late detour over the Col de Sarenne and the finishing climb up Alpe d'Huez's 21 hairpins.

Kuss had forced his way clear and looked set for the biggest win of his career until he crashed twice inside the final seven kilometres, opening the door for Carapaz to sweep past and finish alone in front of the roaring crowds that line the mountain every July.

It was the Ecuadorian's second stage win of this Tour and his third career Tour de France stage victory, and it mathematically wrapped up the polka-dot King of the Mountains jersey for the EF Education-EasyPost rider, a fitting reward after days spent hunting points in the day's breakaways.

Remco Evenepoel crossed the line second on the stage, while Kuss picked himself up to salvage third place despite the crashes -- a cruel way to end a day in which he had ridden the strongest legs on the mountain.

Behind the stage drama, the overall picture barely moved. Tadej Pogačar defended the yellow jersey comfortably, and with only Sunday's ceremonial run into Paris left on the route, the Slovenian now heads to the Champs-Élysées with a lead of roughly six and a half minutes over Evenepoel.

Barring a mishap on the final stage -- traditionally a low-risk procession before a bunch sprint -- Pogačar will collect his fifth Tour de France title on Sunday, a tally that would equal the record held by Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain.
At 27, Pogačar would join that select company having already won in 2020, 2021, 2024 and 2025, cementing his place among the sport's dominant figures of any era.

Pogačar chose not to contest the stage finish himself, instead riding in support of teammate Isaac del Toro, who held onto third place overall. The young Mexican's closest challenger for the final podium spot and the white jersey, France's Paul Seixas of Decathlon CMA CGM, lost ground on the Sarenne climb and now trails del Toro by roughly 24 seconds heading into the last day.

That gap leaves Seixas, at just 19, with one last chance in Paris to snatch back the podium place and the best young rider's white jersey, though history suggests overturning even a small deficit on the largely processional final stage is a tall order.

For Carapaz, the win adds to a career that already includes Grand Tour victories at the Giro d'Italia and Vuelta a España, and takes him to ten Grand Tour stage wins overall -- a marker of one of the most versatile climbers of his generation.

title: World champion Norris snatches Hungarian GP pole from Hamilton by 0.012 seconds
dek: Lando Norris out-qualified Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by the tightest of margins at a scorching Hungaroring, while Max Verstappen spun and Ferrari face a stewards investigation over an alleged blocking incident.
body: Lando Norris arrived at the Hungaroring as Formula 1's reigning world champion and left qualifying with the one result that had eluded him so far this season: pole position, snatched from Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari by a scarcely believable 0.012 seconds.
Norris's McLaren stopped the clock at 1:17.207 in a sweltering Q3 session, with track temperatures reported around 50°C testing tyres and drivers alike on the tight, twisting Budapest circuit.
Hamilton, who has been chasing his first pole since moving to Ferrari, crossed the line at 1:17.219 - agonisingly close but not quite enough to deny Norris what is his first pole of the 2026 season.
Charles Leclerc completed a strong afternoon for Ferrari in third, just over two tenths back, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli fourth ahead of Norris's title rival and teammate Oscar Piastri in fifth.
Max Verstappen endured a scrappy session for Red Bull, spinning at the final corner during Q3 but still salvaging sixth on the grid, ahead of George Russell's Mercedes and Isack Hadjar's Red Bull.

The session was not without controversy. Hamilton is set to be investigated by the stewards over an alleged incident in which he impeded Piastri, who was forced to abandon his final flying lap as a result.
Antonelli is also facing scrutiny, with stewards examining whether the young Mercedes driver failed to sufficiently lift off the throttle under yellow flags shown late in the session.
Further down the order, Fernando Alonso provided one of the qualifying's feel-good stories, hauling his Aston Martin into Q2 despite the team's well-documented power deficit this season.

The margins at the top were about as tight as qualifying gets, but the significance goes beyond the stopwatch: it is Norris's first pole since being crowned champion, and a timely response after a season in which Ferrari and Mercedes have often had the edge over one lap.

With overtaking notoriously difficult around the narrow, twisting Hungaroring, Norris's pole - and Hamilton's proximity on the front row - sets up what should be a tense grand prix, with the stewards' rulings on the Piastri and Antonelli incidents still to be decided before lights out.

title: Robi Shapira Haifa's youth B side crowned Gulf League champions in a double-title season
dek: Mohamed Badran's goals help power a squad built almost from scratch to the Ligat Mafraz crown, completing a rare double for the fan-founded Haifa club alongside its Youth Gimel side's Northern League triumph.

verificationSources.label: ONE report on Robi Shapira Haifa's Youth B Gulf League title
