title: Not just a championship: the challenges awaiting LeBron James in Philadelphia
dek: James, 41, has called joining the 76ers his "last decision" - but fitting into a stacked roster, finding answers on defence and living up to Philadelphia's brutal fan pressure all come before any title talk.
body: LeBron James called it his "last decision," and it turned out to be the most startling one of his career: after a decade on the Lakers, the 41-year-old is joining the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million contract, choosing them over the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat and other contenders. But as ONE lays out, signing the deal was the easy part - fitting into his new team, staying healthy and surviving one of America's toughest fan bases may be a far bigger test than winning a fifth ring.

James arrives with a resume that speaks for itself: a four-time NBA champion, four-time MVP, 22-time All-Star and the league's all-time leading scorer. But last season's numbers told a more human story - 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists across 60 games, his lowest scoring average since his rookie year, with 22 games missed to back and foot problems.

In Philadelphia he joins arguably the most talented roster he has played on in more than two decades, alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and rising guard VJ Edgecombe. That talent is also the problem. Most of those players are used to having the ball in their hands, and head coach Nick Nurse now has to work out who gives up minutes, touches and shots to make room for a 41-year-old former MVP.

ONE draws the comparison to LeBron's arrival in Miami alongside Dwyane Wade - a process that took time and friction before the roles settled. Nurse, by reputation an excellent tactician, is reported by ONE to be less sure-footed when it comes to discipline and man-management, a dynamic that will be tested immediately with this many voices in one locker room.

A former coach quoted in the piece describes James as possessing elite-level basketball intelligence and professionalism - but notes that at this stage of his career, he no longer wants to be the one carrying the whole team on his own. That shift matters for a Sixers side that has spent years waiting for someone else to share the leadership load with Embiid.

Defence is the other open question. James is no longer the dominant defender he once was, Embiid continues to battle recurring physical issues, and much of the defensive burden already falls on Brown. Philadelphia will need answers against the league's biggest physical threats - centres like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo - and its most dangerous guards, from Stephen Curry to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

The move also scatters James's family across the country. His son Bronny stays behind with the Lakers, continuing his own NBA career on the other coast, while wife Savannah and daughter Zhuri adjust to a new base and younger son Bryce continues his college career at the University of Arizona.

Philadelphia's supporters are, by reputation, among the most demanding in American sport. The Sixers have not won a championship since 1983 and have not reached the NBA Finals since 2001. Anything short of genuine contention will invite the kind of scrutiny James has rarely faced in this form, even during his most difficult seasons in Los Angeles.

There is a quieter thread running through the move too: James reunites in the front office with Mike Gansey, Philadelphia's president of basketball operations, who competed against him for Ohio's Mr. Basketball award as a high schooler more than two decades ago and finished runner-up to him in 2001.

Health, more than talent, may end up deciding how this season is remembered. Embiid's injury history remains the single biggest variable in any Sixers plan, James is managing the wear of a 23rd NBA season, and Brown has had his own issues with his Achilles and wrist. If all three stay on the floor together, Philadelphia has a genuine top-tier roster. If not, the questions about fit and leadership will only get louder.

title: Manchester United plot a £2 billion, 100,000-seat stadium to replace Old Trafford
dek: The club is pressing ahead with plans for what would be Britain's biggest stadium, built 350 metres from its current home as part of a wider Trafford Wharfside regeneration led by Sir Jim Ratcliffe.
body: Manchester United's ambitions for a new home have crystallised into something startling in scale: a 100,000-seat stadium, initially costed at around £2 billion, that would be the largest in Britain and would sit almost within touching distance of the ground it replaces.

ONE reports that the new arena is planned for a site roughly 350 metres from the current Old Trafford, on industrial land at what the club calls the Trafford Wharfside district — ground that, according to the report, previously hosted a go-kart track. Independent reporting places the plot between John Gilbert Way, Wharfside Way and Europa Way, just north-west of the existing stadium.

The design brief has already shifted once in public. Foster + Partners, the architecture practice United appointed for the project, first unveiled a dramatic canopy-topped concept; more recent images have shown a more conventional bowl-shaped ground, though the club has stressed those renderings are not final either.

Collette Roche, chief executive of the stadium development company, framed the latest step — publication of the Wharfside Masterplan — as "another significant milestone in our journey to create a new world-class home for Manchester United at the heart of a vibrant and transformational district for Trafford and Greater Manchester."

The project is not just a football venue. United and their development partners are pitching a full district around it: a tree-lined boulevard styled on Wembley's approach for matchday crowds, waterfront bars and restaurants, a rebuilt tram station, and residential towers overlooking the Manchester Ship Canal. Separate reporting puts the wider scheme at 15,000 new homes and 48,000 local jobs, with the club claiming it could generate £7.3 billion a year for the UK economy.

None of that comes cheap, and the financing question hangs over the entire venture. United's own accounts show total debt approaching £1.3 billion, a legacy largely traced to the Glazer family's leveraged 2004 takeover, and the club is currently paying upwards of £30 million a season in interest alone. United's leadership insists the new stadium will ultimately pay for itself through higher matchday and commercial revenue, funnelling extra income back into the playing squad, but analysts have flagged that lenders may push the Glazers and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to put up more of their own capital than first envisaged.

Ratcliffe, the INEOS billionaire who took a controlling stake in football operations in 2024, has been the driving force pushing the timeline forward. The stated goal is a "spade in the ground" by the end of 2026, with the stadium targeted for completion in time for the 2030-31 season.

Fan groups are watching the process closely, and not uncritically. Duncan Drasdo, chief executive of the Manchester United Supporters' Trust, has said the priority is to avoid the pitfalls other clubs have hit when leaving historic homes: "We want to make sure we end up with an atmospheric stadium, not a soulless bowl, as we've seen with other clubs when they've moved to a new ground."

What happens to the old Old Trafford remains an open question. ONE reports that its fate — full demolition, partial preservation, or conversion into housing — has not been formally decided, and will likely be settled only once the new stadium plans are locked in.

According to the report, detailed designs are expected to be ready by late 2026 or early 2027, after which they would go to formal submission with planning committees. A public consultation with fans, residents and local businesses is due to begin shortly, a step that will shape everything from the boulevard's design to how the club manages the disruption of building a stadium of this size a few hundred metres from a live, matchday-operating ground.

For a club that has spent much of the past decade playing catch-up off the pitch as well as on it, the stadium has become the clearest marker of how Ratcliffe's ownership wants United to be judged — not just by trophies, but by whether it can deliver Britain's biggest football ground without the debt burden swallowing the project whole.

title: Daniel Mérida wins maiden ATP title after years he could not afford a coach
dek: The 21-year-old Spaniard beat Damir Džumhur in Umag for his first tour-level trophy, a breakthrough built on budget flights, shared hotel rooms and years of self-funded travel.

verificationSources.label: ATP Tour — Merida joins Alcaraz & Sinner in Umag title history
ATP Tour — Daniel Merida player overview

body: Daniel Mérida lifted the first ATP Tour trophy of his career on Saturday, beating Damir Džumhur 6-1, 5-7, 6-2 in the final of the Plava Laguna Croatia Open in Umag — a breakthrough that arrives after years in which the 21-year-old Spaniard could not afford to travel with a coach.

The win, coming in just his seventh main-draw appearance on tour, makes Mérida the third-youngest champion in the history of the Umag ATP 250, behind only Carlos Alcaraz, who won there as an 18-year-old in 2021, and Jannik Sinner, who took the title at 20 years and ten months in 2022.

Mérida, from Madrid, had already signalled his rise this season by reaching the final of the Bucharest ATP 250 on clay in April, and arrived in Croatia off the back of qualifying runs into the main draws at Roland Garros and Wimbledon. The Umag title lifts him to a career-high ranking of 58.

What gives the run its edge is the story behind it. In an interview with Clay Tenis, Mérida described years spent traveling alone on tour because he could not afford a personal coach, booking his own early-morning flights, sitting through layovers and taking buses between tournaments to save money while better-funded rivals moved with full support teams.

He has spoken previously about the everyday economics of life outside the sport's elite bracket — sharing hotel rooms, budgeting meals carefully and cutting small extras he could not justify spending on while chasing ranking points on the second-tier circuits.

His tennis beginnings were modest rather than glamorous: he started out playing padel with his father before switching to tennis, a path that eventually took him to the boys' quarter-finals at Roland Garros in 2021, where he lost to eventual junior champion Luca Van Assche.

None of that hardship was visible in Umag, where Mérida dropped the second set before closing out the decider against the experienced Bosnian to seal the title in just over two hours. "It's a huge achievement," he said afterwards, "and it motivates me to keep improving."

ONE, citing his rise from outside the world's top 180 earlier this year, framed the win as the clearest sign yet that the years of counting every euro on the road are starting to pay off for a player who had to build his career without the safety net most of his peers take for granted.

title: Sinner and Djokovic pull out of Montreal Masters ahead of US Open
dek: The world No. 1 and the 24-time Grand Slam champion both cite their health after a gruelling Wimbledon fortnight, handing Alexander Zverev the top seeding in Montreal.
body: Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic have both withdrawn from the Montreal Masters, ONE reports, dealing a heavy blow to the star power of the ATP Masters 1000 event just weeks before the US Open.
Tennis Canada confirmed the pair's exits from the National Bank Open presented by Rogers, which runs August 1-13 in Montreal, after both had originally been entered in the draw.

Sinner, the world No. 1, is coming off a punishing Wimbledon campaign in which he beat Djokovic in the semi-final and Alexander Zverev in the final to retain his title. "After carefully considering all the factors together with my team, we have made the difficult decision to withdraw from Montreal," the Italian said. "It is never easy to miss such an important event, but we believe this is the right decision to prioritize my health. I am disappointed not to be there and look forward to returning to Montreal in the future."

Djokovic, who reached that same Wimbledon semi-final before falling to Sinner in straight sets, gave no further public explanation beyond the shared emphasis on managing his body through the demanding hard-court swing.
Their withdrawals were compounded by news that Carlos Alcaraz has also pulled out of Montreal, sidelined by a wrist injury, stripping the field of three of the sport's biggest draws in one stroke.

Tournament director Valerie Tetreault made no secret of her frustration, saying Masters 1000 events "are among the flagship tournaments on the tour, and fans rightfully expect to see the world's best compete." Both Sinner and Djokovic also skipped last year's Toronto edition, when the men's event was staged in the other host city under the National Bank Open's city-alternating format.

With the headline acts gone, Zverev - the reigning French Open champion and beaten Wimbledon finalist - is now projected as Montreal's top seed, with Canadian favourite Felix Auger-Aliassime, who will have the home crowd behind him, seeded second.

The rest of the field still carries plenty of quality: Alex de Minaur, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Taylor Fritz are among the other top-10 players committed to Montreal, alongside Ben Shelton, who arrives as the defending champion from last year's edition.
The tournament now serves as the last big tune-up before the US Open, which begins August 30 in New York - the major both Sinner and Djokovic are clearly husbanding their bodies for.

title: Beer Sheva fear Ventura exit after Kangwa's sale to Panathinaikos
dek: The reigning Israeli champions are bracing for a second big departure, with Lucas Ventura reportedly unsettled after watching Kings Kangwa's wages triple in a move to Greece.

verificationSources.label: Radio Darom - Beer Sheva agree Kangwa deal with Panathinaikos

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva have barely had time to enjoy their first Israeli title in a decade, and already the reigning champions are staring at the prospect of losing a second key player this summer.

ONE reports that Lucas Ventura, the Brazilian full-back who has become a fixture in Ran Kozjuk's side, is now pushing to leave the club after watching teammate Kings Kangwa's move to Panathinaikos roughly triple his own salary.

According to the report, club sources describe Ventura as more motivated by a financial upgrade than by any particular pull toward a bigger European league or a fresh professional challenge — a reading that will unsettle a Beer Sheva hierarchy already absorbing one departure.

The unease reportedly boiled over on the training pitch this week, when Ventura did not train properly and was pulled out of the session by Kozjuk. ONE says the club has downplayed the incident as minor and already resolved, but its timing — coming straight after Kangwa's exit was finalised — is unlikely to be a coincidence.

Kangwa's departure is now official business. Beer Sheva have agreed to sell the Zambian midfielder to Panathinaikos in a deal ONE puts at around €4 million plus a 25 percent cut of any future transfer fee, with Israeli outlets including Israel Hayom and Radio Darom reporting the overall package, including bonuses, could rise toward €4.5 million.

Panathinaikos saw off competition from AEK Athens, who had offered around €3.5 million but attached conditions — reportedly including a request that Kangwa not be released to face Israeli opposition in Champions League qualifying — that Beer Sheva were unwilling to accept, according to Radio Darom.

Kangwa, widely regarded as the best foreign player to pass through Beer Sheva in recent seasons, stayed on despite the interest to help the club through their Champions League qualifying tie against Vikingur before making his exit, ONE notes.

A club representative quoted by ONE explained the logic behind letting him go: once Kangwa received an offer worth close to a million euros a year, and had been agitating for a step up since the previous season, the club felt it could no longer justify standing in his way.

The sale is understood to have been greeted quietly with satisfaction at rival clubs. ONE reports that both Maccabi Tel Aviv and Beitar Jerusalem were pleased to see a player of Kangwa's calibre leave a direct title rival.

For Beer Sheva, the timing is awkward. The club won the championship in May under Kozjuk, beating Maccabi Tel Aviv 4-2, and rewarded the coach with a new two-year contract on the back of it. Losing Kangwa was always going to sting; losing Ventura in the same window would be a far heavier blow to a squad built to defend the title.
Club officials are said to be searching for a replacement of similar quality to Kangwa, wary that a double exit could derail Beer Sheva's championship defence before it has even begun.

title: Vozinha, the World Cup's viral goalkeeper, agrees move to Chile's Colo-Colo
dek: The 40-year-old Cape Verde stopper who stunned Spain and pushed holders Argentina to extra time has reached a verbal agreement to join Chilean giants Colo-Colo, club president Aníbal Mosa confirms.
body: A month after his gloves turned him into one of the World Cup's most improbable stars, Vozinha is on his way to Chilean football. ONE reports that the 40-year-old Cape Verde goalkeeper has reached an agreement to join Colo-Colo, the country's most decorated club, with confirmation coming directly from club president Aníbal Mosa.

"We have reached an agreement with him," Mosa told the Argentine outlet Olé, ending days of speculation that had followed Vozinha since Cape Verde's World Cup run ended. The Chilean club later said the move puts it "in the global spotlight," a nod to both the goalkeeper's footballing pedigree and the attention his story has generated worldwide.

Vozinha, whose real name is Josimar José Évora Dias, was born on June 3, 1986 in Mindelo and had spent his career largely out of the spotlight, turning out for clubs in Angola, Moldova, Cyprus, Slovakia and Portugal. He arrived at the World Cup as a free agent, having just left Chaves of Portugal's second division, with reports linking him to interest from Inter Miami among others.

None of that prepared the football world for what followed. Cape Verde, the second-smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup, reached the tournament for the first time in its history, and Vozinha became the unlikely face of the run — at 40, the oldest outfield story of the summer, keeping a clean sheet against Spain and becoming an instant social media sensation.

The adventure ended on July 3 in the round of 32, when holders Argentina needed extra time to see off Cape Verde 3-2. Lionel Messi opened the scoring before Deroy Duarte equalised; Lisandro Martínez put Argentina back ahead in extra time only for Sidny Lopes Cabral to level again, before a stoppage-time own goal finally ended the underdogs' run.

Vozinha's performances throughout the tournament, including saves that kept Cape Verde competitive against far wealthier opposition, earned him a place among the World Cup's most talked-about players and, by several accounts, a spot in the tournament's team of the competition.

Colo-Colo, based at the Estadio Monumental in Santiago and chasing a return to the Copa Libertadores in 2027 under coach Fernando Ortiz, now wants to add that story to its own history. Mosa has been candid that the move carries commercial as well as sporting value for a club looking to raise its international profile.

According to the reporting picked up by ONE and matched by outlets in Chile and the United States, the agreement is still verbal at this stage. Vozinha is expected to travel to Santiago in the coming days for a medical examination before signing a contract that multiple reports put in place through December 2027, followed by an official presentation at the Estadio Monumental.

For a goalkeeper who was jobless a matter of weeks ago, it is a remarkable turn: from released free agent to a marquee arrival at one of South America's grandest clubs, all inside a single World Cup summer.

title: "Now or never": Gloukh's moment of truth at Ajax
dek: Dutch pundits believe the Israeli playmaker has been handed a tailor-made system under new coach Míchel after a stuttering debut season in Amsterdam.

verificationSources.label: Ajax.nl - Míchel appointed new Ajax head coach
NL Times - Why Ajax chose Míchel as new manager

body: A year after Ajax paid Red Bull Salzburg close to €15 million to bring him to Amsterdam, Oscar Gloukh is being told by Dutch football watchers that this pre-season is the moment his career at the club is decided.

ONE reports that Dutch analysts see the Israeli attacking midfielder at a genuine crossroads heading into the 2026/27 campaign, arriving under new head coach Míchel with what several commentators are calling the ideal set-up to finally deliver on Ajax's investment.
"Usually with Gloukh it's all or nothing," Dutch commentator Peter Zwart said, according to the report. "If he doesn't seize this opportunity now, he simply won't get another one at Ajax."

Gloukh's first season in the Eredivisie was, by most accounts, a struggle. He made 29 league appearances and scored six goals, contributing nine goals and an assist across all competitions, but was used mainly as a winger rather than in his preferred central playmaking role under previous managers John Heitinga and caretaker Fred Grim.

Ajax churned through three head coaches across that campaign before turning to the Spaniard Míchel, formerly of Girona, who signed a contract running to 2028 after leaving the Catalan club following its relegation from La Liga.

According to ONE, Míchel's system - built around short passing combinations and lighter defensive demands on his attacking players - is viewed in Amsterdam as a far better fit for Gloukh's game than the more physical, wing-based role he was often asked to play last season.

Dutch analyst Tim Goudijk is quoted in the report saying Gloukh's underlying problem last year was confidence rather than ability. "Gloukh needs trust. Last year that simply didn't exist," Goudijk said, adding that the resulting insecurity pushed the 22-year-old into rushed, careless decisions on the ball.
ONE notes Gloukh gave an encouraging early sign of the reset, playing well and contributing to two goals in a pre-season friendly against Voždovac.

Gloukh, born in Rehovot, has 29 caps and five goals for the Israel national team since debuting in November 2022, and has previously stated he intends to fight for his place at Ajax rather than seek a move away after just one season.

The stakes described in the report are straightforward: with a new coach, a new tactical framework and no shortage of competition for places in Ajax's attack, Dutch observers believe Gloukh has been given the platform to prove last season was an aberration - and that he may not get a second chance if he does not.

title: Israeli defender Roei Zahavi joins Romanian third-tier club Păulești
dek: The 21-year-old left back leaves Beitar Haifa for a one-year deal, teaming up with fellow Israeli passport holders Ohad Portman and Niv Levi at the Liga III side, ONE reports.
body: Roei Zahavi, a 21-year-old left back who spent last season with Beitar Haifa, has signed for CS Păulești of Romania's third-tier Liga III, ONE reports.

The one-year deal was arranged through his representative, the Israeli attorney and agent Shai Avni, taking Zahavi three divisions below the Romanian top flight but into a dressing room that already has a distinctly Israeli flavour.

Păulești, based in Prahova County, already carries two Israeli passport holders on its books: 20-year-old defender Ohad Portman, who joined the club earlier this year, and 21-year-old midfielder Niv Levi. With Zahavi's arrival, the club will field three Israeli-citizenship players next season, according to the report.

All three qualify to play in Romania on dual nationality rather than as foreign imports, a route a number of young Israelis without a foothold at home have used in recent years to keep their careers alive in European football.

Zahavi's path to this point has run through several of Israel's development leagues rather than a flagship academy. ONE traces his youth career through Hapoel Matar Asher, Hapoel Mishgav, Hapoel Hadera and Maccabi Tzur Shalom before he broke into senior football with Beitar Haifa.

Financial terms were not disclosed, and neither Păulești nor Beitar Haifa has issued a formal statement beyond the ONE report — typical for a move at this level of the football pyramid, where lower-league transfers rarely come with a press conference.

For Zahavi, the switch offers a route to regular senior minutes and a foothold in a European league system, even three tiers down, at an age when Israeli defenders outside the top division often find their options narrowing fast.

title: Real Madrid's €100 million bid for Diomande rejected by Leipzig
dek: The Spanish giants have opened talks for RB Leipzig's Ivorian winger, but Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain are also in the race for one of the summer's hottest properties.
body: Real Madrid have already had a first offer for Yan Diomande knocked back, with ONE reporting that an opening bid of around €100 million for the RB Leipzig winger failed to move the Bundesliga club, who are holding out for considerably more.

The 19-year-old Ivorian has become one of the most fought-over properties in Europe this summer, and Madrid's approach is only the most prominent of several. Spanish and German outlets, including Bild, AS and Sport, have reported that Leipzig are demanding somewhere between €120 million and €130 million before they will even consider letting him go.

Real Madrid are not alone in being turned down. Liverpool had a bid of close to €100 million rejected earlier in the process and remain interested, though reports in England suggest the Premier League club are reluctant to go much higher. Paris Saint-Germain have also been tracking Diomande for months, with several reports claiming the French champions are his preferred destination and have already made progress on personal terms.

Diomande's rise has been rapid. Born in Abidjan, he made his name at Spanish second-tier club Leganés — becoming the club's youngest-ever La Liga scorer — before Leipzig paid around €20 million for him last summer. He repaid that outlay almost immediately, scoring a hat-trick against Eintracht Frankfurt in December to become one of the youngest players in Bundesliga history to do so, and finishing the campaign as one of the league's standout attacking talents.

His stock has risen further this summer after a prominent role for Ivory Coast at the 2026 World Cup, where his performances against the likes of Germany and Ecuador have added to the sense among Europe's biggest clubs that he is worth chasing now rather than waiting.

Leipzig, for their part, are publicly resisting the pressure. Sporting director Marcel Schäfer has said the club's intention is for Diomande to remain and play for them again next season, and Leipzig have also been trying to persuade him to sign a new contract rather than push for an exit.

None of the fee figures being reported — Madrid's opening €100 million, Leipzig's €120–130 million valuation, or suggestions of a possible compromise around €120 million — represent an agreed transfer. Nothing has been signed, and Leipzig have shown no sign of softening their asking price so far this window.
With Liverpool, PSG and now Real Madrid all circling, and Leipzig digging in, Diomande's situation looks set to be one of the more closely watched transfer sagas of the European summer.

title: How Barcelona walked away from Diomande and signed Gordon instead
dek: ONE reports Deco's club chose to spend big on Anthony Gordon in May rather than chase Yan Diomande, who has since become a €100m-plus target for Real Madrid, PSG and Liverpool

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports - Anthony Gordon transfer news
Sky Sports - Yan Diomande transfer news
Al Jazeera - Barcelona sign Anthony Gordon

body: Barcelona's move for Anthony Gordon back in May now looks like the moment the club quietly closed the door on a much bigger transfer chase, according to a report from Israeli outlet ONE, which says Deco's recruitment team weighed up Yan Diomande before choosing to put their money behind the Newcastle winger instead.

Gordon's switch to Camp Nou was completed on 30 May for a fee reported at around €80m, split between an initial €70m and roughly €10m in add-ons, with performance clauses that could send Newcastle further payments tied to trophies and appearances. He signed a five-year contract as one of the marquee arrivals of Barcelona's summer.

ONE reports that Barcelona's hierarchy had held early contact around Diomande in May, when the Ivorian winger's price tag was seen as more modest than it is today, but ultimately judged Gordon the more realistic and immediate reinforcement for Hansi Flick's wide areas.

That decision has aged awkwardly. Diomande, a 19-year-old who lit up the 2026 World Cup for Ivory Coast, has since become one of the most fought-over players in Europe, with his price climbing well past the level Barcelona reportedly considered.

Real Madrid have already had an opening bid in the region of €100m turned down by RB Leipzig, who are said to value the winger closer to €130m. Sky Sports has reported Real Madrid's rejected offer publicly, with suggestions a fee nearer €120m could eventually get a deal over the line.

Paris Saint-Germain have tracked Diomande for months and were, at one stage, considered his preferred destination, while Liverpool have also registered interest but are reportedly unwilling to go beyond roughly £85m. Should any of the suitors meet Leipzig's valuation, it would become the biggest sale in the Bundesliga club's history, surpassing the departures of Josko Gvardiol and Benjamin Sesko.

Real Madrid's interest has been reinforced off the pitch too: Vinicius Junior sent Diomande a gift from his personal brand earlier this year, a gesture widely read in the Spanish press as part of the club's charm offensive, given Diomande shares representation with several players close to Real Madrid's dressing room.

None of this directly touches Barcelona now — their business with Gordon is done, and he arrives with Premier League pedigree after scoring 17 goals in all competitions for Newcastle last season. But ONE's framing places the Diomande saga alongside the Gordon deal as a case study in how quickly a club's calculated caution in one negotiation can turn into a market they can no longer afford to enter.

The wider picture is one of another Spanish superclub derby playing out at the very top of the market, with Real Madrid, PSG and Liverpool all still circling a teenager who was a relative unknown before this year's World Cup — and Barcelona, for now, watching from the sidelines after choosing a different winger in May.

title: Ziv Arie: a Petah Tikva derby is never just another game, even in the Toto Cup
dek: The new Maccabi Petah Tikva coach makes his derby bow against city rivals Hapoel Petah Tikva this evening, with two players handed full debuts and captain Mohammad Hindi left out of the starting line-up.
body: Ziv Arie will take charge of his first Petah Tikva derby this evening, and the new Maccabi Petah Tikva coach is in no mood to treat it as a warm-up fixture, even though it counts only for the Toto Cup.
"A derby is not just another match, even in the Toto Cup," Arie said, according to ONE. "We will arrive with purpose, to give the fans something to enjoy."

Maccabi host bitter city rivals Hapoel Petah Tikva at HaMoshava Stadium, the ground the two clubs share, in what doubles as Arie's competitive debut on the Maccabi bench. He was appointed head coach in late May, succeeding Noam Shoham, less than two months after leaving Hapoel Jerusalem.

The fixture carries extra weight for Maccabi, who return to Ligat Ha'al this season after spending the previous campaign in the second-tier Liga Leumit. A strong start against their local rivals, even in a pre-season cup tie, would be a statement of intent as Arie builds his squad for the top flight.

According to ONE, Arie will be without defender Eitan Tibi and full-back Lee-Yom Dan, who is nursing an ankle injury, for the derby. Midfielder Ariel Lugasi also misses out as he continues his recovery from a ligament tear, though he is expected to be fit in time for the start of the league season.

In a notable selection call, captain Mohammad Hindi has been left out of the starting eleven. Arie's central defensive pairing for the derby is Fabrício and Pablo Correa, ONE reported, while winger Ibrahim Soma and English signing Kyle Spence are both handed their first starts for the club.
The occasion also marks the unveiling of Maccabi Petah Tikva's new kit for the 2026-27 season, giving supporters their first look at the strip in a competitive match.
With Ligat Ha'al survival and a fresh coaching era both on the agenda, Arie's message to his players and fans alike was simple: derby night still matters, whatever the competition.

title: Trump calls LeBron James 'maybe a racist' as he prefers Michael Jordan
dek: The president needled the NBA legend hours after James announced he was leaving the Lakers for the Philadelphia 76ers, saying he prefers Michael Jordan because 'I only like people who like me.'
body: Donald Trump reignited one of American sport's longest-running personal feuds on Friday, telling reporters in the Oval Office that LeBron James is "maybe a racist" and declaring, once again, that Michael Jordan is the player he actually rates.
ONE reports that the president was pressed on the subject by a Fox News correspondent and used the moment to settle an old score rather than the basketball debate he was ostensibly being asked about.

"I only love people who love me, so for me it's Michael Jordan, without a doubt," Trump said, according to the report, before turning to James directly: "Maybe he's a racist. Maybe he just doesn't love me."

Other US outlets that covered the same remarks, including CNN and the Washington Post, quoted Trump praising Jordan as a golfing friend — "a really good guy" — while dismissing James in near-identical terms over the pair's political history.

The timing was pointed. Trump's comments landed just hours after James announced he would join the Philadelphia 76ers for what will be a record-extending 24th NBA season, ending an eight-year run with the Los Angeles Lakers.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported the deal as a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, pairing James in Philadelphia's frontcourt with former MVP center Joel Embiid for the 2026-27 campaign.

James explained the decision to keep playing in his own message to fans: "I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship." He added that he had considered retirement before concluding, "I still truly love this game, and I have more to give."

The Trump-James rivalry is not new. The two have traded barbs for roughly a decade, with Trump previously mocking James's intelligence and James backing Trump's political opponents, including Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Barack Obama.

Friday's comments, coming from the Oval Office rather than a campaign rally or social media post, are the latest and among the most direct escalations of that feud, and are likely to draw fresh criticism in the United States over the president's language.

For now, James's basketball future is the bigger story on the court: at 41, he heads into a new season with a new franchise and a new co-star in Embiid, still chasing what would be a fifth championship ring in a 24th professional season unlike almost any other in NBA history.

title: Spanish reports: Lonnie Walker closing in on Real Madrid move after single Maccabi season
dek: One year after choosing Tel Aviv over Madrid, Lonnie Walker IV is reportedly on the verge of a reversal — Spanish outlets say his move to the Bernabeu is close, even as Maccabi holds the final word.

verificationSources.label: Eurohoops - Real Madrid reportedly in talks to sign Lonnie Walker
Basketnews - Real Madrid reportedly in negotiations to sign Lonnie Walker

body: A year ago, Lonnie Walker IV chose Tel Aviv over Madrid, holding out for an NBA exit clause that Real Madrid would not give him. Spanish reports now suggest he is about to make the move anyway, one EuroLeague season later.

ONE reports that Spanish media regard a deal between Walker and Real Madrid as close, with the guard seen as one of the leading candidates to fill the backcourt spot vacated by Mario Hezonja. Journalist Nacho Bravo of Copa went further on social media, calling the transfer "closed" and posting an image of Walker in Real Madrid colors — though ONE notes the deal has not been formally finalized.

Other Spanish outlets are more cautious but point the same way. Eurohoops and Basketnews both describe Real Madrid as being in active negotiations for the 27-year-old American, who is remembered in Madrid for torching the club with a 27-point night at the Bernabeu last October that helped Maccabi steal a 92-91 win there.

Real Madrid's interest in Walker is not new. The club pursued him last summer too, before his insistence on an NBA opt-out clause pushed him toward Maccabi Tel Aviv instead, according to Eurohoops and Madridistanews.
Spanish analyst Sergio Vegas, cited by ONE, called the fit "excellent," saying Walker "has everything" and that a second season in Europe could see him take another step forward.

The numbers back the interest. Walker averaged 15.2 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.3 assists across 28 EuroLeague games this past season while shooting 35.1 percent from three, and posted 15.6 points a game domestically for Maccabi in Israel's top flight.

There is a financial wrinkle. Walker earns roughly $2.2 million a year on his Maccabi contract, and with his NBA exit option now expired, any move to Real Madrid would require Maccabi's sign-off. ONE reports that sources close to the situation believe the club would not stand in the way of a sufficiently strong offer, while a separate report from 24segundosenblanco put Real Madrid's proposed annual salary at around €2 million.

Nothing is signed, and Maccabi has made no public comment. But with several Spanish outlets converging on the same story within the same news cycle, the direction of travel looks clear even if the final numbers are not yet locked in.

title: Study claims Messi has Brazilian roots through great-great-grandfather
dek: A three-year genealogical investigation, reported by Brazilian outlet Globo and picked up by ONE, traces the Argentina captain's maternal line through São Paulo state decades before his family settled in Rosario.

verificationSources.label: beIN Sports - Could Messi Have Played for Brazil?
Yahoo Sports - The Messi family inquiry
Terra - Bisavô de Messi nasceu no interior de SP

body: Lionel Messi has spent two decades being claimed, argued over and idolised as the ultimate Argentine footballer. Now a genealogist says the family story is more complicated than that, and briefly ran through Brazil.

ONE reports on a three-year historical investigation, first published by the Brazilian outlet Globo, which traces part of Messi's maternal line to a stretch of São Paulo state more than a century before he was born in Rosario.

The research was carried out by the Italian historian Fiorenzo Santini, described as a banker by profession and a genealogist by passion, who began digging into the Messi and Cuccittini family surnames as the player rose to prominence at Barcelona.

According to the study, Messi's great-great-grandfather, Raniero Coccettini, left the town of San Severino Marche in Italy with his wife, Rosa Richezza, arriving in Brazil in 1899 through the port of Santos as part of the wave of Italian emigration to South America at the time.

The family is said to have settled and worked in the Ribeirão Preto area of São Paulo state for several years, where at least one child was reportedly born, before the household moved on to Rosario, Argentina, in the early 1900s.

The study's central claim is that Italian immigration officials in Brazil altered the family surname on arrival, and that further changes to the spelling followed after the move to Argentina — a common fate for Italian names processed through South American ports at the turn of the 20th century. That, according to the research, is how the family eventually came to be recorded as Cuccittini, the maiden name of Messi's mother, Celia.

The findings, as ONE notes, amount to a historical curiosity rather than a change of nationality: they raise the theoretical question of whether Messi's ancestry could have made him eligible to represent Brazil, without suggesting any such possibility was ever real or pursued.

Messi has never renounced or complicated his Argentine identity, which he affirmed most recently by lifting the World Cup with the albiceleste. His only acknowledged tie to the old country came in 2022, when the town of San Severino Marche — his father's ancestral home, separate from this newly reported maternal Brazilian episode — made him an honorary citizen.

Neither Messi nor his family have commented on the Globo research, and ONE's report, like the wider Brazilian coverage it draws on, presents the findings as the product of one historian's private archival work rather than an official genealogical record.
Still, the story has travelled fast, picked up by outlets from Brazil to the Gulf as a lighthearted footnote to a career that has otherwise been defined entirely by Argentina, Barcelona and Paris.

The study attributes the family's eventual surname, Cuccittini (Messi's mother's maiden name), to spelling changes made during immigration processing in Brazil and Argentina.
Messi and his family have not commented on the findings.
Messi was made an honorary citizen of San Severino Marche, his father's ancestral Italian town, in 2022.

title: Pogačar shatters 30-year-old Alpe d'Huez record at the Tour de France
dek: The Slovenian smashed Marco Pantani's storied 1995 mark by more than a minute on stage 19, sealing his fifth stage win of this year's race with two days left in Paris.
body: Tadej Pogačar climbed into cycling folklore on Thursday, obliterating the legendary Alpe d'Huez climbing record on his way to a fifth stage win of this year's Tour de France.

The Slovenian reached the summit of the 13.8-kilometre climb, with its 21 hairpin bends, in 35 minutes and 27 seconds, tearing more than a minute off the mark Marco Pantani set in 1995 during one of the most feted rides in Tour history.

Pantani's time of 36:50, set the year he also won the Giro-Tour double, had stood for close to three decades as one of the sport's most revered benchmarks. Pogačar's assault on it, delivered in the heat of a live yellow-jersey fight rather than a solo raid on the record book, only added to the scale of the achievement.

Stage 19 covered 127.9 kilometres from Gap before finishing on the fabled Alpine climb. Pogačar launched his decisive attack with roughly 11.7 kilometres still to race, riding away from the rest of the general classification group and never looking back.

Lenny Martínez crossed the line second, six seconds down, with Richard Carapaz completing the podium a further three seconds back. Both were left shaking their heads at the pace UAE Team Emirates' leader had set on an ascent that has broken far lesser riders.
"It's really cool to win up here," Pogačar said afterwards, describing a "mad atmosphere all the way up the climb" as tens of thousands of fans lined the switchbacks, many in Slovenian colours.

The victory extended his overwhelming grip on this year's race. He now leads Remco Evenepoel by seven minutes and 11 seconds overall, a gap that makes a sixth Tour de France triumph an all-but-formal matter with just two stages remaining before Sunday's finish in Paris.

Alpe d'Huez has hosted Tour finishes since 1952 and carries a mythology matched by few climbs anywhere in sport, its names of past winners painted onto the road by fans each July. Pogačar's time now sits among the very fastest ever recorded there, alongside names such as Pantani, Lance Armstrong and Marco Giovannetti from cycling's most storied — and, in some cases, most scrutinised — eras.

With the overall standings settled in all but formality, attention now turns to Saturday's final mountain test and Sunday's ceremonial procession into Paris, where Pogačar is set to collect what would be a fifth career yellow jersey.
facts: Tadej Pogačar won stage 19 of the 2026 Tour de France, from Gap to Alpe d'Huez (127.9km), on July 24, 2026.
His climb time on the 13.8km Alpe d'Huez ascent was 35 minutes 27 seconds.
That broke the previous record of 36 minutes 50 seconds set by Marco Pantani in 1995.
Lenny Martínez finished second on the stage, six seconds behind Pogačar; Richard Carapaz was third, nine seconds behind.
It was Pogačar's fifth stage win of the 2026 Tour de France.
Pogačar leads Remco Evenepoel by 7 minutes 11 seconds overall with two stages remaining.

title: Ramat Gan, 3 June 1964: The Asian Cup that Israel won and could never defend
dek: Long before Europe, Israel was a football power in Asia — and for one week in 1964, the smallest confederation member of all became its champion.

verificationSources.label: AFC official site — Moments and Milestones: The 1964 AFC Asian Cup
Wikipedia — Israel at the AFC Asian Cup
Middle East Eye — Why Israel competes in Europe, and what UEFA could do

body: On the evening of 3 June 1964, roughly 35,000 people packed Ramat Gan Stadium — the largest crowd the tournament would draw — to watch Israel try to finish what it had started five days earlier. This was the third AFC Asian Cup, the first ever staged outside East or South Asia, and Israel was both host and unbeaten leader of a four-team round-robin that had been whittled down from seventeen original entrants after a wave of withdrawals during qualifying.

Israel had opened the tournament on 26 May with a tight 1-0 win over Hong Kong at Ramat Gan, then travelled to Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv three days later to beat India 2-0. That left one final test: South Korea, twice champions of Asia and chasing a third straight title. A win for Israel would clinch the tournament outright; anything less would open the door for the Koreans.

It did not stay close for long. Moshe Leon put Israel ahead after twenty minutes, and Gideon Tish doubled the lead before halftime. South Korea pulled a goal back in the second half, but the deficit held: Israel won 2-1 and finished the tournament with a perfect record — three matches, three wins, six points — to be crowned champions of Asia for the only time in its history.

Among the Israeli side that week was a nineteen-year-old forward from Netanya named Mordechai Spiegler, who had made his international debut against Hong Kong barely five months earlier. He finished the tournament with two goals, level with India's Inder Singh as joint top scorer. It was an early glimpse of a career that would define a generation of Israeli football: Spiegler went on to play for Paris Saint-Germain and, in the 1970s, alongside Pelé for the New York Cosmos, and in 1970 he scored Israel's only goal in its only World Cup finals appearance, a 1-1 draw with Sweden in Mexico. He remains Israel's all-time leading scorer with 32 international goals.

The trophy itself was presented amid a burst of national pride. President Zalman Shazar attended the closing ceremony at Ramat Gan alongside the heads of the Asian football federations then in Israel — a reminder that in 1964, Israel's place inside Asian football was not merely accepted but actively hosted and celebrated. Government photographer Moshe Pridan captured the team hoisting the cup, images that survive today in Israel's National Photo Collection.

It was, in context, the culmination of a run of near-misses. Israel had finished runners-up at the Asian Cup in both 1956 and 1960, losing out each time to South Korea. The 1964 title, won on home soil with a squad drawn mostly from Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Tel Aviv and Hapoel Petah Tikva under coach Yosef Merimovich, was the breakthrough those two silver medals had been building toward — and across all six Asian Cup matches that fortnight, a combined 99,000 spectators had turned out, an average of roughly 16,500 per game, in a country of barely two and a half million people.

Israel remained an Asian football nation for another decade, finishing third at the 1968 Asian Cup before withdrawing as scheduled 1972 hosts amid mounting political pressure. That pressure came to a head in September 1974, when Kuwait tabled a motion at the AFC congress to expel Israel from the confederation; it passed 17 votes to 13, with six abstentions, following a tense build-up that included a hostile final against Iran at that year's Asian Games in Tehran.

Israel spent the following years as a footballing nomad, shuffled into Oceania's qualifying pathway before eventually being welcomed into UEFA — first on a provisional basis in 1991, then as a full member on 31 May 1994. Israeli clubs and the national team have played as a European entity ever since.

Which is what makes 3 June 1964 such an unrepeatable date. Because Israel no longer competes for the Asian Cup, the trophy the team lifted in Ramat Gan that evening can never be defended again in the competition it was won in — a continental title frozen permanently in the record books as Israel's only one. Six decades later, it stands as the strange, singular souvenir of a chapter of Israeli sport that history quietly closed the door on.
facts: Israel hosted and won the 1964 AFC Asian Cup with a perfect record, beating Hong Kong 1-0, India 2-0 and South Korea 2-1.
The decisive match, a 2-1 win over South Korea at Ramat Gan Stadium on 3 June 1964, drew the tournament's largest crowd, around 35,000.
Mordechai Spiegler finished the 1964 Asian Cup as joint top scorer with two goals; six years later he scored Israel's only-ever FIFA World Cup finals goal, against Sweden in 1970.
Total attendance across the tournament's six matches was 99,000, an average of about 16,500 per game.
Israel's full AFC Asian Cup record was: runners-up in 1956 and 1960, champions in 1964, third place in 1968, and withdrawal as scheduled 1972 hosts.
Israel was expelled from the Asian Football Confederation in September 1974 by a 17-13 vote and later joined UEFA officially on 31 May 1994, meaning the 1964 title can never be defended again.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva set to land €4m as Kangwa completes move to Panathinaikos
dek: The Zambian playmaker who inspired a cup and league double in the Negev is heading to Greece, with add-on clauses that could push the fee even higher.

verificationSources.label: Nogomania - Kangwa valued at €4m amid European interest

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva are on the verge of banking around €4 million for Kings Kangwa, with Sport5 reporting the Zambian midfielder is close to completing a move to Greek giants Panathinaikos.

Kangwa arrived in the Negev in the summer of 2024 from Red Star Belgrade for a reported €800,000, a fee that now looks like a bargain given the size of the sale being discussed barely two years later.

He leaves having been central to the most successful stretch in Hapoel's recent history: 83 appearances yielding 29 goals and 19 assists, a State Cup triumph in his debut season and, last term, the club's first Israeli Premier League title in eight years.

According to Sport5, the fee could climb further through add-on clauses tied to Kangwa's success in Greece — bonuses are said to be attached to Panathinaikos winning the league title or advancing through the rounds of European competition.

Kangwa is expected to sign a four-year contract in Athens worth roughly €800,000 a season, a package that reflects Panathinaikos' determination to beat off rival interest from fellow Greek side AEK Athens, who had also been credited with a strong offer for the midfielder earlier in the window.

Sport5 notes a quirk in the timing: the move only becomes official once Kangwa has completed his final appearance for Hapoel, in a European qualifying playoff against Víkingur. Because he has already been registered and used by Hapoel in that competition this season, UEFA eligibility rules mean Panathinaikos cannot field him in their own playoff-stage qualifiers.

For Hapoel, the sale caps a lucrative reinvention of a player who cost a fraction of what he is now fetching, and the club's management is reported to already be searching for a replacement forward to lead the line next season.

Confirmation from either club is still pending, but the terms outlined by Sport5 align with figures already circulating in transfer databases and among Greek outlets tracking Panathinaikos' recruitment push this summer.

Sport5 reports the fee includes potential add-ons if Kangwa helps Panathinaikos win the Greek title or progress in European competition.
He is set to sign a four-year contract with Panathinaikos worth around €800,000 per season.

title: The defender Bnei Sakhnin passed on three years ago is closing in on a Premier League move
dek: Chibuike Nwaiwu failed a trial in Sakhnin back in 2023 — now Fulham have agreed personal terms with the Nigeria international in a deal reportedly closing in on €30 million.

verificationSources.label: FootballPlace: Fulham agree personal terms with Chibuike Nwaiwu
OwnGoal Nigeria: Crystal Palace move to hijack Nwaiwu transfer
Businessday NG: missing Enyimba player Chibuike Nwaiwu spotted in Israel

body: Three and a half years ago, according to Sport5, Bnei Sakhnin gave a trial to an unheralded Nigerian defender and decided he was not worth a contract. That player, Chibuike Nwaiwu, is now closing in on a Premier League move to Fulham in a deal reportedly worth close to €30 million.

Nwaiwu, 22, arrived in Israel in November 2023 under strange circumstances. His club at the time, Nigerian champions Enyimba, had declared him missing after he left the team without authorisation. He resurfaced training with Bnei Sakhnin, sparking speculation of a move to Ligat Ha'al — but the club never signed him, and he was back in Nigeria within weeks.

It did not slow him down for long. Back at Enyimba, the 1.93-metre centre-back helped the club win the 2022-23 Nigeria Premier Football League title, before moving on to Austria's Wolfsberger AC in 2024, where he started in the final as Wolfsberg won their first-ever domestic trophy, the 2024-25 Austrian Cup.

In January 2026, Trabzonspor paid around €6 million to bring him to the Turkish Süper Lig. He barely paused for breath: 21 appearances, three goals and an assist later, Nwaiwu had helped the club lift the Turkish Cup and finish third in the league table.

That form has driven a rapid rise in his value — Transfermarkt currently rates him at around €10 million, a figure the market is already well past. Fulham, needing central-defensive cover, have agreed personal terms with Nwaiwu on a contract through 2030, according to reports in England and Nigeria.

The two clubs are still closing a gap on the transfer fee. Trabzonspor opened by demanding close to €30 million; Fulham's offer has risen to around €27 million guaranteed plus add-ons, with a sell-on clause reportedly attached for the Turkish side. Nwaiwu is expected to travel to England for a medical once terms are finalised.

Crystal Palace are shadowing the deal. With Maxence Lacroix closing in on a move to Chelsea, Palace have identified Nwaiwu as a possible replacement at the back — though he is understood to be their fallback option behind Augsburg's Chrislain Matsima, leaving Fulham the clear favourites to land him.

Nwaiwu already has three caps for Nigeria's senior side, having first been called into the Under-23 squad in 2023 ahead of Olympic qualifying. For a player an Israeli top-flight club chose not to sign three years ago, it is a startling turnaround — one Sport5 flagged, fittingly, under a headline that simply read "crazy."

title: The Hapoel Tel Aviv flop now closing in on a scoring title in Estonia
dek: Bubacarr Tambedou lasted six appearances at Hapoel Tel Aviv before being let go in 2024 — now he is banging in goals for FCI Levadia and driving their run through Conference League qualifying, Sport5 reports.
body: Two and a half years ago, Hapoel Tel Aviv gave up on Bubacarr Tambedou after barely four months. Now the Gambian forward is one of the hottest scorers in European qualifying football, and the Israeli club that discarded him is the punchline in his story, Sport5 reports.

Hapoel signed Tambedou from Estonia's Paide Linnameeskond in January 2024, a move TheNerveAfrica reported was worth around €100,000 to Paide at the time, though Sport5's own figure for the deal runs closer to €150,000. Whatever the exact number, it barely mattered: he made just six appearances in yellow-and-black before the club released him within four months.

The player himself has since described that spell in bleak terms. Sport5 quotes him saying he felt completely alone in Israel, without proper language support or coaching stability behind him, to the point that he considered walking away from the contract altogether: "I couldn't continue like this... maybe you pay me half and I just go."

What followed did not immediately look like vindication. Tambedou joined Georgian side Dinamo Batumi in the summer of 2024 and scored just three goals across a full season there, numbers that read like confirmation of Hapoel's decision rather than a rebuttal of it.

Everything changed when he returned to Estonia in January 2025, signing for FCI Levadia. Last season he managed a respectable 8 goals and 3 assists. This season, per Sport5, he has exploded: 14 goals in 20 league matches in Estonia's top flight, the Meistriliiga, none of them from the penalty spot, working out to roughly a goal every 98 minutes.

He has carried that form into Europe. Levadia thrashed Welsh side Caernarfon Town 5-0 in each leg of their Conference League first qualifying round, a 10-0 aggregate rout in which Tambedou scored and assisted across both matches.

The bigger statement came in the second qualifying round, away to Sweden's IFK Göteborg, a side from a stronger domestic league than Estonia's. Levadia won 2-1, with Tambedou setting up the opener for Brazilian forward Wendell by winning a duel down the left flank before Göteborg conceded an own goal late on. Sport5 puts his combined output in this season's qualifying campaign at 3 goals and 3 assists from three matches.

Off the pitch, his time in Estonia has not been without complications. Sport5 reports that Tambedou was convicted of theft in Estonia in 2023 — taking around €105 worth of goods from a store — and fined €120, a conviction that went on to complicate the renewal of his visa.

None of that has slowed his football. Levadia hold his registration on a contract running through December 2026, and Sport5's framing is blunt: a player once quietly released by an Israeli club as a non-factor is now scoring at a rate that could put him on the radar of considerably bigger leagues before his deal is up.

For Hapoel Tel Aviv, there is no controversy to answer for — plenty of young strikers arrive from smaller leagues and fail to adapt, and six games was a fair trial by most standards. But as a footnote to their squad-building history, Tambedou's turnaround, from a player begging to leave on reduced terms to one chasing a share of Estonia's scoring charts and embarrassing a Swedish top-flight side in Europe, is a striking one.

title: Oryan Goren, 17, makes his Barcelona first-team debut in preseason win
dek: The Israeli midfielder came off the bench as Hansi Flick's side beat CE Europa 4-1 in their opening preseason friendly at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper.
body: Oryan Goren, the 17-year-old Israeli midfielder rated as one of La Masia's brightest prospects, got his first taste of first-team football on Friday, coming off the bench as Barcelona beat CE Europa 4-1 in a closed-doors preseason friendly at the club's Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper.

Hansi Flick used the low-key opener, played behind closed doors as Barcelona's World Cup contingent continued their break, to hand minutes to a raft of academy players. Goren was among a wave of substitutes introduced at the interval after Barcelona had gone into the break firmly in control.

Barcelona's goals came from Ibrahim Diarra, Héctor Fort, Ebrima Tunkara and Álex González, with Flavio André scoring the visitors' consolation. Sport5 reports that Goren, along with several other academy graduates, was given a run-out in the second half as Flick rotated heavily.

It is a small but symbolic step for a player Barcelona has been grooming since 2023, when he left Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth setup in Israel to join La Masia. Born in Savyon, Goren plays as an attacking midfielder and has already drawn comparisons to some of the academy's most gifted recent graduates for his vision and composure on the ball.

This season he has been a regular for Barcelona's youth sides while also training repeatedly with the senior squad, and Sport5 notes he even featured in a defeat to Maccabi Haifa during the club's earlier preparations. He also has experience against opponents two years his senior in the UEFA Youth League setup.

The Israeli press draws a direct parallel to Guy Asulin, who trained under Pep Guardiola's Barcelona squad in preseason back in 2009 before going on to score in Wembley Cup fixtures against Tottenham and Al Ahly — a reminder that a preseason cameo does not guarantee a path to regular first-team football, but it is often the first visible marker of a serious opportunity.

For now, Goren's involvement is confined to Barcelona's preseason program, and Friday's appearance came in a match with no competitive stakes. But being included in Flick's matchday plans at all, even in a behind-closed-doors friendly, points to how highly the coaching staff already rate him ahead of the 2026-27 season.

title: Mantel and Mamu break Israeli records on opening day of the national athletics championships
dek: Pole vaulter Yarden Mantel cleared 4.16m and quarter-miler Noam Mamu ran 46.58 seconds as the 90th Israel Athletics Championship got under way at Givat Ram Stadium in Jerusalem.
body: Two Israeli age-group records fell inside a few hours of each other on the opening day of the 90th Israel Athletics Championship, as pole vaulter Yarden Mantel and 400m runner Noam Mamu both improved marks they already owned at Givat Ram Stadium in Jerusalem.

Mantel, competing for Maccabi Tel Aviv, cleared 4.16m to break her own Israeli under-20 and under-23 pole vault records by a single centimetre, having taken the mark to 4.15m earlier this season. The clearance extended a run that has made her the dominant figure in Israeli pole vault: she has now won the national title in four straight years, from 2023 through 2026.

Born in Kfar Saba in January 2007, Mantel has climbed the age-group ranks quickly, reaching the World U20 Championships in Lima in 2024 and steadily adding centimetres to her best each season. At 19, she is still eligible for both the under-20 and under-23 record books, and Wednesday's jump ticked both boxes at once.

Mamu's record fell in the men's 400m, where the Hapoel Emek Hefer runner stopped the clock at 46.58 seconds to take another bite out of the Israeli under-23 mark — a record he had already reset just four days earlier, running 46.78 at a meet in Liège, Belgium. Wednesday's run shaved two more tenths off that mark.

The 20-year-old, from Migdal HaEmek, has been one of the standout quarter-milers to come through the Israeli system in recent years: a four-time national 400m champion, a two-time national 800m champion, and a silver medallist over 800m at the 2022 European U18 Championships, which were also held at Givat Ram.

The two records set an early tone for a championship that draws roughly 250 of the country's leading track and field athletes to Jerusalem over two days, with free admission for spectators. The event doubles as a domestic proving ground and a staging post for athletes building toward the international season.

There was other business to settle on the opening day besides the records. Mercy Afrifah of Maccabi Tel Aviv won her first senior national title, taking the women's 100m in 11.72 seconds; her brother, Blessing Afrifah, holds the Israeli senior record over the same distance.

Linoy Levi of Maccabi Ramat Hasharon won the women's 110m hurdles in 13.66, and Arbel Hanzel of Lider Jerusalem took the men's 1500m in 3:48.57, according to Walla Sport and Davar's coverage of the meet.

For Mantel and Mamu, though, the day belonged to the record books. Both are still young enough to keep climbing the age-group lists, and both arrived at Givat Ram already the record holders they were trying to beat — a reminder that in Israeli athletics right now, the fastest-improving competition is often against themselves.

title: Philipsen finally breaks through to win Tour de France stage 17
dek: The Belgian sprinter ended a 17-day wait with victory out of a chaotic breakaway finish in Voiron, while Tadej Pogačar's overall lead stayed untouched.
body: Jasper Philipsen finally has something to show for this Tour de France. After seventeen stages of near-misses and frustration, the Belgian sprinter won stage 17 into Voiron, timing his effort out of a sprawling breakaway to deny the bunch a shot at the win altogether.
The stage covered 174.7km from Chambéry to Voiron, with roughly 2,200 metres of climbing packed mostly into the opening two hours before the road flattened out for a long run to the line.

The finish was decided not by the peloton but by a breakaway of around 40 riders that escaped early and never came back, with green jersey holder Mads Pedersen among the most combative, attacking repeatedly and winning the intermediate sprint along the way.

Jasper Stuyven tried to make the split count for himself, launching a lone attack out of the front group inside the closing kilometres, but the chasers behind him refused to let a winning move stick and reeled him back in before the finish.

That set up a bunch gallop within the breakaway itself, and it was Alpecin-Premier Tech who controlled it. Mathieu van der Poel delivered his teammate Philipsen perfectly into the final sprint, and Philipsen powered clear for a comfortable win ahead of Mauro Schmid of Team Jayco AlUla and Olav Kooij of Decathlon CMA CGM.

It was Philipsen's first stage victory of this year's race, a rare drought for a rider who has won at least one stage in every Tour he has finished since 2022. "It's a relief, not only for myself but for the team," Philipsen said afterwards.

Van der Poel, who has carried much of Alpecin-Premier Tech's ambitions through this Tour, was happy to play the support role. "This does feel a bit like winning it myself," he said. "It's also easier once you've already won a stage yourself. Then it's easier to play that card, although as a team we simply rode an incredible stage today."

The result also shook up the points classification. Pedersen faded to eighth in the finish-line sprint after his early exertions, and his green-jersey lead over Philipsen shrank to just seven points with several stages still to come.

At the top of the general classification, nothing changed. Tadej Pogačar kept his yellow jersey with a 4:32 advantage over Remco Evenepoel, with Isaac del Toro holding third overall, roughly 20 seconds clear of Paul Seixas in fourth.
Notably absent from that picture is Jonas Vingegaard, who crashed out of the race during stage 15 with a suspected collarbone injury and has not been seen since among the GC contenders.

title: Israeli basketball prospect David Musis set for move to Florida Atlantic
dek: The 18-year-old forward-center, fresh off a breakout season with Ramat HaSharon, is heading to NCAA basketball just as he prepares to lead Israel's Under-18 team into the European Championship.
body: One of Israeli basketball's most closely watched teenagers is packing his bags for American college hoops. David Musis, the 18-year-old forward-center who broke out with Ramat HaSharon this past season, is heading to Florida Atlantic University, Sport5 and ONE both report.

At 2.10m, Musis has long stood out physically, but it was his production in the Youth Premier League that turned heads: 24.1 points and 11.4 rebounds per game across 18 appearances, shooting an efficient 62.6% on two-pointers and a startling 40.4% from beyond the arc for a player his size.

Those numbers were enough to convince Ramat HaSharon's coaching staff to fast-track him. He was promoted mid-season to the senior roster competing in Israel's National League, where he held his own against grown men, averaging 9.5 points and 4.7 rebounds in 16.5 minutes a night at 60.3% from the field.

He only grew into the role as the campaign wound down. Over Ramat HaSharon's final four league games, Musis averaged 14.3 points and 7.5 rebounds in just over 20 minutes, capped by a 21-point, 13-rebound double-double in a playoff opener against Nahariya.

That trajectory — from promising youth talent to a difference-maker in a senior professional league at 18 — is exactly the kind of profile American college programs scout for, and Florida Atlantic has moved to bring him into its system, according to the Israeli reports.

Musis's path to the game itself was unconventional. He grew up in Holon and played soccer before switching codes, later relocating to Herzliya as his basketball career accelerated. He has cited Nikola Jokic as a stylistic model, unusual for a big man building his offensive game around footwork and touch rather than pure athleticism.

Speaking to Israeli media about his ambitions, Musis has been direct about where he sees this heading. "College basketball can actually help me develop, but long-term I'm thinking about reaching the NBA — aiming as high as I can," he said, a comment that reflects why a program like Florida Atlantic, an NCAA tournament regular in recent years, appealed to him over staying in the Israeli system.

The timing of the move is notable: Musis is currently with Israel's Under-18 national team ahead of the FIBA U18 European Championship in Trento-Rovereto, Italy, where Israel opens the tournament against Greece on July 25. Teammates have reportedly taken to calling him "GOAT" within the squad, a reflection of how highly he is regarded among his own age group.

Nothing has yet been confirmed directly by Florida Atlantic itself, and the move is being reported for now on the strength of Israeli outlets close to the club and player. But if it goes through as described, Musis would become the latest young Israeli big man to bypass a longer domestic apprenticeship for the American college pipeline — a route several Israeli prospects have used in recent years to raise their profile before turning professional.

title: LeBron James takes a fraction of his old salary to sign with the 76ers
dek: The 24th NBA season of LeBron's career will also be his least lucrative one — he has agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal with Philadelphia, a huge drop from the $52.6 million option he turned down in Los Angeles.
body: LeBron James has just taken the biggest pay cut of his career, and he did it on purpose. Sport5 reports that the 40-year-old has agreed to a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers — roughly a sixth of the $52.6 million option he walked away from in Los Angeles, a reduction the outlet frames as a 6.5-fold cut.

The numbers, confirmed by ESPN and CBS Sports, are almost jarring for a player of his stature: $3.876 million in 2026-27, rising to $4.1 million in 2027-28 via a player option. The first-year figure is his lowest NBA salary since his 2003-04 rookie contract with Cleveland, which paid him $4.02 million.

It is, in effect, a veteran's-minimum deal — the kind typically reserved for role players and bench fixtures, not a four-time MVP who was still earning superstar money with the Lakers as recently as last season.

James announced the move himself on social media, calling it his "last decision" — a nod to his famous 2010 television special — and framing it explicitly as a choice made for reasons other than money. "This is my last decision," he said. "I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind."

In a longer statement explaining the switch, he added: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time."

The move ends James's second Lakers spell and sends him into his 24th NBA season pairing with center Joel Embiid, giving Philadelphia a star duo built around chasing a title rather than accumulating regular-season wins. According to ESPN, the Golden State Warriors, Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves were among the other teams in the mix before he settled on the 76ers.

James marked the announcement with an Instagram highlight reel set to Meek Mill's "Dreams and Nightmares," the adopted anthem of Philadelphia's sports teams — a symbolic embrace of his new city before he has played a single minute there.

For a player who has never taken less than the max as a free agent in his prime, the willingness to sign for the league minimum underlines how deliberately James is now managing the end of his career: fewer dollars, in pursuit of one more shot at a ring.

title: Bundesliga star Kevin Kampl trades the pitch for a Mallorca vegetable farm after family tragedy
dek: The former RB Leipzig and Slovenia midfielder walked away from football in January after losing his brother and father within months of each other, and has found peace growing tomatoes, watermelons and olives on Spain's Balearic coast.
body: Kevin Kampl once patrolled midfields in front of 40,000 fans in Leipzig, Dortmund and Leverkusen. These days he is more likely to be found bent over a row of tomato plants on a small finca outside Palma, Mallorca, where the 35-year-old Slovenian international has rebuilt a life that football could no longer hold together.

Kampl walked away from professional football in January, when he and RB Leipzig mutually agreed to terminate the contract that still had time to run. The decision followed the two heaviest blows of his life arriving within months of each other: the death of his older brother Seki, 51, of a heart attack on October 22, 2025, and the death of his father not long after.

"The last two and a half months have been the worst of my life," Kampl said in a January interview, describing daily visits to his brother's grave. "I still can't fully grasp it - we were inseparable."

Sport5 reports that Kampl and his family have since resettled on a Mallorca property where he grows watermelons, tomatoes, onions, peppers and olives, pressing some of the olives into his own oil. He shares the work with his wife, Vanessa, and their two sons.
"It was a devastated year - there's no other word to describe it," Kampl said, according to Sport5. "But the quiet and peace we have in Majorca helped us all tremendously."

The retirement closed an eight-and-a-half-year chapter at RB Leipzig that began in 2017, when the Saxony club paid a reported €20 million to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen. Kampl went on to make well over 200 appearances across all competitions, winning the DFB-Pokal in 2022 and 2023 and starting as Leipzig reached a Champions League semi-final.
He was given a guard-of-honour send-off before a Leipzig Bundesliga fixture against Bayern Munich, teammates and staff applauding a player who had become one of the dressing room's senior voices.

Kampl's path to the Bundesliga began at Leverkusen and a loan spell at Borussia Dortmund, before Leipzig made him a fixture of their midfield through domestic cup runs and European nights. Born in Solingen, Germany, he held dual citizenship but chose to represent Slovenia, winning 28 caps between 2012 and 2018 before stepping back from international duty.
He has not cut ties with the club entirely. "I always follow what Leipzig does, and I will continue to do so," he said.

For a player who spent a career chasing results, the finca offers something else: physical work that helps him switch off, and seasons that, unlike a league table, owe nothing to Saturday's scoreline.
