body: Hapoel Haifa used a walk through their home city rather than a studio shoot to launch their new away kit for 2026/27, sending two of their defenders on a guided tour of Haifa landmarks as the black shirt was unveiled on Friday.

The strip, produced by the club's own graphic designer Araz Vaknin, draws on sites around Haifa that are all more than 103 years old, an attempt to root the design in the city's history rather than a generic away-day template.

To mark the release, Dario Župarić and Ivan Kričak were taken on a tour of the city guided by Prof. Yossi Ben-Artzi, a historian and geographer at the University of Haifa who has spent decades studying and helping preserve the city's heritage. The route took the pair from the Carmel through the Bahai Gardens and down to the Bat Galim neighbourhood.
The black shirt is intended for Hapoel Haifa's matches away from Sammy Ofer Stadium this coming season, including the club's next meeting with local rivals Maccabi Haifa in the Haifa derby.
According to ONE, the club is not finished with its kit rollout: a white set is set to follow shortly, completing the wardrobe before the 2026/27 Israeli Premier League campaign gets under way.

Neither Župarić nor Kričak, both centre-backs recruited to shore up Hapoel Haifa's defence, is a native of the city, which made the pairing with Ben-Artzi's guided history lesson a deliberate touch by the club's marketing team rather than an incidental photo opportunity.

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva have given supporters their first look at what the team will wear in 2026/27, unveiling three new kits — home, away and third — in a video posted to the club's social media channels.
All three shirts carry a refreshed version of the club crest, applied across the full kit set for the first time this season.

The designs are again the work of Aviad Fader, a Hapoel Petah Tikva supporter who has produced the club's kits every year since its return to the top flight — his fifth consecutive year on the job, according to the club.

Musonda, one of the players fronting the campaign, joined Hapoel Petah Tikva on loan from APOEL Limassol during the off-season, one of several new faces the club has added to the squad heading into the new campaign.

title: Mark van Bommel appointed new Belgium head coach
dek: The former PSV, Wolfsburg and Antwerp boss succeeds Rudi Garcia and will lead the Red Devils into Nations League action against Italy in September.
body: Belgium's football federation confirmed Mark van Bommel as the new head coach of the national team on Thursday, ONE reported, ending a search that began the moment Rudi Garcia's tenure ran out at the World Cup.

The 49-year-old Dutchman has signed through the end of Euro 2028, which Britain and Ireland will co-host, and is due to formally take up the post on August 15 before diving straight into Nations League preparations.

Garcia's contract was not renewed after Belgium's exit from the 2026 World Cup, where the Red Devils fell in the quarterfinals to eventual champions Spain. The Belgian federation had been searching for a coach who could reshape the squad without abandoning its remaining pockets of talent.

Van Bommel arrives with a playing pedigree few candidates could match: 79 caps for the Netherlands, a runner-up medal from the 2010 World Cup final, and championships won in the Netherlands, Spain, Germany and Italy across a career at PSV, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and AC Milan.

His coaching path has been steadier than spectacular in places — spells at PSV Eindhoven and Wolfsburg produced mixed results — but it was at Royal Antwerp where he made his name as a manager, guiding the club to the Belgian Pro League and Cup double in 2023, the team's first league title since 1957.

He will be joined on the Belgium bench by three fellow Dutchmen: Boudewijn Zenden, the former Liverpool and Barcelona winger, ex-AZ Alkmaar midfielder Maarten Martens, and the experienced Reinier Robbemond. ONE also noted van Bommel previously assisted his father-in-law, Bert van Marwijk, with the Saudi Arabia and Australia national teams.

"This is a great honor for me to be appointed Belgium national team coach," van Bommel said in comments carried by ONE. "Together with my team we will build a disciplined, ambitious and brave team capable of competing with the best national teams in the world."

Van Bommel's first assignment will be a stern one: an away trip to Rome to face Italy in the Nations League on September 25, immediately testing how quickly he can imprint his ideas on a Belgian squad still searching for direction after its golden generation's slow fade.

title: Beitar Ma'ale Adumim's youth side wins promotion to the national league

body: Beitar Ma'ale Adumim's Boys B side has won its way back into national youth football, sealing the Judean Shfela regional championship and, with it, promotion to Israel's new national U-17 league, ONE reports.
The margin was comfortable rather than dramatic: Ma'ale Adumim finished four points clear of Maccabi Gan Yavne, who took second, with Maccabi Ironi Ashdod completing the podium in third.

The team topped the table across two full rounds of fixtures, going 10-2-0 in the first and following up with a 9-0-3 record in the second — form good enough to hold off the chasing pack for the duration of the campaign.

The numbers behind the title tell their own story. Ma'ale Adumim scored 88 league goals, the second-highest tally in the division, while conceding only 17 — comfortably the meanest defence anyone in the Shfela group could field this season.

Much of the attacking output ran through captain Harel Abergil, who finished as the league's outright top scorer with 23 goals. At the back, goalkeeper Ido Ofer was central to a defensive record few sides came close to matching.

Coach Shai Cohen, a familiar figure in Jerusalem-area youth football after previous spells in charge of Beitar and Hapoel Jerusalem's junior sides, guided the promotion push. "We're happy with the achievement, but we hoped to do this more convincingly," Cohen said, according to ONE, crediting fitness coach Yaki Yuniov's conditioning work for the squad's stamina through a long season.

The promotion carries extra weight locally: it marks Ma'ale Adumim's first return to national-level youth competition since the 2021-22 season, giving the club's development pathway a tangible marker of progress heading into 2026-27.

body: Tamir Berman is on the move again, but this time he barely needs to pack — ONE reports the central defender has left Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv to sign for Hapoel Kfar Shalem, swapping one side of the Hatikva Quarter for the other.

The headline writes itself in Tel Aviv football circles: Bnei Yehuda and Kfar Shalem are neighbourhood rivals separated by little more than a few streets, and both currently call the modest Hatikva Neighborhood Stadium home. For Berman, this is as literal a cross-town move as Israeli football offers.

The 25-year-old is Argentine-Israeli, Jewish by heritage, which means he does not count against Kfar Shalem's foreign-player quota — a detail that made him an attractive squad option to begin with when Bnei Yehuda brought him over from Italian football in July 2025.
He went on to make 24 Liga Leumit appearances for Bnei Yehuda last season, chipping in two goals from the back, before the club apparently moved him on this summer.

Kfar Shalem, for their part, are rebuilding around a familiar face on the touchline. Noam Shoham has returned for a second stint as head coach, arriving fresh off guiding Maccabi Petah Tikva to promotion into Ligat Ha'al — a track record the Hatikva Quarter club will hope he can repeat closer to home.

The team finished last season fighting for promotion through the Liga Leumit playoffs before falling short, and the Berman signing is part of a wider reinforcement push as Shoham looks to have his squad ready in time for pre-season.
ONE also reports Kfar Shalem are close to adding Amit Nimni, son of Maccabi Tel Aviv legend and club record scorer Avi Nimni, with his signing expected to be finalised this week.

Other names mentioned by the outlet as recent or expected additions include Matan Beit Yaakov, Dror Nir, Iby Ransom and goalkeeper Tomer Tzarfati, with the club said to be targeting three further signings before the new campaign begins.
No contract length or transfer fee has been disclosed for Berman's move, and Kfar Shalem have not yet issued their own confirmation of the deal.

title: Bnei Herzliya sign well-travelled American guard DJ Brewton

body: Bnei Herzliya have added a well-travelled American guard to their roster for next season, announcing the signing of DJ Brewton on a deal for the coming Israeli Basketball Premier League campaign with a club option to extend it a further year, ONE reports.

Brewton, 26 and listed at around 6-foot-3, is a versatile guard-forward who spent last season hopping between three different European leagues — a itinerant path that nonetheless left him with a Polish championship medal by the end of it.

He began 2024-25 in Lithuania with BC Jonava, averaging roughly 14 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.9 assists in just under 29 minutes a night, form that earned him a spot on the league's foreign five and a place on the second all-star team.

Midway through the season he moved on to Italian side Udine, before a further switch took him to Legia Warsaw in Poland, where he helped the club to the Polish league title while averaging 14.5 points, four rebounds and 3.4 assists in just over 25 minutes per game — production that saw him named to Poland's foreign five as well.

"DJ is an interesting, versatile player we've been monitoring since last summer," Bnei Herzliya head coach Yehu Orland said of the signing. "He plays multiple positions, handles the ball well, demonstrates strong one-on-one ability, solid defense and toughness."
Brewton struck an upbeat tone about the move. "I'm excited to join Bnei Herzliya and look forward to the upcoming season," he said. "I believe we can accomplish great things together."

The signing gives Orland another ball-handling option as Bnei Herzliya, coached by the former IBPL Sixth Man of the Year, build out their squad for a season in which the Herzliya club will again look to compete in Israel's top flight.

title: How long should you rest between sets at the gym?
dek: A training explainer from ONE breaks down why the right rest interval depends on whether you are chasing strength, size or endurance.

verificationSources.label: ONE - כמה זמן צריך לנוח בין סט לסט באימון במכון?

body: How long should you actually wait before starting your next set? It is one of the most common questions in any weight room, and according to a training explainer published by ONE, the honest answer is that there is no single correct number for everyone.

The rest period, ONE reports, should be matched to the specific training goal. For pure strength and maximum power work — heavy compound lifts such as squats, deadlifts and bench presses — the recommendation is a lengthy three to five minutes between sets, because the central nervous system needs more time than the muscle itself to be ready to produce maximal force again.

For muscle growth, or hypertrophy training, the window narrows to roughly one and a half to three minutes. Resting less than a minute, the article notes, does not allow full recovery and tends to reduce the number of repetitions achievable in the following set, while the optimal range balances physiological recovery with keeping the muscle under enough mechanical tension.

Training for muscular endurance calls for the shortest breaks of all, around 30 to 90 seconds. Short rest intervals force the muscles and cardiovascular system to work through accumulated fatigue and improve lactate clearance, though they require dropping to noticeably lighter weights to sustain the higher volume.

The exercise itself matters too, according to ONE: compound movements that recruit large muscle groups demand more recovery time than isolated, single-joint exercises. Individual factors such as training experience, age and personal physiology also shift how much rest a lifter genuinely needs — beginners, the piece cautions, may feel ready to go again quickly even though their form has not fully recovered.

The practical takeaway is simple. Rather than guessing, ONE recommends using a stopwatch or gym timer to stay consistent and avoid starting the next set too soon, since the right amount of rest is ultimately dictated by the goal of the session, the complexity of the movement and the individual doing the lifting.
facts: Recommended rest for strength/maximum power work (squats, deadlifts, bench press): 3-5 minutes.
Recommended rest for muscle hypertrophy (growth) training: 1.5-3 minutes.
Recommended rest for muscular endurance training: 30-90 seconds.
Rest periods under one minute are said to limit recovery and reduce achievable repetitions in the next set.
Compound, multi-joint exercises are said to require longer recovery than isolated exercises.
The article recommends timing rest periods with a stopwatch/timer rather than estimating.

title: Rapyd's Shtilman offers $100 million for Recanati family's Maccabi Tel Aviv stake
dek: The club's own shirt sponsor has made a non-binding bid for the Recanatis' full 58% controlling holding, weeks after the family bought out the Federmans to take charge of the basketball giant.
body: Arik Shtilman, the Rapyd co-founder and chief executive who already sponsors Maccabi Tel Aviv's basketball team, has gone from backer to would-be buyer. ONE reports he has submitted a non-binding offer worth roughly $100 million to purchase the Recanati family's entire 58% controlling stake in the club.

According to ONE, Shtilman's letter to Udi and Shai Recanati frames the move as loyalty rather than a hostile approach. He describes himself as committed to the club's future after years as a fan and its central sponsor, and pledges to invest personal time, resources and "significant capital" in Maccabi's long-term success.

The bid lands only weeks after the Recanati family exercised its right of first refusal to buy out the Federman family's Fedanco Sport holding for around $50 million, ending the Federmans' long era at the club and lifting the Recanatis' stake to 58%.

That sale effectively unwound an agreement Shtilman had reached in May to buy half of Fedanco Sport himself and join Maccabi's board, part of a wider plan to inject $30 million into the club alongside additional investors. The Recanatis' decision to activate their first-refusal rights shut that route down entirely.
Shtilman is no stranger to Maccabi's finances. Rapyd has been the club's shirt and naming sponsor since 2024, with the team playing domestically and in the EuroLeague as Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv.

ONE reports the new offer covers the Recanati family's full 58% holding, or alternatively a controlling core of it, and proposes a 30-day due-diligence window with completion targeted within 90 days — a tight timeline that signals how quickly Shtilman wants to move.

The picture is complicated by a parallel process ONE says is already under way: the Recanati family is reportedly in separate talks to sell around half of its stake to American investor Jason Levin for roughly $50 million, a deal that would also see Levin take Maccabi's seat on the EuroLeague's board of shareholders in place of Danny Federman.

ONE further reports that Guy Harel, the former Maccabi Jerusalem chief executive who also acts as an agent for Maccabi Tel Aviv head coach Oded Katz, helped facilitate contact between the Recanatis and Levin.

Neither the Recanati family nor Shtilman has commented publicly on the $100 million offer, and it is unclear whether the family — having just taken outright control after years as one of the club's three traditional power centres — has any appetite to sell out so soon.

Maccabi Tel Aviv is a six-time EuroLeague champion and the dominant force in Israeli basketball, so any change of control would rank among the largest ownership transactions in the country's sporting history — and would turn a sponsor into an owner almost overnight.

title: Klopp warns he will quit as Germany coach if media targets his family
dek: In his first press conference since replacing Julian Nagelsmann, the new head coach drew a hard line on privacy — and said he would walk away without compensation if the federation ever decides it no longer wants him.
body: Jürgen Klopp used his unveiling as Germany's new head coach on Friday to set out the terms of his return to management in blunt personal language — promising commitment to the job while warning he would walk away the moment anyone crosses the line with his family.

"If they behave inappropriately and don't leave my family alone, I will leave," Klopp told reporters at the DFB's campus in Frankfurt, in comments reported by ONE and echoed across German and international outlets. He made clear that criticism of his coaching was fair game, but that intrusion into his private life was not something he would tolerate in exchange for the job.

The 59-year-old was equally blunt about job security, framing his position in the sport's harshest terms. "If they say tomorrow I'm bad — I will go. When they no longer want me, I'll leave without compensation," he said, rejecting any notion that he would cling to the post or negotiate a payoff if results turn against him.

Klopp signed a four-year contract with the German federation, a deal reported to run through the 2030 World Cup, ending nearly two years away from the touchline. He left Liverpool in May 2024 after almost nine years at Anfield, then took a background role as Red Bull's global head of soccer from January 2025 before agreeing to return to frontline coaching for his native country.

He replaces Julian Nagelsmann, who resigned after Germany's stunning last-32 exit from the 2026 World Cup, beaten on penalties by Paraguay in a result that plunged German football into fresh soul-searching over the national team's direction.

Klopp will be joined on the touchline by familiar faces from his Liverpool and Dortmund years: assistant coaches Peter Krawietz and Pep Lijnders both follow him into the national set-up, alongside former Germany international Sven Bender.

On the playing squad, Klopp was candid about the gap in individual talent between Germany and the sport's current superstars. He acknowledged the team does not have players of the calibre of Kylian Mbappé or Ousmane Dembélé, but insisted that need not be decisive. "We can still win," he said, framing the rebuild around collective organisation rather than star power.

He also served notice that no one arrives with a guaranteed shirt, name-checking Bayern Munich and national team fixture Joshua Kimmich as an example — a pointed signal that reputation alone will not secure a place under the new regime.
Klopp described taking charge of Die Mannschaft as "the peak of my career," pushing back on any suggestion he would treat the national job as a lighter, part-time posting compared to his club career.

The appointment marks one of the most eye-catching returns to a dugout in recent memory, putting one of the game's most recognisable coaching personalities in charge of restoring a team that has slipped well below its own historic standards on the biggest stage.

title: Two of Spain's World Cup matches flagged in betting integrity report
dek: The Copenhagen Group listed Spain's scoreless draw with Cape Verde and a marathon VAR delay against Saudi Arabia among seven alerts from the tournament, though FIFA insists no manipulation was found in any match.
body: Spain lifted the World Cup in Argentina's own backyard of grief three weeks ago, but two of the matches on their route to the final are now sitting in a betting watchdog's file marked 'irregular'.

The Copenhagen Group, an independent body that advises the Council of Europe on the manipulation of sports competitions, says it monitored all 104 games at the 2026 tournament and issued seven 'yellow alerts' — its second-tier classification for matches showing multiple signs of unusual activity, such as odd betting swings or suspicious chatter on social media. Two of those seven involve Spain.

The first came from Spain's group-stage meeting with debutants Cape Verde, which finished 0-0 in a result almost nobody in the football world expected. On the crypto-based prediction platform Polymarket, some $4.8 million was wagered specifically against Spain winning the match — an amount the Copenhagen Group flagged as statistically striking given Spain's status as tournament favourites. Reports at the time noted at least one bettor who had staked heavily against Cape Verde holding on lost roughly $1 million when the draw held.

The second concerns Spain's 4-0 win over Saudi Arabia, also in the Group H stage. Video review took an unusually long time — about three and a half minutes — before a goal by Barcelona forward Ferran Torres was ruled out for offside. The length of the delay, rather than the decision itself, is what drew the watchdog's attention.

Spain were not alone in being singled out. Among the other five alerts, the Copenhagen Group pointed to the red card shown to South Africa's Themba Zwane in the 84th minute of his side's opening match against Mexico, and to betting markets that opened around Folarin Balogun's disciplinary status before his red card and suspension were controversially overturned following intervention reportedly involving FIFA president Gianni Infantino and US President Donald Trump.

FIFA has firmly rejected any suggestion of wrongdoing. Its own Integrity Task Force, which conducted a parallel review of the tournament, stated flatly that 'no suspicious activity was detected in betting markets and no indications of match manipulation were found in any tournament match' — a direct contradiction of the Copenhagen Group's seven flagged incidents.

Christian Kalb, a betting-industry expert who has previously worked with the Copenhagen Group, cautioned against reading too much into the alerts on their own. He said such signals can stem from entirely legitimate causes — hedging by large liquidity providers or ordinary shifts in market odds — rather than any attempt to fix a result.

Nothing in the report accuses any player, official or federation of wrongdoing, and no disciplinary process has been opened against Spain, Cape Verde or Saudi Arabia over either match. The Copenhagen Group's alerts function as a monitoring tool rather than a finding of guilt, and its own methodology stresses that a 'yellow' rating reflects statistical irregularity, not proof of manipulation.

Spain went on to beat France in the semi-final and edged Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the final to win their second World Cup, meaning the report lands as an awkward footnote to what was otherwise a triumphant tournament for La Roja.

title: Jürgen Klopp returns to the touchline as new Germany head coach
dek: The former Liverpool manager has signed a four-year deal through the 2030 World Cup, taking over from Julian Nagelsmann after Germany's shock Round of 32 exit to Paraguay.
body: Jürgen Klopp is coaching again — and this time it's the biggest job in German football. The DFB has appointed the former Liverpool manager as head coach of the national team, ending a spell away from the touchline that had stretched more than two years.

ONE reports that Klopp has signed a four-year contract taking him through the 2030 World Cup, with the appointment confirmed after Julian Nagelsmann's departure in the wake of Germany's Round of 32 elimination at this summer's World Cup, where they were beaten by Paraguay on penalties.
Klopp, 59, formally takes charge on August 15, leaving him just over three weeks to prepare before his first assignment: Germany's Nations League fixtures in September.

"It's an enormous honour to sit here today," Klopp said at his unveiling. "When you become part of it, you feel the power and responsibility even more." He went on to call the role "the pinnacle of my career."

The move ends an 18-month spell away from coaching proper. Klopp stepped down at Liverpool in May 2024 after nine trophy-laden years, then took a front-office role in January 2025 as Red Bull's global head of soccer, overseeing a network of clubs that includes RB Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg, before walking back into a dugout.

He arrives with familiar faces around him. Peter Krawietz and Pepijn Lijnders, both long-serving lieutenants from his Liverpool bench, join the Germany set-up alongside Sven Bender, the former Borussia Dortmund midfielder and ex-international who rounds out the new coaching staff.

The in-tray is heavy. Manuel Neuer is expected to retire from international football for a second time, and reports around the appointment suggest Klopp could also lose several senior figures — Antonio Rüdiger, Leroy Sané, Leon Goretzka, Pascal Groß and Oliver Baumann have all been mentioned as possible retirees as Germany rebuilds after a chastening World Cup.

Captain Joshua Kimmich stays on, and Klopp is expected to shape the new-look side around him alongside Florian Wirtz — now, like his new coach, at Liverpool — and Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala, the two players widely seen as the spine of Germany's next generation.

Nagelsmann had taken Germany to the semi-finals of Euro 2024 on home soil, but the early World Cup exit to Paraguay, appearing at only their third finals since 1958, proved too costly for the DFB to overlook.

For a federation still absorbing that setback, handing the reins to a coach with Klopp's pedigree — a Bundesliga and Champions League winner at Dortmund, a Premier League and Champions League winner at Liverpool — is being read at home as a statement of ambition rather than a stopgap fix before the next World Cup cycle.

title: Real Madrid open talks to sign Lonnie Walker away from Maccabi Tel Aviv

body: Real Madrid have opened negotiations to sign Lonnie Walker IV away from Maccabi Tel Aviv this summer, ONE reports, citing the Spanish basketball journalist Chema de Lucas.

De Lucas broke the news on X, writing that Real Madrid "negocia el fichaje de Lonnie Walker" — Real Madrid are negotiating the signing of Lonnie Walker. The claim was quickly picked up by several Spanish basketball outlets tracking the EuroLeague market.

According to ONE, Walker still has two years remaining on the three-year, roughly $10 million contract he signed with Maccabi last summer, but both sides are said to be open to finding an exit arrangement that would let him leave. The American guard is understood to be seeking a fresh challenge, while Maccabi would be willing to let him go if the right solution is found.

It would not be the first flirtation between the two parties. Real Madrid were reportedly close to landing Walker back in November, only for that move to collapse over the NBA exit-clause terms the player wanted and the Spanish club would not accept.

How any deal would actually work remains the open question. ONE notes it is still unclear whether Real Madrid would take on Walker's full Maccabi salary, share the cost, or whether Maccabi would need compensation of some kind to release him early.

The report lands a day after Sportando separately reported that Walker could part ways with Maccabi this summer, with EuroLeague clubs already said to be monitoring his situation as they look to strengthen their backcourts for the new season.

Walker's contract had included NBA exit windows running to July 15 in both 2026 and 2027, according to Basketnews — meaning any departure now, with that date already passed, would have to be negotiated as a mutual separation rather than triggered by a built-in clause.

On the court, Walker has been one of Maccabi's more productive perimeter scorers this season, averaging close to 15 points and around two assists a game in the EuroLeague, despite losing several weeks to a dislocated finger.

For Maccabi, moving Walker on would remove a significant salary commitment from the roster heading into the new campaign — one of the club's stated priorities this offseason. For Real Madrid, adding an experienced NBA-calibre scoring guard would address a perimeter need as they reshape their roster around Europe's continental contenders.
Nothing has been confirmed by either club, and the structure of any transfer — buyout, salary split or otherwise — has yet to be reported in detail.

body: Three brothers from the same Tel Aviv fighting family will headline their own promotion on Monday, and by their own admission, they are still getting used to the scale of what they built. Ahavat HaShem, Ruach HaShem and Kibedy Gordon sat for a press conference on Thursday ahead of GFN 1: Israel vs. the World, the debut card of their new venture, Gordon Fight Nights.
"We didn't believe the event would reach such a historic magnitude," one of the brothers said at the presser, according to ONE, adding: "This is the first time, but not the last."

The card lands at the Menora Mivtachim Arena in Tel Aviv, the city's main indoor arena and regular home to Maccabi Tel Aviv's basketball games, and is built around a triple main event that puts each Gordon brother in his own Muay Thai bout against an international opponent.

Ahavat Gordon, the youngest of the three and already a two-time European Muay Thai champion, faces the highest-profile name on the card in John Lineker, the Brazilian former UFC and ONE Championship bantamweight star known for his one-punch power. It is a striking step up in profile for the 20-year-old, who fights in the 65-kilogram division and carries an unbeaten professional Muay Thai record into the bout.

Ruach Gordon, the eldest brother and a World Games silver medallist for Israel, meets Maximus Bejenuta, while Kibedy Gordon takes on Jose Alberto Quinonez, rounding out a main event built entirely around the family name.

The rest of the main card carries its own recognisable names. Natan Levy, the former UFC lightweight, moves to kickboxing rules against Lando Vannata, while Ilay Barzilay meets Lucas Almeida in MMA and Nili Block faces Isabele Celestrino in Muay Thai. A six-bout preliminary card, pitting Israeli fighters against opponents from across Europe and South America, opens the night.

Promoters have billed the event as Israel's first major independent combat-sports card of this scale, spanning Muay Thai, kickboxing and MMA under one roof, with international broadcast coverage through MILLIONS.co set to begin at 11 a.m. ET.

For a family long known individually on the Muay Thai and kickboxing circuit, turning that reputation into a promotion of their own marks a new chapter. Ahavat has fought for world and European titles since his mid-teens, while Ruach has represented Israel on the international stage for years; putting both of their names, plus their brother's, on the same marquee is the clearest sign yet of how far the family's ambitions have grown.
The full bout order for Monday's card was still described as subject to change as fight week began, organisers said, with final details to be confirmed closer to the event.

title: Refaelov: 'I was one of those who pushed for Bachar to sign a new deal'
dek: Maccabi Haifa's sporting director opened pre-season by revealing his role in retaining coach Barak Bachar, addressing Dolev Haziza's exit and confirming Kenji Gorré as new captain.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - official: Bachar extends contract, Refaelov named sporting director

body: Lior Refaelov spent a decade and a half as one of Maccabi Haifa's most cherished attacking players. Now working from the other side of the desk as the club's sporting director, he opened the Greens' 2026/27 pre-season campaign on Thursday with an unusually candid press conference — including the admission that he was quietly lobbying to keep coach Barak Bachar long before it became official business.

"I was one of those who pushed for Barak to sign already in March for another season," Refaelov told reporters, according to ONE. He said the club had grown weary of constant upheaval on the bench and in the dugout. "There was almost a professional revolution every summer, and it's very hard to operate that way."

The comments add texture to a decision Maccabi Haifa had already made public in May, when the club confirmed Bachar would continue as head coach for the new campaign, with Refaelov stepping into the sporting director's chair after hanging up his boots. Refaelov's version, delivered two months later, frames that outcome as something he pushed for internally rather than simply administered.

Much of the session, however, centred on the summer's most emotional departure. Refaelov confirmed that winger Dolev Haziza has left the club, calling it "one of the hardest decisions I made personally." He said the timing was deliberate — the club waited until deals for Bruninho and Yair Mordechai were finalised before sitting Haziza down.

"I'm sure he was angry, and I'm sure he received it in a way that wasn't even respectful," Refaelov said, acknowledging how the process looked from Haziza's side. He added that his affection for the player remains undimmed: "I have much love for him, and when I saw his farewell video today I was very moved."

On leadership, Refaelov confirmed winger Kenji Gorré will wear the captain's armband next season alongside goalkeeper Omri Glazer and Ali Mohammad. "Today we informed him that he will be captain next season, together with Glazer and Ali Mohammad," he said, praising Gorré's character.

The choice carries extra weight given Gorré's summer. The Dutch-born winger represented Curaçao at the 2026 World Cup, where the Caribbean island — the smallest nation ever to reach the tournament — was drawn into Group E alongside Germany, Ecuador and Ivory Coast. Refaelov said Gorré arrives back in Haifa "from the World Cup charged with purpose to mobilize all the energies he experienced there."

Elsewhere in the squad rebuild, Refaelov said Yarin Levi's return to the fold is being treated as effectively a new addition. "I'm treating him as a new signing, along with players who joined and loaned players who returned," he said, pointing to a squad being reshaped around a mix of youth, fresh faces and reintegrated loanees. Brazilian midfielder Bruninho arrived from Karpaty Lviv, while Yair Mordechai joined on a four-year deal from Hapoel Ironi Kiryat Shmona. Winger Manuel Benson's recovery from injury was also discussed as part of the squad picture.

Refaelov did not shy away from the club's recruitment difficulties either, acknowledging that security concerns have complicated conversations with prospective signings and their families — a recurring theme for Israeli clubs courting foreign players in the current climate. He also took personal responsibility for past transfers that failed to work out, saying the issue was often adaptation rather than a lack of quality.

He laid out three guiding principles for the season ahead: rebuilding the connection with supporters, raising internal standards, and re-establishing a clear professional identity after a turbulent campaign. He also flagged Maccabi Haifa's recurring injury problems as an area the club intends to address through changes to its medical and fitness procedures.

The tone throughout was less a victory lap than a reckoning with a difficult season past — but Refaelov's willingness to detail the reasoning behind both the Bachar reappointment and the Haziza exit suggests a club trying to project more stability, and more transparency, heading into 2026/27.

title: Hapoel Holon sign American-Jamaican guard Drew Thelwell
dek: The Israeli club continues rebuilding its roster for the new season, adding the 24-year-old point guard fresh off a promotion-winning campaign with Pau-Lacq-Orthez in France.

verificationSources.label: Eurohoops - Predrag Krunic named Hapoel Holon head coach

body: Hapoel Holon have added another body to their backcourt, agreeing terms with Drew Thelwell, the American-Jamaican point guard, as the club keeps reshaping its roster ahead of the new Israeli Basketball Super League season, ONE reports.

Thelwell, 24 and 1.91m, arrives from Pau-Lacq-Orthez, where he spent his rookie professional season after leaving American college basketball. He helped the French club win promotion out of the second tier, averaging 10.9 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists a game along the way, according to ONE.

Before turning pro he spent four seasons at Morehead State before using a fifth year of college eligibility at Iowa, where in 2024-25 he averaged 9.5 points, 3.0 assists and 2.2 rebounds a game for the Hawkeyes, per the report.
He has also become a regular for Jamaica's senior national team, putting up 15.0 points, 4.8 assists and 3.8 rebounds a game across six FIBA World Cup qualifiers, ONE notes.

Head coach Predrag Krunić, the Bosnian who took over the Holon bench this year, welcomed the signing: "Drew is a player who can play at high intensity on both ends of the floor, in defense and in attack," he said, according to ONE.

Sporting director Daniel Ravitz was equally upbeat, calling Thelwell "a young, promising point guard who capped his first season in Europe with a title-winning campaign" — a reference to Orthez's promotion-clinching run in France's second division.
Financial terms and the length of the contract were not disclosed in the report.

The move fits the pattern of Hapoel Holon's off-season approach: bringing in young, upwardly-mobile guards from Europe and the American college ranks as the club looks to build depth in its backcourt for the coming campaign.

title: Ironi Tiberias open season without coach and six players amid banned-infusions case
dek: Head coach Eliran Chodeda, captain Guy Hadida and several teammates are suspended over a banned-infusions investigation as Tiberias begin the campaign against Bnei Sakhnin in the Toto Cup.
body: Ironi Tiberias will open their Ligat Ha'Al season on Saturday evening missing their head coach and six players, a squad hollowed out by a suspicious-infusions scandal that has engulfed the club just as preparations for the new campaign were supposed to be getting under way.

The northern club host Bnei Sakhnin at 20:30 in the first round of the Toto Cup's northern group, and ONE reports the team will be without head coach Eliran Chodeda, technical director Chen Sol and captain Guy Hadida, all of whom have been suspended, along with players Niv Gotlib and David Kaltin.

The suspensions stem from an investigation into banned infusions, opened after Maccabiat (MS) Ashdod, relegated following a playoff meeting with Tiberias, filed a complaint alleging that Tiberias players received prohibited substances followed by large volumes of saline solution before a match on May 3 — a method the complaint says was meant to mask the substances from any post-match doping test.

Israel's anti-doping authority acted on the complaint by suspending the coaching staff and the implicated players pending further proceedings, and prosecutors have since pushed for severe sanctions, reportedly ranging from lengthy bans of several years to lifetime suspensions for some of those named.

Tiberias have strongly disputed the findings, calling the suspensions a "populist and scandalous" decision reached without a proper hearing or laboratory testing, and insisting the substance administered was a legal saline solution given within World Anti-Doping Agency limits. An urgent appeal to have the suspensions lifted before the new season is already under way, according to Ynet.

Two more first-teamers are unavailable for reasons unconnected to the infusions case. Gal Meatuq remains sidelined amid an unresolved transfer-fee dispute with Maccabi Petah Tikva, while Samir Farhoud is still serving out a suspension carried over from an altercation in last season's State Cup final.

With Chodeda barred from the touchline, Tiberias have turned to Maurice Ozen, currently the club's youth academy technical director, to take interim charge of the first team. Ozen previously managed Tiberias in the 2019/20 season and remains a well-known figure locally from his time at Hapoel Beit She'an.

The arrangement is expected to be short-term: assistant coach Moti Krispel is completing the professional coaching certification required to take permanent charge, with Ozen holding the fort in the meantime.
"This preparation is far from ideal," the club said in a statement carried by ONE, "but we have no excuses. Those who play well enough will come and give everything to win."

It is an unusually turbulent way for a Ligat Ha'Al club to begin a season, with the Toto Cup opener against Sakhnin now serving as an early test of how much a squad and a makeshift coaching staff can absorb before the league campaign itself gets under way.

title: Suspicious betting? Seven alerts raised over World Cup matches despite FIFA's clean bill of health
dek: An independent integrity monitor tied to the Council of Europe flagged seven low-level suspicious betting cases from the tournament, including a red card, a disallowed goal and a $4.8 million wager on Spain, even as FIFA insists it found nothing untoward.
body: Five days after the final whistle in the 2026 World Cup, an uncomfortable question is being asked about the tournament's integrity: did anyone try to manipulate a match, and would anyone even know?

ONE reports that the Group of Copenhagen, an independent sports-betting monitoring body linked to the Council of Europe, tracked all 104 matches of the finals and singled out seven cases as "yellow alerts" — its second-lowest tier, denoting multiple indicators of irregularity that fall well short of proof but warrant a closer look. Fifteen matches in total received extra scrutiny, concentrated around the tense finish to the group stage, with twelve separate incidents examined for integrity risk.

The findings sit awkwardly alongside FIFA's own account. The governing body's Integrity Task Force has stated flatly that it identified "no suspicious betting activity or indications of match manipulation" in any fixture across the entire competition — a direct contradiction the Group of Copenhagen's report does not shy away from.

The most detailed case involves Folarin Balogun. The United States forward was shown a red card, and on July 2 the prediction-market platform Polymarket opened a market asking simply whether he would play against Belgium — three days before FIFA's Disciplinary Committee confirmed his suspension had been lifted. According to the report, no comparable betting market appeared for any of the other fourteen players sent off during the tournament, none of whom had their bans suspended.

A second flagged case centres on Spain's goalless group-stage draw with Cape Verde, where roughly $4.8 million was staked on Polymarket against Spain winning outright — a striking sum for a fixture pitting a heavy favourite against a World Cup debutant.

Spain features again in a third case: a VAR review lasting some three and a half minutes before a Ferran Torres goal was ruled out in the team's 4-0 win over Saudi Arabia. The delay itself, rather than the eventual decision, drew the monitor's attention.

The opening match of the tournament also made the list. South Africa's Themba Zwane was sent off in the 84th minute of the Group A curtain-raiser against Mexico, an incident the report includes among its seven flagged episodes.

None of this amounts to an allegation that any player, official or match was actually corrupted. A yellow alert, in the Group of Copenhagen's four-tier scale running from green through yellow and orange to red, is explicitly a trigger for further review rather than a finding of wrongdoing — it can be set off by nothing more sinister than an unusual swing in odds or a rumour circulating on social media.

What has amplified the story is scale. The Group of Copenhagen estimates roughly $240 billion was wagered worldwide on this World Cup, close to double the amount bet on Qatar 2022 — a market large enough that even minor statistical anomalies attract attention, and one prediction markets like Polymarket have made far more visible than in previous tournaments.

FIFA has not publicly detailed how it reconciles its own clean assessment with the Council of Europe-linked body's findings, and no disciplinary or criminal process has been opened over any of the seven cases. For now, the story is one of two respected integrity processes reaching different conclusions from the same tournament — not evidence that a World Cup match was fixed.

title: Socceroos winger Cristian Volpato loses licence after alleged positive cocaine test
dek: The Sassuolo forward, fresh off Australia's World Cup campaign, was pulled over twice on Sydney's Anzac Bridge before a roadside drug test allegedly returned positive.
body: Cristian Volpato's summer has taken a sharp and unwelcome turn. Weeks after helping Australia through the group stage at the FIFA World Cup, the Sassuolo winger allegedly returned a positive roadside test for cocaine during a late-night traffic stop in Sydney, and has had his international driver's licence suspended for six months.

New South Wales Police stopped Volpato twice in the space of two hours on the Anzac Bridge, one of Sydney's main harbour crossings. The first stop came just after 11pm on Thursday, when he was clocked doing 86-94 km/h in a 60 km/h zone. He was fined and passed a breath alcohol test at the scene.

A little over two hours later, at around 1.10am on Friday, police stopped him again on the same bridge, this time allegedly travelling at 109 km/h — close to 50 km/h over the limit. A roadside drug test taken during that second stop allegedly returned a positive reading for cocaine, according to a police statement reported by Australian outlets including SBS News.

A secondary oral fluid sample was taken for laboratory confirmation, the standard follow-up procedure in New South Wales before any formal charge is laid. As things stand, Volpato has not been charged with a criminal offence — the immediate consequence has been the six-month suspension of his licence.

ONE, the Israeli outlet that first flagged the story locally, reported the incident under the player's name as "Christian" Volpato; his correct playing name, as registered with Sassuolo, the Australian federation and FIFA, is Cristian Volpato.

The 22-year-old was one of the more talked-about figures of Australia's World Cup, having switched international allegiance from Italy — where he had represented the Azzurrini at Under-19 and Under-20 level — to the Socceroos shortly before the tournament. He made three appearances at the finals.

Born in the Sydney suburb of Camperdown, Volpato came through Roma's academy before joining Sassuolo, where he remains under contract in Serie A. Neither the club nor Football Australia had issued a public statement on the matter at the time of writing.
The episode is an awkward one for a player who had used the World Cup to raise his profile after a modest run of club form, and it now leaves a cloud over his return to pre-season training in Italy.

A secondary oral fluid sample was taken for laboratory confirmation; no criminal charge has been laid to date.

title: Hapoel Rishon LeZion bets on youth as it rebuilds for the future
dek: More than 100 children turned out for the club's summer training camp, the first visible step in a youth strategy the Liga Leumit side hopes will carry it back to the top flight.

verificationSources.label: BE106 Rishon LeZion – youth camp registration

body: Hapoel Rishon LeZion kicked off its summer not with a marquee signing but with more than a hundred children and teenagers on the training pitch, in what the club is presenting as the first real step of a rebuilt youth strategy, ONE reported.

The Liga Leumit club's youth department ran a summer training camp for close to 100 boys and girls, split into small groups and worked through stations covering technique, finishing, individual tactics and pressing games, alongside coordination and physical conditioning.

Ophir Kupel, the department's professional manager, said the camp was run "at the highest professional level, with the department's best coaches," with close attention paid to technical detail, physical work and team play. Alongside the football work, players sat in on enrichment sessions covering nutrition, mental resilience and a broader sporting lifestyle.
Arik Ben Yididya, the department's administrative manager, organised the camp together with Kupel — part of a push the club says goes beyond one summer session.

ONE frames the camp as the visible face of a larger commitment: an advanced football academy the club is investing in financially, built on the idea that Hapoel Rishon LeZion's route forward runs through developing its own players rather than leaning on a wealthy owner to buy success.

That framing lines up with where the club sits: Hapoel Rishon LeZion currently play in Liga Leumit, Israel's second tier, and are chasing promotion back to the top flight. A functioning academy pipeline would let the club develop players internally rather than relying solely on transfer budgets it does not have.
A separate notice from the youth department, carried by local outlet BE106, listed the preparatory camp as running from July 12 to July 28 — consistent with the timing of the camp described by ONE.

Alongside the football curriculum, the club says it is building the program around values like self-confidence, discipline, teamwork and friendship — the kind of framing clubs increasingly use to sell academy places to parents, but one that also reflects a genuine shift in resourcing toward the youth ranks.

title: World Climbing cancels vote to suspend Israel from competitions
dek: A last-minute motion from USA Climbing, Australia and Cyprus averted a vote on banning Israel, Russia and Belarus from international competition, with a disciplinary review ordered instead.
body: A push to suspend Israel from international climbing competitions collapsed just hours before it was due to be put to a vote, ONE reports. World Climbing, the sport's global governing body formerly known as the IFSC, had called an extraordinary general assembly for Thursday to decide whether the Israeli federation should be barred from competition alongside Russia and Belarus.

The push originated with the Palestinian Climbing Federation and activist groups such as Climbers for Palestine, who argue that Israeli climbers and organisers have developed climbing sites on land they say belongs to Palestinian territory, and accuse the Israel Climbing Federation of appropriating routes in the West Bank.

More than 70 national federations logged on for the virtual assembly, but the suspension vote itself never happened. In an eleventh-hour intervention, USA Climbing, joined by the federations of Australia and Cyprus, put forward an alternative motion asking the assembly to shelve the ban vote altogether.

That alternative passed by a slim majority. Instead of voting Israel, Russia and Belarus in or out, the assembly instructed World Climbing's Executive Board to build a general framework, grounded in good governance, proportionality and non-discrimination, for deciding in future which national federations may take part in its events.

The immediate suspension threat has been lifted, but not the scrutiny. ONE reports that allegations of possible regulatory violations by both the Israeli and Russian climbing federations will now be referred to World Climbing's disciplinary committee for review.

Individual athletes are unaffected by Thursday's proceedings: their eligibility to compete under their national flags remains unchanged regardless of the outcome of any future federation-level process.

Climbing becomes the latest sport to wrestle publicly with campaigns to exclude Israel from international competition, with advocates pointing specifically to disputes over access to bouldering and cliff sites in the West Bank as their central grievance.

For now, Israeli climbers can compete without interruption, with no federation currently suspended from the World Cup or World Championship calendar. But with the Executive Board now tasked with drafting a formal framework, the question of Israel's place in international climbing looks likely to resurface once that work is complete.
facts: World Climbing, formerly the IFSC, held a virtual extraordinary general assembly on Thursday, July 23, 2026, with more than 70 national federations attending.

A slight majority of federations backed the alternative, instructing the Executive Board to draft a principles-based framework for future participation decisions.
Allegations that Israel's and Russia's climbing federations breached regulations will be referred to World Climbing's disciplinary committee.
Individual athletes' eligibility to compete is unaffected by the vote's cancellation.

title: Beitar Jerusalem's win at AEK Larnaca is only their sixth European away victory ever
dek: Brayan Carabalí's second-half free kick settled a 1-0 win in Cyprus, giving Beitar back-to-back European away victories for the first time in the club's history ahead of next week's return leg in Romania.
body: Beitar Jerusalem beat AEK Larnaca 1-0 away in Cyprus on Thursday to open their Conference League second qualifying round tie, and by the numbers alone it is one of the rarer results in the club's European history: only the sixth away win Beitar have managed in 28 attempts in continental competition.

The only goal came in the 77th minute at the AEK Arena – George Karapatakis, when Brayan Carabalí curled a direct free kick past the Cypriot goalkeeper. The Colombian centre-back's strike arrived five minutes after AEK were reduced to ten men, with Mike van der Hoorn sent off in the 72nd minute.

ONE, reporting on the significance of the result, notes that Beitar have now won on the road in Europe for the first time in successive seasons — following last year's 2-1 victory at Sutjeska in the same competition. In a fixture list stretching back to 1996, that has never happened before.

The club's full away-win ledger in Europe, as laid out by ONE, reads: Floriana 5-1 (1996/97), Torshavn 1-0 (1998/99), WIT Georgia 4-1 (2000/01), Vasas 3-0 (2017/18), Sutjeska 2-1 (2025/26) and now AEK Larnaca 1-0 (2026/27) — six wins from 28 away trips over three decades.

The gaps between those results tell their own story: 17 years separated the win in Georgia from the one over Vasas in Hungary, and a further eight passed before Sutjeska. Beitar's away form in continental football has long been the club's soft underbelly, and Thursday's result, coming barely a year after ending that drought altogether, points to something changing.

It was also a first competitive outing as head coach for Almog Cohen, who moved from the club's sports director role into the dugout this summer after Beitar finished runners-up in the Israeli Premier League last season. Barak Itzhaki left the post at the end of the campaign.

The return leg is scheduled for July 30 — but not in Cyprus, and not in Jerusalem either. With UEFA continuing to bar European fixtures from being staged in Israel because of the security situation, Beitar will host AEK Larnaca at the Ilie Oană Stadium in Ploiești, Romania, a roughly 15,000-capacity ground the club has used before for matches designated as "home" games.

A one-goal cushion is a workable but hardly decisive lead to carry into that second leg. Still, for a club whose European away record has been defined more by long famines than by results like Thursday's, banking a clean sheet and a goal in Larnaca gives Beitar a rare position of comfort heading into the second half of the tie.

title: Hezonja's NBA comeback is stuck waiting on LeBron James
dek: Real Madrid's Liga ACB MVP has real NBA interest from Golden State and Cleveland, but ESPN reports both are waiting to see where LeBron James lands before committing to anyone else
body: Mario Hezonja spent six years rebuilding a reputation the NBA had all but written off, turning himself back into one of the EuroLeague's most dangerous forwards at Real Madrid. Now, with genuine NBA suitors circling again, his comeback has stalled for a reason that has nothing to do with him at all: LeBron James still hasn't decided where he's playing next season.

ONE reports that the Croatian, once the fifth overall pick of the 2015 draft, has interest from multiple NBA teams, but that Golden State and Cleveland are effectively sitting on their hands until James resolves his own free agency. Both clubs see Hezonja as a fallback wing option rather than a priority, which leaves him waiting on a decision that isn't his to make.

ESPN's Shams Charania, speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, said Hezonja "is coming from the EuroLeague back to the NBA" but "cannot choose his destination until James makes his free-agency decision." When a co-host joked that Hezonja had been stuck at the airport for three weeks "like Tom Hanks" in The Terminal, Charania simply replied, "Exactly."

It is a strange twist for a player once regarded as one of the bigger busts of his draft class. Orlando took Hezonja fifth overall in 2015 ahead of players like Devin Booker, and across 330 NBA games with the Magic, Knicks and Trail Blazers he managed only 6.9 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists a game before leaving the league in 2020.

Europe is where he rebuilt himself. Since joining Real Madrid for the 2022–23 season, Hezonja has grown into one of the continent's most productive scoring wings, and last season he was named Liga ACB MVP while averaging 17.5 points a game on 36.6 percent three-point shooting as Real Madrid reached the EuroLeague final, where they fell to Olympiacos.

That form is precisely why NBA interest has resurfaced. Hebrew outlets Walla Sport and Sport5 reported that Hezonja used an NBA exit clause in his Real Madrid contract, which ran until July 20, to inform the club he intends to leave for a return to the league that once gave up on him.

The problem is timing. Golden State and Cleveland are both among LeBron James's finalists as he weighs his next move, alongside teams such as Miami and Philadelphia, and neither wants to commit a roster spot or salary-cap flexibility to Hezonja until they know whether they've landed the 41-year-old four-time champion.

James declined his player option with Cleveland to enter free agency, and ESPN has reported that all interested teams have now made their final pitches. Charania has said James is "getting closer and closer" to a decision, though no firm timetable has been set, leaving the entire market — Hezonja included — in a holding pattern.

For a player who once seemed to have exhausted his NBA chances, the frustration is almost a good problem to have. Hezonja rebuilt his career from scratch in Europe and earned his way back to the league's doorstep — he is simply discovering that getting through it now depends on somebody else's phone call.

title: Maccabi Haifa land Wolves defender Nigel Lonwijk on a three-year deal
dek: The Surinamese-Dutch centre-back, who spent last season on loan at Luton Town, becomes the champions' fifth summer arrival as they refresh their back line before the new campaign.
body: Maccabi Haifa have put the finishing touches on the defensive reinforcement they spent the summer chasing, confirming the signing of centre-back Nigel Lonwijk from Wolverhampton Wanderers on a three-year contract, ONE reports.
The 23-year-old underwent a medical in Haifa before putting pen to paper, closing out a pursuit that Israeli outlets had been tracking closely for the past week as talks with Wolves progressed.

Lonwijk is a Surinamese-Dutch defender who came through PSV Eindhoven's academy before Wolves signed him in 2020. Since then he has been farmed out on a string of loans in the English lower divisions, at Huddersfield Town, Wycombe Wanderers and Plymouth Argyle, where he won the League One title in 2022/23.

Last season he was loaned to Luton Town in League One, making 45 appearances and scoring twice while picking up nine yellow cards. Standing 1.90 metres, he is primarily a centre-back but has also been used at right-back, giving Maccabi Haifa a defender who can slot into a back three or a back four.

ONE puts the transfer fee to Wolves at around €600,000, though other Israeli reports, including Israel Hayom, have cited a slightly lower figure closer to half a million euros. His salary in Haifa is projected at roughly €400,000 a season, according to Sport5 and Walla Sport.

Lonwijk becomes Maccabi Haifa's fifth permanent signing of the summer window, following the arrivals of Yair Mordechai, Wanderson, Omri Glazer and Andrea Novakovic, as the club continues to rebuild around Frenkie de Jong's former youth coach's core group ahead of a season that will include Champions League qualifying football.

The addition addresses a defensive department that has seen turnover this summer, with the club keen to add height, physicality and versatility at the back rather than relying solely on returning faces.

Maccabi Haifa are expected to formally unveil Lonwijk in the coming days, with pre-season friendlies giving new manager and staff an early look at how he fits alongside the club's existing centre-back pairing.

title: Dolev Haziza set to sign for Maccabi Netanya, ending six-year Haifa stay
dek: The attacking midfielder is due to complete a two-year deal on Thursday after Maccabi Haifa agreed to release him from a contract that ran through 2027, ONE reports.
body: Dolev Haziza is due at Maccabi Netanya's training ground on Thursday to put pen to paper on a two-year contract, ONE reports, ending a six-year association with Maccabi Haifa that brought three championships and the captain's armband.

The move had been all but agreed for days, with the sides said to be waiting only for the conclusion of Tisha B'Av before finalising paperwork and staging a formal unveiling. Negotiations reportedly ran late into the night beforehand as the last details were ironed out.

The 31-year-old attacking midfielder joined Haifa from Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv in 2019 and became one of the club's most reliable attacking outlets over the following seasons, contributing goals and assists from wide areas and through the middle. He scored six times in 29 appearances last season alone, according to Ynet.

His Haifa exit was set in motion when manager Barak Bakhar indicated Haziza no longer figured in his plans, despite the player still holding a contract with the club through the summer of 2027. He did not take part in Haifa's pre-season training camp while the move to Netanya was worked out.
As part of the exit, Maccabi Haifa agreed to compensate Haziza for tearing up the remaining year of his deal, with Sport1 (Maariv) and Walla Sport both reporting a payout of roughly €120,000.

ONE reports that Maccabi Netanya will cover approximately ₪80,000 net per month of Haziza's wages under the new deal — a package the club has structured as it builds toward a more competitive season under manager Roni Levi.

The signing represents Maccabi Netanya's sixth addition of the transfer window, part of a recruitment push overseen by general manager Gil Lev under owner Ross Kestin's Aliyah Capital Partners ownership group, which took control of the club last year.

For Haifa, it marks the end of an era for a player who made 75 senior appearances, scored 14 goals and added 14 assists across his time at the club, winning three Israeli championships along the way before losing his place in Bakhar's squad plans.

title: Hapoel Petah Tikva optimistic over Arroyo loan as Zrihan emerges as target
dek: The club expects Shakhtar Donetsk to sign off on a loan for Bolivian defender Diego Arroyo, while it awaits a compensation ruling over Rishon LeZion's Roy Zrihan ahead of Saturday's Toto Cup derby with Maccabi Petah Tikva.

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva's pursuit of Bolivian defender Diego Arroyo is entering its final stretch, with the club voicing confidence that Shakhtar Donetsk will complete the paperwork on a loan move in the coming days, ONE reported Friday.

According to the report, the loan conditions between the two clubs have already been agreed in principle. What remains is for the Ukrainian side to sign off formally — a step Hapoel Petah Tikva are said to be optimistic will happen shortly.

Arroyo, 22, joined Shakhtar from Bolívar of Bolivia in February 2025 in a deal reported at roughly a million dollars, one of the most expensive transfers involving a Bolivian player. He has made only limited appearances for the Ukrainian club since, making a loan spell in Israel a plausible next step in his development.

The club is also working a second defensive target, ONE reports: Roy Zrihan, a product of Hapoel Rishon LeZion's academy who signed a five-year contract there. Hapoel Petah Tikva are said to be waiting on a compensation committee to rule on his transfer status before they can move the deal forward.

Coach Omer Peretz has been trimming his preseason squad in the meantime, releasing several trialists over recent days. Of those still involved, forward candidates Omer Korsia and Majed Dahleh and defender Ido Ben Zaev are not expected to feature in this weekend's fixture.
New forward signing Klay, who arrived on Tuesday, trained with the squad for the first time on Thursday and is tipped to be among the substitutes rather than start.
In defense, Alex Musonda's injury absence means Israeli is set to line up alongside Uriel Dagni at the back.

The squad business comes ahead of Saturday's opening round of the Toto Cup, when Hapoel Petah Tikva host newly promoted city rivals Maccabi Petah Tikva at HaMoshava Stadium in a 20:30 kickoff. An open training session was held Friday morning, with hundreds of fans reported in attendance.

It is the first meeting between the two Petah Tikva clubs in two and a half years; both are now set to face off twice more in Ligat Ha'al proper, once Maccabi Petah Tikva's promotion to the top flight takes effect in December and again in February. For Hapoel, the derby serves as an early gauge of a squad rebuilt around a top-flight playoff return last season — the club's first in two decades.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv stun Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0 to open European campaign
dek: Sayed Abu Farchi scored twice as Kenny Miller's side put one foot in the Europa League third qualifying round with a rout in Moldova.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv could hardly have asked for a better opening statement to their European season, taking apart Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0 away in Moldova in the first leg of their Europa League second qualifying round tie on Thursday night.

The final score line, delivered against a club UEFA rank among the strongest in the qualifying draw and who had not conceded in their previous two European outings this summer, left little doubt about which side controlled the tie.

Sayed Abu Farchi, the 20-year-old striker who has pushed his way into the first-team picture over the past year, scored twice - a fifth-minute header from Ido Shahar's cross to open the scoring, and a 74th-minute penalty to make it 4-0.
Dor Peretz doubled Maccabi's lead in the 29th minute, Sagiv Yehezkel struck early in the second half to make it 3-0, and Issouf Sissokho completed the rout in the 78th minute.

Kenny Miller, the former Scotland striker in his first season as Maccabi's head coach, had made clear before kick-off that Europe was not a box-ticking exercise for a club of Maccabi's stature. "When you represent a big club, competing in Europe is essential - the expectation is to reach the group stage," he said in the buildup, according to the Jerusalem Post.
Club officials, quoted by ONE, called the result "a very significant moment" - winning 5-0 away in Europe in only the team's second competitive match of the season.

The win arrives on the back of a strong run of form: Maccabi lifted the State Cup in May and beat Hapoel Beersheba 3-1 in the Super Cup before this trip to Moldova, with Miller sticking to a similar starting XI throughout.

It was not entirely straightforward off the pitch. Christian Blitz, who had come on as a second-half substitute after returning from injury, was forced off again shortly afterwards and left the pitch visibly upset, a fresh fitness concern for the club to manage.

The second leg is scheduled for next Thursday, July 30, with Maccabi again playing their "home" fixture in Batumi, Georgia rather than at Bloomfield Stadium - a continuation of the away-from-home arrangement Israeli clubs have used for European fixtures amid the ongoing security situation.

A first-leg cushion of this size makes Maccabi firm favourites to advance to the third qualifying round, where they would face the winner of Qarabag's tie with CSKA Sofia; a slip in the second leg would send them instead into the Europa Conference League qualifying path.

title: Panathinaikos closing in on Kings Kangwa transfer from Hapoel Beer Sheva, Greek media report
dek: The Zambian international's move to Athens edges nearer as Panathinaikos reportedly agree a package worth around €4 million, pushing AEK Athens out of the race.
body: Hapoel Beer Sheva are set to lose one of the players who powered their title-winning season, with Greek media reporting on Friday that Panathinaikos are closing in on a deal for Zambian international Kings Kangwa. ONE reports the move could be finalised within days.

According to the report, Panathinaikos' offer — worth about €3.8 million plus performance-related add-ons — meets Hapoel's asking price, and the 27-year-old is keen on the switch to Athens and an improved contract.
Greek outlet Sport24 puts the total package higher still, at roughly €4.5 million once bonuses are included, a proposal it says comfortably tops what city rivals AEK Athens had been offering.

AEK had been tracking Kangwa for months as a possible replacement for Orbelín Pineda and reportedly raised their bid to around €4 million, but pulled out of the race after Hapoel Beer Sheva refused to release him before this summer's Champions League qualifying rounds — games AEK needed him free to miss.

Panathinaikos' interest is not new. Gazzetta reports the Greens made first contact back in May and had already reached an informal understanding with the player, but held off pushing the deal through until their managerial situation was settled.

That piece fell into place when Jacob Neestrup was confirmed as Panathinaikos' new head coach in late May, succeeding Rafa Benítez. The Danish coach has since signed off on the Kangwa signing, with sporting director Stefanos Koutoulis leading the negotiations with Beer Sheva.
Kangwa is no bit-part squad player. A regular for Zambia with 46 caps and seven goals, he has represented the Chipolopolo at the last two Africa Cup of Nations tournaments, in 2023 and 2025.

His route to Israel has taken in Zambian side Happy Hearts, Buildcon, three seasons at Arsenal Tula in Russia and two years at Red Star Belgrade, where he won the Serbian SuperLiga and Serbian Cup double in 2022-23, before a loan spell in Belgium with Kortrijk preceded his return to Hapoel Beer Sheva in 2024.

Back in Beer Sheva colours, he has been central to a golden run: the club's 2025-26 Israeli Premier League title, the 2024-25 State Cup and the 2025 Super Cup all came with Kangwa a regular fixture in the side.

Nothing has been confirmed by either club as of Friday, and the figures still come from Greek reporting rather than official statements — but with the player pushing for the move and Panathinaikos' offer said to match Hapoel's valuation, the transfer appears to be edging toward completion.

title: Maccabi Haifa give Lonwijk first taste of training as Tsunami is named for the derby
dek: New defender Nigel Lonwijk joined his Maccabi Haifa teammates for the first time on the sidelines of a session, while Brazilian left-back Wanderson 'Tsunami' has been included in the squad for Saturday's Toto Cup derby against Hapoel Haifa.

body: Barak Bachar's Maccabi Haifa returned to the Kfar Galim training ground on Thursday with two new faces on view for very different reasons — one working alone on the sidelines, the other already being fitted into the squad for Saturday's derby, ONE reports.

Nigel Lonwijk, the Dutch-Surinamese defender arriving from Wolverhampton Wanderers, took part in his first session with his new teammates, but only in supervised running drills away from the main group. Sport5 and Sport1 reported Haifa had agreed a fee of around €500,000 with Wolves for the 23-year-old, who has had loan spells at Fortuna Sittard, Plymouth Argyle, Grasshopper Club Zürich, Wycombe Wanderers, Huddersfield Town and Luton Town since leaving PSV Eindhoven's academy for Wolverhampton in 2020.

The move had not been officially announced by Maccabi Haifa at the time of the report, and ONE says Lonwijk will not be considered for Saturday's Toto Cup opener given he only landed in Israel this week and is still completing his medical before putting pen to paper.

There was a more advanced case in the same session. Wanderson, the Brazilian left-back known throughout his career as 'Tsunami,' was named in Bachar's squad for the derby. Maccabi Haifa confirmed on July 19 that the 30-year-old, previously of Botafogo-PB and Cuiabá among other Brazilian clubs, had signed a two-year contract after passing his medical.

ONE reports Tsunami is a contender to feature from the opening whistle, either at left-back or as a third central defender, depending on how Bachar chooses to set up his back line against a Hapoel Haifa side eager to spoil the champions' season launch.

Saturday's Toto Cup Al fixture at Sammy Ofer Stadium doubles as the traditional Haifa derby and marks the official start of Maccabi Haifa's 2026/27 campaign — a fixture that rarely lacks needle regardless of the competition's lower stakes.
Not every regular was present on Thursday. Defenders Yarin Levi and Zohar Zaseno sat out the session while observing the Tisha B'Av fast, according to ONE's report from the training ground.
In goal, Omri Glazer is expected to continue as Bachar's first choice, with Gad Amos, who arrived from Tiberias, deputising as his backup heading into the derby.

For Bachar, Saturday offers the first live look at how his rebuilt back line functions under pressure. Tsunami's introduction is likely to say more about the manager's derby-day thinking than the still-settling Lonwijk, whose full debut looks a matter of when rather than if once his transfer is completed.

title: Bnei Eilat's new owners vow to climb a league every season
dek: The Red Sea club's fresh ownership group has put in 1 million shekels and installed Kobi Refua as sporting director, saying the target is the national league within three to four years.
body: Bnei Eilat's new owners are not shy about the scale of their ambition. Speaking on ONE's Sicha Hayom programme, the trio behind the club's takeover — known by the names Dodo, Nelly and Tory — said their aim is simple to state and brutal to execute: win promotion every single season until Bnei Eilat reach the national league.

The takeover itself began almost by accident. The group had acquired a business interest in Eilat and initially planned only to sponsor the club from the sidelines. It was the city's mayor, they said, who pushed them to go further and take full control of the operation instead of merely writing cheques from a distance.

Since then they have put roughly 1 million shekels into the project, a serious sum for a club playing in Liga Bet, the fourth tier of Israeli football and two full divisions below the Ligat Ha'al summit.

The most significant move so far has been off the pitch. Kobi Refua, a coach with senior experience at Hapoel Tel Aviv, Bnei Yehuda and Ironi Kiryat Shmona, has been brought in as sporting director with sweeping authority over football matters, including the choice of head coach. The owners describe him as the figure the entire project now runs through.

Eilat's football history offers a cautionary backdrop. The city's teams have repeatedly found Liga Alef, the tier directly above, a difficult place to survive — Bnei Eilat's own best campaign, a third-place finish in 2010-11 that carried them into the promotion playoffs, remains the high-water mark from a club founded only in 2006. The new owners say they are alive to that record but insist they have assembled, in their words, a Liga Bet squad built specifically to win Liga Alef promotion fights rather than merely reach the division and stall there.

The transfer business backs up the rhetoric. Striker Gil Yitzhak, who came through the Beitar Jerusalem academy before spells including Maccabi Jaffa, has signed for what Sport5 reported as a historic fee by the club's standards, on terms said to be worth around 450,000 shekels for the season — well above what a fourth-tier side would typically pay.
Yitzhak's deal is also understood to carry a goals-based bonus, though the owners have not disclosed the figure attached to it.
Alongside him, midfielder Gadi Kanyuk arrives after time at Hapoel Haifa, giving Refua's rebuilt squad experience from considerably higher up the pyramid than Liga Bet football usually attracts.
The ownership group has pointed to the template set by Alon Barak's earlier stint building Bnei Eilat as the model they want to replicate and improve on.

None of it guarantees anything on the pitch — Liga Bet is unforgiving and the step up to Liga Alef has broken bigger Eilat projects before. But with money, a recognised sporting director and a three-to-four-year clock now running, Bnei Eilat's new owners have at least made clear there will be no quiet, incremental version of this plan.
