title: Mbappé reportedly lobbying Olise to join him at Real Madrid
dek: The France captain has told Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez he has convinced Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise to make the move to the Bernabéu, ONE reports — though Bayern insist their man isn't going anywhere.

verificationSources.label: Bavarian Football Works — Bild report roundup

body: Kylian Mbappé has apparently decided that landing Real Madrid's next Galáctico is partly his job too. According to Germany's Bild, relayed by ONE, the France captain has personally worked on France teammate Michael Olise to push the Bayern Munich winger toward the Bernabéu — and has already told club president Florentino Pérez that he believes he has succeeded.

The report describes a sustained charm offensive built around the two players' close bond in the France squad. Mbappé is said to have talked up life in Madrid to Olise directly — the football project, but also the lifestyle, from the restaurants to the climate — while assuring him that Real Madrid genuinely want him.

The timing lines up with France's summer at the World Cup. Les Bleus were eliminated in the semi-finals on July 14, beaten 2-0 by Spain, and Bild's report ties Olise's hardened resolve to leave Bayern directly to that exit — with the 24-year-old reportedly concluding his odds of winning the Champions League are considerably better in Madrid than in Munich.

Pérez has made no secret of wanting a marquee addition since his re-election as Real Madrid president, and Olise has emerged as a prime target, with Spanish reports over recent weeks floating a bid in the region of €220 million for the winger. Whether Real actually go that high remains to be seen, but the interest from the Bernabéu is not in doubt.

Bayern's position is the opposite of accommodating. The club has explicitly rejected the idea of selling Olise, regarding him as a core piece of their squad rather than a player to be cashed in on, and — according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano — are working on a new and improved contract to tie him down rather than field offers.

Olise signed for Bayern from Crystal Palace in the summer of 2024 for a fee of around €53 million and has since become one of the Bundesliga's most productive wide players. He remains under contract in Munich until 2029, with no release clause, which gives Bayern real leverage even against a club of Real Madrid's stature.

Bild's report does add a caveat: Olise, while telling French teammates of his wish to leave, is not expected to force the issue or turn himself into a problem for Bayern this summer. Sport Bild's reporting suggests any deal would only move if Olise himself goes to both clubs' hierarchies and makes his desire to leave explicit.

title: Fulham chase Real Madrid pair García and Mastantuono as Arbeloa raids old club
dek: New Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa wants to reunite with two players from his brief spell in Madrid — a permanent deal for striker Gonzalo García and a season-long loan for teenage sensation Franco Mastantuono, according to a report from ONE.
body: Fulham have opened talks with Real Madrid over two players from Álvaro Arbeloa's old dressing room, the Israeli outlet ONE reports — a permanent move for young striker Gonzalo García and a season-long loan for Argentine playmaker Franco Mastantuono.

Arbeloa, unveiled as Fulham head coach on July 8 after Marco Silva departed for Benfica, knows both players well. He took charge of Real Madrid Castilla in May 2025, then found himself running the senior side on an interim basis after Xabi Alonso's exit in January, before José Mourinho arrived to take permanent control. García broke through under him at Castilla, while Mastantuono made his early Real Madrid appearances during that same stretch.

García, 22, is a product of Real Madrid's academy who forced his way into the first-team picture last season, contributing to the club's Champions League and LaLiga triumphs along the way. Fulham are preparing a formal offer and see him as an attacking reinforcement for the new Premier League campaign.

Real Madrid are open to selling him — reports in Spain suggest the club had planned for García to leave even before Mourinho's arrival — but want to protect their long-term interest, either through a buy-back clause or a sell-on percentage, rather than a clean-break sale.
Mourinho, for his part, wants to run the rule over García during preseason training before Real Madrid sign off on any exit, meaning a final answer on his future is unlikely to arrive immediately.

Mastantuono is a different proposition: at 18, he is one of the most closely guarded prospects in Madrid. He joined from River Plate in 2025 after becoming Argentina's youngest ever full international, and Real Madrid regard him as part of their long-term core rather than a player to be sold.

That is why any move for the winger would be a loan rather than a permanent departure, with the fee structure still to be worked out and Real Madrid, according to some reports, still reluctant to let him leave at all this window. Fulham are pushing for the arrangement to include no option to buy attached, in line with what Madrid have indicated they will accept.

Fulham are not alone in the chase — Tottenham have also made contact with Real Madrid to sound out the conditions of a possible Mastantuono loan, adding urgency to Arbeloa's efforts to get a deal wrapped up quickly.

Nothing is close to signed on either front. Both moves hinge on Mourinho's preseason evaluations in Madrid and on face-to-face talks between the manager and the two players before Real Madrid's board engages formally with Fulham's proposals.

body: Hapoel Haifa is going back to a forward it already knows well. ONE reports that coach Haim Silves has identified William Agada, the Nigerian striker who once wore the club's shirt on loan, as one of his top targets to reinforce the attack this summer, and that the club is now in negotiations to bring him back to the Carmel.

The pursuit is a reunion of sorts. Agada spent the 2020/21 season on loan at Hapoel Haifa from Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem, and it was there, still only 21, that he first showed the finishing that would define his career, scoring regularly for a Silves side that leaned on him up front.

From Haifa he returned to Jerusalem, where he was the club's top scorer in 2021/22 with eight league goals as Hapoel Jerusalem fought to stay in the Israeli Premier League. Across four seasons in Israeli football, split between Jerusalem and the Haifa loan spell, he scored 37 league goals - a return that eventually carried him out of the country altogether.

Sporting Kansas City signed Agada from Hapoel Jerusalem in July 2022, and he quickly became a fixture in MLS, twice finishing as the club's top scorer. He moved on to Real Salt Lake in 2025 before a further switch this past January to Real Zaragoza in Spain's second division, where he is currently under contract through the end of the season.

That contract situation is why ONE frames Agada as "relatively expensive" for Hapoel Haifa to land - any deal now would likely mean negotiating a fee, or a loan, with a European club rather than a free pickup. According to the report, agent Yoav Katz is handling the talks on Agada's behalf.

If completed, the move would give Silves a genuine second scoring threat alongside Alon Torgeman, pairing a proven Israeli Premier League finisher with a forward who already knows the dressing room, the coach and, by his own account from his first Haifa spell, the feeling of being trusted as a starter.

Agada has barely featured for Zaragoza since his January arrival, and a summer switch back to a league where he has a track record of goals would not be unprecedented for a player looking to rebuild his minutes. title: Winner's odds make Maccabi Tel Aviv the only Israeli favourite tonight

body: Three Israeli clubs kick off their European campaigns on the same evening, and according to the odds Winner has put up for the night, only one of them is expected to win.

ONE reports that the bookmaker prices Maccabi Tel Aviv as clear favourites for their trip to Sheriff Tiraspol in the Europa League second qualifying round, at odds of 2.05 against 2.90 for the Moldovan champions. It is a different story for the other two: Beitar Jerusalem, away to AEK Larnaca in the Conference League, are underdogs at 3.05 with the Cypriots priced at 1.95, and Hapoel Tel Aviv are underdogs even at home, at 2.85 against 2.00 for Bulgarian side Ludogorets Razgrad.
All three are first legs of second qualifying round ties, played on Thursday July 23, with the second legs following a week later on July 30.

Maccabi arrive in Tiraspol with genuine momentum. They lifted the Israeli Super Cup on July 16 with a 3-1 win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva, and this is their fourth straight season in continental competition, a run of European experience Sheriff — who needed a 1-0 win at Aluminij just to survive the first qualifying round — cannot match. Win or lose over the two legs, the tie's outcome already has a route mapped out: the winner meets whoever comes through Qarabağ against CSKA Sofia in the Europa League third qualifying round, while the loser drops into the Conference League to face the loser of St Gallen against Benfica.

Beitar Jerusalem head to the AEK Arena in Larnaca off the back of a penalty-shootout defeat to Hapoel Tel Aviv in the Toto Cup, and Winner's odds reflect a club still finding its footing against a Cypriot side with recent continental pedigree.

Hapoel Tel Aviv, by contrast, arrive at Bloomfield Stadium unbeaten in six matches, but that hasn't been enough to make them favourites against Ludogorets, who are chasing a European group-stage berth for an eleventh consecutive season. The fixture is a landmark one regardless of the result: it is Hapoel's first appearance in European competition since a 2014-15 Europa League qualifying exit to Astana, and their first-ever entry into the Conference League.

None of this amounts to a prediction — Winner's odds are a market snapshot, not a result, and two-legged qualifying ties have a habit of flipping on a single away goal or a red card. But the numbers do capture where Israeli football's three European entrants stand on paper tonight: one clear favourite, and two clubs being asked to prove the bookmakers wrong.

title: LeBron James stalls free agency, banking on a trade for Irving or Davis
dek: Three weeks after leaving the Lakers, the 41-year-old still hasn't picked his next team — reportedly because he's waiting to see if a suitor can first engineer a reunion with Kyrie Irving or Anthony Davis.
body: More than three weeks into free agency, LeBron James still hasn't said where he's playing next season — and according to a report picked up by ONE, that's by design. The 41-year-old is deliberately slow-playing his decision, several outlets now report, in the hope that one of his suitors can first pull off a trade for either Kyrie Irving or Anthony Davis.

James left the Lakers after eight seasons once the NBA's free-agency negotiating window opened on June 30, ending an era in which he restored the franchise to relevance but never recaptured the 2020 championship high with Davis at his side. Since then, the league's most closely watched free agent has offered almost nothing about his thinking beyond hints that a decision is coming.

Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor reported this week that James is holding off specifically to see whether a team courting him can also engineer a reunion with Irving or Davis — the two co-stars who delivered two of his four championships. Irving helped end Cleveland's 52-year title drought in 2016; Davis partnered him for the bubble title with the Lakers in 2020.

Neither reunion looks straightforward. Irving, now with the Dallas Mavericks, is still working back from the torn ACL that ended his 2024-25 season early, and Dallas has given no indication it intends to move him. Davis, dealt to Washington in the blockbuster that sent Luka Dončić to the Lakers, still has two years and roughly $120 million left on his contract — an expensive, complicated piece for any team to pry loose from the rebuilding Wizards.

That hasn't stopped teams from trying to make the numbers work anyway. Reports have floated Cleveland exploring a package built around James Harden to bring Irving back and effectively recreate the Cavaliers' 2016 title nucleus — LeBron, Irving and Kevin Love reborn as a 2026 vintage.

Golden State's interest runs in a similar direction. The Warriors have long coveted pairing James with Stephen Curry, and Walla Sport reports the club has also been working to land Davis from Washington as part of the same push — an attempt to build a roster deep enough to persuade James that the fit, not just the name recognition, is real.

Miami and Philadelphia round out the group most consistently named as finalists, with Jimmy Butler's Heat and a 76ers team still built around Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey both making their pitches. Neither has been linked to an Irving or Davis trade, but both are seen as offering a clearer, ready-made path to contention.

Then there's the long shot with the loudest pitch. Minnesota's Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball have personally phoned James to recruit him to the Timberwolves, according to reporting picked up widely in the American press — even though Edwards has separately admitted Minnesota isn't among the three teams James is said to be seriously considering. The calls say less about Minnesota's chances than about how badly rival locker rooms want to be the ones to land him.

Through it all, James's camp is projecting patience rather than urgency. His longtime agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, has said simply: "We're not going to be rushed." It's a notably different posture from the made-for-television 'Decision' era of James's career — no cameras, no fixed date, just a 41-year-old waiting to see what his former teammates' teams do first.

The stakes for whichever franchise wins him are not symbolic. James averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists for the Lakers last season, still an every-night contributor entering what would be his 24th NBA campaign. For four teams, and perhaps a fifth making noise from the outside, that production is worth the wait — even if the trade James is reportedly hoping for never actually happens.

title: Al-Hilal make surprise move for Dembélé as PSG contract talks stall
dek: Saudi champions Al-Hilal have quietly reached out to Ousmane Dembélé's camp as the Ballon d'Or winner's stalled renewal talks with PSG threaten to collapse, according to reports.
body: Ousmane Dembélé's contract standoff with Paris Saint-Germain has picked up an unexpected suitor. Sport1 reports that Al-Hilal have made preliminary contact with the French forward's representatives, opening the door to a move that would blow up months of stop-start renewal talks in Paris.

The report, citing French journalist Sacha Tavolieri, says Al-Hilal have not yet approached PSG directly. The Saudi club is first sounding out whether Dembélé himself would even consider a move to the Saudi Pro League before deciding whether to make a formal offer to the French champions.

The timing is pointed. Dembélé, who won the 2025 Ballon d'Or after inspiring PSG's continental treble under Luis Enrique, has been locked in slow-moving contract talks with the club for months. His current deal runs to June 2028, but PSG have been pushing to extend it and remove any uncertainty over their biggest star.

The gap between the two sides has been the sticking point. PSG have offered around €30 million a year over a new three-year deal, while Dembélé's camp has been seeking closer to €60 million annually — roughly double his current salary, which already makes him the club's highest earner.

Al-Hilal, bankrolled by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, have made no secret of their ambition to keep landing marquee attacking talent. They have already signed winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham United this summer and see a player of Dembélé's stature as the kind of statement addition that would elevate the club's profile further.

For now, according to the report, Al-Hilal are holding off on any approach to PSG until they get a clearer signal from Dembélé's side that he would be open to the move. Only then would talks with the French club begin in earnest.

PSG, for their part, are not expected to entertain a sale easily. Having built their recent success around Dembélé and repeatedly stated their intention to tie him down long-term, the club has shown no appetite to let its Ballon d'Or winner leave while a new contract is still, at least in theory, on the table.

Still, the fact that a rival club felt it worth testing the waters underlines how far apart PSG and Dembélé's camp remain on salary. If the renewal talks in Paris do collapse, Sport1's report suggests Al-Hilal would be ready to move quickly — and they may not be the only ones watching from the outside.

title: Maccabi Netanya close to loan deal for Sheffield United winger Nwachukwu
dek: The Israeli top-flight club is finalizing terms with Sheffield United for a loan-with-option move for Christian Nwachukwu, a 20-year-old Nigerian winger currently out on loan in Turkey, according to Sport5.
body: Maccabi Netanya are closing in on a deal to bring Nigerian winger Christian Nwachukwu to Israel on loan, with an option to make the move permanent further down the line, Sport5 reports.

Nwachukwu, 20, is Sheffield United property, having been signed by the Championship club from Bulgaria's Botev Plovdiv in February 2025 for a reported fee in the region of €1.2 million on a contract running to the summer of 2027. This past season he was farmed out on loan to Serikspor in Turkey to accumulate first-team minutes.

According to the report, Netanya's American owner Ross Kastin is pushing for exactly this kind of profile — a young, developing talent his club can coach up and potentially sell on for a profit, rather than an established, expensive veteran. Kastin's Aliya Capital Partners took control of the club from longtime owner Eyal Sagal, and his stated strategy since taking over has centered on player trading alongside on-field ambition.

A fleet-footed left-sided winger capable of playing on the right or through the middle, Nwachukwu made his name at Botev Plovdiv, where he was part of the squad that won the Bulgarian Cup and also picked up Europa League experience, before scoring four goals in his breakthrough campaign that persuaded Sheffield United to move for him.

Sport5 reports the deal is being brokered through agent Satio Chachmon, and describes it as close to completion rather than finished — the structure being discussed is a loan with a purchase option, which would let Netanya evaluate Nwachukwu in Ligat Ha'al before committing to a permanent transfer fee.

The move would fit the pattern of Netanya's summer rebuild under Kastin's ownership, with the club also said to be working on bringing in a defender and monitoring the futures of players already on the books, including forward Aziz Aouatrah, with a replacement plan in place should he depart.

Separately, Sport5 notes that goalkeeper Omer Niron has returned unexpectedly to full training after completing rehabilitation from the ankle injury that ended his season early, a development the outlet frames as a signal to clubs who had been circling him as Netanya's number one is otherwise occupied.

Nothing is signed yet, and the loan-with-option structure still needs to be finalized between the two clubs, but if it goes through, Nwachukwu would become the latest young overseas prospect to test himself in Israeli football before, potentially, moving back up the ladder in Europe.

title: Tiberias warns it will field an all-youth side if hit with any further points deduction
dek: Owner Arie Kalmanzon calls a withdrawn tribunal petition "a meaningful and positive step," but a senior club official says Ironi Tiberias will turn to its academy and let unhappy players go if the Israel Football Association docks even one more point over the double-contracts affair.
body: Ironi Tiberias have issued a blunt warning to Israeli football's disciplinary establishment: take even one more point off the club over the so-called double-contracts affair, and Ligat Ha'al will be watching an entirely youth-led side for the rest of the season. "If they deduct even one point from us, we'll go up with youth players," a senior club official said this week, according to Sport5. "We'll turn it into an economic year, and any player who wants to leave will be released."

The threat followed a hearing on Wednesday before the Israel Football Association's supreme disciplinary tribunal, where Tiberias had petitioned over the ongoing proceedings tied to its handling of player contracts. The judges declined to grant the dismissal the club's petition sought, siding instead with the federation's prosecutor.

Tiberias then withdrew the petition altogether — but owner Arie Kalmanzon insisted the club still came away encouraged, describing assurances he said were given by the prosecution's lawyer during the session. "The judges discussed the petition but refused to dismiss it outright, as the prosecutor had asked," Kalmanzon said, according to Sport5. "We withdrew it. We felt a meaningful and positive step had been taken."

The case dates back to a plea agreement approved by the disciplinary tribunal in April, after Tiberias was found to have signed undisclosed supplementary agreements with players — arrangements that bypassed the league's budget-oversight process, a practice known in Israeli football as "double contracts." That settlement cost the club eight points in the 2025/26 season, a further six points for the current 2026/27 campaign, a fine of 500,000 shekels and a ban on registering new players in the January 2027 transfer window. Former club figure Miki Bitan received a seven-year suspension from football activity over the affair.

Those six points are already gone from Tiberias's ledger before a ball has been kicked in the new Ligat Ha'al season, and this week's hearing raised the prospect of the federation coming back for more. Sport5 did not specify how many additional points are under consideration, only that the club now regards any further deduction as a red line.

The contracts case is not the only disciplinary front the club is fighting. Head coach Eliran Hudeda remains sidelined in a separate matter, after the Israel Anti-Doping Agency and the federation opened an investigation into allegedly excessive saline infusions given to Tiberias players before a match against Ashdod last season — a complaint Ashdod itself filed. Tiberias has maintained the fluids were legal and administered within permitted limits.
With Hudeda unable to work the touchline, the club has turned to Maurice Ozen, the veteran head of its youth department, who has been approved to serve as interim first-team coach for one month.

The squad Ozen inherits for now is already stretched thin. Several players are suspended, the club's foreign-player quota is close to full following the summer arrival of Ivorian midfielder Chris Quacko, and new signing Gal Metuak has yet to be registered to play while his contract paperwork is finalised.

None of it has dented the club's spending ambitions. Tiberias have set a budget of 21 million shekels for the season, three million more than last year, with 13.5 million earmarked for player salaries — a sign the ownership still intends to compete near the top of the table even as it fights the federation on two fronts.

For a club that has spent the close season lurching between tribunal hearings and doping inquiries, the youth-team threat reads as much as a statement of frustration as a genuine tactical plan. But with the disciplinary process still unresolved, Tiberias's hierarchy has made clear it sees a further points penalty as the point at which cooperation ends.

That same settlement cost the club eight points in 2025/26, a 500,000-shekel fine, and a ban on registering new players in the January 2027 window; former club figure Miki Bitan received a seven-year suspension.

title: Abada nets a brace, Baribo strikes late as Blorian tastes first MLS win
dek: Three Israelis were involved across MLS on the same night — Liel Abada scored twice for Charlotte, Tai Baribo salvaged a point for DC United, and new Sporting Kansas City signing Or Blorian started at left-back in a 2-1 win over Minnesota.

source.name: ONE
source.originalTitle: עבדה ובריבו כבשו, ניצחון לבלוריאן וקנזס סיטי

body: MLS returned to full swing on Wednesday night with three different Israelis leaving their mark across three different grounds — a rare cluster of good news for the country's growing contingent in American soccer, even if only one of the three walked away with all three points.

The headline act was Liel Abada. Charlotte FC's Israeli winger scored twice as his side raced into a 2-0 lead over Atlanta United, latching onto a Pep Biel pass to open the scoring before doubling it with a far-post header just before halftime — Charlotte's official channel labelled it simply a 'brace' for the 24-year-old, who has become one of the most reliable attacking outlets in MLS this season.

Atlanta, missing Emmanuel Latte Lath amid transfer talk and starting Fafa Picault in his place, would not go quietly. Elías Báez pulled one back in the 57th minute, and Miguel Almirón completed the comeback with a well-worked equalizer in the 76th, leaving Charlotte to settle for a 2-2 draw at home despite Abada's night.

Across the country, Tai Baribo produced the moment DC United needed at Houston Dynamo. With his side trailing in the club's first match since the FIFA World Cup break, the Israeli forward rose to flick in a header in the 78th minute, converting a centering ball from Nathan Ordaz to make it 1-1 — his ninth goal of the season and enough to salvage a point on the road.

Baribo has been in prolific form since his move from Philadelphia Union to DC United earlier this year, a switch that included scoring against his former club on his debut back in February. His late leveller against Houston kept United unbeaten in the reopening weekend after the international break, in a match that finished 1-1.

The best result of the night for an Israeli belonged to Or Blorian. Sporting Kansas City beat Minnesota United 2-1 at Sporting Park in the club's first home match since the World Cup hiatus, with Dejan Joveljić opening the scoring — his team-leading seventh goal of the campaign, set up by a Manu García interception — before García added a second himself. Devin Padelford's 75th-minute header for Minnesota proved only a consolation.

Blorian started the match at left-back, his second appearance for the club and first since a full debut in a 3-2 defeat at St. Louis City SC the previous week. It marked the Israeli's first taste of victory since arriving in Kansas City.

The 25-year-old central defender joined Sporting KC on a pre-contract in June, agreeing a three-year MLS deal through the 2028-29 season with club options extending to 2030-31. He arrives after spending his entire career in Israel, most recently with Hapoel Be'er Sheva, where he made 186 competitive appearances and contributed two goals and four assists last season.

Blorian, who holds both Israeli and Portuguese citizenship, has four caps for the Israel national team since making his debut in October 2025 and has featured in World Cup qualifying. His move to MLS adds a third Israeli face — alongside Abada and Baribo — to a league that has quietly become a notable landing spot for players from Israel's top flight and beyond.

title: Tel Aviv, 1 May 2004: The night the Final Four broke the scoreboard
dek: Playing a European final on their own floor for the first time, Maccabi Tel Aviv did not just win it — they demolished Skipper Bologna 118-74, the most one-sided championship game the Euroleague had ever seen.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv official archive — 2003-04 Euroleague Final recap

body: For three days at the end of April 2004, Yad Eliyahu Arena — wrapped for the occasion in Nokia's sponsor livery — stopped being just Maccabi Tel Aviv's home gym and became the center of European basketball. The city had won the right to host the Euroleague Final Four, and for the first time a club would get the chance to play for the continent's biggest club prize in front of its own crowd.

Maccabi Elite Tel Aviv, as the team was known under its title sponsorship that season, opened on 29 April with a tense semifinal against CSKA Moscow, the Russian giants who had eliminated Israeli teams in Europe before. Pini Gershon's side pulled away to win 93-82, while in the night's other semifinal Skipper Bologna needed overtime to edge past Montepaschi Siena, 103-102.

That set up a final on 1 May between the two semifinal winners — and it turned into one of the most lopsided nights in the competition's history. Maccabi never trailed. They led 31-13 after the first quarter, extended it to 55-30 by halftime, and were up 80-51 through three periods before running away to a 118-74 final margin: 44 points, the largest winning margin in a Euroleague championship game.

The shooting numbers were almost absurd for a final of this magnitude: 28-of-38 from the field (69 percent), 14-of-23 from three-point range (61 percent), and 20-of-24 at the free-throw line, against 35 rebounds and 31 assists as a team. American guard Anthony Parker, who had returned to Tel Aviv after a stint in the NBA, scored 21 points and was named Final Four MVP. He was backed by David Bluthenthal's 20 points, Šarūnas Jasikevičius's 18 and Israeli forward Tal Burstein's 17.

It was Maccabi's fourth European championship, following the club's breakthrough titles of 1977 and 1981 and its more recent 2001 crown — but the first won at home. Team captain Gur Shelef became the fourth different Maccabi captain to lift the trophy, and Gershon, already a cult figure in Israeli sport, added another chapter to his coaching legend.

The Israeli players on that roster — Burstein, Shelef, Yotam Halperin and Avi Ben-Chimol among them — shared the floor with an international cast that had made Yad Eliyahu Europe's toughest road venue: Parker, Jasikevičius, Bluthenthal, Maceo Baston and Croatian center Nikola Vujčić, who later described walking out to the home crowd's roar as making him feel like his legs were flying beneath him.

The blowout was so complete that with roughly five minutes left and the outcome long decided, several Maccabi starters came off the bench already wearing 'We Are the Champions' T-shirts underneath their warm-ups — a premature bit of celebration that, by one retelling, briefly complicated matters when Gershon needed to make a late substitution and found some of his players already out of uniform.

CSKA Moscow, the beaten semifinalists, salvaged bronze by beating Montepaschi Siena 97-94 in the third-place game, but the tournament's story had already been written on the main court. For a club and a country that measured its place in European basketball by how it fared on other people's floors, winning a final by 44 points at home was less a victory than a coronation.

The following season Maccabi would do it again, beating CSKA Moscow in Moscow to become the first club since 1991 to retain the Euroleague title — but it is the 2004 final, played in front of its own fans on its own hardwood, that is still remembered in Tel Aviv as the night the scoreboard simply gave up.

Gur Shelef became the fourth different captain in club history to lift the Euroleague trophy.

title: Manor Solomon handed surprise start in Tottenham's pre-season opener
dek: The Israeli winger, reportedly told this summer he was not part of Roberto De Zerbi's plans, lined up for Spurs' 1-0 win over MK Dons under the head coach who once managed him at Shakhtar Donetsk.

source.name: Sport5
source.originalTitle: מפתיע: מנור סולומון בהרכב טוטנהאם בהכנה
source.author: Sport5 editorial team

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports match report — Tottenham 1-0 MK Dons

body: Manor Solomon walked out at Hotspur Way on Tuesday in a Tottenham shirt for the first time in longer than anyone at the club seemed to expect, starting on the right wing as Spurs opened their pre-season programme against MK Dons.

Tottenham won 1-0, the game settled by a stunning long-range volley from summer signing Mateus Fernandes. Solomon played the first half before head coach Roberto De Zerbi, who used 21 players across the 90 minutes to run the rule over his squad, took him off along with the rest of the starting group.

The selection itself is the story. Sport5 described it as a surprising inclusion, and Israeli fans reacted with astonishment on social media — several posting question-mark emojis at seeing Solomon's name in the XI at all.

That reaction has context. English reports out of London in recent weeks said De Zerbi had told Solomon directly that he was not part of his plans for the new season and was free to look for a move elsewhere, with Fiorentina — where the winger spent the second half of last season on loan — keen on signing him permanently but reluctant to trigger the reported £8.5 million option-to-buy clause in full.

Solomon addressed the uncertainty himself in comments carried by Israel's Sport1 in recent weeks. "I also know he really appreciates me," he said of De Zerbi, "but the situation at Tottenham is different." The two worked together before either arrived in west London, when De Zerbi coached Solomon at Shakhtar Donetsk.

It has been a difficult stretch in north London for the 26-year-old since his move from Shakhtar. A run of serious injuries repeatedly derailed his chances of becoming a regular contributor, and Tottenham instead sent him out on loan — first for an impressive season-long spell at Leeds United, then, over 2025-26, to Villarreal and Fiorentina.

It was at Fiorentina where Solomon did his most meaningful work, scoring twice in 16 appearances as the Italian club fought off relegation and retained its Serie A status. That form is understood to be behind the club's continued interest in a permanent deal.

De Zerbi's own situation at Tottenham has been extraordinary. He was appointed on 31 March 2026 as the club's third head coach of a chaotic campaign, replacing Igor Tudor, and inherited a squad fighting an unfamiliar battle against relegation.

He pulled it off by the finest of margins. Tottenham secured their Premier League status on the final day of the season with a 1-0 win over Everton, a result that sent local rivals West Ham down to the Championship instead.

Against that backdrop, a coach still shaping his squad for a fresh campaign starting Solomon in a pre-season friendly is being read in Israel as more than a routine rotation — a possible signal that De Zerbi wants a longer look at a player he already knows well, even as his Tottenham future remains unresolved.

title: Maccabi Haifa rated Israel's most valuable club in new Ligat Ha'al rankings
dek: A Sport5 valuation model built for a new pre-season quiz puts Maccabi Haifa just ahead of Maccabi Tel Aviv as the richest club in Israel's top flight, with Hapoel Be'er Sheva a distant third.

verificationSources.label: Sport5: מי הקבוצה ששווה הכי הרבה כסף בליגת העל?

body: Which Ligat Ha'al club is actually worth the most? Sport5 built a new interactive value quiz to make readers guess — and paired it with its own attempt at an answer: a club-by-club financial ranking of Israel's top flight ahead of the new season.
According to Sport5's model, Maccabi Haifa comes out on top, valued at roughly €83.8 million (about ₪300 million).

Maccabi Tel Aviv is close behind in second place, at an estimated €79.85 million (around ₪280 million) — a gap of only a few million euros separating Israel's two biggest clubs from one another, but a far wider one from the rest of the division.
Hapoel Be'er Sheva was rated third, at roughly €39 million (about ₪137 million) — less than half of Maccabi Tel Aviv's figure and under a third of the division-leading Maccabi Haifa number.
Beitar Jerusalem followed in fourth at an estimated €30.6 million (about ₪108 million), with Hapoel Tel Aviv rounding out the top five at roughly €23.6 million (around ₪82 million), Sport5 reported.

To arrive at the figures, Sport5 said its model combined four inputs: each squad's current market value as tracked by Transfermarkt, an estimate of the club's youth academy worth, projected subscriber and membership revenue, and prize money earned from UEFA competitions over the previous five seasons.

Sport5 was careful to frame the numbers as an estimate rather than an audited or legally binding valuation. The outlet noted the model does not account for factors professional buyers would weigh — real estate holdings, sponsorship potential or projected future revenue — the kind of detail that feeds Forbes-style valuations of Europe's biggest clubs.
That comparison is deliberate: Israeli football has no equivalent standardised, published valuation system for its clubs, which is part of why Sport5 said it built the model in the first place.

Turning the numbers into a quiz format — inviting fans to rank the clubs themselves before revealing Sport5's answer — is a familiar pre-season device for the outlet, timed to land as Ligat Ha'al sides return to training and supporters start arguing about where their club really stands, financially as much as on the pitch.

title: Real Madrid eye Rodri as Kroos's long-term successor
dek: With his Manchester City contract entering its final season, Real Madrid have quietly stepped up their pursuit of the Ballon d'Or winner as the man to fill Toni Kroos's old role, Sport5 reports.

verificationSources.label: Get French Football News — citing L'Équipe on Real Madrid's Rodri interest
Sports Mole — Man City 'hopeful' Rodri will sign new deal amid Real Madrid interest

body: Real Madrid have quietly intensified their long-standing pursuit of Rodri, with the club viewing the Manchester City and Spain midfielder as the ideal heir to Toni Kroos's old role in the centre of the pitch, according to a Sport5 report that cites France's L'Équipe and Sky Sports.

Sport5's report describes a low-key meeting between Rodri's representatives and Real Madrid officials — not a formal negotiation, but framed as evidence that the interest has moved beyond casual transfer speculation into something more deliberate.

The timing is not incidental. Rodri's contract at the Etihad Stadium runs only until the summer of 2027, meaning he is about to enter the final season of his current deal — a situation City would rather not let drift, given the risk of losing him for a cut-price fee, or for nothing at all, further down the line.

According to L'Équipe, as relayed by Sport5, City's valuation sits at a minimum of €100 million. Real Madrid, though, believe the shrinking contract works in their favour and are reportedly hopeful of negotiating him down closer to €60 million rather than meeting City's full asking price.
Madrid's approach is said to include an offer of a contract running through 2030 — a deal that would take Rodri, now 30, into his mid-thirties in Real Madrid colours if it were to go through.

There is a personal dimension to the interest, too. Rodri came through Atlético Madrid's academy as a boy, before a spell at Villarreal took him away and a return to Atlético brought him back ahead of his 2019 move to Manchester City. Sport5's report describes him as open, in principle, to a move back to his native Madrid before his career winds down.

Toni Kroos's own voice has added weight to the speculation. Since retiring, the World Cup-winning midfielder has publicly said Real Madrid need a player of Rodri's profile to fill the void he left in central midfield, calling it a role that is close to essential to how the team is supposed to function.

None of this amounts to a deal being close. Sport5 frames the report as the opening stage of what could become a long-running saga rather than an imminent transfer, and Manchester City have given no public indication that their Ballon d'Or winner is for sale at any price this summer.

For now, Rodri remains under contract at City, and separate reporting suggests the club has already put a renewal offer to him — one he has yet to sign, amid the reported interest from Madrid and his own apparent openness to a return to Spain.

title: Finals MVP Iffe Lundberg agrees new Maccabi Tel Aviv deal through 2028
dek: The Danish guard, who inspired Maccabi to the Israeli title and was named Finals MVP, has ended months of on-off talks by re-signing rather than testing the market, Israeli outlets report.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv has locked up the guard who carried them to the Israeli championship. Iffe Lundberg has agreed a new contract with the club, Sport5 and Israel Hayom both report, ending months of stop-start negotiations over his future in yellow.

According to Israel Hayom, the new deal runs for two seasons through the end of 2027-28 at a reported salary of $1.8 million per year, a significant raise on his previous terms. Sport5, which first reported the fresh agreement, adds that the contract carries a club option for a further season.

The two sides had been talking for months, with a financial gap holding up a resolution. Israel Hayom reports that Maccabi improved its offer in recent days, narrowing the difference and allowing the sides to close the deal this week. An official club announcement is still pending.

Lundberg, a 31-year-old Danish international, joined Maccabi during the 2025-26 season under head coach Oded Kattash, arriving from Partizan Belgrade. Sport5 reports he held offers from other clubs but chose to stay, telling teammates he loves the club and Israel and values the status he earned there.

That status was forged on the court. Lundberg averaged 11.0 points and 3.6 assists in the EuroLeague and 10.5 points and 3.8 assists in the domestic regular season, figures he produced despite battling injuries — including a partial Achilles tendon tear that sidelined him for weeks.

He was at his best when it mattered most. In the playoffs he lifted his numbers to 14.1 points, 5.1 assists and 3.3 rebounds a game, and was named Finals MVP as Maccabi beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 3-1 to claim the club's 58th Israeli championship, sealing the series with an 83-79 win in Game 4.

Retaining him now removes one of the more pressing items on Maccabi's off-season to-do list, and keeps a proven EuroLeague-level playmaker in Kattash's rotation as the club, freshly extended through 2029 himself, builds toward next season.

title: Seck signs for Saudi Arabia's Al-Faisaly — but his four years at Maccabi Haifa go unmentioned
dek: The Senegalese defender left Haifa as a title winner and a Champions League regular, yet Al-Faisaly's welcome post skipped his most recent club entirely, ONE reports.
body: Abdoulaye Seck's four seasons at Maccabi Haifa ended quietly on June 30, when his contract simply expired. His arrival at his next club has made more noise than his exit did — not for what was said, but for what wasn't.

The 34-year-old Senegalese centre-back has signed for Al-Faisaly, the Saudi Pro League club promoted to the top flight last season, ONE reports. He joins as a free agent after weeks of searching for his next destination once his Haifa deal ran out.

Al-Faisaly marked the signing with the kind of welcome post clubs typically use to introduce a new arrival, running through the stops of Seck's career to date. According to ONE, one club was conspicuously left off that list: Maccabi Haifa, the team he had just spent four years with.

ONE frames the omission as no accident, suggesting it reflects the strained political relationship between Saudi Arabia and Israel rather than any oversight. Al-Faisaly has not issued a separate statement addressing the gap, and the suggestion should be read as ONE's own reading of the announcement rather than a confirmed club position.
It is a curious footnote to what was, by any football measure, a substantial spell in Israel. Seck arrived in Haifa in 2022 from Belgian side Royal Antwerp and quickly became a fixture at the back.
Across four seasons he made 147 appearances for Maccabi Haifa, scoring 14 goals and adding five assists — a heavy return for a defender.

The trophy haul backs up the numbers: an Israeli championship, a Toto Cup, and European nights that took Haifa into the Champions League group stage and as far as the round of 16 in the Conference League.

Seck's profile away from Haifa is well established too. He was part of Senegal's squad that won the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations, the country's first-ever continental title, and has continued to be a regular for the national team since.

For Al-Faisaly, newly promoted and building a squad for life in Saudi Arabia's top division, Seck's experience and pedigree are the obvious appeal. For Haifa, it is simply the end of an era at centre-back — one that, on the evidence of his new club's own announcement, its opponents in Saudi Arabia would rather not be reminded of.

title: Cubarsí's late block preserved Spain's World Cup crown
dek: Ferran Torres scored the final's only goal, but ONE reports it was a last-ditch, 120th-minute clearance from teenage defender Pau Cubarsí that actually kept Argentina out and sealed Spain's second World Cup.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports - Cubarsí wins FIFA Young Player award
The Analyst (Opta) - why Cubarsí deserved Young Player award

body: Spain's second World Cup title will be remembered, in the record books, for Ferran Torres's extra-time strike against Argentina on July 19 at MetLife Stadium. But according to ONE, the moment that actually protected that lead came nearly fifteen minutes later, deep into a final that very nearly slipped away.

With Spain clinging to a 1-0 lead in the 120th minute, ONE reports that Argentina came desperately close to an equalizer: a cross from Giuliano Simeone found Marcos Senesi arriving at the back post, and only a full-stretch intervention from 19-year-old centre-back Pau Cubarsí kept the ball out — deflected over for a corner with, by ONE's account, as little as 80 centimeters to spare before it crossed the line.

That block, as ONE tells it, was the real title-winning moment of the final — the sort of play that rarely makes a highlight reel headline but decides where a trophy ends up. It has not been independently timestamped by other outlets consulted for this story, though it is consistent with a match that, by every account, went to the wire.

The broader shape of the night is beyond dispute. Torres put Spain ahead in the 106th minute of extra time, and Argentina spent the closing stretch chasing the game a man light: midfielder Enzo Fernández was shown a second yellow card, and with it a red, for a foul on Cubarsí himself in second-half stoppage time — reducing Lionel Messi's side to 10 men before extra time had even begun.

Cubarsí's block, whatever its exact margin, was the culmination of a tournament in which the Barcelona academy graduate barely put a foot wrong. He was named FIFA's Young Player of the Tournament immediately after the final, recognition for a run of performances that made him one of the most talked-about defenders at the World Cup.

The numbers back up the eye test. In the final alone, Cubarsí made more clearances — six — than any other player on the pitch and ranked third among Spain's players for duels won, according to match statistics from the game. Only Golden Ball winner Rodri completed more passes than Cubarsí across the tournament as a whole.

His semi-final display against France was similarly assured: four clearances, two ball recoveries and a 100% record in aerial duels as Spain reached the final. Marking Argentina's Julián Álvarez out of the game in the final itself — the striker managed just a dozen touches — was arguably his signature job of the tournament.

According to figures cited by ONE, Cubarsí's cumulative tournament numbers ran to 31 clearances and 27 successful tackles, with a top recorded speed of 34.1 km/h and more than 66 kilometers covered across Spain's run to the trophy — a workload that underlines how central he was to Luis de la Fuente's defensive setup, though these totals have not been independently corroborated against other statistical trackers.

Former Spain and Mallorca defender Miguel Ángel Nadal, quoted by ONE, was unequivocal about the final clearance: "The way he anticipated the striker and threw himself at the ball was simply brilliant." Pundit Paco Jémez added that Cubarsí is a defender without obvious flaws — "it's very difficult to find a weak point in him... he reads the game exceptionally well," he told the outlet.

Two years ago, Cubarsí was a teenager fighting for a place in Barcelona's first team; on the biggest stage in football, he ended the tournament as the player most credited with keeping the trophy in Spanish hands — Torres's name on the scoresheet, but Cubarsí's boot, ONE argues, the reason the scoreline held.

title: Hezonja's NBA Comeback Hits a Snag as Real Madrid Gains Leverage
dek: Mario Hezonja told Real Madrid this week he was leaving for the NBA, but a reportedly botched exit-clause payment has handed the Spanish club the upper hand in what happens next.
body: Mario Hezonja's stated return to the NBA has run into an unexpected complication, and it is Real Madrid, not the Croatian forward, who now holds the stronger hand in deciding what happens next.

Earlier this week Hezonja informed Real Madrid of his intention to exercise the NBA exit clause in his contract, which runs through 2029. But according to Marca, cited by both ONE and Sportando, he did so without completing the process properly — Spanish league (ACB) rules require the notice to be accompanied simultaneously by payment of the clause, reported at $1 million. Hezonja gave notice; the payment and an official NBA offer have not materialised.

That technicality matters. Because the contractual conditions were not fully met, Real Madrid is now understood to have the right to demand greater compensation for releasing him — or simply to keep him at the club — rather than waving him through on the terms he expected.
The club's negotiating position is reinforced by the fact that it has already brought in Mikael Jantunen as a replacement forward, easing any urgency to let Hezonja leave on favourable terms.
Hezonja's representatives have responded by offering to increase the buyout figure in an attempt to unblock the move, per the reporting, though no resolution has been announced by either side.

Part of the holdup on Hezonja's end appears to be the market itself: NBA interest is real, but reported offers so far have been non-guaranteed contracts rather than the kind of firm deal that would justify triggering — and paying for — the exit clause in full.

There is a fallback scenario if the NBA plan collapses. Hezonja's Real Madrid contract reportedly contains no exit clause for other European clubs, meaning any move within the EuroLeague would require Madrid's cooperation regardless. He has nonetheless been linked as a potential target for clubs including Dubai Basketball and Olympiacos should the NBA route fall through.

The stakes for Hezonja are shaped by the season he just had. The 31-year-old helped Real Madrid reach the 2025-26 EuroLeague Final and was named Liga Endesa's regular-season MVP — form that has revived NBA interest in a player whose earlier stint in the league, after going fifth overall to Orlando in the 2015 draft, never fully took off across stops with the Magic, New York Knicks and Portland Trail Blazers.

For now, nothing is settled. Real Madrid has the leverage, Hezonja wants out, and the coming days should show whether an NBA team is willing to put a guaranteed offer on the table — the one thing that could break the standoff.

title: Manor Solomon back in lilywhite as Tottenham edge MK Dons in pre-season friendly
dek: The Israeli winger played 45 minutes and nearly added a second before Roberto De Zerbi emptied his bench, with Mateus Fernandes' stunning early volley enough to see off newly-promoted MK Dons at Hotspur Way.

verificationSources.label: Tottenham Hotspur official site - match report
Tottenham Hotspur official site - fixture confirmation

body: Manor Solomon pulled on a Tottenham shirt again on Wednesday evening, starting as Roberto De Zerbi's side opened their summer schedule with a 1-0 friendly win over MK Dons at Hotspur Way, according to ONE.

The only goal arrived inside three minutes. Mathys Tel swung in a corner, MK Dons goalkeeper Craig MacGillivray could only punch it back into space, and new signing Mateus Fernandes met it with a first-time volley that cannoned in off the inside of the post — a debut strike to remember for the Portuguese midfielder, signed this summer from West Ham.

Solomon was handed a place in the front line alongside Fernandes, Tel and Dominic Solanke, with Conor Gallagher and Sandro Tonali — another summer arrival, making his own Spurs bow — anchoring midfield. The Israeli winger came closest to a second goal with a slick one-two with Gallagher, only for MacGillivray to block with his legs.

De Zerbi made ten changes at half-time, sending on a second-string XI featuring Martin Dubravka in goal and Richarlison up front, and the club's own account of the match credited MK Dons with forcing more corners and pushing hard for an equaliser late on before Spurs held their lead to the final whistle.

It was a behind-closed-doors run-out against a MK Dons side who go into the new campaign in League One after winning automatic promotion from League Two last season — not the fourth tier as this week's headlines in Israel suggested, but still a heavy step down from Premier League opposition and a useful early test of sharpness for Spurs.

For Solomon, the appearance is another small step in trying to re-establish himself at Tottenham after an unsettled two years away from north London. He spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Leeds United, scoring the goal that clinched the Championship title with a 2-1 win over Plymouth Argyle in May 2025, only to find playing time far harder to come by on a subsequent loan at Villarreal in La Liga.

Tottenham recalled him from Spain in January and sent him straight back out, this time to Fiorentina in Serie A, where he made 16 appearances before that loan ran its course at the end of the season. He is now back in De Zerbi's squad for pre-season with his long-term future still unresolved.

The Israian international's homecoming comes at a club trying to move on from a genuinely miserable campaign. Tottenham survived in the Premier League only on the final day of 2025-26, beating Everton to finish 17th, two points above West Ham, after a run that included six straight defeats and a 15-match winless streak in the league.

De Zerbi himself only arrived at the end of March, appointed on a five-year contract to replace Igor Tudor with Spurs sitting just a point above the relegation zone at the time. Wednesday's win over MK Dons was another building block as he assembles a squad for a season Tottenham fans will hope looks nothing like the last one — with a Premier League opener at Brentford now exactly a month away.

title: Lundberg agrees new multi-year deal to stay at Maccabi Tel Aviv
dek: Weeks after being named Finals MVP, the Danish guard has struck fresh terms with the Israeli champions following months of stop-start talks, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv - original 2024 signing announcement

body: Iffe Lundberg has agreed a new multi-year contract with Maccabi Tel Aviv, ONE reports, ending months of stop-start talks and keeping the Danish guard in yellow weeks after he was named MVP of the Israeli championship series.

According to ONE, the new deal runs two seasons with a mutual option for a third, worth roughly $1.5 million a year. Israel Hayom, reporting separately, put the number closer to $1.8 million annually through the end of the 2028 season — the two outlets agree on the shape of the extension even if the precise salary figure has not been confirmed publicly.

Getting there took time. ONE reports Lundberg's camp initially asked for around $10 million over three seasons, a figure the club rejected outright. Sport5 tracked the back-and-forth as it played out, reporting Maccabi's offer rising in stages — from roughly $1.2 million to about $2 million a year — before the gap finally closed.

Maccabi had every incentive to get a deal done. Lundberg was named MVP of the playoff final series after the club beat rivals Hapoel Tel Aviv to the Israeli championship, and despite arriving as a scoring guard he ended up plugging holes in the frontcourt rotation that had troubled Maccabi for years, according to ONE.

Copenhagen-born and 31, Lundberg joined Maccabi in the summer of 2024 on the back of five EuroLeague seasons with CSKA Moscow, Virtus Bologna and Partizan Belgrade, plus a brief four-game run with the Phoenix Suns in the NBA. His first Tel Aviv contract, worth about $1.3 million, was split with Partizan Belgrade under a co-financing arrangement, with Maccabi covering roughly 60% of the salary.

There is still work to do this off-season. ONE reports Maccabi also needs to resolve the situation around American guard Lonnie Walker IV — whose existing contract carries buyout options — and wants to add further backcourt depth, with the center spot still flagged as the position the club is most eager to strengthen.
For a roster still sorting through those open questions, tying down a Finals MVP through 2028 removes at least one major variable before the new season begins.

title: Miami Heat deny LeBron signing after leaked 'introduction' video sends NBA into frenzy
dek: A since-deleted YouTube link titled a LeBron James introductory press conference for July 27 set off a market-moving frenzy — but the Heat say it was a social-media mistake, not a done deal.
body: For a few frantic minutes on Tuesday, it looked like the biggest domino in NBA free agency had fallen. A YouTube link, briefly live on Miami Heat channels, carried the title "LeBron James Introductory Press Conference | July 27, 2026" — and the internet did what the internet does.

The link led nowhere, an offline stream with no actual footage, but the title alone was enough. Prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi both moved sharply toward a Heat signing before the post vanished as quickly as it appeared, according to ONE and multiple US outlets that tracked the leak in real time.

Miami moved to shut down the speculation almost immediately. A team spokesperson said the video was published by mistake "while the team prepared for all possible scenarios" during the free-agency period — in other words, a placeholder page built in case James does choose Miami, put live too soon.

It is not a small thing that a franchise would already have an introductory press conference page built and ready to go. It suggests the Heat rate their chances of landing James highly enough to prepare the rollout in advance, even as the actual decision remains unmade.

James, 41, is roughly three weeks into a free agency that began when he informed the Los Angeles Lakers he would not return for the 2026-27 season, opening the door to what would be a 24th NBA season elsewhere. He has not signed with anyone.

The Heat are one of three teams widely reported as finalists, alongside the Cleveland Cavaliers and Philadelphia 76ers, with ESPN's Shams Charania among those tracking the process closely and naming Cleveland as the team many around the league consider the frontrunner.

Rich Paul, James's longtime agent, has made clear there is no deadline pressure on his client. "We're not going to be rushed," Paul has said of the process. "It's his choice to make and when he makes the choice, he'll make it."
That patience is exactly what made Tuesday's leak so combustible — in a market starved for a decision, a single mistitled link was enough to move real money and dominate NBA chatter for an afternoon.

For now, nothing has changed: James remains unsigned, the Heat's video was an internal error rather than an announcement, and the only certainty is that whichever team does eventually land him will have earned a much bigger headline than this one.

title: Barda: Hapoel Tel Aviv face 'Champions League-level' test as European exile ends
dek: Twelve years after their last continental campaign, Hapoel Tel Aviv open Conference League qualifying against Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad on Thursday — at a neutral venue in Hungary.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv end a 12-year absence from European competition on Thursday when they open their Conference League second qualifying round tie against Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad — a side head coach Elyaniv Barda rates as good as anything the Champions League has to offer.
"I expect a good match against an excellent opponent, a Champions League-level team," Barda said this week, according to ONE. "We'll try to do our best."

The first leg kicks off Thursday at 21:30 Israel time, but not in Tel Aviv. Like other Israeli clubs competing in Europe amid the ongoing security situation, Hapoel will play as the nominal home side at a neutral ground abroad — in this case the DVTK Stadion (Diósgyőri Stadion) in Miskolc, Hungary.
Barda made clear the club would have preferred otherwise. "We would have been very happy to host at home in Tel Aviv, but unfortunately this is the situation we cannot change," he said.

It marks Hapoel's first continental fixture since their 2014-15 Europa League exit to Kazakhstan's Astana in the second qualifying round — a 12-year gap that has left the club starved of European nights even as fierce rivals Maccabi Tel Aviv and Maccabi Haifa have continued to feature regularly.

Ludogorets arrive as a considerably more experienced European operator, having reached the group or knockout stage of a continental competition in ten straight seasons. Domestically, though, the Bulgarians enter this tie in transition: they finished third in last season's league, ending a run of 14 consecutive Bulgarian championships, and appointed a new manager over the summer. Israeli outlets including Sport1 and Walla described the draw as among the toughest Hapoel could have received.

Captain Omri Altman struck a more defiant tone than his coach about the away-from-home arrangement. "I'm certain from the first minute we'll feel at home, with 6-7 thousand fans coming from Israel," he said, per ONE — a figure referring to travelling Hapoel supporters rather than the ground's total capacity.

The tie is a two-legged affair: Thursday's opener in Hungary is followed by the return leg in Bulgaria on July 30. The winner advances to the third qualifying round, one step closer to the Conference League's lucrative league phase.
For a club that has spent over a decade watching Europe from the outside, even a tough draw against a battle-hardened Bulgarian side represents a chance simply to be back in the conversation.

title: Ashdod Claw Back From Two Down to Draw 2-2 With Bulgaria's Pirin in Friendly
dek: Trailing 2-0 at the break against Pirin Blagoevgrad, the newly relegated Israeli side rallied through Ily Tamam and a crossbar-rebound finish from Admond Asenta as preparations continue for life in Liga Leumit, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - אשדוד חזרה מפיגור כפול ל-2:2 מול יריבה בולגרית

body: It took M.S. Ashdod less than an hour to erase a two-goal deficit against unfamiliar Bulgarian opposition, salvaging a 2-2 draw with second-division Pirin Blagoevgrad in a preparation friendly, ONE reports.

The result matters more for what it says about the work still ahead than for anything on the scoreboard. Ashdod are rebuilding for their first season back in Liga Leumit, the National League, having been relegated from Ligat Ha'al last term after a decade in the top flight.

Pirin, who ply their trade in Bulgaria's Vtora Liga, made the early running. They led 1-0 by the 23rd minute and doubled the advantage from the penalty spot in the 39th, leaving Ashdod to survey wreckage of their own making at the interval.
There was late first-half frustration too: Ashdod thought they had pulled a goal back through Khalaila in the 35th minute, only for the effort to be chalked off for a tight offside call.

The response after the break was more encouraging than the concession that preceded it. Ashdod created a string of chances early in the second half — Dor Micha's cross found Deboush, who was denied by the Pirin goalkeeper, while Viktor Ouchai's own effort whistled narrowly past the crossbar, both inside the 48th minute.
The pressure told. Ily Tamam converted in the 56th minute to make it 2-1 and set up a grandstand finish against a Bulgarian side unaccustomed to being pegged back.

Ashdod completed the comeback in the 68th minute in scrappy but effective fashion: Amitai Yamin's free kick cannoned back off the crossbar, and Admond Asenta was alert enough to react first and bundle in the rebound for 2-2.
According to ONE, that was how the match finished, with a share of the spoils in a fixture that exists purely to sharpen fitness and combinations ahead of the competitive season.

For a squad reshaped after relegation, a two-goal comeback against senior professional opposition — even in a friendly, even against a lower-division Bulgarian club — is the kind of resilience Ashdod's coaching staff will want to see carry over once the Liga Leumit campaign begins in earnest.

title: Miller: Maccabi Tel Aviv "Fit and Ready" for Sheriff Tiraspol Test
dek: Ahead of his first European campaign in charge, head coach Kenny Miller says Maccabi's Super Cup form proves they are ready for Thursday's Europa League qualifier in Moldova.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C. — Kenny Miller appointed Head Coach
Sport1 — Maccabi Tel Aviv preview vs Sheriff Tiraspol

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv open their Europa League campaign on the road on Thursday, and head coach Kenny Miller says the club's recent form leaves no doubt about the team's readiness for the challenge.

"We saw in our performance against Beersheba that we are fit and prepared," Miller said at a press conference previewing the first leg against Sheriff Tiraspol, referencing Maccabi's Israeli Super Cup victory over Hapoel Be'er Sheva on July 16, which the Yellow-and-Blue won 3-1.

For Miller, a 46-year-old Scot and former Celtic and Rangers striker who was confirmed as Maccabi's permanent head coach last month, Thursday's tie carries personal significance. "This is my first European campaign as head coach and it's very exciting," he said.

The coach was careful to temper the optimism, noting that away fixtures in European competition are never straightforward and that navigating a two-legged tie demands careful game management over both matches rather than a single all-out push.

Miller also pointed to improved squad depth heading into the tie, with several players working their way back toward full match fitness after injury, giving him more options than earlier in the summer.

The format itself underlines Maccabi's unusual travel schedule: Thursday's first leg is played in Moldova, while the return fixture on July 30 — in which Maccabi are the nominal home side — will be staged in Batumi, Georgia rather than at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv.

Defender Roy Revivo, one of the mainstays of Miller's back line and an Israel international, echoed his coach's anticipation. "It's very exciting, we're anticipating this greatly," he said, describing Sheriff as "an aggressive and strong team" that will test Maccabi from the opening whistle.

Revivo also addressed the absence of Maccabi's own supporters from the away leg, a recurring reality for Israeli clubs in continental competition this season. "We really miss our fans and want to make them happy with a victory," he said.

Sheriff Tiraspol arrive as Moldova's dominant force of the past two decades, with 21 domestic championships to their name, all won since the turn of the century. They reached this round by eliminating Slovenia's Aluminij 1-0.

The winner of the tie advances to the Europa League's third qualifying round; the loser drops into Conference League qualifying, leaving Maccabi with a clear incentive to protect their place in Europe's second-tier competition over the two legs.

title: Netanya's asking price sinks Nir'on's move to Maccabi Haifa
dek: Maccabi Haifa have abandoned their pursuit of goalkeeper Omer Nir'on after Maccabi Netanya demanded an outright sale rather than a loan, ONE reports, leaving Haifa to rebuild a goalkeeping department that is losing both its incumbents.

source.name: ONE
source.originalTitle: בשל דרישות נתניה: התפוצץ מעבר ניראון לחיפה

body: Maccabi Haifa's plan to bring in goalkeeper Omer Nir'on as cover for next season has collapsed completely, according to a report from ONE, with Maccabi Netanya's financial demands proving too steep for a deal that had looked close to straightforward only weeks ago.

ONE reports that Netanya's opening demand ran to around NIS 1 million in loan fees with a purchase option attached, or alternatively a makeweight player valued at roughly NIS 1.5 million heading back the other way. Haifa, according to the report, were taken aback by figures of that size for a goalkeeper who barely played down the stretch last season.

The bigger sticking point was structure rather than price alone. Netanya made clear they had no interest in a loan at all — they wanted Nir'on sold outright, and preferably to a club that would make him its first-choice goalkeeper rather than a bench option, which is exactly the role Haifa had in mind for him.

That mismatch cuts to the heart of why the deal made sense for Haifa in the first place. Nir'on, 25, was being lined up as understudy to Georgiy Yermakov — except Yermakov himself is on his way out of Sammy Ofer Stadium. Walla Sport reports the Ukrainian goalkeeper is closing in on a move to Metalist Kharkiv worth in the region of €3 million, a fee the Haifa board has found hard to turn down even though it would rather have kept him.

Sharif Kiwan, Haifa's long-serving No. 1, has also been trying to leave, and the picture in goal at Sammy Ofer Stadium has shifted from one report to the next: Ynet linked him to newly promoted Hapoel Ra'anana, while Walla Sport later reported him angling for a loan at Hapoel Ramat Gan. Walla added that Haifa wanted a Nir'on signing settled before letting Kiwan go anywhere — a plan now back to square one.

None of it changes Nir'on's contractual situation at Netanya, where he still has two years to run on a deal worth around NIS 1.2 million a season. ONE notes that Netanya had, at an earlier stage, been prepared to let him leave for nothing if a buyer took on his wages — a position that hardened into the sale-only stance that ultimately killed the Haifa talks.

The goalkeeper's own year has been difficult regardless of the transfer speculation. Nir'on impressed early last season before a dip in form was followed by shoulder surgery in London, and he has spent much of his rehabilitation on the sidelines rather than in a shirt at all, whichever club it belongs to.

For now, he stays put in Netanya. Haifa, ONE reports, will have to look elsewhere for a second goalkeeper — either a younger Israeli option or a signing out of the National League — a considerably less tidy solution than the one that just fell through.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv Land Wanted Teen Ben Simeon on Three-Year Deal
dek: The 2008-born Israel youth international swaps Akko for Bloomfield Stadium after also drawing interest from Hapoel Beersheba and Maccabi Tel Aviv, ONE reports.

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have moved to secure one of Israeli youth football's more coveted names, signing Jonathan Ben Simeon to a three-year contract with a club option for two further years, ONE reports.
The 2008-born defender-midfielder, who has already featured for Israel's youth national team, arrives from Hapoel Acre, where he had also broken into senior first-team football despite his age.
According to the report, Hapoel Tel Aviv paid a transfer fee of roughly ₪80,000 to prise him away from Acre — a modest sum by senior-team standards, but a marker of how highly the club rates him.

The signing did not happen in a vacuum. ONE reports that Hapoel Beersheba and Maccabi Tel Aviv were also chasing Ben Simeon's signature before Hapoel Tel Aviv won out, with agents Roy Daniel and Yarden Perin brokering the move.

The Hebrew headline's question — whether this time he'll "go all the way" — nods to last season's near-miss for Hapoel Tel Aviv's youth side, which topped the youth league table for most of the campaign before losing the championship to Maccabi Tel Aviv in a tight finish.
Club officials cited in the report point to the creativity and quality Ben Simeon adds to that squad, with an eye on fast-tracking him toward the senior setup if he settles in quickly.
He is expected to be available in time for the opening round of the league season, with August 15 given as the date he becomes eligible to feature for his new club.
For Hapoel Acre, it is the latest example of a smaller-market club developing talent that bigger sides come calling for — a familiar pattern in Israeli football's lower and mid-table youth pipelines.

title: Deputy Chairman Meiri Meets Hapoel Center's Tzadaf as Football Association Camps Edge Toward Joint Ticket
dek: Talks between the Maccabi and Hapoel centers appear to be thawing ahead of Israel Football Association elections, with both sides converging around backing incumbent chairman Shino Zoaretz.

verificationSources.label: ONE - בדרך לרשימה משותפת: מאירי נפגש עם צדף
ONE - מרכז הפועל מאיים להציב מועמד מול שינו זוארץ
ONE - כנרת צדף בדרך להפוך למנכ"לית מרכז הפועל

body: The long-running standoff between Israeli football's two great institutional powers may be easing. Attorney Moran Meiri, deputy chairman of the Israel Football Association, sat down this week with Kaneret Tzadaf, CEO of the Hapoel Center, and Gal Levi, the center's deputy director, in what ONE reports is a step toward fielding a joint ticket in the association's upcoming leadership elections.

The meeting caps months of friction. According to ONE's earlier reporting, Hapoel Center had threatened to run a rival list, and even a rival candidate, against incumbent chairman Moshe "Shino" Zoaretz after feeling shortchanged in board representation following the last election cycle.

Hapoel officials had floated former government minister Issawi Frej as a potential standard-bearer against Zoaretz. But ONE reports the center has since concluded that Frej stands no realistic chance against an incumbent who continues to enjoy broad, sweeping support across the football establishment - prompting the shift toward negotiating terms for a unified slate instead of an open contest.

With the principle of cooperation now largely accepted by both sides, ONE reports the talks move next into the harder, more granular territory: how a combined list would actually be built, the formula for dividing board seats between the Maccabi and Hapoel centers, and who besides Zoaretz would fill out the ticket.

Zoaretz, who first took the chairmanship in December 2022 after unseating Oren Hasson in the federation's first direct leadership election, has built a wide coalition since - a standing underlined by his recent election to UEFA's executive committee, one of only two spots secured among five candidates. That broader stature is precisely what has left rival camps calculating that opposition is no longer worth the fight.

The timing adds urgency to the negotiations. Israeli football association elections are formally expected around December 2026, though there have been growing calls within the sport to move the vote up to as early as August - meaning any agreement on a joint list would need to be locked in well before then.

For now, no formula has been finalized and the composition of a combined ticket remains under discussion. But the Meiri-Tzadaf meeting marks the clearest signal yet that Israeli football's two dominant power centers are working to avoid another bruising internal election fight.
