title: Almog Cohen: 'You Can't Buy the Experience Larnaca Has'
dek: Beitar Jerusalem's head coach says budgets have narrowed but AEK Larnaca's continental know-how remains the bigger threat as the sides meet in Cyprus in the Conference League's second qualifying round, ONE reports.

source.name: ONE
source.originalTitle: אלמוג כהן: את הניסיון של לרנקה אי אפשר לקנות
source.author: ONE

verificationSources.label: Sport1 — Beitar Jerusalem lineup and injury news vs AEK Larnaca
Beitar Jerusalem FC — official injury update on Luka Gadrani
Walla Sport — Beitar Jerusalem drawn against AEK Larnaca, fixture dates

body: Almog Cohen has been in charge of Beitar Jerusalem for barely a season, but even he admits the financial gap with Cypriot football has all but closed. What hasn't closed, the head coach told reporters in Cyprus on Wednesday, is the kind of pedigree AEK Larnaca has built over a decade of grinding through European qualifiers. "The experience of Larnaca is something you can't buy," Cohen said, according to ONE.

Beitar travel to face Larnaca on Thursday at 19:30 local time in the first leg of the Conference League's second qualifying round, with the return fixture in Jerusalem on July 30. Win the tie and Cohen's side still face a playoff round before reaching the competition's league phase — a reminder of how far the project has to travel before Beitar can call itself a European regular again.

Cohen used the press conference to explain, in his own terms, why Cypriot clubs have overtaken Israeli ones as fixtures in Europe despite operating out of a smaller domestic league. "Today the budgets are already almost identical," he said. "In the end, in Cyprus there is no limit on the number of foreign players" — a regulatory gap that, as he described it, lets Larnaca field sides carrying ten or eleven non-Cypriot players in continental competition, far beyond what an Israeli club can field at home.

Tactically, Cohen's read on the tie centres on tempo. "If the game is played at high speed, that could give us an advantage," he said, adding: "I think that could be our key" against a Larnaca side built to control matches through composure and know-how rather than pace.

The coach also addressed the fitness doubt hanging over Luka Gadrani, the Georgian centre-back who has anchored Beitar's back line since arriving from Kairat Almaty. Asked about it, Cohen said he did not expect the issue to change his plans, pointing to the depth he has available at centre-back.

That depth will likely be tested. Sport1 reported separately that Gadrani, who has been carrying discomfort traced to an injury from international duty with Georgia over the summer, was left out of training this week, with Gil Cohen or Liel Darei in line to deputise if he is unavailable. Beitar's own statement on the injury said an MRI had ruled out damage to the cruciate ligament or meniscus, diagnosing instead a bruise and a strain of the lateral ligament. Midfielders Adi Yona and Tomer Yosefi are also missing through injury, Sport1 added.

Midfielder Boris Enow, who also spoke to reporters in Cyprus, struck a respectful tone toward the hosts. "We respect AEK Larnaca a great deal, especially because of their experience in this competition," he said, according to ONE. "But tomorrow we will come to play our game." He added that the Cypriot heat holds no fear for a squad used to similar conditions back home in Israel.

Larnaca arrive in good European standing of their own. Cyprus's reigning vice-champions have become one of the country's most consistent performers in continental qualifying in recent seasons, and this summer appointed Mauro Camoranesi — part of Italy's 2006 World Cup-winning squad — as head coach, a statement of intent from a club that has made Europe part of its identity.

For Beitar, the tie is the first serious test of Cohen's rebuild since he moved from the club's sporting-director office into the dugout. A result in Larnaca on Thursday would put Jerusalem in control of the return leg and offer early evidence that his high-tempo blueprint can trouble a side with far more continental miles on the clock.

title: Wembanyama and Irving Signal Support for Mamdani's Call to Arrest Netanyahu
dek: ONE reports the San Antonio and Dallas stars backed the New York mayor's video urging Washington to enforce the ICC warrant against the Israeli prime minister.
body: Two of the NBA's biggest names have waded into the diplomatic storm swirling around Benjamin Netanyahu's legal status in the United States. According to a report by the Israeli outlet ONE, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama and Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving showed support for a video posted by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani calling for the Israeli prime minister's arrest.

Mamdani released the video this week acknowledging that his own administration lacks the independent legal authority to enforce the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant against Netanyahu should he set foot in New York. "It is clear that we do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant," Mamdani said, while calling on the federal government to "join the ICC and execute this warrant" instead. He went on to describe Netanyahu as a "war criminal" who is not welcome in the city — comments confirmed by multiple outlets including CNN and NBC News.

The ICC issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli defense minister Yoav Gallant in late 2024, alleging crimes against humanity and war crimes tied to Israel's conduct of the war in Gaza, including the use of starvation as a method of warfare. Israeli officials have flatly rejected the accusations. President Donald Trump responded to Mamdani's video by declaring that Netanyahu "will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form," while on American soil.

It is against that backdrop that ONE reports Wembanyama and Irving engaged with, and effectively endorsed, Mamdani's post — a notable moment given how rarely active NBA stars insert themselves directly into a dispute over an Israeli leader's legal jeopardy on foreign soil.

For Irving, the gesture fits a well-documented pattern. The Mavericks guard has repeatedly voiced support for Palestinians over the past two years, from wearing a keffiyeh at a postgame press conference to donning a chain shaped like a map of Israel colored in the Palestinian flag during a nationally televised game. He has also, more controversially, weathered a suspension and the loss of his Nike endorsement in 2022 after sharing material widely condemned as antisemitic, for which he later apologized to Jewish communities.

Wembanyama's involvement, as characterized by ONE, is different in kind: the French big man has largely stayed out of Middle East politics during his rise to superstardom, and the report frames this as one of his first public forays into the subject. That alone is likely to draw outsized attention in Israel, where Wembanyama has become a familiar face after facing off against Israeli internationals in the NBA and on the European stage.

None of the parties involved — Wembanyama, Irving, Mamdani's office or the NBA — has issued a formal statement specifically addressing the players' engagement with the post beyond what ONE has reported, and the claim has not yet been independently corroborated by other outlets in our checks. The underlying political dispute between Mamdani, Trump and Netanyahu's government, however, is extensively documented and continues to develop by the day.

The episode is the latest reminder of how directly American sports figures — particularly in the NBA, where player activism has long been tolerated and often encouraged — keep getting pulled into the geopolitics surrounding Israel and Gaza, two-plus years after October 7 reshaped the conversation across US locker rooms.

title: IDF names Gaza referee, footballers and coaches it says doubled as Hamas and Islamic Jihad operatives
dek: The Israeli military has published a list of twelve Palestinian sports figures from Gaza — including a FIFA-listed assistant referee — whom it says served in Hamas and Islamic Jihad military wings while killed during the war.
body: The IDF has gone public with the names, roles and alleged militant affiliations of twelve Palestinian sports figures from Gaza, arguing that men long presented to the world as footballers, a referee and coaches were, in its account, active operatives in Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad who were killed by Israeli forces during the war.

The disclosure, reported by ONE and corroborated by an IDF statement carried in English by i24NEWS and Fox News, names Mohammed Sami Mohammed Khattab — described as a FIFA-listed international assistant referee — whom the military alleges was a member of Islamic Jihad's Central Camps Brigade.

Also named is Mohammed Barakat, capped three times for the Palestine national team and captain of a Khan Younis club side, whom the IDF says was a Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative allegedly involved in the October 7 attack. Ahmad Abu al-Ata, a defender who played for Gaza sides Ittihad Al-Shuja'iya, Al-Tofah and Al-Ahli Gaza, is described as a Islamic Jihad platoon commander.

The rest of the list includes goalkeeper Mahmoud Osama al-Jazzar, midfielder Tariq Ziad Hussein al-Hour, coach Ali al-Kurd of Al-Qadsiah in Rafah, youth fitness coach Mohammed Mansour, team captains Mohammed Amad Hassouna and Mahmoud al-Rifai, and players Abdullah Riyadh Khattab, Mohammed Nidal al-Hawajri and Mohammed al-Hour, a member of a Palestinian beach soccer squad. The IDF assigns each an internal military role, ranging from squad and platoon command to combat and anti-tank positions.

"Following an intelligence assessment, the IDF can now disclose these terrorists' organisational affiliations and operational roles," the military said in the statement carried by Fox News, framing the release as a rebuttal to what it called a "false campaign portraying the IDF as deliberately targeting members of the soccer community."

None of the claims about individual roles can be independently verified from open sources, and no forensic or judicial material accompanying the identifications has been made public. Fox News said it contacted the Permanent Observer Mission of the State of Palestine to the United Nations for comment and had not received a response at the time of publication; ONE's report likewise carries no reply from the Palestinian side.

The release lands in the middle of one of the most contentious threads of the Gaza war's sporting fallout. The Palestinian Football Association has said roughly 1,009 members of its wider sporting community, including more than 400 footballers, have been killed since the war began in October 2023 — a toll the federation has repeatedly cited in lobbying FIFA and the IOC, through its president Jibril Rajoub, to suspend Israel from international competition.

Individual cases have drawn wide attention on both sides of that argument. The July killing of former Palestine international Suleiman al-Obeid, dubbed the "Palestinian Pelé" by the PFA, while he reportedly waited for aid, prompted global condemnation; the IDF said at the time it was unaware of casualties in the area that day. Wednesday's list appears designed to pre-empt or answer criticism of exactly that kind by asserting that specific individuals killed in the conflict were combatants rather than civilians.

The dispute also sits against the destruction of Gaza's football infrastructure, including the demolition of the rebuilt Palestine Stadium in Gaza City, which forced the Palestinian national team to relocate World Cup qualifying fixtures to Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates.

ONE's report does not indicate that FIFA, the Asian Football Confederation or any Gaza club has responded to the specific names published this week. Until an independent body examines the underlying evidence, the IDF's list stands as a military assertion rather than an adjudicated finding, even as it adds a new and sharply contested chapter to the argument over who, exactly, Israel has been fighting in Gaza's stadiums and training pitches.

title: Beitar legend Eli Ohana reportedly set for guaranteed Likud Knesset spot
dek: Channel 12 says Netanyahu is expected to reserve 'King Ohana' a safe place on Likud's list for the autumn election — a first formal step into national politics for the Beitar Jerusalem icon.

verificationSources.label: Ynetnews — Eli Ohana joins Bayit Yehudi (2015 background)

body: Eli Ohana, the Beitar Jerusalem forward Israeli football still calls "King Ohana" more than a quarter-century after he hung up his boots, may be about to add a Knesset seat to his trophy cabinet. ONE reports that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to reserve Ohana a guaranteed slot on Likud's list for the coming general election.

The move would come through Israel's "shiryun" mechanism, which lets a sitting party leader place a fixed number of allies directly onto the list, bypassing the vote of registered members. Netanyahu has been negotiating exactly that kind of arrangement with Likud's constitution committee ahead of the party's internal primary, scheduled for August 17, before the general election set for October 27.

Nothing is finalised. Ohana's inclusion depends on how many reserved slots Netanyahu ultimately secures and where the Beitar legend is placed within them — details ONE says have not yet been settled publicly.

For a large slice of the Israeli public, Ohana needs no introduction. Now 62, he starred for Beitar Jerusalem across two spells between 1980 and 1999, helping the club to its first league title and cup silverware alongside strike partner Uri Malmilian, and later won the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup with Belgium's KV Mechelen in 1988 before a spell at Portugal's Braga. He earned dozens of caps for Israel between 1984 and 1997.

His football afterlife has been almost as prominent as his playing career: Ohana managed Beitar Jerusalem, Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv, Maccabi Petah Tikva and Hapoel Kfar Saba, and served as Beitar Jerusalem's chairman from 2017 to 2022, a period that included the club's high-profile Shield of Honor recognition from President Reuven Rivlin in 2017.

Politics, though, is not entirely new territory. Ohana was placed among the top slots on Naftali Bennett's Jewish Home list ahead of the 2015 election for the 20th Knesset, only to withdraw within days after the appointment drew sharp public backlash. In 2018 he re-emerged briefly to back Ze'ev Elkin's unsuccessful bid for Jerusalem mayor.

A guaranteed Likud slot this time would mark Ohana's first genuine entry into national politics rather than a supporting or symbolic role — assuming Netanyahu follows through once the primary process concludes next month.

For now, the story remains a single, sourced report relayed by ONE via Channel 12 News, and Beitar's faithful will be watching the Likud list as closely as they watch the club's own results this summer.

title: Indictment Looms for Ironi Tiberias in Banned IV-Infusion Case
dek: The Israel Football Association's prosecutor is expected to file charges within days over allegations that Tiberias players received oversized saline infusions before a relegation-defining match, as the club fights to have the lead investigator disqualified.
body: Ironi Tiberias is bracing for a second serious disciplinary indictment this year, with the Israel Football Association's prosecutor, Gilad Bergman, expected to file charges against the club within days, ONE reports, over allegations that players received banned intravenous infusions before a match that decided the club's survival in the top flight.

The affair traces back to a complaint filed by Ashdod after Tiberias beat them 3-0 in a relegation-deciding fixture last season. Ashdod alleged Tiberias players had been given saline infusions far exceeding the limit set under World Anti-Doping Agency rules, which cap permitted IV volume at 100 millilitres in most circumstances because larger infusions can be used to mask the presence of other prohibited substances in a player's system.

Israel's National Anti-Doping Agency responded by provisionally suspending five Tiberias players — among them Guy Hadida, Niv Gottlieb and Yonatan Tefer — along with three staff members, including head coach Eliran Hudeda, technical director Chen Sol and fitness coach Shlomi Dardo. The agency has singled out Hudeda as the central figure in its inquiry.

According to ONE, roughly ten people connected to the club have already been questioned as part of the investigation, which was carried out by investigator Din-Or Prager on the federation's behalf. Bergman has said the prosecution is working to complete its evidence and that the indictment will land imminently.

Tiberias is not taking the threat quietly. Through attorney Eyal Yafe, the club petitioned the federation's disciplinary court this week seeking to disqualify Prager and halt the indictment altogether, arguing the investigation was biased and that the investigator has a disciplinary history of his own, including a prior finding against him for threatening and cursing at judges.

The club has also accused the federation of selective enforcement, pointing to material that surfaced during the probe suggesting other Israeli Premier League clubs may have used similar infusions without facing comparable scrutiny.

The federation has pushed back hard. It accused Tiberias of leaking investigative material to the press and framed the club's legal maneuvering as an attempt to dodge accountability. "Embarrassing and transparent attempts to evade responsibility, feign innocence and use underhanded tactics will not succeed," the federation said in a statement reported by Walla! Sport, adding that the club would get its day in court.

Club owner Aryeh Kalmanzon has denied any wrongdoing specific to the infusions, telling Israeli media the club conducted its own checks and found nothing improper. "We ran tests — everything is fine. Ashdod filed a complaint about banned substances... we don't understand what's wrong here," he said.

The timing is brutal for a club already reeling from a separate scandal. Tiberias was found to have run a parallel, undisclosed payment system with players for roughly four years — the so-called "double contracts" affair — and reached a plea bargain approved by the disciplinary court on April 1, 2026, that cost the northern club a combined 14 league points across two seasons, a 500,000-shekel fine and a ban on registering new players from January 2027.

Tiberias only reached the top division three years ago on the back of heavy investment, and Kalmanzon has previously described the double-contracts punishment as harsher than the club deserved but one it accepted for the sake of its players. A second indictment, this time carrying the added stigma of an anti-doping case, threatens fresh points penalties and suspensions just as the club tries to plan for the coming season.

For now, the disciplinary court must first rule on Tiberias's bid to knock out the lead investigator before Bergman can formally file. If that petition fails, as the federation expects, the indictment ONE describes as imminent would open a new and more damaging front for a club still absorbing the fallout from its last brush with the football association's enforcement arm.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva close in on Atlanta United's Amador as Lopes successor
dek: The Portuguese left-back, currently nursing an Achilles issue in MLS, is reported to be Beer Sheva's pick to fill the void left by the departing Hélder Lopes.

verificationSources.label: Atlanta United sign defender Pedro Amador — MLSSoccer.com
Hélder Lopes player page — Hapoel Beer Sheva FC

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva have identified their man to replace Hélder Lopes at left-back, with ONE reporting that the club is closing in on a deal for Pedro Amador, the 27-year-old Portuguese defender currently on the books at Atlanta United.

According to the report, Beer Sheva wanted an experienced, internationally-tested left-sided defender who could step straight into the side ahead of a European qualifying campaign, and Amador — a player who came through Braga's academy before making his name at Moreirense — fits that profile.

Amador moved to MLS on a free transfer in the summer of 2024, signing with Atlanta United through the 2026 season with a club option for 2027. Before that switch he made more than 100 appearances across Portugal's top two divisions, the bulk of them in four seasons with Moreirense.

The move would end the Hapoel Beer Sheva career of Hélder Lopes, the Portuguese left-back who has been a fixture at the club since 2021 and made well over 150 appearances in all competitions, evolving in recent seasons into an attacking outlet as much as a defender.

There is a complication, however. ONE notes that Atlanta United's head coach, Tata Martino, has disclosed that Amador is currently carrying an Achilles injury — with the club yet to make clear whether it is a minor issue close to resolving or something more serious that could delay his availability.

That uncertainty means Beer Sheva are planning to put Amador through a full battery of medical examinations before signing off on the transfer, standard practice for any club bringing in a player with a recent injury concern, but a step that carries extra weight here given the timing.

No transfer fee has been disclosed, and the deal is not yet finalized — this remains, for now, a move in progress rather than a done one, with the medical assessment likely to determine how quickly it can be completed.

title: Bnei Eilat's Youth B Side Go Unbeaten to Win Southern District Title
dek: Shabtai Tassel's Ne'arim Bet side won 17 and drew three of 20 games without a single defeat, finishing eight points clear of Maccabi Kiryat Gat as Bnei Eilat's 2011-born cohort pushes toward the National League, ONE reports.

source.name: ONE
source.originalTitle: ליגת האלופות: בני אילת - נערים ב'
source.author: ONE

verificationSources.label: Israel Football Association - Bnei Eilat Ne'arim Bet (U16) team record
Israel Football Association - Bnei Eilat club record

body: Bnei Eilat's Youth B side did not lose a single league game all season, and this week the Red Sea club collected the reward: the Southern District Ne'arim Bet championship, ONE reported, capping an unbeaten campaign for the academy's 2011-born age group.

The numbers behind the title are stark. Bnei Eilat won 17 of their 20 league fixtures and drew the other three - a 90 percent success rate - to finish eight points clear of runners-up Maccabi Kiryat Gat when the table closed.

It was also the division's most productive attack. Eilat scored 96 goals across the season, the most of any team in the Southern District, though their defence was more porous than the record suggests: 21 goals conceded left them with only the second-best defensive record in the league, five worse than Kiryat Gat's.

David Shalom finished as the division's outright top scorer with 18 goals, with strike partner Oren Nachmani contributing 15 and Idan Shitz adding 13 more. Even the back line got in on it - defender Ian Leviv Sarhan scored three - while goalkeeper Uri Ganon anchored an unbeaten season between the posts.
"I think my team was very balanced," coach Shabtai Tassel said, according to ONE. "We had very strong attacking players, but also genuine defenders who gave everything."

Tassel, who has coached at the club for 15 years, also pointed to a quirk of the pandemic years the squad grew up in: "It's a little strange to say, but our advantage was that in Eilat the situation was relatively calm compared to the rest of the country" - a reference, he told the outlet, to the city's lighter Covid-19 disruption during the age group's formative seasons.

The title marks a breakthrough for Bnei Eilat's 2011 cohort, who are on course to progress from district level toward the National League. ONE noted the path is not entirely smooth, however: the club's other side in the same age group had a mixed season, leaving open questions about how the full cohort will cope once it steps up a level.
For Tassel personally, the championship is another marker of a rare kind of managerial longevity in youth football. "Fifteen years at one club," he said, "doesn't come easy."

title: Ten-woman Hapoel Jerusalem lead PAOK at half-time in Champions League debut
dek: The reigning Israeli women's champions played more than 70 minutes with ten players after a 19th-minute red card, yet went into the break 1-0 up away to PAOK in their maiden European qualifying tie, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE — מחצית ראשונה: פאוק סלוניקי - הפועל ירושלים
2026–27 UEFA Women's Champions League qualifying rounds — Wikipedia

body: Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem's first taste of European football has arrived with a twist worthy of a soap opera: reduced to ten players before the half-hour mark, the reigning Israeli women's champions were still leading PAOK 1-0 at half-time in their Champions League qualifying semi-final in Veria, Greece, according to ONE.

The Greek city is hosting one of five four-team mini-tournaments that make up the first qualifying round of the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League, with only the winner of each group advancing to the second qualifying round. PAOK, as hosts, drew Jerusalem in one semi-final on Wednesday, while Montenegro's Budućnost Podgorica met Azerbaijan's Neftçi Baku in the other.

Jerusalem's evening got complicated in the 19th minute, when goalkeeper Daniela Solera was shown a straight red card for handling the ball outside her penalty area, ONE reported. It left the Israeli side to see out the rest of the half, and potentially far more, with ten women on the pitch against a full PAOK line-up on home soil.

Replacement keeper Lili Tzuk was thrown in immediately and had to be alert from the restart. In the 22nd minute she turned away a direct free kick from PAOK's Maria Mitko, and by the 37th she was called upon again, this time keeping out a header from the hosts, per ONE's live coverage.

Rather than retreat behind the ball with a player down, Jerusalem kept pushing forward. In the 38th minute Hili Shalom worked an opening down the right and squared for Smadar Cohen, whose effort was saved not once but twice by the PAOK goalkeeper, ONE reported.

The breakthrough came three minutes later. ONE reported that a Jerusalem player identified in its coverage only by the surname Gakoni headed the visitors into a 1-0 lead in the 41st minute — a startling scoreline given the numerical disadvantage.

That is the position ONE's report describes at the interval, and it should be read as exactly that: a half-time snapshot, not a final result. The full-time score was not yet available at the time of writing.

The stakes are unusually high for an Israeli women's club appearing at this level for the first time. Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem won the 2025-26 Israeli Women's Premier League, the club's maiden top-flight title and the first won by a Jerusalem-based women's team, after three straight runner-up finishes. This tie in Veria is the reward: a European debut, with a place in the Champions League's second qualifying round on offer to whoever tops the four-team group.

In the parallel semi-final, Neftçi Baku eliminated Budućnost Podgorica on penalties after a goalless draw, putting the Azerbaijani side into Saturday's mini-tournament final regardless of what happens between PAOK and Jerusalem. The winner of Wednesday's tie in Veria will face Neftçi on July 25, with that final's winner progressing into the Champions League path proper.

For a club that only formed its senior women's section in 2020 and climbed from the third tier to an Israeli title in five seasons, simply being in Veria with a half-time lead — even with ten players — already counts as a landmark night. Confirmation of the full-time score, and of whether Jerusalem's European adventure continues past round one, will follow once it is verified.

title: IDF names Palestinian footballers and coaches it says doubled as Hamas, Islamic Jihad operatives
dek: The military published a list of players, coaches and a referee killed in Gaza since October 2023, saying their public sporting identities masked roles in militant groups' armed wings — a claim partly corroborated when Islamic Jihad itself later named one of the dead as a fighter.
body: The IDF has published the names of eleven Palestinian footballers, coaches and match officials it says were killed in Gaza while secretly serving as fighters for Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad, pushing back at what it calls a false narrative that the military has deliberately targeted innocent sportspeople.

In a statement carried by ONE, the military said the men were "presented to the public as civilians" — footballers, coaches and, in one case, a match official — while in reality holding roles inside the two groups' armed wings in the Gaza Strip. Some, the IDF said, took part in the October 7 assault on Israeli communities.

"In many cases, they were portrayed internationally only as players, with no mention of their affiliation with terrorist organizations," the IDF said, framing the disclosure as a response to weeks of claims — which it says are false — that strikes on the sporting community were intentional and indiscriminate.

The list names players including Mohammed Barakat, whom the IDF describes as a Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative, and Mohammed Mansour, identified as a player-turned-coach who the military says also served as a deputy commander in a Hamas battalion. Nine other men are named in the same statement.

The most notable case is Ahmed Abu al-Atta, a forward for Gaza City club Al-Ahli who was killed in a strike on his home. The Palestinian Football Association had mourned him purely as a player — but Palestinian Islamic Jihad's own military wing subsequently claimed him as one of its fighters, an admission separate from the IDF's own list that lends outside weight to the military's broader claim.

That overlap matters: Gazan armed factions have, in a handful of other cases unrelated to football, likewise later acknowledged that people initially mourned publicly as journalists or aid workers had in fact been members of their fighting ranks, according to reporting reviewed alongside this story.

The Palestinian Football Association, for its part, has said roughly 1,009 members of the Palestinian sporting community — players, coaches, referees and administrators — have been killed since the war began in October 2023, a toll it has cited in appeals to FIFA and other governing bodies.

That casualty count sits at the centre of a parallel, and largely separate, campaign by Palestinian officials and some international federations pressing for sporting sanctions against Israel over the war's toll on Gaza. The IDF's naming of alleged operatives is a direct rebuttal aimed at that campaign.

Neither FIFA nor the Palestinian Football Association had issued a public response to this specific list at the time of writing, and the IDF's claims about the other individuals named have not been independently corroborated in the way the Abu al-Atta case was.

The dispute is unlikely to settle quickly. Gaza's football scene, already gutted by nearly two years of war and reduced to playing home World Cup qualifiers in Sharjah after Gaza's own stadium was struck, has become one more front in the wider information battle over how the conflict is being fought and reported.
facts: The IDF released a statement naming individuals it says served as Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives while publicly working as footballers, coaches or a match official in Gaza.
The IDF said the disclosure was meant to counter claims that it deliberately targeted innocent members of the sporting community.
The list, reported to run to eleven names, includes player Mohammed Barakat and coach Mohammed Mansour, whom the IDF describes as a Hamas battalion deputy commander.

One of the men named, Ahmed Abu al-Atta, a forward for Gaza's Al-Ahli club killed in a strike on his home, was separately claimed by Palestinian Islamic Jihad's own military wing as one of its fighters.
The Palestinian Football Association has said roughly 1,009 members of the Palestinian sports community have been killed since the war began in October 2023.
The claims come amid a wider push by Palestinian officials and some sporting bodies for sanctions against Israel over the war's impact on Gaza's sporting community.

title: Hapoel HaEmek Extends Assistant Coach Yablonovsky's Contract by Three Seasons
dek: The Afula-based club is locking in continuity on its bench, keeping Golan Yablonovsky alongside head coach Sharon Avrahami and adding Oded Hendler as a second assistant.
body: Hapoel HaEmek have moved to lock in the coaching staff behind their surprise run to the top of the Israeli Basketball Premier League table, announcing a three-season contract extension for assistant coach Golan Yablonovsky, ONE reports.

The extension comes on the heels of head coach Sharon Avrahami's own three-year renewal, agreed after he steered the Emek Valley club to first place in the standings and a State Cup semi-final in his very first season in charge, according to Walla Sport.

Yablonovsky joined Avrahami's bench when the pair arrived together for the 2025-26 season. He had previously worked as an assistant at Beni Herzliya under Dan Shamir, and for several years has also served alongside Avrahami with Israel's youth national teams, helping the squads to fifth place at the European Cadets Championship and sixth at the European Under-18 Championship.
"Hapoel HaEmek has become a home for me," Yablonovsky said, according to ONE. "When you find a place that gives to you and you give back to it, you know you are in the right place."

Avrahami was equally warm about his assistant. "Golan is much more than an assistant coach for me," he said. "He is very dominant within the staff and an excellent professional who helps us run the whole system."
The bench will not look identical to last season, though: Oded Hendler joins as a second assistant coach, arriving from Hapoel Galil Elyon in the Upper Galilee.

On the floor, several key contributors are staying put as well. Captain Roy Netzia, centers Niv Mesgav and Gil Noyovich, forward Lucas Goldenberg and guard Cameron Henry are all continuing with the team, giving Avrahami a settled core to build around.

With European qualification among the club's stated ambitions for next season, per Walla's reporting, Hapoel HaEmek's off-season message has been unmistakable: keep together the roster and staff that delivered its best campaign in years.

title: Monza reportedly approach Maccabi Tel Aviv over defender Tyrese Asante
dek: The Serie A club have opened contact about the Dutch-Ghanaian centre-back, according to ONE, days before he is due to play Maccabi's Europa League qualifier against Sheriff Tiraspol.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv face Sheriff Tiraspol - Jerusalem Post

body: Monza have made contact with Maccabi Tel Aviv about signing Dutch centre-back Tyrese Asante, ONE reported on Wednesday, as the Serie A club look to add defensive reinforcements before their transfer window closes.

According to ONE, the interest was first reported by the Italian journalist Gianluigi Longhi, who wrote that Asante has effectively agreed to the move personally and is now waiting on the two clubs to strike a deal. No transfer fee has been reported, and neither Monza nor Maccabi has confirmed an approach or a fee.

It is not the first time Asante has attracted attention from abroad. ONE noted that Sassuolo, Beşiktaş and Qarabağ all made inquiries in January but stopped short of tabling a formal offer for the 24-year-old.

For now, Asante remains part of Kenny Miller's squad. He is included in the group set to face Sheriff Tiraspol on Thursday at 20:00 in the first leg of the Europa League second qualifying round, the opening test of Maccabi's European campaign this summer.

Born in The Hague and of Ghanaian descent, Asante joined Maccabi Tel Aviv from ADO Den Haag in July 2024 on a three-year contract after three seasons in the Dutch second tier. He has since made himself a regular fixture at centre-back and has been capped by the Netherlands at under-21 level.

His time in Tel Aviv has already been decorated: Asante was part of the Maccabi side that won the 2024/25 Israeli championship, and he added the State Cup last season - the club's first domestic cup in five years - even as Maccabi slipped to third place in the league table.

Monza, relegated from Serie A last season and now competing in Serie B, have been rebuilding since the death of former owner and Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi. A move for Asante would fit a club looking to strengthen a defence as it aims for an immediate return to the top flight.

Any deal is likely to wait until after Maccabi's European fixtures against Sheriff Tiraspol are settled, with the second leg scheduled for the following Thursday. Until then, the report from Italy remains just that - an approach, not an agreement.

title: Former owner Shaul Eisenberg sues, says Hapoel Tel Aviv's name belongs to him
dek: Shaul Eisenberg, who ran Hapoel Tel Aviv's basketball club for two decades before stepping away in 2007, is demanding NIS 12.6 million and warning the team may have to drop its own name after Ofer Yannay's takeover of majority ownership.

verificationSources.label: ONE — השם הפועל תל אביב זה של שאול אייזנברג
Ynet — שאול אייזנברג פנה להנהלת הפועל ת"א וטען לשימוש אסור בשם המועדון
ICE — שאול אייזנברג תובע 12.6 מיליון שקל: "הפועל ת"א שייכת לי"

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv's basketball club is facing a legal challenge over the one asset that predates every player, coach and owner it has ever had: its own name. Shaul Eisenberg, who controlled the club for roughly two decades until 2007, says the rights to "Hapoel Tel Aviv" are his, not the team's, and he has taken the fight to court.

Eisenberg's attorney, Dr. Matan Gutman, laid out the claim on ONE's "Sihat HaYom" programme: "The Hapoel Tel Aviv name belongs to Shaul Eisenberg." It is a blunt line, but it rests on a specific paper trail going back to 2009.

According to Gutman, when Eisenberg's ownership era ended, he reached an agreement, brokered through the late Ofer Eliahu, under which the Hapoel Ussishkin fan association was permitted to use the "Hapoel Tel Aviv" name only on condition that the association itself exclusively held and managed the team. Should that arrangement change, Gutman says, the naming rights were to revert to Eisenberg.

That condition is now at the centre of the dispute. Hapoel Tel Aviv recently confirmed that Ofer Yannay, the businessman who has bankrolled the club's rise into the EuroLeague alongside partners including Gili Raanan, Micky Malka and Alan Howard, would become majority shareholder with 51% of the club — leaving the fan association holding a minority 19% stake.

Eisenberg's camp argues that handover breaches the 2009 terms outright. Per Ynet, he sent an urgent letter to association chairman Rami Cohen, to Yannay and to the club's board, asserting that once the association ceded control to a third party, the club forfeited its right to trade under the Hapoel Tel Aviv name at all.

The dispute has since moved from warning letters to an actual courtroom filing. Eisenberg, represented by Gutman and attorney Nir Friedman, has lodged a NIS 12.6 million claim in the Tel Aviv District Court against Hapoel Ussishkin, the basketball club itself, Yannay, Avi Zeidenberg, the team's management company, attorney Roei Miller and the widow of the late Ofer Eliahu.

Within that claim, Eisenberg is separately demanding NIS 100,000 a month for continued use of the club's name for as long as the rights remain outside his hands — a running toll rather than a one-off payment.

It is a familiar fight for Hapoel Tel Aviv's basketball operation. Eisenberg has raised versions of this same ownership claim before, including during the club's earlier financial troubles, but the stakes are higher this time: the team he is challenging is no longer a struggling domestic outfit but a EuroLeague side attracting billionaire investment.

ONE reports that a court hearing on the matter has been set for September, with Gutman expressing confidence that Eisenberg's position will hold up. Hapoel Tel Aviv has not issued a detailed public rebuttal of the specific claims aired on "Sihat HaYom."

For now, the club continues to play, train and market itself as Hapoel Tel Aviv while the question of who actually owns that name sits before a judge — an unusual footnote to a summer in which the team's on-court ambitions have never looked bigger.
facts: Shaul Eisenberg owned and ran Hapoel Tel Aviv's basketball club for roughly two decades before stepping away from Israeli top-flight competition in 2007.
Eisenberg's attorney, Dr. Matan Gutman, said on ONE's "Sihat HaYom" programme that "the Hapoel Tel Aviv name belongs to Shaul Eisenberg."

The claim traces to a 2009 agreement under which the Hapoel Ussishkin fan association could use the club's name only while it exclusively held and managed the team; per Eisenberg's side, naming rights revert to him if that changes.
Hapoel Tel Aviv recently announced Ofer Yannay would become majority shareholder with 51% of the club, with the fan association's stake reduced to 19%, a move Eisenberg says breaches the 2009 terms.

Eisenberg has filed a NIS 12.6 million lawsuit in the Tel Aviv District Court against Hapoel Ussishkin, the basketball club, Ofer Yannay, Avi Zeidenberg, the club's management company, attorney Roei Miller and the widow of the late Ofer Eliahu.
He is separately demanding NIS 100,000 per month for the club's continued use of the "Hapoel Tel Aviv" name until the rights are returned to him.
ONE reports a court hearing on the matter is scheduled for September 2026.

title: Figo: Real Madrid Always Wants the Best
dek: The Portuguese great backs a Rodri move to the Bernabéu, names his Ballon d'Or favourites and says Mourinho's only job now is to start winning again.

verificationSources.label: Real Madrid official announcement on Mourinho

body: Luis Figo has never been shy about Real Madrid's appetite for star power, and this week the Portuguese great weighed back in on one of the summer's most persistent transfer sagas: Rodri to the Bernabéu.

"I know there has been talk of the possibility of Rodri coming to Real Madrid," Figo said, quoted by ONE. "I think it will be difficult, because he's under contract with Manchester City, but everyone knows that Real Madrid always want to sign the best players in the world."

It is a familiar refrain from a man who knows the club's recruitment culture better than most — Figo's own move from Barcelona to Madrid in 2000 remains one of the most explosive transfers in the game's history. Rodri, for his part, has a deal at City that runs well beyond this window, and City have shown no appetite to sell.

Figo also had praise for the Spain and City midfielder's World Cup, even if the numbers did not jump off the page. "For me, Rodri has had a great World Cup, even though, in terms of goals or assists, he hasn't stood out that much," he said.

Asked to look ahead to the Ballon d'Or, Figo argued the World Cup should not be the only yardstick and pointed to a spread of candidates who excelled across the full season. He named Kylian Mbappé, whose tournament in the finals was outstanding, alongside a Paris Saint-Germain player who won the Champions League again — a nod to the club's continued European dominance.

He also flagged PSG pair Vitinha and Désiré Doué. "I might single out Vitinha and Doué, who've had a great season even though the World Cup didn't go so well for them," Figo said, while also naming Real Madrid's own Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham among the contenders.

The conversation eventually turned to Madrid's own dugout, where José Mourinho began his second spell as head coach this summer after being officially unveiled on June 11. It is a three-year appointment, one of club president Florentino Pérez's marquee promises on the back of his re-election, and it returns Mourinho to the Bernabéu for the first time since his 2010-13 stint.

Figo made clear that results, not spectacle, will define whether the appointment is judged a success. "I think the most important thing for Real Madrid now will be to start winning again after two years without a trophy," he said, alluding directly to the pressure now on Mourinho.

It is a blunt assessment from a club legend, but a fair one: two trophyless seasons is an unfamiliar drought at a club built on the exact appetite Figo was describing — for the best players, and for silverware to match.

title: Maccabi Haifa's next defensive target comes with a fitness question mark
dek: ONE reports Haifa are closing in on Wolves loanee Nigel Lonwijk to help rebuild a defence stripped of Abdoulaye Seck and Lisav Eissat — but the 23-year-old's last three seasons have been repeatedly interrupted by hamstring trouble.

verificationSources.label: ONE — מועד לפציעות? ההיסטוריה של נייג'ל לונוויק
Wolves.co.uk — Lonwijk signs new deal ahead of Luton loan
Walla Sport — בעקבות מכירת ליסב עיסאת

body: Maccabi Haifa's defence is being rebuilt almost from scratch this summer, and according to a report on ONE, the next name in is a 23-year-old Dutch centre-back whose recent history reads like a warning label: two separate hamstring injuries in the space of three seasons.

ONE reports that the reigning champions are set to add Nigel Lonwijk, a Wolverhampton Wanderers player who has spent his entire senior career out on loan, to a backline that has lost several familiar faces this window. Neither Haifa nor Wolves have confirmed a deal, and it is being reported as a move in progress rather than a done transfer.

The need is real. Abdoulaye Seck, the Senegalese centre-back who anchored Haifa's defence for four seasons and was part of the 2022-23 championship squad, left as a free agent when his contract expired at the end of June. Romanian international Lisav Eissat, only 21, was sold to Bristol City in the Championship. And Brazilian centre-back Pedrão has struggled to recover from a serious knee injury, with his own Haifa future in real doubt.

Those exits are why Haifa have been busy adding names at the other end of the pitch, too — goalkeeper Omri Glazer returned to the club on a three-year deal to replace the departing Georgi Yermakov, while Brazilian defender Wanderson "Tsunami" de Freitas Soares and striker Andrea Novakovic have also signed. Lonwijk would be the piece meant to stabilise the back line itself.

On the pitch, there is plenty to like: at 1.95m, right-footed and comfortable in a back three or four, Lonwijk came up through PSV's academy before joining Wolves' youth setup in 2020. He has never played a senior match for Wolves themselves, instead building his career through a string of loans — Fortuna Sittard, then a League One title with Plymouth Argyle in 2022-23.

It's what came after Plymouth that ONE's piece is really about. Sent to Grasshopper Club Zürich in Switzerland for 2023-24, Lonwijk suffered a hamstring injury in pre-season and didn't make his debut until late October. He lasted one match — reinjuring the same hamstring in that game — before the loan was scrapped in mid-November and he was moved on to Wycombe Wanderers to salvage the rest of the season in League One.

The following year brought more of the same. Loaned to Huddersfield Town for 2024-25, Lonwijk again suffered a hamstring problem, this time ruled out for roughly four months from around March 2025 — a second significant soft-tissue injury in as many campaigns, and exactly the kind of pattern that gives recruitment staff pause.

Then came a turnaround. Wolves sent him out for a third straight season, this time to Luton Town in League One, and Lonwijk stayed largely fit throughout 2025-26 — more than 45 appearances across all competitions, a regular starter, and part of the Luton side that won the EFL Trophy.

That is the tension at the heart of ONE's report: a player who looked injury-prone for two straight seasons just produced the most durable campaign of his career. Whether that represents a genuine turning point, or simply one good season sandwiched between fitness breakdowns, is precisely the gamble Haifa would be taking if the move goes through.

For a club that has just lost the leadership and physical presence Seck provided at the back, banking on a defender with that recent history — however promising his last season looked — is a decision Haifa's medical and fitness staff will have weighed carefully before giving the green light.

title: Jason Levien set to take Maccabi Tel Aviv's seat on the EuroLeague board
dek: The American attorney-turned-club-owner is expected to replace Dani Federman as Maccabi's representative, the latest ripple from a summer of upheaval atop the club's ownership.
body: Jason Levien, the American attorney and sports executive who has cycled through ownership stakes in the NBA, MLS and European football, is expected to become Maccabi Tel Aviv's representative on the EuroLeague board of directors, replacing longtime club figure Dani Federman, according to a report by ONE.

The switch is the latest consequence of a summer that has scrambled the top of Israeli basketball's ownership charts. The Recanati family, Maccabi's dominant shareholder, exercised its right of first refusal to buy out the entire stake held by the Federman family's holding company, Padenko Sport.

That deal, confirmed by the club, saw the Recanatis pay roughly $50 million for the Federman family's shares, lifting the family's total holding in Maccabi Tel Aviv to 58 percent, Ynet reported. Danny Federman, whose father David Federman had been a fixture in the club's boardroom for years, served as co-CEO alongside Eli Driks from 2011 and remained influential in Maccabi's management even after leaving that post.

With the Federmans out, their seat on the EuroLeague board — one of the more consequential positions in European club basketball, given the competition's control over scheduling, expansion and revenue distribution — appears to be passing to Levien, a 52-year-old attorney with law and public policy degrees from the University of Michigan.

Levien's path into sports ownership began on the other side of the table. He worked as a licensed NBA agent, and his best-known deal saw him negotiate a $71 million contract extension for Luol Deng with the Chicago Bulls.

He later joined an investor group that bought into the Philadelphia 76ers before moving into an executive chair himself, becoming CEO and managing partner of the Memphis Grizzlies in 2012. ESPN ranked the Grizzlies first in North America that period for front-office efficiency and fan experience.

In 2016, Levien and American partner Steve Kaplan led a takeover of roughly 68 percent of Welsh football club Swansea City. The ownership proved contentious: supporters and British media criticized the pair for treating the club more as a financial asset than a community institution, and Swansea slid into relegation to the Championship during their tenure. The partnership ended in late 2024.
Levien currently serves as co-chairman and CEO of MLS side D.C. United and chairs the Brisbane Bullets of Australia's NBL, giving him an active ownership footprint across three continents.

His connection to Israeli basketball runs deeper than a boardroom appointment would suggest. Early in his career as an agent, Levien represented Omri Casspi and Yotam Halperin, two of the first Israeli players taken in the NBA draft — a relationship that dates back roughly two decades.

Neither Maccabi Tel Aviv nor EuroLeague has formally announced the board change, and ONE frames Levien's appointment as expected rather than finalized. The move would nonetheless hand a experienced, if polarizing, figure in global sports ownership direct influence over decisions shaping the competition Maccabi has long treated as its top priority.

body: Maccabi Haifa's summer rebuild at the back has a name and a face: Nigel Lonwijk, the 23-year-old Dutch defender, landed in Israel this week to complete his move to the reigning champions, ONE reports.

The transfer sees Maccabi pay Wolverhampton Wanderers around €600,000 for a player who has spent the last several seasons out on loan rather than featuring for the Premier League club itself, and who now signs a three-year contract in Haifa.

Lonwijk, of Surinamese-Dutch background, stands 1.90 metres and is described by ONE as quick, comfortable on the ball and blessed with a strong right foot despite being deployed mainly on the left side of defence. The club sees him as capable of playing left-back, filling in at right-back, or slotting into a back three when required.

He arrives having spent last season on loan at Luton Town, who competed in England's third tier, League One, after successive relegations from the Premier League. According to ONE's report, Lonwijk made 45 appearances there in all competitions, scored twice and picked up nine yellow cards.

That run of playing time is precisely why Maccabi moved for him: after several loan spells away from Molineux — including earlier stints at Fortuna Sittard, Plymouth Argyle, Grasshopper, Wycombe Wanderers and Huddersfield Town — Lonwijk built a track record of regular football without ever nailing down a place at Wolves themselves.

For Maccabi Haifa, the deal is described as their fourth signing of the summer, part of a wider reshaping of the squad that won last season's title and now has continental football and a title defence to prepare for.

The Israeli champions have been active reinforcing several areas of the pitch this window, and a mobile, left-sided defender with Championship-level experience fits a squad that needs both quality and depth heading into a demanding season.
Formal confirmation from Maccabi Haifa of the fee and contract terms, along with any presentation of the new signing, is expected to follow now that Lonwijk is in the country.

title: Ivić: "I was shocked by the bonus at Maccabi Tel Aviv"
dek: The Serbian coach who steered Maccabi Tel Aviv to a 31-point title romp in his debut season says an unprecedented bonus scheme was part of what drove him to one of the most dominant campaigns in Israeli football history.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — איביץ': "הייתי בהלם מהבונוס במכבי ת"א"

body: Vladimir Ivić delivered one of the most one-sided title campaigns Israeli football has seen this century, and in a new interview he has revealed a detail that helped explain the hunger behind it: a bonus structure at Maccabi Tel Aviv that, in his words, left him in shock.

"I was shocked by the bonus at Maccabi Tel Aviv," Ivić said, in comments given to the Serbian outlet Sport24 and carried by Sport5. "It had never happened to me before in my career. It gave me motivation."

According to the report, Maccabi built incentives into his contract that went beyond anything he had encountered previously — a bonus simply for finishing the season as runner-up, and a considerably larger one attached to winning the championship outright. Ivić said no club had ever offered him a runner-up bonus before.

The context matters. Per the interview, Ivić took the job in the summer of 2018 after a year without a coaching post, walking into a Maccabi Tel Aviv side that had just finished third and had gone three years without lifting the title — hardly a position of strength for a club of that size and history.

What followed exceeded anything the bonus clauses might have anticipated. In his very first season in charge, 2018–19, Ivić's Maccabi won the Israeli Premier League by a record 31-point margin, losing only a single league match all campaign — one of the most dominant title runs in the competition's history — and added the Toto Cup for a domestic double in his debut year.

He then retained the title the following season, 2019–20, making him the first Maccabi Tel Aviv coach in years to deliver back-to-back championships, before leaving the club that July for a brief and unsuccessful spell at Watford.

Ivić returned to Bloomfield Stadium for a second stint in June 2022, but that chapter proved far less smooth: he departed by mutual agreement with the club in January 2023, roughly halfway through his new two-year deal.

Since then his coaching path has taken him to Russia's Krasnodar and now to the UAE, where he currently manages Al Ain in the Pro League. But it is the first spell in Tel Aviv, and the financial incentive that came with it, that he still singles out as a formative moment — proof, in his telling, that a well-designed bonus can be as much a motivator as a paycheck.

title: UEFA Won't Let VAR Use World Cup's 'Mistaken Identity' Rule to Overturn Diving Calls
dek: European football's governing body has told its video assistant referees to leave the World Cup's most contentious innovation on the shelf this season, after the rule sent Switzerland's Breel Embolo off in tears against Argentina.
body: UEFA has quietly ruled out one of the more divisive VAR experiments to come out of the 2026 World Cup, instructing its video assistant referees not to use the tournament's expanded "mistaken identity" protocol to overturn diving or simulation decisions, Sport5 reports.

The rule itself was an IFAB creation, widened before the World Cup to let VAR intervene whenever the referee appeared to have carded the wrong player for an offence. In theory it was meant to fix simple confusion cases — a booking pinned on the wrong shirt number in a crowded box.

In practice, it produced the most talked-about refereeing moment of the tournament. In Argentina's 3-1 extra-time quarter-final win over Switzerland on July 11, Portuguese referee João Pinheiro initially booked Argentina's Leandro Paredes for a foul on Breel Embolo. VAR sent him back to the monitor, ruled that Embolo had in fact dived, scrubbed Paredes' yellow card and booked Embolo instead — his second of the match, and an automatic red in the 72nd minute.

It was the first sending-off of its kind in World Cup history: a VAR intervention that flipped a card from the player originally penalised to the player originally fouled. Argentina, level at 1-1 through Alejandro Garnacho...

Argentina, pegged back to 1-1 by Dan Ndoye's finish after Alexis Mac Allister's opener, took full advantage of the extra man. Julián Álvarez broke the deadlock in extra time and Lautaro Martínez added a late second, sending Argentina through to a semi-final against England while Switzerland went home fuming.

Swiss coach Murat Yakin did not hide his anger afterwards, telling reporters, in comments carried by Ynet, that the rule "has no connection to football, in my opinion." The Embolo decision became a rallying point for critics who argued VAR had drifted from correcting factual errors into second-guessing a referee's judgment calls.

According to the reports now emerging, UEFA has drawn the same line internally. The governing body has told its VAR teams that "mistaken identity" should apply only to clear-cut identification errors — cases where the referee has quite simply carded the wrong individual — and not to situations where the underlying question is whether a foul, dive or simulation happened at all.

That distinction effectively shelves the World Cup version of the rule for Champions League and Europa League matches this season. UEFA's view, as relayed by Sportskeeda and Yahoo Sports, is that letting VAR relitigate a subjective call like simulation under the identity-error banner risked expanding video review's reach further into referees' on-field judgment than the body is comfortable with.

It leaves an unusual split heading into the new European season: a VAR tool trialled on football's biggest stage, credited by IFAB as a fix for a genuine blind spot, will not travel intact into the continent's leading club competitions — at least not yet, and not for the type of incident that made it famous.
facts: UEFA has instructed its VAR officials not to apply the World Cup's expanded "mistaken identity" rule to diving/simulation decisions in its own competitions.
The rule, introduced by IFAB before the 2026 World Cup, lets VAR correct a card issued to the wrong player for an offence.
It was used for the first time in World Cup history on July 11, 2026, when Switzerland's Breel Embolo was sent off after VAR overturned a yellow card originally given to Argentina's Leandro Paredes.
Referee João Pinheiro made the original call; Argentina went on to win 3-1 after extra time to reach the semi-finals against England.
Swiss coach Murat Yakin publicly criticised the rule after the match, saying it had no connection to football.
UEFA's rationale, per Sportskeeda and Yahoo Sports, is that mistaken identity should cover only factual identification errors, not subjective interpretive calls such as diving.

title: Maccabi Haifa turn to Wolves loanee Nigel Lonwijk to replace Eissat at the back
dek: Sport5 reports Maccabi Haifa have agreed a deal for Dutch centre-back Nigel Lonwijk, a 1.95m Wolverhampton Wanderers player who has spent his entire career out on loan, as the club's answer to Liseb Eissat's move to Bristol City.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — נייג'ל לונוויק. תואם עיסאת: הכירו את הבלם החדש של חיפה
Wolverhampton Wanderers FC — Lonwijk signs new deal ahead of Luton loan
Yahoo Sports — Bristol City sign defender Eissat on four-year deal

body: Maccabi Haifa believe they have found their answer to the centre-back problem created by Liseb Eissat's summer exit, with Sport5 reporting the Israeli champions have agreed to sign Dutch defender Nigel Lonwijk from Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Lonwijk is an imposing physical presence at 1.95 metres (6ft 5in), born in Goirle in the Netherlands in October 2002. He came up through PSV Eindhoven's academy before Wolves signed him as a teenager, and he has worn the club's shirt ever since — without ever making a single senior appearance for the Molineux side.

That is not a typo. Six years into his Wolves career, Lonwijk's entire footballing education has come away from base, on an unbroken chain of loans: Fortuna Sittard in the Netherlands, then a run through the English lower leagues at Plymouth Argyle, Grasshopper Club Zürich in Switzerland, Wycombe Wanderers, Huddersfield Town and, most recently, Luton Town.

The Luton loan, in League One last season, was arguably his best yet. Sport5 credits him with more than 30 league appearances, often deployed out of position at right-back rather than his natural centre-back slot, averaging 10.3 sprints, 3.1 tackles and 2.5 aerial duels won (a 58% success rate) per game. He also helped Luton lift the EFL Trophy.

Durability has been the one question mark. Sport5 notes he suffered three separate hamstring injuries across two seasons, though he stayed fit and available throughout last season at Kenilworth Road — a track record Haifa will hope continues once he swaps English winters for Israeli summers.

Sport5 puts his market value at around €1.2 million, a modest figure that reflects a player still searching for his first senior minutes at his parent club despite six loan spells and a league title with Plymouth in 2022–23.

The comparison in the report's own headline is deliberate. Eissat, a Romanian international who came through Haifa's own academy, left this summer for Bristol City in a reported €2.5 million deal after 33 first-team appearances for the club and a loan spell at Hapoel Hadera. Sport5 draws a direct line between the two — similar build, similar defensive instincts — while stopping short of calling Lonwijk the better player; by its own assessment, Eissat remains the stronger of the pair for now.

Where Lonwijk would fit in is also becoming clearer. Haifa have separately been finalising a deal for a Brazilian defender known in the Israeli press simply as "Tsunami," a 30-year-old who can play at left-back or centre-back and arrives after a spell in Turkey's second tier, having previously played for Levski Sofia in Bulgaria. Sport5's framing suggests the Dutchman would supply the physicality and one-on-one strength in the pairing, leaving more of the distribution and game management to his more experienced partner.

None of this has been confirmed through official Maccabi Haifa channels yet — this is a Sport5 report of an agreed deal, and the article does not spell out whether the move is a permanent transfer or another loan, nor an official fee. Given Lonwijk's contract situation at Wolves and the pattern of the past six seasons, a permanent switch would represent a notable change of course for a player Wolves have never actually fielded.

title: Portuguese left-back Pedro Amador closing in on Hapoel Beer Sheva move
dek: The Atlanta United defender is reported to be on the verge of joining the reigning Israeli champions as a replacement for veteran left-back Hélder Lopes.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — Pedro Amador on the verge of signing for Hapoel Beer Sheva
Atlanta United FC — Atlanta United signs defender Pedro Amador

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva, freshly crowned as Israel's champions, are closing in on a left-back who has spent the last two seasons plying his trade in MLS. Sport5's Tomer Levi reports that Pedro Amador, a 27-year-old Portuguese defender contracted to Atlanta United, is on the verge of putting pen to paper in Beer Sheva.

The move, as Sport5 frames it, is a succession plan rather than a raid for a starting shirt: Amador is being lined up to eventually take over from Hélder Lopes, the 37-year-old left-back who has anchored that flank for the champions and who is expected to move on this summer.

Amador's road to Israel has run through some of Portugal's better-known academies and second-tier ambitions. He came up through Sporting Lisbon's youth system before senior spells at Belenenses and Braga, then helped Moreirense win promotion back to Portugal's Primeira Liga in the 2022/23 season.

Atlanta United signed him on a free transfer in July 2024, handing him a deal through the 2026 MLS season with a club option for 2027. He made an immediate mark, starting 15 of his 16 appearances that first year and contributing eight assists from full-back. This season he has featured seven times in MLS play plus three cup appearances for the Georgia club.

Should the transfer go through, Amador would become Hapoel Beer Sheva's fifth arrival of the summer window and only their second import, after Brazilian winger João Victor, who joined in a reported €1.7 million deal. Goalkeeper Marco Wolff, defender Itay Rotman and midfielder Niv Yehoshua have also joined this window, per Sport5.

The rebuild comes from a position of strength. Manager Ran Kozhuk led Beer Sheva to their sixth championship in club history this past season, beating Maccabi Tel Aviv 4-2 in the title-deciding match, and has since signed on for two more years in the dugout — giving him a mandate to reshape the squad for a season that will likely include continental football.

None of this has been confirmed yet by either club. Sport5's report describes the deal as imminent rather than done, and there has been no statement from Hapoel Beer Sheva or Atlanta United on Amador's future as of Wednesday.

He joined Atlanta United on a free transfer in July 2024 (deal through 2026, club option for 2027) and has 7 league plus 3 cup appearances this season.
If completed, the move would be Hapoel Beer Sheva's fifth signing of the summer and second foreign recruit, after Brazilian winger João Victor.

title: 14 Age-Group Records Fall at Israel's Youth Swimming Championship
dek: Nearly 900 swimmers raced over five days as Michal Oguinetz swept every individual freestyle title on offer and Maccabi Rishon LeZion topped the club standings.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 — 14 שיאי גילאים באליפות הארץ לנוער בשחייה

body: Israel's national youth swimming championship closed on Tuesday after five days of racing, and by the time the final relay touched the wall, 14 age-group records had fallen — four set by individuals, ten more in relay events. Sport5 reports the meet drew close to 900 swimmers, roughly 5% more than last year's edition, making it one of the larger fixtures on the country's age-group calendar.

The standout individual performer was Michal Oguinetz of Hapoel Beit Shemesh. The 14-year-old broke the national age-14 record in the 100m freestyle and, per Sport5, swept all four individual freestyle titles on offer in her age group — the 50m, 100m, 200m and 400m. It continued a strong summer for Oguinetz, who according to Israel's swimming portal isrswimming.com also lowered national age-14 marks in the 50m and 100m freestyle at the Mediterranean cadet championships (COMEN) last month.
Adi Maoz of Maccabi Rishon LeZion supplied the other headline individual swim, taking the age-13 record in the 100m backstroke in 1:07.15, Sport5 reported.

Omer Shani of Maccabi Rehovot broke the age-14 mark in the 50m breaststroke, and Dor Weiss of TLV Swim closed out the individual honors with the age-15 record over 1500m freestyle, stopping the clock at 15:48.19 — by far the longest individual test of the championship.

Relays did the heavy lifting on the record sheet, accounting for ten of the 14 marks broken, several of them in mixed events. AS Ramat Hasharon set the pace with five relay records across different age groups, Sport5 said, while Maccabi Rehovot, Maccabi Kiryat Bialik, Maccabi Rishon LeZion and Maccabi Ramat Gan each contributed one of their own.

In the overall club standings, Maccabi Rishon LeZion finished on top with 4,264 points, ahead of Maccabi Ramat Gan on 3,686 and Maccabi Haifa on 3,446 — a result that lines up neatly with Adi Maoz's individual record for the winning club.

The championship doubled as a reminder of the pipeline feeding Israeli swimming's senior ranks. Sport5 noted that three of the competitors — Ofir Simcha and Sean Wornowkov of Maccabi Kiryat Bialik, and Mark Teller of Maccabi Ramat Gan — had only recently returned from the European Junior Swimming Championships in Munich, which ran July 7–12, before lining up again on home soil days later.

For a domestic age-group meet, that kind of overlap with a continental championship says something about the depth Israeli swimming is building beneath its senior team, and it is the backdrop against which this week's record haul should be read: a season capped not by one standout swim, but by a broad spread of clubs and age groups pushing the national record book at once.

title: Brazili accuses Almeida of exploiting his 'willingness to fight' after Brazilian misses weight by 15kg
dek: Israeli MMA prospect Eilai Brazili says Lucas Almeida arrived in Israel well over the agreed limit ahead of Monday's Tel Aviv headliner, calling it disrespectful to him and to local fans.
body: Eilai Brazili is unbeaten in seven professional fights and about to headline in his own country for the first time — but the build-up to Monday's bout at the Menora Mivtachim Arena in Tel Aviv has been dominated not by the fight itself, but by his opponent's scales.

Speaking to ONE ahead of the card, the Israeli fighter said Brazilian opponent Lucas Almeida arrived in the country roughly 15 kilograms over the agreed fight weight. "This is the greatest disrespect there is — you show up 15 kilos over the permitted weight," Brazili said, adding that he still expected Almeida to have a significant amount left to cut before fight night.

"He's exploiting my willingness to fight in order to gain an advantage," Brazili told the outlet, framing the weight discrepancy as a deliberate ploy rather than a simple miscalculation. He said the situation was disrespectful both to him personally and to the Israeli fans who bought tickets to see a fair contest.

Brazili didn't hide his confidence about how he expects the fight itself to unfold, predicting that Almeida's weight-cutting troubles will catch up with him in the cage. "He'll pay a heavy price for this — I'll tire him out and finish him in the first round," he said.

The bout is part of a 14-fight card organized by the Gordon brothers, with organizers expecting a crowd of more than 10,000 at the arena — a notable scale for an MMA event on Israeli soil and, according to ONE, the biggest stage of Brazili's career to date as he headlines at home for the first time.

Brazili will have elite company in his corner. Jean Silva, currently ranked sixth in the UFC's featherweight division and Brazili's training partner at the Fighting Nerds gym in Brazil, is traveling to Israel to work his corner for the fight. Silva has previously spoken about his affection for Israel and its people, and his presence carries extra weight given he is making the trip during what ONE and Sport5 both describe as a sensitive security period.

Away from the build-up talk, Brazili also touched on a personal moment: a meeting with actor and singer Idan Amedi, the "Fauda" star and IDF reservist who was seriously wounded during reserve duty in Gaza. "Yes, we met — he's inspiring," Brazili said of the encounter.

Lucas Almeida, a Brazilian fighter with UFC experience, has not yet publicly responded to Brazili's comments. ONE's report reflects Brazili's account of the weigh-in situation; the final numbers will only be confirmed at the official weigh-ins closer to fight night.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem's Women Open Israel's Champions League History Against PAOK
dek: Fresh off their first-ever Israeli title, Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem face Greek champions PAOK today in Veria in a knockout semi-final that opens Israel's first-ever appearance in the Women's Champions League.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com — Women's Champions League first qualifying round starts 22 July

body: Israeli women's football steps onto a European stage for the first time this evening, when Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem face PAOK Thessaloniki in Veria, Greece, in a knockout tie that decides who advances in the club's debut UEFA Women's Champions League campaign.

Kick-off is 17:30 CEST (18:30 Israel time) at the Veria Municipal Stadium, roughly 75 kilometres from PAOK's home city, with the Greek champions standing as the clear obstacle between Jerusalem and a place in the next round of the competition's opening qualifying stage.

The tie is one half of a four-team mini-tournament format UEFA uses at this level. Neftçi Baku of Azerbaijan met Montenegro's Budućnost Podgorica in the other semi-final earlier in the day, also in Veria. The two winners will meet in Saturday's final on July 25, with the beaten semi-finalists playing off for third place the same afternoon — Hapoel's reward for advancing would be another shot at reaching the competition's league phase; defeat would still leave a consolation match to close out the trip.

Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem arrive in Greece as newly minted champions of Israel. The club, formed as a senior women's side only in 2020 and built from the fan-owned Hapoel Jerusalem project, won the 2025–26 Israeli Women's Premier League — its first top-flight title after three straight runner-up finishes — and that breakthrough is what has carried it into continental competition for the first time.

According to ONE, manager Tsach Shamroni has treated the build-up with the seriousness the occasion demands, having his staff review eight full recordings of PAOK matches and running double training sessions through a three-week preparation camp before flying the squad to Greece.
"We arrive with the goal of winning," Shamroni said, per ONE's report. "Currently all focus is solely on PAOK."

The 18-player squad for the trip includes several new signings brought in to strengthen the group for its European debut — goalkeeper Daniela Solera, defender Tal Feingesicht and midfielder Ella Ben-Tzvi among them, with a forward listed by the outlet as Reyza also part of the squad, though the transliteration of that name could not be independently confirmed.

Missing from the group is Doris Boaduwaa, the Ghanaian forward who was central to Hapoel's title-winning campaign. She is on international duty instead, part of Ghana's Black Queens squad preparing for the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, which kicks off on July 25 — the same day Hapoel's own mini-tournament in Veria concludes.

PAOK, by contrast, are established regulars on this stage, having represented Greece in Women's Champions League qualifying for several seasons running, which makes Jerusalem's task in its first continental fixture a genuinely difficult one against a side with far more European pedigree.

Whatever happens on the pitch tonight, Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem have already made history simply by getting here — the first Israeli women's team ever to compete in a UEFA Women's Champions League qualifying tie, a landmark for a club that only fielded its senior side for the first time six years ago.

title: Neymar trades the pitch for the poker table while Santos fly to Venezuela
dek: Rested by Santos for a Copa Sudamericana trip to Caracas, the Brazilian forward turned up at a São Paulo poker tournament instead — reviving questions about his commitment as his career winds down after Brazil's World Cup exit.

verificationSources.label: ONE — הבלוף של ניימאר: מחזרה למגרש, אל שולחן הפוקר
