title: Kangwa scores but Beersheba fall to Vikingur in Champions League opener
dek: The Zambian striker's second-half equaliser wasn't enough as Reykjavik struck twice, leaving Israel's champions needing a comeback in next week's return leg.
body: Hapoel Beersheba's return to the Champions League got off to a painful start on Tuesday night, as the Israeli champions went down 2-1 away to Vikingur Reykjavik in the first leg of their second qualifying round tie in Iceland.

Nikolaj Hansen struck twice for the Icelandic champions, either side of a second-half leveller from Kings Kangwa, to hand Vikingur the advantage heading into next week's return fixture, which Sport5 reports will be played in Hungary rather than at Beersheba's usual home ground.

Kangwa pulled Beersheba level shortly after the interval, continuing the sharp scoring form that has made him the club's talisman over the past two seasons. It was not enough, though, as Hansen's second goal, deep in the second half, restored Vikingur's lead and ultimately won them the first leg.

According to Sport5, Kangwa posted a short message after the final whistle pledging that Beersheba would give everything in the second leg, telling supporters the team would fight to turn the tie around next week.

Head coach Ran Kozuk was quoted by the outlet acknowledging the difficulty of facing what he called a well-drilled, quality Vikingur side playing in their 15th season in this format, but stressed the equation was now simple: Beersheba must win next week to advance.

The defeat is a setback for a Beersheba side that enters the new season on the back of a Israeli Premier League title, but the tie is far from over — away goals and a full 90 minutes remain to close the gap.

Kangwa's evening continues a turbulent summer for the 26-year-old, whose future has been the subject of persistent transfer speculation, including reported interest from AEK Athens. For now, though, his focus and his goals remain firmly with Beersheba's European campaign.

title: Maccabi Haifa Goalkeeper Kayouf Ruptures Achilles Before Season Even Starts
dek: An MRI confirmed the worst for Sharif Kayouf after he was helped off the pitch in a preseason rout by Hapoel Kfar Saba, ending — for now — his hopes of a move to Hapoel Ramat Gan.
body: Maccabi Haifa's preseason has taken a grim turn. Goalkeeper Sharif Kayouf tore his Achilles tendon in Tuesday's friendly against Hapoel Kfar Saba, a match Haifa lost heavily, 5-0, according to Sport5.

Kayouf needed assistance from the club's medical staff to leave the field after going down, and the initial fears were confirmed by an MRI scan showing a full tendon rupture, Sport5 reported. He will now require surgery and is expected to miss the entire season before a competitive ball has even been kicked.

The injury lands at an awkward moment for the 25-year-old. Sport5 reports he had spent several weeks waiting for Maccabi Haifa's clearance to join Hapoel Ramat Gan, a move now thrown into doubt by the severity of the injury.
Kayouf was not the only casualty of the friendly. Brazilian defender Pedrão also picked up a knock during the first half and was withdrawn, replaced by Eder Gaitán, per the same report.

Kayouf, from the Druze town of Isfiya, has been part of Maccabi Haifa's setup since signing his first professional contract with the club in 2019, working his way up through loan spells at Hapoel Kfar Shalem and Hapoel Afula before establishing himself as a squad goalkeeper in the Israeli Premier League. He has also represented Israel at youth level through the U21s.

With Kayouf sidelined long-term, Haifa will need to sort out its goalkeeping options before the competitive season begins — one more problem to manage after a lopsided defeat in a match that was supposed to be about building form, not losing personnel.

title: Versano Breaks Israeli U18 Hurdles Record as Afrifah Completes Sprint Double in Jerusalem
dek: Hila Versano set a new national under-18 mark in the 400m hurdles and Marcy Afrifah swept the 100m and 200m as the Israeli Athletics Championship closed out at Givat Ram Stadium.

verificationSources.label: Israel Athletics Association (IAA) — youth/cadets championship coverage

body: Jerusalem's Givat Ram Stadium closed out the Israeli Athletics Championship on Tuesday with two of the meet's sharpest storylines saved for last: a national under-18 record from Hila Versano and a sprint double from Marcy Afrifah.
Versano, who runs for Maccabi Tel Aviv, clocked 59.53 seconds in the women's 400m hurdles to break the Israeli record for girls under 18. She crossed the line second overall in the race itself.

The race went to Noa Levi, the country's dominant 400m hurdler of recent seasons, who won comfortably. ONE's report puts her winning time at 48.82 seconds — a figure that would obliterate the world record and is almost certainly a misprint — so we're not repeating that number here pending confirmation from the Israel Athletics Association.

None of that takes away from Versano's night. Breaking a national age-group record while finishing runner-up to an established senior champion is exactly the kind of result that points to genuine depth building behind Israel's top hurdlers.

In the sprints, Marcy Afrifah completed a clean double over 100m and 200m. ONE did not report her winning time in the 100m, but in the 200m she held off rival Alina Drotman for the second time this season, stopping the clock at 24.19 seconds.

Afrifah, who also competes for Maccabi Tel Aviv, is the younger sister of Blessing Afrifah, Israel's European U23 200m champion and a 2024 Olympian — sprinting pedigree that now runs through the family.

The men's 200m went to Gal Ard in 20.68 seconds, while the long jump produced the day's most dramatic finish: Yishai Efraimov trailed for most of the competition before leaping 7.66m on his sixth and final attempt to overtake both Eden Sela and Nikita Mirkin, who had each reached 7.44m.

Romi Tamir added a jumps double of her own, following her long jump title with gold in the triple jump at 13.12m. Noam Mamo took the men's 800m in 1:53.50, and Kroan Halabi-Kabalan closed out a distance double, backing up Monday's 1,500m win with victory in the women's 800m in 2:07.09.
For Israeli track and field, though, it's Versano's mark that will carry furthest — a new bar for the country's under-18 hurdlers, set on the biggest stage the domestic calendar offers.

title: Partizan Belgrade joins Hapoel Jerusalem in race for Wendell Moore Jr.
dek: The Serbian giant is chasing the free-agent forward as a replacement for the departed Sterling Brown, putting it in direct competition with Hapoel Jerusalem for the 24-year-old NBA journeyman.
body: Hapoel Jerusalem's pursuit of Wendell Moore Jr. just got more complicated. ONE reports that Partizan Belgrade has entered the race for the 24-year-old American forward, turning what looked like a straightforward Israeli signing into a competitive chase.

Hapoel Jerusalem had already flagged Moore as a target for the coming season, according to the report. Now the Serbian EuroLeague power wants him too, and Partizan carries obvious pull: bigger stage, bigger money, and the promise of Europe's top continental competition.

Partizan's interest is not just a rumor picked up second-hand. The Belgrade sports outlet FanSport reported separately that the club sees Moore as its primary target to replace Sterling Brown, the guard-forward who left Partizan over the summer. FanSport described Moore as a modern, multi-positional defender who thrives in transition — exactly the profile Partizan is said to be missing on the wing.

Moore, 1.96 meters tall, arrives with a real basketball pedigree even if his NBA career never quite settled. He won the Julius Erving Award as college basketball's top small forward in 2022, capping a breakout junior season at Duke in which he averaged 13.4 points, 5.3 rebounds and 4.4 assists while shooting 50 percent from the field.

The Dallas Mavericks took him 26th overall in the 2022 NBA Draft, but he never played for them — he was dealt to the Houston Rockets as part of the Christian Wood trade before the season even began, then moved again to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Since then Moore has bounced between rosters and two-way deals, appearing for the Detroit Pistons, the Charlotte Hornets and the Boston Celtics, with stints in the G League for the Iowa Wolves, the Greensboro Swarm and the Maine Celtics. That path — flashes of promise, no fixed NBA home — is precisely why he is now available to European suitors.

For Hapoel Jerusalem, adding a defender of Moore's draft pedigree and college accolades would be a statement signing ahead of a season in which the club will again try to compete on multiple fronts domestically and in the EuroCup. Losing him to Partizan, by contrast, would be a reminder of how often Israeli clubs find themselves outbid once a bigger European name joins the conversation.
Nothing is finalized. Both interests are still at the reported stage, and Moore remains unsigned as talks are believed to continue on more than one front.

As of this report, Moore is unsigned and no agreement with either Hapoel Jerusalem or Partizan has been announced.

title: Chelsea complete British transfer-record signing of Morgan Rogers
dek: The England international leaves Aston Villa for £117 million, becoming the most expensive player in British football history and Chelsea's costliest ever signing.
body: Chelsea have officially completed the signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117 million, ONE reported, a fee that makes the 23-year-old England international the most expensive player in British football history.

The deal also becomes Chelsea's own record purchase, surpassing the £115 million they paid Brighton for Moises Caicedo in 2023, and was confirmed by the club itself in an official statement on chelseafc.com rather than left as unconfirmed transfer talk.

"I'm so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid," Rogers said in Chelsea's announcement. "I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading."
Rogers has signed a long-term contract running to 2033, tying him to Stamford Bridge for years to come as Chelsea continue to build a young, high-ceiling squad around head coach Xabi Alonso.

Sky Sports and ESPN, both reporting the same £117 million figure, noted that Rogers had also been a top target for Arsenal but ultimately opted for Chelsea, with Alonso's project said to be a decisive factor in his decision.

At Villa, Rogers will be remembered for a remarkable rise: signed from Middlesbrough in 2024 for a fraction of his eventual sale price, he broke through under Unai Emery and became one of the Premier League's most productive attacking midfielders.
In the 2025-26 season alone he scored 14 goals and added 12 assists in 55 appearances, helping Villa qualify for the Champions League while also lifting the Europa League trophy.

At Chelsea, Rogers reunites with Cole Palmer, a former teammate from their days together in Manchester City's academy, giving Alonso two attacking players with a shared history at the heart of his rebuild.

Rogers has become a regular fixture for England since his senior debut in November 2024, winning 22 caps and featuring for the Three Lions at this summer's World Cup, including appearances against Ghana and Panama.
The size of the fee has already stirred debate in the English game over transfer inflation, but for Chelsea it underlines the scale of their ambition under Alonso heading into the 2026/27 season.

title: Ronaldo Likes Instagram Post Accusing FIFA of Rigging World Cup for Argentina
dek: Days after Portugal's own elimination, Cristiano Ronaldo's verified account liked a Spanish TV clip branding FIFA a "mafia" that favored Lionel Messi's Argentina all the way to the final.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo's World Cup ended in Dallas on July 6, beaten by the country that would go on to lift the trophy itself. Two weeks later he was back in the headlines anyway, not for anything he did on a pitch but for what his thumb did on Instagram.

Ronaldo's verified account liked a video post from the Spanish breakfast show Espejo Público, aired on Antena 3, that accused FIFA of tilting the tournament in Argentina's favor and openly floated the idea of institutional corruption at the sport's governing body.

The clip centered on remarks from journalist Pilar Rodríguez Losantos, who told viewers "Argentina should have been eliminated at least five matches ago," and suggested FIFA president Gianni Infantino's organization wanted to see the trophy handed to Lionel Messi.
Fellow panelist Rubén Amón went further on air, describing FIFA as "a mafia organization, shameful and corrupt" in his assessment of how the tournament had been managed.

The segment aired in the buildup to the final, but Ronaldo's like registered publicly only after Argentina's run actually ended — a coincidence of timing that turned an obscure Spanish talk-show clip into a global talking point almost overnight.

Ronaldo's own tournament had already finished in the round of 16, where Spain beat Portugal 1-0 at Dallas Stadium on a stoppage-time strike from substitute Mikel Merino — a defeat widely described as the last World Cup match of Ronaldo's international career.

Argentina, defending champions from 2022, made it all the way to the final only to fall to the same opponent. Spain won 1-0 after extra time in New Jersey on July 19, Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute as Emiliano Martínez made a record 11 saves in a losing effort. Messi, playing what is expected to be his last World Cup final, left the field in tears after collecting his runner-up medal.

FIFA has not addressed the specific Instagram post, but tournament refereeing chief Pierluigi Collina has previously dismissed suggestions of bias in officiating decisions during the tournament, and Argentina defender Lisandro Martínez said he found the standard of officiating "excellent."

No evidence has surfaced to support claims that matches were manipulated in Argentina's favor. Ronaldo has not commented publicly on the like, and a single tap on a post is not proof he endorses every claim within it — but given the long rivalry between him and Messi, and the raw nerve still exposed after Sunday's final, the gesture was enough to set off a fresh round of debate across football social media.

No evidence has emerged to substantiate the corruption or match-fixing claims referenced in the post Ronaldo liked.

title: Modrić agrees new Milan deal, signing off on retirement talk for now
dek: The 40-year-old Croatian is set to formally extend his stay at San Siro through June 2027, Italian and Israeli outlets report, days after Croatia's World Cup exit.

body: Luka Modrić is not done yet. AC Milan's 40-year-old midfield metronome has agreed to extend his stay at San Siro for another season, ONE reports, with the formal signing expected within days.

Citing transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano and Italian sources, ONE says Modrić has agreed a new one-year deal that will run until June 2027 — closing, for now, the retirement speculation that had trailed him since Croatia's exit from the World Cup.

Italian outlets including SempreMilan and Yahoo Sports, drawing on reporting from MilanNews and Fabrizio Romano, say the extension keeps Modrić's terms broadly unchanged from last season: roughly €3.5 million a year plus performance bonuses.
The new contract is expected to be put on paper this week, with several reports pointing to Wednesday as the likely signing date.

Modrić joined Milan as a free agent last summer after 13 years at Real Madrid, where he became one of the most decorated midfielders of his generation, winning the Champions League repeatedly and the 2018 Ballon d'Or.

His first season in Serie A produced 37 appearances across all competitions, with two goals and three assists, a workload interrupted at times by a jaw injury but otherwise a rare show of durability for a player who turned 40 in September.

The renewal comes just weeks after Croatia's run at the 2026 World Cup ended in the round of 32, beaten 2-1 by Portugal — a result that reopened questions about how much longer Modrić intends to keep playing at the top level, at club and country alike.

For Milan, locking down their captain-in-all-but-name for a second season answers at least one of those questions: whatever he ultimately decides about international football, the Rossoneri will have him running their midfield again in 2026-27.

title: Another suspect held over grenade attack on restaurant chain owned by Beitar Jerusalem's owner
dek: A man in his 20s from Bat Yam was arrested and taken in for questioning over a stun grenade thrown at a Japanika branch linked to Beitar Jerusalem owner Barak Abramov, the latest arrest in a wider wave of attacks tied to a criminal turf war.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — Abramov: violence won't affect Beitar
Walla — arrest in Kiryat Ono grenade probe

body: Police have arrested another suspect in the investigation into a wave of grenade and gun attacks on branches of the Japanika restaurant chain owned by Beitar Jerusalem's controlling owner, Barak Abramov, ONE reports.

The suspect, a man in his 20s from Bat Yam, was detained by the Central Unit of the Tel Aviv Police District and transferred for questioning at the district's headquarters, according to the report. He is suspected of throwing a stun grenade at the Japanika branch in Kiryat Ono in the early hours of July 13.

Police told ONE he is due before the Tel Aviv Magistrate's Court, where detectives will ask for his remand to be extended while the investigation continues. Officers said the probe is ongoing and that "all investigative directions are being examined." As is standard practice before any indictment, his name has not been released.

The Kiryat Ono incident is one of more than a dozen attacks reported against Japanika branches across the country since early July, according to Israeli media, with grenades thrown at outlets in Ramat Gan, Afula, Netanya, Givatayim and Rosh Pina and gunfire directed at the chain's Herzliya branch. Several suspects, including an alleged crime organisation leader, have already been arrested over the wider wave.

Japanika is the restaurant chain built and controlled by Abramov, who consolidated it and other ventures into his Andorra Investments Group before completing his takeover of Beitar Jerusalem in August 2022, buying the club after previously owning second-tier side Bnei Yehuda.

Investigators believe the attacks stem from a feud between rival crime organisations rather than any dispute involving Abramov personally, and have described him as a victim of the campaign rather than a suspect.

Abramov has sought to reassure Beitar's fan base as the case has unfolded, telling Ynet that "we are confident that recent events will not affect the club, and that nothing will spill over into Beitar's path in the league and in Europe."
With further arrests already made and the court process for this latest suspect still ahead, police say the investigation into who ordered and carried out the attacks remains active.

title: Naor Barkol Leaves Youth Ranks Behind to Coach Holon Yermiyahu
dek: After more than a decade exclusively in youth football, the Holon-born coach takes his first senior job at Liga Alef South side Holon Yermiyahu.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Naor Barkol appointed Holon Yermiyahu coach
ONE archive - Mousa Ben-Haim's history with Holon Yermiyahu

body: Naor Barkol is coming home. The 39-year-old, who spent more than a decade coaching only in youth departments, has been named head coach of Liga Alef South club Holon Yermiyahu for the coming season, ONE reports — his first senior job at adult level.

Barkol is a Holon native through and through. He came up as a central defender in the youth ranks of Tzafririm Holon and went on to play for the club's adult team, before injury forced him into early retirement at 27 — the moment he pivoted into coaching, starting out in that same Tzafririm Holon youth department.

His most recent post was in charge of MS Ashdod's youth team, a job that ended abruptly and, by his own account, mysteriously. "To this day I don't know how to put my finger on the reasons that led to my dismissal," he said, referring to a departure that reportedly came a day after his side won 1-0 away to Ramat Hasharon. Before Ashdod, he had coached Ramat Hasharon's own U-17 side.

Now he is stepping up. "After so many years in the youth departments, I feel I've exhausted that chapter," Barkol said. "I see the opportunity I've been given as a springboard to the higher levels of Israeli football."

Holon Yermiyahu are preparing for their tenth consecutive season in Liga Alef South. The club, founded in 2014 and renamed in 2017 in honour of Holon playing great and former assistant coach Haim "HaSilon" Yirmiyahu, finished last season's shortened campaign in mid-table — and the ambitions are rising this time around.
Club owner Lior Shulman and sporting director Mousa Ben-Haim, who has his own long history with the club as both player and coach, brought Barkol in to lead the new project.
His bench will include two more former players: assistant coach Haim Pontormeli and goalkeeping coach Doron Rosenkovich round out the staff, per the club's presentation of the new setup.
"We're building a team with high aspirations," Barkol said. "We are choosing players for the squad carefully, and holding on to the ones we're very satisfied with."

title: Duarte penalty puts Abu Fani's Red Star ahead of Larne in Champions League qualifier
dek: Israel midfielder Mohammed Abu Fani started as Crvena Zvezda led Larne 1-0 early in the second half of their Champions League second qualifying round first leg in Northern Ireland, Bruno Duarte converting a VAR-awarded penalty.

verificationSources.label: ONE — live match report, Larne v Red Star Belgrade, penalty and minute-by-minute detail
Sports Mole — fixture preview confirming venue, kick-off, Tre Fiori qualifying path and Arnautović's return

body: Mohammed Abu Fani took his first competitive step onto the European stage for Red Star Belgrade on Tuesday, starting in central midfield as the Serbian champions led Larne 1-0 shortly into the second half of their Champions League second qualifying round first leg at Inver Park.

The only goal, and the one Red Star carried into the interval, came from the penalty spot. In the 26th minute the referee stopped play to check an incident on the pitchside monitor and pointed to the spot; Bruno Duarte stepped up and side-footed his effort low into the bottom corner, sending the visitors in front.
As of the 47th minute — the point this report captures — Red Star's lead remained intact, with the tie still live for Larne on home soil and the second half only just under way.

For Abu Fani, this was his first taste of continental football in Red Star colours, coming five days after he played every minute of the club's 5-0 SuperLiga-opening rout of Mačva Šabac — his first appearance since arriving from Ferencváros in June on a deal Serbian outlets valued at around €1m over three years.

The Israel international has quickly become a fixture in Dejan Stanković's midfield plans. After the Mačva game, the head coach said Abu Fani, still working back to full sharpness, had his "blessing" to lose the ball occasionally given the calm and control he brings to Red Star's build-up play.

Larne arrived at this stage having never before reached a Champions League second qualifying round tie in the club's history. The Northern Irish side eliminated San Marino's Tre Fiori in the first round, winning 1-0 away on 7 July and 2-1 at home a week later, to earn Tuesday's visit from one of European football's most decorated clubs.

Red Star, chasing a place in the competition's league phase for the third time in four seasons, arrive as clear favourites, having retained the Serbian SuperLiga title last season by a ten-point margin. Austria forward Marko Arnautović also featured for the visitors, back in club colours days after his country's run at the 2026 World Cup.

The tie moves to Belgrade for the second leg next week, with Red Star defending a 1-0 lead at the Rajko Mitić Stadium — without the cushion of an away-goals rule UEFA scrapped in 2021, meaning a single Larne goal in the return fixture would level the tie again.

title: Hapoel Be'er Sheva Held Scoreless in Reykjavik as Champions League Qualifier Nears Half-Time
dek: Israel's reigning champions were locked at 0-0 with Víkingur Reykjavík 44 minutes into the first leg of their Champions League second qualifying-round tie, the clubs' first-ever meeting.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com — Víkingur R. vs H. Beer-Sheva match page
Sport1/Maariv — Kozuk on João Victor injury

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva's hopes of taking a foothold in their bid for a first-ever Champions League campaign proper were still alive but unresolved deep into the first half in Reykjavik on Tuesday, with Israel's champions locked at 0-0 against Víkingur Reykjavík 44 minutes into their Champions League second qualifying-round opener, ONE reported from the Icelandic capital.

It is the first competitive meeting between the two clubs. Víkingur are hosting the first leg on their compact, artificial-turf ground at Víkingsvöllur; the return fixture follows next week at Turner Stadium in Be'er Sheva. The aggregate winner advances to the third qualifying round, one tie away from the Champions League's league phase, while the loser is dropped into Europa League qualifying.

Hapoel arrive in Iceland as Israel's freshly restored champions, having ended an eight-year wait for the title in May under coach Ran Kozuk. Their build-up to Europe, however, was jolted by a defeat in the traditional season-opening Super Cup meeting against Maccabi Tel Aviv, who won that fixture 3-1, according to Ynet and Sport1. "Disappointing — I expected a lot more," Kozuk said afterwards, per Ynet.

That match also cost Hapoel their marquee summer arrival. João Victor, the Brazilian defender signed for a reported €1.7 million, went down with what the club fears is a significant hamstring tear after coming on as a stoppage-time substitute. ONE reports he is expected to be sidelined for roughly one to one-and-a-half months. "It doesn't look promising, but we'll wait for the tests and hope for the best," Kozuk said, according to Sport1-Maariv.

Víkingur are no pushovers at home. Iceland's reigning champions needed two legs to see off Hungary's Győr, winning 3-2 on aggregate in the first qualifying round, and they have lost just once in their last eight matches on home soil across all competitions. Their squad includes the well-travelled Gylfi Sigurðsson, formerly of Tottenham and Everton, alongside forward Nikolai Hansen.

Neither side had broken through by the midpoint of the first half, leaving the tie finely poised heading into the second period in Reykjavík — and, whatever the final score in Iceland, into next week's second leg in the Negev.

title: Argentina and Spain reportedly closing in on a November Finalissima rematch in Qatar
dek: Weeks after their dramatic World Cup final, ONE reports that advanced talks are underway to finally stage the long-delayed Finalissima between Europe's and South America's champions at Lusail Stadium.

verificationSources.label: World Soccer Talk — new date reported for Argentina-Spain Finalissima
ESPN — Spain 1-0 Argentina, 2026 World Cup final report

body: Argentina and Spain were denied a proper decider in March, when politics and logistics got in the way of a match nobody wanted to miss. Fate paired them anyway five weeks ago in the World Cup final. Now, according to ONE, the two federations are back at the table trying to finish the job: advanced negotiations are reportedly underway to finally stage the postponed Finalissima in November, at the very stadium where it was originally supposed to happen.

The Finalissima pits the reigning European champion against the reigning South American champion — Spain qualify as winners of Euro 2024, Argentina as holders of the Copa América 2024 crown they won in the tournament's 2022 revival against Italy at Wembley. This latest edition was first pencilled in for 27 March 2026 at Lusail Stadium in Qatar, the same arena where Argentina beat France on penalties to win the 2022 World Cup.

That fixture never happened. Qatar suspended sporting activity after missile strikes hit Iran in late February, forcing organisers to scramble for a new venue. UEFA and Spain's federation pushed for Real Madrid's Bernabéu; CONMEBOL and Argentina's federation wanted Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental instead. The two sides could not agree, and the match was scrapped in mid-March.

Football supplied its own resolution regardless. Spain and Argentina met at the World Cup itself on 19 July at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, with Ferran Torres settling a goalless, suffocating final in the 106th minute of extra time to hand Spain their second World Cup title and end Lionel Messi's tournament in near silence.

That result, ONE notes, is exactly why the appetite for a genuine Finalissima has not gone away. Per Argentine media reports picked up by ONE, and first flagged by ESPN Argentina's Martín Arévalo, Qatar's government has already moved to reacquire hosting rights for a November staging, with Lusail again the leading candidate venue.

Nothing here is official yet. Neither UEFA nor CONMEBOL, nor the Spanish or Argentine federations, have confirmed a date, and ONE is careful to frame this as negotiations at an advanced stage rather than a done deal — a distinction that matters given the same fixture collapsed once before over exactly this kind of logistical wrangle.

For Argentina, the calculus is also personal. If Messi keeps playing into the back end of the year, a November date at Lusail would hand him one more shot at silverware with the national team, on the same ground where he lifted the World Cup in 2022 — a full-circle occasion the Argentine press has already begun to build around him.

Spain, for their part, have barely paused for breath since East Rutherford; Madrid gave the squad a homecoming parade before nearly two million people this week. A rematch so soon after such a tight final would arrive with genuine stakes attached, not just ceremony, and explains why a report with no official confirmation behind it has still travelled as far and as fast as it has.
facts: ONE reports, citing Argentine media, that advanced negotiations are underway to stage a Finalissima between Spain and Argentina in November 2026, with Lusail Stadium in Qatar the leading venue.
Qatar's government has reportedly already moved to reacquire hosting rights for the fixture, according to the report relayed by ONE and first sourced to ESPN Argentina's Martín Arévalo.

The Finalissima was originally scheduled for 27 March 2026 at Lusail Stadium but was cancelled after Qatar suspended sporting activity following missile strikes on Iran, and UEFA/Spain (who wanted the Bernabéu) and CONMEBOL/Argentina (who wanted the Estadio Monumental) could not agree on an alternative venue.

Spain and Argentina met anyway in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final on 19 July at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey; Spain won 1-0 after Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute of extra time, giving Spain their second World Cup title.
Neither UEFA, CONMEBOL, the RFEF nor the AFA has officially confirmed a November Finalissima date as of this report.
The Finalissima is contested between the reigning UEFA European champion (Spain, Euro 2024) and the reigning CONMEBOL Copa América champion (Argentina, 2024).

title: Shuki Nagar Named Professional Director at Maccabi Amit Be'er Ya'akov
dek: The well-travelled former Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv defender moves into a new role overseeing football development at the growing central-Israel youth club.
body: Shuki Nagar, whose playing career took him through some of the biggest dressing rooms in Israeli football, has been officially appointed professional director at Maccabi Amit Be'er Ya'akov, the club announced, as reported by ONE.

From next season Nagar will take charge of the club's football department, with a particular focus on the youth ranks, working alongside administrative manager Matan Ben Avu and football-school director Yaakov Bar Shalom.

Nagar, a left back born in 1977, came through the youth system at Beitar/Bnei Yehuda and was widely regarded as one of the country's most promising defenders before injuries slowed his rise. He nonetheless built a long top-flight career, moving to Maccabi Haifa in a reported $450,000 deal and featuring in the club's run to the UEFA Cup quarter-finals in 1998-99.

He went on to play for Hapoel Be'er Sheva, Ashdod, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Beitar Sakhnin and Hapoel Petah Tikva among other sides, picking up an Israel State Cup winner's medal and a Liga Leumit championship along the way, before dropping into the lower divisions later in his career.

After hanging up his boots, Nagar moved into administration, serving as CEO of Maccabi Yavne from 2014 until the club's relegation in 2016, and more recently working as an academy coach and a school sports teacher.

Be'er Ya'akov's deputy mayor, Noam Shasun, welcomed the appointment. "I am delighted to announce Shuki Nagar's joining the club," he said, according to the club's statement carried by ONE. "I wish him great success in his new position, and I am confident that together we will advance the club and continue cultivating the next generation of football talent in Be'er Ya'akov."

Maccabi Amit Be'er Ya'akov, named in memory of a local soldier killed in operational activity, fields a large youth setup alongside a senior team competing in Liga Bet, one of the regional divisions in the Israeli football pyramid. The club has said it also plans to add a new pitch to expand training capacity across its age groups.

For a municipality-backed project still building out its senior football ambitions, landing a coach with Nagar's playing pedigree and administrative experience from Maccabi Yavne is a notable step up in profile, even if the appointment sits well outside the national headlines.

title: Best Attack, Best Defence: M.S. Dimona's Youth Side Sweeps to a Shfela League Title
dek: The Negev club's 2010-born Ne'arim Alef team clinched the regional championship with two rounds to spare, scoring more and conceding fewer than anyone else in the division, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE — M.S. Dimona, Ne'arim Alef, Shfela league report
Israel Football Association — M.S. Dimona club page

body: It is the kind of season a small-town football club waits years for: M.S. Dimona's Ne'arim Alef side, players all born in 2010, sealed the Shfela regional league championship with two full rounds still to play, according to ONE.

The numbers behind the title are as emphatic as the timing. Dimona finished 16 wins, two draws and just two defeats — a success rate above 83 percent — while posting the league's best figures at both ends of the pitch: 73 goals scored, the division's highest tally, against only 23 conceded, its stingiest defence. The title was decided by a three-point margin over the closest challengers, Maccabi Ashkelon and Beitar Kiryat Gat.

Eitan Shabat finished as the league's outright top scorer with 23 goals, while captain Noam Pensporker chipped in seven of his own from a leadership role. Behind them, goalkeeper Shilo Zaguri anchored the meanest back line in the Shfela group.

ONE quotes head coach Rotem Nisan crediting continuity for the runaway campaign: roughly 90 percent of the squad had already played together a year earlier, and the group trained and played intensively — two or three matches most weeks — to chase the title down. Nisan worked alongside assistant coach Lior Sanker throughout the season.

The championship carries a competitive reward beyond the trophy: it lifts Dimona's 2010 age group into a higher tier of youth football for the coming season, a meaningful step up for a club whose youth division has historically operated on modest resources in Israel's south.

It has been a landmark year more broadly for Nisan's work in Dimona. ONE notes he also guided the club's Ne'arim Bet team — the age group below — to the quarter-finals of the State Cup, the furthest any Dimona youth side has advanced in the club's history.

The season's celebrations extended beyond the pitch in Israel: the squad's reward, per ONE, included a trip in which the young players trained alongside FC Barcelona's coaching staff, a rare taste of top-level structure for a group from one of the country's smaller footballing towns.

For a club used to competing on a shoestring against bigger-city academies, a title won with the league's best attack and best defence — and sealed with games still to spare — is as clean a statement as a youth programme can make.

title: Bnei Yehuda pause for Nitzan Shirazi, 12 years after his death
dek: On the day their former player and coach would have turned 55, Bnei Yehuda stopped morning training for a minute of applause and a club statement remembering a man who never left the Hatikva Quarter's heart.

verificationSources.label: ONE — Bnei Yehuda marks 12 years since the death of Nitzan Shirazi
Mako — footballer and coach Nitzan Shirazi has died
BE106 — Eli Levi's staff to continue at Bnei Yehuda into 2026/27

body: Bnei Yehuda broke off morning training on Tuesday for a minute of applause, marking what would have been Nitzan Shirazi's 55th birthday and, with it, 12 years since the club lost one of its own.
Shirazi, who rose from the club's youth ranks to become one of its head coaches, died on July 22, 2014, at Ichilov Hospital in Tel Aviv after a battle with cancer. He was 43.

According to ONE, the club issued a statement describing Shirazi as someone who left an indelible mark on the organisation and on the people who worked alongside him, a presence still felt in the Hatikva Quarter more than a decade on.

Current head coach Eli Levi, who has led the club's first team since being appointed in October, spoke for many at Bnei Yehuda who remember Shirazi personally. "Nitzan was a man of people," Levi said, according to ONE. "He was a professional, a leader, modest and beloved. What I remember most is his smile."

Shirazi's connection to the club ran from childhood. He joined Bnei Yehuda's youth academy at eight years old, worked his way up through the age groups and broke into the senior team at 17, later representing Israel's youth national side.

An injury cut short his playing career, and he moved into coaching, eventually taking charge of Bnei Yehuda's first team. Under him the club reached the 2006 State Cup final and competed in the UEFA Cup, a period still remembered as one of the more ambitious eras in the club's modern history.
He went on to coach Maccabi Petah Tikva and Hapoel Haifa, and in his final post as head coach of Hapoel Tel Aviv he lifted the State Cup in the 2011/12 season, beating Maccabi Haifa 2-1 in the final.
Football ran in the family. Shirazi was the son of Meir Shirazi, a former Bnei Yehuda player and manager, and the club's tribute this week is as much a nod to that lineage as to his own career.

Tuesday's gesture was modest by design: a pause in a routine training session, not a staged ceremony. But for a club that has marked the anniversary in previous years too, it is now part of how Bnei Yehuda keeps Shirazi's memory inside its daily life rather than confined to a single date on the calendar.

title: Evenepoel destroys the clock by Lake Geneva as Lipowitz's Tour ends in the barriers
dek: The world champion tears 28 seconds out of Tadej Pogačar's lead on a lakeside time trial, but the day's cruellest twist is a broken collarbone for his own team leader Florian Lipowitz.

verificationSources.label: Cycling Up To Date — Stage 16 result report
Cycling Up To Date — Stage 16 classifications update
Bike World News — 2026 Tour de France Stage 16 Results
Cyclingnews — Lipowitz abandons after stage 16 crash
Cyclingnews — Biniam Girmay joins NSN Cycling Team
Cycling Weekly — Paul Seixas confirmed for Tour debut

body: The 2026 Tour de France came to the shores of Lake Geneva on Tuesday for its only individual time trial, a 26.1-kilometre dash from the spa town of Évian-les-Bains to neighbouring Thonon-les-Bains, and Remco Evenepoel used it to remind the peloton exactly why he wears the rainbow jersey. The Belgian world time-trial champion covered the course in 32 minutes 19 seconds, carving through the rolling hills above the lake before plunging back to its shore, and beat every rider in the race by at least half a minute.

Only the race leader came close to matching him. Tadej Pogačar, who arrived in Haute-Savoie in yellow with a five-minute cushion, conceded just seven seconds at the first time check but could not hold Evenepoel's pace on the finishing straight, crossing the line 28 seconds down. It was, by the standards Pogačar has set this July, still an excellent ride against the watch — merely not an other-worldly one, which is what Evenepoel produced.

Mattias Skjelmose completed the stage podium for Lidl-Trek, a minute and four seconds off the winning time, underlining a week in which the Dane has quietly kept himself in the mix without ever threatening the top of the classification. Evenepoel's ride was built around the Côte de Larringes, the stage's lone categorised climb, which he is reported to have ascended at close to 37 kilometres an hour — a speed that startled even his own team car.

The stage's defining moment, though, had nothing to do with power numbers. Florian Lipowitz, sharing team leadership at Red Bull-BORA-hansgrohe with Evenepoel and sitting fifth overall, was flying — second-fastest at the third checkpoint — when his back wheel slid from under him on a sharp right-hand bend on the technical descent into Thonon. He slammed into the barriers and abandoned the race clutching his shoulder, in what looked like a broken collarbone. It ends, brutally, the German's Tour and the two-headed gamble his team had built around him and Evenepoel for the final week.

In the overall standings, Pogačar remains exactly where he has been for most of this Tour: in yellow, and comfortably so. The UAE Team Emirates-XRG leader now holds a buffer of 4 minutes 32 seconds over Evenepoel, with his own teenage teammate Isaac del Toro third at 6:51. Paul Seixas, the 19-year-old sensation who became the youngest Tour starter since 1937 when Decathlon CMA CGM lined him up in Barcelona, sits fourth at 7:11, with Juan Ayuso of Lidl-Trek fifth at 9:22.

Pogačar's advantage, battered but intact, sets up an Alpine week in which Evenepoel must find time on the road rather than against the clock — a considerably harder proposition given how this Tour has gone so far. Skjelmose, del Toro and Seixas all remain within striking distance of a final podium spot, and with Lipowitz gone, the fight for the final white-jersey and top-five places has been reshuffled overnight.

Isaac del Toro, the young Mexican who has been one of the revelations of the race, leads the best young rider classification outright, with Seixas 20 seconds back and Ayuso a further 2:31 behind — a white-jersey battle that now doubles as a dress rehearsal for the podium fight above it.

Away from the general classification, Mads Pedersen continues to dominate the points competition for Lidl-Trek, his green jersey secure on 417 points with a 31-point cushion over Jasper Philipsen of Alpecin-Deceuninck and a healthier gap still over Biniam Girmay, now riding for the newly rebranded NSN Cycling Team after his winter move from Intermarché.

The mountains classification tells its own story about this Tour: it is Pogačar, not a specialist climber chasing polka dots for their own sake, who leads it, with 70 points from the peaks he has already shredded the field on. Valentin Paret-Peintre of Soudal Quick-Step and Richard Carapaz of EF Education-EasyPost sit some way back in second and third, both still hoping the high mountains ahead offer a route to snatch the jersey from a man who has no need of it.

With two rest days already banked, on July 13 and again Monday, the race now turns toward its Alpine finale, building to the summit finish at Alpe d'Huez before the traditional procession into Paris on the Champs-Élysées. Tuesday's time trial was billed as Evenepoel's best remaining chance to close the gap on the road; he took a bite out of it, but the size of Pogačar's lead means the Belgian will need considerably more than 28 seconds a day if he is to depose him in the final week.

For Red Bull-BORA-hansgrohe, the day is a study in contrasts: a stage win and a share of the overall podium picture for Evenepoel, set against the abrupt, painful end of Lipowitz's campaign. The team came to this Tour with two genuine leaders and leaves the Alps with one — a reminder of how quickly grand tour fortunes can turn on a wet line through a single bend above a lake.
facts: Stage 16 was a 26.1km individual time trial from Évian-les-Bains to Thonon-les-Bains, raced 21 July 2026.

title: AEK Athens pulls out of Kings Kangwa deal after Beer Sheva refuse to rest him for Vikingur
dek: The Greek club wanted its target left out of Hapoel Be'er Sheva's Champions League qualifier to protect his eligibility for their own European run — when Beer Sheva said no, AEK walked away from a deal that had already been agreed on money.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Beer Sheva travel to Iceland

body: A transfer that looked all but done fell apart in a matter of hours on Tuesday, and the reason had nothing to do with money: AEK Athens has withdrawn its offer for Hapoel Be'er Sheva's Kings Kangwa because the Israeli club would not agree to rest him for a Champions League qualifier.

According to Sport5, which cited the Greek outlet Sport 24, AEK made the sale of Kangwa conditional on him sitting out Beer Sheva's second qualifying round first leg against Iceland's Víkingur on Tuesday evening. Beer Sheva refused, insisted on fielding him regardless, and AEK immediately ended the talks.

The logic behind AEK's demand was procedural rather than football-related. Under UEFA's eligibility rules, a player who appears for one club in a European qualifying round is cup-tied for that competition's later rounds with any other club that same season — so if Kangwa played for Beer Sheva against Víkingur, he would not be able to feature for AEK later in the Champions League.

For AEK, who are building their own continental campaign, that made his availability from day one a priority worth insisting on. For Beer Sheva, giving up their in-form Zambian midfielder on the eve of a European tie they still have to win was a non-starter.

Sport5's report is explicit that the collapse was not about valuation. AEK had already agreed to meet Beer Sheva's asking price for the transfer, and personal terms with Kangwa himself were reportedly finalised. The Víkingur clause was the single sticking point, and it proved fatal.

The saga had been running for weeks, with figures moving as the two clubs negotiated. Earlier reporting had AEK's bids climbing from roughly €2.5 million to offers in the region of €3.5 million plus add-ons, against a Beer Sheva valuation closer to €4 million, while Kangwa's personal terms were said to be worth around €1 million a season.
With the deal now off, Sport5 reports AEK will turn their attention to alternative options for the wing position they had earmarked Kangwa to fill.

For Beer Sheva, the immediate business is football rather than transfer fees. The first leg against Víkingur, the reigning Icelandic champions, is being played on their artificial pitch at Víkingsvöllur, with the return leg in Israel a week later. Kangwa remains part of the squad Ran Kozuk takes into that tie.

The episode is a reminder of how often continental qualifying calendars now collide with the transfer market — a club chasing a signing has to weigh not just the fee, but whether the player can even appear for them once he arrives, and this time that calculation cost AEK a deal it had otherwise all but completed.
facts: AEK Athens has withdrawn its offer for Hapoel Be'er Sheva's Kings Kangwa, according to Sport5 citing the Greek outlet Sport 24.
The deal collapsed after Beer Sheva refused AEK's request to rest Kangwa for their Champions League second qualifying round first leg against Iceland's Víkingur on July 21, 2026.
Under UEFA eligibility rules, playing for Beer Sheva in that qualifying round would have made Kangwa cup-tied and ineligible for AEK's own Champions League campaign this season.
There was reportedly no dispute over the transfer fee or Kangwa's personal terms — AEK had agreed to meet Beer Sheva's asking price and had a wage agreement in place with the player.
AEK will now explore alternative options for the wing position, per the report.
Kangwa remains in Hapoel Be'er Sheva's squad for the tie against Víkingur, reigning champions of Iceland, with the first leg away and the return leg in Israel a week later.

title: Messi's cryptic tunnel speech before World Cup final fuels conspiracy claims against FIFA
dek: A viral clip of Messi telling Argentina to "forget everything" before Sunday's final has fans guessing, while an Argentine journalist alleges — without evidence — that FIFA steered the result toward Spain to help Gianni Infantino win re-election.

verificationSources.label: ESPN — Spain wins World Cup final
Walla Sport — mystery of Messi's speech
ESPN — Slavko Vinčić named final referee

body: Two days after Lionel Messi walked off a World Cup final pitch in tears, in what is widely assumed to be his last appearance at the tournament, Argentina is still picking over Sunday's 1-0 extra-time loss to Spain — and a wild, unproven theory that FIFA rigged it.

The smaller mystery came first. Tunnel footage from before kickoff at MetLife Stadium showed Messi gathering his teammates for one final word, telling them, according to the exact remarks reported by ONE: "Come on guys, stay calm. The most important thing is to keep our composure. Let's forget about everything. Just play. Focus only on the game."

It was the "forget about everything" line that set off a frenzy back home. Clips circulated for hours with fans and pundits asking what exactly Messi wanted his players to put out of their minds, and pointing to Enzo Fernández and Lisandro Martínez, who both appeared visibly emotional in the moments before the whistle, as evidence something heavier than nerves was in the air.

Israeli outlet Walla, which separately covered the clip, reported that Argentine sources close to the squad framed it differently: Messi wasn't addressing dressing-room strife but trying to shut out the noise from Spain's pre-match comments about refereeing, which had reportedly irritated the Argentine camp. Spain won the game 1-0 after extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal in the 106th minute.

Into that emotional vacuum stepped Pablo Carrozza, an Argentine journalist close to AFA president Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia, who went public with a far more serious allegation: that FIFA president Gianni Infantino had reached an understanding with UEFA to ensure a European champion, as ONE reports.

Carrozza's theory, as relayed by ONE, is that Infantino already had CONMEBOL's backing for a second term but needed UEFA's votes too, and that a Spanish title was the price of getting them. It is a serious charge from a well-connected reporter — and, as of now, entirely unsubstantiated. No evidence has been produced, and neither FIFA, UEFA, the Spanish federation nor the AFA has responded to it.

Carrozza reportedly built his case around circumstantial details rather than proof. One is the choice of referee: Slovenian official Slavko Vinčić took charge of the final, a pick that surprised some observers given the well-documented friction this tournament between Infantino and UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin. Argentina, according to the claim, had a poor history with Vinčić, while Spain's experience with him had been more favorable.

Carrozza also pointed to the tournament's individual awards as suspicious, per ONE's report — Spain's Rodri won the Golden Ball as the competition's outstanding player, ahead of Messi, who took the Silver Ball, and Kylian Mbappé, who was awarded the Bronze Ball. Mbappé also picked up his second career Golden Boot after starting France's third-place match, which England won 6-4. Both awards were decided by FIFA's technical panel, and nothing has surfaced to suggest their legitimacy is actually in question.

A further claim attributed to Carrozza — that Argentina were whistled for 24 fouls to Spain's 19 yet picked up five yellow cards and a red to Spain's none — could not be independently verified against match-statistics providers, and should be read as part of his allegation rather than as a confirmed figure.

He additionally suggested FIFA's broadcast coverage had leaned on shots of Spanish football legends in the stadium rather than Argentine ones, framing it as one more small tilt in Spain's favor. That, too, is Carrozza's interpretation of the broadcast rather than an established fact.

Argentina's own response to the final has been notably muted. Coach Lionel Scaloni was the only representative of the squad to face reporters afterward, calling the loss painful but conceding that Spain deserved the win — a far cry from Carrozza's version of events, though Scaloni was not asked directly about the conspiracy claims.

For now, the theory remains what it was when it surfaced: a provocative allegation from one journalist with AFA connections, unaccompanied by evidence, floating around the genuine heartbreak of Messi's last World Cup ending in defeat.

Spain's Rodri won the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player; Messi took the Silver Ball and Kylian Mbappé the Bronze Ball. Mbappé also won his second career Golden Boot.
Slovenian referee Slavko Vinčić was appointed to take charge of the final amid reported tension between FIFA president Gianni Infantino and UEFA.
Argentine journalist Pablo Carrozza alleged, without producing evidence, that FIFA arranged for a European champion to help secure Infantino's re-election with UEFA's backing.
Lionel Scaloni was Argentina's only representative at the post-match press conference and said Spain deserved the victory.
No formal response to the conspiracy allegations has been issued by FIFA, UEFA, the Spanish federation (RFEF) or the Argentine federation (AFA).

title: FIFA opens investigation into Argentina after ugly brawl at World Cup final
dek: Nahuel Molina, Leandro Paredes and assistant coach Roberto Ayala are all under scrutiny after chaotic scenes followed Spain's 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina in New Jersey.
body: Barely had Ferran Torres's extra-time winner settled the 2026 World Cup than the final descended into a brawl that FIFA is now investigating, with several Argentina players and a member of Lionel Scaloni's coaching staff facing possible disciplinary action.

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in New Jersey on July 19, with substitute Torres scoring in the 106th minute to give La Roja their second World Cup title. Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made 11 saves in a losing effort, but it was what happened after the final whistle that has dominated the fallout.

Broadcast footage showed Argentina right-back Nahuel Molina appearing to strike Spain captain Rodri in the midriff as players poured across the pitch, an incident widely cited as the spark for the mass confrontation that followed.

Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle had already gone, having barrelled into Eric García and knocked him down, then reportedly caught the Spain defender in the throat before turning on 21-year-old Gavi and spinning him to the ground.

Perhaps the most damaging moment for Argentina came from the touchline rather than the pitch: assistant coach Roberto Ayala was filmed appearing to punch Spain's Dani Olmo, in an incident missed by the main broadcast but captured on separate footage and not mentioned in the referee's initial report.

ONE reports that FIFA's disciplinary code sets a minimum three-match ban for violent conduct, but that harsher sanctions are possible given the incidents played out at the end of a final watched by hundreds of millions of people, with Article 13 — covering damage to the game's reputation — also in play. FIFA has confirmed a formal investigation is under way into the post-match scenes.

The federation's problems do not begin and end with the final whistle in New Jersey. FIFA had already opened a separate probe after Lisandro Martínez and unused substitute Giovani Lo Celso held up a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" ('The Falklands are Argentina's') following Argentina's semi-final win over England — a display that prompted a formal complaint from the British government.

It would not be the Argentine federation's first sanction over that banner: FIFA fined the AFA 30,000 Swiss francs (about $37,000) after players displayed the same message at a 2014 warm-up match, a precedent that could weigh on any new penalty.

ONE also notes the Argentine federation's wider disciplinary record, including previous sanctions tied to the team's 2022 World Cup title celebrations, as context for how FIFA might approach penalties this time around.

No sanctions have been announced yet, either for the individuals involved in the final-whistle brawl or for the federation itself, and there is no confirmed timeline for when FIFA's investigation will conclude.
facts: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 World Cup final, with substitute Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute.

No sanctions have yet been announced against any player, coach or the Argentine federation.

title: Grimberg and Mordechai on target as Maccabi Haifa lead Hapoel Kfar Saba 2-0 in preseason friendly
dek: A 16-year-old academy forward and the club's big-money summer signing both scored inside the opening 20 minutes as Haifa tested its squad ahead of the 2026/27 season.
body: Maccabi Haifa were cruising in the latest of their preseason friendlies on Tuesday, leading Liga Leumit side Hapoel Kfar Saba 2-0 midway through the first half, according to a live report from ONE.

The Greens broke through early. Adam Grimberg, a 16-year-old forward who has been pushed up from Haifa's youth ranks and capped at Israel under-17 and under-18 level, opened the scoring in the 15th minute. Five minutes later it was 2-0, with Yair Mordechai — the midfielder Haifa signed this summer on a four-year deal from Ironi Kiryat Shmona — adding the second.
ONE's report covers the match only up to the 27th minute, so Tuesday's friendly was still in progress when this story was filed; there is no confirmed final score yet.

The fixture is part of a run of warm-up matches Haifa have scheduled before the new Ligat Ha'al season, a stretch that has already included a 2-1 win over Dundee. Coaching staff have used the games to rotate personnel and take a longer look at squad depth, including academy prospects like Grimberg, before competitive football resumes.

Hapoel Kfar Saba, who play their football a division below in Liga Leumit, have provided competitive preseason opposition for Haifa in past summers, including a match in which Kfar Saba beat a rotated Haifa side 3-1. Tuesday's meeting was arranged in that same spirit of friendly, low-stakes preparation rather than as a competitive fixture.

Mordechai's goal will be an early, encouraging sign for Haifa fans after the club moved quickly in the transfer market to bring him in following a prolific spell at Kiryat Shmona, where he scored ten goals and added six assists last season.

title: Playoff Hero Or Poni Leaves Nahalal Yizrael for Hapoel Hadera's Youth Ranks
dek: The attacking midfielder whose stoppage-time free kick kept Nahalal Yizrael in Israel's top youth flight is joining Hapoel Hadera's Youth A squad for next season, after his own age group was relegated.

verificationSources.label: Israel Football Association – Or Poni player record
Israel Football Association – Nahalal Yizrael club record
Israel Football Association – Hapoel Hadera club record

body: Or Poni spent the dying seconds of a playoff decider keeping Nahalal Yizrael in Israel's Premier League youth division back in the spring, curling home a stoppage-time free kick against Hapoel Haifa. Now, ONE reports, the attacking midfielder is leaving the club that made him for the bigger stage of Hapoel Hadera's Youth A squad.

The move stems from a shift up the age groups rather than any falling-out: Nahalal Yizrael's 2009-cohort team was relegated this year, and Poni, wanting to keep playing at the top level, has signed with Hadera for next season instead.

It caps a breakout campaign. Poni made 33 appearances for Nahalal Yizrael, starting 30 of them and playing the full 90 minutes in 22, finishing with ten goals and seven assists — numbers ONE describes as among the biggest rises of the season in the Youth A Premier League.

His signature moment came in the playoff decider that settled Nahalal Yizrael's fate. Facing Hapoel Haifa, promoted up from the National League, in a match played in Bat Yam, Nahalal Yizrael dominated for long stretches but couldn't turn chances into goals, then conceded a late equaliser. Poni settled it himself, scoring in the final minute for a 2-1 win that preserved the club's place in the top flight.

"I'm very excited about this transfer," Poni told ONE. "I found here a level of conduct I hadn't known before, a facility at the highest level in the north, an excellent team — with God's help we'll have a great season together. I'm hungry to do my maximum to have a bigger season than last year."

Poni is a product of the club he is now leaving. He joined Nahalal Yizrael's Under-12s three seasons ago under his father Shahar's guidance, having come up through the youth ranks at M.K. Neve Yosef Haifa and Maccabi Haifa's "Ktzaf" development group.

Looking back on a season he called full of "ups and downs," Poni told ONE that results were slow to arrive early on, but coach Idan Weitzman "didn't let us lower our heads for a moment." His own turning point came in round nine — a stoppage-time free kick in a defeat away to Hapoel Be'er Sheva, his first goal of the campaign. A first win followed in round ten, 3-0 over Kiryat Shmona, in which Poni scored and assisted, and Nahalal Yizrael went on a five-match winning run that carried them to 13th in the regular-season table.

Poni also pointed to the disruption of the ongoing war as a factor behind a difficult stretch before the playoffs — a strain that has run through Israeli football's lower and youth divisions for the past two seasons.

Asked what drew him to Hadera, Poni cited both the pull of staying in the Premier League and the practicalities of the move: "Hadera is a wonderful place for me, both in terms of convenience and in terms of the team, the facility and the management." He thanked his parents and Weitzman, "who invested extra hours working with me... so I could be my best version. Now it's time to work and prove myself."
Hadera's Youth A squad, who will be led next season by coach Osher Gal, is currently at a pre-season training camp in Nahariya as it prepares for the new Premier League campaign.

There's a family footnote to the move: Poni's father Shahar is also changing dugouts this summer, taking charge of Hapoel Nof Hagalil's Youth B team while stepping up as assistant coach with the senior side.

title: AEK Athens pull offer for Beersheba's Kangwa after club refuses to rest him for Vikingur tie
dek: The Greek club wanted assurances that Kings Kangwa would sit out tonight's Champions League qualifier so he could still play for them in Europe this season. Hapoel Beersheba said no — and AEK walked away.

verificationSources.label: africasoccer.com — AEK eye move for Kangwa
Israel Hayom — offers submitted for Kangwa

body: AEK Athens have walked away from their pursuit of Kings Kangwa, ONE reports, after Hapoel Beersheba refused a Greek request that would have kept the Zambian midfielder out of Israel's Champions League qualifier in Reykjavik.

According to the report, AEK wanted Kangwa's move finalised before Beersheba's second qualifying round tie against Vikingur Reykjavik — with one condition attached: that he not take the field for the Israeli champions in that game.

The reasoning was purely technical. Under UEFA's rules, a player who appears for one club in a European tie becomes cup-tied and cannot then turn out for another club later in the same competition. AEK wanted Kangwa available for their own playoff-round campaign, and playing for Beersheba against Vikingur would have ruled that out.

Beersheba said no. ONE reports the club confirmed Kangwa would be part of the squad for the Icelandic trip regardless of the transfer talk, even knowing that stance risked costing them a deal already in an advanced state.

Notably, the sticking point was not money. ONE's report indicates AEK's financial offer had already met, or bettered, what Beersheba were asking — a shift from earlier in the saga, when Israeli outlets reported the two sides sitting several million euros apart.

Kangwa, 27, is understood to have already agreed personal terms with the Greek club and had been pushing his employers to sanction the switch quickly. Once Beersheba held firm on playing him, AEK pulled the offer without further negotiation, per the report.
AEK's director of football, Javier Ribalta, will now turn to other midfield targets, ONE says, ending — for now — a transfer saga that has run through much of the Israeli club's summer.

Beersheba had already turned down two other bids for Kangwa earlier this summer, from clubs in Russia and the Czech Republic, insisting throughout that any departure would have to meet their valuation of the player.

The episode lands on a significant night for the club. Hapoel Beersheba, Israel's reigning Premier League champions, are facing Vikingur Reykjavik for the first time ever in this Champions League qualifying round, having also lost 3-1 to Maccabi Tel Aviv in last week's Israeli Super Cup.
For now, Kangwa remains a Beersheba player — and, by his own club's insistence, an eligible one for continental duty tonight.

title: Pilot's cruel mid-flight prank convinces grieving Argentina fans they had won the World Cup
dek: A cabin full of Argentina supporters erupted in celebration when their pilot announced a World Cup final win — before he delivered the punchline: Spain had actually taken the trophy.
body: Two days after the final whistle in New Jersey, the World Cup found a new way to break Argentine hearts — this time at 35,000 feet, and entirely on purpose.

A pilot flying a cabin packed with Argentina supporters, many still in their sky-blue-and-white shirts and Messi No. 10 jerseys, took to the intercom to deliver news of the final. According to footage that has since spread widely on social media and was reported on by ONE, he built the moment like a commentator calling a photo finish: "This was a very tight match through the end, including extra time. Both teams gave everything, but unfortunately..." — and left the sentence hanging.

Passengers, cut off from live coverage for the length of the flight and depending entirely on the cockpit for the result, took the pause as their cue. The cabin erupted — fans leaping from their seats, hugging strangers, screaming as though Argentina had just retained the trophy they won in Qatar four years earlier.

Then came the rest of the sentence: "Spain won." The celebration died in an instant. Passengers who moments earlier had been embracing were left in silence, according to the footage and multiple outlets that picked up the clip, including Yahoo Sports, WION and LBC.

The real result was no joke. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in Sunday's final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, with Ferran Torres — on as a 62nd-minute substitute — scoring the winner in the 106th minute for his first goal of the tournament. It was Spain's second World Cup title.

Argentina, reduced to 10 men, had goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to thank for keeping the game alive as long as it lasted; he set a World Cup final record with 11 saves. Lionel Messi, 39, completed his sixth and probably final World Cup without adding to the title he lifted in 2022.

ONE reported that Argentine media reacted with fury to the airborne prank, branding it a "terrible act" carried out in "questionable humour." Critics also noted the pilot took a real risk exposing himself that way, mid-flight, to a cabin of fans who for a few seconds genuinely believed they were celebrating a second straight world title.

Online reaction has been split down the middle since the clip began circulating, including on TikTok. Plenty of viewers — largely from Spain and elsewhere in Europe — have defended the prank as good-natured rivalry banter and joked the pilot deserves a pay rise. Others have called it needlessly cruel to a cabin full of fans still processing a heartbreaking defeat.

The airline operating the flight and its destination have not been made public in any of the reporting, and it remains unclear whether the pilot has faced any response from his employer over the stunt.

title: Banda's Lecce stand-off could still hand Maccabi Petah Tikva a bonus payday
dek: The winger missed Lecce's pre-season report date amid interest from Saudi Arabia's Al-Fateh — but the detail worth watching in Israel is a 15% sell-on clause tying his next move to Maccabi Petah Tikva's finances.

verificationSources.label: Calcio Lecce — Lecce, Banda arriva in ritiro

body: Lameck Banda finally walked into US Lecce's pre-season training camp on Tuesday, drawing a line under a stand-off that had briefly turned into a full-blown case in the Italian press. The more interesting question for Israeli football finance is what happens if the Zambian winger walks straight back out again — this time onto a flight to Saudi Arabia.

Banda had failed to report when Lecce's squad reassembled for pre-season last week, telling the club that unspecified bureaucratic and logistical problems were keeping him from returning to Italy. Lecce were unconvinced enough to put out a formal statement voicing concern over the absence and reserving the right to pursue disciplinary measures over what it called a breach of his contractual obligations — a deal that, on paper, runs to June 30, 2027.

The subtext was not hard to read. Italian outlet Calcio Lecce reported that Saudi Pro League club Al-Fateh have been in advanced talks to sign Banda, dangling a contract through 2029, with interest also said to be coming from clubs in the United Arab Emirates. Lecce, according to the same reporting, want at least €6 million for a player who cost them a fraction of that three years ago — well above the roughly €2.5 million that the highest UAE bid is said to have reached so far.

None of that is confirmed as an actual transfer yet; it remains agent-and-newspaper territory rather than a signed deal, and Banda was back working under coach Eusebio Di Francesco by Tuesday morning regardless. But the episode was enough to put his name, and his ownership history, back in Israeli headlines.

Banda arrived at Maccabi Petah Tikva on loan from Russia's Arsenal Tula in August 2021, having already spent a season on loan at Maccabi Netanya. Petah Tikva liked what they saw enough to buy him outright for around €300,000, and it did not take long for the investment to look shrewd: Banda scored ten goals across competitions in his one full season in the yellow and black.

Lecce came calling in August 2022, signing him on a permanent four-year deal with an option for a fifth season. Petah Tikva let him go for a reported €2 million plus a 15 percent sell-on clause on any future transfer fee, according to Ynet and Walla Sport's reporting at the time — turning a €300,000 punt into one of the biggest sales in the club's history. Only Manor Solomon's move to Shakhtar Donetsk (€6m) and Liel Abada's transfer to Celtic (€4m) rank higher.

Banda made history of his own in Lecce colours, becoming the first Zambian player to appear in Serie A when he came off the bench against Inter Milan on his debut. He has since become a regular contributor for the Salento club, including in last season's fight to preserve their top-flight status.

That 15 percent sell-on clause is the reason Petah Tikva's finance department has an interest in a saga they have no control over. If Lecce do eventually cash in on Banda — whether to Al-Fateh at anywhere near their stated €6 million valuation, or to a Gulf rival at a lower fee — a further six-figure sum is contractually owed back to Petah Tikva, on top of what they already banked in 2022.

It is a small but recurring feature of the transfer model built at Petah Tikva under sporting director Avi Luzon: buy promising, undervalued talent cheaply, sell high, and keep a slice of whatever comes next. Banda's Lecce exit already ranks among the club's biggest paydays; a Saudi deal this summer would simply add a coda to it, with Petah Tikva collecting a fee for a transfer they will read about in the Italian press same as everyone else.

For now, the immediate crisis at Lecce's training camp has passed, and Banda is back among his teammates. Whether that quiets the Al-Fateh interest for good, or merely delays it, is the open question — and one Israeli football finance will keep half an eye on for reasons that have nothing to do with who wins promotion or survival battles in Serie A.

title: Omri Glazer completes homecoming to Maccabi Haifa on three-year deal
dek: Israel's national-team goalkeeper leaves Red Star Belgrade to rejoin the club where he first became a Ligat ha'Al name, reuniting with head coach Barak Bakhar at Kiryat Eliezer.

verificationSources.label: ONE — רשמית: עומרי גלזר חתם לשלוש שנים במכבי חיפה

C14 — חיזוק אדיר לירוקים: עומרי גלזר סיכם רשמית במכבי חיפה

body: Omri Glazer is going home. Maccabi Haifa announced on Tuesday that the Israel national-team goalkeeper has signed a three-year contract, ending a three-season stint at Red Star Belgrade and returning him to the club where he first made his name in Israeli football.

According to ONE, which broke the news, Haifa paid Red Star roughly €250,000 for Glazer's registration and will pay him close to €400,000 a year, making him one of the squad's highest earners — figures reported by several Israeli outlets but not yet confirmed in a club statement.

The move completes a full circle. Glazer, 30, came through Hapoel Ra'anana's youth ranks before Maccabi Haifa signed him in the summer of 2016. Over five seasons at Kiryat Eliezer he grew into the club's undisputed No. 1, helping Haifa win the 2020-21 Ligat ha'Al title and earning the league's Goalkeeper of the Season award that year.

He left for Hapoel Be'er Sheva in 2021 and kept collecting silverware, lifting the 2021-22 Israel State Cup and the 2022-23 Israel Super Cup while picking up a second Goalkeeper of the Season honor along the way.

In June 2023 he made the jump abroad, signing for Red Star Belgrade in Serbia. It proved a significant chapter: Glazer made 51 appearances for the Serbian giants, kept 22 clean sheets, played nine Champions League matches and won three domestic championships.

His signature moment in Serbian red-and-white came against Manchester City in the 2023-24 Champions League group stage, when he made 13 saves in a losing effort — still one of the standout individual goalkeeping displays of that tournament, even in a 3-1 defeat.

The picture soured last season, when Red Star brought in a new first-choice goalkeeper and Glazer found himself behind the pecking order, according to ice.co.il's reporting on his time in Belgrade — a big part of why a return to Israel, and regular football, became attractive.

That return also reunites him with head coach Barak Bakhar, who is now in his third spell in charge at Maccabi Haifa after being reappointed last October following Diego Flores' dismissal. ONE's report frames the pairing as familiar territory for both men, given their history working together.

Sporting director Lior Rafalov, who now oversees recruitment at Haifa alongside Bakhar on the touchline, was quoted by ONE describing Glazer as arriving with "rich experience domestically and in Europe" — the kind of senior presence a club chasing back-to-back challenges wants between the posts.

Glazer himself struck a sentimental note in comments carried by ONE, saying he was "happy to return to where it all started" and that he had "always felt" there was another chapter to write in Haifa's green shirt.
He has already passed a medical and joined the Haifa squad, per the report, giving Bakhar an established, senior-level option in goal heading into pre-season.

Beyond the club game, Glazer remains Israel's first-choice goalkeeper, having started for the national team throughout its Euro 2024 qualifying campaign — adding a further layer of significance to a move that returns one of the country's most capped young goalkeepers to Ligat ha'Al's biggest stage.
