title: Behind Douglas Owusu's failed Plzeň medical — and how it steered him to Hapoel Tel Aviv
dek: A knee problem flagged during Czech medical tests wrecked a club-record move to Viktoria Plzeň and left the Red Star Belgrade winger without competitive minutes for months. Now he is Hapoel Tel Aviv's most expensive signing ever.
body: Douglas Owusu's summer has been a lesson in how fast a career can swing on the findings of a doctor's scan. Sport5 lays out the story behind the collapse of what would have been a club-record move for the young Ghanaian winger — and how that failure ultimately rerouted him to Bloomfield Stadium.

Owusu, 20, arrived at Red Star Belgrade from Radnik Surdulica in January for a reported €2.2 million, quickly building a reputation as one of the most sought-after teenage wingers in the Balkans. Within months, Czech side Viktoria Plzeň had agreed what was reported as their most expensive transfer ever — a fee in the region of €3.3 million plus roughly €1 million in performance add-ons, according to Ghanaian outlet GhanaSoccernet, which broke the terms of the deal.

The move never got that far. Owusu travelled for his medical in the Czech Republic, and according to Czech outlet Deník Sport — cited by ONE — the examination flagged a knee problem that had not been fully documented beforehand. Plzeň walked away, and Serbian outlet Meridian Sport confirmed soon after that the transfer had 'definitively collapsed,' with Red Star ruling out even a loan elsewhere.

The fallout left Owusu in limbo at Marakana. Sport5 reports he trained under coach Dejan Stanković and appeared in a pre-season friendly against Zenit St Petersburg without getting on the pitch, but he did not feature in a single registered league or Champions League qualifying match for Red Star for the rest of the season.

That period without game time, paired with the lingering knee question mark, shaped how Israeli clubs approached him this summer. According to ONE, both Tel Aviv rivals scouted the same player: Maccabi Tel Aviv moved first but, wary after the Plzeň scare, would only discuss a loan rather than a permanent deal. Hapoel Tel Aviv took the opposite approach and offered to pay Red Star Belgrade an outright fee.

That willingness to buy rather than borrow appears to have been decisive. Red Star's leadership opted for the certainty of a fee from Hapoel over Maccabi's loan proposal, according to ONE's reporting on the chase between the two clubs.

Ynet, breaking the completed transfer, reported the deal is worth around €2.5 million on a four-year contract — making Owusu the most expensive signing in Hapoel Tel Aviv's history. Club CEO Gai Primor travelled to Belgrade to finalise the details before the move was announced.

At Red Star, Owusu made 12 league appearances in the second half of last season and scored twice, statistics that underline why both Tel Aviv clubs kept faith in him despite the medical red flag that sank the Plzeň deal. Hapoel's medical team will now have run its own examination before completing the signing, a step that carries extra weight given what happened in the Czech Republic.

For Hapoel, the gamble is as much financial as physical: a club-record fee for a winger who spent months unable to convince Red Star to even risk a loan spell elsewhere. For Owusu, it is a chance to finally get consistent football again after a transfer saga that started with a record fee for Plzeň and nearly ended his season on the sidelines.

title: M.S. Ashdod beat Maccabi Jaffa 2-0 and Bnei Yehuda edge Kafr Qasem 1-0 in Toto Cup
dek: Osama Khalaileh's penalty and a late Maor Kuba strike sent Ashdod to victory at Maccabi Jaffa, while a Stav Nahmani header was enough for Bnei Yehuda at Kafr Qasem in round two of the Liga Leumit's Toto Cup group phase.
body: M.S. Ashdod and Bnei Yehuda both won on the road in round two of the Toto Cup's Liga Leumit group phase on Monday, August 3, 2026, two of the more eye-catching results on a night when the second tier's Toto Cup campaign began to take shape.

Ashdod, playing away at Maccabi Jaffa, needed until late in the game to break the deadlock. Osama Khalaileh converted from the penalty spot in the 79th minute, and Maor Kuba doubled the lead in the third minute of stoppage time, finishing off a cross from Khalaileh to make it 2-0, according to Sport5.

The win comes in Ashdod's first campaign back in the Liga Leumit after a decade in the top flight. The club, one of Ligat Ha'al's more established names over the past ten years, were relegated at the end of the 2025/26 season and are now rebuilding in the second tier.

Bnei Yehuda's night was tighter. Away at M.S. Kafr Qasem, the only goal came in the 53rd minute when Stav Nahmani rose to head home from a corner, giving the Tel Aviv club a 1-0 win to open their account for the round.

The result matters a little more for Bnei Yehuda than a standard early-season group game: they arrive in this year's Toto Cup as the competition's reigning champions, having lifted the trophy for the first time in the club's history last season after winning the final on penalties.
Both wins keep Ashdod and Bnei Yehuda well placed in their respective Toto Cup groups as the Liga Leumit's pre-season cup competition builds toward its knockout stages later in the year.
Sport5, the source for both results, did not report on injuries or further team news from either fixture.

title: Barcelona eye shock Rodri move as Milan reject Fenerbahçe's Leão bid
dek: Spanish giants circle Manchester City's midfield anchor while Rossoneri owner Gerry Cardinale holds firm against a loan approach for Rafael Leão.
body: Two of the biggest transfer sagas of the European summer edged forward on Monday, with Barcelona reportedly circling Rodri in Manchester and AC Milan digging in over Rafael Leão in a separate stand-off with Fenerbahçe.

According to ONE, citing Cadena SER, Barcelona are keeping close tabs on Rodri's situation at Manchester City, though the Catalan club stress it is not currently their top transfer priority. Real Madrid, by contrast, are said to be relaxed, believing that if the reigning Ballon d'Or holder does leave the Etihad, the Bernabéu remains his preferred destination.

The Spanish reporting, led by Cadena SER's Nil Solà, frames Barcelona's interest as opportunistic rather than a fully formed pursuit — the club reportedly sees Rodri as a genuine 'top' option at defensive midfield and would be willing to act if Real Madrid's own negotiations with City stall, though any deal would still depend on the player himself signalling a willingness to move to Camp Nou rather than the Bernabéu.

Rodri, 30, has been City's midfield metronome since arriving from Atlético Madrid in 2019 and captained Spain to their World Cup triumph earlier this year, a run that has only sharpened suitors' interest even as his contract situation in Manchester remains unresolved.

In Milan, the club's stance on Leão has hardened rather than softened. ONE reports that Fenerbahçe presented a loan offer with a purchase option for the Portugal winger, only for the Rossoneri to reject it outright, insisting a temporary departure is not a viable option.

That account matches reporting from Fabrizio Romano, who wrote on X that AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale made clear in talks that a loan-with-option structure is off the table, and that the only route to a deal is a permanent sale for a serious fee — reported elsewhere as a minimum of around €50 million.

Contacts between the two clubs are continuing, and Romano indicated Fenerbahçe are not walking away, with a fresh, improved offer possible in the coming days as the Istanbul side pushes to land the 27-year-old before the window closes.

Leão's own camp appears to be pushing for an exit too: the winger has reportedly parted ways with his long-standing agent and brought in lawyers to help accelerate a move away from San Siro, with interest also said to extend to Premier League clubs including Manchester United.

Neither deal is close to completion, and both remain firmly in the report-and-rumour stage rather than confirmed business — but with barely a month left before the major European windows shut, Real Madrid, Barcelona and Milan all face pressure to show their hand.

title: Manor Solomon closing in on West Ham switch on three-year contract
dek: Tottenham and West Ham are negotiating a permanent transfer for the Israel international winger, with the deal expected to be finalised within days, according to ONE.

verificationSources.label: Yahoo Sports - Tottenham and West Ham in negotiations over Solomon

body: Manor Solomon looks to be on his way out of Tottenham Hotspur, with West Ham United closing in on a permanent transfer for the Israel international winger, ONE reported.
According to the report, Solomon is expected to sign a three-year contract at the London Stadium, with the deal understood to include a club option for a fourth season.

The two London clubs are still working through the numbers on a fee, with ONE suggesting that finalising the transaction could take a few more days. English outlets covering the talks, including Yahoo Sports and Inside Futbol, have described the negotiations as advanced, with a resolution expected within 48 to 72 hours of their reports on Monday.
Solomon is said to have wanted the move to West Ham from the outset, giving the Hammers a clear run at a player who has spent the past two seasons away from north London on loan.

The 27-year-old spent the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Leeds United, contributing ten goals and 12 assists in 39 Championship appearances as the Yorkshire club won promotion back to the Premier League.

West Ham, relegated from the Premier League last season under new manager Nuno Espirito Santo, have already reshaped their attack this summer. They agreed a reported £68 million sale of Dutch winger Crysencio Summerville to Saudi side Al Hilal, a departure that leaves an obvious gap on the flank for Solomon to fill.

Solomon's path to a possible West Ham switch has taken him through some of European football's more turbulent corners. He rose through Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth ranks before Shakhtar Donetsk paid roughly €6 million for him in January 2019, and he won three Ukrainian Premier League titles in Donetsk colours.

Russia's invasion of Ukraine forced him out of the country in 2022, sending him on loan to Fulham before he signed for Tottenham as a free agent in 2023 when his Shakhtar contract expired. He has struggled since to establish himself as a regular at Spurs, spending both of the last two seasons out on loan.

A permanent switch to West Ham would give Solomon the stability of an extended contract and a clear role in the Hammers' rebuild for the Championship, should the transfer be completed as ONE and other outlets currently expect.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem sign Serbian center Dušan Miletić
dek: The 2.14m rebounder arrives on a two-year deal from Romania's Cluj, the latest addition to a busy off-season rebuild under Saša Obradović.
body: Hapoel Jerusalem have strengthened their frontcourt for the new season, confirming the signing of Serbian center Dušan Miletić on a two-year contract that runs through the 2027/28 campaign, ONE reported.
Miletić, 28, stands 2.14 metres tall and arrives in the capital after a strong season with Romanian club U-BT Cluj-Napoca, where he was one of the more productive big men in last season's EuroCup.

In continental play he averaged 12.6 points, 7.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists in just 22.1 minutes a night, a workload that still left him ranked fourth in the competition for rebounding, and he helped Cluj reach the EuroCup quarter-finals while also winning the Romanian league title.
His route to Cluj ran through Lebanon, where he had a brief spell with Al-Riyadi Beirut in June and helped the club to a domestic championship before completing his move to Israel.

Hapoel Jerusalem coach Saša Obradović, who has overseen an active rebuild in the capital this summer, welcomed the addition: "He is a player with experience, high basketball intelligence and a competitive approach. He is an excellent rebounder, very versatile, and brings toughness and physicality," he said, according to ONE.
Miletić struck an enthusiastic tone on the move: "I am very happy to join Hapoel Jerusalem and grateful for the opportunity and trust. I am excited to now wear the red uniform."

The center is the latest reinforcement in a significant off-season overhaul at the club, which has already brought in American guard Shake Milton, the former Philadelphia 76ers man who joins after a season with Partizan Belgrade.

With EuroCup and Winner League commitments both on the schedule, Jerusalem's remodelled roster will be tested early, and Miletić's rebounding and physicality give Obradović a genuine new option in the paint to pair with the incoming backcourt talent.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva rejected 1.5m euro Russian bid for Abu Romi, cousin reveals
dek: Anis Abu Romi says Akron Tolyatti's approach for his cousin never had a chance — owner Alona Barkat wrote back immediately that the winger was not for sale.
body: Mohammad Abu Romi had a route out of Israel this summer, and it went nowhere fast. His cousin Anis, speaking on an Israeli sports talk show, revealed that Russian club Akron Tolyatti tabled a serious offer for the Hapoel Beer Sheva winger — and that owner Alona Barkat shut it down almost as soon as it landed.

According to Anis, Akron proposed around 1.5 million euros to buy Abu Romi outright, with personal terms of roughly 700,000 euros a season attached — more than four times his current wages in Beersheba. Barkat's reply, he said, came in writing and left no room for negotiation: the 22-year-old is not for sale.

"We had an offer from Russia, but beyond Alona refusing to sell for 1.5 million..." Anis said on the program, before adding that Barkat "first of all sent a letter that Abu Romi is not for sale, plain and simple." Asked what he thought the player was actually worth, he put the figure at "not less than 1.5 million euros" — suggesting the family view Akron's bid as closer to a starting point than a knockout offer.

The interest is easy to explain. Abu Romi has become one of the form players in Israeli football since his move to Beersheba from Ironi Kiryat Shmona, sealed in a deal worth around 400,000 euros on a three-and-a-half-year contract. He has since helped the club to a league title and made his mark internationally, earning eight caps for the Israel national team.

For Barkat, who has run Hapoel Beer Sheva since 2007 and built the club into one of the country's dominant forces, the calculus is straightforward: a 22-year-old who is already delivering silverware and looks capable of a far bigger move later is worth more to the project than a quick cash injection now, even a substantial one.

Akron Tolyatti, who play in the Russian Premier League, are not the kind of buying club whose interest typically forces a sale in Israeli football, and the political and logistical complications of a move to Russia for an Israeli international would have added further friction to any deal even before Barkat's letter arrived.

None of this necessarily closes the book on Abu Romi leaving Beersheba. His cousin's comments read as a family confident that a bigger offer, from a bigger league, will eventually come — and that this summer's approach was simply premature.

For now, though, the message from the club's owner has been unambiguous, and Abu Romi's focus returns to Beersheba, where he remains one of the reigning champions' most valuable assets heading into the new season.
facts: Russian club Akron Tolyatti offered Hapoel Beer Sheva roughly 1.5 million euros plus personal terms of about 700,000 euros a season for winger Mohammad Abu Romi.
Beersheba owner Alona Barkat rejected the bid, sending written confirmation that Abu Romi was not for sale.
Abu Romi, 22, joined Beersheba from Ironi Kiryat Shmona for around 400,000 euros on a three-and-a-half-year contract.
He has helped Beersheba win the league championship since arriving and has earned eight caps for the Israel national team.
The details were revealed by Abu Romi's cousin, Anis, in a television interview, not via an official club statement.

title: Maor Siso vows Kiryat Yam will keep aiming high despite one of Liga Leumit's smallest budgets
dek: The coach says a 3-1 Toto Cup win over top-flight Maccabi Bnei Reineh has sharpened belief in a squad built on a shoestring, with two positions still to fill before the National League season resumes.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Kiryat Yam coach interview

body: Maor Siso doesn't pretend Kiryat Yam can spend like the clubs above them. What he insists on, the National League coach told ONE, is that the budget won't be an excuse for how high his team aims this season.

"We aspire to the top, even though we have one of the lowest budgets in the league," Siso said, framing the club's approach to 2026/27 not as damage limitation after a first season in the division, but as a genuine push to establish themselves.

The comments came on the back of a statement result: Kiryat Yam beat Maccabi Bnei Reineh 3-1 in the Toto Cup group stage, a notable scalp given Bnei Reineh play their football a tier higher, in the Israeli Premier League. It was exactly the kind of pre-season signal a modest, newly established Leumit side wants heading into the new campaign.

Squad-building is still a work in progress. Siso said Kiryat Yam are missing two players before he considers the roster complete, but he sounded content with what he already has, pointing to healthy internal competition for places as he continues to work alongside the club's professional manager on further additions.

He was warm about the environment behind the scenes too, describing a staff stocked with people who have previously worked in the top flight and a club culture he called family-oriented — the kind of infrastructure, he suggested, that doesn't always come with a rock-bottom budget, and one that feeds a winning tradition already lifting morale inside the squad.

Siso also used the interview to draw a clear line under last season. Kiryat Yam's historic promotion campaign began with a four-point deduction and turned messy at times as the newly promoted side fought to establish itself in the division. This time, the coach promised, there will be no such turbulence — just a calm, settled campaign built around the group he is assembling.

That backdrop matters. Kiryat Yam won Liga Alef North to reach Liga Leumit for the first time and, despite starting 2025/26 in the red on points, finished a credible sixth in their debut season in the division — proof, in Siso's telling, that the club's ambitions aren't just talk.

title: Liga Leumit reveals fixture list for August 18 season opener
dek: Israel's second-tier season kicks off with eight round-one matches, and the league has now mapped out the first three rounds of fixtures.

body: Israel's second-tier season now has a starting date. The Liga Leumit's league management has published the fixture list for the opening rounds of the 2026/27 campaign, ONE reports, confirming that the new season will get under way on Tuesday, August 18.
All eight round-one matches will kick off at 19:30, giving fans across the league's provincial towns and city clubs a fixed date to plan around after months of pre-season build-up.

The opening round pairs Hapoel Ra'anana with Maccabi Ahi Nazareth, Hapoel Afula with MS Ashdod, and Maccabi Jaffa with MS Kiryat Yam. Maccabi Bnei Reineh will host Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv in one of the weekend's more eye-catching fixtures.

Elsewhere in round one, Hapoel Kfar Shalem take on MS Kafr Qasem, Hapoel Akko host Maccabi Kiryat Gat, and Hapoel Rishon LeZion welcome Hapoel Kfar Saba. Ironi Modi'in will complete the round by hosting Maccabi Herzliya.
According to ONE, the league has also locked in the following two rounds: round two is scheduled for August 23-24 and round three for August 30-31, both with a 19:00 kick-off time.

The league management indicated that fixtures beyond round three will be published at a later date. ONE reports the delay stems from shared stadium usage between Liga Leumit and Ligat Ha'al clubs, as well as the knock-on effect of Israeli teams' results in European qualifying rounds this summer.

For clubs building squads over the close season, the confirmed opening date gives a firm target for pre-season friendlies and squad registration, even as the wider calendar for autumn fixtures remains a work in progress.

title: Aarhus, OFI Crete, Braga and Atalanta: the rivals standing between four Israeli clubs and Europe's group stages
dek: Hapoel Beer Sheva, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv are all still alive in Champions League, Europa League and Conference League qualifying — ONE sizes up who could be waiting for them in the playoff round.

verificationSources.label: ONE — הכירו את היריבות של הקבוצות הישראליות באירופה
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — Maccabi's potential play-off opponents
Atalanta.it — 2026/27 UECL play-offs: Atalanta drawn against Hapoel Tel Aviv or GKS Katowice
The Jerusalem Post — Israeli soccer clubs advance to the third round of European qualifying

body: Four Israeli clubs are fighting through European qualifying this fortnight, and all four already know who is waiting at the next turnstile if they get there. ONE has run the rule over the rivals standing between Hapoel Beer Sheva, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv and a place in the lucrative league phases of the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League.

Beer Sheva have the most direct route to glamour. They opened their Champions League third qualifying-round tie away to Red Star Belgrade on Monday, with Serbia's giants standing between them and a playoff spot worth a place in the competition's league phase. Get past Red Star, and Beer Sheva would meet the winner of Aarhus of Denmark and Azerbaijan's Sabah for the right to reach the Champions League proper.

ONE rates that potential tie against Aarhus close to a coin flip. The Danish champions of 2024 have been unsettled by managerial upheaval and, according to the outlet, have been playing home fixtures away from their own stadium while it undergoes renovation — hardly the ideal build-up for a club still hunting a first appearance in the competition's new-look league phase.

Even a defeat to Red Star wouldn't end Beer Sheva's continental summer: the losing side in that Champions League playoff drops into the Europa League playoff round. ONE has pencilled in Viktoria Plzen of the Czech Republic as that fallback opponent, and gives the southern club roughly a 40% chance of getting past a side with regular European pedigree.

Maccabi Tel Aviv's route runs through the Europa League. Having eliminated Moldova's Sheriff Tiraspol 6-0 on aggregate, including a 1-0 win in the second leg, the Yellow-and-Blue now face Bulgaria's CSKA Sofia in the third qualifying round, with the first leg played in Batumi, Georgia — Maccabi's adopted continental home while the security situation in Israel keeps its European fixtures abroad.

Win that, and Maccabi would face Greek Cup holders OFI Crete in the playoff round, with the Cretans hosting the first leg on August 20 and the return in Israel a week later. ONE calls this the friendliest draw of the four ties, pointing to OFI's poor recent record against clubs of Maccabi's calibre and giving the Israeli champions around a 70% chance of advancing.

Slip up against OFI, though, and Maccabi would instead land in the Conference League playoff against Switzerland's Lugano — a much tighter assignment that ONE scores at roughly 50-50. Either way, reaching the playoff round already guarantees Maccabi a place in continental football beyond the summer, with the only question being which competition.

Beitar Jerusalem's path is the toughest of the four, and it starts with Austria Wien. After eliminating Montenegro's Sutjeska, Beitar host the Austrian side in Romania — first leg in Ploiești on Thursday, before a return trip to Vienna on August 13 — in the Conference League's third qualifying round.

Survive that, and Beitar would run into either Braga of Portugal or Belarus's Dinamo Minsk for a playoff spot. ONE leans heavily toward Braga advancing and gives Beitar only around a 15% chance in that scenario, describing a club with a Europa League semi-final on its recent résumé as nearly the equal of the continent's very best sides at this level.

Hapoel Tel Aviv have the unenviable draw of the summer. The Reds squeezed past Bulgaria's Ludogorets 4-2 on aggregate, a tie settled by a brace from Emmanuel Boateng, and now face Poland's GKS Katowice over two legs on August 6 and 12 for the right to reach the Conference League playoff round.

Waiting there, regardless of which of Hapoel or Katowice comes through, is Atalanta — the 2024 Europa League champions, now rebuilding under Maurizio Sarri after Gian Piero Gasperini left for Roma last year. ONE puts Hapoel Tel Aviv's chances at just 5%, by some distance the longest odds facing any Israeli club this window, and frames a possible meeting with the Italian side as closer to a lottery ticket than a football match.

Taken together, the draws capture where Israeli football sits in Europe right now: genuine contenders in every one of the continent's three club competitions, but drawing some of the sternest possible opposition at the business end of qualifying, and doing it all on the road because of the security situation at home. Results from the third qualifying-round ties over the coming days will determine which of these rivalries actually materialise.

The winner of Maccabi Tel Aviv vs CSKA Sofia meets OFI Crete in the Europa League playoff round (first leg August 20 in Greece, return August 27); the loser would instead face Lugano of Switzerland in the Conference League playoff.

Beitar Jerusalem, having eliminated Sutjeska, face Austria Wien in the Conference League third qualifying round (first leg Ploiești, Romania, second leg Vienna on August 13); the winner meets Braga or Dinamo Minsk in the playoff round.

Hapoel Tel Aviv advanced past Ludogorets 4-2 on aggregate, with Emmanuel Boateng scoring twice, and face GKS Katowice of Poland in the Conference League third qualifying round (August 6 and 12); the winner faces Atalanta, the 2024 Europa League champions now managed by Maurizio Sarri, in the playoff round.

title: Don Nelson, NBA coaching great and five-time champion as a player, dies at 86
dek: The second-winningest coach in league history and architect of "Nelson-ball" passed away peacefully at home, his family said, after 31 seasons prowling NBA sidelines.
body: Don Nelson, one of the most influential figures in NBA history and the second-winningest coach the league has ever seen, has died at the age of 86, ONE reported, citing a family statement confirmed by outlets including ESPN, CBS News and NBA.com.

"On Sunday morning our beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family," the family said in a statement, adding that he died at home.

Nelson spent 31 seasons as an NBA head coach across four franchises — the Milwaukee Bucks, two spells with the Golden State Warriors, the New York Knicks and the Dallas Mavericks — compiling a regular-season record of 1,335 wins and 1,063 losses, second only to Gregg Popovich on the league's all-time list. He won seven Central Division titles and a three-time NBA Coach of the Year award, and led teams to 18 playoff appearances.

His lasting imprint on the sport came less from silverware than from style. Nelson pioneered what became known as "Nelson-ball": small, switchable lineups, pace-and-space spacing and a willingness to play power forwards and centers on the perimeter years before that became basketball orthodoxy. The approach, refined most famously with the "We Believe" Warriors who upset the top-seeded Dallas Mavericks in the 2007 playoffs, is widely credited as a forerunner of the small-ball revolution that now defines the modern NBA.

Before he coached, Nelson was a champion player. He won five NBA titles with the Boston Celtics between 1965 and 1976, playing alongside Bill Russell and John Havlicek, and the Celtics retired his No. 19 jersey in 1978 in recognition of his contribution to those title runs.

As a coach he also had international success, leading the United States to gold at the 1994 FIBA World Championship in Toronto, a rare high point for the program in the years between Olympic "Dream Teams."

Nelson was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2012, capping recognition for a career that touched nearly every era of the modern league, from his Celtics playing days in the 1960s and '70s through his final coaching stint with Golden State, which ended in 2010.

In retirement he settled on Maui, where he took up avocado and coffee farming and largely stepped back from public life. After the devastating Lahaina wildfires of August 2023, Nelson donated part of his property to house families who had lost their homes, a gesture that drew renewed attention to the low-key life he had built on the island long after he left NBA benches behind.

title: Court orders gymnastics body, Olympic Committee and Wingate Institute to pay two injured gymnasts 1.6 million shekels
dek: A Tel Aviv magistrate's court found the Israel Gymnastics Federation, the Olympic Committee of Israel and the Wingate Institute failed to protect two national-team apparatus gymnasts whose shoulders were left permanently disabled by years of undertreated training injuries.
body: Two former national-team apparatus gymnasts have won a landmark compensation case against the very institutions that trained them, after a Tel Aviv magistrate's court ruled that the Israel Gymnastics Federation, the Olympic Committee of Israel and the Wingate Institute failed to protect them from injuries that left both with permanent shoulder disabilities.

ONE reports that Judge Dr. Menachem Klein ordered the three bodies to pay a combined sum of roughly 1.6 million shekels, in what the outlet describes as a precedent-setting ruling for Israeli sports law.

According to the report, the case centred on repeated shoulder injuries the two gymnasts suffered while training with the national squad between 2008 and 2016. Despite recurring complaints of pain, the athletes were, for years, referred only to physiotherapy rather than to orthopedic or sports-medicine specialists.

Court-appointed medical experts found far more serious damage than the defendants had acknowledged. The first gymnast was assessed with 35% disability in each shoulder, while the second was found to have 20% disability in the left shoulder. The gymnastics federation, the Olympic Committee and Wingate had argued for a disability rating of only 10% per shoulder.

The court ultimately set the first gymnast's permanent disability at 23.05% and awarded him 1,118,000 shekels, while the second gymnast, assessed at 19.25% permanent disability, was awarded 505,000 shekels.

The gymnasts' attorney, Yaniv Gavish, argued during the proceedings that the sporting bodies had prioritised team achievements and competition participation over the athletes' physical health, according to ONE. He said the neglect led directly to surgeries the pair required and to the likelihood that they will need joint-replacement operations later in life.

The Wingate Institute, based near Netanya, has for decades served as the training base for Israel's Olympic gymnastics programme, while the Israel Gymnastics Federation and the Olympic Committee of Israel jointly oversee the sport at the national level — all three were named as defendants in the suit.

ONE did not identify the two gymnasts by name in its report. The ruling marks one of the first times an Israeli court has held national sporting federations and their training institute directly liable for long-term harm caused by inadequate medical oversight of young elite athletes.

title: Israel U18 women beat Romania 85-66 to win Eurobasket Division B title
dek: Maya Zilbershlag named tournament MVP as Roei Eisenberg's side complete an unbeaten run in Tulcea, Romania, and secure promotion to Division A.

verificationSources.label: FIBA U18 Women's EuroBasket 2026, Division B (official)
FIBA — All you need to know: U18 Women's EuroBasket Division B 2026
Yahoo Sports — Zilbershlag, Israel embrace challenge at U18 Euros

body: Israel's national under-18 women's basketball team stormed to the Division B title at EuroBasket in Tulcea, Romania on Sunday, beating the hosts 85-66 in the final to complete a perfect 7-0 run through the tournament and secure promotion to Division A.

The result, confirmed on FIBA's official tournament site, capped nine days of competition in the Black Sea port city that began on July 31. Israel won every one of its seven games on the way to the final, including a 78-63 semi-final victory over Austria.

There was little late drama to the decider itself. "The girls put on quite a show here. From the opening, there was no question who would win," coach Roei Eisenberg told ONE, which covered the campaign from Tulcea.

Guard Maya Zilbershlag, who is set to start her freshman year at Purdue this autumn, was named the tournament's Most Valuable Player — an honour FIBA's own coverage also confirmed. She arrived at the event off a strong 2025 U18 EuroBasket, where she led the tournament in scoring at 18.4 points per game.

Ma'ayan Gurin was also named to the tournament's all-star team, according to ONE, while teenager Mika Kanitz made her tournament debut in the final itself — a mark of the squad's depth even in a title-clinching match.

The win lifts Israel back into Division A of the U18 Women's EuroBasket for next summer, returning the age group to the continent's top tier. Eisenberg was already looking further down the pipeline afterward, telling ONE: "There are 6-7 girls who can easily enter the senior national team."

"There is women's basketball in Israel," he added — a pointed line given how often the women's game is overshadowed domestically by the men's, and a signal that this teenage group could shape the senior national team's fortunes within a few years.

Zilbershlag's rise has followed a similar trajectory. She has averaged 14.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists across five previous EuroBasket age-group tournaments, and helped Israel's under-20 side reach a European final for the first time earlier this summer, taking silver behind France.

Sunday's title in Tulcea rounds off an unbeaten summer for Israel's junior women's national teams, adding a Division B European crown to the under-20 silver won weeks earlier — evidence, in Eisenberg's telling, that grassroots investment in Israeli women's basketball is starting to bear fruit.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv draw Netanya, Hapoel Tel Aviv face Kiryat Shmona in Toto Cup semi-finals
dek: Both Tel Aviv giants learn their route to the Toto Cup final on the same Sunday night, with group-stage pacesetters Ironi Kiryat Shmona standing in Hapoel's way.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport — Kiryat Shmona advance to semi-final
Ynet — Kenny Miller confirmed as permanent Maccabi Tel Aviv coach

body: Israel's Toto Cup group phase has produced its semi-final draw, and it has handed both of Tel Aviv's big two a route to the next round on the very same evening. Maccabi Tel Aviv were paired with Maccabi Netanya, while Hapoel Tel Aviv were drawn against Ironi Kiryat Shmona, ONE reported.

Both ties are set for Sunday, August 16, kicking off simultaneously at 20:00, according to the outlet. Maccabi Tel Aviv's tie with Netanya will be played at Netanya's home stadium, while the Hapoel Tel Aviv-Kiryat Shmona semi-final goes ahead at HaMoshava Stadium in Petah Tikva.

Kiryat Shmona arrive as the form side of the four semi-finalists. Sport5 reported that the northern club topped its group with a perfect record of 12 points from a possible 12 — the best mark of any team in the group phase — while Maccabi Netanya advanced as the lowest-seeded of the four.

For Maccabi Tel Aviv, it is the first real cup test under Kenny Miller since his appointment was made permanent. The Scot was confirmed as head coach for the 2026/27 season, with an option for a further year, having steered the club to the State Cup as interim boss during the previous campaign's playoffs, Ynet and the club reported at the time.

Hapoel Tel Aviv, by contrast, go into their semi-final under a coach who already knows what it takes to go deep in cup football. Elyaniv Barda, in the job since December 2024, has taken the Reds from the second-tier Leumit League into European competition in little more than a year, after previously guiding Hapoel Be'er Sheva to a State Cup and a league title.
Sport5 reported that the Toto Cup final itself is provisionally pencilled in for December, though an exact date has not yet been confirmed.

The two Tel Aviv ties are not the only business on the weekend's card. ONE reported that Sunday also features ranking playoffs further down the group-stage table — Bnei Sakhnin against Hapoel Petah Tikva for 13th-14th place, and Ironi Tiberias hosting Maccabi Petah Tikva for 11th-12th.

A day later, the round continues with Maccabi Haifa hosting Hapoel Jerusalem at Sami Ofer Stadium and Hapoel Ramat Gan facing Beitar Jerusalem at a neutral ground in Rehovot, both kicking off simultaneously on the Monday, per ONE's schedule.

For Miller and Barda, though, Sunday's double-header in Netanya and Petah Tikva is the story that matters most: two of Israeli football's biggest institutions, both hoping to bank silverware in sight before a ball is even kicked in the new league season.

title: Hapoel Beit She'an to replace Herzliya as Israel's UEFA Regions' Cup representative
dek: The amateur side steps in for next month's European tournament in Latvia after Hapoel Herzliya withdrew, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE — Hapoel Beit She'an to replace Herzliya in the amateur cup
ONE — UEFA amateur cup shaping up close to Rosh Hashanah
UEFA.com — 2026/27 UEFA Regions' Cup preliminary and intermediate round draw
UEFA.com — Ironi Nesher club page, UEFA Regions' Cup

body: Hapoel Beit She'an have been confirmed as Israel's representative at next month's UEFA Regions' Cup, stepping in after Hapoel Herzliya withdrew from the amateur continental tournament, ONE reported.

Beit She'an had already been named the Israel Football Association's official alternate following a draw held among four Israeli amateur clubs back in June, according to the outlet. With Herzliya now out, that standby status has been confirmed and the northern club will fly the flag for Israel in Latvia.

The UEFA Regions' Cup is UEFA's biennial competition for regional and amateur representative sides rather than professional league clubs, run in parallel to the Champions League and Europa League pyramid. Countries without a formal regional structure, Israel among them, typically send the winner of a dedicated domestic amateur qualifying process.

This edition's intermediate round is scheduled for September 1-9, with matches to be played on September 2, 5 and 8 in Latvia, ONE reported. Israel has been drawn in a group alongside hosts Latvia, Hungary, and the Federación Canaria de Fútbol, the Canary Islands body representing Spain — the country whose regional sides have won the competition four times, most recently through Aragón in 2025.

The timing is awkward. ONE's earlier reporting noted the trip falls right around Rosh Hashanah and clashes with the opening rounds of Israel's domestic league season, which kicks off in late August — a scheduling squeeze that will complicate whichever club made the trip.

Israel's amateur game has sent a rotating cast of representatives to the competition over the years, including Maccabi Tzur Shalom and a combined Karmiel/Safed selection in past editions. ONE also noted that Ironi Nesher had been set to represent Israel in the 2023/24 edition but was withdrawn on security grounds after Kazakhstan was designated as host country that year.

For Beit She'an, a club that has spent recent seasons in Israel's lower divisions after folding and reforming in the 2000s, the call-up is a rare continental assignment squeezed into the final days of pre-season. No squad or travel details had been released at the time of ONE's report.
Herzliya's reasons for pulling out were not detailed in the report. The Israel Football Association has not yet issued its own statement confirming the swap.

title: From $7 to $684: what it costs to watch Israel's stars abroad
dek: New SeatPick data maps out the going rate to watch Oscar Gloukh, Manor Solomon, Daniel Peretz and Israel's other exports across Europe and MLS — and the gap between the cheapest seat and the priciest is enormous.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz - Manor Solomon set to join West Ham from Tottenham
Times of Israel - Anan Khalaili set to sign with Crystal Palace

body: Ever wondered what it actually costs to go and watch Israel's football exports play? According to fresh data compiled by the ticket comparison platform SeatPick and reported by ONE, the answer swings wildly — from a $7 seat in Washington D.C. to a $684 ticket in south London, depending entirely on which club, and which opponent, a fan picks.

The comparison covers ten Israeli internationals scattered across eight clubs in England, the Netherlands and MLS, tracking each club's cheapest available ticket, a typical entry price and the average across the season.

MLS remains by far the budget option. DC United, home to new signing Tai Baribo since his move from Philadelphia Union, tops the cheap list: tickets start from $7, with a typical entry price of $13 and a seasonal average of $66.

The other MLS clubs on Israel's export list cluster close behind. New England Revolution, where striker Dor Turgeman and defender Ilay Feingold both play, start from around $10 with an average near $99. Charlotte FC — home to Liel Abada and Idan Toklomati — starts from roughly $17 and averages about $102, while FC Dallas, who signed midfielder Ran Binyamin from Hapoel Tel Aviv, starts from about $24 and averages $95.

There is one sizeable exception even within MLS's budget bracket: fixtures against Lionel Messi's Inter Miami. SeatPick's data puts those games in the $284-$293 range on average — a reminder, as the platform's own numbers show, that the opponent can matter as much as the home club.

Cross the Atlantic and prices climb sharply. Southampton, where goalkeeper Daniel Peretz completed a permanent move from Bayern Munich, starts from $74 and averages $144. West Ham — who this week agreed a reported £7m deal to sign winger Manor Solomon from Tottenham — starts from $45 with an average of $125.

The steepest prices on the list belong to Crystal Palace and Ajax. Palace, who are closing in on a move for winger Anan Khalaili from Belgium's Union SG in a deal reported at around €28m ($32.5m) — which would make him the most expensive Israeli player in history — averages $326 a ticket, but a fixture against Arsenal alone averages $684, the single highest figure in the entire dataset. Ajax, home to attacking midfielder Oscar Gloukh, isn't far behind at $353 on average.
"Fans tend to start their search by club or by the star they want to see, but the data show the identity of the opponent matters just as much," Guy Kogel, SeatPick's CTO and co-founder, told ONE.

The spread underlines just how far Israeli football's footprint abroad has spread this transfer window — from bargain seats at DC United to a five-figure trip to Amsterdam or south London — and how much choice of fixture, not just choice of club, now shapes the bill for fans wanting to follow their countrymen.

title: Ironi Tiberias hand entire youth academy to home-grown coaching staff
dek: Eleven appointees, most with playing careers or deep personal ties to the club, will run every age group from under-8 to under-19 as Tiberias heads into a new season in Ligat Ha'al.

verificationSources.label: Walla Sport - Ironi Tiberias, Ligat Ha'al table

body: Ironi Tiberias have decided that the people best placed to shape the club's next generation are the ones who grew up in it. ONE reports that the entire youth department for the 2026/27 season will be staffed by a home-grown team - eleven appointees who either played for the club, many of them in its senior side, or carry long-standing ties to Tiberias.

At the head of it all is Kfir Ben David, a former club captain who has spent recent years working his way from the pitch into the boardroom and now the touchline. He takes over as professional director of the youth department while also coaching its flagship National League youth side.

Beneath him, the club has built out a full coaching ladder rather than a token appointment or two. Eitan Pechima takes the under-19s, Moshiko Asor the under-17s, and Roei Sarah the under-15s, with Sarah doubling as academy coordinator. Adi Tadmor joins as goalkeeping coach and Shalev Ohana as the youth department's analyst.

The younger age groups have been covered too: Shlomi Ben David with the under-12s, Niv Suiva with the under-10s and Matan Degani with the under-8s. Bar Nikton was named fitness coach across the department, and Shlomi Hachmon takes on operations.

The club framed the appointments as a statement of identity as much as a staffing decision, saying in comments carried by ONE that "the future of Ironi Tiberias starts here" with a team of professionals committed to developing players, promoting excellence and building the club's next generation.

The reshuffle lands at a significant moment for the club. Ironi Tiberias' senior side has been competing in Ligat Ha'al, Israel's top flight, after climbing the leagues in recent seasons, and the academy now operates out of the city's historic municipal stadium overlooking the Sea of Galilee.

For a provincial club with limited resources next to Israel's traditional powers, leaning on figures who already know the badge - rather than importing outside names - is as much a financial call as a sentimental one, and one Tiberias clearly hope will keep talent, and loyalty, running through the club for years to come.

title: Israeli athletics federation blames missing poles and early starts for World U20 struggles
dek: A statement from the Israel Athletics Association defending its young stars' below-par showing in Eugene reads like a catalogue of excuses, ONE reports — and one athlete had already gone public with her own complaint.

verificationSources.label: ONE — שלל תירוצים: ההודעה המוזרה של איגוד האתלטיקה
World Athletics — Yarden Mantel athlete profile

body: Israel's Athletics Association put out a media statement this week meant to explain the underwhelming showing of its youngest athletes at the World U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon. The result, according to ONE, read less like an honest review and more like a list of excuses.

The championships ran from August 5 to 9 at the University of Oregon's Hayward Field, drawing athletes from well over a hundred countries for track and field's flagship under-20 event. For Israel's small delegation it was a largely forgettable week — no finalists among the country's entrants, and several athletes who fell well short of their season's best form.

The federation had a different explanation for nearly every setback. Pole vaulter Yarden Mantel, per the association's own account, had to compete without her personal poles after officials failed to ship her equipment to the United States in time. Forced to make do, she no-heighted at her opening bar of 3.80 metres.

ONE notes that Mantel had already voiced her frustration over the mishap before the federation's statement appeared — meaning the association's explanation arrived as an awkward follow-up to a complaint from one of its own athletes, rather than a proactive account of what went wrong.
High jumper Joshua Harel, born in 2008, ccleared 2.17 metres to finish eighth in his final, a mark the federation said was undercut by an iliopsoas injury he picked up during the competition itself.

The remaining explanations were broader, and ONE suggests harder to swallow. Hila Varsano and Gal Nathanel were both eliminated in the 400 metres hurdles without reaching the semifinals, while Liam Aqua ran below his personal bests in both the 100m and 110m hurdles. The federation's catch-all reasoning was that early-morning heats make personal bests 'much harder' to produce.

It is on that point that ONE pushes back hardest, noting that every other federation's athletes faced the same start times, on the same days, at the same Hayward Field — and that early sessions did not stop plenty of rivals from setting personal bests and advancing through the rounds.

The episode lands awkwardly for a federation already facing scrutiny over its handling of team logistics, just as it tries to present this crop of teenagers — Mantel, Harel, Aqua, Varsano and Nathanel among them — as the foundation of Israeli athletics' next generation.

title: Hapoel Petah Tikva admit they need three or four more players before the season starts
dek: After a 3-1 Toto Cup defeat to Hapoel Jerusalem, sources at the club tell ONE that the picture will improve once reinforcements arrive — with a loan move for Bolivian defender Diego Arroyo the most advanced deal on the table.

verificationSources.label: Shakhtar Donetsk official — Diego Arroyo signing
ONE — Lotem Asers linked with Hapoel Petah Tikva

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva's preseason continues to disappoint. The club went down 3-1 to Hapoel Jerusalem in what amounted to a dead rubber at the tail end of the Toto Cup group phase, with both sides already out of contention for the knockout rounds — it was Petah Tikva's third straight defeat of the summer, following a 0-2 loss to Maccabi Netanya.

Afterwards, sources at the club moved to manage expectations rather than pretend the display had been good enough. "In the league this will look better, because last year too we hadn't clicked yet in the Toto Cup," the club told ONE. "But there's no doubt we need three or four more players to arrive here."

It is an unusually blunt admission for a club to put its name to, and it underlines how much rides on the transfer business Omer Peretz's staff still have to complete before the Ligat Ha'al season opens on August 22 against Ironi Tiberias. Petah Tikva have looked short of depth and cohesion in the warm-up games, defensively above all.

The most advanced deal on the table is for Diego Arroyo, the Bolivian defender under contract at Shakhtar Donetsk. Personal terms are said to be largely agreed, but the move depends on the Ukrainian club — which paid a reported $1 million to sign Arroyo from Bolívar in February 2025 — sanctioning a loan exit. Shakhtar have so far held off approving it, wanting a replacement lined up of their own before letting him leave.

At the back, Gabonese centre-back Alex Moucketou-Moussounda is working his way back from a hamstring strain and is close to full training. He remains a doubt for Petah Tikva's next Toto Cup outing, against Bnei Sakhnin, with the staff wary of rushing him given the priority is having him ready for the league opener rather than a dead-rubber cup tie.

Lotem Asers has separately been reported by ONE as a candidate to join the club this window, one of several names the technical staff are weighing as they try to add the bodies Peretz says are missing before the campaign proper begins.

With just under two weeks left before Ironi Tiberias arrive to open the season, time is short. Budget constraints mean Petah Tikva are unlikely to land everyone on their wish list, but the club's own words make clear that at least one further arrival is considered essential before a ball is kicked in anger.

title: Liverpool 2-3 Monaco: Iraola admits his side lack the energy to last 90 minutes
dek: New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola took charge at Anfield for the first time and saw a 2-0 lead collapse into a defeat to Monaco, saying his squad still need time to build up their fitness.

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports - Liverpool appoint Iraola as Slot's successor

body: Andoni Iraola's first evening in the Anfield dugout ended in defeat, and in a blunt admission about the state of his new squad's conditioning. Liverpool surrendered a two-goal lead to lose 2-3 to Monaco in Sunday's pre-season friendly, and the Spaniard did not dress it up afterwards.

"There isn't enough energy to play 90 minutes," Iraola said, according to ONE. "Those who played their first or second match showed energy, the problem is that right now they probably don't have the energy for 90 minutes. They started to get tired, and that's something that will take time. We need more training with them, but we can take a lot of positives from today, and also a lot of negatives."

Liverpool had made a lively start. Alexander Isak put them ahead in the 16th minute, and Florian Wirtz doubled the lead 13 minutes later, giving the Anfield crowd an early glimpse of the front two Iraola is building his attack around. But Monaco, the Ligue 1 side who finished as Liverpool's opponents on this pre-season stop, clawed their way back into it before the break.

Aleksandr Golovin converted a penalty on the stroke of half-time to make it 2-1, and Mika Biereth levelled early in the second half. Monaco completed the turnaround in the 88th minute through substitute Paris Brunner, sealing a 3-2 win that mirrored, uncomfortably for Iraola, a similar collapse from a two-goal lead against Leeds United the previous week.
"We played a good first half but we don't have much more in terms of the level required to play like this," Iraola said, per ONE. "And then they were a lot better in the second half."

The manager, who took over at Anfield in June after Liverpool sacked Arne Slot following a disappointing title defence, made wholesale changes at the interval as he tries to spread minutes across his squad before the Premier League season begins. Alisson and Virgil van Dijk both featured, alongside Luis Díaz and Mohamed Salah, while Victor Muñoz made his first non-competitive appearance for the club as a substitute.

Iraola, who arrived at Liverpool on a two-year deal after leading Bournemouth to a top-six finish and their first European qualification, was the club's only candidate for the job once Slot was dismissed. He now has to knit together a squad still building match sharpness with the new season fast approaching, and said he hopes to have further options available, including Curtis Jones, for the next warm-up match against Como.

"As soon as we made some changes, they start to get tired, we cannot sustain that level, so we have work to do," Iraola said of the pattern that has now repeated itself in back-to-back friendlies. There is no Israeli involvement in this fixture, but with Liverpool among the clubs Israeli football fans follow most closely, Iraola's opening weeks on Merseyside will be watched with interest before the competitive season kicks off.

title: Maccabi Petach Tikva beat Hapoel Ramat Gan 2-1: 'When we're together longer, we'll look a lot better'
dek: Samuel Owusu and Liran Hazan scored either side of the hour to give Ziv Arie's side their first win of the Toto Cup campaign, with the club pointing to a squad still settling in.

verificationSources.label: ONE — match reaction and squad-building report
ONE — Hapoel Ramat Gan miss the semi-finals, lose 2-1

body: Maccabi Petach Tikva finally have something to build on. Ziv Arie's side beat Hapoel Ramat Gan 2-1 on Sunday in their final Toto Cup Group A fixture, a first win of the pre-season campaign after three straight defeats in the competition.

Samuel Owusu, the Ghanaian winger signed this summer from Serbia's OFK Beograd, put Maccabi Petach Tikva ahead in the 63rd minute, and Liran Hazan doubled the lead 12 minutes later. Amit Tzur pulled one back for Hapoel Ramat Gan in the 84th, but the visitors had needed a win to reach the Toto Cup semi-finals and instead finished two points adrift of group winners Maccabi Netanya, according to ONE's report of the match.

For Maccabi Petach Tikva, promoted back to the top flight and now working under a new head coach after Ziv Arie replaced Noam Shoham in May, the result carried more weight than three cup points. It was the clearest sign yet that a squad assembled largely from scratch this summer is starting to knit together.

"When we've been together for a while with the full squad, we'll look a lot better," the club said afterwards, according to ONE — a message aimed as much at supporters' patience as at the dressing room itself.

Owusu was singled out as the game's central figure, continuing the early promise he has shown since his move from Serbia. Alongside him, English recruit Kyle Spence, who joined this summer on a one-year deal with the option of a second, is also settling in quickly.

There is more still to come. Itay Tibi is expected to make his debut this weekend against Hapoel Tiberias, while Ariel Lugasi has returned to the squad after a year without official minutes. Lee-Yam Dan, working back from injury, could also be involved by Saturday.

On the incoming side, Yoav Koren — who scored seven goals last season for Hapoel Kfar Saba — is expected to complete his move to the club by the weekend, once Hapoel Beer Sheva's continental commitments against Red Star Belgrade are out of the way. Not every piece has fallen Maccabi Petach Tikva's way, though: right-back target Noam Schwartz will not be joining after all, instead signing for Hapoel Ramat Gan — the very team his prospective new club just beat.

None of it changes where the priorities lie. The club has made clear that the Toto Cup group phase, now finished for both sides, was always secondary to building a squad capable of holding its own in the league season that follows.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv recall center Shane Hunter from Legia Warsaw loan
dek: The American big man, signed to a three-year deal in 2024, is being brought back into Oded Kattash's frontcourt after a productive season on loan in Poland.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are ending Shane Hunter's loan spell early, recalling the American forward-center from Legia Warsaw and folding him straight into Oded Kattash's frontcourt for the coming season, the club confirmed and ONE reports.

Hunter, 25, signed a three-year contract with the yellow-and-blue in the summer of 2024 but never actually suited up in Tel Aviv. Instead he was immediately loaned out to continue developing against senior competition in Europe, first with Legia Warsaw in Poland.

The bet paid off. Across last season Hunter averaged 9.2 points, 5 rebounds and 1.3 blocks a game for Legia while shooting 63 percent on two-point attempts, numbers that speak to his efficiency as a rim-runner and finisher inside. In the Basketball Champions League specifically, he was even more productive: 8.8 points, 6.5 rebounds and a block a night, with a 12.0 efficiency rating.

"Shane Hunter completes a deep and versatile frontcourt for us," Kattash said, according to ONE. "He gained important experience in Europe last season. He is a big man who moves very well without the ball, shoots at a high percentage from two-point range, rebounds well, is highly mobile in the pick-and-roll and affects opposing shots with his blocking."

At 2.08 meters (6'10"), Hunter arrived at Maccabi with a track record of winning. Before signing with the Israeli champions, he spent a season with Sweden's Norrköping Dolphins, where he averaged 14.3 points, 8.6 rebounds, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks across 30 regular-season games and helped the club to the domestic title, earning Finals MVP honors in the process.
He played his college basketball at Nova Southeastern University in Florida before making the jump to professional ball in Europe.

The recall gives Kattash another mobile, shot-blocking big to work with as Maccabi rebuild their frontcourt depth ahead of the new campaign, with Hunter now expected to compete for real minutes in Tel Aviv rather than continue developing on loan.

title: UEFA, AFC and Concacaf accuse Infantino of breach of trust over World Cup rights sale
dek: In an unprecedented joint letter, the presidents of three of football's six continental confederations say Gianni Infantino's abandoned plan to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights was pushed through "through deception" and demand a fully independent investigation.

verificationSources.label: ONE — סערה בעולם הכדורגל: המכתב המשותף נגד אינפנטינו
France 24 — UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC slam Infantino, say football 'belongs to no individual'
Inside World Football — AFC, Concacaf and UEFA presidents tell Infantino football is not his possession
Al Jazeera — UEFA confirms legal letter served to FIFA after Infantino's World Cup plan

body: Football's governing order rarely fractures in public. On Monday it did: UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf published a joint letter accusing FIFA president Gianni Infantino of a fundamental breach of trust, in one of the most direct challenges an Infantino leadership has faced since he took charge of world football's governing body in 2016.

The letter, signed by UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin, AFC president Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa and Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, along with the three confederations' general secretaries, was published as reported by ONE and corroborated by multiple international outlets.

At issue is a now-abandoned FIFA plan to sell roughly a fifth of the commercial rights to the World Cup — ticketing, broadcasting, licensing and sponsorship revenue — to outside investors, in a scheme reported to be worth around $4.2 billion and to involve, among others, an investment firm linked to Joshua Kushner. FIFA dropped the proposal only days after it became public, amid a global outcry.

The three confederations say the manner in which the plan was advanced, not just its substance, is what has broken trust. "When trust is broken through deception, and someone places themselves before the collective that entrusted authority to them, that duty is abandoned," the letter states, according to ONE's report.

They describe the process as rushed through on a compressed timeline and without meaningful consultation of member federations, calling it evidence of "deep leadership failure" rather than an isolated lapse in judgment.

"Football's strength has always been in its unity, and we call on leaders to serve the game instead of trying to control it," the letter adds — a pointed line given that UEFA, AFC and Concacaf between them represent the overwhelming majority of FIFA's member associations and clubs.

The confederations are demanding a fully independent, external investigation into how the sale was developed and presented, explicitly rejecting the idea that FIFA can credibly review itself. UEFA has separately reiterated an earlier demand that "all relevant documents and records must be preserved" to allow any inquiry to proceed unimpeded.

The letter follows a tense fortnight for FIFA. UEFA has already served what it described as a formal legal letter warning of possible legal action over the failed sell-off, and Infantino himself used a public letter in late July to accuse critics of the 2026 World Cup of "spreading hate," a response that did little to calm the row.

Notably, the joint statement stops short of explicitly calling for Infantino's resignation. But a coordinated public rebuke from three of the sport's six continental confederations — bodies that rarely align so visibly against the man who sits atop world football — signals a level of institutional anger that FIFA has not faced in years.

No Israeli federation or club is party to the letter, but the dispute matters far beyond Zurich: any FIFA governance shake-up, or a genuine external investigation into the World Cup's commercial rights, would ripple through every confederation and member association, including the Israel Football Association, which sits under UEFA.

title: Maccabi Haifa academy graduate Amit Arzi signs new long-term contract
dek: The 21-year-old midfielder, back from a season on loan at Hapoel Kfar Saba, has committed his future to the club that has raised him since he was eight.

verificationSources.label: ONE — הכישרון של מכבי חיפה חתם על חוזה חדש במועדון
Maccabi Haifa official site — Amit Arzi player profile

body: Maccabi Haifa have tied down one of their own academy products, confirming that midfielder Amit Arzi has signed a new long-term contract with the club, ONE reports.
The deal is for two years with a club option for a further two, keeping Arzi, 21, in green through at least the 2027-28 season.

Arzi joined Maccabi Haifa's youth setup at the age of eight and worked his way through every age group before breaking into senior football roughly two years ago. Last season he went out on loan to Hapoel Kfar Saba, one of Haifa's partner clubs in the second tier, where he played regular first-team minutes and, by the club's own account, impressed enough to earn a route back.

"Maccabi is my home since I was a small child," Arzi said after putting pen to paper. "I'm thrilled to sign a long-term contract and will do everything to prove myself and help the team achieve its goals."

Professional manager Lior Rafalov praised the progress Arzi has shown. "Amit is in an excellent growth process," Rafalov said. "In his last two years in the youth ranks he stood out especially, and last season, as part of our cooperation with Hapoel Kfar Saba, he played a full season at a high level. He's come back stronger, and his performances in training are impressing us a great deal."

The new contract comes after a turbulent stretch for the player last year, when a proposed loan move to Liga Leumit side Bnei Reineh broke down over playing-time guarantees, sending him to Kfar Saba instead. That episode ultimately worked in his favour: the extra senior football appears to have convinced the Sammy Ofer Stadium hierarchy he is ready to be part of their long-term planning rather than moved on.

For a club that has built its recent transfer strategy on selling academy graduates for significant fees, keeping Arzi under contract also protects his value — whether that means a role in Haifa's own squad this season or, eventually, another loan spell with first-team minutes elsewhere.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv basketball set six-game preseason tour through Bulgaria, Serbia and Sardinia
dek: Dimitrios Itoudis's squad will test themselves against Partizan Belgrade, FMP and a Cagliari tournament field including Bayern Munich before the EuroLeague opener against the Bavarians in Sofia on September 24.

verificationSources.label: EuroLeague game center: Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv vs FC Bayern Munich, 2026-09-24
Eurohoops: Hapoel Tel Aviv to begin the season in Sofia amid security concerns

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have mapped out their run-in to the 2026/27 season, with ONE reporting that Dimitrios Itoudis's squad will play six preparation games across three countries before a ninth-of-September domestic curtain-raiser.
The tour opens in Bulgaria with two matches away to Balkan Botevgrad, on August 29 and August 31, giving the Greek coach his first look at how a reshaped roster fits together under game conditions.

From there the squad moves to Serbia for a testing back-to-back: Partizan Belgrade on September 5, followed a day later by FMP, both EuroLeague-and-ABA-League-standard opposition that should sharpen the group ahead of the continental campaign.

The preparation period concludes in Sardinia, where Hapoel will take part in a four-team tournament in Cagliari on September 12 and 13, playing two games against a field that, according to ONE, includes Bayern Munich, ASVEL Villeurbanne and Roma.

Once the friendlies are done, the competitive calendar starts quickly. The Winner Cup group stage opens on September 8, before the Israeli Super Cup on September 17 pits Hapoel against city rivals Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The EuroLeague season then begins on September 24 against Bayern Munich — a fixture EuroLeague's own schedule confirms for that date. It will not be played at Hapoel's usual Tel Aviv home: the club has already announced it is relocating its EuroLeague home games to Arena 8888 in Sofia, Bulgaria, for the season because of the security situation in Israel, a switch reported separately by Eurohoops.

That relocation adds extra context to the preseason itinerary — the trip to Bulgaria is also a chance for the squad to get a feel for the country that will effectively serve as their European base for the year ahead.

ONE's report gives no further detail on personnel moves, but the club has been reshaping its roster over the summer, and Itoudis is expected to use all six warm-up games to settle on his rotation before the games start to count.

title: Maccabi Petah Tikva 2-1 Hapoel Ramat Gan: Toto Cup dream ends for Ramat Gan Givatayim
dek: A late Amit Tzur strike wasn't enough as Messay Dego's newly promoted side missed out on the semi-finals, with Maccabi Netanya going through in their place.

verificationSources.label: Sofascore — Maccabi Petah Tikva v Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim

body: Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim's run in the Toto Cup is over. A 2-1 defeat away to Maccabi Petah Tikva in the final round of group play on Sunday leaves the newly promoted club out of the semi-finals, with Maccabi Netanya going through in their place.

Samuel Owusu put the hosts ahead shortly after the hour before Liran Hazan doubled the lead — Maccabi Petah Tikva's first win of the campaign. Amit Tzur, one of several young players given a chance by coach Messay Dego this summer, pulled a goal back late on, but there was no time left to complete a comeback.

Ramat Gan needed a win in Petah Tikva to leapfrog Netanya and reach the knockout stage. Instead they finish second in their group, missing out on the extra fixture — and the gate revenue and profile that would have come with it — for a club still building itself up after its return to the top flight.
"Maccabi Petah Tikva defeated us in the small details," the club said in its reaction to the defeat, according to ONE. "They were more physical and wanted it more; we woke up too late."

There were still positives for Dego to take into the new Ligat Ha'al season. ONE reports that Ofek Ovadia and Omer Yitzhaki both impressed in group-stage minutes alongside Tzur, evidence the head coach's willingness to blood younger players is paying off even in a losing cause.

Off the pitch, the club continues to reinforce its squad. According to Sport1-Maariv, a deal for Cameroonian striker Marius Novicki, 29, is close to completion, while ONE reports Ramat Gan are also in talks over Serbian defender Sergjan Mijalovic — additions the coaching staff hope will strengthen a squad adjusting to life back in the top flight.

Dego, an Addis Ababa-born former Israel under-21 international who took Ramat Gan up from the second tier last season, signed a contract extension over the summer to continue the project. The Toto Cup exit is unlikely to change the club's broader planning, but it does close off one route to an early trophy push.

Ramat Gan's next test comes in a friendly against Beitar Jerusalem as preparations continue for the start of the Ligat Ha'al season, where simply consolidating top-flight status will be the priority after Sunday's disappointment.

title: Israel's men book a place in the 4x200m freestyle relay final at the European Championships
dek: Denis Loktev, Eitan Ben-Shitrit, Alexey Glivinskiy and Daniel Krichevsky clocked 7:06.71 to reach Tuesday's final in Paris, while Aviva Barzily and Tom Minis advanced in the 200m backstroke.

verificationSources.label: ONE - נבחרת השליחים לגברים עלתה לגמר 4X200

body: Israel's men's 4x200m freestyle relay swam their way into Tuesday's final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, touching in 7:06.71 in Monday's heats to qualify as the fourth-fastest quartet in the field.

The team of Denis Loktev, Eitan Ben-Shitrit, Alexey Glivinskiy and Daniel Krichevsky held off the chasing pack to secure their lane for the final, continuing Israel's recent run of competitiveness in the event.

Germany set the pace in the heats with 7:04.83, with Britain (7:05.07) and Lithuania (7:05.93) also inside the top three. Israel's time put them within a stroke or two of the podium contenders heading into the final.

It is familiar territory for this event for Israel, whose 4x200m free relay reached the final at the Paris Olympics two years ago after breaking the national record in the heats, before finishing last in that showdown. Monday's swim suggests the squad, now with Krichevsky and Ben-Shitrit in the mix, is aiming to go a step further this time.

Elsewhere in the pool, Aviva Barzily and 21-year-old Tom Minis both advanced through the women's 200m backstroke heats. Barzily went 2:11.55 to finish 10th, while Minis lowered her personal best to 2:12.40 to book her own semifinal spot.

There was less joy in the men's 50m butterfly, where none of Israel's four entrants advanced. Miron Haruty led them home in 23.51, with Martin Kertabi setting a personal best of 23.77, Tom Sale touching in 24.42 and Michael Leitrovskiy in 24.47.
In the women's 100m freestyle, Daria Golovati (55.37) and Leah Polonsky (55.84) also competed without reaching the next round.
Mark Teller shaved 0.06 seconds off his personal best in the men's 100m breaststroke, stopping the clock at 1:00.80.
Attention now turns to Tuesday, when Loktev, Ben-Shitrit, Glivinskiy and Krichevsky will look to improve on their heat time and push for a top finish in the 4x200m freestyle relay final.

title: Shahar Shalmon to stay at Maccabi Ashdod for a third season as Ben Dor joins Maccabi Petach Tikva
dek: Guard extends his run with the Premier League new boys after two straight promotions, while the young center swaps Hapoel Galil Elyon for a Liga Leumit move, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE — שחר שלמון ממשיך באשדוד, בן דר עבר ללאומית
Ashdod Net — מכבי אשדוד: רביב פיטשון ושחר שלמון ממשיכים לעונה נוספת

body: Maccabi Ashdod's rise through the Israeli basketball pyramid keeps its core intact. Shahar Shalmon, the 23-year-old guard who has been part of back-to-back promotions with the club, has agreed to stay on for a third straight season, ONE reported on Sunday — this time in the top-flight Ligat Ha'al rather than the second-tier Liga Leumit he has known so far.

Shalmon, who stands 1.90m, came through the Maccabi Rishon LeZion youth system before joining Ashdod ahead of the 2024/25 campaign. He has been a fixture of the club's climb ever since, and last season, playing in Liga Leumit, he averaged 6.8 points and 4 rebounds a game — modest numbers, but enough to make him a fan favourite in a squad built around continuity rather than marquee names.

His return was echoed by a separate report from Ashdod Net, which named Reviv Pitschon alongside Shalmon as players the club is retaining as it prepares for its first season in the top division. For a newly promoted side, keeping a homegrown-feeling piece like Shalmon around is as much a statement of identity as it is a basketball decision.

The same ONE report carried a second, smaller item from elsewhere in the league: Ron Ben Dor, a 19-year-old center listed at 2.07m, is on the move. Ben Dor, who played this past season for Hapoel Galil Elyon, is joining Maccabi Petach Tikva, with the report tying the switch to Liga Leumit.

No transfer fee, contract length or quotes from either club accompanied the report, and Ben Dor's exact registration status — whether he departs Galil Elyon's senior roster or its development ranks — was not spelled out. At 19 and already 2.07m, though, he fits the profile of a big man clubs like to bring in on a development track rather than a marquee signing.

Between the two items, the picture from ONE is one of a Liga Leumit engine room quietly restocking itself: a proven promotion piece staying loyal to the club that gave him his platform, and a teenage center looking for more minutes with a new one.
