title: Moscow, 8 May 2005: The 7–0 Run That Made Maccabi Back-to-Back Champions of Europe
dek: A year after breaking the Tel Aviv scoreboard, Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Tau Cerámica in the Olimpiysky Arena to become the first club to retain the EuroLeague crown — with Šarūnas Jasikevičius doing the damage.

verificationSources.label: EuroLeague official site — 2005 Final Four MVP: Sarunas Jasikevicius, Maccabi
Wikipedia — Alexander Gomelsky EuroLeague Coach of the Year

body: Twelve months earlier, Maccabi Tel Aviv had blown the season apart in a way nobody expected, thrashing Skipper Bologna in a Tel Aviv final so lopsided it is remembered for the scoreboard, not the scoreline. The harder question, in the spring of 2005, was whether Pini Gershon's team could do it again. No club had managed to defend the EuroLeague title since the competition adopted its modern format in 2000–01; Kinder Bologna, Panathinaikos, Barcelona and Maccabi itself had each taken a turn at the top, one season at a time, before handing the trophy on.

The 2005 Final Four was staged in Moscow's Olimpiysky Arena, a cavernous venue built for the 1980 Olympics, with host club CSKA seen by many as the team to beat on its own floor. That script tore up in the semifinals on 6 May: Tau Cerámica Vitoria, the ambitious Basque club built around Dejan Bodiroga and a deep Spanish and Serbian rotation, stunned CSKA 85–78, while Maccabi eased past Panathinaikos 91–82 to set up a final nobody had quite predicted.

Two days later, in front of 13,607 fans, Tau pushed Maccabi hard. The Basque side had matched the Israelis possession for possession into the second half, and with the game locked at 62–60 in the third quarter it still felt like anyone's final. Then Šarūnas Jasikevičius, the Lithuanian guard who had already won a EuroLeague title with Maccabi the year before, took the game by the throat, igniting a 7–0 run that tipped the balance for good.

Maccabi pulled clear and closed out a 90–78 win that never again looked in serious doubt. Jasikevičius finished with 22 points, six rebounds and five assists, numbers that made him an easy choice as Final Four MVP — his second such honour in as many years, and one that put him alongside Arvydas Sabonis as the only Lithuanians to win it. Around him, Maceo Baston added 18 points and Nikola Vujčić chipped in 13 points and 7 assists from the middle, the kind of scoring balance that had carried Maccabi through the whole campaign.

The victory made Maccabi the first club to retain the EuroLeague championship since the tournament's rebrand under ULEB five years earlier — a repeat that had eluded Bologna, Panathinaikos and Barcelona before them. It was the club's fifth European title in all, stretching back to Ralph Klein's continental breakthroughs of the 1970s, and it confirmed Maccabi, coached by the brash and unapologetic Gershon, as the dominant force in European basketball of the mid-2000s.

Gershon's reward went beyond the trophy itself: he became the first coach honoured with what is now known as the Alexander Gomelsky Trophy for EuroLeague Coach of the Year, an award instituted that same season and named for the Soviet coaching legend who had died only months earlier. For a coach whose confrontational public style had made him as many critics as admirers, back-to-back EuroLeague titles were an answer that needed no translation.

The roster that took the floor in Moscow was a snapshot of how Maccabi built its dynasty — a handful of naturalized and imported stars around a core of Israeli internationals. Derrick Sharp, the Orlando-born guard who had become an Israeli citizen through marriage in the 1990s and would go on to captain the club for over a decade, anchored the backcourt alongside Jasikevičius. Israeli players Tal Burstein, Gur Shelef and Yotam Halperin filled out the rotation behind the likes of Vujčić, Baston and Anthony Parker, the mix of homegrown talent and recruited firepower that had become the club's trademark under Gershon.

For Maccabi Tel Aviv, the Moscow final closed out a two-year run that Israeli basketball had never produced before and has not fully repeated since — not simply winning Europe's biggest club prize, but winning it back. Twenty years on, the 90–78 scoreline in the Olimpiysky Arena is remembered less for the trophy itself than for the seven straight points that decided who would keep it.
facts: Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Tau Cerámica Vitoria 90–78 in the EuroLeague final on 8 May 2005 at the Olimpiysky Arena in Moscow, in front of 13,607 spectators.

It was Maccabi's second consecutive EuroLeague title, after beating Skipper Bologna in the 2004 final in Tel Aviv, making Maccabi the first club to retain the EuroLeague crown since the competition's modern ULEB-era format began in 2000–01.

Lithuanian guard Šarūnas Jasikevičius was named 2005 Final Four MVP after scoring 22 points with 6 rebounds and 5 assists in the final, sparking a decisive 7–0 run in the third quarter when the score was tied at 62–60.
In the 6 May 2005 semifinals, Maccabi beat Panathinaikos 91–82, while Tau Cerámica upset host club CSKA Moscow 85–78 to reach the final.
Head coach Pini Gershon became the first recipient of the award now known as the Alexander Gomelsky Trophy for EuroLeague Coach of the Year, introduced that same season.
American-born guard Derrick Sharp, a naturalized Israeli citizen since the mid-1990s, played on the title-winning roster alongside Israeli internationals Tal Burstein, Gur Shelef and Yotam Halperin.

title: Israel's U-20 water polo team beat Belarus 17-11 to open European Division One in Portugal
dek: Amir Shafrir scored five as Israel's young reserve squad opened its bid for promotion back to Europe's top flight with a comfortable win in Oeiras.

verificationSources.label: ONE — נבחרת העתודה בכדורמים ניצחה את בלארוס
Wikipedia — 2026 Men's European U-20 Water Polo Championship Division I

body: Israel's national U-20 reserve water polo team opened its campaign at the second-tier European Championship with a 17-11 win over Belarus in Oeiras, Portugal, on Monday, ONE reported.
The young Israelis set the tone early, taking the first quarter 6-3, and put the match beyond doubt with a 5-0 scoring burst through the third period that Belarus never recovered from.
Amir Shafrir led the scoring with five goals, with Tomer Arzi adding four. Kai Mitak and Raz Shrir each scored three, and Itay Goshen chipped in with two as Israel's attack fired on all levels.

The tournament, known in Israel as "Division B" and officially the Men's European U-20 Water Polo Championship Division I, runs from 10-16 August and doubles as a route back to Europe's elite tier for the teams that finish in the top two of their group.

Israel were drawn in a pool with Ukraine, Switzerland, Great Britain and Belgium. A parallel group features Georgia, Poland, Lithuania, Finland, hosts Portugal and Belarus's fellow returnees Russia, who came back into European competition this year after their ban was lifted.

Head coach Marco Ćurić framed the win as a first step rather than a destination. "Our main goal is to compete for promotion to Division A," he said, adding that the priority was "to build a strong team with clear identity, discipline and fighting spirit."

The squad leans young even by U-20 standards, built mainly around players born in 2008 and 2009 — some of them two to three years below the category's age ceiling, a sign of the depth Israeli water polo is trying to develop at youth level.
Israel are back in the water on Tuesday against Belgium, with the throw-in set for 11:00 Israel time, in a match that will go a long way toward shaping the group's promotion picture.

title: Harry Kane closes in on Bayern Munich deal through 2029
dek: The England captain is reportedly set to extend his contract by two years, with talks in advanced stages and a signing possible within days.
body: Harry Kane looks set to stay in Munich well beyond his 33rd birthday. ONE reports that Bayern Munich are closing in on a contract extension for their England captain that would run through 2029, keeping him at the club until he is 36.

The story, first reported by The Times in England, says the two sides are aligned on the major terms and that officials expect the deal to be signed within days, once Kane returns from his summer break.

Kane's current contract runs to the summer of 2027. The new terms, according to the report, would add two further years without significantly altering his base salary, which sits at around €25 million gross per season. Instead, the club is expected to restructure his performance bonuses, tied to personal and team success, rather than raise his fixed pay.

The move would end months of speculation over Kane's long-term future, with his name periodically linked to a return to the Premier League — including retirement-day talk of Tottenham Hotspur, the club he left for Bayern in 2023 — and to Barcelona.

ONE's report suggests Kane's priorities have shifted since he arrived in Bavaria. Rather than chasing Alan Shearer's all-time Premier League scoring record back in England, he is said to be focused on winning more trophies with Bayern, where he and his family have settled comfortably.

The numbers explain Bayern's eagerness to tie him down. Kane was the Bundesliga's top scorer for a third consecutive season in 2025/26, finishing with 36 league goals, and racked up 73 goals in all competitions for club and country across 65 matches between August 2025 and July 2026 — one of the most prolific single-season hauls of the century, behind only Lionel Messi's 2011/12 campaign.

Since his club-record move from Tottenham in August 2023, Kane has scored well over 140 goals in fewer than 150 appearances for Bayern, but a Bundesliga title and Champions League success with the club have so far proven elusive.

Neither Bayern nor Kane's camp has yet confirmed the extension, and the report should be read as advanced negotiation rather than a done deal — but with terms broadly settled, a formal announcement appears to be only a matter of time.
facts: Harry Kane's current Bayern Munich contract runs until summer 2027.
A reported extension would keep him at the club until 2029, when he turns 36.
His base salary of around €25 million gross per year is expected to stay largely unchanged, with bonus structures revised instead.
Kane was the Bundesliga's top scorer for a third straight season in 2025/26 with 36 league goals.
He scored 73 goals in all competitions for club and country across 65 matches between August 2025 and July 2026.
The report originated with The Times in England and was relayed by ONE.
Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur for a club-record fee in August 2023.

title: Hapoel Be'er Sheva carry 1-0 lead into Red Star Belgrade Champions League return leg
dek: Ran Kozuk's Israeli champions travel to Belgrade defending a slender first-leg advantage won with ten men, one step from a first-ever Champions League league phase.

verificationSources.label: ONE - preview with Ran Kozuk quotes
Ynet - first-leg report, 10 men, red card
Sport5 - Serbian preparations for return leg

body: Hapoel Be'er Sheva head to Belgrade on Tuesday carrying the narrowest of advantages into the biggest fixture of their season, protecting a 1-0 lead over Red Star Belgrade with a maiden Champions League league-phase place within reach for the reigning Israeli champions.

The tie sits delicately poised after last week's first leg, which Hapoel technically hosted but played at the neutral Haladás Stadium in Szombathely, Hungary, as Israeli clubs continue to stage UEFA fixtures away from home. Zahi Ahmed settled it with the only goal of the night, finishing in the 38th minute to put the Israeli side in front.

Getting there was not straightforward. Matan Baltaksa was shown two yellow cards in the same passage of play and sent off in the 58th minute, leaving Hapoel to defend their lead with ten men for more than half an hour against a Red Star side chasing an equaliser. They held on.

Now comes the sterner test: a trip to Red Star's own fortress, the Rajko Mitić Stadium — known to every Serbian fan as the Marakana — where the hosts have historically been at their most dominant. With the away-goals rule long scrapped from UEFA's books, a draw in Belgrade would be enough to send Hapoel through on aggregate.

"We're aware of what we'll face tomorrow," said Hapoel manager Ran Kozuk, quoted by ONE ahead of the trip. "We've already faced them, so we've discovered additional things" about how to approach the return fixture, he added, while cautioning that Red Star remain "a very good team" that tends to dominate whoever they play at home.

Among those Kozuk is counting on is Igor Zlatanović, the Serbian forward who has emerged as one of Hapoel's most important attacking players this season — and who, according to earlier reports in Serbia, was himself once on Red Star's radar as a transfer target before he committed his future to Be'er Sheva.

The stakes could hardly be higher for a club that has never before reached the Champions League's league phase. Hapoel Be'er Sheva enter this qualifying round fresh off winning the Israeli Premier League title, and advancing past a name as storied as Red Star Belgrade would rank among the most significant European results in the club's history.
Kick-off in Belgrade is set for Tuesday evening, with Hapoel needing only to avoid defeat to book their place among Europe's elite for the first time.

body: Bnei Yehuda used the countdown to the new Liga Leumit season to put a health message front and centre, unveiling a pink goalkeeper shirt for the 2026/27 campaign on Monday evening dedicated to raising awareness of cancer and the importance of early detection.
The Tel Aviv club, which plays in Israel's second tier this season, presented the jersey as what it called its "blessed initiative" ahead of the league's opening rounds, according to ONE.

"Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv Football Club is proud and excited to unveil the pink goalkeeper shirt for the 2026/27 season, and dedicates it to raising awareness of the fight against cancer and the importance of early detection," the club said in a statement carried by the outlet.

The statement continued with a direct appeal to supporters: "Behind this shirt stands one simple and important message that we want to convey to every woman: go get tested. Early detection can save lives."
"We are proud to use our platform to raise awareness, to remind and to encourage timely testing," the club added. "This time, pink is much more than a colour."

No individual goalkeeper was named in connection with the shirt, and the club did not identify a partner health organisation in the statement reported by ONE. The jersey is intended for the full 2026/27 season rather than a single fixture.

title: William Agada returns to Hapoel Haifa for second spell
dek: The Nigerian striker is back in the red-and-white on an annual salary of around €180,000, six years after a loan stint that produced six league goals.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Agada seals deal with Hapoel Haifa
Sport5 - earlier report on developing Agada-Haifa talks

body: Hapoel Haifa have gone back to a familiar face to lead their attack. ONE reports the club has sealed an agreement with William Agada, the 26-year-old Nigerian striker who spent a productive loan season in the red-and-white shirt back in 2020/21 and is now returning as a fully-fledged signing.
According to ONE, the deal was finalised on Monday evening and is worth an annual salary of roughly €180,000 to the player, whose agent Shahar Greenberg brokered the terms with the club.

Club owner Yoav Katz welcomed the move in a statement carried by ONE: "We are happy to bring home a player we know very well. William is a fast, quality striker with experience, and I am confident he will contribute a great deal to the team and help us achieve our goals."

Haifa know exactly what they are getting. Agada arrived on loan from Hapoel Jerusalem for the 2020/21 campaign and scored six league goals, a return that helped mark him out as one of the more effective young forwards in the Israeli top flight at the time.

His roots in Israeli football run deeper still. Agada first arrived at Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem as an 18-year-old in 2018 and, across his spells there and at the renamed Hapoel Jerusalem either side of the Haifa loan, racked up more than 60 goals in Israeli football before he turned 23.

That form earned him a move across the Atlantic. Sporting Kansas City signed Agada in 2022, and he spent close to three seasons in Major League Soccer before being traded to Real Salt Lake in April 2025. Between the two MLS clubs he scored 23 league goals, according to ONE's tally of his American career.

This past January he switched continents again, joining Real Zaragoza of Spain's Segunda División for the second half of the season. His return to Haifa now comes just months after that loan spell in Spain wound down.

For Hapoel Haifa, the signing is aimed squarely at adding firepower up front for the coming Israeli Premier League season, with the club looking to Agada's pace, know-how and goal record from his first stint to strengthen a forward line that needs sharpening before the campaign begins.

title: West Ham's Manor Solomon and Southampton's Daniel Peretz set for England's first Israeli derby
dek: A Carabao Cup second-round draw pits Solomon against Peretz just days after his move from Tottenham, with Bristol City's Lisav Eissat also in the mix across the season

verificationSources.label: West Ham United - Carabao Cup draw
Jewish Chronicle - Daniel Peretz permanent Southampton move
East London Times - West Ham 3-1 Portsmouth

body: For the first time, two Israeli internationals will line up against each other in English football when West Ham United travel to Southampton in the Carabao Cup second round, as ONE reported on Monday, with the tie scheduled for the week of August 25-26.

The draw, made on Monday, sent West Ham to St Mary's just days after the club completed the signing of Manor Solomon from Tottenham Hotspur in a deal worth an initial £5 million, with a further £2m in potential add-ons. Solomon, capped 48 times by Israel, has put pen to paper on a three-year contract with West Ham, who moved for the winger as they look to rebuild after relegation from the Premier League.

Waiting for him will be Daniel Peretz, the Southampton goalkeeper who completed his own permanent switch to the south-coast club earlier this year after impressing on loan from Bayern Munich, signing a four-year deal reported at around €7m. Peretz, who began his career at Maccabi Tel Aviv before moving to Germany, has become one of the more talked-about Israeli exports in English football since helping Southampton to last season's FA Cup success over Arsenal.

Both clubs now sit in the Championship after West Ham's relegation, meaning Solomon and Peretz are also set to face off twice more in league action this season, with league fixtures pencilled in for October 24 and December 19, according to ONE.

There is a third Israeli-connected name in the mix too. Bristol City signed defender Lisav Eissat from Maccabi Haifa on a four-year deal this summer, a player who came through the Haifa academy and had a loan spell at Hapoel Hadera. Eissat, notably, has opted to represent Romania at international level rather than Israel, but ONE's report groups him with Solomon and Peretz as part of the wider story of Israeli-developed talent now dotted through the English second tier.

Bristol City are set to meet Southampton and West Ham multiple times in the Championship campaign, with ONE listing fixtures against Peretz's side on September 12 and February 13, and against Solomon's West Ham on December 12 and January 1.

West Ham reached this stage by beating Portsmouth 3-1 at London Stadium on August 8, with Valentin Castellanos scoring twice and Jarrod Bowen also on target. Southampton have not yet played their first-round tie at the time of writing.

The Solomon-Peretz meeting is being framed by ONE as a milestone moment for Israeli football's growing footprint in England, and the outlet poses the obvious follow-up question for the season ahead: which of the two will finish the campaign in the stronger position, at a promotion-chasing West Ham or with Southampton in the Championship.

title: Mourinho blocks Roma and Aston Villa moves to keep Endrick at Real Madrid
dek: The Real Madrid coach vetoed late loan offers for the Brazilian forward, backed by club president Florentino Pérez, after his preseason form convinced Mourinho he deserves a real chance this season.

verificationSources.label: Goal.com — Endrick decides Real Madrid future as Mourinho makes final call
Managing Madrid — Roma, Aston Villa interested in Endrick loan deal

body: José Mourinho has closed the door on a Bernabéu exit for Endrick, rejecting late loan offers from Roma and Aston Villa to keep the young Brazilian forward inside his Real Madrid squad for the coming season, ONE reports.

The decision, according to the Israeli outlet, carries the full backing of club president Florentino Pérez, who signed off on retaining Endrick rather than sanctioning another temporary departure with the European transfer window set to close on September 1.

Mourinho's reasoning centres on tactical flexibility. ONE reports the Portuguese coach views the 20-year-old as more than a central striker, valuing him as a right-winger who can cut inside and create danger — a role Endrick played to strong effect at Palmeiras before his move to Spain.

Endrick's performances through preseason training are said to have been the deciding factor, convincing Mourinho that the forward has earned a genuine chance to compete for minutes this season rather than be loaned out again.

The financial backdrop explains why Madrid are reluctant to let him go. ONE reports the club paid Palmeiras a base fee of €35 million plus up to €25 million in add-ons for Endrick two years ago, and that agent fees, wages and bonuses have pushed the total outlay beyond €80 million.

Roma had positioned themselves as favourites for a loan, banking on regular Champions League football and a promise of first-team minutes to tempt the Brazilian, while Aston Villa entered the race with a late proposal of their own — interest also reported independently by Diario AS and other outlets.

Endrick spent the second half of last season on loan at Lyon, where ONE credits him with eight goals and five assists in 21 appearances (other reports put the assist tally as high as seven or eight). The form was enough to earn him a place in Brazil's squad at the 2026 World Cup under Carlo Ancelotti.

Despite the interest from Serie A and the Premier League, Endrick has committed to fighting for his place in Madrid this season. ONE notes he has not entirely ruled out a fresh loan move in January should regular playing time continue to elude him.

title: Adva Cohen fights through to 3,000m steeplechase final at European Championships
dek: The Israeli record holder recovered from a stumble at the water jump to finish eighth in her heat in Birmingham and book her place in this week's final.
body: Adva Cohen is through to the final of the women's 3,000m steeplechase at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham after grinding out eighth place in a tense qualifying heat at Alexander Stadium, ONE reported.

It was not a straightforward passage. Cohen went out fast, sitting in fourth for the early laps, before a poor landing at a water jump cost her momentum and dropped her back to seventh. She fought to stay in touch through the closing stages and crossed the line eighth, in 9:37.15, enough to advance.

The result keeps alive Cohen's hopes of a strong finish at a championship where she arrives as Israel's national record holder in the event. Her personal best of 9:19.90, set at last year's World Championships in Tokyo, remains well clear of Monday's heat time and shows she has faster in her legs for the final.

Cohen, 30, has built a habit of showing up on the European stage. Her breakthrough came in Berlin in 2018, where she stunned the field to finish fifth in the final — still the best Israeli result in the event at a European Championships. Two years ago in Rome she also reached the final, finishing 12th, according to World Athletics records.

Born in Jerusalem, Cohen first made her name on the American collegiate circuit — winning national junior college titles before continuing at the University of New Mexico — and has since developed into one of Israel's most consistent international distance runners.

Making a European final is no small feat in a discipline as physically punishing as the steeplechase, where a single bad water jump, like the one that briefly derailed Cohen on Monday, can end a race in an instant.
Israel's team in Birmingham will now be watching to see whether Cohen can build on Monday's scrap and push toward the front of the field when the final is run later in the championships.

title: Sheran Yeini says he and Eran Zahavi could team up at Maccabi one day
dek: The former Maccabi Tel Aviv captain, now dancing his way through a reality show, tells ONE it 'would be fun' to combine forces with his old strike partner at the club that raised them both — though nothing is in the works yet.
body: Sheran Yeini spent nineteen years marshalling Maccabi Tel Aviv's back line, not learning routines under a mirror ball. But with the former captain now a contestant on Israel's 'Dancing with the Stars', his old day job kept intruding on the conversation — and it was a passing line about a former strike partner that stood out.

Asked about life after football, Yeini told ONE it 'would be fun if Eran and I combine forces at Maccabi someday' — a reference to Eran Zahavi, the club's record-scoring forward and, like Yeini, a product of its youth system. He was quick to stress it isn't something the pair are actively planning, more an idea he wouldn't rule out.

The comment carries weight given who is making it. Yeini captained Maccabi Tel Aviv for much of his career, making 555 appearances and scoring 19 goals across nineteen seasons, and lifted six championships and two State Cups wearing the armband. He retired in May 2024, at 37, immediately after Maccabi's latest title triumph, and won 32 caps for Israel, captaining the national team in his final appearances.

Zahavi's own playing career ended more recently. The forward announced his retirement on 1 January 2026, three weeks shy of his 38th birthday, having gone out on the back of Maccabi Tel Aviv's second consecutive championship. He now runs a business portfolio spanning real estate, restaurants, advertising and startup investments.

Yeini, who has likewise moved into business investing since hanging up his boots, said Zahavi 'lives and breathes football' regardless of his current focus elsewhere — a remark that reads as much as an observation about where his old teammate's heart still lies as anything else.

For now, the framework for any formal role for either man at Maccabi remains entirely speculative; Yeini's comments to ONE were musing on a hypothetical, not announcing a plan. Both men, though, retain the kind of standing at the club — as boyhood products turned title-winning captains — that keeps such talk alive whenever they're asked about it.

The interview itself was prompted by Yeini's current, considerably less familiar assignment: competing in season five of 'Dancing with the Stars' on Keshet 12, partnered with dancer Karin Sorochinsky. He told ONE that messages from Maccabi supporters urging him to keep going on the show have been landing steadily — a sign that, on the dance floor or off it, he hasn't lost his audience.

title: Hapoel Lod chairman Ragev: "I may have gotten the wording wrong, I'm sorry it happened"
dek: Ophir Ragev broke his silence on claims he threatened a lawyer's life during a fight over unpaid debts blocking his club's registration, saying he was "emotional" but denies a genuine threat.

body: Ophir Ragev, chairman of Liga Bet club Hapoel Lod Bnei Regev, broke his silence this week on allegations that he threatened a lawyer's life, telling ONE's "Today's Conversation" programme that he "may have gotten the wording wrong" and was "emotional" when he sent the message at the centre of the affair.

"I apologised for it, and I was also called out for it," Ragev said on air, responding directly to attorney Ohad Cohen, who had appeared on the same programme earlier to describe what he said were explicit threats on his life.

The dispute traces back to Hapoel Lod's scramble to register players for the 2026/27 season. According to ONE's earlier report, the club faced a registration deadline with the Israel Football Association while still owing money under arbitration rulings obtained by clients of Cohen, a sports lawyer and co-chair of the Israeli Bar Association's sports law committee.

Cohen told ONE he received a threatening text message late one Thursday night, sent via a family member's phone, and said it amounted to a genuine threat on his life. He filed a police complaint for murder threats, and a restraining order barring Ragev from approaching him was subsequently issued. "Red lines have been crossed," Cohen said at the time. "Threatening a lawyer's life for doing their job is a serious crime."

Ragev, for his part, acknowledged sending a harsh message but disputed Cohen's characterisation of it as a death threat. He said he would not threaten someone while already blocked from contacting them directly, and framed his outburst as frustration over the club's financial and administrative troubles rather than genuine intent to harm anyone.

Hapoel Lod carries the name of Ragev's late father, Bnei Regev, the club's longtime mythical figure who died in 2024 and after whom the city's municipal stadium was later renamed in tribute. Ophir Ragev has been steering the club through a turbulent period since taking over, with unresolved player debts repeatedly threatening its ability to field a team.

Police brought Ragev in for questioning near his home after Cohen handed over the messages, and the case remains in the hands of investigators. ONE did not report a resolution to the arbitration debts or confirm whether Hapoel Lod's registration for the coming season has since been finalised.

The affair has drawn attention within Israeli football's legal community given Cohen's standing in the sport, and it leaves an awkward backdrop for a club still trying to rebuild on the pitch under a name meant to honour its founder.

title: Kapitolnik through to high jump final at European Championships in Birmingham
dek: The Israeli record-holder cleared 2.23m in qualifying at Alexander Stadium, booking his place among Europe's best with the final still to come.
body: Yonathan Kapitolnik is through to the high jump final at the European Athletics Championships, ONE reports, clearing 2.23m in qualifying at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham on Monday to book his place among the continent's best.

The 23-year-old from Ganei Tikva went through the qualifying round in tidy fashion: 2.15m at the first attempt, 2.19m on his second try, then 2.23m — again on the second attempt — to secure his spot in the final without needing to push into the riskier territory near his personal best.

It is a result that matters for an athlete who has spent this season fighting instability and minor injury trouble rather than chasing new heights. Kapitolnik went out early at the World Championships in Tokyo last year, failing all three attempts at 2.25m, so simply landing cleanly in a major final is itself a marker of progress.

Kapitolnik remains Israel's standard-bearer in the event. His personal best of 2.31m, set indoors in early 2025, sits alongside a resume that includes gold at the 2021 World U20 Championships and the 2021 European U20 Championships, a final appearance at the senior World Championships in Eugene in 2022, and six Israeli national titles in a row.
He has spent the past year based in the United States, having signed with the University of Illinois track and field programme in late 2025 after competing collegiately in Europe.

The men's high jump final in Birmingham is the next assignment for Kapitolnik, part of an 18-strong Israeli team competing at the championships hosted for the first time in Britain, at the Commonwealth Games venue redeveloped for Birmingham 2022.

title: Barda warns Hapoel Tel Aviv's 2-0 lead over Katowice guarantees nothing
dek: Ahead of Wednesday's Conference League qualifying return leg in Poland, head coach Elyaniv Barda and defender Doron Leidner say the first-leg scoreline counts for little once the whistle blows.
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv travel to Poland on Wednesday holding a two-goal cushion, but head coach Elyaniv Barda is making sure nobody at the club mistakes that for a job already done.

The Israeli side beat GKS Katowice 2-0 in Tel Aviv last week in the first leg of their Conference League qualifying tie, with goals from Stav Turiel and Roei Alkukin. The return leg kicks off in Katowice on Wednesday at 19:00 Israel time, with a place in the next round of qualifying at stake.

"This is only the first half of the encounter between two quality teams who both want to do their best," Barda said, previewing the second leg, according to ONE. He said his side must "improve what we didn't do well enough" in the opening match despite the winning scoreline.

The coach was blunt about the danger of complacency on the road. "Every match starts 0-0 and you can't know what will happen, so we must be very ready, especially when they're playing at home with good home results," he said.

Defender Doron Leidner echoed the message, stressing that the aggregate lead reflects only one half of the tie. "We gave our hundred percent to get here," he said. "We analyzed them and they analyzed us — we know what we need to improve."

Katowice have been solid in front of their own fans this season, and Barda's comments suggest Hapoel are wary of a Polish side pushing hard from the first whistle to claw back the deficit. A draw or a win in Katowice would be enough to send Hapoel Tel Aviv through; only a heavy defeat would turn the tie around.

For a club that spent last season in the Israeli second tier before winning promotion, advancing through another European qualifying round would be a significant marker of progress under Barda, who took charge of Hapoel Tel Aviv while they were still in the Leumit League.

body: Hapoel Akko booked their place in the Toto Cup Leumit final on Tuesday evening, beating hosts Maccabi Herzliya 2-0 at Herzliya Municipal Stadium in a semifinal that came to life only after the interval.

The first 45 minutes offered little for the travelling Akko supporters, with both Liga Leumit sides cancelling each other out and neither goalkeeper seriously tested. Herzliya, playing in front of their own crowd, arguably shaded the opening period without turning territory into clear chances.
Akko emerged transformed after the break. Six minutes into the second half, Muhammad Badarna broke the deadlock to put the visitors ahead and immediately shift the balance of the tie in their favour.

Herzliya pushed for an equaliser but could not find a way through a well-organised Akko defence, and the game was put beyond doubt in the 90th minute when Carlos Serenta added a second, sending the small pocket of Akko fans in Herzliya into celebration.

It completes a satisfying week's work for coach Adham Hadiya, who used the platform to talk up his squad's ambitions for the season ahead. "We have experienced players alongside young, talented ones committed to progressing, and I believe we'll be the surprise team of the league season this year," he said afterwards.
Herzliya coach Nitzan Demari pointed to his side's promising first-half showing but conceded his team struggled to find a tactical response once they fell behind early in the second period.

Akko now await the winner of the tournament's other semifinal, between M.S. Ashdod and Bnei Yehuda, for a place in the Toto Cup Leumit final - a first taste of silverware pressure this season for a club that spent last year fighting in the lower half of Liga Leumit.

Both Akko and Herzliya remain focused primarily on their Liga Leumit campaigns, where the two sides finished close together in the table last season, but a cup run offers a welcome secondary target and a shot at a trophy for whichever of the four remaining teams goes all the way.

body: Elche's interest in Roy Revivo has "cooled considerably," according to ONE, with the Spanish club stepping back from a chase for the Maccabi Tel Aviv left-back after the two sides failed to close a persistent gap over his valuation.

The newly promoted La Liga side had an offer of around €2 million turned down by Maccabi, who are holding out for a fee closer to their own valuation of the 23-year-old. Other Israeli outlets have reported similar numbers in recent days, with Ynet putting Elche's opening bid at roughly €1.7 million against a Maccabi asking price nearly double that, underlining just how far apart the two clubs remain.

Revivo is contracted to Maccabi Tel Aviv until June 2027 and is valued at around €4.5 million by Transfermarkt. The left-back, 1.85 metres tall and comfortable providing width from the back, had a productive 2025/26 season by his own attacking output, recording 15 assists in 52 appearances for the league champions.

He is the son of Haim Revivo, one of the most celebrated Israeli footballers of his generation, and has already made his own mark in the national set-up - he represented Israel at the 2024 Paris Olympics and was named the Israeli top flight's Defender of the Season for 2023/24.

Elche, under new coach Martín Anselmi following Eder Sarabia's departure after last season's survival battle, had identified the left flank as an area to strengthen this summer. According to ONE, the club may yet return with a fresh offer before the market closes, but for now other suitors have entered the conversation - with clubs from Italy and Portugal said to be presenting terms that better suit both Maccabi and the player.

The Spanish transfer window shuts on September 2, giving all parties roughly three weeks to either bridge the gap or move on to alternatives. For now, ONE's report suggests neither side is in a rush to blink first.

Maccabi have shown little appetite to let a key contributor leave on the cheap just months after winning the league, and Revivo's camp will be watching closely to see whether Elche - or one of the newer names circling - is prepared to meet a figure the champions consider fair.

title: Hapoel Beer Sheva plan to spend Champions League windfall on new signings
dek: Boss Ran Kojok wants a foreign striker and a defensive midfielder before the playoff tie against Sabah, with the club's European earnings already topping €7 million, ONE reports.

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva's run to the brink of the Champions League group stage has done more than lift the mood in the Negev - it has filled the club's coffers, and manager Ran Kojok wants to spend some of that windfall before the transfer window shuts.

According to ONE, Beer Sheva have already banked €7.9 million from this season's European campaign alone, a sum that could climb to €18.6 million if they get past Sabah, the champions of Azerbaijan, in the playoff round and reach the Champions League group stage proper for the first time in the club's history.

Other Israeli outlets have cited a slightly different split of the same windfall - closer to €6 million guaranteed simply for reaching the playoff round, rising past €18 million for the group stage - but on any reading, this is the richest European payday Beer Sheva have ever earned, and money the club intends to reinvest in the squad rather than bank.

Per ONE's report, Kojok is targeting two specific positions: a foreign striker and a foreign defensive midfielder. No talks are described as advanced, and with the first leg against Sabah approaching fast, the club's recruitment staff have only a narrow window to close a deal before facing the Azerbaijani champions.

On the domestic front, Beer Sheva have registered interest in Maor Levi and Roei David, ONE reports. David is understood to be trying to engineer a move to MLS, and Beer Sheva could yet offer him a stepping stone or improved terms at home if that route stalls.

There is also unfinished business closer to the dressing room. Eliel Peretz, the midfielder Beer Sheva signed to a three-year deal that runs to the summer of 2027, is described as a retention priority, with formal talks over a new contract due to open once the Sabah ties are settled.
On the outgoing side, ONE names one departure as effectively done: Yoav Korn is expected to leave Beer Sheva for Maccabi Petah Tikva.

title: Pachuca 1-0 Charlotte FC: Abada and Toklomati start as Bautista snatches stoppage-time winner
dek: Liel Abada and Idan Toklomati both began for the Israeli-laden MLS side, but Alan Bautista's 90th-minute strike denied Charlotte a perfect run through Leagues Cup Phase One.
body: Charlotte FC's perfect run through this year's Leagues Cup came apart in the cruellest way on Tuesday night at Bank of America Stadium, where Alan Bautista struck in the first minute of stoppage time to give Pachuca a 1-0 win over a home side that had started two Israeli internationals, Liel Abada and Idan Toklomati.

Abada, the winger Charlotte signed from Celtic as a young designated player in 2024, and Toklomati, who arrived from Maccabi Petah Tikva, both took the field from kickoff as Charlotte chased a third straight Phase One win that would have all but sealed a quarterfinal berth.

Neither Israeli found the net. Toklomati was the first off, withdrawn in the 57th minute for Archie Goodwin, while Abada played on until the 72nd minute, when he was replaced by new signing Allan Saint-Maximin.

Charlotte still had the game in their hands late on. In the 81st minute, Pachuca's Sergio Rodriguez fouled Saint-Maximin inside the box and the referee pointed to the spot. Goodwin stepped up, but his penalty was saved by the Pachuca goalkeeper, according to Mexican outlets covering the match.

Pachuca made Charlotte pay almost immediately. Bautista found space inside the area in the second minute of stoppage time and finished coolly with his left foot to snatch all three points, sending the small pocket of travelling fans into celebration and silencing the home crowd.

The defeat was Charlotte's first of this year's Leagues Cup campaign, after the club had opened Phase One with two consecutive wins. ONE reported that the loss ended what had been an unbeaten run for the MLS side heading into the group's final round of fixtures.

For Abada and Toklomati, the result was a rare setback in what has otherwise been a season of growing prominence for Israeli players in MLS. Alongside teammates such as fellow Israeli forward Baribo and New England Revolution's Ilay Feingold, the pair are part of a small but expanding contingent of Israeli internationals now plying their trade in the American league.

Attention for Charlotte now turns to whether Tuesday's loss affects their position in the Leagues Cup standings, with the club having entered the match needing a positive result to guarantee their place in the knockout rounds.

title: Wimbledon, 8 July 2006: The Mixed Doubles Final That Made Andy Ram Israel's First Grand Slam Champion
dek: On Centre Court, a doubles specialist from Israel and a 21-year-old Russian partner beat Bob Bryan and Venus Williams to give Israeli tennis its first professional major title.

verificationSources.label: Haaretz — 'Wimbledon: Israeli First as Ram Wins Doubles With Zvonareva'
ESPN — 'Ram, Zvonareva win Wimbledon mixed doubles'

body: For six decades of Israeli tennis, the Grand Slams had been a place to compete, not to win. Amos Mansdorf reached major quarterfinals in the 1980s, Shlomo Glickstein had his moments, and a run of gifted juniors — Shahar Peer, Ana Smashnova, Dudi Sela — had lifted junior Grand Slam trophies. But no Israeli had ever stood on a Grand Slam court as a senior champion. On the afternoon of Saturday, 8 July 2006, on the most famous tennis court in the world, that changed.

Andy Ram, a 26-year-old from Netanya who had built his career as a doubles specialist rather than a singles star, walked onto Wimbledon's Centre Court paired with Vera Zvonareva of Russia for the mixed doubles final. Their opponents were about as daunting as a final draw could produce: Bob Bryan, one half of the great American twins act, and Venus Williams, five-time Wimbledon singles champion and one of the most dominant players of her generation.

Ram and Zvonareva had already survived a tough route to the final, beating the third-seeded Zimbabwean pair of Wayne and Cara Black 6–3, 7–6 in the semi-finals. But the final carried an extra complication for their opponents: Bryan had played the men's doubles final with his twin brother Mike only hours earlier, winning that title as well, and he arrived on Centre Court for the mixed final with tired legs and a heavy afternoon already behind him.

It showed. Bryan's serve was broken repeatedly as Ram and Zvonareva took control, and the Israeli-Russian pairing closed out the match 6–3, 6–2. Zvonareva sealed it fittingly, with an ace on their first match point — a clean, emphatic finish to a final that had looked competitive on paper and turned one-sided on the day.

For Ram, the moment carried a significance beyond the trophy itself. It was the first Grand Slam title won by an Israeli player at the professional, senior level — a distinction separate from the junior Grand Slam success of compatriots like Peer, Smashnova and Sela. Ram, who had spent his career largely in doubles rather than chasing singles glory, had delivered something no Israeli before him ever had.

The win also reflected a broader shift underway in Israeli tennis in the mid-2000s, as a generation of players — Ram foremost among them — began pushing into the sport's biggest events and, for the first time, its biggest finals. Ram's Wimbledon breakthrough would prove to be the first chapter rather than the whole story: within two years he added a French Open mixed doubles title in 2007 with Nathalie Dechy, before pairing with countryman Jonathan Erlich to win the Australian Open men's doubles in 2008 — a partnership that would become one of Israeli sport's most celebrated doubles acts.

But it was Wimbledon 2006 that came first, and it was Wimbledon 2006 that broke the ceiling. Israeli papers ran the story as a national milestone rather than a tennis footnote — a small country's tennis player winning on the lawns of the All England Club, a place that had, until that Saturday, never produced an Israeli name on its honours boards.

Ram's route to that Centre Court final had nothing improbable about raw talent — he had been a fixture on the doubles tour for years — but everything improbable about the moment: a doubles specialist from a country with no Grand Slam pedigree, partnering a rising Russian star, beating a genuine American superstar and a twin who had just won his own final that same day. It was the kind of Grand Slam final line score — 6–3, 6–2 — that reads simply in the record books but carried an outsized weight for the country whose flag went up, for the first time, beside a Grand Slam trophy.

title: Daria Golovaty misses 200m freestyle final at European Championships
dek: The Israeli record holder shaved off time in the semifinal but finished 14th overall in Paris, as Anastasia Gorbenko advanced in the 400m medley.
body: Daria Golovaty's bid for a first individual final at a European Championships fell just short in Paris on Wednesday, as the Bat Yam swimmer was eliminated in the semifinals of the women's 200m freestyle.

Golovaty, who touched in 1:58.72 to win her heat comfortably a day earlier, shaved further time off in the semifinal, clocking 1:58.48. It was not enough: she finished seventh in her semifinal heat and 14th overall, missing the cut for Thursday's final, ONE reports.

It leaves the 20-year-old, Israel's national record holder in the event, to reflect on a championships in which she has been consistently fast without quite breaking through to the medal races. Her Israeli record of 1:57.87 was set at trials at the Wingate Institute in June 2024.

Golovaty arrives at these Championships as a European champion already, having anchored Israel's 4x200m freestyle relay to gold in Belgrade in 2024. She also swam at the Paris Olympics that summer, finishing 11th with the relay squad.

The 200m free was not the only event on the Israeli team's radar in Paris on Wednesday. Anastasia Gorbenko, the defending champion in the women's 400m individual medley, advanced to Thursday's final after qualifying seventh in the heats in 4:42.23.
Gorbenko, born in Haifa, won the title in Belgrade two years ago and remains Israel's headline act in the pool at these Championships, which run in Paris from July 31 to August 16.

With Golovaty out of contention in the 200m free, the Israeli delegation's hopes of a first medal at these Championships now rest more heavily on Gorbenko's shoulders heading into the 400m medley final.

title: Maccabi Haifa complete loan deal for goalkeeper Omer Nir'on
dek: The 25-year-old joins from Maccabi Netanya as back-up to Omri Glazer, with Haifa holding an option to make the move permanent for 1.4 million shekels.
body: Maccabi Haifa have strengthened their goalkeeping department, agreeing a loan deal for Omer Nir'on from Maccabi Netanya, ONE reported on Wednesday, ending weeks of on-off negotiations between the two clubs.

The 25-year-old moves to the Sammy Ofer Stadium for the remainder of the season, with Haifa holding a purchase option worth 1.4 million shekels should they wish to make the transfer permanent next summer.

Nir'on arrives to serve as back-up to Omri Glazer under head coach Barak Bakhar, rather than to challenge for the starting jersey. Glazer returned to Haifa this summer after a spell with Serbian giants Crvena Zvezda, signing a three-year contract with the club he left in 2023.

For Nir'on, the move ends a two-and-a-half-year stint at Netanya, whom he joined in January 2024 after beginning his senior career at Beitar Jerusalem. He made 20 appearances for the Sharon club last season, conceding 40 goals and keeping just one clean sheet.

Talks between the clubs had reportedly stalled at times over Netanya's valuation of the goalkeeper before the sides settled on the loan-with-option structure. Haifa had been searching for reinforcements between the posts after their previous backup options moved on.

The deal gives Bakhar a settled goalkeeping pair heading into the new campaign, with Glazer restored as first choice and Nir'on providing experienced cover for a squad preparing for a season that will again include European football.

title: Jules Koundé's agent seen at Barcelona's training complex amid sale talk
dek: Jonathan Kebe met with sporting director Deco at the Joan Gamper facility, ONE reports, as Barcelona weigh cashing in on the France defender with Tottenham among the interested Premier League clubs.
body: Jules Koundé's representative was spotted walking into Barcelona's Joan Gamper training complex this week, ONE reports, sitting down with sporting director Deco in a meeting the club framed as part of a routine round of agent talks but which lands squarely amid growing speculation over the defender's future.

Agent Jonathan Kebe's visit was one of several such meetings Deco has been holding with players' representatives this summer, according to the report, but Koundé's situation carries particular weight: he signed a contract extension through 2030 barely a year ago, yet finds himself increasingly peripheral to Hansi Flick's plans.

Flick left Koundé out of Barcelona's title-clinching win over Real Madrid last season and has continued to manage his involvement carefully, with fitness issues compounding a drop-off in form after a standout first campaign under the German coach.

Barcelona's financial position is central to the calculation. The club needs sales to help fund a pursuit of Rodri and Julian Alvarez, and with Ronald Araujo already dispatched on loan to Liverpool, Koundé has emerged as one of the more obvious names the hierarchy could move on to balance the books.

Interest from the Premier League has simmered all summer. Tottenham have been the most persistently linked suitor, reportedly readying an offer close to Barcelona's valuation, which independent reporting has put in the region of €60-80 million for the 27-year-old France international.

Koundé said during France's World Cup campaign this summer that he hoped to stay at Camp Nou, and he has since returned to pre-season training with the squad. But a meeting between his agent and the man who runs Barcelona's transfer business is unlikely to cool the chatter over where he plays his football this season.

title: Beitar boss Almog Cohen: 'We saw last week we need to make minimum mistakes'
dek: Trailing Austria Wien 2-1 on aggregate, Beitar Jerusalem's coach and striker Shon Weissman size up a must-win Conference League return leg in Vienna.

verificationSources.label: Beitar Jerusalem official site - Almog Cohen preview
Sofascore - Austria Wien claim 2-1 win at Beitar Jerusalem

body: Beitar Jerusalem's European campaign hangs by a thread heading into Thursday night, when the Israeli side must overturn a 2-1 aggregate deficit against Austria Wien in Vienna simply to stay alive in the Conference League's third qualifying round.

The first leg, played at a neutral venue in Ploiești, Romania rather than at Beitar's own Teddy Stadium, went the Austrians' way despite Beitar taking an early lead through Noam Muche in the 19th minute. Vasilije Marković equalized right on half-time, and substitute Sanel Šaljić, finishing off a Daniel Nnodim assist, put Austria Wien ahead for good in the 69th minute.

Speaking to reporters before the return leg, head coach Almog Cohen zeroed in on the lapses that cost his side in Romania. "I think the key points for us are to be stable with the ball, especially in European games, to make minimum mistakes, because we saw that every mistake of ours cost us," he said, according to ONE.

Cohen, who moved from Beitar's sporting-director role into the dugout this season, said the club has done its homework on the opponent. "We showed the players the match many times and we have some information on Austria Wien... we will come prepared and we believe, and with God's help, we want to come win here and advance to the next round," he added.

Striker Shon Weissman brings a personal thread to the tie: before rejoining Beitar this summer, he spent time in Austria with Wolfsberger AC, where he was the Austrian Bundesliga's top scorer in the 2019-20 season with 30 goals in 31 games.
"First of all it's interesting to return here, I played here just two months ago," Weissman said. "It's cool to return, especially with an Israeli team and with Beitar's symbol."

The forward pointed to the opening 45 minutes in Ploiești as evidence his side belongs in this tie. "We showed in the first half of the previous match that we are a quality team that can win any match," he said.

He also touched on the toll of a season already dominated by travel. "I returned to the country and thought I'd be more in Israel, but meanwhile we're more abroad than in Israel, and it's not simple, especially without Teddy," Weissman said, as reported by ONE.
Kickoff at Austria Wien's Generali Arena is set for Thursday at 21:30 Israel time. The winner advances to the playoff round, where either Braga or Dinamo Minsk awaits a place in the group stage.

title: Espionage fears push Almog Cohen to hide Beitar Jerusalem's line-up before Vienna showdown
dek: The Beitar coach cut short a full training session in Austria after staff spotted cameras trained on the pitch, ahead of a Conference League second leg his side must win by two goals.

verificationSources.label: Sofascore - Austria Wien claim 2-1 win at Beitar Jerusalem
UEFA.com - Austria Wien vs Beitar match info

body: Almog Cohen was not prepared to hand Austria Wien a single extra clue. With Beitar Jerusalem needing to overturn a 2-1 first-leg deficit in Thursday's Conference League third qualifying round return, the coach cut the team's final training session in Vienna short after his staff noticed cameras trained on the pitch, ONE reports.

Rather than run a full tactical rehearsal that could be picked up and analysed by the hosts, Cohen limited the session to defensive shape and set-piece work, keeping his attacking plans and likely starting eleven under wraps until kick-off.

The caution reflects how tight the tie has become. Beitar led through Noam Muche in Ploiesti before Austria Wien struck twice, through Vasilije Markovic just before half-time and Sanel Saljic in the second half, to leave Cohen's side needing to win by two clear goals in Vienna, or by one with away goals no longer separating the sides under UEFA's current rules, to advance.

According to ONE, Cohen held three separate meetings with his players in the buildup, stressing the need to protect possession and show "greater maturity in play." The coaching staff's review of the first leg reportedly concluded that Austria Wien's goals owed more to Beitar's own errors than to anything the Austrians did particularly well going forward, a diagnosis that shaped this week's message.

There is better news on the injury front. Georgian defender Luka Gadrani is available again after missing recent matches, while attacking midfielder Tomer Yosefi is set for a bigger role in the side. Forward Shon Weissman, who picked up an ankle injury during the first leg, remains a doubt for the second leg.

Kick-off at the Generali Arena is set for 21:30 local time, with ONE reporting that roughly 1,150 Beitar fans are expected to travel for the match. In a smaller gesture beyond the football, the club has agreed to display appeals for two missing women from Vienna on screens around the ground during the game.

title: León 3-2 Inter Miami: Messi returns days after father's death as Herons crash out of Leagues Cup
dek: Lionel Messi came off the bench hours after burying his father Jorge in Argentina, but a Daniel Arcila brace sent Club León through and knocked Inter Miami out of the Leagues Cup at the group stage.
body: Lionel Messi returned to a football pitch on Wednesday night for the first time since burying his father, coming off the bench for Inter Miami in a Leagues Cup group game against Club León that ended in a 3-2 defeat and eliminated the Herons from the tournament.

Messi had missed Miami's previous fixture, a loss to CF Monterrey, after flying to Rosario following the death of his father and long-time agent, Jorge Messi, who passed away on August 7 at the age of 68 after a long illness at a clinic in the Argentine city. He made a rapid turnaround back to Florida, arriving on Wednesday morning to be available for the León match.

He was named among the substitutes and entered at the start of the second half in place of Daniel Pinter, who had put Miami ahead in the 42nd minute. Local broadcasters and reporters at Chase Stadium described the crowd erupting into chants of "Messi, Messi, Messi" as he walked onto the pitch, though the emotional reception could not turn the result.

León hit back three minutes into the second half through Daniel Arcila, before Yannick Bright restored Miami's lead in the 53rd minute. Juan Domínguez leveled it again for the Mexican side in the 61st, and Arcila completed his brace with the winner in the 83rd minute — a goal initially flagged offside before being confirmed by VAR.

The defeat left Inter Miami with just three points from three group games — a 4-2 win over Atlético San Luis, the loss to Monterrey and Wednesday's collapse against León — and no path into the knockout rounds. It is, by several American outlets' accounts, the club's worst Leagues Cup showing since Messi's arrival in 2023, a year after Miami reached the final of the same competition.

Interim head coach Guillermo Hoyos, who moved over from his sporting director role after Javier Mascherano's abrupt departure in April, said Jorge Messi's death had weighed heavily on the squad through a difficult week, according to ONE's report from Florida.

Messi himself still managed five shots, three of them on target, along with two completed dribbles and four key passes in his 45 minutes on the pitch — an active cameo that suggested he was determined to play through the grief rather than sit the tournament out entirely.

The same night in the Leagues Cup brought a smaller Israeli footnote: FC Dallas, featuring Israeli midfielder Ran Binyamin, were also eliminated after a 3-1 loss away to Toluca in Mexico. Binyamin, signed from Hapoel Tel Aviv earlier this year, came on as a second-half substitute and picked up a yellow card as Dallas' own group-stage campaign ended in Estadio Nemesio Díez.

Inter Miami now turn their attention back to MLS, where they are due to face Nashville SC this weekend, with Messi expected to remain part of the group as the club tries to salvage its domestic season after an early Leagues Cup exit.

title: Oren Smadja: 'It wasn't easy to make this decision' as judo hero enters politics
dek: Two years after losing his son Omer in Gaza, the Olympic bronze medalist and former national judo coach says grief pushed him to join Gilad Erdan's Unity party for the October 27 Knesset election.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Smadja to run in Knesset elections

body: Oren Smadja, Israel's pioneering Olympic judo medalist, has stepped into politics, announcing he is joining Gilad Erdan's "Unity" party ahead of the October 27 Knesset election. "It wasn't easy to make such a decision," Smadja said, in a statement carried by ONE.

The 56-year-old former national judo coach framed the move as the end of a long personal struggle. "After two years since Omer's fall, years during which I was in a grave mentally and emotionally, I decided it was time to rise and act again for the state," he said.

Smadja's son, Omer, was killed in June 2024 by mortar fire in the Netzarim corridor in central Gaza, where he was serving as a reservist in Battalion 9203 of the Alexandroni Brigade. He fell on his father's 54th birthday.

According to ONE, Smadja's decision crystallized after a conversation with another bereaved father, a conversation he described as pushing him past two years of what he called being "in a grave" emotionally and spiritually.
"I'm doing this with pain, with longing, but also with a deep sense of mission and a desire to give myself to the state I love so much," Smadja said of his decision to campaign.

Erdan travelled to Smadja's home to make the pitch in person, ONE reports, inviting him to join campaign visits with voters around the country. Smadja will run alongside fellow candidates Yuli Edelstein and Aliza Bloch on the Unity list.

Polling has so far suggested Unity may struggle to clear the electoral threshold, according to ONE, though the addition of a nationally recognizable figure like Smadja is widely seen as an attempt to broaden the party's appeal.

Smadja won bronze in the under-71kg category at the 1992 Barcelona Games, becoming Israel's second-ever Olympic medalist a day after Yael Arad's silver in the same sport. He went on to coach Israel's national judo team for 15 years before stepping down in May 2025.

At the Paris 2024 Olympics, weeks after Omer's death, judoka Peter Paltchik dropped to his knees before Smadja after winning bronze, telling his coach the medal was "for Omer." Smadja's wife, Liat, now works as a paramedic on a Magen David Adom ambulance dedicated to their son's memory.

title: Turin, 19 June 1979: The Silver That Remains Israeli Basketball's Highest Peak
dek: In a rented Italian arena, Ralph Klein's Israel upset Yugoslavia, stunned a continent, and reached a European final no Israeli national team has reached since — with Miki Berkovich named the tournament's finest player even in defeat.

verificationSources.label: FIBA Hall of Fame — Mickey Berkowitz
Global Sports Archive — Israel vs Yugoslavia, 11 June 1979
Wikipedia — Israel men's national basketball team

body: The scoreboard at the PalaRuffini in Turin told a brutal story by the final buzzer: Soviet Union 98, Israel 76. But nobody in Italian basketball that June had expected Israel to be on that scoreboard at all, in a gold-medal game, four days before the biggest closing weekend the European Championship could offer.

EuroBasket 1979 ran from 9 to 19 June across four Italian cities — Mestre, Siena, Gorizia and Turin — and it was supposed to belong, as it always did in that era, to the Soviet Union, the reigning continental power stacked with Vladimir Tkachenko, Sergei Belov and Anatoly Tarakanov. Israel arrived as a middling entry with no history of troubling the tournament's summit.

Ralph Klein, the Berlin-born "Mr. Basketball" who had already turned Maccabi Tel Aviv into European champions in 1977, was in charge of the senior national team, and his squad opened the group phase in Gorizia with a defeat to France before delivering the shock of the tournament: a 77-76 win over Yugoslavia on 11 June at the PalaGrappate, a result that put the continent on notice.

Israel carried that momentum into the second group phase in Turin, going 3-2 to finish behind only the Soviet Union and secure a place nobody had pencilled in for them — the gold-medal final, against the very team that had just beaten Yugoslavia 96-77 to get there themselves.

The final, on 19 June at the PalaRuffini, was as one-sided as the pedigree suggested it might be. The Soviets pulled away in the second half, with Tkachenko scoring 29, Belov 22 and Tarakanov 22 as the USSR claimed its twelfth European men's title, 98-76.

For Israel, Yanay led the scoring with 18, Miki Berkovich (known internationally as Mickey Berkowitz) added 16, Lou Silver scored 12, and Menkin, Motti Aroesti and Kaplan chipped in the rest, with captain Barry Leibowitz marshalling the effort from the backcourt.

The defeat did nothing to diminish the individual story of the tournament. Berkovich, then 25 and already a fixture at Maccabi Tel Aviv, averaged 23.6 points across the championship and was named EuroBasket 1979's Most Valuable Player — a rare instance of the award going to a player whose team fell in the final, and recognition that stood alongside his later induction into the FIBA Hall of Fame.

For Klein, it was a second continental peak inside three years, following his 1977 European Champions Cup with Maccabi, but this one carried a different weight: it was earned in the colours of the country itself, against the sport's dominant Cold War power, on a neutral floor in northern Italy.

Israel has never come closer to a European basketball title since. Through the team's next four decades and more than thirty EuroBasket appearances — including tournaments as recently as 2022 and 2025 — the silver from Turin has stood alone as the national side's best finish, a fact repeated in FIBA and federation histories to this day.

It is a different kind of archive story from Maccabi Tel Aviv's club triumphs of the same period: no Final Four crowd, no blue-and-yellow choreography, just a small national squad from a country with roughly a hundredth of the Soviet Union's population, walking off a court in Turin with silver medals and a tournament MVP award that had no business being theirs by reputation alone.

Berkovich would go on to play into the 1990s, become an Israel Prize laureate, and remain, by most reckonings, the finest player Israeli basketball has produced. But it is the summer of 1979 — the upset of Yugoslavia in Gorizia, the run through Turin, the 76 points that weren't enough against the Soviets — that supplied the single result the national team has spent every year since trying, and failing, to match.

The silver remains, as of 2025, the best-ever finish by Israel's men's national basketball team in EuroBasket history, across more than thirty tournament appearances.

The Soviet Union's win was its 12th European men's basketball title, led by Vladimir Tkachenko (29 points), Sergei Belov (22) and Anatoly Tarakanov (22) in the final.

title: Titles at any price: the giant test facing Pérez and Mourinho at Real Madrid
dek: A ONE podcast breakdown of Real Madrid's record-spending summer finds two men on trial as José Mourinho's second spell begins under Florentino Pérez's watch.

verificationSources.label: Al Jazeera - Mourinho named Real Madrid coach on three-year deal
ESPN - Vinícius Jr. agrees new six-year Real Madrid deal
ESPN - Real Madrid beat Deportivo in friendly with Brahim goal
CBS Sports - Real Madrid fire Xabi Alonso, Arbeloa takes over

body: Real Madrid open the 2026-27 season with two men effectively on trial: club president Florentino Pérez, freshly re-elected, and José Mourinho, the manager he has bet the club's near future on for a second time. A new ONE podcast episode, hosted by Uri Reich, Amit Levinthal and Chami Almog, lays out exactly how high the stakes are after the most turbulent Madrid summer in years.

The trigger for the reset was painful: Real Madrid went through the 2025-26 season without a major trophy, their second barren campaign in a row. Xabi Alonso, who had arrived with fanfare in June 2025, was sacked in January 2026 after a heavy defeat to Barcelona, with club legend Álvaro Arbeloa installed as caretaker for the rest of the season.

Pérez's answer was to reach back to a manager he first hired in 2010. Mourinho, who led Madrid to the 2011-12 La Liga title and broke a string of domestic scoring records during his first spell before leaving in 2013, returned this July on a three-year contract. Madrid reportedly had to pay Benfica around €15m to release him early, roughly €9m more than the exit clause would have cost had the move been completed before the end of May.

The rehiring is a calculated gamble. Mourinho's most recent stops, at Roma, Fenerbahçe and Benfica, produced a Conference League title but no domestic championships, and his 15-month spell in Istanbul ended without silverware. The ONE hosts frame his second Bernabéu tenure as a test of whether the 'Special One' can still deliver at the very top, and of whether Pérez can justify handing him the keys again.

Money has not been the obstacle. According to the podcast, this has been the most expensive transfer window in Real Madrid's history, built around Yan Diomande, signed from RB Leipzig for a fixed fee near €125m that can rise with add-ons toward becoming the club's record purchase. Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí have also arrived as Mourinho reshapes a squad the hosts say still lacks a genuine left-back and a controlling presence in midfield.

Some of that rebuilding work was visible, and some notably wasn't, in Wednesday's pre-season friendly in Galicia. Real Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruña 1-0, Brahim Díaz scoring the only goal shortly before half-time, with Bernardo Silva and Dumfries starting and Espí introduced at the break. Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé, Cucurella, Konaté and Yan Diomande were all left out, still working back at Valdebebas.

Off the pitch, Pérez has secured the piece of business the club considers most urgent. Vinícius Júnior signed a new contract through 2032 this month, ending months of speculation about a possible move to Arsenal and locking down the player Madrid see as central to life after this transfer window. The podcast frames it alongside the futures of Bellingham and Mbappé as the connective tissue Mourinho now has to make work as one team.

The declared target, as the hosts put it, is nothing less than stopping Barcelona winning a third straight La Liga title while chasing a 16th European Cup. Pérez himself has said publicly that the club will "fight until the end" for that trophy. With a rebuilt, expensive squad and a manager back for redemption, Real Madrid's margin for another trophyless season looks vanishingly small.

title: Roey Levy and Ariel Gal sit third after strong start to the 470 sailing worlds
dek: The Israeli duo posted finishes of 10th, 3rd and second in the opening races at Enoshima, trailing only Switzerland and France as the class begins jockeying for position ahead of Los Angeles 2028 qualification.

verificationSources.label: Sail-World: 470 World Championship 2026 in Enoshima - Day 1
Sail-World: Who will claim the 470 Worlds in Enoshima?

body: Roey Levy and Ariel Gal have made a promising start to the 470 World Championship in Enoshima, Japan, sitting third overall after the first three races of the regatta, ONE reports.
The Israeli pair scored a 10th, a 3rd and a 2nd, giving them five net points. That leaves them behind only Switzerland, who lead on three points, and France in second on four, in a fleet of 74 boats.
A second Israeli crew, Nitai Chason and Noga Tiano, are also in the field but further back, lying 17th overall after finishes of 2nd, 12th and 14th in the same three races.

Racing at Enoshima, the sailing venue used for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, was delayed by a day after poor conditions on Sunday forced organisers to abandon the opening day's schedule and send crews back ashore. The qualification series resumed once winds settled, allowing the three races that now shape the early standings.

The championship carries extra weight beyond the medals on offer this week. ONE notes that the next edition of the 470 worlds will begin distributing qualification places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, sharpening the competition among a mixed fleet that already includes Olympic medallists and reigning world champions alongside rising junior talents.

Levy and Gal are not newcomers to the podium. The pair have built their reputation over several seasons as the standard-bearers of Israeli youth sailing in the 470 class, collecting age-group world and European titles as they've progressed toward senior competition.

With racing continuing at Enoshima through August 17, the qualification series will eventually split the fleet into gold and silver groups before a final series decides the world title. A strong opening for the Israeli duo puts them in position to fight for a top group place, though five points from three races is still an early marker in a week-long event.

For Israeli sailing, a sport with a proud Olympic pedigree built on windsurfing medals over the past two decades, a competitive showing from the 470 pair adds another name to watch on the road to the 2028 Games.

title: Beitar Nordia Jerusalem unveil new kits for 2026/27 season
dek: The Liga Alef club's yellow-and-black modular strips, designed for a third straight year by Itai Dahan's Didaa Studio, will be worn from the senior side down through every youth grade.

verificationSources.label: Bizmakebiz — Didaa Studio / Itai Dahan profile

body: Beitar Nordia Jerusalem have unveiled their new official kits for the 2026/27 season, rolling out the fresh look from the senior squad all the way down through every youth age group, ONE reported.

The new strips come as two modular sets in the club's familiar yellow and black, built so players and fans can mix and match pieces across the campaign while the colours, the menorah crest and the wider club identity stay constant.

The kits were designed by Itai Dahan, owner of the Jerusalem branding studio Didaa Studio, who is now working with the club for a third consecutive year. Umbro manufactured the finished product, according to the report.

"As a child who collected football shirts, it's a great honour to design kits today and see them on the pitch," Dahan said, a line that captures the personal stake he has taken in the project since first partnering with the club.

Beitar Nordia's leadership said the design process involved close collaboration with club management to make sure the kit reflected the organisation's values, and stressed that giving young players professionally designed uniforms — not just hand-me-down templates — feeds a sense of belonging and pride that starts in the academy.

The club itself has an unusual backstory even by Israeli football's crowded standards. Founded in 2014 by Beitar Jerusalem supporters who rejected the racism and violence associated with parts of that club's fanbase, Nordia took its name from the identity Beitar Jerusalem briefly adopted in 1947 and built itself as a fan-owned, community-first alternative. It competes in Liga Alef, Israel's third tier, with home matches at the Hebrew University Stadium in Jerusalem's Givat Ram.

A kit relaunch is a modest headline in the context of Israeli football's top flight, but for a fan-run club still establishing itself in the lower leagues, presenting a coherent, professionally produced identity from first team to youngest academy group is treated internally as a statement of intent heading into the new season.

title: Sarri's overhauled Atalanta is not the side Hapoel Tel Aviv might expect in Bergamo
dek: Three coaches in a year, a scrapped back three and a captain sold to Saudi Arabia — ONE reports the Atalanta that Hapoel meet in the Conference League playoff is going through its biggest shake-up in a decade.

verificationSources.label: Atalanta official site — UECL playoff draw vs Hapoel Tel Aviv
Il Post — Juric sacked, Palladino appointed, November 2025
Eurosport Italia — Palladino sacked, Sarri era begins
ANSA — Djimsiti's farewell to Atalanta, Al-Diriyah move
