body: Hapoel Tel Aviv now know exactly what stands between them and the Conference League's group stage: Atalanta, the Europa League winners of 2024, in a two-legged playoff that opens in Bergamo on Thursday, August 20, and is decided a week later, on August 27, at the DVTK Stadium in Miskolc, Hungary — the venue Hapoel are using for their home leg.

On paper it looks a daunting draw. But ONE reports that the Atalanta side Hapoel will actually meet is barely recognisable from the ruthless, attacking outfit that reached a Champions League quarter-final and lifted a European trophy over the past two seasons. Off the back of nearly a decade of stability under Gian Piero Gasperini, the club has been through a chaotic year.

Gasperini's successor, Ivan Jurić, lasted only a few months. Appointed in the summer, he won just four of his first 15 matches in charge and was sacked in November with Atalanta down in 13th place, days after a home defeat to Sassuolo — his third managerial exit inside a single year, following earlier spells at Roma and Southampton.

Raffaele Palladino, fresh off stints at Monza and Fiorentina, was brought in as his replacement and signed a contract through 2027. It did not last either: Palladino himself was axed months later as Atalanta continued to search for stability, clearing the way for a permanent appointment.

That appointment, confirmed in May, was Maurizio Sarri. The 67-year-old signed a three-year deal running to 2029, and the club paired him with a new sporting director, Cristiano Giuntoli, who previously worked alongside Sarri at Napoli and had most recently overseen recruitment at Juventus. Giuntoli's early business included signing Gianluca Gaetano from Cagliari to add creativity in midfield.

The tactical implications are significant. ONE notes that Sarri is dismantling Atalanta's decade-long identity built around a back three, switching instead to a classical 4-3-3 with full-backs and orthodox wingers — a genuine departure from the Gasperini blueprint that made the club one of Serie A's most distinctive teams.

The rebuild has coincided with upheaval in defence. Berat Djimsiti, the 33-year-old Albania captain who made 334 appearances across more than eight seasons in Bergamo, completed a move to Saudi Arabia's Al-Diriyah for around €3 million, confirmed officially on August 10 as he bid an emotional farewell to the club.

Sweden international Isak Hien, meanwhile, will not be available at all. He underwent surgery on a thigh injury sustained at this year's World Cup and is not expected back until October — meaning Sarri's new-look defence will face Hapoel without one of its senior centre-backs still bedding in a system it has never played before.

None of this makes Atalanta anything less than the clear favourites; a squad that reached the latter stages of the Champions League as recently as last season retains far more individual quality than Hapoel can call on. But a club mid-transition, with a rookie system, a rebuilt spine and a coach only three months into the job, is a different proposition to the well-drilled Gasperini machine of old.

Hapoel arrive with momentum of their own, having eliminated Poland's GKS Katowice 3-2 on aggregate to reach this stage. Two games against a name as big as Atalanta's would once have looked like a formality for the Italians; this year, ONE's reporting suggests, there is a genuine opening for the underdog to exploit.

title: New book traces how Yaakov Shahar ran Maccabi Haifa like his own business
dek: Historian Moshe Talsnik's study of the club's transformation under its longtime owner is out now, ONE reports
body: Long before Israeli football had spokespeople, sports psychologists or position-specific fitness coaches, one owner decided his club should be run the way he ran his showroom floor. A newly published book argues that Maccabi Haifa's transformation from a struggling sports association into a professional operation traces back almost entirely to one man's business instincts.

The book, "HaMumchim LeKaduregel" ("The Football Experts"), is the work of Dr. Moshe Talsnik, who spent years researching the subject for a doctoral thesis before turning it into a full study, ONE reports. Its focus is Ya'akov "Yankale" Shahar, the businessman who bought Maccabi Haifa in 1992 and reshaped it in his own image over the following decade and a half.

"Shahar decided to manage the club like his own business, and he succeeded," Talsnik writes, according to ONE, describing a string of practices that were unheard of in Israeli football at the time but standard in the corporate world Shahar came from.

Shahar acquired the club through his company Kesher Sport in 1992. Independently, he is also known as the longtime chairman of Mayer's Cars and Trucks, Israel's importer of Volvo and Honda vehicles - the kind of corporate background Talsnik's book credits for the professionalism Shahar brought to Kiryat Eliezer.

Among the innovations detailed in the book, per ONE, was the hiring of Guy Peleg as the club's first-ever spokesperson, at a time when Israeli clubs rarely bothered with structured media relations. Giora Spigler is named as an early collaborator who helped Shahar build out the club's new professional framework.

The study also covers the introduction of sports psychology and dedicated fitness and position-specific training methods - now standard across professional football but novel in Israel when Maccabi Haifa adopted them under Shahar's ownership.

Talsnik's research charts the club's evolution from 1992 through 2006, a period that turned Maccabi Haifa into one of Israeli football's dominant forces and repeat league champions, built on the kind of off-field structure most rivals lacked.

Shahar's standing in the Israeli game was formally recognised in October 2017, when he received a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Israeli Football League Management at a ceremony attended by then-president Reuven Rivlin.
The book is being marketed as essential reading for Maccabi Haifa supporters wanting the inside story of how their club became a business success story as much as a football one, ONE notes.

title: Ceuta coach says he would rather not play this weekend amid migration crisis
dek: José Juan Romero says it feels wrong to focus on football as Segunda División club Ceuta prepares to open its season away to Andorra amid a severe local migration emergency.
body: José Juan Romero, the coach of Spain's Segunda División side Ceuta, says he would rather his team not be playing at all this weekend, as the enclave grapples with a severe migration emergency. "If it were up to me, Ceuta wouldn't be playing this weekend," Romero said at a pre-match press conference, according to ONE.

Ceuta, the Spanish autonomous city on Morocco's northern coast, has been consumed since late July by a fresh wave of crossings at the Tarajal border post, with Spanish outlets including El Faro de Ceuta and Infobae reporting tens of thousands of people entering the enclave in a matter of weeks - a scale local media describe as far beyond the city's capacity to manage.

"It's a bit embarrassing, or awkward, to talk about football with what we're living through in the city," Romero said, adding that his players and staff are "deeply affected" by what is unfolding around them.

The manager said his own family had called off a planned visit to Ceuta because of safety concerns tied to the crisis - a personal detail he offered as evidence of how disruptive the situation has become even for those with no direct role in the emergency response.

Romero drew a direct comparison with the migrant crossing crisis of May 2021, when thousands stormed the Ceuta border fence in an episode that made international headlines at the time. This summer's situation, he said, is markedly worse.

He also criticized what he sees as insufficient attention paid to Ceuta's plight beyond the city's own borders, telling reporters that if a demonstration planned for Sunday fails to draw a response, "we'll need to do other things to make sure we're heard."

None of it changes the fixture list. Ceuta, promoted alongside Andorra last season and one of the surprise packages of the third tier, is still scheduled to open its Segunda División campaign away to Andorra this weekend, with Romero's remarks framed as a protest rather than a threat to field a weakened side or skip the match.

title: Celta Vigo's La Liga opener against Osasuna postponed after fungus wrecks the Balaídos pitch
dek: Celta apologised to supporters after a fungal outbreak damaged the playing surface at Balaídos, forcing La Liga to push the season-opening fixture back to August 27.
body: Celta Vigo's opening match of the new La Liga season has been postponed after a fungal outbreak tore through the playing surface at Balaídos, the club's home stadium, leaving it unfit for a top-flight fixture.
The match against Osasuna, originally due to kick off on Sunday, will now be played on Thursday, August 27, after La Liga, Celta and Osasuna agreed jointly to push the date back, ONE reports.

According to Celta's own statement, league inspectors had already checked the Balaídos turf the previous week and signed off on remediation work already under way to eradicate the disease. But a run of adverse weather in the days that followed set that recovery back sharply, and a further evening inspection convinced officials the pitch could not host a competitive match on schedule.

La Liga said simply that the postponement was needed "due to an illness that has affected the stadium's pitch," language that underlines how unusual the disruption is for a fixture in the league's opening round.

Celta Vigo issued a public apology to supporters, saying it regretted the inconvenience caused by what it called "exceptional circumstances" and thanking fans for their patience as groundstaff work to restore the surface before the rescheduled date.

Balaídos has been earmarked as one of the stadiums under consideration for renovation ahead of a possible 2030 World Cup bid on the Iberian peninsula, adding an awkward backdrop to a pitch failure just as the new season was getting under way.

For now, both clubs are left waiting more than a week longer than planned for their first competitive outing of the campaign, with groundstaff racing to get the Balaídos turf back into playable condition before August 27.

title: Gal Arad misses European 200m semi-final by seven thousandths of a second
dek: The Israeli sprinter clocked the same time as his Turkish rival in Birmingham, but photo-finish precision handed Deniz Kaan Kartal the last semi-final berth by 0.007 seconds.
body: Gal Arad's bid to reach a European Championships semi-final ended in the cruellest way possible on Thursday, as the Israeli sprinter was eliminated from the men's 200m at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham by seven thousandths of a second.

Arad crossed the line in a hand-timed 21.02 seconds in his first-round heat, exactly matching the clock reading of Turkey's Deniz Kaan Kartal for what looked, in the moment, like a shared place on the qualifying line. Only one of them was going through.

Officials went to the full electronic timing to separate the pair, and it settled the argument by the barest of margins: Kartal was given 21.012, Arad 21.019. Seven thousandths of a second — the width of little more than a fingernail over 200 metres — put the Turkish sprinter into Thursday evening's semi-finals and sent Arad home from the event.

It is a brutal way to exit a championship for an athlete who arrived in Birmingham in the form of his career. Arad, 26, lowered his Israeli 200m mark to 20.63 seconds earlier this year while training in the United States under coach Vince Anderson, and had targeted a run inside his personal best to force his way through to the last 24.

According to ONE, the men's 200m first round proved unusually tight at the business end, with several sprinters, including Norway's Kenny Emi Tijani-Ajayi, going through to the semi-finals on personal-best or near-personal-best times. Italy's Filippo Dezza and Germany's Joshua Hartmann headed the overall qualifiers.

There was a fuller picture of Israel's day in Birmingham. ONE reported that discus thrower Estelle Velano finished 28th in qualifying with a best throw of 51.37 metres, well short of a place in the final, while steeplechaser Adva Cohen was due back on the track in the evening session for the women's 3,000m final, aiming to improve on the qualifying time of 9:37.15 that carried her through.

For Arad, there is no shortage of context to soften the disappointment. He has spent the past two years rebuilding his season around US collegiate-circuit training, chasing a place among Europe's sprint elite, and a time of 21.02 in a European Championships heat — even one that ended in elimination — is not far off the level that took him to that 20.63 lifetime best in April.

The margin that beat him, though, is the story: seven thousandths of a second, the kind of gap that exists only on paper and on the photo-finish frame, but which is entirely real when it decides who runs again and who packs up and goes home.

title: Hapoel Holon name Maoz Daniel as new main sponsor
dek: The real estate firm, previously the purple club's secondary backer for two seasons, has signed a three-year deal to become Hapoel Holon's primary sponsor.
body: Hapoel Holon have upgraded a two-season sponsorship relationship into a full front-of-shirt partnership, officially unveiling real estate company Maoz Daniel as the purple club's new main sponsor, ONE reported.

Maoz Daniel had served as Holon's secondary sponsor for the previous two campaigns, with its branding appearing on the penalty circle and around Toto Hall. Under the new agreement, reported to run for three years, the company's logo moves to the players' jerseys as the club's lead commercial partner.

"We are proud to deepen our partnership with Hapoel Holon and become the main sponsor," Maoz Daniel co-CEO Itamar Malka said, according to ONE, describing shared values of excellence and community commitment that he said had made the step a natural one after the company's initial involvement with the club.

Hapoel Holon chairman Eitan Lanciano welcomed the move, praising the Malka family, who own Maoz Daniel, as having become "true purple fans" over the past two seasons and calling them part of the club's extended family.

Maoz Daniel is described in the club's announcement as one of Israel's most experienced real estate developers, with residential projects ranging from apartment blocks to luxury towers around the country under the company motto "quality of life above all."

The announcement lands as Israeli basketball clubs finalise their commercial and squad plans ahead of the new Winner League season, with Holon among the sides looking to build financial stability off the court to match their ambitions on it.
Financial terms of the new deal were not disclosed.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv in talks for Go Ahead Eagles winger who wants the move
dek: Thibo Baeten is reportedly open to joining the Israeli champions, though Go Ahead Eagles have already knocked back Maccabi's opening loan-with-option proposal.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have opened negotiations with Go Ahead Eagles over left winger Thibo Baeten, and the Israeli champions have an unusual ally in the talks: the player himself, who according to reports is keen on the move.

ONE reports that the 24-year-old Belgian, who plays mainly off the left but can also operate on the right, is interested in making the switch to Israel and is open to joining Maccabi Tel Aviv. Dutch outlet Voetbalprimeur carried the same line, reporting that Baeten "graag de overstap wil maken naar Israël" — that he is eager to make the move.

That willingness matters, because Go Ahead Eagles are not under any pressure to sell. Baeten only recently extended and is contracted to the Eredivisie club through the summer of 2029, giving the Dutch side a strong hand at the negotiating table.

Maccabi's opening move, according to both ONE and Voetbalprimeur, is a loan deal with a purchase option that could become mandatory if certain conditions are met during the loan spell — a structure increasingly common in cross-border deals designed to ease the buying club's upfront outlay.

Go Ahead Eagles have already rejected that first proposal, Voetbalprimeur reported, though the two clubs remain in contact as they try to find terms both sides can accept. Baeten's market value is estimated at around €500,000.

Baeten arrived in Deventer from Beerschot in the summer of 2023 and had a loan spell at Roda JC before returning to Go Ahead Eagles, where he has featured regularly on the flank without yet becoming a prolific scorer.

For Maccabi Tel Aviv, reigning champions of Israel after last season's 26th league title, added competition and depth on the wing would strengthen a squad preparing for another campaign that includes European football.

Nothing is finalised, and Go Ahead's rejection of the opening bid suggests there is still a gap to bridge — but with the player already signalling where he wants to go, Maccabi have reason for optimism that a deal can eventually be structured.

title: Bezos-led investor group agrees deal for a third of Liverpool
dek: 1892 Holdings, fronted by former QPR chairman Amit Bhatia, values the Premier League champions at more than $7 billion and can move to full control within a year
body: Fenway Sports Group has agreed to sell roughly a third of Liverpool to a new investment consortium fronted by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, ONE reported on Friday, in a deal that values the reigning Premier League champions at just over $7 billion.

The buyer is 1892 Holdings, named for Liverpool's founding year, a consortium led and managed by the British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia. Bhatia, who spent five years as chairman of Queens Park Rangers before stepping down from that club this week, is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, daughter of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, whose family trusts are also part of the group.

Bezos is not investing directly but is the lead backer of K5 Sports, one of the funds inside the consortium. The other major partner is EE Capital, the family office of Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin and his wife Elaine. It is Bezos' first move into ownership of a professional sports franchise.

According to the reporting, the stake being sold is close to 30 percent of the club, in a transaction valuing Liverpool at just over $7 billion, or roughly £5.5 billion. The consortium has also secured an option to buy its way up to majority control within the next 12 months, at a valuation of around $8 billion.

Fenway Sports Group, which has owned Liverpool since 2010, will keep majority ownership and day-to-day operational control of the club for now. In a statement, FSG confirmed it had entered a definitive agreement for the minority sale.

Bhatia is set to become Liverpool's new vice-chairman and will join an expanded club board, alongside fellow consortium figures Elaine Saverin and Bryan Baum of K5 Sports. Bezos himself will not take a board seat, the reports said.

The sale comes after years of speculation about outside investment in Liverpool, including previous reported interest from other high-profile figures that FSG had previously played down. Completion of the deal remains subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions.

For Liverpool, the investment lands just weeks into the new Premier League season and hands the club fresh financial firepower from one of the world's richest men, even as FSG insists its long-term control of the Anfield operation is not changing for now.

title: Gorbenko swims fastest in 200m medley heats to lead Israel into European final
dek: The three-time defending champion posted 2:11.87 in Paris to top qualifying, while teammate Lea Polonsky narrowly missed out on a final berth of her own.

verificationSources.label: SwimSwam — 2026 European Championships: Day 5 Prelims Live Recap
European Aquatics — Paris 2026 day five report

body: Anastasia Gorbenko will go into Saturday's 200m individual medley final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris as the fastest qualifier, after clocking 2:11.87 in Friday's heats to top the field ahead of the continent's best.

The 23-year-old, competing for Maccabi Kiryat Bialik and Israel's national team, was up by close to a body length off the backstroke leg before Ireland's Ellen Walshe clawed back ground through the breaststroke 50s. Gorbenko held on to win her heat and finish quickest overall.
Walshe qualified second in 2:12.12, with Britain's Abbie Wood (2:12.23) and 16-year-old Amalie Smith (2:12.45) rounding out the fastest four heading into the final.

It is familiar territory for Gorbenko, who arrives in Paris as the reigning European champion in the event for a third straight time, having won the title in Budapest in 2021, Rome in 2022 and Belgrade in 2024. A win on Saturday would make it four in a row.

There was disappointment elsewhere for Israel's swimming team. Lea Polonsky finished second in her own heat in 2:13.43, a promising swim that nonetheless was not quite enough to reach the final — ONE reports she finished ninth overall and will start as first reserve, ready to step in should another qualifier withdraw.

The two swimmers had shared a podium together at the last edition of these championships in Belgrade, where Gorbenko took gold in the 200m medley and Polonsky claimed silver, so Friday's split outcome will sting a little for the squad even amid Gorbenko's strong showing.

Gorbenko's medley form has been the highlight of an otherwise mixed week for Israel in the French capital, with the team also chasing places across the breaststroke and backstroke programmes as the championships enter their closing stages.

Saturday's final gives Gorbenko, an Olympic finalist and the 2024 world championship silver medallist over 400m medley, the chance to add another continental gold to an already decorated career — and to keep Israel's flag near the top of the medal table in Paris.

title: Ferran Torres faces 'real monsters' in the fight for a place at Paris Saint-Germain
dek: World Cup hero must beat out Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and new signing Maghnes Akliouche after his move from Barcelona, Spanish media warn.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Barcelona and PSG reach agreement in principle on Torres

body: Ferran Torres arrives in Paris as a World Cup winner, but Spanish media are already warning the adulation he earned this summer will not follow him across the border.

Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain have completed a deal for the Spain forward, ONE reports, with the French club having pushed hard throughout the negotiation to keep the fee below the €50 million mark "almost as a matter of pride," according to the outlet. The two sides ultimately landed at €48.5 million, ONE says, well below Barcelona's original asking price of close to €60 million and only slightly above PSG's opening offer of around €40 million.

Other outlets have put the total package somewhat higher, in the €50-55 million range including add-ons, and the clubs have yet to confirm an official figure — a detail worth flagging even as the broader move is beyond doubt.

Barcelona held firm through the early summer before their financial position tightened in August, according to ONE, which eased the deal through and took Torres's salary off the Catalan club's books at a convenient moment.

The transformation behind the transfer happened almost overnight. Torres went from a squeezed-out attacker at Barcelona to a national hero in the space of ninety minutes plus extra time, scoring the winner in Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the World Cup final on July 19 in New Jersey — the goal that delivered La Roja their second world title.

But that heroism buys him nothing in Paris, the Spanish sports daily Sport warned, in comments relayed by ONE: "real monsters await him in attack," the paper wrote, describing a PSG front line stacked with talent regardless of who is arriving from Barcelona with a World Cup medal in his pocket.

The competition is real and specific. Torres will be fighting for minutes alongside Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé, Georgian winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and young Frenchman Désiré Doué — and now also Maghnes Akliouche, the Monaco playmaker PSG signed for a reported €50 million of his own just over a week before the Torres deal was finalized.

Adding to the pressure, Torres will answer to Luis Enrique, who has managed him before with the Spain national team. ONE's report suggests the relationship will not translate into special treatment — Enrique is not expected to hand out favors based on history once Torres is competing for a shirt inside his own squad.

The message from Spain's press, as ONE frames it, is blunt: World Cup glory earns respect, but it does not guarantee a starting role at a club that has spent the summer restocking its attack with elite, young talent. Torres signed a five-year contract to make the move — now comes the harder part of justifying it on the pitch.

title: Israel's youth top flight kicks off with six games this Saturday
dek: Ligat Ha'Al Noar's 2026/27 season begins with six fixtures today and three more on Monday, when champions Maccabi Tel Aviv host promoted Hapoel Jerusalem.
body: Israel's Youth Premier League, Ligat Ha'Al Noar, opens its 2026/27 season on Saturday with six matches around the country, ONE reports, kicking off a campaign that has grown to a record 19 clubs.

With an odd number of teams in the division, each round features nine fixtures and one club with a bye. Beitar Jerusalem sit out round one, while the other 18 sides are split across Saturday and Monday.

The headline meeting is Maccabi Herzliya against Hapoel Tel Aviv at 17:00. Herzliya are looking for stability in their second straight season at this level, while Hapoel Tel Aviv arrive aiming higher after finishing last season empty-handed on goal difference. The teams' last meeting went firmly Hapoel's way, a 5-0 win, according to ONE.
Also at 17:00, Hapoel Kfar Saba host Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv, the reigning Israeli Youth Cup holders, with Kfar Saba starting a fourth consecutive season in the top flight.

At 18:00, M.S. Ashdod welcome Hapoel Hadera, who return to Ligat Ha'Al Noar after a 13-year absence. In the same time slot, Hapoel Ra'anana host Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon, and Hapoel Petah Tikva take on Ironi Kiryat Shmona, whose place in the expanded division helped push the league to 19 teams this season.
Saturday's programme closes at 19:30 with Hapoel Rishon LeZion against Hapoel Haifa.

The round continues on Monday with three further games, led by champions Maccabi Tel Aviv hosting Hapoel Jerusalem, promoted back to the top flight after 13 years away, at 19:35. Hapoel Beersheba face Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Netanya host Maccabi Petah Tikva later that evening, per ONE.
The regular season runs to 19 rounds before splitting into upper and lower playoff groups from mid-January, with the campaign scheduled to finish by late May.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv make offer to Serbian defender Nikola Maraš after Alavés release
dek: The 30-year-old centre-back, released by Deportivo Alavés this week, has received a proposal from Maccabi Tel Aviv and is weighing a move, according to ONE.
body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have opened talks with Nikola Maraš, a free-agent Serbian centre-back who parted ways with Deportivo Alavés this week, according to a report from ONE.

The 30-year-old, who stands 1.89 metres tall, saw his contract at the La Liga club run out on August 13, ending a stint in Vitoria-Gasteiz that began in 2023. ONE reports he has already begun looking into practical details of a possible move, including housing and quality of life in Tel Aviv, ahead of the transfer window closing.

Maraš came through the Partizan Belgrade academy before starting his senior career at FK Rad in Belgrade. A move to Portugal's Chaves in 2017 was followed two years later by a switch to Spain, first on loan and then permanently, with Almería, where his transfer fee is reported at roughly €1.3 million.

He joined Alavés for around €1.5 million in 2023, but loan spells at Rayo Vallecano, Levante and Sporting Gijón in the years since suggest he never fully nailed down a starting role at the Basque club. His market value, once as high as €2 million in 2018, has settled at around €600,000, per ONE's report.
Internationally, Maraš has earned two caps for Serbia's senior team, adding to appearances at under-20, under-21 and under-23 level earlier in his career.

According to ONE, any deal remains contingent on developments elsewhere in Maccabi Tel Aviv's squad, with the club still trying to resolve situations involving other foreign players before it can commit to a new arrival. The Yellow-and-Blues are working within Israel's foreign-player quota, which currently sits at eight per club in the Israeli Premier League.

Nothing is finalised yet — Maraš is described as still weighing the offer rather than having agreed terms — but a free transfer for an experienced, La Liga-tested centre-back would represent low-risk business for Maccabi as they continue reshaping their backline for the season ahead.

title: Stanković's exit leaves Abu Fani's Red Star Belgrade future in doubt
dek: The Israeli midfielder was Dejan Stanković's personal recruit in Belgrade, but with the coach gone after a Champions League exit to Hapoel Beer Sheva, ONE reports his place at the club is no longer certain
body: Three months ago, Mohammad Abu Fani was Dejan Stanković's prize signing at Red Star Belgrade. Now, with Stanković gone from the dugout, ONE reports the Israeli midfielder's place at the Serbian giants is suddenly in question.

Abu Fani joined Red Star from Ferencváros this summer in a deal worth around €1.5 million, signing a three-year contract reported at close to €750,000 a season. The move was driven above all by Stanković, who had coached him in Budapest and pushed hard to bring him to Belgrade.

The connection went back further than that. Stanković first took real notice of Abu Fani years earlier, when the midfielder helped knock Red Star out of Champions League qualifying while playing for Maccabi Haifa.

This time it was a different Israeli club that did the damage to Red Star's European campaign, and it happened with Abu Fani on the pitch. Hapoel Beer Sheva beat Red Star 1-0 in the first leg of their Champions League third qualifying round tie in Beer Sheva on August 4, then won 2-0 in Belgrade a week later to complete a 3-0 aggregate upset and advance to the playoff round.

Abu Fani's own contribution did little to help his cause. He was substituted at halftime of the first leg, and in the return match in Belgrade he came off the bench only to be sent off in stoppage time for a rash, frustration-driven foul. Serbian media rated him among the poorest performers on the night.

Stanković's own night ended just as badly. The coach was shown a red card himself after a heated clash with the referee, and according to reports from Belgrade he told his players in the dressing room straight after the final whistle that he was resigning.
Red Star moved quickly to replace him, appointing former Liverpool winger Albert Riera as head coach on a two-year deal.

That leaves Abu Fani, in ONE's words, without the coach who "had no place" for him to lose - the report's title translates roughly to "without Stanković, Abu Fani has no place at Red Star." With his patron gone and a poor tie against an Israeli opponent fresh in the club's memory, ONE reports that Riera will now have to judge Abu Fani entirely on his own terms.

The outlet adds that several Israeli clubs are already tracking the situation, hoping to bring the 28-year-old international home before the transfer window shuts - though as of now that interest remains speculative rather than any advanced move.

Abu Fani made his name at Maccabi Haifa before his switch to Ferencváros in 2023, and has been a regular for the Israel national team. Belgrade was meant to be the next step up; instead, three months in, his time there already looks uncertain.

title: Aerobic training and muscle building can coexist, if you get the balance right
dek: ONE's fitness desk pushes back on the old gym myth that cardio kills muscle gains, laying out how the two can be combined without one sabotaging the other.

verificationSources.label: ONE - האם שילוב של אירובי עם בניית מסת שריר אפשרי?
Sports Medicine (Springer) - The Effects of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training on Muscle Fiber Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

body: For years the working assumption in a lot of Israeli gyms has been blunt: pick a lane. Chase a bigger squat or chase a faster 10K, but don't expect to do both well. ONE's fitness desk pushes back on that binary, arguing that a properly structured programme can deliver meaningful aerobic fitness and muscle growth at the same time.

The piece centres on what exercise scientists call the 'interference effect' - the idea that aerobic and resistance training compete for the body's recovery resources. According to ONE, the two disciplines actually draw on different metabolic pathways, and real interference tends to show up only when aerobic volume or intensity is excessive and recovery between sessions is inadequate, not from moderate cardio on its own.

In fact, ONE reports that sensible amounts of aerobic work can support hypertrophy rather than undermine it, by improving recovery between heavy sets and enhancing blood flow and nutrient delivery to working muscle.

Nutrition still does the heavy lifting, so to speak. The article stresses that anyone trying to combine the two training styles needs a caloric surplus and sufficient protein intake, since neither type of training will build muscle in an energy deficit.

Sequencing matters too. ONE's guidance is to put strength work first in a session, ahead of any aerobic component, or to separate the two by several hours or even a full day, so lifters aren't running on empty when it's time to move heavy weight.

The choice of cardio also counts. Low-impact modalities such as cycling, swimming and the elliptical cause noticeably less muscle damage than running, according to the piece, making them friendlier training partners for anyone prioritising muscle growth.

The article is credited to Shai Lev, who has run ONE's health and fitness section since 2013 and is described as a basketball coach, gym trainer and certified TRX instructor. It does not cite named researchers or specific studies to back its claims, presenting them instead as established training-floor wisdom.

Independent research broadly backs the thrust of the advice. A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis in the journal Sports Medicine, examining concurrent aerobic and strength training, found that whole-muscle hypertrophy is not meaningfully reduced when the two are combined compared with strength training alone - though there is a small effect at the individual muscle-fibre level, one that is more pronounced when the aerobic component is running rather than cycling, and more likely to matter for trained athletes than for beginners.

The practical upshot for gym-goers, per both the ONE piece and the wider science, is that cardio doesn't have to be the enemy of size. Keep the aerobic dose moderate, favour low-impact modalities, eat enough to support growth, and schedule the two sessions so lifting always gets first claim on your energy.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv advance loan talks for Nicolaescu and Henry Addo
dek: The Israeli champions are working to move on three players outside their plans - Ion Nicolaescu, Henry Addo and Kervin Andrade - preferring temporary exits over outright releases.

verificationSources.label: ONE - שיחות מתקדמות להשאלת ניקולאסקו והנרי אדו
Walla Sport - ניקולאסקו יחזור רק בנובמבר, מכבי ת"א מחפשת חלוץ זר
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC - Vanharen appointed as Sporting Director

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are pushing to send two more fringe players out on loan before the European transfer window shuts, with ONE reporting advanced negotiations to move on Moldovan striker Ion Nicolaescu and winger Henry Addo.

Neither player figures in the club's plans for the season, and Maccabi's preference, as with other squad members they no longer need, is to arrange a loan rather than terminate a contract outright and release a player for nothing.

The Nicolaescu talks are complicated by administrative detail as much as football logic. According to ONE, the interested club plays in a league that caps first-team squads at 21 players, forcing its recruitment staff to weigh up whether to reserve one of those precious spots for the striker now or wait until he is fit and available before committing.

That timing question is not trivial. Israeli outlets including Walla Sport have reported separately that Nicolaescu, sidelined by injury, is not expected to return to full training until around November, which leaves any prospective loan club staring at months of paying wages for a player who cannot yet play.

ONE also notes that under the relevant regulations, Maccabi can only formally free up his registration slot - effectively "freezing" him off the active squad list - if Nicolaescu himself agrees in writing and signs off on the arrangement.

Addo's situation looks further advanced. ONE describes talks over a loan to a Portuguese club as being at a mature stage, though the Portuguese side has not been named. The report adds that Maccabi turned down several credible loan offers for the winger over the summer at the players' own request, a stance the club is not willing to entertain a second time.

The moves are part of a broader squad trim overseen by sporting director Steven Vanharen, the Belgian appointed to the role in June. ONE reports that Vanharen used a press conference to confirm the club continues to work on outgoing loans, including for Venezuelan forward Kervin Andrade.

For Andrade, Maccabi are said to be relaxed about terms, not insisting on an obligatory purchase clause and open to what is commonly called a "dry" loan - one with no strings attached beyond the season, so long as it leaves the door open for a possible return to Tel Aviv further down the line.
None of the three moves is finalised, and Maccabi's priority in each case remains the same: clear space and reduce the wage bill without simply cutting players loose.

title: Ashri Dror named youth captain as Kiryat Shmona's academy eyes fresh start
dek: The 16-year-old midfielder from Yesod HaMa'ala says he wants to stay focused and take responsibility for his teammates as Ironi Kiryat Shmona's academy begins a new Youth Super League season.

verificationSources.label: ONE - קפטן הנוער של ק"ש דרוך לעונה החדשה

body: Ashri Dror will carry the captain's armband for Ironi Kiryat Shmona's youth team this season, and the 16-year-old midfielder says the group arrives determined to put three difficult years behind it, ONE reports.
Dror travels roughly 20 kilometres to train and play, commuting from his hometown of Yesod HaMa'ala to represent the club he has grown up supporting locally in the Galilee panhandle.
He operates mainly in central midfield but has also filled in at the back when the team has needed him there, a versatility that has become part of his appeal to the club's coaching staff.

In his first season with the squad he scored seven goals and was a regular contributor to the team's play, form that earned him call-ups to train alongside Ironi Kiryat Shmona's senior squad, according to the report.
"The most important thing is to stay focused on the goal, and not let things around me affect me," Dror said, addressing the pressure that comes with wearing the captain's band as a teenager.
He was equally direct about what leadership means to him day to day: "I want to take responsibility and help the team, something that has followed me throughout my career."

ONE notes that the youth setup has endured three challenging seasons with limited access to home facilities, testing the group's patience before this campaign. Even so, the club won a cup under current coach Omer Levinson in the 2022/23 season, a marker the current squad is keen to build on.

Looking ahead, Dror was careful not to set himself apart from the collective effort. "I want to continue to progress, improve, and reach the highest levels I can," he said, framing his own development as tied to the team's fortunes rather than personal statistics.

For a club whose first team is preparing its own Israeli Premier League campaign, the emergence of a committed, locally rooted captain in the academy ranks is the kind of story Kiryat Shmona's supporters will want to follow through the season.

title: Daniel Peretz posts the best save percentage in English professional football
dek: The Southampton goalkeeper and Israel international finished the season with a 77.1% save rate, the highest of any keeper in England to play at least 15 matches, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: FC Bayern - Daniel Peretz completes permanent move to Southampton
The Jewish Chronicle - Peretz joins Southampton on permanent deal

body: Daniel Peretz's rise from Bayern Munich reserve to Championship mainstay has now been stamped with a number to prove it: according to ONE, the Israeli goalkeeper finished the season with a 77.1% save percentage, the best of any goalkeeper in professional English football to play at least 15 matches.

That ranking, ONE reports, spans the Premier League and the English Football League combined — meaning Peretz's efficiency between the posts topped every qualifying keeper in the English game this season, not just those in the second tier where Southampton play.

The stat caps a remarkable year for the 26-year-old, who arrived at St Mary's on loan from Bayern Munich in January and barely looked back. He started 25 league matches for Southampton, was part of a stretch in which the club went 21 games unbeaten with him playing every minute, and helped drive a run to the FA Cup semi-finals and the Championship promotion play-offs.

Southampton were later thrown out of those play-offs after admitting to spying on the training sessions of Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough — a scandal that overshadowed the closing weeks of the campaign but did not dent the club's faith in their goalkeeper.

In June, Southampton made the move permanent, agreeing a four-year contract with Bayern Munich reportedly worth around €7 million (£6.05m) for a player Bayern had signed from Maccabi Tel Aviv back in 2023 but never fully established in Munich.

Peretz, an established Israel international, becomes only the second Israeli to represent Southampton after midfielder Eyal Berkovic, who played for the club in the 1996-97 season — a link ONE's report and the club's own announcement both note with pride.

For a goalkeeper who spent long stretches on loan at Hamburg SV searching for regular football before finding it at Southampton, topping England's save-percentage charts is the clearest evidence yet that the move paid off.

body: Hapoel Holon's summer rebuild kept moving on Saturday, when American guards Rivaldo Soares and Claudell Harris Jr. landed at Ben Gurion Airport to begin pre-season with the Winner League club, ONE reports.
As has become tradition for new arrivals in Holon, a group of supporters was waiting at the terminal to welcome both players before they headed to join their new teammates.

Soares is no stranger to the club or the league. The 26-year-old wing, an Oklahoma alumnus of Cape Verdean descent, returns to Hapoel Holon after a season with Dziki Warszawa in Poland, where he averaged 11.1 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.4 assists a game, according to Eurobasket.
"I'm excited and grateful to join Hapoel Holon. From what I've heard, it's a club with a winning culture, amazing fans and high ambitions," Soares said on landing.

Harris Jr., 23, arrives from Promitheas Patras of the Greek League, where he posted 10.1 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game in his first professional season after finishing his college career at Mississippi State, Boston College and Charleston Southern. The 1.93m guard becomes the fourth import signed by Holon this off-season, per Sportando and Eurobasket.
"I'm very excited to be part of the Hapoel Holon family. I've heard so many good things about the people and the city of Holon," Harris Jr. said.

The two guards are the latest pieces in a squad overhaul that has moved quickly through August. Forward Adama Sanogo touched down in Holon on Tuesday, while new head coach Predrag Krunić arrived on Friday to begin work on the bench, ONE reported.

Forward Greg Lee, who joins after a productive season with ESSM Le Portel in France, was also due into Israel later on Saturday as Hapoel Holon continues assembling its roster ahead of the new Winner League campaign.

title: Johannes Liebmann shatters 1500m freestyle world record to complete Paris distance double
dek: The 19-year-old German swam 14:26.79 at the European Aquatics Championships, becoming the first man ever under 14:30 and adding the world record to the 800m freestyle gold he won three days earlier.
body: Johannes Liebmann produced one of the most startling distance swims anyone has ever seen on Saturday, tearing almost four seconds off the men's 1500m freestyle world record at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.

The 19-year-old German touched the wall in 14:26.79, obliterating Bobby Finke's mark of 14:30.67 from the 2024 Paris Olympics and becoming the first man in history to swim inside 14 minutes 30 seconds for the distance.

Liebmann went out hard from the first length and never let up, swimming roughly two and a half seconds inside world-record pace by the 400m mark and continuing to pull away through the second half of the race, according to European Aquatics, the sport's continental governing body.
He touched well clear of Hungary's Zalan Sarkany, who took silver in 14:39.45, with Germany's Oliver Klemet completing an all-European podium in bronze in 14:40.64.

"The time is insane but I knew I could go fast and that was the plan, go fast in the beginning and keep that pace, get clear of the others," Liebmann said afterwards, quoted by European Aquatics. "But then it hurt quite a lot! To hear the crowd cheering in the last 200m was a great, great feeling."

The swim also erased the previous European record of 14:32.80, held by Italy's Gregorio Paltrinieri, and the championship record Paltrinieri had set at the same event back in 2016 — meaning Liebmann walked away with three records from a single race.

It capped a remarkable week for the teenager, who had already won the 800m freestyle title in Paris three days earlier in a European record of 7:37.59, resetting a continental mark he himself had set back in April. The 1500m world record completed a distance double at the same championships.

Liebmann's rise has been rapid. He took silver in the 1500m freestyle at the 2024 European Junior Championships before adding another junior silver over the distance in 2025 — now, barely a year later, he holds the senior world record outright.

body: La Liga's traditional curtain-raiser delivered a lopsided opening night on Saturday, with Deportivo Alavés seeing off 10-man Getafe 3-0 at Mendizorrotza to launch the 2026-27 season.

The contest turned before the break. Getafe right-back Kiko Femenía was sent off, ONE reports, for a reckless, studs-up challenge on Alavés winger Abde Rebbach, leaving the visitors to play the entire second half a man short.

Alavés could not immediately capitalise, taking the game goalless into the second half despite their numerical advantage. The breakthrough finally came in the 73rd minute, when Nahuel Tenaglia turned home the opener to put the hosts ahead.

With Getafe's resistance broken and legs tiring, Alavés added gloss to the scoreline in stoppage time. Mariano Díaz got on the scoresheet himself before Mikel Rodríguez rounded off the rout, sending Mendizorrotza into celebration on the opening weekend of the campaign.

It was a notable night for Díaz in particular. The 33-year-old forward, once of Real Madrid and Olympique Lyonnais, is rebuilding his career at Alavés and was heavily involved throughout, contributing to the second-half surge that turned a tight, one-man-advantage game into a rout.

For Getafe, José Bordalás's side will have to regroup quickly after an opening-day setback compounded by their own indiscipline - a familiar story for a club that often finds itself playing with fewer than eleven men against the run of play.

Alavés, by contrast, could hardly have asked for a better start to the new campaign, banking three points and a clean sheet in front of their own supporters as La Liga's 38-round marathon gets under way.

title: Hapoel Haifa 4-0 Hapoel Beer Sheva: furious Kozuk apologises to fans after disgraceful Toto Cup display
dek: Ran Kozuk fumed after his understrength Hapoel Beer Sheva side crumbled in Haifa, just days before what he calls the biggest match in the club's history against Sabah in the Champions League playoff round.

body: Ran Kozuk did not hide his anger on Saturday evening after a Hapoel Beer Sheva side stripped of most of its regulars was taken apart 4-0 by Hapoel Haifa in a Toto Cup ranking match played for fifth and sixth place.
"I think what we produced today was simply an outrage," the head coach said afterwards, according to ONE. "This is not acceptable for Hapoel Beer Sheva, regardless of which lineup takes the field."

Kozuk went further, apologising directly to the supporters who turned out for what was, on paper, a dead rubber. "I apologise to the fans who came here," he said, insisting that the standard his club sets itself cannot fluctuate depending on how much is riding on a given fixture.

The match itself was one-sided from early on. Hapoel Haifa, under Haim Silves, opened the scoring through Shai Elias in the 29th minute before Liran Rotman doubled the lead four minutes later. Alon Turgeman made it three shortly after the hour, and Rotman completed his brace in the 67th minute to seal a 4-0 rout, according to ONE's match report.

Silves was pleased with his own team's showing but used the post-match platform to vent his own frustration - not at the scoreline, but at the postponement of Hapoel Haifa's league opener, which he described as "very disappointing."

For Kozuk, the humiliation lands at an awkward moment. Hapoel Beer Sheva are only days away from what the coach himself has called the most important match in the club's history: the first leg of a Champions League playoff round tie against Azerbaijan's Sabah FK, with a place in the competition's league phase at stake for the first time.

Beer Sheva reached that stage by eliminating Red Star Belgrade in the third qualifying round, winning 1-0 away before completing the job at home, a 3-0 aggregate victory over one of the Balkans' most storied clubs. The first leg against Sabah is scheduled for the coming week, with the return fixture to follow.

Kozuk's message after the Haifa defeat was less about the Toto Cup placement itself and more a warning shot to his squad: that sloppiness cannot be switched on and off depending on the stakes, with a genuinely historic European night now bearing down on the club.

title: Israel's under-16 women fall 72-61 to Turkey to close European Championship group stage
dek: Michal Abudraham's 21 points and 10 rebounds were not enough as the Israeli cadettes finished third in Group B and move on to face Serbia in the last 16.
body: Israel's under-16 women's basketball team closed the group phase of the FIBA U16 Women's EuroBasket Division B with a 72-61 defeat to Turkey on Sunday, a result that leaves the young Israeli squad to regroup before the knockout rounds begin.

Turkey set the tone early, opening a lead of as much as 11 points inside the first half. Israel clawed back into the contest through the second and third quarters, trading baskets and briefly threatening to turn the game around, but the fourth quarter belonged to the hosts of this leg of the tournament, who outscored Israel 24-12 down the stretch to seal it.

Michal Abudraham was the standout for Israel, finishing with 21 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks in a near-complete performance that nonetheless could not prevent the loss. The 14-year-old, who also turns out for Herzliya in Israel's domestic girls' league, has been one of the squad's most consistent contributors through the tournament.

Rona Tzlal chipped in 13 points and three assists, while Ella Meoz Barda added a well-rounded 10 points, five assists and four rebounds. Between them, the trio accounted for the bulk of Israel's offensive output as the rest of the roster struggled to find a rhythm against Turkey's pressure.

The defeat means Israel finish third in Group B with a 1-2 record, having opened the group stage with a commanding 68-37 win over Italy before a second loss set up Sunday's group-closing meeting with Turkey.

Despite the setback, Israel's cadettes have done enough to advance to the round of 16, where they are set to face Serbia on Tuesday. It is now a straight knockout — win and the tournament continues, lose and the campaign is over.

For a squad built around teenagers still years from senior international basketball, reaching the knockout stage of a continental championship is itself a marker of progress, even if Sunday's finish leaves room for improvement against the tournament's stronger sides.

title: Lens 1-0 PSG: ten-man hosts hold firm to win Trophée des Champions
dek: Florian Thauvin's first-half strike was enough for Lens to stun European champions Paris Saint-Germain, even after playing more than 50 minutes with ten men at Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

verificationSources.label: beIN Sports - PSG pushes until the end but 10-man Lens holds on to win Trophée des Champions

body: RC Lens pulled off one of the most stunning results of the pre-season calendar on Sunday night, beating European champions Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 in the 2026 Trophée des Champions at a raucous Stade Bollaert-Delelis — and did it while playing more than fifty minutes with a man down.
Florian Thauvin put the hosts ahead in the 32nd minute, pouncing on a loose ball at the far post to beat PSG's goalkeeper and send the home crowd into raptures.

The celebrations were still ringing round the stadium when, seven minutes later, Kyllian Antonio was sent off for a reckless, over-the-ball challenge on Maghnes Akliouche — leaving Lens to protect their lead with ten men from before half-time against a European champion side with every incentive to pour forward.

Luis Enrique's PSG, who had lifted the European Super Cup with a 2-1 win over Aston Villa just four days earlier, duly dominated possession and territory for most of the remaining hour. But they could not turn control into goals: Désiré Doué crashed a first-half effort against the crossbar, Ousmane Dembélé fired wide, and Fabián Ruiz had a second-half strike ruled out by VAR for offside.

Lens were not chance-free themselves — Matthieu Udol also had a goal disallowed — but their numerical disadvantage told in the closing stages as PSG poured players forward through a string of substitutions without finding a way past a stubborn home defence.

Then, with eight minutes left, PSG's night got worse still: substitute Nuno Mendes was shown a straight red card for an elbow on Lens winger Michal Skoras, turning the closing stages into an unlikely ten-against-ten shootout that Lens, remarkably, kept a lid on.

Thauvin was reported to have been furious with officials over the Antonio dismissal, telling the fourth official that "it's a trophy we're playing for, not a friendly match" — before his side made sure the final result backed up the sentiment.

The win is Lens's first Trophée des Champions title in the club's history. They had qualified for the traditional season-opener as Coupe de France holders, while PSG were there as Ligue 1 champions and reigning European champions on the back of their continental Super Cup triumph earlier in August.

New France head coach Zinedine Zidane was among the crowd at Bollaert-Delelis, watching a Ligue 1 underdog knock the European champions off their perch before a ball had even been kicked in the new domestic season.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are still pushing to bring Gabi Kanichowsky back to Bloomfield Stadium, with ONE reporting that talks with his current club, Hungarian champions Ferencvaros, have run for more than six weeks without a breakthrough.

According to the report, the Israeli champions regard the 28-year-old midfielder as a priority target for the rest of the summer window, having concluded internally that letting him leave for nothing a year ago, rather than meeting his contract demands at the time, was a mistake.

ONE says negotiations began in late June, with Ferencvaros initially valuing Kanichowsky at around €2.5 million. That asking price has since eased to roughly €2m, though a significant gap between the two clubs reportedly remains.

Complicating any swift return, Kanichowsky himself would face a tax penalty of about €250,000 tied to the terms of his move to Hungary, on top of whatever fee the clubs eventually agree, ONE reports. Despite that, the outlet says the player is willing to come back to Maccabi Tel Aviv if the two clubs can find common ground.

The saga was significant enough to come up on a Maccabi Tel Aviv-affiliated podcast this past Thursday, where Kanichowsky was again flagged as one of the club's leading targets for the remainder of the window, according to ONE.

Kanichowsky is a Ra'anana-born product of Maccabi Tel Aviv's academy who was re-signed by his boyhood club in August 2021. Over four seasons he made 188 appearances and won league titles under Robbie Keane, part of a double in his final campaign, before leaving as a free agent for Ferencvaros in July 2025 on a three-year deal.

Since moving to Budapest he has remained a regular contributor and won the 2025-26 Magyar Kupa with the club. Ferencvaros' immediate focus, though, is Europe: they face Trabzonspor over two legs in the UEFA Europa League play-off round, in Turkey on 20 August and at home on 27 August, fixtures ONE suggests could yet shape how the transfer talks develop.
For now, no agreement is in place, and ONE's reporting makes clear the financial gap between the clubs, and the tax bill facing the player, still stand between Kanichowsky and a return to Tel Aviv.

title: David Roddy lands in Israel to begin new chapter at Hapoel Jerusalem
dek: The former NBA forward touched down at Ben Gurion Airport on Sunday night, saying it will "take time to adjust" to life and basketball outside the United States.
body: David Roddy touched down at Ben Gurion Airport on Sunday night, becoming the second Hapoel Jerusalem import to arrive in Israel ahead of the new season, after point guard Jared Harper.

The 25-year-old American forward has signed with the Jerusalem club for the 2026/27 season, with a club option for a further year, marking his first taste of professional basketball outside the United States after four seasons bouncing around the NBA.

"The project happening here this year is excellent and I love it," Roddy said on arrival, according to ONE. He was candid about the adjustment ahead: "It will take time to adjust to playing outside the USA."
He described his own game in simple terms: a player who loves competing, versatile, and able to pass, shoot and defend.

Roddy said the club's ambitions for the season are clear-cut — win the EuroCup and secure qualification for the EuroLeague, a target Hapoel Jerusalem has chased in recent seasons under owner Ori Allon's rebuild.

His path to Jerusalem has been a winding one. Colorado State's standout forward was picked 23rd overall by Philadelphia in the 2022 NBA draft and immediately traded to Memphis on draft night. From there he moved through Phoenix, Atlanta, Philadelphia again and Houston before finishing last season with the Denver Nuggets, totalling well over 170 NBA appearances.
He also featured for the United States national team in World Cup qualifying matches in February, giving him recent experience of international-style basketball ahead of the switch to Europe.

In Jerusalem, Roddy joins a foreign contingent that already includes Devante Cacok and Jalen Smith alongside Harper, all playing under head coach Sasha Obradović. Hebrew media reports have put the value of his deal at somewhere between roughly $1 million and $1.5 million for the first season, though the club has not published an official figure.

Roddy is expected to begin training with his new teammates in the coming weeks as Hapoel Jerusalem builds toward a campaign in which both a domestic title push and a EuroCup run are firmly on the agenda.

body: The Hebrew-language MMA scene got its full debrief on UFC 330 this week, with the 52nd episode of ONE's "Noquaout" (Knockout) podcast walking through a Philadelphia fight night that produced a UFC record and two title defences.

Hosts Yaniv Kaminsky and Olga Rubin were joined in the studio by guest Uri Shokron for a card-length conversation that opened, inevitably, with the main event: Islam Makhachev's welterweight title defence against Ian Machado Garry.

Makhachev won a clear unanimous decision, with judges' scores of 49-46, 49-46 and 48-47, but the fight was no coronation. Garry forced the champion to work for seven takedowns across five rounds and left visible facial damage on him, a physical toll the hosts spent real time dissecting.

The result carried extra weight beyond the belt: it was Makhachev's 17th consecutive win, breaking the UFC record for consecutive victories that had stood in Anderson Silva's name. Kaminsky, Rubin and Shokron used that milestone as a launching point to debate where Makhachev now sits among the promotion's all-time greats and what, if anything, is left for him to prove at welterweight.

Attention then turned to the co-main event, where Mackenzie Dern defended her strawweight title against Gillian Robertson. Dern dominated on the ground across five rounds, repeatedly taking Robertson's back and coming close to a finish, and the podcast broke down the specific grappling sequences that keyed her win before turning to what a statement performance like that means for her position at 115 pounds.

The conversation also looked ahead. Jean Silva's newly confirmed opponent was a hot topic in the studio: the Brazilian featherweight will headline Noche UFC against Yair Rodriguez on September 12 in Glendale, Arizona, and the hosts weighed in on how the returning former title challenger stacks up as a measuring-stick fight for one of the division's rising finishers.

Flyweight champion Joshua Van also came in for scrutiny, with the hosts making clear he had gotten under their skin during the broader UFC 330 news cycle — part of a wider discussion about whether the young champion's recent conduct raises any real concerns about one of the sport's most talked-about prospects.
Episode 52 of Noquaout is available now on Spotify and Apple Podcasts, continuing the show's run as one of the main Hebrew-language outlets tracking the UFC card by card for Israeli fight fans.

body: Sasa Obradovic has arrived in Israel to begin work as Hapoel Jerusalem's head coach, landing at Ben Gurion Airport with the club's new center Dusan Miletic in tow, ONE reported.

The Serbian, appointed in June on a three-year deal that runs through the 2028-29 season, wasted no time setting the tone for the campaign ahead. "First of all, I'm already waiting to start. I'm very excited about opening this season," he told the outlet on arrival.

Obradovic, 57, is one of the more decorated names to take charge of an Israeli club in recent years. He guided Monaco to the 2023 EuroLeague Final Four and has also coached Crvena Zvezda and Alba Berlin during a European career spanning more than two decades, most recently taking over Crvena Zvezda before his move to Jerusalem.
He praised the club's recruitment work in building the roster around him, thanking owner Matan Adelson: "I truly thank President Adelson and the management for building an amazing team."
"I really believe our wonderful fans will enjoy the season. I'm truly looking forward to starting," Obradovic added, according to ONE.

Miletic, the Serbian big man who arrived with him, is fresh off winning the Lebanese championship with Al Riyadi and was one of the standout performers in last season's EuroCup with U-BT Cluj, averaging 12.6 points and 7.6 rebounds. He has signed a two-year contract with the Reds.

The pairing reflects the scale of Hapoel Jerusalem's ambitions under Adelson's ownership, with the club making no secret of its intention to push for EuroLeague qualification through EuroCup success this season.

Obradovic's landing marks the formal start of pre-season preparations in Jerusalem, with the coach and his new recruit now set to link up with the rest of the squad as the club builds toward the opening of the campaign.

title: Maccabi Ashdod complete import roster with signing of forward Markis McDuffie
dek: The American forward, fresh off a season at French club Nancy, joins on a one-year deal as Ashdod's fifth and final import ahead of their return to the Israeli top flight.

verificationSources.label: ONE - השלימה את מצבת הזרים: מרקיז מקדאפי חתם באשדוד

body: Maccabi Ashdod have completed their quota of foreign players ahead of the new season, announcing the signing of American forward Markis McDuffie on a one-year contract, ONE reports.

The 6-foot-8 forward, who turns 29 next month, arrives after a stint at French club SLUC Nancy, part of a well-travelled European career that has taken in stops in Hungary, Italy, France and Turkey since he went undrafted out of Wichita State in 2019.

His numbers have swung with the level of competition: 20.4 points per game during a spell at Udine in Italy's second tier, 14.5 points and 4.5 rebounds a game in Serie A with Napoli, and 16.9 points and 5.8 rebounds at Dijon in France. Last season at Nancy, in a stronger French top flight, his output settled at 6.1 points and 2.4 rebounds per game. A season earlier, at Piacenza, he averaged 16.3 points and 6.3 rebounds and was named to the Italian second division's all-league second team.

Ashdod's professional director, Nati Cohen, framed the signing as the final piece of the club's roster build for a season that will see them competing in Israel's top flight after their promotion. According to ONE, Cohen said McDuffie brings "a lot of experience in top European leagues" along with "energy, athleticism, high-level individual ability and rebounding" that completes the squad puzzle.

McDuffie becomes the fifth and, per the report, final import on Ashdod's roster, joining Augustin Rubit, Isaiah Hill, Robert Turner and Qudus Wahab as the club's foreign contingent for the campaign ahead.
With the import slots now filled, attention in Ashdod turns to preseason preparations as the club builds toward its first games back among Israel's elite.

title: Athens, 19 August 2004: The Bronze That Arrived Before the Gold
dek: Five days before Gal Fridman's windsurfing gold made headlines, judoka Arik Ze'evi quietly opened Israel's medal count in Athens — beating a Dutchman by ippon after a detour through the repechage.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — Judo at the 2004 Summer Olympics, Men's 100kg
Wikipedia — Israel at the 2004 Summer Olympics

body: On the morning of 19 August 2004, in the packed and sweltering Ano Liossia Olympic Hall on the northern edge of Athens, Ariel "Arik" Ze'evi walked out for a bronze-medal contest that would make him, however briefly, the answer to a trivia question: the man who won Israel's first medal of the Athens Olympics.

Ze'evi arrived in Athens with a pedigree few Israeli judoka could match. Born on 16 January 1977 in Bnei Brak and raised through the Hapoel Bnei Brak judo club, he had already won the European title twice, in 2001 and 2003, and had carried the Israeli flag at the opening ceremony days earlier — a recognition of a decorated career that, at the Olympic level, had so far produced only a fifth-place finish at Sydney 2000.

The men's 100kg draw did not go cleanly for him. In the semifinals, Ze'evi lost by ippon to South Korea's Jang Sung-ho, a result that would ordinarily end a competitor's day. Olympic judo, though, offers a second life through the repechage, and Ze'evi took it. He beat Cameroon's Franck Martial Moussima, then defeated France's Ghislain Lemaire — at the time ranked second in the world — to earn his place in the bronze-medal bout.

Waiting across the tatami was Elco van der Geest of the Netherlands. The contest did not go the distance: Ze'evi threw him for ippon, the clean, decisive score that ends a judo match outright, and stood as an Olympic medalist for the first time in his career.

It was a modest medal by the raw arithmetic of a Games table — one bronze, in a half-heavyweight division that rarely makes front pages. But its timing gave it outsized weight at home. It was the first medal won by any Israeli athlete at the Athens Olympics, arriving five days before windsurfer Gal Fridman's gold turned the country's attention fully to the Games. For a few days in late August 2004, Ze'evi's bronze was the whole of Israel's Olympic story.

The medal also closed a personal loop. Ze'evi had gone to Sydney four years earlier as a promising 23-year-old and come home with nothing to show for it beyond a fifth-place finish. Athens, contested in front of Greek crowds in a hall built for exactly this kind of drama, turned him from a nearly-man into an Olympic medalist — and did so on Israeli judo's biggest individual stage since Yael Arad's and Oren Smadja's medals in Barcelona twelve years before.

Ze'evi's career did not end in Athens. He added two further European titles, in 2004 itself and then, remarkably, in 2012 at the age of 35 — a title that made him a four-time European champion, a record among Israeli judoka. He returned to the Olympics twice more, at Beijing in 2008, where he fell in the repechage without a medal, and at London in 2012, where his final Olympic bout lasted only 43 seconds before a loss to Germany's Dimitri Peters.

None of those later Games produced another medal. The bronze from the Ano Liossia hall on 19 August 2004 remained, to the end of his competitive career, Ze'evi's only Olympic podium finish — a single afternoon that made him, for a few days at least, the face of Israel's Olympic effort, before the country's gaze shifted to the water off Saronic Gulf and to the gold that followed.

title: Court rejects Ashdod's bid to delay National League opener against Afula
dek: Attorney Avishai Ifrgan, representing Hapoel Afula, says timing — not substance — sank Ashdod's petition to postpone the Liga Leumit curtain-raiser while a disciplinary case against Ironi Tiberias plays out.

verificationSources.label: ONE — attorney Avishai Ifrgan on the ruling
ONE — Afula's response to the petition

body: A legal fight over the Liga Leumit season opener has ended badly for MS Ashdod, after the Israel Football Association's Supreme Disciplinary Court threw out the club's bid to postpone its curtain-raiser against Hapoel Afula.

Ashdod had asked the panel to delay the fixture, arguing that going ahead before an ongoing disciplinary case against Ironi Tiberias is resolved would lock in what its petition called an "irreversible reality" — one that could cost the club its route back to the Israeli Premier League.

In court, Ashdod's lawyers, Bar Vaknin and Eli Peri, framed their client as the "primary victim" of the alleged scheme at Tiberias and warned that letting the season kick off regardless could leave outcomes that can never be undone.

The Tiberias case stems from an indictment filed by the association's prosecution on July 27, alleging an organized effort in which club staff coordinated and financed the purchase of equipment and the administration of intravenous infusions to players, along with recruiting outside help, around a decisive survival match against Ashdod last season.

The three-judge panel — Prof. Miguel Deutsch, Prof. Yaniv Vaki and attorney Ortal Klein — sided with Afula. It found that Ashdod only approached the leagues committee on a Thursday evening and filed its petition the following day, weeks after the indictment became public, and that the club's case rested on "speculative foundational assumptions" about how the Tiberias proceedings would ultimately end.

The judges also noted the practical stakes: Tiberias's disciplinary hearings are not expected to conclude before late October, with the first evidentiary session set for September 10, and postponing the league's opening round now would cause serious damage to running the competition.
Even so, the panel left a door open, stating that if circumstances change, it will fall to the professional leagues committee to consider how to proceed.

Speaking to ONE after the ruling, attorney Avishai Ifrgan, who represented Afula, said he was pleased the panel had accepted his side's position, and boiled the case down to one question of timing. "The claim is about timing — why didn't you do this a week and a half ago?" he said.

Ifrgan also separately represents three Tiberias players who have been suspended for more than five weeks pending the outcome of the same disciplinary case. He declined to detail their situation so as not to appear to prejudge it, and clarified he holds no current official role at the association: "I'm not a power broker at the association — I once was — and I'm not one at Tiberias either."

With the petition dismissed, kickoff between Ashdod and Afula goes ahead as scheduled, and any further reckoning over the Tiberias affair will now play out through the disciplinary tribunal rather than the fixture list.

title: "An excellent coach, but not a magician": Hapoel Petah Tikva legend defends Omer Peretz after four straight losses
dek: Eli Mahfoud says Peretz needs reinforcements, not miracles, as Hapoel Petah Tikva head into the league opener at Ironi Tiberias off a battered preseason.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "עומר פרץ מאמן מצוין, אבל הוא לא קוסם"
PT News — fan reaction to fourth straight loss
Sport1/Maariv — Peretz and Hapoel Petah Tikva preparing for the opener

body: Hapoel Petah Tikva walk into Saturday's Israeli Premier League opener at Ironi Tiberias under a cloud, and it took a club legend to try to talk the fan base down from the ledge. Eli Mahfoud, who spent 14 years and 362 games in the club's midfield, told ONE's Sicha Hayom podcast that coach Omer Peretz remains "an excellent coach, but he's not a magician" — a pointed reminder that results this preseason have had less to do with the man on the touchline than with what he has had to work with.

The comment lands after a brutal run: four straight defeats in the Toto Cup, the last of them a 1-0 loss away to Bnei Sakhnin that closed out the competition and arrived barely a week before the league kicks off. It was hardly the platform anyone at HaMoshava Stadium wanted heading into a top-flight season.

The defeat set off a wave of frustration among supporters online, according to PT News, with fans demanding to know where the club's reported 31 million shekel budget had gone and pointing to new arrivals — among them Rivolayeh, Badash and Nasser — as underwhelming compared with players who left over the summer. Some called for academy graduates to be given a chance instead.

Mahfoud's read is more measured. He pointed to concrete, fixable problems: the squad is missing three or four key players, several of those available are short of full fitness, and the club's recruitment has been constrained by budget rather than by Peretz's judgment. In his telling, the team is simply still under construction two matchdays before it matters.

It is not the first time Petah Tikva have looked ragged in August only to find their footing later. Mahfoud drew a direct line to last season, when a similarly shaky start preceded the run that carried Peretz's side up out of the second tier and back into the top flight.

That promotion is precisely why Peretz, 40, is not going anywhere regardless of how the Toto Cup went. The club signed him to a two-year contract extension through the end of the 2027/28 season and raised his salary by roughly a third, cementing him as one of the most sought-after young coaches in Israeli football. It is a vote of confidence the club has shown no sign of walking back.

Mahfoud went further than simple reassurance, using the platform to press a broader argument about how the club should be run: he favors a model in which an incoming investor partners with organized supporters rather than taking sole ownership, arguing that combining financial backing with fan involvement would give Petah Tikva a more sustainable path than relying on one owner's pocket.

For now, the more immediate fix is a football one. Mahfoud believes Petah Tikva remain a stronger outfit than most of what they will face this season, and that one or two league wins — starting away at Ironi Tiberias — would be enough to restore the confidence that four Toto Cup defeats have drained. The opener will be the first real test of whether he is right.
