title: Marathon medals prove Israel has a strong team, Ayale says after European gold
dek: Gashau Ayale, Tadesse Getahon and Aymero Alemayehu helped Israel retain the team title in Birmingham, with Ayale adding an individual bronze
body: Israel's national marathon team came home to a hero's welcome this week, days after retaining the team title at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham — and Gashau Ayale, who added an individual bronze to the collective gold, says the run proves the strength of the squad he leads.

"There is no feeling like wrapping myself in the Israeli flag in front of all of Europe," Ayale said, according to ONE. "These medals first and foremost prove we have a strong team, where everyone gives everything they have."

The team of Ayale, Tadesse Getahon and Aymero Alemayehu finished with a combined time of 6:28:37, enough to hold off Germany and France for gold — Israel's second consecutive and third overall team title at the European Championships, following the breakthrough in Munich in 2022.

Ayale crossed the line third individually in 2:09:21, backing up the silver he won at the previous championships with another podium finish. Getahon was fifth in 2:09:31 and Alemayehu eighth in 2:09:45, with the trio's tight finishing times underlining the strength of the group as a unit rather than a single star turn.

Germany's Amanal Petros took individual gold in a championship-record 2:09:11, with Italy's Pietro Riva second in 2:09:18. But it was the team competition, decided on combined time across three finishers, where Israel made its mark for the third time in the event's history.

Alemayehu, one of several Ethiopian-born runners who have become Israeli citizens and record-holders over the past decade, spoke of the significance of doing it again on foreign soil. "Bringing this pride to the State of Israel, and doing it a third time running at the European Championships — that's very moving," he said, per ONE.

The result extends a golden run for Israeli marathon running that has included Ayale's national record of 2:04:53 set in Seville and a steady stream of European medals since the program's first team title. Maru Teferi, Yitayew Abuhay and Bukayo Melada also competed for Israel in Birmingham as the country fielded a deep squad across the men's field.

President Isaac Herzog telephoned Ayale after the result to congratulate the team, telling him the runners had "brought great pride to the State of Israel" by representing the country with honor at the championships.

For a program built largely around runners who came to Israel from Ethiopia and rose through its club system — Ayale runs for Maccabi Tel Aviv, Getahon for Hapoel Emek Hefer and Alemayehu for Hapoel Athletic Oren — the team result offers proof that Israel's marathon strength no longer rests on one name, but on a genuine depth of contenders capable of standing on a European podium together.

title: Bnei Yehuda and Ashdod named favourites as Leumit captains give their season verdict
dek: In ONE's pre-season captains' survey, rivals across Israel's second tier tipped Bnei Yehuda and MS Ashdod for promotion — and Ironi Modi'in and Maccabi Achi Nazareth for the drop.

verificationSources.label: ONE — מי יעלו ומי ירדו: הקפטנים בלאומית עונים על הכל

body: With Liga Leumit's new season almost upon us, ONE went back to a format it has used before the last few campaigns: put the same set of questions to captains right across the division and see where the answers converge. This year the closest thing to a consensus pick, echoed by players who will be trying to beat each other every second week from August through the spring, was that Bnei Yehuda and MS Ashdod are the two sides best placed to go up.

Roughly fourteen captains took part, drawn from clubs stretching from the Hatikva Quarter in Tel Aviv to the Negev coast and the Galilee, among them Golan Bani of Bnei Yehuda, Reef Masika of Maccabi Kiryat Gat, Roy Harel of Hapoel Kfar Saba, Arthur Aleinikov of MS Kiryat Yam, Erik Yanko of Maccabi Jaffa, Shnir Shuker of Hapoel Ra'anana, Mor Neeman of Hapoel Acre and Yaniv Brick of Hapoel Afula, alongside the captains of Hapoel Kfar Shalem, Hapoel Rishon LeZion, Maccabi Herzliya, MS Kafr Qasem, Maccabi Achi Nazareth and Ironi Modi'in.

On promotion, Bnei Yehuda drew the most nods from rival dressing rooms — a reflection of the size of the club's fan base and the pull of its Hatikva Quarter home, even after several seasons stuck outside the top flight. MS Ashdod, the coastal club that has bounced between divisions in recent years, was the other name that kept recurring when captains were asked to pick the two teams they expect to see in Ligat Ha'al next season.

The relegation picture, according to the same poll, points toward Ironi Modi'in and Maccabi Achi Nazareth as the two clubs most captains fear could go down — though, tellingly, neither of those clubs' own representatives, Nir Laks and Amjad Suleiman, agreed with the outside assessment of their own teams.

Suleiman did offer one of the survey's wryer lines, telling ONE that the Leumit has a habit of catching everyone out early: within the first three or four rounds, he said, a manager or two is usually already out of a job as results scramble the pre-season predictions — a dynamic that makes any captains' poll, including this one, worth taking with a pinch of salt.

Away from the table-topping questions, ONE also asked its panel for the game's lighter answers: who they rate as underrated, who they'd back in goal, and what they might have done for a living instead of football. MS Kafr Qasem's captain, Samah Mar'ab, said veterinary medicine was his fallback plan had a playing career not worked out.

Several captains also used the platform to press for changes to how the division is run, from calls for video review to gripes about Friday fixture scheduling — recurring themes in a league that operates with a fraction of Ligat Ha'al's broadcast money and technology.

None of it is binding, of course. Israeli second-tier promotion races are notoriously unpredictable, and last season's eventual pair to go up, Maccabi Petah Tikva and Hapoel Ramat Gan, were far from everyone's pre-season picks either. But as a snapshot of dressing-room opinion on the eve of a new campaign, ONE's captains' survey is as good a form guide as any — even the players inside it seem to know how quickly it could be proven wrong.

title: Gal Levi to referee Maccabi Tel Aviv, Omer Biran gets Maccabi Haifa in Ligat Ha'al opener
dek: The Israel Football Association has confirmed match officials for the opening round of the 2026/27 season, with Hapoel Be'er Sheva, Hapoel Tel Aviv and their opponents held over because of European commitments.

verificationSources.label: Israel Football Association referee registry — Omer Biran

body: The Israel Football Association has published its referee appointments for the opening round of the 2026/27 Ligat Ha'al season, ONE reports, with Gal Levi and Omer Biran handed the two fixtures involving the league's Tel Aviv and Haifa giants.

Levi will take charge of Hapoel Jerusalem's home game against Maccabi Tel Aviv on Sunday, the second day of the new campaign, when Maccabi travel to the capital to open their league season away from home.

Biran, meanwhile, has been given Maccabi Haifa's opening match against Hapoel Ramat Gan on Saturday, the day the 2026/27 season actually kicks off. It is a notable return to the big occasions for the young official: according to Walla and Israel Hayom, Biran stepped away from refereeing for several weeks last year after his younger brother, Golani sergeant Rei Biran, was killed in Khan Younis in July 2025, before coming back to the whistle in time for this pre-season.

Elsewhere in round one, ONE reports David Focksman will referee Maccabi Petah Tikva's clash with Ironi Kiryat Shmona, Snir Levi has been given Ironi Tiberias against Hapoel Petah Tikva at Bra'el Stadium, and Na'al Odeh will oversee Maccabi Netanya's home game with Bnei Sakhnin at Miriam Stadium.

The rearranged fixtures will be slotted in later in the calendar once the European picture for Be'er Sheva and Hapoel Tel Aviv becomes clearer.
For now, attention turns to Saturday's kick-off, when Maccabi Haifa host Hapoel Ramat Gan under Biran's whistle before Levi takes charge of Maccabi Tel Aviv's trip to Teddy Stadium a day later.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Hapoel Tel Aviv 2-1 as Athena Cup women's derby returns after 24 years
dek: Elizabeth Motzarela and Diana Burges struck either side of a Maria Almatzri equaliser as Maccabi's rebuilt women's side won the Tel Aviv derby in the Athena Cup's opening round, while Hapoel Katamon Yam thrashed Maccabi Kishronot Hadera 3-0 on the same night.

verificationSources.label: BE106 Yavne — derby preview, return after 24 years

body: The Tel Aviv women's football derby returned to Israeli football for the first time in 24 years on Thursday evening, and Maccabi Tel Aviv marked the occasion with a 2-1 win over Hapoel Tel Aviv in the opening round of the Athena Cup.
Elizabeth Motzarela put Maccabi ahead in the 52nd minute, Maria Almatzri levelled for Hapoel four minutes later, and Diana Burges settled it with the winner in the 84th, ONE reports.

The fixture had not been staged in well over two decades, and its revival drew notice even though it was played away from either club's usual base, at the Kalal Stadium in Yavne, with free admission for supporters, according to a local Yavne news report.

Maccabi's women's section only returned to competitive football last year, after folding in 2002. It was reconstituted in 2025 through a merger with the ASA Tel Aviv women's club, and now competes as Maccabi ASA Tel Aviv — Thursday's derby win was an early marker for the reborn side.

Elsewhere in the same round, Hapoel Katamon Yam produced the biggest scoreline of the night, beating Maccabi Kishronot Hadera 3-0. Smadar Cohen opened the scoring in the 11th minute, and Jaeli da Silva Gomes did the rest, doubling the lead three minutes later and completing her brace in the 76th.

The round also saw Maccabi Holon beat Netanya 4-0 and Hapoel Ra'anana come from behind to beat Kiryat Gat 2-1, ONE reported, with the four matches producing 14 goals between them to open the new Athena Cup campaign.
The competition's second round is scheduled for Tuesday, with Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Katamon Yam both carrying opening-night wins into the next set of fixtures.

title: Youth international Kerem Ashkenazi returns north to sign with Galil Elyon
dek: The 18-year-old guard, capped for Israel's under-18 side at this summer's European Championship, has signed with Hapoel Galil Elyon's senior squad, the club that developed him before the war sent him south to Maccabi Tel Aviv's academy, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: Galil Ole — Ashkenazi's original 2023 signing with Galil Elyon

body: Kerem Ashkenazi is heading home. The 18-year-old guard, who wore Israel's colours at this summer's European Under-18 Championship, has signed with Hapoel Galil Elyon's senior team, ONE reports — a return to the Upper Galilee club that first spotted him as a teenager.

Ashkenazi, from the northern community of Beit Hillel, put pen to paper with Galil Elyon on a long-term deal back in 2023, when he was just 15. The club has built part of its identity around developing homegrown talent from the Upper Galilee, and Ashkenazi was seen as a flagship prospect.

The war changed those plans. With the north disrupted and Beit Hillel among the communities affected, Ashkenazi relocated south and spent last season in Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth academy instead of continuing his development at home.

It was a productive detour. According to ONE, Ashkenazi averaged 8.1 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game for Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth side last season, numbers that helped keep him in the frame for Israel's national youth setup.
That form carried him to this summer's European Under-18 Championship, where he featured for Israel's youth national team as the squad opened its campaign in Trento, Italy.

Now, with conditions in the north settling, Ashkenazi has opted to return to Galil Elyon — this time on a contract with the senior team rather than the youth ranks he left behind. Galil Elyon compete in the Israeli Basketball Premier League, representing the Upper Galilee and Golan communities from their Kfar Blum base.

For a club that has long leaned on local talent, getting back a player of Ashkenazi's pedigree, and doing so on a senior deal, is a statement of intent as much as a squad addition. Neither ONE nor the club has published further comment on his role or expected playing time for the coming season.

body: M.S. Ashdod's youth side made it two wins from two to open the new Israeli Youth Premier League season, hammering Hapoel Jerusalem 5-1 away at the Emek HaArazim pitch on Thursday evening, ONE reports.

Liroy Hanan did the early damage, scoring in the 27th minute and adding a second just before the interval to send the visitors in 2-0 up at the break. Lior Zaken-Givati made it three shortly after the hour, and Mayssara Abu Balal, introduced from the bench, put the game further out of reach soon after.
Yonatan Sorkin pulled a consolation back for the hosts in the 80th minute, but Liam Malka restored Ashdod's five-goal cushion with a strike in the 87th to seal the rout.

It continues a flying start for coach Elad Gavai's group, who needed a stoppage-time winner to edge Hapoel Hadera 2-1 at home in Saturday's opening round. Two wins from two now puts Ashdod provisionally top of the table, according to ONE.
For Hapoel Jerusalem, it was a second straight defeat to begin the campaign, having lost 0-1 to Maccabi Tel Aviv in their own opener on Monday.

"The players showed a lot of character, determination and football, and I'm happy we managed to win," Gavai said afterwards, while cautioning that the perfect start counts for little on its own in a long season.

Ashdod's academy has been on an upward trajectory in recent seasons, and an early statement result on the road in Jerusalem will only sharpen expectations as the Youth Premier League campaign gets under way in earnest.

title: Trabzonspor 0-1 Ferencváros: Kanichowsky's 29-minute cameo helps see out first-leg win
dek: Kristoffer Zachariassen's early header settled the Europa League play-off opener in Turkey, with Gabi Kanichowsky sent on for the closing half hour as Ferencváros defended the lead.

verificationSources.label: VAVEL — Trabzonspor vs Ferencvaros live score

body: Ferencváros left Turkey with a precious away win on Thursday night, beating Trabzonspor 1-0 in the first leg of their UEFA Europa League play-off, with Israeli international Gabi Kanichowsky introduced from the bench to help see the result home.

The only goal came in the 17th minute. Olivér Nagy swung a cross into the box and Kristoffer Zachariassen rose above the Trabzonspor defence to head past goalkeeper André Onana, giving the Hungarian champions the lead they would not surrender.

Kanichowsky, an Israel international who joined Ferencváros from Maccabi Tel Aviv last year, was sent on in the 61st minute in place of Philippe Rommens. He was on the pitch for the final half hour plus stoppage time — roughly 29 minutes, as reported by ONE — as the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

The midfielder picked up a yellow card late on for remonstrating with the referee, which leaves him one caution away from a suspension in the competition. He otherwise helped Ferencváros manage the closing stages as Trabzonspor, with Mohamed Salah and Paul Onuachu leading the home attack, searched for a way back into the tie.

Trabzonspor's best chance of the night fell to Onuachu, whose header from close range came back off the crossbar, but the Turkish side could not find a breakthrough against a well-organised Ferencváros defence marshalled by goalkeeper Dénes Dibusz.

The result gives the Hungarian side a favourable platform heading into next week's return leg at the Groupama Arena in Budapest on 27 August, with a place in this season's Europa League league phase at stake. The loser of the tie drops into the Conference League.

It is the latest step in an eventful first year in Hungary for Kanichowsky, who has featured for Ferencváros in continental competition throughout the summer, including a start in the previous qualifying round against Górnik Zabrze, and remains a regular fixture in Robbie Keane's Ferencváros squad as well as the Israel national team setup.

title: Djokovic: "I refused the Covid vaccine and I paid the price"
dek: In a new Amazon Prime documentary, Novak Djokovic revisits his 2022 Australian deportation and says he has no regrets about standing by his refusal to be vaccinated.

verificationSources.label: Ynet — "סירבתי להתחסן נגד הקורונה ושילמתי את המחיר": ג'וקוביץ' פותח הכל
About Amazon — everything to know about "Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter"
Amazon MGM Studios press site — Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter

body: Novak Djokovic has used the release of his own Amazon Prime documentary to revisit the most polarising stretch of his career, saying flatly that he knew the cost of refusing the Covid-19 vaccine and has made peace with paying it.

"I never said I'm for or against vaccines. I stood by what I believe in — the freedom to choose what enters my body," Djokovic says in the film. "I lost Grand Slams and didn't play in the USA for years because of this. It's okay, I paid the price."

The remarks come from "Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter," a 92-minute feature directed by Jason Hehir — the filmmaker behind Michael Jordan's "The Last Dance" — which premiered worldwide on Prime Video on Thursday, 20 August.

The documentary devotes a significant chunk of its runtime to the saga that defined Djokovic's 2022: his deportation from Australia on the eve of the Australian Open after his vaccine exemption was challenged and his visa revoked, a saga that also cost him entry to the United States and, with it, the US Open and other American tournaments for an extended period.

Djokovic has told the story before, but rarely with the same tone of resignation. Speaking to the BBC in the past he insisted, "I was never against vaccination but I've always supported the freedom to choose what you put in your body," a line that echoes almost word for word what he says in the new film.

The documentary features interviews with, among others, Rafael Nadal, Andre Agassi, Pete Sampras, Boris Becker and Jim Courier, alongside Djokovic's wife Jelena and members of his family, offering what the production describes as unprecedented access to a player who has often kept the press at arm's length on the subject.

Djokovic, now 39, used the same conversation to push back on any suggestion that his career is winding down. "Why would you want me to retire when I'm still competing at the highest level? I'm still top five in the world," he said, pointing to a run of six semi-final-or-better finishes in his last seven Grand Slam appearances.

The film does not shy away from the messier details of the episode — including the backlash after Djokovic was found to have breached isolation rules following his positive Covid test in December 2021, and the scrutiny over an interview he gave shortly afterward. But its central thread, in Djokovic's own words, is that he weighed the cost of his stance against his principles and chose the latter, tournament results included.

Three and a half years on from the Melbourne deportation, Djokovic remains one of the sport's dominant figures, still ranked inside the world's top five and still chasing majors as he heads toward the end of a career that has already delivered 24 Grand Slam singles titles.

title: Sex-for-favours scandal engulfs South Korea's football federation
dek: A decade-old government report, buried for years, reveals the Korea Football Association paid for escorts and massage-parlour visits for visiting referees around 2011-2012 — and the fallout is now spreading through Asian and Japanese football.
body: A scandal that has been simmering in Seoul for a fortnight is now rippling well beyond South Korea's borders, after Ynet picked up reporting on a government audit accusing the Korea Football Association (KFA) of buying sexual services for foreign referees more than a decade ago.

According to the reports, cited by Ynet and corroborated by CNN and South Korean outlets, the KFA arranged and paid for visits to massage parlours and escort services for visiting match officials on at least eight occasions between 2011 and 2012, a period covering World Cup and Olympic qualifying fixtures. The bills, filed under vague or false headings such as "drinks" or standard massages, totalled close to 5.6 million won — roughly $3,950.

The practice first surfaced in a 2016 audit by South Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, but the findings sat unpublished for nearly a decade until the broadcaster JTBC exposed them earlier this month. Prosecutors had in fact reviewed the credit-card evidence back in 2017 and decided against pursuing charges, citing insufficient grounds.

Ynet's report — under the headline "Mini bribes for referees, lies and cover-up: the scandal rocking South Korea" — frames the affair as part of a wider reckoning for the KFA, which is also facing a parliamentary inquiry and a police raid tied to the 2024 hiring of former national-team coach Hong Myung-bo.

Hong, now in charge of the senior side, was summoned to a National Assembly hearing on July 30 over his salary and the process that led to his appointment — a separate governance row that has kept the federation under sustained public and political pressure through South Korea's underwhelming 2026 World Cup campaign.

The referee affair has since spread beyond South Korea. The Japan Football Association has confirmed it is investigating four Japanese officials alleged to be among the referees who received the benefits, drawing the story into the wider Asian football community just as continental qualifying business resumes.

In one incident detailed in the audit and widely reported since, four match officials who had overseen a fixture against Oman were taken by KFA staff to a massage parlour, with the association spending 760,000 won (about $536) on the visit alone.

The KFA issued a public apology over the weekend, saying it "deeply apologises for the concern caused," while stopping short of directly disputing the specific findings. The federation says the practices ended in 2013 after it introduced a "clean card" expense system and hired dedicated liaison staff to manage relations with visiting officials.

Under South Korean law, prostitution is illegal, and commentators have noted a 15-year statute of limitations could still theoretically apply to some of the conduct described, though no fresh criminal case has been announced.

title: Israel's next swimming star isn't slowing down: 'I'm aiming as high as I can'
dek: Tomer Shuster, 22, broke two Israeli backstroke records and reached his first major final at the European Championships in Paris — and after nearly walking away from the sport at 18, he insists this is only the beginning.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — Men's 50m backstroke, 2026 European Aquatics Championships

body: Eighteen months ago, Tomer Shuster was close to walking away from swimming altogether. Last week in Paris, the 22-year-old from the moshav of Talmei Yaffe in Israel's south produced the two biggest swims of his career, breaking a pair of Israeli backstroke records that had stood for the better part of a decade and reaching his first major international final.

Racing the 50 metres backstroke at the European Aquatics Championships, Shuster clocked 24.62 in the preliminaries — a personal best that also locked in his spot at next year's World Championships — before going faster again in the semifinal, touching in 24.36 to erase Jonathan Kopelev's Israeli record of 24.60, a mark that had stood since 2016.

That swim carried him into his first-ever European Championships final, where he finished fifth in 24.44, agonisingly close to the podium in a race won by the Czech Republic's Miroslav Knedla in 24.11.

Days later he broke a second national record, going 53.39 in the 100m backstroke — confirming, alongside the 50m final, that Shuster is now the standard-bearer for a new generation of Israeli backstroke swimmers.

It very nearly didn't happen this way. At 18, feeling he had stalled, Shuster came close to quitting the sport for good. What changed his mind, he told Ynet, was a swim of 57.16 seconds in the 100m backstroke at a competition at the Wingate Institute — a time that earned him recognition as an outstanding athlete during his military service and, with it, the space to keep training seriously rather than walk away.

The war that followed the October 7 attacks reshaped his path again. Shuster relocated to train with coach Yael Ashkenazi's squad at Maccabi Rishon LeZion, having come up through the Negev Swimmers programme under Amir "Fish" Cohen, and built his career largely on his own terms — turning down a conventional university track and working as a lifeguard to support himself financially along the way.

Even this year's build-up to Paris was not straightforward. A cliff-jumping accident left him with a fractured metatarsal and three dislocated toes, an injury serious enough to threaten his season — yet he recovered in time to compete at the World Championships in Singapore weeks later.

"I always strive to reach the highest level, and where do you do that? On the international stage," Shuster said, describing the mentality that has taken him from a near-retirement at 18 to a European final at 22.
Of the records themselves, he was characteristically matter-of-fact: "I've given everything my whole life, including in the record-breaking performances."

He is refusing to treat Paris as a peak. Shuster is already targeting next year's World Championships in Budapest, and beyond that has one eye on qualifying for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics — the goal that has quietly driven him since he almost gave up the sport four years ago.
For a swimmer who once wondered whether he had gone as far as he could, the message from Paris was unambiguous: he is only getting started.

title: The serial injury victim and the most unlikely gold in Olympic history
dek: Steven Bradbury nearly bled to death on the ice in 1994 and broke his neck in 2000. Two years later, in Salt Lake City, he became the first Southern Hemisphere athlete to win a Winter Olympic gold — without throwing a single punch for the line.

verificationSources.label: Olympics.com — Steven Bradbury, Australia's last man standing
Wikipedia — Short-track speed skating at the 2002 Winter Olympics, Men's 1000m

body: Some Olympic gold medals are won in a photo finish. Steven Bradbury's was won by standing still while everyone around him fell down — and it came after two accidents that, by any normal medical logic, should have ended his career long before he ever reached Salt Lake City.

Bradbury was a short-track speed skater from Brisbane, part of an Australian team with no serious Winter Olympic pedigree, when disaster first struck in 1994. In a World Cup race in Montreal, a rival's blade sliced through all four quadriceps muscles in his right thigh. He lost around four litres of blood in under a minute, needed well over a hundred stitches, and by his own account nearly died on the ice. Recovery took roughly a year and a half.

He fought his way back. Then, in September 2000, another skater fell in front of him during a training session; Bradbury tried to jump the fallen man, clipped him instead, and went head-first into the barriers. He fractured three vertebrae in his neck and needed a halo brace bolted into his skull to stabilise his spine while it healed. Doctors told him his career was over.

Bradbury didn't accept that verdict. He rebuilt himself again, made Australia's team for a fourth Olympics, and arrived in Salt Lake City in February 2002 as anything but a medal favourite — more a veteran making up the numbers in a field built around younger, faster skaters.

The men's 1,000m field for that Olympics included Apolo Anton Ohno of the United States, already being talked up as the sport's next big star, South Korea's Ahn Hyun-soo, China's Li Jiajun and Canada's Mathieu Turcotte. Bradbury advanced through his heats in unglamorous but effective fashion — in one earlier round he progressed only after a disqualification ahead of him, a pattern that would repeat in the final in far more dramatic form.

In the final itself, Bradbury settled in at the back of the pack, trailing the leaders by a wide margin as the race approached its closing metres. Short-track racing at that distance is chaotic by nature — skaters bunched together at speed, jostling for position on tight turns — and with roughly 50 metres to go, the chaos consumed the leaders. Ohno, Ahn, Li and Turcotte all went down together in a pile-up on the final turn.

Bradbury, so far behind that he was clear of the collision, simply skated through the wreckage and crossed the line first. He did not need to sprint, overtake or fight for the position — he was already in it by the time the leaders hit the ice.

It made him the first Winter Olympic gold medallist in Australian history, and the first ever from the Southern Hemisphere. Ohno recovered to take silver despite a cut sustained in the fall; Turcotte claimed bronze.

The manner of the win turned Bradbury into a global talking point rather than a forgotten also-ran. "I know I didn't win it fair and square, in the sense that I was the fastest skater," he said afterwards, framing the victory as the product of persistence through years of setbacks rather than a fluke of one race — a case he had earned the right to make given what it took just to be standing on the ice.

The moment outlived the Games themselves. "Doing a Bradbury" entered Australian vernacular, and was formally added to the Macquarie Dictionary in 2016, defined as achieving an unexpected or seemingly underserved success through the failure of others rather than one's own brilliance.

Two decades on, the race remains one of the most replayed clips in Winter Olympic history — not because of the skating, but because it captures, more starkly than almost any other sporting moment, how a career built on repeated physical catastrophe produced the most improbable gold medal the Games had seen.

In 1994, a rival skater's blade cut through all four quadriceps muscles in his thigh during a World Cup race in Montreal; he lost roughly four litres of blood and needed about 18 months to recover.
In September 2000, a training-session collision fractured vertebrae in his neck; he needed a halo brace with skull-mounted bolts, and doctors advised him against returning to the sport.

In the 2002 final, leaders Apolo Anton Ohno (USA), Ahn Hyun-soo (South Korea), Li Jiajun (China) and Mathieu Turcotte (Canada) crashed out together near the finish, allowing Bradbury — well behind the pack — to cross the line first.
It was the first Winter Olympic gold medal in Australian history and the first for any Southern Hemisphere athlete.
The phrase "doing a Bradbury" was added to the Macquarie Dictionary in 2016.

title: Meir Buhbut leaves Bnei Reineh for Hapoel Beit She'an
dek: The 21-year-old forward, who scored 43 youth-league goals two seasons ago but never featured for Bnei Reineh's first team, joins Liga Alef North side Hapoel Beit She'an as his fourth senior club.
body: Meir Buhbut, a 21-year-old forward who spent the past three-plus seasons on Maccabi Bnei Reineh's books, has signed with Hapoel Beit She'an, ONE reported.

It is a significant drop down the pyramid. Bnei Reineh have been playing in Ligat Ha'al, Israel's top flight, while Beit She'an compete in Liga Alef North, the third tier — but for Buhbut it is a chance at regular senior football that never materialised at his previous club.

He joined Bnei Reineh's academy in December 2022 and quickly stood out at youth level, scoring 43 goals for the club's Under-19 side in the 2023/24 season along with a cup goal — numbers that made him one of the more talked-about young forwards in the country's youth game.

A loan spell in 2024/25, split between Liga Alef and Liga Bet North, brought seven further league goals as he got his first taste of adult football. Back at Bnei Reineh last season, he was included in the senior squad but made only three appearances, all in the Toto Cup, without ever getting on the scoresheet or featuring in the league.

According to ONE, Buhbut comes from a Haredi family of ten children and took up organised football relatively late, joining Hatzor's academy at 13 and a half before later football stops in Tiberias on his way to Bnei Reineh.

Hapoel Beit She'an will be his fourth senior club. He arrives under head coach Guy Dayan as the club prepares for a season that opens with an Israel Cup fifth-round tie at home to MS Tira on August 28, ahead of the Liga Alef North campaign kicking off on September 4.

For a club at that level, landing a forward with Buhbut's youth scoring record is a notable pickup, and Beit She'an will hope regular first-team minutes can unlock the finishing form he showed in the junior ranks.

title: Ziv Arieh: the decision to join Maccabi Petah Tikva was easy
dek: Maccabi Petah Tikva's new head coach previewed Saturday's Ligat Ha'al opener against Ironi Kiryat Shmona, with defender Aviv Salem describing a squad still searching for stability.

verificationSources.label: ONE – original report and press conference quotes

body: Ziv Arieh used his first press conference as Maccabi Petah Tikva head coach to frame Saturday's Ligat Ha'al season opener against Ironi Kiryat Shmona as a straightforward step, telling reporters the move to the club had never felt complicated.
"The decision to come was easy — once I left Hapoel Jerusalem, this option came along," Arieh said, according to ONE. "I see good players here and I believe in the squad."

Arieh's appointment in late May capped a swift return to the touchline. He had spent close to seven years in charge of Hapoel Jerusalem, guiding the capital club up into Ligat Ha'al and leaving this spring as the longest-serving coach in the team's modern history before Petah Tikva moved to bring him in.

He now inherits a Maccabi Petah Tikva side that is itself back among Israel's elite after winning promotion from Liga Leumit, and Arieh was careful on Friday not to get ahead of himself about what the season could bring.

Rather than talk up distant targets, he kept the focus tight on Saturday's 8pm kickoff, acknowledging Kiryat Shmona as a worthy opponent while insisting his own group is capable of competing from the first whistle even as it is still bedding in.

Speaking alongside him, defender Aviv Salem struck a similarly measured tone, describing a Maccabi Petah Tikva squad that is "going through a process" to find its footing. "We are undergoing a process to become stable," he said.

Salem, who joined the club during the January transfer window after a spell at Hapoel Tel Aviv that did not work out, pointed to a group mixing younger players with squad members carrying experience from the lower divisions — part of the rebuild Petah Tikva has undertaken since sealing its promotion.

For Arieh, Saturday's trip against Kiryat Shmona doubles as the first real test of that project, with a new coach and a newly promoted roster both looking to show, from round one, that last season's climb back to Ligat Ha'al was no fluke.

title: Disasi agrees Crystal Palace loan as Parrott completes Real Betis move
dek: Chelsea's Axel Disasi is closing in on a season-long loan to Crystal Palace, while Ireland forward Troy Parrott has sealed a switch from AZ Alkmaar to Real Betis in a deal worth up to €20m.
body: Two pieces of late-summer transfer business moved into their closing stages on Thursday, with Chelsea centre-back Axel Disasi set for a loan switch to Crystal Palace and Ireland forward Troy Parrott completing a move from AZ Alkmaar to Real Betis, ONE reports.

Disasi's deal to Selhurst Park is a paid loan for the 2026/27 season with no option to buy, according to reporting from RMC Sport and transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano that ONE's report drew on. Palace will pay Chelsea a loan fee and cover the 28-year-old Frenchman's wages for the duration of his stay.

The France international has been frozen out at Stamford Bridge since being left out of Enzo Maresca's plans in January 2025, and has already had loan spells away at Aston Villa and West Ham United since then. A permanent Chelsea exit has not materialised, but another temporary switch looks set to take him to south London instead.

Palace's interest is tied to their thinning centre-back options after Marc Guehi departed for Manchester City and Maxence Lacroix left in the opposite direction to Chelsea this summer. Disasi was reported to be undergoing a medical as talks over personal terms were finalised, with the move still short of an official announcement from either club at the time of writing.
In Spain, Real Betis have confirmed rather cleaner business. Troy Parrott's transfer from AZ Alkmaar has been completed, RTE reported, with the Irish forward signing a contract that runs until 2031.
The fee is reported at roughly €16m, with add-ons that could push the total value of the deal toward €20m as Parrott's stock has risen sharply over the past year in the Netherlands.

Spanish outlets covering the deal have suggested Parrott's own insistence on playing Champions League football pushed AZ into lowering their initial valuation, clearing the way for Betis — who qualified for Europe's top continental competition last season — to get their man.

Parrott has become a regular for the Republic of Ireland under Heimir Hallgrimsson and heads to La Liga with his career trending sharply upward after a difficult run of injuries and false starts earlier in his development at Tottenham.
Both deals fit into a European transfer window edging toward its September 1 deadline, with clubs across the Premier League and La Liga still shuffling their squads before the new season settles in.

title: Hapoel Nir Ramat Hasharon 2-1 Maccabi Ironi Ashdod (aet): coach hails patched-up side's heart in State Cup
dek: Assi Elimelech fielded five youth players after 16 senior squad members were ruled out over incomplete medical checks, but his makeshift Hapoel Nir Ramat Hasharon side still ground out an extra-time win to set up a State Cup tie with F.C. Jerusalem.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia - Hapoel Nir Ramat HaSharon F.C.

body: It was billed as a straightforward State Cup opener, but Hapoel Nir Ramat Hasharon had to survive extra time and a squad crisis to get past Maccabi Ironi Ashdod, winning 2-1 to reach the competition's fifth round.

Coach Assi Elimelech revealed afterwards that the club had gone into the match with barely half a team available. Only nine players had completed the medical clearance required to play, he said, and two of those were themselves carrying injuries.

With 16 members of the senior squad unable to take part because their medical checks had not been finalised, Elimelech was forced to throw five youth-team players into the lineup to make up the numbers.

"I take the big heart they showed, though there's not much to learn from this match, since the players who should play weren't actually playing," Elimelech said, according to ONE — a wry summary of a night where the result mattered more than the performance.

Despite the makeshift XI, he insisted his side had still controlled the tie and looked the more threatening team, with Ashdod managing few clear chances of their own across the 120 minutes before Nir Ramat Hasharon's extra-time winner settled it.
The win sends the club through to a home fifth-round tie against F.C. Jerusalem, another Liga Alef South outfit, in the next stage of the State Cup.

The result comes in the second season since Nir Ramat Hasharon's relegation from Liga Leumit in the summer of 2025. The club was bought in January 2026 by film producer Yoav Gross and a group of fellow businessmen, who have made a swift return to the national league their stated goal.
For now, though, Elimelech's more immediate problem is straightforward: getting his suspended and unregistered players through the paperwork before medical clearance stops being an excuse.

title: Sage says Crystal Palace happy to keep Muñoz despite Khalaili and Mingueza arrivals
dek: The new Crystal Palace manager addressed speculation over Daniel Muñoz's future on the eve of the season opener at Everton, as Anan Khalaili prepares to fight for a place on the right flank.
body: Pierre Sage used his first pre-match press conference as Crystal Palace manager to knock down talk that Daniel Muñoz is on his way out of Selhurst Park, just as the club's newest Israeli signing, Anan Khalaili, prepares to compete with the Colombian for the same shirt.

Palace open their Premier League season at Everton on Saturday at 17:00, and Sage was asked directly whether Muñoz's position was under threat now that the club has brought in both Khalaili and the Spanish full-back Oscar Mingueza this summer.

"We currently have four defensive players who can play there, three of them with a dominant right foot and only one left-footed," Sage said, according to ONE. "Regarding Muñoz, I've heard a lot of reports like you mentioned, but he is happy to be with us and we are happy he is here."

The remark was as much a message to the dressing room as to reporters. Muñoz has been strongly linked with a move all summer after an outstanding World Cup with Colombia, with reports in the English press this month naming Everton, Tottenham and even Barcelona and Chelsea among his suitors, and Palace said to have set an asking price in the region of £25 million.

For now, Sage's line is that the 28-year-old stays and simply has more competition than before. Khalaili, who signed from Royale Union Saint-Gilloise this month in a deal reported at roughly £21 million, the most expensive transfer for an Israeli player in history, arrives with his path to Palace only cleared after a proposed move to Inter Milan collapsed at the medical stage.

Mingueza, a free-transfer arrival from Celta Vigo and Sage's first signing since taking over from Oliver Glasner, adds a further option who can operate on the right side of defence, deepening the queue Khalaili will have to navigate for a starting berth.

Sage's comments suggest Khalaili is likely to begin life in south London fighting for minutes rather than walking straight into the XI, with Muñoz still very much first choice in the manager's eyes heading into Saturday's trip to Merseyside.

Nothing in Sage's answer closed the door on a Muñoz departure before the transfer window shuts, but for the moment the message from the Palace dugout is one of stability at right wing-back, even with an Israeli record signing waiting in the wings.

title: Dolgopyat wins third European floor title with 14.466 in Zagreb
dek: The Tokyo Olympic champion topped the podium again on floor exercise as Israel's men's team also secured its place at October's World Championships.

verificationSources.label: ONE — 'בפעם ה-3 בקריירה: דולגופיאט אלוף אירופה בקרקע'

Davar1 — נבחרת ישראל בהתעמלות מכשירים השיגה את הקריטריון לאליפות העולם

body: Artem Dolgopyat is a European champion again. The Tokyo Olympic gold medallist won the men's floor exercise final at the European Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Zagreb on Friday, scoring 14.466 to take the title for the third time in his career.

It completes a run that stretches back six years: Dolgopyat first won European floor gold in 2020 in Mersin, defended it in 2022 in Munich, and has now added a third in Croatia — a level of consistency almost no one else in his event has matched over that stretch.

Silver went to Arsenii Dukhno, competing as a neutral gymnast, with 14.333, while Britain's Harry Hepworth took bronze on 14.300. Dolgopyat had gone into the final as the form pick, having topped his qualifying subdivision with 14.766 to sit second overall heading into Friday's showdown.

The gold is his eighth European Championships medal in total — three gold, four silver and a bronze — a haul built entirely on floor exercise and vault since his senior debut for Israel, and one that puts him among the most decorated gymnasts the continent has produced this decade.

It sits alongside a resume that already includes Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021, Olympic silver in Paris last year, and a world title won in Antwerp in 2023, with two further world silvers from 2017 and 2019. At 29, and with a Los Angeles Olympic cycle now underway, Friday's win is a reminder he remains the man to beat on the apparatus.

The result carries extra weight for Israeli gymnastics beyond Dolgopyat's own medal count. Israel's men finished 10th in the team qualification round in Zagreb with a combined 238.659 points, enough to book the squad's place at the World Championships in October — a significant marker for a program built around a handful of senior gymnasts.

Dolgopyat was not the only Israeli to reach an individual final in Zagreb. Ron Piatov also advanced, qualifying eighth for the parallel bars final with a score of 13.966, giving Israel two apparatus finalists at a single European Championships.

Dolgopyat, born in Dnipro, Ukraine, moved to Israel with his family at 12 and settled in Rishon LeZion, where he still trains and competes for Maccabi Tel Aviv. Fourteen years on from that move, Zagreb was simply the latest stop on a career that has repeatedly delivered on the biggest stages — and shows no sign of slowing down.

title: Argentina to appeal FIFA bans handed down over World Cup final brawl
dek: The AFA says it will challenge FIFA's disciplinary rulings, including a ten-match suspension for Leandro Paredes, after ugly scenes at the final whistle of the 2026 World Cup final against Spain.
body: The Argentine Football Association has confirmed it will formally appeal the string of suspensions and fines FIFA handed down over the brawl that erupted at the final whistle of the World Cup final against Spain, and is keeping the Court of Arbitration for Sport in reserve as a last resort.

Spain won the July 19 final 1-0 after extra time, but the aftermath turned ugly as players from both squads clashed on the pitch once Spanish substitutes and staff poured on to celebrate. FIFA opened a disciplinary case within days and has now issued its rulings.

Leandro Paredes was hit hardest. Argentina's midfielder was suspended for ten international matches and fined $90,000 after footage showed him grabbing Spain defender Eric Garcia by the throat before wrestling Gavi to the ground.

Given the density of the FIFA international calendar, a ten-match ban amounts to roughly a year on the sidelines for the national team, with Paredes not due to be available again until well into 2027.

Right-back Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven matches and fined $90,000 after being cited in two separate incidents, while forward Thiago Almada received a one-match ban and a $30,000 fine for unsporting conduct. Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala was also banned for three matches and fined $30,000.

Spain did not escape FIFA's attention either. Gavi was hit with a one-match suspension and a $30,000 fine for his part in the confrontation, though the bulk of the sanctions fell on the Argentine camp.

The AFA itself was fined a combined $321,000 for a raft of tournament violations, among them a "Las Malvinas son argentinas" banner referencing the Falkland Islands, discriminatory chanting from sections of the crowd and objects thrown onto the pitch. FIFA has also ordered that Argentina's next home fixture be played with the stadium half-empty.

In a statement, the AFA said its legal department would move quickly to request FIFA's full grounds for each ruling so it can lodge formal appeals with the governing body's appeal committee, while explicitly reserving "the future option of appealing to the CAS as a final recourse."

None of the bans affect club football, so Paredes, Molina and Almada remain available for their respective sides. The dispute is squarely about Argentina's national team schedule, and the outcome of any appeal will determine how much of the world champions' immediate post-World Cup era Paredes actually gets to play.
facts: FIFA issued disciplinary rulings against Argentina players and staff over their conduct after the final whistle of the July 19, 2026 World Cup final, which Spain won 1-0 after extra time.
Leandro Paredes received the heaviest sanction: a ten-match international ban and a $90,000 fine, after grabbing Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestling Gavi to the ground.
Nahuel Molina was banned for seven matches and fined $90,000; Thiago Almada was banned for one match and fined $30,000.
Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala was suspended for three matches and fined $30,000; Spain's Gavi was suspended one match and fined $30,000.

FIFA fined the AFA $321,000 in total for violations including a Falkland Islands-referencing banner, discriminatory chanting and objects thrown on the pitch, and ordered a 50% stadium closure for Argentina's next home match.
The AFA said it will request FIFA's grounds for the rulings before filing appeals with FIFA's appeal committee, while reserving the option of escalating to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Maccabi Petah Tikva 3-1 in Youth Premier League
dek: Two goals either side of half-time and a Roy Gafni penalty send the defending youth champions to six points from six as Petah Tikva's late rally falls short.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv FC — youth department squad list

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth side served early notice of its title intentions, beating Maccabi Petah Tikva 3-1 away on Friday to move to six points from two rounds at the start of the 2026/27 Youth Premier League season, ONE reported.

The defending champions took control before the break with two goals in the space of three minutes. Ido Yosef put Tel Aviv ahead in the 38th minute, and Itay Mehaager doubled the lead three minutes later to send the visitors in 2-0 up at half-time.
Petah Tikva pulled one back midway through the second half when Liam Weinstein converted in the 67th minute, giving the home side hope of a way back into the contest.
Any nerves were settled in the 75th minute, when Roy Gafni stepped up to convert a penalty and restore Tel Aviv's two-goal cushion, closing out the scoring at 3-1.

Coach Dan Roman was candid in his assessment afterwards, saying he was satisfied with the first-half performance but "very unsatisfied" with how his side played after the break, adding that he would rather fix such issues "when you're winning."

Roman singled out goalkeeper Eidan Traou for praise following a strong second-half display between the posts, saying the player — in his third year in the youth ranks — gives the team "a lot of confidence" and delivered exactly what is expected of him.

The result keeps Tel Aviv perfect through two rounds as they bid to defend last season's title. They host Hapoel Kiryat Shmona next, while Petah Tikva travel to face M.S. Ashdod looking for a first win of the campaign.

title: UEFA fines Hapoel Beer Sheva, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv nearly €48,000 combined
dek: Beer Sheva absorbs more than half the total over three separate Champions League qualifiers, with Beitar and Hapoel Tel Aviv also sanctioned for spectator conduct in Europe.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com - Víkingur R. vs H. Beer-Sheva

body: UEFA has handed down a combined €47,575 in fines against three Israeli clubs — Hapoel Beer Sheva, Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv — over spectator-related incidents during this summer's European qualifying rounds, ONE reported.

Hapoel Beer Sheva took by far the heaviest hit, fined €24,250 across three separate fixtures in Champions League qualifying. UEFA imposed €6,000 for the home leg against Víkingur Reykjavík, €10,000 — the single largest individual penalty of the round — for the home tie against Red Star Belgrade, and a further €8,250 for the away leg in Serbia.

Beer Sheva swept past Víkingur to reach the third qualifying round and then got the better of Red Star Belgrade to stay alive in the Champions League picture, progress that has come bundled with a growing disciplinary bill from UEFA.
Beitar Jerusalem were fined €18,325, the second-heaviest sanction of the three, stemming from their Conference League qualifying tie away to AEK Larnaca in Cyprus.

Hapoel Tel Aviv drew the lightest penalty, €5,000, tied to their home leg against Poland's GKS Katowice in Conference League qualifying — still a reminder that no Israeli club in Europe this summer has come through fan-conduct scrutiny unscathed.

ONE did not detail the specific nature of each incident beyond spectator conduct, but the fines fit a familiar pattern: Israeli clubs have repeatedly been sanctioned by UEFA's disciplinary body in recent European campaigns over issues in the stands, from pyrotechnics to other supporter behaviour.

With three different Israeli sides now carrying fresh marks on their UEFA disciplinary record inside a single qualifying window, the cumulative €47,575 underlines how quickly those penalties can add up as more clubs advance further into Europe's club competitions.

title: Arsenal beat Coventry City 3-0 to open Premier League title defence
dek: Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard scored as the champions brushed aside newly-promoted Coventry at the Emirates.
body: Arsenal wasted no time reminding the Premier League who is champion. Mikel Arteta's side opened the defence of their title with a comprehensive 3-0 win over newly-promoted Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium on Friday night, and the contest was effectively over before half-time.

Kai Havertz broke the deadlock in the 15th minute, converting after Riccardo Calafiori won the ball back high up the pitch and set up the chance. Bukayo Saka doubled the lead eight minutes later, pouncing after Coventry goalkeeper diverted a low cross into his path.

Martin Ødegaard put the result beyond doubt just four minutes into the second half, sweeping home Arsenal's third with the game barely restarted. It was a ruthless opening statement from a side determined to show last season's title was no one-off.

Frank Lampard's Coventry, playing their first top-flight match in decades after promotion, never got a foothold. According to Opta data cited by Sky Sports, the visitors failed to register a single touch in the Arsenal penalty area or make a tackle in the entire first half — the first team to suffer that indignity in a Premier League match since records of the kind began in 2007.

Arteta made changes in the closing stages, withdrawing Saka and Declan Rice around the 68th minute with the game long since settled, a sign of a manager already managing his squad's legs with a long campaign ahead.

It was as routine a start to a title defence as any manager could hope for — control from the first whistle, three different goalscorers, and a clean sheet to boot. For Coventry, the size of the gap between the Championship and the Premier League was laid bare on their return to the top flight.

title: Real Betis open La Liga season with 1-0 win over Real Sociedad
dek: Rodrigo Riquelme's second-half finish settled a tight opener at the Cartuja, with Álvaro Vallés denying Real Sociedad late on to preserve Manuel Pellegrini's clean sheet.
body: Real Betis began the 2026-27 La Liga season the way Manuel Pellegrini would have drawn it up: grinding out a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad at the Estadio de la Cartuja on Friday, despite spending long stretches of the second half under siege.

The breakthrough came on 63 minutes. Cucho Hernández, played in down the right in a move started by Antony, drilled a low cross into the box, and Rodrigo Riquelme arrived to finish first time from close range, giving Betis a lead they would not relinquish.

The first half had been largely a stalemate, with Betis controlling territory but Real Sociedad's defence holding firm without conceding a clear chance. Álex Remiro was rarely troubled before the break.

That changed once Betis went ahead. La Real threw men forward in search of an equaliser, and by full time had actually out-created the hosts on expected goals, 1.58 to 1.06, according to Sofascore's data.

Remiro kept his side in it at the other end too, pushing away a stinging effort from Isco among several second-half saves. But it was Betis goalkeeper Álvaro Vallés who had the last word, producing what Flashscore described as a sensational late stop to deny Orri Oskarsson and secure the points.
Pablo Fornals was named man of the match for his work shielding Betis's back line as the visitors poured forward in the closing stages.

The result extends an already lopsided recent history between the sides — Betis have lost only twice in their last 14 meetings with Real Sociedad — and leaves the Basque club still without an away win in their last seven La Liga trips.

For Pellegrini, now well into his sixth season at the helm, it is exactly the kind of opening-day result that sets a tone: unconvincing for large periods, but built on game management and goalkeeping when it mattered most.

title: Paris, 13 May 2001: The Only Year Europe Crowned Two Champions
dek: In the single season European basketball split in two, Pini Gershon's Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Panathinaikos 81–67 in the Bercy arena to win the rebel FIBA SuproLeague — ending a twenty-year wait for a continental crown, on a night the club had to share the title of "champion of Europe" with a team it never played.

verificationSources.label: The Jerusalem Post — Nate Huffman, star basketball player for Maccabi Tel Aviv, dies at 40
The Times of Israel — Maccabi Tel Aviv legend Nate Huffman dies at 40

body: On the afternoon of 13 May 2001, inside the sloped glass-and-steel pyramid of the Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy, Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Panathinaikos 81–67 to become champions of Europe for the third time. It should have been a simple, glorious sentence. It wasn't quite that simple, because for one strange season, European basketball had two champions of Europe at once — and Maccabi's rivals in Barcelona and Bologna would have argued the "real" one was crowned somewhere else entirely.

The story begins in July 2000, when a breakaway group of clubs, backed by television money and organisational ambition, founded a new body called Euroleague Basketball and launched their own competition outside FIBA's control. FIBA had never trademarked the name "EuroLeague" and had no way to stop the new venture using it. So FIBA rebranded its own long-running top competition — the one Maccabi had already won in 1977 and 1981 — as the FIBA SuproLeague. Clubs had to choose a side. Real Madrid and Barcelona went with the new Euroleague. Maccabi Tel Aviv, along with Panathinaikos, CSKA Moscow and Efes Pilsen, stayed loyal to FIBA.

It meant that for the 2000–01 season, and that season only, European basketball crowned two separate, rival champions from two separate top-tier competitions. Kinder Bologna won the breakaway Euroleague. Maccabi Tel Aviv won FIBA's SuproLeague. Neither side played the other. Both, technically, could call themselves champions of Europe.

Maccabi arrived in Paris under Pini Gershon, the coach who had taken over the club in 1998 and rebuilt it around a mix of hardened Israeli internationals and imported American talent. Nadav Henefeld, once an NCAA Freshman of the Year at Connecticut, captained a team built around point guard Ariel McDonald, wing Anthony Parker, forward Tal Burstein and the physical, relentless American centre Nate Huffman, with Derrick Sharp, Gur Shelef, Radisav Ćurčić and David Sternlight filling out the rotation.

In the semifinal on 11 May, Maccabi survived a tense contest with CSKA Moscow, winning 86–80 to set up a final against a Panathinaikos side that, a year earlier in Tel Aviv, had lifted the very same trophy. This time there would be no repeat. Maccabi controlled the final from early on, pulling away in the second half to win 81–67 in front of a crowd inside the Bercy that had, fittingly, watched the club's coronation before — Maccabi had beaten Real Madrid in that same arena to win its first European title back in 1977, under Ralph Klein.

Huffman was immense in the final, finishing with 21 points and nine rebounds, numbers in keeping with a playoff run in which he averaged 17.5 points and nine boards a game; his performances across the season won him both the Israeli league MVP award and, from the SuproLeague itself, Player of the Year. It was Ariel McDonald, though, who was named Final Four MVP, his composure at the point guiding Maccabi through both the semifinal grind and the final's decisive stretches.

For Gershon and his players, the trophy meant more than another line in the club's record book. Maccabi had been champions of Europe in 1977 and again in 1981, under Klein, in a golden era built around Tal Brody and Miki Berkovich. After 1981, two decades passed without another continental title, through coaching changes, near-misses and heartbreaks. Paris in 2001 ended that wait — Maccabi's third European crown, and its first in twenty years.

It also turned out to be a historical curiosity in its own right. The FIBA/ULEB split lasted only that one season; from 2001–02 onward, the two rival competitions merged back into a single, unified Euroleague, the format that has run ever since. That made Maccabi's 81–67 win over Panathinaikos the last continental club title FIBA Europe would ever organise on its own — a trophy from a competition that, by the following autumn, no longer existed under that name.

Gershon's Maccabi did not stop there: the same coach would lead the club to two more European titles in 2004 and 2005, cementing a run that turned the Yad Eliyahu-based club into one of the sport's dynasties. But Paris 2001 was the hinge — proof, after twenty lean years, that the club built by Klein and Brody could still be built again.

Nate Huffman stayed on with Maccabi through 2002, later playing in Italy and Israel again before retiring, and remained a beloved figure in Tel Aviv, running youth basketball camps with former Maccabi player Constantin Popa. He died in October 2015, aged 40, of bladder cancer, at his family home in Battle Creek, Michigan — a reminder, a decade and a half after Bercy, of how briefly and brightly that Maccabi team burned.

In the semifinal on 11 May 2001, Maccabi beat CSKA Moscow 86–80 to reach the final.

The 2000–01 season was the only season in which European club basketball had two rival top-tier champions: FIBA's SuproLeague (won by Maccabi Tel Aviv) and the breakaway ULEB Euroleague (won by Kinder Bologna), after Euroleague Basketball split from FIBA in July 2000.
Ariel McDonald was named Final Four MVP; Nate Huffman, the SuproLeague's Player of the Year, scored 21 points with 9 rebounds in the final.

Head coach Pini Gershon's roster included Ariel McDonald, Anthony Parker, Nadav Henefeld (captain), Tal Burstein, Nate Huffman, Derrick Sharp, Gur Shelef, Radisav Ćurčić and David Sternlight.

title: Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City: Ødegaard says champions want to attack the title, not defend it
dek: Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard scored as Mikel Arteta's side opened their Premier League title defence with a routine win over newly promoted Coventry City — and the Arsenal captain framed the club's ambitions in strikingly different terms, according to ONE.
body: Arsenal wasted no time reminding the Premier League who is champion. Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka scored inside the first 23 minutes at the Emirates Stadium, and Martin Ødegaard added a third early in the second half, as Mikel Arteta's side opened their title defence with a comfortable 3-0 win over newly promoted Coventry City.

It was as routine as a season opener against Coventry could be for a team that spent all last season chasing, then finally catching, its first league crown in 22 years. Arsenal wrapped up the 2025-26 Premier League with a game to spare, their 14th top-flight title and Arteta's first as a manager, ending a wait that stretched back to Arsène Wenger's Invincibles of 2003-04.

This time the champions came out swinging rather than sitting on what they had already won. According to a report by Israeli outlet ONE, captain Ødegaard set the tone before a ball was even kicked, saying Arsenal's mentality this season is not to defend the title but to go after it again. "We don't feel we need to defend anything," Ødegaard said, according to ONE. "We want to do it again, and that's our mentality — we want to attack the title."

He backed the words up with a goal of his own, converting four minutes into the second half to put the result beyond doubt. Speaking after the match, Ødegaard pointed to the depth now available to Arteta: "The quality in the squad is unbelievable. You can put anyone on the pitch and they can perform at the highest level," he said, adding that the opening-night nerves eased once Havertz's early strike settled the game down.

Arteta agreed with his captain's read of the performance. "There was a lot to like," the Arsenal manager said. "We were really dominant and flowed with the ball, connecting well with one another... Overall the performance was positive with some big individual performances."

The win carried personal significance for Arteta too. His 150th Premier League victory as a manager arrived in his 249th match in charge of Arsenal, making him only the fifth manager in the competition's history to reach the landmark inside 250 games — following Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Sir Alex Ferguson, all of whom got there faster.

Much of the pre-match talk had centred on Arsenal's newest attacker, Christos Tzolis, and he did not disappoint on his competitive debut. The Greek winger, signed from Club Brugge for a reported £34 million on a five-year deal to replace Leandro Trossard, lined up on the left and gave Coventry's back line a torrid evening.

Arteta said afterwards he "was really impressed" by what he saw from the new signing, while Sky Sports co-commentator Jamie Carragher put it more bluntly on air: "What a left-winger Arsenal have got."

Ødegaard, too, was full of praise for the 24-year-old. According to ONE, the Arsenal captain called Tzolis "brilliant" and described him as "intense and very difficult to defend against... intelligent, always lifting his head."

Arteta pointed to the understanding already forming between his front players, with Saka and Ødegaard combining down the right and Tzolis stretching the game on the opposite flank. "When you talk about connection and chemistry, those three have that," he said.

For Coventry City, newly promoted and handed the champions on the opening weekend, it was a chastening reintroduction to the top flight, and a reminder of the gap Arsenal have opened up on much of the division after last season's title run. If Ødegaard's words are anything to go by, the champions have no intention of easing off — one win from one game, with the captain already talking about attacking rather than defending, sets an ambitious marker for the 37 fixtures still to come.

title: Palace manager rules out Real Madrid move for Wharton, hails Israeli signing Khalaili
dek: Pierre Sage says his Conference League-winning midfielder needs another year at Selhurst Park, using the same press conference to talk up the club's record £21m capture of Anan Khalaili.
body: Crystal Palace's new manager Pierre Sage used his final press conference before Saturday's season opener against Everton to close down talk of a Real Madrid move for Adam Wharton — while making sure the room also heard about the club's record-breaking Israeli recruit.

"I think now is not the moment to do that," Sage said of a possible sale, according to ONE. "I think he is able to play in another club, in a big club, here or everywhere in Europe. But I think one year with us, with a new dynamic, will be good for him, and we need him. That's why I think he will stay with us."

Wharton, 22, has been strongly linked with Real Madrid this summer, with Manchester City and Liverpool also credited with interest in the England midfielder. His stock has never been higher: he made 34 Premier League appearances last season and was named man of the match as Palace won the UEFA Conference League final, a run that has pushed his estimated market value beyond £80 million.

Sage, appointed in June to replace Oliver Glasner, stopped short of ruling out a future exit, hinting the situation would be reassessed next summer. For now, though, he was unambiguous that Palace have no intention of selling a player under contract until 2029 with the new Premier League season about to begin.

The same press conference doubled as an update on Palace's transfer business, and here the club's Israeli contingent took centre stage. Sage confirmed the signing of Anan Khalaili, the Israel international who completed a £21 million move from Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise earlier this month.

The deal makes the 21-year-old the most expensive Israeli player in history, eclipsing every previous transfer involving an Israeli footballer. Khalaili, comfortable at both full-back and on the wing, has signed a contract at Selhurst Park running to 2031.

His arrival in south London came only after a proposed switch to Inter Milan collapsed. Khalaili had agreed personal terms and passed a medical with the Serie A club, but the transfer fell through when he failed to clear a medical examination required by the Italian Olympic Committee, opening the door for Palace to move in.

Sage described Khalaili as part of a squad rebuild that has already brought six new arrivals through the door this summer, and said he expects one or two further additions before the transfer window closes.

For Wharton, the message from his manager is clear: stay, help Palace defend their European trophy and push the club forward, with a bigger move to be revisited only once this season is done. For Khalaili, the challenge now is breaking into a Premier League squad that starts its title defence of the Conference League and its top-flight campaign in the same week.

title: Al-Nassr 4-0 Al-Riyadh: Ronaldo marks post-wedding return with record-equalling goal
dek: Ten days after marrying Georgina Rodríguez, the 41-year-old came off the bench to level Mohammed Al-Sahlawi's all-time scoring record for the Saudi club.

verificationSources.label: ONE - הנישואים של כריסטיאנו החזירו לו את הנעורים

body: Saudi and Portuguese outlets are calling it football's most unlikely rejuvenation story: ten days after marrying Georgina Rodríguez in Portugal, Cristiano Ronaldo came off the bench to help fire Al-Nassr to a 4-0 win over Al-Riyadh, scoring a goal that made him the club's outright leading marksman of the professional era.

The Roshn Saudi League fixture, played at the Prince Faisal bin Fahd Stadium in Riyadh, saw Ronaldo introduced in the 62nd minute. Just 21 minutes later, with Al-Nassr already cruising, he turned in a low cross from teammate Ayman Yahya with his left foot to open his goal account for the season.

It was more than just a consolation strike in a routine rout. The goal took Ronaldo to 103 league goals for Al-Nassr in the professional era, level with club legend Mohammed Al-Sahlawi's long-standing record, from 108 appearances that have also produced 19 assists — 122 goal contributions in total.

According to the Saudi newspaper Al-Riyadiyah, the strike carried a second landmark too: it means Ronaldo has now scored in 25 consecutive seasons, moving him past Zlatan Ibrahimović, who had held the record outright at 24.

ONE reports that Saudi media have framed the outing as proof the 41-year-old's marriage has restored his youth, pointing to his energy in the warm-up and his animated, coach-like presence on the touchline during the stretches he was not on the pitch.

It was Ronaldo's first appearance since Portugal's World Cup ended in heartbreak on July 6, when Spain's Mikel Merino scored a 91st-minute winner in a 1-0 last-16 defeat in Dallas. Ronaldo confirmed afterwards that he would not attempt to play in a seventh World Cup.

He and Rodríguez, together since 2016, married on August 11 in a private ceremony in the Portuguese resort town of Cascais, attended by their five children and four witnesses, before confirming the news themselves on social media.

Al-Nassr's head coach, Ange Postecoglou, had eased Ronaldo back gradually, resting him for the club's Saudi Pro League opener — a 3-0 win over Al-Fateh on August 15 — and for a King's Cup tie against Al-Diriyah, before restoring him to the matchday squad against Al-Riyadh.

Postecoglou has been candid that managing his star forward's workload, and his sheer appetite for playing, is one of the defining challenges of his time at the club, saying it is a habit that "needs managing" given Ronaldo's age and the demands of Saudi Arabia's climate.

For now, though, the numbers are doing the talking: a share of Al-Nassr's all-time scoring record, a new consecutive-seasons landmark, and a player who, by his own club's account, looks anything but finished.

body: Barcelona may already have stumbled onto their long-term answer at centre-forward, and he is only 18. ONE reports that Hansi Flick has been won over by Hamza Abdelkarim, the young Egyptian striker now considered a genuine option to lead the line this season following the club's departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

Abdelkarim arrived at Barcelona on loan from Al Ahly in January before the Spanish club triggered a permanent option, a deal completed for a fee in the region of €1.5 million. He has since been fast-tracked out of the academy system and into first-team training under Flick.

The German coach's admiration became public property when Abdelkarim scored twice off the bench in a pre-season friendly against Birmingham City wearing the No. 9 shirt — the first player to do so for Barcelona since Lewandowski's exit. "That's what I ask of a No. 9," Flick said afterwards, praising the teenager's movement and instinct inside the box.

According to ONE, Barcelona's hierarchy is now moving to reward that impact with an improved and extended contract, with the striker's modest release clause set to jump roughly tenfold, from around €15 million to €150 million — a figure not yet officially confirmed by the club.

Abdelkarim's rise has been rapid. He was Egypt's youngest-ever player at a World Cup after Hossam Hassan picked him for the 2026 tournament in June, and he arrives at Barcelona with a reputation built on 12 goals in 21 appearances for Egypt's under-17s.

Even so, ONE notes Barcelona are not relying solely on the teenager and continue to weigh alternatives at centre-forward, chiefly Monaco's Folarin Balogun, 25, who scored 19 goals in 43 appearances last season and is also drawing interest from Tottenham and Aston Villa.
For now, though, the No. 9 shirt sits on the back of a player who was in Al Ahly's academy system barely a year ago — and Flick, by his own admission, likes what he has seen.

title: Simeone includes Julián Álvarez in squad for Villarreal clash, warns fans off the abuse
dek: The Atlético Madrid coach confirmed his wantaway striker will be part of Sunday's matchday squad and said he will not tolerate insults directed at him as the Barcelona transfer saga drags on.
body: Diego Simeone drew a line, for now, under the Julián Álvarez affair on Saturday, confirming the unsettled Argentine will be part of Atlético Madrid's squad for Sunday's home LaLiga game against Villarreal and warning his own supporters against abusing the striker.

Álvarez has spent the opening days of the season at the centre of a messy transfer saga, with the forward making no secret of his desire to leave for Barcelona. Simeone left him out of the squad entirely for Atlético's league opener against Málaga, citing his physical condition after a stop-start pre-season.

That match ended with a section of the Metropolitano crowd, in the south stand, directing insults at Álvarez over his push to leave the club he joined from Manchester City. Simeone's initial response to the jeering was muted, and only in the build-up to the Villarreal game did he address it directly.

"My respect for the fans is absolute, but I will not accept curses or insults," Simeone told reporters, according to ONE, drawing a clearer line than he had in the immediate aftermath of the Málaga match.

The coach was unambiguous about where Álvarez stands within his squad, regardless of the noise around his future. "Julián is important, we need him, and we are going to support him," he said, adding a near-identical line moments later: "He's very important, we need him, we're going to look after him."

Simeone also pushed back on any suggestion that Álvarez's professionalism has slipped amid the transfer speculation. "Julián trains in the best possible way, with respect toward his teammates," he said, describing the striker's conduct on the training ground as beyond reproach.

Asked to look ahead, the Argentine coach steered the conversation firmly back to football. "The important thing is Villarreal, and nothing else," he said, keen to shift focus away from the transfer noise and onto a Sunday fixture Atlético need to win to build early-season momentum.

Kick-off at the Metropolitano is set for 18:00 Israel time on Sunday, with ONE carrying the match live. Whether Simeone actually starts Álvarez, and how the home crowd reacts if he does, remains the open question hanging over the club's start to the campaign.

The Barcelona move itself remains unresolved, with talks between the clubs continuing in the background. For now, Simeone's message is that his squad list, not the transfer saga, will decide who plays.
