title: Beitar Jerusalem held 2-2 by Hapoel Rishon LeZion as Maccabi and Hapoel Petah Tikva win on Youth Gimel opening weekend
dek: Yossi Sabah and Itamar Duga had Beitar's youth side ahead before Nitai Ziv struck back for Rishon LeZion, while Maccabi Petah Tikva thrashed Hapoel Hadera 4-0 as Israel's top Youth Gimel division opened its third straight season, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - בית"ר סיימה בתיקו, מכבי והפועל פ"ת ניצחו

body: Israeli youth football kicked back into gear this weekend as the top flight of the Youth Gimel age group opened its third consecutive season, and the results did not lack for goals. Four matches — one played on Friday, three on Saturday — produced 12 goals between them, with Beitar Jerusalem the headline name left frustrated by a draw, ONE reported.

Beitar's opener, away to Hapoel Rishon LeZion on Friday, set the tone for the weekend. The hosts led at the interval through Yahli Haziza's finish in the 17th minute, only for Beitar to hit back twice after the restart: Yossi Sabah levelled early in the second half, and Itamar Duga put the visitors in front in the 46th minute.

Rishon LeZion, coached by Lidor Malka, refused to fold. His side found a second equaliser through Nitai Ziv to salvage a 2-2 draw. "We played a team that thrashed us in preseason, but I knew the league would be different," Malka said, according to ONE.

Saturday's programme brought three more fixtures. At Hapoel Tel Aviv, visitors Hapoel Raanana claimed a 1-0 win through Omer Grayev, who struck in the 39th minute after scoring eight goals for Hapoel Kfar Saba last season. "It's always nice to open a season on the right foot, especially with a win like this against an excellent side like Hapoel Tel Aviv," Raanana coach Liad Yagel said, per ONE.

The day's biggest scoreline came at Hapoel Hadera, thrashed 4-0 at home by Maccabi Petah Tikva. Michael Yaakov opened the account inside eight minutes, and further goals from Harel Ness in the 55th minute and Ido Kahana in the 76th were rounded off by Eliraz Twito.

Hapoel Petah Tikva completed the weekend's set of results with a 2-1 win at Hapoel Kfar Saba. Ori Tzarkatzi put the visitors ahead in the 21st minute, and an own goal in first-half stoppage time made it 2-0, before Or Ganish pulled one back for the hosts from the penalty spot in the 57th minute.

None of it will trouble the senior game, but for a division built to develop the next generation of Israeli footballers, an opening weekend with 12 goals, two comebacks and one dramatic late equaliser was as good an advertisement as any for the season ahead.

title: Dolgopyat's third European floor gold puts him on course to be Israel's greatest-ever athlete
dek: A 14.466 in Zagreb gave Artem Dolgopyat a third continental floor title and, ONE argues, a serious claim to being the finest athlete Israel has produced.

verificationSources.label: Israel National News — Dolgopyat wins third European title

body: Artem Dolgopyat stuck his landing in Zagreb on Friday evening, raised his arms, and added another line to what is quietly becoming the most decorated individual career in Israeli sporting history. His 14.466 on floor exercise at the European Gymnastics Championships was enough for gold, his third continental title on the apparatus, and it has prompted ONE to ask a question that no longer sounds like hyperbole: is Dolgopyat already Israel's greatest athlete?

The final in Croatia was tight only on paper. Arsenii Dukhno, the Russian gymnast competing as a neutral under the World Gymnastics 2 designation, took silver with 14.333, while Britain's Harry Hepworth was third on 14.300. Dolgopyat, 29, controlled the routine from the opening tumbling pass and never looked troubled by the field around him.

It was his third European floor title, following victories in 2020 and 2022, and it moves him level with Romanian great Marian Drăgulescu's record haul of medals on the apparatus at the championships, according to ONE. Between the Olympics, World Championships and Europeans, Dolgopyat has now reached 15 major finals on floor exercise and left with a medal from 12 of them — missing out just three times.

The floor résumé sits inside a wider body of work that already ranks among the best Israel has produced in any sport: two Olympic medals — gold at Tokyo 2020 and silver at Paris 2024 — three World Championship medals and eight European Championship medals across his events. Few Israeli athletes in any discipline have sustained that level of podium consistency for close to a decade.

ONE's comparison points to two other Israeli greats as the benchmark. Arik Ze'evi, the judoka who competed at four Olympics and retired with nine European Championship medals including four golds, has long been held up as the standard for longevity and continental dominance. Swimmer Anastasia Gorbenko, by ONE's count, has gone one better again with six European gold medals and no colour below it.

By that measure Dolgopyat is closing in on Ze'evi's medal count but still trails Gorbenko's run of pure gold — a gap ONE frames as the last obstacle between him and the title of Israel's finest-ever competitor.

What tips the argument in Dolgopyat's favour, in ONE's telling, is what still lies ahead. At 29, and with the discipline and mileage he has shown deep into his career, a third Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028 is a realistic target. A medal there — of any colour — would make him the first Israeli athlete to stand on an Olympic podium three times, a distinction that would be difficult for any rival, past or present, to match.

Dolgopyat's story has always carried an extra layer beyond the scoresheets. Born in Ukraine, he moved to Israel with his family at 12 and rose through the ranks of Israeli gymnastics to become, in Tokyo, the country's first-ever Olympic gold medallist in the sport. Five years and a Paris silver later, Zagreb was another reminder that his prime shows no sign of ending.

title: Kiryat Shmona plot a quiet season after losing Mordechai and Martínez
dek: Shay Barda begins a fourth season in charge with a reshaped, budget-conscious squad after top scorer Yair Mordechai left for Maccabi Haifa and Cristian Martínez was sold to Slovan Bratislava.

verificationSources.label: Israel Hayom - כך יאיר מרדכי הגיע למכבי חיפה

body: Kiryat Shmona head into the new Ligat Ha'al season without the two players most responsible for last season's goals, and ONE's close-season audit of the northern club finds a squad, and a coach, who believe they can get by without them.

The headline exit is Yair Mordechai, whose breakout campaign in Kiryat Shmona colours earned him a four-year contract at Maccabi Haifa on a free transfer this past May. Kiryat Shmona still came away with roughly 700,000 shekels in training compensation for a player who was directly involved in 16 goals last season — 10 scored, six assisted.

The second departure hit the wallet more than the trophy cabinet. Panamanian midfielder Cristian Martínez — referred to in Hebrew coverage simply as Martins — was sold to Slovan Bratislava on a three-year deal, a move that gathered pace after he was named man of the match in Panama's group game against Croatia at this year's World Cup. He reunites with countryman César Blackman, already established at the Slovak champions.

Between them, Mordechai and Martínez were the two names Kiryat Shmona fans most associated with last season's attack, which is why ONE frames the summer less as routine turnover and more as a squad being rebuilt specifically around their absence.

Steadying the ship is Shay Barda, who begins his fourth season in charge. He joined in the summer of 2023 straight after relegation and got Kiryat Shmona back into the top flight within a single campaign, form that has since earned him a contract extension and, per ONE, a strong hand in shaping the squad.

The confirmed incoming business is modest by design. Goalkeeper Nikola Jurković has arrived as back-up to Daniel Tenenbaum, while defender Shon Edri, 22, and left-back Shay Sbach have both signed one-year deals that carry a club option for a further season — the kind of low-risk, developmental signings that have become Barda's trademark in Kiryat Shmona.

ONE's report also lists a longer roll of squad additions — among them Alexander Solla, Tales Costa, Roubeté Abdulazada, Awajú Aspeah, Amadou Sanneh and Niv Gabai — though the exact English spellings of those names, transliterated from Hebrew, have not been independently corroborated beyond ONE's own coverage.
Outward traffic beyond the two headline sales includes Aviv Abraham and Lial Dare, both moving on as Barda trims a squad that was never built for great depth in the first place.

One situation remained unresolved at the time of ONE's report: forward Adrian Ogryska, signed from abroad in the summer of 2025, had yet to have his future formally settled, though the expectation inside the club was that he would stay and lead the line again.

ONE puts the total summer budget, youth department included, at around 30 million shekels — enough to keep the operation running but not to chase anything beyond a settled mid-table finish. Kiryat Shmona, still playing home fixtures in Netanya for a third consecutive season, are projected to land somewhere between seventh and ninth, with a returning defence and Ogryska's threat up top offsetting a squad that, on paper, still looks thin.

title: Jonathan Motley: 'I sat too much on the bench at Hapoel Tel Aviv'
dek: The EuroCup Finals MVP opens up on a frustrating Euroleague debut season before completing his summer move to Crvena Zvezda.

verificationSources.label: Eurohoops: Johnathan Motley completes move from Hapoel to Crvena Zvezda
Sportando: Crvena Zvezda officially signs Johnathan Motley
Basketnews: Milos Teodosic returns to Crvena Zvezda in new role
Israel Hayom: the crisis of Jonathan Motley at Hapoel Tel Aviv

body: Jonathan Motley has never been shy about numbers, and the one that stuck with him from his final season at Hapoel Tel Aviv was minutes, or the lack of them. Days into his new life at Crvena Zvezda, the American center told Sport5 he had grown frustrated watching games from the bench in Tel Aviv. "I love to play basketball," he said. "I think last season I sat too much on the bench and feel that is not good for me."

It was a striking admission from a player who, only a year earlier, had been the toast of Israeli basketball. In the 2024-25 season Motley powered Hapoel to the club's first-ever European trophy, the BKT EuroCup, then was named Finals MVP after averaging 22.0 points as Hapoel beat Dreamland Gran Canaria for the title.

That triumph earned Hapoel a place in the EuroLeague for the first time, and Motley stayed on for the ride. But the step up proved harder than expected: his production dropped to 8.3 points a game in EuroLeague action last season, even as he shot an efficient 65.4 percent on two-pointers, while in Israel's domestic Winner League he averaged 14.1 points across his two seasons in red.

In July, with his role diminished, Motley completed a multi-year move to Crvena Zvezda — Red Star Belgrade — joining a Serbian club rebuilding around new head coach Ibon Navarro ahead of the 2026-27 EuroLeague campaign. He arrives alongside fellow summer signings David Kramer, Chris Jones and Nikola Djurišić.

Jones, in particular, gives Motley a head start. The two played together in Hapoel's second unit, and the American forward said the reunion means plenty. "It is very significant for me, because we were together in the second unit," Motley said. "He was my center most of the time and I played with him more than anyone else. He probably 'cooked' for me 40 to 50 percent of the baskets."

Motley has also been leaning on Red Star connections from further afield. He met Boban Marjanović in New York over the summer, and the veteran Serbian center — a hero figure at the club — offered a very practical piece of advice about life in Belgrade. "The main advice was to be careful in meetings with fans of other teams, because I can meet them on the street," Motley recalled. "He told me to be careful, enjoy and have fun."

Vasilis Mitseas, another familiar face, talked up the move before it happened. He "told me all the good things I can expect from the fans, from Belgrade and also from Serbia," Motley said. "I am really looking forward to it."

Then there is Milos Teodosic, the Serbian playmaking great who has returned to Red Star in an off-court capacity. Motley did not hide his excitement at being around him again. "Milos is my man," he said. "He was an amazing passer. I can't wait to see him already. We are very close."

For all the goodwill, Motley was clear about what he actually wants from the move: regular postseason basketball. "I have never missed the EuroLeague playoffs and that is my goal," he said. "I want to play in the EuroLeague playoffs, because I have never stayed out of it. I hope I can bring that to the team."

Hapoel Tel Aviv has already thanked Motley publicly for two seasons that included the most successful European run in the club's history. Whether the bench frustration that pushed him out fades in Belgrade will go a long way toward shaping Red Star's own chase for a EuroLeague playoff return this season.

title: Marseille 4-0 Strasbourg: Gouiri brace and late double seal statement Ligue 1 opener
dek: Amine Gouiri scored either side of a red card for Strasbourg's Samir El Mourabet as Bruno Genesio's side ran riot at the Vélodrome to open the season.
body: Olympique de Marseille opened the 2026-27 Ligue 1 season with a statement, tearing apart Strasbourg 4-0 at a packed Stade Vélodrome, with Amine Gouiri scoring either side of a Strasbourg red card to set the tone for Bruno Genesio's team.

The first half was a cagey, goalless affair, but Marseille needed only a minute of the second period to break the deadlock. Igor Paixão fed Angel Gomes, who slipped in Gouiri for a first-time finish that sent the Vélodrome into raptures barely 60 seconds after the restart.

Strasbourg's afternoon then unravelled further. Defender Samir El Mourabet was shown a straight red card after referee Ruddy Bouquet was sent to the pitchside monitor and identified an off-the-ball swipe at Pierre-Emile Højbjerg, leaving the visitors to play the remainder of the match a man short.
Gouiri made the extra man count from the penalty spot in the 68th minute, calmly converting to complete his brace and put the result beyond reasonable doubt.

Marseille were not finished. Substitute Keyliane Abdallah added a third late on, before Højbjerg — stripped of the club captaincy over the summer — rounded off the scoring in second-half stoppage time to make it 4-0.
It was an emphatic response from Genesio's squad, who arrived at the season having faced financial strain and criticism from sections of the Marseille support during the close season.

For Strasbourg, freshly reinforced under their Chelsea-linked ownership model in recent seasons, it was a chastening way to begin the campaign, undone by a slow start and a costly moment of indiscipline.
Genesio's side will look to build on the opening-day statement when they travel to face Monaco on August 30, in what already shapes up as an early test of their title credentials.

title: Arsenal 3-0 Coventry: Havertz, Saka and Odegaard open title defence in style
dek: Debutant Christos Tzolis set up two goals as the champions began their Premier League defence with a comfortable win over newly promoted Coventry City at the Emirates.

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports transfer report on Tzolis

body: Arsenal opened their Premier League title defence with real authority on Friday night, brushing aside newly promoted Coventry City 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium to launch the 2026-27 season in ruthless fashion.

Mikel Arteta's side needed only 15 minutes to break the deadlock. Christos Tzolis dispossessed Coventry defender Van Ewijk, releasing Riccardo Calafiori, who found Kai Havertz in space; the German striker steered a first-time finish into the far corner.

Tzolis, Arsenal's marquee summer arrival, was at the heart of the second goal too. Eight minutes after the opener, his low cross was parried by Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth straight into the path of Bukayo Saka, who rolled the ball into an empty net.

The Greece international's hand in both goals made for a memorable Premier League debut. Arsenal signed the 24-year-old winger from Club Brugge for £34m in the close season, a club-record fee for the Belgian league, as a direct replacement for Leandro Trossard, and he wasted little time repaying that outlay.

Arsenal added a third just four minutes into the second half. Saka combined with Ben White down the right, and the ball eventually fell to Martin Odegaard, whose scuffed effort deflected in off a wrong-footed Rushworth to make it 3-0.

Coventry, back in the top flight for the first time in 25 years under former Chelsea midfielder Frank Lampard, barely got a foothold. Per Opta data collected since 2007, the visitors became the first team in Premier League history to record no touches in the opposition box and no tackles in an entire first half; their first tackle of the match did not come until the 69th minute, by which point they already trailed 3-0. Coventry's expected-goals tally for the match finished at just 0.28.
Sport5, covering the match for Israeli readers, summed up the gulf in class succinctly: Arsenal, the headline read, had given the newly promoted side "an important lesson."

For Arteta, the performance offers an ideal platform from which to defend the title Arsenal ended a 22-year wait to win last season. Friday's rout was also an early reminder that the champions have strengthened rather than stood still, with Tzolis looking every bit the shrewd addition to a squad already rich in attacking talent.

Coventry, by contrast, face a long road to prove they belong among the elite. A trip away from home next will offer a far truer test of how much Lampard's side can find once the shock of the top flight wears off.

title: Car rammed into house linked to Maccabi Tel Aviv coach Kenny Miller in Scotland
dek: Sport5 reports Police Scotland are treating Friday's incident in Waterfoot, Lanarkshire as part of a wider organised-crime feud, with sources stressing the Maccabi head coach was not the target and has no involvement in the case.

verificationSources.label: Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C. — Kenny Miller appointed head coach
Scottish Daily Express — Kenny Miller's Audi targeted in 2022 arson attack

body: A car was deliberately rammed into a house in Waterfoot, Lanarkshire on Friday evening, in an incident Sport5 reports is linked to the family of Maccabi Tel Aviv head coach Kenny Miller.
According to the Israeli outlet, the property belongs to Billy Steel, who is connected to Miller and his wife Laura. Nobody was hurt in the attack.

Sport5, citing Scottish sources, reports that the incident is tied to a feud among organised crime networks — understood to involve the Daniel crime family and Dubai-based figures on one side and a rival gang on the other — rather than to Miller himself. Sources quoted stressed the crash "has nothing to do with the Maccabi Tel Aviv coach" and that there is no suggestion Miller is involved in any criminal activity.

Police Scotland is investigating the ramming as part of a broader wave of gangland attacks that has swept parts of Scotland this year, with dozens of arrests already made across the country in connection with the wider feud.

It is not the first time an incident in Lanarkshire has touched Miller's circle. In January 2022, his Audi Q7 was doused with an accelerant and damaged outside a flat in Hamilton where he and Laura were staying with her mother, in an attack Police Scotland confirmed it investigated at the time, though no fire was successfully started.
Miller, 46, is a former Scotland international who played for Hibernian, Rangers, Celtic, Wolves, Cardiff City and Bristol City among others during a long club career before moving into coaching.
He took charge of Maccabi Tel Aviv on an interim basis last season, guiding the club to the Israeli State Cup, and was handed the head coach's job permanently in June 2026.

There is no indication the Friday incident will affect his position at Maccabi Tel Aviv, and Sport5's report frames it purely as a matter for Police Scotland's ongoing gangland investigation in Scotland.

title: Pyatov agonisingly misses parallel bars medal on countback in Zagreb
dek: The Israeli gymnast matched bronze medallist Joe Fraser's score of 14.300 but finished fourth on execution at the European Championships, a day after Artem Dolgopyat struck floor gold.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — 2026 European Men's Artistic Gymnastics Championships
Haaretz — Dolgopyat takes third European gold

body: Ron Pyatov came within a whisker of a first European senior medal on Saturday, finishing fourth in the men's parallel bars final at the European Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Zagreb after tying the bronze medallist's score but losing out on execution marks.

The Israeli, competing for Maccabi Tel Aviv, had qualified into the eight-man final in eighth place with 13.966 points. In the final itself he raised his game considerably, putting together a routine that earned 14.300 — matching Britain's Joe Fraser mark for mark.

Under gymnastics tiebreak rules, ties are broken by the higher execution score, and Fraser's superior execution mark saw the 2019 world parallel bars champion take bronze while Pyatov was pushed down to fourth, agonisingly close to the podium.
Gold went to the home favourite Illia Kovtun, the Croatia-based world and Olympic silver medallist on the apparatus, with 14.700, while Turkey's Ferhat Arıcan took silver on 14.433.

It capped a big weekend for Israeli gymnastics in Zagreb. A day earlier, Artem Dolgopyat had claimed his third European title on floor exercise, scoring 14.666 to beat the field including Great Britain's Harry Hepworth, who took bronze on 14.300 — the same mark that would decide Saturday's parallel bars podium.

For Pyatov, who has been building toward major finals through the World Cup and Challenge Cup circuit over the past year, a fourth-place finish at a European Championships final marks his best result yet on the senior international stage, even without the medal to show for it.

The Israeli team will hope to build on the display as the Zagreb championships move toward their closing events, with Dolgopyat's floor gold and Pyatov's near-miss both pointing to strength in depth for the national programme.

title: Real Madrid 2-1 Espanyol: Carlos Espí's late strike gives Mourinho a winning return
dek: Substitute striker Espí scores in stoppage time as José Mourinho's second spell as Real Madrid manager begins with a dramatic away win.
body: José Mourinho's long-awaited return to the Real Madrid dugout could hardly have gone more true to type. Trailing until the closing seconds against Espanyol, his side found their winner deep into stoppage time through a substitute few outside Valencia had heard of six months ago — and walked away 2-1 winners to open the Portuguese's second spell in Madrid with the smile of a man who always finds a way.

Jude Bellingham had given Real Madrid the perfect start at the RCDE Stadium on Saturday, heading in from an Arda Güler free-kick in the ninth minute. Espanyol responded before the half-hour mark, Álex Calatrava turning in Javi Hernández's cut-back for his first LaLiga goal to level the contest at 1-1.

The game looked destined for a draw until the first minute of stoppage time, when Carlos Espí — on for barely ten minutes — pounced on a loose ball in the box after Kylian Mbappé had been crowded out by two defenders. His low, first-time finish sent the away end into raptures and handed Mourinho victory in his first competitive match back in charge of the club he first managed between 2010 and 2013.

It was Espí's full debut for Real Madrid, and, as ONE reported this week, his emergence as a match-winner fits a story the Spanish and Israeli press have been building for weeks: the tale of Real's most unexpected new hero. In Madrid he is already being talked about as an heir to Joselu, the striker whose stoppage-time goals off the bench became folklore during the club's run to the 2024 Champions League title.

Espí's arrival at the Santiago Bernabéu came together in a matter of hours. He had been closing in on a move to Brighton in the Premier League when word reached him that Real Madrid had entered the race; he immediately broke off talks with the English club and signed for Mourinho instead.

Real Madrid and Levante agreed the transfer on 30 July, with Spanish and English outlets reporting a fee built around the €25 million release clause in Espí's Levante contract. Real Madrid's own statement did not disclose a figure, but confirmed he had signed through to 2031 — a striking commitment to a player who was largely unknown a year ago.

The rise has been rapid. Born in Tavernes de la Valldigna, in the Valencia region, Espí joined Levante's academy in 2022 after starting out at local club UD Alzira. He scored 11 of his goals in the second half of last season alone, a burst that played a direct part in keeping Levante in LaLiga, and was voted the division's best under-23 player. Real Madrid had already tried to take him to their Castilla reserve side back in March 2024, only for Levante to refuse.

He is now the fifth arrival of Mourinho's rebuilt squad this summer, following the higher-profile signings of Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konaté and Marc Cucurella, with record buy Yan Diomande also given his first involvement off the bench in Saturday's win. Espí is expected to operate as Mourinho's forward option from the bench — physical, direct, and able to change a stuck game, in the mould that once suited Joselu and, before him, Gonzalo García, whom Espí effectively replaces in the squad.

For Mourinho, the outcome doubled as a personal statement. Saturday marked his first match in Real Madrid's dugout in 13 years, since he left the club in 2013, and the win extended an eye-catching managerial record: he has now won his managerial debut with every club he has taken charge of, seven in a row across his career.

Real Madrid, chasing a return to the top after two trophyless seasons and the shadow of Barcelona's recent domestic dominance, will hope Espí's stoppage-time intervention is the first of many rather than a one-off headline. For now, an unheralded striker from Levante has given Mourinho's second era in Madrid the perfect opening line.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem unveils new club emblem after fan revolt over leaked design
dek: The basketball club brought in two fan graphic designers to help finish the badge after supporters petitioned against an earlier version that leaked online.
body: Hapoel Jerusalem's basketball club finally unveiled its new emblem on Sunday, ending weeks of public wrangling that pitted the ownership's rebranding ambitions against a fanbase deeply attached to its old crest, ONE reported.

The saga began when an initial redesign, commissioned from a branding agency, leaked on social media roughly a week and a half before a planned launch event. Supporters did not just object to the idea of a new badge — they revolted against the specific design that had leaked, and the club shelved the unveiling.

A petition titled "Don't touch Hapoel Jerusalem's emblem" gathered well over a thousand signatures within hours, describing the crest as more than graphics — "the connection between generations of fans," per Ynet. Sport5 reported the tally climbing past 1,300 in the following days.
Club management responded by pausing the process and putting three alternative designs to a members' vote, Walla reported at the time, though even that consultation failed to fully calm the backlash.

For the final version unveiled Sunday, ONE reports the club brought in two supporters who work as graphic designers, Adam Amorai and Itamar Libergel, to help finish the emblem alongside the branding team.

The result keeps the club's familiar elements — the laborer figure, a basketball and Jerusalem's lions — but renders them in a more modern style intended, the club said, to bridge Hapoel Jerusalem's past and its future.

The wider campaign carries the slogan "Devotion Inspires" and was developed by the agency Firma after research that included fan focus groups and interviews with hundreds of supporters, according to ONE.
"This strategic rebrand is a declaration of intent about what kind of club we want to become," owner Matan Adelson said, describing it as the next chapter rather than a break from the club's story.
CEO Oren Ariely called the moment a "critical juncture" for the club, saying Hapoel Jerusalem wants to lead "not just on the court, but in fan experience, digital presence, community and innovation."

The row over a badge landed in a tense summer around the club. Hapoel Jerusalem had a quiet transfer window and lost guard Cadin Carrington to city rivals Hapoel Tel Aviv, even as Tel Aviv clubs strengthened their rosters, while new head coach Sasha Obradovic prepares to take over on the bench.

Adelson, the American businessman who bought a controlling stake in the club in 2023, has repeatedly said he wants Hapoel Jerusalem to grow into a leading brand capable of competing for a Euroleague place. The new emblem is the clearest visual marker yet of that ambition — even if it took a fan revolt to get there.

title: Itamar Roitman joins Hapoel Galil Elyon as head of scouting and assistant coach

body: Hapoel Galil Elyon have strengthened their basketball backroom staff ahead of the new season, bringing in Itamar Roitman as head of scouting and assistant coach, ONE reports.

The Upper Galilee club confirmed the appointment in a statement, saying it was pleased to welcome Roitman to its ranks as he takes charge of the scouting department alongside his assistant coaching duties.

Roitman arrives with a working relationship already in place with Galil Elyon's head coach, Idan Avshalom. The pair previously worked together at Elitzur Netanya, where Roitman served as a scout and assistant to the professional manager.

At Netanya, Roitman was closely involved in identifying and recruiting the club's foreign players, giving him direct experience in the kind of market knowledge Galil Elyon's management is now hoping to tap into.

Avshalom himself moved to Kfar Blum in January, taking over the Galil Elyon bench after Guy Yizraeli was dismissed midway through the previous campaign, so the reunion effectively rebuilds part of the coaching partnership the two had at Netanya.

For a club competing in Israel's top basketball flight from the Upper Galilee, adding a dedicated scouting lead is a modest but notable investment in professional infrastructure as the roster is finalised before the new season.

title: Maccabi Haifa 2-1 Hapoel Ramat Gan: Bruninho brace answers the doubters on opening night
dek: Channel ONE asked whether the Brazilian signing alone could carry Maccabi Haifa this season — on Ligat Ha'al's opening weekend, he scored twice to beat newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan.
body: On the eve of Ligat Ha'al's kickoff, Channel ONE's nightly chat show Sicha HaYom put the obvious question to its panel: is Bruninho, Maccabi Haifa's big summer buy, really enough on his own to carry the team? Forty-eight hours later, on the actual pitch, the Brazilian gave about as emphatic an answer as a footballer can.
Maccabi Haifa opened the 2026/27 season with a 2-1 win over newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan at Sammy Ofer Stadium on Saturday, and Bruninho scored both of the home side's goals.

He put Haifa ahead in the 22nd minute with a driven strike from distance after Ramat Gan failed to properly clear their lines, then doubled the lead just a minute into the second half, capping a first-half performance in which he was comfortably the best player on the pitch.

Ramat Gan, back in the top flight this season after a 13-year absence, did not fold. Maxim Falckouschenko pulled a goal back in the 61st minute, teed up by Luan Campos, to set up a nervy finish for the hosts.

It got nervier still in stoppage time. Referee Omer Biran pointed to the spot for Maccabi Haifa in the 89th minute and, after a VAR review, stuck with his call — but Eitan Azulai's penalty was saved by Ramat Gan goalkeeper Amit Raif, sparing the visitors an even heavier defeat.

Head coach Barak Bachar, starting his third spell in charge of the club, made no secret of where the credit belonged afterwards. "Bruninho proved he's quality," he said, according to Sport1. "It's a madhouse here."

The result will have been a relief inside the club after a shaky pre-season that included defeats in the Toto Cup. It also goes some way to justifying the outlay on Bruninho, who signed for Haifa in late June on a three-year deal reported at around €1.75 million — said at the time to be the third-highest transfer fee in the club's history.

Bruninho, full name Bruno Roberto Ferreira da Silva, is a 26-year-old winger from Belo Horizonte who came through the Atlético Mineiro academy before spending much of his career on loan in Brazil's second tier. He arrived in Haifa from Ukrainian side Karpaty Lviv, where he had impressed with goal contributions before newly installed sporting director Lior Refaelov pushed to get the deal over the line.
It is early — one round, one performance — but Bruninho has at least given Haifa's fans a concrete reason to believe the question posed on ONE's airwaves this week has an encouraging answer.

title: A new era: how Liverpool are rebuilding their attack after Salah's exit
dek: Andoni Iraola opens his first full season at Anfield leaning on Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, as Liverpool count the cost of missing out on Yan Diomande and chase Bradley Barcola to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah's move to Trabzonspor.

verificationSources.label: Sky Sports - Isak joins Liverpool in British-record deal

body: Liverpool begin the 2026-27 season having to answer a question that looked unthinkable a year ago: how do you replace Mohamed Salah? The Egyptian's exit from Anfield was finalised this summer when he signed for Turkish club Trabzonspor, closing a nine-year spell in which, ONE reports, he scored 257 goals in Liverpool's colours.

It is the first time since 2015 that Liverpool have opened a season without their biggest attacking threat, and the club have changed manager in the same window. Andoni Iraola has taken over from Arne Slot, whose solitary season in charge ended in a fifth-place finish.

ONE reports that Iraola's Liverpool begin the new campaign at home to Newcastle, with the Basque coach expected to lean on the high-pressing, direct approach he built his reputation on at Bournemouth rather than Slot's more controlled possession game.

The scale of the rebuild shows in the numbers. With Salah gone, Cody Gakpo — who has scored 50 goals in Liverpool colours, according to the report — is now effectively the club's senior scorer among the current squad, a stark illustration of how much of the goal threat has walked out the door.

The attacking burden instead falls on Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Isak arrived from Newcastle last September in a British transfer-record £125 million deal but endured a stop-start first season on Merseyside, managing only four goals amid persistent injury trouble, ONE reports.

Wirtz, one of the club's marquee signings of recent windows, is expected to operate just behind Isak and link up with a midfield already stocked with Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch. Iraola, per the report, wants Isak focused as much on movement off the ball to create space for team-mates as on his own scoring.

Liverpool's succession plan for Salah did not go entirely to script. The club had identified Yan Diomande, then of RB Leipzig, as a potential long-term answer on the right flank, but the teenager snubbed Anfield in favour of Real Madrid, where Jose Mourinho's project and a direct approach from the coach reportedly proved decisive. The move, worth close to £120 million, became the most expensive transfer for an African player in history.

With that avenue closed, ONE reports Liverpool have turned their attention to Bradley Barcola at Paris Saint-Germain, though the numbers remain far apart — PSG said to be holding out for roughly £145 million against a Liverpool offer in the region of £100 million.

None of it changes the scale of what Iraola inherits: a squad still adjusting to life after its biggest star, a forward line yet to prove it can replace 257 goals, and a fanbase watching to see whether the next Anfield era can match the last one's highs without the player who defined so much of it.

title: István Kovács named referee for Hapoel Beer Sheva's Champions League playoff decider against Sabah
dek: The Romanian official, who took charge of last season's Champions League final, will oversee the second leg in Azerbaijan with Beer Sheva a result away from a first-ever league phase appearance

body: UEFA has handed the whistle for Hapoel Beer Sheva's Champions League playoff second leg against Sabah to István Kovács, the Romanian referee who took charge of last season's Champions League final between Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Milan, ONE reports.

The Israeli champions travel to Azerbaijan for Tuesday's return fixture holding a 2-1 lead from the first leg, meaning a draw alone is enough to send Ran Kozhoharov's side into the Champions League league phase for the first time in the club's history. It is the third time Beer Sheva have reached this playoff round, having lost narrowly on both previous occasions.

Kovács, 41, is one of UEFA's most established senior officials. Beyond last season's final in Munich, he has taken charge of finals in all three UEFA club competitions and has worked the past two European Championships and the past two World Cups, where he was the referee for the 1,000th match in World Cup history.

His reputation, however, is a mixed one. Kovács is known as a strict, card-heavy official, and he was suspended by UEFA until the end of last season after a contentious decision in a Champions League quarter-final between Barcelona and Atlético Madrid.
He will be assisted on the touchline by fellow Romanians Mihai Marica and Ferencz Tunyogi, with Germany's Bastian Dankert operating the video assistant referee system.

The first leg, played at Bucharest's Ghencea Arena as Beer Sheva's designated home fixture, swung Israel's way after Veljko Simić had put Sabah ahead early. Igor Zlatanović and Javon East scored to complete the turnaround and hand the Israeli champions the advantage heading into Azerbaijan.

Tuesday's second leg kicks off at 19:45 Israel time at the Bank Respublika Stadium in Masazir, on the outskirts of Baku. Victory or a draw there would guarantee Beer Sheva a place — and a substantial financial windfall — in next season's Champions League league phase for the first time in the club's history.

title: Maccabi Haifa open season with 2-1 win over Hapoel Ramat Gan as Ben Sahar says Yarin Levi's answer must come on the pitch
dek: A section of Sammy Ofer Stadium whistled the returning midfielder during the Ligat Ha'al opener, but former Haifa forward Ben Sahar insists most fans back him and that his best reply will be performances, not words.
body: Maccabi Haifa opened their 2026/27 Ligat Ha'al campaign with a 2-1 win over Hapoel Ramat Gan at Sammy Ofer Stadium on Saturday, but the storyline dominating the post-match conversation had little to do with the scoreline. It was about Yarin Levi, and whether the whistles that greeted him from a corner of the crowd are the start of a genuine problem.

Bruninho settled the contest almost single-handedly, curling a 20-metre effort into the corner to open the scoring and then converting early in the second half after Silva Kani squared the ball to him. Ramat Gan hit back through Maxim Palkushchenko in the 61st minute, but Haifa held on for the three points under Barak Bakhar, who begins a third stint in charge after signing a new contract over the summer.

Levi, 21, returned to Haifa this summer after two productive seasons on loan at Beitar Jerusalem, where he established himself as a key midfielder and was named the Ligat Ha'al's Discovery of the Season in 2024/25. The club has since committed to him long-term with a new, upgraded contract, seeing him as a player to build the squad around.

The reunion has not been entirely smooth. At his first open training session back in green, fans lifted Levi onto their shoulders but he did not join in a chant aimed at Beitar Jerusalem, a moment that went viral and drew calls from some Maccabi Haifa fan organisations for the club to move him on. Levi later posted on social media insisting he never intended to offend anyone, telling supporters he was "happy and excited to return to wearing the green shirt" and looking forward to seeing them at Sammy Ofer.

Appearing on ONE's "Sicha HaYom" programme after Saturday's win, former Haifa and Chelsea forward Ben Sahar addressed the whistles directly. "I actually heard that most fans were with him, clearly there's a small part that whistles, but Yarin Levi's best answer should come on the pitch," he said.

Sahar, who retired from playing in April after a career that also took in Portsmouth and Hapoel Tel Aviv, added that Levi looked to be building match fitness after his summer move. "Yarin Levi entered into fitness, you can see him finally arriving and not afraid, as he should be," he said on the programme.

He was equally pointed in his praise for Bruninho after the Brazilian's double. "Maccabi Haifa looks a bit better, especially Bruninho — without him the team would have looked different," Sahar said, crediting the forward with carrying much of the attacking threat in the opening round.

The defence drew a more critical assessment. "Defensively Maccabi Haifa still isn't good enough," Sahar said, suggesting a change in personnel could help matters. "I would go with Silva Kani, who would manage speed-wise" — a nod to pace as an antidote to the space Ramat Gan found in getting back into the game.

For now, the win keeps Bakhar's side top of the early table on goal difference alongside the other opening-day winners, and buys some breathing room in the Levi saga. Whether the whistles fade or grow louder will, as Sahar suggested, likely be decided less by statements and more by what Levi does with the ball at his feet in the weeks ahead.

title: Revivo says he remains committed to Maccabi Tel Aviv despite transfer talk
dek: Amid a stalled move to Spain's Elche, the left-back tells ONE his priority is the here and now: "While I'm here, I will do everything for the team and the fans."

body: Roy Revivo has spent the summer at the centre of one of Israeli football's messier transfer sagas, and on Sunday the Maccabi Tel Aviv left-back broke his own silence to insist that whatever happens next, his effort for the yellow-and-blue is not in question.
"It's no secret that my dream is to play abroad, but let it be clear to everyone — while I'm here, I will do everything for the team and the fans," Revivo said, in comments carried by ONE.

The 23-year-old, son of former Israel international Haim Revivo, has become one of the country's most sought-after defenders after establishing himself at left-back for both Maccabi Tel Aviv and the senior national team, for whom he has won 20 caps and featured at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

His future has been dragged out for weeks by interest from Elche, with the La Liga club's offer for Revivo reported to have climbed toward roughly €3.3 million as they push to complete a deal before the Spanish transfer window closes on 2 September.

The talks have repeatedly stalled over structure rather than headline price: Maccabi have been holding out for a bigger cut of any future sale, while also asking Revivo and his family to give up part of the 15 percent of the fee contractually owed to them personally — a sticking point his father has since criticised publicly.

The strain has shown. Revivo did not travel with the squad for a recent European fixture, with the player and new head coach Kenny Miller said to have agreed it was better for him to stay behind given his emotional state amid the uncertainty.

Elche are not his only suitors — reported interest from clubs in Italy and Portugal has also been strengthening — but with Revivo under contract at Bloomfield Stadium until June 2027, Maccabi retain full leverage over any exit, and nothing is imminent.
For now, Revivo's message was less about where he ends up and more about how he intends to conduct himself until a move, if one comes, is actually done.
